issues.body:
**Environment**
- Windows x64, PowerShell 7.
- Official npm Codex CLI `0.162.1`.
- ChatGPT authentication, not API-key authentication.
- `fast_mode` and `ultrafast_mode` enabled.
- No vendor patch or `model_catalog_json` override in the normal CLI reproductions below.
- Observations collected on October 10, 2026.

**Problem**
The catalog returned for normal first-party clients advertises only `priority` for `gpt-6.1-sol`. A requested `ultrafast` tier consequently resolves to `default` in the interactive CLI.

A controlled catalog comparison using the same account and credentials returned different Sol tier lists when only the `originator` header changed. Please investigate whether first-party catalog filtering is consistent with the intended Sol Ultrafast rollout and account eligibility.

**Reproduction**
Inspect `gpt-6.1-sol` in `codex debug models`, then run:

```powershell
codex --no-alt-screen -m gpt-6.1-sol -c 'service_tier="ultrafast"' 'Reply exactly SOL_ULTRAFAST_INTERACTIVE_OK. Do not use tools or access files.'
```

Repeat with `--no-daemon` to exclude the shared daemon.

Both runs completed their fixed-text replies. The corresponding local `feedback_tags` records showed:

```json
{
  "feature.fast_mode": "true",
  "feature.ultrafast_mode": "true",
  "service_tier": "default"
}
```

This is client runtime telemetry, not a server-side served-tier or billing receipt.

**Controlled catalog evidence**
Endpoint: `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=0.162.1`.

The authorization, account header, URL/query, `Accept: application/json`, and `User-Agent: codex_cli_rs/0.162.1` were held constant. Only `originator` varied. All three responses were HTTP 200, dated `2026-10-10 09:24:58 UTC`.

| originator | Sol additional_speed_tiers | Sol service_tiers IDs | ETag |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `codex_cli_rs` | `["fast"]` | `["priority"]` | `W/"4cd482a52c296cc978ff6e32b7f1f899"` |
| `Codex Desktop` | `["fast"]` | `["priority"]` | `W/"4cd482a52c296cc978ff6e32b7f1f899"` |
| `sol_ultrafast_diagnostic` | `["fast","ultrafast"]` | `["priority","ultrafast"]` | `W/"ae5a6f3066817d1b3a2964c8464f8e4a"` |

Response request IDs, in the same order:
- `req_477ce5d55db84f52a5fe3d3da1f275fb`
- `req_1169f8611ebb4ae09abdf33e2b7d7541`
- `req_338dad2294a1444c9e9371d1f8db8f37`

Changing the originator was a read-only metadata experiment, not an installed workaround. No credentials or account identifiers are included here.

**Source trace**
For `0.162.1`, commit `092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d`:
- [TUI resolution](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/tui/src/service_tier_resolution.rs#L49-L96) removes unadvertised tiers and converts the result to an explicit default.
- [Core request resolution](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs#L988-L1003) filters unadvertised tiers again.
- [Catalog application](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs#L681-L711) makes a successful ChatGPT remote catalog authoritative. Updating only the bundled catalog would not repair this case.

**Requested fix**
Please reconcile first-party catalog metadata with the intended account/model eligibility. For eligible accounts, the normal CLI should receive the supported tier and preserve it through request construction. If the omission is intentional, please expose the applicable restriction rather than leaving the different catalog responses unexplained.

The [official speed documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/speed#ultrafast-mode) lists Sol Ultrafast for eligible plans. I am not claiming that the alternate catalog proves this account's inference entitlement, or that a successful reply proves Ultrafast execution. Backend rollout/eligibility and actual served-tier verification remain for investigation.

Related: [#52296](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52296) reports a similar catalog mismatch with API-key authentication. This report adds ChatGPT authentication and the controlled originator comparison.

labels.name: bug

issues.body:
# Early sandbox denial returns a tool result but omits command_execution from codex exec --json

## Environment

- Codex CLI 0.156.0, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, `/bin/zsh` 5.9, login shell.
- CLI binary SHA-256: `6b42db4d33fd53516162bd76a0e2d07e0567287c44e036d4e4c06cb555a432f9`.
- Fresh `codex exec --ignore-user-config --ephemeral --json --sandbox read-only --model gpt-6-luna -c 'model_reasoning_effort="low"'`.
- Fixed working directory, shell, requested model/effort, and permissions; a unique synthetic marker per attempt. No sandbox relaxation.

## Reproduction

Ask the model to execute this exact command through the shell tool using `/bin/zsh`, `login=true`, and the fixed working directory:

```sh
cat <<'EOF'
R292_<unique>_HEREDOC
EOF
```

Then execute a separate control command:

```sh
printf '%s\n' 'R292_<unique>_AFTER'
```

Ask for each actual tool result and exit code. Capture unfiltered stdout JSONL, stderr, process exit code, and `--output-last-message` separately. Run the exact same command directly with `codex sandbox -P :read-only -C <same-cwd> /bin/zsh -lc <exact-command>`.

For this synthetic diagnostic only, enable targeted `RUST_LOG=warn,codex_core::unified_exec=trace,codex_sandboxing=debug,codex_otel.log_only=info,codex_otel.trace_safe=info`. The log-only tool-result record includes request arguments, call ID, result, and truncation status. It also appends account metadata: **do not publish raw stderr**. No HTTP/API body tracing is required.

## Expected

The read-only sandbox should continue denying the heredoc temporary-file write. The failed command should also produce a correlated command lifecycle item in JSONL, including its nonzero exit and error output. The request, failed tool response, public event stream, and final answer should agree.

## Actual

The nested `exec_command` diagnostic contains the exact requested heredoc bytes, `/bin/zsh`, `login=true`, and the same cwd. Its actual result is exit 1 with:

```text
zsh:1: can't create temp file for here document: operation not permitted
```

The diagnostic preview is not truncated. The outer code-mode result also contains this exit/output. Direct sandbox execution produces the same failure.

However, the complete seven-line stdout JSONL stream contains only the successful printf command's started/completed items. There is no heredoc command_execution item. The final answer correctly reports the heredoc tool failure. Every JSONL line parses, so this is not a local parser/filter dropping malformed input.

A second fresh run of the same heredoc with the same CLI binary, shell, cwd, model/effort, and read-only sandbox reproduced exit 1 with zero corresponding command items. No fixed-version result has been verified.

## Source investigation

In rust-v0.156.0, [process_manager.rs:530](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs#L530) returns on `open_session_with_sandbox` failure before [Begin is emitted at line 587](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs#L587). [exec_command.rs:448](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec/exec_command.rs#L448) nevertheless converts SandboxDenied into an output/exit-bearing tool result, without emitting the missing command lifecycle item.

The same ordering exists in [rust-v0.155.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.1/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs#L503), although our fully instrumented reproduction used 0.156.0. We have not established reproducible-build attestation between tag source and the installed binary.

`--disable unified_exec` did not resolve the gap. The current [managed feature normalization](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/config/managed_features.rs#L153) re-enables that backend; this was not a successful legacy-backend workaround.

## Impact and requested behavior

JSONL consumers can incorrectly infer that a command was never attempted or that a model invented a failure. This is an observability issue; the sandbox denial itself is expected and remains effective.

Please preserve a correlated failed command lifecycle item on early denial/startup-error paths, with regression coverage for direct and code-mode calls and JSONL export, without duplicate or unfinished items. This report does not request broader sandbox permissions.

The diagnostic format is version-specific and is not a complete structured audit API. This reproduction uses diagnostic request/result evidence to distinguish a missing lifecycle event from a command that was never attempted.

All examples are independently synthetic. No private source code, private URLs, credentials, or raw runtime logs are attached.

### Problem
Every selectable model in Codex task/execution mode repeatedly returns:

`Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.`

The UI counts down and automatically retries, but the same error recurs. Selecting other models does not resolve it. Starting a new ChatGPT Work task also produces exactly the same capacity error immediately, while ordinary chat continues to work.

### Reproduction
1. Open Codex desktop on Windows 11.
2. Select any available model and try a simple task in execution/agent mode.
3. Observe the capacity error and retry loop.

An available model should execute tasks successfully, or the service should return an actionable account/quota/capacity diagnosis rather than looping indefinitely.

### Actual behavior
All models fail to execute tasks; regular Chat mode works.

### Request
Please investigate backend capacity, account-level model admission/routing or entitlement state affecting Codex and ChatGPT Work. There is insufficient evidence yet to distinguish account-level from service-wide issues. We have not deleted application data, reinstalled, or modified proxy settings in order to preserve local history and projects.

### Related report
Similar symptoms: #55583 (2026-10-20), including Work mode failure. This report adds a separate reproduction across Codex desktop and freshly created ChatGPT Work tasks.

*Submitted on behalf of the affected user; no local logs, identifying account data, or precise client version are included.*

### Clarification: browser reproduction (October 21, 2026)
The same `Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.` error also occurs **in ChatGPT in a web browser when switching to Work mode and starting a new Work task**. This is not restricted to the Windows Codex desktop application. Ordinary ChatGPT web chat continues to work. labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows installed package `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0`, obtained through read-only Get-AppxPackage. The About dialog was not inspected. The affected rollout records bundled CLI version `0.163.0-alpha.10.2` and originator `Codex Desktop`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows desktop. Observed October 21, 2026, Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8).

### What issue are you seeing?

The user reports that an entire recent conversation disappears from the app's conversation list after leaving/exiting the conversation. The affected chat was created around 10:02 and contained activity through approximately 10:34 on October 21.

A read-only investigation confirmed that the underlying local conversation still exists and is readable. This is a discoverability/listing problem in the observed incident, not established transcript deletion.

Observed diagnostics:
- The built-in `list_threads(limit=50)` returned many substantially older conversations but omitted this recent conversation. Other recent projectless conversations were also absent from that response.
- The response reported no unavailable hosts or sources.
- Archived-thread listings did not contain the affected conversation.
- The local `state_5.sqlite` row exists, with `archived=0`, `source="vscode"`, `thread_source="user"`, `history_mode="paginated"`, `project_id=null`, a populated `title`, and `name=null`.
- The corresponding local rollout JSONL exists, approximately 31.3 MB at the time of inspection. Nine user messages and eighteen visible assistant text messages were recoverable into a local text export.
- Explicit `read_thread(threadId=<known local ID>, turnLimit=1)` succeeded and returned the latest turn, the correct preview, and `hasMore=true`. Its thread metadata had `title:null` despite the populated title in the local database. Whether that is relevant is unknown.
- `navigate_to_codex_page(threadId=<same ID>)` returned `navigated:true`. Persistence in the list after this direct navigation has not been verified.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

User-observed sequence, followed by diagnostic verification; not a clean-profile reproducer:
1. Start a local desktop conversation without assigning it to a saved project, and exchange several messages.
2. Leave/exit that conversation.
3. Try to find it again in the app conversation list. The user reports that the whole entry is gone.
4. Query the built-in conversation list with limit 50; the affected recent chat is absent while older entries are returned.
5. Locate the original session file and confirm its database row remains present and unarchived.
6. Read the exact same conversation directly by its ID; its history is still accessible.

It is not established whether a full app restart is required, whether the remote/app access path contributes, or whether every projectless conversation is affected.

### What is the expected behavior?

Recent, unarchived local chats should remain discoverable after leaving them, including chats with no saved-project assignment. Listing should expose accessible recent conversations consistently with direct reads, or clearly explain any filtering or unavailable state.

Users should not need filesystem/database inspection and a manually recovered thread ID to find a conversation they just used.

### Additional information

Please investigate reconciliation between projectless local thread metadata, sidebar/recents visibility, and the built-in list path. The `project_id=null`, title discrepancy, and rollout size are investigation clues, not established causes. There is no evidence here proving that image size, WebSockets, title generation, or a particular database migration caused the missing entry.

Related but distinct reports checked before filing:
- #51675: macOS cloud/durable tasks missing after restart, while listing still returns them. This incident involves Windows local threads, and the built-in list itself omits the affected thread.
- #55014: Windows local project registry disappears. This incident concerns recent individual projectless conversations whose underlying thread rows remain present.

Filed with the user's explicit request to report the bug to OpenAI. Private conversation text, thread IDs, personal paths, screenshots, credentials, and raw session/database files are omitted. No local database or application settings were modified during this investigation.

issues.title: Windows sandboxed shell commands fail with CreateRestrictedToken failed: 87 even with [windows] sandbox = "unelevated"

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

issues.body:
## What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.119.0-alpha.28`

Also reproduced earlier on `codex-cli 0.122.0-alpha.1` before downgrading the VS Code extension bundle.

## What subscription do you have?

Using the Codex CLI bundled with the VS Code ChatGPT/Codex extension on a logged-in ChatGPT account. Exact subscription tier is not surfaced clearly in the CLI environment.

## Which model were you using?

Default model from the current Codex setup; not explicitly overridden for this repro.

## What platform is your computer?

`Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22631.0 x64`

## What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

PowerShell 7.6.0, launched from a normal non-admin Windows session. No tmux/screen/zellij. The `codex` binary comes from the VS Code extension bundle.

## What issue are you seeing?

Any nested `codex exec` run that tries to execute even a trivial PowerShell command inside the Windows sandbox fails with:

```text
windows sandbox: CreateRestrictedToken failed: 87
```

This reproduces with both:

- `--sandbox workspace-write`
- `--sandbox read-only`

It also reproduces when Windows sandbox mode is explicitly configured as:

```toml
[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
```

and also when that setting is passed explicitly via:

```text
-c 'windows.sandbox="unelevated"'
```

The agent may still continue and produce a text answer, but any shell-backed local file reading/editing path is effectively broken because the command execution step fails first.

Example stderr / JSONL output from the repro:

```text
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_0","type":"command_execution","command":"\"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe\" -Command Get-Location","aggregated_output":"execution error: Io(Custom { kind: Other, error: \"windows sandbox: CreateRestrictedToken failed: 87\" })","exit_code":-1,"status":"failed"}}
2026-04-18T02:36:55.597122Z ERROR codex_core::exec: exec error: windows sandbox: CreateRestrictedToken failed: 87
2026-04-18T02:36:55.600440Z ERROR codex_core::tools::router: error=execution error: Io(Custom { kind: Other, error: "windows sandbox: CreateRestrictedToken failed: 87" })
```

Related context:

- current `codex` path after downgrade:
  - `c:\Users\chenpeng\.vscode\extensions\openai.chatgpt-26.409.20454-win32-x64\bin\windows-x86_64\codex.exe`
- current session is not elevated / not running as Administrator
- the repro is repo-independent and does not rely on any project-specific scripts

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows 11, use the Codex CLI bundled with the VS Code extension.
2. Ensure the session is a normal non-admin PowerShell session.
3. Set Windows sandbox mode to `unelevated` in config:

   ```toml
   [windows]
   sandbox = "unelevated"
   ```

4. Run the following minimal repro:

   ```powershell
   @'
   Run exactly one shell command: Get-Location
   Then answer with only the resulting path.
   '@ | codex -a never -c 'windows.sandbox="unelevated"' exec --sandbox workspace-write --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --color never --json -C D:\chenpeng\Documents\coding\skills-development -
   ```

5. Observe that the nested shell command fails with:

   ```text
   windows sandbox: CreateRestrictedToken failed: 87
   ```

6. Repeat with `--sandbox read-only`; the same error still occurs.

Observed thread ids from minimal repros:

- `019d9e72-ae2e-7ca0-b017-92efdc5aace6` on `0.119.0-alpha.28`
- `019d9e73-2e64-7833-b1c9-9e13e47c82a0` on `0.119.0-alpha.28` (`read-only`)
- `019d9e6e-713c-7992-beb5-a260b049ea69` on `0.122.0-alpha.1`

## What is the expected behavior?

The nested shell command should run normally inside the selected sandbox, or fail with a more specific permission/policy message if the command is actually disallowed.

In particular, setting Windows sandbox mode to `unelevated` should not still fail at sandbox token creation for a trivial `Get-Location` command.

## Additional information

- I searched existing `openai/codex` issues for `CreateRestrictedToken`, `windows sandbox`, and `unelevated` before filing. I found related Windows sandbox issues, but not one with this exact `CreateRestrictedToken failed: 87` repro.
- This is blocking attempts to build a genuinely repo-aware automatic executor on Windows using safe settings like `-a never` plus `--sandbox workspace-write`, because the agent cannot reliably execute even basic local shell reads inside nested `codex exec`.
- A higher-level symptom is that automation degrades into partial / patch-only behavior: the model may still answer, but it cannot reliably inspect local files through shell execution.

issues.body:
### Summary

On a physical Apple M1 Mac, real-time voice chat fails to start. After that failure, otherwise-working composer dictation becomes unavailable with `Microphone is already in use`. Fully quitting and reopening the desktop app restores dictation.

Please investigate cleanup of the internal voice/microphone session on startup timeout or cancellation. This report does not establish that another application holds the physical microphone exclusively.

### Environment

- Physical MacBook Air, Apple M1, macOS 15.7.4 (arm64).
- Currently installed desktop app version verified on October 21, 2026: **26.1013.40934**, bundle ID `com.openai.codex` (installed as ChatGPT.app).
- The timestamped failure sequence below is from October 19; the exact build for that earlier sequence has not been independently verified.
- ChatGPT-account sign-in. Subscription details are not included.

### User-observed behavior and reproduction on the affected installation

1. Use composer dictation normally. The affected user has successfully used dictation many times.
2. Start real-time voice chat. The user reports that each attempt fails.
3. After the failed attempt, try composer dictation again.
4. Dictation fails with a microphone-in-use message, prompting the user to close other microphone-using applications.
5. Fully quit and reopen the desktop app.
6. Dictation works again, as confirmed by the user.

This is an observed sequence on one affected installation, not a claim of deterministic reproduction on a clean machine. Real-time voice chat and dictation must be distinguished: dictation is not generally broken.

### Sanitized diagnostic evidence

The desktop log shows the following sequence on October 19, 2026 (UTC):

```text
10:28:07.006 error [avatar-overlay-realtime]
Voice chat took too long to start
cancellationOrigin=host_timeout timeoutMs=10000

10:28:10.463 error [electron-message-handler]
[Composer] unable to start dictation
errorCode=0 errorMessage="Microphone is already in use"
errorName=NotReadableError

10:28:58.904 error [electron-message-handler]
[Composer] unable to start dictation
errorCode=0 errorMessage="Microphone is already in use"
errorName=NotReadableError
```

Thus, dictation fails about three seconds after the real-time voice startup timeout, and another attempt roughly 52 seconds after the timeout still fails. The user reports recovery after an app restart.

A read-only permission check on October 21 showed the microphone permission for `com.openai.codex` is allowed. No recording was made for diagnosis.

### Expected behavior

If real-time voice startup fails or times out, the app should release its microphone/session ownership and return to an idle state, allowing dictation to work without restarting the app. If a separate active in-app voice session is intentionally blocking dictation, the UI should identify that session and provide an actionable way to stop it, rather than only suggesting another application is using the microphone.

### Related DeviceCheck context — not a confirmed cause of this cleanup problem

Related report: #52001.

On October 21, opening voice settings also generated repeated failures for `GET /settings/voices?spoken_language=zh-CN&voice_mode=wingman`:

```text
errorCode=devicecheck_token_generation_failed
errorMessage="DeviceCheck token generation failed"
```

Recent macOS `mobileactivationd` / `devicecheckd` logs also contain:

```text
Error Domain=com.apple.MobileActivation.ErrorDomain Code=-4
"UCRT is unavailable."
DCCertificateGenerator: Failed to fetch client certificate.
```

These establish a concurrent device-attestation/settings failure, but do not prove it caused every real-time voice startup failure, nor that the ultimate cause is hardware, proxy routing, or an OpenAI service outage. A client-recorded status 500 is not proof of an upstream HTTP 500 response.

Regardless of why real-time voice cannot start, its failure should not leave otherwise-functional dictation blocked. This separate report focuses on that recovery/cleanup behavior.

Submitted with AI assistance at the affected user's explicit request. Private account IDs, credentials, conversation/project content, private filesystem paths, and full raw logs are omitted.

issues.body:
# OpenAI report: embedded MCP App first launch stalls with Browser Control attached

Updated 2026-10-20 for submission. No private transcript, screenshots, cookies,
headers, OAuth values, signed media links, or raw logs are included.

## Latest reproduction with deployed diagnostics

The diagnostic instrumentation is now deployed, not merely tested locally:

- Commit: `3aa5d5cfe3015871e6244c8e1261fe7213ffd0ae`.
- Serving revision at verification: `figma-animator-r3aa5d5cfe301-0199c16e7c38`, 100% traffic.
- Clean-checkout CI passed 510 tests, with zero failures; deployment and live health probes passed.
- The existing OAuth connection's Refresh tools operation completed before the test.
- Same app ID and existing BlueChew audience; no permission changes or replacement app.
- Subscription/workspace shown in ChatGPT: BlueChew Business.
- Platform: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm` (`uname -mprs`).

On 2026-10-20 at 12:29 CDT (17:29 UTC), exactly one fresh read-only
`figma_media_browser({})` launch was requested, without a previous `uiSessionId`.
Browser Control remained attached. No Try again, debugger detachment, forced
continuation, or guard changes were used. The panel stayed blank and ChatGPT
displayed `Couldn’t display Figma Animator MCP`.

The server recorded `mcp.ui.launch.requested` at `17:29:25.331 UTC`:

```json
{
  "launchId": "dd3bc0d6-d68c-4b8d-8bc5-c2529899a909",
  "bundleId": "f6ea57a1bac598777b461ba1f3eb6546d605b953b99da722ec8575a80689f2b8"
}
```

The first assistant response did not retain the launch ID. It was supplied from
the correlated server event in a follow-up requesting only the status tool.
`animator_get_launch_status` completed at `17:30:46.879 UTC`, and ChatGPT displayed:

```json
{
  "status": "awaiting_render_ack",
  "rendered": false,
  "evidence": "none",
  "launchId": "dd3bc0d6-d68c-4b8d-8bc5-c2529899a909",
  "bundleId": "f6ea57a1bac598777b461ba1f3eb6546d605b953b99da722ec8575a80689f2b8"
}
```

No rendering event or acknowledgment-tool invocation appeared in the
revision-scoped log query covering this launch. The viewer was closed only after
saving blank-panel evidence, to read the conversation in the narrow layout. It
was not reopened. The status query did not launch or retry the UI.

The supported debugger cursor was captured before launch. The bounded filtered
trace was not truncated and captured a sandbox-origin `Fetch.requestPaused`,
resource type Document, HTTP 200, event sequence 504, request
`interception-job-15837.0`. It also captured an earlier OpenAI CDN Document pause.
This is not a complete network trace and does not expose continuation completion.

The live status verifies the absence of a client acknowledgment for this launch;
it does not by itself identify a bridge root cause. The visible host failure card
is separate evidence of the failed panel launch.

## Summary

A fresh ChatGPT web Figma Animator panel launch fails while the official Chrome
Browser Control connection remains attached. A supported debugger event read
captures an HTTP 200 HTML Document response from the ChatGPT web-sandbox origin.
The panel later displays `Couldn’t display Figma Animator MCP`. A supported
`Page.getFrameTree` request is refused because Browser Use is resolving a paused
document response. The actual internal continuation outcome is unavailable.

## Environment

- macOS; Google Chrome through the official extension-backed Browser Control.
- Desktop app: 26.1013.40934, build 20770, production channel.
- Official desktop updater reported `up_to_date` on 2026-10-20.
- Bundled browser plugin: 26.1013.40934.
- Latest backend/UI revision tested: `3aa5d5cfe3015871e6244c8e1261fe7213ffd0ae`.
- Existing app: `asdk_app_6ad28c02de6c8191a5e5476c13f0edd7`.
- Endpoint: `https://figma.meds-marketing.dev/mcp`; existing BlueChew audience.
- Installed Chrome and extension versions were not re-collected for this
  reproduction; please collect them in any internal reproduction.

## Minimal steps

1. Use an authorized account with the existing Figma Animator MCP connection.
2. Keep official Browser Control attached throughout.
3. In a new ChatGPT chat, request:

   > Use the existing Figma Animator MCP app to call figma_media_browser with {}
   > and open its browser UI. This is a read-only fresh-launch test. Do not
   > generate media, reuse a uiSessionId, or retry a failed UI launch.

4. Observe the panel, and use the supported CDP event reader to inspect
   `Fetch.requestPaused`. For a new capture, obtain a cursor before step 3,
   page to completion, and record any truncation.
5. After the stalled launch, request `Page.getFrameTree` through the supported
   tab CDP capability. Do not force continuation or change interception.

Expected: the panel mounts and displays its Figma browser on the first attempt
while Browser Control remains attached.

Observed: blank panel followed by the host failure card. No Try again,
debugger detach, forced request continuation, or guard changes were used.

## Earlier reproduction and guard evidence

Reproduction captured on 2026-10-20, approximately 16:35–16:37 UTC:

- Event sequence 279: `Fetch.requestPaused`, `resourceType: Document`,
  `responseStatusCode: 200`, `content-type: text/html`, `content-encoding: br`.
- Origin: ChatGPT `web-sandbox.oaiusercontent.com`; query/fragment omitted.
- Request correlation: `interception-job-12963.0` (local debugger identifier).
- Filtered event page was not truncated. This is not a complete network trace.
- Supported query returned exactly:
  `Raw CDP is unavailable while Browser Use is resolving a paused document response.`
- Screenshot retained privately; not attached because it includes workspace context.
- All 20 current-day desktop log files under the officially documented macOS
  log directory were searched. No continuation method, guard, or matching request
  entries were found. IAB route warnings do not establish this Chrome failure's cause.

The assistant reported successful display despite the host failure card. Its
text is not rendering evidence. The earlier test used revision
`656081dd815fe7e161d827c534cd40a85e7c03c3`, before acknowledgment instrumentation.
The latest deployed reproduction above supplies the new evidence.

## Investigation requested

Please correlate the active owned-document set at the guard rejection with:

1. The exact paused request and frame/target/session ownership.
2. Continuation start, completion, rejection, timeout, or a handler that never
   reached continuation.
3. The safe method/error classification and terminal request state.
4. The corresponding ownership release or retention decision.

Please provide a supported diagnostic build/API or a fixed release retaining
the document guard. Do not unblock raw CDP around an unresolved document.

Static inspection and an isolated mock show that the bundled handler can suppress
a rejection and retain ownership. They do **not** establish that this live request
rejected, or prove a common root cause with other reports.

Related upstream report: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/55166

Official escalation guidance:
https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/troubleshooting

## Deployed application instrumentation

Each UI-producing tool response carries `uiLaunch` with a random launch ID,
bundle SHA-256 and `awaiting_render_ack`. An app-only callback can acknowledge a
nonhidden, nonzero app layout after two animation frames. A read-only status tool
returns the receipt or leaves rendering unverified. This distinguishes mounted
app evidence from tool success; it does not prove preview images loaded or replace
independent visual verification. No application code can acknowledge a sandbox
document that never starts the app's JavaScript.

1. Open a project in the Codex desktop app.
2. Create a new chat.
3. Manually type a minimal plain-text message, such as `你好`, without attachments or file references.

The chat fails to start with the error above. This reproduces both in a newly added project and in a new chat within an existing project. The error appears after sending the first message, rather than when clicking to create the chat.

The new chat starts and processes the message.

- A minimal plain-text message reproduces the issue; attachments are not required.

- Restart results and logs have not yet been collected.
- A recent-version regression is suspected, but has not been established by testing an earlier version.

No project source code, credentials, or private logs are included in this report.

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 ### What issue are you seeing? # Windows desktop: ChatGPT conversation fails to resume with rollout_not_found; later turns absent and browser reporting flow fails ## Summary An existing ChatGPT-backed conversation in the Windows desktop app cannot be reopened or continued. The UI reports `no rollout found for thread id ` and cannot load messages. At least one later user turn and part of its assistant response are present in a previously captured conversation-reference preview but absent from the current history returned for the same conversation. While preparing this report, browser automation also timed out and then repeatedly failed to attach to the existing GitHub tab. These additional errors are included below as separately observed symptoms; a shared root cause has not been established. ## Environment - Date observed: 2026-10-21 (Asia/Shanghai). - Windows x64, OS build `10.0.26200.0`. - Desktop app MSIX package version: `26.1013.4894.0`. - Local app-server/CLI reports: `0.163.0-alpha.10.2`. - Affected conversation is reported by the chat-reading tool as `kind: chatgpt`, not a local Codex rollout. - Its latest reported status is `systemError`. - Model and subscription tier were not collected; the primary failure occurs while loading/resuming the chat. ## Primary problem: conversation cannot load ### Steps observed 1. Use an existing ChatGPT-backed conversation in the Windows desktop app. 2. Reference that conversation in another chat. A captured reference preview contains a later follow-up question and part of the response. 3. Later reopen/continue the original conversation in the desktop app. 4. The conversation view is blank and displays errors instead of loading the messages. Retrying the load/resume path produces further errors. 5. Read the same conversation through the chat-reading tool: it returns five completed turns, stops before the follow-up preserved in the earlier preview, and reports `hasMore: false` with no next cursor. This was observed for one existing conversation; a fresh-account minimal reproduction has not been established. Opening the same conversation on ChatGPT web/mobile has not been tested. ### Actual behavior The UI displays: ```text 继续聊天未成功 no rollout found for thread id 无法加载消息 ``` Relevant normalized/redacted desktop log events: ```text method=thread/read code=-32600 message="thread not loaded: " method=thread/queue/list code=-32603 failureReason=rollout_not_found message="failed to read thread: invalid thread-store request: no rollout found for thread id " method=thread/resume code=-32600 failureReason=rollout_not_found source=thread_hydration message="no rollout found for thread id " vmEvent=thread_resume_failed hostId=local vmProduct=unknown Failed to resume conversation Failed to hydrate subagent route ``` ### Expected behavior - Reopening an existing ChatGPT-backed conversation should load its available history and allow continuation through the correct backend. - A conversation-reference preview and the current chat history should not silently disagree about the existence of a later turn. If a branch/version is being displayed, the UI should make that distinction clear. - A failed resume should preserve accessible history and expose an actionable error/recovery path. ## Additional problem encountered while reporting 1. The browser tool attempted to open `https://github.com/openai/codex/issues` in Edge. 2. After approximately 30 seconds, the tool returned: ```text js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request ``` 3. The GitHub tab was nevertheless created and appeared in the browser inventory. I manually opened New issue and asked the agent to continue filling it. 4. Rebinding the existing tab, reading its DOM, and reclaiming it as a user tab repeatedly returned: ```text Debugger unattached ``` 5. A supported Windows Computer Use fallback initialized and found the Edge window, but stopped before reading or filling the form with: ```text Computer Use has been stopped for this turn because it could not determine the current browser URL on Windows with enough confidence to enforce policy. Stop your work and send a final message noting why Computer Use ended. ``` Expected: a failed browser call should leave a recoverable connection state, or provide a clear reconnection/handoff procedure. This report does not request bypassing the browser URL safety check; it requests reliable URL detection and recovery after a timeout. ## Diagnostic hypothesis — not a confirmed root cause The combination of `kind: chatgpt`, local `thread/resume`, `rollout_not_found`, and `Failed to hydrate subagent route` suggests checking whether the conversation/reference is being routed to a local Codex rollout/resume path incorrectly, or whether its backend/source identity is being resolved inconsistently. This does not establish that the messages were permanently deleted, that the browser timeout shares the same cause, or that any specific app update caused the issue. Please investigate the missing-turn discrepancy separately if appropriate, and split the browser/tool recovery problem into a separate issue if needed. ## Impact and evidence - Existing chat cannot be reopened or continued. - A later follow-up appears missing from current history, creating concern about data preservation. - Attempting to file the bug through the agent is also blocked by browser-control failures. - Screenshots of the UI errors and the timeout were captured; originals remain local because they contain a conversation identifier and unrelated private UI content. - Full conversation IDs, local usernames/paths, chat content, and unrelated browser tabs are intentionally omitted from this public report. Focused diagnostics can be provided through an appropriate private support channel. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? just open some window and use gpt "Chat" mode(not work),all window in same dialog,and choose one window to talk for a few round,then open some other thing,and you might find those new dialogs won't back,while these old talk(in old windows) remain. ### What is the expected behavior? ### Additional information _No response_

issues.body:
# Suggested GitHub issue title

`[Bug][Desktop][Subagents] One task processed 242.3M tokens and consumed 11 percentage points of weekly quota in 2h44m`

## Summary

During one Codex Desktop coding task on September 16, 2026, Codex processed **242,318,802 telemetry-reported tokens across 1,545 model responses in 2 hours, 43 minutes, and 45 seconds**.

The account's weekly usage meter rose from approximately **50% used to 61% used** during the incident. That is an observed increase of 11 percentage points, not a claim that raw telemetry tokens map one-to-one to quota accounting.

Most of the volume was repeated cached-context processing:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Model responses | 1,545 |
| Input tokens | 241,805,518 |
| Cached input tokens | 237,203,328 |
| Uncached input tokens | 4,602,190 |
| Output tokens | 513,284 |
| Reasoning output tokens | 151,891 |
| Total tokens | **242,318,802** |
| Cached share of all input | **98.1%** |
| Average input per response | **156,508** |
| Observed weekly usage movement | **+11 percentage points** |

Using a rough effective-usage weighting of cached input at 0.1x, uncached input at 1x, and output at 5x, the incident represents approximately **30,888,943 weighted tokens**. Reasoning output is already included in output and was not added again.

This was not a productive quarter-billion-token workload. It was a context-amplification and orchestration failure. A large inherited conversation was replayed across hundreds of small model turns, while a reviewer and implementation agents were reactivated in a serial loop. Codex had no task-wide budget, no useful warning, and no automatic stop even as the weekly allowance visibly fell.

This appears related to, and may share a root cause with:

- [#44884 — Extreme cached-context amplification in long-running tool-heavy Codex sessions](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44884)
- [#39808 — Subagent fan-out can increase usage because each agent pays fixed context/tool/skill overhead](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/39808)
- [#41875 — Align wait_agent default timeout with prompt-cache TTL to cut parent-agent polling cost](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41875)

This report adds a bounded, single-task reproduction in Codex Desktop and identifies a particularly expensive multi-agent failure mode: repeated follow-up turns on long-lived agents, a reviewer that reports issues one at a time, and task accounting that does not naturally aggregate reused agents across root-turn ownership boundaries.

## Impact

The failure consumed roughly one tenth of the account's weekly allowance in under three hours. The user received no warning that the task had entered a pathological usage pattern. The work was not released or deployed, and the outcome was not remotely proportional to the quota consumed.

This makes autonomous coding unsafe to leave running even when the user gives a bounded implementation request. A user cannot reasonably infer from ordinary progress messages that small tool operations and review follow-ups are repeatedly processing about 150,000 input tokens each.

Severity: **High — quota exhaustion, cost visibility, and product reliability.**

## Environment

- Product: Codex Desktop on Windows
- Shell: PowerShell
- Account plan reported by the usage API: Pro
- Root coordinator: `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning
- Additional OpenAI subagents used for implementation, review, OCR analysis, acceptance review, and one installer repair
- Workload: a large TypeScript application with a long existing Codex conversation, screenshots, attachments, tool schemas, prior implementation history, and multiple requested checks
- No local LLM was invoked during this incident

## Incident window

- Start: `2026-09-16T17:51:35.032Z`
- End: `2026-09-16T20:35:19.645Z`
- Duration: `02:43:44.613`

## Per-agent breakdown

The labels below describe roles and intentionally omit local thread identifiers.

| Role | Responses | Input | Cached input | Uncached input | Output | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Coordinator | 367 | 54,975,601 | 54,374,016 | 601,585 | 77,039 | 55,052,640 |
| Independent reviewer | 571 | 95,228,055 | 93,178,880 | 2,049,175 | 150,662 | 95,378,717 |
| Routing/UI implementation agent | 404 | 60,153,394 | 59,288,832 | 864,562 | 165,121 | 60,318,515 |
| OCR/large-packet analysis agent | 181 | 28,184,695 | 27,341,824 | 842,871 | 95,121 | 28,279,816 |
| Acceptance/wiring reviewer | 15 | 2,713,831 | 2,486,016 | 227,815 | 19,590 | 2,733,421 |
| Installer repair agent | 7 | 549,942 | 533,760 | 16,182 | 5,751 | 555,693 |
| **Total** | **1,545** | **241,805,518** | **237,203,328** | **4,602,190** | **513,284** | **242,318,802** |

The independent reviewer alone generated 571 model responses and 95.4 million total tokens. The coordinator and primary implementation agent added another 771 responses and 115.4 million total tokens.

## What happened

1. The task began inside a very long Codex Desktop conversation containing extensive prior history, screenshots, pasted documents, system/tool descriptions, and previous work summaries.
2. Multiple subagents were started with too much inherited context. They did not receive compact, purpose-built briefs.
3. The implementation and review work was split across long-lived agents.
4. Review became an open-ended serial loop: the reviewer returned one issue; the coordinator sent a follow-up to an implementation agent; the reviewer resumed and found another issue; the cycle repeated.
5. Hundreds of small model turns each carried a very large cached-input component. Average input was about 156,500 tokens per response.
6. Waits, status checks, tool results, and follow-up dispatches created additional response boundaries carrying the same large context.
7. Live quota readings were checked and visibly moved through approximately 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 57%, 58%, 59%, 60%, and 61% used. Codex continued because there was no task budget or circuit breaker.
8. A standing worker-routing rule treated 10% remaining quota as the threshold for changing execution providers. Codex effectively treated that as permission to keep spending until the account approached exhaustion. That was a bad orchestration decision, but the product provided no guardrail against it.

The user's request for independent review did **not** require a reviewer to stay in an unbounded issue-by-issue loop. One bounded review pass, a consolidated defect list, one repair pass, and one final verification would have satisfied it. Codex failed to choose that shape.

## Why this is a product failure as well as an agent judgment failure

The model made poor orchestration decisions. That should be stated plainly. It spawned too much work, passed too much history, failed to consolidate review findings, and continued after the burn rate was obvious.

The product still needs to prevent this class of failure. Codex is sold for autonomous, tool-using development. A user cannot inspect every hidden response boundary, cached-context replay, or subagent reactivation while a task runs. The application knew the context size, response count, descendant-agent structure, and usage-meter trajectory, but it did not warn or stop.

There was no:

- task-wide token, response, or quota budget;
- live aggregate covering the coordinator and every descendant agent;
- projection such as “this task has used about 8% of your weekly allowance”;
- warning that hundreds of responses were repeatedly carrying more than 100,000 cached tokens;
- cap on reviewer/implementer follow-up cycles;
- compact-context default for new subagents;
- automatic checkpoint and stop when usage became disproportionate to progress;
- requirement for a reviewer to consolidate findings before another implementation pass.

## Accounting method

The totals were produced from local Codex rollout telemetry using a read-only scan:

1. Select the incident UTC window.
2. Include the root Codex thread and all descendant/reused subagent threads involved in the task.
3. Read per-response `token_usage_record` values.
4. Deduplicate globally by `(thread_id, response_id)`.
5. Sum `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, and `total_tokens`.
6. Compute uncached input as `input_tokens - cached_input_tokens`.
7. Do not add `reasoning_output_tokens` to output because it is a subset of output.

One important observability defect surfaced here: an ordinary root-turn report can omit usage from a reused subagent when later follow-ups remain attributed to that agent's original `root_turn_id`. A correct task-wide report required scanning across root-turn boundaries and deduplicating all participating threads. The product should do this automatically.

Raw logs are not attached because they contain private prompts, file paths, screenshots, and tool output. A redacted aggregate is available, and a sanitized analysis script/output can be provided privately to maintainers.

## Reproduction pattern

This is a workload-shape reproduction rather than a minimal deterministic test:

1. Start a long-running Codex Desktop conversation with a large inherited context.
2. Ask for a substantial implementation and independent review.
3. Spawn several subagents using default/full inherited history rather than compact task briefs.
4. Keep the same agents alive through many `followup_task` cycles.
5. Let a reviewer return findings serially instead of in one consolidated pass.
6. Run tool-heavy work with many small shell, test, wait, and status boundaries.
7. Inspect per-response `token_usage_record` data after context exceeds 100,000 tokens.
8. Observe hundreds of responses with roughly 100,000–200,000 mostly cached input tokens and comparatively tiny outputs.
9. Observe the account usage meter fall without a task-level warning or stop.

## Expected behavior

- A task should expose one live usage total that includes the coordinator and all descendant or reused agents.
- Subagents should default to a compact, purpose-built brief. Full conversation inheritance should be explicit and visibly priced.
- Users should be able to set a maximum task budget by weekly-quota percentage, weighted tokens, model responses, and wall time.
- Codex should pause and request confirmation at the budget boundary while preserving task state.
- The UI should warn when a task enters a pathological pattern, such as many consecutive responses with more than 100,000 cached input tokens and less than 1,000 output tokens.
- Pure wait/poll operations should avoid a fresh model inference where the architecture permits.
- Review agents should return a consolidated report by default. Repeated reviewer/implementer cycles should have a small default cap.
- Usage reporting should distinguish cached input, uncached input, output, and estimated quota impact.
- Automatic compaction or checkpoint/handoff should occur before the context becomes expensive enough to consume a material part of the weekly allowance.

## Actual behavior

- One bounded task produced 1,545 model responses in under three hours.
- The task processed 242.3 million tokens, 237.2 million of them cached input.
- Average input was about 156,500 tokens per response.
- The account's weekly usage meter rose by 11 percentage points during the incident.
- No task-wide warning, limit, approval boundary, or automatic stop occurred.
- The default reporting path did not naturally show all usage from reused agents across root-turn boundaries.
- Work continued even after repeated usage checks demonstrated rapid quota loss.

## Requested fixes / acceptance criteria

1. **Task-wide accounting:** The displayed total includes the root task, all descendants, and later follow-ups to reused agents, regardless of `root_turn_id` ownership.
2. **User-set hard budgets:** A user can cap weekly-quota percentage, effective tokens, responses, and wall time for a task.
3. **Automatic circuit breaker:** Codex pauses before exceeding that budget and preserves a resumable checkpoint.
4. **Safe context defaults:** Subagents receive a compact task brief by default; full-history inheritance requires explicit selection.
5. **Pathology warning:** Codex detects repeated high-context/low-output turns and warns before material quota loss.
6. **Low-cost waiting:** Deterministic waits and status polling do not require repeated full-context model calls.
7. **Bounded review loops:** Independent review is consolidated, with a visible and configurable pass limit.
8. **Clear live telemetry:** The UI shows cached input, uncached input, output, descendant-agent usage, current task share of weekly usage, and projected remaining cost.
9. **Cross-turn correctness:** Usage remains attributable to the active user task even when a long-lived subagent is reactivated from a later root turn.
10. **Regression test:** A multi-agent tool-heavy test with a large starting context must stop or warn before a configured task budget is exceeded.

## Final note

I am not alleging that cached input was billed as uncached input or that raw local token totals map directly to subscription accounting. The account meter and local telemetry are different measurements. The concrete failure is that Codex generated an enormous volume of repeated context processing, the weekly meter moved sharply during the same bounded incident, and the product offered no practical way to see, budget, or stop it before the damage was done.

issues.body:
### Summary

Minimising and restoring the Windows Codex desktop app briefly shows blank/white content, then restores the conversation at the **top** instead of the previously visible bottom. This is repeatable in a long existing conversation.

A controlled user check on 20 October 2026 kept the **normal Windows RDP viewer open and visible** and minimised **only Codex inside the remote desktop**. The user confirmed: "White briefly, then chat jumps to top."

### Environment

- Windows desktop Microsoft Store package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0` (read from installed package metadata; About-dialog display version was not independently captured).
- Host Windows build: `26200.9711`, display version `25H2`, x64.
- Access: standard Windows Remote Desktop Connection, remote desktop `2560 × 1600` at `175%`.
- One long existing conversation. No private conversation contents or IDs are included.
- RDP client was verified visible and not minimised during the read-only diagnostic. No connection handover, display/scaling change, app restart, cache reset or simulated scroll/navigation was performed for the controlled reproduction.

### Steps to reproduce on the affected installation

1. Open an existing long conversation in the Windows Codex app.
2. Scroll to the current messages at the bottom.
3. Keep the RDP viewer itself visible and connected.
4. Minimise only the Codex app window inside that desktop.
5. Restore Codex.

### Actual result

The app content is briefly blank/white. It then renders, but the conversation is at the top and the user must scroll back down. The duration of the white interval was not measured.

The user reported the same minimise/restore trigger on 19 October and reproduced it again in the controlled 20 October check.

### Expected result

Restore the app promptly with its conversation reading position preserved. If the user was following the latest messages, keep the bottom/follow-latest position. If reading older content, preserve the visible message anchor through any reflow rather than forcing either end.

### Control and limited workaround

The user also tested leaving Codex restored, switching to another app inside the same remote desktop with Alt+Tab, and switching back **without minimising Codex or RDP**. The user confirmed that the chat kept its position.

This is only a workaround for switching between applications. The user specifically needs to expose the desktop to see desktop gadgets; Alt+Tab does not provide that. Minimising/restoring Codex must preserve position so ordinary desktop access remains usable. A subsequent user check in the same full-screen RDP desktop held Windows+comma for temporary desktop peek, then released the keys. The user confirmed: "Gadgets visible; chat position preserved." This is a verified viewing-only workaround on this installation; it does not replace persistent desktop interaction or correct minimise/restore behaviour.

### Diagnostic boundaries

- Read-only client checks found `RemoteDesktop_SuppressWhenMinimized` absent in the checked current-user and machine 32/64-bit registry views. This setting concerns a minimised **RDP viewer**; it is not an established explanation for minimising **Codex inside a visible viewer**. No registry value was changed.
- Current application-log inspection found no explicit `render-process-gone`, GPU-crash/device-lost, or scroll-reset/restore markers under the narrow patterns checked. This is not proof that no renderer/repaint/reload fault occurred. The collection was a post-reproduction inspection, not a synchronised before/after performance trace.
- The application remained running/responding at inspection. No crash, GPU cause, memory corruption or RDP root cause is claimed.
- Related but not established as a duplicate: #49255 concerns upward history pagination and renderer crashes in a different Windows app build. This report adds a specific minimise/restore trigger and an Alt+Tab control.

Please investigate conversation scroll anchoring and render restoration on window restore, and identify a supported fix/version or targeted diagnostic capture if needed.

No raw logs, session transcripts, screenshots, account identifiers, credentials or private project paths are attached.

issues.body:
**Expected:** after a normal Quit, opening the ordinary desktop icon should reliably leave a usable application window, including while the previous instance is finishing shutdown.

**Observed:** the first rapid reopening briefly displayed an incompletely loaded/white window and disappeared. A later activation persisted. This is one measured manual quit/reopen sequence, not a validated cold-boot failure or a measured failure rate. The old instance had been opened in a preceding user-run activation-helper comparison; both new attempts in this measured sequence used the ordinary desktop icon. The helper did not modify app binaries or settings.

**Environment:** Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (build 19045), x64, packaged desktop application; application-update tool reports version 26.1013.40934, build 20770, production channel, up_to_date. The separate MSIX identity version is 26.1013.4894.0. Native executable metadata reports version 155.0.8059.80; the installed application requires the Owl shell, so a stock Electron singleton implementation is not assumed. The executable signature is Valid. Windows Settings Repair had already been attempted.

**Measured sequence, relative to creation of the first new instance:**

- 0 ms: first new instance created through the ordinary icon while the previous instance was finishing shutdown.
- By +349.7257 ms: the new instance's exit was observed, with recorded exit code 0.
- About +3497.6073 ms: the shared old AppX container was destroyed.
- At +3544.6724 ms: the previous main instance's exit was observed, also code 0.
- A later ordinary activation used a new container and continued initializing its window.

The short-lived new instance demonstrably joined the old instance's container. Its exit was observed approximately 3.1479 seconds before container destruction; therefore the data does not establish that container destruction killed it. EXIT timestamps are observer detection times, not exact kernel exit times. Code 0 does not identify the caller or establish an absence of startup failure. The transient window's exact owning PID was not established.

**Candidate, not a proven root cause:** quit cleanup and single-instance reactivation may overlap. A bounded static inspection finds that one JS second-instance queue guard changes only at the quit event, with a main-window show path lacking an equivalent local quitting check; cleanup includes a 5-second budget. This does not prove that the short-lived process reached that JS path or exhausted that budget. A separate early policy/flag relaunch-with-exit-0 path also exists; its use in this incident is unknown. A PID-specific log file is created lazily, so a missing file does not prove JS was never reached.

Please advise on a supported diagnostic or fixed release for native/Owl and JS quit/reactivation handoff. No supported user setting for this issue was identified in a bounded documentation review, and the configured update channel offers no update at the check time. No native exit initiator or actual singleton/relaunch branch has been captured.

The existing five-minute observer finalized with partial diagnostic coverage because one additional process could not be opened (error 87); core target handles were held before their observed exits. No new reproduction was performed for this assessment. No configuration, proxy, TUN, driver, or software changes were made. No account details, subscription information, machine identifiers, personal paths, full logs, dumps, or source code are included. labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running? codex-cli 0.163.0 ### What subscription do you have? Pro $200 ### Which model were you using? gpt-6.1-sol ### What platform is your computer? Ubuntu 24.04, Linux x86_64 ### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)? VS Code ### Codex doctor report ```json ``` ### What issue are you seeing? Codex CLI 0.163.0 consistently hangs on Ubuntu 24.04 when the `plugins` feature is enabled together with either `apps` or `tool_suggest`. The issue affects normal interactive Codex CLI sessions and was also observed when accessing Codex through VS Code Remote SSH and remote clients. When a message is submitted, Codex successfully creates a thread and starts a turn, but the actual model response never completes. The CLI remains waiting indefinitely, and a non-interactive execution must be terminated using a timeout. **Observed behavior:** - `thread.started` is emitted successfully. - `turn.started` is emitted successfully. - WebSocket connection and warmup complete successfully. - The actual user inference request does not reach completion. - Neither `item.completed` nor `turn.completed` is emitted. - The process exits with code `124` after a 90-second timeout. The issue is reproducible with two feature combinations: - `plugins=true` + `apps=true` - `plugins=true` + `tool_suggest=true` **Disabling only `plugins` resolves the issue**, even when `apps`, `tool_suggest`, and `multi_agent` remain enabled. This suggests an interaction involving plugin initialization, tool discovery, MCP binding catalog construction, or startup prewarm handling rather than a basic authentication or network connectivity failure. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? **Environment** - OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x86_64) - Codex CLI version: 0.163.0 - Authentication: ChatGPT login - Model: `gpt-6.1-sol` - Execution: Local Ubuntu terminal, including SSH sessions **Step 1 — Create an isolated test directory** ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/codex-plugin-repro cd /tmp/codex-plugin-repro ``` **Step 2 — Reproduce with Apps + Plugins enabled** ```bash timeout -k 5s 90s codex exec \ --ignore-user-config \ --ignore-rules \ --ephemeral \ --skip-git-repo-check \ --sandbox read-only \ -m gpt-6.1-sol \ --enable apps \ --enable plugins \ --disable tool_suggest \ --disable multi_agent \ --json \ "Reply with exactly: CODEX_DIAG_OK. Do not use tools." ``` **Result: HANG** - `thread.started` - `turn.started` - No `turn.completed` - Exit code: `124` **Step 3 — Reproduce with Plugins + Tool Suggest enabled** Repeat Step 2 with the following feature flags: ```bash --disable apps \ --enable plugins \ --enable tool_suggest \ --disable multi_agent ``` **Result: HANG** - `thread.started` - `turn.started` - No `turn.completed` - Exit code: `124` **Step 4 — Verify that disabling Plugins resolves the issue** Repeat Step 2 with: ```bash --enable apps \ --disable plugins \ --enable tool_suggest \ --enable multi_agent ``` **Result: PASS** - `thread.started` - `turn.started` - `item.completed` - `turn.completed` - Exit code: `0` - Model output: `CODEX_DIAG_OK` All tests use the same model, prompt, ephemeral execution, and read-only sandbox. The only relevant differences between the reproduction cases are the feature flags. ### What is the expected behavior? Codex should successfully process a simple text-only prompt regardless of whether `apps`, `plugins`, and `tool_suggest` are enabled together. Expected behavior: 1. The thread and turn initialize successfully. 2. Plugin discovery and MCP/tool initialization complete without blocking the turn. 3. The actual user request is sent to the model. 4. The model generates the requested response. 5. Codex emits `item.completed` and `turn.completed`. 6. The CLI exits with code `0` and prints `CODEX_DIAG_OK`. If plugin discovery or initialization fails, Codex should return a clear error or gracefully skip the unavailable plugin functionality rather than indefinitely blocking unrelated model inference. Optional plugin features should not prevent basic text-only chat operations from completing. ### Additional information

Feature combination test results

Extensive A/B testing was performed to isolate the failing feature combinations.

Apps | Plugins | Tool Suggest | Multi-Agent | Result -- | -- | -- | -- | -- OFF | OFF | OFF | OFF | PASS ON | OFF | OFF | OFF | PASS OFF | ON | OFF | OFF | PASS OFF | OFF | ON | OFF | PASS OFF | OFF | OFF | ON | PASS ON | ON | OFF | OFF | HANG (124) OFF | ON | ON | OFF | HANG (124) ON | OFF | ON | OFF | PASS ON | ON | ON | OFF | HANG (124) ON | ON | ON | ON | HANG (124) ON | OFF | ON | ON | PASS

These results indicate that plugins works independently, but combining it with apps or tool_suggest consistently triggers the hang in this environment.

Relevant diagnostic logs

The failing apps + plugins execution produced these diagnostic markers:

mcp_servers="codex_apps"
event.name="mcp.binding_catalog"
startup.phase="startup_prewarm_build_tools"
startup.phase="startup_prewarm_build_prompt"
websocket.warmup=true
event.name="codex.websocket_request"
event.kind=response.completed
startup.phase="startup_prewarm_websocket_warmup"
startup.phase="startup_prewarm_total"
startup.phase="startup_prewarm_resolve"

No websocket.warmup=false request or completed turn was observed before the 90-second timeout.

The response.completed event in this failing execution belongs to the WebSocket warmup request, not the actual user prompt.

In successful executions, the following additional events appear:

websocket.warmup=false
event.name="codex.websocket_request"
event.name="codex.turn_ttft"
event.kind=response.completed

The CLI also emits item.completed and turn.completed.

The last observed startup_prewarm_resolve marker is a potential investigation point, but does not by itself prove a deadlock in that function.

Network and authentication diagnostics

codex doctor --json reported:

  • auth.credentials: OK (ChatGPT authentication configured)

  • network.provider_reachability: OK (HTTP 405 response)

  • network.websocket_reachability: OK (HTTP 101 Switching Protocols)

  • app_server.status: OK (0.163.0 background server running)

WebSocket warmup and real model inference both succeed when plugins is disabled.

The server has functional IPv4 connectivity but no public IPv6 default route. However, this does not explain the feature-dependent behavior, and successful authenticated WebSocket inference over the available network has been verified.

Troubleshooting already performed

The issue persisted after:

  • Upgrading Codex CLI from 0.162 to 0.163.

  • Reinstalling Codex CLI.

  • Reinstalling and disabling/re-enabling the VS Code Codex extension.

  • Restarting Ubuntu 24.04.

  • Terminating Codex-related processes.

  • Clearing Codex caches and local data, followed by reauthentication.

  • Comparing Tailscale and standard SSH connections.

  • Verifying firewall and network connectivity.

  • Reproducing the issue using fresh ephemeral CLI sessions.

Verified workaround

[features]
apps = true
plugins = false
tool_suggest = true
multi_agent = true

This configuration successfully completes the reproduction test with exit code 0 and the expected model output.

Request for investigation

Please investigate possible interactions among:

  • Plugin discovery and initialization.

  • MCP binding catalog construction (mcp.binding_catalog).

  • Apps and Tool Suggest integration with Plugins.

  • Startup prewarm and turn-context resolution.

The issue appears to be related to feature-dependent startup or tool discovery processing, rather than a general model API connectivity failure.

issues.title: App-server: expose per-child input consumption evidence for safe drain

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI app-server over stdio, embedded in a host integration. Native behavior was
observed on 0.162.1; the experimental 0.163.0 schema was inspected separately.
These are pinned-version observations, not a claim about the newest release.

### What feature would you like to see?

A supported, body-free way for a host to prove which accepted child-agent inputs
were consumed by terminal native turns. A consumed-input watermark, accepted-ID
set on a terminal turn, or equivalent native processing barrier would work.

The host needs to drain accepted work before replacing its runtime. It cannot
safely treat an earlier completed turn, message acceptance, empty user queues or
model-reported completion as proof that a newer overlapping child input was
processed. Please point me to a supported equivalent if one already exists.

In a bounded native test, two overlapping follow-ups produce two interaction
observations but only one later child turn covering both assignments. The six
expected local effects and the parent's turn complete. The typed observations do
not identify which accepted input generation that child turn consumed, so the
host retains uncertainty rather than replaying or declaring the queue drained.

A bounded reproduction:

1. Start a child and let its first finite assignment finish.
2. Send the same child a follow-up containing a finite held command.
3. While that follow-up is active, send another finite follow-up.
4. Let the child and parent reconcile their outcomes and finish.
5. Inspect parent `subAgentActivity` and child turn metadata through app-server.
   The question is how to correlate every accepted input with actual consumption,
   including several inputs folded into one turn.

Bind the evidence to native instance, child identity, input identity/generation
and terminal turn. Late, reordered or duplicate observations must not close newer
work. User submission queues and inter-agent mailboxes need distinct semantics.
Child closure also precedes any required owner reconciliation.

Acceptance should cover overlapping inputs, completion before the host sees
acceptance, unload/reload, queued-only inputs, cancellation, nested children and
late commands. Only consumption/closure metadata is needed.

### Additional information

The inspected 0.163.0 schema adds persisted-item and UI read-state methods while
its relevant child/turn/queue structures match 0.162.1. UI read state is not
recipient consumption evidence. Ordinary turn completion and steering are
described in the [official app-server guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server),
but I have not established the requested child-input contract from it.
Documentation search absence alone does not establish that no implementation exists.

Related [#50581](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50581) requests existing V2
lifecycle/reply attribution in `exec --json`. This request concerns app-server's
host-visible per-input consumption semantics, including overlapping follow-ups;
merely exporting a wakeup or terminal activity is insufficient for that purpose.

## Summary

On **21 October 2026**, the **Codex VS Code extension on macOS** repeatedly failed queued follow-up instructions with `exceeded retry limit, last status: 429 Too Many Requests`. After these failures, pressing the **Play / resume** button runs **only the last queued message**, rather than recovering the earlier failed queued instructions in their original order.

This breaks multi-step, dependency-based development workflows: the last task can execute without preceding verification, fixes or tests. **This is a new symptom for me; I had not previously encountered this repeated 429 + queue-recovery behavior.**

## Environment

- Product: OpenAI Codex extension for **Visual Studio Code**, not the standalone Codex desktop app or CLI
- Host OS: **macOS** (visible in screenshot; exact OS version and architecture not collected)
- Model shown: **GPT-5.6 Sol**, **High** reasoning effort
- Permissions shown: **Full access**
- Observation: **21 October 2026 at approximately 10:43 AM MYT (UTC+8)**, with earlier failing messages in the same chat
- Exact VS Code version, Codex extension version, account quota readings, and request IDs: **not yet collected**

## Observed behavior

1. A Codex conversation contains a sequence of dependent follow-up requests while working on an existing project.
2. Queued requests fail one after another, each showing:
   ```text
   exceeded retry limit, last status: 429 Too Many Requests
   ```
3. At least **four** failed error entries are visible in the provided screenshot. Example queued instructions shown: retest fixes with a Playwright CLI skill; fix if needed; retest with a beta tester and give a verdict. The previous session also references summarizing project status.
4. The UI presents a Play/resume button after the failures; the latest interrupted attempt reports **“You stopped after 0s”**.
5. Pressing Play executes **only the most recently queued instruction**, not the entire unexecuted sequence.
6. Earlier prerequisite prompts have not successfully completed. As a result, running the last message alone causes a **workflow-continuity failure**: a downstream review/verdict can proceed without prior testing or repairs.

These are user-observed UI symptoms. I have not inspected extension logs or verified whether the 429s come from service capacity, quota enforcement, or a model-specific restriction. I also cannot establish whether the missing instructions were removed from internal queue storage or merely not replayed.

## Steps to reproduce (observed sequence, not yet a controlled reproduction)

1. Open the Codex extension in VS Code and continue a project conversation.
2. Queue multiple dependent follow-up instructions, e.g. (A) run tests, (B) fix failures, (C) retest and give verdict.
3. During a period when Codex receives `429 Too Many Requests`, observe successive queued instructions fail after retries.
4. Click Play/resume after the failures.
5. Observe that only the final queued instruction runs, while earlier failed tasks do not automatically resume first.

## Expected behavior

- **429 handling:** Clearly report whether the cause is rate limiting, quota, or transient capacity; ideally provide a retry-after indication when available.
- **Durable queue:** Preserve each failed/unexecuted queued instruction and its ordering across transient API failures.
- **Correct resume:** Resume at the **earliest incomplete queued instruction**, or explicitly offer to retry all unfinished messages in sequence. Do not silently skip prerequisite steps.
- **Safety/clarity:** If resuming the full queue is impossible, mark failed tasks as incomplete and warn before executing a downstream queued instruction that depends on them.
- **Context integrity:** Avoid giving the impression that prior verification or fixes occurred when earlier prompts never ran.

## Impact

High impact for unattended or long-running VS Code development sessions that depend on sequential Codex tasks. Re-running only the final message is **not equivalent to resuming the workflow** and may yield unverified completion claims.

## Related issues

- **#50224** — my earlier VS Code report on intermittently failing normal and queued messages; this report adds a **specific repeated HTTP 429 trigger and final-message-only recovery behavior**.
- **#30513** — queue advancing/replay/context inconsistency in VS Code, though its reported sequence differs.
- **#55507** — contemporaneous reports of the same `429 Too Many Requests` error in a different Codex client.

A screenshot is available from the affected VS Code conversation showing the repeated 429 errors, model selection, queued instructions and resume button. I can provide the image, extension version and sanitized diagnostics if needed.
