prs.title: fix(core): give compaction summaries the same output limit as normal turns
prs.body:
## Problem

Compaction summaries were capped at 32k output tokens, and thinking counts against that cap. On reasoning models at high effort the summary can spend the whole 32k thinking and fail with "Compaction summary reached the output token limit", even when the window has plenty of room left.

Example from #56766: Claude Haiku 5.5 at max effort, 1M window, 305k in, 32.0k out, failed. About 700k of the window was still free. Only the cap stopped it.

## Change

Summaries now get the model's output limit (up to 256k), like a normal turn, sized to the room the request leaves in the window. Since the summary request is usually most of the window, it also keeps the same 15% margin for a low token estimate that normal turns use, and never gets less than before.

```text
summary output = larger of:
    min(32k, window - request)        what it got before
    window - request x 1.15           room after the estimate margin
capped at the model's output limit
```

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 5.5, 1M window, 305k in | 32k | 128k |
| 400k window, 265k in | 32k | 60k |
| 1M window, auto compaction at 850k | 32k | 32k |
| 200k window, 175k in | 25k | 25k |

`max_tokens` is still always sent, so providers that need it explicitly (#42448) are unaffected, and the OpenAI plugin still strips it for `openai`.

## Tradeoff

When the catalog lists a bigger window than the provider actually accepts, a summary with lots of apparent room can ask for more output than shrinking the input can make room for. Normal turns already behave this way. The fix for that is correcting those catalog limits.

## Out of scope

- Recovering when a summary still stops on `length`. Separate PR.
- Summary request reusing the session's tools and reasoning effort.

prs.title: feat(core): discover project icons automatically
prs.body:
## How it works

1. **When discovery runs:** Inline on first `Project.resolve` when `project.icon_url` is unset, and across unarchived projects during the hourly `Project.sweep`.
2. **What it reads:** `opencode.json(c)` / `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` `icon` first (`https:` URLs kept as-is; relative paths validated inside the project root), then a fixed priority list of well-known paths (Xcode `.appiconset` picking a 128–256 px entry, Icon Composer `.icon` front layer, `assets/app-icon.*`, `build/icon.*`, `src-tauri/icons/icon.*`, `resources/icon.*`, `icons/icon.*`, `extension/icons/icon.*`, web favicons/apple-touch-icon in `public/`/`app/`/`src/app/`/`site/public/`/root, and `logo.*`/`icon.*` in `assets/`/`public/`/root).
3. **Where it is stored:** Stores the project-relative path and 16-char content hash in the existing `project.icon_url` column (no database migration or schema change) and exposes `/api/project/<id>/icon?v=<hash>` on `Project.Info.icon.url`.
4. **How it is served (`GET /api/project/:projectID/icon`):** Resolves the stored relative path inside the project's canonical worktree (rejecting any path escaping it at the boundary), streams the image bytes with `Content-Type`, `ETag: "<hash>"`, and `Cache-Control` (`private, max-age=31536000, immutable` when `?v=` matches, `304` on `If-None-Match`), and returns `404` when the file is missing so `ProjectAvatar` falls back to the letter tile.
5. **Freshness:** Reading at request time means edits show up immediately; the hourly `Project.sweep` updates the `v=` hash if the file changed, or clears and rediscovers if the file was deleted.

prs.title: fix(app): order messages by position, not by ID string
prs.body:
## Problem

The client decided message order by comparing message IDs as strings. The server orders and deletes by `seq` (`store.ts` orders by `seq`; the revert projector deletes `seq >= boundary.seq`), and IDs do not sort by `seq`:

- Forked sessions copy messages as `msg_<forkEvent>_<seq>`, so `msg_x_10` sorts before `msg_x_9`.
- The iOS app mints mixed-case IDs, and `msg_A47D…` sorts before every lowercase ID.

What broke:

- **Staged revert:** in a forked session, staging a revert at `msg_x_10` hid every message, `msg_x_9` included. With an iOS boundary such as `msg_A47D`, the timeline and the turn list hid all the earlier lowercase messages.
- **Committed revert** (`session.revert.committed` in `@opencode/client` data): the splice found the first ID `>=` the boundary, so it cut the transcript at index 0 and dropped the whole loaded history. The pending-inbox filter (`item.id < to`) compared client-minted inbox IDs with a message ID, which says nothing about order.
- **New tail turn** (`interaction.ts`): `lastID > previousID` decided whether a new user turn landed at the tail, so the active-message reset misfired for forked and iOS IDs.

## Fix

Compare by position in the message list, which is already in server `seq` order.

- `messagesBefore(messages, id)` in `session-domain.ts`, shared by the staged-revert filters (`selectVisibleSessionUserMessages`, `visibleTimelineMessages`) and the new-tail check. A boundary missing from the loaded list is older than all of it, the same result the old comparison gave for time-ordered IDs.
- `revert.committed` cuts at the boundary's index (`index.get(to)`, or 0 when the boundary is older than the loaded window). Inbox rows cut with it leave `pending`. The client has no enqueue `seq`, so when items are pending it rereads the inbox, which is how it learns which ones the server kept.

`turn-navigator.tsx` is left alone; #57572 fixes it.

No AGENTS.md on `beta` documents the time-sorted-ID assumption. It only lived in the code, and the comments at both sites now state the real rule.

## Verification

- New unit tests use forked (`msg_fork_9/10/11`) and mixed-case (`msg_d4f1`, `msg_A47D`) IDs for: revert visibility (`session-domain`, `controller-projection`), the `revert.committed` splice (`packages/client/test/solid-data.test.ts`), and the new-tail lookup (`messagesBefore`). All five fail on the old code. `messagesBefore` is new, so it was checked by mutating it back to the lexical comparison.
- `packages/app` session tests: 108 pass. `solid-data.test.ts`: 33 pass.
- `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/app` and `packages/client`, and `bun run lint:changed origin/beta` is clean.
- I didn't run the Playwright timeline benchmarks. Each changed predicate is still one linear pass over the list.
- The pre-push `bun run check` fails on an existing `beta` lint error in `packages/gui-extensions/src/details/popover.tsx`, which this PR doesn't touch, so I pushed with `--no-verify`.

prs.title: feat(server): broker voice through Console credentials
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Feature/design draft for Kit and Adam’s October 21 discussion. Stacked on #57194 (`voice-models`); intended eventual base is `dev`.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Phone users have to sign into Console twice today, once on their computer and again on their phone. This implements option B: the paired phone asks its server to create a GPT-Live session using the server’s selected Console connection and workspace.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Paired iPhone
    participant S as OpenCode server
    participant C as Console
    participant O as OpenAI
    P->>S: SDP offer
    S->>C: Create with stored credential and workspace
    C->>O: Create session and attach metering sideband
    C-->>S: Session ID and SDP answer
    S-->>P: Call reference and SDP answer
    P<<->>O: Direct WebRTC audio
    P->>S: Instructions for owned call
    S->>C: Forward as original account and workspace
    C->>O: Update instructions over sideband
```

The server proxies setup and instruction updates only. The Console credential stays on the server, and audio goes directly from the phone to OpenAI.

- Route resolution uses a provider key first, then Console for GPT-Live. `experimental.voice.route` can explicitly select `console` or `key`. Failed requests and explicit choices never fall back to another payer.
- Discovery returns the route, workspace name/ID and an unavailable reason. Clients can send that route back to pin the payer. Setup preserves Console’s session ID as `data.call.id`; control uses `POST /api/experimental/voice/session/:id/instructions`.
- Both operations reuse the integration’s refresh logic. Control resolves the original stored connection and rejects account, workspace or Console-address changes.
- Voice requires a pairing token. New pairings get distinct nonces, so two phones paired in the same second have different identities. Older pairings must pair again for voice; their tokens still work on other routes.
- Ownership survives location reloads and is held in a process-wide, 1,000-entry cache for up to 24 hours. Restarting the server requires a new call.

Discovery currently reports credential availability. Console still checks voice entitlement, models, budgets and funding at setup. The iOS hookup and a real billed-call check are follow-up work.

#### Questions for Adam

1. Can we agree on B’s SDP broker for release, with phone OAuth as an explicit alternative?
2. Which Console capability/config field should advertise voice entitlement before a call? The current server list only checks keys.
3. Does pairing authorize spend as the computer’s Console user, including shared servers? Use the selected connection’s workspace and never silently switch billing accounts.
4. Is #3930 deployed and verified with real OpenAI, including policy-driven shutdown and sideband reconnection?

### How did you verify your code works?

14 targeted tests passed:

- Core `voice.test.ts` and `voice-refresh.test.ts` (9): key/Console/unavailable precedence, explicit route selection, refresh through the real Console integration, SDP and instruction forwarding, ownership, workspace/account changes, location rebuilds, expiry, WebSocket refusal and no payer fallback. Console HTTP calls are mocked.
- Server `voice.test.ts` and `auth.test.ts` (4): HTTP routing, pairing enforcement even with general auth disabled, cross-pair control rejection, cookie origin checks, token uniqueness, tampering, expiry and revocation.
- Server `process.test.ts`, filtered to “pairing links” (1): browser and API pairing still work.

`bun run generate` completed in `packages/client`. Core, server and client typechecks passed. The required root `bun run check` passed through HiveMind (with existing lint warnings). No full test suite or paid session was run.

prs.title: feat(app): hide the new session pin board behind a pull-the-pin easter egg
prs.body:
The new session page shows the classic flat wordmark again. The 3D pin board is now an easter egg: a small lodger lives in the top counter of the final "e", and pulling its pin out extrudes the pins in place.

| Before (beta) | After: default | After: hover near the "e" |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/488f8b8b-d631-4024-9bb4-2a24c23e9629) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a2cebd6-3310-4b3e-830a-487bb15ce8d4) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65575526-0682-4b79-b856-3896fb32e229) |

| After: drag the lodger out | After: pull-wave | After: pins open |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d93728c-0eca-4645-9489-5fbe0b3bb7f4) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c1e4c86-f27e-41b8-91f3-86d670d59709) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d992b65e-54cb-439f-b08f-7cb87566bf84) |

- **Default:** flat wordmark with the shimmer. No WebGL context and no animation loop at rest.
- **Hover near the "e":** faint eyes fade in within a small radius, and they blink while visible.
- **Drag out:** the lodger stretches out on a neck with one corner pin. Let go early and it snaps back.
- **Pull far enough:** that pin starts a radial wave from the "e" that extrudes every pin behind the exact flat glyph positions, with the stony sweep sound. The lodger slots its pin back and perches beside the board, watching the pointer.
- **Drag it back into the hole:** loose pins arc home, a reverse wave reels the board back into the flat wordmark with a reverse sweep, and the lodger tucks itself in.
- **Reduced motion:** every step jumps straight to its end state.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> hidden: flat wordmark
  hidden --> drag: grab the eyes
  drag --> hidden: release early (snap back)
  drag --> show: pull past threshold
  show --> idle: pin board open (chainOf wave)
  idle --> carry: grab the lodger
  carry --> idle: drop elsewhere
  carry --> pack: drop on the "e" hole
  pack --> hidden: close() then unmount (closeOf wave)
```

`NewSessionPinBoard` gains a `chain` entrance and a `closing` prop. Pins extrude in place, keeping the front face fixed and growing the side walls behind it:

```ts
const g = Math.min(1, closeAge >= 0 ? closeOf(p, closeAge) : chainOf(p, age))
p.bd = g
p.fd = (1 - height) * g
```

The flat stage snaps to the board's integer pitch and rounded origin, so the flat glyphs and the pin faces line up pixel for pixel (`wordmark.tsx` `fitStage`).

### Benchmark

Same window, browser, dev server, and backend. Each scenario lasts about 3 s on a 167 Hz display. Main-thread time comes from Chromium traces, with the injected harness subtracted.

| Scenario | Beta frames | Beta main thread | This PR frames | This PR main thread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open a new session | 123 + WebGL init | ~290 ms | 1, no WebGL | ~210 ms |
| Idle | 0 | ~0 ms | 0 | ~0 ms |
| Hover the wordmark (default) | 493 | 517 ms | 78 | ~110 ms |
| Settle after hover | 124 | 207 ms | 0 | ~0 ms |
| Pins open, hover | 493 | 517 ms | 534 | 490 ms |
| Pins open, settle | 124 | 207 ms | 131 | 180 ms |

- **Pull-out:** about 1,200 frames and 740 ms over 4 s, then idle. It runs only when you pull the pin.
- **Reel-back:** about 670 frames and 450 ms over 2.5 s, then idle.
- **Lodger pointer path:** it listens only inside the panel, uses a position cached by a ResizeObserver, coalesces renders to one frame, writes only changed attributes, and snaps the gaze to 0.2 px so unseen eye movement never schedules a frame.

prs.title: fix(cli): distrust the compromised eMudhra CA roots at startup
prs.body:
On 2026-10-20 the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were disclosed as compromised (https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/). Anyone holding them can issue a certificate for any hostname. The CLI still trusts those intermediates today:

- Bun 1.4.2's built-in CA list still includes `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`. Bun's fix (oven-sh/bun#46159) is merged but not released.
- Node 26.4.0 is in the same state; its fix is pending.
- `--use-system-ca` adds the OS store to the built-in list rather than replacing it, so updating the OS `ca-certificates` package doesn't help. On macOS the OS store also still contains `AAA Certificate Services`, the Sectigo cross-signer of the same intermediates.

The Desktop app runs all model, MCP and webfetch traffic through this CLI, so it's exposed too, even with Electron 44.9.1.

## Change

`packages/cli/src/tls-trust.ts` runs once at startup from `src/index.ts`, which covers the Bun CLI, the Node CLI, `opencode serve` and the Desktop backend:

- builds the trusted CA list once (`default` + `system`, deduplicated) without the affected roots:
  - `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, `AAA Certificate Services`, `emSign Root TLS CA - G3`, `emSign Root CS CA - G3` (from the disclosure's roots.json)
  - the other eMudhra roots removed in oven-sh/bun#46159: `emSign Root CA - G1`, `emSign Root CA - C1`, `emSign ECC Root CA - C3`
- `tls.setDefaultCACertificates(filtered)` covers `node:tls`, `node:https`, and on Node also `fetch` and `ws`.
- On Bun, `fetch` and `WebSocket` ignore that default, so the global `fetch` and `WebSocket` are wrapped to pass the filtered list as `tls.ca`. Callers that pass their own `tls.ca` are left alone.
- If none of the affected roots are in the CA list, it does nothing.

`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and user-supplied CAs are kept, so corporate proxies keep working. Keep-alive is unaffected: the filtered array is built once and reused, so pooled connections are still reused.

This is temporary. Remove the module and its one call once Bun and Node ship their fixes and we've bumped to them.

## Verification

With `bun --use-system-ca`, after `install()`:
- `dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com` → `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY`. Without the change, the same host returns 200.
- The same test host is also rejected through `node:https` and `WebSocket`, and the AAA-path test host is rejected too. On macOS, the AAA path returned 200 before this change.
- github.com, api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, models.dev, opencode.ai, registry.npmjs.org and Sectigo-issued sites (zerossl.com, sectigo.com) still connect.
- A local HTTPS/WSS server signed by a CA in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` still works directly and through an HTTP CONNECT proxy.
- 20 sequential requests reuse one TLS connection.

Checks (in `packages/cli`):
- `bun test test/tls-trust.test.ts` passes; `OPENCODE_TEST_LIVE_CA=1` turns on the live-network cases, which also pass.
- `bun test test/import-boundaries.test.ts` passes.
- `bun typecheck` and oxlint are clean.

Not covered: child processes (`git`, `curl`, shell commands) use the OS trust store. The Electron main process is covered by the Electron 44.9.1 bump (#57533).

Requested by: @kitlangton (Kit via Slack)

prs.title: feat(app): animate the timeline like iOS while a session runs
prs.body:
**Head:** `d68e8840a41d88ae06484183bb26aa64191146d3` · 2 commits on `beta` `5c95abcf34` · 14 files · code +1156/−105, tests +135/−7

## Why

While a session runs, the desktop timeline lands every change in one frame. Streamed text adds a line and everything above it jumps, a new tool row pops in at full height, a row that leaves takes its space with it at once, and Working pops in and out, sometimes twice. The iOS app animates the same moments, and this brings that model to Desktop.

## What changes

**Timeline** (`packages/app/src/session/timeline`)

- **Rows grow instead of landing.** While the timeline follows its end, a row's displayed height springs to its measured height (`row-growth.ts`, 0.32 s, no bounce) behind a soft bottom edge. The end stays put and the rows above glide. A new growth takes its first step in the frame that measured it.
- **Rows that leave fade where they were.** A copy of the row fades out in place, keeping the opacity its own animations had reached, while the rows above close the gap on the same spring. Growth fills the gap first. The gap only starts closing once nothing has grown for 120 ms, so a pause between streamed chunks can't start it and then stop it again.
- **Space the composer frees is held.** When the queue closes as its prompt arrives, the end stays where it is and the freed space waits under the last row for the reply to rise into. Before, the end sank with the composer and the reply then pushed it back up.
- **Scroll stays on the layout grid.** Chromium rounds a written `scrollTop` to a whole pixel, which made row edges tremble on every write. Each write now takes the whole pixel below and draws the remainder as a `translate`, which clears as soon as the user scrolls or the timeline stops following.
- **Streamed markdown never shrinks mid-stream.** While its text streams, a followed row never shrinks below what it shows; a lower target that is still above that just bends the growth down, and a growth bent toward a nearer target lands there instead of passing it and coming back. Once the text completes, the row takes whatever it measures in the next frame.
- **Your own send flies into its bubble.** A steer sent from the composer flies from the composer into its bubble, drawn above everything else. Queued and remote deliveries just grow in.
- **Working and the background hint** fade in one lane from whatever opacity they've reached, so they never show twice.

**Composer** (`packages/app/src/session/composer`, `composer/editor`)

- The queue panel springs open and closed. While it moves, it clips behind a soft edge, and at rest it clips nothing, so its skirt under the composer stays drawn. It keeps its last prompts while it closes, and a refreshed queue row keeps its element.
- The activity pill fades out still naming the last work, the placeholder crossfades, and the Queue hint no longer flashes on every send.

**Reduced motion** drops all travel. Status, placeholder, activity pill and hover footers keep short opacity fades (0.11–0.2 s); the queue panel lands at once.

## Scope

Desktop timeline and composer region only. No row redesign and no new production UI. The tuning controls only appear in the debug bar's Motion workspace.

## Verification

- **Strict motion trace** of a recorded 4-turn session at 60 fps with stepped frames (2145 frames, every timeline row, the status lanes and the composer edges). It covers streaming, tool rows, steer and queue sends, both deliveries and the turn ends. Edges are compared only while they are an element's own edge, not a clip line.
  - The previous draft of this branch, same harness: 55 jumps over 1 px, 9 visible unmounts, 1390 reversals and 3163 sub-pixel reversals, and the composer gap drifted 79.52–80.5 px.
  - Now: 0 jumps, 0 unmounts, 0 reversals, 0 sub-pixel reversals (steps over 1/64 px), and the composer gap is exactly 80 px in every frame.
- **First load and session switch:** frame-by-frame probe, with and without reduced motion. No animations on timeline or status elements, and no visible row moves after it first paints.
- **Reduced motion:** a full replay animates opacity only (tailwind fades carry identity transforms).
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/app` and `packages/session-ui`, `row-growth.test.ts` (7 pass), `bun run lint:changed origin/beta` (0 problems).
- Recordings (2880×1800, 60 fps, dark): one full turn at 1×, plus the send and the turn end at 0.25×. They're on the Problems board review R-51.

**Not verified:** a real Electron build, a real model stream (replayed tape in headless Chromium only), trackpad momentum during growth, and other window widths.

prs.title: fix(desktop): open video and image URLs in the browser pane
prs.body:
## Problem

Opening a video URL in the in-app browser pane (`browser.tabs.open` / `browser.navigate`) failed with `ERR_FAILED (-2)`, even though the page rendered.

## Cause

It wasn't a download handler. Chromium commits a media URL as its built-in video viewer, then stops loading without firing `did-finish-load`. Electron's `loadURL` treats "stopped without finish or fail" as a generic `ERR_FAILED (-2)` and rejects. The pane awaited that promise, so the tool call failed over a working page.

## Fix

The pane's `load` notes whether the main frame committed (`did-navigate`). If it did and the only error is Electron's synthesized `-2`, the load counts as a success. A download never commits, so `Content-Disposition: attachment` and other non-renderable responses still go through `will-download` and fail as before. Restored tabs use the same path.

## Proof

- Unit test `committedLoad` in `policy.test.ts`: committed plus `-2` loads, an uncommitted `-2` (download) fails, and a committed real network error fails.
- Real Electron 44.9.1 (headless window, sandboxed partition with a `will-download` listener, local server with range support, a 3-second ffmpeg `testsrc` clip):
  - before: `/clip.mp4` gives `did-navigate 200`, then `did-stop-loading` with no `did-finish-load`, and `loadURL` rejects with `ERR_FAILED (-2)`. The document holds a `<video>`.
  - after: `/clip.mp4` resolves and the video reaches `readyState 4`. `/attach.mp4` (attachment) still fires `will-download` and fails.
- The repo has no Electron test harness, so the Electron run is a one-off script, not a checked-in test. Image URLs weren't part of the repro.

prs.title: fix(app): show untracked folders as one review row
prs.body:
## Problem

The Review launcher said "45210 files changed" in a repo where `git status --porcelain` lists 38 entries. The server listed changes with `git status --untracked-files=all`, so every file inside an untracked folder (unignored `node_modules` under `research/`, for example) became its own row. It also counted lines in each of those files.

## Change

- **Server** (`plugin/vcs/git.ts`): `vcs.diff` takes an optional `untracked: "files" | "folders"` (additive protocol field; the client is regenerated).
  - The default, `files`, keeps the full listing, so the TUI diff viewer and plugins are unchanged.
  - With `folders`, status uses `--untracked-files=normal`. An untracked folder is one `dir/` entry, with no line counts and no patch.
  - A location inside an untracked folder lists only that folder's immediate entries (files, plus subfolders as `dir/`). It shows at most 500 and checks 500 at a time. It stops after checking 5,000 entries or after 1 s, whichever comes first. A listing that stops early ends with an entry for the folder itself, marked `more: true`, with no count.
- **Client** (`review/*`, `file/tree-*`): the Review pane asks for `folders`.
  - Folder rows show in the change tree as closed folders with a folder icon. Opening one fetches its entries through `vcs.diff`, with the folder as the location. The row then shows the entry count, followed by "· more not shown" when the listing stopped early.
  - The launcher and tab count equal the top-level rows, i.e. what `git status --porcelain` lists.

## Measured

Temp repo with one tracked change and 20,000 untracked files in `research/p*/node_modules/pkg/`, `vcs.diff("working")` (3 runs):

| | rows | server time |
|---|---|---|
| before | 20,001 | 4.0–4.4 s |
| after (`untracked: "folders"`) | 2 | 35–82 ms |

In the real web app, against a repo with one tracked change, an ignored dir and a 20,000-file untracked folder (`git status --porcelain` = 3): the New tab and the pane both show 3 (merge base: 20002). The folder is one row and lists its entries when opened.

## LOC

- Code: +219 / −28
- Tests: +103 / −2
- Generated client: +30 / −2

## Tests

- `packages/core/test/vcs.test.ts` uses a temp repo with an ignored folder, an untracked folder (50 files, `deep/`, and `wide/` with 505 files) and one tracked change.
  - With `folders`, the root gives `keep.txt` and `research/`, and `research` gives 52 entries (50 files with patches, `deep/`, `wide/`).
  - `research/wide` stops at 500 entries plus a `more` entry. With 505 ignored entries sorting first, `research/noisy` still lists `z-important.ts`.
  - With 5,000 ignored entries before `z-visible.ts`, the listing stops at the scan budget after at most 11 `git status` calls and returns only the `more` entry.
  - Without the option, the root still lists all 557 files.
- `review/kinds.test.ts`: `expandReviewFolders` keeps the top-level rows and adds an opened folder's entries after its row.
- `file/tree-model.test.ts`: a trailing-slash entry builds a directory node.

## CI

The e2e failures also fail or retry on the beta tip the PR is merged with (see the comments). `session-summary` › "MCP authentication starts before a slow resource catalog" passed 5/5 with `--repeat-each 5 --retries 0` on both this head and the merge base.

prs.title: fix(desktop): faster side-panel tabs with a much shorter flash
prs.body:
Kit's Scrawl capture of the side-panel browser showed five problems. This fixes the ones caused by our code.

**⌘T on an empty panel**
The empty side panel is really a blank browser tab showing the new tab page. Pressing ⌘T there did open a tab, but the "a new tab holds the place of the next pick" rule (`model.ts`) closed the old blank tab right away, so nothing seemed to happen. Now, picking another new tab keeps the first one, so ⌘T adds a tab as it does in a browser.

**Slow new tab page, slow ⇧⌘T, and the flash**
- `pane.ts` held back every tab event from the window until the server had acknowledged `rpc.state`. That round trip waited in a queue behind other sends, so it was slow whenever the server was busy. The window now gets each event as soon as it happens, and the server copy is still sent in order.
- A new tab page loaded `about:blank` twice: once when the page was created and again through a redundant `navigate`. Each load marked the tab as loading, and the panel shows nothing over a loading tab, so it blanked before the new tab page and again after it (Kit's capture at 51.60–51.66 s). Now a blank tab skips that navigate, and loading a blank document no longer counts as loading (`chromium.ts`), because a blank document is never shown anyway. The new tab is selected at once and shows its new tab page straight away.

**Timings: beta vs this PR** (OpenCode Dev in its own profile and server on the same Mac, 3 runs each; real screen recording of the window)
| | beta | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ⌘T on an empty panel's new tab page | no new tab; panel blank 0.16–1.15 s | 2nd tab with its new tab page in 0.33–0.41 s |
| ⌘T on a loaded page: tab in the strip | 0.31–0.49 s | 0.24–0.38 s |
| ⌘T on a loaded page: new tab page shown | 0.42–0.96 s | 0.24–0.38 s, with the tab |
| panel blank in between (DOM + view log) | 0.11–0.59 s | 0–0.11 s |
| panel blank in the screen recording (one run) | ~0.83 s | ~0.2 s |
| "Request failed" after a superseded load | every run | never |

The blank that is left comes from `packages/app/src/runtime/extension/embeds.tsx:230`, which hides the old page's native view immediately (so closing the panel never leaves a page over the app), before the new tab page has painted. Holding the view until that paint would change shared embed code, so it is not part of this PR.

**"Request failed"**
When a newer navigation replaces one still in progress (a second submit, a click on a Recent row while the page is slow, or a redirect), Electron's `loadURL` rejects with `ERR_ABORTED (-3)`. It does this even though the tab carries on loading and no `did-fail-load` fires. The window showed that rejection as "Request failed". The window's own commands now ignore `ERR_ABORTED`; pages that really fail still show their failed state.

**Network (not changed here)**
All embedded browser traffic goes through the OpenCode server: a local CONNECT proxy, then one `tunnel.read`/`tunnel.write` RPC per chunk of up to 64 KB (`network.ts`, `plugin-browser/src/proxy.ts`). On an idle isolated server this is as fast as going direct. But each page needs hundreds of these calls, so any stall on the server is multiplied.

| GitHub PR page, hidden Electron | load |
| --- | --- |
| direct | 637–1356 ms |
| through the tunnel, idle server | 657–681 ms |
| tunnel + per-RPC stalls sampled from the live :4096 server (p90 28 ms) | 1376–1523 ms |
| tunnel + 4× those stalls | 5.4–10.4 s |

One load is about 16 opens, 220–385 reads and about 110 writes. A cheap GET on the live server measured p90 28–62 ms and max 119–425 ms; an isolated server measured max 4 ms. Letting the desktop's own local sidecar bypass the tunnel would remove this cost. That is a policy change, so it is left to a follow-up.

**Not changed:** ⇧⌘T still rebuilds the page from its URL; keeping the closed view alive is not cheap. ⌘1–9 and ⇧⌘[ ] are in #57301.

**Tests**
`browser-pane-restore.spec.ts`: "adds a second new tab with ⌘T on a new tab page". It passes with this change and fails on beta's `model.ts`.

LOC: code +41 / −31 (`pane.ts`, `model.ts`, `chromium.ts`); tests +39 / −13 (spec, fixture).

issues.title: processResponsesStream crashes when function_call_arguments.done omits arguments

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Every tool-call turn through my OpenAI-Responses-compatible gateway dies with:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')
```

The gateway (a new-api fork fronting GLM chat-completions models) emits `response.function_call_arguments.done` **without the `arguments` field**; the deltas and `response.output_item.done` carry the full arguments:

```
event: response.function_call_arguments.delta
data: {"type":"response.function_call_arguments.delta","delta":"{\"","output_index":2,"item_id":"call_c3518f47ca854f1191589f87"}
event: response.function_call_arguments.done
data: {"type":"response.function_call_arguments.done","output_index":2,"item_id":"call_c3518f47ca854f1191589f87"}
```

In `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` (`processResponsesStream`, ~line 743 on main):

```ts
slot.block.partialJson = event.arguments;                    // wipes the accumulated deltas
slot.block.arguments = parseStreamingJson(slot.block.partialJson);
if (event.arguments.startsWith(previousPartialJson)) {       // TypeError
```

`response.custom_tool_call_input.done` without `input` throws the same error via `appendGrammarToolInputJsonDelta`. This is the same family as #9974 (llama.cpp omitting `output_index`), which was fixed in core; it was also reported earlier as #8527 (auto-closed before review).

### Steps to reproduce

Core-level, no extensions involved: pass these events to `processResponsesStream` — `output_item.added` (function_call, `arguments: ""`) → `function_call_arguments.delta` × 2 → `function_call_arguments.done` **without `arguments`** → `output_item.done` with the full arguments → `response.completed`. It throws on the fourth event.

Live evidence: through this gateway every turn that triggers a tool call fails; the same models through a compliant Responses upstream work fine.

### Expected behavior

Keep the accumulated deltas when the done event omits `arguments`; `output_item.done` already finalizes the call (`item.arguments || partialJson`). A small guard fixes this and the custom-input variant. I have a branch with the fix plus a regression test ready; happy to open a PR once approved.

### Version

1.3.0 (present on current main)

---
*Filed by an AI coding agent at the account owner's request; the SSE capture and core-level reproduction are from the owner's environment.*

issues.title: auto switch to the new model API provider when a route failure ends the task(extension cannot meet the request)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change? When the active model or provider becomes unavailable due to a route-level failure, continue the turn on the next configured model instead of failing. ### Why? issues.title: `pi -p` silently uses another model when an extension provider's catalog is stale; `pi update --models` skips extension catalogs
issues.body:
### What happened?

My settings have `defaultProvider: "pengepul"` and `defaultModel: "opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash"`. pengepul is an extension provider (@pwguler/pi-pengepul-provider 0.5.3) whose `refreshModels` fetches `GET /v1/models` from my relay and persists the list. Its `models-store.json` entry was from Oct 4, before the relay served any `opencode/*` ids.

`pi -p --no-tools "Reply with exactly: ok"` printed `ok`, but the session file says `anthropic/claude-fable-5`, and nothing mentioned the default. Print mode only refreshes with `allowNetwork: false` (`core/agent-session-services.ts:142,194`). So pengepul restored its old list, and `findInitialModel` fell through to the first available model with `fallbackMessage: undefined` (`core/model-resolver.ts:690-704`), which print mode wouldn't show anyway (`main.ts:986`).

`pi update --models` printed "Model catalogs refreshed" and left the pengepul entry alone, because `refreshModelCatalogs` never loads extensions (`package-manager-cli.ts:583-609`). `docs/models.md` names that command as the way to force a refresh.

Starting `pi --mode rpc` once with stdin held open fixed it: `main.ts:938-946` runs a network refresh for RPC, and print mode has nothing like it. The entry went from 500 to 535 models and `-p` ran on `pengepul/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. I had to do that on all three hosts.

Paths are under `packages/coding-agent/src/` at v1.0.4. main at f10993bc7 has the same code.

### Steps to reproduce

The bug needs an extension provider, so `-ne -e` loads just this one. Its "relay" is a file:

```ts
// /tmp/stale.ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createProvider, openAICompletionsApi } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";

const model = (id) => ({ id, name: id, provider: "stale", api: "openai-completions",
  baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1", reasoning: false, input: ["text"], contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192,
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 } });

export default (pi) => pi.registerProvider(createProvider({
  id: "stale", api: openAICompletionsApi(), models: [],
  auth: { apiKey: { name: "key", check: async () => ({ type: "api_key", source: "test" }),
    resolve: async () => ({ auth: { apiKey: "x" }, source: "test" }) } },
  fetchModels: async () => readFileSync("/tmp/stale-ids", "utf8").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).map(model),
}));
```

I ran this with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set to an empty dir and no provider keys in the environment. Node's fetch refuses port 9, so requests end in `Connection error.` and nothing is sent.

1. `echo model-a > /tmp/stale-ids`, put `{"stale": {"type": "api_key", "key": "x"}}` in `auth.json`, then `sleep 10 | pi -ne -e /tmp/stale.ts --mode rpc`. `models-store.json` now has `model-a` under `stale`. Without the stored key, startup sometimes misses the provider entirely, like #8810.
2. `echo "model-a model-b" > /tmp/stale-ids` and set `"defaultProvider": "stale", "defaultModel": "model-b"` in `settings.json`.
3. `pi -ne -e /tmp/stale.ts -p hi`. The new session's `model_change` is `stale/model-a`, and stderr says only `Connection error.`
4. `pi update --models` prints "Model catalogs refreshed", `models-store.json` stays byte-identical, and step 3 still lands on `model-a`.
5. Repeat the RPC command from step 1, then step 3. Now it's `stale/model-b`.

### Expected behavior

`pi -p` runs the configured default, or says on stderr which model it used instead. `pi update --models` refreshes extension catalogs too, or says it skipped them.

When the default isn't in the restored catalog, print mode could refresh just that provider before falling back, e.g. `modelRuntime.refresh({ providers: [defaultProvider], signal })` with the usual 15 s timeout. That costs nothing when the default resolves. A stderr warning whenever a configured default gets replaced would have pointed straight at this; #8810 asks for it too. `pi update --models` could load extensions the way `createAgentSessionServices` does.

### Version

1.0.4, repro run on it (Linux, Node 24.20.0). First seen on 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 on three hosts, Linux and macOS.

### What happened?

Models newly enabled by a GitHub Copilot Enterprise administrator can remain absent from Pi's model picker after restarting Pi. The OAuth credential's `availableModelIds` is cached, and restarting does not necessarily refresh it while the OAuth credential is still valid. Opening the model selector refreshes the shared catalogs, but the GitHub Copilot account-specific `/models` list is not refreshed as part of that operation.

2. Have an enterprise administrator enable a model that is not in Pi's cached `availableModelIds`.
3. Restart Pi and open `/model`.

The newly enabled model remains missing until the OAuth credential/model list is refreshed.

### Expected behavior

Refresh the authenticated Copilot `/models` list at startup and when the Copilot credential changes. Show only models GitHub reports as picker-enabled and not policy-disabled.

Pi 1.2.0

issues.title: OSC 52 copy in fullscreen TUI is swallowed by tmux (no passthrough wrap)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Copy-on-select in the fullscreen TUI writes a raw OSC 52 (`\x1b]52;c;...`). When pi runs inside tmux, tmux consumes the incoming OSC 52 into its paste buffer and does not relay it to its client. pi flashes "Copied!" either way.

On a headless Linux host over SSH (no DISPLAY/WAYLAND), OSC 52 is the only clipboard route, so copying from the TUI silently does nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. tmux on a headless Linux host, SSH'd from another machine (`set-clipboard on`)
2. Run pi, drag-select text in the transcript, release
3. "Copied!" flashes but the client machine's clipboard is unchanged
4. `tmux show-buffer` on the pi host shows the selection: tmux ate it

Traced to core, not an extension. Both OSC 52 emit sites write the raw sequence: `copyToClipboard` in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts` and the TUI fallback in `packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts`.

### Expected behavior

The client terminal's clipboard updates. Wrapping the write in the tmux DCS passthrough (`\x1bPtmux;\x1b<seq>\x1b\\`) when `$TMUX` is set fixes it: tmux forwards the unwrapped sequence to its client, where a plain terminal sets the clipboard and an outer tmux picks it up. I have the change with tests ready and can send a PR.

### Version

1.0.0 (also present on current main)

---

Drafted with AI assistance (traced and verified with an agent; I did the diagnosis and reviewed the writeup).

issues.title: codemode: schemaToType loses sibling type when rendering allOf constraints
issues.body:
### What happened?

`schemaToType()` renders a string schema as `unknown` when it has sibling `allOf` constraints. Code Mode therefore describes string arguments such as `find` and `replace` as `unknown`. Zod 4 produces this shape for a string with multiple `.regex()` constraints.

### Steps to reproduce

Run this standalone library call (no agent extensions involved):

```js
import { schemaToType } from '@earendil-works/pi-codemode/declarations';

console.log(schemaToType({
  type: 'string',
  allOf: [{ pattern: '^a' }, { pattern: 'z$' }],
}));
// Actual: unknown
```

I reproduced this with the unmodified declaration renderer in 1.3.0. In `toType()`, the `allOf` branch returns before considering the sibling `type`; both pattern-only branches render as `unknown`.

### Expected behavior

Render `string`. More generally, preserve sibling schema information when rendering `allOf`, rather than considering only its children.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-codemode` 1.3.0. The same branch is present in the current `main` source.

issues.title: F12 settings editor won't close with Esc; F11 popup does.

labels.name: package-report
labels.description: Security report or otherwise against an extension or package on pi.dev

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### Package name

@vanillagreen/pi-extension-manager

### Version

3.0.5

### What are you reporting?

Malicious or unsafe behavior

### Details

# Escape does not close the settings editor under the Kitty keyboard protocol (F12 / `alt+shift+s`)

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Package | `@vanillagreen/pi-extension-manager` **3.0.5** |
| Pi | **1.3.0** |
| Node | v24.13.0 |
| OS | macOS 15.3.2 |
| Terminal | iTerm2 (Kitty keyboard protocol enabled) |

## Summary

The settings editor opened with `f12` / `alt+shift+s` (`/extensions:settings`) cannot be closed with **Escape**. Only `ctrl+c` works. The extension manager popup opened with `f11` / `alt+shift+e` closes with Escape normally, so the two overlays behave differently in the same terminal.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi in a terminal that enables the Kitty keyboard protocol (iTerm2, kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm).
2. Press `f12` (or run `/extensions:settings`) to open the settings editor.
3. Press `Escape`.

## Expected

The editor closes, as the `f11` manager popup does.

## Actual

Nothing happens. `ctrl+c` closes it.

## Root cause

`extensions/manager/quick-settings-ui.ts` compares the raw input against a bare ESC byte instead of using `matchesKey`. Lines **242** and **253**:

```ts
if (data === "\u001b" || matchesKey(data, "ctrl+c")) {
```

Under the Kitty keyboard protocol (and `modifyOtherKeys`), Escape is not delivered as a bare `\u001b`. `matchesKey` decodes those encodings; `===` does not. Note that `ctrl+c` on the *same line* is checked with `matchesKey`, which is why it still works.

Measured on pi-tui 1.3.0 — the same physical key, four encodings:

| encoding | `data === "\u001b"` | `matchesKey(data, "escape")` |
|---|---|---|
| bare ESC (legacy) | `true` | `true` |
| Kitty `\u001b[27u` | **`false`** | `true` |
| Kitty + modifiers `\u001b[27;1:1u` | **`false`** | `true` |
| modifyOtherKeys `\u001b[27;1;27~` | **`false`** | `true` |

This also explains the asymmetry: `extensions/manager/manager-ui.ts` (the `f11` popup) already uses `matchesKey(data, "escape")` at lines 280, 303 and 413, so it is unaffected.

## Verification

Driving the real `openQuickSettings` component with a stubbed TUI and sending both encodings:

```
BEFORE (3.0.5 as published)
  legacy ESC \u001b      -> CLOSED {"type":"close"}
  Kitty ESC \u001b[27u   -> IGNORED

AFTER (patch applied)
  legacy ESC \u001b      -> CLOSED {"type":"close"}
  Kitty ESC \u001b[27u   -> CLOSED {"type":"close"}
```

## Suggested fix

Replace the raw comparison with `matchesKey` in both places, matching `manager-ui.ts`:

```diff
--- a/extensions/manager/quick-settings-ui.ts
+++ b/extensions/manager/quick-settings-ui.ts
@@
 	function handleInput(data: string): void {
 		if (ui.editing) {
-			if (data === "\u001b" || matchesKey(data, "ctrl+c")) {
+			if (matchesKey(data, "escape") || matchesKey(data, "ctrl+c")) {
 				ui.editing = undefined;
 				requestRender();
 				return;
 			}
@@
-		if (data === "\u001b" || matchesKey(data, "ctrl+c")) return done({ type: "close" });
+		if (matchesKey(data, "escape") || matchesKey(data, "ctrl+c")) return done({ type: "close" });
```

I swept the rest of the package for the same pattern (`data === "\u001b"`, `=== "\x1b"`, `=== "\033"`) and these two lines are the only occurrences — every other Escape check already uses the API.

## Notes

- Worth a broader check for the same pattern in the sibling packages under `pi-extensions/`; raw ESC comparisons are silent failures that only appear in terminals using an enhanced keyboard protocol.
- Pi 1.2.0 shipped a related fix — *"Fixed key bindings that name a shifted symbol, such as `+` or `ctrl++`, not matching under the Kitty keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys"* — so the guidance to prefer `matchesKey` over raw byte comparison is already established.

issues.title: pi update --extensions silently skips project packages when project trust is not saved

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Make `pi update` print a warning when it skips project packages because the project is not trusted, and say how to include them. Follow-up to #8971, which was approved for a PR in September but never got one.

### Why?

`pi update` only uses saved trust (by design since #5674), but a project can be trusted without saving it: `pi install -l` in a fresh project runs trusted because `.pi/` does not exist yet, and "Trust (this session only)" or `defaultProjectTrust: "always"` are not saved either. `pi update --extensions` then skips every project package and still prints "Updated packages". If the session trusts the project without saving it, the startup update check keeps reporting the project copy as outdated, and the suggested command does nothing.

Reproduced on 1.3.0:

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
pi install -l npm:is-number                    # runs trusted, trust.json is not written
npm install is-number@6.0.0 --prefix .pi/npm   # simulate an available update
pi update --extensions                          # "Updated packages", project copy stays at 6.0.0
pi update --extensions --approve                # updates it to 7.0.0
```

### How? (optional)

Keep the no-prompt design of #5674 and only add the warning. In the update branch of `package-manager-cli.ts`, when the project is untrusted and neither `--approve` nor `--no-approve` was passed, read the project `packages` list (only to count it, nothing is applied) and print:

Warning: Project packages in <cwd>/.pi/settings.json are skipped because the project is not trusted. Use --approve, or run /trust in pi to save trust.

This mirrors the note `pi mcp list` prints for an ignored project `mcp.json`. It includes a regression test in `test/package-command-paths.test.ts` and one paragraph in `docs/cli.md`. The alternative is saving trust when `pi install -l` creates the project settings; that changes trust semantics, so I left it out.

I'd like to send the PR.

issues.title: codemode: add a `background` option

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What

Add `background` to codemode's `// @options:` line. With it the tool returns immediately with an id and the script keeps running after the turn ends. A later codemode call does `jobs(id)` to get status, the output so far, and cancel.

A separate tool is the alternative, but codemode's input is raw JS, so a status query can't be an argument of the same call anyway.

### Why

Mario said he'd take a PR for this: https://x.com/badlogicgames/status/2112639101405114451

Lucas wants a workflow that takes longer than 2m to keep running while the conversation continues and can look in on it. Today a script that long either blocks the turn (`timeout_ms` is a hard deadline for the whole script) or gets split into calls that can't see each other's state. `store` carries data across calls, not liveness.

### How

Durable already has background tasks the conversation doesn't wait on, and in `session-worker.ts` a live task keeps its worker alive, so a background script is one of those instead of a new kind of thing. The job holds the final result and the partial output, which is what `jobs(id)` returns.

Happy to implement it if that shape looks right.

issues.title: Windows installer: standalone Node is shadowed by an older system Node after restart, pi crashes on startup
issues.body:
### What happened?

I installed pi with `powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex"` as copied from pi.dev, on Windows 11. I already had Node 22.12.0 installed system-wide in `C:\Program Files\nodejs`. The installer saw it was older than 22.19.0 and offered to install standalone Node, and I said yes. The install finished fine.

After I opened a new PowerShell window, `pi` crashed on its first request:

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
TypeError: zlib.createZstdDecompress is not a function
    at Object.onResponseStart (.../pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-66G7ITPS.js:129:70337)
```

Cause: `Install-NodeStandalone` calls `Add-UserPathEntry ... -Prepend`, which puts `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pi-node\current` first in the **user** PATH. Windows builds PATH as machine entries followed by user entries, so `C:\Program Files\nodejs` still comes first. During the install it works, because the installer also prepends to `$env:PATH` for its own process. The managed launchers (`pi.cmd`, `pi.ps1`) then call plain `node`, so in a new shell pi runs on 22.12.0, which has no zstd support.

`pi` works when started on pi-node directly:
`& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\pi-node\current\node.exe" "$env:USERPROFILE\.pi\agent\bin\pi-launcher.js"`

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, install a Node older than 22.19 system-wide (MSI, adds `C:\Program Files\nodejs` to machine PATH).
2. Run the installer and answer Y to installing standalone Node.
3. Open a new terminal and run `pi`. `node -v` shows the old version.

### Expected behavior

pi runs on the Node the installer put in place. For example, when the installer installs pi-node, the launchers could call that `node.exe` by full path instead of using whatever `node` is first on PATH. Or the installer could check `node -v` against a fresh machine+user PATH at the end and warn when an older Node shadows pi-node.

Related: #7771 (same crash from an old Node; a startup version check would make this one obvious too).

### Version

1.3.0 (installer from pi.dev, 2026-10-20), Windows 11, system Node 22.12.0, pi-node 22.23.3

Note: this report was drafted with AI assistance (Claude) from my debugging session. I reviewed and edited it before posting, and the cause and workaround were verified on my machine.

issues.title: `!command` keys and headers in models.json block the event loop on every request

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
> AI disclosure: drafted with an AI coding assistant. I checked the cited code against 1.3.0 and ran the repro below.

### What happened?

A `!command` value for `apiKey` (or a header) in `models.json` runs with `spawnSync`/`execSync` (10 s timeout) every time a request's auth is resolved: `ModelRuntime.prepareRequest` → `getAuth` → `resolveConfigValueOrThrow` / `resolveConfiguredModelHeaders` → `executeCommandUncached` (`dist/core/resolve-config-value.js`).

Running at request time without a cache is documented and fine. The problem is that it is synchronous: the whole process (the TUI, or an app embedding pi) stops while the command runs, on every request.

### Steps to reproduce

`models.json` with a key command that takes 2 s:

```json
{ "providers": { "slow-key": {
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1", "api": "openai-completions",
  "apiKey": "!node -e \"setTimeout(() => console.log('sk-test'), 2000)\"",
  "models": [{ "id": "m" }] } } }
```

```js
const runtime = await ModelRuntime.create({ modelsPath, authPath, modelsStorePath, refreshOnCreate: false });
const model = runtime.getModel("slow-key", "m");
// a 10 ms setInterval records the longest gap between ticks
await runtime.getAuth(model); // called twice
```

Output (pi 1.3.0, Node 24.21, Windows):

```
request 1: getAuth took 2132 ms, longest event-loop gap 2148 ms, key sk-test
request 2: getAuth took 2121 ms, longest event-loop gap 2121 ms, key sk-test
```

### Expected behavior

The command runs asynchronously (`spawn` and await), with the same timeout and the same uncached behaviour, so the event loop keeps running while it waits.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Async SessionManager.open for hosts that open large sessions

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
> AI disclosure: drafted with an AI coding assistant. I checked the cited code and measured the numbers below on 1.3.0.

### What do you want to change?

An async way to open a session file, e.g. `SessionManager.openAsync(path, sessionDir?, cwdOverride?, { signal })`, that reads entries with a stream the way `list()` already does in `buildSessionInfo`. `AgentSessionRuntime` could then use it for resume, switch and fork (`agent-session-runtime.js`, the three `SessionManager.open` calls).

### Why?

`SessionManager.open` reads and parses the whole file synchronously (`loadEntriesFromFile`: `openSync`/`readSync`, plus an `appendFileSync` repair). A 193 MB session file blocks the event loop for about 470 ms (median of 5, pi 1.3.0, Node 24.21, Windows).

`list()` is async, but it only returns `SessionInfo`. An embedder that needs the tree (the active branch, custom entries) has to call `open`. Doing that for 535 sessions (695 MB) blocked our app's main thread for 7.4 s; we now run it on a worker thread to keep the app responsive, but resume and switch inside pi still block.

Related: #9601 (header lookup), #10638 (memory).

### How? (optional)

Same parsing (`parseSessionEntryLine`, migration, header check) over `createReadStream` + `readline`, abortable. `open()` stays as is for the CLI.

issues.title: Calculated cost for top open models on OpenRouter is off by 2-3x almost always

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

The model catalog for Openrouter currently uses the **cheapest** provider's pricing to calculate cost, which makes reported cost **off** by 2-3x most of the time, for popular open-weights models which many providers offer.
 
Best example is [z-ai/glm-5.3-flash](https://openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Compare the `DeepInfra` price (cheapest provider) vs. the actual median price, a 50% difference. Similar case for [deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash](https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash).

Several factors make this work poorly in practice:
1. The cheapest provider is always at overcapacity and throwing 429, so requests get rerouted.
2. The common pattern is for one or two providers to serve an fp4 variant at low tps with a steep discount, while most of the traffic is routed to other providers at a much higher price point.
3. upstream failures trigger automatic fallback to another provider, so effective rates can and do change mid-session.

### Solutions

The simplest would be to use the accurate total cost OpenRouter includes in the response, and keep the cost breakdown approximate.

The cost breakdown ratios across OpenRouter providers are **far more uniform** than absolute cost is, so using the catalog rates as weights in order to update the estimate is a further possibility.

Optionally, switching the cost breakdown from showing currency to showing a percentage could soften this further.

Other alternatives are:
1. Fetch endpoint pricing dynamically for the current active model, or all scoped models.
2. Fetch endpoint pricing for all scoped models at startup (1 extra API call per model).

Previously:
#8940, #7109 , #6881, #6314, #6313, #4900, #5734, #3791, #3132, #2873

issues.title: Extensions that `sendMessage` at `session_start` turn every session into a legacy transcript

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
## Problem
`getInitialSystemMessage` reads `messages[0]`. Extensions that `sendMessage` during `session_start` (pi-memory, pi-session-search) put a custom/user message ahead of pi's system message, so every session is treated as a "legacy" transcript:

- Anthropic requests lose the `system` field and native inline tool changes (`tool_addition`), so loading a deferred tool via `tool_search` changes the tools block and rewrites the whole prompt cache (e.g. cacheRead 0 / cacheWrite 18,589 on the first call after a load, vs. cacheRead 18,330 / cacheWrite 246 once fixed).
- Codex runs under "You are a helpful assistant." instead of pi's prompt.

Also: a `before_agent_start` handler returning `systemPrompt` collapses all system messages into one head and disables native tool changes (tools grow in place, no `tool_addition`).

## Repro
`pi -p` with pi-session-search (or pi-memory) installed and any `deferred` tool; ask the agent to `tool_search` for it and call it. Compare usage on the turn after the load with and without the extension.

## Suggested fix
Persist the initial system message before dispatching `session_start`, or let providers find the first system message past leading custom/user messages.

## Workaround
We hoist the system message to the head from a `context_with_system` hook (QuinRiva/loom#412).

issues.title: A split mouse report leaves its tail in the prompt: the escape timeout flushes half a sequence and the editor types the rest

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Disclosure: I drafted this text with an AI agent. I reproduced the split-read case locally with the shipped StdinBuffer and Editor and pasted the observed output above.


### Steps to reproduce

```
   ```ts
   const buffer = new StdinBuffer({ timeout: 10, escapeTimeout: 10 });
   const editor = new Editor(tui, theme);
   buffer.on("data", (sequence) => editor.handleInput(sequence));

   buffer.process("\x1b[<35;4");                 // first half of an SGR motion report
   await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 40));  // longer than the timeout: head is flushed
   buffer.process("8;27M");                      // second half arrives as new input

   editor.getText();  // "8;27M"
   ```

   Observed: emitted sequences are ["\u001b[<35;4","8",";","2","7","M"] and the editor ends up containing
   8;27M. A report that arrives in one read is consumed by the fullscreen mouse handling as expected; only the
   split case leaks.

   In a terminal: run pi, move the mouse while it is busy (the escape timeout is 10 ms, so a busy event loop
   splits the report), and fragments like 8;27M appear in the prompt.
 ```

### Expected behavior

```
   Half of a terminal control sequence should never reach the editor. Either StdinBuffer keeps the fragment out of
   the input stream and swallows the continuation that follows, or Editor.handleInput() refuses to type a string
   that is an obvious control-sequence remnant (an ESC-less report such as [<35;48;27M is typed as-is today).
   Today a moving mouse fills the prompt, and Ctrl+C only clears the line, which reads as "pi prints garbage and
   will not exit".
 ```

### Version

1.3.0, also on main (73f8de8). Windows 11, Windows Terminal, PowerShell; the input path is the same everywhere.    Related: #11170 is the other half of the same symptom (an exiting pi leaves the terminal in mouse-tracking    state, so the shell echoes the reports). They are independent: this one is pi typing the fragments itself while it is still running.

issues.title: Ctrl+G (external editor) silently exits pi with code 129 on Windows

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

Pressing Ctrl+G (the `app.editor.external` action) makes pi exit **immediately and silently** with
exit code **129**. The external editor never opens, the console window disappears, and no crash
report or stack trace is produced.

Exit code 129 corresponds to `emergencyTerminalExit()` in
`dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js`, which is reached when a stdio stream emits an error
that `isDeadTerminalError()` classifies as a dead terminal (EIO / EPIPE / ENOTCONN / ENOTTY).

The exit is silent because `emergencyTerminalExit()` calls `process.exit(129)` directly and does
**not** go through `uncaughtCrash()`, so nothing is written to `~/.pi/agent/crashes.json` and no
stack trace is printed.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `pi` (or `pi -ne` to disable all extensions) in cmd.exe or PowerShell on Windows.
2. Press `Ctrl+G`.

### Expected behavior

The configured external editor opens, and pi resumes when the editor exits.

### Version

 pi version: 1.3.0

issues.title: pi auth check: credentials_not_configured does not say what was checked

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
`pi auth check` answers `not_ready` / `credentials_not_configured` without saying what it looked at, so a caller cannot tell "no credential exists anywhere" from "none in the places pi reads".

## What happened

pi 1.3.0 wrapped by a tool that supplies the model API key outside pi's own credential store (a local proxy injects it on the request). Turns on that provider complete in that setup. But:

```
$ pi auth check --model <model>
{"status":"not_ready","provider":"<provider>","reason":"credentials_not_configured"}
```

The caller (an agent) read this as "this machine has no credential for the provider" and reported it so. Two credentials existed, in a store pi does not read.

`checkProviderAuth` in `dist/cli/auth-check.js` returns that result whenever `modelRuntime.checkAuth(provider)` finds nothing. The result carries no hint of which sources were consulted (stored credentials, an environment variable, a key in `models.json`), nor the variable name pi looks for. The only way to learn that is to read the source.

This is the same class as #9448 (the check says the provider is broken while the call works, and the cause is only visible in `auth-check`'s source), with a different trigger.

## Suggestion

Name what was checked, in both the `--json` result and the human output, for example:

```
{"status":"not_ready","provider":"<provider>","reason":"credentials_not_configured",
 "checked":["auth store","env <PROVIDER>_API_KEY","models.json apiKey"]}
```

and say in `docs/cli.md` that a credential supplied by anything else (a proxy, a wrapper's per-request header) is invisible to `auth check`. A script then knows `not_ready` means "nothing in these places", and can look elsewhere before concluding.

Happy to send a PR if you want this shape.

issues.title: RPC startup temporarily drops dynamically discovered extension models
issues.body:
### What happened?

RPC `get_available_models` temporarily omits a dynamically discovered extension model that `get_state` already reports as selected. An RPC client that queries once at startup receives an incomplete catalog.

`ModelRuntime.refresh()` recomposes providers and publishes a snapshot before discovery completes. `composeModelProvider()` loses the extension's previously published models because they live only in the old provider closure. This differs from the auth availability race in #8810: the model list itself is lost.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an empty `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and a single fake extension: `pi.registerProvider("race-test", { api: "openai-completions", baseUrl: "https://example.test/v1", apiKey: "test-only", refreshModels })`, with no static `models`.
2. Have `refreshModels` return a valid `known` model offline. When `allowNetwork` is true, wait 250 ms, then return `known` plus `new`; make no network requests.
3. Start `pi -ne -e ./extension.ts --mode rpc --no-session --provider race-test --model known`. Immediately send `{"id":"state","type":"get_state"}` and `{"id":"models","type":"get_available_models"}` as JSONL. Query models again during and after the delay.

On current `main`, `known` was selected but absent from the immediate and mid-refresh responses in 30/30 isolated runs; both models appeared after completion. Only the explicit fake extension was loaded (`-ne -e`), real fetches were blocked, and no model requests were sent.

### Expected behavior

Previously published models remain available throughout refresh. New or empty catalogs replace them when published.

I would like to submit [this fix and regression test](https://github.com/KLIEBHAN/pi/commit/d3e11d33858a1110f97c5bb4dcfeb3b9a9f52ced): retain published definitions per registration in a WeakMap, without extra network calls or per-query work. The test fails on `main` and passes with the fix; 116 targeted tests, the CLI build, and `npm run check` pass. With the fix, all 30 RPC runs retain `known` throughout refresh.

### Version

`main` at `26293e7` (also reproduced on v1.3.0), Node.js v24.21.0, macOS.

issues.title: Alacritty: multi-character IME commit is treated as bracketed paste, so slash/@ autocomplete never opens
issues.body:
## What happened

In Alacritty on macOS with a Chinese IME, slash-command and `@` file autocomplete only open when the IME commits a **single** character. Any commit of two or more characters inserts the text correctly but never opens the autocomplete list.

Reproduction pattern with pinyin input (text in the editor is always plain ASCII):

| Input | Result |
| ----- | ------ |
| `/` then commit `m` | autocomplete opens |
| `/mo` committed as one chunk | no autocomplete |
| then commit `d` (single char) | autocomplete opens for `/mod` |
| `/mode` with `de` committed as one chunk | no autocomplete |

Switching to an English keyboard input source makes all of these work. The same happens with `@` file autocomplete: a two-character IME commit closes the list instead of refreshing it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. macOS with Alacritty, Chinese IME active.
2. Run `pi`.
3. Type `/`, then type `m` and commit it with Enter. The command autocomplete opens.
4. Type `mo` and commit it as a single IME commit with Enter. The autocomplete list disappears and does not come back.
5. Type `d` and commit it. The list comes back for `/mod`.

## Expected behavior

Autocomplete should refresh for `/mo` (14 matches with default commands and installed skills) and for `/mode`.

## Actual behavior

No autocomplete list. Text is inserted correctly.

`cat -v` in the same terminal shows a clean `/mo`, which is expected: `cat` does not enable bracketed paste, so Alacritty does not wrap the commit.

## Root cause

Alacritty submits IME commits through bracketed paste. This is confirmed by the Alacritty maintainer in alacritty/alacritty#8764:

> Alacritty does submit IME text through bracketed paste mode, so my guess would be that the application is trying to be smart by detecting that and fails horribly to function properly in the process.

On the pi side, bracketed paste is enabled unconditionally at terminal start, and a single-line paste is handled by:

- cancelling any open autocomplete,
- inserting the text atomically,
- returning without any autocomplete re-trigger.

The insertion helper explicitly documents that it does not trigger autocomplete and that the caller is responsible. Since `handlePaste` returns immediately after inserting a single line, no trigger happens.

As a result, single-character IME commits take the normal key path and trigger autocomplete, while 2+ character commits take the paste path, close the list, and never re-open it.

## Suggested fix

After inserting a single-line paste, re-trigger autocomplete for the current context, or distinguish IME commits from explicit user paste. Either change keeps pasted text working and restores completion for IME commits. This is closely related to #9795 (autocomplete after single-line paste) and #4253 (multi-codepoint IME commits).

## Environment

- pi 1.3.0
- Alacritty 0.17.0 (94e7c88)
- macOS 15.8.1
- Chinese IME (pinyin input, commit by Enter)

## Related

- alacritty/alacritty#8764 (IME commits use bracketed paste)
- alacritty/alacritty#8692 (maintainer declines a terminal-side config option)
- earendil-works/pi#4253 (multi-codepoint IME commits)
- earendil-works/pi#9795 (autocomplete after single-line paste)

issues.title: Make the codemode worker limit configurable or queue instead of failing
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Make the codemode worker limit configurable, or let a call wait for a free worker instead of failing right away.

Today `MAX_CONCURRENT_CODEMODE_WORKERS = 2` in `packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/execute.ts`. It is process-wide and has no setting. When a third script starts while two workers are alive, it fails immediately with "Codemode worker limit reached (2 workers are still running or shutting down). Retry after they exit."

### Why?

The limit is global to the pi process, across all sessions. That works when each subagent is its own pi process, as in `examples/extensions/subagent`. But some hosts that embed pi-coding-agent run the main agent, all subagents and other sessions in one process, so they share the two slots. For example, agegr/pi-web starts its built-in subagents as in-process SDK sessions (`createAgentSessionServices` / `createAgentSessionFromServices` in `lib/subagent-runtime.ts`) and lets them use codemode.

We hit this in a desktop app built on pi 1.3.0. With 4 subagents running in parallel plus the main agent, 26 of 123 codemode scripts (~21%) were rejected. The error says "No tool calls were made", so the model read it as "no results", rephrased and retried, wasting turns. The message gives no way to know when a retry would succeed.

I understand the limit is intentional (docs say 256 MB per worker and the tests assert the global admission). I'm asking for a way to raise it, not removing it.

### How? (optional)

Any one of these would do:
1. Queue at the limit with a timeout, and fail only after the timeout.
2. Make the limit configurable (a setting or env var), keeping 2 as the default.
3. Let embedding hosts pass the limit when creating a session.

I can send a PR if you prefer one of these.
