powershell tool falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 when pwsh 7 is the Microsoft Store build
issues.body:
### What happened?

With PowerShell 7 installed from the Microsoft Store (7.6.7, no MSI), the built-in `powershell` tool runs Windows PowerShell 5.1.

`getPowerShellConfig` in `utils/shell.js` finds pwsh with `where pwsh.exe` and checks the first hit with `fs.existsSync`. The Store build puts an app-execution alias on PATH (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a zero-length reparse point). On that alias `existsSync` is false and `statSync` throws EACCES, while `lstatSync`, `accessSync`, and spawning it all work. So the check rejects a working pwsh and silently falls back to `powershell.exe`.

Windows 11 Pro 26300, Node 26.8.1, managed install. The resolver is identical in 1.0.0 and 1.2.0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Only the Store PowerShell 7 installed (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell`), no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`.
2. `pi -ne -p -t +powershell,-bash "Use the powershell tool to run: $PSVersionTable.PSEdition"` → `Desktop`.
3. Resolver directly:
   ```
   node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/shell.js').then(m=>console.log(m.getPowerShellConfig().shell))"
   ```
   → `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`
4. `where pwsh.exe` → the WindowsApps alias. On that path: `fs.existsSync` → `false`, `fs.statSync` → EACCES, `fs.lstatSync` → 85-byte reparse point, `spawnSync` → prints `Core`.

### Expected behavior

pwsh 7 is used, as `docs/windows.md` says ("runs commands through pwsh.exe when available"). Microsoft is steering users to the Store/MSIX build and retiring the MSI, so more Windows users will hit this.

Fix is small: in the Windows branch of `findExecutableOnPath`, verify the `where` hit with `fs.lstatSync` or `fs.accessSync` instead of `existsSync`, or trust `where` the way the Unix branch trusts `which`. Workaround I use today: `$env:Path = "$PSHOME;$env:Path"` before starting pi, so the real package folder comes first (a user-PATH entry alone is not enough from pwsh, because the Store build prepends its alias folder to PATH at startup). Happy to send a PR if you want one.

Related: #8582 has the same symptom from a different cause (a `where` timeout under load); this one is deterministic on an idle machine.

### Version

1.2.0

issues.title: [Windows] a pi that dies without running its teardown leaves the terminal in mouse-tracking state and the shell prompt floods with escape sequences
issues.body:
## What happened?

On Windows, if pi exits through a path that does not run its terminal teardown, the pane keeps every
mode the fullscreen TUI enabled: any-motion mouse tracking (`?1000 ?1002 ?1003 ?1006`), focus
reporting (`?1004`), the pushed kitty keyboard protocol, bracketed paste, a hidden cursor and the
alternate screen. The PowerShell/PSReadLine prompt that owns the pane then receives the terminal's
`ESC[<35;48;27M` motion reports and `ESC[I` focus reports as **typed input** and echoes them:

```
PS D:\Publit> [<35;48;27M[<35;49;26M[<35;50;19M[<35;51;18M...
```

Every mouse move appends another fragment, Ctrl+C does not clear it, and only closing the terminal
helps, because the state lives in the terminal instance, not in the shell.

It hit me with a session that had been running for hours: pi died on its own with no error and the
pane was unusable from then on. There is no JS-level trace (`~/.pi/agent/crashes.json` absent, the
session jsonl ends with a tool call that has no result), so pi never got a chance to clean up.

## Steps to reproduce

The death itself is not reproducible on demand; the missing cleanup is, and it is the whole bug.

```ts
const terminal = new ProcessTerminal();
const tui = new TuiAltScreen(terminal, false, undefined, { mouse: true });
tui.start();
process.exit(0);            // any exit path that skips stop()
```

Captured stdout: `ESC[?1006l`, `ESC[?1004l`, `ESC[?1049l` and `ESC[?2004l` are never written. With a
normal start + `stop()` they are each written once.

Two gaps:

- the enable sequences are only undone in `beforeTerminalStop()`/`afterTerminalStop()` and
  `ProcessTerminal.stop()`; nothing registers a process-level fallback, so any exit that throws before
  `stop()` leaves the terminal dirty;
- on Windows `SIGHUP` is not handled (`signals = ["SIGTERM"]`, and `SIGHUP` is only pushed when
  `platform !== "win32"`), so closing the console or ending the task from Task Manager runs no cleanup
  either.

A hard kill (`taskkill /F`) or a native abort cannot be fixed from inside the process. I am asking for
the paths that *can* run JavaScript to restore the terminal, so a dead pi does not break the shell that
inherits the pane.

## Expected behavior

Every exit path that can run JavaScript writes the restore sequences, and the shell prompt stays usable
when pi dies. If the hard-kill case is an accepted limitation, documenting it would already help; the
only current workaround is a manual escape-sequence reset in the affected pane.

## Version

1.3.0, also on main (73f8de8). Windows 11, Windows Terminal, PowerShell 5.1 + PSReadLine; any terminal
that supports these modes shows the same.

Related, both closed: #10780 (duplicate), #10079 (not planned). The gap they describe is still on main,
which is why I am reporting it again with the repro above.

issues.title: TUI: unclosed `$$` swallows or corrupts every Markdown table after it (streaming transient, permanent if the closing `$$` never arrives)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

In the TUI, any Markdown table that appears after an unclosed `$$` display-math block stops rendering as a table. Two variants, both reproduced with pi's own bundled renderer (`Markdown` component from the 1.3.0 bundle, `dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-6MWTY2OB.js`):

**Variant 1 — orphan opener (no other `$$` below):** everything after the `$$` line is swallowed as "pending math" and emitted as raw text. The table is never drawn, even after the message is fully complete.

**Variant 2 — a later `$$` exists somewhere below:** the lazy `[\s\S]*?` in the block-math regex matches across the table up to the *next* `$$` opener, so the table becomes the "math body" of the first block and gets fed to the LaTeX renderer. The table renders as one garbled inline run appended to the math line, and the *last* formula ends up as raw text with a stray `$$`:

```
               ±
Δ G^±_eff = Δ G - qEd | 方案 | 做法 | 评价 | |---|---|---| | A | B | C | 后面的
公式：

E_c = \Delta G^{\pm}/(qd)
$$
```

**Why it matters (streaming):** during streaming the closing `$$` has not arrived yet, so **every table that follows a display-math block is temporarily in one of these broken states** until the closing delimiter streams in. If the model forgets the closing `$$` (common enough), the corruption is permanent for the rest of the message — not just that one table. This surfaces as "tables randomly fail to render" in long assistant messages that mix LaTeX and tables (e.g. physics/chemistry answers).

**Root cause** in `tokenizeBlockLatex` (same bundle file):

```js
let dollarMatch = /^ {0,3}\$\$[ \t]*(?:\n)?([\s\S]*?)\$\$[ \t]*(?:\n|$)/.exec(source);
```

- The lazy `[\s\S]*?` happily spans blank lines, paragraphs, and entire GFM tables, so an unclosed `$$` pairs with the *next* `$$` opener anywhere below (variant 2).
- The fallback `pendingDollar = /^ {0,3}\$\$[ \t]*(?:\n)?([\s\S]*)$/` combined with `looksLikePendingDollarMath()` (which matches `|`, `-`, `=`, …) treats a following table as "pending math" and emits it raw forever (variant 1). A table's `|---|---|` delimiter row matches `looksLikePendingDollarMath` via `|` and `-`, so tables are especially susceptible.

### Steps to reproduce

**Unit-level (deterministic):** instantiate the bundled `Markdown` component (`dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-6MWTY2OB.js`, needs `initTheme()` first) on the inputs below and call `.render(60..100)`.

Variant 1 — orphan `$$`, table never renders:

```markdown
$$

| a | b |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |
```

Variant 2 — unclosed `$$` followed later by another `$$`:

```markdown
Some formula:

$$
\Delta G^{\pm}_{\rm eff} = \Delta G^{\pm} - qEd

| 方案 | 做法 | 评价 |
|---|---|---|
| A | B | C |

后面的公式：

$$
E_c = \Delta G^{\pm}/(qd)
$$

结尾。
```

**In the TUI:** ask for an answer that contains a `$$` display formula followed by a Markdown table, with the model omitting one closing `$$` (or watch mid-stream while the `$$` block is still open — the same broken state appears transiently and self-heals only if the closing `$$` eventually arrives).

### Expected behavior

- A block-math token should not span a GFM table: the `$$ … $$` body should terminate at a line that starts a table (header + delimiter row), and the table should fall back to normal Markdown parsing.
- Ideally also: while streaming (unclosed `$$` at end of input), the pending-math fallback should not swallow structured block content like tables — rendering the `$$` as literal text plus the table as a table would make the transient state correct from the start and self-heal cleanly when the closing `$$` arrives.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Environments CI fails: @earendil-works/pi-telemetry has no source export condition
issues.body:
### What happened?

The `Environments` workflow's `tests` job fails on `main` for the whole OS matrix, at the "Durable env tests" step:

```
Error: Failed to resolve entry for package "@earendil-works/pi-telemetry". The package may have incorrect main/module/exports specified in its package.json.
 ❯ ../chord/src/context/index.ts:1:1
 ❯ ../chord/src/state.ts:6:1
```

All six test files fail to load, so the job exits 1. Latest `main` is red on this too.

Cause: `packages/chord/src/context/index.ts` imports the root of `@earendil-works/pi-telemetry` (added by the telemetry chain `48909d987` → `2ec55d808`). Every vitest config in the repo resolves with `conditions: ["source"]`, and packages consumed that way declare a `"source"` entry — `chord`, `env`, `durable`, `codemode`, `mcp`, `evals` all do. `packages/telemetry/package.json` declares `"source"` only on `./render`, so `.` and `./testing` fall through to `./dist/index.js`, which nothing in this job builds (only `build:daemon` runs, then straight to vitest).

### Steps to reproduce

```
git checkout main   # 48c8f3228
npm ci --ignore-scripts
cd packages/durable
npx vitest --run test/env-node.test.ts
```

Or, smaller: with the package linked into `node_modules`, `node --conditions=source -e "console.log(import.meta.resolve('@earendil-works/pi-telemetry'))"` prints `.../dist/index.js` instead of `.../src/index.ts`.

### Expected behavior

Resolution picks `src/index.ts` under the `source` condition, the way `@earendil-works/chord` already does. Adding `"source": "./src/index.ts"` to `.` and `"source": "./src/testing/index.ts"` to `./testing` (mirroring what `./render` already does) fixes it: the four failing `tests` jobs turn green — https://github.com/jiangchuanso/pi/actions/runs/39448469156 — and published consumers are unaffected, since default conditions still resolve `dist`.

Happy to send that two-line change as a PR once I have `lgtm`, per CONTRIBUTING.

### Version

main @ `48c8f3228` (2026-10-20), packages at 1.3.0.

(Drafted with an AI agent; verified by actually running the workflow on a fork.)

issues.title: bedrock-converse: usage.input not normalized across model families — false cache-miss notices, doubled input cost
issues.body:
### What happened?

On Bedrock, `usage.input` means different things depending on model family, and pi doesn't normalize it. Anthropic models report it net of cache. OpenAI-family models report it gross — `input` already contains `cacheRead` + `cacheWrite`. `bedrock-converse` copies `inputTokens` straight through, so on those models:

- a "Cache miss: ~150k tokens re-billed" notice fires on nearly every turn of a session where cache is actually hitting ~100%
- displayed cost roughly doubles — `calculateCost` bills `input` at full rate *and* `cacheRead`/`cacheWrite` on top

Two-turn repro below (`pi -ne`, builtin tools, same prompt, same provider):

```
OpenAI-family:  in=  8369  cr=     0  cw= 8367     in = cw + 2
                in= 12401  cr=  8367  cw= 4032     in = cr + cw + 2
Anthropic:      in=     2  cr=     0  cw=13923
                in=     2  cr= 13923  cw= 7262
```

Turn 2's `cacheRead` equals turn 1's real prompt exactly, so the cache is fine — `input` is just gross. Bedrock's own `totalTokens` is the additive sum, inflated the same way, so it can't disambiguate either.

Related: #6355 fixed footer/compaction assuming `input` *includes* cache tokens, while `detectMiss` in `cache-stats.ts` computes `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`, which only holds if it *excludes* them. Both conventions are in tree.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne -p "read <~8k token file> then reply with one word: OK" --model <openai-family model via bedrock-converse>`
2. inspect `usage` on both assistant messages in the session file
3. `input == cacheRead + cacheWrite` on every turn; with `showCacheMissNotices: true` a long session shows a miss notice nearly every turn and a large bogus `/session` re-billed total

### Expected behavior

`usage.input` net of cache regardless of model family. No miss notice when `cacheRead` already covers the previous turn's prompt.

### Version

0.84.3

Happy to do the fix if you want it — normalize in the adapter behind a per-model flag. Sniffing it arithmetically isn't safe: a net-reporting model on a fresh long prompt (`input=50000 cacheRead=0 cacheWrite=40000`) also satisfies `input >= cacheRead + cacheWrite`.

Pi defaults to a single context window variant per model (e.g., 1M for Luna), even when users have access to multiple context options. This limits discoverability and forces users to manually select different context windows, missing opportunities to optimize for their specific use case.

Expose all available model context window variants in model discovery, displaying them with their context size:

- gpt-6-luna [github-copilot]
- gpt-6-luna@1m [github-copilot]

prs.title: feat(ai,coding-agent): add the Scaleway provider
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds Scaleway Generative APIs as a built-in OpenAI-compatible provider. Closes #6165.

- **Auth:** `SCW_API_KEY` (IAM secret key from the Scaleway console) or `/login scaleway`
- **Endpoint:** serverless `https://api.scaleway.ai/v1`; dedicated deployments via a
  `baseUrl` override in `models.json`
- **Default model:** `deepseek-v4.1-flash` — vision input, 256k context / 32k output,
  reasoning efforts `none` / `low` / `high` / `max` sent as native `reasoning_effort`

## Compat

Scaleway's documented OpenAI-compat gaps are encoded as generated compat flags:
`store` unsupported, no developer role, `strict` tool schemas ignored, usage in
streaming, and `max_completion_tokens` as the output cap.

The catalog is generated from models.dev in `processScalewayModels`. Scaleway is
exempted from the cross-provider DeepSeek-V4 rule: it accepts `reasoning_effort`
natively and does not require `reasoning_content` on replayed assistant messages
(verified against the live API).

## Testing

- `packages/ai/test/scaleway-models.test.ts`: no-network payload, thinking-level-map,
  and env-key tests
- Scaleway blocks in the live suites (`stream`, `abort`, `total-tokens`,
  `image-tool-result`, ...) gated on `SCW_API_KEY`
- Verified live: `none`/`low`/`high`/`max` efforts accepted, `medium` rejected, and
  image tool results read correctly by the default model

## Note on `npm run check`

The branch reports type errors that are pre-existing models.dev drift also present on
`main` (stale `mimo-v2.5-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-r1`, and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`
references after upstream catalog changes). Nothing in this PR contributes errors; the
Scaleway additions type-check and pass their tests against a fresh
`npm run generate:models` hydration.

prs.title: fix(ai): drop models that open ai rejects for openai-codex
prs.body:
Hi, human Lucas here,

The model catalogue for openai-codex contains models that openai refuses to serve.
This PR removes them from the model catalog.  Looks like the tests here never run automatically, as they were all red because of openai's removal of support for these models.   I've bumped the model to use to 6.1-sol to fix all the tests.    Only one test is left red: the context overflow one, because openai actually doesnt error out, it accepts up to 872k.


Everything below here, including the PR itself is writen by ai.  groetjes uit amsterdam.


Problem: `openai-codex` authenticates with a ChatGPT account, but the Codex backend rejects two models in pi's catalog for those accounts. Live check on a ChatGPT account:

```
gpt-5.5              error  The 'gpt-5.5' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.
gpt-5.3-codex-spark  error  The 'gpt-5.3-codex-spark' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.
gpt-6.1-sol          stop
gpt-5.6-sol          stop
```

`/backend-api/codex/models` doesn't list either model anymore. It returns only the `gpt-5.6-*` and `gpt-6*` models. Model pickers currently offer both rejected models, and every request to them fails.

Fix: remove both entries from the hand-maintained Codex list in `generate-models.ts`. Tests and probe scripts that used `getModel("openai-codex", "gpt-5.5")` now use `gpt-6.1-sol`, the `openai-codex` default in `defaultModelPerProvider`. The context overflow test uses `gpt-5.6-sol` instead to keep its prompt smaller. Tests that build their own `gpt-5.5` model objects (pricing multipliers, reasoning clamps) are unchanged.

Testing:
- `npm run check` passes.
- Ran every Codex test in the touched files against the live backend with a ChatGPT account (`-t "[Cc]odex"`): 41 passed and 1 failed. That covers SSE and WebSocket streaming, tools, thinking, images, abort, empty messages, unicode, token totals, responseId, and cache affinity. `cross-provider-handoff` didn't run because it needs provider API keys in env vars.
- The one failure, `context-overflow` for Codex, doesn't depend on this change. The test sends about `contextWindow + 10k` tokens (282k) and expects an error. Codex accepted 330k input tokens and returned `stop`. `/backend-api/codex/models` reports `context_window: 272000` (500000 for gpt-6.1-sol) but `max_context_window: 872000` for every model, so 282k can't overflow any current Codex model. Out of scope here. The fix is either to size the test from `max_context_window` or to change what `contextWindow` means for Codex.
- In a fresh unbuilt clone, `./test.sh` fails only in suites that need `dist/` output (`lazy-module-load`, `models-entry`, ...).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

- Replaced the old `Ling 2.6` and `Ring 2.6` models with the new `Ling 3.0`, `Ling 3.0 Flash VL`, and `Ling 3.1 Flash` models, updating their properties such as context window, token limits, costs, and input types.
- Changed the default Ant Ling model to `Ling-3.1-flash` throughout the codebase and documentation.

**API Compatibility and Reasoning Format:**
- Removed the legacy `thinkingFormat: "ant-ling"` compat value and unified Ant Ling’s API compatibility to use the DeepSeek-compatible `thinking` and `reasoning_effort` fields. 
- Updated the logic for building API parameters and model detection to use the DeepSeek format for Ant Ling, and removed special-case handling for the old Ant Ling format.

prs.body: fixes #10154 cjk bold breaks all the time in the tui. marked follows commonmark flanking rules, so a closing `**` sitting between cjk punctuation and a following character can't close, and `**这是测试。**后面` shows up with the asterisks still in place. that's just how models write bold in chinese, japanese and korean, so long replies end up half rendered. this wires in the `emStrong` tokenizer from [`marked-cjk-friendly`](https://github.com/tats-u/markdown-cjk-friendly/tree/main/packages/marked-cjk-friendly) (same author as `remark-cjk-friendly` and `markdown-it-cjk-friendly`). the tokenizer treats cjk chars like punctuation for flanking checks, so english text parses exactly as before. only `emStrong` gets picked: the package also ships a `del` tokenizer, which would bring back the single-tilde strikethrough that `StrictStrikethroughTokenizer` deliberately turns off. the dep is tiny: no dependencies, no install scripts, pinned to `0.1.2`. lockfile and coding-agent install-lock are refreshed. ###### Testing - `node --test test/markdown.test.ts` in `packages/tui`: the new cjk test fails on main and passes here, 83/83 overall - `npm run check` - manual: opened the same session with `--session` on main vs this branch ###### Screenshots btw html export has the same bug, since export ships a separately vendored marked. this pr leaves html alone to stay small. want a follow-up for that, or should html stay as is?

prs.title: fix(ai): find the initial system message past leading extension messages
prs.body:
Extensions that sendMessage() during session_start put a custom message ahead of pi's system message, and getInitialSystemMessage() only accepted index 0. Providers then built the request as if the session were a legacy transcript: Anthropic requests lost the system field and native tool anchoring, so loading a deferred tool rewrote the whole prompt cache, and Codex ran under the fallback prompt.

This changes the transcript utilities to locate the initial system message past leading non-system messages instead of reading index 0, and fixes the three providers that assumed the prompt was the first entry (anthropic-messages, openai-responses, openai-completions, mistral-conversations). Transcript order is unchanged.

Includes unit coverage in transcript-tool-changes.test.ts and an agent-session regression test that reproduces the reported cache-rewrite scenario.

Fixes #11157

prs.title: fix(ai): keep the prompt cache across tool changes on Responses
prs.body:
Fixes #10940.

## Problem

After any tool removal or redeclaration, `resolveTranscriptTools` stopped anchoring additions for the rest of the session and sent the full current tool list at the top level. Every later deferred load rewrote `tools` and invalidated the cached prefix.

Example: initial `[keep, drop]`, removal of `drop`, then a load of `loaded`. The top-level tools went from `[keep]` to `[keep, loaded]`, and `additional_tools` was no longer emitted.

## Backend semantics (verified live, October 2026)

Probed with strict schemas on OpenAI (ChatGPT sign-in), Codex, and Copilot. Constrained decoding shows which definition the server applies:

- `additional_tools` items accumulate. A later item replaces same-name definitions from earlier items.
- A later item cannot replace a top-level tool: top-level v1 followed by `additional_tools` v2 keeps v1.
- No item removes a tool: `tool_choice` naming a removed tool is still accepted, while an undeclared name is rejected.

Codex Responses Lite takes this into account. It sends no top-level tools, puts the full catalog in a leading `additional_tools` item, and announces removals as developer text.

## Change

- `resolveTranscriptTools(messages, support)` takes `"none" | "additions" | "changes"`. `anchorsAdditions` is replaced by `foldedSystemMessages`.
- `"changes"` (models with `additional_tools` and mid-conversation system messages):
  - Every tool is declared in `additional_tools` items, starting with one at the head of the input. There is no top-level tool list.
  - Removals are announced as text.
  - Every later item is preceded by an incremental-update notice that lists the tools that are still unavailable.
- `"additions"` (tool search, Kimi tool messages): a removal or redeclared name moves the top-level boundary once. Later additions stay anchored.

The notice and the redeclaration rule both come from live failures:

- Without the notice, the luna models read the latest item as the complete tool set after a removal. They called removed tools again or skipped tools that were still available.
- Kimi K3 ignores a removed tool that a later tool message declares again.

## Validation

Unit tests cover:
- a growing request prefix across removal followed by loads, on `additional_tools`, tool search, and Kimi
- removal notices
- redefinition via `additional_tools`
- the boundary rules

Live matrix, 3 repetitions of 5 agent-loop scenarios with strict tools (baseline, removal then loads, schema redefinition, grammar tool redefinition, removal then insisting on the removed tool then re-add):

- Targets: Codex gpt-5.6-luna/sol/terra, gpt-6-luna/sol/astra, gpt-6.1-sol; OpenAI gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-6-sol; Copilot gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-6-luna, gpt-6-sol; Codex tool-search mode; Kimi K3.
- 0 request errors. All `additional_tools` targets pass every turn.
- The remaining Kimi and tool-search failures produce the same payload as before this change.
- First request after a tool change: 18/36 cache misses before the change, 0/24 after. The remaining misses, about 8%, also occur in the scenario with no tool changes.

Not covered: the plain OpenAI platform API, OpenCode (expired keys), and Azure.

Behavior change: sessions on `additional_tools` models now send their tools as `additional_tools` items. Existing sessions miss the cache once after upgrading.

This PR description is AI-generated.

issues.body:
## Context

Deferred review findings from PR #14129 — `feat(core): skip re-injecting an unchanged UserPromptSubmit hook context block` (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14129).

Round R5 of `qwen-code-review-bot` opened 13 `[Suggestion]` threads on head `7102b9675f556b178ff0cd657f20a0bff1522714`. Two of them were verified as **REAL** defects during the R5 closeout round, but neither can be fixed inside PR #14129 without widening the diff beyond that PR's promise or without changing a data-structure semantic that this PR does not own. They are recorded here so they are not lost.

Two other R5 findings (R5-8, R5-9) were test-only and **were** fixed in `8adb7e8e7b4ba0e7c4cede34426d5b022baa5163`.

---

### 1. R5-10 — REAL: the compaction rescues mutate the `Content` entry that `recordChatCompression` captured by reference

- **Finding id:** R5-10
- **Thread id:** `PRRT_kwDOPB-92c6uihm8` (comment `4330713365`)
- **Bot-anchored line:** `packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts:3459`
- **Coordinates verified against head `7102b96`:**
  - `packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts:3456-3459` — pre-send rescue reassigns `userContent.parts` *after* `tryCompress` (called at `:3431`) has already recorded a snapshot whose last entry **is** that same `userContent` object (passed in as `pendingUserMessage` at `:3436`).
  - `packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts:4562-4565` — reactive rescue reassigns `lastContent.parts` on an entry reachable through `setHistory`'s aliased array.
  - The record site itself lives in `packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.ts` (`recordChatCompression`), which is **not** one of the 13 files PR #14129 touches.
- **Verdict:** **REAL** (not hypothetical). The trigger path is concrete and is the path this PR itself added: `tryCompress` copies the *array* but shares the *entry object*; serialization is deferred twice before `JSON.stringify`, so whether the wrapped block appears in the durable `chat_compression` line is decided by write scheduling. The reporter measured 5 of 14 probe arms where the on-disk snapshot and the in-memory `activeBranchRecords` entry disagreed for the same record UUID. Consequence on resume: the copy is rebuilt with no receipt restore while the turn's own record carries `hookContext: ''`, so it arrives unstamped and the next identical prompt injects a second byte-identical copy — permanent duplication on resume, in the feature that exists to remove duplication.
- **Why it was not fixed in PR #14129:** both available fixes leave the PR's scope.
  - *Clone at capture* — the reporter's suggested `payload.compressedHistory.map((c) => ({ ...c, ...(c.parts ? { parts: [...c.parts] } : {}) }))` in `chatRecordingService.ts` is ~2 lines, but it adds a 14th file to the PR and changes what durable `chat_compression` snapshots alias for **every** compression path in the product, not just the hook-context one. That is a recording-semantics decision, not a hook-dedup decision. It must preserve symbol keys (`markApiHistoryPrompt` stamps the entry at `llm-chat.ts:3421`; `chatRecordingService.ts:3259` derives `promptIds` via `getApiHistoryPromptId`), so a JSON round-trip copy is not acceptable.
  - *Reorder the append before `tryCompress`* — not available: the rescue only knows that compaction replaced history *after* `tryCompress` returns, which is its entire reason to exist.
- **What the fix needs to do:** decide, once and deliberately, whether `chat_compression` snapshots own their entries. Preferred shape is the entry-level spread copy in `recordChatCompression` (spread, not JSON, to keep symbol keys), plus extending the two rescue tests in `llm-chat.test.ts` to capture the `recordChatCompression` payload with a deep copy at call time and assert no captured entry's text equals the wrapped block while `chat.getHistory()` still holds it. Removing the entry-level copy must turn that assertion red.
- **Human-gate condition hit:** ① data-structure semantics (what a recorded snapshot owns) and ④ clearly widens the diff beyond the PR's promise.

---

### 2. R5-12 — REAL: the reactive rescue's `else` branch produces the one entry shape the dedup predicate can never match

- **Finding id:** R5-12
- **Thread id:** `PRRT_kwDOPB-92c6uihnD` (comment `4330713378`)
- **Bot-anchored line:** `packages/core/src/hooks/user-prompt-submit-context.ts:116`
- **Coordinates verified against head `7102b96`:**
  - `packages/core/src/hooks/user-prompt-submit-context.ts:114-116` — `hasUserPromptSubmitContext` returns `false` for `parts.length < 2`. A receipt-stamped **sole-part** user entry can therefore never match, however genuine its receipt is.
  - `packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts:4567` — the reactive rescue's `else` branch does exactly `self.history.push(createUserContent([hookContextPart]))`: a sole-part user entry carrying a real receipt.
  - Reachability is confirmed by the PR's own test: `summaryAck()` is `[userText('summary'), modelText('ack')]`, i.e. the compressed history tails with a **model** entry, so `'re-appends a suppressed hook block when a reactive compaction replaces history'` (`llm-chat.test.ts:3740`) drives that `else` branch on every run.
- **Verdict:** **REAL** (not hypothetical). The next turn's scan finds nothing matchable and appends a second identical copy; both copies are then re-sent every turn until the next compaction. The reporter measured this as a bounded 2× standing cost, because the following turn's ≥2-part delivery re-arms suppression. It also falsifies the "suppression re-arms from the fresh part" sentence in **both** design docs (`docs/design/user-prompt-submit-context-dedup.md` and its `.zh-CN.md` twin) — re-arm comes from the following delivery, not from that part.
- **Why it was not fixed in PR #14129:** neither candidate fix is a shrink, and they pull in opposite directions.
  - *Reporter's preferred fix* — "merge the rescued block into an entry that also carries user text" — is **not available** on that branch: the branch exists precisely because `lastContent?.role !== 'user'`, so there is no user entry to merge into. Doing it would mean inventing a synthetic user-text part.
  - *Alternative* — relax the predicate to accept a receipt-stamped sole part — requires changing three pinned things together in one deliberate change, per the reporter's own constraint: the pinned test `user-prompt-submit-context.test.ts` ('does not match a sole tagged part, which is treated as user-authored'), the display projection at `packages/core/src/utils/transcript-records.ts:234-235` (keyed off `parts.length > 1`), and both design docs' acceptance wording. Relaxing only the predicate makes suppression and display classify the same entry differently.
- **What the fix needs to do:** pick a side of the sole-part rule and move all of its dependents in one change. Either (a) keep "a sole tagged part is user-authored" and stop the reactive `else` branch from producing that shape, or (b) accept a receipt-stamped sole part and update the pinned test + the `transcript-records` projection + both docs together. Also correct the "suppression re-arms from the fresh part" sentence in both docs either way. Add the second `sendMessageStream` with the same payload to the existing reactive-rescue test, asserting exactly one wrapped copy across `chat.getHistory()` — that assertion is red today.
- **Human-gate condition hit:** ① data-structure semantics (which entry shape counts as injector-owned) with a deliberate cross-file contract change.

---

### Registered by the R5 closeout round (run `qwen-pr-closeout/jmvhhouazml`, head `8adb7e8e7b`, 2026-10-21)

The nine threads listed below were open on PR #14129 at head `8adb7e8e7b`. Each was verified against that
head by reading the code, then answered on the PR with evidence and resolved. **Resolving those threads
records this deferral, not a fix.**

Nothing was pushed this round. All nine are `[Suggestion]`, the PR has zero unresolved Criticals, and
`main` has `dismiss_stale_reviews=true`, so any push invalidates every green lane on the current head and
re-rolls the ~25-minute `web-shell E2E Smoke` lane — which has already flaked red twice on this PR with
`connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4170` and only cleared on retry. Re-rolling that die for Suggestion-severity
findings, none of which is a PR-introduced regression, is a net loss.

| id | verified coordinates @ `8adb7e8e7b` | verdict | why it is not fixed in PR #14129 |
|---|---|---|---|
| R5-1 | `docs/design/user-prompt-submit-context-dedup.md:19-25` | REAL (doc accuracy) | Doc-only wording; must be edited together with `.zh-CN.md:13-14`. Rides a code push, and there is none this round. |
| R5-2 | same doc `:179` | REAL (doc accuracy) | Same. Mirror `.zh-CN.md:79`. |
| R5-3 | same doc `:184` | REAL (doc accuracy) | Same. Mirror `.zh-CN.md:80`. |
| R5-4 | same doc `:202-203` | **REAL — export surface verified** | See below. |
| R5-5 | `packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/Session.ts:9339`, `:9359-9366`, `:9505`, `:9514-9516` | REAL hole in the new one-owner invariant, **not a PR-introduced regression** | Fix is an architecture decision — human-gate ①. See below. |
| R5-6 | `Session.ts:9505` | REAL coverage gap, **production code is correct** | Test-only. `Session.test.ts` is ~285 s and no PR-time lane executes the ACP suite. |
| R5-7 | `packages/core/src/core/client.ts:4706-4712` (re-stamp) vs the `:4881` ToolResult gate, `:5008`, `:5040` | REAL coverage gap, **not a regression**; the reporter's minimal fix is **inert** | Only effective fix is the R5-12 predicate contract change. See below. |
| R5-11 | `packages/core/src/core/turn.ts:724`, `:744`, `:749-751` | REAL coverage gap (test-only) | Test-only; rides a code push. |
| R5-13 | `packages/core/src/services/session-api-history.ts:217-223` | REAL coverage gap (test-only) | Test-only; rides a code push. Same restore path R5-10 depends on. |

#### R5-4 — export surface verified against `origin/main`

`git show origin/main:packages/core/src/hooks/user-prompt-submit-context.ts | grep '^export'` returns only the
tag re-export block and `stripTrailingUserPromptSubmitContextPart`. At head `8adb7e8e7b` the module additionally
exports `createUserPromptSubmitContextPart` (`:39`), `restoreUserPromptSubmitContextReceipt` (`:54`) and
`hasUserPromptSubmitContext` (`:105`) — three new functions on the public `./userPromptSubmitContext` subpath
(`packages/core/package.json:57`; the PR does not touch `package.json`, the subpath pre-existed). On top of that
the PR adds `LlmChatSendOptions.suppressedHookContext` on an `export interface` (`llm-chat.ts:675`) and a
positional parameter on `export class Turn` (`turn.ts:710`).

⇒ The acceptance bullet "No new configuration, schema, or public API surface beyond the one exported predicate"
(`docs/design/user-prompt-submit-context-dedup.md:202-203`, on a doc stamped `Status: Implemented`) is factually
contradicted. The finding is REAL. Correcting it means rewriting that bullet, adding a Proposed-solution paragraph
for the rescue mechanism and its one-owner rule, naming the new send option and `Turn` parameter, correcting the two
"re-injects one duplicate and then re-arms" sentences (`:157-163`, `:197-201`) to match the behaviour pinned by
`llm-chat.test.ts` and `Session.test.ts`, and mirroring every edit in `.zh-CN.md:86`, `:88`. That is one commit over
two files — worth doing, but it only rides a code push, and this round has none.

Note the overlap with **R5-12** above: R5-12 already records that the "suppression re-arms from the fresh part"
sentence in both docs is falsified. The doc correction should be done once, covering both.

#### R5-5 — why the fix is a human gate, not a cheap repair

`hookRescueContext` is cleared at `Session.ts:9366` once Session's own `tryCompressChat` returns `COMPRESSED`, and
the forward at `:9514-9516` is gated on it still being truthy. So after Session's own compaction,
`options.suppressedHookContext` is `undefined` at both llm-chat rescue sites (`llm-chat.ts:3451` and `:4556`): if a
*second* compaction happens inside the same send, zero owners re-append the block. The structural claim is REAL.

It is not a regression — the reporter's own measurement says the merge base loses the block on the same trigger,
because it had no rescue at all. And the reporter's own constraint rules out the cheap fix: a forward-after-consume
change "must restore the one-copy guarantee by another means (idempotent rescue sites), or the duplicate returns at
llm-chat.ts:4556". Making both llm-chat rescue sites idempotent with an already-present scan is a change to the
rescue mechanism's one-owner invariant, i.e. an architecture decision (human-gate ①), and it changes product
behaviour — so it cannot ride a Suggestion-only round. The naive one-line version reintroduces exactly the duplicate
this PR exists to remove.

#### R5-6 — code correct, coverage missing

`historyPromptId:` is passed at only one of the four `#sendMessageStreamWithAutoCompression` call sites
(`Session.ts:7342`); `:8280`, `:11241` and `:12572` do not pass it. On those laps `options.historyPromptId` is
`undefined`, so `|| hookRescueContext` at `:9505` is indeed the sole reason the send takes the options-carrying
branch. The reporter's mutation witness (drop the disjunct → 1262 still pass; drop the option spread → FAIL)
confirms the gap is in the tests, not in the code. There is nothing to fix in production. The missing case belongs
in `Session.test.ts`, a ~285 s suite in `packages/cli`, and per this repo's lane layout no PR-time lane executes the
ACP suite — so a case added there would also be unverifiable by CI on the PR.

#### R5-7 — the suggested minimal fix is inert

Every structural claim checks out at head `8adb7e8e7b`: the re-stamp is `client.ts:4706-4712`
(`requestToSend[requestToSend.length - 1] = createUserPromptSubmitContextPart(appendedHookContext)`); the enclosing
ToolResult-only gate is `client.ts:4881` (`if (messageType === SendMessageType.ToolResult) {`); inside it the
exploration reminder is `requestToSend.push({ text: explorationReminder })` (~`:5008`) and the tool-result memory is
`requestToSend = [...requestToSend, toolResultMemory.prompt]` (~`:5040`). The UserPromptSubmit gate at
`:4032-4044` excludes `Retry|Steer|Cron|Notification|Teammate|Goal` but **not** `ToolResult`, and the verdict block
sits outside `startsInteraction` (used at `:3964` and `:4332`). So the hook can fire on ToolResult turns and the
block can be displaced off the trailing position.

But re-stamping later cannot help. `hasUserPromptSubmitContext`
(`packages/core/src/hooks/user-prompt-submit-context.ts:105-125`) requires
`parts[parts.length - 1].text === wrapUserPromptSubmitContext(context)` **and** the receipt on that same last part.
Once a reminder or the memory text is appended after the block, the block is no longer last, so the predicate
returns `false` whether or not the receipt is present. "Re-stamp after the ToolResult-lane appends (or at commit
time)" therefore changes nothing observable — it is an inert patch.

The only effective fix is the reporter's own broader alternative: relax the predicate to an any-position
receipt+text scan. By the reporter's own note that requires changing the "while it stays the trailing part"
acceptance wording in both design docs, and it collides with the pinned test `does not match a sole tagged part`
(`user-prompt-submit-context.test.ts`) and the display projection at `transcript-records.ts:234-235`. That is the
same deliberate cross-file contract change already registered here as **R5-12**, and it should be decided once,
together with R5-12, not twice.

Reordering the append so the block lands after the ToolResult lane would instead change the wire payload's part
order — product behaviour — and is a restructure well past three lines.

Not a regression either: before this PR the block was appended unconditionally on every turn including ToolResult
turns, so the PR only fails to *extend* dedup to that lane.

#### R5-11 / R5-13 — test-only, cheap, good next-round candidates

Both are coverage gaps on lines this PR added (`turn.ts:749-751` spread plus the `:724` ctor param;
`session-api-history.ts:217-223` restore). Both are verified test-only: no production change is implied, and the
reporter's mutation witnesses identify exactly which surviving mutation each new case must kill. They only land
riding along with a real code fix, and this round has none. R5-13 covers the same restore path **R5-10** depends on,
so settling R5-10 first may change what R5-13 should assert — do them in that order.

issues.body:
Follow-up from #13571 review thread R1-14. The extraction-cadence experiment (`QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_EXTRACT_NOOP_SKIP_TURNS`, off by default) adds several production sites and gates. For the ones below, removing the site leaves the suite green. The design record makes any default change depend on paired runs, and each of these is a switch or gate those runs rely on.

Already pinned on #13571: `getExtractNoopSkipTurns` parsing and its 0–3 clamp (`extract-cadence.test.ts`), and the in-flight-across-switch outcome drop (`does not re-arm a session from a run that was in flight across a switch`).

Still unpinned. Each new test should go red when its own site is deleted, and only then:

1. **`memory_tool` disarm** in `MemoryManager.scheduleExtract`. Arm the cadence with an engaged no-op, then schedule a turn whose latest entry writes a memory file. Assert `skippedReason: 'memory_tool'` and that the following turn extracts.
2. **Cadence-skip task record.** Assert that the skip stores `{ status: 'skipped', metadata: { skippedReason: 'cadence' } }`.
3. **Cadence-skip telemetry.** Pass a config to `extractParams` (as the `session_mismatch` case does) and assert a `MemoryExtractEvent` with `skipped_reason: 'cadence'`.
4. **`extractorEngaged`** in `runAutoMemoryExtract` (`extract.ts`). Assert it follows the agent's tool activity.
5. **`discardExtractCadence` from `Config.startNewSession`.** Assert that the switch drops both ids through `startNewSession`, not through a direct manager call.
6. **ACP close flush** (`acpAgent.ts`). No CLI test observes `flushPendingExtract`.
7. **`belowCompactionWarn` spreads** in `client.ts` and `Session.ts`. Today only `manager.test.ts` passes the flag directly.

Constraint: `shouldSkipForCadence` returns early unless `belowCompactionWarn === true`. Both the arming turn and the turn that must not skip therefore have to go through the suite's `turn()` helper; otherwise the disarm cannot be observed.

<details><summary>中文说明</summary>

来自 #13571 review thread R1-14 的后续项。提取节奏实验（`QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_EXTRACT_NOOP_SKIP_TURNS`，默认关闭）新增了若干生产调用点和判定门。下面这些点删掉之后测试仍然全绿。设计记录规定，修改默认值要以配对运行为前提，而这些都是配对运行依赖的开关或判定门。

14. **读集 `accessed` 分类器与只写返回值 scope 标记之间没有测试固定**（`extractionAgentPlanner.test.ts:495`）：返回的 `touchedProjectScope`/`touchedUserScope` 必须保持只写，而合并了 `filesRead` 的 `accessed` 只喂 `extractorEngaged`。`:479-497` 的 `it.each` 是唯一带根内读的用例，且只断言 `hasToolActivity`、`extractorEngaged`、`touchedTopics`；其余 scope 断言全用写或根外读。所以把两次分类器调用合成一次 `[...filesRead, ...filesWritten]` 喂返回值，整套件仍绿（见证：35 passed，只剩既有环境性 `memoryDiscovery` 失败）。生产中提取 agent 被要求先读已有 memory 文件，因此对已有用户 memory 内容的项目每次运行都会读用户根文件；合并后 `touchedUserScope` 在没写过的项目上变真，而 `manager.ts:1842` 没有 `touchedTopics` 门，会对每次都调 `recordUserMutation`，写下用户 memory 变更记录，并在 `state.metadata.pendingReason` 有值时（`manager.ts:2640-2642`）为从未变化的 memory 多排一整次 User Dream。修法：补一条「根内只读不写」用例，断言 `touchedUserScope === false` 而 `extractorEngaged === true`，在合并变异体下变红。

15. **补充门的根条件从未在「异根 pending」下被执行**（`manager.test.ts:2288`，守 `manager.ts:1290`）：唯一到达运行的迁移用例停在节奏门（`turns(6)`，从 `skippedFrom` 2 起跨度 4）；真正触发补充门的三条都经 `tmp.projectRoot` 且条目键在同根；跨根用例（`does not carry a snapshot across roots…`）在 `turnAt(tmp.projectRoot, 45)` 时已无 pending，因为 carry guard 先丢掉了它。删掉根条件后 142/142 仍绿。生产中该门承重：在项目 A arm + skip 会把快照停在 A 的 cursor base；`/cd` 到 B 不触发 discard，条目仍是 A 键且带 A 的 pending；B 的第一个新增超过 40 条的轮次（一次长 agentic 轮，约 20 次工具调用）满足 `45 - 2 > 40`，于是把 A 的 parked turns 当作 `skippedHistory` 传进 B 的提取，forked extractor 读 A 的对话并把结果写进 B 的 memory 根——正是 carry guard 自己注释描述的跨项目拼接（`manager.ts:1500-1504`）。修法：补一条真的走到补充门、且 pending 属异根的用例，断言不发生跨根拼接，删根条件时变红。

16. **`discardExtractCadence` 的多 id 删除只固定了一半**（`manager.test.ts:2298`，守 `manager.ts:1600`）：没有任何调用点让**第一个**参数带上活状态。把 `manager.ts:1600` 变异成只删 `sessionIds[sessionIds.length - 1]` 后 142/142 仍绿。生产调用是 `discardExtractCadence(previousSessionId, nextSessionId)`（`config.ts:6327`）——离开的 id 是**第一个**参数，所以在变异体下它保留 `armed: true`、已部分花掉的 skips 与 parked 快照。在代码注释自己点名的 `/resume` 回到旧 id 路径上（`manager.ts:730-733`，"the discarded id can come back"），那个会话会继承最多 N 个被抑制的轮次，而 close flush 的 `liveSessionId` 门此时又匹配，于是 fork 出一份从已被切换丢弃的时间线上切下来的快照。修法：补一条「第一个 id 带活状态、第二个不带」的用例，断言两者都被丢弃，在只删末位变异体下变红。

17. **成功后 flush 删除的 `settled.pending === pending` 条件没有测试固定**（`manager.test.ts:2369`，守 `manager.ts:1742-1744`）：唯一的成功 flush 用例在 flush 前已花完预算（2 次里跳过 2 次——`manager.ts:1403` 的 `state.skips >= budget` 使 fork 期间不可能再跳过），三条替换快照用例根本到不了删除处（它们在 fork 前的 `state.pending !== pending` 检查 `manager.ts:1705` 就拒绝并返回 false）。所以把删除放宽成 `if (settled)` 对套件完全不可见。生产窗口真实且很长：预算 2，轮 1 arm，轮 2 skip 并停 S1；ACP close flush fork S1，而该 fork 可跑到 `maxTimeMinutes: config.getMemoryAgentTimeoutMinutes() ?? 2`（`extractionAgentPlanner.ts:447`）。落在这个窗口内的轮次仍有预算（2 中花了 1），skip 并停 S2，`recordCadenceOutcome` 会把它承接下去（`runSeq < seqOf(previous)`）。flush 随后返回 true 并删除条目，把 S2 一起带走：S2 停下的轮次再也不会被任何边界提取，而 close 路径却被告知 true（「pending 轮次已提取」）。修法：补一条在 flush 进行中停一份替换快照的用例，断言 flush 既不删除它也不返回 true，在放宽删除的变异体下变红。

</details>

issues.title: [Bug] XML recovery repeats prefix scans on large multi-call responses

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/performance
labels.description: Performance and optimization

labels.name: scope/latency
labels.description: Response time optimization

issues.body:
## What happened?

XML tool-call recovery becomes increasingly slow when a completed response contains many valid calls. A bounded direct-parser reproduction confirms the cost on current main `e3c5360e5a71` and PR #13579 at `f6f8af8be25f`.

| Blocks | Plain input bytes | Main plain ms | PR plain ms | Quoted-content bytes | PR quoted-content ms |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 17,100 | 16.10 | 17.44 | 22,400 | 24.01 |
| 200 | 34,200 | 87.03 | 80.86 | 44,800 | 139.85 |
| 400 | 68,400 | 565.04 | 575.06 | 89,600 | 989.68 |

The plain-block cost already exists on main. PR #13579 correctly recovers outer calls whose content contains literal XML call examples; that newly accepted input class encounters the same repeated prefix scanning. Main rejects these identical quoted-content inputs without recovery, so its shorter timings for them are not equivalent feature performance.

All 2,100 recovered outer calls across the nine positive measurements had exact arguments and empty remaining text. The inner `read_file` examples stayed inside the outer content and were never dispatched. This is a source-level postprocessing measurement, not a live-model or CLI latency benchmark. Each size was measured once; the data shows strongly superlinear growth without establishing an exact asymptotic degree. The reviewer's larger 2,000-block workload was not rerun.

### How to reproduce

Run this read-only probe with `npx tsx parser-perf.ts` from the repository root at either pinned revision:

```ts
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks';
import { tryRecoverXmlToolCalls } from './packages/core/src/core/xml-tool-call-fallback.ts';

const plain = [
  '<invoke name="write_file">',
  '<parameter name="content">Anonymous plain payload.\nAnonymous marker\n</parameter>',
  '<parameter name="file_path">anonymous.md</parameter>',
  '</invoke>',
  '',
].join('\n');
const quoted = plain.replace(
  'Anonymous plain payload.\nAnonymous marker\n',
  'Usage:\n<invoke name="read_file"><parameter name="file_path">anonymous.txt</parameter></invoke>\n',
);
for (const blocks of [100, 200, 400]) {
  for (const [kind, block] of [['plain', plain], ['quoted', quoted]] as const) {
    const input = block.repeat(blocks);
    const start = performance.now();
    tryRecoverXmlToolCalls(input);
    console.log({ kind, blocks, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(input), ms: performance.now() - start });
  }
}
```

Calling the parser does not execute tools or write the named fixture files. The observed mechanism is the final per-block fence/example filtering, which repeatedly slices and splits the preceding response and searches parameter ranges. PR #13579 also uses that helper while classifying quoted values. [Exact current-main source](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e3c5360e5a718549f7ace9be61ef830ed097a81a/packages/core/src/core/xml-tool-call-fallback.ts), [review follow-up](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579#pullrequestreview-5472672743).

## What did you expect to happen?

Large valid multi-call responses should recover the same outer calls and preserve literal argument content without repeatedly scanning every preceding block.

## Client information

Controlled parser reproduction: macOS arm64, Node v22.22.0, tsx 4.20.3; unmodified Git-object copies of both pinned TypeScript modules using the same existing dependencies. One child process completed in 3.32 seconds; no repeated runs or tool execution. Main module SHA256: `a6052efbda59bc1bf27367ac5de28a0c1834b43b1abfb9aa9cfb6af22024a505`; PR module SHA256: `711fab51837d8ce64f12d93389b06091d90cae61ccbb4d5905ae09f8ef6f0ab1`.

<details>
<summary>Installed client information (sanitized; not the parser benchmark target)</summary>

```text
Qwen Code v0.25.0-nightly.20261007.8003d28042
Model: [redacted]
Fast Model: [redacted]
Auth: openai
Platform: darwin arm64 (27.0.0)
Node.js: v22.22.0
Session: [redacted]
Git commit: cce7fed039
LSP: disabled
```

Local model/provider identifiers, session identifier and unrelated local execution configuration are omitted or redacted.

</details>

This records the non-blocking performance follow-up separately from #13579's correctness repair after repeated review rounds.

中文：已在准确 main/PR 源码上有界复现，main 本身已有普通多调用块耗时增长；PR 新支持的内容引用场景进入同一过滤路径。400 个引用内容块约 990ms，所有外层参数保持正确、内层示例未派发。仅一次受控纯解析器观察，没有真实模型/CLI 延迟或精确复杂度结论；作为非阻塞后续性能项跟踪。


## Round-5 review finding recorded here: R5-1

PR #13579 round-5 review raised this same cost as `[Critical]` R5-1 ([thread](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579#discussion_r4234229508)). It is recorded here instead of being fixed in that PR, whose scope ledger limits it to fully-closed quoted-value recovery. Line numbers below are verified at PR head `6d9ebdc46da79a1bec7015ffde642cbf529541e1`, `packages/core/src/core/xml-tool-call-fallback.ts`.

**Which passes are unbounded.** Six `positionInsideFence` call sites (`:205`, `:222`, `:552`, `:553`, `:576`, `:577`); each one slices `text.slice(0, index)` and walks every line of that prefix against the whole `parameterRanges` list.

- `maskValuesBefore` (`:201`) restarts that scan from offset 0 once per quoted value (`:205`) and pushes a span (`:206`) that lengthens the list every later line test walks — the two costs compound.
- `isEligibleBlock` (`:552`, `:553`) and `passesFenceGuard` (`:576`, `:577`) pay it twice per **candidate** block, so the cost is reachable on turns where most documentation is correctly suppressed.

`MAX_LEXER_SCAN_LENGTH` (`:21`) is used at exactly one place, `:153`, and bounds only marked's inline-lexer pass. It does not bound any `positionInsideFence` pass, so an oversized turn pays the fence scans in full.

**Measurements.** R5-1's A/B witness (identical bytes, measured at PR head `f6f8af8be25f`, before the round-5 guard landed): 23.8 KB 2 ms → 28 ms, 63.4 KB 6 ms → 440 ms, 158 KB 41 ms → 6410 ms, 237 KB 55 ms → 20786 ms; controls: 640 plain sibling calls BASE 546 ms / HEAD 543 ms. The PR author separately measured the compiled parser on a different corpus at 1,378 ms for 93,887 bytes and 29,174 ms for 250,387 bytes ([thread reply, 2026-10-09](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579#discussion_r4234229508)). Both are source/parser-level measurements, not live-model latency. The table at the top of this issue is a third independent measurement of the same mechanism.

**Why the reviewer's incremental rewrite is not a drop-in fix.** The suggestion is to carry the fence cursor and `openFence` state across calls because the requested positions increase monotonically. But `parameterRanges` is mutated *while* it is being scanned (`maskValuesBefore` pushes at `:206`), then pushed to again from the eligibility loop (`:603`), then re-sorted and merged in place (`:614`) before a second `computeExampleRanges` pass runs over it. Any cached cursor or fence state has to be invalidated by every one of those mutations, so bounding these passes means restructuring the range-list lifecycle, not adding a cache. The alternative the reviewer offers — bound the passes the way the lexer is bounded and fail closed past the bound — changes which blocks stay eligible, i.e. it changes recovery behaviour, and `exampleTagPositions`' existing over-cap `null` sentinel already shows how that interacts with the intent guard.

**Scope for a fix.** Bound or incrementalise all six call sites together, and pin the bound itself with a test that counts the helper's iterations or scanned characters on a many-block input — a pure complexity refactor reddens no existing assertion. R2-7 on the same PR asked for this shape. `sequential documentation masks` (test:1477) and `reviewed XML ownership and documentation regressions` (test:1385) must stay green, which is what would prove a cached-cursor version is equivalent rather than merely faster.

中文：第 5 轮 review 的 R5-1（`[Critical]`，无上限同步扫描）记录在本 issue，不在 PR #13579 内修。已核实该 head 上共 6 处 `positionInsideFence` 调用（`:205` `:222` `:552` `:553` `:576` `:577`），每处都从偏移 0 重扫整个前缀；`MAX_LEXER_SCAN_LENGTH` 只在 `:153` 门控 marked 词法分析，不管这些扫描。reviewer 建议的「跨调用携带游标」不是即插即用：`parameterRanges` 在被扫描期间就被 `:206` 修改，之后又在 `:603` 追加、在 `:614` 原地重排合并，再跑第二遍 `computeExampleRanges`，缓存必须被每次修改失效，因此要重排 range 列表的生命周期；改成「超长度即失败关闭」则会改变恢复行为。修的时候六处要一起收，并用测试固定上限本身。

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Port the ideas from https://github.com/Rianico/dsh-better-edit into Qwen Code as a replacement for the current read/edit files.

### Why is this needed?

The edit tool is currently the worst part of my workflow. The agent constantly trips on exact old_text matches, frequently has to re-read large sections of a file multiple times, even re-writes both old and new text multiple times in its thought process to prepare for the tool call.

With the tool linked above, all of this disappears and the context window no longer fills up with a dozen redundant copies of the same paragraph or function.

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.body:
### What happened?

## What happened?

Creating the first conversation in the Web UI after starting `qwen serve` on Windows fails repeatedly with HTTP 504:

```
Create session failed (workspace: F:\src\AgentWorkbench): POST /session: AcpSessionBridge initialize timed out after 3601ms
```

Observed pattern (single daemon run, 2026-10-20):

- Right after startup, the daemon's own ACP preheat fails: `ACP preheat failed, will retry on first session: AcpSessionBridge initialize timed out after 7400ms`
- The first three `POST /session` attempts all fail with 504 and `AcpSessionBridge initialize timed out after 4854 / 1637 / 3601ms` (total request durations 12660 / 10407 / 10408 ms), each immediately preceded by `channel exited (code=1, signal=none, transport=ok, 0 session(s) torn down)`
- Subsequent attempts barely succeed: 9002 ms / 9884 ms
- Once the channel is warm, creation takes ~0.5 s and everything is fast
- Loading an existing session right after a page load fails the same way: two open tabs (embedded view + external browser) both got 504 (`initialize timed out after 3596ms`)
- The client does not matter — identical behavior from a regular browser and from an embedded Qt WebEngine view; this is entirely server-side

Key log evidence (`~/.qwen/debug/daemon/daemon.log` / serve stdout). A fresh Web UI page load triggers workspace endpoints whose durations line up with daemon event-loop stalls:

```
09:56:27 [WARN] maxMs=6425.673727 daemon event loop stall detected
09:56:27 route=GET /workspaces/F%3A%5Csrc%5CAgentWorkbench/channels  durationMs=453  status=200
09:56:29 route=GET /workspaces/F%3A%5Csrc%5CAgentWorkbench/memory    durationMs=2099 status=304
09:56:29 route=GET /workspaces/F%3A%5Csrc%5CAgentWorkbench/extensions durationMs=2601 status=304
09:56:29 route=GET /workspaces/F%3A%5Csrc%5CAgentWorkbench/skills    durationMs=2687 status=200
09:56:35 route=GET /workspaces/F%3A%5Csrc%5CAgentWorkbench/git       durationMs=7871 status=200
...
10:00:34 route=GET /workspaces/F%3A%5Csrc%5CAgentWorkbench/git       durationMs=5154 status=200
10:00:43 [WARN] maxMs=8388.607999 daemon event loop stall detected
10:00:43 route=GET /workspaces/F%3A%5Csrc%5CAgentWorkbench/git       durationMs=9636 status=304
```

(Stall warnings also appear during daemon startup itself, before any page load: `maxMs=1118`, `2613`, `3305`.)

The three failed creates:

```
qwen serve: channel exited (code=1, signal=none, transport=ok, 0 session(s) torn down)
10:00:28 [WARN] route=POST /session errorType=BridgeTimeoutError AcpSessionBridge initialize timed out after 4854ms
10:00:28 [WARN] route=POST /session clientId=webui_89c6cca2… durationMs=12660 status=504

qwen serve: channel exited (code=1, signal=none, transport=ok, 0 session(s) torn down)
10:00:45 [WARN] route=POST /session errorType=BridgeTimeoutError AcpSessionBridge initialize timed out after 1637ms
10:00:45 [WARN] route=POST /session clientId=webui_91e37dca… durationMs=10407 status=504

qwen serve: channel exited (code=1, signal=none, transport=ok, 0 session(s) torn down)
10:01:01 [WARN] route=POST /session errorType=BridgeTimeoutError AcpSessionBridge initialize timed out after 3601ms
10:01:01 [WARN] route=POST /session clientId=webui_7804fc2e… durationMs=10408 status=504
```

Then marginal successes, then fast once warm:

```
10:01:50 route=POST /session clientId=webui_02a356e7… durationMs=9002 status=200
10:04:01 route=POST /session clientId=webui_6e98c6f6… durationMs=9884 status=200
10:06:01 route=POST /session clientId=webui_6cc0d132… durationMs=502  status=200
```

The ACP child itself also reports long stalls in this workspace (from daemon.log, during startup and during turns):

```
[serve pid=332   cwd=F:\src\AgentWorkbench] [perf] acp agent event loop stall: max=14587.789311ms
[serve pid=12284 cwd=F:\src\AgentWorkbench] [perf] acp agent event loop stall: max=17263.755263ms
```

Steps to reproduce:

1. On Windows, run `qwen serve` with a workspace whose `git status` is slow (nested submodules and/or an old git version; my repo's `git status --porcelain` takes ~3.8 s standalone).
2. Open the Web UI (the fresh page load triggers the workspace scans).
3. Immediately create a new conversation → expect `AcpSessionBridge initialize timed out` (504). Retry 2–3× → eventually 200 after ~9–10 s.
4. Create another conversation → < 1 s (warm channel).

### What did you expect to happen?

## What did you expect to happen?

- Creating the first session on a cold daemon should not hard-fail: either the ACP initialize budget should accommodate realistic Windows cold starts, or the server should retry internally / return a retryable "still warming up" response instead of a 504.
- Workspace scans (git/skills/memory/extensions) should not stall the daemon event loop for seconds, so a page load cannot starve a concurrent session handshake.
- A timed-out initialize should ideally not discard the channel back to a cold start, making every retry pay the full cold-start cost again.

### Client information

- qwen-code **0.25.3** (npm global install on Windows)
- Client: Web Shell UI served by `qwen serve` (mode=http-bridge, listening on `http://127.0.0.1:4170`), accessed from a regular desktop browser; also reproduced from an embedded Qt WebEngine view with identical behavior (the embed is not a factor)
- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19044); Node v22.20.0
- Daemon startup workspace: `C:\Users\…`; the failing session's workspace: `F:\src\AgentWorkbench` — a git repo with a chain of nested submodules (`spdlog`; `SARibbon` → `qwindowkit` → `qmsetup` → `syscmdline`)
- git 2.7.2 (old — no `core.untrackedCache` / `core.fsmonitor`)
- Always-on context (QWEN.md context files + auto-memory) for this workspace: ~10,248 tokens
- Daemon startup timing for reference: `processToListenMs=2711`

### Login information

The failure happens during ACP session initialization, before any model call, so I don't think auth is a factor here. Web Shell HTTP access is token-gated and authenticated fine (the failures are 504, not 401). For completeness:

- Login method: [FILL IN — e.g. Qwen OAuth / DASHSCOPE_API_KEY / other provider]
- Provider & model used: [FILL IN]

### Anything else we need to know?

Root-cause analysis (numbers are from the logs; the causal reading is my inference — happy to be corrected):

1. On this machine/workspace the ACP child's cold start + initialize round-trip takes ~7–10 s: preheat alone times out at 7.4 s, and successful creates took 9.0 / 9.9 s.
2. The initialize wait budget is much smaller: the observed "timed out after" values are 1.6–4.9 s, apparently the remaining budget of a ~10.4 s route deadline.
3. Workspace endpoints (git status in particular — 3.8–9.6 s on this repo) appear to run in-process and block the daemon's event loop for multiple seconds during page load. During a stall, the child's initialize response sits unread; the deadline fires → `BridgeTimeoutError` → 504.
4. Each failed handshake coincides with `channel exited`, so the next attempt pays the full cold-start cost again → consecutive 504s until one attempt squeaks under the deadline.

Suggestions (up to maintainers):

- Make the ACP initialize handshake budget configurable (settings key or env var) and/or raise the default on Windows.
- Reuse or keep warming a partially-started channel across consecutive create attempts (retry with backoff) instead of kill → cold restart.
- Move `git status` and the other workspace scans off the main thread, or cache them, so they cannot block request handling.

Other notes:

- Full daemon logs available (`~/.qwen/debug/daemon/daemon.log` + captured serve stdout) — can attach the relevant time windows on request.
- Not a recent regression: the same `BridgeTimeoutError` pattern appears in my daemon logs since at least August (0.25.3 is just my current version).

issues.body:
### What happened?

Version: 0.25.3 (npm global) · macOS arm64 · model `dewu/qwen3.8-flash`, `contextWindowSize: 1000000`

## Symptom

```
Warning: Loaded always-on context (QWEN.md context files + auto-memory) uses about 10,685 tokens,
more than 10,000 tokens — the smaller of that and 15% of this model's 1,000,000 token context window.
Consider trimming long always-loaded context or moving details into on-demand files.
```

The suggested remedy barely moves the reported number, so the warning reads as unactionable.

## Findings

**1. `CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4` underestimates CJK-heavy content ~2x.** The estimate is
`Math.ceil(memoryContent.length / CHARS_PER_TOKEN)` — a flat char/4 regardless of script. Chinese runs
≈1 token/char, so CJK text costs 4x what the divisor assumes. Measured on my own three loaded files
(24,689 chars total, 2,513 CJK): code gives **6,173**, realistic ≈**8,057**. Direction is corpus-dependent
— pure-CJK is underestimated, ASCII-heavy is roughly right — so the number is not merely conservative, it
is unsound as a threshold test. Fix: tokenize properly, or weight W/F ranges at ~1 char/token.

**2. The dominant contributor is unnamed, and it is mostly not user-trimmable.** The call site joins
`[getUserMemory(), getAutoMemoryPrompt(), getAutoMemoryContext()]`. In legacy mode `autoMemoryContext`
holds the **full MEMORY.md catalog for both scopes** — here 121 lines / 19,068 chars vs AGENTS.md's 5,621.
So the index drives the breach, yet "trim long always-loaded context" points users at QWEN.md/AGENTS.md.
I cut AGENTS.md by 2.5 KB and the warning did not budge. Naming the split in the message would make the
advice actionable.

**3. No way to raise or silence the bound.** Threshold is hardcoded `min(0.15 × window, 1e4)`
(`MEMORY_CONTEXT_WARNING_RATIO=.15`, `MEMORY_CONTEXT_WARNING_MAX_TOKENS=1e4`). For any model with ≥1M
window the bar is pinned at 10k, i.e. 1% of available context — while there is a
`QWEN_CODE_SUPPRESS_YOLO_WARNING` precedent for exactly this kind of notice but none here.

## Repro

Workspace with a large CJK AGENTS.md/QWEN.md plus >~100 memory entries; restart and observe the warning.

## Not claimed

I did **not** establish that structured recall fails to shrink this specific prompt. My A/B
(`QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_STRUCTURED_RECALL=0|1`, headless, answered "FLAT" both times) is weak evidence — it
rests on asking the model to introspect its own context, and headless may not exercise the same path.
Treat item 2 as measured from source and file sizes only.

### What did you expect to happen?

The advice ("trim long always-loaded context") targets QWEN.md/AGENTS.md, but the measured total is dominated by the auto-memory index catalog, which users can't trim without losing memories — so the warning is not actionable. Also CHARS_PER_TOKEN=4 mis-estimates CJK.

### Client information


Qwen Code: 0.25.3 (b28b0d948f)
Runtime: Node.js v26.2.0 / npm 11.17.0
LSP: disabled
OS: darwin arm64 (27.0.0)

prs.title: fix(web-shell): pause requests offline and recover automatically
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Unifies Web Shell's native HTTP calls through the SDK and adds shared availability control for each active service connection. After a transport failure, business requests and reconnect loops pause while one bounded recovery probe runs. Successful health and authenticated capability checks automatically resume reads and session attachment.

The UI shows a localized connection warning with Retry, including fullscreen and modal artifact views. Cached reads and unsent drafts survive disconnection; terminal and local-file connections wait for recovery. Prompt submissions, uploads and other writes are not replayed automatically. User-facing connection messages use “service / 服务”.

## Why it's needed

A page waiting for its first prompt can keep showing a connected state after its service stops. Independent polling then continues to fail without an explanation in the UI and can distort business API success rates. A shared gate stops subsequent business traffic instead of merely slowing each poller independently.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open the welcome page without submitting a prompt, enter a draft and browse a workspace directory. Stop the service: a persistent connection warning should appear and the draft should remain.
2. Observe network traffic after in-flight requests settle: business calls should stop, leaving one shared health probe sequence with 5/15/30-second delays. Requests rejected locally should not become HTTP requests.
3. Restart at the same address and credential without reloading or clicking Retry. The warning should disappear, reads and directory browsing should resume, and the draft should remain editable. No prompt or write should be replayed.
4. Check authentication rejection and explicit Retry, caller cancellation/timeouts, old responses after recovery, provider unmounts, and fullscreen/modal warning visibility. Deterministic regression tests cover these boundaries; the browser run below covers one real no-session provider.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Current build, real test-owned service, headless Chromium; screenshots show offline → automatic recovery on the same page. All 16 browser checks passed. Stop detection: 3.473s. Offline observation: 54.056s, zero business requests after banner detection. Probe gaps: 5.004/15.002/30.002s. Same-address restart recovered automatically in 25.944s. The preserved draft remained editable, and a new directory GET returned 200. No model prompt, write request or Git mutation was performed; there were no browser page errors.

| Before recovery: offline warning and retained draft | After automatic recovery: warning removed and draft retained |
| --- | --- |
| ![Service offline, draft retained](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/offline-after-backoff.png) | ![Service automatically recovered, draft retained](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/recovered-draft.png) |

[Actual directory browse after recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/recovered-directory-and-editable-draft.png) · [Sanitized network timeline and assertions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/network-evidence.json) · [Bilingual evidence notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/README.md)

Initial-load Retry was separately verified in both workspace and standalone error pages: **16/16 checks passed** in the real built UI with Playwright injecting only initial capabilities502/health503 failures. Explicit Retry sent health then capabilities before the pending backoff; the error cleared, the editor was usable, and no write was sent. Normal App mounting also performed capabilities reads after recovery (2 total for workspace,3 for standalone). This is fault-injected evidence, separate from the real stop/restart run above.

[Workspace initial error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/workspace-initial-error.png) → [after Retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/workspace-retry-recovered.png) · [Standalone initial error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/standalone-initial-error.png) → [after Retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/standalone-retry-recovered.png)

Local verification after merging current origin/main: all 12,723 Web Shell tests and 4 SDK request tests passed. The original six CI failures were reproduced; an independent red/green check confirmed that the updated loading assertions fail against the old implementation (4 cases) and pass with the fix (13 boot/loading cases). Root build, bundle and typecheck, PR-file ESLint/formatting, nine lint-freshness helper tests and diff checks passed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ arm64: package tests and real browser stop/restart |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22.14.0, local 0.25.3 build, headless Chromium, isolated loopback service and temporary workspace/runtime. The test-owned processes and directories were cleaned up; existing development services were untouched. Browser evidence corresponds to `df78833baca69679b198c1a0412ebc52be048a5f`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: shared availability decisions affect every panel under the owning provider. Regression tests cover false outage classification, client ownership, stale responses, cancellation and cleanup. Separate providers retain independent recovery loops.
- Not validated / out of scope: real active-model/SSE restoration, multi-panel stop/restart, audio/LAN and OS integrations. Host success-rate filtering for probes still needs integration evidence; initial failed/in-flight requests and retries hidden inside host transports cannot be eliminated by this gate.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no server route or ownership changes. The SDK request entry is additive; older supported peer SDKs retain one native REST compatibility path. Recovery never resubmits writes.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-09-daemon-request-recovery.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-09-daemon-request-recovery.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized.

## Linked Issues

No linked GitHub issue.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 此 PR 的改动

将 Web Shell 的原生 HTTP 请求统一进入 SDK，并为每个活动服务连接增加共享可用性控制。传输失败后暂停业务请求与重连循环，仅保留一个有超时上限的恢复探针；健康检查和带认证的 capabilities 检查成功后，自动恢复读取与会话附着。

界面显示带重试入口的本地化连接提示，覆盖全屏和模态 artifact 视图。断连时保留读取缓存与未发送草稿，终端和本地文件连接等待共享恢复；不会自动重放 prompt、上传或其他写操作。面向用户的连接提示使用“服务 / service”。

### 为什么需要

等待首条 prompt 的页面可能在服务停止后仍显示已连接，各自独立的轮询随后持续失败，界面却没有说明，还可能拉低业务接口成功率。共享门禁直接阻止后续业务流量，而不是让每个轮询各自降频。

### 评审验证计划

1. 在欢迎页不提交 prompt，输入草稿并浏览 workspace 目录。停止服务后，应出现持续连接提示，并保留草稿。
2. 等待在途请求结束后观察网络：业务请求应停止，只剩一个共享健康探针，按5/15/30秒退避。本地拒绝的操作不应变成 HTTP 请求。
3. 同地址、同凭证重启，不刷新或点击重试。提示应自动消失，读取与目录浏览恢复，草稿仍可编辑；不能重放 prompt 或写操作。
4. 检查认证拒绝与手动重试、调用方取消/超时、恢复后的旧响应、Provider 卸载，以及全屏/模态提示可见性。确定性回归测试覆盖这些边界；下述浏览器验证覆盖一个真实、无会话的 Provider。

### 证据（恢复前后）

使用当前构建、独立真实服务和无头 Chromium；截图展示同一页面从离线到自动恢复。16项浏览器检查全部通过。停机后3.473秒发现断连；横幅出现后观察54.056秒，业务请求为0；探针实际间隔为5.004/15.002/30.002秒。同地址重启后25.944秒自动恢复。保留的草稿仍可编辑，新目录 GET 返回200。没有提交模型 prompt、发送写请求或执行 Git 写操作，也没有浏览器 pageerror。

| 恢复前：离线横幅与保留草稿 | 自动恢复后：横幅消失，草稿保留 |
| --- | --- |
| ![服务离线，草稿保留](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/offline-after-backoff.png) | ![服务自动恢复，草稿保留](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/recovered-draft.png) |

[恢复后的实际目录浏览](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/recovered-directory-and-editable-draft.png) · [已脱敏的网络时间线与断言](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/network-evidence.json) · [双语证据说明](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/README.md)

另在工作区和独立会话的首次加载错误页验证了手动重试：**16/16项检查通过**，使用实际构建UI与真实服务，仅通过Playwright注入首次capabilities502/health503故障。点击重试后在原定退避触发前先发health再发capabilities，错误页消失、编辑器可输入，无写请求。恢复后App挂载还会正常读取capabilities（工作区合计2次，独立会话3次）。这属于故障注入证据，与上面的真实停机/重启验证分别记录。

[工作区首次错误](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/workspace-initial-error.png) → [重试后](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/workspace-retry-recovered.png) · [独立会话首次错误](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/standalone-initial-error.png) → [重试后](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/92a3da81845a86e2db973dc11a406dc61bf259c8/daemon-recovery/standalone-retry-recovered.png)

### 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：共享可用性判断会影响归属该 Provider 的所有面板。回归测试覆盖误判、客户端归属、过期响应、取消与清理；不同 Provider 仍各自维护恢复循环。

## What this PR does

Moves the model-picker refresh control from a full-width text button under the list to an icon button beside the search field. Failures still appear as a localized alert under that row. The `/model` dialog keeps the same icon after the list so opening the dialog still focuses the model rows.

The previous refresh button sat under the model list and competed with the entries themselves. Putting refresh next to search keeps the action available without taking a whole row in the picker.

4. Hover or focus the icon: the accessible name should be "Refresh models" / "刷新模型列表".
5. Trigger a failed refresh and confirm the error alert still appears under the search row, then retry until the new model is selectable.
6. Open `/model` (or the settings model dialog) and confirm Enter still selects the highlighted model rather than activating refresh.
