prs.title: fix(core): split shell commands on bash's separators, not JavaScript whitespace
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Bash's lexer discards exactly space, tab and newline when it decides word boundaries; JavaScript's `/\s/` matches `\r`, `\v`, `\f`, `\u00a0` and the rest of Unicode whitespace, every one of which bash treats as an ordinary word character. The shell command splitter used `/\s/` in its backward scan for the character before an `&` or `|`, so `echo x >\r& rm -rf /tmp/x` read the `\r` as spacing and kept both commands in one segment — the `rm` never reached the command roots that the shell tool's permission checks and git attribution read.

This change treats only space, tab and newline as separators, moves the predicate into a small leaf module shared by the splitter and the permission rule parser (which carried its own copy of the constant), trims segments with the existing bash-aware helper so a redirection target made of `\r` or `\u00a0` survives, and switches the second `/\s/` scan in `hasNonFinalTopLevelBackgroundOperator` to the same predicate so `echo x >\r& y` is recognised as a redirect followed by a background operator instead of a `>&` dup-redirect.

## Why it's needed

`getCommandRoots` decides which sub-commands the shell tool asks about and what it reads for git attribution; a command missing there is invisible to both. `echo x >\r& rm -rf /tmp/x` is two commands to bash, but the splitter saw one, so the second command's root was never surfaced for confirmation. The background-operator check feeds the same misreading: with `\r` skipped as whitespace, `>\r&` looked like the `>&` redirect form and the operator was not reported.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/core`, run `npx vitest run src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts src/permissions/rule-parser.test.ts`. On `main` the new cases fail — the trailing `rm` is absent from both `getCommandRoots` and `splitCommands`, and `hasNonFinalTopLevelBackgroundOperator('echo x >\r& rm -rf /tmp/x')` returns `false`; on this branch they pass and the existing CRLF cases stay green.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible surface; the tests are the evidence.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the predicate is deliberately narrower than `/\s/`, so any caller that relied on the splitter treating `\r` / `\v` / `\f` / `\u00a0` as whitespace now gets a split. That is the intended behaviour — bash splits there — and a narrower separator set can only add splits, never merge two commands into one.
- Not validated / out of scope: other packages that re-implement bash word splitting are untouched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12089.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

Bash 的词法分析在划分词边界时只丢弃空格、制表符和换行；JavaScript 的 `/\s/` 还会匹配 `\r`、`\v`、`\f`、`\u00a0` 等全部 Unicode 空白，而这些在 bash 里都是普通的词字符。命令切分器在回溯扫描 `&` 或 `|` 前一个字符时用了 `/\s/`，于是 `echo x >\r& rm -rf /tmp/x` 里的 `\r` 被当作空白，两条命令被并成一段——`rm` 从此没有进入 shell 工具权限检查与 git 归因所依赖的命令根列表。

本改动只把空格、制表符和换行视为分隔符；把该判定抽到一个叶子模块，供切分器与权限规则解析器共同复用（后者原本自带一份重复常量）；段的裁剪改用已有的 bash 感知辅助函数，使由 `\r` 或 `\u00a0` 构成的重定向目标不会被 `String.prototype.trim()` 吃掉；并把 `hasNonFinalTopLevelBackgroundOperator` 里第二处 `/\s/` 扫描也切到同一判定，使 `echo x >\r& y` 被识别为「重定向 + 后台操作符」，而不是 `>&` 的重复描述符重定向。

`getCommandRoots` 决定 shell 工具要询问哪些子命令、以及读取哪些内容做 git 归因；在那里消失的命令对二者都不可见。对 bash 而言 `echo x >\r& rm -rf /tmp/x` 是两条命令，但切分器只看到一条，于是第二条命令的根从未被提交确认。后台操作符判定受同一误读影响：`\r` 被当空白跳过后，`>\r&` 看起来就是 `>&` 重定向形式，操作符因此未被上报。

验证方式：在 `packages/core` 下运行 `npx vitest run src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts src/permissions/rule-parser.test.ts`。在 `main` 上新增用例失败——`rm` 既不在 `getCommandRoots` 也不在 `splitCommands` 中，且 `hasNonFinalTopLevelBackgroundOperator('echo x >\r& rm -rf /tmp/x')` 返回 `false`；在本分支上它们通过，且原有 CRLF 用例保持绿色。

主要风险：该判定刻意比 `/\s/` 更窄，因此任何依赖切分器把 `\r` / `\v` / `\f` / `\u00a0` 当空白的调用方，现在会得到一次切分。这正是期望行为（bash 就在这里切分），且更窄的分隔符集合只会增加切分，绝不会把两条命令并成一条。

破坏性变更：无。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): browse managed auto-memory in /memory (listing, read, toggles)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The web-shell /memory panel gains a third tab, "Auto memory", that browses the managed auto-memory store: entries are listed grouped by scope (project scope under the workspace's managed memory root — `<memory-base>/projects/<workspace>/memory/`, or `<workspace>/.qwen/memory` with `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_LOCAL=1` — and user scope under `<memory-base>/memories/`; the daemon reports the resolved directories in `projectDir`/`userDir`) with title, description, and size, and selecting an entry reads its content through the daemon with a 1 MiB read cap and an explicit truncation flag. The tab also exposes the managed settings `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` and `memory.enableManagedAutoDream` as toggles (written to user scope), and on a local daemon advertising the `workspace_local_open` capability a per-scope "Open folder" button opens the scope's directory on the daemon host.

On the daemon side this adds `GET /workspace/auto-memory` and `GET /workspace/auto-memory/file?path=...` (the file route re-validates the requested path against the two managed roots server-side, symlink-canonicalized, before opening it; failures map to typed statuses: 400 outside/non-regular, 404 missing, 403 untrusted workspace), exposed over ACP as `_qwen/workspace/auto-memory` and `_qwen/workspace/auto-memory/file`. The SDK gains `DaemonClient.workspaceAutoMemory()`, `workspaceAutoMemoryFile(path)`, and `openAutoMemoryFolderLocally(scope)`; the web shell gains the `useDaemonAutoMemory` hook, the `AutoMemoryPanel` component, and the new tab in `MemoryMessage`. i18n adds the needed en/zh-CN strings and removes the now-unused "not available yet" placeholders.

## Why it's needed

Issue #13396: the web-shell /memory panel did not render managed auto-memory at all — the folder entry and the auto-memory/auto-dream toggles were dead ends labeled "not available from web-shell yet". Desktop and web-shell users have no TUI, so the memory panel is their only place to inspect what the agent has remembered or to switch memory capture on and off.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `pnpm install`, then start the development daemon and web shell (repo `dev` script) for a workspace that already has auto-memory entries, or create one under the project's managed memory directory (e.g. `<workspace>/.qwen/memory/` with `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_LOCAL=1`).
2. Run `/memory` in the web shell — the panel now has three tabs: Project, User, and the new "Auto memory".
3. In the Auto memory tab: expect entries grouped under "Project memory" / "User memory" with per-scope file count and total size; click an entry to see its content; a file over 1 MiB shows the truncation notice instead of failing; the toggles reflect the effective settings and persist to user scope when flipped.
4. On a local daemon advertising `workspace_local_open`, an "Open folder" button appears per scope; on a remote daemon it is hidden.
5. Web-shell unit tests (from `packages/web-shell`): `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/components/messages/AutoMemoryPanel.test.tsx client/components/messages/MemoryMessage.test.tsx client/daemon/workspace/hooks/useDaemonAutoMemory.test.tsx` → 24/24 pass.
6. Daemon unit tests (from `packages/cli`): `npx vitest run src/serve/workspace-auto-memory.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-local-open.test.ts` → the new suites pin the read boundary (outside-root refusal, symlink escape, missing file, 1 MiB truncation, torn read, untrusted-workspace fail-closed, relative-path refusal) and the folder-open target (200 with scope, 404 missing dir, 400 non-directory).
7. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `prettier --experimental-cli --check` are clean for the touched packages in the same environment.

### Evidence (Before & After)

No live-session screenshots in this verification pass (unit/type/format checks ran in a one-off Docker container; interactive before/after screenshots can follow if maintainers want them). Before: the /memory panel had no auto-memory section at all — the "not available from web-shell yet" placeholder strings were the only trace. After: the Auto memory tab described above; behavior is covered by 45 unit tests — 24 web-shell (panel rendering, reads including truncation and 404, toggle persistence and error notices, folder-button gating, tab switching) and 21 daemon-side (path confinement, read contract, listing, HTTP status mapping, folder-open target, relative-path refusal).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment

One-off `node:22-bookworm` Docker container with a full pnpm workspace install (unit tests, `tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check`). No live Desktop/daemon session was driven as part of this PR's verification.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the file-read route accepts an arbitrary `path` query, so it re-validates the resolved path against the two managed roots on the server (symlink-canonicalized) before opening it — outside-root and symlink-escape reads are refused (400), missing files 404, and anything outside a trusted workspace 403 (fail-closed). This boundary is now pinned by daemon unit tests. Content reads are capped at 1 MiB with a `truncated` flag rather than failing. The panel is read-only for entries (no write/delete UI), and the toggles only write user-scope settings.
- Not validated / out of scope: no interactive live-session run (macOS/Windows ⚠️); "Open folder" relies on the existing `workspace_local_open` daemon flow and is unit-tested with mocks only; no write/edit UI for auto-memory files. The read-contract helpers (BOM detection, no-follow open, torn-read refusal) are shared with, but separately implemented next to, the explicit memory route — extending the existing module instead was considered, but the two stores have different root semantics (workspace-qualified vs user-global), which the tests pin on both sides.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — additive routes, SDK methods, and i18n keys; the removed i18n keys had no remaining references in web-shell.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13396

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Web Shell 的 /memory 面板新增第三个选项卡「Auto memory（自动记忆）」，用于浏览托管的 auto-memory 存储：条目按作用域分组列出（项目作用域位于该 workspace 的托管内存根目录——`<memory-base>/projects/<workspace>/memory/`，或在 `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_LOCAL=1` 时为 `<workspace>/.qwen/memory`——用户作用域位于 `<memory-base>/memories/`；daemon 在 `projectDir`/`userDir` 中报告解析后的目录），显示标题、描述和大小；点击条目时通过 daemon 读取其内容，读取上限 1 MiB，超出时显式标记截断。该选项卡同时以开关形式暴露两个托管设置 `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` 与 `memory.enableManagedAutoDream`（写入用户作用域）；在声明了 `workspace_local_open` 能力的本地 daemon 上，每个作用域还有一个「打开文件夹」按钮，用于在 daemon 所在主机上打开对应目录。

Daemon 侧新增了 `GET /workspace/auto-memory` 与 `GET /workspace/auto-memory/file?path=...`（文件路由在打开前会在服务端把请求路径做符号链接规范化后重新校验到两个托管根目录之内；失败映射为类型化状态：400 越界/非普通文件、404 不存在、403 未受信 workspace），并通过 ACP 以 `_qwen/workspace/auto-memory` 与 `_qwen/workspace/auto-memory/file` 暴露。SDK 新增 `DaemonClient.workspaceAutoMemory()`、`workspaceAutoMemoryFile(path)` 与 `openAutoMemoryFolderLocally(scope)`；Web Shell 新增 `useDaemonAutoMemory` hook、`AutoMemoryPanel` 组件以及 `MemoryMessage` 中的新选项卡。i18n 补齐了所需的 en/zh-CN 文案，并移除了不再使用的「尚不可用」占位键。

## 为什么需要

Issue #13396：Web Shell 的 /memory 面板此前完全不渲染托管 auto-memory——文件夹入口和 auto-memory/auto-dream 开关都是写着「web-shell 暂不可用」的死胡同。Desktop 与 Web Shell 用户没有 TUI，内存面板是他们查看代理记了什么、或开关记忆捕获的唯一入口。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. `pnpm install` 后，用仓库的 `dev` 脚本启动开发态 daemon 与 Web Shell，workspace 需已有 auto-memory 条目（或自行在项目托管内存目录下创建，例如 `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_LOCAL=1` 时的 `<workspace>/.qwen/memory/`）。
2. 在 Web Shell 中运行 `/memory`——面板现在有三个选项卡：Project、User，以及新增的「Auto memory」。
3. 在 Auto memory 选项卡中：条目应分组显示在「Project memory」「User memory」之下，并显示每个作用域的文件数与总大小；点击条目可查看内容；超过 1 MiB 的文件显示截断提示而不是报错；开关反映当前生效的设置值，切换后持久化到用户作用域。
4. 在声明了 `workspace_local_open` 能力的本地 daemon 上，每个作用域出现「打开文件夹」按钮；远程 daemon 上隐藏。
5. Web Shell 单元测试（在 `packages/web-shell` 下运行）：`npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/components/messages/AutoMemoryPanel.test.tsx client/components/messages/MemoryMessage.test.tsx client/daemon/workspace/hooks/useDaemonAutoMemory.test.tsx` → 24/24 通过。
6. Daemon 单元测试（在 `packages/cli` 下运行）：`npx vitest run src/serve/workspace-auto-memory.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-local-open.test.ts` → 新增用例钉住读取边界（越界拒绝、符号链接逃逸、文件缺失、1 MiB 截断、torn read、未受信 workspace fail-closed、相对路径拒绝）与打开文件夹目标（200 带 scope、404 目录缺失、400 非目录）。
7. 同一环境下 `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` 与 `prettier --experimental-cli --check` 对所涉包均干净。

### 证据（前后对比）

本次验证不包含真实会话截图（单测/类型/格式检查在一次性 Docker 容器内完成；如维护者需要交互式前后截图，可后续补充）。之前：/memory 面板完全没有 auto-memory 部分——只有「web-shell 暂不可用」的占位文案。之后：即上文所述的 Auto memory 选项卡；行为由 45 个单元测试覆盖——24 个 Web Shell（面板渲染、含截断与 404 的读取、开关持久化与错误提示、打开文件夹的显隐、选项卡切换）+ 21 个 Daemon 侧（路径收敛、读取契约、列表、HTTP 状态映射、打开文件夹目标、相对路径拒绝）。

### 测试平台

|     操作系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境

一次性 `node:22-bookworm` Docker 容器，完整 pnpm workspace 安装（单元测试、`tsc --noEmit`、`prettier --check`）。本次 PR 验证未驱动真实的 Desktop/daemon 会话。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：文件读取路由接受任意 `path` 查询参数，因此在打开文件前会在服务端把解析后的路径（符号链接规范化）重新校验到两个托管根目录之内——越界与符号链接逃逸的读取一律拒绝（400），文件缺失 404，未受信 workspace 403（fail-closed）。该边界现由 daemon 单元测试钉住。内容读取以 1 MiB 为上限并以 `truncated` 标记截断，而不是直接失败。面板对条目只读（无写入/删除 UI），开关只写用户作用域设置。
- 未验证/范围之外：未做交互式真实会话验证（macOS/Windows ⚠️）；「打开文件夹」依赖既有的 `workspace_local_open` daemon 流程，仅用 mock 做了单元测试；不提供 auto-memory 文件的写入/编辑 UI。读取契约辅助函数（BOM 检测、no-follow 打开、torn read 拒绝）与显式 memory 路由共享同一契约但为独立实现——曾考虑扩展既有模块，但两个存储的根语义不同（workspace 限定 vs 用户全局），两侧均已有测试钉住。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无——路由、SDK 方法与 i18n 键均为新增；被移除的 i18n 键在 web-shell 中已无引用。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #13396

</details>

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): simplify existing local project onboarding
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Trusted single-user local deployments can choose an existing project directly from the Workspace menu. The service automatically registers a suitable parent outside Git worktrees, grants the importing actor OWNER access, and starts sessions in the selected project. Existing owned storage is reused, including while another session holds it. Imports retain durable identity checks and replay safely after an uncertain response or restart.

The composer uses the persisted working directory automatically. Working directory, Refresh, and pagination now live in the Workspace menu, removing the separate relative-directory section while preserving drafts and model selections.

## Why it's needed

Opening an existing local project currently requires manual parent registration and a separate grant before directory selection becomes usable. The additional relative-directory controls repeat internal storage layout in the main composer. This change makes local onboarding a single directory-selection flow while retaining the existing storage and actor authority.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Enable local directory import on a loopback single-user deployment with trusted actor authentication, Workspace files, durable local execution, and verified recovery. Starting with no registered Workspace, open **Workspace → Choose existing directory** and select an existing Git project. Expect automatic OWNER access and sessions starting in that project, with existing files unchanged and the registration marker outside the worktree.
2. Cancel directory selection and confirm that no Workspace is created and the draft/model stay unchanged. Import successfully, then change the working directory through the menu; Cancel should discard edits and Save should affect the next session.
3. Retry an import after its response is lost. Expect the same request/key and a single logical Workspace. Import another project under the same parent during an active session; expect storage reuse without interrupting that session.
4. Restart with new imports disabled. Existing imported Workspaces and file access should remain usable, while new imports are refused. Invalid/private directories, foreign markers, revoked grants, and mixed request fields must not create new authority. Deployments without the local capability retain their authorized-directory flow.

### Evidence (Before & After)

**Before:** existing-directory selection requires an authorized parent Workspace, and the composer displays a separate relative-directory section. **After:** a fresh local actor can browse/import directly; the composer uses the project default and exposes optional directory editing in its menu. Independent native macOS checks covered real file queries and model `read_file`, active-parent reuse, lost-response retry, restart, and desktop/mobile browsers at 1280px and 390px. A separate PR comment records test commands, results, and limitations.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ Native API, model tools, browser and restart checks |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ Native execution not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22, JDK 21, MySQL 8.4, local Java Broker and built Hosted Harness, Chromium desktop/mobile viewports. Native acceptance used an isolated database and private Runtime state with no pre-registered storage.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: local import is an explicit, default-off single-user host capability. It requires a loopback OPEN listener and trusted actor header; the registered parent shares file scope and a physical-owner lease across projects and is not a filesystem sandbox.
- Not validated / out of scope: native Linux/Windows execution, whole-host reboot, SSH onboarding, and shared remote deployment changes. The initial full Java suite was interrupted after an existing short-lease test failed; that case passed in focused reruns, and affected Java/MySQL checks passed. The full suite is not claimed green.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no SQL migration. Imported-root receipts require compatible Java readers; ordinary creation receipts omit the unused field and remain readable by previous versions. Turning off new imports preserves existing imported roots.

Designs: [local import — English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-local-directory-import.md), [本机导入 — 中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-local-directory-import.zh-CN.md); [directory selection — English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-16-managed-workspace-directory-selection.md), [目录选择 — 中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-16-managed-workspace-directory-selection.zh-CN.md). Both language pairs include matching decisions, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## What this PR does

受信任的本机单用户部署可以直接从 Workspace 菜单选择已有项目。服务自动登记 Git 工作树之外的合适父目录，授予导入者 OWNER 权限，并在所选项目内启动会话。已有自有存储会直接复用，包括另一会话仍占用它的情况。导入保留持久化身份验证，并支持响应不确定或重启后的安全重放。

输入框自动使用持久化的工作目录。“工作目录”、“刷新”和分页入口移入 Workspace 菜单，移除单独的相对目录区域，同时保留草稿和模型选择。

## Why it's needed

目前打开已有本机项目，需要先手工登记父目录，再单独授权，才能使用目录选择。额外的相对目录控件又在主输入区重复展示内部存储布局。此改动将本机接入简化为一次目录选择，同时保留现有存储和 actor 权限边界。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. 在回环监听的本机单用户部署中启用本机目录导入，同时启用受信任 actor 认证、Workspace 文件、持久化本机执行及验证恢复。从没有登记 Workspace 的状态打开“Workspace → 选择已有目录”，选择已有 Git 项目。预期自动获得 OWNER 权限，会话从项目内启动，已有文件保持原样，登记标记位于工作树之外。
2. 取消目录选择，确认没有创建 Workspace，草稿和模型不变。成功导入后通过菜单修改工作目录；取消应丢弃编辑，保存应作用于下一次会话创建。
3. 模拟导入响应丢失后重试，预期使用相同请求和 key，并只生成一个逻辑 Workspace。在会话运行期间导入同一父目录下的另一个项目，预期复用存储且不中断已有会话。
4. 关闭新增导入后重启，已有导入 Workspace 和文件访问应继续可用，新导入应被拒绝。非法或私有目录、外来标记、已撤销授权及混合请求字段都不得产生新权限。未启用本机能力的部署保留现有授权目录流程。

### Evidence (Before & After)

**修改前：** 选择已有目录要求先有获授权的父 Workspace，输入框另有一块相对目录区域。**修改后：** 全新本机 actor 可直接浏览并导入目录；输入框使用项目默认目录，可从菜单按需修改。独立原生 macOS 验收覆盖真实文件查询、模型 `read_file`、运行中父目录复用、响应丢失重试、重启，以及 1280px 桌面和 390px 手机宽度浏览器。测试命令、结果及限制单独记录在 PR 评论中。

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ 原生 API、模型工具、浏览器和重启验收 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ 本地未验收原生执行 |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22、JDK 21、MySQL 8.4、本机 Java Broker 和已构建 Hosted Harness，以及 Chromium 桌面/手机视口。原生验收使用独立数据库及私有 Runtime 状态，未预登记存储。

## Risk & Scope

- 主要风险或取舍：本机导入是显式启用、默认关闭的单用户主机能力，要求回环 OPEN 监听和受信任 actor 头。登记的父目录在项目间共享文件范围和物理 owner 租约，不构成文件系统沙箱。
- 未验证或范围外：原生 Linux/Windows 执行、整机重启、SSH 接入，以及共享远程部署改动。首次 Java 全量运行在一个既有短租约测试失败后被中断；该用例专项重跑通过，受影响 Java/MySQL 检查通过，不声称全量测试全绿。
- 兼容性或迁移：不需要 SQL 迁移。导入根回执要求兼容的 Java 读取端；普通创建回执省略未使用字段，继续支持旧版本读取。关闭新增导入不会停用已有导入根。

设计文档：[本机导入英文版](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-local-directory-import.md)、[本机导入中文版](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-local-directory-import.zh-CN.md)；[目录选择英文版](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-16-managed-workspace-directory-selection.md)、[目录选择中文版](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4dbe62d4cee855ccfeaf3c7ab835448f6699b475/docs/design/2026-10-16-managed-workspace-directory-selection.zh-CN.md)。两组中英文文档的设计决策、约束和验收标准保持一致。

## Linked Issues

无。

</details>

issues.title: A saved session document larger than 8 MiB can no longer be resumed or forked, and the refusal names no remedy — the journal is what pushes it over
issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed for: `"transport bound"`, `"exceeds full-history"`,
session document size limit, resume + size, journal + resume. Closest matches:

- **#6842** (open) — the session journal has no bound and grows without limit.
  That is the growth side of the same structure; this report is the *access*
  side: once the file crosses a hard 8 MiB transport bound, the session can no
  longer be opened at all.
- **#6688** (closed) — same class (an oversized input is refused before anything
  runs), different path (`exec` argv vs the session document).
- #6161, #6175, #6361 — unrelated changes that only matched the search terms.

# What happened?

```
$ codewhale resume 481c2659-…
error: selected saved history could not be captured; no mutation attempted
  caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The source is retained (good), but there is no way forward. `codewhale fork`
refuses the same way, and I could not find any CLI path that reduces a saved
document: `codewhale --help` lists no prune/compact command, and `codewhale thread`
offers only list/read/resume/fork/archive/set-name/clear-name. The message does
not name the size, the field that dominates it, or any remedy.

Measured on the affected session (the file is 13 982 336 bytes against an 8 MiB
bound, i.e. 8 388 608 bytes):

| part of the document | size (approx, as serialized in the file) |
|---|---|
| whole file | 13.98 MB |
| `journal.entries` (3870 entries) | 8.96 MB |
| `messages` (1361 messages) | 2.96 MB |
| `work_state` / `metadata` | 0.38 MB / 0.13 MB |

The conversation itself is well inside the bound. Only the 1361 journal entries
on the active leaf path are projected into messages
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:262`, `:329`); the remaining 2509 entries
are abandoned branches — yet the whole document has to fit.

# Steps to reproduce

The check is a plain file-size comparison, so any saved document over the bound
reproduces it deterministically; I did not build a synthetic one, my numbers are
from a real session (a long session with heavy sub-agent use, which is what grows
the journal — see #6842).

1. `stat -c%s ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json` — compare against 8 388 608.
2. `codewhale resume <id>` (and `codewhale fork <id>`) → the error above.

Code path, read from `main`:

- `prepare_mounted_session` reads the source with
  `load_session_snapshot_bounded(&id, MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES)`
  (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:9943`). Every `codewhale resume` goes through this
  (`run_interactive_with_notice`).
- The read refuses before parsing when the *file* is larger than the limit:
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3406`
  ("session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained").
- `MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`
  (`crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:79`; the entry-count sibling is at `:78`).
- The same constant bounds the serialized mutation request, which embeds the
  whole document as JSON: `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:221` —
  so raising only the read would not be enough; the transport itself is bounded.

Recovery that worked by hand (and is what a supported path would need to do):
keeping only the active leaf path in `journal.entries` took the file from
13.98 MB to 7.61 MB and the session resumed. It costs the abandoned branches'
structure (`/branch` history), which is why it should be an explicit,
maintainer-designed operation rather than a user's manual surgery. The same
operation is not the only lever — any bound change has to keep the request under
the same limit, because the document travels inside it.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
today (`MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES` is unchanged).

# Where did it happen?

- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Impact: the session is readable in files but unreachable from the product; the
only routes left are manual surgery on the JSON or discarding the session.

Options as I see them (maintainer's call):

- **A. Transport only what the operation needs.** The canonical handoff needs
  the messages, the journal witness (leaf + entry count) and the metadata; the
  journal body is copied only because the target document is the source document.
  A host-side rebuild of the target document would remove the journal from the
  payload entirely.
- **B. Make the bound count the projected history, not the file**, or expose it
  as a bounded, documented knob. `messages` here was 2.96 MB of a 13.98 MB file.
- **C. Keep the bound and make the failure actionable**: name the size and the
  dominant field, and provide a supported prune/compact command that drops
  journal entries outside the active path (with a dry run and a backup), so an
  oversized session is recoverable. Also worth a pointer to #6842.

Open questions: is 8 MiB a memory/allocation guard or an API payload guard? Should
a journal that is not projected into messages count against it at all? What is a
user expected to do today when a session crosses it — is discarding the session
the intended outcome?

Verification (for A/B/C, once the direction is chosen):

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs
```

Out of scope:

- Bounding the journal itself (#6842).
- Changing the conversation, or auto-truncating history on resume.

issues.title: 0.10.2: every Bash/shell operation Codewhale starts or tracks is inspectable and stoppable

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: ux
labels.description: User experience, interaction, or presentation polish

labels.name: v0.10.2
labels.description: Targeting v0.10.2

issues.body:
## Problem (user report against 0.10.1 and the 0.10.2 candidate)

With many successful `run` cards, a long completed output collapses to `N lines omitted ⌥V:output`. A still-running silent recursive search shows `run running · stale · no output 2m 07s`. After newer cards arrive, the user cannot reliably open the operation that is still running, or the exact completed call they picked. Whether the control is unreachable, selects the wrong operation, shows only a snapshot, or loses the record has not been established. Reproducing that is the first step.

## Scope

Every shell route Codewhale starts or tracks in a session, using the existing tool-call, job, session and agent identifiers:

* foreground Bash / `run` (the visible label is not the backend identity; inventory the real tool names and aliases first)
* commands moved to the background, and commands started in the background
* named PTY / terminal sessions
* shell work owned by delegated agents

States where supported: queued or waiting, running with output, running silent, completed, failed, cancelled, refused.

## Acceptance

1. Option+V / Alt+V and mouse click open the exact operation, including while a silent command runs and newer cards arrive. A new card never takes over the target.
2. The inspector shows the full command and working directory (existing redaction rules), owning agent, truthful state, elapsed time, last output, retained stdout/stderr and exit result when known. Silent running work says "no output yet". Silence is never shown as failed, completed or hung.
3. Expanding a grouped success card exposes each constituent call.
4. Refresh uses authoritative events or bounded reads, without consuming the model's output cursor. Follow mode stops when the user scrolls back. Scroll and copy work. Esc restores the composer draft, scroll position and selection.
5. Stop or cancel acts only on the selected live operation, under the existing ownership and authorization checks. Closing the inspector or moving on in the conversation never stops a process. Inapplicable controls are disabled.
6. Compact default presentation, plus a reachable list of current work.
7. Proof: focused tests with real nonzero counts, and controlled PTY journeys on the installed candidate at normal and narrow sizes. Local tests alone do not establish the interaction.

## Relation to existing issues

* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6912 (GitHub #6912): PTY Terminal view in the work dock. Covers PTY sessions only.
* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6909 (GitHub #6909): detach a blocked shell wait with Ctrl+B or steering. Already in the local 0.10.2 line.
* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6899 (GitHub #6899): one terminal board with approve, reply and attach. v0.11, not required for 0.10.2.
* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6436: optional running-command line on foreground shell cards.

This issue is the bounded 0.10.2 inspection requirement. It must not add a second task store or execution loop.

## Status

Filed 2026-10-09 during the 0.10.2 takeover. No implementation and no code claim yet. Candidate paths, to be claimed exactly before any edit: crates/tui/src/tui/ui/activity_detail.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/mouse_ui.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/work_surface/{model,input,interaction}.rs, crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/jobs.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/ui/handlers.rs, crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs, crates/tui/src/tools/terminal_session.rs.

issues.title: codewhale resume refuses any session whose saved history still holds a raw sub-agent handoff — the canonical acknowledgement compares the Engine-restored messages with the saved document
issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed in this repository: `"mailbox acknowledgement"` → 0,
`"selected saved history"` → 0, `"exceeds full-history"` → 0, `"retained outcome"`
→ 6 unrelated results (release and PR titles). Closest reports, each a different
mechanism: #6102 (closed — resume failed with ENOENT while resolving the runtime
store dir), #6225 (closed) and #6418 (closed) — older "cannot restore/resume"
reports. None of them mention this comparison.

# What happened?

`codewhale resume <id>` fails deterministically for a saved session, and no
retry or recovery route works:

```
$ codewhale resume f5ba9347-…
error: canonical history operation mounted-history:48204ec8-…; retained outcome must be recovered using this exact key
  caused by: canonical history mailbox acknowledgement changed
```

Expected: the session resumes. The suggested recovery ("retained outcome must be
recovered using this exact key") cannot succeed, because the recovery path runs
the same acknowledgement: `settle_prepared_history_operation` also calls
`synchronize_history_operation` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1032`;
the fresh path is `:1663`).

# Steps to reproduce

1. In a project, run `codewhale` and have the session spawn a sub-agent (the
   `agent` tool) so a `subagent_completion` handoff is appended to the live
   history. Let the turn end and quit.
2. Confirm the saved document still holds the RAW envelope: the message has
   exactly two text blocks, block 2 is exactly
   `<turn_meta>\nInput provenance: subagent_handoff (non-authoritative)\n</turn_meta>`
   and block 1 starts with `<codewhale:runtime_event kind="subagent_completion"
   visibility="internal">` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:15`).
3. `codewhale resume <id>` → the error above.

Observed on a 351-message, 3.97 MB session with 5 such envelopes: every attempt
failed. After neutralising the recognition of those 5 messages in the saved data
(renaming the transport tag so the restore projection becomes a no-op), the same
command resumed normally and printed `Resumed session: …`.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
(today): `synchronize_history_operation` is unchanged at
`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`.

# Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Written from reading `main` (not a guess at the cause):

- `RuntimeThreadManager::synchronize_history_operation`
  (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:11684`) sends `Op::SyncSession` and then
  requires `observed.messages == session.messages` (`:11708`-`:11713`), i.e. the
  Engine's post-restore messages must equal the saved document byte for byte.
- The Engine's restore first replaces every live sub-agent handoff with a
  restored checkpoint: `Engine::restore_session_history`
  (`crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:2931`) calls
  `runtime_handoff::project_owned_messages_for_restore`
  (`:2959` → `crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:918`,
  rewrite decision in `rewrite_message_for_restore`, `:927`, recognition in
  `raw_runtime_handoff_text`, `:1042`).
- So the two sides are structurally different objects whenever the saved
  document still holds a raw envelope, and the equality can never hold. The
  document only becomes "projected" after a *successful* restore persists it,
  which is exactly the step this check forbids — the first canonical resume of a
  session that used sub-agents is the failing case.

Suggested fix directions (maintainer's call):

- **A. Make the acknowledgement projection-aware.** Compare against
  `project_owned_messages_for_restore(session.messages.clone())` (plus the
  compaction checkpoint step `compaction::restore_compaction_checkpoint`, to
  mirror `restore_session_history` exactly). The same codebase already does this
  for the sibling rollback check: `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:1406` projects
  `.messages` before demanding that the Engine acknowledged them.
- **B. Persist the projected form** so a saved document is always in the form a
  restore produces (bigger change; it would drop raw envelopes from saved
  sessions earlier than today).

Related, found while recovering this session: a refused canonical attempt still
publishes a holder thread plus an uncommitted turn operation in the Runtime
store. Once the document is repaired, the next attempt then stalls on the holder
checkpoint (`saved holder checkpoint differs from the saved history; refresh
history`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1255`) and, with the
checkpoint refreshed, on `saved holder has a successor outside the selected
document` (`:1281`) — the holder fingerprints the pre-repair bytes. A refused
attempt could avoid publishing a holder, or the repair path could refresh it.

Done when:

- [ ] a saved session whose history still contains a raw `subagent_completion`
      (or `subagent_failed` / `waiting_for_subagents` / `agent_topology`)
      envelope resumes through the canonical path;
- [ ] `codewhale fork` works for the same session;
- [ ] the acknowledgement still refuses a genuinely changed history (an Engine
      that did not install the document), i.e. the check is not simply removed;
- [ ] a regression test in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` (`mod mounted_history_tests`)
      saves a fixture session containing one raw handoff envelope and asserts the
      mounted resume succeeds.

Verification:

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/lib.rs mounted_history_tests::
```

Out of scope:

- The sub-agent handoff wire format and the restore rendering itself.
- The size bound on the saved document (separate report).

issues.title: Windows runtime floor blocks read-only piped commands under Full Access, on a native (non-npm) install

labels.name: windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

## Summary

Follow-up to #6827. The Windows runtime floor (`SessionRuntimeRisk`, `crates/tui/src/core/authority/auto_review.rs`) refuses ordinary read-only commands that pipe test output, with `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation`. It does this while the session shows **Full Access**, although the floor's own test says Full Access skips it.

Refused:

```
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\runner -q --tb=line 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 6
cd C:\Users\me\repo\apps\extension; node .\node_modules\vitest\vitest.mjs run 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 30
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe format .; Write-Output "fmt=$LASTEXITCODE"; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\e2e --collect-only -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3
```

Every refusal reads:

> Built-in safety gate requires approval: Windows command input cannot be classified safely enough to exclude termination of Codewhale npm launchers; use a direct PID- or port-specific command.

The same commands without `2>&1 | Select-Object ...` run fine. None of them stops a process.

## Two problems

1. **Full Access does not skip the floor.** `windows_runtime_floor_holds_across_reviewing_postures_but_skips_full_access` (around line 2104) asserts that under `ApprovalMode::Bypass` "Full Access skips the platform hold with the rest of the floor". The TUI status bar shows `Full Access` and `operate`, and the operator and its Fleet sub-agents are still blocked. Either the operate/Fleet posture does not carry `Bypass` into tool review, or sub-agents get a different `ApprovalMode`.
2. **Unparseable means blocked, even for read-only pipelines.** When `command_invocations(command)` returns `None`, `windows_session_runtime_risk_scoped` returns `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation` (around line 1371). A pipeline into a read-only cmdlet (`Select-Object`, `Select-String`, `Where-Object`, `Format-*`, `Out-String`, `Measure-Object`) with `2>&1` cannot terminate anything, but it is held. Agents use this pattern constantly to trim test output.

3. **The npm-launcher hold fires on a non-npm install.** This machine uses the native installer, so there is no `node.exe` launcher in Codewhale's process tree. Yet the hold's reason is "termination of Codewhale npm launchers". `windows_tool_runtime_risk` does not check the install method, so the floor applies to every Windows install. #6906 already detects npm installs with `codewhale_release::current_install_method()`, and the same check could scope this hold. (A broad `node.exe` kill could still hit *another* npm-launched session on the same machine. That is a narrower risk, and it does not apply to read-only pipelines either way.)

## Impact

In one Fleet run of about 70 minutes (DeepSeek V4 Flash, about 8 workers), one implement sub-agent had 12 refused or failed tool calls out of about 60. 4 were this gate; each refusal costs a model turn while the agent re-plans. The operator hit it repeatedly as well. It is avoidable: the agent can drop the pipe. But every model reaches for this pattern first, so it fails again and again.

## Expected

- Under Full Access, the floor does not apply, as the existing test asserts. Or, if the floor is meant to apply under Full Access in operate/Fleet mode, the test and the docs should say so.
- A pipeline whose stages are all known read-only cmdlets, with stream redirection like `2>&1`, is classified as non-terminating rather than unclassified.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Windows 11, Codewhale from the native Windows installer (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin\codewhale.exe`, launched through `codewhale.bat`; **not** npm), started from PowerShell in Windows Terminal.
2. Select Full Access and run in operate mode, with Fleet sub-agents.
3. Have the agent run: `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5` (any command, piped into `Select-Object`).
4. It is refused with the message above. Without `2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5`, it runs.

### Codewhale version 版本

codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Windows

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

GitHub Releases download (native Windows installer)

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek / deepseek-v4-flash

### Terminal and shell 终端

Windows Terminal + PowerShell 5.1

### codewhale doctor (optional)

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

- Evidence: `.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.json`, worker events marked `refused or failed`, and checkpoint tool results carrying the safety-gate text.
- Related: #6827 (the original gate), #6906 (agent environment line for the npm launcher), #6011 (tool-call error diagnostics).
- I am happy to send a PR for part 2 (read-only pipeline classification) once the intended Full Access behaviour in part 1 is confirmed.

issues.body:
**Title:** `Widen the 300s browser-callback windows on MCP OAuth and provider PKCE sign-in`

**Body:**

## Problem

Two human-in-the-loop auth waits are hard-capped at 300 seconds, and both are walls the user has to climb with a browser in their hand:

* MCP OAuth browser callback: `crates/tui/src/mcp/oauth.rs` wraps the callback wait in `timeout(Duration::from_secs(300), ...)` (\~line 1719 on current main).
* Provider sign-in (PKCE) callback: `crates/tui/src/oauth.rs` sets `CALLBACK_TIMEOUT = 300s` (\~line 1361).

Five minutes is tight for the flows these windows actually gate: the user must switch to a browser, authenticate through an IdP (SSO with 2FA is common), possibly fetch a code from email or an authenticator, and come back — sometimes across a device→phone handoff. When the window fires, the sign-in aborts and the user has to start over; on slow corporate SSO this reproduces reliably.

## Proposal

Raise both callback windows to 900s, keeping the existing cancellation paths unchanged (a user-initiated cancel still aborts the wait immediately). This is the smallest change that removes the failure mode; a config knob would also work but adds surface for little gain.

## Why an issue first

This touches auth/credential flows, which the contribution guide flags as a trust-boundary surface best discussed before a PR. Happy to send the two-line change with tests once there's a nod here, or to fold it into whatever direction maintainers prefer (e.g. config-driven windows).

## Context

Comes from the same fork-side timeout audit that already landed upstream as [#6740](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6740>)–[#6744](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6744>) (idle watchdog, MCP `tools/call` budget, vision envelope, js child kill, submission-id echo); the audit's remaining auth-adjacent surfaces were held back for exactly this discussion. Reference implementation: Pinvou/CodeWhale commit `d349f2537` (audit surfaces 14–15: OAuth callback 300s→900s, PKCE callback 300s→900s).

### 0.10.2 source-freeze preparation — 2026-10-08

Owner: Codex subagent core_next_slice under release integrator. Artifact-only packet; no shared source, HEAD, Cargo, push, provider call, or publication changes during freeze. Declared future application paths: `crates/tui/src/mcp/oauth.rs`, `crates/tui/src/oauth.rs`, `crates/tui/src/mcp/tests.rs` (widen the actual callback waits 300→900s and synchronize existing help-text assertion). Preserve existing callback state/issuer/path validation and MCP cancellation/drop ownership. Inspect existing timeout/cancellation tests before adding targeted cases. Reference commit verified through live GitHub: `Pinvou/CodeWhale@d349f253704e9fdfa03241599af077b787ae3ded`, author @asto18089 [asto18089@126.com](<mailto:asto18089@126.com>), committer GitHub/web-flow. Preserve contributor credit for adopted OAuth changes. Parent reviews and applies; no claim of compiled/tested code yet.

Artifact packet prepared and handed to release integrator: `artifacts/takeover-0102-20261007/contributor-review/6865/ready.patch` (three claimed files; +7/-5). Patch [SHA-256](https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-256/practice-targets-pick-note-set-per-instrument-show-current-target-note) `ced466ffeef6ea3725a3582dfe33d3390183d97255626aff0cfaf9d0694f23e5`; source/proposal hashes, reference commit authorship and OAuth-only original diff, review notes and focused test selectors accompany it. Both actual waits widen to 900s and MCP help text matches. Existing MCP cancellation/drop, fixed-port release, callback lock-release, provider state and issuer/client validation are retained; no new timer framework/test seam just for literal constants. Important evidence boundary: the provider polling function currently has no CancellationToken; this patch preserves that behavior and does not claim new immediate provider-cancel support. Contributor credit verified as `Co-authored-by: asto18089 <asto18089@126.com>`. Artifact rustfmt/apply-check passed; no shared source/HEAD changes, Cargo/tests or live provider requests. issues.body:
Hi — Brian from AICraft (the AICraft row in `docs/PROVIDERS.md`). Not asking for anything. Three things we ran into while running the endpoint, all measured on our own traffic. Take whatever's useful.

## 1. A cold model looks broken

First call to a cold model, across three different models: 145s, 105s, 91s. The same three calls once warm: 2s, 0.5s, 0.5s. With the catalog pre-warmed, a full sweep is about 25s.

The gap between those two sets of numbers is what makes this worth writing down. The latency is per-model and it disappears after the first call. Nothing is wrong with the model; it has not been loaded yet.

A client timing out at 60s will report those models as unavailable, and the report will be wrong. Our first probe did exactly that, and we read it as 23 broken models. Raising the probe timeout to 180s or more, and sending one cheap call per model when a provider is selected, removes the problem.

## 2. Listed and callable are two different states

Two entries in our catalog were enabled and visible to users. Every call to them returned 502 for several days. Not intermittently — every call.

Two things made that hard to see. Upstream's message was "resources busy" every time, which reads like a temporary condition; it isn't, when it is the same message on every attempt, because a genuinely busy upstream returns successes in between. And the error text our gateway passed to clients was a generic placeholder, with the original only in the container logs, so from the client side there was nothing to diagnose.

Whether this is fixed on the provider side or the client side, the useful distinction is the same: an entry that is listed is not an entry that works. Only offer one after a probe has succeeded, and drop it if the probe keeps failing.

## 3. A truncated response can report success

We asked for a long code generation with `max_tokens: 16000`. It came back cut off halfway through a file, and `finish_reason` said `stop`, not `length`. Of the 16000 tokens, about 10,900 were reasoning and about 5,100 were output. Raising the cap to 64000 changed nothing.

The same mechanism shows up wherever a reasoning model is used for something small. We had an inline classification step configured at `max_tokens: 50`; reasoning consumed the budget, the content came back empty, and the step degraded quietly instead of failing.

In both cases the response is well-formed and the terminal frame is valid. Only the arithmetic disagrees. A genuine `stop` leaves the budget unfilled, so if `completion_tokens` equals the `max_tokens` that was requested, the response was cut at the ceiling. Retrying does not help, because the same prompt stops at the same token count; that is what distinguishes it from a 502 or a timeout, which are worth retrying.

This is the one of the three with a client-side half, and while writing this I went looking for it in your tree. What I found instead was the two other halves already handled: `error_taxonomy.rs` separates a permission failure from a server error rather than collapsing both into something retryable, and the retry state is keyed per provider, so one route's 429 doesn't stall another. But in the streaming path I could not find anything that compares the reported `completion_tokens` against the ceiling the request asked for, and `finish_reason` is checked only for being non-empty. That is the right test for whether a stream ended cleanly, and the wrong one for whether the model finished its answer. `tools/truncate.rs` shows you already have the instinct for this on tool results — it stamps `truncated: true` and names a recovery route — and the same treatment doesn't reach a turn the model stopped short.

If that distinction is deliberate, ignore this part; I only had the source to go on.

issues.body:
## Summary

I need a way to run CodeWhale **without any sandbox at all** on my own development machine. The kernel-level Seatbelt sandbox is breaking basic shell commands daily, and I've exhausted every workaround.

## Two Sandbox Layers

CodeWhale has two layers:

1. **Internal sandbox** (`--sandbox-mode`) — controllable via config, I have it set to `danger-full-access`
2. **macOS Seatbelt** — kernel-level, compiled into the binary, **not controllable by any config flag**

Layer 2 is the problem. `danger-full-access` bypasses `sandbox-exec` for child processes, but the main TUI process retains Seatbelt restrictions.

## What's Broken (even with danger-full-access)

| Operation | Blocked by |
|-----------|-----------|
| `open -a TextMate file.md` | Seatbelt |
| `ps aux` | Seatbelt |
| `osascript` | Seatbelt |
| `which rsvg-convert` | PATH stripped |
| `git push` | Intermittent |
| `python3.12 script.py` | Intermittent |
| `echo test > ~/Desktop/file` | Seatbelt |
| `find /opt/homebrew` | PATH/Seatbelt |

## Workarounds Tried (all insufficient)

1. `--sandbox-mode danger-full-access` — only affects internal sandbox, not Seatbelt
2. Per-project `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in config.toml — same
3. Rebuilding from source — sandbox baked into build, same behavior
4. Custom `lbl exec` relay (launchd plist → watcher → relay) — works but requires TCC grants, exact bash paths, single-quoting hacks, and breaks on brew upgrades. A Rube Goldberg machine just to run `which convert`.
5. `tasks gate_run` — inconsistent, works for some commands but not general shell
6. `open.txt` trigger + launchd polling — unreliable

## Request

A true zero-sandbox mode. Options, in order of preference:

1. **`--no-sandbox` CLI flag** that strips Seatbelt at runtime
2. **Separate "dev" build** without the Seatbelt entitlement — I'll sign it myself
3. **Entitlements file I can edit** before building from source, with docs
4. **Sanctioned escape hatch** — e.g., `cw exec --unsandboxed` that spawns outside Seatbelt

I'm on my own machine doing local dev. I'll accept any warning, waiver, or "here be dragons" banner. I just need the assistant to stop fighting me at the kernel level.

## Environment

- macOS 15.x, Apple Silicon (M4 Max)
- CodeWhale 0.9.1
- Config: `danger-full-access`, project trusted
- Homebrew tools at `/opt/homebrew/bin`

>
> **What remains**

> - Upstream PR to nexu-io/open-design adding Codewhale to od mcp install (external contact: needs a human to open it)
> - Upstream runtime definition using codewhale exec --output-format stream-json; check model discovery, cancellation and session resume against their adapter contract

>

> - The headless prerequisite the issue asks to audit already exists: codewhale exec --output-format stream-json (crates/cli/src/lib.rs:232 and 244, crates/tui/src/lib.rs:463; documented at docs/AGENT_RUNTIME.md:146 and docs/INSTALL.md:796)
> - Self-serve MCP auth dependency shipped (CHANGELOG.md:2910, #5747)
> - No commit in v0.10.1 history references #5806 (git log v0.10.1 --grep '#5806' is empty)

---

OpenDesign (github.com/nexu-io/open-design, Apache-2.0, 93k★) is an open-source Claude-Design-alternative studio that turns coding-agent CLIs into design engines: prototypes, decks, design systems (DESIGN.md), plugins, HTML/PDF/PPTX/MP4 export. It integrates agents two ways (their `docs/agent-adapters.md`):

1. **MCP path (cheap, mostly docs):** `od mcp install <agent>` writes the agent's MCP config for OD's stdio server (project/design-system/template listing, live file reads). Codewhale's MCP client + self-serve MCP auth (#5747) should already talk to it. Work: verify our side end-to-end, add a docs page (`docs/mcp.md` section or `docs/design.md`) with the manual config while `od mcp install codewhale` doesn't exist, and open a small upstream PR adding Codewhale to their install list.

2. **Native runtime path (upstream PR):** OpenDesign can *launch and stream* supported agents (`apps/daemon/src/runtimes/defs/`): structured streaming, model discovery, cancellation, session resume. A Codewhale runtime definition there makes Codewhale a first-class design engine in their Studio. Requires on our side: a headless/print invocation mode with machine-readable events if `codewhale exec` doesn't already cover it — audit before the PR.

Why bother: it gives Codewhale users a design-studio surface we don't have to build (design systems, deck/prototype templates, artifact preview/export), and it's a distribution channel — their compatibility table lists 26 CLIs and Codewhale isn't on it.

Future design-tooling angle (founder): their DESIGN.md design-system format + design-templates + MCP (agents read live design files) could feed our Tideline/web design work — e.g. the shell canvas round-trip. Any adoption must respect per-directory licenses (their bundled skills carry their own; provenance lives in their `docs/references.md`).

Sequencing: not 0.9.12 scope. After release: (a) verify MCP interop + docs, (b) upstream runtime-def PR, (c) evaluate DESIGN.md for our design pipeline.

> - Tombstone the `daytona` slot and env names in crates/secrets/src/lib.rs; move docs/DAYTONA_CLOUD_DISPATCH.md to a historical note and retire computer/snapshots/cloud-agent.
> - One real end-to-end `codewhale dispatch` run on the current Computer contract with admission, metering, cancellation and failure receipts.
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Legacy launcher is still the production path: `pub struct LiveDaytonaLauncher` at crates/tui/src/cloud_dispatch.rs:1404, trait DaytonaLauncher at cloud_dispatch.rs:1213, impl at cloud_dispatch.rs:1528.
> - Still wired into every caller: crates/cli/src/dispatch.rs:9 and :114, crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/dispatch.rs:8 and :105, crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/jobs.rs:107.
> - Credential slot not tombstoned: DAYTONA_TOKEN_SLOT = "daytona" at crates/secrets/src/lib.rs:48, with DAYTONA_API_KEY and CWC_DAYTONA_TOKEN env names at secrets/src/lib.rs:50-52.
> - docs/DAYTONA_CLOUD_DISPATCH.md and computer/snapshots/cloud-agent/{Dockerfile,README.md} are still present in the v0.10.1 tree (git ls-tree); 65 'daytona' matches remain in cloud_dispatch.rs alone.
> - v0.10.0..v0.10.1 touched cloud_dispatch.rs only for cancel-race and audit fixes (af661abf6e, 430308f624), not for retirement; no commit in history references #5836.

---

## v0.10.0 planning update — 2026-09-19

This remains open. The Engine still wires `LiveDaytonaLauncher` into cloud dispatch; changing the product direction has not removed that runtime path. The provider-specific target in the original proposal below is historical, not a current implementation requirement.

Remaining acceptance is provider-neutral: one shared Engine/control-plane Computer contract; retirement of the legacy launcher and credential slot; fail-closed admission and metering; authenticated private access; cancellation and failure receipts; and a real end-to-end execution.

The reusable image requirements from #5837 are retained here: reproducible pinned Engine images, non-root execution, credentials supplied only through the approved post-create boundary, and real execution receipts. Closing that obsolete image proposal does not mark hosted Computers complete.

---

## Original report (retained for context)

Founder direction 2026-09-02 (TRUTH_LEDGER): Daytona is removed product-wide; AWS Lambda microVMs are the single managed Computer substrate. This issue covers the engine side. The apps-side flip (`MANAGED_SANDBOX_PROVIDER` pin + Daytona retirement) is tracked in the `Hmbown/codewhale-apps` repo.

## Daytona surface in the engine

- `crates/tui/src/cloud_dispatch.rs` — `LiveDaytonaLauncher::create_sandbox` (HTTP `POST {DAYTONA_API}/sandbox`), fail-closed proposal/confirm flow
- `crates/tui/src/dispatch_runner.rs`, `crates/cli/src/dispatch.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cloud/tests.rs`
- `crates/secrets/src/lib.rs` — `daytona` secret slot
- `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/dispatch.rs`, `jobs.rs`, `config.rs`; `crates/tui/src/computer_meter*.rs` references
- `docs/DAYTONA_CLOUD_DISPATCH.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md`, `computer/snapshots/cloud-agent/` (Daytona-shaped image — replacement tracked separately)
- `crates/tui/src/lib.rs`, `crates/cli/src/lib.rs` wiring

Note the snapshot README already records that the product dispatcher wiring for the Daytona snapshot is absent (no clone, env injection, or toolbox execution) — the engine dispatch path never reached product completeness.

## Deliver

- Extract an explicit Computer provider boundary in the engine (or ratify the alternative: engine consumes the apps control-plane provider contract over HTTP for cloud work — decide in this issue, document in `docs/`).
- Implement the Lambda microVM path under the same admission/meter rules the control plane enforces (`aws-lambda-microvm` adapter already exists in `codewhale-apps/services/control-plane/src/sandbox/`).
- Tombstone the `daytona` secret slot: readable/settleable, never usable for a new call.
- Move `docs/DAYTONA_CLOUD_DISPATCH.md` to a historical note; historic dispatch records remain readable and terminally settleable only.

## Acceptance

- No code path in the engine can create/resume a Daytona sandbox.
- `codewhale dispatch` (cloud-agent) acquires a Lambda microVM Computer end to end in a real run, with receipts.
- Clippy/fmt/tests green; docs tell one provider story.

issues.title: Continuous Self-Learning from Dialog (Automatic Skill Evolution)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: context
labels.description: Context management / context

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
## Problem
CodeWhale has a powerful Skills System where users can manually create `SKILL.md` files that the agent can reference. However, the knowledge remains static:

1. **No automatic pattern extraction** - The agent doesn't recognize when it's solving the same type of problem repeatedly
2. **No skill evolution** - When a user provides corrections or better approaches, the agent doesn't update existing skills
3. **No cross-session learning** - Lessons learned in one session don't automatically improve future sessions
4. **Manual overhead** - Users must proactively identify patterns and write skills themselves, which breaks flow

**Example**: A developer builds 3 FastAPI endpoints with MongoDB over a week. Each time, they go through similar steps (configure connection, create models, implement CRUD, add error handling, write tests). The agent executes these steps each time but never "learns" that this is a repeatable pattern worth codifying as a skill.

## Proposed Solution
Implement a **self-learning loop** that automatically observes, extracts, and codifies patterns from successful interactions:

#### Core Components:

**1. Pattern Detection Engine**
- Monitor dialog history for repeated solution patterns
- Identify multi-step workflows that occur 3+ times
- Detect corrections and incorporate them into skills
- Track successful outcomes vs. failures

**2. Automated Skill Generation**
- Create `SKILL.md` files based on detected patterns
- Generate structured YAML frontmatter with:
  - Name, description, version
  - Step-by-step instructions
  - Common pitfalls (learned from corrections)
  - Usage examples from real dialog
  - Confidence scores based on success rate

**3. Skill Evolution System**
- Update existing skills when better approaches are discovered
- Merge related skills into more comprehensive ones
- Archive unused or low-confidence skills
- Version tracking with change history

**4. Learning Triggers**

```toml
# Example configuration
[learning]
auto_create_skills = true          # Default: false (requires confirmation)
confidence_threshold = 0.8          # Only auto-create if pattern confidence > 80%
pattern_occurrence_threshold = 3    # Pattern must appear 3+ times
enable_cross_session_learning = true
skill_review_frequency = "weekly"   # Suggest reviewing skills periodically
```

**5. User Control & Transparency**

- Preview suggested skills before creation (/suggest-skills)
- Approve/deny skill creation (/approve-skill fastapi-crud)
- Review learning history (/learning-history)
- Manual override and pruning (/delete-skill old-pattern, /merge-skills)

## Use Case

Scenario: A development team building a FastAPI + React + MCP application over 6 months:

Month 1: Manual Mode

- Developers work with CodeWhale, solving problems

- Agent silently observes patterns but doesn't act

- Team reviews /suggest-skills weekly and creates the most useful ones manually

Month 2-3: Semi-Automated Mode

- Agent automatically creates skills for patterns with 90%+ confidence

- Team reviews and approves skills weekly

- Skills begin covering 40% of repetitive tasks

Month 4-6: Fully Automated Mode

- Agent creates, updates, and merges skills autonomously

- Skills cover 80% of repetitive patterns

- Development speed increases 2-3x for common tasks

Specific Example:

```text
Session 1: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth"
Session 2: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth and role-based permissions"
Session 3: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth, roles, and rate limiting"

→ Agent detects the pattern and creates skill "fastapi-jwt-crud"
→ Future request: "Build user management API" 
→ Agent uses the skill, saving 30 minutes of work
→ User adds "also needs email verification" 
→ Agent updates the skill with email verification step
→ Next team member gets the improved skill automatically
```

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Pros | Cons |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Manual Skills** | Full control, simple to implement | High overhead, knowledge loss between sessions |
| **Third-party Learning Tools** | Could use external ML | Integration complexity, additional dependencies |
| **Prompt-based Learning** | Simple to implement | Temporary, lost between sessions |
| **MCP-based Learning** | Extensible, modular | Requires separate MCP server, not built-in |


This proposal leverages CodeWhale's existing infrastructure (skills, hooks, MCP) while adding intelligence on top, keeping everything integrated and user-friendly.

## Impact 

This feature would transform CodeWhale from a static assistant into an adaptive pair programmer that grows with its users. It's technically feasible using CodeWhale's existing infrastructure (skills, hooks, MCP) and would provide immense value to both individual developers and teams.

For Individual Developers:

- ⚡ 2-3x faster for repetitive coding tasks

- 🧠 Preserves knowledge - don't need to remember every best practice

- 🔄 Continuous improvement - your assistant gets smarter every day

For Teams:

- 📚 Shared knowledge base - skills become team documentation

- 🎯 Consistent code quality - best practices automatically enforced

- 🚀 Faster onboarding - new members learn patterns through skills

For the CodeWhale Project:

- 🏆 Unique competitive advantage - no other open-source agent has this

- 🌟 Stronger community - users will share their learned skills

- 📈 Increased adoption - teams will choose CodeWhale for the learning capability

Metrics to Track:

- Number of skills created automatically vs. manually

- Time saved per task (before/after learning)

- Skill usage rates and success rates

- User satisfaction scores



## Additional context

### Why Now?

- The skills system is already built - this adds the "learning" layer

- MCP provides the perfect hook for pattern detection

- Users are already asking for smarter assistants

#### Potential Challenges & Mitigations:

- False positives → Confidence thresholds and human approval (especially initially)

- Skill bloat → Automatic archiving and merging of similar skills

- Security → Version control and rollback for skills, opt-in feature with clear controls

### Implementation Phases (Suggestion)

#### Phase 1: Pattern Detection (MVP)

- Add /suggest-skills command that analyzes current session

- Show proposed skill template for user approval

- Implement via MCP server (external)

#### Phase 2: Automated Creation

- Detect patterns without prompting

- Auto-create skills with configurable confidence threshold

- Add /approve-skill and /reject-skill commands

#### Phase 3: Evolution

- Update skills when corrections are detected

- Merge related skills automatically

- Track skill usage and confidence scores

#### Phase 4: Cross-Session Learning

- Share learned skills across all projects

- Aggregate best practices from multiple sessions

- Privacy controls for sensitive code

### Example

```bash
$ codewhale

> Build a FastAPI endpoint for user registration with email validation

[Agent builds the feature through 8 steps]

> Now build a product listing endpoint

[Agent notices pattern...]

🧠 I've noticed you're building FastAPI CRUD endpoints with validation.
   I've seen this pattern 3 times this week.

   Would you like me to create a skill called "fastapi-crud-with-validation"? [y/n] y

✅ Skill created! It includes:
   - MongoDB connection setup
   - Pydantic model generation
   - CRUD endpoint implementation
   - Email validation pattern
   - Error handling best practices

   Type `/skill fastapi-crud-with-validation` to use it next time.

[Next week...]

> Build a blog post API

💡 I see you're building FastAPI CRUD again. Using skill: fastapi-crud-with-validation
   [Executes in 3 steps instead of 8, with best practices applied]

> Also add category filtering

🔄 I've added category filtering to the skill. This will be available for future tasks.
```

labels.name: cleanup

labels.name: tui
