labels.name: tracking
labels.description: Parent issue that tracks a multi-part effort

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.9.12 (filed 2026-09-10, measured on the 0.9.13 development tree).
>
> **What remains**
> - Move `Config` and its helpers out of crates/tui/src/config.rs (12,974 lines) into crates/config; this is still the prerequisite for most other extractions. Resolve the config-persistence ownership question (#6143) first.
> - Break the remote_control/ModalView cycle (crates/tui/src/remote_control.rs:3189 and crates/tui/src/tui/views/mod.rs:1313) so `remote_control` can leave.
> - Drive scripts/runtime-boundary-baseline.json down (prod 69, `config|tui` 23) and re-run scripts/split/module_graph.py to re-measure the connected component; replace the 118/128 and 727,748 figures in the body.
> - Then move mcp, hooks, tools and core into their existing near-empty crates, strictly one extraction at a time.
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - The stated blocker is unchanged: the TUI's own `crates/tui/src/config.rs` is still 12,974 lines with `pub struct Config` at :2200, not a re-export of codewhale-config.
> - The `remote_control` <-> UI cycle is still there: crates/tui/src/tui/views/mod.rs:1313 calls `crate::remote_control::view_is_approval_for_gate`, and crates/tui/src/remote_control.rs:3189 takes `&dyn crate::tui::views::ModalView`.
> - `crate::utils` still depends on `crate::config::effective_home_dir()` (crates/tui/src/utils.rs:1055).
> - The numbers in the title are stale and the crate grew: `git grep -c '' v0.10.1 -- 'crates/tui/src/*.rs'` sums to about 1,254,000 lines (the issue cites ~957,700).
> - The shadow-crate gap widened: crates/tui/src/tools is ~202,300 lines vs crates/tools/src 1,377; crates/tui/src/core ~84,200 vs crates/core/src 4,463; crates/tui/src/mcp ~26,200 vs crates/mcp/src 109 (same line-count method at v0.10.1).
> - Progress since filing: a `codewhale-runtime` crate exists (crates/runtime/src, ~8,300 lines, including goal_loop.rs) with a CI boundary ratchet — commit 24a7b99a73 'refactor(split): codewhale-runtime crate and boundary ratchet (RS-0..RS-7) (#6586)', in v0.10.1.

---

## Where the decomposition actually stands

Three modules left `crates/tui` in 0.9.13 — `localization` (7,087 lines, `ddc38548d`), `palette` (5,850) and `command_safety` into the existing `execpolicy` crate (2,951) (`063f914f2`). The crate went **973,442 → ~957,700 lines**.

Those were chosen because a dependency census that excluded doc comments and `#[cfg(test)]` blocks showed them at or near zero real coupling. `localization`'s single `crate::` reference turned out to be a sentence inside a doc comment.

## The blocker, found by attempting the next one

`remote_control` (8,828 lines) was scored as a zero-dependency leaf and **is not**. It has 12 real production edges, including a grouped `use crate::{…}` that a naive `crate::[a-z]` census misses entirely. Worse, it forms a genuine two-node cycle with the UI:

```
crates/tui/src/tui/views/mod.rs:1168   crate::remote_control::view_is_approval_for_gate(view.as_ref(), gate)
crates/tui/src/remote_control.rs:3139  view: &dyn crate::tui::views::ModalView,
```

A crate cannot contain half a cycle, so no manifest arrangement makes that build.

Its transitive closure is **118 of 128 top-level modules — 727,748 production lines in 689 non-test files**. The hub is `crate::config`: the TUI's *own* 13,304-line `config.rs` (`pub struct Config` at `:2817`), which is **not** a re-export of `codewhale-config`. Even `crate::utils` is inside the component, because `utils.rs:740,859` call `crate::config::effective_home_dir()`.

**Breaking `crate::config` out of the UI crate is the prerequisite for essentially every remaining extraction.** Until it moves, most modules are one component.

## Why this matters, in measured terms

C00 measured warmed one-line edits: a **provider edit at 30.31s / 8,714 MB RSS**, a **renderer edit at 46.62s / 8,947 MB**, against **0.92s / 269 MB** for the same shape of edit in a small crate. `docs/BUILD_PERFORMANCE.md:18` puts a cold `cargo build -p codewhale-tui` at 94s, of which the crate itself is 70s and the critical path.

## The target, stated plainly

`crates/tui` should contain `tui/` — the ~266k lines of actual UI. Everything else belongs to the crate that already owns its name. The striking part is that those crates **already exist and are nearly empty**:

| Concern | Real crate | Shadow inside `tui` |
| -- | --: | --: |
| `tools` | 1,311 | **154,135** |
| `core` | 5,593 | **58,621** |
| `mcp` | 4,569 | 13,097 |
| `hooks` | 1,598 | 7,542 |

There is 117× more tool code inside the UI crate than in the crate named `tools`.

## Proposed order

1. **`crate::config` out of the UI crate** — the prerequisite. Likely merges into `codewhale-config`, which already exists at 46,768 lines.
2. Re-run the closure analysis afterwards; most of the 118-module component should fragment.
3. Then the large blocks by real coupling: `plugins`+`skills` (mutually coupled, move together), `mcp` (into the existing crate, not a new one), `runtime_api` (zero inbound), `fleet`, `client`.
4. `tools` (154k) and `core` (59k) last — they are the mass, and both have existing near-empty owners.

## Rules learned the hard way

- **Run extractions strictly one at a time.** Each rewrites consumers crate-wide; two in parallel destroyed each other's work in this session.
- Check whether a `crate::` hit is code before trusting a census — comments and test blocks inflated every early estimate.
- Move code, do not rewrite it. Moved tests passing unchanged is the proof an extraction is correct.
- No re-export shims: `docs/design/TUI_DECONSTRUCTION.md:176,185-186` forbids leaving one with deferred consumers.

issues.title: [Feature] Pluggable agent memory: a generic backend seam with causal-memory / mem0 as reference implementations

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: context
labels.description: Context management / context

labels.name: plugins
labels.description: Plugins, skills, hooks, extension host and plugin import

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
## Background

Codewhale's agent memory is currently a hardwired, single-implementation native feature with no pluggable third-party backend entry:

- The `MemoryBackend` enum has only `Native` / `Off` variants (`crates/tui/src/config.rs:1985`) — no `Custom`/`External`/`MCP`.
- `NativeMemoryStore` (`crates/tui/src/native_memory.rs:51`) is a concrete struct (Markdown source + SQLite FTS5 index) with no trait, so a third party cannot supply their own store.
- The plugin activation capability list `PluginActivationCapability` (`crates/tui/src/plugins/activation.rs:26`) has no `Memory` category, so a plugin cannot declare "I provide a memory backend".
- `docs/MEMORY.md` states that native is the only memory system, the planned Moraine MCP backend was removed, and `backend` accepts only `native` / `off`.

Today a third-party memory system can only be side-mounted through the generic MCP channel (most external memory systems expose an MCP server). It can be wired in, but it is not a first-class backend recognized by `[memory]` — `# quick-add`, the `remember` tool, and the `/memory` command all remain pinned to native.

## Goal

Upgrade memory from "single, hardwired implementation" to a **generic, pluggable, optional** seam:

- Keep native as the default, zero-dependency local backend.
- Define a stable backend seam that **any** third-party memory system can implement — not one tailored to a particular vendor.
- Make `[memory] backend` a first-class config choice, with the existing `remember` / recall / `/memory` lifecycle routing to whichever backend is selected; a backend only implements "store" and "retrieve".
- Ship causal-memory and mem0 as the **first two reference implementations** to prove the seam is generic across very different backend shapes — not as the endpoint of the work.

## The seam is open to any memory system

The abstraction is deliberately transport- and vendor-agnostic, so the following (and others) can all be implemented behind the same interface:

- **causal-memory** — causal/decision memory (local, MCP stdio/HTTP).
- **mem0** — fact/preference recall (remote service, API/SDK + MCP).
- **Zep, Letta (MemGPT), LangMem, MemOS, Mem0** — any agent-memory platform exposing a service API or MCP.
- A custom in-house store — implement the trait directly.

The only requirement is that a backend can answer "store an entry" and "retrieve relevant entries for a query".

## Reference implementation #1 (focus): causal-memory (developed in-house)

causal-memory is our open-source agent memory system (Rust, Apache-2.0, `JingxuanC/causal-memory`). Its core differentiator is a **causal core + inhibition modeling**: facts, temporal state, and `decision → outcome` causal edges live on a single SQLite store, driven by a hippocampus-style engine (typed spreading activation with excitatory *and* inhibitory edges, Hebbian co-occurrence reinforcement, Q-value dynamics, immutable SWR consolidation). Agents recall not only *what* happened and *when* it was true, but *why* it worked and *what would happen if* they acted differently.

Why it is the first backend we build:

1. **Causal information is the most fragile type under text compaction.** The causal table lives outside the agent's context window, so compaction cannot touch it — in a real-LLM compaction benchmark causal-memory retains 100% causal-table recall while mem0 drops to 45%. This directly patches the "re-hits the same bug the same wrong way" hole after long-session compaction.
2. **Clearly ahead of mem0 on causal capabilities** (CausalEval): C7 belief update 100% vs 80%, C2 intervention prediction 75% vs 40%, C4 inhibition distinction 80% vs 50%.
3. **Integration surface is ready**: 14 MCP tools (stdio + HTTP transports), a Python `Memory` facade, and an existing DSH plugin shape — wiring into Codewhale's MCP/plugin channel is nearly zero new code.
4. The honest caveat: pure fact recall (LoCoMo 79.1% vs mem0 91.6%) is not its strong suit — that is exactly mem0's strength. The two are complementary, which is why a generic seam beats "pick one".

## Reference implementation #2: mem0

mem0 is the fact-recall specialist (LoCoMo 91.6%) and is chosen as the second reference implementation precisely because its shape is the opposite of causal-memory's: a **remote hosted service** with an API/SDK, rather than a local store. If the seam can absorb both, it is general enough for the rest of the ecosystem.

## Plan (phased)

- **Phase 0 — baseline (already landed)**: native as the only backend, `[memory]` opt-in, `#` quick-add, `remember`/recall tools. Landed in v0.9.x.
- **Phase 1 — define the generic backend seam (core change)**: introduce a `MemoryBackend` trait with a minimal, transport-agnostic method set (`store` / `search` / `prompt_block`, plus a health/`status` probe); add an `External`/`Custom` variant to the `MemoryBackend` enum; make `[memory] backend` resolve a backend by **kind + connection parameters** (process/stdio command, HTTP service URL, or MCP server name) rather than hardcoding vendor names. Native becomes a default impl of the trait; `Off` stays as-is. Add a `Memory` capability to `PluginActivationCapability` so a backend can ship as a plugin bundle.
- **Phase 2 — two reference implementations to prove genericity**: land **causal-memory** first (MCP stdio + HTTP), then **mem0** (remote API/SDK). Success criterion: the trait needed no vendor-specific escape hatches to absorb two very different backend shapes.
- **Phase 3 — bring-your-own-backend**: document the driver/adaptor contract so any third party (Zep, Letta, LangMem, a custom store, …) can add a backend — ideally as an external plugin bundle, without a core change.
- **Phase 4 — wrap-up**: update `docs/MEMORY.md`, `config.example.toml`, and the `[memory]` config contract; add backend selection + fallback (degrade to off or native when a backend is unavailable); document the KV-cache effect (the boundary of memory injected into the system-prompt prefix is unchanged).

## Integration surface

- **Reuse the existing MCP/plugin channel**: causal-memory is already an MCP server and can land first as a plugin bundle (`McpStdio`/`McpRemote`) as the Phase 2 bootstrap — no need to wait for the trait abstraction before trying it out. Any MCP-speaking memory system gets the same path for free.
- **Add a native trait backend**: make `[memory] backend = "causal-memory"` (or any registered backend) a first-class config option, with the `remember` tool, `/memory` command, and `#` quick-add all routing to the selected backend.
- **Open the plugin capability**: a `Memory` activation capability lets a third party ship a backend as a reviewed plugin, exactly like they ship skills, MCP servers, or hooks today.

## References

- Current memory implementation: `crates/tui/src/native_memory.rs`, `crates/tui/src/config.rs` (`MemoryBackend` / `MemoryConfig`)
- Memory docs: `docs/MEMORY.md`
- Plugin activation capabilities: `crates/tui/src/plugins/activation.rs`
- causal-memory: https://github.com/JingxuanC/causal-memory (README includes the CausalEval / compaction-survival benchmarks)
- Original memory EPIC: #489

> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.9.13 (body: '0.9.13 ships /pet'; filed 2026-09-14).
>
> **What remains**
>
> * Human with a Kitty-protocol terminal: run the pet/QA.md real-terminal procedure (docked/full, resize, Escape image cleanup, braille fallback, tmux/SSH, reduced motion) and record measured frame timing, CPU, RSS and input latency
> * Run shared-owner acceptance with the TUI habitat and the desktop view on one live session (one producer, one audio lease, owner restart, competing owner, storage failure) and record it in pet/QA.md
> * Forward accepted Engine metadata to the pet from crates/app-server, not only the TUI producer
> * Record the default-appearance decision against crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/appearance.rs Default, and tick off item 5 after confirming owner.rs:931-946 covers the failed case as well
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
>
> * Item 5 (typed completion outcome) appears done: crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/owner.rs:931-946 at v0.10.1 feeds turn_outcome completed vs interrupted through the projection and asserts an interrupted turn gets no Done presence and no done_effect_id
> * Item 3 (Engine metadata beyond the TUI) not done: git grep -i pet in crates/app-server/src at v0.10.1 returns only an unrelated 'competing' test name (daemon_windows.rs:327); no pet metadata forwarding
> * Item 4 (default appearance) cannot be confirmed as decided: crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/appearance.rs:15-27 has a single hard-coded Default with no record of the 'Codewhale by default' decision
> * Item 1 (real-terminal qualification) has no receipt: pet/QA.md:28 still describes the Kitty-probe plus fallback-terminal check as a procedure, and pet/QA.md:253-254 says native active-session delivery and device transport remain open
> * Item 2 (shared-owner acceptance across TUI and desktop) has no receipt in pet/QA.md or pet/SHARED.md at v0.10.1; could not verify it was ever run
> * Issue comment from the 0.10.0 readiness pass ([#6370](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6370>)) states nothing on the list was executed; no commit in v0.10.0..v0.10.1 and no CHANGELOG line references #6155

---

0.9.13 ships `/pet` ([#6154](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6154>), from [#6110](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6110>) plus the prepared shared-owner/Kitty patch). What it ships on is test evidence and the prepared-archive receipts; these acceptance items were explicitly not done and stay open here (split out of #6109 so the umbrella can track the cross-surface owner work):

1. **Real-terminal visual qualification** of the Kitty pixel habitat: docked→full transitions, continuous motion, resize, Escape image cleanup, a fallback (braille) terminal, tmux/SSH behaviour, reduced motion. Measure delivered frame timing, CPU, RSS, bandwidth and input latency in the terminal; the only numbers today are the raster microbenchmark (17.09 ms mean / 19.55 ms p95, \~150 KB/frame, excludes transport) and a 30 Hz simulation. 60 fps is a target, not a measured result. Computer Use access to Ghostty/Terminal was denied in the preparing session; do not relabel browser or native screenshots as terminal proof.
2. **Shared-owner acceptance**: open the TUI habitat and the desktop/browser view on one live session, compare identity/tick/digest at a retained frame, interact from either side, close and reopen the TUI, confirm continued ownership, one producer, one audio lease, durable appearance. Exercise owner restart, a competing owner, source change, storage failure.
3. **Engine metadata attachment beyond the TUI**: only the TUI producer forwards accepted Engine metadata today; app-server does not (#6139, #6152).
4. **Founder direction "Codewhale by default"** for the appearance: not interpreted in 0.9.13 (the eight prepared presets are unchanged). Decide what the default look is and make it the default.
5. **Completion outcome fidelity**: the pet projection keeps only a derived `failed`; carry the typed `completed|interrupted|failed` terminal status and receipt identity through the metadata projection so a cancelled turn never gets a success gesture (see the animation packet in `artifacts/pet-review-20260912/CORE-PET-GPUI-CONTRACT.md`).

Contract and evidence: `pet/SHARED.md`, `pet/QA.md`, `docs/design/DOT_WHALE_PET.md`, `artifacts/pet-review-20260912/{PREPARED-PET-HANDOFF,RUST-PET-MODE-TAKEOVER,CORE-PET-GPUI-CONTRACT}.md`.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against v0.9.13 (filed 2026-09-18); body later updated 2026-09-23 against v0.10.0.
>
> **What remains**
> - Decide whether a goals index across threads belongs in Core (no /v1/goals route exists); the client can only read goals one thread at a time
> - Tracking section with 'waiting for' sublines has no served source; define it or drop it from scope
> - Category picker has no Core field to persist to; keep categories as a chat seed only or add a field
> - Qualify hosted goal create, stop and continuation across devices, which the issue body records as unqualified
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Core serves one authoritative goal per thread: /v1/threads/{id}/goal with GET, PUT and DELETE at crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2499, plus /goal/complete at :2504 and /goal/block at :2505 (handlers at :8299 and :8391)
> - There is no cross-thread goal list or tracking route: git grep for '"/v1/goals', '"/v1/watches' and '"/v1/schedules' over crates at v0.10.1 returned nothing
> - Goals carry no category: git grep -i 'category|categories' on crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs at v0.10.1 returned nothing
> - Goal creation is conversational in the Engine already: the host no longer parses prose into goals and the model calls create_goal (CHANGELOG.md:1706-1709)
> - The web projection described in the issue body (codewhale-platform branch feat/beta-readiness-20260923) is outside this checkout and could not be verified here; git log v0.10.1 --grep '#6327' is empty

---

Goal tracking surface: a Tracking section for monitored items with "waiting for …" sublines, a Goals section for longer-horizon items, and creation through a category picker (health, relationships, finance, career, interests, productivity, other) that refines the goal conversationally in chat before tracking starts. Blocked on Core tracking routes.

Acceptance:

* Categories, sublines, and states render from served routes.
* Creation hands off to chat and lands back as a tracked goal.
* No client-side goal store: unavailable routes show as unavailable.

### Web beta implementation — 2026-09-23

Claim: web-next Goals currently stores intents only in browser-local storage. Replace the live surface with authoritative per-conversation Engine goals via the existing account/tenant runtime binding. Preserve local drafts for explicit export rather than silently assigning them to an account. Creation continues through the conversation composer. Claimed platform paths: apps/web-next/{lib/goals.ts,components/goals.tsx,components/conversations.tsx,tests/goals.test.ts}; services/control-plane/src/{server.mjs,runtime/http-runtime-client.mjs,integrations/chat/codewhale-runtime.mjs}; their focused tests and the existing private runtime route contract if required. No second goal store or scheduler. Review will reuse current workbench/read contracts and scoped approvals separately.2026-09-23 source evidence: platform branch feat/beta-readiness-20260923 at e4ecfc0a02f061a5b4d7c0bb5e3f284c927e5f8a projects authoritative Engine goals through ownership-checked GET /v1/threads/:id/goal, including runtime capability, account-binding and timeout checks. issues.title: feat(engine): soft model-facing context notice while auto-compaction is enabled (no competing save/compact ceremony)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: context
labels.description: Context management / context

labels.name: compaction
labels.description: Context management / compaction

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
## Problem

With automatic compaction enabled (model-aware default-on for known windows),
the model receives no model-facing context-pressure signal at all.

`context_pressure_line` returns `None` whenever `self.config.compaction.enabled`
(`crates/tui/src/core/engine/compaction.rs`), with the comment that asking the
model to warn the user created a competing save/compact ceremony before the
request-boundary guard could act (#5620). The warning/critical wording in
`context_pressure_message` (`crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs`) therefore only
reaches the model when automatic compaction is **disabled** for the session.

Defaults make the blind window structural, not edge-case:

- auto-compact threshold defaults to **80%** (`auto_compact_threshold_percent`,
  `settings.rs` / `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`);
- model-facing warning thresholds are **85% / 95%**
  (`CONTEXT_WARNING_THRESHOLD_PERCENT` / `CONTEXT_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD_PERCENT`
  in `context_inspector.rs`) — and those only apply when auto is off;
  with auto at 80%, an 85% line could not fire before the cut anyway;
- UI pressure (sticky status / toast / inspector) is human-facing only
  (sticky path: PR #5629 for #5620).

So on a default session the engine compacts at ~80% while the model never sees
a notice that the window is filling. The model cannot:

- wrap the current step into a clean stopping point before the boundary;
- prefer `memory_checkpoint_put` while there is still headroom;
- tell the user a compact is imminent (off-loop / fleet style).

#5620 correctly removed the **actionable ESCALATED / "run /compact"** line when
auto-compact owns the cut. That is not the same as a **passive soft notice**
that does not ask the model to run compact or run a save ceremony.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional **soft, model-facing notice** while auto-compact is enabled,
distinct from the existing manual-path warning/critical messages.

Design constraints (aligned with #5620 and the session-pinned prefix rules):

1. **Append-only turn metadata / user-role `<turn_meta>` block** — never splice
   into the session-pinned system/tool prefix (KV-cache / `docs/CACHE.md`
   contract). Same host as today's pressure line
   (`append_resource_metadata_lines`).
2. **No competing ceremony:** wording must **not** say "run /compact", "stop for
   save/compact", or otherwise direct the model to take over compaction from
   the engine. Engine remains the only force path. Informational only — not a
   standing system-prompt directive (prompt authority is a protected surface;
   see closed-unmerged #5661).
3. **Notice threshold is configurable**, and must sit **below** the active
   `auto_compact_threshold_percent` (candidates: fixed offset under that
   setting, e.g. −10 pp, or an absolute % such as ~70%). Exact key/derivation
   is an open question below. Optional second step just below the auto fire
   line; auto fire at the existing threshold unchanged.
4. **Byte-stable when inactive** — emit only when over the notice threshold
   (same discipline as #5187 / goal budget lines).
5. Keep the existing manual-path text when auto-compact is **disabled**
   (unchanged).
6. **Honor `runtime_chat_isolated`:** today's `<turn_meta>` is omitted when
   `!runtime_chat_isolated` is false (`engine.rs`); the soft notice must follow
   the same rule (or the issue must explicitly propose an exception).

### Open questions for maintainers

- Notice percent key: derive from `auto_compact_threshold_percent` (e.g. −10 pp)
  vs separate `context_notice_percent` setting?
- One line vs two stages under auto?
- Should the notice recommend `memory_checkpoint_put` explicitly, or stay
  purely informational?
- Relation to **#6217** (`context_status` tool): passive notice vs pull meter —
  complementary, or should the notice come from the same canonical meter?

### Alternatives considered (design sketches)

| Option | Shape | Effort | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Passive soft line in turn metadata when auto ON | Smallest delta to `context_pressure_line` | Low | Must keep wording non-actionable vs #5620 |
| B. Separate notice thresholds config only | Config without new copy | Low | Still needs copy + KV-cache note |
| C. Only #6217 pull tool, no passive line | Model must poll | Med | Easy to miss; no automatic heads-up |

(A) is the suggested first slice; B/C can follow.

## Use case

Long unattended / off-loop runs (multi-agent, overnight). Auto-compact fires at
80% with no signal to the model. The model cannot close a tool chain cleanly,
cannot save a checkpoint just before the boundary, and cannot surface "compact
incoming" to the operator. Work that should end at a natural boundary is cut
mid-phrase by the request-boundary guard.

## Alternatives considered

- **`auto_compact = false`:** restores 85/95 model lines, but opts out of the
  default product behavior and reintroduces manual ceremony (#5620's concern).
- **`memory_checkpoint_put`:** exists, but the model has no model-facing signal
  under auto ON telling it *when* headroom is becoming scarce.
- **#6217 `context_status`:** pull-based; does not replace a passive heads-up
  (and may share the same canonical meter).
- **Revert #5620 / reinstate ESCALATED:** would re-open the competing
  save/compact problem the fix was for — explicitly not proposed here.
- **#5661 agent directive:** closed unmerged (prompt authority protected);
  this proposal stays informational turn metadata, not a system-prompt rule.

## Impact

Highest for default users (auto ON, known window): every long session either
absorbs a silent engine compact or forces operators into `auto_compact=false`.
Complementary to sticky UI pressure (PR #5629 for #5620) and to open #6217.

## Additional context

Code anchors (local checkout, `main`-aligned, workspace version 0.10.0):

- Early return when auto ON: `crates/tui/src/core/engine/compaction.rs` —
  `if self.config.compaction.enabled { return None; }` (#5620 rationale).
- Manual-only messages: `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs` —
  `context_pressure_message` (warning ≥85%, critical ≥95%).
- Injection: `append_resource_metadata_lines` → `<turn_meta>` on a `Role::User`
  message; omitted when `runtime_chat_isolated`.
- Thresholds: `crates/tui/src/tui/context_inspector.rs` (85.0 / 95.0);
  auto default 80% in `settings.rs` / `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.
- Checkpoint tools already model-visible: `crates/memory/src/protocol.rs` —
  `memory_checkpoint_put` / `memory_checkpoint_get`.
- Closed history: **#5620** (removed ESCALATED under auto; sixteen tool reads
  / three automatic compactions), **#4073** (≥85% escalation on the path auto
  ON no longer uses), **#5661** (directive PR closed unmerged).
- Open adjacent: **#6217** (model-facing `context_status` meter).

Comparison context (why this is worth doing now):

- **Claude Code** injects a model-facing "context is running low" reminder on
  the auto path (see anthropics/claude-code#79665 for the reminder text/behavior).
- **opencode** and **vtcode** stay harness-silent toward the model but still
  compact on preflight/auto thresholds (opencode: `autoCompact` /
  `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT`; from the docs comparison in our research —
  not re-run against their tree this session).
- Codewhale is the unusual case of "engine owns compact **and** model gets
  zero signal."

_No secrets or session logs in this issue. Static code + docs analysis; not
verified on a live 0.10 session._

issues.title: feat(compaction): optional model-invoked self-compact (with note-to-self) as a complement to engine-owned auto-compact

labels.name: enhancement

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
## Problem

Auto-compaction in Codewhale is entirely harness-owned: when
`auto_compact_threshold_percent` is reached, the engine cuts at the request
boundary. There is **no tool the model can call** to compact (or to request a
compact) at a boundary the model chooses.

Closest existing surface:

- `memory_checkpoint_put` / `memory_checkpoint_get` — save/resume working state
  *if* the model knows a compact is coming (no model-facing pressure under auto
  ON today — see companion proposal for soft notice);
- `/compact <focus>` and Ctrl+L — **operator-only** (`Op::CompactContext` is
  host-sent from TUI / runtime, not in the model tool catalog);
- `[compaction] summary_instructions` / `retained_user_message_tokens` —
  operator knobs for *how* summarization runs, not *when*.

So the model cannot:

- compact when it just finished a coherent milestone and before the next noisy
  tool burst;
- attach a short note-to-self / handoff intent at the moment it decides to cut;
- recover mid-session when it *knows* history is degraded, without waiting for
  the 80% line (or asking the operator to type `/compact`).

For contrast: **Claude Code** prompts the model to *ask the user* to compact
(model-facing reminder, still human-gated); **opencode** auto-compacts from the
harness without a model-invoked compact tool. Neither exposes "model decides to
cut now" as a tool either — but Codewhale also has no conversational fallback
under default auto ON, so the gap is larger here.

Harness-only compaction is fine for interactive TUI use. It is weak for
off-loop / fleet style sessions where the model is the only party that knows
the task shape (headless `exec` has no `/compact` at all today).

## Proposed solution

Add an **optional, model-invoked compaction path** that sits *beside* engine
auto-compact, not instead of it. **Default: OFF** (opt-in via capability /
config until the companion soft-notice UX exists).

### Design constraints

1. **Engine keeps force.** Auto threshold, emergency path, and survival
   contract remain the backstop. Self-compact is best-effort, not a second
   authority that can race the guard (#5620 lesson: no competing ceremony —
   but a *single explicit model action* is a different contract than a prose
   "please compact now" line in every turn).
2. **Single turn-loop / single compact owner:** reuse the existing manual
   compaction op path (`handle_manual_compaction_op` / `Op::CompactContext`)
   rather than a parallel implementation. One summarizer, one survival
   contract, one artifact save.
3. **Note-to-self:** optional short `note` (or `focus`) argument on the tool,
   passed into the same channel as `/compact <focus>`
   (`CompactionConfig.focus`) / operator `summary_instructions` so a deliberate
   note can influence the summary or be re-stated after it — without inventing
   a second memory store.
4. **Gate: default OFF.** Tool catalog entry behind capability/scope (same
   pattern as `Capability::Checkpoint`); opt-in only (config flag or posture).
   Do not ship default-on before the companion notice issue lands.
5. **Idempotence / concurrency:** one compact per tool call. While a pass is
   running, further requests are rejected or dropped as redundant — today a
   concurrent manual `/compact` gets "already in progress", and a deferred
   manual is dropped when an auto pass starts/settles
   (`compaction_flow.rs`). A model tool should follow the same rules, not
   invent a merge.
6. **KV-cache:** tool schema is session-pinned prefix — state the effect
   (catalog change only if gated; no volatile thresholds in the tool
   description that churn every turn).

### Shape options (maintainers decide)

| Option | Shape | Effort | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. `self_compact` tool → existing manual compact op (+ optional note) | Thin wrapper over today's path | Low–Med | Need clear tool description so models do not spam it |
| B. Allow model to emit the same steer/op the UI sends on Ctrl+L | Minimal new surface | Med | Authorization / who may compact mid-turn |
| C. No tool; only soft notice (companion) so the model asks the user | Smallest | Low | Still needs a human in the loop — weak for off-loop |

Recommended framing: **A**, **default OFF**, after or with soft notice so the
model actually knows when the action is useful.

### Open questions for maintainers

- Opt-in mechanism: capability bit, settings flag, or posture-only?
- Should a model-initiated compact skip the "ask user" step entirely when
  posture is full auto, or always confirm?
- Does `note` merge with operator `summary_instructions` or only affect a
  one-off pass?
- Interaction with #6217: should the tool description embed the same remaining
  budget numbers (careful: churn)?

## Use case

- Long refactor: model finishes module N, context is 70–75%, next step will
  explode tool output — self-compact now with a note "module N done, start N+1
  from tests/".
- Off-loop worker with no human watching `/settings`: cannot run `/compact`
  itself today (and headless `exec` has no manual compact path).
- Recovery after a noisy tool: model decides history is past usefulness and
  cuts before the engine's 80% line (optional, if allowed).

## Alternatives considered

- **Status quo:** operator types `/compact` or waits for 80% — works for
  interactive, not for autonomous boundaries.
- **Only `memory_checkpoint_put`:** preserves state across *engine* compact,
  but does not let the model choose the cut or attach note-to-self for the
  summary pass.
- **Re-enable prose "run /compact" in turn_meta under auto ON:** rejected by
  #5620 (competing ceremony) — a real tool is an explicit action, not ambient
  instruction spam.
- **Full three-threshold notice/warning/force stack in the model:** larger UX
  surface; soft notice (companion) + optional tool is the smaller coherent
  slice.
- **Claude Code-style "ask the user" only:** needs a human; does not cover
  off-loop workers.

## Impact

Unlocks off-loop / fleet patterns already present in the product (sub-agents,
headless runs) without removing engine-owned defaults. Interactive TUI users
can ignore the tool while default stays OFF. Pairs with soft notice (companion
issue) and meter (#6217).

## Additional context

- Tool catalog precedent (model decides when to spend an action): closed
  **#4196** (agent-callable verify/critique).
- Checkpoint tools already gated by capability:
  `crates/memory/src/protocol.rs` (`Capability::Checkpoint`).
- Manual compact path already exists and is operator-only today
  (`Op::CompactContext`, `handle_manual_compaction_op`, `/compact <focus>`).
- Engine-owned force under auto ON is intentional (#5620 close rationale:
  sixteen tool reads / three automatic compactions, no ESCALATED ceremony).
- Reference design outside this repo (not a dependency): self-compact Pi agent
  (disler/self-compact-pi-agent, video 3b0U4_02bAE) — staged thresholds, a
  model-called compact tool, note-to-self around the ~270k mark (from the
  talk transcript; design contrast only).
- Companion proposal: soft model-facing notice while auto ON — **#6425**.

_No secrets or session logs in this issue. Static analysis of local fork +
public docs; not yet validated on a live release build._

> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against 0.10.0 (filed 2026-09-24 as a 0.10.2 spec item, G6).
>
> **What remains**
> - Add auto_review.model and auto_review.effort to AutoReviewConfig (crates/tui/src/config.rs:2735); keep subagents.reviewer_model (config.rs:1739) separate
> - Default to the route's cheapest low-effort catalog model, else parent model with reasoning_effort Low in consult_reviewer (crates/tui/src/core/engine/reviewer.rs:136)
> - Split context_text into a stable policy/transcript prefix with cache_control and the proposed action as the last block
> - Live-provider proof that a second review reports cache_read_input_tokens > 0
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Guardian request still sends reasoning_effort: None, exactly as the issue describes: crates/tui/src/core/engine/reviewer.rs:136
> - No cacheable prefix: the single context block has cache_control: None and the policy is a plain SystemPrompt::Text: crates/tui/src/core/engine/reviewer.rs:127 and :131
> - The guardian uses the caller's model (client.model()), no dedicated route: crates/tui/src/core/engine/reviewer.rs:121
> - AutoReviewConfig has only allow and block; no model or effort keys: crates/tui/src/config.rs:2735-2740
> - No commit in v0.10.0..v0.10.1 references #6480 (git log --grep empty)

---

**Config:** new `auto_review.model` and `auto_review.effort`. Do not reuse `subagents.reviewer_model`, which is the code-review role.

**Default model:** the route's cheapest catalog model that advertises low effort. If none does, use the parent model with `reasoning_effort: Low` (today it is `None`, `reviewer.rs:~136`).

**Request shape:**

* The request has a stable prefix, with `cache_control` on the policy block and on the transcript prefix.
* The proposed action is the last block.
* The response cache stays bypassed, because every decision is fresh.
* Concurrent reviews share the cached prefix without locking.

**Tests**

* `guardian_uses_low_effort_and_configured_model`
* `guardian_request_marks_cacheable_prefix`
* `proposed_action_is_last_block`
* The existing usage-attribution receipts must not change.

**Acceptance:** on a real provider, a second review reports `cache_read_input_tokens > 0`. This needs a live-provider proof.

**Size:** S–M. **Blocked by:** G2. **Spec:** codewhale-ops `approvals/specs/G-auto-review-0.10.2.md` (G6).

<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against 0.10.0 (filed 2026-09-24 as a 0.11 spec item, A1).
>
> **What remains**
> - Add an Engine-owned GrantStore keyed by (thread_id, owner_agent_id) with Once/Conversation/Repo scopes, deny-first
> - Engine consults it before emitting ApprovalRequired and records ApprovedByGrant/DeniedByGrant receipts
> - Delete the three stores (tui/app.rs:2163-2169, runtime_threads.rs:5267 and :8536, network_policy.rs:380) and drop the session params from core/authority.rs:685
> - Line references in the issue body are stale (e.g. runtime_threads ~5977 is now 5267; app.rs ~2065 is now 2163); still blocked by spec items C3 and R2
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - TUI store still present: crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:2163 and :2169 (approval_session_approved / approval_session_denied), read at crates/tui/src/tui/ui/approval_routing.rs:19-39
> - Runtime store still present: crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:5267 (RuntimeApprovalGrant), :8536 (session_grant_for), used at :17454
> - Network store still present: crates/tui/src/network_policy.rs:380 (NetworkSessionCache)
> - No unified store: `git grep 'struct GrantStore|ApprovedByGrant|DeniedByGrant|approval_grants.jsonl'` over v0.10.1 crates is empty; no grants.rs under crates/tui/src/core/engine (ls-tree)
> - resolve_approval_request_disposition still takes session_approved/session_denied: crates/tui/src/core/authority.rs:685-689
> - 0.10.1 changed grant semantics but not ownership: CHANGELOG.md:763-767 ('Allow for this conversation' records a grant per tool and argument class)

---

**Today there are three separate grant stores, and they don't share anything:**

* TUI: `App.approval_session_approved` / `approval_session_denied` (`tui/app.rs:~2065`, written in `ui/apply.rs:~2764-2830`, read in `ui/approval_routing.rs:10-40`)
* runtime: `RuntimeApprovalGrant` (`runtime_threads.rs:~5977-6090`)
* network: `NetworkSessionCache` (`network_policy.rs:~378-436`)

**Change**

1. **One store.** Add `core/engine/grants.rs` with a `GrantStore` keyed by `(thread_id, owner_agent_id)`. Scopes are Once, Conversation and Repo.
   * Denies are checked first, and a deny beats any later grant.
   * Turn-scoped denies clear at the end of the turn, as they do today.
2. **The Engine decides.** In `turn_loop.rs:~4237`, the Engine looks up grants before emitting `ApprovalRequired`, and records an `ApprovedByGrant{grant_id,scope}` or `DeniedByGrant` receipt. No UI surface re-checks.
3. **Decisions carry a scope.** They come back as `Approved{id, scope}`. The runtime's `remember:true` maps to Conversation, and Repo persists rules through the Engine.
4. **Delete the old stores.** All three are removed, and `resolve_approval_request_disposition` drops its session parameters.
5. **Grant history** goes to `approval_grants.jsonl` (see R2), which also lets conversation grants be rebuilt after a restart.

**Tests**

* `grant_store_deny_beats_later_conversation_grant`
* `runtime_and_tui_share_one_grant`
* `child_conversation_grant_scoped_to_owner`
* `force_prompt_bypasses_grant`
* `grant_rows_replay_after_restart`
* `runtime_allow_scope_repo_persists_rule`

**Acceptance:**

* `git grep approval_session_approved` and `git grep session_grant_for` return nothing.
* Every auto-approval has a receipt.

**Size:** L (\~900 lines net, including deletions). **Blocked by:** C3 and R2. **Spec:** codewhale-ops `approvals/specs/A-grants-authority-0.11.md` (A1).

issues.body:
## Problem

Standing instruction authority has two fixed ceilings, neither steerable by an operator, and both failure modes are invisible from the user's side.

**The ceilings (hard-coded, no config key).**

- `MAX_PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 48 * 1024` — `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:384`. Everything that reaches the model as standing instruction authority — the repository-root → workspace `AGENTS.md` chain, the global fallback layer, `.codewhale/rules/*.md`, and any imported foreign files — shares this one budget. Documented as fixed at `config.example.toml:360`.
- `MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE = 100 * 1024` — `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:366`. A context file over this is not trimmed: `load_context_file_with_symlink_policy` returns `Err(ProjectContextError::TooLarge)` (`:1083`; error text `crates/tui/src/project_context/types.rs:22`), the caller collects it as a warning and moves to the next candidate filename (`:565`), so that file's contribution is missing — while the chain still assembles ancestor files (`:620-665`) and merges the global fallback layer (`:684`, `merge_global_and_project_instructions` at `:946`). The agent then runs on a *broader* instruction set than the operator wrote, with nothing saying so.

`Config::instructions_paths()` selects *which* extra files load; their only ceiling is the fixed per-file truncation above, and no key controls either ceiling.

**Observed on a real workspace.** Global `~/AGENTS.md` = 54 KB, project `AGENTS.md` = 88,918 → 94,224 → 118,673 bytes over three days. The session log carries, once per launch:

```
WARN project_context: Dropping broadest-scope project instructions at the aggregate budget was=102031 now=49152 cap=49152
```

i.e. the broadest scope is dropped first, every session, and the project file has just crossed the 100 KiB line that turns it into a `TooLarge` skip.

**The notice gap — this is the part that hurts.** Nothing at session start says any of this happened:

- `as_system_block` (`types.rs:88`) emits instructions + rules + constitution; `ProjectContext.warnings` is **not** part of the prompt, so the model is not told either;
- the warnings surface only in `/context report` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:500-508`) and `GET /v1/workspace/instructions` (the source map added in #6168);
- the trim itself is a `tracing::warn` (`project_context.rs:448`) plus a marker line inside the content (`:391`).

So an operator with a mature global + project instruction pair cannot tell that half their standing law was cut, or which file lost.

**The two ceilings behave differently for the same nominal 100 KiB, and the docs name a marker the code never emits — happy to split the marker-name fix into its own issue if you prefer.** `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:1261-1262` and `docs/zh_hans/CONFIGURATION.md:680` say of `instructions = [...]`: "Each file is capped at 100 KiB; oversized files are truncated with a `[…elided]` marker rather than skipped." The behaviour is real: `render_instructions_block` caps each source at `INSTRUCTIONS_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 100 * 1024` (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:98`) and truncates it (`:277-289`). What it emits is `[…truncated: N of M bytes omitted — consider splitting this instructions file]` (`:283`); the name `[…elided]` appears only in the rustdoc for `InstructionSource::File` (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:229`) and in those two docs. So the defect is the marker name, not the ceiling.

The asymmetry is the real problem: **the `instructions = [...]` array trims an oversized file and says so in-context; the `AGENTS.md` chain drops the file entirely.** One path is told to split its file; the other loses a layer and is told nothing.

## Proposed solution

Optional knobs, with today's behaviour as the default:

1. `[context] instruction_budget_bytes` (default 49152, with an absolute ceiling) — the shared aggregate budget. The `[context]` table already exists (`ContextConfig`, `crates/tui/src/config.rs:2332`; live key today: `project_pack`), so this is a new key, not a new table.
2. `[context] instruction_file_max_bytes` (default 102400) — per-file ceiling for the `AGENTS.md` chain, and for the `instructions = [...]` path, which carries the same 100 KiB cap hard-coded today.
3. **Skip vs trim stated explicitly, and the chain gets what the array already does.** For a file over the per-file ceiling, either trim with the marker the `instructions = [...]` path already uses (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:283`, including its "consider splitting" hint) or refuse with a message naming the file, the size, and the limit. Silently dropping a whole instruction layer should not be one of the options.
4. **A first-turn notice.** When content is trimmed or a candidate file is dropped, put one bounded line into the run's first turn — e.g. `project instructions: dropped <path> (118673 bytes > 102400); global layer trimmed to budget` — on the same disclosure channel as the sub-agent budget block, so the model can tell the operator and the operator sees it without running a report command.

## Use case

- A user whose global preferences and project `AGENTS.md` together exceed 48 KiB currently cannot tell which half the agent actually read. They discover it by noticing the agent breaking a rule that is written in the file.
- A project whose `AGENTS.md` legitimately needs >100 KiB (an architecture + invariants + workflow document) has no way to load it at all — the layer is dropped, and the failing file is named only in a warning that no default surface shows.
- Tuning: raising the budget for a documentation-heavy repo is a per-user decision, exactly what a config key is for.

## Alternatives considered

- **Split the files** (the workaround): the right first move for the reporter and it needs no code, but it does not solve the visibility half, and it does not help a project that needs >100 KiB.
- **Raise both constants, change nothing else**: makes the budget a moving target with no surface to see it, and a project file over the per-file ceiling would still disappear silently.
- **Keep the skip, fix only the docs**: the docs already claim truncation; making them match a silent skip keeps the operator blind.
- **Put every warning into the system prompt verbatim**: unbounded and re-sent every turn; a single first-turn notice costs one line.

## Impact

Standing instructions shape every turn, so a silent trim silently changes behaviour — and it is invisible in `/cost`, `/tokens`, and the context meter because those measure tokens, not sources. Affected: anyone with a mature global + project instruction pair over 48 KiB, and anyone whose project file crosses 100 KiB.

## Additional context

- Both ceilings and their failure messages verified against `upstream/main` `a2216fc0c`; behaviour reproduced with `codewhale 0.10.0 (dev)`.
- Existing markers: `project_context.rs:391` (broader-scope drop) and `:392` (rules block); `fragments.rs:309` (foreign rule trim).
- `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md` agent-ready standard: the reproduction above is exact and code-referenced.

issues.body:
Part of the runtime/TUI crate split. Read first: `docs/design/TUI_DECONSTRUCTION.md` and the mover `scripts/split/move-modules.py` (it `git mv`s a top-level module, edits the `mod` lines, adds the name to the TUI's single path-alias block in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs:143-152`, and sweeps stale path strings). A lowercase reading of this task is "move small files"; the point is that these are **runtime-side subsystems with already-clean boundaries** — process supervision, shell dispatch, credentials exchange, runtime policy/logging, feature registry — that belong in the headless crate and will grow there.

Run slices one at a time — do not stack two `RS-n` slices in one working tree.

## Goal

Move ten modules from `crates/tui/src/` into `crates/runtime/src/`. Each one has **zero upward references** today (verified by `scripts/split/module_graph.py --report`), so no ratchet entry changes; their only dependencies are modules already resident in `crates/runtime` (or each other):

- `child_env` (1,423 lines) — no deps
- `logging` (134) — no deps
- `external_credentials` (938) — no deps
- `dsh_credentials` (148) — depends on `external_credentials` (moves in this batch)
- `shell_dispatcher` (994) — depends on `host_terminal` (already in runtime)
- `runtime_policy` (167) — no deps
- `process_tree` (935) — no deps
- `features` (375) — no deps
- `runtime_log` (588) — no deps
- `working_set` (2,505) — depends on `workspace_discovery` (already in runtime)

## Plan

1. Dry-run first: `python3 scripts/split/move-modules.py --dry-run child_env logging external_credentials dsh_credentials shell_dispatcher runtime_policy process_tree features runtime_log working_set` — read the printed path sweep. `--dry-run` writes nothing.
2. Run it for real, one module list in one change.
3. `crates/tui/tests/feature_registry.rs:10` carries `#[path = "../src/features.rs"] mod features;`. Update the include to the new location (`../../runtime/src/features.rs`) or switch the test to the runtime export if `features` is made `pub` there. Keep `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` green — it is the `docs/features.toml` drift guard and must keep failing on flag drift.
4. `grep -rn 'crates/tui/src/\(child_env\|logging\|external_credentials\|dsh_credentials\|shell_dispatcher\|runtime_policy\|process_tree\|features\|runtime_log\|working_set\)' --include='*.rs'` must be empty (the sweep leaves CHANGELOG history alone; that is intended).
5. `python3 scripts/split/module_graph.py --check` — totals must be unchanged (these modules never counted). If a count moved, a real reference appeared; fix it, do not raise the baseline.
6. `scripts/split/widen.py` only if the compiler reports privacy errors from the move.

## Done when

- [ ] The ten modules live under `crates/runtime/src/` with `pub mod` lines in `crates/runtime/src/lib.rs`; the TUI's `mod` lines are gone and the alias block names all ten
- [ ] `crates/tui/src` no longer contains these files; no stale path strings outside CHANGELOG
- [ ] `cargo check` for both crates is clean and `feature_registry` passes
- [ ] Ratchet `--check` passes with **no** baseline edit

## Verification

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-runtime --all-targets --locked
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --locked
scripts/dev-test.sh runtime
scripts/dev-test.sh tui features
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry --locked
python3 scripts/split/module_graph.py --check
```

Quote the real `test result: N passed; M failed` lines and the ratchet `PASS` line in the PR.

## Out of scope

- `conformance` — it is `#[cfg(test)]`-gated and its user (`extension_host/protocol/tests.rs:471`) is also in the runtime closure; a cross-crate `cfg(test)` module is invisible to the other crate's test build, so it moves together with its user in RS-14
- `test_support` — carries `#[cfg(test)]` and UI fixtures; that split is RS-11
- `computer_meter` — it is `pub mod` today, i.e. a published-surface decision; handle it in RS-14's public-surface inventory
- Behaviour changes anywhere; new re-exports; new tests or comments (repo rule)

---

**Series:** RS-8 #6935 · RS-9 #6936 · RS-10 #6937 · RS-11 #6938 · RS-12 #6939 · RS-13 #6940 · RS-14 #6941 (keystone; blocked by the rest). Umbrella: #5316.

issues.title: Turn snapshots fail with "git commit-tree failed: fatal: <sha> is not a valid object" since 2026-10-12 (0.10.0 after rollback from 0.10.1); old user turns are re-delivered
issues.body:
Hello,

I would like to report a defect in CodeWhale 0.10.0. We run it on Windows 11 in daily work, and the instance
in question holds a long-running session (about 99 MB) that we would very much like to keep. The problem has
been with us since 12 October 2026.

**Environment**

- CodeWhale **0.10.0** (npm package installed globally). Binary: `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\codewhale\bin\downloads\codewhale.exe`,
  100 331 520 bytes, last written **2026-10-12 15:48**.
- Current version in npm: **0.10.1**.
- Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 10.0.26100, git 2.55.0.windows.5.
- Data dir `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale`; workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale`.
- Session journal `sessions\fd452c83-….json`: **98 989 231 bytes** (it was ~72 MB on 2026-10-12 and grows).

**Symptom 1 — every turn snapshot fails**

```
WARN snapshot: snapshot 'pre-turn:2: <first words of a user message>' failed:
     git commit-tree failed: fatal: 6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9 is not a valid object
```

**Symptom 2 — old user turns are re-delivered as new input**

Because snapshots never complete, past turns are never marked done and are fed back. The order is stable and
reproducible: in the most recent run the app re-delivered turns 2, 3 and 4 — the same three messages, in the
same order, as in every previous run (logs `tui-2026-10-14-20628`, `-14004`, `-23528`). The user sees his own
old messages answered again.

**Symptom 3 — shell operations frequently fail**

```
WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: shell work-graph registration skipped;
     running without a bound operation shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=To-do state is busy; operation was not registered

WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: failed to reconcile shell lifecycle shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=operation binding shell:shell_<hex> is not registered
```

273 such lines in the logs; on the user's side roughly every 3rd–4th shell call fails. Possibly the same root
cause as the snapshot failure.

**Symptom 4 — at startup the store looks empty**

```
WARN snapshot: boot prune failed: git log failed: fatal: bad object HEAD
```

**When it started**

- first occurrence: **2026-10-12T16:00:16Z** — `snapshot prune failed: commit-tree failed: fatal: c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c is not a valid object`;
- 458 lines containing “is not a valid object” in total, over four runs;
- only two lost objects in total: `6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9` and `c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c`.

**What correlates with the date**

On the same day the user updated to **0.10.1** and then **rolled back to 0.10.0**. The package directory is
stamped **2026-10-12 15:48** (the rollback), and the first snapshot failure is at **19:00** local time.
Hypothesis: a snapshot store was begun by 0.10.1, and after the rollback 0.10.0 cannot complete that chain.

**What we tried**

- Reinstalled the same version (`npm install -g codewhale@0.10.0`) — **no effect**. The store is not part of
  the program files; `boot prune failed: bad object HEAD` still appears and snapshots still fail with the same SHA.

**Where we looked for the store (found nothing)**

Workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale` (not a git repo; only `.codewhale\state` with subagent state);
`%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` (no `work-graph`, `objects`, `refs`, `.git` — only `sessions\.work-graph-import-archive`);
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `%APPDATA%` (depth 4); `%TEMP%`; the app package dir (only `bin`, `scripts`, `test`,
`package.json`, `README.md`); the app's `state.db` is empty and stale (2026-10-04).

**Questions**

1. Where are the snapshot store and the work-graph kept, and how can a corrupted chain be repaired on the
   user's side?
2. How can the **turn queue / parent-commit pointer** be reset so that snapshots work again and old turns stop
   being re-delivered **without discarding the session**? The session is 99 MB and losing it would be costly.
3. Is the `To-do state is busy` shell failure the same root cause as the snapshot failure? Both began in the
   same period.

**Related: cannot move to 0.10.1 with a long session**

On 2026-10-12 we also tried 0.10.1: it installs cleanly, but resuming our session fails:

```
error: selected saved history could not be captured
caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The session file was ~72 MB then and is **98 989 231 bytes** now, so this bound will trigger even more readily.
We cannot test 0.10.1 — and therefore cannot check whether it fixes the snapshot store — while it stands.
Is there a way to raise or bypass it?

**Materials available on request**

Full log excerpts (458 snapshot lines, 273 work-graph lines), the environment dump, and our extended Russian
report. Happy to attach or translate anything you need.

Thank you for the tool, and for taking the time to look at this. I will gladly provide any further logs,
dumps or reproductions you need.

Best regards,
Sergej Malevich

issues.title: A new approach to significantly reduce token consumption

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What problem does this solve? 要解决什么问题？

Significantly reduce context overhead

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx

A significant reduction in token consumption through FastCtx, rather than through model compression or conversation summarization. The actual amount of token savings depends on how the Agent is used and the type of tasks.

Core principles:

**1. Batch reading:** Read multiple files or code ranges in a single call, reducing the number of tool invocations and repeated reads.
**2. Limit output length:** Set output budgets for file reading, searching, and command execution to avoid irrelevant content consuming context.
**3. Reduce redundant operations:** Simplify command execution through structured tools, minimizing syntax errors, failed retries, and redundant work.
**4. Optimize truncation handling:** Clearly indicate omitted content and allow on-demand log retrieval, avoiding repeated execution of already completed commands.
**5. Simplify tool descriptions:** Shorten MCP tool descriptions to reduce token consumption from the tool definition itself.
**6. Background task execution:** Run time-consuming tasks such as building and testing in the background, and retrieve results only when needed, reducing repeated polling and output.

### Where? 在哪里？

_No response_

Release notes

Sourced from @​modelcontextprotocol/client's releases.

@​modelcontextprotocol/client@​2.3.0

Minor Changes

  • #2901 433eb41 Thanks @​claude! - The HTTP client transports and the OAuth client helpers now follow a redirect only when it stays within the origin of the request (same scheme, host and port, or http to https on the same host with default ports) and keeps the method (a 307 or 308, or any redirect of a GET). Any other redirect is not followed. A transport then fails the request with an error that names the target; the session is kept and later messages still send. OAuth metadata discovery moves on to the next well-known URL, and any other OAuth request fails with an error that gives the status. Same-origin redirects that keep the method keep working on Node, up to five in a row, and no code changes are needed there. If your endpoint redirects to another origin, configure the transport with the URL it redirects to. A requestInit.redirect of 'error' or 'manual' is passed to fetch as it is for the requests a transport sends to the server (POST, GET and DELETE of the Streamable HTTP transport, POST of the SSE transport); for its OAuth requests, and for any other value, requestInit.redirect is not consulted by default. Browsers do not expose the target of a redirect to a page, so there a redirected request fails instead of being followed. Setting redirectPolicy: 'follow' on a transport leaves its redirects to the fetch implementation, as before this change.

Patch Changes

  • #2599 5238fba Thanks @​freya0926! - A server can now serve, and a client can now call, tasks/get and tasks/cancel of the Tasks extension (SEP-2663) on a 2026-07-28 connection, when the handler is registered and the request is sent with an explicit schema. Every other method that a protocol revision removed is still refused. If one server factory serves both eras and such a handler is meant for 2025-era clients only, register it only when ctx.era === 'legacy'.

  • #2846 63c0fca Thanks @​Sthreal! - Receiving a large message as a single SSE event over Streamable HTTP, such as a tool result of tens of megabytes, is now fast: a 50 MB result that took about 13 seconds arrives in under a second. The client now requires eventsource-parser 3.0.8 or later. SSEClientTransport reads through the eventsource package and gets the same speed-up once that also resolves eventsource-parser 3.0.8 or later.

  • #2908 633dd3e Thanks @​claude! - The license field of the package manifests is now Apache-2.0; the LICENSE file shipped in each package carries the full terms, including the MIT text for earlier contributions. No code change.

  • #2903 e765b3b Thanks @​claude! - With versionNegotiation in 'auto' or pin mode, a server/discover probe answered with a 2xx that carries no usable reply (a body that is not JSON under application/json, a bare 204, a missing or unaccepted content type) still rejects connect() with EraNegotiationFailed; an empty SSE stream or a 202 surfaces as the probe timeout instead. The message now says the server answered with an unusable reply (...) instead of reading like a network failure. To connect to a 2025 server behind a front that answers the probe this way, pass connect(transport, { prior: { kind: 'legacy' } }) or use mode: 'legacy'.

  • #2905 c0cd01a Thanks @​claude! - SSEClientTransport now retries the SSE connection once after onUnauthorized() resolves, as documented. If the retry is also answered with 401, start() rejects with SdkHttpError (ClientHttpAuthentication) instead of calling onUnauthorized() again. A 401 on a later reconnect of a stream that had opened still gets one refresh.

    • @​modelcontextprotocol/core@​2.3.0

prs.title: fix(tui): keep a to-do row's status word when its title is long
prs.body:
## What and why

The work surface gives a row's label the whole width and the detail only what is left, and drops the detail under four columns. A to-do whose title fills the strip loses its status word. With a three-step to-do list at 80×24, before:

```
 To-do · 1/3 · 2 left
 1 · ✓ Read the README to learn the layout                            completed
 2 · ▸ Search the workspace for every README and compare their install secti...
 3 · ○ Write up the differences                                         pending
```

After:

```
 To-do · 1/3 · 2 left
 1 · ✓ Read the README to learn the layout                            completed
 2 · ▸ Search the workspace for every README and compare their ...  in progress
 3 · ○ Write up the differences                                         pending
```

The step that lost its word is the in-progress one, the row most worth reading. `todo_rows_carry_their_status_words` already pins that the words are projected and painted; this keeps them painted when the title is long. Plan-step (to-do) rows, picked by the same `plan_step_row_ids` set the strip's filter uses, now reserve the detail's width, capped at half the row, before the title is truncated. A title that fits renders as before, and the hover still carries the full title.

Other rows keep giving the label the room. I tried the reservation on every row first, and at 60 columns the Context budget row cut its numbers (`6.5k of 128.0k · 5% · com...`) to show more of the `/context for the full source map` hint, so it stays on to-do rows only. The first version keyed on the `graph:` id prefix; on a side rail that also matched the operation and blocker nodes listed under the to-dos, so the second commit checks the plan-step ids instead and those rows keep the label-first layout. Background task rows (`status · id`) aren't changed either.

## Issue

No-Issue: a long to-do title drops its status word in the work surface; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock that answers with `read`, `file_search` and a three-item `todo_write`, with this change and with a build from before it. The screens above are 80×24. At 60×16 the in-progress row goes from `Search the workspace for every README and compare...` to `Search the workspace for every READM...  in progress`; at 48×16 row 1 goes from `...` in place of its word to `completed`, and row 2 gains `in progress`. At 120×30, where the titles fit, the strip is unchanged.
- Walked the Cost, Git, Context and Files tabs at 80×24 and 60×16 with both builds: identical.
- With `work_surface_placement = "left"` and a 60-column rail, main drops `in progress` from the long row and this shows it; the `Read 1 files · Searched 1 patterns` row under the to-dos is unchanged. The strip rows are the same with and without the second commit. I couldn't get the mock to produce an operation or blocker node, so for those rows I'm relying on the id check: they take the same path as on main.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15347 passed, none failed, including the work surface tests and the shared-body-vs-frozen-body comparison.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on cc4b96dc0; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): put the approval footer's separators between its hints
prs.body:
## What and why

The approval card's footer starts with a dangling dot and runs its last hint into the one before it. A `bash` approval at 100×30, before:

```
❯ [3 / d / n] Don't allow (Enter)
  [Esc] Stop this turn
    ·  Pg↑/↓ review  ·  ⌥V details  ·  Esc stop  s allow now, and always ask before this again
```

After:

```
❯ [3 / d / n] Don't allow (Enter)
  [Esc] Stop this turn
  Pg↑/↓ review  ·  ⌥V details  ·  Esc stop  ·  s allow now, and always ask before this again
```

`ApprovalControlsHint` still opens with the `  ·  ` that once joined it to the "Choose: ..." prose; the per-option key badges replaced that prose, and the footer now starts its own line. `ApprovalSaveAskRuleHint`, appended right after it, has only two spaces, so "Esc stop  s allow now" reads as one item. This moves the separator from the front of `ApprovalControlsHint` and `ApprovalControlsHintChild` to the front of `ApprovalSaveAskRuleHint`, in all 15 packs, so the line starts at the option rows' column. Nothing else in the strings changes. A child agent's card already joins its `g go to agent` hint with `  ·  ` in `child_footer_controls`.

What it doesn't do: when the footer wraps (80 columns and narrower), the second row still starts at column 0. That wrapping is in the vendored `DecisionBand`, which I left alone.

## Issue

No-Issue: the approval footer's separators are misplaced; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock that asks to run a `bash` command, with this change and with a build from before it. The screens above are 100×30. At 80×24 and 60×20 the footer reads the same way before it wraps, and under `LC_ALL=zh_TW.UTF-8` it reads `Pg↑/↓ 回看  ·  ⌥V 詳情  ·  Esc 停止  ·  s 本次允許，以後每次先詢問`. In each case the footer row is the only line that changed.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-localization`: 54 passed, none failed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15347 passed, none failed, including the approval tests that look for the footer hints.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on cc4b96dc0; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: refactor(commands): adopt portable core navigation Shapes (FEAT-031)
prs.body:
## Summary

Completes the **13-command core navigation slice** behind portable command Shapes, in preparation for later crate extraction. No intended user-visible behavior change.

Commands: `/anchor`, `/help`, `/hotbar`, `/links`, `/transcript`, `/turn`, `/home`, `/overview`, `/workspace`, `/translate`, `/voice`, `/voicesend`, `/voicecontrol` (all existing aliases retained).

- Commands own parsing, branching, formatting and rendering; host adapters supply typed facts and narrow effects. Shared metadata/results/actions/payloads have no App/TUI dependency.
- Keep the existing `u32` capability identities; use bits 30/31 for navigation/voice input. Unrelated commands do not gain these new facet slots. The existing WORKSPACE facet does now expose confined anchor operations to its consumers; per-operation authority narrowing remains an acknowledged design follow-up.
- Remove the obsolete App-bound implementations, retain confined anchor I/O and workspace semantics, and move the unchanged voice capture runtime outside the movable command closure. Builtin voice shortcuts cannot be hijacked by a shadowing user command.
- Compile the actual complete production root independently through unpublished `tests/portable-core-navigation`. Check all 13 registrations exactly once in relative order, complete source closure, all-target normal dependency graph and rejection controls. Integrate CI/developer routing and release-order validation.

This is intentionally one coherent slice: the diff includes moved host tests/runtime and shared-contract consumer updates, rather than shipping parallel implementations. **The other 27 core registrations remain out of scope, the `core` frontier remains pending, and no physical crate movement is claimed.**

## Current security repair — ccbc86312 (2026-10-20)

Fixed the two red bridge audits with a narrow lockfile-only update: `follow-redirects` **1.16.0 → 1.16.1** in Feishu and WeCom. No SDK/manifests/other package changes and no audit exceptions. Clean locked installs, syntax checks, **19 Feishu tests** and **17 WeCom tests** passed; both local audits report zero vulnerabilities.

Both hosted audits are now **SUCCESS at ccbc86312**, with downloaded artifacts confirming zero vulnerabilities: [Feishu](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/39494873546/job/118877201577), [WeCom](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/39494873546/job/118877201722). Other new-head checks and maintainer merge timing remain separate. [Repair details](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7009#issuecomment-6301145344).

## Earlier follow-up — 2152e4df6 (2026-10-20)

The maintainer-account review approved the prior implementation, with merge held until after the 0.10.2 tag and fresh main/CI qualification. The WORKSPACE authority split is explicitly tracked on the maintainers' side.

[2152e4df6](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/2152e4df6) fixes the two remaining small nits: proof-message spacing and builtin voice lookup by `VOICE_INFO.name`, not array index. User-command overrides remain bypassed. Preserved the maintainer's latest `49767fceb` merge; no published history was rewritten or force-pushed.

Fresh integrated checks: **1,215 native command tests**, **9 portable tests**, **7 proof controls**, formatting and scoped TUI Clippy passed. Existing assertions cover shadowed voice, pure named dispatch and missing-name failure. Compiled-host input refreshed. New-head CI is running; previous full-suite/coverage results below are historical, not new-head measurements. [Reply](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7009#issuecomment-6299241753).

## Earlier review follow-up — 6e73d36cb

Preserved the maintainer's `fc5ac7d904` merge, then addressed the two merge blockers and the developer-routing/proof-maintenance findings in [6e73d36cb](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/6e73d36cb). [Point-by-point response](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7009#issuecomment-6236636441).

- Blocking-call allowance relocated, total unchanged at 540; both localization guides corrected.
- Native command paths run host tests again; proof tolerates unrelated registrations while rejecting omissions, duplicates and reordering. Heavy main/PR lint now checks source and normal dependency closure.
- Fresh focused checks: **1,215 native command tests (all 34 relocated host tests), 9 portable tests, 7 proof controls, 34 blocking-call controls**, workflow regression, formatting and web facts/docs passed.
- Workspace/anchor per-operation authority remains an explicitly documented **unresolved design follow-up**. No silent widening or renumbering of `u32`.
- This new commit is signed off; existing published history was not rewritten. New-head hosted CI/review and maintainer merge remain pending.

## Original preservation and verification (historical inputs below)

- Captured 1,125 native observations across 15 locales before migration; subsequent replays were byte-identical for messages, actions, state and persisted bytes. Preserved all 44 original scoped test identities and strengthened existing behavior assertions.
- Fresh Linux full workspace: **19,075 passed, 0 failed, 34 configured skips**. Instrumented full workspace: the same counts. Doctests: 3 passed, 8 ignored.
- Native/PTY selection: 58 passed. Actual portable navigation: 9 passed plus 7 rejection controls. Config portability: 35 passed. Architectural boundary/migration controls: 30/63 passed.
