prs.title: perf(picker): stop rebuilding catalogs per model row when /model opens
prs.body:
## Summary

Opening `/model` froze the whole TUI. On a machine with 52 configured
routes and 3,444 catalog rows it took 3-4 seconds; it now takes ~150 ms,
measured both before and after with temporary in-process marks that are
not part of this PR.

Four independent causes, each fixed in its own commit:

**1. One relay's catalog was rebuilt once per model row.** Three separate
seams each repeated work that depends only on the route:

- `cached_entry_for_route` returned a deep clone of the whole cached
  entry, so every row cloned every offering. On a 176-model relay that
  was 30,976 `CatalogOffering` copies for one picker open.
- `catalog_offering_for_route` then rebuilt the provider's owned
  bundled + Models.dev row map per row, cloning ~60 rows and allocating a
  fresh `BTreeMap` each time.
- `resolve_for_model` re-ran the credential resolver (secret store
  included) and the auth-class classification per row, and
  `route_identity_for_model` inside it ran the class walk a second time.

`with_cached_entry_for_route` lends the entry to a callback;
`source_rows_for_provider` is memoized on the live generation;
`RouteReadinessScope` hoists the route-scoped readiness facts.

**2. `route_is_valid_for_model` re-projected the whole bundled catalog per
row.** It called `RouteResolver::new()`, and `new()` = `from_offerings(
default_offerings())`, which re-projects every text-chat row of the
committed Models.dev asset plus the corrections pass and the
de-duplication maps. On 176 rows that is 176 full catalog projections.
`RouteResolver::bundled()` now shares one `OnceLock`-guarded resolver;
`new()` and `with_configured_models` are unchanged for callers that add
route-specific offerings.

**3. The `auto` row built a full `ModelInventory` for one line of text.**
`auto_picker_hint` read four router facts and paid for every configured
route's every model through runtime route resolution: 308 ms of a
1048 ms build. The router block never reads `candidates`, so
`ModelInventory::auto_router_only` skips only the candidate loop. No
logic is duplicated.

**4. `offerings_for_provider_identity` scanned the whole merged catalog
per row.** It walked every offering and computed
`catalog_partition_key` -- a `trim().to_string()` -- for each one, so a
3,444-row build over a few thousand offerings spent tens of millions of
string allocations on provider lookups. This was the largest single
stage (662 ms of 757 ms). `SharedSnapshot` now carries a
`provider -> rows` index built once with the snapshot.

## Measurements

Stage marks from the temporary instrumentation, same machine, opening
`/model` once per run:

| stage | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` row | 308 ms | 1.1 ms |
| per-row metadata | 663 ms | 79 ms |
| per-row readiness | 16.8 ms | 13.5 ms |
| per-row receipt | 12.8 ms | 10.1 ms |
| per-row push | 12.3 ms | 4.7 ms |
| **total picker build** | **1048 ms** | **149 ms** |

Per-route detail moved with it: `openrouter` (390 rows) 108.6 ms ->
17.0 ms, `edenai` (334 rows) 95.9 ms -> 17.8 ms, `openai` (177 rows)
48.0 ms -> 7.7 ms.

These numbers come from one machine and are quoted as an indication of
which seams mattered, not as a guarantee. The next bottleneck on a
large-route setup is `cloud_facts::overlay::snapshot()`, which takes the
process-wide overlay **write** lock once per row for every non-custom
provider; this PR does not touch it.

## Correctness

Nothing here changes observable behavior; each commit is a caching or
hoisting change behind an existing seam.

- `catalog_offering_for_route` keeps all five outcomes exactly: listed
  (row cloned and completed from lower layers), fetched-but-unlisted
  (only an attested-unlisted row, never a fall-through to the bundled
  merge), `fetched_at == 0`, absent entry, and cache error.
- `source_rows_for_provider`'s memo key is `(live generation, cloud
  generation or a sentinel, live layer present)`. The generation is
  sampled **before** the caller reads `LIVE_SNAPSHOT`, the ordering
  `merged_snapshot` already documents, so a concurrent refresh cannot
  leave stale rows tagged with the current generation.
- `SharedSnapshot`'s index uses the same `catalog_partition_key`
  derivation and preserves offering order, so `offerings_for_provider`
  returns the same rows in the same relative order as the scan it
  replaces.
- `auto_router_only` cannot change a router field: every one of them is
  derived from `config` after the loop, never from `candidates`.
- `RouteResolver::bundled()` is `Self::new` under a `OnceLock`, and
  `new()` has no environment, config, clock or network input, so it
  cannot freeze a stale answer. `resolve` takes `&self`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Performance (no behavior change)

## Testing

- [x] `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- provider_lake model_picker provider_picker provider_readiness client::catalog_tests model_inventory pricing` -> **411 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored**
- [x] `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- route::` -> **102 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored** (commit 2 adds a public API in this crate)
- [x] `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib` -> clean
- [x] `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on all four changed files -> clean
- [x] `cargo build --release -p codewhale-cli -p codewhale-tui` -> Finished
- [x] The reported symptom was re-measured end to end on the reporting
      machine: 3-4 s before the chain, ~150 ms after.

## Notes for review

- Two additions are worth calling out because they are not pure caching:
  a second permanently resident `RouteResolver::bundled()` projection
  (a few MB; the client already keeps one), and a 32-entry memo of
  provider partitions that is evicted alphabetically rather than by use.
- The `SharedSnapshot` index normalizes provider keys through
  `catalog_partition_key` (trimmed). No producer of padded provider
  strings was found, so this is a latent change, not an observed one.
- No new tests: project policy. The changed paths are covered by the
  existing suites above; a direct assertion that `bundled()` and `new()`
  resolve identically would be the one test I would add if asked.

## Related Issues

No-Issue: reported as local `/model` latency; no upstream issue was opened.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

prs.title: fix(tui): drop the hotbar setup rows' description stub beside the detail pane
prs.body:
## What and why

From 100 columns up, /keys (Hotbar setup) puts the action list and the selected action's details side by side. The list column is then 40 to 48 wide, and the marker, recommended tag, name and status take 39 of it, so a row's description never gets more than nine columns. At 100×32, before:

```
 │app actions                              Command palette                                        │
 │▸  rec Command palette        ready    … palette.open                                           │
 │   rec Compact session        ready    …                                                        │
 │   rec Cycle reasoning        ready    … Category: app                                          │
 │   rec Operate mode           ready    … Status: ready                                          │
```

After:

```
 │app actions                              Command palette                                        │
 │▸  rec Command palette        ready      palette.open                                           │
 │   rec Compact session        ready                                                             │
 │   rec Cycle reasoning        ready      Category: app                                          │
 │   rec Operate mode           ready      Status: ready                                          │
```

At 120×32 and 140×40 the rows read "Open…", "Shrink…", "Step…", "Do…". The full description is already in the detail pane ("Open the command palette." further down on the right).

So when the layout is split, the rows leave the description out and the detail pane shows it. `render()` already has `layout.stacked`, so it's passed down to `action_row_line`. The stacked layout below 100 columns and the 80-column `render_lines` export keep their descriptions, and a disabled row's reason still follows its status.

## Issue

No-Issue: Hotbar setup rows show a lone "…" or one word of description beside the detail pane, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and opened /keys at 60×16, 80×24, 97×30, 98×30, 100×32, 120×32 and 140×40, with this change and without it. The four stacked sizes (up to 98×30) are byte-identical before and after. At 100, 120 and 140 the rows end after the status column, and so does the slash tab at 100.
- The one existing `action_row_line` test call passes `true` for the new argument, and its word-boundary truncation assertions still hold.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15347 passed, none failed, including the hotbar setup tests.

prs.body:
## What and why

When the frame is too short for all eleven /statusline items, the list shows what fits and scrolls with the cursor, but nothing says more items are below. At 40×12, before:

```
 │ Choose what the footer shows:      │
 │                                    │
 │  ▸ [✓] Mode  (plan · work ·…)      │
 │    [✓] Model  (the model id…)      │
 │    [✓] Context window %  (tokens…) │
 │    [✓] Session cost  (running…)    │
```

```
 │ Choose what the footer shows:      │
 │                                    │
 │  ▸ [✓] Mode  (plan · work ·…)    █ │
 │    [✓] Model  (the model id…)    █ │
 │    [✓] Context window %  (token…)│ │
 │    [✓] Session cost  (running…)  │ │
 │  Space toggle   a all   n none     │
```

/theme, /help, the session and file pickers and the settings list already use `render_panel_scroll_rail` for this, so the item rows here do too. prs.title: fix(tui): end a clipped /feedback description at a word, with an ellipsis
prs.body:
## What and why

The /feedback picker lets the card edge cut each option's description, so below about 80 columns the rows end mid-word with nothing to say the text was cut. At 40×12, before:

```
 │ ▸ 1. Bug report    Report a proble │
 │   2. Feature request    Suggest an │
 │   3. Security vulnerability    Rev │
```

After:

```
 │ ▸ 1. Bug report    Report a…       │
 │   2. Feature request    Suggest…   │
 │   3. Security vulnerability    Re… │
```

At 60×16 the third row went from "Review the security pol" to "Review the security…".

/mode had the same problem and truncates its hints at a word boundary at the width left after the prefix, so this does the same: it measures the number, label and gap that are actually painted and truncates the description to the rest with `codewhale_ratatui::text::truncate_words`. That's the same word-boundary cut, but it spends `...` in ASCII-safe mode, where the backend would otherwise draw `…` as a lone `.` and "Review the security…" would read as a finished sentence. The third row at 40×12 has three columns left, so it gets the shortest form, "Re…" ("Re." in ASCII-safe mode). It's still not a whole word, but it now shows it was cut. Where the descriptions fit, as at 80×24 and 100×32, nothing changes.

## Issue

No-Issue: /feedback descriptions are cut mid-word at narrow widths, no issue filed for it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and opened /feedback at 40×12, 50×14, 60×16, 80×24 and 100×32, with this change and with a build of d5f6699cc (the file is unchanged since). 80×24 and 100×32 are byte-identical before and after; the three narrower sizes differ only in the description text.

prs.title: ci(sync): skip the CNB mirror when its token secret is absent
prs.body:
## What

`sync` fails on every push to a mirrored branch when the `CNB_GIT_TOKEN` repository secret is absent: "CNB_GIT_TOKEN secret is not set; cannot push to CNB." That is a repository-secret state, not a property of the commit — forks can never inherit the secret, so they report a red check no contributor can fix.

A `credentials` gate job probes the secret and skips the push when it is absent, emitting a notice that names the missing secret. Configured repositories keep the previous behavior, including the existing hard failure inside the push step, which still covers a caller pinned to an older revision of this workflow plus the window where the secret is deleted between the gate's probe and the push step.

`docs/CNB_MIRROR.md` documents the skip path and distinguishes "skipped because absent or misspelled" from "failed because expired" in the rotation section.

## Tests

- Workflow-parse level: jobs `credentials` + `sync`, `sync.if = needs.credentials.outputs.configured == 'true'` (verified locally; CI exercises the rest).
- The skip path is exercised by forks of the repository, where the secret cannot exist.

Co-authored with @zhuowp (original patch in the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork, #64); adapted to this workflow's retry/concurrency/`workflow_call` plumbing.

No-Issue: CI-only; forks cannot inherit CNB_GIT_TOKEN, so Sync to CNB fails on every fork push

prs.title: fix(tui): keep nested list indentation in rendered markdown
prs.body:
## What and why

The transcript's markdown parser trims each line before it looks for a list marker and keeps only the marker and the text, so a nested list renders flat. A reply with

```
- Top level item
  - Second level, indented two spaces
    - Third level, indented four spaces, long enough to wrap at forty columns
- Another top level item

1. Step one
   - detail a under step one
   - detail b under step one
2. Step two
```

renders at 80×24, before:

```
▏ - Top level item
▏ - Second level, indented two spaces
▏ - Third level, indented four spaces, long enough to wrap at forty columns
▏ - Another top level item
▏
▏ 1. Step one
▏ - detail a under step one
▏ - detail b under step one
▏ 2. Step two
```

After:

```
▏ - Top level item
▏   - Second level, indented two spaces
▏     - Third level, indented four spaces, long enough to wrap at forty
▏       columns
▏ - Another top level item
▏
▏ 1. Step one
▏    - detail a under step one
▏    - detail b under step one
▏ 2. Step two
```

Before, the details under "1." read like siblings of the numbered steps. `ListItem` now records the source line's leading whitespace and the renderer paints it before the bullet, so wrapped rows still hang under the item's text. The indent is capped at half the width so a pathological line can't push the text out of the pane. Lists without leading whitespace render as before.

What it doesn't do: a list item's own continuation line in the source (`- item` then an indented line of prose) is still a paragraph and renders flush left, and a tab counts as one column. A top-level list the model indents by one to three spaces now shifts right by that much, since the renderer paints what was written.

## Issue

No-Issue: nested markdown lists render flat in the transcript; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock that streams a canned reply, with this change and with a build from before it. The screens above are from the nested reply at 80×24; 40×12 shows the same indentation. A reply whose lists all start at column 0 (`-`, `*`, `1.` to `10.`, with wrapped items) renders the same list rows before and after at 80×24 and 40×12. In a longer reply, `   - nested bullet` under `2. Second item` now sits under "Second item", with its wrapped path row under it.
- Checked that nothing outside `crates/tui/src` matches on `ListItem`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15347 passed, none failed, including the markdown render tests and the incremental-vs-full reparse test, whose corpus has a nested list.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on cc4b96dc0; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

issues.body:
## Summary

On heavy-traffic agents (frequent user messages arriving mid-turn + subagent workflows), the internal constant `STEERING_TOOL_SKIP_MESSAGE` (**"Skipped to process an incoming message."**) sometimes reaches the end user as the turn's final visible reply on messaging channels (WhatsApp in our case).

## Source findings

In `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts` (built: `dist/agent-core-iKDcH8nh.mjs`):

```js
const STEERING_TOOL_SKIP_MESSAGE = "Skipped to process an incoming message.";
```

It's emitted as an error-flagged tool result (`status: "skipped", deniedReason: "steering"`) when a steering message interrupts an in-flight tool call. This is model-facing context, never user-facing content.

## Reproduction pattern

1. Agent is mid-turn executing a tool call (write/exec etc.) in a multi-tool turn
2. A new inbound user message arrives (steering)
3. Runtime skips the in-flight tool and injects the skip note as the tool result
4. The turn ends (or is yielded for subagent settlement) without substantive user-facing content
5. The skip note / internal status text is dispatched as the final reply → visible on WhatsApp

Same family: "Turn yielded." settlement notices and subagent-settle context have been observed leaking the same way on settlement turns with no user-facing payload.

## Expected behavior

Internal notes (steering skips, yield confirmations, settlement context) should be filtered from the outbound message pipeline — a turn with no user-facing content should stay silent (or use the NO_REPLY mechanism), never forward internal runtime state.

## Environment

- OpenClaw on macOS (arm64), WhatsApp channel, high-steering workload (video-digest subagent pipeline)
- `channels.whatsapp.streaming.block.enabled = false` did not prevent it (skip note travels the final-reply path, not streaming)

Happy to provide gateway logs or a fuller trace if useful.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash). Not a beta-release blocker.

## Summary

WhatsApp final replies can fail on the first delivery attempt with `No active WhatsApp Web listener` while the inbound connection remains healthy, then arrive only after durable delivery recovery.

## Steps to reproduce

The deterministic source regression exercises `dispatchAssembledChannelTurn` with real durable delivery and synthetic channel transports:

1. Register a connected inbound channel adapter in the gateway registry.
2. Start an inbound turn under that registry, with durable final delivery enabled.
3. Have the reply dispatcher enter a different agent registry containing a separate, unconnected registration for the same channel.
4. Deliver the final reply. Both a DM and a group target select the unconnected registration on unmodified main (`4e002cf7`).

The corresponding live symptom was observed repeatedly on an npm installation with the official WhatsApp plugin: send a short message requesting a pong, observe the missing-listener error after model completion, then successful recovery several seconds later without reconnecting WhatsApp.

## Expected behavior

The original inbound channel's connected adapter sends its reply on the first attempt. The current agent/caller policy and authority remain in force.

## Actual behavior and logs

One redacted live timing sample, September 19, 2026 (PDT):

```text
20:48:06.735 inbound message
20:48:12.750 model completed
20:48:12.830 first delivery failed: No active WhatsApp Web listener (account: default)
20:48:19.112 recovery retry
20:48:19.328 sent message
```

Other observed failed-first-send samples incurred approximately 5–10 seconds waiting for recovery. The connection did not need to reconnect for recovery to succeed.

## Environment

- OpenClaw and official `@openclaw/whatsapp`: 2026.9.5, npm installation.
- Live host: Linux, Node 24.18.0.
- Source regression: main `4e002cf7`, macOS, Node 24.18.0.
- Model/provider: no model or provider request is needed for the deterministic regression; the live failure occurs after model completion.

## Impact and evidence

Observed in direct messages and a configured group. Replies arrived late; message loss was not established. A local 2026.9.5 repair binding durable replies to the inbound adapter removed the failed initial attempt in three subsequent live tests. Two warm requests took 3.726 and 3.828 seconds end to end. The first request after restart still took 14.467 seconds due to preparation/model time, but also sent on its first attempt.

The exact registry transition is deliberately constructed in the regression. Live diagnostics captured successful listener selection after the repair; the failing production owner transition was not captured before it. The new source regression fails on unmodified main and passes after the same ownership repair.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Summary

`$include` resolution now walks documents on an explicit work stack (stack-safe), but the config-loading stages that run **after** include resolution still recurse over the resolved value. A config whose nested value survives include resolution crashes one of the later stages with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, so the operator sees an opaque CLI/Gateway crash instead of a clean schema rejection.

Three recursion points sit on the resolved-value path:

1. `src/infra/deep-merge.ts` — `mergeDeep` and `sanitizePlainObject` clone/walk the resolved tree recursively.
2. `src/config/env-substitution.ts` — `substituteAny` walks containers recursively while substituting `${...}` values.
3. Legacy migration probes — load-time `structuredClone(root)` calls (Node's built-in clone is itself recursive) in the legacy config migration probes.

### Steps to reproduce

`deep-config.json` (generated with a script, 4000 levels):

```json
{ "x": { "x": { ... nested 4000 times ... } } }
```

`openclaw.json`:

```json
{ "$include": "./deep-config.json" }
```

```bash
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=./openclaw.json pnpm openclaw config read
# → read failed: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

The include resolver itself accepts the document (it is stack-safe), then the crash happens later in the load chain. Catching the exact stage: patch the `catch` in the config io snapshot path with `process._rawDebug(e.stack)` and run the CLI sources via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` (the installed CLI runs dist, which predates any local change).

### Expected behavior

A deeply nested config is either rejected with the normal, actionable schema error (`Unrecognized key` / validation message) or handled iteratively — not an opaque stack-overflow crash from a stage after the one that already promises stack safety.

### Actual behavior

`RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` from deep-merge, env substitution, or a migration-probe clone, depending on how far the load chain gets.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 / current main

### Operating system

Linux

### Install method

pnpm (repo checkout)

issues.body:
## Summary

In a multi-account Discord setup, a **Gateway-routed** session reply is delivered under the wrong bot identity. Inbound correctly resolves to account `B`, the agent bound to `B` runs the turn, and the reply then goes out as account `A` (the account named `default`).

The equivalent **CLI** path is fine, because it can pass `--reply-account`. There is no equivalent for Gateway-routed inbound, and no per-channel or per-binding outbound account setting, so the reply falls back to the default account.

## Setup

- Six Discord accounts under `channels.discord.accounts`, one of them literally named `default`.
- `channels.discord.defaultAccount` is **not** set.
- A binding routes inbound to the right agent:
  ```json
  { "type": "route", "agentId": "sentinel", "match": { "channel": "discord", "accountId": "sentinel" } }
  ```
- Only the `sentinel` account has the target channel in its `guilds` config.

## Actual behaviour

- Inbound meta for the session reports `account_id: sentinel`.
- The `sentinel` agent runs the turn.
- The reply is posted by the `default` bot, so the message renders under the wrong app name and avatar.
- Identity appears fixed for the life of the session: a session already running keeps replying under the wrong identity for every remaining turn.

Posting to the same channel directly with the `sentinel` bot token succeeds, so this is not credentials, permissions, or channel config — it is isolated to the session reply path.

## Expected behaviour

When inbound resolves to account `X`, and `X` owns the channel, the reply should be delivered as `X` without anyone passing a flag.

## Where it looks like it goes wrong

Delivery resolves the account as:

```js
accountId: opts.replyAccountId ?? opts.accountId
```

So a fallback chain already exists. The CLI path populates `replyAccountId` from `--reply-account`. The Gateway-routed inbound path appears to populate **neither** from the already-resolved inbound account, so resolution falls through to the default account.

## Why config cannot work around it

- `bindings[].accountId` is inbound matching only.
- `channels.discord.defaultAccount` is global — pointing it at `sentinel` would misroute every other channel's replies.
- `agents.entries.*` has no reply/delivery account property (checked against the config schema, not just the docs).

Per `docs/channels/channel-routing.md`, `defaultAccount` "chooses which account is used when an outbound path does not specify `accountId`" — which is exactly what is happening here, except the outbound path *should* have had one available from inbound.

## Impact

Beyond cosmetics: it makes per-channel agent separation unenforceable, and it silently attributes one agent's statements and mistakes to another. In our case an entire multi-hour conversation from one agent was rendered as a different agent.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.9.4`
- Channel: Discord, multi-account
- macOS, Node v24

## Workarounds, both poor

- Post via the correct bot's token directly — double-posts alongside the session reply.
- Ensure the session is born with `--reply-account` — does not help Gateway-routed inbound sessions.

issues.body:
### What happened
A compaction-quality safeguard (rejects finalized compaction summaries that fail internal quality checks — distinct from a separate house-side "flush guard" which exits 0 and isn't involved here) blocked compaction on a growing session three times in a row, with a *different* rejection reasonCode each time (e.g. missing_section → missing_identifiers → duplicate_section) while the session sat at ~74% of its context cap and climbing. The same class hit two other agents on the same gateway within a couple of days, at similarly high context-fill percentages.

### Why it's a defect
The rejection gate is deterministic (same quality checks every time), but the summarizer producing the candidate summary is non-deterministic, so a session that happens to produce borderline summaries can fail the gate indefinitely on different grounds each retry, with zero operator-visible signal that compaction is stuck. A session repeatedly failing this safeguard while still growing will eventually hit its hard context cap with no compaction ever landing.

### Expected behavior
- After N consecutive safeguard rejections on the same session, fall back to a mechanical/deterministic compaction path (or expose an explicit operator override) rather than leaving the session to retry indefinitely.
- Surface an alert/log signal at N consecutive blocks so this is diagnosable before the session hits its cap, not after.
- Consider varying the summarization sampling/prompt on retry so the same borderline output isn't effectively re-rolled blind against the same gates.

### Evidence
Three consecutive same-session rejections within ~50 minutes, three different reasonCodes, session at ~74% of a ~270k-token cap and growing; two more same-class rejections on two other agents within the same 48h window on the same gateway.

### Environment
OpenClaw 2026.8.x, multi-agent single gateway.

issues.body:
### Summary

On macOS the desktop app accepts only **one Talk Mode turn per launch**. The first voice exchange after launching works end to end; from the second turn onward the app captures nothing — neither the wake word nor push‑to‑talk. Quitting and reopening the app restores exactly one more turn.

### Versions / environment

- macOS app: **2026.9.4** (build 2609000490) — the latest published macOS build
- Gateway / CLI: **2026.9.5** (also reproduced with gateway 2026.9.4)
- macOS **27.0**, MacBook Air M4
- `talk.realtime.mode = stt-tts`, `talk.realtime.transport = gateway-relay`, `talk.speechLocale = es-ES`
- App prefs: `swabbleEnabled = 1`, `voiceWakeTriggersTalkMode = 1`, `voicePushToTalkEnabled = 1`, `talkRealtimeRelayEnabled = 1`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway running. Launch the macOS app.
2. Say the wake word and ask something → transcribed, agent replies, TTS plays. Works.
3. Ask again, either with the wake word or with push‑to‑talk (right Option) → **nothing at all reaches the gateway**: no transcript event, no RPC, no log line, no error.
4. Quit and reopen the app → step 2 works again, exactly once.

### Expected vs actual

**Expected:** after a Talk turn finishes, capture re-arms and further turns work.
**Actual:** capture is dead until the app is relaunched. The app stays connected (two established sockets to `127.0.0.1:18789`) and still serves other RPCs (`browser.request`, `openclaw.chat`), but emits no talk-related RPC.

### Evidence (transcript timestamps, local time)

| app launched | first turn | reply | further attempts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~10:02 | 10:03:26 | 10:03:29, `talk.speak` 10:03:31 | none arrived |
| ~10:07 | 10:07:36 | 10:07:40 | 3 attempts over 90 s, none arrived |
| ~10:24 | 10:25:09 | 10:25:12 | none arrived |

Between the successful `talk.speak` and the next relaunch the gateway log contains **no entries at all** originating from the app.

### Ruled out by testing

- **Permissions** — Microphone and Speech Recognition both granted in System Settings.
- **`talkShiftToStopEnabled`** — set to `false` with the app closed, verified it persisted across launch. No change.
- **TTS playback clobbering the input device** — set `tts.auto = off`, relaunched, spoke three times: still only the first turn arrived. So it is not the audio output path.
- **Another process holding the microphone** — a browser page using `getUserMedia` was closed; no change.
- **Model / provider route** — reproduced with `freellmapi/auto` and with `anthropic/claude-opus-5` (claude-cli runtime).
- **App/gateway version skew** — reproduced with app 2026.9.4 + gateway 2026.9.4, before any update.

### Impact

Voice is effectively unusable: every exchange requires quitting and reopening the app. This is the primary way the user interacts with the assistant.

### Note on diagnostics

The app writes nothing to the macOS unified log — `log show --predicate 'process == "OpenClaw"'` returns no entries during the failing window — so there is no app-side diagnostic available from outside the app.

### Current workaround

A launchd agent watches the gateway log for `talk.speak` completion and relaunches the app after each exchange, which restores listening automatically.

issues.body:
## Use case
Deployments with multiple session types (long-lived group sessions vs. private 1:1 sessions) have very different transcript growth profiles. Compaction thresholds are currently global-only (`agents.defaults.compaction.*`), so one policy must fit all session types.

Concrete pain: a high-traffic group session accumulates transcript an order of magnitude faster than a private session. Keeping the group healthy forces a choice:
- tight global byte lever (`maxActiveTranscriptBytes`) → over-compresses private sessions that would benefit from the model's full native window, or
- global lever above the model window (never fires) + scheduled resets (`session.resetByType.group: daily`) → coarse, long-lived context lost by design.

## Request
Per-session (or per-session-type / per-channel) compaction overrides, same granularity as session reset policy:
- `session.compactionByType.group.*` / `...direct.*` (mirroring `resetByType`), and/or
- `resetByChannel`-style compaction override keyed by channel id.

Ideally accepts the same keys as `agents.defaults.compaction` (mode, maxActiveTranscriptBytes, keepRecentTokens, etc.).

## Workaround today
Global `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` above the effective model window (guard never fires) + `session.resetByType.group` daily resets + file-based state persistence. Functional but coarse — hence this request.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw `2026.9.4` (dist `3a9d69d`), running on nvm `v24.19.0`
- Linux (OpenCloudOS); gateway is a root `systemd --user` unit `openclaw-gateway.service`
- Reproduced over the WeCom channel (via an iLink relay), but **any** channel (webhook / direct) is affected

## Summary
When the gateway is force-killed (e.g. a stuck drain hits the systemd stop timeout and gets SIGKILL) and a new process recovers the interrupted session, the recovered session's `rootWork` ends up with `released = true`. Because `command-queue` captures async context via `AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot()` and `enqueueCommandInLane` calls `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()`, and that function returns `true` when `currentRootWork.getStore()?.released` is true **without logging anything**, every subsequent top-level inbound message is silently rejected with `GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted`.

The gateway looks perfectly healthy (active / listening / RPC responsive) yet accepts zero new work. Only a full process restart recovers it (a fresh `AsyncLocalStorage`) — which proves this is an in-process leaked state, not a config or on-disk problem.

## Root Cause (located in the 2026.9.4 dist)
**`gateway-work-admission-DaOR_dL4.mjs`** — `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()`:
```js
if (restartDraining || restartSignalPending) return true;
const current = currentRootWork.getStore();
if (current) return current.released;   // <- SILENT: no "admission closed" log
return suspendPhase !== "accepting";
```
The third branch (`current.released`) returns `true` with **no log line**. Compare with `markGatewayRestartDraining()`, which always logs `admission closed: restart drain`. `released` is written at line 54 (`admission.released = true;`) on release/reset paths.

**`command-queue-CwgsqkaH.mjs:595`** — `enqueueCommandInLane`:
```js
if (isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()) return Promise.reject(new GatewayDrainingError());
const runInAsyncContext = AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot(); // carries the leaked released rootWork store into admission checks
```

## Why top-level messages are hit
A freshly received top-level message is enqueued through `enqueueCommandInLane`, which runs inside the async context **inherited** from the request handler. If that context (via the snapshot) still references the leaked `released` rootWork — e.g. the session-recovery / teardown path never established a brand-new rootWork for the inbound request — the subordinate gate rejects it. A brand-new process has a clean `AsyncLocalStorage`, which is exactly why "restart fixes it" and also proof of an in-process leak.

## Reproduction
1. Have a session issue a blocking tool call that waits indefinitely for user input (e.g. `ask_user`) with **no max-lifetime cap**.
2. While that tool call is suspended, force-kill the gateway (e.g. `systemctl --user stop` hits the drain timeout, or SIGKILL) -> systemd restarts it.
3. The new process runs `main-session-restart-recovery` for that interrupted session; the session `rootWork` is marked `released = true` during recovery/teardown.
4. That `released` rootWork context leaks into subsequent inbound request handling via `AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot()`.
5. Send a new top-level message -> `GatewayDrainingError`, and **no** `admission closed` log appears. All other gateway metrics stay normal.

## Proposed Fix
- Top-level / inbound messages should be admitted under a **fresh** rootWork rather than inheriting a possibly-`released` continuation scope. I.e. `enqueueCommandInLane` (or the inbound path) should perform the admission check outside any leaked continuation context; or `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed` should not block a brand-new top-level message because of an inherited `released` rootWork.
- Alternatively: when a rootWork is `released` due to recovery/teardown, ensure its `AsyncLocalStorage` store is not inherited by unrelated subsequent requests (correctly reset context after session recovery).
- **Lowest-cost observability fix:** add a single log line to the `current.released` branch, e.g. `admission closed: released rootWork (subordinate)`. This alone would make such silent rejections visible in health checks — we spent many hours locating this because that branch is completely silent.

## Workaround (shipped locally)
A local watchdog detects "ghost draining" (a `GatewayDrainingError` present in the window but zero intentional-restart signals like `SIGUSR1` / `restart.request` / `admission closed: restart drain` / `graceful shutdown`). On a hit it safe-restarts the gateway to clear the leaked state, with a cooldown to prevent restart storms, then alerts to re-verify the channel callback.

## Severity / Impact
- **High:** the gateway becomes a silent black hole for all inbound messages; health checks show nothing wrong; the only symptom is a per-message `GatewayDrainingError` log. Manual process restart is required to recover (or the watchdog above).
- Affects **all** channels (WeCom / webhook / direct) and triggers downstream cascade — e.g. WeCom pauses the callback URL after repeated anomalous responses (HTTP 200 but abnormal body), requiring a manual re-verify in the admin console.

issues.body:
# [Windows] `openclaw update` always fails: "candidate snapshot" mkdir ENOENT on a path containing an illegal `?` (mangled `\\?\` long-path prefix)

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10.0.26200 (x64)
- Node: v24.18.0
- OpenClaw: 2026.9.4 → 2026.9.5 (npm global install, `~\.openclaw` state dir)
- Gateway launched by a user-local wrapper (`gateway.vbs` → `gateway.cmd`), registered as a Scheduled Task (`OpenClaw Gateway`, AtLogon trigger)

## What happens

Every attempt to update (both via the `/update` chat command and the in-app update flow) ends in a failed update run. The first failure class is always the **candidate snapshot** step:

```
Phase: requested → staging → validating → repairing → finished
validating — global update...
  ✓ global update (86.9s)
  ✗ candidate snapshot (13.5s)
    snapshot: Candidate state snapshot failed (exit): ENOENT: no such file or directory,
    mkdir '~\AppData\Local\Temp\openclaw-update-canary-Q2QGGl\?\$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR\agents\main\agent' (13495ms)
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: runtime-verification-failed.
Failed: candidate snapshot — Exit code: 1
Failed: repairing — candidate rehearsal
Failed: package update — Exit code: 1
```

Structured failure record (`~\.openclaw\logs\support\openclaw-update-failure-*.json`):

```json
{"error":"runtime-verification-failed","result":{"status":"error","mode":"npm","reason":"runtime-verification-failed","root":"~\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\node_modules\\openclaw","before":{"version":"2026.9.4"},"after":{},"recovery":{"serviceRestartSafe":true,"version":"2026.9.4"},"steps":[{"name":"package update","exitCode":1,"stderrTail":"...iled (exit): ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir '~\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\openclaw-update-canary-ceNIEq\\?\\$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR\\agents\\main\\agent'"}]},"omittedDetails":0}
```

## Analysis

The paths in these logs are **redacted** — `~` stands for `%USERPROFILE%` and `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` stands for the state dir (see `dist/diagnostic-support-redaction-*.mjs`:

```js
addPathPrefixVariants(prefixes, options.stateDir, "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR");
addPathPrefixVariants(prefixes, options.env.USERPROFILE, "~");
```

). Undoing the redaction, the failing path is approximately:

```
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\openclaw-update-canary-<id>\?\C:\Users\<user>\.openclaw\agents\main\agent
```

Two problems with that string:

1. It contains a literal `?`. `?` is not a legal character in Windows paths, so `mkdir` can only fail with `ENOENT`.
2. The `\?\` fragment looks like a **mangled `\\?\` long-path prefix** that was *concatenated after* the temp canary directory instead of starting the path. (A `\\?\` prefix is only valid at the very beginning of an absolute path.)

So the canary snapshot appears to build its target path by joining the temp canary dir with a `\\?\`-prefixed absolute path, which normalizes into an unusable path. The result is that the validation phase can never pass on Windows and the update is always marked failed even though `global update` itself succeeded (86.9s).

## Impact

- `/update` is unusable on this host: it fails at validation every time, leaves `Update run: ⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: ...` behind, and never installs/restarts cleanly.
- Subsequent stages also fail once validation is skipped/retried in other ways:
  - `managed-service-handoff-helper-failed` — caused by `schtasks disable` returning `ERROR: Access is denied` while the gateway's Scheduled Task ran with `RunLevel=Limited` (a local-privilege issue on our side, since raised to `Highest`).
  - `restart-unhealthy` — gateway came back but did not pass the post-restart health check.

## Expected

`openclaw update` completes on Windows, or fails with a message that names the real cause instead of an un-constructible path.

## Notes / possibly relevant

- Three channel plugins (`@openclaw/feishu@2026.9.5`, `@openclaw/whatsapp@2026.9.5`, `openclaw-plugin-yuanbao@2.18.3`) additionally fail to register on 2026.9.5 with `Error: Bundled companion is outside the plugin's captured module graph: ...\Temp\openclaw-plugin-build-<id>\package-0\node_modules\...\dist\channel-plugin-api.js` (reproducible via plugin reload / reinstall; `openclaw-qqbot` and `openclaw-weixin` load fine). Possibly a separate issue — reported here only as context.
- `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR` were all unset (Process/User/Machine) on this host; they are now set at User scope. The failure above predates that change and was reproduced after it.

## Reproduction

1. Install OpenClaw globally on Windows (npm), with the state dir at `%USERPROFILE%\.openclaw`.
2. Run `/update` (or the in-app update flow) from a chat.
3. Watch the validation phase: `candidate snapshot` fails with the ENOENT mkdir above.

issues.body:
## Summary

Changing a **non-channel** plugin config under `plugins.entries.*` (for example `active-memory.config.agents`) triggers a hot reload that disposes **all** loaded plugin instances — including stateful channel plugins (`openclaw-lark`, `discord`, `openclaw-weixin`) that hold long-lived WebSocket/long-poll connections — **without reconnecting those channels**. The result: the in-flight streaming reply is cut off ("stopped / 已停止"), the channel's inbound listener goes dead, and all messages sent until a manual Gateway restart are silently dropped with `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools`.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), macOS 27.0 (arm64), Node 26.8.2, npm install
- Gateway reload mode: default `hybrid`
- Channels loaded: `@larksuite/openclaw-lark` (Feishu), `discord`, `openclaw-weixin` — all long-lived connections
- Non-channel plugin changed: `active-memory` (`plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents`)

## Repro steps

1. Run Gateway with default `hybrid` reload mode and at least one long-connection channel plugin (Feishu/Discord/WeChat).
2. Edit only a non-channel plugin's config, e.g. `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents`, and save `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.
3. Observe the Gateway log:
   - `config change detected; evaluating reload (plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents)`
   - the reload plan runs `reloadPlugins` (prefix `plugins` → `kind:"hot"`, `actions:["reloadPlugins","disposeMcpRuntimes"]`)
   - since `channels.*` was **not** touched, `restartChannels` in the plan is empty → channel connections are never re-established
4. Try to send a message via the affected channel → `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin discord/openclaw-lark was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools`.
5. A streaming reply that was in progress when the reload fired gets cut mid-stream (client shows "已停止 / stopped").
6. Inbound messages continue to be dropped until a full Gateway restart.

## Observed behavior

- `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin openclaw-lark was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools` and same for `discord`.
- Active streaming reply card forcibly truncated mid-send.
- Inbound listener inactive; subsequent user messages not dispatched.
- Only a full `openclaw gateway restart` restores the channels.

## Expected behavior

Changing a **non-channel** plugin's config must not tear down long-lived channel connections. Options:

- Only reload plugins that are actually affected by the changed path (do not dispose unrelated channel plugins), **or**
- When `reloadPlugins` fires, force all running channel plugins into `restartChannels` so their WebSocket/long-poll connections are rebuilt in the same cycle, **or**
- Classify `plugins.*` reloads as `restart` (smooth restart) rather than a half-reload that disposes channel instances without reconnecting.

## Root cause (from source)

In `config-reload-plan` (`buildGatewayReloadPlan`), the default policy maps the `plugins` prefix to `kind:"hot"` with `actions: ["reloadPlugins", "disposeMcpRuntimes"]`. `reloadPlugins` disposes **every** loaded plugin instance. Because the edit did not touch `channels.*`, the plan's channel restart list is empty, so channel plugins are disposed but their connections are never rebuilt. Stateless plugins (active-memory, browser) survive a module reload; long-lived channel plugins do not.

## Workaround (current)

Set `gateway.reload.mode: "off"` to disable auto hot-reload and restart the Gateway explicitly after config changes. This avoids the mid-stream breakage but disables the convenience of hot reload entirely.

## References

- Related but distinct: #149612 (provider plugin reload leaves session lane stuck — different symptom, same "reload disposes runtime" family).

### Summary

Add a supported Windows meeting-audio backend so paired Windows Chrome nodes can use `agent` and `bidi` talk-back modes, not only `transcribe`.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 supports isolated meeting audio through `blackhole-2ch` on macOS and `pipewire-pulse` on Linux. On Windows, backend resolution intentionally throws:

> Local Chrome meeting talk-back is unsupported on win32; use transcribe mode or a macOS/Linux Chrome node.

This blocks a common topology: the Gateway runs on a Linux server, while a paired Windows desktop hosts Chrome for Zoom/Meet/Teams. Chrome automation and transcription can run there, but `agent`/`bidi` speech output cannot, so the agent cannot join as a separate speaking participant.

Command overrides alone do not provide a workaround because platform backend selection rejects `win32` before the audio commands are used.

### Proposed solution

Add a first-class Windows meeting-audio backend, using supported Windows audio primitives (for example WASAPI loopback plus an appropriate virtual capture/render device integration), with the same isolation guarantees as the existing macOS and Linux backends.

Requested behavior:

1. `openclaw zoommeetings setup` can provision or validate a supported Windows audio path and report actionable dependency errors.
2. A paired Windows Chrome node supports `transcribe`, `agent`, and `bidi` modes.
3. Participant playback is captured without including room audio or the laptop's physical microphone.
4. Agent speech is injected as the meeting microphone without feeding participant playback back into the meeting.
5. `speechOutputVerified` and interruption/barge-in checks work on Windows.
6. The implementation includes Windows-specific regression tests and setup documentation.

The backend need not mandate a particular third-party virtual cable if OpenClaw can provide or recommend a more robust supported path. If an external driver is required, setup should detect it explicitly rather than silently falling back to a physical mic.

### Alternatives considered

- **Use transcription only on Windows:** works for observe-only use, but does not provide the advertised GPT Live talk-back workflow.
- **Use a macOS/Linux desktop node:** supported today, but requires purchasing or maintaining another machine when the user's always-on local computer is Windows.
- **Turn a headless Linux Gateway into a desktop audio host:** technically possible with a persistent GUI session, Chrome, and PipeWire-Pulse, but brittle and operationally awkward for Zoom admission prompts/CAPTCHA.
- **Patch in VB-CABLE/VoiceMeeter commands:** stock runtime rejects `win32` before command overrides, and an unsupported local patch would need its own lifecycle and safety testing.

### Impact

- **Affected users:** users whose Gateway is remote/headless and whose available paired desktop node is Windows.
- **Severity:** workflow blocker for meeting talk-back; transcription remains available.
- **Frequency:** every `agent` or `bidi` meeting attempt on Windows.
- **Consequence:** users need a separate macOS/Linux desktop or cannot use GPT Live as a speaking meeting participant.

### Evidence/examples

- Backend selection in v2026.9.5: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/meeting-bot/audio-backend.ts#L52-L73
- Windows regression test: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/meeting-bot/audio-backend.test.ts#L8-L34
- Meeting audio setup guide: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/docs/plugins/meeting-plugins.md#L106-L150

Concrete topology: Linux Gateway + paired Windows desktop Chrome node; the human joins from an iPhone while the agent joins as a separate Zoom guest using `bidi` + GPT Live.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

### Additional information

There does not appear to be an existing public issue, PR, or milestone for Windows meeting talk-back support. Maintainer guidance on the preferred Windows audio architecture and whether this is on the roadmap would be helpful.

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow a skill already hosted on the bound execution node to satisfy the same Gateway-selected skill when both trees have the same verified revision, avoiding redundant per-session resource delivery.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw already advertises node-hosted skills and excludes `node://` skills from worker resource delivery. However, when a Gateway skill and a bound-node skill have the same name, the Gateway entry wins and the node entry is renamed. The selected Gateway tree is therefore uploaded for every worker session even when an identical copy exists on the node.

For coding workers with a stable skill set, this adds startup latency and can exceed the aggregate 8 MiB worker-delivery limit. Selecting fewer skills prevents failure but does not remove redundant transfer.

### Proposed solution

- Give node-hosted skill descriptors an immutable revision covering the complete skill tree under the existing bundle rules.
- When preparing a session for a specifically bound node, let a same-name node skill satisfy a selected Gateway skill only when the revisions match.
- Preserve the canonical skill name and `node://` locator for a verified match, and omit that tree from resource delivery.
- On missing or mismatched revision, retain the existing Gateway-delivery behavior; never silently execute stale node content.
- Keep collision renaming for unrelated or unmatched node skills.

This should be additive to the node protocol and require no new user configuration.

### Alternatives considered

- Larger delivery cap: delays the same failure and still transfers unchanged files.
- Select fewer skills: safe fallback, but reduces capability and still retransmits every session.
- Prefer node skills by name alone: unsafe because Gateway and node content can drift.
- Operator-specific prefixed node skill names: brittle and exposes node IDs in agent configuration.

### Impact

- Affected: operators using persistent remote coding or execution nodes with shared skill sets.
- Severity: blocks worker placement once selected skill trees exceed 8 MiB.
- Frequency: every remote session transfers unchanged trees; hard failure occurs at the cap.
- Consequence: slower startup, wasted bandwidth, and failed remote coding placements.

### Evidence/examples

Observed with a remote coding worker: 101 selected skills crossed the 8 MiB limit. Restricting the baseline to 23 skills reduced delivery to 1,347,425 bytes, confirming that skill resources—not repository or prompt size—caused the failure.

Current source already skips `node://` entries during resource delivery, so verified node-local substitution fits the existing architecture.

### Additional information

Supporting files referenced by a skill must be covered by the revision, not only `SKILL.md`. Mismatch should fall back to current delivery behavior rather than fail a session that can still be served safely.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add a public, machine-discoverable graceful-stop handshake for externally supervised Gateway hosts so the external supervisor can commit to no replacement before the Gateway performs its own normal graceful shutdown.

## Problem to solve

When `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external` is used, the external supervisor owns lifecycle decisions, but there is currently no public Gateway-to-supervisor stop authorization/acknowledgement contract.

That leaves a gap for intentional stop. The Gateway can drain work and can arm restart handoff behavior, but an independent external supervisor has no public way to atomically say “this exact Gateway generation may stop and I will not replace it” and then let the Gateway exit through its own graceful shutdown path.

On Windows in particular, relying on an external SIGTERM-equivalent is not a portable contract. Native service-stop commands target OpenClaw's built-in service owner, while `Stop-Process`, `taskkill`, closing a Job Object, or similar process termination shortcuts can bypass normal shutdown cleanup. The result is that a correct external supervisor must currently fail closed rather than implement intentional stop.

This is adjacent to, but distinct from, restart problems such as #90158: restart already has durable replacement handoff semantics, while intentional stop needs an explicit no-replacement authorization path.

## Proposed solution

Expose a small authenticated Gateway RPC/event handshake that reuses the existing Gateway transport, lifecycle state, process identity, drain/suspend machinery, and graceful shutdown implementation.

A concrete shape is:

- Capability: `external-supervisor-stop-handshake-v1`, advertised only when the current Gateway host actually provides external-stop lifecycle support.
- RPC: `gateway.externalSupervisor.register` to bind the supervisor control connection to the exact hosted Gateway generation.
- RPC: `gateway.externalSupervisor.stop.request` to request intentional stop for the exact `pid` + `processInstanceId`.
- Event: `gateway.externalSupervisor.stopRequested` carrying a correlated `requestId`, target identity, reason, and expiry.
- RPC: `gateway.externalSupervisor.stop.respond` with accept/reject for that exact request and connection.

Required semantics:

1. The Gateway requests stop authorization from the registered external supervisor.
2. The supervisor accepts only after persisting its intentional-stop / do-not-replace decision for that exact process generation.
3. On ACCEPT, the Gateway invokes its existing internal graceful shutdown path and exits naturally. No OS signal is required.
4. On REJECT, timeout, disconnect, stale request, wrong PID, wrong `processInstanceId`, or replay, the Gateway remains running and fails closed.
5. Existing restart/restart-handoff behavior remains unchanged and additive.
6. The public capability is feature-detected; consumers must not version-branch.

The contract should be generic for any external supervisor and contain no supervisor-product-specific assumptions.

## Alternatives considered

- `gateway.suspend.handoff` + external SIGTERM: useful for supervisors that deliberately own signaling, but it still requires the supervisor to deliver a platform-specific process signal and does not provide a no-replacement authorization handshake.
- `openclaw gateway stop`: manages the built-in native service owner rather than an independently hosted `gateway run` process.
- `Stop-Process`, `taskkill`, Job Object close, or raw process termination: can bypass the Gateway's own graceful shutdown path and are not an acceptable public lifecycle contract.
- A new ad-hoc localhost HTTP/callback service: duplicates transport/authentication that the Gateway RPC channel already provides and creates a second lifecycle side channel.

## Impact

Affected users/systems: operators embedding or self-hosting OpenClaw under an external lifecycle supervisor, especially on Windows but also cross-platform hosts that want signal-independent stop semantics.

Severity: workflow blocker for a correct intentional-stop implementation under external supervision.

Frequency: every intentional stop when the external supervisor, not OpenClaw's native service wrapper, owns replacement policy.

Consequence: supervisors must either refuse stop, fall back to unsafe process termination, or introduce a private side channel. A public handshake enables deterministic stop without weakening restart semantics or graceful cleanup.

## Evidence/examples

A prototype implementation has been validated against current `main` with:

- exact PID and `processInstanceId` mismatch rejection;
- REJECT keeps the Gateway alive;
- no-ACK expiry keeps the Gateway alive and rejects late responses;
- ACCEPT triggers the existing internal graceful shutdown path;
- source-built Windows Gateway exits naturally with exit code 0 and no signal;
- no restart handoff is created for intentional stop;
- targeted Gateway, lifecycle, infra, protocol-coverage, core typecheck, and source-build checks passing.

The implementation keeps the existing restart handoff contract intact and makes the new capability conditional on a live external-stop host.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The proposed change is intentionally narrow: one public lifecycle capability, three RPC methods, one event, exact-generation safety, tests, and documentation. It reuses existing Gateway auth and graceful shutdown code rather than adding a second shutdown state machine.

### Bug type
Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Official OpenClaw 2026.9.5 Control UI still stalls in WebSocket-driven String.replace / JavaScriptCore Yarr processing during a Computer Use session in a Safari-installed web app, after the fix that closed #143713.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed sequence (not yet a minimized deterministic payload):
1. Open the local Control UI chat in a Safari-installed web app and run an agent turn with text/tool output and a progress card.
2. Invoke the OpenAI Computer Use get_app_state tool against that web app. The first observation returns the complete chat accessibility tree and screenshot.
3. Attempt to collapse the sidebar. The tool reports elementHasNoFrame. A subsequent observation takes approximately 11 seconds, returns only the window/menu shell, and shows the same frozen chat screenshot.
4. While hung, measure WebContent CPU, sample the process for five seconds, and independently probe Gateway health/readiness.

This is one captured live occurrence. Computer Use output/observation coincides with the stall; causation by the accessibility call itself is NOT established.

### Expected behavior
Chat updates, navigation and accessibility observations remain responsive. The initial observation in this same turn returned the complete page; the later one lost the page subtree during the stall.

### Actual behavior
The chat timer and displayed output froze. WebContent reached approximately 100% of one CPU core for about a minute (29 samples >=95%, sampled every two seconds). All 2,418 sampled main-thread stacks in a five-second native sample were in incoming WebSocket processing followed by String.replace and JavaScriptCore Yarr. Gateway health continued returning HTTP 200. The page later caught up without an agent-initiated reload or Gateway restart, so this is a prolonged stall, not a proven infinite loop.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1); live Gateway build 2026.9.5-release-ec9c1a13db89-2026-09-18T18-51-37.323Z

### Operating system
macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon, 16 GiB RAM; WebKit 22625.1.29.11.27

### Install method
Official npm package, local LaunchAgent Gateway; browser-based Control UI in a Safari-installed web app, NOT the native OpenClaw companion app.

### Model
GPT-6 Astra

### Provider / routing chain
OpenClaw -> Codex harness 0.154.0 -> OpenAI

### Additional provider/model setup details
OpenAI Computer Use app version 1001103. No model/provider-specific cause established. Computer Use could still observe Finder and open its Edit menu while diagnosing this occurrence.

### Logs
Sanitized five-second native sample captured September 19, 2026, 12:29:27 UTC:

```text
2418 com.apple.main-thread
  2418 WebCore::WebSocket::didReceiveMessage [queued task]
    2418 WebCore::JSEventListener::handleEvent
      ... JavaScript calls ...
      2418 JSC::stringProtoFuncReplace
        2418 JSC::replaceUsingRegExpSearch
          2418 JSC::Yarr::interpret
            2418 JSC::Yarr::Interpreter<char16_t>::interpret
              ... matchDisjunction / checkCharacterClass / backtracking ...
```

Concurrent first 90 samples (~178 seconds): Gateway /healthz HTTP 200 in all samples, median 1.19 ms, maximum 39.02 ms. /readyz: ready=true, eventLoop.degraded=false. macOS memory-pressure level 1 (normal). WebContent physical footprint at sampling: 900.7 MiB. Computer Use client CPU in the first 46 samples: 0.2–3.1%, median 1.1%; Gateway CPU median 1.5% over that interval. CPU percentages are per-core process measurements, not whole-machine utilization.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Raw screenshots and process sample retained privately because they contain local paths and conversation content. Only the sanitized stack and aggregate measurements are published.

#143713 was closed by merged #147528 (ad157baa20b15c84198674a732f9729cbb9e3115). GitHub compare confirms v2026.9.5 contains that commit (ahead_by=1960, behind_by=0). The prior fix addresses malformed progress raw-content preprocessing. The present sample does NOT identify the exact JavaScript expression, so this may be another preprocessing path rather than failure of that specific scanner.

### Impact and severity
High: the affected browser chat cannot be reliably operated or observed during the stall while the agent/backend continues working. One directly captured occurrence on 9.5; related earlier 9.4 evidence is linked from #143713. No data loss observed.

### Additional information
Searched open issues for Yarr, RegExp/WebSocket, Computer Use freeze, and references to #143713/#147528; no matching open follow-up found. This report covers the remaining live symptom after closure, without claiming the same exact root cause or a newly introduced 9.5 regression.

Current-main runtime reproduction: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. Main SHA observed during triage: b39f188eae55a6ac485af095584dc8d45151a61b; not installed or tested. No Core/dependency changes, restart, or private payload publication performed. Suggested next investigation: isolate the incoming payload/expression and bound synchronous assistant/tool-text preprocessing; retain normal sanitization behavior.

AI-assisted diagnosis/report: OpenAI Codex, GPT-6 Astra.

issues.body:
# [Windows] Event loop stalls of 60–68s: main thread blocked in a synchronous FS syscall while the port keeps listening — external probe + perf + native stack evidence

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), Node.js v24.18.0
- Windows 11 Pro (build 26100), x64, laptop (ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 11, only Modern Standby/S0 available)
- Gateway runs as a Scheduled Task, bound to `127.0.0.1:18789`
- One long-lived gateway process (pid 10524, uptime 3.5 days at the time of the captures below) — the stalls below are **not** restarts or crashes

## Symptom

The gateway repeatedly stops answering for ~1 minute while staying alive:

- the TCP port keeps accepting (`listening: true` throughout),
- the process keeps the same pid and thread count,
- WebSocket clients time out and reconnect (observed as repeated "closed before connect" / WS handshake entries in the daily log).

Three gated "clean" stalls were captured on 2026-09-19 (times local, UTC+8):

| Detected (local) | Stall duration | Consecutive probe failures | Host load at detection (cpuQueueLength) | Dump |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10:31:22 | 63.4 s | 12 | (not recorded in that capture) | missing (procdump produced no file) |
| 10:58:46 | 65.1 s | 12 | 73 | captured |
| 11:10:18 | 67.9 s | 12 | 54 | captured |

An external probe (a separate Node process, outside the gateway process tree) polls the gateway every 5 s and records `wedge_verdict` lines once a stall crosses 60 s. All three rows above were gated as "clean": no host sleep/wake within the guard window, same gateway pid, per-probe failures within bounds — i.e. these are **host-awake stalls of the gateway itself**, not Modern Standby freezes (this machine also produces frequent S0-idle freezes of the gateway; those are excluded by the same gating and are *not* what this issue is about).

## Evidence chain (10:58 stall, the cleanest capture)

Three independent observers recorded the same stall:

**1. External probe** — 12 consecutive probe timeouts over ~65 s, port listening the whole time, pid unchanged (`alerts.jsonl` / `probe-timeline.json`).

**2. Perf sampler (7 s cadence during the stall, `perf.csv`)** — for the entire stall window the gateway process shows:

- `gw_pctCPU = 0` (every sample across the window)
- 13 threads, all present, `gw_faultsPerSec = 0`, working set flat
- while the *host* was busy: `cpuQueueLength` 64 → 21, sysCalls ~70–120k/s, system-wide soft page faults 36–92k/s

So during the stall the gateway is not being starved of CPU by the busy host — it is **waiting**, not computing.

**3. Native stack** (`procdump64 -mm`, symbols resolved via `msdl.microsoft.com`):

```
.  0  Id: 291c.3678  "MainThread"
ntdll!NtQueryAttributesFile+0x14
KERNELBASE!GetFileAttributesW+0xa9
node!uv_fs_open+0x6bb
node!uv_fs_access+0x127
<frame in JIT/unattributed code>
```

The main thread is parked inside a **synchronous filesystem attribute query** issued through libuv's sync-FS path. While that single syscall is in flight the whole event loop is blocked — which matches all three observers: probes time out, CPU is 0%, the port still accepts.

## Second form (11:10 stall)

The 11:10 dump shows a different stack, and I do not want to over-claim a single root cause:

```
.  0  Id: 291c.3678  "MainThread"
node!v8::RegExp::GetFlags+0x9e048   (nearest exported symbol; JIT region)
node!v8::RegExp::GetFlags+0x9d375
node!RSA_get0_q+0x3fed4
<unattributed frames>
```

Only 3 frames resolve (JIT code, no JS symbols in the dump), and the host was moderately busy (cpuQueue 54). Together with the 0%-CPU pattern in the first stall, the common denominator across both captures is: **long-running synchronous work on the main thread (one waiting on a sync FS call, one executing JIT'd JS) with no event-loop yielding**, leaving the listener up but the process unresponsive. I am reporting both stacks as-is rather than forcing them into one mechanism.

## Related observations (context, not claims)

- The gateway's own liveness log on the same day recorded heartbeat delays and `process was frozen ~Xms` entries (many of those are the S0 Modern Standby freezes, which the probe gating excludes separately).
- During this period the state DB (`state/openclaw.sqlite`) had a ~674 MB WAL that had not checkpointed for ~20 h, and the log shows `slow SQLite transaction hold` entries; I suspect this amplifies main-thread latency, but I have not proven a causal link, so treat it as context only.

## Limitations

- No JS frames: the dumps are `-mm` minidumps without a JS inspector session, so I cannot name which application-level code initiated the sync FS access.
- The 10:31 capture has `perf.csv` + timeline but the procdump file is missing (the tool exited non-zero without writing; known flakiness on my side, not OpenClaw's).
- Host was moderately busy at detection in 2 of 3 clean captures; the 0%-CPU-gateway-during-stall pattern is what argues against host contention as the cause of stall #1.
- Stall frequency on this machine over 5 days was 19 gated events, of which only these 3 passed the "host awake, not contaminated" gate; everything else was Modern Standby. Sample size is small.

Happy to upload the dumps (~2.8 MB each) and raw `alerts.jsonl` / `perf.csv` / `probe-timeline.json` / gateway log tails if useful.

Supersedes the process-freeze report in #149106 (that one mixed in host-side freezes and lacked stacks; closing it in favor of this). Related but distinct: #140010 (post-wake reconnect failures, S0 thaw).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

After upgrading from 2026.9.4 to 2026.9.5 (manual \`npm install -g openclaw@2026.9.5\`, since the in-place updater fails at \`global install swap\` — see #152747, #146637, #145954), every gateway lane that resolves the default \`minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3\` model fails locally with \`Unknown model\` before any provider request is made. The heartbeat lane and any \`session:agent:main:main\` turn fail with the same error.

The minimax-portal plugin in 2026.9.5 ships **only runtime discovery** in its manifest:

\`\`\`json
// dist/extensions/minimax/openclaw.plugin.json
"modelCatalog": { "discovery": { "minimax": "runtime", "minimax-portal": "runtime" } }
\`\`\`

\`dist/extensions/minimax/provider-discovery.js\` builds a static catalog from \`MINIMAX_TEXT_MODEL_ORDER\` only inside \`staticCatalog.run(...)\` and does not seed \`models.providers["minimax-portal"].models[]\` itself. After upgrade, that runtime discovery never publishes successfully — the only related log line is:

\`\`\`
[agents/prepared-model-runtime] provider catalog refresh failed:
  Error: prepared model runtime process lifetime closed
\`\`\`

Result: \`openclaw models list\` shows the model (picker merges the hosted catalog), \`openclaw infer model inspect --model minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3\` returns \`Model not found\`, and every live run falls back to \`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash\`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh OpenClaw 2026.9.4 installation, npm-global, Linux x64, Node 26.8.1, npm 11.19.0. Working primary: \`minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3\` with \`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash\` as fallback. OAuth for \`minimax-portal\` healthy (expires in 355d, 5h quota 100% left).
2. \`npm install -g openclaw@2026.9.5\`, then restart the gateway.
3. \`openclaw models status\` shows 32 allowed models including \`minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3\` (tag \`default,configured\`).
4. \`openclaw infer model run --model minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3 --prompt 'reply with exactly: OK'\` → \`Unknown model: minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3. Found agents.defaults.models["minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3"], but no matching models.providers["minimax-portal"].models[] entry.\`
5. \`journalctl --user\` shows the heartbeat and main lanes failing with the same \`FailoverError\`; fallback to \`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash\` always succeeds.

### Expected behavior

Either the runtime discovery publishes the seeded \`MINIMAX_TEXT_MODEL_ORDER\` (\`MiniMax-M3\`, \`MiniMax-M2.7\`, \`MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed\`) into the snapshot, or \`models.providers["minimax-portal"].models[]\` is non-empty so \`Unknown model\` never fires. Currently neither path works on a clean 2026.9.5 install.

### Actual behavior

\`\`\`text
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=55
  error="Unknown model: minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3.
  Found agents.defaults.models[\"minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3\"], but no matching
  models.providers[\"minimax-portal\"].models[] entry.
  Add { \"id\": \"MiniMax-M3\", \"name\": \"MiniMax-M3\" } to
  models.providers[\"minimax-portal\"].models[] to register this provider model."
  errorName=FailoverError
\`\`\`

User-facing wrapper (heartbeat delivery): \`⚠️ The configured model is unavailable from the provider — it may have been renamed, retired, or is not offered on this account. This needs a config update (agents.defaults.model); retrying or starting a new session won't fix it.\`

The wrapper is misleading — the provider account is fine (\`openclaw models status\` reports OAuth quota healthy) and the model still answers on a direct call to \`https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1/messages\`.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), upgraded from 2026.9.4
- Platform: linux/x64
- Node: 26.8.1
- npm: 11.19.0
- Install: npm-global via linuxbrew, prefix \`/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew\`
- Provider auth: OAuth profile \`minimax-portal:setup-20bc32b0-a84d-4766-86b1-f62fb8884065\`, ok, expires in 355d, 5h 100% left, Week 83% left
- Working install of \`opencode-go`\` (no issue): \`opencode-go/provider-discovery.js\` ships a \`createUpstreamProviderCatalog(...)\` against \`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models\` + \`https://models.opencode.ai/api.json\`; the minimax plugin has no equivalent live endpoint (only \`MINIMAX_TEXT_MODEL_ORDER\` is computed in \`staticCatalog.run\`, which apparently does not execute when \`prepared model runtime process lifetime\` is closed).

### Evidence (sanitized)

\`\`\`text
journalctl --user --since "2026-09-19 13:00" | grep -E "Unknown model: minimax-portal" | wc -l
13

journalctl --user --since "2026-09-19 13:00" | grep "provider catalog refresh failed"
[agents/prepared-model-runtime] provider catalog refresh failed:
  Error: prepared model runtime process lifetime closed
\`\`\`

First appearance of the error on this host: 2026-09-19 13:06:51 — 1m 36s after \`openclaw@2026.9.5\` finished installing. The same host had zero occurrences before the upgrade on 2026-09-19.

### Workaround (verified on this host)

Add the static seed from the plugin to user config:

\`\`\`sh
# backup
cp ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak-20260919-minimax-portal-m3

# patch
openclaw config patch --file minimax-portal-models.json \
  --replace-path models.providers.minimax-portal.models
\`\`\`

with \`minimax-portal-models.json\` containing the three models from \`MINIMAX_TEXT_MODEL_ORDER\` (\`MiniMax-M3\`, \`MiniMax-M2.7\`, \`MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed\`), \`api: "anthropic-messages"\` and \`baseUrl: "https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1"\` per model (NOT at provider level — provider-level \`api\`/\`baseUrl\` overrides per-model transport and breaks sibling providers, as seen in the opencode-go fix from #145954 cluster).

Result on this host after the workaround:

- \`openclaw infer model inspect --model minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3\` → ok, \`api: anthropic-messages\`, 1M context
- \`openclaw infer model run --model minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3 --prompt 'reply with exactly: OK'\` → HTTP 200 from \`api.minimax.io\`, response \`OK\`
- No further \`Unknown model: minimax-portal\` errors in heartbeat/main lanes

This is a workaround, not a fix — the plugin manifest should ship a static seed or a working runtime discovery.

### Related

- #152747 — same failure on 2026.9.4 → candidate, npm-global, Linux x64
- #146637 — same failure on 2026.9.3 → 2026.9.4, npm-global + Node 24.21.0
- #145954 — closed duplicate of #144712, same root-cause cluster (retained tree verification)
- #144712 — canonical report, timeout and diagnostic fixes merged in commit f50d4ce71e3e
- PR #144758 — fix for baseline \`PackageIntegrityTimeoutError\`
