issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Control UI stutters while hovering session rows and scrolling the sidebar on Windows, and it is worse with reduced motion enabled: a 26s trace shows 19,063 `scrollbar-color` transitions and 17.0s of style recalculation, with no setting available to turn those transitions off.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have reduced motion enabled (Windows: Settings -> Accessibility -> Visual effects -> Animation effects off), so `matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches` is true.
2. Open the Control UI in Chrome and record about 25s in DevTools -> Performance while switching sessions, scrolling the sidebar and hovering session rows.
3. Stop the recording: the Animations track contains only `scrollbar-color` entries, and the Main thread shows 284 `Recalculate Style` events totalling 17,017ms.

### Expected behavior

With reduced motion already matching, the CSS in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` is meant to suppress motion, so scrolling the sidebar and hovering rows should not produce multi-hundred-millisecond style recalculations.

### Actual behavior

Style recalculations of up to 843ms (1,418 elements in one pass); 19,063 `scrollbar-color` transitions across 1,013 distinct nodes, 403-1,479 new ones per second for 22 seconds; `Layout` is not involved (70 events, 158ms).

Cause as far as I could trace it: the root declares an inherited `scrollbar-color` (`ui/src/styles/base.css`, `:root`), and the reduced-motion block in the same file (the block setting `transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*, *::before, *::after`) never sets `transition-property`, which therefore keeps its initial value `all`. So while reduced motion is active, every element has an armed transition for every property, including the inherited `scrollbar-color`, and each style recalculation can restart them.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.3 (1391f7c), Control UI build 2026.9.3-release-1391f7cd2d40-2026-09-08T07-46-00.264Z

### Operating system

Windows 11

### Install method

npm global install

### Model

Not involved: this is Control UI rendering and CSS.

### Provider / routing chain

Not involved in this report.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable.

### Logs

No gateway logs are relevant. The extracted browser-trace numbers are in the evidence section below.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Measured on the reporter's machine with reduced motion enabled. The numbers below are extracted from a
Chrome performance trace recorded while using the Control UI; no trace file is needed to read them.

Recording: 26.3s DevTools performance trace, 195,883 events, 16 logical cores.

| Style recalculation (`UpdateLayoutTree`) | |
| --- | --- |
| events | 284 |
| total | 17,017ms |
| slowest single events | 843ms, 741ms, 702ms, 623ms, 619ms, 597ms |
| elements re-styled per event | max 1,418; 39 events > 500; 4 > 1,000; median 18 |
| `Layout` | 70 events, 158ms |
| `ScheduleStyleRecalculation` / `InvalidateLayout` | 268 / 94 |

Slowest recalculation events, with the stacks that requested them:

- 843ms, 1,418 elements — `Eg` @ `control-ui-boot-chat-*.js` <- `reconcileImplicitEndAnchor` @ `control-ui-boot-chat-*.js` <- `update` @ `control-ui-boot-chat-*.js`
- 741ms, 1,396 elements
- 702ms, 988 elements — `AT` @ `control-ui-boot-shared-*.js` <- `jT` @ `control-ui-boot-shared-*.js`
- 623ms, 996 elements — `Vu` @ `control-ui-boot-shared-*.js` <- `handleEvent` @ `lit-runtime-*.js`
- 619ms, 1,014 elements — `AT` @ `control-ui-boot-shared-*.js` <- `jT` @ `control-ui-boot-shared-*.js`

| `Animation` events | |
| --- | --- |
| total | 64,780 |
| with an animated property name | 19,261 |
| of those, `scrollbar-color` | 19,063 |
| distinct animated nodes | 1,013 |
| states seen | `running`: 19,063 (none finishing) |
| new `scrollbar-color` transitions per second | min 403, max 1,479, over 22s |

Animated properties, by event count:

```
scrollbar-color          19063
color                       69
opacity                     23
background-color            22
shimmer                     14
stroke-dasharray            14
background-position-x       10
background-position-y       10
```

Nodes carrying the `scrollbar-color` transitions, top 10 by event count:

```
path                                                       1893
svg                                                        1709
circle                                                     1255
OPENCLAW-TOOLTIP                                            755
line                                                        537
SPAN class='sidebar-recent-session__text'                   388
A class='sidebar-recent-session__link'                      387
SPAN class='sidebar-recent-session__details'                387
SPAN class='sidebar-recent-session__details-endcap'         387
SPAN class='sidebar-recent-session__title-row'              387
```

To reproduce the numbers without the reporter's machine: record ~25s in DevTools -> Performance while
scrolling the sidebar and hovering session rows with reduced motion enabled, then count the
Animations track entries and the Main thread's `Recalculate Style` events.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Control UI users with reduced motion enabled; observed in Chrome on Windows.

Severity: moderate; roughly 65% of the recorded 26.3s window is style recalculation caused by these transitions (17.0s of 26.3s).

Frequency: always while scrolling the sidebar or hovering rows.

Consequence: visible stutter and input lag in the Control UI, and no in-app way to avoid it. Turning animations off in the OS (already the case here) does not help, because that is what activates the reduced-motion CSS.

### Additional information

What I would ask for: a way to turn UI transitions off from the app itself.

I hit this stutter, narrowed it to the `scrollbar-color` transitions, and the workaround I now run locally is a browser-local switch in Settings -> Appearance -> Theme that sets a root attribute and disables `transition-property`. That fixed it for me. Anyone else hitting the same stutter has no such lever today, and the only OS-side control makes it worse rather than better.

Two ways to give everyone that lever, maintainer's choice:

1. Stop arming the transitions: add `transition-property: none !important` (or an explicit property list) to the existing reduced-motion block in `ui/src/styles/base.css`. One line, and no element can then start a `scrollbar-color` transition.
2. Ship an explicit setting, so users are not dependent on the OS toggle at all.

Last known good version / first known bad version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (found while profiling, not while bisecting a version range).

issues.body:
### Environment

- openclaw 2026.9.2 (3928bad)
- Node 22.23.2, Debian 12, SQLite 3.40.1
- Telegram channel, forum group with topics; gateway run under a leader-gate wrapper

### Summary

After a turn ends while a `Bash` tool call is outstanding, the affected per-topic lane can stop dispatching. Subsequent inbound messages are written to `channel_ingress_events` with `status='claimed'` and `attempts=0`, and then never attempted. The claim is taken once and not renewed, and no worker picks the row up. From the user's side the bot shows a typing indicator and never replies.

Other lanes are unaffected. The gateway itself stays healthy throughout: it accepts new websocket connections, answers `cron list`, and logs no event-loop stalls. Only the one lane is stranded.

Restarting the gateway clears it, and the stranded rows then complete normally.

### Observed sequence

1. A turn in one topic runs a `Bash` tool call.
2. `diagnostic` begins emitting, every 30s:

```
stalled session: sessionId=<uuid> sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:group:<chat>:topic:<topic>
  state=idle queueDepth=1 reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call
  activeWorkKind=tool_call lastProgress=tool:Bash:started lastProgressAge=194s
  activeTool=Bash activeToolCallId=<id>
```

Note `state=idle` together with `activeWorkKind=tool_call`.

3. The tool call ends. I sampled the agent process tree three times at 20s intervals and found **no child processes at all**, so nothing was still running. The stall lines also stop.
4. A new inbound message for that topic is accepted and written as `claimed`, `attempts=0`, `claim_owner` = the *live* gateway pid (not a stale owner from a previous process).
5. `claimed_at` is not refreshed on subsequent polls, and `attempts` never increments. The row simply sits there.

### Evidence

Two occurrences on the same day, same topic, both preceded by a blocked `Bash` call. Delay is time from receipt to completion, where completion only happened after a gateway restart:

| received (UTC) | attempts | delay to completion |
|---|---|---|
| 01:43:47 | 0 | 1,126 s |
| 01:45:50 | 1 | 3,745 s |
| 01:54:30 | 2 | 5,193 s |
| 02:09:03 | 0 | 4,369 s |
| 02:20:59 | 0 | 3,747 s |
| 05:02:01 | 0 | 621 s |

Between 04:29 and 05:02 no other message arrived on any Telegram lane, so the second occurrence is a single stranded row rather than a general backlog.

### Ruled out

- **Stale claim from a dead process.** `claim_owner` matched the running gateway pid.
- **A hung child process.** No descendants of the agent process existed while the row sat unattempted.
- **Gateway unresponsiveness.** Handshakes succeeded throughout at ~2 s, and no `liveness heartbeat delayed` entries were logged during the second occurrence.
- **Database contention.** Hot queries on the state DB run in 2–4 ms in isolation; plans use their indexes; the slow-transaction rate is flat across the whole day and does not correlate with these events.

### Impact

A topic goes silent while appearing to be working, because the typing indicator stays on. The only remedy I found is a full gateway restart, which is heavy: it drops every in-flight turn across all lanes to recover one.

### Possible direction

The combination `state=idle` + `activeWorkKind=tool_call` looks like the lane's in-memory busy flag outliving the work it was tracking, so the dispatcher never considers the lane free again while the queue layer keeps handing it claims. Two things that would help operationally regardless of the root cause:

- Release or re-queue a claim that has not been attempted within its lease, rather than holding it indefinitely.
- Let the existing `blocked_tool_call` detector, which already notices this within 30 seconds, clear or fail the lane after a bound instead of only reporting it.

Happy to gather more detail from a live occurrence if there is specific instrumentation that would help.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Model routing / provider failover

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A provider error that carries **no HTTP status** is not treated as failover-eligible, so a
configured fallback chain is never consulted and the run dies with no reply.

Observed with xAI returning `Internal error during token generation`:

```
[openai-transport] [responses] error provider=xai api=openai-responses model=grok-4.6
  name=Error status=undefined code=null type=error causeName=undefined causeCode=undefined
  message=Internal error during token generation
[agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: runId=<run> isError=true model=grok-4.6 provider=xai
  error=⚠️ Agent run failed (model: xai/grok-4.6). rawError=Internal error during token generation
```

The agent has `{"primary": "xai/grok-4.6", "fallbacks": ["openai/gpt-5.6-sol"]}`. The fallback
is never attempted.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent with a primary model and at least one fallback.
2. Cause the provider to return an error with no HTTP status — an SDK/transport-level error
   where `status` is `undefined` and `code` is `null`, rather than a 4xx/5xx response.
   (Ours arrives from xAI mid-generation as `Internal error during token generation`.)
3. Observe the run end `isError=true` with no reply and no fallback attempt.

### Expected behavior

A provider error that prevented any output should be failover-eligible, and the configured
fallback should be tried — whether or not the failure carried an HTTP status.

### Actual behavior

**Failover is never attempted.** The failed run's complete journal footprint is five lines,
and none of them is a `[model-fallback]` line:

```
turn milestone
embedded run agent end: isError=true model=grok-4.6 rawError=Internal error during token generation
terminal session persistence failed   (SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError — see #150372)
message processed
run announce ended stopReason=stop
```

The chain is not refused or exhausted — it is not reached.

This appears consistent with `classifyProviderErrorPayloadReason`, which returns the reason
only for `auth`, `auth_permanent`, `billing`, `rate_limit`, `server_error`, `overloaded`, and
`null` otherwise. A statusless transport error is classified as none of those.

**Failover itself is healthy on this host** — 146 `[model-fallback]` events in 14 days, firing
on `model_not_found` (24), `runtime_rejected` (10), `format` and others. It is this error class
specifically that never becomes a candidate.

### Incidence

Three occurrences in seven days, all `xai/grok-4.6`:

```
2026-09-15T08:18:42
2026-09-15T14:06:57
2026-09-17T09:52:05
```

Each one ends a user's task outright. The 2026-09-17 run had consumed 4m29s and 123.0k tokens
(109.2k in / 13.8k out) before the provider failed.

Two of the three also hit #150372, so the child session additionally loses its durable
"ended before a reply" notice — the user sees a task stop with no explanation.

### What was ruled out

Recorded so reviewers do not re-derive it:

- **Not a model override.** The dispatching `agent_run` call was read from the parent
  transcript: `agentId=<agent>, model=(NOT SET)`. A nearby
  `[model-fallback] configured fallbacks disabled by user model override` line belongs to a
  **different run on a different session** 17 seconds later.
- **Not context overflow.** 109.2k input tokens, well inside the window, and no overflow
  diagnostic was emitted for the run.
- **Not a gateway restart or session rotation.** Neither occurred near the failure.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.3 (1391f7c)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-1011-aws, Node v24.18.0

### Install method

npm global (`/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)

### Model

xai/grok-4.6 (primary), openai/gpt-5.6-sol (configured fallback, never attempted)

### Provider / routing chain

xai → grok-4.6 via `openai-responses`

issues.body:
### Version / platform
OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (97e6e3c), macOS 26 (Apple silicon), gateway as a launchd user agent (`KeepAlive: true`).

### Summary
Renaming an agent id in `openclaw.json` is accepted by the hot reload and the running gateway keeps working — but the old agent directory is left in place, and the **next cold start fails** validating it, then the crash-loop breaker suppresses channel autostart, so every Telegram/Discord channel stays down until started by hand.

### Steps
1. Agent `macx-discord` exists with `~/.openclaw/agents/macx-discord/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`.
2. In `openclaw.json`, rename the entry to `macx` (bindings updated). `openclaw config validate` passes; hot reload applies; the gateway serves the renamed agent for hours.
3. Restart the gateway (`launchctl kickstart -k …`).

### Observed
```
[gateway] sidecars failed to start: Error: OpenClaw agent database /Users/…/.openclaw/agents/macx-discord/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite belongs to agent macx-discord; requested agent macx.
Gateway failed to start: … Run openclaw gateway status --deep for diagnostics.
```
Four unclean boots in a row (launchd KeepAlive), then:
```
[telegram] channel autostart suppressed by crash-loop breaker; refusing automatic start for telegram. Start a channel manually with: openclaw gateway call channels.start --params '{"channel":"telegram"}'
```
`openclaw channels status`: `error: gateway restart-loop breaker tripped: 4 unclean boot(s) within 300000ms` for every channel.

### Expected
Either migrate/rename the agent directory when the id changes (#112665 asks for a safe rename), or validate only the directory of the requested agent and ignore directories with no matching config entry — and warn at rename time that the old directory must be moved.

### Workaround
Move `~/.openclaw/agents/<old-id>` out of `agents/` before restarting; after the restart, `openclaw gateway call channels.start --params '{"channel":"telegram"}'` (once per additional `accountId`) and `… '{"channel":"discord"}'`.

Related: #112665 (safe agent ID rename).

issues.body:
## Summary

Coordinate the remaining work needed for Skill Workshop to capture useful procedural discoveries during ordinary work and demonstrate that an authorized skill revision improves a later task. Build on existing learning, proposal, evaluation and publication contracts; measure gaps before adding mechanisms.

This is a contributor proposal for discussion, not an accepted roadmap or a claim that OpenClaw lacks self-learning.

## Problem to solve

After an agent discovers a reliable procedure or receives a useful procedural correction, the operator needs to know whether that lesson was captured in the right skill, whether it was applied, and whether it works beyond the original example.

Those are separate outcomes. A pending proposal is not an active skill; a valid file is not behavioral proof; completion of maintenance does not necessarily mean a file changed. The proposed outcome is reliable, inspectable reuse—not more generated skill files.

The supplied static review identified possible coverage gaps between foreground authoring, immediate repair and delayed experience review. It did not measure their frequency or run behavioral trials. In particular, short-turn admission is a hypothesis to investigate, not sufficient evidence for lowering a scheduler threshold.

## Existing behavior and related ownership

OpenClaw already documents immediate repair and experience review. Workshop owns proposal application, while automatic background maintenance can edit its directory directly. These paths must not be given identical validation or publication guarantees by implication. See [self-learning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/self-learning.md) and [Workshop ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skill-workshop.md).

| Existing work | Relationship to this proposal |
|---|---|
| steipete’s merged [#100692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100692), closing [#95477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95477) | Existing reusable-workflow suggestion work. Reconcile its current behavior and subsequent changes before proposing additional recognition guidance. This umbrella does not reopen the old “missing self-learning” premise. |
| [#123992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123992), closed with linked fix #123994 | Existing evaluator-result visibility work. Reuse or verify its projection rather than proposing outcome visibility as entirely new. |
| Zeus-Deus’s [#111943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111943) | Adjacent model/reasoning policy proposal. No routing or model-policy change is included here. |
| anyech’s [#141102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141102) | Existing collection-review eligibility/diagnostics discussion. Keep that decision on its owning issue; reuse its eventual contract. |

This is a coordination proposal, not a takeover of those items. If an existing umbrella already owns the remaining scope, attach the work there instead of opening a competing tracker.

## Proposed solution

Keep proposals and publication in Workshop, loading and refresh in the skills runtime, and permissions and execution capacity with their existing owners. Prefer an optional evaluator plugin over a new core controller. A quality result never grants authority to publish.

### Dependency-ordered workstreams

These are candidate PR units, not existing PRs or assignments. A workstream proceeds only after its gap and owner boundary are established.

| Unit | Change and independent value | Dependency / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Characterize learning coverage** | Establish a synthetic behavior matrix for manual, foreground and experience-review paths, including current modes and runtime eligibility. Reconcile #100692 and later changes. | First evidence milestone. Separate contract tests from live-model trials. A prompt-text assertion does not prove recognition. Submit a standalone characterization PR only if maintainers want that artifact; otherwise carry its useful fixtures with the first demonstrated fix. |
| **B. Close demonstrated foreground capture gaps** | Improve existing guidance or authoring behavior only where A demonstrates a missing case. Prefer the owning skill or pending proposal; create a distinct skill only for a distinct procedure. | Depends on A. Show correct capture without an explicit learning request, no duplicate for covered work, and no failed attempt stored as a working solution. Preserve publication semantics and mode/permission boundaries. |
| **C. Demonstrate reuse and explain outcomes** | Use existing status, usage and evaluation projections to connect a proposal, its applied revision and a later task. Add only missing information. | Baseline fixtures from A; integrate B if needed. A fresh session must discover and use the authorized revision on changed input. Distinguish pending, applied, evaluated, failed, unavailable and abstained states. Do not silently reload the current session. Coordinate collection diagnostics with #141102. |
| **D. Reference behavioral evaluator** | Exercise exact candidate and baseline revisions through the existing evaluation extension contract; produce interpretable task outcomes. Prefer an optional plugin. | Requires agreement on placement and supported API. Use isolated synthetic tasks, baseline/candidate comparison or a no-skill control where meaningful. An incorrect skill must fail; evaluator absence must not be reported as a pass. Storage and publication remain Workshop-owned. |
| **E. Bounded evaluation and revision** | Optionally coordinate evaluate → revise → re-evaluate → stop through existing owners, without another persistent scheduler or proposal store. | Depends on D and explicit policy agreement. Bound attempts, elapsed time and resource use; honor cancellation; invalidate stale results. Any required-evaluation policy must define missing/error/timeout/skipped outcomes without changing advisory behavior silently. |
| **F. Short-turn review admission, only if justified** | Admit a demonstrated high-value short-turn case through the existing reviewer when foreground capture remains insufficient. | Depends on A/B evidence and a maintainer admission-policy decision. Preserve quiet-time, capacity, identity and authority controls; avoid duplicate or recursive review. No blanket threshold reduction or model call after every message. Omit this unit if the earlier work solves the gap. |

**First milestone:** A, the justified portion of B, and C. Reliable capture and reuse must not depend on building an optimizer.

**Second milestone:** D, then E if accepted. F is an evidence-triggered branch, not a mandatory feature.

### Proof required

Use scenarios covering a useful new procedure, a correction to a used skill, an already-covered lesson, routine work, a successful recovery, an unresolved attempt, denied authority and unavailable runtime capability.

For reuse, withhold the original solved answer and change the input. For optimization, reserve validation cases not used to select edits. Correctness and critical regressions take precedence over token or tool-call savings. Human review or inconclusive results are legitimate outcomes.

Fixtures, skill text and transcripts are evidence, not permission. Tests must not act on real external accounts or collect private conversations, credentials or personal facts.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use existing guidance unchanged:** preferred if characterization demonstrates sufficient coverage; retain useful regression proof rather than adding a feature.
- **Rely on explicit learning requests:** remains valid, but does not establish whether useful discoveries are consistently captured during ordinary work.
- **Lower review thresholds globally:** adds work without establishing that the lost cases contain reusable lessons.
- **Build a new learning service:** duplicates existing owners and is unnecessary unless a specific missing contract is demonstrated.
- **Apply an evaluation gate only to proposals:** cannot support a universal validation promise while direct maintenance remains outside that path. Either state the narrower guarantee or obtain agreement on a coherent change to the owner contract.

## Impact

Affected users are operators relying on learned skills across sessions. The intended benefit is fewer repeated procedural corrections and clearer evidence about what was learned. Frequency and magnitude have not been measured; no reliability percentage, runtime regression or release blocker is asserted.

## Evidence/examples

The input research was a static review pinned to OpenClaw `ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d`; it reported no executed tests or agent trials. Its relevant source pointers are [foreground guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts), [review admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts), and [proposal evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/service-evaluation.ts). These are research provenance, not freshly reproduced current-main defects.

The related tracker items and current documentation above were inspected while revising this proposal. Current-source history and behavioral reproduction remain the first implementation step. Hermes supplied UX inspiration in the original research; neither Hermes parity nor a claim of mandatory automatic benchmarking is an acceptance criterion.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on scope and ownership. I would start with the coverage evidence and the smallest demonstrated foreground gap.

## Additional information

**Maintainer decision requested:** does the first milestone belong on a new coordination issue or an existing owner surface? Separately, should a reference behavioral evaluator start as an external plugin, and is an optional required-evaluation/revision policy wanted at all? Neither question assumes approval for a new core contract.

Initial scope excludes a new memory backend, model training, registry, persistent controller, external skill installation, automatic sharing, protected third-party skill edits, model-routing changes, mandatory auto-publication, age-only retirement and same-session context replacement.

### Closure criteria

- [ ] Each workstream is completed with evidence, shown unnecessary, or explicitly deferred with maintainer agreement and a linked owner where appropriate.
- [ ] Accepted learning cases demonstrate correct capture and later reuse; negative controls show meaningful abstention and preserved authority.
- [ ] Evaluation claims identify the tested revision, environment and limits; untested direct maintenance receives no implicit validation badge.
- [ ] No duplicate proposal store, scheduler, publication authority or ownership takeover was introduced.
- [ ] Accepted changes include relevant regression tests, documentation and actual runtime evidence where required.

Intermediate PRs should use `Related: #<umbrella>` and explain which workstream they advance. Only the change satisfying all remaining closure criteria should close the umbrella. Preserve the original contributors’ authorship when extending or reusing their work.

issues.body:
### Summary
The retry-after failover e2e added in #148580 spends ~340s on its first case per worker, and a cold suite run is dominated by it. Profiling shows the cost is runtime TypeScript transpilation of the bundled plugin set: when OpenClaw runs from source (as the e2e harness does via tsx/vitest), `resolvePluginRuntimeArtifactPreference` returns "source", so every bundled plugin is compiled in-process by Jiti even though the compiled artifacts already exist under `dist/`. This is the source-mode analogue of #136385, which fixed the built-host case in #136399.

### Impact (measured, 4-core Linux, Node 24.20.0)
- First case ~341s; second case in the same worker ~49s.
- Worker CPU profile: jiti ~41% self, jiti/babel ~8%, node:fs ~19%, idle ~7%.

### What fixes it
Run the fixture against the built runtime, so the loader resolves bundled plugins to their compiled artifacts instead of transpiling them. Measured: first case ~341s -> ~5s; warm suite ~29s. `tsgo:core:test` passes and both cases pass.

### What does not fix it
Setting the artifact preference on a source-executing run (an env/load-option opt-in) was tried and left Jiti unchanged in the profile: the flag reached the worker but bundled plugins were still transpiled. So the fix is to execute the fixture built, not to flip a preference on a source host.

### Related
Follow-up to #143274 / #148580. See also #136385, #136399.

issues.body:
### Summary

Expose the mid-turn prompt-size estimate (the one the context-overflow precheck already computes) to plugin tool hooks, so plugins can enforce context budgets during a tool loop.

### Problem to solve

A plugin that wants to act *during* a tool loop (e.g. brake a runaway loop before it exceeds the context budget) has no access to the runtime's own prompt-size estimate.

- `contextBudgetStatus.estimatedPromptTokens` (readable via `api.runtime.agent.session.getSessionEntry()`) is only updated at prompt-build time, so a plugin cannot observe growth that happens inside a single turn.
- The runtime already computes a mid-turn estimate: the log line `[context-overflow-midturn-precheck] ... estimatedPromptTokens=<N> promptBudgetBeforeReserve=<N> overflowTokens=<N>` shows it re-running repeatedly while tools execute.
- That value is not exposed to plugins. `after_tool_call` handlers return `void`, and `PluginHookBeforeToolCallResult` only offers `params` / `block` / `blockReason` / `requireApproval` — there is no estimate field anywhere in the tool-hook contract.

Observed consequence: in a single turn with a long tool loop, a session grew from ~36K to ~96K prompt tokens, then to ~115K, crossing the compaction threshold; auto-compaction then failed and the turn ended in error. A plugin could have braked earlier, but only had a stale pre-turn number.

### Proposed solution

Any of the following, whichever fits the architecture:

1. Add an estimate object to the tool-hook events/context, e.g. on `before_tool_call` (event or `PluginHookToolContext`):
   `contextEstimate?: { estimatedPromptTokens: number; contextTokenBudget: number; remainingPromptTokens: number; shouldCompact: boolean; source?: string }`
2. Expose a runtime accessor for the latest estimate, e.g. `api.runtime.agent.session.getContextEstimate({ sessionKey })`.
3. Or emit an explicit `mid_turn_precheck` hook carrying the values that are already logged today.

(1) is preferred: it removes the round trip and gives hooks the same numbers the runtime itself uses.

### Alternatives considered

Having the plugin estimate from the `llm_input` hook payload (system prompt + prompt + history messages + tools, divided by a chars-per-token constant). This works but is approximate, platform-dependent (CJK vs latin), and duplicates logic the runtime already runs on every tool result — it also tends to over-estimate, which risks braking legitimate work.

### Impact

Benefits any plugin doing context governance (compaction/budget/braking) rather than only observation. Frequency: every tool-loop iteration. Consequence today: plugins can only react one turn late, so a runaway single turn can cross the compaction threshold before any plugin can intervene.

### Evidence/examples

Type contract evidence (plugin API):

```ts
// dist/agent-harness-runtime-*.d.ts
after_tool_call: (event: PluginHookAfterToolCallEvent, ctx: PluginHookToolContext) => Promise<void> | void;

type PluginHookBeforeToolCallResult = {
  params?: Record<string, unknown>;
  block?: boolean;
  blockReason?: string;
  requireApproval?: { title: string; description: string; scope?: ApprovalScope; severity?: ... };
};
```

Runtime log evidence (already computed, not exposed):

```
[context-overflow-midturn-precheck] sessionKey=... provider=... route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=115396 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=111072 overflowTokens=4324 toolResultReducibleChars=0 effectiveReserveTokens=20000 ...
```

Only three hooks can inject context today (`before_prompt_build`, `agent_turn_prepare`, heartbeat contribution) — all are turn-boundary, not mid-loop.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No

### Additional information

Environment where this matters most: small-context local models (e.g. a 131072-token window served locally) driving tool-heavy agents, where a single turn's tool output can exceed the remaining budget and compaction cannot always recover (in our case compaction consistently fails on this provider, which makes mid-turn braking the only mitigation before the session must be reset).

issues.body:
### Summary

If the gateway restarts while a Google Meet capture is running, the meeting session is lost and the durable transcript is never finalized: `stopped_at` stays `NULL` forever and no summary is written. Nothing reconciles it on the next start.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.4, `@openclaw/google-meet` 2026.9.4, `--mode transcribe --transport chrome`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `openclaw googlemeet join <url> --mode transcribe --transport chrome`; wait until captions produce a few utterances.
2. Restart the gateway while still in the meeting.
3. `openclaw googlemeet status --json` → `sessions: []`; `openclaw googlemeet doctor` → no session.
4. `openclaw transcripts list` still shows the session with `no summary.md`; in the state DB `meeting_transcript_sessions.stopped_at` is `NULL` and there is no row in `meeting_transcript_summaries`.
5. The Chrome tab may still be in the meeting, but nothing is capturing any more and nothing will close the transcript.

### Expected

At least one of:

- On startup, the meeting-bot bridge finds transcript sessions with `stopped_at IS NULL` that no longer have a live meeting session and finalizes them (set `stopped_at` to the last utterance time, write the summary, mark `metadata.finalizedBy = "recovery"` or similar).
- Or it re-attaches to a still-open Meet tab for that session (the `recover-tab` path already knows how to find it) and resumes capture.
- Gateway drain/restart should stop active meeting captures cleanly (the same path as `leave`) before exiting.

issues.body:
## Summary

For direct Anthropic API-key sessions, OpenClaw delegates context pruning to Anthropic's server-side `clear_tool_uses` edit (per `docs/concepts/session-pruning.md`). That path has no bootstrap-content protection, and once a clearing event happens there is no mechanism to re-inject the content that was cleared. In long-running, tool-heavy agent sessions this causes the agent to silently lose access to instruction/reference files it read earlier via a `read`-style tool call, with no signal beyond a log line.

## What the docs currently say

From `docs/concepts/session-pruning.md`:

- Server-side path (Direct Anthropic API-key requests): "OpenClaw derives the request parameters... `keep`: The 3 most recent tool uses and their results." No exception is documented for early/bootstrap tool results.
- Client-side path (`cache-ttl` mode) has an explicit safety rule: *"nothing before the session's first user message is ever pruned (protects bootstrap reads like `SOUL.md`/`USER.md`)"* — but this rule is stated only under the "Client-side pruning" section.

So for the server-side (Anthropic API-key) path specifically, it's unclear whether any equivalent protection exists, and reading the doc top-to-bottom it's easy to assume the bootstrap-protection applies universally when it apparently does not.

## Why this matters in practice

Our setup uses several long-running coding/review agents on direct Anthropic API-key auth (so the server-side clearing path applies). Agent instructions require reading certain reference/instruction files via an explicit tool call near session start (not baked into the system prompt) — e.g. a "read this session-state file first" convention, plus on-demand style/standards docs read mid-task.

In sessions with many tool calls (file reads, searches, exec output) — easily reached once total input tokens cross `max(50000, floor(contextWindow*0.3))` for large-context models — the server clears everything except the 3 most recent tool uses. Any instruction/reference file content loaded earlier via a tool call is gone from context for the rest of the session, with only a log line (`server-side context edit: cleared N tool results (M input tokens)`) marking that it happened — nothing user- or agent-visible, and no automatic recovery.

We observed this concretely: an agent applied a general workflow rule it had documented for itself, without re-checking a task-specific precondition it had verified earlier in the same long session via a tool-read — consistent with that earlier tool result having been cleared. Multiple agents on the same instruction set made the same mistake independently, which is what led us to dig into the pruning mechanism rather than assume a reasoning/model-quality issue.

## Ask

1. **Clarify the docs**: state explicitly whether the server-side (Anthropic API-key) clearing path has *any* protection for early/bootstrap tool results, analogous to the client-side "nothing before the first user message" rule — or confirm it does not, so this isn't ambiguous.
2. **Consider a mitigation**, e.g. one of:
   - A way to mark specific tool calls/results (not just whole tool *names* via `contextPruning.tools.{allow,deny}`) as "pinned" / excluded from both clearing paths, so a one-time "load this reference file" read survives the whole session even as ordinary large tool outputs get pruned around it.
   - Detecting a clearing event (client- or server-side) and offering an optional hook to automatically re-run/re-inject specific prior tool calls (e.g. re-read a fixed list of paths) so critical context is restored rather than silently dropped.

Happy to provide more reproduction detail if useful — this surfaced through normal usage rather than a minimal repro, so let me know what would help most.

### Bug type

Behavior defect / crash of a waiting run

### Summary

For runs hosted by the CLI runner (direct `openclaw agent` / plugin execution with block-reply delivery to a connected channel), answering a pending `ask_user` question from the channel can still fail the waiting run: the persisted answer is treated as an unrelated newer user row by the transcript append fence — the same symptom #145551 described and #149617 fixed for the gateway embedded-runner host.

#149617 made the question custody callback (`admitTranscriptAnswer`) the only writer of temporary persisted-answer receipts, and wired it into the gateway embedded-runner authority creation (`src/agents/harness/tool-authority.runtime.ts`, inside `withSessionTranscriptQuestionAnswers`). The other production caller of `createAgentQuestionAnswerAuthority` — the CLI runner binding in `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` — does not pass `admitTranscriptAnswer`, so at claim time the custody hook is an optional-chain no-op (`state.answerAuthority?.admitTranscriptAnswer?.(sourceRecorder)` in `src/agents/harness/gateway-question.ts`) and the fence scope holds no `UserTurnTranscriptAdmissionReceipt` for the persisted answer row.

Note the mechanism is an in-process `AsyncLocalStorage` closure over the creator's recorder, while the answer row is persisted by the gateway process; a CLI-process-side wiring alone cannot receive the gateway-side receipt. Fixing this for cross-process answers likely requires the receipt (or an equivalent admission) to travel with the `question.waitAnswer` resolution, or a fence-side bounded admission for rows belonging to a registered question.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a CLI-hosted run (e.g. `openclaw agent` / plugin execution) that calls `ask_user` with block-reply delivery to a connected channel.
2. Reply to the question from the channel.
3. The gateway persists the reply as a new user row in the shared SQLite transcript; when the CLI run resumes and appends its tool result through the fenced accessor, the newer unrelated user row is not admitted and the append is rejected → waiting run fails.

### Expected behavior

Answering from the channel resolves the question and the waiting CLI-hosted run continues once, storing the answer as the tool result (same outcome #149617 delivered for gateway-hosted runs).

### Actual behavior

The waiting run fails after the answer is persisted; the channel observes a run-failure notification.

### OpenClaw version

main @ `173734d52d5` (2026-09-16)

### Operating system

Cross-platform

### Model

Any

# [#05] 主会话重启恢复逐 store 同步读，导致开机冻结 63.6s

**Labels 建议**：`bug` `performance` `startup`
**版本**：openclaw 2026.5.27（237 agents，会话存储位于 U 盘）

## 症状

网关 **ready 后约 10 秒**开始，出现一次**约 63.6 秒**的连续事件循环阻塞（不是两次 31s，而是单次长阻塞；速率受限的探针会误读为两段）：

```
[看门狗] {"driftMs":63579,"uptimeS":74,"handles":["Server","Server","FSWatcher"],"requests":[]}
[看门狗] {"driftMs":63661,"uptimeS":74,...}   （多次复现 63.5–63.7s）
```

特征：**零 CPU、无 libuv 句柄/请求、无日志**（阻塞前后均无输出）。限时 `--trace-sync-io`（35 秒后强杀）取"沉默前最后一条同步 I/O 栈"命中：

```
Detected use of sync API
    at statSync (node:fs)
    at getFileStatSnapshot (dist/store-load-*.js)
    at loadSessionStore (dist/store-load-*.js)
    at recoverStore (dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js)
    at recoverRestartAbortedMainSessions (dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js)
```

## 根因

`dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js`：

```js
async function recoverRestartAbortedMainSessions(params = {}) {
  const resumedSessionKeys = params.resumedSessionKeys ?? new Set();
  for (const storePath of await resolveRestartRecoveryStorePaths(params)) {   // ← 全部 agents 的会话存储
    const storeResult = await recoverStore({ storePath, resumedSessionKeys }); // ← 内部 loadSessionStore（同步）
    ...
  }
}
```

`resolveRestartRecoveryStorePaths()` 收集 `resolveAgentSessionDirs(stateDir)` + `resolveAllAgentSessionStoreTargetsSync(cfg, ...)` → 237 条路径；`recoverStore → loadSessionStore` 为**同步**读。U 盘 ~260ms/个 × 237 ≈ **62s**，由 `scheduleRestartAbortedMainSessionRecovery`（默认延迟触发）在 ready 后执行。

## 建议修法

- 循环内每 store 后让出宏任务（**我们实测**：开机探针 `maxGap` 从 **31,020ms×2 → 1,372ms**，且恢复结果不变）：
  ```js
  for (const storePath of await resolveRestartRecoveryStorePaths(params)) {
    await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r));    // 让 I/O 回调插队
    const storeResult = await recoverStore({ storePath, resumedSessionKeys });
    ...
  }
  ```
- 或 `recoverStore` 改为异步读（`fs.promises`）；
- 或在无 `running/abortedLastRun` 候选时先做一次轻量筛选（例如只读 mtime 或索引文件）再逐 store 深读。

## 影响

每次开机（含登录后自启动）都有 ~1 分钟"网关假死不响应"；用户视角是"刚开机时没法用"，且与其它启动任务叠加后更难归因。

issues.body:
# [Bug] Session keeps answering from a fallback model after the turn-local fallback; Control UI chip follows it

## Summary

After a turn where the configured primary model fails (here: a billing/quota error), the
session does **not** return to the selected primary on the next turn. It keeps answering
from a *different provider/model*, and the Control UI model chip moves along with it, so the
operator silently spends quota on a model they never picked.

This contradicts the documented contract in `docs/concepts/model-failover.md`:

> Fallback execution is turn-local. The reply runner persists only fallback notice state so
> `/status` and transition notices can distinguish the selected model from the model that
> answered. **It does not persist the fallback as the next turn's model selection.**

and

> **Runtime fallback**: the fallback candidate applies only to the current turn. **The next
> turn starts from the selected primary again.**

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.4 (npm global install)
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200) x64, Gateway as a Scheduled Task
- `agents.defaults.model.primary` = `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`
- Configured fallbacks span several providers; `modelPolicy.allow` is a 19-entry list that
  includes `qwen-token-plan/*`, `deepseek/*`, `qwen/*` and `volcengine/doubao-*`

## Observable evidence that the answering model persists across turns

Per-window model rows recorded for the **same** `session_key` (gateway session store):

```text
09-03 12:55:54  deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash         agent:main:main
09-03 12:56:00  volcengine/doubao-seed-2-1-turbo   agent:main:main     <-- same session, 6s later
...
09-14 02:15:17  qwen-token-plan/qwen3.8-flash      agent:main:dashboard:b765f895-…
09-14 03:27:25  volcengine/doubao-seed-2-1-turbo   agent:main:dashboard:1b20c050-…
09-14 05:32:50  volcengine/doubao-seed-2-1-turbo   agent:main:dashboard:f67b5eba-…   <-- whole turns
```

The `f67b5eba` session answered a long writing task **entirely** on
`volcengine/doubao-seed-2-1-turbo-260628` while `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` was the configured
primary. That is not a single turn-local fallback; the substitution stuck for the session.

## Trigger condition (gateway log, same day)

```text
agent/embedded   embedded_run_failover_decision  decision: fallback_model  failoverReason: billing
agent/embedded   auth_profile_failure_state_updated  provider: qwen-token-plan  reason: billing  windowType: disabled
model-fallback/decision  model_fallback_decision  decision: candidate_failed / candidate_succeeded
```

i.e. a billing failure put the profile into a disabled window, the chain advanced to another
candidate, that candidate answered — and subsequent turns kept using it.

## The pin is visible, but nothing tells the operator how it got there

`openclaw status` reports the stale selection:

```text
Session agent:main:main is pinned to qwen-token-plan/qwen3.8-flash; config primary
qwen/qwen3.8-flash will apply to new/unpinned sessions.
  Reason: session override
  Clear with: /model default
```

and `docs/concepts/models.md` states explicitly:

> Changing `agents.defaults.model.primary` does not rewrite existing session pins.

So the documented remediation for "I changed the model setting and my session still runs a
different model" is `/model default` — but a session pinned by an *automatic* fallback is
reported with the same "session override" reason as one pinned by a deliberate user choice.
From the operator's side there is no way to tell which happened, and no prompt asking
whether the substitution should be kept.

## Actual behaviour

A model substitution caused by a transient provider/billing failure survives beyond the turn
that needed it, silently moves the Control UI model selection, and keeps consuming quota on a
provider the user did not select.

## Expected behaviour

Per the documented contract, the next turn starts from the selected primary again. If a
substitution is retained across turns for a legitimate reason (e.g. an `auto` pin while the
origin is still in a disabled window), then:

1. it should be labelled as **automatic**, not surfaced as a generic "session override";
2. the Control UI should mark it distinctly from a user selection and offer a one-click
   "return to primary" (the store already has `modelOverrideSource: "user" | "auto" | "default"`
   to key that off); and
3. because this crosses **billing boundaries** between providers, there should be a visible
   notice the first time a turn is answered by a model outside the selected provider —
   "silent cross-provider spend" is the part that costs people real money.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a primary model plus a fallback chain that includes a second provider.
2. Make the primary fail with a billing/quota error (so the profile enters a disabled window).
3. Send a message — the fallback answers.
4. Send a second message.

Observed: the second turn is still answered by the fallback model, and the UI model chip now
shows the fallback provider/model.

## Prior reports (checked before filing)

Three issues describe this family, **all closed** — which is why I am filing against 2026.9.4:

- **#30483** "Agent automatically switches model without user instruction" (closed) — reporter's
  cause was a hardcoded Anthropic fallback; different mechanism from the quota-driven path here.
- **#59928** "Primary model not respected after fallback" (closed, filed on **2026.4.2**) —
  same observable complaint ("a session does not reliably return to or stay on the configured
  primary model after fallback occurs; model selection in the UI/session appears …").
- **#63178** "Per-session /model override lost after compaction/fallback" (closed) — the
  opposite direction (an override disappearing), same `modelOverrideSource` state machine.

Open issues in the area (#109726, #127381, #140155, #92473, #145506) cover fallback triggers,
cost accounting, notice routing and a compaction-induced false fallback — none covers
**a fallback substitution surviving into later turns and moving the Control UI selection**.

If #59928 was closed on the assumption that turn-local fallback (and the v2026.6.1 automatic
clearing) fixed this, the rows above show it is still reproducible on 2026.9.4 — that issue may
want reopening instead of a fresh report, whichever the maintainers prefer.

## Version note

`docs/concepts/model-failover.md` says automatic clearing of stored `modelOverrideSource: "auto"`
entries shipped in **v2026.6.1**, and that OpenClaw "periodically reprobes the original primary,
clears the auto selection on recovery". On 2026.9.4 the substitution is still surviving across
turns while the origin is in a disabled window — so either the reprobe is not clearing it, or
the entry is being written under a source that is exempt from auto-clearing.

## One thing I could not verify

I was not able to read the stored `modelOverrideSource` value for the affected sessions from
this install (the session entries are not in a plain JSON file under `agents/<id>/`), so I
cannot state definitively whether these pins were written as `"auto"` or `"user"`. If they
were written as `"user"` **without any user action**, that is the more serious variant of this
bug, because per the documented selection policy a `"user"` override is exact and strict and
therefore exempt from automatic clearing. Worth checking on a reproduction.

issues.body:
## Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash).

## Summary
On a self-hosted gateway, an existing Workboard card disappeared from board listings for several hours and later reappeared with the **same card ID and intact metadata**, without any move/archive/delete action. The orchestrator agent relying on listings missed the card during the gap.

## Observed behavior
1. Card `ebab346f...` (default board) was active with comments/claims recorded on Sep 14.
2. On the morning of Sep 15 the card stopped appearing in board listings; orchestrator dispatch/review flows no longer saw it.
3. Later the same day the card reappeared with the same ID and full metadata (comments, proof, events intact). No deletion or move event exists for the gap window.

## Correlated evidence
- The gateway process restarted 3 times in the same window without a configured cause (process etime analysis places one restart at ~04:52 local).
- One restart overlaps a concurrent SQLite `VACUUM` on a *different* local database (separate memory store, window 02:54-05:09 local) - possibly coincidence, but it points at SQLite WAL/checkpoint contention around restarts.
- Separately, subagent sessions around the restarts went through transcript repair with dropped tool calls, so brief state-inconsistency windows existed.

## Expected behavior
Cards are durable rows in the workboard store; listings must always reflect committed state. A card should never vanish from the board and return later without an explicit move/archive/delete event.

## Impact
Orchestrator agents driving work off board listings silently miss cards (missed dispatches/reviews). Anti-duplication logic can also conclude the card is gone and re-create it, producing duplicates.

## Environment
- OpenClaw gateway: 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), gateway-native Workboard plugin, SQLite-backed
- Linux x86-64, npm global install (linuxbrew)
- Single gateway host, default board

## Possible directions
- Check whether workboard reads can serve a stale/empty snapshot after a gateway restart (WAL reader vs checkpoint state).
- Emit/require board events for disappearance windows (audit trail shows nothing for the affected card).
- Add an integrity diagnostic detecting rows present in the store but absent from listings.

Related but distinct: #114649 (cards vanish from a *named-agent filtered view* due to agentId assignment; here the card vanishes from the board entirely and returns).

## Summary

When the primary model (`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, ChatGPT/Codex transport) fails with a usage-limit error, the first run surfaces the raw provider error ("⚠️ API rate limit reached. Please try again later.") to the user without attempting any configured fallback. The failure is classified as `rate_limit` and written to the auth-profile cooldown state only AFTER the run ends (~1s later). The immediately following run correctly skips the cooled-down provider and succeeds on the first fallback. The fallback chain works — but never on the first occurrence.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent session with primary `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` (chatgpt-codex transport) and fallbacks [zai/glm-5.3, ollama-cloud/kimi-k3];
2. Exhaust the provider usage quota;
3. Send a message → the user receives the bare provider error; there is no `model-fallback/decision` line in the run's journal window; message outcome=error;
4. Resend ~3 minutes later → `skip_candidate … detail="Provider openai is in cooldown"` → zai/glm-5.3 succeeds and the answer is delivered.

## Expected behavior

A rate-limit/usage-limit error during a run should trigger mid-run failover to the configured fallbacks within the SAME run; the user should never see the bare provider error while healthy fallbacks exist.

## Actual behavior

The first occurrence is terminal and user-visible, with zero fallback attempts; classification + cooldown are applied post-mortem; the second run's cooldown skip works correctly.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (build 1391f7c)
- Linux gateway, systemd user unit, Telegram channel
- Session `agent:main:telegram:direct:<redacted>` (sessionId 719e30c2-…)
- Model `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` (provider openai, chatgpt-codex/responses transport, Plus plan)
- Fallback chain → zai/glm-5.3 → ollama-cloud/kimi-k3

## Evidence (gateway journal, local time UTC+6, verbatim)

**Run 1 (failed):**

- 10:45:02 inbound message (47 chars)
- 10:45:17 milestone: runId=2a4bb94e-5327-4e65-b1e4-e4364223ecee, stages=fallback_prepare_harness×8 + fallback_resolve_runtime
- 10:45:19 embedded run agent end: isError=true, model=openai/gpt-5.6-sol, provider=openai, error="⚠️ API rate limit reached. Please try again later.", rawError="Codex error: The usage limit has been reached"
- 10:45:20 "auth profile failure state updated: provider=openai, reason=rate_limit, window=cooldown, reused=false" — recorded AFTER the run had already ended
- 10:45:23 message outcome=error (21230 ms)
- **No `model-fallback/decision` line anywhere in this run's window.**

**Run 2 (succeeded, same request):**

- 10:48:45 "model fallback decision: decision=skip_candidate, requested=openai/gpt-5.6-sol, reason=rate_limit, next=zai/glm-5.3, detail=Provider openai is in cooldown"
- 10:48:47–10:49:01 zai glm-5.3 fetch → 200
- 10:49:06 candidate_succeeded → answer delivered

## User impact

Every first message after quota exhaustion returns a bare error instead of an answer despite healthy fallbacks; on messaging channels it looks like a total assistant outage.

## Notes

- Not config-fixable (the chain itself is healthy — run 2 proves it).
- The provider error arrives over the WS chatgpt-codex transport, so no per-request HTTP status is logged (error class = usage limit, 429-family).
- Related prior art: #22136 (opposite phase of the same mechanism: there the cooldown blocked fallbacks for hours; here next-run skip works, only the first-occurrence run is unprotected — likely the same code area with an opposite timing edge).
- Possibly related closed prior art: #131792 (embedded mid-turn 429 not triggering fallback), #143364 (subscription 429 misclassified as "short window", retried on the same model). Reproduced on 2026.9.3 via the chatgpt-codex WS transport.

# Control UI: page-level navigation never updates the URL, and /settings + /dashboard render the chat shell on direct load

## Summary

The Control UI's client router does not install the browser location for
page-level navigation. Two symptoms follow from the same defect:

1. Clicking top-level navigation (sidebar links, command palette) switches the
   rendered panel but never calls `history.pushState`, so the address bar keeps
   whatever path the tab was loaded on.
2. A direct load of the registered `/settings` or `/dashboard` routes renders
   the plain chat/session shell instead of the settings or dashboard UI.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: v2026.9.4 (build `2026.9.4-release-3a9d69db306c`)
- Install: native CLI under `~/.local/lib/openclaw-cli`, Gateway on
  `127.0.0.1:18789` behind a Caddy reverse proxy
- Browser: Chrome (reproducible in any; it is a client-router issue)

## Reproduction

### A. URL never updates on in-app navigation

1. Open `https://<host>/` (loads the chat shell).
2. Click the sidebar **플러그인** (Plugins) link.
3. The plugins panel renders, but the address bar still shows `/`.
4. Click **자동화** (Automations) — the panel switches, URL still `/`.
5. Refresh, or copy the URL into a new tab — you land back on Home, not the
   page you were on.

Expected: each page-level navigation pushes its canonical route
(`/plugins`, `/automations`, `/dashboards`, …) so refresh, back/forward, and
bookmarks work.

### B. `/settings` and `/dashboard` render the chat shell on direct load

1. Open a new tab directly to `https://<host>/settings`.
2. The server returns 200 and the SPA loads, but the content is the plain
   chat/session view — no settings panel, drawer, or section list.
3. Same for `https://<host>/dashboard` — renders the chat shell; the only
   dashboard element is the collapsed side-panel tab present on every view.

Both are registered routes in the client route table
(`settings:{path:'/settings'}`, `dashboard:{path:'/dashboard'}`), so this is not
a missing-route fallback — the router resolves the route id but does not render
its page. Leaf routes such as `/settings/plugins` and `/dashboards` do render
correctly on direct load.

## Root-cause analysis (from the shipped bundle)

In `dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-core-*.js`:

- The router's `navigate` is invoked with `history:'none'` for dynamic/plugin
  route transitions, and page-level sidebar navigation does not push a history
  entry at all. `window.history.pushState`/`replaceState` exist in the bundle
  but are not driven by page-level navigation.
- `ro()`/`no()` resolve `/settings` and `/dashboard` to their route ids, but the
  resolved location is never installed/rendered as a page, so the shell falls
  through to the default session view.

## Related (already worked around locally)

`/plugins` additionally returned a bare server `404 Not Found` on direct load
because `classifyControlUiRequest` excluded the whole `/plugins` namespace from
Control UI serving while the client registers `plugins:{path:'/plugins'}`. We
narrowed the exclusion to `/plugins/*` locally so the SPA is served; plugin-owned
routes under `/plugins/*` are unaffected because they are handled by an earlier
request stage. Worth fixing upstream so the canonical client route is servable.

## Impact

- Deep links, bookmarks, refresh, and back/forward are broken for every
  page-level view.
- `/settings` and `/dashboard` are unreachable as real pages.
- Combined with the `/plugins` 404, the Plugins page was completely
  un-bookmarkable/un-refreshable.

issues.title: [Bug]: PR preflight throws at 121 jobs against the 120 Node matrix cap

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: clawsweeper:needs-info

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

labels.name: impact:other
labels.description: This issue has meaningful maintainer-visible impact outside the owned taxonomy.

issues.body:
Since `ece550b7c2d`, `preflight` throws on any pull request whose diff reaches the core extension impact rule, and `openclaw/ci-gate` goes red before a single test job starts.

```
Error: Canonical pull_request Node matrix has 121 jobs, exceeding limit 120
    at file:///home/runner/_work/openclaw/openclaw/[eval1]:506:9
```

### What produces the count

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1704` caps a pull-request matrix at 120 non-dist rows. When `createChangedNodeTestShards` cannot plan a diff precisely it returns `null`, and the target then runs the full compact plan plus every extension fallback row (`ci.yml:1606-1620`). On the `github` runner profile that is 79 compact rows and 44 fallback rows, 121 of which are non-dist.

One changed core file is enough to reach it. From a clean checkout:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e '
const { createNodeTestShardBundles } = await import("./scripts/lib/ci-node-test-plan.mts");
const { createChangedNodeTestShards, createChangedExtensionFallbackShards } = await import("./scripts/lib/ci-changed-node-test-plan.mts");
const changedPaths = ["src/config/types.ts"];
const changed = createChangedNodeTestShards(changedPaths, { runnerBackend: "github" });
const shards = changed ?? [
  ...createNodeTestShardBundles({ includeReleaseOnlyPluginShards: false, changedPaths, compact: true, compactMode: "pull-request", runnerBackend: "github" }),
  ...createChangedExtensionFallbackShards(changedPaths),
];
console.log(shards.filter((s) => !s.requiresDist).length);
'
```

| revision | rows |
| --- | --- |
| `b09af220ef3`, the parent | 120, exactly at the cap |
| `ece550b7c2d` fix(chat): show saved interrupted replies only once (#149405) | 121 |
| `472a5e958de`, main now | 121 |

`ece550b7c2d` added `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.receipt.test.ts`. Fallback rows are bin-packed to `CHANGED_EXTENSION_JOB_SECONDS` (240) in `scripts/lib/ci-changed-node-test-plan.mts:95`, so one more extension test file bought one more bin. 43 became 44 and the total crossed.

### Reach

Every diff the precise planner declines that also has core extension impact. `hasCoreExtensionImpact` is true for a changed `src/` path inside the plugin SDK import graph, so a change to a plain core file such as `src/config/types.ts` reproduces it on its own. A diff that stays inside `extensions/` keeps its precise plan and is unaffected, which is why most pull requests are still green.

### Observed

#147886, run 35050213004. `preflight` and `openclaw/ci-gate` both failed, no Node test job started. The same count reproduces on main with none of that branch's commits, which is how I arrived at the table above.

I have not opened a fix because the number reads as a runner budget decision rather than a planner defect. Two directions look reasonable, raising the pull-request cap, or packing the fallback rows into the headroom the compact plan leaves. I am glad to send whichever you prefer.

issues.title: Heartbeat-woken turn text output has a single delivery slot (alert path) — pending alert delivery can be silently dropped when superseded by the next wake; and any non-ack text is pushed as an "alert"

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:message-loss
labels.description: Channel message delivery can be lost, duplicated, or misrouted.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
### Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.9.4** (Homebrew install, macOS arm64), gateway with Telegram channel
- Heartbeat enabled per-agent (interval-based job)

### What happened

**Case 1 — silent loss (high impact):**
A background-woken turn (heartbeat poll wake) produced a substantive multi-paragraph status report as its final text output. The report exists verbatim in the session transcript. Gateway logs show **zero delivery records** for it — no heartbeat event, no send, nothing. ~40s later, a second background wake (subagent completion event) in the same session produced a short ack text; that one **was** delivered, ~11s after being output, and the delivered message carried the "First heartbeat alert:" preamble — which is only prepended when no alert has ever been sent for that policy session entry. This proves the earlier report was never sent (otherwise the first-alert preamble would not appear on the later message).

**Case 2 — over-broad "alert" semantics (noise):**
Separately, on the same day, interval heartbeat turns that ended with long plain-text summaries (some literally concluding "nothing new, ending silently") were each pushed to the owner's DM as messages, with heartbeat event `status=sent, indicatorType=alert`. Three such pushes in one morning. Any non-ack final text — including self-described "silent" wrap-ups — is treated as an alert and pushed (when `showAlerts` is true, the default).

### Source-level findings (from reading the installed dist bundle)

1. `resolveIndicatorType`: `sent → alert`, `ok-empty/ok-token → ok`, `failed → error`. Delivery itself defines "alert" — there is no content-based judgment, so a "nothing to report" summary still arrives as an alert push.
2. Heartbeat dispatch: for a heartbeat turn, non-ack text is delivered **only** through the alert path; if `!channel || !to || !showAlerts`, the text is finished as `skipped` (`no-target` / `alerts-disabled`) and **dropped — it never falls back to the normal chat reply routing**.
3. All background wakes (heartbeat poll, subagent completion events, system events) are routed through the same heartbeat/session-event wake handler, so this single-slot alert delivery applies to completion-event-woken turns too (confirmed by the delivered ack in Case 1 going out as an alert).
4. There appears to be a pending-delivery window: the Case-1 report's alert never settled before the next wake replaced the run, and the text was lost with no tombstone (no event, no log, no undelivered marker).

### Impact

- Substantive reports generated in background-woken turns can be **silently lost** (no error anywhere), while trivial acks get delivered — worst kind of loss (important content dropped, noise delivered).
- Long "nothing new" summaries are pushed as alerts, training users to ignore heartbeat pushes.

### Suggestions (either would help)

1. **Durability:** when an alert-path delivery is pending and the run gets superseded, don't drop the text silently — persist it as an undelivered/pending final delivery (the `pendingFinalDelivery` replay machinery seems close) or at least emit a heartbeat event with a `dropped/superseded` reason so operators can detect loss.
2. **Routing/config:** offer a config option for heartbeat-woken turns' final text to route through the normal reply pipeline (same as a user-facing reply) instead of the single alert slot, or make alert-vs-ack classification smarter than "any non-ack text = alert".

### Reproduction sketch (sanitized)

1. Configure heartbeat for an agent with a Telegram DM target (defaults: `showOk=false, showAlerts=true`).
2. While a heartbeat-woken turn is producing a long final report, trigger another session-event wake (e.g. a subagent completion) shortly after the report is emitted but before the turn fully settles.
3. Observe: the report never arrives; the next wake's output arrives (with the first-alert preamble if no prior alert was sent).
4. Separately: let an interval heartbeat turn end with any long plain-text summary → it is pushed to the DM with `indicatorType=alert`.

issues.title: Model-fallback tainted turns: recovery retries re-run the same source message multiple times, each re-sending the answer via message tool (4-6x duplicate Telegram replies)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr

labels.description: Channel message delivery can be lost, duplicated, or misrouted.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), self-hosted gateway, Linux x64, Node v24.21.0
- Channel: Telegram, multi-account (3 enabled bot accounts, separate agents via `bindings[]`), polling mode, owner direct chats
- Inbound trigger: voice notes (with transcription)
- Models: agent primary `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` with fallback chain (`ollama/deepseek-v4-flash:cloud`, ...). Primary provider was in rate-limit cooldown during the window (model-fallback `skip_candidate ... reason=rate_limit` → `candidate_succeeded` decisions in the same minutes).

## Observed behavior

A single inbound Telegram voice note from the owner produced **4-6 visible duplicate replies, each from a separate assistant turn**. Two different agents on two different bot accounts reproduced the same pattern the same day, under the same rate-limit-cooldown conditions.

Outbound timeline for one account (gateway log, `outbound send ok` entries):

- 14:25:57 inbound voice note
- 14:25:57 → 14:26:57 sends 1718, 1720, 1721, 1722, 1723, 1724, 1725 — each a separate send from a **separate agent turn re-invoked for the same source message**

Session transcript shows every re-invocation arriving with the standard message-tool delivery note ("Final assistant text is not automatically delivered in this run. Use the `message` tool to send the final user-visible answer."), so the model re-sends the answer each pass. The **first attempt's `message(action=send)` had already succeeded** before the retries fired. Eventually the model notices prior sends in transcript and withholds — so the visible symptom is duplicate bubbles, and the secondary symptom is agents "learning" to suppress sends.

## Expected behavior (per docs)

`docs/gateway/config-channels/mention-gating-and-history.md`:

> "For substantive source turns OpenClaw now attempts **one** guarded recovery retry; ... **already delivered turns are not retried**."

Observed: multiple re-runs of the same source turn, each producing another visible send. Either the retry cap is not enforced on this path, or the "already delivered" guard does not recognize message-tool sends from earlier attempts of the same source message.

## Suspected mechanism

When the primary model is in rate-limit cooldown and the turn runs on a fallback model, the turn ends tainted/failed in a way that re-triggers the recovery-retry path repeatedly. The delivery guard appears to consider the turn undelivered because its bookkeeping doesn't count the successful `message(action=send)` from the earlier attempt.

Related: #143714 documents the recovery-retry machinery misfiring on empty responses (heartbeat case, maintainer-labeled). This report is the same machinery producing **duplicate user-visible deliveries on real message turns** under model fallback + voice-note transcription. Closed #99510 was an older, different duplicate-delivery path.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Telegram direct chat with the owner; send a voice note (transcription on)
2. Agent model: primary provider rate-limited so the turn runs on a fallback model
3. Agent answers via `message(action=send, final)`; send succeeds
4. Observe multiple additional turns for the same source message, each re-delivering

## Impact

- 4-6x duplicate replies per message in owner direct chats
- Downstream model confusion: agents begin suppressing sends to compensate (observed), risking the opposite failure (no delivery)

Happy to provide full sanitized logs and transcript excerpts.

issues.title: Windows node: allow unsandboxed exec mode for trusted nodes

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Marked as stale due to inactivity

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:security
labels.description: Security boundary, credential, authz, sandbox, or sensitive-data risk.

issues.body:
## Feature Request

### Problem

The Windows node executes agent commands (`system.run`) under a restricted sandbox token. This sandbox:

- **Read-only filesystem** — any write to `C:\dev\…` returns "Access is denied", even after granting full ACLs to the sandbox user (verified: the restriction is the exec token, not file ACLs)
- **No child process creation** — `node.exe`, `npm`, `powershell`, `tasklist`, `git`, `electron` all fail with `0xC0000142` (DLL init failed); only `cmd` builtins, `findstr`, and Python survive
- **No localhost sockets** — connecting to `127.0.0.1:9222` (e.g. a CDP debug port on a locally-launched Electron app) fails with `WinError 10013`
- **Virtualized home dir** — `LOCALAPPDATA` points to `Packages\sandbox.{guid}\AC` instead of the real user profile

The tray Permissions page exposes toggles for Windows node, System tools, individual commands (`system.run`, etc.) — all of which can be enabled. But there is **no option to disable the sandbox itself** and run commands as the real user with full filesystem write access and child-process creation.

### Impact

Agents cannot:
- Run `npm run build` or `npm run desktop` on a Windows project
- Write or edit project files (code fixes, config patches)
- Attach to locally-running dev servers or debug ports (CDP, etc.)
- Run `git pull` / `git push` / `gh` on a Windows checkout

The workaround is to hand the operator a copy-paste command for every step that needs real execution, then read results back read-only. This works but adds a round-trip per step and prevents autonomous workflows on Windows.

### Request

Add a tray option (or gateway config flag) like:

> **Allow unsandboxed system commands (full user access)**

that, when explicitly enabled for a trusted node, runs `system.run` commands as the real logged-in user instead of the sandbox token — giving the agent the same filesystem write access, child-process creation, and localhost networking that the operator's own terminal has.

This should be:
- **Off by default** (current sandbox behavior preserved)
- **Per-node** (not global)
- **Clearly labeled as a security trade-off** (the agent can now modify files and launch arbitrary processes)
- Optionally gated behind the existing exec allowlist/security policy so the operator still controls *which* commands are permitted

### Context

- OpenClaw gateway on WSL, paired with a Windows tray node
- `gateway.nodes.commands.allow` includes `system.run` and `system.run.prepare`
- `tools.exec` = `{host:auto, security:allowlist, ask:on-miss}`
- All tray toggles for the node and system tools are ON
- Verified that the sandbox is the exec token itself, not file ACLs or missing permissions

issues.body:
### Summary

Make dashboard widget size presets and the saved width understandable in Widget options.

### Problem to solve

A small widget fills a narrow dashboard, then occupies only a quarter of the dashboard when the window becomes wider. In the macOS Companion split view, this can look like a broken dashboard layout after choosing a size preset.

The menu currently shows SM/MD/LG/XL with grid dimensions, but does not explain their relative widths, show the saved width, or explain the narrow-dashboard override. Choosing a preset also fixes the height, which is easy to miss when the widget previously used Auto height.

### Proposed solution

- Label presets with their relative width: quarter, half, two-thirds, full.
- Show the saved width out of 12 columns, including custom widths and widgets using Auto height.
- Explain that narrow dashboards fill the available width and wider dashboards restore the saved width.
- Explain that presets fix height and Auto height fits the content again.

### Alternatives considered

Always expanding a single widget to full width would override the user's saved size. Changing the responsive breakpoint would alter existing layout behavior. Clear feedback in the existing menu addresses the confusion without either change.

### Impact

Affected: users resizing dashboard widgets, particularly in the Companion split view or a narrow dashboard pane.
Severity: confusing layout feedback, not data loss or a blocked resize operation.
Frequency: reproducible when a partial-width widget's dashboard crosses the narrow layout breakpoint.
Consequence: users can mistake intentional responsive sizing for a failed resize and repeatedly adjust the window or widget.

### Evidence/examples

Observed with OpenClaw 2026.9.4 on macOS and reproduced using the upstream synthetic board fixture. With SM selected, a 1,128px dashboard renders the widget at 273px; at a 544px dashboard width, the same saved three-column widget fills the dashboard. XL correctly fills the wide dashboard.

The existing documentation already describes the responsive behavior: https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/dashboards

The proposed PR will include visually inspected before/after screenshots containing only synthetic fixture data.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

This is a focused Control UI usability improvement. It preserves persisted dimensions, resize operations, responsive layout rules, and widget isolation.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
