### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.9.2 the `NO_VISIBLE_REPLY_FALLBACK_TEXT` notice ("No reply was generated for this message. This is usually a temporary model failure - please try again.") is delivered to a Telegram DM 1-2 seconds after the same turn's `agent.run.finished` was recorded with `status=succeeded`, and a real answer for that turn arrives 30-60 seconds later.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed (not reduced to a minimal constructed repro):

1. Run 2026.9.2 with a Telegram DM channel, model `anthropic/claude-opus-5`.
2. Send a message that causes the agent to run `exec` tool calls and end the turn without emitting a text reply payload.
3. Observe the fallback notice delivered to the chat 1-2 seconds after `agent.run.finished` for that run is written to `audit_events` with `status=succeeded`.
4. Observe a real, substantive answer arriving 30-60 seconds later as a separate message.

Observed 4/4 times within a 9-minute window. I did not attempt a reduced repro against the live gateway, so the minimal trigger condition is not established here.

### Expected behavior

A turn whose own `agent.run.finished` audit record states `status=succeeded` should not additionally produce a user-facing notice stating that the model failed and that the user should retry.

No known-good earlier version was tested, so this is not grounded as a regression against a specific prior release; the reference is the system's own contradicting audit record for the same turn.

### Actual behavior

The fallback notice is delivered as a separate chat message shortly after a successful run. Correlating `audit_events` in `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` against the Telegram message cache:

| fallback message | delivered | preceding `agent.run.finished` | status | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #268 | 00:56:27 | run `9a91ebbc…` at 00:56:25 | `succeeded` | 2s |
| #272 | 00:59:32 | run `eceeeed4…` at 00:59:30 | `succeeded` | 2s |
| #274 | 01:00:28 | run `5171ac7e…` at 01:00:26 | `succeeded` | 2s |
| #278 | 01:04:59 | run `d9eb3eba…` at 01:04:57 | `succeeded` | 2s |

The same database does contain genuinely failed runs across its wider history (`agent_run`: 120 `succeeded`, 11 `failed`, 19 `blocked`, 1 `timed_out`), but none of those fall inside this window. Each of the four notices follows a `succeeded` run.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2

### Operating system

Windows 11

### Install method

npm global; gateway launched via Windows Task Scheduler (`schtasks`)

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

Main agent: `agents.defaults.model = anthropic/claude-opus-5` (direct Anthropic provider via an auth profile).
Heartbeat agent: `agents.defaults.heartbeat.model = anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.

Two further providers are configured in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` but are not the default route for the affected agent: a local `ollama` provider (`http://127.0.0.1:11434`) and a `litellm` provider (`http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1`, `api: openai-completions`). The affected turns ran on the default Anthropic route.

### Logs

```shell
# audit_events around each of the four notices (local times, Europe/Berlin)
# --- notice #268 delivered 00:56:27 ---
00:55:49  agent.run.started     started
00:56:00  tool.action.started   started    tool_name=exec
00:56:05  tool.action.finished  succeeded  tool_name=exec
00:56:25  agent.run.finished    succeeded            <-- notice delivered ~2s later

# --- notice #272 delivered 00:59:32 ---
00:58:26  agent.run.started     started
00:58:39  tool.action.started   started    tool_name=exec
00:58:39  tool.action.finished  succeeded  tool_name=exec
00:59:01  tool.action.started   started    tool_name=exec
00:59:18  tool.action.finished  succeeded  tool_name=exec
00:59:30  agent.run.finished    succeeded            <-- notice delivered ~2s later

# --- notice #274 delivered 01:00:28 ---
00:59:46  agent.run.started     started
00:59:57  tool.action.started   started    tool_name=exec
01:00:00  tool.action.finished  succeeded  tool_name=exec
01:00:08  tool.action.started   started    tool_name=exec
01:00:08  tool.action.finished  succeeded  tool_name=exec
01:00:26  agent.run.finished    succeeded            <-- notice delivered ~2s later

# --- notice #278 delivered 01:04:59 ---
01:04:32  agent.run.started     started
01:04:39  tool.action.started   started    tool_name=exec
01:04:43  tool.action.finished  succeeded  tool_name=exec
01:04:57  agent.run.finished    succeeded            <-- notice delivered ~2s later

# run status distribution across the whole local audit_events table
agent_run status=succeeded : 120
agent_run status=started   : 147
agent_run status=blocked   :  19
agent_run status=failed    :  11
agent_run status=timed_out :   1
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots retained. The evidence is the `audit_events` correlation above, read from `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` (opened read-only), plus the four cached Telegram messages carrying the fallback text in `plugin_state_entries` under `telegram / telegram.message-cache`.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Telegram DM users on 2026.9.2 whose turns end without a text reply payload.
- Severity: Annoying / misleading rather than blocking. No message is lost; the real answer still arrives.
- Frequency: 4/4 qualifying turns in the observed 9-minute window.
- Consequence: The user is told a request failed and should be retried when the audit record shows it succeeded. Retrying duplicates work that already completed. In a conversation where such turns are common, the notice appears between the question and the real answer on most of them.

### Additional information

Hypothesis, clearly separated from the observations above because I could not confirm it:

The notice is emitted in the finalize path under this guard:

```js
const noVisibleReplyFallbackAllowed = () =>
     noVisibleReplyFallbackDirected
  && !suppressDelivery
  && !sendPolicyDenied
  && state.sourceReplyDeliveryMode !== "message_tool_only"
  && !emptyFinalAllowedAsSilent
  && !deliberateSilentTerminalReply
  && !pendingContinuation
  && !sessionWriterDeliveryRevoked
  && !channelTransformSuppressed
  && !getObservedReplyDelivery()
  && !replyAcceptedByActiveRun
  && !turnLedger.hasVisibleDelivery();
```

Visible delivery appears to be recorded only in `prepareReplyPayloadForSideEffects`, which requires outbound text/media content:

```js
if (outcome.payload.isReasoning !== true
    && outcome.payload.isCommentary !== true
    && hasOutboundReplyContent(outcome.payload, { trimText: true })) onVisibleAccepted?.();
```

whereas `ask_user` prompts are routed through a separate branch:

```js
function requiresDurableToolResultDelivery(payload) {
  return resolveSendableOutboundReplyParts(payload).hasMedia
    || hasExecApprovalPayload(payload)
    || hasExecApprovalUnavailablePayload(payload)
    || hasAskUserPayload(payload);
}
```

If a turn's only user-facing output is an `ask_user` button prompt, it may never reach `onVisibleAccepted`, leaving `turnLedger.hasVisibleDelivery()` false even though the buttons were delivered and rendered. Exec-approval prompts sit in the same branch and would be affected by the same reasoning.

What I could not confirm:

- That the message immediately preceding each notice was an `ask_user` prompt. The reporting user observed a button prompt displayed immediately before the notice, but the local Telegram message cache has gaps throughout the range (17 missing IDs between 170 and 280) that are not specific to these events, so the cached record does not establish it.
- That `turnLedger.hasVisibleDelivery()` returns false on these turns. The code above was read from the shipped `dist/` bundle, not instrumented at runtime.

Unrelated but present on this install, in case it matters for triage: the 2026.9.1 -> 2026.9.2 update reported `post-core-update-failed` because the post-update doctor could not enter maintenance ("Gateway service ownership or shutdown could not be verified") while the gateway was owned by Windows Task Scheduler, with `recovery.serviceRestartSafe: false`. The package files updated and the gateway was subsequently restarted onto 2026.9.2, but that repair pass never ran.

Possibly related existing issues, none of which cover a `succeeded` turn being reported as a model failure: #137281 (same text, TTS reply stripped to nothing), #116348 (request to suppress/rate-limit this fallback), #133418 (`ask_user` option rendering on LINE).

issues.body:
## Summary
Every `sessions_spawn` call that creates a dashboard-channel subagent (used to delegate a task to a different model, e.g. an agent on `openai/*` delegating to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) fails before doing any work, 100% reproducible across multiple independent attempts with zero concurrent load:

```
embedded tool authority registration does not match its attempt
```

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (npm package install), systemd-managed gateway
- Parent agent running `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, spawning a subagent pinned to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` (Claude Pro account via native claude-cli auth, no Anthropic API key configured)

## Repro
1. From an agent's main session, call `sessions_spawn` with `runtime: "subagent"`, `context: "isolated"`, a different `model` than the parent, `expectsCompletionMessage: true`. This creates a child session like `agent:<id>:dashboard:<uuid>`.
2. Spawn is accepted (`status: "accepted"`), a real child session/run is created.
3. Within under a second, the child's first turn fails:
   - `[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:<id>:dashboard:<uuid> ... error="embedded tool authority registration does not match its attempt"`
   - `Embedded agent failed before reply: embedded tool authority registration does not match its attempt`

## Root cause (traced in the installed compiled build)
In `src/agents/harness/tool-authority.runtime.ts`, `withPreparedEmbeddedRunToolAuthority` builds an `embeddedRunToolAuthorityBinding` callback closed over the *current attempt's* `sessionId/sessionKey/sessionFile/agentId/runId/fingerprint`, registered via `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity`.

In `src/agents/tools/gateway-caller-context.ts`, `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity` resolves the binding as:
```js
const embeddedRunToolAuthorityBinding = identity.embeddedRunToolAuthorityBinding ?? inheritedOwner?.embeddedRunToolAuthorityBinding;
```
The newly-spawned child's own embedded-run setup does not supply its own `embeddedRunToolAuthorityBinding` in `identity` at the point registration happens (confirmed via debug logging), so this falls back to whatever is inherited from the ambient `AsyncLocalStorage` context. Since `sessions_spawn` runs as a tool call *inside* the parent's own turn, the ambient context still carries the **parent's** binding, closed over the parent's own session/run identity. When the child's real registration later invokes what it thinks is its own callback, it's actually invoking the parent's, comparing the child's real identity against the parent's expected one — a guaranteed mismatch every time, not a race.

## Evidence
Captured via temporary debug logging right before the throw:

```json
{
  "expected": {"sessionId":"faec06bd-...","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","sessionFile":"agent:main:main","agentId":"main","runId":"afdf9716-..."},
  "actual":   {"sessionId":"01f55e1e-...","sessionKey":"agent:main:dashboard:e008b0d4-...","sessionFile":"sqlite:main:01f55e1e-...:/home/.../sessions.json","agentId":"main","runId":"45a85d40-..."}
}
```
`expected` is the **parent** session's own identity; `actual` is the genuinely new child. This is the parent's leftover binding firing for the child's registration, not a stale-value bug within one run.

## Impact
Any `sessions_spawn` creating a dashboard-channel child to delegate to a different model fails outright, before any work happens. In our case the parent agent has a separate fallback (invoking the target model's CLI directly via `exec` instead of `sessions_spawn`) that masks the failure with an eventual successful result via a different mechanism, which is how we noticed the native spawn path was silently broken despite the user-visible outcome succeeding.

## Suggested fix direction
Ensure the child's own embedded-run setup always supplies its own `embeddedRunToolAuthorityBinding` in the `identity` passed to `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity`, so the `?? inheritedOwner?.embeddedRunToolAuthorityBinding` fallback is never reached for a genuinely new spawned run. Alternatively, tighten the inheritance rule (`!suppliedRun || inheritedRun === suppliedRun`) so a new operational run instance never inherits a binding meant for a different run even when its own is absent.

issues.body:
### Problem
The session progress card is a visibility tool, but "forgetting to clear the card after task completion" happens repeatedly in practice. In a single day on one machine we observed **4/4 sessions violating** card hygiene — most commonly, a fully-green plan checklist gets kept as a "final state" instead of being cleared. Stale cards make it impossible for an observer (hovercard / sidebar) to distinguish "just finished" from "stalled".

### Proposal
Add optional parameters (or global config) to the `progress_card` tool:

- `expireAfter`: duration or absolute timestamp; card auto-clears on expiry
- `completedBehavior`: `"keep" | "clear" | "fade"` — default disposition when all plan steps reach `completed`

### Why
- Card hygiene currently depends on session self-discipline; an explicit lifecycle option removes that dependency
- Task cards already have a deliberate 7-day terminal retention; session progress cards have the *opposite* lifecycle need and currently lack any explicit option

### Data
Observed on a single machine with 20+ active sessions. Three symptom classes (never cleared / never refreshed / all-green kept), shared root cause: motivation gradient degrades across the card's three-step lifecycle (set → update → clear). Detailed violation samples and root-cause analysis available on request.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.9.2 (npm install)
- Node: 26.8.1
- Platform: linux
- Provider: `anthropic` with `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` (Claude Code CLI reuse, authenticated via `claude setup-token` / `openclaw models auth paste-token`)

## Config used

```json5
{
  agents: {
    entries: {
      "claude-code": {
        model: { primary: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5" },
        models: {
          "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5": {
            agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    defaults: {
      subagents: {
        allowAgents: ["claude-code"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## What works

Direct one-shot invocation works correctly:

```
openclaw infer model run --agent claude-code --prompt "test"
```

Returns a valid 200 response from `provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-5` (resolves to Claude Sonnet 4.5), using the subscription token — no issue there.

## What fails

When the `main` agent (a different agent, model `minimax/MiniMax-M3`) attempts to delegate to `claude-code` via `sessions_spawn` (subagent spawn), every attempt fails immediately:

```
error: embedded tool authority registration does not match its attempt
```

Log line: `lane=session:agent:claude-code:subagent:<uuid>` — fails within 1-2ms, before any actual model call.

## Ruled out

- Not an auth issue: `openclaw models auth paste-token --provider anthropic --agent claude-code` succeeded, direct invocation works fine.
- Not a naming issue: renamed the agent entry to `claude-cli` (matching the `agentRuntime.id`) and re-tested — identical error, same failure mode. Reverted this test agent afterward.
- Not a stale-state issue: reproduced identically on a freshly restarted gateway (no warm subprocess carried over from prior direct-invocation tests).
- Already on latest: `openclaw update --dry-run` confirms `2026.9.2` is current, no pending update to try.

## Code analysis (dist bundle, may not map 1:1 to source line numbers on `main`)

The throwing check is generic (used by all runtimes), in `tool-authority.runtime-*.js`:

```js
if (registration.sessionId !== sessionId
    || registration.sessionKey !== sessionKey
    || registration.sessionFile !== sessionFile
    || registration.agentId !== void 0 && registration.agentId !== agentId
    || handle.runId !== runId
    || !fingerprint
    || handle.toolAuthorityFingerprint !== fingerprint)
  throw new Error("embedded tool authority registration does not match its attempt");
```

Tracing where `registration.agentId` could come from a mismatched identity, `gateway-caller-context-*.js` has this inheritance logic inside `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity`:

```js
const inherited = gatewayToolCallerStorage.getStore();
const suppliedRun = identity.operationalRunInstance;
const inheritedRun = inherited?.operationalRunInstance;
const inheritedOwner = !suppliedRun || inheritedRun === suppliedRun ? inherited : void 0;
...
agentId: inheritedOwner?.agentId ?? identity.agentId.trim()
```

If the new (child/subagent) `identity` does not carry an `operationalRunInstance` (`!suppliedRun`), the code falls back to inheriting the **parent's** stored identity (`inherited`) wholesale — including the parent's `agentId` — rather than using the subagent's own `agentId`. That would produce exactly this symptom: the subagent's tool-authority registration ends up carrying the parent's `agentId` ("main"), which then fails the equality check against the subagent's expected `agentId` ("claude-code") in `tool-authority.runtime`.

**Hypothesis** (not confirmed against the claude-cli bridge's actual call site, which I could not fully trace in the minified bundle): the `claude-cli` agent runtime does not populate `operationalRunInstance` when preparing its embedded tool authority for a spawned subagent turn, triggering the parent-inheritance branch above instead of establishing an isolated identity for the child.

## Repro steps

1. Configure two agents: `main` (any model/runtime) and a second agent using `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`.
2. Add the second agent's id to `agents.defaults.subagents.allowAgents`.
3. Authenticate the second agent via `claude setup-token` + `openclaw models auth paste-token --provider anthropic --agent <id>`.
4. Restart gateway.
5. From `main`, trigger a subagent spawn targeting the claude-cli agent (e.g. via `sessions_spawn` in a live session).
6. Observe immediate failure: `embedded tool authority registration does not match its attempt`.

Direct invocation of the same claude-cli agent (`openclaw infer model run --agent <id>`) works fine — only the subagent-spawn path is affected.

issues.body:
### Version

`OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)`

### Summary

`config_revision` is a **content hash** of scheduler definition state, not a counter. It therefore cycles: any sequence of writes that returns a job's definition to an earlier state reproduces the earlier revision value exactly. There is no monotonic witness for "this scheduler row has been mutated since I last looked", which makes a whole class of crash-recovery decisions undecidable for anything coordinating scheduler mutations from outside the gateway.

### What I measured

`cron_run_receipts.config_revision` on the installed build holds values of the form:

```
sha256:1G__-1NsDidK2gKeG5W0498-l5IDwhuiPYwavTPSiKk
sha256:1HOYtlFadU6BZwZ3msfTBkJXMzi1a_HnZ5SiMuagEA4
sha256:2SylwFJVGuO1-5Zz8IGZaV4qWH3GydRhR4T53pGtP4Q
```

A content hash over definition state. Disable a job and re-enable it and the value returns to what it was before, because the definition state did. That is correct for the job it does — detecting that a definition changed under you — and unusable as an ordering or write-count witness.

The nearest alternative, `scheduleActivatedAtMs`, does advance on a mutation, but it is generated *inside* the update transaction, so an external caller cannot record its post-write value before the write it is trying to survive.

### Why it matters

A supervisor that repoints a scheduler row does so as a multi-step sequence: disable the row, write the new payload, re-enable it. If it publishes a fence describing the change and then dies mid-sequence, crash repair has to decide between two histories that end in an identical state:

- **Stale crash:** the fence was published, the row was disabled, the process died. The row should be re-enabled.
- **Legitimate:** the repoint completed, the fence's publisher died before clearing it, and an operator disabled the row later. The row must be left alone — re-enabling it would revive something a human deliberately turned off.

Both end at a disabled row whose payload matches the fence's target, with the same fence body, the same publisher identity, and a `config_revision` that can be made equal by choosing a suitable starting state. The two histories differ only in **write count** — one write versus three — and nothing durable records write count.

Without a witness, repair must take the conservative branch and leave the row disabled, which strands the stale-crash case permanently. That is survivable but wrong, and it is only survivable because prevention (refusing to act when the row changed under the decision) keeps the state rare.

### What would fix it

Either of these makes the two histories distinguishable:

- **A monotonic mutation counter on scheduler rows** — a strictly increasing integer bumped once per applied write, exposed alongside `config_revision` and readable before a mutation. Content hashing and ordering are different jobs; `config_revision` should keep doing the first.
- **Persist a caller-supplied causal witness inside the same scheduler transaction as the mutation**, so an external coordinator can record "the revision immediately before my own write" atomically rather than racing it.

I am not asking for `config_revision` to change semantics — hashing definition state is the right primitive for change detection. The gap is that there is no second primitive for ordering.

### Reproduction

```sh
sqlite3 ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite \
  "select distinct config_revision from cron_run_receipts limit 5;"
```

Every value is a `sha256:` digest over definition state, with no ordering information.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add a runtime-enforced checkpoint policy for long foreground agent runs so that, after a configurable silent-time or tool-call budget, OpenClaw publishes a meaningful status update and cleanly yields before more work is dispatched.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw can stream tool activity and models can be instructed to send commentary during multi-step work. Neither mechanism guarantees that a direct foreground WebChat run will stop at a user-defined checkpoint.

In repeated real-world maintenance workflows, an agent was given explicit workspace instructions to:

- publish a user-facing status update at least every 30–45 seconds;
- stop after a small number of tool calls;
- report the verified state and exact next step before continuing.

The model sometimes followed those rules, but it also repeatedly continued with “one more check” and exceeded the intended stage boundary. One such run eventually ended with a timeout/abort before a final handoff. This is not primarily a tool failure: the missing control is a runtime-owned boundary around the *foreground agent loop*.

Current facilities solve adjacent problems but not this one:

- progress streaming shows activity but does not enforce a semantic checkpoint or yield;
- queue steering allows new user input at model boundaries but does not create a boundary on a quiet run;
- per-tool timeouts bound individual calls, not the number or duration of successive calls;
- the overall turn timeout aborts late and may provide no clean last-known-state handoff;
- TaskFlow provides durable background orchestration, but ordinary interactive WebChat work still runs as one foreground turn unless explicitly moved into a task flow;
- prompt or `AGENTS.md` rules remain model-behavior constraints and are therefore not reliable enforcement.

This makes users uncertain whether the agent is progressing, drifting into unrelated checks, or stuck. It also forces them to supervise or manually interrupt work that should be safely bounded.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Configure workspace instructions requiring a visible status every 30–45 seconds and a stop after a fixed number of tool calls.
2. Start a direct WebChat request that needs several diagnostic or implementation calls.
3. Observe that the agent may emit an initial preamble but continue beyond the requested time/tool budget.
4. The UI can show low-level activity, but there is no runtime guarantee of a concise checkpoint containing verified state, meaning, and next action.
5. If the foreground run later times out or is aborted, the user may receive no controlled yield or durable continuation point.

Because model behavior is nondeterministic, the exact number of calls varies. The reproducible architectural fact is that OpenClaw currently has no configurable foreground-loop checkpoint enforcement; compliance depends on the model following instructions.

## Proposed solution

Introduce an opt-in, runtime-owned checkpoint policy for foreground agent runs, with agent defaults and optional channel/session overrides. An illustrative shape could be:

```yaml
agents:
  defaults:
    foregroundCheckpoints:
      enabled: true
      maxSilentMs: 30000
      maxToolCalls: 4
      action: checkpoint-and-yield
```

The exact schema is only a suggestion. The behavioral contract is more important:

1. Track elapsed time since the last user-visible semantic update and the number of completed tool calls since that update.
2. When either budget is reached, do not dispatch another tool call.
3. At the next safe model boundary, require a compact checkpoint with:
   - the current phase;
   - the last verified state;
   - the meaning or risk;
   - the exact next step;
   - whether user approval is required.
4. Publish that checkpoint to the originating WebChat and persist enough continuation metadata to resume safely.
5. End/yield the foreground turn cleanly. A later user message or explicit continuation mechanism starts the next bounded stage.
6. If the model does not produce the checkpoint within a short grace period, emit a deterministic fallback status from runtime-known data and end the turn safely.

Safety constraints:

- Never cancel an in-flight tool solely because the checkpoint budget elapsed; enforce the boundary after the tool settles.
- Preserve existing per-tool timeout and abort semantics.
- Do not expose raw tool output, secrets, private paths, or hidden reasoning in the fallback status.
- Keep the feature opt-in and backward-compatible.
- Allow `status-only` as an alternative action for users who want periodic checkpoints without yielding.

## Alternatives considered

### Prompt or workspace instructions

This is the current workaround. It is useful guidance but cannot serve as enforcement because the same model that performs the work decides whether to stop.

### Existing progress streaming

Progress drafts improve visibility, but tool names or activity receipts do not provide a guaranteed semantic checkpoint or prevent another tool call from starting.

### Shorter overall turn timeout

A hard timeout limits total duration but terminates at the wrong abstraction level. It can interrupt useful work and does not guarantee a clean status, persisted checkpoint, or safe continuation.

### Per-tool timeouts

These protect individual tool calls. They do not bound a long chain of individually successful calls or extended model analysis between calls.

### TaskFlow/background tasks

TaskFlow is appropriate for work deliberately started as a durable background workflow. Requiring every non-trivial interactive request to be manually converted into TaskFlow leaves the common foreground WebChat path unprotected.

## Impact

- **Affected users:** operators using WebChat or another interactive channel for multi-step administration, coding, research, or maintenance.
- **Severity:** medium to high for consequential work; an uncontrolled long turn can waste time, increase risk, and erode operator trust even when individual tools are safe.
- **Frequency:** intermittent and model-dependent, which makes instruction-only mitigation difficult to validate.
- **Practical consequences:** repeated manual supervision, avoidable interrupts, lost handoff context after timeouts, unnecessary tool calls, and delayed work on other priorities.

This is especially relevant to service-first and approval-gated deployments where the operator expects short, understandable stages and must remain in control.

## Evidence/examples

Related issues cover important adjacent capabilities:

- #13207 — streaming progress and mid-run injection; its original report explicitly noted that manual checkpoint messages are behavioral/unreliable. It was later closed because streaming and queue steering shipped.
- #45522 — durable long-running orchestration and progress; closed after TaskFlow shipped.
- #100388 — WebChat compaction progress and diagnostics.
- #103461 — narrated agent status updates and activity receipts.
- #105622 — bounded tool execution and abort signals.
- #83966 — configurable timeout metadata for Codex plugin runtime tools.

None of these defines a runtime-enforced *foreground agent-loop* checkpoint based on silent time or completed-tool count, followed by a controlled yield and durable handoff.

Test environment where the gap was observed:

- OpenClaw `2026.8.2`
- Control UI / WebChat
- OpenAI Codex runtime
- multi-step maintenance and diagnostic workflows

No private infrastructure details or credentials are needed to reproduce the architectural gap.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

This request is not asking OpenClaw to expose hidden reasoning or raw logs. The desired output is a small, redacted operational checkpoint. It also does not replace TaskFlow; it provides a safe bridge between ordinary foreground conversation and work that should be promoted into durable background orchestration.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Follow-up named in #138396 (second stage of #138226). The paired-node Claude CLI approval path registers and replays the node-returned `systemRunPlan` unchanged while supplying `agentId`/`sessionKey` separately from the caller context, so it has the same latent record/replay split that #138226 hit on the node-exec path: if the node's plan omits identity (`sessionKey: null` / `agentId: null`), the Gateway record binds the caller identity (fallback) while the approved replay forwards the plan's null identity (strict), and the replay is rejected with `APPROVAL_REQUEST_MISMATCH`.

Source-level finding surfaced by review of #138396; not reproduced live. Current paired-node handlers build the plan from the request identity, so the split only manifests with version skew (an older Companion/node host that omits identity) or a handler change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair a node whose Claude CLI handler returns an approval plan without `sessionKey`/`agentId` (older node host, or simulate by stubbing `buildSystemRunApprovalPlan` input in `src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude-handler.ts` to omit them).
2. Trigger a paired-node Claude CLI run that requires approval from a chat session with a real `sessionKey`.
3. Approve (allow-once).

### Expected behavior

Registration and replay carry the same identity, so the approved run executes. Producer normalizes the plan once (the shape landed for node exec in #138396: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases.ts` `prepareNodeSystemRun` folds `cwd/agentId/sessionKey = plan.x ?? request.x ?? null` into the plan before it is used for both registration and replay).

### Actual behavior

`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-node-claude.ts` (`registerExecApprovalRequestForHostOrThrow` call) passes `systemRunPlan: approval.systemRunPlan` verbatim together with `agentId: contextParams.agentId` / `sessionKey: contextParams.sessionKey`; the later `invokeNode({ decision, plan: approval.systemRunPlan })` forwards the same un-normalized plan. Record side (`src/infra/system-run-approval-context.ts` `resolveSystemRunApprovalRequestContext`) resolves `plan?.sessionKey ?? request sessionKey`; replay side (`resolveSystemRunApprovalRuntimeContext`) takes the stored plan strictly → binding mismatch when the plan omits identity.

### OpenClaw version

main (`c3032a3420` at filing); latent on any version with this code shape.

### Operating system

N/A (source-level)

### Install method

N/A

### Model

N/A

### Provider / routing chain

Paired-node Claude CLI (`agent.cli.claude.invoke`) → Gateway exec approval → node replay.

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

Not reproduced live. The node-exec sibling of this split was observed live in #138396 (reporter's redacted trace: `expected.sessionKey = agent:…:discord:channel:<id>`, `actual.sessionKey = null`, `request.systemRunPlan.sessionKey = null`).

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- #138396 second-stage commit and PR body "Scope notes" describe the node-exec fix and name this path as the remaining sibling.
- Five independent review passes on that PR converged on this file as the analogous latent split.

### Impact and severity

Low today (current handlers populate identity); would become a hard approval failure (`approval id does not match request`) if a node host omits identity. Fix shape is small and mirrors #138396: normalize the plan once in the paired-node producer before registration and replay.

*(Filed by Sho (human) + Alpha (AI agent) as the follow-up promised in #138396.)*

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a policy-restricted Codex turn in a sandbox that remaps the workspace, the workspace `AGENTS.md` is never delivered: the injection report shows `native_unverified` with no injected content, while SOUL.md and the other bootstrap files arrive normally. Observed at runtime with `workspaceAccess: "none"`; `workspaceAccess: "ro"` takes the same code path but was not separately tested.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent on the Codex harness with a sandbox that remaps the workspace and a tool policy that makes turns restricted (same trigger as #125431):
   ```json5
   {
     plugins: { entries: { codex: { enabled: true } } },
     agents: { entries: { repro: {
       model: "openai/gpt-6-astra",
       workspace: "<agent workspace>",
       tools: { deny: ["nodes"] },
       sandbox: { mode: "all", scope: "session", workspaceAccess: "none" },
     } } },
   }
   ```
2. Put a unique marker in the workspace `AGENTS.md`, and a different marker in `SOUL.md` as a control, with an instruction to reply with both markers (or `MISSING` for any it was not given).
3. Start the Gateway and run one turn, e.g. `openclaw agent --agent repro --session-key agent:repro:check --message "<trigger>"`.
4. Inspect the session's system prompt report (`injectedWorkspaceFiles`) and the reply.

### Expected behavior

Per `docs/plugins/codex-harness-runtime.md`, "an ordinary policy-restricted turn has no native filesystem environment, so OpenClaw carries the bounded workspace `AGENTS.md` snapshot as thread-level developer instructions instead." That should also hold when the sandbox remaps the workspace: AGENTS.md is reported `verified` with `injectedChars == rawChars`, and the model can follow it.

### Actual behavior

- Report: AGENTS.md `injectionStatus: "native_unverified"`, `injectedChars: null`. SOUL.md is `verified` and fully injected.
- The AGENTS.md marker appears nowhere in the Codex rollout. The reply contains the SOUL marker and reports the AGENTS marker as `MISSING`.

**Cause.** `prepareAgentWorkspaceContext` projects context files onto the execution workspace before it selects the root instruction document, and the selection still compares against the source `workspaceDir`:
- [`src/agents/harness/workspace-context.ts#L74-L80`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b6bf52d83e8e49303f0c61cbc8a4b57399667542/src/agents/harness/workspace-context.ts#L74-L80) maps every file through `projectPath`, then calls `buildAgentWorkspaceInstructionSnapshot(contextFiles, params.workspaceDir)`.
- [`src/agents/harness/workspace-instructions.ts#L31`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b6bf52d83e8e49303f0c61cbc8a4b57399667542/src/agents/harness/workspace-instructions.ts#L31) (`selectAgentWorkspaceInstructionFiles`) matches the root AGENTS.md by path under `workspaceDir`.
- With `workspaceAccess` `none` or `ro`, the Codex attempt uses the sandbox workspace as its execution workspace ([`run-attempt-connection.ts#L407-L410`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b6bf52d83e8e49303f0c61cbc8a4b57399667542/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-connection.ts#L407-L410)). The projected paths no longer lie under `workspaceDir`, so the snapshot is empty and the restricted-turn carrier added in #126891 has nothing to carry. (`none` was observed at runtime; `ro` follows from the same branch in the source and was not separately tested.)

[`docs/plugins/sdk-entrypoints.md#L282`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b6bf52d83e8e49303f0c61cbc8a4b57399667542/docs/plugins/sdk-entrypoints.md#L282) currently documents this as intended ("projecting the root instruction path away from `workspaceDir` produces an empty root snapshot"), which contradicts the runtime doc quoted above.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5. Runtime observation on a source build of `main` at `aa7fc04f`; the selection code is unchanged on `main` at `b6bf52d8`, where a unit-level reproduction also fails.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Linux 6.8)

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm install`, `pnpm build`), Gateway started with `openclaw gateway run`

### Model

`openai/gpt-6-astra`

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway → bundled Codex app-server harness (`@openai/codex` 0.162.1) → OpenAI via ChatGPT/Codex sign-in (device code)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Sandbox: Podman backend, `openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim` image, `network: "none"`, read-only root, `scope: "session"`, `workspaceAccess: "none"`. For a clean signal, the test agent also had a `session_status`-only tool allowlist, and heartbeat, cron and memory plugins were disabled; none of these are needed to trigger the selection bug.

### Logs

```shell
Session report excerpt (unpatched):
AGENTS.md  injectionStatus=native_unverified rawChars=73 injectedChars=null
SOUL.md    injectionStatus=verified          rawChars=277 injectedChars=277 truncated=false
tools given to the model: ["session_status"]; tool calls in the turn: 0
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Bounded manual runtime check: an isolated Gateway, one turn per build, the same config and fixtures (`workspaceAccess: "none"`), no tool use.
- **Unpatched build:** as above. AGENTS.md was not injected, its marker was absent from the Codex rollout, and the reply reported it `MISSING`.
- **Patched build** (selection by source path, then projection; PR to follow): the report showed AGENTS.md `verified`, 73/73 characters, not truncated. The Codex rollout's developer message contained the complete AGENTS.md, with no native project-doc loading, and the reply contained the AGENTS marker.

Disclosure: my automated checker classified both runs INCONCLUSIVE because of limitations in its evidence collector, not because of the observations above. It expected a report field the Codex harness does not emit, and it did not recognize some Codex rollout record types. A follow-up read-only inspection of the patched run's rollout confirmed the complete AGENTS.md fixture in the Codex developer-message record; the single record the checker could not classify was a copy of the model's reply.

These are single manual runs on a non-deterministic model. The deterministic proof is the regression tests in the PR, which fail on `main` and pass with the fix.

### Impact and severity

Same failure class as #125431: the agent's operating rules (authority boundaries, approval rules, tool routing) are silently absent on restricted turns, while the sibling bootstrap files arrive, so the agent looks fully configured. This affects Codex-harness agents that combine a remapping sandbox with a tool policy that makes turns restricted. That was observed with `workspaceAccess: "none"`; `"ro"` is implicated by the same source path but untested.

### Additional information

- Related: #125431 (closed by #126891, which added the restricted-turn carrier). This is the remaining sandbox-remapped case of that carrier; non-sandboxed restricted turns are not affected.
- Related: #120600 (open). This report covers restricted turns only. It does not address unrestricted sandboxed turns, which still rely on Codex's native project-doc discovery inside the sandbox.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Shared xAI OAuth refresh fails while fencing historical peers because a retained database belonging to a fully deleted agent is rediscovered and rejected by the deletion journal.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed production sequence; deterministic isolated reproduction: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

1. Retire an older agent using the supported native deletion workflow while preserving its historical files (`deleteFiles:false`). Complete its deletion journal through supported recovery if necessary.
2. Continue using the remaining main agent with shared xAI OAuth fallback configured.
3. On two ordinary Discord requests on 21 October, primary preparation failed locally and fallback refresh attempted to fence historical OAuth peers.
4. Both requests failed with the deleted-agent database error below. No disruptive replay or credential edits were performed for this report.

### Expected behavior
The auth-peer lifecycle and completed agent-deletion lifecycle should agree about retained historical state: using the surviving agent should not require ordinary runtime admission into the deleted agent. Preserve refresh-generation safety and the deletion fence; do not bypass either guard or reactivate the deleted agent merely to refresh shared credentials.

### Actual behavior
The historical-peer refresh fails locally with `OpenClaw agent database is unavailable while agent luna is deleted.` The fallback cannot answer. The channel displays expired-login advice even though the recorded failure is a local peer/database-access failure, not proof of credential expiry or an upstream HTTP 401.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.5, locally patched build `1fb3b708cc45e70b5aad8af74a78bf3698a58962`; not a pristine-release or current-main runtime reproduction.

### Operating system
Native Windows 11 x64.

### Install method
npm global, native Scheduled Task Gateway.

### Model
OpenAI/Codex primary; xAI OAuth fallback. This failure occurs during local credential preparation, before successful fallback inference.

### Provider / routing chain
Discord -> OpenClaw -> OpenAI/Codex; configured fallback -> xAI OAuth. No API-key route.

### Additional provider/model setup details
One surviving everyday agent (`main`). Older agents were retired on 19 October. The Luna deletion journal is complete, retained history remains, and normal Gateway startup explicitly skips that completed-deletion database. The deletion transaction previously required supported offline recovery after the separately reported online lease-loss issue #177778. No unconfigured agent is being intentionally selected for this request.

The installed build contains eleven managed local repairs (cron publication fencing, bounded SQLite diagnostics, finalization lease budget, Windows restart handling, browser cancellation/deadline composition, Codex outer grace, off-main memory observation, Windows Doctor capture links, Doctor retry advice, Windows scratch cleanup, and required-reply visibility). These are disclosed confounders; no claim of stock runtime reproduction.

### Logs
Sanitized 21 October Europe/London (UTC+1):

```text
01:43:50.762 primary: MCP runtime cleanup could not confirm closure
01:43:50.771 model fallback decision
01:43:51.691 auth-triggered model runtime refresh failed:
  SqliteWorkerError: OpenClaw agent database is unavailable while agent luna is deleted.
01:43:56.039 fallback:
  Failed to fence every historical OAuth refresh peer.
  SQLite worker stopped before its result was received:
  OpenClaw agent database is unavailable while agent luna is deleted.
  outcome-unknown

01:56:42.655 primary: MCP runtime cleanup could not confirm closure
01:56:42.665 model fallback decision
01:56:47.809 fallback: same historical-peer/deleted-agent/outcome-unknown chain
01:56:48.793 original request outcome=error
```

The original MCP cleanup trigger is unproven and is not the defect asserted here. Neither sequence establishes that a fresh token-endpoint request was rejected.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
The user screenshot shows two ordinary requests answered only with `Couldn't sign in to xai. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works.` plus reauthentication commands. Screenshot omitted because it contains unrelated private conversation. Exact scoped logs and private deletion/retention receipts are retained.

Source inspection on installed source and current main `554b779bc7d50d86313fcb017ca38e0ecc679e83` identifies the conflicting owners:

- `src/agents/auth-profiles/candidate-stores.ts`: `listCandidateAuthProfileStores` includes state-root and registered historical databases without a completed-deletion disposition.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-peers.ts`: `listPeerCandidates` excludes the owner, then `fenceOAuthRefreshPeers` attempts normal fenced writes to discovered file candidates.
- `src/state/agent-deletion-journal.ts`: `assertAgentDeletionIdentityClaimAllowed` correctly rejects the deleted agent identity with the exact observed error.

This is source evidence, not a current-main execution or proof that simply filtering every deleted candidate is a safe fix. A regression should cover shared OAuth refresh after completed deletion with retained historical files, preserving both OAuth generation fencing and deletion admission.

### Impact and severity
Two confirmed fallback attempts in one private Discord channel failed at 01:43 and 01:56. The primary had already failed independently, so the fallback failure left both requests unanswered. Broader frequency and regression boundary: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information
The misleading failure-summary symptom is tracked in #165135. PR #165197 changes OAuth-classified aggregate presentation, but this SQLite outcome-unknown error propagates before typed OAuth wrapping/attempt aggregation and is outside that patch's coverage. The deletion lease-loss transaction in #177778 is separate; its journal was completed before these incidents. Related #159007/#159013 address deletion-time resource retirement, and #168957 historical-peer catalog-worker writes; neither establishes a repair for this observed completed-deletion conflict.

AI-assisted report, checked against production logs, the retained consolidation record and source. No auth/deletion guard was weakened and no production failure was injected.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A non-delegated durable background task can reach a terminal state yet leave its requesting group without a terminal result when completion is routed only through a disabled heartbeat.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set the requesting agent's heartbeat cadence to disabled.
2. From a group/channel session, start a non-delegated command that detaches into a durable background task.
3. Let the task succeed or time out after the initiating model turn has ended.
4. Inspect task state and the source conversation.

### Expected behavior

For a non-delegated task with a deliverable requester origin, terminal success or failure should be directly delivered exactly once to that origin even when no heartbeat runs. Delegated child tasks may retain parent-synthesis routing.

### Actual behavior

An observed timed-out task entered terminal state with delivery status `session_queued`. Completion queued a requester-session event and requested an immediate heartbeat; the disabled heartbeat returned a non-retryable `disabled` outcome, and no terminal message reached the group.

### OpenClaw version

v2026.8.1-beta.1 overlay base. The carried behavior was audited against main `81002dd250c3`; this report does not claim a later-main reproduction.

### Operating system

macOS arm64

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable: task terminal routing is independent of provider selection.

### Logs

```shell
Observed task state: terminal timed_out
Observed delivery state: session_queued
Observed heartbeat result: disabled
Observed source-channel terminal delivery: absent
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Existing #52305 and merged #78687 establish session-targeted wake support, but they do not guarantee consumption when a heartbeat is disabled. The local focused task-registry suite passed 110 tests after a direct idempotent delivery repair; this issue requests an upstream owner-boundary decision, not adoption of that patch verbatim.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: group/channel users of durable non-delegated tasks with disabled heartbeats.
- Severity: High; completed or failed accepted work has no user-visible outcome.
- Frequency: deterministic under the described conditions.
- Consequence: users must ask again to discover task completion or failure.

### Additional information

This one upstream filing intentionally tracks both overlay patch #96 (durable background-job configuration) and patch #104 (the final exactly-once completion owner); they are one terminal-delivery behavior, not two issues. The fix should preserve parent-review/synthesis semantics for delegated children and exact-once delivery across restart. AI-assisted, reviewed by a human operator.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Two related issues occur when a session is pinned (session-level model override) to a model that stops responding after tool calls. (1) After the agent idle-timeout kills the run, the session remains stuck at 'running' and the Stop control does nothing. (2) Messages sent by the user during that window are silently discarded — they never appear in the transcript and no failure is reported.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pin a session to a model that does not respond after a tool call (observed with a provider returning no response within 120s after `exec` invocations).
2. Wait for the agent idle-timeout to kill the run.
3. Observe the session UI: it remains stuck at 'running' / '处理中'; clicking Stop has no effect.
4. While still stuck, send a message to that session.
5. Observe the transcript: the message never appears (`pendingInputs: 0`, absent from history), with no failure feedback.

### Expected behavior

Any run — success, failure, or timeout — must converge the session state to a terminal state, and the Stop control must be able to stop an actually-running run. A message that cannot be admitted should report failure or enter a visible pending queue instead of being silently dropped.

### Actual behavior

(1) Session state stays at `running` with no live run behind it; Stop is non-functional. (2) The user message is silently and unrecoverably discarded. Switching the session back to a responsive model caused `status: done` immediately, confirming the run was already dead while the state machine still reported `running`. The transcript of one affected session shows several assistant `toolCall` entries (provider: zhipu, model: glm-5.3-flash) immediately before the stall.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

MSTeams inbound debounce normalizes conversation.id before keying, so same-sender replies in different channel thread roots can be batched into one agent turn.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.7.2 with `messages.inbound.debounceMs > 0`, `channels.msteams.groupPolicy: open`, and `channels.msteams.requireMention: false`.
2. Construct two MSTeams channel activities for the same app, channel, and sender inside one debounce window.
3. Use conversation ids `19:channel@thread.tacv2;messageid=root-a` and `19:channel@thread.tacv2;messageid=root-b`, with matching `replyToId` values and bodies `message in thread A` / `message in thread B`.
4. Pass both activities through `createMSTeamsMessageHandler`, including the real inbound debouncer, then flush the debounce window.
5. Observe the number and context of agent dispatches.

### Expected behavior

Two agent dispatches should occur. Each body and session key should remain bound to its originating thread root (`root-a` and `root-b`). OpenClaw already treats distinct MSTeams channel thread roots as distinct session keys in `message-handler.thread-session.test.ts`.

### Actual behavior

Only one dispatch occurs. Its `BodyForAgent` is `message in thread A\nmessage in thread B`, while the dispatch uses the most recent activity context. The two route-distinct thread replies are therefore handled as one agent turn.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.2

### Operating system

WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS on Windows 11

### Install method

Source archive from GitHub codeload, run with pnpm/dev test commands

### Model

N/A - no model inference is required for this message-handler reproduction

### Provider / routing chain

N/A - focused source-level MSTeams message-handler test

### Additional provider/model setup details

Configuration used for the focused repro:

```yaml
messages.inbound.debounceMs: 100
channels.msteams.groupPolicy: open
channels.msteams.requireMention: false
```

No provider credentials or external Teams tenant are required for this source-level message-handler test.

### Logs

```shell
Source locations:
- `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:1039-1051`
- `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:1061-1095`
- `src/auto-reply/inbound-debounce.ts:354-434`

Focused command:
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ingress-lifecycle.test.ts -t "keeps debounced channel thread replies isolated by thread root"`

Result: 1 selected test failed. Expected 2 dispatches; observed 1 dispatch with both thread bodies.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Focused test: `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ingress-lifecycle.test.ts`, test name `keeps debounced channel thread replies isolated by thread root`.

Observed result:
- expected dispatch count: 2
- observed dispatch count: 1
- observed body: `message in thread A\nmessage in thread B`

Relevant contracts:
- `docs/concepts/messages.md:33-35`: inbound debounce batches rapid consecutive text.
- `docs/channels/msteams.md:819-821`: thread replies retain their original thread root.
- `message-handler.thread-session.test.ts:30-45`: distinct channel thread roots resolve to distinct session keys.

The same debounce-key shape was present on upstream main commit `3506a55218530ee56674a865a77d84f7191b3e09` when checked on 2026-08-25.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Microsoft Teams channel users when inbound debounce is enabled and the same sender replies in two distinct channel threads inside one quiet window.
Severity: Medium; this crosses a thread/session boundary and can place text from one thread into another thread's agent context.
Frequency: Deterministic under the reproduced timing and routing conditions.
Consequence: Two independent thread messages become one agent turn using the most recent thread context, risking cross-thread context contamination and misrouted replies.

### Additional information

Root cause: the debounce key uses `appId`, `senderId`, and `normalizeMSTeamsConversationId(conversation.id)`. That normalization removes the `;messageid=<thread-root>` suffix, so different thread roots in the same channel alias to one bucket.

Suggested fix direction: retain the channel thread root (`conversationMessageId` / `replyToId`) as a debounce-key dimension whenever thread-specific session routing applies.

This is distinct from #130038, which concerns durable ingress dedupe using raw `activity.id`; this report concerns inbound debounce merging across thread roots.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An ambient heartbeat whose heartbeat file is intentionally empty/comments-only skips every interval by design, but each skip is recorded as a *failed* task in `openclaw tasks list --status failed`, even though the heartbeat event layer reports the run as ok-empty/silent with consecutiveErrors=0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Leave the agent's heartbeat file empty/comments-only (the stock template reads: "Keep this file empty (or with only comments) to skip heartbeat API calls").
2. Let the ambient heartbeat run for several hours (`agents.defaults.heartbeat = {"every":"30m"}`).
3. `openclaw cron get <heartbeat-id>` → `lastRunStatus:"skipped"`, `lastError:"heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file"`, `consecutiveSkipped` rising, `consecutiveErrors:0`.
4. `openclaw tasks list --status failed` → one row per interval (~48/day) for the heartbeat cron, reason `heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file`.

### Expected behavior

An intentional ok-empty skip should be recorded as *skipped* (or excluded from `--status failed`), consistent with `openclaw system heartbeat last` already reporting `status:"ok-empty"`, `silent:true`, `indicatorType:"ok"`. A designed no-op should not surface as a failed task.

### Actual behavior

Each intended skip is labeled *failed* in task accounting: `openclaw tasks list --status failed` accrues ~48 rows/day for the heartbeat cron, all with reason `heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file`, and `consecutiveSkipped` climbs unbounded (observed 330). Failed-task counts and any monitor/audit built on `--status failed` are inflated with false positives, despite `consecutiveErrors:0` and `openclaw system heartbeat last` reporting `ok-empty`/`silent`/`indicatorType:"ok"`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro (build 26200)

### Install method

npm global (openclaw); local gateway, login-item

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 (agent default; not exercised — the empty-file skip returns before any model call)

openclaw -> local LiteLLM proxy -> anthropic (agent default; not exercised — skip returns before any provider request)

### Additional provider/model setup details

The failing path is model/provider-independent: `heartbeat-runner-*.js` calls `contentEffectivelyEmpty(heartbeatScratchContent)` and returns `skipReason:"empty-heartbeat-file"` before any model or provider request. Config: `agents.defaults.heartbeat = {"every":"30m"}`; `agents.entries.main.heartbeat` unset (inherits). Related theme: #83143.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In affected Web Dashboard sessions, a tool-backed run can receive HTTP 200 from the provider but produce no visible assistant reply after the original turn and OpenClaw's isolated finalization both end with stopReason=length.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing Web Dashboard session using `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` via a per-session model override.
2. Run a multi-tool task that produces a long assistant/tool turn.
3. Observe the provider request complete with HTTP 200 and the turn settle without a final visible answer.
4. Observe OpenClaw start isolated finalization; when that also ends with `stopReason=length`, no assistant reply or terminal error is shown.
5. Retry in the same session; the run may end aborted/killed, while a fresh session using the same provider/model responds normally.

This was observed in two independent sessions. The exact task content is private and is not required to identify the logged failure path.

### Expected behavior

Every accepted user turn should end with either a visible assistant reply or a visible terminal error/recovery action. If isolated finalization is also truncated, OpenClaw should preserve a recoverable session state and surface the failure instead of leaving the dashboard silent.

### Actual behavior

The dashboard accepts the message and tools/provider calls run, but no assistant reply or error appears. Logs show that the settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer, isolated finalization was attempted, and finalization failed with `stopReason=length`. A following retry can end with `status=killed` and `abortedLastRun=true`. New sessions continue to work.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)

### Operating system

CachyOS (Linux x64, rolling release)

### Install method

npm global; systemd user gateway; Node.js 26.8.1

### Model

openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Web Dashboard -> OpenRouter -> z-ai/glm-5.3-flash

### Additional provider/model setup details

The model is selected through a per-session user override. This intentionally disables configured fallback models. Provider requests for the affected turns returned HTTP 200. A control session using the same effective provider/model completed normally with `stopReason=stop` and a visible reply, so the model route alone is not sufficient to reproduce the failure.

### Logs

```shell
Redacted excerpts from the affected run:


settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer ... running isolated finalization
settled-turn finalization failed: ... unsuccessful stop reason: length — preserving original failure
failed to persist prompt error entry: AbortError: This operation was aborted
lane task error ... This operation was aborted


Observed session state after a retry:


status=killed
abortedLastRun=true


One smaller affected session had about 20 message events and an estimated ~18k-token prompt; its long run recorded 22,218 output tokens across the run before `stopReason=length`. A second, much larger session showed repeated length stops and one incomplete/malformed tool-call error. No identifiers, prompts, or credentials are included here.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No attachments because the affected conversations are private. The redacted log excerpts above capture the terminal failure path. A fresh control session on the same provider/model produced a visible reply.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Web Dashboard users with long or tool-heavy existing sessions.
Severity: High for the affected session because the user receives neither an answer nor an actionable error.
Frequency: Observed in two independent sessions; fresh sessions still respond.
Consequence: Existing work cannot reliably continue, retries may leave the session killed/aborted, and users may repeat provider calls without visible output.

### Additional information

One affected session began exhibiting the problem before upgrading to 2026.9.4, so this is not solely an upgrade regression. The current version still reproduces the failure.

Related closed issues:
- #47993 — empty visible reply after malformed thinking/tool-call output
- #48361 — silent agent after provider errors
- #63210 — recovery from `stopReason=length` in main-agent sessions
- #62322 — unstable state after aborted runs

The distinguishing current evidence is the combination of a settled post-tool turn without a final answer, failed isolated finalization due to `length`, and a subsequent killed/aborted session state on 2026.9.4.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## Summary

I am seeing apparent thread-continuity failures in Codex-backed dashboard sessions.

Follow-up messages submitted within what appears to be the same OpenClaw dashboard session can create separate Codex rollout/thread records rather than continuing the existing thread. In the UI, earlier discussion then becomes difficult or impossible to retrieve, giving the impression that conversation history or prior decisions have disappeared.

I have not yet confirmed the underlying cause, so I am reporting this as a suspected thread-resumption/continuity issue rather than data loss.


### Steps to reproduce

Start OpenClaw normally and confirm the Gateway is running.
Open the OpenClaw Control UI and start a new Codex-backed dashboard session using the Codex app-server harness.
Send an initial message that establishes some context or decision, e.g. ask the agent to remember a simple value for the next turn.
Without changing the model, restarting the Gateway, resetting the session, or opening another dashboard conversation, send a second message referring to the information established in the first message.
Continue with another one or two follow-up messages in the same dashboard session.
Inspect the resulting Codex rollout/thread metadata and compare the thread_id associated with each turn.
Observe that follow-up messages may create separate Codex threads/rollouts rather than continuing the thread created by the initial message.
Return to or refresh the Control UI session and observe whether the earlier conversation remains accessible.

### Expected behavior

## Expected behaviour

When a user sends a follow-up message within an existing Codex-backed OpenClaw session, I would expect the turn to continue the associated Codex thread, or for the previous thread to remain clearly discoverable and resumable.

If a new Codex thread is intentionally created, the UI should make that transition visible and provide a way to return to or resume the previous thread.

### Actual behavior

## Strongest observed case

In one dashboard conversation on 11 September, eight separate user messages produced eight distinct rollout files.

The OpenClaw dashboard session itself remained the same from the user's perspective, but each resulting rollout appeared to begin as a new Codex thread rather than continuing the previous one.

I can provide a smaller two-message reproduction with:

* OpenClaw dashboard session key
* timestamps
* resulting Codex thread IDs / rollout metadata
* relevant redacted gateway logs

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2` stable 

### Operating system

 Linux `7.0.0-30-generic`, x64 

### Install method

Gateway: `systemd --user`, loopback, token auth * Codex app-server harness 

### Model

Model: `gpt-5.6-terra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Control UI → OpenClaw Gateway → Codex app-server harness → OpenAI Codex → gpt-5.6-terra

### Additional provider/model setup details

## Additional observations

The local Codex thread database currently contains:

* 745 recorded turns
* 445 threads
* only 36 threads with more than one turn

Among the most recent 20 threads, 18 were single-turn.

These aggregate counts support the continuity concern but do not, by themselves, establish the cause.

I also observed:

```bash
openclaw codex sessions --json
```

returning `0 sessions` while Codex rollout files and thread history clearly exist on disk.

I am treating this as a separate or related discovery issue rather than evidence of data loss, since I have not confirmed the intended semantics of that command.



### Logs

```shell
## Diagnostics available

I can provide, with sensitive content redacted:

* a two-message reproduction from one dashboard session
* OpenClaw session key and Codex thread IDs
* gateway logs covering the reproduction
* SQL queries used to inspect thread counts
* relevant rollout metadata
* confirmation of whether any restart, model change, or session reset occurred between turns

I have preserved the existing database and rollout files and have not run cleanup/reset operations on them.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

## Impact

For longer research or engineering sessions, earlier discussion and agreed decisions can become inaccessible through the normal Control UI even though the underlying rollout data remains present on disk.

This can make it appear that the conversation history has been lost.


### Additional information

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

During macOS setup, onboarding remained stuck after OpenRouter credentials/model were configured through the CLI and gateway inference succeeded; recovery required clearing the pending onboarding preference and completing the skip/local-connection flow.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

Once the local provider configuration supports successful inference, onboarding should allow reaching the normal app. The grounded comparison is the same installation after the recovery steps below: text chat worked using the same OpenRouter configuration. No known-good earlier release has been established.

### Actual behavior

The user could not complete initial API-key onboarding. The displayed setup was for OpenAI, while the available key was for OpenRouter. Credentials and model were then configured through the CLI. A setup inference probe initially reported no OpenRouter key; after restarting the gateway, OpenRouter inference succeeded, but the native onboarding flow remained stuck. It was eventually recovered by clearing openclaw.onboardingSystemAgentPending, choosing Set up later, selecting the Local connection, and restarting the app.

This report concerns the stuck onboarding/recovery state. It does not claim that an OpenAI credential field should accept an OpenRouter key, that the key was invalid, or that the preference alone caused the failure.

### OpenClaw version

Observed 2026-09-12; contemporaneous gateway log identifies native client OpenClaw/2609000490. Exact semantic app version at that moment was not captured.

### Operating system

macOS; contemporaneous client log reports Darwin/25.6.0. System subsequently checked as macOS 26.6.2.

### Install method

Native macOS app, reinstalled using the desktop installer; local gateway

### Model

openrouter/auto configured during recovery; initially no working model configuration

### Provider / routing chain

Native macOS onboarding → local gateway → OpenRouter using openai-completions; OpenAI-oriented key setup was initially displayed

### Additional provider/model setup details

The OpenRouter credential was saved through the supported CLI auth command, and openrouter/auto was configured as the default model. No credential values or authentication database contents are included. Gateway restart was part of the recovery.

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized observations from the 2026-09-12 gateway log (local timestamps; identifiers and filesystem paths omitted):

18:22:13 config hot reload applied (auth.profiles)
18:22:26 config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.openrouter, agents.defaults.model, agents.defaults.models)
18:22:44 setup-inference probe: No API key found for provider "openrouter"
18:24:35 gateway startup: agent model openrouter/openrouter/auto
18:24:52 model-fetch response: provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=openrouter/auto status=200
18:27:19 model-fetch response: provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=openrouter/auto status=200

These logs corroborate provider recovery. The stuck native onboarding state and preference recovery were observed during troubleshooting, not established by these gateway log lines alone.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Historical sequence from the affected installation, not a deterministic clean-install reproduction:
1. Reinstalled the native app and attempted onboarding with an OpenRouter key while an OpenAI setup screen was shown.
2. Saved the OpenRouter key through the CLI and configured openrouter/auto.
3. Restarted the gateway; a text inference test succeeded.
4. Native onboarding remained stuck.
5. Removed the openclaw.onboardingSystemAgentPending preference, used Set up later, selected Local connection, and restarted the app. Normal text chat became usable.

No screenshot or exact UI error string from the initial failure was retained. The currently working installation has not been reset to reproduce this issue.

### Impact and severity

Observed during one user’s macOS reinstall/onboarding attempt. It blocked completing setup through the ordinary UI and required CLI configuration plus manual onboarding-state recovery. Frequency across other installations is unknown.

### Additional information

Please investigate how native onboarding reconciles externally configured provider credentials and model readiness, and whether a pending system-agent setup can leave onboarding blocked after inference succeeds. The observed recovery involved several steps, so no single root cause or production-ready code fix is claimed. There is insufficient evidence to classify this as a regression.

Prepared with AI assistance from the troubleshooting record and sanitized gateway log observations. No API keys, tokens, personal conversation excerpts, device/session identifiers, or user-specific paths are included.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `@openclaw/sms@2026.9.1` installed (by `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/sms`), enabled in `plugins.entries.sms`, and listed by the gateway at start (`http server listening (19 plugins: … sms …)`), the Control UI's Channels → SMS page still opens on an install step asking for `@openclaw/sms` / `clawhub:@openclaw/sms` and offers no configuration fields. Clicking install reinstalls the plugin, which changes `plugins.installs.sms.installPath` and forces a gateway restart; the page loses its connection in the restart and comes back at the same install step. Three cycles, no way past it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/sms` on `2026.9.1`; restart the gateway; confirm `openclaw plugins inspect sms --runtime --json` reports it installed and enabled.
2. Open the Control UI → Channels → SMS.
3. Click the install it asks for; watch the gateway log; when the page reconnects, look at where it is.

### Expected behavior

The page recognises the installed plugin and shows the SMS configuration fields (account SID, from number, auth token, public webhook URL, DM policy, signature validation). An install of a package already installed at the compatible version is a no-op, and in any case does not restart the gateway under the page that asked for it.

### Actual behavior

The page asks to install; the click logs

```
Resolved @openclaw/sms to @openclaw/sms@2026.9.4, but that version is incompatible with this OpenClaw runtime; using newest compatible @openclaw/sms@2026.9.1.
[gateway/reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.sms, plugins.installs.sms.installPath, plugins.installs.sms.resolvedAt, plugins.installs.sms.installedAt)
[gateway/reload] config change requires gateway restart (plugins.installs.sms.installPath, plugin source changed) — deferring until 2 gateway request(s) complete
[gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
[gateway/ws] webchat disconnected code=1012 reason=service restart
[gateway] http server listening (19 plugins: … sms …)
```

and the reconnected page asks to install again. The one write the page made across three cycles was `channels.sms = {"enabled": true, "dmPolicy": "pairing"}`. The owner ended up asking the agent to write the configuration itself with `openclaw config patch`.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.9.1` (commit `ad6fe23`), the official Docker image `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.9.1-browser`

### Operating system

the image's Debian, in Docker on an Ubuntu 24.04 host

### Install method

Docker Compose; onboarding by `openclaw onboard --non-interactive`

### Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the ChatGPT subscription sign-in

### Provider / routing chain

OpenAI (ChatGPT sign-in) → `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, no fallbacks configured

### Additional provider/model setup details

none beyond the above

### Logs

```shell
as above.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

The Control UI cannot configure the SMS channel at all on this release when the plugin was installed from the CLI; the owner is sent in circles, each circle a gateway restart that drops every connected client. Related: #141801 (the same reload on a CLI install restarting a live channel).

### Additional information

Observed on `2026.9.1`, official `-browser` image, Docker Compose on Ubuntu 24.04; the Control UI opened in a paired laptop browser behind a reverse proxy. The resolver's choice of `2026.9.4` as the target and its fallback to `2026.9.1` may be a second, separate bug (it should resolve to the runtime-compatible version first).

Hi OpenClaw team,

I’ve been building an independent Android fork from `openclaw/openclaw` (`apps/android`) to validate a narrower use case: a direct, chat-first mobile surface for interacting with OpenClaw agents.

I’m **not** asking to upstream the fork as a whole.  
I’d like to ask whether maintainers would be open to discussing either:

1. a chat-first mode/surface in the official Android app, or  
2. selective upstreaming of a small set of validated UX/media improvements.

### Why this direction
Across testing, I consistently see demand for:
- faster path from app launch to agent chat
- lower setup/navigation friction
- practical gateway connectivity (including LAN/Tailscale scenarios)
- reliable Android media handling (image/audio/video)

### What has worked well in the fork
- chat-first navigation and conversation emphasis
- stronger media receive/render behavior
- more stable fullscreen image/video playback
- Tailscale-friendly connection UX
- simpler onboarding for chat-centric users

These changes have been validated on both emulator and physical Android devices.

Reference project:  
<https://github.com/memphislee09-source/clawchat2-public>

If this direction is interesting, I’m happy to reduce the discussion to 1–2 focused proposals (rather than discussing the fork broadly), and prepare concrete diffs/PR slices.

If not, that’s also very helpful clarity. In that case, I’d still appreciate guidance on whether focused Android UX/media PRs would be welcome.

Thanks for your time.
