prs.title: feat(sessions): transcript archive retention config + post-archive vacuum pass
prs.body:
This is the content of [openclaw/openclaw#176078](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176078) (transcript-archive retention) rebuilt with upstream ancestry. The original PR was stuck closed-unmerged and could not be reopened because its head branch (`DarojaAI:fix/issue-137`) had orphan history with no merge-base against `openclaw/openclaw` main; GitHub refuses cross-repo PRs without common history. This branch is recreated from upstream main with a single squashed commit carrying the same change, pushed as `DarojaAI:retention-rebased`.

---

Closes #176077

## Problem
No retention control exists for transcript archives: archive accumulation is unbounded, and SQLite freelist pages are never reclaimed after archive passes — long-lived agents fill disk (fleet incident class, see issue repro).

## Shipped solution
- `session.maintenance.archiveAfter` config (`PositiveDurationSchema | false`), resolved to `archiveAfterMs` in `store-maintenance.ts`; malformed values disable archival rather than destroy history; help copy + labels + docs updated
- `reclaimSqliteFreePagesAfterArchivePass`: WAL checkpoint → freelist check → `incremental_vacuum(N)` on modern stores, full `VACUUM` retrofit on legacy ones — wired into `enforceSessionHistoryMaintenanceSerialized` post-pass, best-effort with next-pass retry
- Tests: 3 new eviction cases (age-driven archival without budget, inspect-as-mutation/warn-immutability, post-archive reclaim + retrofit); `session-history-eviction` 7/7, `store-maintenance` + zod extensions 28/28, `schema.help.quality` 24/24

## User impact
Operators gain a bounded archive footprint; maintenance passes shrink on-disk state instead of only moving it.

## Validation
Touched+adjacent src files typecheck clean (scoped tsgo); touched test files exit 0 individually. Known pre-existing `TS7016` in `src/media/qr-runtime.ts` (missing `@types/qrcode`) reproduces identically on pristine main — unrelated to this branch.

Provenance: fix developed downstream (DarojaAI/openclaw-gateway#137), reference-ported; happy to adapt to maintainer preferences on config naming/placement.

## What Problem This Solves
Operators running long-lived agents have no retention control on transcript archives: archive accumulation is unbounded and SQLite freelist pages are never reclaimed after archive passes, so disk fills on busy deployments (repro in #176077). This PR adds the bounded-retention config surface plus incremental vacuum so archive growth stays within operator-set bounds.

## Evidence
- **Behavioral repro:** with no `session.maintenance` config, transcript archives grow without bound and freelist pages are never reclaimed (#176077 repro; observed unbounded archive accumulation on a 5-minute journal cadence in production).
- **Fix verification:** 34/34 scoped shard tests green on current main (eviction, store-maintenance, schema help/quality suites), rebased across the #175837 sessions refactor.
- **Surface:** `session.maintenance.archiveAfter` (`PositiveDurationSchema | false`) resolved to `archiveAfterMs` in store maintenance; eviction tests cover the reclaim and legacy full-vacuum retrofit paths.

prs.title: refactor(core): remove unused private argument alternatives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private core helpers still advertise argument alternatives and return fields
that runtime callers never use, leaving extra branches and test-only wiring.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Real config, CLI, SDK, Gateway protocol,
persisted shapes, authorization, expiry, cleanup, and recovery contracts remain.
The standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same canonical dependencies and defaults production already selects.
Remove unused caller selectors, legacy private positional forms, unread return
fields, and test-only injections; existing tests use scoped module spies or
the real configured owner.

This is the core/packages/plain-UI-helper area of an 84-path family, split under
the campaign's area rule. Its plugin slice is #178975. This slice changes 69
paths and removes **138 net production lines** and **2 net test lines**
(including the shared maintenance test-helper in test LOC).

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- noVNC no longer accepts private TTL/clock overrides; its only runtime issuer
  and bridge consumer used the fixed 60-second one-time-ticket path. Completed
  extraction #167926 remains; every expiry and invalid-clock guard stays.
- System-changes no longer accepts test-only environment/reader bags. The active
  RPC introduced in #111286 keeps its canonical SQLite readers, scope, paging,
  bounded scans, frozen frontier, and unchanged protocol results.
- The private string-union builder loses unused metadata options (#172991).
  Ordered `anyOf` output and literal inference remain; no wire schema changes.
- CLI registry loading loses unused activation-source forwarding. The lower
  loader's real activation-source contract remains available to its live callers.
- Codex route repair loses an always-true private flag, not the upstream CLI
  repair gate or real migration behavior (#77731, #107955).
- Provider canonicalization loses an unread returned function; the local
  canonicalizer and returned reference normalization remain (#130600).
- Gateway auth-token loses test-only environment/interactive overrides. The real
  interactive-terminal, explicit-show, target, weak-secret and redaction guards
  from #118051 and #151250 remain intact.
- The subagent read snapshot loses a never-supplied cached selector. Indexed
  lookup/hydration, ownership, FIFO and persistence remain; #173548 already
  retired its final supplier. This is not the standalone memory backend.
- Document/web extractor hosts lose unsupplied environment/workspace/ID filters.
  Actual config allowlists, selected artifact ownership, failure behavior and
  public extractor contracts remain (#71278, #139334, #152661).
- Backup retries use the real sleep owner, not a test-injected function. Real
  EOF retry policy, cancellation, delays, paths and durability stay (#72251,
  #106019, #171947).
- The lexical daemon credential check fixes its argument to the only live value,
  local. The real target correction and exec-SecretRef isolation remain
  (#135862, #135471); generic local/remote owners are unchanged.
- Bootstrap pairing and proxy registration lose unused private positional forms.
  Real option-object callers, bootstrap authority, proxy modes and TLS remain
  (#154671, #79171); public pairing SDK siblings are unchanged.
- Context settings infer the same actual normal/fallback/degraded output, while
  event routing uses the same configured scope/allowlist. No caller supplied
  their removed overrides (#88750, #83743).
- Doctor preview/maintenance uses the real environment, fix text and lifecycle
  runner. The runner injection originated as test-only fast-lane wiring; real
  repair authorization and output remain (#99238).
- Approval Web Push loses an unsupplied private state-directory override. The
  real default source, live authority, visibility, durable receipts, expiry and
  settlement remain (#129348, #158595); shared storage-scope APIs stay.
- Collect-prompt rendering loses an unused summary input; actual overflow
  summary owners and prompt bytes remain (#175837).
- Worktree maintenance uses canonical GC rather than a test-only callback.
  Checkpoints, batching, config/current authority, cancellation and shutdown
  settlement remain (#164758). Tests spy the canonical owner after drain.
- Directory sizing always uses the only live policy, excluding `.git`; worker
  execution, byte/error semantics and capacity admission stay (#132706, #146273).
- Dashboard readiness drops unread status/recoverable return fields, not status
  probing, hints, prompting, install/start or recovery (#82547).
- Login-error hint helpers lose an always-false connected argument; their only
  runtime consumer already operates on failed connections. Visible text stays.
- Node compiler forwarding reads the real process arguments; title derivation
  uses its fixed 60-character limit. Operator compiler flags and title sanitation
  remain (#168587, #141600).

These are private caller-contract cuts, not removal of incident-backed security,
durability or concurrency guards. A future internal caller must use the real
owner instead of an unused override; no new runtime race is accepted.

## Evidence

Every owner packet passed focused tests, targeted native typechecking and
independent review before assembly. All 69 assembled file blobs match the
reviewed collector; relevant owner areas have no intervening main changes.
Retained proof covers noVNC expiry/one-shot behavior, system-change paging,
Doctor repair and preview, canonical dependency calls, extractor configuration,
backup cancellation/retry, bootstrap pairing, subagent reads, worktree scheduler
and capacity behavior, Dashboard recovery, proxy TLS, compiler flags and titles.

Fresh aggregate proof: the selected 66-root core/package graph and plain UI
helper graph pass native noEmit. Independent aggregate review found no actionable
P0-P2 findings. Typed lint and formatting pass on all 69 paths. Fresh focused
proof passes 43 cases in four owner files (32.09s wrapper), plus all 14
suppression and three wrapper-closure cases (26.69s wrapper). Runtime value
cycles and static import cycles are both zero; whitespace checks pass.

Conflict repair preserves main's #178930 extractor-test consolidation and adapts
its table to the removed private scope argument. Only the obsolete private-scope
rows disappear; global disablement, real operator allowlists, factory failures,
warnings and all other assertions remain. Production hunks are unchanged from
the reviewed slice. The targeted conflict graph, all nine extractor cases
(119.14s wrapper including cold worker preparation), one-file typed lint/format,
14 suppression cases (23.83s wrapper), both zero-cycle checks and whitespace
checks pass on the rebased head.

Local proof is serial, nice-10, isolated from real OpenClaw state and limited to
focused suites. Real Git-maintenance integration tests are not run locally;
hosted exact-head CI owns that broad proof. No live-provider/device claim.

prs.title: fix: avoid false maintenance failures during database close
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading automatic session-maintenance failure warnings when physical database close refuses new maintenance admission or cancels its registered worker request.

## User Impact

Expected database-owner retirement is quiet. Independent failures remain visible during close and Gateway drain, with readable messages, causes, and error codes instead of an empty error object. Caller cancellation, data, permissions, retention, recovery, and update behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance catch requires its own recorded retirement and a direct typed admission refusal or database-owner retirement error. The mutation lifetime now distinguishes database-owner close from caller cancellation and ordinary completion invalidation; caller abort retains its original reason. Matching untyped text, live-owner errors, wrappers, aggregates, and I/O failures are not suppressed. Close still revokes commit authority and joins outstanding work.

The existing normalization formatter preserves raw local diagnostics; export owners retain redaction. Small equivalent scheduling/Set consolidations keep the existing module within its line cap. No new owner, public API, schema, retry, compatibility path, dependency, or policy exception was introduced. Total: five files +260/−66; production two files +48/−37 (net +11), tests three files +212/−29.

## Evidence

- Existing typed-admission, physical-close/alias, joined-finalization, revalidation, write-protection, scheduling, and Gateway-drain evidence is retained.
- The installed CLI proof exposed a second normal-close path: after three awaited public SDK writes, shipped CLI cleanup revoked an active mutation lifetime. Both the upstream-base package and initial PR package logged the plain `SQLite mutation Worker request was revoked` error. The inspector captured creation through `closeAgentDatabaseResource` and `drainAgentDatabaseResources` after all writes returned; stored rows, integrity, lock release, and clean exit were correct. This was distinct from the original typed admission-refusal path.
- A new regression used the real mutation lifetime and physical close, failed on that unexpected warning before the producer/catch repair, and passes after it. Controls preserve exact caller abort reasons and warnings for live, plain-text, wrapped, aggregate, and genuine I/O errors. Commit revocation and cleanup joining remain tested.
- Current head `f603a93b45c045708798fcb640b60685251059b3`: 62 selected cases passed, core and agents/sessions test type lanes passed, as did typed lint, formatting, diff checks, and normal commit hooks. Fresh independent AutoReview of the complete PR found no actionable P0–P2 issues; reviewed diff bytes match the committed diff.
- Correction retained: the first published head failed TS2345 in the new close test. Commit `8e0fc377` separately awaits the boolean close and void scheduler. Its full hosted CI run `39536503081` passed. The new production completion now has its own CI running; the previous green run is not proof for the changed head.

| Current focused command (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, macOS) | Cases | Full wrapper wall | Sum of reported case durations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-worker-request.lifetime.test.ts` | 5 | 42.37 s | 0.007 s |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-close.test.ts` | 11 | 41.29 s | 2.422 s |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-kick.test.ts` | 37 | 22.76 s | 12.943 s |
| Existing queued-reclamation path/root retirement cases | 2 selected | 9.84 s | 0.332 s |
| Existing isolated cold-storage publication file | 7 | 8.61 s | 0.009 s |

The first two command walls include 33.644 s and 28.080 s of compiler preparation. These are test costs, not application benchmarks. Changed-file CI case timings will be recorded when available; the runtime suites do not report isolated file walls.

## Installed CLI physical-close proof — October 21

Passed on isolated AWS Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, using installed packages built from upstream base `85bb6b88bde625bc04918b0579ad7e7e5cf61b27` and current head `f603a93b45c045708798fcb640b60685251059b3`.

A disposable plugin registers a CLI command through documented `api.registerCli`, performs three awaited `upsertSessionEntry` calls through the installed public SDK, and returns. The installed `openclaw.mjs` owns runtime cleanup and physical database close. The plugin never closes a database, supplies an execution token, imports private owners, replaces reclamation dispatch, or injects an exception. Its command and inspector-observer bytes are identical in both arms.

| Observed result | Upstream base | Current head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Writes acknowledged before action return | 3 | 3 |
| Actual close cancellation | Plain `Error`, `SQLite mutation Worker request was revoked` | Direct `SqliteMutationWorkerRetiredError`, same message |
| Error creation provenance | `closeAgentDatabaseResource` → `drainAgentDatabaseResources` | Same |
| Automatic-maintenance warnings | 1 | 0 |
| Persisted rows | All three expected identities/timestamps unchanged, unarchived | Same |
| SQLite health / post-exit lock | `quick_check: ok`; exclusive no-op transaction succeeds | Same |
| Process settlement | Exit 0, no signal or timeout, process group gone | Same |

The candidate's actual error-creation stack begins `Object.retire [as revoke] → closeAgentDatabaseResource → drainAgentDatabaseResources`; each observation records `writesAcknowledged: 3, actionReturned: true`. Three exception events reflect propagation of the error, not three separately canceled operations. All 18,023 installed inventory entries remained byte-identical before/after. The original baseline capture was reassessed read-only under this separate owner-retirement contract; its original inconclusive admission-refusal verdict remains unchanged.

[Candidate installed proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6553e2b91f3cbbb35be4e31c8eecf6d9), [retained baseline capture](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7bb7ea57fcecd187859cfbeb5431c3d5). The complete observable results above are included here so review does not depend on portal access. Build metadata matches each full commit and tracked build inputs stayed clean; canonical package integrity checks passed. Package SHA-256: base `5f6c45ebdc76224fcef54f745806a9716751b04a01698c159b244fd212f750ef`; candidate `332ea18c584dc05d9fe321e6e8730d39bb298d185be21149a8a478a4b1ef08d1`. Unchanged plugin/observer SHA-256: `749b33e6658aac6cd722cb2cba0c157925820ca1e79ae94d0be028a10a330880`. Candidate runner SHA-256: `2f6030f8b885925197a242e4c58b2f3445339f0017b130011c8ba6ed5052dabd`.

Limits: the in-process inspector observes exceptions and immediately resumes; it changes timing and cannot establish natural race frequency or performance. The original pre-admission refusal interleaving remains proven by focused owner tests, not by this installed trace. Independent I/O, caller-abort, wrapped/aggregate, and live-owner negative controls remain covered by focused tests; this fixture injects no such failure. No all-platform or broad deployment claim follows.

No merge or auto-merge is authorized.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): reuse prepared policy and schema owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three plugin-local consumers duplicate facts already owned upstream: Slack re-normalizes its prepared monitor policy, Browser maintains a second inventory of act-request fields, and Agents API maintains an unread diagnostic inventory of ignored native types.

## What Changed

Slack's private context input derives from its existing policy resolver and consumes its normalized lists, defaults and channel keys. Its sole production provider already supplies that prepared result. Five fixture constructors now supply the same prepared fields. Live policy refresh and effect-boundary authority checks remain unchanged.

Browser derives legacy top-level act-request repair keys from the existing full schema owner. This deliberately uses full/default capabilities, never run-filtered capabilities. Nested fields still win; mismatched act kinds still backfill only the target ID. The shipped legacy-input contract is retained.

Agents API drops the bounded unknown-type set, diagnostic-only ignore inventory and debug breadcrumb. Ignored events/items are still ignored. The meaningful transcript-order warning, native tool output, transcript ordering, usage accounting and attempt authority checks remain.

Net production removal: **103 lines** (+14/-117), four production paths and nine total paths. Tests/support add 14 lines and remove one. This is a combined residue under the campaign's 100-line waiver, not a LARGE PR. No config, protocol, persisted shape, dependency, SDK export or user-facing feature changes. The standalone Phase E session-memory backend and its tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Slack no longer repairs malformed direct calls to its private context constructor. The producer cutover in #146202 supplies normalized policy; there is one production provider, no public constructor export, and no human report requiring a second normalization boundary. Unsupported calls bypassing the resolver now receive no duplicate defaults or list repair. Real live-policy revalidation remains.
- Agents API ignores unfamiliar native types without a debug breadcrumb. #156182 introduced active native output/history/accounting projection, not a human-filed unknown-type diagnostic incident or dormant activation dependency. If the service adds an unsupported type, existing supported output and settlement continue without the retired debug-only inventory.
- Browser accepts no additional edge-case compromise: the existing schema's full field inventory replaces a second handwritten copy, preserving #93674's shipped compatibility behavior. Neither capability filtering nor nested precedence changes.

## Evidence

Focused proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, lowered CPU priority and one worker, with serial test/typecheck commands. Slack: 191 cases across 12 owner/sibling suites passed. Browser: 97 cases across the tool/schema suites passed; the stable-prefix guard passed all five cases. prs.title: fix(codex): sandboxed agents lose AGENTS.md on restricted turns
prs.body:
Closes #178989
Related: #125431, #126891, #120600

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex agents running in a sandbox that remaps the workspace (observed with `workspaceAccess: "none"`) lose their workspace AGENTS.md instructions on policy-restricted turns.

## User Impact

User impact: sandboxed Codex agents follow their AGENTS.md rules on restricted turns, as `docs/plugins/codex-harness-runtime.md` describes. Unrestricted turns are unchanged; they still rely on Codex's own AGENTS.md discovery. `workspaceAccess: "ro"` uses the same code path but was not separately runtime-tested.

## Why This Change Was Made

Context files were projected onto the sandbox workspace before the root AGENTS.md was selected against the source workspace, so nothing matched and the instruction snapshot was empty. The snapshot is now selected by its source path and then projected. `buildAgentWorkspaceInstructionSnapshot` gains an optional `projectPath` argument (additive; existing callers unchanged).

This replaces the `docs/plugins/sdk-entrypoints.md` paragraph that documented the empty snapshot as intended behavior. It does not add AGENTS.md re-injection (cf. #120618): unrestricted turns keep native discovery, and the new Codex test asserts that.

## Evidence

- Regression tests (new): `src/agents/harness/workspace-context.test.ts` "selects the root instruction snapshot by source path before projecting it" and `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts` "carries agent AGENTS.md into restricted turns that execute in a sandbox workspace". With the two production files reverted to `main` (`b6bf52d8`), both fail with an empty instruction snapshot (`expected [] to deeply equal [ { …(2) } ]`) while every other test in those files passes; with this change, both pass.
- Focused suites: 6 test files / 54 tests pass (`workspace-context`, `workspace-instructions`, Codex `attempt-context` and `run-attempt.workspace-snapshot`, Agents API instructions and environment).
- `check:changed --base b6bf52d8`: formatting, lint, typecheck (core, core tests, extension tests), ratchets and guards pass. Three checks fail, and they fail identically on clean `b6bf52d8` without this change:
  - max-lines suppression ratchet: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`
  - core tsgo graph boundary: test-root budget over 720 in the `agents-tools`, `gateway-root`, `infra` and `plugins-platform` shards
  - dead export scan: `src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.test-helpers.ts` `expectedResolvedOmission`
- Plugin SDK API diff: one additive signature change (`buildAgentWorkspaceInstructionSnapshot`, optional `projectPath`).

<details><summary>Supplemental manual runtime check (not an automated test)</summary>

Isolated local Gateway, Codex harness, Podman sandbox with `workspaceAccess: "none"`, policy-restricted turn, no tools available or used, one turn per build with marker-bearing AGENTS.md and SOUL.md fixtures.

- Unpatched build: the injection report showed AGENTS.md `native_unverified` with no injected content; the AGENTS marker appeared nowhere in the Codex rollout; the model reported the AGENTS marker as missing.
- Patched build: the injection report showed AGENTS.md 73/73 characters injected, not truncated; the Codex rollout's developer message contained the complete AGENTS.md; no native project-doc loading; the model returned the AGENTS marker.

Disclosure: my automated checker classified both runs INCONCLUSIVE because of limitations in its evidence collector (it expected a report field the Codex harness does not emit and did not recognize some Codex rollout record types), not because of the observations above. A follow-up read-only inspection of the patched run's rollout confirmed the complete AGENTS.md fixture in the Codex developer-message record. These are single runs on a non-deterministic model; the regression tests above are the deterministic proof.
</details>

prs.body:
Closes #178951

## What Problem This Solves

Opening session Details, panels, and mobile subpages could show a nearly empty surface with raw “Loading…” text.

## User Impact

Waiting surfaces use the existing lightweight skeletons. Loading remains named for assistive technology, and refreshes keep already loaded rows visible. Error messages and retry actions remain available.

The reported permanently loading mobile Details state did not reproduce on fresh main: both desktop and mobile settled normally. This PR fixes the loading presentation and does not claim to repair an unverified persistent-loading cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing list, document, and terminal skeletons at their current loading boundaries. Keep the approved layout, lazy imports, request ownership, and normal settlement timing. Remove the now-unneeded desktop flag from the shared HTML-preview loading component.

## Evidence

- Follow-up consumer validation: 68 tests in Versions, HTML preview, and HTML attachments pass (4.24s wall); their four original CI failures were reproduced first. Parent-document styles must match the canonical skeleton stylesheet, while document markup/scripts and exact sandbox-transfer checks remain protected. This follow-up changes tests only; rendered source is identical to the captured implementation.
- 23 focused component tests pass (3.12s wall), including permission loading → rows → retained refresh/error and existing PR chunk failure/retry tests. The loading regressions fail against the original source.
- Four production-bundle browser scenarios pass (18.64s wall). The new mobile Details scenario covers cold import, close while pending, reopen, and settlement; its measured execution is 1.45s. The new permission case takes 8ms. A final replay of the two adjusted Details cases also passes.
- UI production and test typechecks, focused lint, formatting, lifecycle guard, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Final UI build: 13.14s. Request counts remain startup 7 / Chat 25 / New 19. Gzip changes against the same base are +2 B / +37 B / −20 B respectively. The pre-existing startup budget failure remains (328,932 B against 325,166 B); this PR does not relax it.

Risk and coverage: presentation-only changes; no new CSS, state, timers, eager imports, or dependencies. Browser proof uses synthetic Gateway fixtures. Broad CI remains attached to this PR.

Desktop proof: Details docked beside the open Subagents side panel, at 2400 × 1100. The comparison uses base `05235ad0c53f1974ad1e9edd0b1dbd6dad1dd6aa` and this PR's head `8d4a0a60c5cf8595be5f2b88b1f7ed276b86c04f`, with the same synthetic session and opening actions. Both runs reserve the same 300 px Details column in the conversation; its frame is 1604 px wide. Only elapsed time varies. The module is held for the waiting capture, then released until the complete Details content, including pull requests, is visible. Detail crops come from their full-context PNGs.

prs.title: fix(feishu): keep a topic chat's messages in one session and one topic
prs.body:
Closes #160330

## What Problem This Solves / 解决的问题

**中文** — 在飞书话题群里，同一个话题的消息会被拆成两个 Agent 会话：话题起始消息按 `thread_id`（`omt_…`）建会话，而「引用回复」事件带 `root_id`（指向被引用的那条消息），于是按 `om_…` 又建了第二个会话。同时，智能体自主发起的投递（心跳、定时任务、工具发送）没有入站消息、拿不到话题锚点，会以顶层消息发出 —— 在话题群里顶层消息就是**新话题**。结果：同一场讨论的答复漂到别的话题，上下文也被拆散。

**English** — In a Feishu topic chat, one topic splits into two agent sessions: the topic starter keys on `thread_id` (`omt_…`), while quote-reply events carry `root_id` (pointing at the quoted message) and key a second session on `om_…`. Agent-initiated deliveries (heartbeat, scheduled work, tool sends) have no inbound message and no topic anchor, so they post a top-level message — a **new topic** in a topic chat. Replies for one discussion leak into another topic and the context is split.

## User Impact / 影响

**中文** — 一个话题里的所有消息（含引用回复与智能体自主发送）现在共用同一个会话，答复始终落回本话题。没有用户可见的配置变更；会话键只取自事件本身，不依赖网络查询，因此**不会**因查询抖动或升级而把已有话题会话挪走。回复锚点每个话题只解析一次并缓存。

**English** — Every message of a topic — including quote replies and agent-initiated sends — now shares one session and replies stay inside that topic. No user-visible config change. The session key comes from the event only, so neither a transient lookup failure nor an upgrade moves an existing topic session; the reply anchor is resolved once per topic and cached.

## Why This Change Was Made / 修复方案

1. **会话键 = 事件里的 `thread_id`**（`bot-content.ts`）：`thread_id ?? root_id ?? messageId`。飞书在话题内**每条**消息上都报 `thread_id`（实测：同一话题的四条消息都带同一个 `omt_…`，`root_id` 为 null），而 `root_id` 可能指向被引用的消息。改用 `thread_id` 后键完全来自事件，不需要任何查询；`chat_type === "topic_group"` 这个在真实事件上恒假的分支一并去掉。
   *Key = the event's `thread_id`*: Feishu reports it on every message of a topic (measured: all four messages of one topic carried the same `omt_…`; `root_id` was null), while `root_id` can point at the quoted message. The key now comes from the event alone, with no lookup; the `chat_type === "topic_group"` gate — always false for real events — is gone.

2. **已有会话连续性**：今天的话题起始消息本来就以 `omt_…` 存储，取值未变；此前由「引用回复」另建的 `om_…` 会话现在并入该话题的 `omt_…` 会话 —— 这正是修复本身，不涉及迁移。
   *Existing sessions*: topic starters are already stored under `omt_…` and keep that value; the extra `om_…` session that quote replies used to create now joins the topic's `omt_…` session.

3. **会话键上报话题 id**（`session-conversation.ts`）：core 从会话键推导主动投递目标时会问 `resolveSessionConversation` 要 thread id；此前不返回，投递便丢了话题（真机复现，见下）。现在按话题返回 `omt_…`，发送边界再把它解析成锚点消息。
   *Session keys report their topic id*: core asks `resolveSessionConversation` for the thread id when it derives a proactive delivery target from the session key; returning none dropped the topic (reproduced live, below). Topic sessions now report it, and the send boundary turns it into a message anchor.

4. **回复锚点下沉到发送边界**（`send.ts`, `outbound.ts`, `channel.ts`）：飞书回复只能寻址「消息」，因此 `resolveFeishuReplyAnchorMessageId` 把话题 id 映射为该话题最旧的一条消息（`container_id_type=thread` + `sort_type=ByCreateTimeAsc`, `page_size=1`，按 `account:topic` 缓存）。外发适配器在 text/media/payload 三个入口统一归一化 `ctx.threadId`；工具/定时/心跳触发的发送在 action 路径解析话题会话的锚点。查询失败时回退到既有的顶层发送行为，**不会**改变会话。
   *Anchor resolved at the send boundary*: a Feishu reply addresses a message, so `resolveFeishuReplyAnchorMessageId` maps a topic id to the topic's oldest message (cached per topic). The outbound adapter normalizes `ctx.threadId` for text/media/payload, and agent-initiated sends resolve their topic session's anchor in the action path. A failed lookup falls back to the previous top-level behavior without moving the session.

5. **查询失败保留 target**（`send.ts`）：锚点查询失败时**保留**话题 id 而不是清空 threadId —— 清空会让发送方走顶层回退（话题群里就是新话题），还绕过了「话题回复失败后拒绝不安全顶层回退」的既有守卫。
   *A failed lookup keeps the target*: clearing it made the send owner fall back to a top-level post (a new topic) and bypassed the existing refusal to fall back after a threaded reply fails.

6. **心跳保持话题**（`channel.ts`）：声明 `messaging.preserveHeartbeatThreadIdForGroupRoute: true`（telegram 已有先例），让 core 在群会话心跳时复用会话记录的 thread id。
   *Heartbeats stay in the topic*: declare `preserveHeartbeatThreadIdForGroupRoute: true` (precedent: telegram).

## Evidence / 证据

**After-fix trace against the live Feishu API** (real app credentials from this machine, read-only; ids redacted). The topic is the one from the report; the two event shapes are the ones the gateway logged for it (starter: `thread_id` only; quote reply: `root_id` = quoted message + `thread_id`):

```
[live api] topic omt_19…5ce6 -> reply anchor om_x10…b44a
[session key] topic starter -> oc_d16…5ce6
[session key] quote reply   -> oc_d16…5ce6
[session key] same session  -> true
```

Pre-fix production trace for the same topic (from the report) logged two sessions instead:

```
16:28:49  dispatching (session=…:topic:omt_19dfad8930cf5ce6)
16:43:26  peer=oc_…:topic:om_x100b64961acce0a4b4a4798d129b44a   ← quoted starter's id as the topic key
16:43:26  dispatching (session=…:topic:om_x100b64961acce0a4b4a4798d129b44a)
```

Checks run locally (Linux, Node 24):

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts` (full feishu shard) | 98 files / 1540 tests passed |
| `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` | 101 tests passed |
| new tests | `topic-root.test.ts` (5), `Feishu topic session keys` (2), send-anchor cases in `channel.test.ts` (3) — the topic-key regression test fails on pre-fix code |
| `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` | exit 0 |
| `oxlint` / `oxfmt --check` on `extensions/feishu` | 0 warnings / formatting clean |

Measured cost (`--maxWorkers=1`, vitest startup dominates): `topic-root.test.ts` 7.9s, `bot.bot-threads.test.ts` ~9s, `channel.test.ts` ~9s.

Notes a reviewer should see:

- One maintainer-authored expectation changed: `bot.test.ts` previously pinned "keeps root_id as topic key when root_id and thread_id both exist". With a topic-id key that case now resolves to `omt_…`, and the old "first turn creates a thread, then stays stable" scenario is split into two explicit tests — one covering a topic chat where every message carries the topic id (one session), and one documenting that a message arriving **before** the provider assigns a topic id keeps its message key. No lookup-free rule can merge those two, and the lookup-based rule is what this revision removes.
- Gaps: the live proof above covers a proactive (no inbound message) delivery into a topic session, which is the reported symptom path. A full inbound→reply round trip in a real topic was not run: posting as the human user needs a Feishu scope the local CLI token does not have (`im:message.send_as_user`), so the inbound half is covered by the channel-boundary tests (starter and quote reply resolve to the same peer; the quoted-message lookup result cannot move the session) rather than by a live message.

## Real behavior proof (live, 2026-09-29) / 真机验证

The patch was applied to a running OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (`@openclaw/feishu` 2026.9.6) on this machine, the Gateway restarted, and a topic session was given a proactive delivery with no inbound message (`openclaw cron add --session-key <topic session> --channel last --announce`). Message placement was read back with the Feishu API (`im/v1/messages` by `thread`), so "which topic did it land in" is observed, not inferred.

| time | applied | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12:04 / 12:06 | topic key + send-boundary anchor + heartbeat flag (no `threadId` in `resolveSessionConversation`) | `V2-OK` / `V3-OK` / `V4-OK` each became a **new topic** (topic starters, `thread_position=-1`) |
| 12:11 | plus `resolveFeishuSessionConversation` reporting the topic id | `V5-OK` landed **inside the original topic** `omt_19dfad8930cf5ce6`, and no topic starter was added |

That run is also how the last gap was found: core derives proactive delivery from the session key and asks `resolveSessionConversation` for the thread id, and returning none dropped the topic — the same symptom as the report. With the topic id reported, the send boundary resolves the reply anchor and the message stays in its topic. Redaction: ids shortened, no credentials, no chat content beyond the two-word test text.

回读命令：`lark-cli im +threads-messages-list --thread-id <omt_…> --as bot` 与 `lark-cli im +chat-messages-list --chat-id <oc_…> --as bot`。


## Revision 10 — review follow-up (`98850cf`)

Merged `main`; the only conflict was `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts`. Resolved it by restoring the documented session-identity contract rather than taking the branch's unconditional thread-first rule:

- Native topic chats (`chat_type = topic_group`) resolve `thread_id` first; ordinary groups keep `root_id` first, so the first turn and bot-created thread replies stay in one session. The earlier thread-first change and the expectations it rewrote are reverted.
- This resolves the P1 findings **Preserve root-keyed sessions when an ordinary group creates a thread** and **Keep existing quote-reply history reachable**: this PR no longer rekeys any ordinary-group or existing quote-reply session. Session identity is unchanged from `main`.
- Feishu's message receive event documents `chat_type` as `p2p` / `group` only, so detecting native topic chats from `chat_mode` would be a separate owner decision; this revision does not silently change that behavior. The proactive-delivery fix below is unaffected.

P1 **Match the session chat to the destination** is fixed in `extensions/feishu/src/action-target.ts`: the proactive anchor fallback now requires the parsed session chat (last segment of a fully qualified session key) to equal the normalized send target before resolving the topic anchor. Tests cover the qualified-key shape and a session whose chat differs from the destination.

Review notes:

- The heartbeat flag assertion is kept: core consumes `preserveHeartbeatThreadIdForGroupRoute`, and no core test exercises the Feishu plugin's declaration. Removing it would let a silent topic-delivery regression back in.
- The topic-session tests are kept as distinct shapes (native topic quote reply, native starter key, ordinary-group continuity, qualified-key anchoring); they do not repeat one peer-selection contract.

Verification on `98850cf`:

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.bot-threads.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/channel.outbound.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/channel.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/topic-root.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 191 passed across 2 shards.
- `tsc -p extensions/feishu/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean (tsgo is blocked on this host by glibc 2.31 vs the prebuilt `tsrs` requirement).
- oxlint 0 warnings, oxfmt clean, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --staged` clean.
- `git diff --check` clean.

Remaining proof gap: a live inbound→reply round trip needs Feishu tenant credentials this checkout does not have; the live after-fix trace in the body above still covers the proactive-delivery path, which this revision does not change.

prs.title: feat: open new agent chats instantly and simplify agent selection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Creating an agent now begins in the Control UI instead of sending the user into Crestodian. The selector opens a name-and-Blobster dialog, publishes a pending agent at the top of the roster, and enters that agent’s chat. The Gateway verifies inference before persistence, saves a named greeting in the transcript, and starts the agent’s own plain-text question with four single-agent roles or a custom role. That opening turn has no tools, so no Ask User card appears. After the reply, the agent asks for a little detail about the user’s goal and continues in the same conversation.

The selector puts **Create new agent** first, followed by **Show all** and compact agent rows. Settings gears appear on hover or focus and open each agent’s settings without changing selection. The old pins, search field, divider, tooltip, and redundant actions are removed. **Show all** still shows sessions across agents. The Agents overview is removed; **Claws** is a Labs-gated discovery page using the shared page header and a multi-agent icon. Per-agent settings routes remain.

Creation retains the attempted internal ID through uncertain responses, reconciles a saved agent before retry, and never uses that ID as a visible label, including in the chat breadcrumb. Existing agents and conversations are not deleted. The memory and test-fixture changes repair CI failures encountered while validating this PR. The current base merge includes main's Watch CI repair; this PR no longer has an iOS Watch diff.

## Evidence

Each image compares the old behavior on the left with the changed UI on the right:

![Agent selector before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7f57b24-b094-45ab-8c4a-0f3d4f1728be)

![Agents overview before and Claws discovery after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2bedb8a-925d-4da9-998e-c890ac95c3c8)

![Agent creation at five seconds before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c678b50-b520-4767-8709-13c047685c12)

The [real-speed creation recording](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe160d37-6605-4ae1-a8ad-693337e2b6ec) shows creation, leaving and returning, and reload. [Current named-dialog and role-question proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175291#issuecomment-6285312700) shows the revised onboarding. Earlier measured real-Gateway runs changed new-chat visibility from 29,788 ms to 28 ms and first visible greeting from 51,015 ms to 28 ms; [timing details and caveats](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175291#issuecomment-6233202884) distinguish provisional display from durable history.

[Direct-Gateway proof on the feature head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175291#issuecomment-6306073438) pairs the old Crestodian prompt with the named Blobster dialog, plain-text role question, tailored follow-up, top-of-roster agent after reload, and a full browser recording. The [exact-head live walkthrough](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175291#issuecomment-6306293687) includes current screenshots and a 54-second recording. The isolated [Tailnet preview](https://patricks-mac-studio.tailc03719.ts.net:8471/chat) serves the current `404354710b6` head without OCM. In a fresh authenticated browser, the Claws catalog settled to real discovery cards and the selector opened the named Blobster dialog with no page errors.

**Authority at the provider boundary:** The real WebSocket integration test now pauses the detached onboarding turn after `agents.create` has returned, revokes that device’s operator token, and resumes the real chat owner. Its response is rejected before any second provider POST. The same test proves an authorized creator reaches the provider and a read-only creator is refused before persistence or model I/O. It passed on the feature head before the main integration (one integration case, 32.6 seconds test time); the integration changed no onboarding production code.

**v2026.10.5 stored-data upgrade:** In disposable OCM environments, published OpenClaw v2026.10.5 created Scout with an isolated workspace and a two-message conversation. A clone retained its own rewritten workspace paths. After binding PR build `be9e5c2473a`, `doctor --fix` migrated client credentials and Scout’s agent database v25 → v31; the candidate Gateway passed `/healthz` (200). The same agent name, session ID, original user text, and assistant reply loaded unchanged. A new turn completed in that session and history became user/assistant/user/assistant. The temporary Gateways, launchers, provider, and worktree were removed afterward; the separate review preview remains running. This proof predates the current main integration, whose PR-owned follow-up commits are tests, docs, and an unused-helper removal.

Focused validation through `404354710b6`:

- The direct Gateway and Vite preview at `404354710b6` return HTTP 200. Its authenticated browser view loaded real Claws discovery cards and opened the selector and named Blobster dialog without page errors. In the earlier full creation recording at `a546d89b080`, the named chat appeared in 68 ms, its saved greeting in 171 ms, the agent asked one plain-text four-role question, and the Researcher reply led to a specific detail question. The new agent remained first after same-browser reload. The model-generated question completed in 15.9 seconds on the local Qwen fixture; the greeting was immediate.
- The agent dialog, avatar picker, and shared Plugins header tests pass **10/10**. The exact selector settings browser test passes **1/1**. The delegated creator Gateway test passes **1/1**. Core TypeScript, the controller guard, style lint, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Earlier affected suites: Claws route/flag and selector/pending-chat UI **137/137**; breadcrumb **59/59**; Bifrost **9/9**; Gateway onboarding **5/5**; authority integration **1/1**; agent mutation **95/95**; config reload **133/133**; memory recovery **23/23**; and iOS lane-order **16/16**. The five actionable ClawSweeper findings on the earlier head were addressed. After the main conflict repair, Claws/workspace unit tests pass **33/33**, immediate creation browser tests **3/3**, sidebar browser test **1/1**, and Gateway creation notices **1/1**; UI typecheck, touched-file lint/format, and controller guard pass.
- The `a7ec06d4fc5` hosted CI and required security review passed. Its mobile editor repair makes an enabled tap enter editing even when drawer or keyboard transitions suppress a focus event; the complete 16-case E2E suite passed twice. The `404354710b6` main integration resolved one sidebar test-helper conflict; sidebar interactions passed **75/75**, focused selector/dialog/Claws/route suites passed **97/97**, and UI typecheck, lint, format, and whitespace checks passed. Hosted CI for `404354710b6` remains the merge gate.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way for the UI and creation behavior. The new greeting is an ordinary saved transcript message; rollback does not delete existing agents or conversations. A state snapshot was taken before the compatibility run’s schema migration.

**Blast radius:** Control UI routing and navigation, Gateway agent creation/onboarding, and CI fixtures. Review should pay particular attention to detached caller authority and existing-user upgrade behavior. Exact-head CI and current review gates remain required before landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Reduces repeated test fixtures and assertion scaffolding in the maintainer-authorized test cleanup campaign (batch d355).

## User Impact

No production or user-visible behavior change. Existing behavioral checks remain the target contract; this consolidates test setup and removes low-value repetition. No schema, dependency, public API, or runtime changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replays the 30 requested commits onto pinned main `b27d3ec05df5ea247caf521a6a9ed7fde48cc083`. All 30 commits were replayed; z0586 has no net changes after conservative conflict resolution. One follow-up removes its now-unused fixture expansion; follow-ups fix four CI-reported callback-return errors and drops three review-flagged file reductions. Final diff: 109 test/support files, +5933/-9381 lines (net -3448); production +0/-0. Additionally removes exactly 13 stale mock-export baseline rows identified by hosted CI.

Conflict handling:
- Dropped z0586 edits to backup-create-stream, backup-create.worktrees, backup-database-resources, and backup-sqlite-snapshot.performance rather than replacing current-main cancellation, ownership, snapshot, or worktree proof. Removed the remaining backup fixture options after confirming no surviving caller used them.
- For the second z0589 commit, retained the preceding replayed versions of processes-panel and question-progress rather than accepting obsolete panel selectors or changing current-main mobile/progress expectations.
- All other requested commits applied without conflicts. Only the mock-export baseline changed: 13 exact stale rows were removed as requested by CI; no entries were added or relaxed. Later CI required per-factory isolation explanations for rewritten mocks; these preserve the existing fake behavior and are not blanket baseline exceptions.
- Rebased once after GitHub reported a merge conflict. All 34 code/test commits remained patch-identical; only baseline context changed. Kept main's neighboring stale-entry removal and retained the same 13-entry shrink.
- Review: dropped auth.xai-upgrade, Matrix summary, and anchor preparation reductions, retaining complete model definitions, well-formed negative security fixtures, and early-spawn failure cleanup from main.
- CI: restored non-returning beforeEach bodies in cli-auth-seam and systemd.environment-preservation, plus void cleanup callbacks in embedding-providers and models/list.refresh-completion. The first two CI runs exposed these callback-return regressions. A later run required explicit export-key comparators and per-factory isolation comments; no assertions, retry limits, or timeouts were weakened.
- No changed path matches this checkout's CODEOWNERS rules.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <changed files>`: passed.

prs.title: feat: use Tavily web search through ClawRouter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter users cannot select its native Tavily route for OpenClaw web search without configuring a separate vendor credential. The native search path also needs to retain the account selected for an automation instead of independently choosing the default account.

## User Impact

Users can explicitly select `clawrouter-tavily` and reuse their configured router endpoint and selected credential. Grant, quota, auth and transport failures remain visible, without switching accounts or providers. No deployment or live configuration changes are included.

## Changes

- Add a lazy native search adapter using the existing catalog and route, preserving source/citation metadata and bounded response handling.
- Share Tavily response normalization with the existing vendor plugin through a minimal two-export SDK subpath; transport, credentials and caching stay caller-owned.
- Carry the resolved attempt profile through the existing model-aware core web-search context only to its matching auth owner. Lock native credential lookup to that selected profile and reject an endpoint mismatch before HTTP.
- Preserve independently landed speech registration when integrating main. Supply the canonical host-context resolver in the existing registry fixture; factory validation remains intact.

This PR covers generic `web_search` query/count. Tavily extract/crawl, dedicated options, caching and composed deployed-Worker/grant acceptance remain open.

## Verification

- Actual two-profile regression was red on the old production caller: selected account A was lost and competing default B reached HTTP. The repaired persisted-cron capture/save/reload/reacquire → core web tool → public auth loader → native loopback path passes with two distinct credentials while default B differs.
- Selected-account success, terminal quota denial, endpoint mismatch before egress and cancellation prove no alternate account/provider fallback. Native tests also cover URL/redirect/private-destination rejection, malformed/empty/bounded payloads, metadata and cleanup.
- T2 core/native boundary: 46 passed; affected integration: 92 passed across 11 files. After real main integration, core 15, speech 10 and plugin index 15 passed; native registration initially exposed a fixture setup failure, then native 31 + SDK fixture 9 + captured-registration 11 passed after the canonical fixture correction. Original failure is retained, not counted as product red proof.
- Changed core/routing/helper type-aware lint and formatting passed; staged line-cap ratchet passed. Commits used normal hooks.
- Final integrated source received fresh independent scoped-clean P0–P2 review in two static passes, including 46 whole-file datasets. No whole-graph or runtime-execution claim: first-pass context limitation and eight historic unchanged dependency omissions remain recorded.
- Original feature build and committed cold-import snapshot passed and remain unchanged-source evidence, not a replacement for current-head CI.
- CI exposed omitted SDK surface accounting: the accepted shared facade adds exactly one public entrypoint and two callable exports. The narrow correction accounts for +1/+2/+2 only; deprecated, wildcard and per-entry constraints stay unchanged. Original CI failure and local fail-before/pass-after remain retained. Existing surface tests now pass (five on macOS; Linux process-lifetime test remains platform-selected), and the production surface command reports exactly 158 / 3815 / 2212, with no unauthorized shipped removals. Fresh independent P0-P2 delta review is scoped-clean; formatting, owning-script type-aware lint, erasability and line ratchet pass. No assertions, skips or test files changed.
- Prior-head broad CI also reported OpenRouter image availability, cold ClawRouter catalog timeout, Reef host TypeScript loading, Matrix room target, macOS DMG and Android SDK repository failures. Raw logs and bounded investigations are retained; passing focused replay is not a repair or permission to call CI green. Current-head CI and exact failure attribution remain gates.

## Required before landing

- Current-head required CI, including types, extension lint and SDK export/API comparison. Local declaration preparation refuses the supported shared dependency paths as escaping the checkout; this environment gap is not reported as a passing typecheck.
- New SDK API acknowledgement for the optional provider `authProfile` context and added Tavily normalization entrypoint. Historic acknowledgement `efa63c150e4c0a1523f2e642e2817458d52e403d2749678453b6ddea267a6c42` covers only the original entrypoint/two exports and does not qualify the added context.
- Parent exact-source/auth/public-SDK examination and enforced reviews. ClawSweeper previously held its automated input check without running; that is not review acceptance, and no guard was bypassed.

Synthetic loopback fixtures use private state and credentials. No live grant/account changes, paid vendor calls, deployed Worker proof or full53 parity claim.

prs.title: fix(auth): preserve configured auth inheritance owner during cutover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared-auth migration and bootstrap selected `agents/main/agent` even when `agents.defaults.authInheritance.agentId` named a different legacy owner. The cutover then switched ownership to `state-db` and stopped reading that owner's local credentials, so peer agents could lose inherited auth.

This revision also closes the security-boundary gaps found during review: Doctor could resolve the source from process-global ambient config instead of the selected config; copied-state planning could inspect an auth source outside the copied snapshot; and an explicitly scoped installation write could combine its environment with the ambient installation's auth owner.

## User Impact

Installations using a non-main auth inheritance owner now preserve that owner's credentials during shared-store cutover instead of disabling inheritance with an empty canonical store. Explicit `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` relocation, canonical `state-db` ownership, and explicitly scoped installations remain isolated from ambient runtime selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Added a single legacy-source resolver that honors `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR`, otherwise the configured inheritance owner (including a custom `agentDir`).
- Used that source for Doctor migration detection and both synchronous/asynchronous fresh-store bootstrap.
- Bound Doctor detection to the selected `cfg` rather than the runtime ambient config snapshot.
- Made copied-state planning resolve the configured inheritance owner and refuse a source outside the snapshot with `shared-auth-source-outside-snapshot`.
- Kept explicit `stateDir`, scoped installation environments, and explicit write environments isolated from the ambient runtime auth owner. Normal runtime worker writes still forward the runtime snapshot config.
- Scoped legacy JSON source fencing to the selected owner.
- Added regressions for selected-config Doctor detection, copied-state source refusal, explicit environment/runtime isolation, scoped-installation isolation through the updater, and runtime bootstrap selection.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/infra/state-migrations.shared-auth-store.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/shared-store-bootstrap.async.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/shared-store-bootstrap.runtime.test.ts src/agents/legacy-inherited-auth-dir.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/path-resolve.shared-store.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/store-update.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 70 passed.
- Base-red for the selected-config and copied-state regressions: the old Doctor path resolves the ambient `research` source instead of the selected `ops` owner, and old copied-state planning returns a planning warning instead of `shared-auth-source-outside-snapshot`.
- Base-red for the scoped-installation regression: an installation B write under an ambient `ops` owner resolves `state-db`; the fix retains B's populated `legacy-main` source.
- Base-red for the explicit-environment regression: the old bootstrap resolves `legacy-main` instead of `state-db`.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` — passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` — conflict markers, line-cap, assertion safety, SQLite worker/dialect, format, config docs, plugin boundaries, import cycles, lint core changed files, and related guards passed. The command remains non-green because of environment/baseline failures: `tsgo` requires GLIBC >= 2.29 while this host has 2.28; existing max-lines findings in unrelated `ui/` files; and existing dead-export findings in `src/agents/tool-search-catalog.ts` and `ui/src/pages/sessions/view.test-support.tsx`.
- No schema changes are introduced.

The sensitive-change gate still requires a maintainer `/allow-security-sensitive-change` approval for the new head.

Closes #178421

prs.title: feat(automations): migrate heartbeat jobs through Doctor
prs.body:
Related: #167796

This is **slice 3 of 4** of the heartbeat-to-Automations migration:

1. #178650 — landed: prevent main-session cron events from being recorded successful before adoption.
2. #178764 — landed: session-controller execution and settlement; additive Claw review schema.
3. This PR — migrate heartbeat data and make ordinary automation jobs authoritative.
4. Planned after this PR lands — remove the retired heartbeat executor and the approved breaking plugin-SDK surfaces.

## What Problem This Solves

Heartbeat monitors cannot become independently editable Automations while their settings, scratch, execution policies, and startup reconciliation remain owned by the old heartbeat path.

## User Impact

Existing monitors and supported legacy heartbeat tasks become ordinary editable Automations, preserving job identity, run history, scratch revisions and explicit deletion, disabled state, scheduling anchors, pending occurrences, and existing tool authority. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` after a manual binary replacement; supported updates run the same migration through Doctor. Edit, disable, or delete the resulting job in Automations or through the CLI. Restart, config reload, and repeated Doctor runs preserve those choices.

This implements Peter's approved October 3/12 migration design and the October 18 additive Claw review decision. Claw Add converts legacy heartbeat declarations into ordinary jobs and shows their positive-integer `everyMs` schedules and `owner` delivery truthfully; existing `{ cron, timezone }`, `none`, and `last-channel` variants retain their meaning.

Doctor emits this notice once when the migration receipt completes:

> Migrated heartbeats now use standard Automations delivery. Heartbeat-specific duplicate suppression and no-route skipping were removed: repeated updates can be delivered, and a missing route no longer skips the run before execution. Delivery failures follow ordinary automation handling. Review the migrated jobs' delivery settings if you relied on either behavior.

The shared state schema advances to **30** so an older scheduler cannot ignore the new job policies. Keep the verified pre-upgrade backup for rollback; do not lower the schema marker. The agent schema remains **31**. Physical executor and public SDK removal remain in slice 4.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Cron service and session controller now own migrated execution from admission through settlement. Main-session system events and agent turns use that boundary; queue acceptance alone is not success. Job-level active hours, idle admission, scratch, structured results, and owner/direct-message delivery replace the corresponding heartbeat behavior. Quiet `no_change` results suppress automatic delivery without hiding execution failures, and optional reasoning accompanies meaningful output. Retained authenticated source, workspace custody, and current permission checks remain in force.

Doctor writes and verifies canonical jobs and context before retiring legacy inputs. Its existing backup and include-aware config owners preserve recovery. Completed provisioning receipts prevent deleted monitors from reappearing, and startup/reload no longer reconcile the old monitor declarations. Explicit setup creates the ambient owner's default proactive check once. Claw Add creates imported jobs disabled until scratch is accepted and activation is verified; an uncertain or conflicting scratch write retains the admitted agent/jobs and reports the required inspection instead of overwriting concurrent edits.

Limits and recovery behavior:

- Missing or ambiguous owner identity never falls back to the last group conversation. A missing route does not skip execution; a configured DM block remains intentional non-delivery.
- A legacy model outside the agent's current allowed policy is dropped with a diagnostic. Doctor preserves allowed overrides and does not expand permission or model allowlists. Changed definitions may require fresh standing approval.
- Ambiguous migration inputs remain recoverable and their pending jobs cannot run. Archived source bytes and explicit scratch tombstones are preserved; stale pending facts are not promoted into a replacement session.
- Scratch becomes model context, so it is not a secret store. It remains revision-guarded and omitted from ordinary job/history responses.
- This does not promise exactly-once arbitrary tool effects across a crash. The existing Cron recovery contract still applies; the main-session system-event regression specifically prevents false success and replay before adoption.
- Legacy protocol-v4 controls remain as adapters. Transport keepalives are unchanged. This slice adds no new global configuration, retention policy, or Claw lifecycle owner.

## Evidence

The focused 123-file selection passed 2,058 cases and identified 13 failures. Each failure was repaired at its owner or fixture and replayed with its affected consumers: the repair selection passed 378 cases, its last two fixture corrections passed 21/21, and the final editor replay passed 14/14. These selections overlap; they are not a combined unique-test total.

- Review identified and repaired an implicit-owner migration bug: stored tasks keep the legacy ambient cadence while empty installations remain unprovisioned. The expanded regression fails on the original candidate; both migration suites now pass **54/54** (45.20 seconds including compilation; 48.29-second wrapper). Explicit disables and unenrolled multi-agent owners remain disabled.
- Doctor's retained migration proof passed **15/15**, serially, including backups, migration refusal, model policy, interrupted outcome transfer, and installed CLI recovery. The five published-updater marker cases also passed **5/5** through the real built CLI with synthetic isolated state; the original child budgets are unchanged.
- The restart/controller regression passed **3/3**, and the heartbeat replay selection passed **3/3**. S1's negative control established the original false-success defect on main; the migration schema and job-policy negative controls also fail at their assertions on the clean S3 base.
- The delivery repair is RED before the fix and GREEN at a synthetic physical transport. Six cases cover admitted reasoning, ordinary suppression, CLI and persisted-descendant reply directives, and original/reset session generations. Prepared delivery passed 5/5; shared-session result behavior passed 5/5.
- Desktop and narrow-browser Automations proof passed **8/8** across three files: editing migrated policies, revision-owned scratch save/reload, and owner delivery without an accidental run or duplicate Add. Editor save/reopen passed 14/14; scratch/page/view/form passed 58/58.
- Core/UI production and affected test type graphs, targeted lint/format, and protocol/native/config/docs/schema/prompt generators passed. Existing unrelated line-cap and core graph-root overages were reproduced on the pinned base without changing their budgets. Final commit-hook qualification passed; the Gateway Cron file passes all 90 cases after a coherent test-module extraction.

Representative completed commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.restart-session-event.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --passWithNoTests=false
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/cron/editor-save.node.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --noEmit -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --noEmit -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json
```

| Remaining qualification | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Exact candidate | `d3d351b8cf8b43b5bc3a2a58b36df1675064bdbf` |
| Linux installed-package proof | Pending: published-stable upgrade, Cron/MCP cleanup, and published dreaming migration |
| Committed-branch independent review | Six-pass committed review finding repaired; committed correction is scoped-clean through P2 |
| Exact-head CI | Pending PR publication |

Line delta against the S3 base: production/tooling **+9,380/−2,812**; tests/support **+10,197/−4,967**; docs **+747/−825**; generated **+5/−5**. The migration must ship complete backup, conversion, execution, and editable-job consumers together; physical executor deletion follows in S4.

Test fixtures and repeated assertions carry unnecessary duplication across CLI, config, sidebar, worker, gateway, channel, script, and board suites.

## User Impact

No production or user-visible behavior change. This batch compacts tests and reuses test-only fixtures; it does not change runtime code, configuration, dependencies, or public APIs.

Replay campaign batch d356 onto pinned main f88c606370965183c6157f47b17ac78c484f38d7. All 30 supplied commits were applied in order, with only the conflict adjustments listed below. Keep distinct behavioral checks and main's newer regression coverage while removing repetitive test plumbing.

- Sidebar pinned agents: retain main's navigationDrawerToggle helper and chat.startup response while moving the test body into a helper; retain the branch's compact mobile-class check.
