prs.title: fix(telegram): route model-confirmation edit through rich funnel
prs.body:
Closes #123886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with `richMessages: true` on their Telegram account and who complete the `/models` picker would see the final "✅ Model changed to…" confirmation rendered on top of / mixed with the stale rich-text markup from the picker's prior provider/model-list step, instead of a clean confirmation message. The picker's intermediate steps (provider list, model list, pagination) already fully replace the rich body correctly; only the terminal confirmation edit was affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `/models` picker sends its initial body as a rich message when `richMessages` is enabled, and every lifecycle edit to that message (provider list, model list, pagination) already routes through the rich funnel in `createTelegramCallbackMessageActions`. The final selection confirmation was the one exception: it always fell back to the legacy HTML `editMessageText` path. Editing a rich-sent message through that legacy text path does not fully replace the prior rich body — Telegram renders the new plain/HTML text mixed with the stale rich markup underneath it.

The fix converts the model-confirmation call site to author rich content via hand-built `RichText`/`InputRichBlock[]` when `richMessages` is enabled, following the existing `progress-draft-preview.ts` precedent for opting a `parse_mode: "HTML"` edit back onto the rich funnel:

- `TelegramCallbackRichTextOverride` lets `editCallbackMessage`/`editCallbackMessageWithButtons` accept an optional `richTextOverride`; when supplied, the edit routes through `getTelegramRichRawApi(bot.api).editMessageText(...)` with hand-built `rich_message` blocks instead of the legacy text funnel.
- `buildModelSelectionConfirmation` (new file) builds both the HTML and rich-block confirmation bodies from one shared text-building function, so the two representations can't drift apart — only model-id HTML-escaping and the runtime placeholder spelling differ per funnel.
- Non-rich accounts (`richMessages` disabled or unset) are unaffected; the legacy HTML path is unchanged for that funnel.

As a side effect of this fix, `bot-handlers.callback-router.ts` grew past the repo's 700-line oxlint `max-lines` cap, so the pre-existing ~290-line `handleTelegramModelCallback` function was extracted verbatim into a new file, `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts`, with no logic changes — pure file-split, kept in this PR so CI stays green (`AGENTS.md`: "Split files around ~700 LOC... never add a `max-lines` suppression").

This PR supersedes closed PR #124173, which introduced rich-block sending but left the confirmation edit on the legacy HTML path — ClawSweeper's own review of that PR classified it as `partial_overlap`, i.e. it fixed the picker's rich-block plumbing but not the actual reported bug (the confirmation still overlapped stale rich text). This change closes that exact gap.

## User Impact

Telegram operators with `richMessages: true` now see a single clean confirmation message when they finish the `/models` picker — no more stale/mixed rich-text markup left behind. Operators without `richMessages` enabled see no behavior change.

## Evidence

- Targeted tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts extensions/telegram/src/model-confirmation-message.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` (and related callback-router/harness specs) — 151/151 passing, including a new regression test asserting `richTextOverride` routes through the rich funnel and 3 new `buildModelSelectionConfirmation` tests asserting HTML vs rich-block parity/escaping.
- Full extension suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` — 3593/3594 passing; the 1 failure (`setup-surface.test.ts > accepts numeric sender ids only`) is a pre-existing, unrelated sandbox-locale artifact (`zh`-locale string vs expected English string), reproducible on `main` before this change.
- Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean.
- Lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on all touched/added files — exit 0, confirms the `max-lines` violation from the file-split is resolved (`bot-handlers.callback-router.ts` now 395 lines, down from 706).
- Format: `pnpm format` — no diff.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning): `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`, `overall: patch is correct (0.96)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof was not feasible in this environment (no bot token configured); the mock-harness/unit proof above exercises the exact changed rich-funnel edit path per the ClawSweeper Review Policy real-behavior-proof gate for channel-visible changes.

## Update (commit 6973bab29b9)

Two fixes on top of the original commit:

- **ClawSweeper P1 finding addressed** — `editCallbackMessage`'s rich-routing branch previously fell back to `buildTelegramRichMarkdown(text)` for *any* rich-account callback edit that wasn't `parse_mode: "HTML"`, not just the model-picker confirmation. That silently ran markdown parsing over arbitrary un-authored text from approval receipts (`terminalizeApprovalMessage`), the plugin SDK's `respond.editMessage`, and the model picker's own intermediate pagination/provider-list/model-list/error edits — none of which are markdown-authored, so incidental `*`/`_`/backtick/`[` characters (e.g. in provider/model ids or user-controlled error text) could be reinterpreted as formatting instead of sent literally. Fixed by making rich routing strictly opt-in per call: it now only fires when the caller explicitly supplies `richTextOverride`'s hand-built blocks (as the model-picker confirmation does); every other caller — regardless of `richMessages`/`parse_mode` — stays on the legacy literal-text funnel, exactly as before this PR. `buildTelegramRichMarkdown` is no longer imported by this file (still used correctly elsewhere: streaming draft previews and the general outbound-delivery pipeline, where callers genuinely author markdown).
- **CI fixes**: `check-test-types` (two `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` blocks needed explicit `vi.fn<T>()` typing plus a null-check helper for `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`-safe `.mock.calls.at(0)` access) and `check-dependencies`/knip (`ModelSelectionConfirmationParams`/`ModelSelectionConfirmation` had no external importer and shouldn't have been exported).

**Correction to my earlier claiming comment on #123886**: I stated "clean typecheck" there; at that point `check-test-types` and `check-dependencies` were actually failing on CI (fixed now, in this commit). Apologies for the inaccurate evidence claim — flagging it here so the record is accurate.

### Updated evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` — 7/7 passing, including a rewritten test asserting plain-text edits with no `richTextOverride` stay on the legacy funnel even when `richMessages` is enabled (inverts the prior test, which asserted the now-fixed over-broad behavior), and updated fallback/error-path tests that now supply an explicit override to exercise the rich funnel.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` (full extension suite) — 3593/3594 passing; same single pre-existing unrelated `setup-surface.test.ts` locale failure noted above, reproduced identically on this branch's pre-fix HEAD via `git stash`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — both clean.
- `knip` production + all-exports check — clean, no new dead exports.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` — no diff. `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files — exit 0.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) rerun on this commit: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`, `overall: patch is correct (0.98)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof remains not feasible in this environment (no bot token configured), unchanged from the original PR evidence.

## Update (commit a0dec118a21): delete-and-reply instead of legacy-edit on rich-edit failure

ClawSweeper's follow-up P2 finding on the prior commit: `editCallbackMessage`'s
catch block fell back to `legacyEditCallbackMessage(text, editParams)` whenever
the rich raw-API edit failed for a non-terminal reason. `richTextOverride` is
only ever supplied for a message that was itself sent as rich (the model
picker's final confirmation edit), so a legacy-text retry there reproduces the
exact stale-rich-markup symptom #123886 reported — the new text lands mixed
with the prior rich body instead of replacing it.

Fixed by extracting a shared `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` helper (delete
the rich-sent message, then send a plain reply) and using it both for this
new failure path and for `editCallbackMessageWithButtons`'s existing "no text
in the message" recovery, which had the same delete-then-reply logic inlined
already — a small dedup alongside the fix, not just a symptom patch.

### Updated evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts`
  — 8/8 passing, including a new test ("deletes and replies instead of
  legacy-editing when the rich edit fails for a non-terminal reason") and the
  `editCallbackMessageWithButtons` describe block's "deletes and replies,
  through the real /model-picker-confirmation call shape, when the rich edit
  fails" case, now reusing the shared helper.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` (full extension suite) —
  3594/3595 passing; same single pre-existing unrelated `setup-surface.test.ts`
  locale failure noted above (reproduces identically on `origin/main`, not
  touched by this branch).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — clean.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on both touched files — exit 0.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — no diff.
- `knip` (production + dependencies) — clean, no new unused exports.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) rerun on this
  commit: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`,
  `overall: patch is correct (0.97)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof remains not feasible in this environment (no
  bot token configured), unchanged from the original PR evidence.


## Update (commit f082965e64c): correct inline comment on rich-funnel invariant

ClawSweeper's re-review on `a0dec118a21` surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P3] Correct the callback-funnel explanation** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts:294-298`. The inline comment claimed the picker's provider/model-list edit steps "already edit through the rich funnel when richMessages is enabled." That's inaccurate: `editCallbackMessageWithButtons` only takes the rich path when the caller explicitly supplies `richTextOverride`, and none of the list/pagination/error edit calls in this file pass one — only the terminal confirmation does.

Verified the finding against real code before fixing:
- `bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts` gates rich routing on `if (!richMessages || !richTextOverride)` falling back to legacy — both conditions are required, not just `richMessages`.
- Grepped all 10 `editMessageWithButtons`/`editCallbackMessageWithButtons` call sites in `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts`: only the final confirmation call supplies rich blocks; every provider-list/model-list/pagination/error edit omits `richTextOverride` and stays on the legacy funnel.

Fix: reworded the comment to state the true invariant — those list/pagination/error steps stay on the legacy HTML funnel, and this terminal confirmation is the one call that explicitly opts into the rich funnel via `richTextOverride`. Comment-only change, no behavior difference.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 149/149 passing.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` — clean.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` — applied.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Note: ClawSweeper's proof-confidence score on this PR is driven by the disclosed, unresolved "no bot token configured in this sandbox" limitation — real Telegram behavior proof for the rich-edit/delete-and-reply path is still outstanding and I can't produce it here. That gap remains honestly disclosed rather than worked around.



## Update (commit 952e6f88239): correct remaining rich-funnel comment (late finding)

ClawSweeper's re-review on `f082965e64c` surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P3] Correct the remaining rich-funnel explanations** — `extensions/telegram/src/model-confirmation-message.ts:4-7`. Flagged as a late finding: the same inaccurate claim fixed at `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts:294-298` in the prior commit was still present in this file's JSDoc header ("the picker's provider/model-list edits already went through the rich funnel"), and duplicated in a regression-test comment at `bot.test.ts:2881`.

Verified before fixing: grepped every `richBlocks` usage in `extensions/telegram/src/**` — `model-confirmation-message.ts` is the sole producer, and the terminal confirmation edit in `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` is the sole consumer. Provider/list/pagination/error edits never supply `richTextOverride` and stay legacy-only, confirming the same corrected invariant already landed in the previous commit.

Fix: reworded both comments to state that legacy HTML is used by every other picker step (and as this confirmation's fallback), while rich blocks are used only by this terminal confirmation, which explicitly opts into the rich funnel via `richTextOverride`. Comment-only change, no behavior difference.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 149/149 passing.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — clean, no reformatting needed.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.



## Update (commit d55b43e32ef): send fallback before deleting the picker

ClawSweeper's re-review on `952e6f88239` (reviewed_at `2026-08-16T01:39:38.304Z`) surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P2] Send the fallback before deleting the picker** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts:115-118`. `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` deleted the rich picker before awaiting `sendMessage`. If that send failed, the model selection had already been applied but the user lost both the picker and its confirmation — a silent-failure outcome per this repo's own severity doctrine (silent failure ranks above crash or missing feature).

Verified before fixing:
- Read `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` in full: it awaited `deleteCallbackMessage()` (swallowing its own errors) and only then called `replyToCallbackChat(text, replyParams)`. Exactly as described.
- Confirmed via `git log --oneline -- extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts` that this helper (and its ordering) was introduced by this PR's own commit `a0dec118a21`, not a pre-existing unrelated defect — squarely in-scope to fix here.
- Confirmed via grep that no existing test covered this ordering (only that both calls occurred, not their order or the rejection path).

Fix: reordered `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` to call `replyToCallbackChat` (send) first, then make `deleteCallbackMessage` best-effort only after a successful send. A send failure now propagates untouched and never triggers a delete, so the picker is never destroyed without a working replacement.

Added two regression tests in `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts`:
- asserts `sendMessage`'s invocation order is before `deleteMessage`'s (fails pre-fix: order was reversed);
- asserts a `sendMessage` rejection propagates and `deleteMessage` is never called (fails pre-fix: delete already happened unconditionally before the send was even attempted).

Both new tests were confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code (via `git stash` of the production change alone) for the intended reason, then pass after the fix.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 151/151 passing.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — applied, clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `.claude/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning) — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.


## Update (commit 4ebf2f18165): forward business context to the fallback picker's deletion

ClawSweeper's re-review on `d55b43e32ef` (reviewed_at `2026-08-16T03:37:58.723Z`) surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P2] Forward business context when deleting the fallback picker** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts:119-121`. `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` sends the replacement with the callback's business context but then calls `deleteCallbackMessage`, whose delete omitted it. On a Business callback whose rich edit fails, the replacement could be sent while deletion silently failed and was swallowed, leaving the stale interactive picker behind.

Verified before fixing:
- Re-read `deleteCallbackMessage`: it called `bot.api.deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id)` unconditionally, while its siblings `legacyEditCallbackMessage` and `replyToCallbackChat` both forward `business_connection_id`.
- Checked grammY's typed API surface (`node_modules/grammy/out/core/api.d.ts`): `deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id, signal?)` has **no** `business_connection_id` parameter at all — unlike `editMessageText`/`sendMessage`/`editMessageReplyMarkup`, which all accept one.
- Cross-checked against the Telegram Bot API's own method list (`@grammyjs/types/methods.d.ts`): `deleteMessage` genuinely has no such field. Telegram instead exposes a dedicated method for this exact case, `deleteBusinessMessages(business_connection_id, message_ids)`, which grammY surfaces as `bot.api.deleteBusinessMessages(...)`. Deleting a business-sent message is a different Bot API call, not `deleteMessage` plus an extra field.

Fix: `deleteCallbackMessage` now calls `bot.api.deleteBusinessMessages(business_connection_id, [message_id])` when the callback carries business context, and falls back to the existing `bot.api.deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id)` otherwise.

Added a regression test in `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` asserting that a Business callback's rich-edit-failure recovery deletes via `deleteBusinessMessages` with the right connection id and message id, and never calls `deleteMessage`. Confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code (via `git stash` of the production change alone — `deleteBusinessMessages` is never called pre-fix) for the intended reason, then passes after the fix.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 152/152 passing.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — applied, clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `.claude/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning) — clean, no accepted/actionable findings ("patch is correct (0.99)").

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.

ClawSweeper's `needs real behavior proof` gate asks for the added Gateway harness to be *executed* against this head, with its terminal output **and** verdict JSON supplied together. prs.title: fix(ui): hide empty sidebar groups when filtering by status
prs.body:
Closes #178972

## What Problem This Solves

With All owners, Active status, and Hide empty groups set to When filtering, the sidebar kept blank headings for groups whose sessions were archived or snoozed.

## User Impact

When filtering now also applies to Active, Snoozed, and Archived status. The default Active view hides native groups without matching sessions. Choose All status or Never to keep empty destinations available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing sidebar projection now uses the selected status as well as the owner filter. It waits for the initial session list before treating a group as empty, preserves collapsed populated groups, and leaves catalog and team sections with their existing owners. No extra requests, stored settings, or layout changes are added.

## Evidence

The original archived-only heading failure reproduced on both desktop and mobile before the fix. The repaired flow passes status transitions, All/Never recovery, and collapsed-group preservation. Six existing owner and empty-destination scenarios also pass, along with all 17 projection tests.

- New desktop/mobile scenarios: 9.93 seconds for the source-server run; individual cases 3.32 and 4.58 seconds.
- Projection file: 0.656 seconds in Vitest, 1.34 seconds including the wrapper.
- Focused lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- UI production, UI E2E, and UI component typecheck graphs pass.
- Independent Codex review: no P0–P2 findings. Proof uses Chromium with synthetic Gateway data.

### Risk and coverage

Active is the default status, so its empty native headings now hide with When filtering. All and Never recovery, initial unloaded lists, populated collapsed groups, owner filters, and the existing partial-roster behavior are covered. Validation used the source-server Control UI and a synthetic Gateway; a production bundle and live Gateway were not run. CI timings are pending.

prs.title: refactor: retire private native-lifecycle test seams
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private scheduler/controller resets, observer read/persist selectors and readview wrappers make fixtures run different plumbing from production. An unused auth run ID also crosses two private layers without a reader.

## Changes

Use native Swarm/controller lifetimes and observe their real accepted work in test support. Keep ordinary Stop drainage, failed-write custody, queued admission, FIFO, physical-store identity and shutdown settlement. Fixtures select isolated native state and close their own work rather than clearing live owner collections through production test exports.

Use the observer's existing read/persist owners directly. Retain the named persist-digest contract, actual source/model/terminal algorithms, independent host attribution, detached async context, result delivery and real persistence errors. Remove already-orphaned model selectors rather than recreate earlier retired branches.

Inline the readview packaging and the sole slot-bound broker object at their existing consumers. Preserve the exact metadata/type/readonly behavior and broker callbacks/accounting. Retire the test-only prewarm item list and unread auth-controller runId, without changing outer run IDs, failure-health policy or current authority.

Remove private Ask User and Dashboard transport/emission selectors. Fixtures intercept the existing native module boundaries, including the UI Guest V2 dispatcher, while retaining the real QuestionManager, admitted context and awaited settlement. Supported lower-level dispatcher contracts are unchanged.

This is the native-lifecycle area of the remaining seam family. Package/provider/static-registry cuts stay separate to keep attribution bounded. The complete 81-path candidate removes 117 net production lines, adds 587 net fixture/support lines, and removes seven obsolete mock-baseline rows plus one obsolete assertion allowance: 462 net lines added overall. Fixture growth is the explicit cost of exercising and settling native owners instead of discarding their collections through production test controls.

No public plugin SDK/config/CLI/Gateway protocol/persisted shape, schema, dependency, permission, retention or durability change. The protected standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No retained security, durability, concurrency or accepted-write settlement guard is removed. The deleted reset/selector controls were private fixture paths, not production recovery features. Source provenance and complete consumer migration are recorded in the lane evidence; no real human incident is dismissed.

## Evidence

Targeted core and UI fixture types, canonical formatting, scoped core/UI lint, the 78-source line-cap check and all 14 suppression-audit cases pass. Complete independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean with no actionable findings (0.91); final source verification completed. The observer fixture preserves its original early side-effect registration and obtains its helper from the already-evaluated module afterward, avoiding duplicate static imports while surviving canonical import sorting. Its focused lint and formatting checks pass.

The main Swarm scheduler suite passes all 16 cases (8.49s suite time; 21.67s wrapper), and prewarm passes all 14 cases (5.32s suite; 24.30s wrapper). Claim-close, observer and Dashboard selections stop before cases at compiled-worker cache prerequisites; the local campaign prohibits broad worker preparation, so these and the remaining dependent suites are not claimed passing. The final formatter-compatible fixture binding has a fresh scoped-clean P0–P2 review (0.98), with final source verification complete. The removed Swarm publication was its only counted assertion, so its obsolete one-row allowance is removed rather than weakening a gate; the assertion ratchet passes.

Exact-head hosted CI will supply broad runtime/cycle/package-boundary proof; no broad local build, E2E, whole-graph compiler, timeout increase, retry, skip or weakened assertion is used. A prerequisite-blocked selection is reported as unrun, never passed.

prs.title: perf: prepare restart recovery readers during Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first chat after a PostgreSQL Gateway restart pays for a cold shared recovery reader after HTTP readiness. SQLite often opens that same reader earlier through incidental cron maintenance.

## User Impact

Prepare the existing recovery reader during startup while keeping chat gated until saved delivery and subagent/exec recovery safely settles. No cron scheduling, retention, database schema, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

PostgreSQL auth-profile reads prepare/register the native agent store before cron subscribes. SQLite auth reads are read-only; its later native registration publishes a topology event that advances cron's first registry sweep. Startup now prepares the existing maintenance reader directly from already-admitted database targets, without depending on that timing accident or performing a recovery query early.

The startup lifetime tracks preparation through shutdown. Preparation does not delay readiness; the existing read owner still controls admission, connection reuse, idle retirement, and the eventual recovery reads.

## Performance

Acceptance rule, recorded before measurement: run three interleaved rounds of base PostgreSQL, candidate PostgreSQL, base SQLite and candidate SQLite on one Testbox with the frozen PGLIVE2 workload. PostgreSQL restart typed `startup-sidecars` retries must fall from 24 toward SQLite's approximately 8, and restart-first-turn model-excluded residual must improve. Verify pre-ready reader preparation and reuse by recovery. Preserve initial/restart readiness, cold/memory/settled residuals, memory-tool spans, work counts and all failed/adverse cells; any single-cell regression of at least 20% needs explicit owner disposition. No performance acceptance is recorded yet.

Frozen baseline: `b27d3ec05df5ea247caf521a6a9ed7fde48cc083`; candidate: `8a0a7e84a5a072bf3c9f1e87dae21653205e037f`. The predecessor import-deferral fix is present on both arms.

## Evidence

- The startup regression fails on the baseline because no recovery reader preparation starts before readiness.
- The pre-rebase candidate passed 36/36 focused Gateway, lane-custody and import-boundary tests under the local load gate. The rebased candidate uses current main’s shared test fixture; its focused tests, TSRS, lint, builds and live comparison must pass remotely before acceptance.
- Fresh independent review of the rebased candidate found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The admitted-target loop lives in the existing startup-session owner; no new state or worker implementation was introduced.

Release-note context: prepare PostgreSQL recovery readers during Gateway startup to reduce the first-chat delay after restart, while preserving saved-input recovery ordering.

Production +34 lines, regression +65 lines. The existing startup lifetime and maintenance reader remain the owners; no new cache or recovery implementation. All final-head PostgreSQL conformance shards must actually run and pass before landing.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```
npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-result.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.media.test.ts

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-08-26T10:52:02.672Z
seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z
seq=2 context.compiled     2026-08-26T10:52:02.741Z
seq=3 prompt.submitted     2026-08-26T10:52:02.746Z
seq=4 model.completed      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=5 trace.artifacts      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=6 session.ended        2026-08-26T10:52:05.371Z
```

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

### What was not tested

- `pnpm test` full suite and `pnpm build` artifacts beyond the local build used for the live run above (targeted suites only, per above).
- Codex app-server live run (its ordering is covered by the new harness tests instead).

## AI-assisted

prs.title: fix(doctor): migration blocked by false transcript mismatches after label repair
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #178960

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users migrating a legacy state directory (e.g. Linux → Windows) would see `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite validate` report false `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch` failures for sessions whose event IDs, counts, and message content are otherwise identical — leaving `openclaw update repair` unable to finalize the migration and the Gateway stopped.
- The mismatches are produced by Doctor itself: its inbound-context label repair rewrites recognized headings (`Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` → `Conversation info: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧`) in SQLite rows only, while the retained JSONL transcripts keep the legacy spelling — and verification compared serialized payloads byte-for-byte, so heading-only normalization was reported as missing content.
- **Related:** #177987 and #169087 describe overlapping migration verification failures; the historical filename/header half of this report already has a merged fix (`transcript_filename_mismatch` is a retained-source issue), while the label-normalization half had no fix on main.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Transcript verification recognizes Doctor's own frozen heading rewrite at the comparison boundary: a retained source payload verifies when either its original serialization or its frozen-rewrite serialization equals the SQLite payload. Repaired sessions settle, the migration receipt can be recorded, and Gateway maintenance can complete.
- **Out of scope:** No change to receipt policy (`isRetainedSourceIssue` codes untouched — mismatch warnings are not blindly accepted), no change to the retained JSONL bytes, and no change to the historical filename/header recovery path.
- **Highest-risk area:** Relaxing the exact-payload comparison in `verifyTranscriptEvents` could mask genuine content conflicts.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Equivalence is decided by the exact frozen rewrite Doctor itself applies (shared module, moved verbatim from the Doctor repair), gated by the existing decoded-spelling pre-filter, and only heading transformations are recognized; any other textual difference (including changed JSON inside the fence) still fails verification, and identity conflicts still throw.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** After Doctor's label repair, a retained transcript with only legacy inbound-context headings verifies in all modes (`ordered`, `contained`, `appendable`), so `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch` is no longer reported for those sessions and the migration receipt condition can be satisfied.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/infra/session-sqlite-transcript-verification.ts` (comparison boundary), `src/config/sessions/legacy-inbound-context-labels.ts` (the moved frozen rewrite — shared verbatim with the Doctor repair), and the regression `recognizes Doctor's repaired inbound-context headings without touching retained transcripts` in `src/infra/session-sqlite-transcript-verification.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree on `origin/main` (beb97b5b7dc) with real on-disk SQLite agent databases via the project's test state harness (`withOpenClawTestState`): the regression imports a retained JSONL transcript into SQLite, replays Doctor's label repair through the production write transaction (`runOpenClawAgentWriteTransaction` + `updateSqliteTranscriptEventJsonInTransaction`), and runs the production verification function against the real database.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/session-sqlite-transcript-verification.test.ts   # RED before fix, GREEN after
  bash skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/config/sessions/legacy-inbound-context-labels.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-session-transcript-labels.ts src/infra/session-sqlite-transcript-verification.ts \
    src/infra/session-sqlite-transcript-verification.test.ts                                  # oxfmt + oxlint + same-dir tests + tsgo:core
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retained-source-verification.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.recovery.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.deferred-plugin.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.discovery.test.ts                                      # affected doctor-session-sqlite shard
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  src/infra/session-sqlite-transcript-verification.test.ts: 4 passed (4)
    ✓ recognizes Doctor's repaired inbound-context headings without touching retained transcripts
    ✓ verifies legacy media / openai / openai-codex without changing historical receipts
  src/commands/doctor-session-transcript-labels.test.ts: 11 passed (11)
  [validate] oxfmt + oxlint passed; tsgo:core 4/4 passed
  doctor-session-sqlite targeted shard: Test Files 4 passed (4), Tests 64 passed (64)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test first failed on `origin/main` (`expected undefined to deeply equal { events: 2, missingEvents: 0, sqliteEvents: 2 }` — exactly the false `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch` path). After the patch, the repaired SQLite rows verify against the untouched retained JSONL in all three modes, the retained file's bytes are asserted unchanged, and a control case where the JSON inside the fence differs still fails ordered/contained verification and still throws the identity-conflict error in appendable mode.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** On unpatched main, `verifyTranscriptEvents` returned `undefined` for the repaired session in every mode → standalone validation records `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch` → `report.issues.every(isRetainedSourceIssue)` fails → no deferred-plugin import receipt → "Doctor cannot repair this state: Legacy session store requires migration".
- **What was not tested:** The reporter's actual Windows state directory (not available); the five historical files with mismatched headers (already covered by the merged filename/header fix and reported separately in the issue).
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review (CI lanes pending)

prs.title: Improve short-term memory promotion quality gate
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory-core deep promotion can promote short-term snippets that are high-signal but non-durable for `MEMORY.md`: transient diagnostics, raw logs, temp paths, failure artifacts, and credential-bearing text pollute long-term memory and make future recall less useful.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial broad text heuristics were rewritten after review into a structure-based gate that only fires on shapes the promotion lifecycle actually passes:

- **Value-backed secrets only.** Concrete value shapes are rejected: `sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `AKIA…`, JWT triples, PEM private-key blocks, and `label=value` assignments with a non-masked value. Bare words like "secret" no longer match, so durable guidance such as "store the API key in ~/.openclaw/credentials/" stays eligible.
- **Normalized-input matching.** Every promotion call site (record, store load, rank, apply) passes `normalizeSnippet()` output; all patterns match that single-line form. Line-anchored stack-frame patterns that could never fire on real store input are gone, replaced by an inline frame matcher (`at run (/path/file.js:1:2)` anywhere in the text).
- **Durable-intent carve-out.** Snippets stating a standing preference (`always use`, `prefers`, `standing rule`, `rule:`, `remember`, `should default to`) stay eligible even when they mention transient-looking vocabulary — mirrors `rem-evidence.ts`'s existing monitoring carve-out. Concrete secret values are never exempted.
- **Narrow error vocabulary.** HTTP status requires an `http` prefix (bare `4xx` patterns would falsely match `file.cc:486` source references), ISO timestamps are structural, fenced JSON dumps require a fence+brace shape, and the transient phrase list aligns with rem-evidence (adds the `token expired` / `refresh_token` family). Generic report headings (`Verdict:`, `What works`, `Result:`) are no longer filtered.
- **Scope note.** The gate covers English diagnostics plus language-independent structure (paths, timestamps, stack frames). Non-English diagnostic phrasing is intentionally out of scope to avoid false positives on non-English durable content.

## User Impact

- Transient diagnostics, raw dumps, temp paths, and credential values no longer enter durable promotion at record, load, rank, or apply.
- Durable guidance that merely discusses credentials keeps promoting.
- Upgrade-safe for existing stores: the narrowed gate matches 0 of 512 real recall-store entries sampled from a production store (31 of them already promoted).

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` clean; oxfmt and oxlint (extensions config) clean on both touched files; `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Vitest: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts` — 91/91 pass. Three new tests: a table-driven predicate case (12 rejected shapes incl. pre-normalized and inline stack frames; 6 retained shapes incl. credential-mentioning guidance and the durable-intent carve-out); a record → store-load → rank lifecycle test proving transient snippets are excluded while durable guidance survives the real pipeline; a direct-apply test proving a non-durable candidate is rejected with reason `contamination filter` and `MEMORY.md` stays untouched.
- Regression tests fail on the pre-fix filter for the intended reasons: the embedded stack frame and `refresh_token expired` snippets were previously promotable, while credential-mentioning guidance and standing rules were previously rejected.
- Real-behavior trace on an isolated state copy (never the live gateway state): `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<copy> pnpm openclaw memory promote --json` over a copy of the production recall store (512 entries plus one injected stack-trace entry) reports `invalidEntryCount: 4` — the three stored `refresh_token expired` auth-error snippets plus the injected stack frame — and ranks 33 candidates, none of them transient.
- Autoreview was skipped by explicit operator decision: the Codex review engine could not authenticate inside the isolated reviewer runtime (HTTP 401 on `api.openai.com`), so the operator accepted agent self-review for this update.


## Review follow-up (`16cf23f`)

- **Merge conflict resolved.** `main` conflicted only in `short-term-promotion.test.ts`; kept main's REM-reflection regression and this branch's added cases.
- **P1 ISO timestamps:** removed timestamp-only rejection. A timestamp now rejects only alongside diagnostic context (`failed` / `failure` / `error` / `root cause` / `exception`). `The service launched at 2026-08-05T03:00:00Z with the new collector.` is retained and covered by the record → store-load → rank lifecycle test.
- **P1 credential templates:** the assignment matcher now captures the value and skips placeholders and scheme-only instructions (`<your-key>`, `${…}`, `{{…}}`, `your-…`, `redacted`, `…`, `Authorization: Bearer`). Concrete values such as `password=hunter2secret` still reject.
- **P2 `Rule:` marker:** the trailing word boundary now applies only to word-ended alternatives, so `Rule: when exit code 1 occurs, rerun the collector` reaches the durable-intent carve-out.
- **Data compatibility:** no schema or store-shape change. This revision retains strictly more existing entries (templates, timestamped facts, `Rule:` guidance); the lifecycle regression proves a timestamped fact survives write, reopen, and rank.
- **Verification:** `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 101 passed. oxlint 0 warnings, oxfmt clean, `tsc -p extensions/memory-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean (tsgo is blocked on this host by the prebuilt `tsrs` GLIBC requirement).
- **Remaining gap:** no live CLI apply/reopen against a production-state copy in this environment; the earlier preview trace in the body still covers the changed predicate, and call-site wiring is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep marketplace discovery poll on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveMarketplaceRef` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.ts` seeds its default-marketplace discovery deadline with `Date.now()` and derives the remaining poll delay via `waitUntil - Date.now()`. The downstream `delay` → `sleepWithAbort` → `setTimeout` consumes that remaining value on the monotonic clock. A wall-clock forward jump (NTP correction, sleep resume, or manual time change) between the seed and a later read made `Date.now() >= waitUntil` true early, abandoning the default marketplace before it appeared — the install fell through to the "not found" path. A rewind stretched the total wait beyond `marketplaceDiscoveryTimeoutMs` (default 60 s), making the install feel stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveMarketplaceRef` owns this discovery budget. All four `Date.now()` calls in the poll loop (seed, native-disable guard, loop-break check, remaining calculation) now use `performance.now()`, keeping both sides on the same monotonic domain. This matches `inspectCodexComputerUse` in the same file (PR #155873) and the migration marketplace discovery fix (PR #168735), which already moved their deadlines to `performance.now()`.

## User Impact

Default Codex Computer Use marketplace discovery keeps its configured 60-second budget across wall-clock changes. A forward clock jump no longer abandons the marketplace early, and a rewind no longer stretches the wait. Users with NTP corrections or sleep/wake cycles during `/codex computer-use install` no longer see spurious "marketplace not found" results or stalled installation.

## Evidence

Verified `0c27fe6` on Linux. The source tree matches the tested candidate.

- **Three-clock behavior matrix** (`Date.now` mocked: first read normal, subsequent reads shifted by offset; `performance.now` left monotonic):

  | Wall-clock offset | Main (Date.now) delays | This head (performance.now) delays |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 0 (steady) | 1 × 2 000 ms | 1 × 2 000 ms |
  | −120 000 (rewind) | 1 × 2 000 ms, loop never exits (budget exceeded) | 1 × 2 000 ms, loop exits via match |
  | +120 000 (forward) | 0 delays — loop broke before first poll | 1 × 2 000 ms, loop exits via match |

  On main, a +120 s forward jump makes `Date.now() >= waitUntil` true immediately, so the poll loop breaks before `sleepWithAbort` is ever called (0 delays) — the default marketplace is abandoned. A −120 s rewind does not inflate the per-poll delay (`Math.min` clamps to `CURATED_MARKETPLACE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2 000`), but the loop-break condition `Date.now() >= waitUntil` can never be satisfied, so discovery waits indefinitely beyond the 60 s budget. This head keeps all three cases at a single 2 000 ms poll delay that exits via a matching `plugin/list`.

- **Tests:** `npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-marketplace-deadline.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-deadline.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex.config.ts` — 6 passed (3 new + 3 existing).

  Reverting only the production clock fix (4 `performance.now` → `Date.now`) fails the +120 000 offset case: `expected 0 to be greater than 0` (`sleepMock.mock.calls.length` is 0 because the loop broke before any poll). The steady (offset 0) and rewind (−120 000) cases pass on both main and this head because `Math.min` clamps the delay value — the rewind bug is a total-duration overrun, not a per-poll inflation.

  Per-case timings (this head): offset 0 → 70 ms, offset −120 000 → 47 ms, offset +120 000 → 26 ms. Full suite duration 29.34 s (transform 56 %, import 39 %, setup 5 %, tests 1 %).

- **What was not tested:** real NTP corrections and sleep/wake cycles are simulated via `Date.now` mocking only; `performance.now()` is left un-faked so it stays monotonic, which is the production condition being verified. The rewind-direction total-duration overrun is not asserted as a wall-clock measurement because the fake-timer harness advances by microtask draining, not by real time; the forward-direction zero-delay break is the concrete regression assertion.

prs.title: test(e2e): prove the session input lifecycle through a real Gateway
prs.body:
Stacked on #177698. The base branch `stack/pr-177698` mirrors that PR's head (`6f5fca7d891`), so this diff contains only the new tests. Retarget to `main` after #177698 lands.

## What Problem This Solves

#177698 reworks how a session admits, steers, queues, recovers and settles input. Its proof today is mostly unit tests over internals, plus captures the author ran privately. There is no committed test that drives the public Gateway surface and checks what a user would actually see: whether a correction reached the running turn, whether anything ran twice, and whether any input was left waiting.

## Why This Change Was Made

These tests drive real public RPCs (`chat.send`, `chat.abort`, `agent.wait`, `chat.history`, `device.pair.*`) and the `sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` tools, against a real Gateway. Only the model is scripted, as a loopback OpenAI Responses server. Assertions read only observable outcomes:

- what each model request received;
- which runs executed;
- the persisted transcript;
- `pendingInputs`.

They never read internal state.

- **`gateway-session-steering.e2e.test.ts`:** one out-of-process QA Gateway child for the whole suite.
  - The requester's correction joins the active run exactly once.
  - `/followup` runs as its own turn after the active run.
  - Stop on the run keeps queued work; Stop on the session cancels it visibly.
  - `sessions_send` to a busy peer: `followup` runs as a separate turn and its reply returns to the requester exactly once; `steer` joins the active run.
  - A subagent result returns to its requester in exactly one announcement.
  - A message sent during an announcement is answered exactly once.
  - A correction sent during recovery compaction reaches the same run exactly once.
- **`gateway-session-steering-people.e2e.test.ts`:** two people (Alice and Bob) signed in through a trusted proxy.
  - Bob's steering is refused without queueing and never reaches the model.
  - With collaborative steering enabled, Bob joins Alice's run and stays the author of his message.
  - After Bob's device is revoked, his queued followup is cancelled before it reaches the model.

  This file boots one in-process Gateway per test. A shared-token Gateway has a single owner identity, and the e2e setup resets in-process runtime state after every test, so these scenarios can't share an in-process Gateway.

The scripted model never sleeps. Where the runtime accepts input asynchronously, the model keeps the run working through real tool boundaries until the input actually arrives, with a hard cap. Every wait is on produced state: model requests, chat and lifecycle events, or `agent.wait`.

## User Impact

None at runtime. The steering and queue contracts in `docs/concepts/queue-steering.md` and `docs/concepts/session-tool.md` now have boundary-level regression coverage.

## Evidence

- On #177698's head (`6f5fca7d891`): 12 of 12 pass, in two consecutive runs.
  - Test time: about 34s for the main file (including about 20s of one-time Gateway startup) and about 45s for the people file (three Gateway boots).
  - Wall time including the build: 139–174s.
  - Both files exceed the 30s target because each scenario needs a real Gateway, and that is the contract under test; no cheaper layer proves cross-process admission, recovery and delivery together.
- On `main` at the PR's merge base (`bd2dbfdeb49`): **the recovery-compaction scenario fails.** The original run works through 200 boundaries and ends `Never received: Correction sent during compaction.`, so the correction was downgraded to a separate later turn. That is exactly the defect #177698 fixes. The other scenarios pass on both versions; they pin behavior #177698 must preserve.
- `oxlint` passes on the three files, and they typecheck under `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.e2e.json`.

### Findings from building these tests

- **Behavior change for review.** A message sent during a subagent announcement in a Control UI conversation runs as a separate turn on `main`; with #177698 it joins the announcement run. Control UI announcements are `result-required`, so this matches #177698's "compatible required-to-required steering", but neither version documents it. The test asserts only what must hold either way: answered once, one announcement, nothing pending.
- **Pre-existing bug, not from #177698 (reproduces on `main`).** If a Gateway restart interrupts a turn and a new message arrives before restart recovery starts (about 5 seconds), both the recovery continuation and the new message stay `queued` indefinitely. The model receives nothing for 180+ seconds, and the Gateway logs `stuck session ... reason=stale_session_state`. Without the new message, recovery runs normally. It is not included here as an expected failure; I'll track it separately.
- **Not covered:** the exact restored state behind the yielded-cohort fix in #177698 (a retired child whose owed wake was never dispatched before restart) can't be reached through public APIs. Its restore-level regressions in #177698 remain the proof.

prs.body:
Closes #178961

## What Problem This Solves

In light mode, Sharing/Public stands out as an isolated white pill, open session controls are difficult to distinguish from hover, and Subagents bot glyphs fade into heavy gray tiles.

## User Impact

Sharing/Public has a clearer surface that follows the active light palette. Details and Panels stay transparent while closed and gain a restrained background on hover or when open. Subagent icons are clearer on desktop and mobile.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scoped theme tokens separate the persistent Sharing surface from the temporary states of the two icon toggles. Control dimensions, human avatars, badges, spinner behavior, and dark-theme colors remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Real synthetic-session flows cover idle controls, open Details, open Sharing, a public session, open Panels, and Subagents. Claw and Knot light/dark captures confirm theme-aware surfaces; measured dimensions and Subagent colors are preserved in the revision, with no page errors.
- Targeted stylesheet lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. `pnpm ui:build` passes; its informational startup-JavaScript size advisory remains 321.2 KiB against 317.5 KiB.

prs.title: fix(gateway): renaming a session group takes 230 ms on a three-agent Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #167716

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: renaming a session group takes about 230 ms on a Gateway with three configured agents and ten on-disk agent stores, even when the group holds one session.

## User Impact

User impact: group rename and delete actions return promptly even when databases from retired agents remain on disk. Empty groups do not wait for unrelated session stores. Web and native clients need no changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The membership snapshot already identifies the stores that hold members of the group. Sweep only those stores instead of every store discovered on disk, including retired agents' stores.

Retirement still rereads all stores in its transaction and refuses to retire a group that has members. If a session is assigned in a skipped store while the mutation runs, it keeps the source group and the request can be retried.

## Evidence

Regression tests in `src/gateway/session-groups.test.ts`, run with the source change reverted and then enabled:

| Test | Source change reverted | With the change |
|---|---|---|
| "sweeps only the stores that hold members of the group" | `expected [ 'main', 'other' ] to deeply equal [ 'main' ]` | One sweep for the rename; none for the empty group |
| "retains a group when a member is assigned in a store the sweep skipped" | Rename resolves because the later sweep moves the late member | Rename rejects with "still has members"; the late member keeps the old group, and a retry moves it and retires the group |

Regression coverage exercises skipped unrelated stores, late assignments in skipped stores, retained source membership, and a successful retry. Category writes preserve session recency and catalog retirement retains its independent membership check.

**Timing:** fresh temporary state per variant, ten real SQLite agent stores, three configured agents, and one member in the renamed/deleted group. Each cell reports the median of three repeated requests after an initial warmup, with the observed range in parentheses.

| Operation | Main | With the change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Delete an empty group, one process with real SQLite workers | 186 ms (178–259) | 10 ms (9–10) |
| Rename a one-member group, loopback Gateway RPC | 228 ms (220–230) | 26 ms (24–73) |
| Delete an empty group, loopback Gateway RPC | 237 ms (212–244) | 16 ms (15–22) |
| Delete a one-member group, loopback Gateway RPC | 279 ms (262–314) | 21 ms (21–28) |

AI-assisted: Claude Code and Codex.

prs.title: fix: avoid false history rewrite warnings for missing tool results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes false history-rewrite warnings and strict prompt-cache assertion failures when the same missing tool result is repaired again on a later request.

## User Impact

Repeated replay keeps its prefix stable and preserves eligibility to reuse measured context usage. Recorded tool results and persisted repair timestamps remain unchanged. No configuration, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transient repair now derives a missing result's timestamp from its owning assistant message, with a stable zero for sparse legacy records. The existing sanitizer owns this choice; transport and compaction consume it. The AI package's fallback retains the owning time for delayed asynchronous calls too. Actual history mutations still trigger the existing diagnostics.

The simplification pass kept these existing owners and added no manager or cache. Production: five files +30/−16; tests: three files +101/−2.

## Evidence

- Six new regression cases failed before the fix for clock-driven timestamp drift; the persisted-creation control passed before and after.
- 137 focused cases passed, including strict observer acceptance for OpenAI Responses and Anthropic, real mutation detection, sparse legacy replay, delayed asynchronous results, transport, compaction, and tool-prefix siblings.
- Core and affected test type lanes, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 issues on the exact committed diff.
- Changed-file command costs (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, macOS):

| File | Cases | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-observability.history.test.ts` | 41 | 31.88 s |
| `src/agents/session-transcript-repair.test.ts` | 29 | 3.60 s |
| `packages/ai/src/providers/transform-messages.test.ts` | 12 | 2.80 s |

The observer command includes a 24.98 s compiler rebuild; its four new cases took 27/2/2/2 ms. Hosted CI for this head passed; it tested GitHub's PR merge revision `dbdc3821a7732660ddb0d77c61667cfc23ae38f0`. The listed wall times are local full-command measurements. These are test-command costs, not application benchmarks. Prior serializer proof remains applicable: the relevant unchanged OpenAI/Anthropic serializers omit tool-result timestamps. No live provider cache-hit improvement, changed compaction decision, or latency improvement is claimed.


## Installed Gateway proof — October 21

The requested real-entry-point replay proof passed on isolated AWS Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, using independently built and installed npm packages from the PR base `85bb6b88bde625bc04918b0579ad7e7e5cf61b27` and unchanged PR head `cbf60bb3f89757207a7149f1fbe93c56258d801a`.

The fixture seeded synthetic historical messages through the installed public SDK, including one missing `read` result and a separately recorded result. It launched each installed Gateway, waited for `/readyz`, and sent two consecutive authenticated `/v1/responses` requests to the same session with `OPENCLAW_PROMPT_CACHE_ASSERT=1`, using the live OpenAI Responses provider (`gpt-5.4-mini`). It did not replace the sanitizer, observer, request handler, or model response.

| Observation | Base | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First request | HTTP 200, completed, expected reply | HTTP 200, completed, expected reply |
| Second request after clock advancement | HTTP 500, failed | HTTP 200, completed, expected reply |
| Strict observer | `historyRewrite`: `toolResult` changed at `envelope.timestamp` | `prefixUnchanged: true`, `changes: null`; no target violations |
| Missing-result timestamp | Changes from `1792553076432` to `1792553081050` on the next request | Remains `1700000000400`, the owning assistant timestamp |
| Recorded history | Original rows unchanged after both requests; synthesized result stays transient | Same |
| Cleanup | Normal SIGTERM, exit 0, no remaining process group | Same |

The unchanged recorded result retained timestamp `1700000000200`. No new tool call was made. All 18,023 installed inventory entries in each arm remained byte-identical before/after. The baseline's normal internal attempts repeated the strict failure; the harness did not retry either operation.

[Successful paired proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c792dfe5d235ddf6b3477ab43f8288fd). Fixture SHA-256: `8ca6c4eaa63fd70cacbb6f98c947da1e7f39d4029677f1a690d2dedef7710655`. Package SHA-256: base `5f6c45ebdc76224fcef54f745806a9716751b04a01698c159b244fd212f750ef`; head `7e8d4001870492a62d619822518bca1f5cd5048bea59625cbf89626d58a652e3`. Build metadata matches the stated commits; tracked build inputs stayed clean.

An earlier fixture used `/health` instead of readiness and received the expected startup 503 before any model request. That attempt is retained as a fixture failure, not behavior evidence. This is a bounded installed-Gateway proof for OpenAI Responses on Linux, not a provider cache-hit, latency, or all-platform claim. Existing in-process Anthropic and mutation-negative-control evidence remains applicable. Associated CI run `39533524704` passed; source has not changed since it ran. Installed proof above uses the exact PR-head package, while hosted CI uses the PR merge revision. Hosted Clawsweeper re-review accepted this proof with no findings or remaining before-merge requests. No merge or auto-merge is authorized.


Hosted CI reported case-duration sums of 0.254 s for all 41 history cases (four new cases: 53/3/4/3 ms), 0.141 s for all 29 transcript-repair cases (new case: 3 ms), and 0.032 s for all 12 transform cases (new case: 5 ms). These sums exclude shared setup and are not file or job wall times. Source: run `39533524704`, jobs `119005155363`, `119005155427`, and `119005155372`, respectively.

prs.title: fix: keep SenseNova minute-window 429s from disabling auth profiles
prs.body:
Related: #148236

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: SenseNova can return HTTP 429 for a TPM/RPM throttle with `code: "insufficient_quota"` and `type: "rate_limit_error"`. OpenClaw reads the quota code in the serialized response detail as `billing`, overriding the explicit minute-window rate-limit message and temporarily disabling the auth profile across models.

## User Impact

SenseNova users who receive this specific throttle response get the existing short rate-limit handling instead of an erroneous billing disable. Actual throttling still occurs; this change does not increase provider capacity or alter retry budgets. Independent balance evidence and HTTP 402 remain billing failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message classifier recognizes `inference exceeds tpm/rpm limit` as a rate limit, but detail classification sees `insufficient_quota` in the response JSON and takes precedence. For HTTP 429 with matching structured `insufficient_quota` and `rate_limit_error` facts plus explicit TPM/RPM wording, the patch treats the quota code as ambiguous. Other billing evidence in the details still takes precedence.

## Evidence

- The observed response, reduced to non-secret error fields, was `429 {"code":"insufficient_quota","message":"inference exceeds tpm/rpm limit","type":"rate_limit_error"}`. The unmodified classifier returned `billing`; the patched classifier returns `rate_limit`.
- The new Vitest regression was red on the original classifier: the observed response returned `billing` instead of the expected `rate_limit` (1 failed, 4 controls passed). It was green with the patch (5 passed). The controls keep an earlier `429003` TPM/RPM response as `rate_limit`, and keep independent `credit balance too low` evidence and HTTP 402 as `billing`.
- Adjacent classifier and assistant-message tests passed (36 tests). The core production typecheck and the test typecheck shards covering agent-root and agent-other tests passed. Both changed files passed targeted oxfmt and oxlint checks.
- The patch passed `git apply --check --whitespace=error` against upstream `main` at `bbc5e3a7c72af083268c80d69b0e086370f2565d` on 2026-10-20. The isolated classifier check also passed.
- The full `pnpm check` graph could not complete because this source copy came from a ZIP and has no `.git` history; several preflight checks require Git. CI on a real checkout should run the complete graph before merge.

## Redacted runtime evidence

These are normalized excerpts from separate local OpenClaw 2026.10.3 events after the classifier patch was active. They contain no session/run/profile identifiers, IP addresses, API keys, phone numbers, request content, or private endpoint URLs. Relative times within each sequence are derived from Gateway JSON log timestamps.

**Observed response shape.** A post-patch assistant transcript recorded a real SenseNova `deepseek-v4-flash` response with `errorCode=insufficient_quota`, `errorType=rate_limit_error`, and `errorMessage="429 inference exceeds tpm/rpm limit"`. The Gateway log for that particular event is no longer retained, so it cannot be joined to the following cooldown sequence.

**Gateway transport and recovery sequence (separate event):**

```text
T+0.000s   sensenova/deepseek-v4-flash upstream response: HTTP 429
T+0.014s   matching run: failoverReason=rate_limit; preview contains "tpm/rpm limit"
T+0.095s   auth_profile_failure_state_updated: reason=rate_limit,
           windowType=cooldown, expires after approximately 30 seconds
T+89.833s  sensenova/deepseek-v4-flash upstream response: HTTP 200
```

The later HTTP 200 establishes that the model accepted a subsequent request; it does not prove that the original user turn recovered successfully. In another recorded 30-second `deepseek-v4-flash` rate-limit window, SenseNova `sensenova-6.8-flash-lite` returned HTTP 200 about four seconds after the cooldown began. That supports continued availability of another model, although an in-flight request cannot be ruled out from response timestamps alone. No SenseNova `billing` classification or profile-disable event was observed in the retained post-patch Gateway logs.

**Billing control and evidence limit.** The PR includes regression tests that preserve billing for HTTP 402 and independent `credit balance too low` evidence. Those are simulated controls, not a live provider billing event. No genuine post-patch billing response was present in the available logs. The retained Gateway log for the transport sequence does not include its original `errorCode`; the typed response above is a separate event. These facts should not be presented as one continuous trace.

## Reproducible local-HTTP recovery path

The new fault-sequence E2E case uses a loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP server and the real `streamSimpleOpenAICompletions` SDK transport. Its 429 response has the observed SenseNova error fields: `code=insufficient_quota`, `type=rate_limit_error`, and `message=inference exceeds tpm/rpm limit`. The test asserts that the SDK-parsed assistant message retains these fields and the response body. It then passes that parsed message into the production embedded runner, model fallback, and persisted auth-profile state owners. The model-attempt boundary is still injected; this is a local HTTP fault-injection test, not a capture from the paid SenseNova endpoint.

The correlated synthetic sequence sends ten 429 responses for `deepseek-v4-flash`, followed by HTTP 200 for `deepseek-flash` on the same profile. The recorded failover reason is `rate_limit`, the cooldown is scoped to `deepseek-v4-flash`, and `disabledUntil` is absent. A following turn obtains HTTP 200 from `deepseek-v4-flash` with that profile. The same test then sends an HTTP 402 billing control through the SDK; it retains the billing error code and sets `disabledUntil`. All endpoint addresses and credentials in the fixture are local/synthetic.

The complete local-HTTP case, including the 402 control, passed before the mechanical extraction of its server/SDK setup into `src/agents/test-helpers/sensenova-fault-transport.ts` (1 passed, 12 skipped). After extraction, the agents-root TypeScript check and targeted oxfmt/oxlint passed. The final local rerun was refused twice by OpenClaw's test-preparation safety fence because it could not verify separation from managed Gateway artifacts; no checkout artifacts were rebuilt, and the fence was not bypassed. PR CI must validate the final head.

## CI failure attribution

The prior-head [`check-prod-types` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39399534944/job/118551967490) failed in `tsgo:core` with 810 diagnostics concentrated in `src/plugin-sdk/control-ui-*` and `ui/src/*` (for example missing `HTMLElement`/`document` and JSX settings). None point to a changed PR file; this PR changes only agent classifier and test files, with no UI, plugin-sdk, or TypeScript configuration changes. The focused agents-root test typecheck passes. This evidence points away from the diff, although the exact upstream baseline has not been independently rerun.

## Upstream fixture integration

Merged current upstream `main` at `700d5ce7028487a9d4fb69505a7329dd5c66b7db` into head `a6a62ee861ba14c07a7c525ed4e8d297519be3d0`. The SenseNova HTTP recovery case now uses #178337's entry-based profile fixture, typed attempt mock, shared database drain helper, and top-level test layout. The PR remains a four-file change against current main; the fault-sequence file adds 121 lines and removes 6. Local targeted oxfmt, oxlint, and agents-root typecheck pass with the upstream fixture helper present. The focused E2E runner did not execute because OpenClaw's test-preparation guard could not verify isolation from managed Gateway artifacts; CI must validate the merged head. GitHub reports `mergeable=true`. Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39538579376) passed, and ClawSweeper's exact-head review found no actionable findings and marked the PR ready for maintainer review. The first integrated-head CI exposed a stray local tool notice prepended during the GitHub upload; commit `a6a62ee861ba14c07a7c525ed4e8d297519be3d0` removes that notice. The local source and its targeted checks were unaffected.

## Latest review and CI repair

ClawSweeper accepted the correlated local-HTTP proof on the previous head and requested removal of the unused synthetic SenseNova attempt branch. That branch is removed on the current head. The prior exact-head `check-lint` log showed format failure only for the two newly uploaded test files because the upload appended an extra trailing blank line; both files now have a single final newline. Local targeted oxfmt, oxlint, and agents-root typecheck passed. The current head's CI passed and the exact-head review found no actionable findings.

prs.title: refactor: keep private runtime phases with their consumers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal flow and runtime owners repeatedly package their own local values for helpers with only one production consumer.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change or migration. Public SDK, protocol, CLI and config contracts, lazy imports, security checks, normal concurrency, and durable session/transcript behavior stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep private phases with the caller that already owns their inputs. Fold the sole stream reducer, bundle-command loader, API-key facts and delivery callback leaves into their existing owners; localize setup, tool assembly, media, voice-event, selection and history-gap frames. Shared policy, callback and persistence owners remain shared. No replacement abstraction is introduced.

The branch removes **513 net production lines** (+1,879/-2,392), excluding tests/support/generated/declarations. Thirty-two paths change overall (+2,059/-2,566), including five removed internal leaves, an exact ten-row mock-baseline shrink and one orphan session-accessor allowance deletion. The meaningful helper tests move to the public command assembler and Discord picker-submit flow with real synthetic bundle/session inputs. The adjacent Discord lint repair explicitly preserves JavaScript code-unit ordering for legacy picker indexes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No guard or recovery policy is removed. Bundle discovery may emit a name-sanitization debug message before a later unreadable-sibling warning; warning content and returned commands are unchanged. This is diagnostic ordering during the same synchronous assembly, not a changed trust boundary or delivery outcome.

Invocation-time captures, async phases, effect authority, FIFO/dedupe, cancellation, deadlines, redaction, prompt bytes, output notices, session settlement and bounded resource protections stay. The standalone session memory backend and its supporting machinery/tests are untouched. No config/schema/protocol/dependency change.

## Evidence

Fresh independent full-branch review completed scoped-clean through P2, with final source verification and no actionable findings. Author simplification removed only private framing, retaining shared algorithms and all boundary guards.

All packets passed targeted native typechecks and formatting. The latest placement packet passed **278 tests across 11 files and seven routed shards** (474.28 s), covering Copilot attempt/session persistence, Discord picker/interaction authority, node events, images/replay and prefix stability. The final tool/history/comparator packet passed **218 tests across nine files and five routed shards** (580.98 s), including all 31 picker cases after the comparator repair. These are grouped wrapper wall times, including cold-worker preparation; not live provider/channel/device proof. Earlier committed packets passed their focused flow, transport, channel, status, bundle and refresh suites.

Local full typed-lint attempts retain eight unchanged SDK declaration-resolution diagnostics: four WhatsApp callback annotations, two Parallel config annotations and two Copilot SandboxContext annotations. The same diagnostics reproduced serially on clean main tooling checkout `1cb69ee6228d0da0bfb79b37530e1e2ff92583ae`; the determining annotations are unchanged. The new image shadowing and Discord comparator findings were repaired, and the affected owner lint checks pass. This is an investigated local limitation, not a claim that all lint passes or that any hosted failure is inherited. No cast, suppression, retry, skip or timeout was added to hide it.

Final assertion safety, mock exports, session-accessor boundary, line caps, suppression audit (14 checks), selected wrapper/eager-import closure (four checks), and runtime/static cycle checks passed, with zero cycles. The actual provider-media handoff suite also passed all four cases, covering ordering, canonical immutability, bounded sandbox abort and one aggregate video byte budget. Exact-head PR CI is the broad proof. Runtime proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG directories, nice priority and one worker; no real operator state, live channel/provider or upgrade claim.
