## What Problem This Solves

Fixes workspace HTML reports being rejected as unsupported when an agent explicitly attaches the final file to the current Control UI/Webchat conversation.

## User Impact

Users can open and download a self-contained HTML report, including a parent agent’s final revision of a child draft, as a durable attachment that survives changes to or deletion of the source file. Existing read and delivery permissions still apply; no configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The internal current-conversation send owner supplies explicit HTML publication intent. Media loading validates the bytes and the existing managed-attachment path saves the snapshot. This intent grants neither file access nor generated-file provenance. Automatic `MEDIA:` replies, external channel handling, and preview sandbox/script controls retain their existing policies. Conditional Webchat guidance directs the agent to this explicit send path.

Format validation and output-directive construction are extracted into focused modules, retaining one implementation and keeping the existing oversized modules within the line-growth rule. No new state, settings, or permission modes are introduced.

## Evidence

Hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39534093805) finished with 84 successful checks and two failed browser checks; the CI gate remains red. The dashboard `board.update` timeout is [source-attributed as unrelated to this PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178940#issuecomment-6307151562): the UI/RPC owners and active test setup are unchanged, the added HTML scenario is excluded in this job, and the original 100-file selection adds no competing workload. Its underlying UI cause remains unresolved. One full replay at the actual CI merge `3fc21e07` passed **432 tests**, three workers, exit 0; this supports the attribution without establishing a repair or reproducing the original machine/cache/scheduling. No source or timeout change was made. ClawSweeper reviewed `e6933e63` with no actionable findings.

- The actual message-tool regression failed on the untouched base with the unsupported-format error; all 15 internal-source integration cases pass with the fix.

- [Fresh exact-head production Gateway/UI build and Chromium proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178940#issuecomment-6307032489) passed: build exit 0; browser exit 0, **1 test passed** (8.034s case, 38.09s invocation). prs.title: fix(zalo): handle unsupported inbound messages with recoverable text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inbound Zalo DMs that contain a URL were arriving as `message.unsupported.received` and being **silently dropped** instead of reaching the message pipeline, so the bot never responded to messages with links (issue #175421).

Zalo keeps the sender's text on some unsupported events (for example URL link-preview cards in DMs), so the content is recoverable rather than truly unreadable.

## What This PR Does

- Routes an unsupported event that carries non-empty `text` through the normal authorized processing pipeline (`processMessageWithPipeline`), so the link/content is handled like a plain-text message instead of being dropped.
- When no text is available (e.g. a sticker or a textless card), sends an authorized inline guidance notice to the sender:
  > Sorry, I can't read that kind of Zalo message. Please resend its content as plain text.
- Skips that notice for blocked/unpaired senders (via the existing `authorizeZaloMessage`), so no fallback is sent to unauthorized parties.

### Durable-ingress correctness (addressing review)

A guidance-notice `sendMessage` failure is **not** swallowed. The handler lets it propagate to the existing ingress failure disposition, which releases/retries transient failures instead of tombstoning the event as a silent success — matching the core durable-ingress contract ("never silently complete on transient failure", `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ts`).

## Evidence

- Focused lifecycle tests in `extensions/zalo/src/monitor.unsupported.lifecycle.test-support.ts` (wired into `monitor.polling-lifecycle.test.ts`) cover: text recovery dispatched once through the authorized pipeline; the inline notice sent for a textless unsupported event; and no dispatch/notice for a blocked sender.
- Static checks pass locally on the changed files: `oxlint` (0 warnings / 0 errors), `tsc` type-check, and format (oxfmt).
- CI: the `changed-extensions-bundle` shard for the Zalo suite and the repository CI gate on this PR head.

> Honest note on live proof: a real end-to-end observation (a paired user's URL-preview DM through a live Zalo account + Gateway + agent) requires a real Zalo account and deployment that this contributor does not have available. Rather than fabricate logs or a recording, this is stated plainly; behavior is backed by the lifecycle tests above and exercised by CI. Happy to add live observations if Zalo access can be arranged.

Fixes #175421

prs.title: fix(ui): report attachment failures with a toast
prs.body:
Closes #178952

## What Problem This Solves

Rejected files and failed attachment reads or video compression leave unusable cards and inline errors in the composer; compression failures can display the same error twice.

## User Impact

Attachment failures show one short, dismissible toast at the top center. Unusable files stay out of the composer, while draft text and valid attachments remain available. Size rejection says **“File too large. Try a smaller file.”**

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission rejects oversized files before reading bytes. The attachment lifecycle removes failed reads and prepared files, releases their pending work, and reports the error once through the existing toast component. New Session retains the failed-read outcome so an earlier Send action cannot submit an incomplete prompt automatically. Accepted attachments keep their existing offer, progress, cancel, and ready states.

## Evidence

- Real file-input flows cover size rejection, read failure, and video compression failure on desktop and mobile, including preserved drafts, valid siblings, retry, toast accessibility, and top-center placement.
- The four read/compression regressions failed before the repair; both complete browser files passed afterward: **10/10**, **16.88s** including canonical bundle setup.

- Final lifecycle/read browser checks passed **4/4** (**11.96s** including bundle setup); the four fixture-adjusted unit cases passed **4/4** (**2.68s**). UI production types, the three affected test type graphs, focused lint/styles, English catalog verification, line-cap and assertion-safety checks pass.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. CI duration will be available in the attached run.

prs.title: feat: manage channel identity links in the existing Profile
prs.body:
Related: #162164 — this is the separate Profile-management slice for channel identity links.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway administrators currently have no Profile UI for explicitly associating a channel sender with a personal OpenClaw Profile.

## User Impact

A connected administrator with the negotiated `operator.admin` scope can view, add, and remove exact channel/account/sender identity links for their currently authenticated personal Profile. The Shared Gateway Owner is not a link target. A link is an administrator-entered association; it does not verify control of the external account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Profile page now exposes the Gateway's existing list/link/unlink methods. It adds no backend method, identity store, or automatic name/email matching. Failed writes preserve entered identifiers, and stale results cannot update a replaced Profile or connection. Linking does not merge people, rewrite transcript attribution, assign session ownership, or change session visibility.

## Evidence

Current head `7c37a92b89511b097ec9f278703b6122a031b8ab` repairs the controller-guard failure from CI 39530576473. The existing plain ProfileState now owns the channel-identity state and applies each delivered Gateway snapshot synchronously. The component derives its view without either createEffect call or its former Gateway subscription; its owned cleanup retires the captured presentation state. A coalesced hide/reconnect regression preserves draft-reset and correctly targeted link behavior. No controller allowance, lint suppression or authorization rule was changed.

The exact four-path candidate passed all 57 cases across five affected modules, with zero failures or skips: channel identities 12, main Profile 21, locale 1, avatar 8 and personal instructions 15. Scoped format and lint both exited 0, with no lint diagnostics. The exact native comment audit passed. One independent P0–P3 Codex/OpenAI review of the four-path diff and nine unchanged public contexts completed with no findings. Reviewer checkout commands were blocked by its sandbox, so its declared assessment is limited to the supplied diff and context, not an unrestricted repository review. Usage telemetry was incomplete.

Normal commit hooks and the nonforce contributor-branch push completed. Fork and canonical PR head were read back as `7c37a92b895`. Automatic [CI 39539097463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39539097463) is in progress; no corrected full-CI result is claimed yet. The local Windows controller-guard command stopped before analysis because its installed TypeScript did not export typescript/ast; the actual CI guard is still required, not waived. These contributor checks do not establish native personal-identity admission, final authorization before I/O, upgrade or maintainer acceptance.

### Previous revision receipts

Previous head `133951cd91452ada9459ad4e9cf48c38958f8fd3` repairs the three source blockers reported by CI 39486941285. The retired controller is replaced with a component-owned state factory using the existing `observeState` mechanism. RPC admission, drafts and request retirement remain synchronous; rendering observes their publication. Client, negotiated-admin scope, Profile and generation checks, direct Gateway event ordering, stale-result retirement and cleanup are preserved. The stale E2E import and unbound method references are removed.

The exact candidate passed all 56 cases across the five affected Profile modules: channel identities 11, main Profile 21, locale 1, avatar 8 and personal instructions 15, with zero skips. This includes the same-turn duplicate-RPC and stale-mutation reload regressions. The earlier locale failure came from two empty presentation-JSON fixtures in the isolated proof; replacing those with exact public source copies made the original locale assertions pass without changing product locale code. Scoped formatting and lint both exited 0; lint still reports the direct-subscription reactivity warning, without a suppression or exemption. The final native comment audit passed. An independent P0–P3 Codex/OpenAI review of all nine changed paths and nine unchanged public contexts completed with no findings; usage telemetry was incomplete.

Normal commit hooks and the nonforce contributor-branch push completed; fork and canonical PR head were read back as `133951cd914`. Automatic [CI 39530576473](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39530576473) completed with failure. All three UI test shards, both selected UI E2E shards, and the five core lint and test-type stripes passed. The remaining source blocker is the [Control UI controller guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39530576473/job/118998974118): the channel-identities component adds two createEffect calls against a zero-call baseline. The CI gate failure follows that check. The source correction is being prepared; no guard exemption or corrected CI result is claimed. Hosted jobs tested merge commit `13945b00be36ae4c98f5df5127ab688e36be71b8`, combining this PR head with main `05235ad0c53f1974ad1e9edd0b1dbd6dad1dd6aa`. This is not a native personal-identity admission, final authorization-before-I/O, upgrade or maintainer-acceptance claim. Earlier receipts below retain their original revisions and proof limits.

Previous head `300db65f9ae68f033caffccff63a8e84e1069bc6` integrates canonical main `15e634e42723ae988a28f03d48e087a2932d38c2` and preserves channel-identity drafts across same-target identity/readiness refreshes. The repaired candidate passed all 54 tests in the three affected Profile suites in secretless Linux isolation. Scoped formatting passed for the repaired files. Existing native comment audits found no introduced comment/suppression/workaround issue in the manual merge and draft-preservation deltas.

The independent Codex review covered the 12 changed feature paths against 13 public contexts. Its sole finding applied Solid 1's `createEffect` signature to this candidate's pinned Solid 2 rc.14. I rejected it after checking both the installed implementation and the [immutable upstream implementation](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/blob/8d23a5a13b23f8bfd5f01ceca5d2a73305d11fd7/packages/signals/src/signals.ts#L559). Solid 2 requires the compute/effect callback pair already present; the proposed one-callback rewrite would fail. The original finding is retained in the review record, not presented as a clean provider verdict. Usage telemetry was incomplete.

The ordinary merge commit and nonforce fork push completed with commit hooks intact; fork and canonical PR head were read back as `300db65`. Exact-head [CI 39486941285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39486941285) completed with 36 successful jobs, 26 skips and four failures. The logs identify unbound method references in profile-page.tsx, a stale community-invite-state import in the real-Gateway E2E test, and rejection of the retired Profile channel-identities controller pattern. The fourth failure is the aggregate gate. These contributor blockers are being repaired without suppressions or weakened checks. This is not a CI success or maintainer acceptance claim. Earlier six UI failures were attributed to the CI base, and this integration includes the upstream fixture repair; the old SDK timeout's cause remains unestablished. The local 54-test result does not establish authenticated native operation, final authorization before I/O, upgrade, or product acceptance.

Earlier head `309647c46d011a861b4cc36544ce8b46c2804e40` fixes the demonstrated `check-guards` failure in [CI 38138567400](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38138567400). Main added `worker-heap-flag.mjs`, but the duplicate scanner omitted it from its explicit targets. The one-line repair includes that file in the scan. No exclude, guard, budget or timeout was relaxed. An independent inventory of all 53,791 tracked paths found no eligible source outside the resulting targets or existing intentional excludes. This is static coverage verification, not execution of the full duplicate scanner. Isolated Codex/Astra P2 review of the complete scanner and exact heap-file context found no actionable issue. Original commit hooks passed, and the published head was read back exactly. Fresh canonical CI remains to be checked.

Its parent `72b34c5a93f82323e0ea7aef68f45331139a5e3e` normally integrates canonical main `5ed6a305669a5619ceb7bdc08936ead5f7f56408`. All nine non-root-English contributor paths are byte-identical to `396297e94e34a0bedf461dbf09932613b8927e23`; the automatically merged root English catalogue keeps the same two channel-identity type/registration additions. The merge has no conflicts and its contributor diff passes whitespace checks. A focused isolated Codex/Astra P2 review of the complete English integration delta and exact unchanged catalogue owner found no actionable issue. No new runtime or visual result is claimed.

The supported Solid bridge retains its host tag, Settings controls, negotiated-admin checks and synchronous Gateway request retirement. Domain state remains in a plain TypeScript controller. The existing channel-link tests and geometry assertions remain intact. Earlier isolated Codex/Astra P2 review found a scheduled-authority concern; the correction restores the synchronous subscription and its owned cleanup. The follow-up review completed with no actionable finding.

[CI 38109971803](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38109971803) identified a render-time signal write and two Solid/ARIA type errors. The retained correction initializes the controller in the existing post-commit effect, preserves synchronous Gateway retirement, uses literal ARIA values and reads nullable links through the Solid accessor. Its exact-source isolated P2 review completed with no actionable finding. [CI 38111092386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38111092386) finished on `396297` with a failure in shared markdown-table focus tests. The latest merge consumes the canonical focus-test correction without adding another test owner. Reviews did not execute project code; current tests, protected final effects and visual parity still require hosted verification.

The preceding main integration retains the intentionally consolidated Profile tests and moves the unique unsaved-name-draft regression into `profile-page.test.ts`. [CI 38107076864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38107076864) at `a230a565` rejected the new Lit production file and separately failed the cold New Session selected-person containment check. The Solid change addresses the demonstrated lint rejection. The containment failure's cause is not established; it is not claimed fixed or inherited. Canonical checks for the new source head are pending.

[Historical canonical CI 37258505016](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37258505016) passed at `f9081de0a2f5697e4967e049e57f4bf5779d6649`. The runtime and visual receipts below remain stamped to their actual earlier tested revisions, not the current merge head.

### Inspected pre-patch/after Profile comparison

The same synthetic personal identity and fixture were run against independently built real Gateways: [baseline 37259530484](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37259530484) at `e87ab44327c049ca6454550addb4a314048ee2fb`, and [candidate 37259532201](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37259532201) at `ae51861738ec9a3095388a3ff64ba4a2a6220095`. Both passed. Later changes through `f9081de0` were test-support repairs, not Profile production changes; this does not relabel the older runtime receipt.

| --- | --- |
| ![Baseline Profile identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dc45cbd-de36-4058-a367-876362216db2) | ![Candidate Profile identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5144751f-4be1-41f2-bd27-63413b56f340) |

The name and email are synthetic. Avatar color and asynchronously loaded agent-sidebar content differ incidentally; this is not a pixel-identical comparison. Fixture/config hashes are identical between runs. The fork-only QA harness is `2ccc4eb272367e5ff97bc361df409355649f419f`, standard Ubuntu24.04, without secrets.

### Real link persistence remains separately demonstrated

[The earlier exact-head run 37251209191](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37251209191) at `a8706622fd5df1741b2fe51db6f0aef4e20cd52b` passed actual Profile add → fresh reload → remove → fresh reload against real Gateway storage. Its inspected, visibly framed captures remain embedded below. This is separate from the pre-patch/after appearance comparison; neither relies on mocked persistence.

The UI consumes the existing Core link/unlink contract. **No stored-data schema or migration is introduced.** This is not installed-old-version upgrade proof, external-account control, automatic actor/memory projection, another person's live sign-in, or a change to Shared owner authority.

<details>
<summary>Existing persistence captures and earlier regression receipts</summary>

Historical behavior head `a8706622fd5df1741b2fe51db6f0aef4e20cd52b`.

### Actual Profile link persistence at this head

[Secretless standard-Ubuntu QA run 37251209191](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37251209191) passed the incumbent production-browser/real-Gateway Profile E2E at that exact product SHA. The workflow was pinned separately to `0914994356f4ce56342b11f0052bcfb40d20d27e`; Node24.21.0, pnpm12.5.1. Receipt: `test_exit=0`, 90 seconds; [artifact11319934937](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37251209191/artifacts/11319934937) contains the receipt and five actual PNGs.

The PR adds no stored-data format or migration; it consumes the existing Core link/unlink contract. This run is not installed-old-version migration proof. That revision's CI needed subsequent fixture/format repairs. Historical canonical CI is linked above; this narrow QA run is not proof of the current Solid head.

### Earlier persisted browser/Gateway behavior at `108cfaf`

The production browser UI at `108cfaf564b3eb5485b9ba3f88aaeeee8bc130e6` was exercised against a real task-owned Gateway. The nine recorded checks passed: initial empty list; UI link success; link persistence after reload; duplicate conflict rejection; preservation of the conflicting input; UI unlink success; unlink persistence after reload; exclusion of the Shared Gateway Owner as a UI target; and rejection of a direct attempt to link that owner.

The served candidate bundle matched SHA-256 `6f0dc35ffa69bf03039690eaee4ed05b4c8450405c0832b25e9672c8fe081465`; the retained result JSON has SHA-256 `87280f35559a09ec7c903471cb4a369d745c763c52d22545f42edbf96fd7584f`.

prs.title: improve: reduce PostgreSQL cold-start inspection loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL Gateway readiness loads SQLite-only inspection and migration code in its fresh agent-schema inspection child.

## User Impact

Reduces unnecessary cold-start loading for PostgreSQL. The inspection child, fresh reader, timeout/cancellation, admission checks, advisory locks and transaction boundaries remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load the SQLite agent/state inspection and maintenance-cache modules only on the SQLite branches. The PostgreSQL child initially loads 265 modules / 3,068,043 bytes instead of 368 / 4,697,149 bytes: 103 modules and 1,629,106 bytes removed. The production change only defers imports and accommodates asynchronous import errors within the existing response boundary. Net diff: production +1 line, tests +38 lines.

## Performance

Owner acceptance: the change deterministically loads 103 fewer modules in the PG inspection child. Over twelve interleaved qualified cells, PG median readiness improved (initial 11.600 → 11.218 s, restart 12.321 → 11.603 s) while the SQLite control stayed flat. The single-cell excursions (initial readiness-to-chat −31%, memory-tool time +20%) were matched by similar SQLite-control movement on the same box (memory-turn residual +112 ms PG vs +138 ms SQLite) and are treated as host noise.

Measurement clarification: the owner statement above is reproduced verbatim. The recorded initial-readiness-to-chat excursion was **+31.38%** (2782→3655 ms), with +5.28% in its same-round SQLite control, not −31%. PG memory-tool time increased +20.20% (232.625→279.625 ms), while its same-round SQLite tool time decreased 18.26%. The +112/+138 ms memory-turn residual changes are differences of whole-campaign medians and a distinct metric. Owner acceptance authorizes landing despite these retained adverse observations; the data alone does not prove they were caused by host noise.

Three interleaved rounds of base/candidate × PostgreSQL/SQLite on one measured 4-CPU Testbox; all 12 live cells qualified. Startup profiles cover the Gateway and workers; workload includes exact typed `startup-sidecars` retries and the real Gateway/agent/model path.

| Median metric | PG baseline → candidate | SQLite baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial readiness | 11.600 → 11.218 s | 9.322 → 9.418 s |
| Restart readiness | 12.321 → 11.603 s | 9.438 → 9.375 s |
| Restart typed retries | 24 → 24 | 8 → 8 |
| First restart refusal → accepted chat | 2.948 → 2.716 s | 2.103 → 2.169 s |
| Memory-turn residual | 3.013 → 3.125 s | 2.057 → 2.195 s |
| Memory-tool span | 232.625 → 253.125 ms | 284.750 → 215.250 ms |

Paired, SQLite-adjusted median readiness changes: −341 ms initial / −181 ms restart. The targeted CLI database-readiness phase improves in each round, with adjusted median changes of −28.3 / −172.6 ms; the entire readiness improvement is not attributed to imports. This does not fix the post-restart gate.

## Evidence

- Real Node inspection regression: red on baseline for the three unwanted modules, green on candidate (2/2); existing Bun worker sibling tests 5/5 pass.
- Build, focused lint, core/infra TSRS and format checks pass. Two independent scoped Codex reviews found no actionable P0–P2 issues; simplification retained only the import deferral and regression.
- Full local PG conformance actually ran on the candidate; six files failed with timeouts or statement cancellation. The same six-file subsets passed 21/21 on both clean baseline and candidate. These replays do not explain the broad-run failure. The owner selects final-head PR CI PostgreSQL conformance as the landing gate; classify any CI failures before landing.
- Frozen warm PG R/T/S (two complete census pairs): 11.333/37.333/46.333 → 11.500/37.500/46.500; extra candidate operation was one auth-profile read in one cell. Third-round census arms both hit the frozen harness's unretried typed startup gate and are excluded. Single-pair C64 observations: PG 5.303→5.321 turns/s, p95 13.424→13.301 s; SQLite 6.084→6.025, p95 11.145→11.396 s. No stable throughput claim.
- Live Testbox workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39531568589 (terminal cancelled during explicit lease cleanup after all product cells; complete artifacts recovered and validated).

Release-note context: PostgreSQL startup avoids loading SQLite-only schema inspection and migration modules. No config/schema/API changes.

prs.title: fix(memory): resume background reindex after foreground turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes background memory rebuilds repeatedly discarding completed indexing work when a foreground agent turn starts. A large rebuild could restart for each turn and fail to publish until activity stopped.

## User Impact

SQLite memory rebuilds now keep their private shadow index across foreground turns and resume on the next sync, including a bootstrap search. Searches continue to use the published index until the replacement is complete. The existing foreground yield points are unchanged.

Owner close, shadow errors, provider or published-identity changes, and an explicit full rebuild discard the retained work. Process restart still starts over. PostgreSQL retains its existing discard-on-yield behavior; resumption there needs a stage-backed spool rather than holding a pooled connection between syncs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The background sync returns when it yields, releasing the existing sync promise and reindex lock. The memory owner retains the shadow and completed-source cursor; it does not leave an awaited stack paused. This lets a foreground bootstrap resume the same work without a dependency cycle.

Completed session sources are skipped, and the shadow's existing memory-file hashes preserve completed memory work. Source-change notifications and targeted sync requests invalidate the affected completed entries before publication. The final publication and Forget/revision boundary remain unchanged. One backend capability preserves PostgreSQL's current lifetime contract.

Removed the discard-and-full-retry path for SQLite foreground yields and the duplicate shadow-close wrapper. The rebuild operation moves into its own owner layer so shadow lifetime is explicit. No schema, cursor table, new lock, freshness probe, or keyword-search change. Net change: production +188 lines, tests +299, docs +4; the growth is retained progress/lifecycle handling and regressions, with existing rebuild code extracted rather than duplicated.

## Evidence

- Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Subsequent changes only correct test API syntax and document deliberate method rebinding.
- Focused owner run: 43 tests passed. Final affected-consumer run: 52 passed. The final seven-case resumption suite, extension test types, and type-aware lint passed after the test declaration corrections.
- Regressions cover no repeated completed groups, bootstrap resume with a timeout guard, changed memory/session sources at first publication, normalized targeted archive requests, close during suspension, unsupported-backend discard, and provider fallback after suspension. The original resume/close behavior regressions fail on the base.
- Production types, type-aware lint, Madge, export collisions, and Knip passed (zero unused exports). T1 calls 171 → 171; deprecated-only compatibility calls 15 → 15; dialect constructs 0 → 0. `check:changed` reports three max-lines suppressions in untouched UI files; the same rule and files fail on exact base `beb97b5b7dc3` (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`). No new static findings remain.
- Initial large synthetic diagnosis: quiet 1 shadow / 0 discards / 1,251 groups / 344.801 seconds to publish; foreground turns every 60 seconds caused 8 shadows / 7 discards / 442 discarded groups / 771.371 seconds to publish. These diagnosis numbers establish the defect and are not candidate savings.

The current-main/candidate large-fixture quiet and 60-second-cadence pairs, plus one frozen-v3.1 standard warm pair, are running. Final SQL/request counts, discarded work, and time to first publication will replace this pending measurement note before landing. PostgreSQL review of the shared owner is also required before landing.

prs.title: fix(update): don't block upgrades on legacy sqlite_stat4 tables
prs.body:
Closes #178584

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` / `openclaw doctor --fix` can fail before activation with `ScopedMigrationSnapshotUnsupportedError: this SQLite runtime cannot recreate sqlite_stat4` when a pre-cutover shared database still contains an empty legacy `sqlite_stat4` table and the Node SQLite build lacks `ENABLE_STAT4`.

## User Impact

User impact: updates and Doctor repairs now complete on those installations by reusing the general Doctor full-image backup (or the updater's verified full image) instead of blocking the client-credential cutover. The live database, statistics, and backup format are unchanged; no new flag or manual step is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The general Doctor backup phase already falls back to a full image when a declared table scope is unrestorable. The fresh credential capture bypassed that selection: it always asked for a table-scoped archive including `sqlite_stat1`/`sqlite_stat4` and propagated the refusal out of the schema-migration transaction.

The full-backup owner now registers its verified image with the existing capture context when it creates, reuses, or accepts an updater snapshot. If the fresh table-scoped capture is refused as unsupported, `captureFreshDoctorMigrationTables` reuses that full image and its content generation. Every other capture error keeps its existing behavior, and the migration transaction/ordering is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and coverage</summary>

- `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup.ts`: `captureFreshDoctorMigrationTables` called `createScopedMigrationSnapshotSync` without handling `ScopedMigrationSnapshotUnsupportedError`.
- `src/infra/sqlite-migration-scoped-snapshot.ts`: the guard correctly refuses a `sqlite_stat4` scope when the runtime cannot recreate it, independent of row count (an empty table triggers it).
- `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup.ts`: the general selector already catches the same error and selects a full image.
- The fix registers the general full image (created / reused / updater-verified) in `src/infra/update-doctor-migration-attribution.ts`, carries the updater image path through `BackupSqliteSnapshotFact`, and consumes it only on the unsupported-scope path.
- Covered paths: standalone Doctor general backup, in-process updater verified snapshot, and child-Doctor general backup. A fresh capture with no full image still reports the original unsupported-scope error (the contract's supported-recovery-report branch).

</details>

## Evidence

Environment: Windows, Node `v24.20.0`, SQLite `3.53.4`, `ENABLE_STAT4=0`, pnpm `12.12.1`, branch head from `main` @ `bbc5e3a7c`.

**Red on base** (production files reverted, regression test present):

```text
FAIL src/infra/client-credential-update.test.ts > ... > falls back to the active full migration backup when legacy STAT4 cannot be recreated
Error: Failed migrating shared state database schema at <tmp>/state/openclaw.sqlite:
ScopedMigrationSnapshotUnsupportedError: Table-scoped migration backup is unsupported:
this SQLite runtime cannot recreate sqlite_stat4
 ❯ prepareDoctorDatabaseMigrations src/commands/doctor-schema-migrations.ts:66:13
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 10 skipped (11)
```

**Green with the fix**:

```text
✓ falls back to the active full migration backup when legacy STAT4 cannot be recreated
✓ reuses the updater's verified full image when legacy STAT4 cannot be recreated
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 10 skipped (12)
```

The fallback test also verifies the retained backup is a full (not `.scoped.bak`) image with `user_version=28`, the original credential token, and the empty `sqlite_stat4`; the credential receipt generation equals the full image's SHA-256.

**Full credential suite** (`client-credential-update.test.ts`): `9 passed | 3 skipped` (PostgreSQL cases skip without a test connection). `doctor-schema-migrations.test.ts`: `11 passed`.

**Backup-owner suites** (`doctor-migration-backup.test.ts`, `doctor-migration-backup.scoped.test.ts`): `22 passed`, `2 failed` only because this Windows host cannot create symlinks (`EPERM` at `fs.symlinkSync` in the pre-existing symlink-damage cases); no backup-selection assertion failed.

**Static checks**:

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json <changed files>` → 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- `oxfmt --write` on changed files and `git diff --check` → clean.

<details>
<summary>Fixture note and gap</summary>

The host has no STAT4-enabled SQLite producer (installed Python SQLite also reports `ENABLE_STAT4=0`), so the regression fixture exposes a valid empty `sqlite_stat4` catalog entry by rewriting a same-column placeholder in a closed synthetic database. The runtime guard and migration transaction are the real ones; the fixture does not mock the refusal.

Gap: the synthetic `withStateMigrationBackupForTest` harness that invokes only the fresh-capture callback, without the general Doctor backup phase, still reports the unsupported scope because no full image exists to reuse. Production Doctor/update paths always run the general backup phase first; that harness path is outside this fallback contract.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private plugin helpers expose alternate clocks, loggers, signals, and timeouts
that production never supplies. Those options leave extra normalization and
branches around a single runtime path.

## User impact

No user-visible behavior change. Existing cancellation, diagnostics, and Feishu
registration behavior remain; only private overrides without runtime callers go.

## What changed

- Codex diagnostics and lifecycle timing use their canonical clock/logger; the
  real config-controlled profiler setting remains explicit.
- QA command settlement starts with its existing SIGTERM policy, preserving
  parent SIGINT/SIGTERM forwarding, SIGKILL escalation, and cleanup verification.
- Feishu AI-agent registration uses its existing 10-second timeout. The separate
  health probe keeps its live caller-selected timeout.

This is the plugin-area split of an 84-path cleanup family, per the campaign's
area-splitting rule: 15 paths, **30 net production lines removed**, and **27 net
test lines removed**. No SDK, config, CLI, protocol, persisted data, dependencies,
or standalone session-memory backend changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Alternate private Codex clocks/loggers are no longer injectable. Whole-tree
  callers omit them; the completed lifecycle split (#108414) did not establish a
  public or in-flight contract. Existing tests use canonical clock/logger spies.
- QA cannot request SIGKILL as its initial cleanup signal. Both runtime
  constructors use SIGTERM; completed cleanup work (#120010, #170889) and real
  cancellation behavior stay. New private callers use the canonical TERM grace.
- QA's Windows adapter cannot inject an alive probe. No caller supplied one;
  its existing close, taskkill, escalation, and verification policy is unchanged.
- AI-agent registration cannot select an alternate timeout. Its only runtime
  caller supplies cancellation, not a timeout. The provider-outage fix (#112807)
  remains intact; registration still times out and reports its existing result.

## Evidence

Three targeted native TypeScript graphs passed. Focused proof: 249 Codex cases
in six files (219.91s wrapper), 32 QA cases in four files (41.37s wrapper), plus
21 unchanged Feishu probe/startup cases retained from the rebase proof. Existing
large integration fixtures and cold worker preparation dominate wall time; no
test cases, waits, retries, or timeouts were added. CI timing is pending.

The complete area diff passed independent review with no actionable P0-P2
findings. Targeted typed lint and formatting passed for all 15 paths; all 14
suppression and three wrapper-source-closure cases passed (23.60s wrapper).
Runtime value cycles: zero. Static import cycles: zero. Whitespace checks passed.
Hosted exact-head CI is the broad proof; no live provider or device claim is made.

prs.title: fix: make Daybreak independent of retiring model aliases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Daybreak workflows rely on Blue/Red aliases retiring October 28, 2026, and must retain automatic recovery through authorized Access configuration without changing the selected model or processing speed.

## User Impact

The chat menu uses segmented Access choices matching Speed and shows **Access above Effort above Speed**, but only when the active account/model/runtime explicitly advertises a Daybreak program. Unavailable options are absent; unknown or empty capabilities hide Access entirely. There are no requested/reported status or explanatory paragraphs below Access. **Use model default** clears the session override; Standard is an explicit selection. If account capabilities no longer expose Access, **Clear saved Access** remains available in the model menu. Clearing is explicit; unavailable program choices and explanatory Access paragraphs remain absent.

The advisory Doctor check reports configured retiring aliases without rewriting models or account pins. **Automatic cyber recovery retries the same model once with authorized Blue Access**, without changing the saved session selection. Exact model pins and an empty model-fallback list do not disable this configuration retry. Ordinary configured cross-model fallbacks remain separate. Review saved session overrides and scheduled jobs separately before retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the aliases retire. A replay-safe, structured cyber refusal in Standard/default mode can retry the same provider/model/runtime/account with Blue Access. Existing Blue/Red requests are not retried or downgraded, and `cyberFailover.mode=off` remains authoritative. Current account/credential/route grants are required before submission; there is no entitlement inferred from a model name, auth type, or another account. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove retired `cyberFailover.model` fields through the existing core/plugin migration owners; explicit mode/cooloff settings and ordinary primary/fallback model configuration are preserved. Program selection (`standard`, `daybreak_blue`, `daybreak_red`) remains independent of Fast/Ultrafast. Empty model configuration (`accessPrograms: {}`) leaves selection unspecified; null is invalid.

Authenticated ChatGPT model discovery supplies caller-specific program metadata. The Gateway projects it as optional `availableAccessPrograms.cyber` on each account/model/runtime choice, preserving unknown versus explicitly empty results. The existing account/catalog lifecycle owns invalidation; no new cache or state store is introduced. Saved session overrides are checked again at execution, and native Codex verifies the same client/account model catalog before its turn starts.

This OpenClaw integration supports the native Codex turn-scoped parameter with ChatGPT authentication and rejects explicit programs with native API-key authentication before submission. This is the integration’s current scope, not an upstream limitation: pinned Codex 0.162.1 rejects API-key programs when its separate feature is disabled and forwards them when enabled. **Platform API-key discovery now reads explicit caller-specific program metadata from the official Codex models endpoint, using the same selected key.** Public `/v1/models` remains the model-inventory authority; metadata cannot add an unlisted model. No model-name, plan, or approval-label inference and no billable Responses probe is used. Custom routes and header overrides cannot inherit official grants. The existing selected-account refresh now reaches the HTTP cache and publishes changed outcomes to open UI consumers. Native Codex API-key execution remains unsupported by this integration; official Platform and ChatGPT Responses endpoints remain separate. The 60-second HTTP-cache lifetime is not a polling timer or instantaneous revocation guarantee. Selected profile/key and route isolate observations; project/organization request-header overrides are ineligible for default-route grants. Missing, empty or failed metadata hides Access while ordinary inventory remains usable.

References: [Daybreak](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/daybreak), [Fast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode), [Ultrafast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode).

## Evidence

### Same-model Access-retry correction

- **Current published candidate:** `a0960ab69e583a5d828f12f42aafd2e0ca8fc4d3`, tree `e9ace570103147574b26d807d1143111b9b306b3`, identical to verified local integration `3abdc3424562348e261777a9e2f3363e627c1d9e`.

- **Original same-model correction candidate:** `9da1573ac40c849228320892e5f11d1bb1f9c617`, tree `a2c240f2377f96df063853514f50af30abf015d1`, identical to verified local head `a3950d2e16a4520c793b2c9c6db6f23c920129f2`. The earlier implementation incorrectly required a different configured model and treated model equality as already elevated. Embedded Responses now changes only `access_programs.cyber=daybreak_blue`; native Codex changes only `cyberAccessProgram=daybreakBlue`. Model/provider/runtime/account, effort, speed and saved session selection are retained.
- **Red/green:** default same-model embedded/native regressions fail on the previous implementation and pass with the correction. Focused groups pass: core/refusal/ordinary-fallback tests (164), native/transport tests (77), Doctor/config tests (48), and cron/prefix/refusal follow-up tests (23). These are grouped runs with overlap, not a unique-test total. They cover strict empty model fallbacks, already-Blue/Red, no/revoked grants, exact credential/route, explicit off, cancellation, committed-work no-replay, one escalation and real wire serialization.
- **Independent review repair:** a second semantic review found that a hook-selected model without a hook-owned fallback list could retry the pre-hook model. A real `before_model_resolve` regression reproduced that mismatch, then passed after capture moved to the finalized physical-attempt identity. Both omitted and empty hook fallback lists are covered. - The previous exact-head ClawSweeper review accepted the six public screenshots and real UI/Gateway/request proof, but found three test-integration issues. All three are repaired: exact native catalog outcomes include empty program metadata, the overflow runtime-plan fixture supplies its required transport, and isolated full-module mocks document their boundary. Hosted CI also exposed a retired ACP test-only import and an incomplete shared Custodian-history mock after upstream owner cutovers. The ACP fixture now captures the real registered public service; the history fixture returns a protocol-valid empty transcript. The new history regression fails before that fixture repair; the original 17 failing Custodian/setup/update E2E cases now pass without changed assertions or timeouts. No production behavior or compatibility guard was added for these fixture repairs.

- Real production-built UI → isolated Gateway → real `sessions.patch`/SQLite → queued admission → OpenAI plugin request-boundary E2E now covers desktop/mobile, Blue-to-Standard and Blue-to-default/null changes, both/Blue-only/unknown/unavailable choices, and stale-selection recovery. Only external catalog/Responses I/O is synthetic; this is not a production entitlement claim. This test found and now protects a first-account-selection defect: a cold private catalog must not erase the current authenticated shared observation; a published empty result still removes Access. The original run passed 7 UI E2E scenarios, 27 catalog regressions, 8 focused command/catalog tests, the full build, core/UI/source-test types and targeted type-aware lint. Counts overlap and are not additive. [Inspected before/after screenshots and full proof description](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177812#issuecomment-6281964647).

- Alias failover and empty-program regressions fail on their respective prior sources and pass with the fixes. The built isolated Doctor diagnostic reports configured references without changing configuration bytes; replacing those references clears the warning.
- Caller-specific metadata parsing, account/model/runtime/route isolation, native discovery lifetime, saved-override rejection, and native turn serialization have focused coverage. The authenticated capability parser regression fails on the prior published head.
- Actual production-built Control UI tests use **synthetic Gateway capability fixtures**, not a claim that any production account is entitled. Scenarios cover unknown, no access, Blue-only, and both programs, rendered control order, absent unavailable options, and save/reset requests.
- The supported upstream contract was personally inspected, including caller-specific `ModelAccessPrograms` and native model/list propagation. The pinned Codex 0.162.1 authentication behavior was checked directly in sibling source at `092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d`, `codex-rs/core/src/cyber_access_program.rs:37–60`: ChatGPT programs are forwarded, while API-key programs are feature-gated (disabled returns `InvalidRequest`; enabled forwards).
- The prior corrected UI/catalog source passed 163 command/runtime/UI tests, including five production-built desktop/mobile UI scenarios, plus 31 focused catalog/transport tests and the OpenAI metadata parser regression. That source also passed the full build, core/extension-test/UI typechecks, targeted lint/stylelint/format checks and five prompt-prefix stability tests. This is prior-head evidence for unchanged UI/catalog behavior, not current remote CI.
- Independent runtime verification then found that the real attempt-dispatch boundary dropped Access before the native plugin. The repair forwards the existing program value without new policy or state. Explicit Standard and Blue now reach the registered plugin callback through the real dispatcher, backend, and harness lifecycle; both regressions failed on the prior source. The repaired boundary and its command/native/transport siblings pass 99 tests, with two additional catalog isolation tests passing. The source-runtime build, core and affected agent-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass. Fresh independent review of the four-file repair is P0–P2 scoped-clean. Two existing entitlement fixtures were made type-correct without weakening assertions.
- Direct agent commands now forward saved Access choices as well as chat turns, and unsupported CLI execution rejects them before starting a model call. The shared run-parameter assembly and harness test lane were extracted into coherent siblings, reducing the oversized owners without discarding coverage. Earlier session-scope checks and Doctor repeated-registration regressions passed; those remain separate prior-head evidence, not current CI.

- The latest review repair keeps a clear-only **Clear saved Access** action in the model menu when Access is hidden, and refreshes queued preferences through the existing session patch and admission owners. Blue-to-Standard and explicit-null transitions reproduced the stale-queue defect; additional delayed-admission regressions caught and now protect the detached run snapshot. Already-admitted turns keep their original selection. Six production-built desktop/mobile UI scenarios pass, including Blue saved before a Standard-only catalog refresh and explicit clearing through `sessions.patch`.
- The final repair passes 90 focused tests across queue/admission, session lifecycle, real bundled Doctor registration, and UI controls, plus core/UI and affected test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint/format, UI i18n/controller checks, and docs link checks. Fresh full-context P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Lifecycle-repair head `64d9f4d` has the identical source tree to tested/reviewed commit `86515985`. The redundant mocked registry call-count case was removed; real repeated bundled registration remains covered. This narrow repair adds no state store, entitlement policy, or runtime transport; earlier paid runtime evidence is reused, not rerun.

- The subsequent exact-head review confirmed both lifecycle fixes and identified one documentation mismatch with pinned Codex 0.162.1. The docs, matching native comment, test name, and this body now distinguish OpenClaw’s ChatGPT-only native integration scope from upstream feature-gated API-key support. No execution logic changed. All 18 native subscription-owner tests, formatting, docs links, and `git diff --check` pass. Prior head `380b556f` has the identical tree to validated documentation commit `4454d24c`. Earlier lifecycle/UI/runtime evidence remains applicable to unchanged behavior.

</details>

### Live API evidence and remaining gaps

Four bounded direct Platform Responses requests on October 19 returned HTTP 200, completed with `OK`, and reported Blue: GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra each with priority and ultrafast. Priority normalized to `fast`; no downgrade occurred. Total usage was 64 tokens. These direct requests verify only the tested project/time, not either application runtime.

After the dispatch repair, independent application-runtime verification on `46e86fd` confirmed both GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra on the OpenClaw runtime with Platform API authentication and Ultrafast: each request completed, returned exactly `OK`, reported the intended model and `daybreak_blue`, and served the requested `ultrafast` tier. Prior Fast runtime evidence for those two models remains applicable to unchanged inputs. Four native Codex subscription requests reached the repaired entitlement guard and were rejected **before inference** because both native model catalogs advertised Standard only; no fallback or Blue success is claimed. Explicit programs with native Codex API-key authentication remain unsupported. OpenClaw subscription runtime cases remain unverified because separate token-sharing authorization was not granted. The verifier’s bounded final rerun used six chat requests and two paid calls, costing $0.059019.

Latest-stable data compatibility was rehearsed from the published `2026.10.5` package to this candidate using synthetic configuration and a session created through the real stable Gateway. Candidate Doctor migrated shared schema 20→29 and agent schema 25→31; a cold candidate Gateway returned healthy and preserved the session identity, label, pin, effort and speed. Explicit configured primary/fallback model and account-profile references, model aliases, and auth-profile order/metadata remained exact. Doctor added normal defaults/metadata; whole-file byte identity is not claimed. This covers migration and boot, not packaged replacement or installed-updater activation. The uncredentialed baseline refused an explicit session model override, so that per-session model/account-pin cell is not claimed. Earlier successful native runs dropped the requested program and are not evidence of Blue execution; the repaired-source native results are the pre-inference entitlement rejections described above. No suppression was relaxed; one obsolete mock-factory baseline entry was removed. Merge conflicts were resolved by the history-preserving refresh above; exact-head hosted CI remains a separate gate. Before/after screenshots are published in the linked proof comment through the repository-documented managed `gh --attach` route, using the verified `roboclaw-bot` identity. prs.title: fix(gateway): reclaim obsolete native captures after startup
prs.body:
Refs #158390

## What Problem This Solves

Obsolete native plugin captures created after Gateway startup can remain on disk for the lifetime of the process.

## User Impact

Long-running Gateways reclaim unreferenced native captures during hourly idle maintenance while live, installed, and retained captures stay available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repeat the existing receipt-aware, lease-protected cleanup after completed passes, preserving its busy deferral and shutdown behavior. This addresses recurring native reclamation; the broader capture-production growth reports remain open.

## Evidence

Real process proof on `464bcfe3117`, using the normal `pnpm openclaw` CLI with isolated state, workspace, temp directory, and loopback port. No injected clock, internal capture calls, source changes, or manual installed-index writes:

1. Installed three small local plugins through `plugins install --link --force --accept-capabilities`, each requiring a real native addon; started `gateway run`.
2. After initial cleanup, reloaded and reinstalled the rolling plugin with another real native addon. The previous generation remained mapped in the Gateway, but was no longer referenced by the installed index. Stable live and installed captures remained referenced.
3. A separate `plugins inspect cleanup-proof-orphan --runtime --json` process loaded a fourth native plugin, then exited. Its capture had no installed-index reference and no open owner handle (`lsof`).
4. Left the same Gateway running through the real hourly cadence. Relevant runtime log output, normalized to UTC and with paths/host details omitted:

```text
2026-10-19T04:10:56.984Z running maintenance:retained-plugin-generations
2026-10-19T04:10:57.043Z cleaned 1 retired native plugin capture(s)
2026-10-19T04:11:06.629Z CLEANUP_PROOF rolling generation=2 nativeExports=4
2026-10-19T05:10:57.011Z running maintenance:retained-plugin-generations
2026-10-19T05:10:57.059Z cleaned 1 retired native plugin capture(s)
```

Filesystem/hash observations from the actual capture paths:

```text
Before hourly repeat: live present; installed present; retained previous generation present;
                      exited-producer orphan present, unreferenced, owner handle closed.
Final observation:    live present, SHA-256 unchanged;
                      installed present, SHA-256 unchanged;
                      retained previous generation present, SHA-256 unchanged;
                      exited-producer orphan absent.
```

The filesystem watcher last observed all four captures at 05:03 UTC, then stopped polling. The final filesystem/hash observation was at 14:34 UTC, after eleven logged maintenance passes; the second pass's removal is shown by the runtime log above. Raw terminal, runtime, mapping, index, and hash evidence is retained privately. The isolated Gateway was then stopped. This CLI run covers the fixed head; the base comparison is the recorded regression below, rather than a second wall-clock CLI run.

- The real Gateway startup regression fails without recurrence and passes with it, removing a capture from an exited producer while preserving live, installed, and retained bytes across both passes.
- 149 focused tests pass across six files (140.28 s wrapper wall time). The changed startup file uses 40.31 s of test time and reuses existing Gateway boot cases.
- Production and Gateway server test projects pass typechecking; targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. All 113 reported CI checks passed on this head.
- The full local typecheck preflight hits the inherited 723-root shard budget failure, reproduced on the unmodified base with unchanged configuration. It is not reported as passing.

AI-assisted implementation with Codex; independent Claude review of the final commit.

prs.title: fix(workspace): exclude generated build caches without losing tracked inputs
prs.body:
Closes #177057

## What Problem This Solves

Workspace capture treated generated build caches under `.artifacts/build-all-cache/` and `.artifacts/build-cache-inputs/` as authored workspace content. An unreadable generated cache could block local or remote workspace capture with `EACCES`, even when source changes and ordinary `.artifacts/` reports were readable.

A blanket exclusion would also drop legitimate files tracked or admitted under those roots. This revision therefore applies the cache policy only when capture has a trusted source inventory.

## Fix

- Keep the shared workspace-path predicate as the single policy point, with build-cache exclusion enabled by an explicit trusted-input context.
- Preserve exact tracked or admitted inputs under both cache roots while excluding new generated descendants.
- Supply trusted inventories from:
  - local managed workspace source admission and its Git index;
  - remote Git capture from `requestedBaseCommit` (falling back to the worker index when the shallow copy lacks that object);
  - native-node transfer from `git ls-files --cached`;
  - managed base refresh from the selected before/after commit trees.
- Keep the prior behavior when no trusted inventory is available.
- Restore prior archive inputs without trusting newly appearing guest cache files.
- Update the workspace access documentation.

No schema changes are introduced.

## Evidence

### Base-red

On the pre-fix predicate both cache roots were selected. With mode `000` on a generated cached file:

```text
localCapture: EACCES
remoteCapture: EACCES
```

### After-fix behavior

The regressions exercise the shared predicate and shipped capture paths with authored and generated files under both roots:

```text
workspace-generated-paths.test.ts
workspace-manifest.test.ts
workspace-managed-skills.test.ts
workspace-reconcile-fs.test.ts
26 passed / 26

node-workspace-transfer-service.test.ts
12 passed / 12

github-publication-base-refresh-actions.test.ts
1 passed / 1

node-worker-workspace-manifest.test.ts
6 passed / 6

local-workspace-projection.test.ts (targeted cache/archive cases)
2 passed / 2
```

`pnpm format:check` passes across 52,683 files. `git diff --check` passes.

The native-node regression starts with tracked `.artifacts/build-all-cache/authored.txt`, generates an untracked unreadable cache output, and confirms that the authored file remains in the transfer manifest while the generated file and its directory are excluded. The base-refresh integration uses upstream tracked files under both cache roots and confirms both survive refresh.

## Operational note

This does not unconditionally exclude the two roots for older or inventory-less captures. That compatibility choice avoids changing saved workspace semantics where the producer cannot prove which cache paths were authored inputs.

## Latest repair

The worker inventory now unions the requested base tree with the current Git index, so a cache-root file staged after the accepted base remains an admitted input.

```text
workspace-generated-paths.test.ts
6 passed / 6
```

That run includes the new valid-base + newly-staged-input regression and the typed Set fixtures.

prs.title: fix(agents): first Claude CLI turn after /new counts pre-reset messages in its history note
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

After `/new` or `/reset`, the first Claude CLI turn gets a short note like `[OpenClaw: 525 earlier messages in this chat ...]`. That number counted every message from before the reset, so a cleared chat claimed hundreds of earlier messages and pointed the model at them. This change makes the note count only the current reset window (the reset's retained prefix plus everything after it), the same window the CLI hook history and model context already use.

### What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Claude CLI session-history note reports pre-reset messages as "earlier messages in this chat" on the first turn after `/new` or `/reset` (and keeps over-counting on later fresh-session turns).

### User Impact

After `/new` or `/reset`, Claude CLI sessions no longer get told that hundreds of old messages are part of the current chat. A fresh chat right after a reset gets no note; once there are post-reset turns, the note counts only those.

### Root Cause

- Before behavior (observed on a real deployment, banner text from the Claude CLI transcripts): every first turn after `/new` carried `[OpenClaw: N earlier messages in this chat from <weeks-old timestamp> ...]` with N between roughly 300 and 1,200, for every reset from 2026-10-11 through 2026-10-20, while the model context itself was correctly cleared.
- Code: `renderClaudeSessionGap` in `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts` slices `entries` from index `0` for a fresh session (`options.freshSession ? 0 : lastClaude + 1`). `entries` comes from `loadCliSessionEntries`, which returns the whole bounded active branch. A native `/new` keeps the session id and only appends a `reset` boundary entry, so the slice includes every pre-reset message.
- Regression: #168781 (`c8a4e51c679`, "preserve Claude CLI chat context across account switches") introduced the fresh-session form of this note with the `0` start. The reset-window contract it bypassed was already settled by #127530 (explicit resets clear prior context) and #132606 (reset history stays closed for bounded history consumers, including CLI lifecycle hooks). The hook reader in the same file (`loadCliMemoryEntries(..., hooks = true)` and the bounded message-tail reader) honors that window; the new note did not.

### Why This Change Was Made

`resolveResetWindowStart` finds the latest `reset` boundary and returns its retained prefix start (`firstKeptEntryId`) or the entry after the boundary. The note's start becomes that index for fresh sessions and `max(windowStart, lastClaude + 1)` for resumed ones. Compaction is deliberately not a cut: summarized turns are still earlier messages in this chat and stay readable through `sessions_history`. No other reader, prompt content, or persisted state changes.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior fixed: banner count on the first Claude CLI turn after `/new` and `/reset`.

Environment: Linux, Node 24.19, this branch and its base `e0e04dcbd84`, real SQLite transcript store in a throwaway `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, dedicated probe session key, `loadCliSessionPromptContext` called exactly as `prepare.ts` calls it for a fresh Claude CLI session (`rawTranscriptReseedReason: "auth-unknown"`, no native session id).

Steps: write 3 pre-reset exchanges (6 messages), append the reset boundary `/new` writes (then `/reset`), read the note, add one post-reset exchange, read again.

Before (base):
```
RED reset-banner regression: /new: first turn banner counted 6 pre-reset messages (want 0); /new: banner counted 8 messages after one exchange (want 2); /reset: first turn banner counted 6 pre-reset messages (want 0); /reset: banner counted 8 messages after one exchange (want 2)
```
After (this branch):
```
GREEN reset-banner: /new and /reset banners count only post-reset messages
```
Larger case (1,000 pre-reset messages, `/new`, 10 post-reset messages): base renders `[OpenClaw: 1010 earlier messages in this chat ...`, this branch renders `[OpenClaw: 10 earlier messages in this chat ...`.

Performance (same machine, same workload: 1,000 pre-reset + 10 post-reset messages, 10 warmup calls, 60 measured `loadCliSessionPromptContext` calls per run, two runs each): base p50 15.17 / 14.47 ms, p90 16.71 / 15.72 ms; this branch p50 14.30 / 14.07 / 14.87 ms, p90 17.17 / 16.40 / 17.27 ms. No measurable difference; the change adds two linear scans over already-loaded entries.

## What was not tested

- A live Gateway `/new` with a real Claude CLI turn on this branch (no test Gateway was used); the proof drives the same loader the CLI runner calls, against the real transcript store.
- The caller-owned in-memory `SessionManager` path was already reset-aware for fresh sessions (its loader applies canonical context selection); the new tests cover it but it did not fail before.

## Verification

- New `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.reset-gap.test.ts`: 5 tests (`/new` and `/reset` for durable and memory owners, plus a retained reset prefix). On the base, the 3 durable-owner tests fail (`expected '[OpenClaw: 4 earlier messages in this…' to be undefined`, `expected '[OpenClaw: 4 earlier messages …' to match /^\[OpenClaw: 2 …/`); with the fix all 5 pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/cli-runner/`: all files pass (including the existing resumed-gap, preserved-turn and prepare tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files.

prs.title: feat(backup): recover local Gateway state with PostgreSQL agents
prs.body:
Related: #178971

## What Problem This Solves

Allows a Gateway with PostgreSQL agents to recover its local identity and store pointers after replacement while its agent history remains in PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

Proposes `openclaw backup local create --output <archive> --json` and `openclaw backup local restore <archive> --json`. The private checkpoint contains the SQLite global database, its matched device/client credentials, and configured PostgreSQL anchors. It excludes PostgreSQL records, configuration, workspaces, and provider secrets managed through external SecretRefs.

Restore requires a stopped Gateway, original configured paths and fresh targets. This remains a **draft awaiting maintainer acceptance of the storage/public CLI design in #178971**; it is not an accepted upstream contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing full backups export PostgreSQL history under offline custody and restore fresh namespaces. A replacement Gateway using the same central stores instead needs its native global/client pair and original UUID/schema pointers. A global-only SQLite snapshot cannot restore that pair.

This reuses the existing updater capture/restore and client receipt owners. Native code validates the archive and configured paths, preserves anchor identities, rebinds client credentials, and regenerates host leases/socket authentication. No PostgreSQL connection is required for local capture/restore.

The archive is a per-database recovery point, not a distributed atomic snapshot. Anchors created after capture require a newer checkpoint. This does not provide namespace discovery after every local pointer is lost.

## Evidence

Qualified on this upstream-only head `9058a7845f6ff2cc3b552f1f65deec774c493159`:
- **90/90 tests passed** across eight native checkpoint, CLI, updater capture/restore, client credential restore, full-backup companion and mixed-engine suites using the supported Node wrapper (414.88 s across three shards).
- The native checkpoint round trip passed in 5.36 s: online capture with a foreign Gateway state owner, fresh-target publication, matched-client rebinding, and exact device key/global witness/PostgreSQL anchor UUID/schema preservation.
- Existing-target, forged-path and mismatched-anchor refusals passed; full-backup client credential/socket sanitization siblings passed.
- Core typecheck, targeted native lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent P0/P1 review of this branch with the unchanged custody/publication owner context found no actionable issues. That reviewer did not independently execute the tests.

The patch contains no hosting overlay and remains cleanly mergeable. The common runtime containing this same patch also passed its full guarded build; no duplicate full UI/package build was run on this branch. Broad upstream CI and real model-provider recovery are not yet qualified.

Maintainer edits, including GitHub's workflow/secrets permission for fork branches, are enabled with the contributor's approval.

prs.title: refactor: simplify plugin metadata and delivery bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins retain private bookkeeping, transport compatibility readers, and small duplicate implementations after their canonical owners are already available.

## User Impact

No intentional user-visible change, configuration change, migration, or required operator action. Authentication, authorization, delivery replay protection, ordinary shutdown settlement, and persisted data shapes remain unchanged. The standalone session memory backend is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu reuses the existing SDK metadata-cache owner and its own API-error decoder. Teams shares its existing thread-routing/visibility owners, and its send-error classifier accepts the formats actually produced by the current Connector, Graph, and private-QA transports. Plivo consumes the verification-owned request identity. IMAP stops maintaining skip counters that have no reader while retaining the warnings themselves and leaving historical state rows alone.

Net production removal: **150 lines** (+54/-204), nine production files, 16 total files including the shrink-only assertion baseline. Tests/support are counted separately (+109/-41). This is a combined residue under the campaign's 100-line floor waiver, not a LARGE PR.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- IMAP skip counters no longer accumulate. The feature introduction (#130230) has no counter consumer or human-filed counter incident; existing operator warnings, cursor/claims, sender checks, and retry behavior remain.
- Feishu concurrent cold group-name lookups share one request and one error log. The original friendly-label request (#35675, implemented by #51032) requires the label, not duplicate lookups.
- Feishu expired group-name entries remain bounded until FIFO eviction instead of triggering a global expiry sweep. Refresh retains insertion position, so heavy chat-key churn may evict a refreshed label early and cause another lookup. #51032's eviction rationale is hypothetical, with no human eviction incident found; expired names are still never returned.
- Feishu fixture clearing retires old in-flight publication. There is no production cache-clear caller or human report requiring an earlier lookup to repopulate a cleared fixture cache. Existing same-account credential-replacement cosmetic staleness remains unchanged, not newly guaranteed away.
- Feishu bot-name lookup uses the existing canonical decoder, as sender-name and Drive already do (#166902). Unsupported monkeypatched, message-less cyclic or BigInt throws can now fail its fallback serialization; the installed Lark/Axios transport throws ordinary errors with string messages, so normal provider errors retain their code classification and logs.
- Teams no longer parses string-valued HTTP statuses. The generic reader dates to the plugin migration; current Connector/Axios, Graph `ProviderHttpError`, and private QA all provide numeric status. An unsupported custom string status is now unknown and does not cause a blind replay. Numeric range checks remain.
- Teams no longer reads `retry_after_ms`, `retryAfter`, or `retry_after` aliases. Current Graph errors provide normalized `retryAfterMs`; Connector errors provide actual HTTP `Retry-After` headers. An unsupported custom 429 containing only an old alias uses the existing bounded default backoff. Header parsing, numeric delay bounds, and the 429-only replay rule from #125127 remain.
- Teams no longer projects `response.body.error.code`, added for pre-native streaming in #60771. Current Axios uses its direct transport code, Graph supplies a normalized direct code, and the native stream owner translates streaming failures itself. Unsupported body-only codes are no longer specialized; the direct-code hint remains available.
- Teams validates the outer unknown error object once at the classifier boundary, rather than again in each private projection. Private helpers have one typed caller; unsupported direct calls bypassing that owner have no public contract or human incident. The network-error classifier still receives the original error.
- Plivo's private parser no longer invents nonce/body-hash identity when called without verification. Both production callers follow the missing-verified-key rejection introduced by the existing verification contract (`1aadf26f9acc` -> `535ef8991cf1`); unsupported direct parser calls can have an undefined dedupe key, while their random event ID remains. Signature verification and replay enforcement are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused proof runs use isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, one worker, lowered CPU priority, and serial heavy commands. IMAP: 71 cases; Teams routing/visibility plus Plivo/webhook: 77 cases; Feishu group-name/SDK/broadcast owners: 24 cases; Feishu bot-name/sender-name/error owner: 30 cases. Targeted strict types and independent P0-P2 reviews passed for those cuts.

Teams error proof covers six owner/sibling suites: 109 cases passed, including messenger retry safety, proactive send, reply finalization, durable ingress, and Graph preparation. New tests use the real Connector API/Common/Axios loopback HTTP path for 403 authentication, 429 with a valid `Retry-After` header, and 504 ambiguity; all three passed before the cut. The initial fixture incorrectly used a non-RFC decimal header, which the existing parser correctly ignored; the corrected integer-header baseline passed. No live Teams message or native-stream expiry bug is claimed.

The final author pass validates the unknown error object once at the classifier boundary. Its 34-case errors/messenger replay passed; the other four suites' inputs are unchanged. Targeted strict types passed after removing an unnecessary test-injected HTTP client that exposed the SDK's nominal CommonJS/ESM type mismatch; the real API constructs the same Common/Axios owner itself, without casts or production changes.

Final independent P0-P2 review found no actionable defects. Scoped import cycles passed across 374 production modules in the four plugins (zero runtime cycles/no new static components); syntax lint, 15-file line caps, formatting/whitespace, and all 14 suppression tests passed. Check-changed classified all 15 paths in dry-run mode only. Broad suites, whole-graph types, builds, and the compiled IMAP packaged-service fixture remain exact-head CI proof under the campaign's host budget. No live channel, Gateway, or external-service proof is claimed.

### CI correction

Exact-head CI for `58c99a1f5c991efabb03fd95ef9c9dbdb7eab1bf` completed all planned leaves. Its only failed leaf was [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39535352744/job/119011015846): the deleted Feishu decoder left an obsolete two-assertion allowance. This is PR-caused, not inherited. The repair removes that unused allowance; production behavior and the previously proven source inputs are unchanged. No CI job was rerun. New exact-head CI is required for the repair.
