prs.title: feat(llm-task): process bounded batches with per-item outcomes
prs.body:
Closes #177325

## What Problem This Solves

Workflows extracting or classifying several independent inputs need bounded fan-out and per-item outcomes without rebuilding that orchestration around every `llm-task` call.

## User Impact

Callers can submit 1–20 inputs, inspect ordered results, keep successful siblings, and explicitly resubmit selected unsuccessful inputs. Existing single-input behavior is unchanged. The optional plugin remains opt-in; this adds no core tool or persistent job service.

New feature proposal: maintainer acceptance of this optional-plugin API is requested, not assumed. `maxTokens` is per item, not a batch spending limit. Cancellation may occur after usage is incurred, and outer agent cancellation may suppress the response. This is not durable recovery or a provider's offline Batch API.

## Why This Change Was Made

`batch.items` shares the existing prompt, schema, routing, and host-authorized isolated-completion path. The existing public concurrency runner limits fan-out to 1–4 (default 2). A single deadline includes queue time, and invalid batch admission fails before inference. Each started input invokes the existing completion API once; the batch scheduler adds no retries and does not change underlying runtime/provider retry policy.

Failures return stable categories rather than raw provider exceptions or rejected model output. Results distinguish successful, failed, interrupted, and never-started items. No model credentials, file access, message delivery, new config settings, dependency changes, or storage migrations are added. Documentation explains manual retry and the non-persistent response boundary.

Related, not duplicated: #137450 adds native Codex output constraints; #161344 connects embedded Lobster stages. All-state PR searches for `llm-task` batch/parallel/concurrency found no matching batch implementation.

## Evidence

- Node 24, isolated source checkout, synthetic inputs only. The plugin lane passed **34 tests across 3 files**, including existing registration and Doctor contracts. Measured run: **30.71s wall time** including worker compilation.
- Production extension typecheck, extension test-type check, targeted typed lint, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. After the final test-fixture type repair, the changed owner suite passed **24 tests in 12.85s wall time** (the other 10 plugin tests retain their unchanged-input passing evidence). Documentation audit: 15,720 internal links checked, zero broken.
- Regression scenarios: out-of-order completion with bounded concurrency; independent JSON/schema/provider failures without scheduler retry; no raw error leakage; admission rejected before any completion; completed/active/queued outcomes on cancellation and whole-batch timeout; strict-schema null placeholders preserve single-input behavior.
- Independent Codex autoreview completed for P0–P2 with **no actionable findings**. The review included the unchanged public concurrency owner; it did not execute project code or prove provider cancellation behavior.
- Previous-head (`fbd1b630`) [CI run 39254802659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39254802659) passed, including production/test types, lint, changed boundary/extension tests, source contracts, guards, docs, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The applicable dependency/security gates also passed. This is not presented as CI for the follow-up commit below; new-head CI is pending. Skipped unrelated lanes are not counted as executed.
- Additional generic prompt-prefix stability check did **not** complete: the unchanged agents-core test lane stalled after worker preparation and was terminated by its no-output watchdog (exit 143). It is not counted as passing. No timeout or assertion was weakened. PR CI remains the broader verification gate.

Implementation is intentionally limited to the existing optional plugin and two documentation files. The shared model prompt and completion-selection rules remain unchanged; the optional tool schema gains the batch argument. Maintainer edits are disabled at the author's request to avoid granting fork Actions/Secrets access; requested changes can be applied by the author.

### Deadline settlement follow-up (2026-10-21)

Follow-up head: `3b00bdbefd677053831294b62bbe4c978643bfda`. The initial live runs retained successful results and stopped queued work, but one timed run returned `completion_failed` for the slow item instead of `cancelled`. Its underlying provider/runtime failure cause was not established and is not inferred from the unit fixtures.

Investigation independently reproduced a missing batch-owner check: if completion resolves or rejects after `expiresAt` but before the timer callback executes, the old code can publish `ok` or `completion_failed` for that expired item. The fix checks the existing deadline at admission and both settlement paths, without changing the deadline, routing, credentials, provider runtime, or error-redaction policy. It keeps earlier successes and prevents queued dispatch.

- The two synthetic regressions both failed on `fbd1b630` for the intended late-result statuses (24 existing tests passed), then all **26 owner tests passed** after the repair: **15.72s wall time**, including cached worker preparation; test execution itself stayed below 5s. Existing registration/Doctor proof remains unchanged.
- Production and extension-test typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. Checks were serialized after a build-lock conflict; the rejected concurrent attempts were infrastructure failures, not counted as passing.
- Fresh canonical Codex autoreview completed **P0–P2 scoped-clean** for this two-file follow-up, with no actionable findings. It did not independently run the tests or establish the cause of the earlier live runtime error.
- The follow-up removes duplicate admission-only deadline logic in favor of one shared check; only the existing tool and its test file changed (production +10/-8 lines, tests +35).

### Live behavior proof (2026-10-21)

Head: `3b00bdbefd677053831294b62bbe4c978643bfda`. Built with the repository's `qaRuntime` build profile and launched through `pnpm openclaw gateway run`. A fresh local-only Gateway used separate config, state, and workspace, with only the optional `llm-task` tool exposed. Requests used the production authenticated `POST /tools/invoke` entry point and the existing host-authorized isolated runtime with a real model, not mocked completions. Native session discovery and additional tool capabilities were disabled. No personal notes, conversations, private source, configuration, credentials, or raw authentication logs are included in this evidence.

Ordered partial outcomes: concurrency 2, shared schema requiring `category` to be `billing` or `technical`, and three synthetic inputs. The task classified an invoice and a startup problem; an explicit negative-control input requested `{"category":7}` to exercise schema rejection. The two successful results survived their sibling's failure and all IDs remained in submission order.

```json
{"http":200,"status":"completed","results":[{"id":"request-a","status":"ok","category":"billing"},{"id":"request-b","status":"error","error":"schema_mismatch"},{"id":"request-c","status":"ok","category":"technical"}]}
{"scenario":"ordered_partial_results","passed":true}
```

Whole-batch deadline: six inputs, concurrency 1, a 10,000ms whole-batch budget. The task requested a tiny JSON object for the fast/queued inputs and a deliberately long numeric-array response for the slow input. The unchanged diagnostic assertion requires retained completed results, an interrupted active item, and at least one never-started queued item in the same run. Only categories/statuses are exported, not the generated array. The clean final-head run passed both scenarios without temporary diagnostic instrumentation:

```json
{"gatewayReady":true,"head":"3b00bdbefd677053831294b62bbe4c978643bfda","cleanSource":true,"syntheticOnly":true}
{"http":200,"status":"timed_out","results":[{"id":"fast","status":"ok","category":"billing"},{"id":"slow","status":"cancelled"},{"id":"queued-1","status":"not_started"},{"id":"queued-2","status":"not_started"},{"id":"queued-3","status":"not_started"},{"id":"queued-4","status":"not_started"}]}
{"scenario":"whole_batch_deadline","elapsedMs":10019,"passed":true}
{"cleanup":"gateway_exited"}
```

The runtime proof is deliberately limited to this tool entry point and these synthetic scenarios, not model quality, a surrounding Lobster workflow, or a provider-side billing cutoff. A response reporting cancellation does not prove that the provider incurred no usage. Failures before the deadline/caller cancellation retain the existing `completion_failed` category; expired settlements are cancelled even when the deadline timer callback has not yet run.

The separate human owner decision is still outstanding: should `batch.items`/`batch.concurrency` and these per-item outcomes be accepted in the bundled optional plugin? No bot recommendation or passing check is presented as maintainer approval.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate session input ownership and authority
prs.body:
## Latest conflict repair (2026-10-20)

Merged upstream `bd2dbfdeb4932c7cc8cefea45dee1cf4fe70a5b5` into this PR branch as `26d5d608da70226c95e584ce7c8bf875e3068761`. The single manual conflict adopts upstream #178693: pass persisted `spawnedBy` to the shared run-retention owner, which chooses child continuation authority. The obsolete caller-side native-only `independentContinuation` argument is removed; controller input custody and exact execution ownership remain.

Validation: 15 Gateway admission/send tests and all three recovered-requester child cases pass, plus core types, scoped typed lint, formatting, and fresh independent P0–P2 resolution review. The child cases use their canonical forked-process test project; an earlier generic threads-project attempt failed before agent admission because the SQLite broker is host-only. No fixture or production guard was weakened. Hosted CI must assess this new head. The combined local deployment recorded below remains the earlier candidate, rather than a claim that this latest upstream merge has also been deployed. Historical behavior captures retain their revisions and limitations.

## Local deployment checkpoint (2026-10-20)

The operator explicitly opted into a combined local deployment containing main consolidation `7605b4fc8c28a628cd4d6b9a3e63bc9f1304ce10`, reply-obligation candidate `66eea4b4ef10f196ba1640398d186884d5557cdd`, reconnect candidate `de1dfafe07c8f0762b9e5fc16d4dfc6b36a3fbeb`, and selected-requester candidate `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`, alongside existing local integrations and the separately restored saved-attempt UI work. The resulting local build is `764886a56987d82f3a3934e2dd7d6a2416ef98da`.

Operational readback confirms the exact loaded build, readiness, health, Node 24, unchanged service environment, and all 25 previously active plugins. This is a combined integration deployment, not standalone validation of each PR or security/session-owner acceptance of any extracted policy. No new business-message, native-effect, revocation or reassignment proof is inferred from operational health. The earlier isolated traces below retain their recorded revisions, scenarios and failed-collector qualifications.

## What Problem This Solves

Several bug-fix PRs address failures in the same session-input lifecycle: valid corrections queue, recovery substitutes the wrong source identity, accepted input becomes replayable, or queued completion work loses its scope before dispatch. Admission, execution, recovery and delivery have been reconstructing ownership differently.

This PR consolidates those repairs around the existing **SessionController**: capture one execution owner, authorize each incoming source independently, and give acceptance, consumption and settlement explicit outcomes. The purpose is to repair the shared lifecycle contract rather than keep patching each symptom.

## User Impact

Compatible, authorized human corrections join the active execution at the runtime's supported boundary. The execution retains its tools, workspace and model-selection policy; the new message does not replace those permissions. Recovery waits for that same operation's replacement backend, while input captured against an old attachment remains fenced.

Accepted input retains its source identity and delivery custody through confirmation uncertainty. A deadline cannot authorize replay of input already accepted by the runtime. Canceled completion work cannot reserve the mailbox ahead of new input.

Ordinary peer messages, returned results and explicit `followup` retain their existing separate-turn scheduling and correlated replies. Existing narrow child/run-scoped exceptions retain their checks. No schema, dependency, configuration option or native Codex fork is introduced.

## Ownership Contracts

1. **One captured execution.** Preparation and delivery address the same operation and backend attachment; they cannot silently target a successor.
2. **Independent source and target validity.** An ended target can allow followup by a still-authorized sender; revocation of the sender cannot authorize replay. Recovery preserves the original source identity.
3. **Explicit custody outcomes.** Rejection, failed source authority, acceptance and unconfirmed consumption stay distinct. Accepted input is held until its owning delivery path settles.
4. **Accepted completion scope.** Bind the existing one-use requester grant to the exact accepted run before ACK, reuse that binding at dispatch, and release it through joined cleanup. Restore reserves only still-owed work and filters retired wakes.

The fourth item repairs an acceptance-to-dispatch gap in the existing accepted-continuation contract; it does not introduce general requester re-entry after a turn. Upstream [#162299](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162299) already retains accepted replies independently of the original invocation. This PR preserves revocation, session/reset, run ownership and Gateway lifetime checks.

Host admission and receipt contracts are shared across bundled adapters; each runtime keeps its own supported delivery boundary. Released external harnesses retain their question contract. Human attribution alone cannot answer another requester's pending question. Types prevent some invalid combinations, while temporal changes still require checks at their effect boundary.

## Policy Split

The consolidation no longer bundles these proposals:

| Deferred behavior | Focused follow-up |
| --- | --- |
| Accept a required human message into optional work and strengthen that execution's reply obligation | [#176245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176245) |
| Share verified cross-socket reconnect comparison identity, while keeping independently revocable sources | [#176972](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176972) |
| Restore a personal-tool requester selection while delivering a returned peer result | [#178750](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178750) (draft; full-flow/final-effect proof and owner decision remain open) |

The associated production machinery and feature-only positive tests are extracted together, with exact add-back patches retained. No dormant promotion flag, accounting owner or requester-reentry path remains in this PR. The neutral reply types remain a type-only leaf for the shared contracts.

**Current recommendation:** land the lifecycle consolidation separately from those behavior choices. A required human message against an optional owner retains followup custody, without injecting or promoting that owner. Compatible required-to-required human steering still works. Ordinary peers remain separate turns; adopting Codex's native peer mailbox requires a supported app-server API, not relabeling peers as human input.

Codex's [native mailbox loop](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2869-L2937) and [human steer operation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L311-L340) have distinct boundaries. OpenClaw uses supported human steering without forcing Stop/restart or an earlier interruption point. [#160842's narrow peer exception](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842#issuecomment-5882083686) is retained.

Security-owner review remains required for the authority-sensitive consolidation. Extracting the policy proposals does not claim approval, waive review, or turn historical evidence into exact-head proof.

## Relationship to Earlier PRs

| PR | Relationship |
| --- | --- |
| #174967 | Includes original source identity, native child/result handoff and ACK/custody repairs; excludes broader busy-peer/followup scheduling. |
| #175763 | Consolidates frozen execution capability and current-caller projection through the actual fallback producer. |
| #175810 | Inherits upstream's accepted native terminal-expectation publication and retains related regressions. |
| #176245 | Includes transcript ordering and separate pending-question permission; **does not replace its optional-work reply-promotion proposal**. |
| #176972 | **Separate follow-up**; verified reconnect cohort sharing is no longer included. |
| #177618 / #177661 | Includes pre-ACK run-scope custody, cleanup and canceled-wake/direct-error repairs; personal-tool requester re-entry is excluded. |

This is a consolidated alternative for the included fixes, not a prerequisite-only foundation. Already merged fixes are inherited. Open originals remain available for maintainer choice. Related #175845, #176086, #176087, #174900, #176311 and #177414 are adjacent recovery/native contracts checked for compatibility, not claimed as superseded.

## Evidence

### Current conflict integration at `7605b4fc8c28a628cd4d6b9a3e63bc9f1304ce10`

Merged upstream `c909114f55fc5889076bf4fbbb61f6ab32bf8146` to resolve the newly reported conflict. The only conflict is in the native completion contention regression: both parents release the held retirement write before readiness; the resolution adopts upstream's single readiness wait before joining retirement, preserving the receipt assertions and cleanup. The resolved file exactly matches incoming upstream. No manual production edit or extracted policy addition is introduced.

**All 22 tests in the two affected native completion suites pass** (94.37s canonical wrapper wall time, including 37.19s worker preparation). Core production and extension-test types, formatting and whitespace checks pass. A fresh independent P0–P2 review of the manual resolution against Git's automatic-merge snapshot reports `scoped-clean`; it is not a new review of every imported upstream change.

Existing native/runtime/compaction/upgrade evidence remains at its stated revisions. No new runtime capture or deployment is claimed for this test-only conflict resolution. Current hosted CI and exact-head security-owner approval remain separate gates; the latest completed contributor review had no findings or further proof asks.


### Conflict integration at `d7cfd0a504836854e7563e94f975f3069629865d`

Merged upstream `f629720edbb9f4b458adae30c7506c1dc5d1adc6` to resolve GitHub's reported conflict. The sole manual resolution combines upstream [#178694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178694)'s parent-first recovery with the consolidation's retired-obligation and frozen-cohort checks. Recovery preparation runs before the final live-cohort check, so a retired or replaced row cannot borrow the pre-await representative. No extracted reply-promotion, reconnect-comparison or personal-requester policy was reintroduced.

**60 affected tests pass:** 55 recovery-priority, mailbox, requester-settle and source-ownership cases across four files, plus all five Codex handoff/cancellation cases in the automatically merged test file. The upstream eight-child orphan recovery regression and existing mixed/retired-cohort controls are retained. Core production types, the owning agent-session test type graph, scoped typed lint, formatting and ordinary commit hooks pass. Wrapper wall times are 65.56s and 27.18s, respectively; most of that is worker/import preparation.

A fresh independent P0–P2 review of the single manual resolution reports `scoped-clean`. That review compares the resolved source to Git's automatic-merge snapshot with both parents supplied; it does not claim to re-review every imported upstream change. Earlier runtime, compaction and upgrade captures retain their original revisions and limitations. No new runtime build, native trace or operator deployment is claimed for this merge.

The previous **PR context and evidence** failure was caused by this body's renamed `Current Validation` heading. Restoring the required authored **Evidence** section passes the same production body-policy evaluator locally. The two failed status contexts both reported that a maintainer must approve the current revision; canceled jobs are not test failures. New-head hosted CI and security-owner acceptance remain gates.

### Policy-split validation at `d383dd4e9bb180d5dd880f21029ac7d586052130`

Narrowed head: `d383dd4e9bb180d5dd880f21029ac7d586052130`, based on the previously reviewed `5d74c50003122fe40da34b36eac16e838e5857d3` over upstream `1429fd5487b508d59b0466fb83a9618c8022f162`.

- The split changes 29 files, with 197 additions and 2,229 deletions relative to the earlier proposal. Feature-only code and positive tests remain recoverable from its published parent and exact add-back patches. The complete narrowed PR remains 161 changed files, 7,423 additions and 1,700 deletions against the integrated upstream base; this is still a substantial consolidation.
- **269 focused tests pass across 16 files**, covering compatible human admission, strict optional-owner fallback, exact handoff, recovery readiness, pending-question contracts, accepted confirmation custody, requester automation scopes, device revocation and authenticated dispatch. After moving the unchanged advisory into the existing backend-resolution module to satisfy the line limit, all four affected controller/control-owner files pass again. The public import is preserved; no limit or assertion was weakened.
- Core production types, all five affected test type graphs, scoped typed lint, formatting, whitespace and ordinary commit hooks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete split reports `scoped-clean`. The final export-order adjustment is mechanical. Test wrapper wall time: 142.67s core cohort and 126.96s Gateway cohort, run concurrently; each includes about 46s worker compilation. Exact-head CI timing is not yet claimed.
- The exact committed runtime build succeeds (97s). It retains the startup-JS advisory: 318.6 KiB against 317.5 KiB; no budget was changed.
- **Fresh exact-head isolated Gateway proof:** a scripted HTTP provider holds the genuine recovery-compaction summary. One human message is sent while it is held. After release, the original execution consumes that input in exactly one provider request and returns its reply; canonical history contains one human row and the stored queue is empty. Compaction start precedes release and completed end follows it, with one persisted compaction. Gateway exits zero; observer, proxy, provider and bus join normally; temporary state is removed, with no timeout or forced kill. All 20,035 frozen source/generated/fixture inputs are independently rechecked unchanged.

This is synthetic production-boundary proof using the built-in OpenClaw runtime and scripted external HTTP inference, not a new real-model or native Codex capture. The first collector attempt failed temporary-path canonicalization before starting the Gateway; the launcher was corrected to resolve the macOS alias, without changing product code or an authority guard. The passing run retains its QA-bootstrap busy-WAL warning as a qualification. No raw credentials, private endpoints, identities or user content are published. Earlier native and upgrade captures remain qualified below. No operator deployment was performed.

## Earlier Revision-Qualified Evidence

The following captures retain their original revision, scenario and failure qualifications. Captures of optional promotion or cross-socket comparison support the extracted follow-ups, **not behavior implemented by this narrowed head**. Historical native traces have not been relabeled as a fresh execution of the split. Accepted-work scope and compaction traces remain bounded evidence for their named owners and revisions.

<details>
<summary>Recorded runtime, upgrade, recovery and CI evidence</summary>


### Conflict integration at `5d74c500031`

Merged upstream `1429fd5487b508d59b0466fb83a9618c8022f162`. The sole manual conflict was upstream's test reorganization in `agent-runner-core.test.ts`; the resolution retains the shared error helper, per-test cleanup and existing cases, plus the claim-change error assertion. Fresh independent source review found no P0–P2 issue. The separate saved-history/outbox UI fix is excluded.

This integration also inherits [#178645](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178645), which supplies explicit native-touch timestamps independently of CDP round-trip latency. The unchanged widget distance, inertia, direction and reader-preservation assertions pass in the focused Chromium run: text 475px total / 240px inertia; widget 474px total / 239px inertia. This macOS run validates integration; it does not establish the cause of the earlier Linux 235px sample.

The affected Bun runs pass all 9 error-handling tests and 21 embedded-maintenance tests, including unlimited maintenance. The original [Linux maintenance failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39476807469/job/118817984566) remains unexplained; no production change or assertion weakening is claimed to fix it. Fresh hosted CI remains required. Earlier native/authority evidence retains its recorded revisions and limitations. No live Gateway or business session was changed or restarted.

### Recovery-compaction follow-up at `24bb99cfcf9`

A human message arriving during recovery compaction could be permanently downgraded to a followup: the same logical operation survived, but its detached backend left an already-resolved readiness promise behind. New input now waits for that exact operation’s next backend. Previously captured attachments remain fenced; Stop, cancellation, finalization, yield, and owner replacement still release or reject waiting input.

Recovery also now publishes its own compaction lifecycle, independently of optional hook text. Hidden runs deliver start/end through the existing authorized session subscription. Hook notices do not duplicate lifecycle/accounting or clear the UI status timer, and optional lifecycle-progress callbacks cannot block compaction.

Validation:
- The old producer fails the human-admission regression. The old Gateway transport fails all three positive compaction-delivery assertions; the three exclusion controls pass. Empty-notice recovery and UI notice-timer regressions also fail before their fixes.
- 174 focused tests pass across the affected owner/sibling suites. The affected controller/steering suites were rerun after the final lifecycle cleanup; 50 Gateway tests passed after extracting event selection into its existing admission module. Core/UI production types, typed lint, formatting, commit hooks, and the runtime/private-QA build pass. The existing startup-JS size advisory remains.
- A real isolated Gateway running the built-in OpenClaw runtime received a scripted HTTP context-overflow response and held its actual summary request. A human message was submitted once while compaction was held. After release, one human-bearing provider request and the human’s reply occurred on the original execution; the canonical human row appeared once and the server pending-input queue was empty. Compaction start preceded release and successful end followed it; compaction was accounted once. The observer, Gateway, provider, proxy, and bus joined normally, with Gateway exit code zero and no forced containment.

All proof inputs and message content were synthetic. This is an actual Gateway/controller/compaction flow with a scripted external Responses provider, not real-model inference or a reproduction of the private live session. Raw captures remain private. The first collector attempt failed its temporary-path canonicalization guard before Gateway startup; it is preserved as setup-only evidence. Earlier native/Muse captures retain their recorded revisions and scenario scope; this change does not claim a fresh native-runtime capture or resolve maintainer/security-owner decisions.

At that earlier checkpoint, this revision had not yet been deployed to the operator Gateway.

### Prior integration and CI diagnosis (`186be068940`)

[Exact CI diagnosis and validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698#issuecomment-6297643331): the six red indicators on the earlier `0f784…` head represent three test failures, the aggregate gate twice, and a security-approval status. Those failures predate the Muse proof publication. That recorded integration merges upstream `e5302ee39c5`, resolves the metadata conflict while retaining the read-only exact-session projection, and adopts upstream #178578's touch-emulator repair. Validation: 91 UI tests, 4 Chromium browser cases against the mocked Gateway, 21 maintenance and 12 Session Share tests under Bun, core/UI types, scoped lint/format and the canonical build pass. The build's startup-JS gzip advisory remains; no budget changed. The two original Linux backend failures remain unexplained; local passes are not claimed as a fix. New-head hosted CI and owner decisions remain gates. Native/Muse captures retain their recorded revisions and source-reuse qualifications.


### Muse Gateway stream proof (executed at `0f784…`)

The [requested Gateway trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698#issuecomment-6297282981) now runs **`0f78424994631408fbeed838bb7df25991d7ba40`** through authenticated chat RPC, the production Muse harness, official SDK **1.4.4**, and a scripted external MSP subprocess. A genuine prefix frame arrives before the native command ACK; the collector requires the client-visible prefix **before releasing the suffix**, so saved-final correction cannot satisfy the live-stream check. Actual wire deltas are `["started:", " hello"]`, matching exactly one saved `started: hello` in two canonical history readbacks. Completion is normal, with no native interrupt; the QA Gateway stops and both external hosts have exit0 receipts and absent PIDs. An independent raw audit passes 91 checks.

This is a synthetic external-MSP Gateway capture, not an official Muse CLI/Meta-inference claim. The linked evidence preserves the first failed collector assertion, the history audit's volatile-timestamp correction, the later empty chat reset, and the unclassified QA-bootstrap checkpoint warning. All outgoing trace fields are whitelisted; no private raw capture is published. Earlier revision-qualified proof and security/session-owner decisions retain their stated scope.


Recorded pre-recovery source: `0f78424994631408fbeed838bb7df25991d7ba40`, integrating upstream `5a0b5006d5fcb72f238c3c587395bf38591971ad`. The sole new conflict adopts the title resolver already merged in [#178510](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178510) verbatim; the transcript-metadata guard remains unchanged. Recorded c3 source: `c3efd0744574c6920dda4af1066b6d6058053a54`, after conflict integration `eb409c37a0189c6842cb86d0dc05b1096ed44fc8` over upstream `da0c2649a1cf94ae3facf061af791cab71c9d157`, including the UI metadata and Muse repairs below. The sole manual conflict adopts upstream's narrowed two-argument local mutation wrapper while preserving both accepted-input custody guards. The earlier three-conflict integration `48e86662660` remains intact: unconditional source-bound preparation, separate source/target validity, and the reply-expectation, owed-wake and mixed-cohort regressions are retained.

At the recorded `48e86662660` integration, **110 steering/mailbox tests across six files, seven UI metadata tests and all three cold-load browser tests pass**, together with core/UI production types, scoped typed lint/format, whitespace and independent review of the three applied resolutions. The title repair has a red-to-green regression: a current exact-session descriptor supplies the title when the bounded shared roster omits the session; deletion still clears it. The [original failing CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39426287216/job/118640655534) reported the same missing-title symptom. Its exact ordering was not captured, so the passing replay is not claimed to establish that ordering or prove a base failure. No assertion, timeout or retry was weakened.

The exceptional queued-authority captures below remain executions of `e44f11ece93e98d89ca46d03e3dee67052e82ac0`. At recorded head `0f784249946`, all **44 source pins** in that fixture were byte-identical; this was source-qualified reuse, not a fresh runtime execution of that merged binary. The recovery follow-up changes affected owners, so it does not extend that whole pin-equivalence claim to `24bb99cfcf9`. Other native/upgrade captures retain their recorded revisions and limitations. Hosted CI is a separate landing gate; consult Checks for its current result. At that earlier checkpoint, this head had not yet been deployed locally.

The [subsequent Muse CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39441274850/job/118693019746) is repaired in `291018c6442fd8a0513fc6023ac22e850c8ee50c`. The SDK's delta iterator is live-only: attaching after the first chunk made the adapter interpret a suffix as the full prefix, corrupting live output while the saved final remained correct. The adapter now reads cumulative fields from the SDK's existing fold and removes its competing text accumulator. A real SDK Session/Turn regression reproduces the exact corrupted output before the fix, with a completed-before-attachment control. All **53 Muse harness/event tests pass under the pinned Bun runtime**, including the CLI transport lifecycle case; extension production types, scoped typed lint/format, whitespace and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. The later lint-only brace correction changes no test behavior.

The inspected Muse producer, lifecycle fixture, package dependency and shared event emitters are unchanged between the CI-tested base `d1b8bccb9d5e273a17e9c76a1c38ab891e180623` and `48e86662660`. This is source-attributed inherited code with an exact deterministic adapter reproduction, not a whole-base runtime reproduction. Automated main classification remains unknown because no matching main job was available. No retry, timeout, expected text or failure assertion was weakened. Hosted CI on the new head is still a separate gate.

The [later cold-load UI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39444094527/job/118703392128) reports missing completed-work duration while title, reply metadata and progress pass. The transcript owner suppressed cached metadata after observing a descriptor, but supplied no descriptor metadata when the bounded shared roster omitted the selected session. The repair projects only the existing read-only transcript fields from a current descriptor matching the displayed transcript incarnation; selected-session permissions, fresh-row precedence, snapshot ownership and observed-absence handling remain unchanged. A real-capability startup → bounded-list regression fails on the preceding producer and passes after repair, with different-incarnation and deletion controls. **44 focused UI tests and all three unchanged cold-load browser tests pass**, together with UI production types, scoped typed lint/format, whitespace and fresh independent P0–P2 review. These synthetic local checks do not establish the exact ordering on the failed Linux CI run. No browser assertion, deadline or retry changed.

Native 0.163.0 explicitly overrides manifest 0.162.1 for these synthetic/local-inference captures. Cancellation is recorded before effect-gate release, so this does not isolate the final cron commit guard. The failed inner-observer attempt instead retained pending custody; its cleanup-time mutation and lack of normal-final proof remain explicit. No authority, guard or delivery outcome was replaced, and no record was manually deleted. Profile/model-policy changes and the separate completion-handoff policy after retirement are outside these captures. Security-owner acceptance remains required.

</details>


</details>

## Remaining Work Before Merge

- Security/session-owner review of the retained authority and accepted-custody contracts. The extracted reply-promotion, reconnect-comparison and personal-requester-reentry proposals are separate decisions.
- Exact-head hosted CI and mergeability. Earlier local passes do not resolve the recorded unexplained Linux failures.
- Keep stored-data compatibility and native/queued final-effect evidence qualified to their recorded source owners, revisions and scenarios. No unobserved final-effect, populated-credential, protected-recovery or live-deployment claim is inferred.

No operator Gateway or business session was restarted or changed for this split.

prs.title: fix(copilot): setup verification fails for SDK-backed agents
prs.body:
Related: #163406

Original contribution: @lifuyue.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e73ea8c2-4672-4a46-a44c-b48bce38ec86)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/cee54e40-f6ec-4f50-b1cd-8c62a7ef2837)

- [CI repair implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6b8cb839-bf7a-4f41-a4b5-8aa9786f42d7)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes setup verification and Ask OpenClaw turns failing when a Copilot SDK agent uses a caller-owned, in-memory session.

## User Impact

An explicitly selected Copilot model can complete setup activation and answer an Ask OpenClaw turn. Persistent sessions retain their exact-target checks. No migration or credential change is required.

Verified setup requires the packaged stdio runtime; custom external executables and in-process transport are unsupported. Restart OpenClaw and repeat verification after replacing the SDK. Automatic model-alias matching remains a separate limitation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The journal uses the caller's in-memory transcript, and system-agent callers supply the existing user-turn recorder. The Copilot harness binds verified inference to the installed SDK and packaged executable using the existing runtime-artifact contract.

The repair preserves fingerprint encoding, startup validation, verified-client isolation, and atomic tool-group writes while adapting the contributor fix to current transcript and SDK contracts.

## Evidence

### Fallback SDK fixture repair (October 21)

Commit `1cf870da4faa59922415818eacb48b5fadf4c35e` (tree `58fbc0105a75171f0835fd818eb8e1c5176a5f5e`) is a direct descendant of integrated `ece9372`. It addresses the P2 in review [5954878618](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163578#issuecomment-5954878618) and exact-head CI job [119008688905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39534582158/job/119008688905). The fallback test manifest now names `@github/copilot-sdk`, allowing the real loader to locate and fingerprint the synthetic package root. Only fixture data changed (+4/-1 after formatting); production identity validation, fallback assertion, mocks, caching logic, SDK version, compiler policy and baselines are unchanged.

**Red/green owner proof:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/copilot/src/sdk-loader.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reproduces the published parent failure before editing: **1 failed / 3 passed**, `Could not locate the installed Copilot SDK package`, exit 1 (1.64 s Vitest / 5.85 s wrapper). The repaired tree passes **4/4**, exit 0 (895 ms Vitest / 2.12 s wrapper; fallback-import case 104 ms). The suite covers fallback import, actionable errors, successful-load caching and failed-load recovery. Targeted oxlint reports 0 warnings/errors; one-file formatting, narrow typecheck with the real import graph, diff check and normal commit hook pass.

[Secretless AWS red/green and static proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_8383d5ebcb31f9c51454ff90f94c4526), exit 0. The task lease release was confirmed after SSH cleanup warnings; no active task process or lease remained. This mechanical fixture-data correction did not receive a new independent full-PR review, and no settled 22/80/143-test or conflict proof was replayed.

**Exact-head CI and review follow-through:** [CI run 39536603445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39536603445) completed successfully on `1cf870da4faa59922415818eacb48b5fadf4c35e`; all 79 planned jobs are complete, with no failed jobs. The [aggregate gate and applicable security reviews](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39537371018) report success. Fresh [review revision 8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163578#issuecomment-5954878618) confirms the fallback-fixture P2 is resolved and reports **Findings: None**. Its sole remaining before-merge item is authenticated SDK 1.0.20 setup verification followed by an Ask reply; CI does not supply that proof. Earlier failed heads/runs remain failed historical evidence.

**Remaining qualification:** authenticated setup verification and an Ask reply using SDK **1.0.20** are still unapproved and unproven. No credentials or live inference were used. The failed `ece9372` CI result remains historical and is not represented as a passing run; new-head CI and the fresh review must be assessed on `1cf870d`.


### Main-conflict repair and scoped qualification (October 21)

Merge commit `ece937200d2b284426ad9dcb9b652155a010efb9` (tree `3e53d523ce805c1f8ca9fb5f366e58124a658d6a`) preserves published `78b4ecdae2cf1b8931fe10f0fa50c67d1a89efe8` as first parent and integrates pinned main `e0e04dcbd84908f148eec50165d4a96ca99cc973` as second parent. Original contributor and previous repair commits remain ancestors; no branch history was rewritten.

The single merge conflict was in `extensions/copilot/src/attempt-session.integration.test.ts` after main’s test consolidation. The resolution keeps main’s namespace imports, shared `makeParams`, transaction tests, and failure/retry/resume/finalization case, and migrates the existing detached-memory success and exact-durable-target rejection regressions. No duplicate runtime helper or retired fixture was restored; no production, dependency, compiler, or baseline change was manually added for conflict resolution. SDK **1.0.20** is inherited unchanged from pinned main.

**Changed-input proof:** secretless AWS ran the resolved integration test and `src/system-agent/agent-turn.test.ts`: **22 tests passed** (5 Copilot cases + 17 system-agent cases; wrapper **88.18 s**). Targeted lint reported 0 warnings/errors. Formatting initially found one assertion-wrapping issue; canonical formatting corrected it. Final-tree formatting, narrow typecheck, diff check and normal merge-commit hook passed. The 22-test/lint proof is reused across that formatting-only change; older 80/143-test results below remain historical, not a new integrated-head full-suite claim.

- [Behavior and lint run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_8dda590bd7e7c548c162bc84a53f941c): tests/lint pass; final formatting check failed on the subsequently corrected wrapping.
- [Final formatting, types and commit](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fae022d85a9bc3cf3f86d4d809ed0de1): exit 0, final tree verified.
- Fresh complete-context independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues in the **one-file manual resolution against pinned main**, before formatting-only wrapping. It was not a fresh review of every inherited file.
- Task processes finished and AWS lease release was confirmed. Existing candidate/trusted-main worktrees were preserved.

**Still outstanding:** authenticated setup verification and an Ask reply on the current inherited SDK **1.0.20**. No credentials or live inference were used. Prior failed CI run `39398592176` and its 809-diagnostic attribution belong to `78b4`; they are not CI qualification of `ece9372`. New-head CI and review must be assessed separately.


### Exact-head CI repair (2026-10-20)

The failed CI at `9d630935e55c` exposed a real setup/Ask regression: the targetless system-agent recorder advertised durable-only prompt-projection operations. Commit `78b4ecdae2cf1b8931fe10f0fa50c67d1a89efe8` removes only those optional operations from this ephemeral recorder, preserving its original identity and lifecycle, Copilot integration, and all generic durable admission guards. The runtime uses its existing in-memory projection path.

Replaced the two mocked-runner prompt-copy cases with a regression through the real embedded LLM projection boundary. The Copilot runtime-artifact mock now preserves actual exports; no isolation exemption or baseline allowance was added.

**Evidence:** Secretless AWS reproduced Groq activation failing before any provider request and the mock-export ratchet failure on the published head. The new projection-boundary regression failed on that head and passes on the repair. All 80 focused tests across 10 files pass, including Groq activation, all four failing guided-onboarding cases, custom-provider setup, prefix stability, Copilot detached/durable transcript paths, and runtime-pool behavior. The final one-line lint spelling correction reran its affected regression plus four-file lint/format, narrow typecheck, and diff check; all pass. Unchanged behavior proof is reused explicitly. Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues.

- [Production-composition red/green proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0acc92194baaef7e87719168429c3f05): tree `5a88929fc32130713aa7869fb02bd619d0d93ca3`; all 80 tests pass; final lint found the subsequently repaired test-property spelling.
- [Final affected proof and normal commit](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5e3151b51e3a9b8f62c0e105fec67b09): tree `96c3bb9f6f36e05b2e268188bd74966357a3c99b`, exit 0. New test body: 19 ms; wrapper: 37.75 s. Full focused selection including required E2E build: 493.18 s.

**Remaining proof gap:** Current Copilot SDK 1.0.19 authenticated setup verification and Ask reply are not yet proven. Historical authenticated proof at `319d780` / SDK 1.0.14 remains historical, not current-head proof. This repair used secretless production-composition tests and loopback provider fixtures; credentialed fork execution was not authorized. No new-head hosted CI result is claimed before publication.

### Earlier current-main integration evidence

Current-source maintainer refresh: `9d630935e55cda2f0c6d422213e9a6966d912c04` against pinned main `ce3f47b60a55d9302c70936c680319a039a68eed`, preserving the contributor head as the first parent.

- The detached-probe regression fails with the current-main journal's exact-target error and passes with the repair; the durable-manager negative control also passes.
- Combined focused coverage is **143 tests across 9 files using input-scoped reuse**, not one all-green run on the final head: 65 unchanged core/journal tests at tree `2ad6009`; 69 unchanged harness/attempt/memory/pool tests at tree `152dea6`; and 9 SDK-loader/runtime-artifact tests rerun at final tree `80f578b` (2.21s Vitest / 6.50s wrapper). The stale durable fixture and rejected-import cache failure were investigated and repaired.
- Production types, affected lint, formatting, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets, and diff checks pass. The final cache repair reran its production types, SDK lint/format, and assertion ratchet. Hosted CI seconds for the refreshed head are not yet available.
- The actual Copilot package-runtime build passed, including its lazy runtime-artifact chunk. Installed SDK/native-runtime capture and validation passed at the final tree: `transport=stdio`, `runtimeArtifactPresent=true`, `validation=true`. That check made no model request.
- Fresh P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable issue in the supplied diff. Extra unchanged context was unavailable to that reviewer. The failed-import eviction does not clear failures after an SDK identity has loaded; restart-on-identity-drift remains intact.
- Current-source proof used fresh secretless AWS leases with exact PR-head and candidate-tree checks. No operator Gateway, credentials, durable probe state, settings, or schema policy changed.
- The authenticated setup/Ask proof below still belongs to `319d780`; it is not a new authenticated run on this head. No full monorepo build or current-head hosted CI is claimed.

Earlier contributor evidence is retained below with its original revision labels.

On cleanup commit `be58a66eca8c99bd51380e18ce33ab04da5d29f1`:

- **62 tests passed / 6 files**, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`: runtime, artifact, SDK loader and memory transcript suites (35 tests; 51.17s Vitest / 55.26s wrapper), plus system-agent turn and setup suites (27 tests; 66.89s / 71.32s). Hosted CI time is not yet known.
- The actual installed SDK/native runtime was captured and revalidated successfully (`transport=stdio`, `runtimeArtifactPresent=true`, `validation=true`); this check makes no model request.
- Extension production types, affected extension lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Independent review found no P0–P2 issues.
- `check:changed` passes the line-cap checks, then stops at the inherited environment-variable budget: 477 `OPENCLAW_*` names versus 476. This PR adds no such variables and does not raise the budget.
- The separate Codex autoreview helper remains unavailable (HTTP 401). No full repository build/test was run; hosted CI is not claimed green.

Authenticated setup/Ask proof was run on the **preceding revision `319d78087cf5e88acf402be8e460cd4e1d7bb291`**, with the real harness/SDK, isolated configuration/state, and no dependency mocks:

```text
provider: github-copilot; model: [historical proof model omitted]; harness: copilot
verifySetupInference({ bindSession: true }): ok=true
runtimeArtifactPresent=true; latencyMs=41124
SystemAgentChatEngine.handle() reply: OPENCLAW_PROOF_OK
action: none; historyTurns: 2
cleanup: zero failures; exit: 0; isolated state removed
```

That proof covers the transport-independent setup/engine flow, not a browser recording. It was accepted by ClawSweeper Revision 3; it has not been relabeled as a new authenticated run on the cleanup commit.


### Earlier-head CI attribution (809 matching diagnostics)

On head 78b4ecdae2cf1b8931fe10f0fa50c67d1a89efe8, [CI 39398592176](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39398592176) fails only its core production-type leaf (job 118548460386) among the CI build/test checks. The completed job log contains the same 809 compiler diagnostics as independently executed clean main 37e60afc6d2ffb3dab5dee16a52f2aae2554d4ab and the repaired archive integration. The comparison normalizes only checkout-root paths; every diagnostic and order match. This run's actual merge base is 2e41793e3ef693c57486e0cf6b356c7c72c872d5, not the executed older main: the compiler configuration, package/lock, offending helper and SDK browser entry are unchanged between those bases. This is signature-based inherited-failure attribution, not a new execution of the newer main.

Main's src/gateway/chat-display-replay.test-support.ts imports Control UI consumers into the Node-only core compiler graph, producing the DOM/JSX errors. This PR does not change that helper or compiler policy. The check remains failed; no rerun, suppression, broad compiler-library change or merge bypass was used. Superseded cancelled context jobs have a later successful context/evidence run.

The review of `78b4` confirmed the durable-projection finding was resolved with no remaining code findings. Current-SDK authenticated setup verification and Ask proof remain outstanding; this earlier-head typecheck classification does not supply that proof or qualify the integrated head.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): restore dashboards independently of transcript validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A warm dashboard reload can miss its early restore because the persisted board waits for a lazily loaded transcript-validator chunk. In the campaign's signed-in deep-link evidence, the dashboard appeared last in a 14-state reload sequence. This corrects the warm-restore dependency on the lazy validator in #178113.

Release the already validated board envelope before loading the transcript validator, and schedule its restoration after initial connection dispatch. Both the early envelope and full-cache path use that ordering. Shape validation, session/scope checks, grant filtering, ticket TTL aging, and authoritative `board.get` reconciliation remain in their existing owners. Transcript hydration retains its existing timing and lifetime. The prior hydration method moves into its own cohesive pane module to stay within the source-file size limit; its old definition is deleted.

## Evidence

11 interleaved pairs per scenario on one quiet AWS Crabbox `c7a.4xlarge`, lease `cbx_3c617a884495`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f146c8e8db1316d7584b88fb8a4ce08e). Repository Playwright Chromium; synthetic Team-scale dashboard, rotating tickets and separate sandbox origin. Connect floor 350 ms, connect latency 240 ms, board.get 160 ms, other RPCs 35 ms. Measurements use final head `0fc10392fc87c34b42cf98bd38377af0858949f2`; the baseline replaces only the four existing restore runtime owners from merge-base `65f3ca05d794`. Both bundles share all other source, dependencies, fixtures, and the sandbox server. The new hydration module is unreferenced by the baseline history owner. No private captures or real account data are included.

| Held-validator primary | Baseline median [IQR] | Candidate median [IQR] | Median paired delta | Better |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Iframe insertion | 808.8 [807.5, 817.7] ms | 359.3 [356.2, 359.7] ms | −450.7 ms | 11/11 |

All 11 candidates insert exactly one iframe before hello while the validator is delayed 800 ms. Hello's paired median is +8.1 ms with overlapping IQRs, below the declared 3% threshold; FCP is unchanged and chat catch-up improves 89.7 ms. Ordinary warm-cache, fast-validator and chat-route controls pass the no-regression gate. Fast-validator LoAF blocking rises 10.0 ms paired with overlapping IQRs and mixed signs (8/11 worse), retained in the tables below.

Predeclared primary: at least 9/11 better with negative median paired delta. Secondary regression: worse non-overlapping IQRs, or at least 9/11 worse pairs with median paired rise above max(10 ms, 3%). No pair was dropped.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark command</summary>

Use the baseline/candidate bundle construction described above, one fixed build ID, the campaign probes, and one `FIXTURE_NOW_MS` captured at the start of the comparison. The benchmark alternates baseline/candidate for 22 runs (11 pairs).

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --bundle-dir "$BASELINE_BUNDLE" --compare-bundle-dir "$CANDIDATE_BUNDLE" \
  --runs 22 --warm-reload --dashboard-widget --chat-dashboard-route \
  --connect-not-before-ms 350 --method-latency-ms connect=240 \
  --method-latency-ms board.get=160 --latency-ms 35 \
  --fixture-now-ms "$FIXTURE_NOW_MS" --probe-dir "$PROBE_DIR" --history-validator-delay-ms 800 --untraced
```

The ordinary dashboard control omits `--history-validator-delay-ms`; the fast-validator control sets it to 1. The chat control uses `--face chat --untraced` without `--chat-dashboard-route` or a validator delay.

</details>

## Validation

Final head: `0fc10392fc87c34b42cf98bd38377af0858949f2`, rebased onto `65f3ca05d794f8cc26ad15fcc16860028fe7467a`. Independent review is clean through P2; the exact-head automated code review also has no findings. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39523676275) is green. This PR remains unmerged for lead review.

Final-head full UI e2e passed on AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, lease `cbx_3c617a884495`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f146c8e8db1316d7584b88fb8a4ce08e): **837 files / 3,617 tests passed; 4 files / 4 tests skipped**. Command wall: 6,216 s; Vitest: 6,095.44 s. The four opt-in skips are `desktop-resize`, `peer-followup-restart`, `chat-steer-deferred-custody`, and `deepseek-search` real-Gateway e2e. Both dashboard-before-hello regressions and all six plugin-skills cases pass within this full run. Focused owners also pass 6 files / 92 tests (23 s); plugin-skills passes separately (35 s command / 31.50 s Vitest). Changed-file lint, UI/script types, and all core test type graphs pass. Runtime hashes match before and after the comparisons, and tracked source stayed unchanged.

The full run on the preceding head exposed a detached-element sampling race in the installed plugin description clamp assertion. Diagnostics showed a connected, correctly clamped row at 1440 px, then a detached sampled handle with zero geometry at 390 px. The repaired assertion queries the current DOM and measures it synchronously inside `page.evaluate`; the exact one-row, clamp, overflow, text, and screenshot requirements remain. No retry, longer timeout, or weaker expectation was added. That failure was not classified as inherited: the unchanged test passed on the original base and a later main snapshot.

The held-validator regression fails on the old restoration path, and a separate full-cache negative control catches bypassing connect-dispatch ordering. Shape validation, session/scope checks, grants, ticket aging, and `board.get` authority retain their owner coverage. `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` walls on the unchanged runtime contracts: gateway connect 3.90 s; dashboard cold load 61.64 s; snapshot custody 9.98 s; board loading 5.88 s; snapshot store 4.42 s. Browser command times include production build/setup; these files exercise real layout and held-network boundaries that unit fixtures cannot establish.

The composite remote payload exited 1 because `check-changed` reported the three repository-wide guards below; the full UI suite itself exited 0. All three reproduce on the unchanged main base `65f3ca05d794f8cc26ad15fcc16860028fe7467a`, on fresh AWS lease `cbx_c8c48e3ca452`, [comparison run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f2f56840c7b89fc10f7ce386ca997f00). The max-lines failure also reproduces with that base compared to itself. No exception or baseline was changed.

| Guard | Matching main-base failure |
|---|---|
| Max-lines suppressions | `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts` |
| Core test-shard root budgets | agents-tools 722, gateway-root 725, infra 728, plugins-platform 728; limit 720. This PR adds no test roots or changes to those configurations. |
| Unused exports | Production: `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts: PluginRuntimeResolver`, `src/transcripts/capture.ts: TranscriptsLogger`. Full-tree scan also reports `extensions/github/src/preview.test-support.ts: conditionalJson`. All are unchanged by this PR. |

The failing guard signatures, passing type/lint checks, and full UI results are retained separately. Both remote source checkouts stayed clean.

## Scope and Release Note

Runtime **+133/−98, net +35 LOC**. The requested exclusion filter reports **+468/−179, net +289**, including the committed benchmark/fixture extensions and `.test.tsx` regression. Growth preserves initial-dispatch lifecycle and cached-board ordering; the superseded hydration method and moved helper definitions are deleted. No new configuration option or durable Gateway schema change.

Release-note context: cached dashboards can attach while transcript validation is pending, without delaying the live handshake under the measured latency profile. The independent early-reveal/theme fix is [#178740](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178740).

prs.title: perf(control-ui): reveal themed dashboard frames during load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A dashboard app can already have drawable pixels in its isolated iframe while the host thread is busy with reload work. Keeping the frame hidden until the host handles the ready message delays the visible dashboard. Simply exposing the frame also caused a browser canvas flash when its initial color scheme differed from the embedding iframe.

Seed the sandbox shell's theme from a stable URL fragment and apply it synchronously before body parsing. Set the embedding iframe to that same scheme, synchronize later theme updates, and refresh the seed only for a real sandbox navigation. The transparent initial frame can composite over the existing skeleton while staying inert until ready. Error, stale, approval, timeout, and retry presentation keep their existing owners. Delete the obsolete double-animation-frame reveal path.

## Evidence

11 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs per theme on one quiet AWS Crabbox `c7a.4xlarge`, lease `cbx_7b6bbd7871e3`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_54e249ae2b1a664b12c153901da394ea). Repository Playwright Chromium, synthetic Team-scale dashboard, rotating tickets, separate sandbox origin and its own font. Connect floor 350 ms, connect latency 240 ms, board.get 160 ms, other RPCs 35 ms. Measurement commit `8da6fc0d5f050fc619861564a106c4a06829706a`; all four reveal runtime files are byte-identical in this independent split and its test-only repair. Both sides use the same candidate sandbox server; isolated bundles compare hidden/revealed presentation under that shell, not old/new server deployments. No private captures or real account data are included.

| First visible chart pixels | Baseline median [IQR] | Candidate median [IQR] | Median paired delta | Better | Iframe flashes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Light | 1194.8 [1156.0, 1253.2] ms | 964.6 [944.7, 978.9] ms | −233.0 ms | 11/11 | 0/11 |
| Dark | 1269.0 [1196.1, 1292.8] ms | 949.5 [944.1, 961.3] ms | −278.6 ms | 11/11 | 0/11 |

Pixels are detected in compositor screenshots of the synthetic chart, not host message or DOM observer timestamps. All runs insert one iframe, and first chart pixels follow insertion. Candidate pixels precede the host’s synthetic app-ready receipt in 11/11 runs per theme: paired median lead 110.2 ms light and 107.8 ms dark. Receipt timestamps describe host dispatch, not network arrival; visible pixels no longer depend on that dispatch. Authored app JavaScript and font startup remain outside this change. The campaign's original signed-in deep-link evidence recorded 14 visual states and dashboard paint at 11.75 seconds; later attribution isolated this host-side reveal wait.

Predeclared primary: at least 9/11 better with negative paired median. Secondary regression: worse non-overlapping IQRs, or at least 9/11 worse pairs with median paired rise above max(10 ms, 3%). Hello, FCP, LoAF blocking, chat catch-up, and chat-route controls pass. No pair was dropped. Combining this with the independent restore fix also passes (light −220.1 ms, dark −205.9 ms paired, 11/11 each), with 0/11 iframe flashes per theme.

Screenshot review screened 5,318 post-navigation frames across reveal-only and combined runs, checked per-run pre-content/first-chart/settled states and full representative timelines. The initial whole-document blank precedes the iframe and is distinguished from an iframe canvas flash. Both themes retain their expected dashboard background through paint and settlement.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark command</summary>

Use the baseline/candidate bundle construction described above, one fixed build ID, the campaign probes, and one `FIXTURE_NOW_MS` captured at the start of the comparison. The benchmark alternates baseline/candidate for 22 runs (11 pairs).

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --bundle-dir "$BASELINE_BUNDLE" --compare-bundle-dir "$CANDIDATE_BUNDLE" \
  --runs 22 --warm-reload --dashboard-widget --chat-dashboard-route \
  --connect-not-before-ms 350 --method-latency-ms connect=240 \
  --method-latency-ms board.get=160 --latency-ms 35 \
  --fixture-now-ms "$FIXTURE_NOW_MS" --probe-dir "$PROBE_DIR" --history-validator-delay-ms 1 \
  --dashboard-paint-marker --filmstrip-only --color-scheme light
```

Repeat the same 11 pairs with `--color-scheme dark`. The chat control uses `--face chat --untraced`, retaining the 1 ms validator delay and omitting `--chat-dashboard-route`, `--dashboard-paint-marker`, `--filmstrip-only`, and `--color-scheme`.

</details>

## Validation

Final head: `675e0c8ad638a22569c5eb02f7d64b805c3eaafc`, rebased onto `05ade6d2df13f660e9df17cbedaeba5eb9f93dfc`. Independent split and test-repair reviews are clean through P2. Fullscreen and A2UI coverage now distinguish visible painting from interaction readiness by waiting for `inert` removal; the held-document fullscreen state remains visible, inert, and covered by its loading status. The repair changes tests only; all four runtime files are byte-identical to the measured version. Final-head proof ran on AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, lease `cbx_e5f9f79bb739`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_101bf02b907e41e1e7ee215dc1a10bbb): **full UI e2e: 838 files / 3,617 tests passed; 4 files / 4 tests skipped**, command wall 6,425 s (Vitest 6,303.95 s). All changed and sibling browser scenarios are included. Focused owner tests: 5 files / 37 tests passed (38 s); UI types passed (15 s); fullscreen 9 tests passed (66 s including build), A2UI 6 tests passed (61 s including build). The four opt-in skipped files are `desktop-resize`, `peer-followup-restart`, `chat-steer-deferred-custody`, and `deepseek-search` real-Gateway e2e. The working tree stayed unchanged. The lease is released. Stop before merge.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39492360621) completed with three underlying failures: a test-mock export ratchet and two UI shards. The mock ratchet is an unchanged upstream doctor test, repaired on main in `2466488c29e2`. The UI failures are the menu-highlight assertion in `menu-surface.browser.test.tsx` and lazy-content assertions in `chat-composer-plus-menu-loading.test.tsx`; their owners/tests are unchanged and do not execute the modified board-frame paths. The exact-head menu-surface pinned-Bun replay passes (22 tests, 13 s). The original failing CI merge `87c1ef107751ea8ce543d879304c65a91760c02e` (PR head `675e0c8a` plus CI base `92477a7`) also passes both original shard inventories with three workers restricted to two CPUs: shard 1/3 266 s, shard 3/3 253 s, including all seven composer-loading cases. This bounded replay used AWS lease `cbx_bf62248fe437`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_bfad0708fbdd9cc0f58cc29bc8b0e1f5). The relevant test/owner blobs are identical to the PR head.

Main snapshot `f5f3ed438533af1a97af9734d2b3518902f6d3b0` passes the same saved shard inventories (129 s / 126 s) and the mock ratchet (14 s), on lease `cbx_6410a35ff63d`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2957e8d12c7edd24c2c36ef79eb9ad17). The failure assertions were verified in the passing logs. Main has dependency updates; its newer retained-focus menu branch is not used by these tests. The AWS host has more memory than the original CI runners, and cache-dependent dispatch ordering can differ. These passing replays do **not** establish a repair or reproduce the same failures on main. The two menu failures remain intermittent/unreproduced; the GitHub run remains red. No GitHub jobs were rerun or branches updated to chase unrelated reds. This is an explicit remaining CI gate for the lead.

Prior exact-runtime proof: frame owner and resilience, theme owner, sandbox/gateway owners, native first-theme regression, and eight sibling browser files pass. The new browser regression fails on the old shell at initial `color-scheme: normal` before any theme delivery, then passes both themes and later updates with the fix. The error/stale/needs-approval and timeout/retry owners remain covered by their existing tests.

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` walls: frame resilience 4.88 s; frame owner 4.31 s; widget theme 3.76 s; native sandbox theme 57.92 s including production build/setup. The browser composition is needed to establish synchronous shell initialization before first iframe canvas paint. The earlier combined-head full UI attempt was superseded during the split and is not claimed as a full-suite pass.

## Scope and Release Note

Runtime and requested production exclusion filter: **+48/−37, net +11 LOC**. Growth preserves the initial-theme/navigation contract; the double-animation-frame state and callbacks are removed. No new configuration option, durable Gateway shape, CSP permission, or approval model change. The fragment does not change the sandbox HTTP request/cache key; ready-message matching retains the complete iframe URL.

Release-note context: dashboard frames show app pixels while the host is busy finishing reload work, without a mismatched-theme browser canvas flash. The independent restore correction is [#178658](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178658).

prs.title: feat(config): add config export --safe for redacted full dumps
prs.body:
Implements #178014

## What Problem This Solves

Operators need a full effective-config dump for bug reports and install snapshots, but today only path-scoped `config get` redacts secrets — people paste raw `openclaw.json` or unredacted trees by mistake.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw config export --safe` prints (or `--out` writes) the full runtime config with the same schema-aware redaction as `config get` / Control UI. Unredacted full export is refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `redactConfigObject` + config UI hints on the whole `snapshot.config`, require `--safe`, and document the read-only command. No new redaction rules; no unredacted export path.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/config-cli.ts`, `src/cli/config-output-mode.ts`, `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`, `docs/cli/config.md`
- Unit: `config export --safe` (3 tests) pass
- Packaged CLI: `node openclaw.mjs config export --safe` redacts `gateway.auth.token`; without `--safe` exits 1

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Full config export must redact secrets; `--safe` is mandatory; non-sensitive fields remain visible.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw config export --safe` → `runConfigExportSafe` → `readConfigFileSnapshotWithPluginMetadata` → `redactConfigObject(snapshot.config, uiHints)` → stdout / `--out`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `redactConfigObject` / schema UI hints (same as `config get`). No new redaction engine. Does not change write paths.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) from this branch; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"gateway":{"mode":"local","port":18789,"auth":{"mode":"token","token":"super-secret-token-xyz"}},"agents":{"defaults":{"heartbeat":{"every":"30m"}}}}' > "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
node openclaw.mjs config export; echo nosafe_rc=$?
node openclaw.mjs config export --safe > /tmp/export-safe.json; echo safe_rc=$?
python3 -c 'import json; p=json.load(open("/tmp/export-safe.json")); assert p["config"]["gateway"]["auth"]["token"]=="__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__"; assert "super-secret-token-xyz" not in json.dumps(p); assert p["config"]["agents"]["defaults"]["heartbeat"]["every"]=="30m"; print("ASSERT_OK")'
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
nosafe_rc=1
stderr: config export requires --safe so the full dump is schema-redacted. Re-run with --safe (unredacted export is not supported).
safe_rc=0
ASSERT_OK
# export JSON includes: "token":"__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__" and "every":"30m"
# export JSON does not include: super-secret-token-xyz
```

Before the fix (same commands on unpatched `upstream/main`): `config export` is not a registered subcommand (unknown command / help only).

### Observed result after fix

Without `--safe` exits 1 with a clear message; with `--safe` prints redacted JSON and keeps heartbeat cadence.

### What was not tested

Control UI export; doctor/migration diffs; closing redaction edge cases tracked by #168147.

### Fix classification

New feature (I1: implements #178014).

## Checklist

- [x] AI-assisted
- [x] Allow edits from maintainers
- [x] Single concern / single commit
- [x] No CHANGELOG.md edit

prs.title: feat(slack): create public channels from message actions
prs.body:
Closes #163782

## What problem this solves

OpenClaw’s Slack message tool cannot create a project channel, forcing operators to leave the workflow or use a separate integration.

## User impact

An operator can explicitly enable Slack channel creation with `channels.slack.actions.channels: true` (or the selected account’s equivalent). The action creates a public channel in the trusted workspace, invites the trusted requester when Slack permits, and returns a reusable workspace-qualified target.

## Design and security boundary

Channel creation is **disabled by default** and is no longer part of the ordinary `messages` action gate. This makes workspace administration an explicit operator choice while preserving existing message permissions.

The generated Slack manifest requests bot-compatible `channels:manage` for creation and `channels:write.invites` for requester invitation. Existing Slack apps must be reauthorized after adopting these scopes.

## Evidence

- Focused Slack channel-create/action-runtime tests passed (47 tests), as did `pnpm config:channels:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` on current head `71d77bfe365c18f9b1f0e9cd75e8158ce8f0bcac`.
- Current-head CI is terminal and passing.
- [ClawSweeper’s current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-5961532592) found no actionable code findings and marked proof sufficient.

## Current-head proof

The reauthorized disposable-workspace proof created a public channel, invited the verified non-admin requester, delivered to the returned target, and rejected disabled-account creation before Slack I/O. [Inspectable redacted terminal evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6159613571) records the final API boundary and managed-Gateway health without identifiers or credentials.

[Isolated v2026.10.3-to-candidate compatibility evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6159849038) validates the persisted reauthorized configuration with both runtimes, proves the reauthorized credential with `auth.test`, and shows a matching non-secret settings/data fingerprint without touching the managed Gateway.

[Enterprise adapter-to-client transport evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6160504251) records allowed create/invite plus missing/conflicting-context rejection before provider I/O and caller closure before invitation.

## Before merge

- [x] **Real behavior proof:** published inspectable, redacted terminal evidence for the allowed create/invite/send path and disabled-account pre-I/O rejection.
- [x] **Data-model compatibility evidence:** published the isolated `v2026.10.3`-to-candidate reauthorization/configuration compatibility record.
- [x] **Enterprise transport trace:** published production-client coverage for allowed and rejected Enterprise workspace contexts; live Grid final-I/O remains unavailable to this contributor.
- [ ] **Upstream OpenClaw maintainer decision required:** an upstream maintainer must accept, reject, or specify the administrative-delegation/default OAuth-grant contract described in the [current ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-5961532592). This is not a Dillon approval and is not a contributor-owned repair.

No contributor-owned code repair or Slack-proof setup remains open. The sole merge gate is the upstream maintainer decision.
