prs.title: fix(ui): six Control UI page titles are not exposed as headings
prs.body:
Closes #178012

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: screen reader users jumping by heading never reach the page's own name on the Control UI Logs, Debug, Devices, Memory, Apps and Activity pages, because the visible page title there is a plain `div` (Activity has no heading at all).

## User Impact

User impact: the heading list (VoiceOver rotor, NVDA H key, browser accessibility tree) now names the page on these six routes, the same as on Sessions, Usage, Portals, Channels, MCP and the other Settings pages. Nothing changes visually.

## Why This Change Was Made

The six page titles render as `<h1 class="page-title">`, the markup the rest of the Control UI already uses for page titles (`hub-page-header.tsx:31`, `SettingsPageHeader` in `settings-ui.tsx:98`, About, Portals). On Apps, the hero "Take OpenClaw everywhere" moves from `h1` to `h2` so the page keeps one level-one heading that names the page; the hero keeps its size and position, only its rank in the heading outline changes.

The `.page-title` and `.apps-hero__title` rules already set margin, font size, weight and line height, and no stylesheet selector depends on the tag, so the browser's default `h1`/`h2` styles cannot move anything.

On Logs, Debug, Devices and Memory the page name becomes the second level-one heading after "Settings" from the Settings sidebar (`settings-sidebar.tsx:500`). That pair is what every `SettingsPageHeader` page (Channels, MCP, Models, Profile, About and the rest) already ships.

Contract:

| Route | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/activity` | no heading; "Activity" is text | `heading "Activity" [level=1]` |
| `/logs` | only h1 is the Settings sidebar title; "Logs" is text | `heading "Logs" [level=1]` after the existing "Settings" h1 |
| `/debug` | same as Logs | `heading "Debug" [level=1]` |
| `/nodes` (Devices) | same as Logs | `heading "Devices" [level=1]` |
| `/settings/memory` | same as Logs | `heading "Memory" [level=1]` |
| `/apps` | "Apps" is text; hero is the only h1 | `heading "Apps" [level=1]`, hero `heading "Take OpenClaw everywhere" [level=2]` |
| Pixels on all six routes | | unchanged on five routes; on `/settings/memory` only the animated mascot differs, as it does between two runs of the same tree (see Evidence) |
| Not handled here | Agents and Model setup also contain a `div.page-title`, but an h1 already names those routes ("Agents"; "Models" from the settings header). Moving focus to the heading on navigation is #127317 and is not part of this change | |

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine at the staged tree, base `0fa95c89bfc`.

**Build.** `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (exit 0). The browser runs use the repo's Control UI E2E harness (`test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`), which serves this tree's Control UI from source and answers Gateway requests from synthetic fixtures. Headless Chromium, 1440x900, screenshots taken with Playwright `animations: "disabled"` (the Memory mascot illustration keeps animating regardless). BEFORE is this branch with only the seven production lines reverted.

**Behaviour, per route.** Headings and accessibility tree read from the DOM (visible `h1`-`h6`, and `ariaSnapshot()` of `main`). The pixels do not change; the proof is the heading tree.

BEFORE (`/apps`): ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/e18d88d23ef91e9c9ead1f93b9166c1c9e7c5af5/pr-10-page-title-headings/before.png)

AFTER (`/apps`): ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/e18d88d23ef91e9c9ead1f93b9166c1c9e7c5af5/pr-10-page-title-headings/after.png)

```
route             visible h1 BEFORE          visible h1 AFTER       title line in ariaSnapshot BEFORE -> AFTER
/activity         (none)                     Activity               - text: Activity Recent sessions ...  ->  - heading "Activity" [level=1]
/logs             Settings                   Settings, Logs         - text: Logs                          ->  - heading "Logs" [level=1]
/debug            Settings                   Settings, Debug        - text: Debug                         ->  - heading "Debug" [level=1]
/nodes            Settings                   Settings, Devices      - text: Devices Paired devices, ...   ->  - heading "Devices" [level=1]
/settings/memory  Settings                   Settings, Memory       - text: Memory Choose how ...         ->  - heading "Memory" [level=1]
/apps             Take OpenClaw everywhere   Apps                   - text: Apps                          ->  - heading "Apps" [level=1]
                                                                    - heading "Take OpenClaw everywhere" [level=1] -> [level=2]
```

Layout check from the same runs: the `.page-title` bounding box and computed `font-size`, `font-weight`, `line-height` and `margin` are identical before and after on every route (for example `/logs` 368,48 56.14x31.19, 26px/650/31.2px/0; `/activity` toolbar row 848.34,16.5 53.31x15, 15px/600/15px/0), as is the Apps hero (684.34,90 381.31x34.5, 30px/700/34.5px/0).

Screenshots: `/activity`, `/logs`, `/debug`, `/nodes` and `/apps` are byte-identical before vs after (`cmp`), and a second AFTER run is byte-identical to the first. On `/settings/memory` the only differing pixels are inside the animated memory mascot illustration (x 430 to 611, y 176 to 341): 15942 pixels before vs after, and 815 pixels between two AFTER runs of the same tree. Outside that box, before vs after differs by 0 pixels.

**Tests.** One assertion per route, `getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })` naming the page; the Apps test also checks that the hero is a level-two heading and that the page has one `h1`. Each changed file, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

```
ui/src/pages/logs/logs-page.test.tsx                     Tests  17 passed (17)   2.34 s
ui/src/pages/devices/devices-page.test.tsx               Tests  39 passed (39)   4.45 s
ui/src/pages/debug/view.test.ts                          Tests  18 passed (18)   2.84 s
ui/src/pages/config/memory.test.tsx                      Tests  11 passed (11)   2.55 s
ui/src/pages/activity/activity-page.presence.test.ts     Tests   2 passed (2)    2.38 s
ui/src/pages/apps/apps-page.test.tsx (new)               Tests   1 passed (1)    2.11 s
ui/src/pages/apps/view.test.tsx (hero owner, unchanged)  Tests   5 passed (5)    2.14 s
```

The Activity assertion sits in `activity-page.presence.test.ts` because `activity-page.test.ts` is over the line cap and the line-cap ratchet rejects growing it.

Owning-directory lanes (`pnpm test ui/src/pages/logs ui/src/pages/debug ui/src/pages/devices ui/src/pages/apps ui/src/pages/activity ui/src/pages/config`):

```
 Test Files  44 passed (44)
      Tests  463 passed (463)
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  65 passed (65)
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 18.04s
```

**Regression proof (red/green).** Production lines reverted to base, tests kept, the seven files above in one run:

```
 ×  ui/src/pages/devices/devices-page.test.tsx > DevicesPage gateway lifecycle > names the page with a level-one heading
 ×  ui/src/pages/debug/view.test.ts > names the page with a level-one heading
 ×  ui/src/pages/logs/logs-page.test.tsx > names the page with a level-one heading
 ×  ui/src/pages/config/memory.test.tsx > names the page with a level-one heading
 ×  ui/src/pages/activity/activity-page.presence.test.ts > names the page with a level-one heading
   → Unable to find an accessible element with the role "heading"
 ×  ui/src/pages/apps/apps-page.test.tsx > AppsPage > names the page with one level-one heading above the hero
   → Unable to find an accessible element with the role "heading" and name "Apps"
 Test Files  6 failed | 1 passed (7)
      Tests  6 failed | 87 passed (93)
```

With the fix: `Test Files  7 passed (7)`, `Tests  93 passed (93)`.

**Other checks.**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>` | 0 errors, 1 warning at `activity-page-view.tsx:168` (unchanged line; the same warning on base) |
| `oxfmt --check <changed files>` | all files formatted |
| `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` | 0 cycles |
| `git diff --check` | clean |
| `pnpm check:changed` | exit 1 on three steps that fail the same way on base `0fa95c89bfc` alone, none naming a changed file: max-lines suppression ratchet (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`), core tsgo shard root budget (`gateway-root` 725 and `plugins-platform` 726 roots), dead export scan (exports in `extensions/`, `src/` and `ui/src/lib/chat/chat-metadata-store.ts`); typecheck UI, Control UI i18n catalog, line-cap ratchet and lint pass |
| `pnpm changed:lanes --json` | lanes `ui` and `coreTests` only |

## Gaps, stated plainly

- No real screen reader was run (VoiceOver or NVDA). The proof is the browser accessibility tree: before, the title is text; after, it is a level-one heading with the page name.
- The browser runs use the mocked Gateway, not a real Gateway. The change is markup only and does not depend on Gateway data.
- The mocked `/nodes` page logs `TypeError: e is not iterable` in both the before and the after run (a fixture shape the harness does not fill); the page and its title render in both runs.
- The mocked `/logs` page shows a Gateway error banner in both the before and the after capture (the harness does not serve the logs stream); it is unrelated to the heading and identical in both arms.
- Logs, Debug, Devices and Memory now have two level-one headings ("Settings", then the page name), matching the other Settings pages; this change does not revisit that pattern.
- On Logs the page title "Logs" is followed by the existing section heading "Logs" (level two); that duplicate name is unchanged here.
- Focus on route change is out of scope (#127317).

prs.title: fix(cli): record trajectory events for pure Claude CLI runs
prs.body:
Closes #80667

**AI-assisted: yes.** The patch was authored by an AI coding agent, reviewed by a separate local review pass (one blocker and one contract gap found and fixed), and every command below was executed in this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sessions that stay on the `claude-cli` backend for their whole lifetime never record runtime trajectory events, so `<session>.trajectory.jsonl` is never produced and post-mortem/export cannot see otherwise successful CLI turns.

Trajectory capture is on by default and documented to record `session.started`, `trace.metadata`, `prompt.submitted`, `model.completed`, and `session.ended` (`docs/tools/trajectory.md`). Only the embedded attempt path wired the recorder; the prepared CLI lifecycle (`src/agents/cli-runner.ts` → `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts`) called the CLI process with no recorder, and the only CLI-adjacent event was `model.fallback_step` from the fallback wrapper. A pure CLI run therefore wrote no lifecycle rows and never materialized a trajectory.

## User Impact

Turns served by the `claude-cli` backend now produce the same trajectory lifecycle events as embedded runs. `openclaw trajectory export` and post-mortem tooling see CLI-only sessions, including failures, aborts, timeouts, and CLI-internal recovery, instead of an empty trajectory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair reuses the existing SQLite trajectory recorder around the prepared CLI lifecycle; it does not add a store, schema, exporter, or config surface.

- New `src/agents/cli-runner/trajectory.ts` owns one recorder per prepared CLI turn: it skips `isolatedCompletion`, `controlOperation`, caller-owned `sessionManager`, and the existing `disableTrajectory` opt-out; records `session.started` + `trace.metadata`; and in a `finally` records exactly one `session.ended` before flushing through the existing `runAgentCleanupStep` budget.
- `runPreparedCliAgent` now settles through that wrapper while preserving the existing `complete` callback and `runWithCliHistoryWriter` boundary.
- `executePreparedCliRun` records `prompt.submitted` from the already-composed `sentPrompt` immediately before dispatch, and `model.completed` only after executor cleanup succeeds.
- The `disableTrajectory` opt-out is now honored end to end for CLI runs: it is part of `RunCliAgentParams`, forwarded by the embedded CLI backend dispatcher, and checked before recorder creation, matching `attempt-trajectory.ts`.
- Recording and flushing are best-effort: failures are logged and never change the CLI turn outcome.

Embedded-agent wiring, CLI auth/session/recovery, the SQLite schema and workers, and the legacy JSONL sidecar behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit/integration proof (red on base, green with the fix).** Test-first; the suite was run before the production change:

```text
# before production change
Tests  7 failed | 3 passed (10)
# after (including two review-fix cases)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  12 passed (12)
```

The new suite drives a real child process through `runCliAgent` and reads the canonical SQLite store. It asserts the five events in order, plus failure, manual abort, timeout, disabled capture, default-on capture, `disableTrajectory` opt-out, isolated runs, CLI-internal recovery (two `prompt.submitted`, one `session.ended`), and cleanup failure.

**Regression runs:**

```text
agents-support: trajectory.test.ts + execute.executable-invocation.test.ts  14 passed
infra:          cli-runner.context-engine.test.ts + trajectory/runtime.test.ts  38 passed
agents-core:    cli-runner.terminal-failure-log.test.ts + cli-runner.helpers.test.ts  13 passed
```

**Checks:**

```text
tsgo core (tsconfig.core.json): pass
check:test-mock-exports --base HEAD^: Mock factory ratchet OK
oxfmt --check (6 files): All matched files use the correct format.
oxlint (6 files): Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
git diff --check: clean
```

### Real-runtime proof (isolated Gateway, successful turn)

This branch was built (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime`) and run in an isolated checkout with an isolated state directory and loopback port:

```text
[gateway] agent model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (thinking=adaptive, fast=off)
[gateway] http server listening (18 plugins: acpx, anthropic, bonjour, canvas, …, xai, zoom-meetings)
```

Config mapped `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` to `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`. `openclaw agent` dispatched a real `claude` child through the shipped Claude CLI backend:

```json
{ "status": "ok", "summary": "completed",
  "result": { "payloads": [{ "text": "PROOF-178007-SUCCESS" }] },
  "meta": { "provider": "claude-cli", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "durationMs": 5610 } }
```

`openclaw sessions export-trajectory --session-key agent:main:proof-success` then materialized the capture:

```text
eventCount: 7   runtimeEventCount: 5
session.started → trace.metadata → user.message → prompt.submitted
  → model.completed → assistant.message → session.ended
model.completed: assistantTexts ["PROOF-178007-SUCCESS"], stopReason "completed"
session.ended:   status "success", stopReason "completed", aborted false, timedOut false
```

**Terminal-outcome proof.** Two earlier real `claude-cli` dispatches through the same Gateway failed before a model reply (a sandbox permission error writing Claude's debug log, then a provider credential 401) and each exported `session.started → trace.metadata → prompt.submitted → session.ended(status="error")`, confirming the failure path records a terminal outcome instead of leaving an empty trajectory.

**Boundary notes.** The integration test uses a real child process and the real recorder/store, so it proves the lifecycle boundary, ordering, and exactly-once ending without a model provider call. `prompt.submitted` records the model-facing logical prompt (composed with the CLI prompt context), not literal argv bytes. On a CLI→API fallback both attempts record rows; trajectory export selects the newest `session.started` cohort, so the exported bundle reflects the settled attempt while earlier failed-attempt rows remain in the database (existing behavior for fallback attempts).

This revives the approach from #168556, which was closed only by the >20-open-PRs rule and had no review findings; the settlement hook moved since then and the patch was re-seated on `runPreparedCliAgent`.

prs.title: feat(cli): dismiss a pending DM pairing code
prs.body:
Closes #177870

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can dismiss a pending DM pairing request in the Control UI, but the CLI can only list or approve it.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw pairing dismiss <channel> <code>` removes that one pending request. The sender stays unapproved, is not notified, and is not bootstrapped as a command owner. Other pending requests stay in place, and the sender can request access again.

An unknown code exits non-zero and names `openclaw pairing list`. A blank `--account` is rejected. When a running Gateway owns the state directory, the CLI uses that Gateway. An older Gateway that does not advertise `channels-pairing-dismiss-owner-v1` does not fall back to a local write.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channels.pairing.dismiss` already removed a request by opaque id for the Control UI. The CLI now sends the same method with the pairing code, matching `pairing approve`, and the store deletes that code without writing `allowFrom`.

## Evidence

Store, Gateway method, command-catalog, and administrative CLI process tests cover the new path. The process suite runs the real CLI child for `pairing dismiss` when the Gateway is live, offline, missing the new capability, refuses the call, or drops the reply.

Shipped CLI, no Gateway running, isolated state directory. Two pending requests were seeded (`VK2U7PMX` for `sender-drop`, `YKHL5DQ6` for `sender-keep`). `channel_pairing_allow_entries` stayed empty.

```text
$ node dist/index.js pairing dismiss routing-fixture VK2U7PMX
Dismissed routing-fixture sender sender-drop.
exit:0

$ node dist/index.js pairing list routing-fixture --json
{
  "channel": "routing-fixture",
  "requests": [
    {
      "id": "sender-keep",
      "code": "YKHL5DQ6",
      "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:32:04.133Z",
      "lastSeenAt": "2026-10-20T03:32:04.133Z",
      "meta": {
        "senderId": "sender-keep",
        "accountId": "default"
      }
    }
  ]
}
exit:0

$ node dist/index.js pairing dismiss routing-fixture MISSING1
No pending pairing request found for code "MISSING1". Run openclaw pairing list --channel routing-fixture to list pending requests.
exit:1
```

Focused tests before this capture:

- `src/pairing/pairing-store.test.ts` dismisses one code, leaves the other, and keeps `allowFrom` empty.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/channel-pairing.test.ts`: 17 passed, including the CLI code dismiss, invalid selectors, and admin-owner authority.
- `src/cli/program/root-command-descriptions.test.ts` catalog matches the registered command.
- `src/cli/admin-state-owner.process.test.ts` pairing-dismiss: live, offline, missing-capability, refused, and lost-reply passed.

prs.title: fix(elevenlabs): forward batch STT providerOptions to speech-to-text
prs.body:
Closes #168580

**AI-assisted: yes.** The patch was authored by an AI coding agent under human supervision; every command below was executed in this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `tools.media.audio.providerOptions.elevenlabs` and `tools.media.models[].providerOptions.elevenlabs` are accepted by config but silently ignored, so Scribe v2 filler-word removal (`no_verbatim`) and audio-event tagging (`tag_audio_events`) cannot be configured.

The media runner merges audio defaults with the model-entry options and passes the result as `req.query` (`src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts`). The ElevenLabs transcript adapter built multipart fields from `model_id`, `language_code`, and `prompt` only and never read `req.query`, so the merged options were dropped before the request left the process.

## User Impact

Voice notes transcribed through ElevenLabs Scribe v2 now honor configured `providerOptions.elevenlabs` for `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize`. Users who already set these options get the transcript they asked for instead of API defaults — for example, false starts and filler words are actually removed, and the user-visible `echoTranscript` carries the cleaned text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair stays in the vendor adapter that owns the request shape:

- A plugin-local allowlist forwards `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from `req.query`.
- Only `string | number | boolean` values are forwarded; arrays, `undefined`, and `null` are ignored.
- The dedicated request fields stay authoritative: a query key can never override `model_id`, `language_code`, or `prompt`.
- Every other query key is ignored on purpose. Fields such as `webhook` change the response contract, and this provider requires a synchronous transcript payload.

No new config option, no SDK change, and no schema change: the configuration surface already documented in `docs/nodes/audio.md` now works. `docs/providers/elevenlabs.md` documents the supported keys, the `scribe_v2` restriction on `no_verbatim`, and the fact that `diarize` speaker labels are not surfaced because the adapter returns transcript text only.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof against the real ElevenLabs API

Executed 2026-10-20 against `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/speech-to-text` with `model_id=scribe_v2` and a restricted user API key. Audio: a synthetic 16 kHz mono WAV generated locally with macOS `say` containing the phrase *"I— I— I mean, uh, um, hello there. This is a test."* Same audio, same key, same command; only the checked-out provider code differs.

**Before the fix (parent commit `109271a9`):** configured options have no effect.

```text
[default (no providerOptions)]        -> "I, I, I mean, uh, um, hello there. This is a test"
[providerOptions: no_verbatim=true]   -> "I, I, I mean, uh, um, hello there. This is a test"
RESULT no_verbatim changed transcript: false
```

**With this PR (`17a219ea`):** the configured option takes effect.

```text
[default (no providerOptions)]        -> "I, I, I mean, uh, um, hello there. This is a test"
[providerOptions: no_verbatim=true]   -> "I mean, hello there. This is a test"
RESULT no_verbatim changed transcript: true
```

`tag_audio_events=false` is also accepted by the real API (HTTP 200, no validation error) on a laughter clip; that clip produced no transcript-text change because the model rendered the laughter as words rather than an audio event, so its visible effect is not claimed here — the multipart forwarding for all three keys is covered by the unit test below.

The configuration reached the adapter through the documented `tools.media.audio` provider-options merge path. No API key, IP address, phone number, or private endpoint appears in this evidence.

**Not covered:** Telegram Test Server voice-note echo. No Test Server credentials were available in this environment; the provider-boundary path above is the shipped path `tools.media.audio` uses for voice notes.

### Shipped OpenClaw CLI invocation

The same configuration was exercised through OpenClaw's own CLI (`infer audio transcribe`), which resolves the configured `tools.media.models` entry and runs the shipped media-understanding pipeline instead of calling the adapter directly. It was run from the source checkout through the same CLI entrypoint (`src/entry.ts` via `scripts/tsx.mjs`) that the repository's CLI process tests invoke, because a full `dist` build in this checkout requires every bundled extension's build-time devDependencies:

```text
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-el-run/config.json \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-el-run/state \
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts infer audio transcribe \
  --file /tmp/falsestart.wav --json
```

Config used (the API key arrives through the provider's `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` environment path and is redacted here):

```json5
tools: {
  media: {
    models: [
      {
        provider: "elevenlabs",
        model: "scribe_v2",
        capabilities: ["audio"],
        providerOptions: { elevenlabs: { no_verbatim: true } },
      },
    ],
    audio: { enabled: true, echoTranscript: true },
  },
},
```

Result matrix — same audio, same provider, same config; only the checked-out code or the config entry changes:

| Run | Code | `providerOptions` | CLI `outputs[0].text` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | parent `109271a9` | `no_verbatim: true` | `I, I, I mean, uh, um, hello there. This is a test` |
| 2 | this PR `17a219ea` | `no_verbatim: true` | `I mean, hello there. This is a test` |
| 3 | this PR `17a219ea` | none | `I, I, I mean, uh, um, hello there. This is a test` |

The CLI envelope reports `"provider": "elevenlabs"` and `"model": "scribe_v2"`, confirming the configured provider entry was the one that ran. Run 3 shows the unconfigured baseline is unchanged, so the transcript change comes from the configured provider option rather than from an unrelated request change.

`echoTranscript` is set in this config, but the CLI transcribe surface does not consume the chat echo path; the Telegram Test Server voice-note echo remains the one uncovered scenario.

prs.title: fix(meetings): one slow browser audio pull ends a talk-back call
prs.body:
Fixes #177633

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one slow browser audio pull ends a meeting talk-back call. The browser audio transport closes the realtime bridge on the first failed pull, so a single browser request that misses its 5 s deadline drops the call, even though the page capture is still alive.

## User Impact

User impact: a talk-back (`bidi`) meeting call now survives one stalled audio pull. The participant loses at most the audio the page dropped while the pull was stuck. Two failed pulls in a row still end the call, and a capture the page reports as closed still ends it at once. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createBrowserMeetingRealtimeAudioTransport` pulls captured audio from the page about three times a second. Any pull error called `fail()`, which stops capture and closes the bridge.

A failed pull does not mean the capture is gone. The node audio transport (`realtime-node-audio-transport.ts`) already tolerates transient input errors, counting `consecutiveInputErrors` up to 5. The browser transport now uses the same counter and warning, with a limit of 2: the page keeps only the newest audio (47 chunks) and closes a capture that goes 10 s without a pull, which two 5 s pulls reach. The count resets after the pull and any audio processing complete without an error, so unusable audio or a failed hand-off to the realtime engine still counts as a failure. Every browser safety and authority check still runs on every pull; nothing is skipped or cached.

## Evidence

### Live run

Live Slack huddle in a lab container: Linux, Chrome 155, OpenClaw built from #177357 (`83d04fa`) with #173898 applied, OpenAI realtime voice. Lab-only stage timing was added inside the browser plugin's `/act` route. IDs are placeholders.

Four talk-back runs failed 5–15 s after the join with `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out`. In each run, successful pulls finished their page work in about 3 ms. The failing pull in the clearest run finished its page work, then waited in the response's URL check until the request was cancelled:

```text
02:07:12.426 guard assert-done
02:07:12.426 fffvt evaluate-start
02:07:12.428 fffvt evaluate-end
02:07:12.681 fffvt guard-exit
02:07:12.682 post json-ok-start      <- resolveTabUrl -> navigation URL check (hostname lookup)
02:07:17.411 post released           <- request cancelled; 4.7 s with no further stage
02:07:17.413 Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out
```

With the SSRF policy active, that check resolves the page hostname on every call. In the same container, 2 of 200 lookups of the Slack hostname took about 5006 ms, exceeding the audio pull's 5 s budget. In another run, the failing pull stalled before its page work started, at a step that run did not split further.

With the hostname pinned in the container's hosts file, a two-way conversation ran for 2 minutes: 371 audio pulls, no failures, and the participant heard the agent answer.

With this change (and #173898) and normal DNS, the same lab ran a two-way conversation for over 12 minutes. Four pulls stalled in the first 30 s; each was retried, participant audio resumed, and the agent kept answering the participant coherently for the rest of the call:

```text
03:07:16.375 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:24.193 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:33.775 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:41.694 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
```

Twelve minutes after the join, `slackhuddles status` still reported `inCall: true`, `audioInputRouted: true`, `providerConnected: true`, `bridgeClosed: false`, and the log had no `capture failed` or session-close entry. Before this change, every normal-DNS run ended at the first such stall. The live run used `8cc7ccc`; later commits only move the counter reset after audio processing and reword its comment; a stalled pull never reaches that point. The participant heard some agent replies cut short. The log shows four `audio output backpressured` warnings, which may explain them; that output path is not touched here and the cut-offs were not matched to log times.

### Tests

`realtime-browser-audio-transport.test.ts` adds "keeps the call through one stalled pull and ends it on a second in a row". It fails on `main` (the first rejected pull ends the call) and passes here. "ends the call when pulled audio keeps failing to reach the model" covers unusable audio and a failed hand-off twice in a row. All 35 `src/meeting-bot` test files pass, and `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean.

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- **Why not change the URL check.** Skipping it for audio pulls, or remembering a tab's approval, could miss a tab that moved to another page or a hostname that started resolving to a private address. Reducing the repeated lookups while keeping those checks is for the browser owners; the timing above is the evidence.
- **Related, not fixed here:** #173896 (audio stops when the join's requester disconnects; #173898 proposes a fix) must be fixed first for talk-back to reach this point. Caption reads still fail with `Gateway requester authority changed` after the join.

</details>

prs.title: clickclack: enforce inbound sender allowlist [AI]
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: ClickClack agent-mode inbound messages could reach command handling without applying the configured sender allowlist.
- Solution: Resolve ClickClack sender access before inbound dispatch and use that decision for `CommandAuthorized`.
- What changed: Added a ClickClack access resolver, wired it through gateway and inbound handling, and added focused gateway/inbound regression coverage.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): No config schema, token handling, outbound delivery, or non-ClickClack channel behavior changed.
- AI-assisted: yes

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- N/A
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

- ClickClack operators can configure `allowFrom` to limit which senders can control an agent. The inbound path should apply that boundary before preparing an agent turn or marking command authorization.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed: ClickClack inbound messages now apply configured sender allowlists before agent dispatch and command authorization.
- Real environment tested: Linux 6.14.0-37-generic x64, Node v22.21.1, built source Gateway launched with `node dist/entry.js gateway --port 45283 --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, a local ClickClack-compatible HTTP/WebSocket fixture, and a local OpenAI Responses-compatible mock model endpoint.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `env pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false node scripts/tsdown-build.mjs`; `node scripts/runtime-postbuild.mjs`; `node .artifacts/clickclack-allowlist-proof.mjs`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts --reporter=verbose`.
- Evidence after fix: With `allowFrom: ["usr_allowed"]`, the fixture recorded 1 ClickClack realtime websocket. Sender `usr_allowed` produced `inboundObserved=true`, `modelRequestObserved=true`, and `replyObserved=true`. Sender `usr_denied` produced `inboundObserved=true`, `modelRequestObserved=false`, and `replyObserved=false`. The focused ClickClack Vitest command exited 0.
- Observed result after fix: The allowlisted ClickClack sender reached the model reply path and received a fixture thread reply. The denied sender was present in fixture inbound messages but did not trigger a model request or ClickClack reply, proving it was dropped before dispatch/command authorization.
- What was not tested: A hosted third-party ClickClack deployment with real user accounts, package-install Docker lanes, and full CI were not rerun in this proof step. The runtime proof used a local ClickClack-compatible HTTP/WebSocket fixture against the real built Gateway.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Source inspection on current main showed ClickClack gateway dispatching non-bot messages without sender access resolution and inbound context construction setting `CommandAuthorized: true`.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: The ClickClack inbound context set `CommandAuthorized` to true without first checking the message author against the resolved ClickClack account allowlist.
- Missing detection / guardrail: There was no gateway or inbound regression coverage for allowed versus denied ClickClack senders.
- Contributing context (if known): The ClickClack gateway forwarded human messages directly into agent handling after bot filtering.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts`, `extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: An allowlisted ClickClack sender is command-authorized, while a sender outside `allowFrom` is dropped before inbound handling.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: It covers the gateway handoff and inbound context construction where the access decision is made.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None identified.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

ClickClack `allowFrom` now gates inbound sender dispatch and command authorization. Accounts that keep the default wildcard allowlist remain open.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
ClickClack event -> bot filter -> inbound handler -> CommandAuthorized=true

After:
ClickClack event -> bot filter -> allowlist access decision -> allowed inbound handler -> derived CommandAuthorized
                                           |
                                           +-> denied sender dropped
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: The command surface is narrowed by applying the configured ClickClack sender allowlist before agent dispatch. Regression tests cover allowed and denied sender paths.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.14.0-37-generic x64
- Runtime/container: Node v22.21.1, local source checkout, built `dist/entry.js`
- Model/provider: local OpenAI Responses-compatible mock endpoint, model `openai/gpt-5.5`
- Integration/channel (if any): ClickClack, local HTTP/WebSocket fixture
- Relevant config (redacted): `channels.clickclack.allowFrom: ["usr_allowed"]`, `replyMode: "model"`, `model: "openai/gpt-5.5"`

### Steps

1. Built source runtime output with `env pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false node scripts/tsdown-build.mjs` and `node scripts/runtime-postbuild.mjs`.
2. Started a local ClickClack-compatible fixture, local mock OpenAI Responses endpoint, and the built Gateway with `node dist/entry.js gateway --port 45283 --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`.
3. Posted a ClickClack inbound message from `usr_allowed` containing `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_ALLOWED`.
4. Posted a ClickClack inbound message from `usr_denied` containing `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_DENIED`.
5. Ran focused regression tests with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts --reporter=verbose`.

### Expected

- `usr_allowed` reaches agent/model handling and receives a ClickClack reply.
- `usr_denied` is visible as a fixture inbound transport message but is dropped before model request, reply dispatch, and command authorization.

### Actual

- `usr_allowed`: `inboundObserved=true`, `modelRequestObserved=true`, `replyObserved=true`.
- `usr_denied`: `inboundObserved=true`, `modelRequestObserved=false`, `replyObserved=false`.
- Mock model request count was 1 and ClickClack thread reply count was 1, matching only the allowed sender path.
- Focused ClickClack Vitest command exited 0.

## Evidence

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Proof command output:

```json
{
  "result": "passed",
  "environment": {
    "os": "Linux 6.14.0-37-generic x64",
    "runtime": "v22.21.1",
    "gatewayCommand": "node dist/entry.js gateway --port 45283 --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured",
    "clickClackFixture": "local HTTP/WebSocket ClickClack-compatible fixture",
    "mockModelEndpoint": "local OpenAI Responses-compatible fixture"
  },
  "config": {
    "allowFrom": ["usr_allowed"],
    "replyMode": "model",
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.5"
  },
  "observations": {
    "websocketConnections": 1,
    "allowedSender": {
      "id": "usr_allowed",
      "inboundObserved": true,
      "modelRequestObserved": true,
      "replyObserved": true
    },
    "deniedSender": {
      "id": "usr_denied",
      "inboundObserved": true,
      "modelRequestObserved": false,
      "replyObserved": false
    },
    "mockRequestCount": 1,
    "threadReplyCount": 1
  }
}
```

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: Built the source Gateway, ran it against a local ClickClack-compatible HTTP/WebSocket fixture with restrictive `allowFrom`, verified an allowlisted sender reached the model reply path, and verified a denied sender did not trigger model or reply dispatch.
- Edge cases checked: Explicit allowed sender `usr_allowed`, explicit denied sender `usr_denied`, ClickClack realtime websocket delivery, model reply dispatch, and focused gateway/inbound regression tests.
- What you did **not** verify: Hosted ClickClack service behavior with real external user accounts, package-install Docker lanes, and full CI in this proof step.

## Review Conversations

- [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Operators with a non-wildcard ClickClack `allowFrom` who expected all workspace users to reach the agent will now see denied senders dropped.
  - Mitigation: Keep `allowFrom: ["*"]` for open bot accounts, or include every intended sender in the account allowlist.

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): add native tts-1 speech provider
prs.body:
Related: #99657 (follow-up native speech capability; does not reopen the original catalog work).

## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter's existing binary speech service route was not registered as a native speech capability, so native TTS, Talk, voice model discovery, and telephony could not select it.

## User Impact

Users with ClawRouter speech access can select `clawrouter/openai/tts-1` for native TTS, Talk, voice-model discovery, and telephony. Existing chat routing and credentials remain unchanged; the service still determines whether a credential may use speech.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Register a plugin-owned speech provider and capability catalog using the public SDK, qualified model `openai/tts-1`, six classic voices, and six supported output formats.
- Resolve ClawRouter credentials specifically for `audio.speech`, including stored and terminal locked profiles; reject profiles owned by other providers. Never fall back to an OpenAI key or treat catalog metadata as an authorization grant.
- Reuse guarded HTTP, bounded binary reads, safe credential-redacted errors, and transport cleanup. Map PCM24k through native telephony conversion.
- Cover native selection and the real local HTTP boundary without production fetch/auth mocks; keep speech-only catalog rows outside chat discovery.

No ClawRouter service changes, richer TTS/STT/realtime, new global auth/default/Fast configuration, or primary/fallback binding changes.

## Evidence

- Native registry/TTS reproduction failed before provider registration, then passed through local HTTP with the adapter.
- 56 affected ClawRouter tests across seven files passed. After test-only typing corrections, all ten speech tests passed again; production source was unchanged.
- Focused type-aware lint (292 rules, no errors/warnings) and focused tsgo passed; formatting and diff checks passed.
- Isolated real Gateway `talk.speak` RPC returned byte-exact valid WAV (92 bytes), `audio/wav`, qualified model, per-call voice/speed, and synthetic ClawRouter Bearer to actual local HTTP.
- Real stored-auth, missing/wrong/locked-profile failures; safe 403, JSON/empty/overflow responses; deadline cancellation with server socket close; PCM24k to 8k mu-law conversion.

That local receipt does not establish a broad typecheck/CI pass or isolated base execution; the later exact-head remote CI result is recorded below. All 50 passing check contexts and 57 skipped contexts were inspected, with no pending/failed context; applicable security/dependency checks passed. The unchanged doctor lint finding did not recur on that run; no repair of that unrelated code or full local changed-gate pass is claimed.

## Landing conflict repair

Current main added a Decisions provider at the same registration point. The prior head was genuinely conflicted; integrated captured main `09042bd8e08eab6245d1b16810ec7da1951f7f38`, preserving both registrations and regenerating the plugin reference. The intended delta against that base is still eight speech-only files. - Focused syntax lint (258 rules, five files), touched formatting, generated inventory check, and diff checks passed. Current type-aware lint refused the canonical global pnpm graph TypeScript realpath before diagnostics; no install was attempted and no current type-aware pass is claimed. The earlier focused typecheck evidence and full changed-gate failure remain recorded above.
- Fresh independent guarded API-only review completed: exit 0, validated `scoped-clean`, zero P0–P2 findings in both evidence passes. Each pass saw only its selected complete-file batch; review did not execute project code. Whole touched production/test files were audited again.
- Prior successful CI remains evidence for the prior head only; fresh exact-head CI is required for this repair. No deployment or paid/live-provider qualification is claimed.

A second actual import conflict followed the landing of the separate Fast-policy sibling. Related: #178860

## What Problem This Solves

Explicit ClawRouter audio selection cannot transcribe uploaded files because the native plugin has no registered media-understanding audio provider.

## User Impact

User impact: operators with a supporting ClawRouter service and eligible scoped key can explicitly select batch/file transcription, including Talk file uploads, without changing chat or speech defaults.

Register the existing public OpenAI-compatible transcription helper through canonical ClawRouter credential preparation, preserving the exact `gpt-4o-transcribe` default, original file bytes and effective media metadata. Shared guarded transport retains endpoint/private-network/proxy policy, bounded errors and cancellation through response EOF; uploads are not replayed on redirects. Unsupported provider options are explicitly rejected rather than silently removed. Existing speech registration is preserved.

This is a narrow consumer change stacked on #178860. The existing media owner normalizes MIME and trims prompt whitespace before the adapter; raw MIME aliases and surrounding prompt whitespace are not promised. Streaming, diarization, other response formats/models and realtime remain out of scope.

## Evidence

- The exact speech base fails registered-runtime reproduction with `Media provider not available: clawrouter`; the candidate passes through real HTTP multipart.

prs.title: feat(cron): pause automations whose creating conversation is gone
prs.body:
**Stacked on #178933** (base branch `automations/execution-context-foundation`). Review that PR first; this diff contains only the pause slice.

Related: #178812
Related: #178811

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation keeps running after the conversation that created it has been removed, archived or reset, acting on resources that conversation no longer has.

## User Impact

User impact: an automation linked to the exact conversation that created it now pauses instead of running when that conversation is gone. "Gone" means the conversation was removed, archived or reset, or its bound worktree no longer exists.
- The run is skipped before any session is created.
- The job is disabled, and the owning agent gets one notice that names the conversation and the `openclaw automations enable <id>` command.
- Restoring the conversation does not resume the job; re-enabling it does.
- Automations without an exact parent link are unaffected: CLI- or operator-created jobs, and older jobs that store only a session key.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pause check.** Before preparing the run session, cron reads the parent conversation's row and classifies it with the execution context builder from #178933.
  - Only jobs that recorded the parent's exact incarnation (`sourceConversation`, or a stored operator source) are checked.
  - A failed read never pauses a job.
- **Outcome.** A pause returns a skipped outcome with a typed `parentUnavailable` fact. Cron's outcome owner disables the job and queues one notice. Both happen only when:
  - the outcome still owns the job's schedule, so a newer operator edit made while the check was in flight wins;
  - the job was enabled before this outcome, so one-shot jobs, whose earlier handling also disables them, still get their notice.
- **No protocol change.** The pause is a plain disable plus a notice. It adds no `autoDisabled` reason, so the Gateway protocol enum is unchanged.
- **CLI loopback.** The CLI MCP grant already carries the admitted run into Gateway tool resolution. A test pins that it is the same run the minted context is bound to.
- **Codex.** Carrying the context to the Codex harness would add a field to the public plugin-SDK harness contract with nothing reading it yet. It lands with the first phase that reads it.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests:** 6 files, 119 tests pass, plus the two follow-up regression tests. The pause tests cover:
  - removed, archived and reset parents;
  - a current parent;
  - an unlinked job (no read);
  - a failed read (no pause);
  - the notice text;
  - one notice per pause, including for one-shot jobs;
  - a stale pause result leaving a newer operator edit alone.

  The last two tests failed before their fixes.
- **New QA lab scenario** `cron-archived-parent-pause` (mock-openai): a job bound to a live conversation runs `ok`. After the conversation is archived, the next forced run is `skipped` with a notice naming the conversation, and the job is disabled.
  - Passes on this branch.
  - On the base branch (#178933) the same scenario fails: the run after archiving still finishes `ok`.
- **QA lab regressions:** single run no duplicate, one-minute ping, natural fire no duplicate, spawn-only child delivery, send then continue, blocked outcome, condition watcher and failed-tool finalization all pass.
- **Static replay on a real Gateway's state copy:** no stored job would pause.
- **`pnpm check:changed --base automations/execution-context-foundation`:** format, lint, both typecheck lanes and the ratchets pass. The same four checks as #178933 fail, only on files this PR does not touch: UI max-lines, the plugins-platform test-shard budget, a deprecated API in `src/infra`, and unrelated unused exports.
- **Autoreview (Codex, P0-P2):** the passes led to both follow-up fixes (one-shot notice, stale ownership). The final pass is scoped-clean.
