prs.title: perf(agents): share PostgreSQL catalog readers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model catalog preparation opens a second PostgreSQL reader worker after reading the same agent's auth store, and credential-map construction loads plugin metadata outside the prepared plugin generation. The extra worker opens a fresh bridge and repeats admission work.

Use the existing lifecycle-owned reader for registered-agent auth and catalog reads already running in a PostgreSQL worker. Keep unregistered custom-path inspection's stored-owner behavior. Resolve credential maps inside the prepared plugin generation. Main-thread catalog transport, SQLite reader custody, write transactions, and advisory locks remain unchanged. There is no new pool, schema, configuration, or freshness probe.

## Measurement and acceptance

Baseline is `bead2a8e542740f943fe57e8391e5e6c11e9773d`, including #178673's independent bridge setup consolidation. Candidate is `a4cf269e835d09a56d9ddb2882111d3a5cf69073`. Both canonical builds use the identical frozen 63-file synthetic Gateway harness, adapter, and metadata observer. Local attribution uses Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.

Initial and restart catalog tasks both change from **3 to 2 logical worker scopes, 7 to 5 connects, 4 to 3 fresh bridges, and 24 to 19 driver queries**. The remaining connects comprise three fresh bridges and two reuses. All six initial/restart tasks per side have those counts, with zero unclassified connects and no extra catalog tasks. PG workflow fingerprints remain 14 per cell. Pooled warm PG R/T/S across nine turns per side is **11.333 / 40.333 / 49.333 → 11.444 / 40.444 / 49.444**. Candidate pair 2 has one additional `authProfiles.read` (that cell is 11.667 / 40.667 / 49.667); pairs 1/3 match baseline. This exception is retained. SQLite warm counts stay R=11.333, S=47. T counts completed driver queries/wire trips, not host-to-bridge messages.

Three interleaved local PG/SQLite pairs completed (12 qualified cells; no samples excluded). Median / nearest-rank p95 in seconds; with three samples, p95 is the maximum.

| Metric | PG baseline | PG candidate | SQLite baseline | SQLite candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial catalog | 2.250 / 2.343 | 2.763 / 2.996 | 2.096 / 2.283 | 1.961 / 1.997 |
| Restart catalog | 2.321 / 2.766 | 1.967 / 2.139 | 1.968 / 2.353 | 1.942 / 2.375 |
| Initial readiness | 8.207 / 8.810 | 8.344 / 9.448 | 7.562 / 8.897 | 7.998 / 8.098 |
| Restart readiness | 9.112 / 9.382 | 11.092 / 12.002 | 7.547 / 10.766 | 8.496 / 8.914 |
| First-use residual | 2.198 / 2.646 | 2.498 / 3.261 | 1.920 / 1.957 | 1.922 / 1.938 |
| Restart first-use residual | 1.859 / 2.053 | 2.476 / 2.602 | 1.552 / 1.817 | 1.675 / 1.947 |

**Local acceptance failed; keep this PR draft.** Landing requires improved catalog time and no cell slowdown of at least 20% beyond its matched SQLite control. The first pair improved, but pair 2 regressed PG initial catalog +33.2%, first-use residual +48.3%, and restart first-use residual +44.4%. Matched SQLite moved -2.8%, -7.7%, and +7.9%; PG/control ratios still regress +37.0%, +60.6%, and +33.8%. Pair 3 regressed restart readiness +31.7%, initial catalog +22.8%, and restart first-use residual +33.2%; SQLite moved -21.1%, -14.1%, and +7.2%. Candidate PG pairs 2/3 each also record one 500 ms `chat.send` admission retry on the first restarted turn; all other cells record none. These regressions remain unexplained and are not waived as host noise. Local C=64 measurements below do not override this failed boot/restart gate.

The shared generation-scope fix also removes one SQLite metadata read per catalog task, so SQLite is not an entirely unchanged code path. Initial tasks are 9→8 native statements in pairs 1/3 and 10→8 in pair 2, whose baseline deferred-migration scope has one additional statement; restart tasks are 8→7. All raw samples and host-load observations are retained.

The single authorized Testbox allocation stayed queued for the full 30-minute limit and ended before any remote sync, build, or benchmark cell. The lease is confirmed completed with no host, and its remote slot is released. No second allocation or provider fallback was attempted. Required Testbox performance proof is absent, independently preventing landing.

### Local C=64 control

One frozen local pair per engine, 320/320 completed turns per cell, zero errors/timeouts/unattempted turns:

| Engine | Baseline turns/s | Candidate turns/s | Baseline p95 | Candidate p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PostgreSQL | 4.784 | 5.217 | 15.321 s | 13.470 s |
| SQLite | 5.011 | 5.444 | 13.386 s | 12.230 s |

Throughput rose similarly for PG (+9.1%) and SQLite (+8.6%), so the PG stress gain cannot be wholly attributed to this change. These are local-only observations from one pair per engine.

## Evidence

- Real-PG regression is red on the baseline: a second registered auth read fails after new database connections are disabled. It passes on the candidate, including the first catalog-cache read, unregistered custom-path compatibility, and draining all readers before a non-FORCE database drop.
- 18 focused tests pass across the new PG regression, catalog replacement/quarantine/transfer and reader lifecycle suites, and prepared plugin scope/metadata suites.
- Core and infra-test TSRS, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Independent P0–P2 review is clean. The initial source-change setup refusals were corrected by freezing source before rerunning; they were not product-test failures.
- All three PostgreSQL conformance shards actually ran and passed on the exact final head in CI run 39498912108. The overall run was subsequently cancelled after this PR returned to draft; its completed conformance results are retained. The corrected PR context/evidence check also passed.

Production delta: +41/-6 lines. Tests: +116 lines. Documentation: +6/-2 lines.

prs.title: fix(database): avoid repeated PostgreSQL startup admission
prs.body:
**Landing held:** local and Testbox timing regressions remain unresolved. This PR has not been submitted for merge.

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL startup workers repeat catalog admission after the last native handle closes, and healthy agent closes misleadingly report an incomplete SQLite checkpoint.

## User Impact

Idle reopen reuses admitted PostgreSQL facts without another fingerprint query. Healthy PostgreSQL agent closes report `postgres-closed`. Schema changes still invalidate admission, including publication on a newly reopened idle anchor. Explicit PostgreSQL state, agent, and Team Reports port/restore validation revokes prior proof before checking the store. Migrations, drift checks, write transactions, advisory locks, and COMMIT boundaries retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the admission registry's existing process lifetime for engine identity, physical schema facts, and search capabilities. Carry registered search definitions with those facts so reopened workers bind the existing indexes. No new cache owner, freshness probe, per-call schema check, protocol, configuration, schema, bridge transport, or session-actor change is introduced.

Model-catalog preparation is a separate cost. Every measured boot/restart catalog task has one root and two nested read requests, seven PostgreSQL bridge connects, 32 driver queries, and zero schema-fingerprint queries. The seven connects cover bundled-discovery policy, selected-agent auth, shared auth store and rotation state, provider-auth plugin metadata, deferred migrations, and plugin catalog cache. Bridge reuse remains with its existing owner. Separate plugin/auth/provider/startup durations and the full PG-only elapsed difference are not established by these measurements.

## Evidence

Baseline `d4a2c1fea7444516a92ca66f1dcf75d71f248828`; final candidate `2c39b9a37498ae1a3abb79a0f8f7a76e60917c40`. Both use the same frozen synthetic Gateway fixture. All 63 harness entries match manifest SHA256 `c1514d9dbe2f164ac23ef7caddcb554015f66177aef5f42593388f8155ced289`; adapter SHA256 `a72a760942d9f49680128e167142c89724c3cbbd216eff77ae61e0a5d7bbebdc`. Exact sources were independently built. Real-model October 20 observations are a different workload and are not pooled with this synthetic comparison.

Acceptance requires eliminated repeat fingerprints, preserved maintenance/drift/rollback behavior, no added warm requests/probes, and resolved material timing regressions. A ≥20% adverse cell is a stop, not discarded as spread.

| Count or behavior | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fingerprint queries on ordinary last-handle reopen | 1 | 0 |
| Fingerprint queries on idle reopen with registered search extensions | 1 | 0 |
| Captured boot/chat/restart workflow fingerprints, every local and remote pair | 14 | 10 |
| Initial state admission fingerprints | 3 | 1 |
| Restart state admission fingerprints | 3 | 1 |
| Genuine state DDL / agent publication / writer / separate-process captures | 3 / 3 / 1 / 1 | 3 / 3 / 1 / 1 |
| Warm PG R/T/S per turn | 11.333 / 48.333 / 57.333 | 11.333 / 48.333 / 57.333 |
| Warm SQLite R/T/S per turn | 11.333 / n/a / 47 | 11.333 / n/a / 47 |
| Healthy PG close receipt | `checkpoint-incomplete` | `postgres-closed` |

R counts causal database worker requests; T counts completed `pg.Client.query` calls, distinct from host-to-bridge messages; S counts driver statements or native SQLite statements at their respective layers. Warm counts use six turns per side locally and 15 per side remotely for PG. Genuine DDL captures and independent inspection-process admission remain necessary.

### One Testbox A/B

One `blacksmith-testbox` lease completed 16 cells: five alternating PG census pairs, one SQLite census pair, and C64 stress pairs for both engines. Actual hardware was **4 CPUs / 15.42 GiB RAM**, despite a requested 16-CPU label. Node 24.19.0, PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector, pg_trgm, unaccent and pg_stat_statements. The payload and all cells exited 0; archive/source/cleanup receipts were verified. The lease is stopped. [The delegated run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39487591970) shows cancelled after intentional lease cleanup, after successful payload completion.

PG census: n=5 per side. p95 is nearest-rank and therefore the maximum here, not a stable population-tail estimate.

| Metric | Baseline median (p95; min–max), s | Candidate median (p95; min–max), s | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial readiness | 12.383 (16.774; 9.543–16.774) | 11.309 (12.486; 8.017–12.486) | -8.7% |
| Restart readiness | 15.897 (17.482; 12.850–17.482) | 14.818 (21.767; 12.254–21.767) | -6.8% |
| Initial model-catalog task | 5.998 (6.766; 4.639–6.766) | 5.058 (6.956; 3.814–6.956) | -15.7% |
| Restart model-catalog task | 5.592 (6.152; 4.173–6.152) | 4.233 (7.345; 3.881–7.345) | -24.3% |
| First-turn residual | 4.848 (6.593; 3.748–6.593) | 3.943 (5.095; 2.954–5.095) | -18.7% |
| First post-restart residual | 5.451 (5.624; 3.932–5.624) | 3.852 (5.965; 3.287–5.965) | -29.3% |

Timing acceptance remains held despite favorable medians. Pair 2 regressed restart readiness **28.6%** and restarted catalog **25.3%**. Pair 4 regressed initial catalog **20.7%** and first post-restart residual **32.2%**. Observed restart-readiness p95 increased **24.5%**. Existing traces show several startup tasks taking longer; catalog starts near readiness, so it cannot explain the earlier multi-second delay before the first HTTP response. Admission-payload clone/transfer time is not measured. Unchanged request counts do not rule out that cost.

Pairs 2–5 also record an additional first-turn catalog-worker task on both refs: three requests, five connects, 20 queries, zero fingerprints. Pair 1 has no extra task. This work is retained in the count ledger; task multiplicity is not assumed constant across flows.

SQLite census is one control pair: initial/restart readiness **8.870→8.425 / 11.226→10.006 s**; catalog **3.493→3.595 / 3.580→4.124 s**; first/restart residual **2.810→2.989 / 3.239→3.552 s**.

| C64 stress, 320/320 turns per side, zero errors/timeouts | Before turns/s | After turns/s | Before p95, s | After p95, s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PostgreSQL | 2.875 | 2.854 | 26.443 | 27.916 |
| SQLite | 3.422 | 3.163 | 23.028 | 25.183 |

These are single stress cells per ref/engine, separate from census. PG throughput is −0.7%, p95 +5.6%; SQLite throughput −7.6%, p95 +9.4%. No warm-path speedup is claimed.

### Local Homebrew PG17 A/B

Two PG census pairs on the shared Mac, separate from Testbox. Median seconds [min,max]; at n=2 nearest-rank p95 equals max.

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial readiness | 10.614 [9.101,12.127] | 12.039 [9.441,14.637] |
| Restart readiness | 12.466 [10.381,14.550] | 16.896 [13.326,20.467] |
| Initial catalog | 2.987 [2.686,3.288] | 3.451 [3.250,3.651] |
| Restart catalog | 3.493 [3.253,3.733] | 4.020 [3.233,4.807] |
| First-turn residual | 2.620 [2.472,2.767] | 3.152 [3.026,3.279] |
| First post-restart residual | 2.994 [2.819,3.170] | 2.940 [2.810,3.071] |

Local median restart readiness is **35.5% worse**, and first residual **20.3% worse**. Pair 14 has additional ≥20% adverse cells. The unchanged SQLite control improves and does not reproduce that PG slowdown. Host load varies, but that is not accepted as sole attribution. Local C64 completes 320/320 per side without errors: **3.199→4.065 turns/s**, p95 **23.541→20.171 s**; candidate host load declined during that run, so it is not a stable throughput claim. Its separate runtime-only initial readiness regresses **23.2%**.

First-use residual measures `chat.send` through `agent.wait`, minus completed model-call duration for the matching run ID. Session creation precedes that timer and can consume the startup-sidecars barrier; this fixture does not measure the entire post-ready chat-refusal interval. Intrusive stage-wrapper experiments and older candidate timings are excluded from final-head acceptance.

### Correctness and review

The three original PostgreSQL regressions were red on unchanged production baseline. Six focused engine/agent suites passed 47 distinct tests; the final 15-test agent suite passed after fixture extraction. An additional 40 Doctor migration/admission-retention tests passed, including real version 24–28 restores, partial-DDL rollback, idle invalidation and shared worker facts. The final correction passed 27 tests across state, agent, Team Reports port and schema-admission suites, including independently reproduced drift regressions.

CI/review caught three retention boundaries: idle schema publication must reattach descriptor-held facts; retained engine versions must follow schema revisions; explicit port/restore validation must revoke runtime proof. All are corrected through existing owners. Core, infra-test and state-test repository TSRS lanes, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, canonical qaRuntime build, simplification and isolated P0–P2 autoreview passed. Final-head GitHub code review and ClawSweeper identify no remaining correctness findings; ClawSweeper retains the timing hold.

All three [PostgreSQL conformance shards](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39486591020) actually ran and passed on final head `2c39b9a`. Broader required CI remains queued/pending. No merge intent has been submitted.

The complete diff is production +45/-8, tests +137/-32, docs +9/-3 (18 files, +191/-43). Added state carries registered search definitions through the existing physical-fact owner. Tests extend existing fixtures for distinct reopen, maintenance and close boundaries; helper code moves to the existing support module.

prs.title: perf(memory): remove redundant publication work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large first-use memory rebuilds repeat connection-policy SQL and cache counts and send one redundant shadow-preflight request per session. The `restoreBusyTimeout` census label covers complete memory-publication requests; it is not a separate maintenance loop. A completed 45-minute large-fixture baseline showed these owners drain, rather than sustain the hourly rates extrapolated from the first five minutes.

## User Impact

Memory indexing performs less database work while preserving the embedding-cache cap, pre-insertion capacity reservation, old-unreferenced eviction preference, and final refusal to publish forgotten content. No configuration, schema, retention, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Memory publication now keeps the connection owner's native busy timeout. It removes the zero/restore PRAGMAs, timeout transport, and host lock-refusal retry loop. The Gateway writer FIFO already owns live writes, and a private shadow has one writer. Native failures still propagate with settlement information. A source edit after its one preparation is picked up by the next ordinary incremental pass.

The existing retained cache size now records whether it is exact. COUNT, capacity reservation, and known deletions preserve exact size; ordinary replacements retain an upper bound. A COUNT corrects that bound only when necessary. The existing write receipt invalidates both the value and its precision. PostgreSQL retains the same token/lease and failed-settlement rules. Pruning still yields between batches of at most 100 rows, and capacity is reserved before insertion.

An unknown PostgreSQL COMMIT outcome cannot retain a usable stale count: the [connection owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/02540d22491c1249d6c2dc66a328d24690ec4586/src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.ts#L132-L163) invalidates the unscoped anchor receipt, marks the connection closed, closes its port, and terminates its worker. Further operations reject that handle. The [settlement owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/02540d22491c1249d6c2dc66a328d24690ec4586/src/infra/sqlite-database-admission.ts#L486-L503) advances the revision, so the memory owner's final retention check also rejects its old count. No additional guard is needed.

Private shadow rebuilds no longer issue `session.current` for every staged session. Discovery filters existing tombstones, Forget advances the published revision, and final live publication rejects a shadow built against an older revision. Direct source/cache checks and PostgreSQL staging/final tombstone checks remain. A late Forget may waste bounded staging or embedding work before refusal, but cannot publish forgotten rows. The obsolete command, helper, callers, tests, and documentation are removed together.

The simplification reuses the publication owner and receipts; no new generations, freshness probes, or handshakes. Production **+123 / -209 lines (net -86)**; tests **+308 / -168 (net +140)**. The native worker-inventory regeneration also refreshes pre-existing source drift; no generated output was hand-edited.

## Evidence

Base: `176482f971749c12ef4cce7e64b6113791209b9b`. Measured/reviewed production head: `02540d22491c1249d6c2dc66a328d24690ec4586`. Final head: `4421b0d88228ae24de9a0b168771bb67032e97f0` (test repair and main integration; all eleven changed memory production files byte-identical).

Four work-count regressions fail on the base at their intended assertions: per-session shadow preflights, native timeout policy statements, and repeated exact cache counts on SQLite and PostgreSQL. The first PostgreSQL attempt stopped because the isolated test database lacked its installed `vector` extension; after provisioning it alongside `unaccent` and `pg_trgm`, that case failed at the expected count assertion. No product failure is inferred from the initial setup error.

The candidate passes 105 SQLite owner tests and 21 native PostgreSQL owner tests. Both full-rebuild Forget regressions pass with the final revision check and fail on canonical published-row assertions when that check alone is removed; the temporary mutation was reversed byte-for-byte. Production and extension-test types, type-aware changed-file lint, format, T1 (171 unchanged), compatibility T1 (15 unchanged), dialect ratchets, Madge (zero cycles), export-name collisions, and all three canonical Knip categories (zero findings) pass. The only remaining `check:changed` failures are three UI max-lines suppressions and core test-root budgets (721/725/728/728); both reproduce identically on this exact base. The initial candidate-only PostgreSQL test line-cap failure was fixed by sharing its repeated cache-header fixture, preserving every assertion, and its owner tests, types, lint, format, and line-cap checks were rerun successfully. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean for P0–P2, with no actionable findings. Exact-head PostgreSQL review is approved; its unknown-COMMIT settlement question is resolved by the existing connection retirement and receipt invalidation above. All six alternating frozen-v3.1 arms and both fresh 45-minute large-fixture arms completed successfully; results follow.


Three-pair medians [range], SQL / requests / MAIN: whole **2,993 [2,988–3,030] / 797 [791–797] / 98 → 2,973 [2,970–2,979] / 788 [788–793] / 98**; compaction/settle/idle **384 [383–384] / 85 [84–85] / 0 → 366 [365–366] / 81 [81–83] / 0**. Each pair removes 18 statements in selected memory operations and three `index-read` requests. Shared warm read families are unchanged; raw whole deltas also include background scheduling differences.

Fresh large-fixture whole workload: **471,271 / 56,892 / 253 → 433,090 / 46,900 / 254**. Connected idle: **407,922 / 52,426 / 0 → 370,387 / 42,423 / 0**. Physical full-cache COUNTs **8,634 → 2**, busy-timeout PRAGMAs **30,329 → 576**, cache DELETEs **25,396 unchanged**; these counts overlap owner totals. Both arms open one shadow and perform 1,251 source-replacement groups. The one extra MAIN statement is an unchanged canonical-validation receipt read during restart; warm/idle MAIN remains zero.

| Connected-idle owner | Base SQL / requests | Candidate SQL / requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Agent publication | 73,254 / 8,135 | 48,854 / 8,135 |
| Shadow publication | 306,037 / 6,257 | 293,525 / 6,257 |
| Cache pruning | 1,432 / 205 | 824 / 206 |
| Reads/preparation | 6,297 / 31,308 | 6,296 / 21,305 |
| Provenance | 5,000 / 5,000 | 5,000 / 5,000 |
| Usage publication + scan | 17 / 4 | 17 / 4 |
| Session maintenance | 166 / 49 | 166 / 49 |

Every five-minute bucket from minute 10 through minute 45 has zero memory/usage work on both sides. These are savings within a draining backlog, not hourly steady-state savings. Short/long warm causal means stay **46.3 / 11.1 / 0** and **65.8 / 13.7 / 0**. The injected turn completes at **100 / 22 / 0** on both sides, but the backlog has already drained, so it does not establish active-memory fairness. prs.title: fix(claude-cli): subagent completions reset the Claude session and lose context
prs.body:
Closes #178953

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `claude-cli` session started from the Control UI loses its native session, and most of its context, whenever a subagent completion or a channel turn runs in it.

## User Impact

Agents that delegate to subagents keep their Claude session across completion announcements and the client turns that follow, instead of being reseeded from saved history each time. Other tool-name changes still start a fresh session, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`screen`, `show_widget`, `suggest_task` and `dismiss_task` exist only when the turn's client provides them (Control UI caps, gateway task delivery). Turns with no client drop them, and since #176577 that changes `promptToolNamesHash` and invalidates session reuse with `prompt-tools`. These four names are now left out of that hash.

The stale-catalog problem #176577 guards against does not return for these tools. They are still listed in the system prompt, so a change restarts a warm process through the live fingerprint's system prompt hash. A resumed Claude CLI process then lists the current MCP tools (see Evidence). A call to one of them on a turn that doesn't serve it gets `Tool not available` from the loopback bridge, because each turn's grant still filters `tools/list` and `tools/call`.

The docs for `prompt-tools` resets now name the excluded tools.

## Evidence

- New test `keeps the Claude session across Control UI turns and caller-less completion turns` in `prepare.completion-tools.test.ts`. It prepares Control UI → subagent completion → Control UI turns and asserts:
  - exactly these four tools differ between the turns;
  - the system prompt changes with them;
  - `resolveCliSessionReuse` resumes the stored session on each later turn.
- The test fails on main (`expected { mode: 'invalidate', … }`, reason `prompt-tools`) and passes with the change.
- Live check of the resume assumption with Claude Code 2.1.305 and a minimal stdio MCP server:
  - a session started with tool `alpha` was resumed (`--resume`, new process) with `alpha,beta` served, and it listed and called `beta` (`SECRET-BETA`);
  - the same check with deferred loading (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`): `ToolSearch select:mcp__probe__gamma` matched after resume and the call returned `SECRET-GAMMA`.
- Running locally with this change since 2026-10-20, no `Tool not available` errors have shown up in the gateway log.
- Touched suites: `prepare.completion-tools`, `prepare.existing-session`, `prepare`, `cli-session` and `prepare.configured-mcp` tests, 187 passed in 5 files.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, and `git diff --check` all passed.

This change was written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and adversarially reviewed by two models (Claude and Codex) before filing.

prs.title: fix: polish Claw publishing flow
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Creators need to turn an existing agent into a shareable Claw from the conversation where that agent already works, review and trim the exact package, and publish it with clear feedback. This adds a subtle share action to the chat header, keeps authoring in the existing main session, streamlines package review, and links the publication result to the canonical ClawHub Claw page. The ClawHub detail route is live in [#4011](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4011).

## Summary

```text
Existing main chat → Create Claw share action → $create-claw in that session
  → compact review modal → explicit publish → pending-security-review toast
```

The modal lets the creator set the name and description and remove workspace files, skills, or plugin requirements before rebuilding the exact archive. Each invocation carries its private draft ID as attached work context, so concurrent creations cannot target the wrong draft and internal IDs stay out of the visible message. The dismissing publication toast links to the canonical ClawHub Claw page.

## Evidence

- **Before:** creation was available from the agent menu, but the main chat header had no dedicated Create Claw action.
- **After:** a compact share-icon Create Claw button appears beside the other header actions; the agent menu action remains. Real Gateway screenshots and the simulated walkthrough video are attached in the PR proof comment.
- **Validation:** 27 targeted backend/UI unit tests and all 3 creator browser tests pass; `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, formatting, and the changed-file line-cap ratchet pass. The `check:changed` run exposed existing main baseline failures in unrelated max-lines suppressions and core test-shard budgets; it was stopped before the full aggregate completed. The hot-reload Gateway walkthrough ends before live publication; upload behavior is covered by simulated response tests.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** narrow

Changes the Claw creator entry point, review state, and publish feedback in OpenClaw’s Control UI and Gateway methods. Creation sends the skill request into the same main session.

prs.title: fix(automations): limit webhook-triggered turns to their own automation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: webhook (`/hooks/agent`) turns get the full automations tool instead of the current-job scope scheduled runs get, although both run through the same automation runner.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent turn started by an inbound webhook or a channel join introduction now gets the same automations tool scope as a scheduled run. Within that turn it can only inspect or remove its own run, not list or change other automations. Scheduled runs and ordinary conversation turns are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is consistency and defense-in-depth hardening. The Gateway already limits agent-runtime callers to automations their own session can see. Before this change, a hook turn's request for another automation passed the tool and was rejected only by the Gateway. The current-job scope was derived only from the `cron` trigger, so turns with trigger `event` that the cron runner starts were left out. They now share it. The condition still requires a job id, so other `event` turns that don't come from the cron runner stay as they were.

Channel join introductions already run with an empty tool allowlist. This change keeps that behavior and adds a test for it.

## Evidence

- **Crabbox real behavior proof (direct AWS, lease `cbx_a903c769bf38`, clean `--fresh-pr` checkout at `048267bca94`):** see the proof comment below, which includes the redacted run output.
  - The QA scenario `hook-turn-automations-scope` runs a real Gateway child and sends an HTTP `POST /hooks/agent` to it, with mock-openai inference. It passes on the PR head:
    - The hook turn's `remove` of a sibling automation is rejected by the tool scope (`Automations tool is restricted to the current automation.`) before any Gateway call.
    - The allowed control, `list` with `includeDisabled: true`, succeeds and doesn't expose the sibling.
    - The sibling is still in `cron.list` afterward.
  - Negative control: the same scenario with only `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` reverted to `main` **fails**. The sibling `remove` gets past the tool and reaches the Gateway, which rejects it as `cron job not found`.
- **Closed-run authority:** hook jobs are built in memory and never stored, so no stored current job exists that a leftover claim could remove after the run. The scope is applied when each attempt constructs its tools. Gateway `cron.remove` keeps its existing live-run check (`bindCronSelfRemovalCommitGuard`), which this PR doesn't change.
- **Unit tests:** a new cron-runner suite drives a hook-shaped job, and the results match scheduled runs. Event-triggered sibling `remove` is rejected, and the offered actions are `status, list, get, remove, runs, next_check`. Join introductions still get no automations tool. 3/3 and 13/13 pass on Crabbox. I removed the mocked option-forwarding construction asserts, since ClawSweeper flagged them as low-value.
- **CI attribution:** `checks-node-changed-10` (`gateway-mcp-app-grant-revalidation.e2e.test.ts`) and `checks-node-changed-18` (`gateway-rpc-chat.e2e.test.ts`) fail the same way on the merge base `50dfbacf1ab`, which doesn't include this PR. Neither failure comes from this PR.
- **Regression QA (mock-openai):**
  - `cron-send-then-continue` and `cron-blocked-outcome` pass.
  - `cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation` fails the same way on unmodified `main`.
  - `cron-explicit-authority-execution` needs the live-frontier lane and wasn't run.
- **Autoreview** (Codex, P1 threshold): no findings.

prs.title: fix: saved Gateway opens can fail when the Gateways menu closes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses a source-identified race where closing the Gateways menu can disconnect a saved Gateway while its first window is still opening.

**Draft:** the exact-head native app/test build and 80 focused tests now pass in a disposable macOS VM. Pristine-base red/green reproduction and broader incident qualification remain outstanding; this is not a claim that the original reported incident is fixed.

## User Impact

The proposed change keeps pending and retained saved-Gateway windows out of idle probe cleanup, including non-menu dashboard opens and native chat windows. Explicit credential retirement, profile removal, and fleet shutdown remain unconditional.

Same-account renewal notification ordering and expiry surfacing as generic shutdown are still unresolved. This focused draft addresses only idle cleanup ownership; those other schedules still need native investigation before this can be considered an incident fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The connection fleet now owns retained consumer demand. Dashboard configuration holds demand before native preflight and transfers it to its window; native chat keeps it through opening and the retained window record. Closing or replacing a dashboard releases its old demand, while hidden windows remain consumers. Idle cleanup rechecks demand at the socket shutdown boundary instead of relying on the menu's private list of opening tasks.

The redundant menu-only tracking is removed. The two constructor dependencies let regression fixtures replace profile storage and transport without replacing fleet, connection, channel, or dashboard-preflight decisions. Origin, TLS trust, authentication, account-bound storage, and expected-chat-store checks are unchanged; there are no message-based error guards or mutation retries.

## Evidence

Native validation is bound to upstream head `fbb30e598cdad1e284058798bc6c6b5eaf80f2e5`, independently checked out by a standalone workflow in Jacqueline’s public fork—not the fork workflow commit. See the [validation report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177970#issuecomment-6282432918), [successful run and downloadable logs](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39361552642), [native job](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39361552642/job/118428661548), and [pinned workflow](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/blob/0df832829e6ed9569fe3d9fdbe0d0c95df418135/.github/workflows/pr-177970-native.yml).

- **Native app/test build passed** on a dedicated GitHub-hosted `macos-26` VM: macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 26.4.1, Apple Swift 6.3.1, arm64. Compiler build time: **573.38 s**; Actions build step: **583 s**. Checkout credentials were not persisted; no operator credentials, personal configuration, or existing Gateway were supplied.
- **80 tests in 7 suites passed in 60.365 s**; launcher/Actions test step: **89 s**. Executed suites: `SavedGatewayOpeningLifecycleTests`, `GatewayMenuStatusStoreTests`, `GatewayConnectionDashboardIdentityTests`, `DashboardBrowserSessionTests`, `GatewayConnectionControlTests`, `ConnectSnapshotStoreGenerationTests`, and `DashboardEmbedCookieTests`. Execution used the repository’s `scripts/test-macos-native.mts default` launcher.
- **New lifecycle suite passed in 24.443 s:** queued idle cleanup during first-open configuration, hidden retained-window protection, retirement after close, and explicit credentials/removal/cancellation controls. The lifecycle case took **5.853 s**; the three interruption cases took **18.587 s** combined. These exercise the shared production owners, not actual AppKit menu/settings/bridge interactions; the cleanup gate is before the fleet disconnect call, not proof of every shutdown interleaving.
- **SwiftFormat 0.63.1 passed:** 0/414 files require formatting (6 skipped), plus 0/33 in the other macOS/shared scope. **SwiftLint 0.65.1 wrapper exited 0 with one file-length advisory:** `DashboardManager.swift` has 1,505 counted lines against the 1,500 limit. This is not zero-violation lint.
- **Source integrity:** the exact candidate SHA was checked before building; no tracked source changes remained afterward. `git diff --check` passed. The uploaded `pr-177970-fbb30e5-native-evidence` artifact contains environment, build, test, lint, formatting, and source-status logs; retention is **3 days**. The report and pinned source/workflow links preserve the results independently of that short-lived artifact.
- Prior authoring checks passed: `git diff --check`, `pnpm docs:list`; independent OpenClaw Auto Review was scoped-clean through P2, with static-context limitations. Earlier syntax-only checks on all eight changed Swift files passed but are superseded by the successful supported-toolchain native build. A separate Xcode 27.1/Swift 6.4 sandbox build hit availability errors in the unchanged protocol-generator plugin, reproduced with the base copy; it is not the successful VM/toolchain result.
- **Remaining gaps:** pristine-base red/green qualification, original real menu/settings/bridge incident reproduction, native-chat lifetime, real close/reopen/reconnect/concurrent-probe flows, and account renewal/change/expiry scenarios. The new tests require the draft’s constructor seams and have not been qualified on pristine base code. **This standalone exact-source fork run does not turn the upstream draft’s skipped native Swift job or CI gate into passing upstream checks.**

Simplification removed menu-private opening-task tracking. Net production delta: +86/-54 lines; regression file: +165 lines. The remaining growth records actual presentation demand in the existing fleet owner.

<details>
<summary>Safe macOS rerun and remaining qualification</summary>

Use a disposable macOS VM or CI worker with no operator credentials, configuration, or running Gateway, latest macOS, and Xcode 26.4+ / Swift 6.3. A temporary HOME on an ordinary desktop is not isolation. Follow [native test safety](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/552a5d7419c9c334db10b39b712dbfcd825797c6/docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md#run-native-tests-safely).

In a clean checkout of this draft head:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
scripts/install-swift-tools.sh .build/swift-tools
export PATH="$PWD/.build/swift-tools:$PATH"
scripts/lint-swift.sh macos
scripts/format-swift.sh macos
swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests
node scripts/test-macos-native.mts default --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --skip-build --filter 'SavedGatewayOpeningLifecycleTests|GatewayMenuStatusStoreTests|GatewayConnectionDashboardIdentityTests|DashboardBrowserSessionTests|GatewayConnectionControlTests'
```

For baseline comparison, use a separate disposable checkout at `552a5d7419c9c334db10b39b712dbfcd825797c6` and the same toolchain/launcher; run the existing suites (omit the new suite) and reproduce the first-open/menu-close flow there, then repeat on the draft. Passing existing baseline tests is not red/green regression proof. Do not copy the new test file alone onto base: its fixture constructor seams are absent. Deterministic red-on-base qualification and native confirmation of the original incident are explicitly outstanding, not replaced by static review.

The focused native build and tests now pass on the exact head above. Before removing draft status, complete the remaining cold menu and non-menu opens, cancellation/close/reopen, native chat, concurrent probes, reconnect, and credential/account lifecycle qualification. Do not run these suites against a personal desktop or existing Gateway.

</details>

Reported and requested by Jacqueline Henriksen; published as a draft at her request, with subsequent exact-head native validation linked above.

prs.title: fix(plugins): Doctor fails with EXDEV when home is on another filesystem
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor/setup can fail with `EXDEV` when an image-installed plugin's native companions and the OpenClaw home are on different filesystems.

## User Impact

Container users with a separate home/state mount can capture image-installed native plugin companions without the impossible cross-device hardlink. No state-directory move, database migration, configuration bypass, or plugin disablement is required.

## Change

Native companion capture compares the source and capture devices before selecting a hardlink. A device mismatch selects the existing guarded copy owner. Same-device hardlinks and the restricted retained-NPM reference fallback remain unchanged; source-boundary, destination-identity, content, and admission checks remain in place.

The real-filesystem regression now selects a writable directory on a verified different device from `/dev/shm`, `/tmp`, or `/var/tmp`. If none is usable, only this environment-dependent case explicitly skips with a prerequisite reason. It retains the actual device inequality, native/companion byte preservation, captured-device, source-link-count, and independent-realpath assertions. Missing, non-directory, permission-denied, and read-only candidate paths are prerequisites; unexpected filesystem errors still fail the test.

This is candidate-side capture behavior. Already-installed update/Doctor drivers retain their shipped behavior until replaced. There are no new flags or schemas, no weakened Doctor action authority, and no second capture implementation. Total delta against the original base: two production lines and 58 test lines added across two files.

## Evidence

### Real Linux regression

Original production red/green proof remains valid:

- Base `07e3328ed3f74333e80072af207890204c82fec4` plus the capture regression: 9 passed, 1 failed. The new case reached the real kernel `EXDEV` at `README.md` in `linkPluginSourceFile`.
- Original fixed source `50b6318585f2e06bc3fac4d0188d492599b981d2`: 10 passed, zero skipped across overlayfs source and tmpfs home. No mocked `fs.linkSync` failure in the real-device case.

Current candidate `b4be713c2e8b03e414ef3b95ec2285f1890ccc82` changes only the fixture prerequisite from that fixed head. Its production repair is byte-identical.

- Reproduced ClawSweeper's prerequisite finding on `50b6318`: `TMPDIR=/dev/shm` put source and destination on device 249; the original test failed `expected 249 not to be 249` before capture. File 60.08s; wrapper 71.83s.
- Repaired `TMPDIR=/dev/shm` case: passed actual cross-device capture and all retained assertions. File 76.82s; wrapper 84.06s. Nine unrelated cases were deselected by the focused selector.
- Entire repaired artifact/admission file with ordinary `/tmp`: **10 passed, zero skipped**. File 160.06s; wrapper 167.26s. The new cross-device case took 9.059s.
- Made `/dev/shm` genuinely unwritable to the test's UID 1000, with `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` on the fixture device. The selected case explicitly skipped: `requires a writable filesystem distinct from the image fixture`. The permission was restored after the run. This is a prerequisite outcome, not capture proof.

Linux x86_64 under Docker Desktop/Rosetta, Node 26.11.1, pnpm 12.12.1, UID/GID 1000, network disconnected during execution. Source/capture devices were kernel facts, not injected errors. Separate invocation-owned transform caches were used.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose

TMPDIR=/dev/shm OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose \
  -t 'captures image-installed native companions'
```

No sleeps, retries, weakened capture assertions, or test-only production seams were added. This is real capture/admission integration proof, not a performance benchmark. Existing persistence cases dominate file time. Current-head CI is recorded below; the local timings are not a CI performance claim.

## October 20 refresh audit

The source/copy owners and artifact test were unchanged between the original base and inspected upstream main `e4ac046c644698d75b983d728978243db4663f3a`; the PR remained mergeable. No rebase was performed just because main advanced.

Today's local downstream package was built from public fork commit `10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b`, incorporating selected upstream `2d03d5632a69d04181844f85b05d5509240dcc14` and this production repair. Both affected production owners match the PR source byte-for-byte:

- `plugin-native-namespace.ts`: SHA-256 `46d7aecd9f87c2d9d96f90e69acc29eb1bd554b9da4883f5b03250b807ae1480`.
- `plugin-source-file.ts`: SHA-256 `c9fdce99d981633508f1a31e3ba36b1ced36f18a456b7e323af60fc48e7b048b`.

This is downstream integration evidence, not an exact-head upstream PR package or upstream release claim. Today's published package inputs and accepted customer build were not modified.

## Installed-entry-point Doctor and upgrade proof

[Reproducible fixture, compact trace, full hashes and actual result artifacts](https://gist.github.com/ceckert/8444c8d992d138c576985851f27da074) are public. The distinction between the exact upstream regression and the installed downstream package is preserved in that evidence.

Resolved the current official npm `latest` to **2026.10.5**, build commit `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`; the isolated installation's lockfile matched registry integrity `sha512-9rCuXMweqVKZIK3KBtGcLzesz9G6+FmQ30lvwomRhmcNWDcOtlBoqdLbPditoJMuTP55jPqXpt1AA0L8tSzFHg==`. No global installation was changed.

Two isolated Linux arm64 runs exercised the installed downstream candidate CLI, Node 26.12.0, UID/GID 1000, network disabled. Image/plugin source was on overlayfs device 185; one unchanged home/state root was on exec-enabled tmpfs device 250. `TMPDIR` was inside that state root. A synthetic local plugin exposed the public Doctor config-repair contract and loaded the already-shipped `@openclaw/fs-safe-linux-arm64-gnu` native addon, with a real adjacent `README.md`. Normal `plugins install ... --force --accept-capabilities` created the actual install provenance; no receipt was fabricated or edited.

- **Fresh installed candidate:** the candidate CLI installed and configured the synthetic plugin, then `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 in **19.302s**. Seven real native-load observations reported 70 exports each from the captured addon on device 250, not source device 185. Actual native and README bytes matched their full SHA-256 values. The plugin setting, workspace path, and workspace Memory file bytes were unchanged.
- **Latest stable to candidate, same state root:** official stable `2026.10.5` / `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8` initialized the baseline with its installed Doctor, installed/configured the plugin through its real CLI, and retained the same home/state/workspace for the candidate. The installed candidate Doctor exited 0 in **20.028s**, with five real native-load observations from device 250 and the same content/settings/data checks passing. This replaces the earlier invalid copied-provenance fixture; it does not edit trust records or reseed failed state.

The observed native SHA-256 was `b67516e9f59b3935f42b0f9aae40faac801a84292c5da70692570c926b5bcd5a`; companion README SHA-256 was `ccbd05385a3badf1b9051e5ab69f631b82a2412ed907489f5da9f661cb67f33e`; the retained Memory sentinel SHA-256 was `682cea37d499876424052fae23f7cbab94d0a5c42a21b35addaf24f11138b78e`. Both runs required actual native load, different source/capture devices, unchanged bytes/settings/workspace, no plugin-repair warning, and exit 0; command completion alone was not accepted as proof.

Installed candidate identity was read from its shipped build info: `2026.10.5`, commit `10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b`, built `2026-10-20T13:05:32.187Z`. As explained above, this is downstream installed-entry-point integration with matching affected production owners, **not an exact b4be713 upstream PR-head package**, nor a complete npm-installer or setup-wizard verdict. Npm's dependency hooks remained blocked; only the inspected package-owned OpenClaw postinstall was explicitly run for the isolated stable prefix so its shipped prebuild inventory was complete. No global tools or published input were changed.

The qualification failures remain failures: initial source/capability confirmation refusals; metadata-only no-op fixtures with no native-load trace; a fixture whose copied install records correctly failed `provenance-invalid`; and a corrected split-filesystem fixture on a `noexec` tmpfs whose captured addon correctly failed `dlopen`. The latter reached real cross-device capture but was not called successful Doctor recovery. The positive runs used a fresh task-only exec-enabled tmpfs and naturally created provenance, not a loader/trust bypass. All proof containers were stopped afterward; evidence was retained.

The earlier local-source production types and targeted lint passed. Current formatting and `git diff --check` pass; a fresh independent P0–P2 review of the staged complete PR found no actionable issues. A new maintained Linux lint attempt stopped at its existing 300-second SDK-declaration prerequisite timeout under emulation; the host alternative refused external dependency links, and a private dependency copy encountered host `Too many open files in system`. None was bypassed or called a passing current lint check.

## Current review and CI

[Exact-head CI run 39443728718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39443728718) completed successfully on `b4be713c2e8b03e414ef3b95ec2285f1890ccc82` at 15:14:37 UTC on October 20: 35 successful jobs, including both UI shards, lint/type stripes and baseline ratchets. The separate authored-evidence heading check initially failed after this body update; its heading was corrected to the required template, and [replacement context run 39444829079](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39444829079) passed. Neither historical failure was erased or rerun merely for green.

[ClawSweeper's October 20 exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177968#issuecomment-6282263661) reports readiness 4/6, proof confidence 4/6, patch quality 5/6, zero findings, and no listed before-merge author action. It independently matched the affected downstream source owners and accepted the scoped installed-entry-point evidence; it could not fetch the linked gist in its review environment. The PR is ready for normal maintainer review, not claimed merged.

## Prior CI failure investigation

Prior-head run [39359944112](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39359944112) failed `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)`: `custodian-onboarding-locale.e2e.test.ts:50` timed out waiting for the onboarding heading (79 other tests passed). The maintained failure report classifies it **unknown**, because scheduled main run 39354695200 had no comparable job; it is not claimed inherited or fixed.

A bounded local attempt used the maintained UI E2E wrapper, the exact failed file, and real Linux Chromium. It failed in setup before executing the CI assertion because the prepared EXDEV checkout lacked Workboard development dependencies (`solid-js`, `@solidjs/compiler`, and `@openclaw/workboard-contract`). This is not a product verdict or passing local replay. No UI assertions, timeouts, or expectations were relaxed; no CI rerun was requested just for green. The later current-head UI jobs passed, but that does not establish the cause of the prior-head failure.

No live customer state, deployment, release, or accepted build was changed for this work.

prs.title: feat(mcp): per-request header provider for volatile turn attribution on OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Per-turn MCP attribution currently has to enter declarative server headers or the connection resolver. Declarative header changes invalidate the catalog; the reported Reef production measurement was **221 re-catalogs across 222 runs**. The existing connection resolver caches requester credentials for five minutes, and changed resolved headers rotate the connection. Neither path can provide fresh turn attribution while retaining a transport and its catalog.

This adds a separate plugin request-header provider for OpenClaw-owned MCP HTTP transports. Upstream main was checked at `7aaef70932b30f4d7410ae00aa65b07089de2ce0`; no equivalent provider existed.

**Deployment consumer.** The Reef embedder plugin (the same production deployment behind the measurement above) adopts this provider on release adoption: it moves `traceparent` and signed per-turn context headers off declarative server configuration and onto this seam, which retires the measured per-run re-catalog. Requester authentication stays entirely on the existing connection-resolver contract — this consumer sends attribution and turn-scoped credentials only, and its stable credentials are unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugins can attach `traceparent`, signed turn credentials, and optional direct-request credentials to individual MCP requests without rebuilding the catalog or connection. Stable authentication remains in static server configuration or the existing connection resolver.

The SDK infrastructure documentation includes registration and embedded-runtime usage. This contract covers OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports; external harness-native MCP clients need OpenClaw materialized tools to use it.

## Design

- Add `api.registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider({ serverName, resolve })`, following connection-resolver registration conventions. Resolver and header-provider registrations share per-server plugin ownership, and the connection resolver is authoritative regardless of registration order: a foreign provider is rejected when the resolver already exists and displaced (removed, error diagnostic on the provider's plugin) when the resolver registers later. Registry state is identical in both orders, so a declared server with a resolver is never partitioned as static.
- Only the host binds run identity. The embedded backend binds MCP attribution to the admitted run's actual `sessionId`/`sessionKey`/`runId` (internal `bindMcpRequestRun`), and the binding is revoked when that run settles. A context the host did not issue (forged) or whose run has settled (stale/reassigned) is dropped: the provider is not called and no volatile headers are sent. The public export from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` is `runWithMcpRequestMetadata(metadata, callback)` — caller tracing metadata only (e.g. `traceparent`), never identity.
- Capture only MCP attribution when materializing tools. Each retained tool/resource/prompt executor opens its own operation scope, preserving attribution under overlapping acquisitions and calls without capturing unrelated cancellation or runtime authority.
- Resolve volatile headers immediately before actual guarded HTTP fetches, including same-origin redirects and authentication/RPC retries. Streamable HTTP and SSE POST/EventSource paths share this boundary. Header values never enter server configuration, catalog identity, or the resolver rotation digest.
- Keep configured headers, authentication, and MCP protocol fields authoritative. Scope provider headers to the configured origin; register returned values and bare bearer tokens for secret redaction. Bound provider resolution to ten seconds and report provider failures without exposing plugin error contents.

## Correctness

Each operation owns an immutable context. Missing context explicitly clears inherited attribution and skips the provider. No transport stores a mutable latest-turn header map. Provider results are freshly merged into a new request header object and are not retained for redirect replay.

Initial SSE discovery can carry its discovery context. Shared streamable notification GETs and legacy SSE reconnects carry no volatile attribution. The streamable initialized-notification send has a short-lived scope so its shared stream parser and reconnect timers cannot retain the opening turn, including reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`. Resumable RPC streams retain their own still-active operation context. Completed scopes cannot supply headers to background callbacks.

Static authentication, requester credential revalidation/rotation, genuine configuration invalidation, `tools/list_changed`, and transport-close recovery retain their existing owners and behavior.

## Evidence

### Guarded caller-authority revalidation (Rev 24 P1, head `34a4b55ad`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper Rev 24).** `fetchWithSsrFGuard` asserts the captured guarded caller authority (`captureGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`, e.g. a live cron-root claim) *before* invoking the transport `fetchImpl`. The header wrapper is that `fetchImpl` and awaits `provider.resolve()`, so authority revoked during resolution was not re-checked before stable credentials and volatile headers reached the server.

**Fix.** `withMcpRequestHeaders` captures the guarded assertion on entry and re-asserts it immediately before dispatch, alongside the existing abort and run-context checks. A revoked caller gets the assertion's own error, and no request is sent.

**Final-effect proof.** The real-runtime e2e adds a call under `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` whose MCP run stays active. Caller authority is revoked while the provider is resolving. The call is rejected, and the recording loopback server's request count is unchanged (no request for `revoked_authority_operation`). **Regression-before-repair:** with the re-assertion removed, the same scenario fails with `promise resolved "{ content: [ ... ] }" instead of rejecting`, meaning the real server received and answered the revoked call. A matching unit case (`mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) fails without the fix and passes with it.

Redacted terminal capture (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text
[pr154043-proof] allowed: real tools/call arrived with volatile header present
[pr154043-proof] canceled: rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged; pending send settled
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
[pr154043-proof] revoked authority: provider resolved, caller authority revoked mid-resolution; rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

At this head: focused suites 8 files / 156 tests passed; core `tsgo` passed; timeout-race ratchet clean for PR files; formatting and lint clean.

### Run-identity authority + final-I/O proof (Rev 22 security item, head `a6194b291`)

**Concern (ClawSweeper Rev 22).** The public `runWithMcpRequestContext` accepted caller-supplied `sessionId`/`runId`, and the documented provider signs those IDs, so a caller could assert a foreign run and obtain a signed header at final HTTP I/O. A captured context also stayed usable after its run settled.

**Fix — bind signed identity to admitted runs (the recommended option).**
- Identity is issued only by the host: `runEmbeddedAttemptWithBackend` calls the internal `bindMcpRequestRun` with the admitted run's identity, keeping enclosing caller metadata.
- Each issued context carries run authority that is revoked when the run settles. `getMcpRequestContext()` returns nothing for a revoked or never-issued context, so the provider is never invoked for it. A run that settles while headers resolve is refused before dispatch by the existing `MCP request context expired` check.
- The public SDK export narrows to `runWithMcpRequestMetadata` (metadata only). Plugins and embedded callers can no longer name a session or run.

**Final-effect proof.** `test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts` now also drives, on the same real MCP SDK client + guarded streamable-HTTP transport + recording loopback server:
- **Foreign:** a forged frozen context `{ runId: "victim-run" }` and the public SDK helper each reach the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees `victim-run`.
- **Reassigned/settled:** a context captured inside a run that has since settled reaches the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees it.

**Regression-before-repair.** With the old trust semantics temporarily restored (any context accepted, no revocation), the proof fails at final I/O. The server received a signed header for the forged run:

```text
- Expected
+ Received
  {
-   "attribution": undefined,
+   "attribution": "synthetic-victim-run",
    "rpcMethod": "tools/call",
  }
 ❯ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts:193:75
```

Redacted terminal capture after the fix (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text

[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O 61ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Unit coverage (`src/agents/mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) adds: forged identity never resolves headers, captured context revoked after its run settles, and a run settling mid-resolution refuses dispatch. `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers.test.ts` now holds each turn open across acquisition and execution, as a host run does, and asserts that a settled turn's executor sends no attribution. On the merged head (current main `3f7689e64`): focused suites (`mcp-request-headers`, `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime{,.request-headers}`, `mcp-transport`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-http-fetch`, `backend`, requester-connect, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers`) 10 files / 159 tests passed; both PR e2e proofs passed; core `tsgo` passed; `plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed (budget pinned to exactly this PR's two exports); formatting and lint clean. The merge resolved main's `mcp-http-fetch.ts` redirect-policy refactor by applying the provider wrap inside the shared builder.

### Registration-order fix + authority-chain proof (head `2587f4f3`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper P1, Rev 8).** `hasMcpServerOwnerConflict` was first-registration-wins across both seams: a request-header provider registered first by plugin A caused plugin B's later `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` for the same server to be rejected. `partitionMcpServersByConnectionScope` then found no resolver and classified the declared server as **static**, exposing its configured connection to requesters the resolver would have excluded. The PR's own registrar test pinned that behavior.

**Fix.** The connection resolver is authoritative regardless of order. `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` still fails closed against a different plugin's resolver; against a different plugin's *provider* it now displaces it — the provider entry is removed and an error diagnostic is reported on the provider's plugin (`MCP server request header provider for "<name>" displaced: connection resolver registered by plugin "<resolver plugin>" owns requester admission`). `registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider` is unchanged (rejected when a different plugin owns either seam). Final registry state is identical in both registration orders. `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure.md` states the rule.

**Regression proof, unit** (`src/plugins/registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers.test.ts`, `it.each(["provider","resolver"])`): with the registrar fix reverted, the provider-first case fails —

```text
AssertionError: expected [ { level: 'error', …(3) } ] to deep equally contain ObjectContaining{…}

- Expected:
ObjectContaining {
  "level": "error",
  "message": StringContaining "displaced",
  "pluginId": "plugin-a",
}

+ Received:
[
  {
    "level": "error",
    "message": "MCP server connection resolver for \"user-mail\" rejected: already registered by plugin \"plugin-a\"",
    "pluginId": "plugin-b",
    "source": "/plugins/plugin-b/index.ts",
  },
]
```

— and passes with the fix (5/5). Both orders additionally assert, under `withPluginRuntimeRegistryScope`, that `partitionMcpServersByConnectionScope` puts `user-mail` in `resolverRequesterServerNames` and `staticServers` is empty.

**Authority-chain proof, real transports** (`test/pr154043-registration-order-proof.e2e.test.ts`, no transport/SDK mocks). plugin-a registers a request-header provider for `user-mail`; plugin-b registers a requester-scoped connection resolver that returns `{ url: <loopback>, headers: { Authorization: "Bearer proof-token" } }` only for `allowed-requester` and `null` otherwise. The declared config is `url: "https://placeholder.invalid/mcp"`; the loopback (`startRequesterScopedMcpProofServer`) 404s without the bearer and records every request. Driven through `materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRun` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`. In **both** orders: `user-mail` partitions as resolver-scoped, never static; the allowed requester materializes tools and executes `requester_probe`, and every loopback request carried the bearer and none carried plugin-a's header; an excluded requester and a run with no `requesterSenderId` get no tools and the loopback request count does not move; plugin-a's provider is never invoked.

With the registrar fix reverted, the provider-first case fails at the static-partition assertion (the exact exposure):

```text
- Expected
+ Received

+ {

+     "url": "https://placeholder.invalid/mcp",

+ }
```


**Merge with main.** Branch merged `upstream/main` (`a08479ac`, plain merge commit). Verification at this head: core `tsgo` 0 errors; unit batch (`agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `backend`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-request-headers`, `mcp-transport`, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers`, `mcp-connection-resolver`) 7 files / 193 passed; `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers` 2 passed; e2e proofs 2 files / 3 passed; `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` 16 passed; `pnpm config:docs:check` OK; full `pnpm lint` (core + extensions) passed; `pnpm check:changed` green through the SDK surface budget, plugin boundaries, wrapper shadowing and core typecheck (the only failure, `typecheck core tests`, is two `assertReliabilityForcedExit` import errors in `src/infra/package-update-activation-*.test.ts`, present on untouched upstream main).

### Cancellation lifecycle fix + real-runtime proof (head `15fdd821`)

The prior head had a defect at the dispatch boundary: an operation canceled while `provider.resolve()` was awaited settles its attribution scope, and the fallback then forwarded the request **without** volatile headers on the retained transport — final I/O after cancellation, under stable connection credentials. The dispatch point now rejects an expired attributed operation with a content-free error instead of falling back; the shared-transport abort check is unchanged. Regression-before-repair was verified both ways: the new unit case fails on the old expression (fetch dispatches), and temporarily restoring the old expression makes the runtime proof's server-request-count assertion fail (expected 5, received 6).

### Original evidence (unchanged)

- Real HTTP and SSE tests send two distinct contexts through **one retained runtime/transport**, overlap acquisitions and asynchronous header resolution, execute retained tools in reverse completion order, and invoke a contextless tool under an unrelated ambient context. Wire assertions cover discovery headers, distinct turn credentials, unchanged static authorization, unchanged fingerprint, and exactly one initialize/tools-list cycle.
- Registrar ownership tests cover same-plugin provider/resolver coexistence, foreign-provider rejection, and (at the current head) resolver displacement of a foreign provider in both registration orders.
- Transport tests cover per-hop header refresh, cross-origin stripping, initial SSE discovery, contextless EventSource reconnects, notification reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`, and attributed RPC resumptions.
- Provider/backend/registry tests cover copied immutable metadata, context expiration and clearing, secret registration, bounded failures, network error preservation, host identity binding, and registration ownership.

prs.title: fix: stop model fallback on transcript admission conflicts
prs.body:
Related: #177909

## What Problem This Solves

A transcript idempotency conflict can be retried and sent through the cross-provider fallback chain even though changing models cannot resolve it.

## User Impact

The run stops on the original transcript conflict without repeating the turn, trying another provider, or suspending the session for a model failure. The underlying transcript admission mismatch still needs investigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the transcript owner's existing conflict message in the shared terminal-error classifier already used by assistant retries and model fallback. No change to compaction, admission, or replay semantics.

## Evidence

On main `8082bfa81ab340099fcb09d36f8188b5666b3db7`, the embedded-entry regression observed 3 attempts for a thrown admission conflict and 12 for an assistant conflict, instead of one. Both existing keyed-turn controls passed. After the fix, all four entry regressions passed, preserving the original error and avoiding session suspension. The complete failover-error unit file passes (53 tests), including direct, cause-wrapped, and aggregate conflicts.

Validation used Node 26.11.1 on Windows with the existing mocked attempt boundary and isolated real auth/session storage; no live provider or paid API calls. Commands:

- `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 27 passed, including all four transcript regressions; 9 other cases failed during SQLite temporary-file cleanup with Windows `EBUSY`. This is not a full-file pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/failover-error.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 53 passed.
- Changed-file core lint, format, `git diff --check`, and targeted classifier typecheck through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` passed.

The initial E2E prebuild was skipped because Canvas assets were unavailable; that runner compiled its current-source subprocess artifacts. The later shipped-CLI proof below used a complete frozen-lockfile install and successful production CLI builds on both commits. The supported optional A2UI asset skip was used; runtime and SQLite guards remained enabled. No live Slack, restart, compaction, or full Gateway validation is claimed. Independent isolated autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

## Shipped CLI proof (October 20)

Ran the same isolated offline fixture on parent `8082bfa81ab340099fcb09d36f8188b5666b3db7`, then restored and rebuilt this PR's unchanged head `9f5d5449b44353e8c0a2b6584fdfb5ae74be27f6`. Both builds used the supported `pnpm openclaw --help` entry, Node 26.11.1, and pinned pnpm 12.12.1 on Windows.

The real embedded CLI agent had primary `openai/proof-primary` and cross-provider fallback `groq/proof-fallback`. Both routes pointed to an isolated local HTTP/SSE response server. No SDK/runner mock threw the error. A public synchronous `before_message_write` hook assigned the same `proof-assistant-collision` idempotency key to every assistant message. The first CLI turn committed synthetic reply A; the second produced reply B and the actual SQLite transcript owner rejected its different bytes under the admitted key. The runtime then tried to record an assistant error message; the hook gave it the same key, causing a second genuine owner rejection to escape the attempt. This deliberately exercises the thrown-error retry/fallback path. It is a double persistence rejection, not a single write.

Each phase ran through the shipped command, with isolated home/config/state/workspace paths:

```sh
pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent proof --session-key agent:proof:runtime-proof --message seed --json --timeout 30
pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent proof --session-key agent:proof:runtime-proof --message conflict --json --timeout 30
```

Observed during the second turn only (seed succeeded on both versions):

| Observation | Parent | PR head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Primary provider HTTP requests | 1 | 1 |
| Cross-provider fallback HTTP requests | 1 | 0 |
| Model-assistant persistence-hook invocations | 2 | 1 |
| Total assistant persistence-hook invocations, including error records | 4 | 2 |
| CLI exit code | 1 | 1 |
