prs.title: fix(ui): Show earlier loses keyboard focus while older history loads
prs.body:
Related: #149618

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a keyboard user who focuses the chat's "Show earlier" control loses focus to the page body as soon as older history starts loading.

## User Impact

User impact: keyboard and screen reader users stay on the control while older messages load (the focused control's name changes to "Loading earlier…"), and can press it again as "Show earlier" once the page lands, instead of being thrown back to the start of the page.

## Why This Change Was Made

The control is now marked busy with `aria-disabled` instead of the native `disabled` attribute, and ignores activation while loading. Native `disabled` makes Chromium blur the focused button at its next rendering step; `aria-disabled` keeps it focusable and still announces it as unavailable. That component guard is what keeps a press while busy from sending anything: the history loader's own guard only covers older-history loads, while the same busy state also covers chat loading, catalog loading and the cron run transcript. The busy look is unchanged (the only `:disabled` style was the hover suppression, now keyed on `aria-disabled`).

| Case | Expected outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Focus on the control, older history starts loading (Enter or the automatic load when the control scrolls into view) | Focus stays on the control; it reads "Loading earlier…", `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-disabled="true"` |
| Enter or click while loading | Ignored; no second `chat.history` request |
| Load finishes and more history remains | Focus stays on the same control, now "Show earlier", active again |
| Load finishes and history is exhausted | Not changed here: the boundary still unmounts and focus is not moved. That needs its own intentional focus transition (see the issue triage) and is left for a follow-up |
| Cron run transcript, which reuses the same boundary | Same component, same behavior; its existing paging test still passes |

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine at the staged tree, base `0631ad4046a`.

Update 2026-10-20: the branch was merged up to main `7d46d4197c4` (one test-file conflict in `chat-transcript-controller.test.tsx`, resolved by keeping the upstream file and re-applying the `aria-disabled` assertion; no production-file change). Owning lanes re-run at the merge head: `chat-transcript-controller` + `chat-view` 146 passed, `chat-pane-history*` 62 passed, `chat-history-loading.e2e` 4 passed (Chromium), `run-transcript.e2e` 5 passed, madge 0 cycles, `tsgo:ui` clean.

**Build.** Control UI built from this tree by the repo's bundled e2e lane (`pnpm test:ui:e2e`), Playwright Chromium headless, mock Gateway with `chat.history` held until released. Synthetic transcript ("Conversation message 41..80", 40 older messages available).

**Behaviour.** Same scenario on both arms: focus the "Show earlier" control, press Enter, wait for the held load, press Enter again, release the load. Values below were read from the DOM with `page.evaluate` two animation frames after each step.

Before (base production code):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9de7ef8e99c4a2bcaa3cfd5e72d9f747d3c4a0be/pr-8-show-earlier-focus/before.png)

- While loading: `document.activeElement` = `body`; button text "Loading earlier…", `aria-busy="true"`, `disabled` attribute present.
- Focus log: `focusout BUTTON.chat-history-boundary__action -> null`.
- After the load lands: `document.activeElement` = `body`; button reads "Show earlier".

After (this PR):

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9de7ef8e99c4a2bcaa3cfd5e72d9f747d3c4a0be/pr-8-show-earlier-focus/after.png)

- While loading: `document.activeElement` = `button.chat-history-boundary__action`, matches `:focus-visible`; text "Loading earlier…", `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, no `disabled` attribute. No focusout events.
- Accessibility snapshot of the boundary while loading (Playwright `ariaSnapshot`, read from the DOM):
  ```
  - button "Loading earlier…" [disabled]:
    - status: Loading earlier…
  ```
  Playwright prints `[disabled]` for both native `disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`, so this line is identical on both arms; the difference is that the button now keeps focus.
- `chat.history` requests after the second Enter: 1.
- After the load lands: `document.activeElement` = `button.chat-history-boundary__action`; text "Show earlier", `aria-busy="false"`, no `aria-disabled`.

### Real Gateway

The issue asks for the corrected flow on a real Gateway with Tab-triggered loading ("Source checks or mock-only tests will not substitute for reproducing the corrected real flow"; "Verify Tab-triggered automatic loading, explicit activation, slow/error recovery, repeated activation, and exhaustion"). This is that flow, on this tree:

- Gateway: `pnpm build` of this tree, started in process by the repo's real-Gateway e2e helper (`createOpenClawTestInstance`, the same setup as `ui/src/e2e/chat-loading-performance.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`), loopback, token auth, no model provider. It serves the Control UI it built. One session seeded with 5,200 synthetic messages ("Focus proof message 1." to "Focus proof message 5200.") through `appendTranscriptMessages`. The UI opens on the 80-message tail; older pages are 1,000 messages.
- Browser: Playwright headless, 1280×720, service workers blocked. Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and WebKit 27.2.
- Arms: before = the two production files reverted to the base and the UI rebuilt (served bundle `/assets/index-yGT8cdac.js`, sha256 `5673761f165c…`); after = this PR (`/assets/index-CqpvEuwf.js`, sha256 `05b94312b51c…`). The bundle path and hash were read back from the page in each run.
- A scratch spec (not part of this PR) drives the page and records one line per change of `document.activeElement`, the boundary's text, `aria-busy`, `aria-disabled` and `disabled`, sampled every animation frame, plus every `focusin`/`focusout`, plus every `chat.history` request and response on the real WebSocket with its request id. Lines below are copied whole from those records; `ms` is relative to the start of each cell.

**Cell 1, Tab-triggered automatic load, no Enter (Chromium).** From `body`, Tab 26 times: sidebar, chat header, `div.chat-thread`, the position marker, then "Show earlier", which sits above the viewport. Focus scrolls it into view and the automatic load starts by itself.

Before:
```
record {"ms": 336, "kind": "focusin", "target": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "relatedTarget": "button.chat-position-rail__marker"}
record {"ms": 391, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 80}

frame {"ms": 413, "dir": "sent", "id": "54:b1a077b0-b447-4766-898f-d471007318a7", "method": "chat.history", "sessionMatches": true, "limit": 1000, "offset": 80, "maxBytes": 3145728}

record {"ms": 484, "kind": "state", "active": "body", "activeIsAction": false, "focusVisible": false, "label": "Loading earlier…", "ariaBusy": "true", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": true, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 1080}
record {"ms": 588, "kind": "state", "active": "body", "activeIsAction": false, "focusVisible": false, "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 1080}
```

After:
```
record {"ms": 390, "kind": "focusin", "target": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "relatedTarget": "button.chat-position-rail__marker"}
record {"ms": 429, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 80}
record {"ms": 450, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Loading earlier…", "ariaBusy": "true", "ariaDisabled": "true", "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 80}
frame {"ms": 451, "dir": "sent", "id": "54:5b33f8eb-f56b-44ee-827d-d5192e28732c", "method": "chat.history", "sessionMatches": true, "limit": 1000, "offset": 80, "maxBytes": 3145728}
frame {"ms": 495, "dir": "recv", "id": "54:5b33f8eb-f56b-44ee-827d-d5192e28732c", "method": "chat.history", "ok": true, "messages": 1000, "hasMore": true, "nextOffset": 1080}
frame {"ms": 495, "dir": "sent", "id": "55:7e267176-bd45-4c3a-99bb-a0fabca68495", "method": "chat.history", "sessionMatches": true, "limit": 1000, "offset": 1080, "maxBytes": 3145728}
record {"ms": 512, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Loading earlier…", "ariaBusy": "true", "ariaDisabled": "true", "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 1080}
record {"ms": 639, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 1080}
```
No `focusout` from the control in the after cell. On both arms the requests are the same: offset 80 (applied, 80 to 1,080 messages) and the existing next-page prefetch at offset 1,080.

**Cell 2, explicit activation (Chromium, after only).** On the landed page from cell 1, with focus still on "Show earlier", press Enter, Enter, Space. Messages go from 1,080 to 3,080 with two requests (offset 2,080, then the prefetch at offset 3,080) and focus stays on the control:
```
record {"ms": 83, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Loading earlier…", "ariaBusy": "true", "ariaDisabled": "true", "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 2080}
record {"ms": 324, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 3080}
```
The before arm has nothing to press here: focus is already on `body` (`"focusedBeforeEnter": false`).

**Cell 3, slow response and repeated activation (Chromium).** Same real Gateway and Tab path, but the browser holds each older-page response for 4,000 ms (Playwright `routeWebSocket` passthrough to the real Gateway; nothing is mocked or edited). Two animation frames after `aria-busy="true"` the page is captured, then Enter and Space are pressed while busy.

Before: `{"activeIsAction": false, "active": "body", "label": "Loading earlier…", "ariaBusy": "true", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": true, "focusVisible": false}`; after the load the composer (`textarea`) is focused, not the control.

![real-gateway-busy-before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/e18d88d23ef91e9c9ead1f93b9166c1c9e7c5af5/pr-8-show-earlier-focus/real-gateway-busy-before.png)

After: `{"activeIsAction": true, "active": "button", "label": "Loading earlier…", "ariaBusy": "true", "ariaDisabled": "true", "disabledAttr": false, "focusVisible": true}`; `chat.history` requests sent before the busy presses 1, after them 1; after the load `{"activeIsAction": true, "active": "button", "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null}`.

![real-gateway-busy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/e18d88d23ef91e9c9ead1f93b9166c1c9e7c5af5/pr-8-show-earlier-focus/real-gateway-busy.png)

```

frame {"ms": 426, "marker": "holding response 50:cb566e29-50c2-4e3f-acc9-3678bba1ea5b for 4000 ms"}

frame {"ms": 4428, "dir": "recv", "id": "50:cb566e29-50c2-4e3f-acc9-3678bba1ea5b", "method": "chat.history", "ok": true, "messages": 1000, "hasMore": true, "nextOffset": 1080}
frame {"ms": 4441, "dir": "sent", "id": "51:2c0bc7fe-21cb-45c0-aa6e-95352c145514", "method": "chat.history", "sessionMatches": true, "limit": 1000, "offset": 1080, "maxBytes": 3145728}
record {"ms": 4504, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 1080}
```
The second request at 4,441 ms is the existing next-page prefetch after the first page lands, not a press while busy.

Wall time: 57 to 80 s per real-Gateway run, including the e2e lane's own UI build and the Gateway start (test 26.8 to 29.2 s for the three cells). Full records for all four runs: `evidence/round3/focus-records.txt`.

### WebKit

The Solid testing guide (`.agents/skills/solid/references/testing.md`) says "Overlay and focus changes need WebKit proof as well as Chromium". Both proofs above were repeated in Playwright WebKit 27.2 on the same machine. The shared e2e suite only launches Chromium, so a scratch three-line launcher switch (not part of this PR, diff in `evidence/round3/logs/webkit-suite.diff`) launches WebKit instead; every WebKit run printed `[cui8] launched webkit 27.2`.

**The PR's e2e file in WebKit** (`pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts`, mock Gateway, service workers blocked):

```
after, run 1:      ✓ keeps keyboard focus on the earlier-history action while older history loads 1027ms
                   Tests  4 passed (4)
after, run 2:      ✓ keeps keyboard focus on the earlier-history action while older history loads 1090ms
                   Tests  4 passed (4)
after, run 3:      ✓ keeps keyboard focus on the earlier-history action while older history loads 1080ms
                   Tests  4 passed (4)
before (production files at the base, tests kept):
     × keeps keyboard focus on the earlier-history action while older history loads 1030ms
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ ui/src/e2e/chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts:116:35
      Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
```
WebKit fails the base at the same busy focus check as Chromium. Wall time 18 to 19 s per run (15.55 to 16.35 s test duration). The `PushManager.getSubscription` stall seen in Playwright WebKit after an authenticated connect did not occur: these suites block service workers.

DOM readings from the first round's screenshot spec in WebKit (mock Gateway, held `chat.history`, two animation frames after the busy state):
- Before: `"activeElement": "body"`, `"ariaBusy": "true"`, `"disabledAttr": true`, focus log `focusout BUTTON.chat-history-boundary__action -> null`; after the load `"activeElement": "body"`.
- After: `"activeElement": "button.chat-history-boundary__action"`, `"activeMatchesFocusVisible": true`, `"ariaBusy": "true"`, `"ariaDisabled": "true"`, `"disabledAttr": false`, no focusout; `chat.history` requests after the second Enter: 1; after the load the same button is focused, "Show earlier".

**The real Gateway in WebKit.** Same harness, same seeded session. WebKit's Tab order does not reach "Show earlier" on either arm: from the position marker the next stop is the composer (`"unreachedTabStops": [..., "button.chat-position-rail__marker [Synthetic focus assistant, marker 80 of 80]", "textarea [Chat composer]", ...]`). The control is focusable (`tabIndex` 0, visible, not inert) but sits 8,717 px above the viewport in the scrolled thread; this is the same at the base and is not changed here. In WebKit the cells therefore focus the control with `focus()`, which scrolls it into view the way Tab does in Chromium and starts the same automatic load.

Before, cell 1:
```
record {"ms": 353, "kind": "state", "active": "button.chat-history-boundary__action", "activeIsAction": true, "focusVisible": true, "label": "Show earlier", "ariaBusy": "false", "ariaDisabled": null, "disabledAttr": false, "boundaryPresent": true, "messages": 80}

| `git diff --check` | clean |

## Gaps, stated plainly

- History exhaustion is not handled: when the last page lands, the boundary unmounts and a focused control is still lost. That needs a deliberate focus target and is out of scope here.
- Covered: the mock-Gateway e2e and the real Gateway, each in headless Chromium 156 and Playwright WebKit 27.2 on macOS. Not covered: Firefox, physical Safari or the macOS app's WKWebView, mobile/touch, and a screen reader run; the announcement claim rests on the accessibility snapshot.
- In WebKit, Tab from the position marker goes to the composer and never reaches "Show earlier" while it sits above the viewport, on the base and with this PR alike. The WebKit real-Gateway cells therefore focus the control with `focus()` (which scrolls it into view and starts the same automatic load); the Tab-triggered cell is Chromium only. Why WebKit skips it is not investigated here.
- The real-Gateway slow-response cell delays the real responses in the browser (4,000 ms), it does not slow the Gateway. Error recovery through the full flow is not exercised, and the real-Gateway runs are one run per arm and browser, not a frequency measurement.
- The regression waits two animation frames before each focus read. Measured without that wait: the base still reports the disabled button as focused during the busy check, so the red arm passes that check and fails only at the post-load focus check; the fixed code stays green either way (one red run and three green runs without the wait). With the wait the red arm fails at the busy check. A future engine change in Chromium's focus fixup timing could move where the red arm fails.
- The committed test does not cover the automatic load started by scrolling the control into view; it isolates Enter as the trigger so the request count is deterministic. That path is shown on the real Gateway above (cell 1) from a scratch spec that is not part of this PR.

All four are mounted only while an error is set, which is the case `role="alert"` announces. prs.title: fix(plugins): admit authenticated owner into run generation
prs.body:
## Summary

- preserve the authenticated in-process plugin owner when an admitted agent run acquires its prepared model-runtime generation
- load only that owner alongside the selected model backend
- keep prepared-generation hook isolation authoritative; this revision removes the earlier root/request registry overlay
- include the owner constraint in generation reuse, owner identity, lifecycle matching, and workspace grouping

## Root cause

The Gateway already authenticated `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId` and persisted the owner on plugin-created sessions, but `prepareAgentRunDispatch` passed only the selected model backend into `acquireAgentRunPreparedModelRuntime`. The resulting generation contained the provider backend but omitted the initiating plugin's `llm_input` and `llm_output` hooks.

## Verification

- prepared runtime owner-selection suite: 27/27
- real prepared-registry loading suite: 9/9
- focused Gateway propagation assertion verifies the authenticated owner reaches runtime acquisition
- formatting and oxlint pass on all changed source and test files
- runtime bundle build passes under Node 24

The registry-loading regression uses the real plugin loader and hook runner, and verifies an authenticated owner's `llm_output` hook fires from an otherwise narrower prepared generation.

prs.title: fix: ephemeral nodes fail to reconnect after setup code expires
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A provider that replays the original `connect <setup-code> --ephemeral` command after enrollment cannot reconnect once that code expires, even when the node still has a valid saved pairing. The CLI rejects the expired envelope before the existing credential owner can apply its saved-token recovery policy.

## User Impact

That narrow replay path can reconnect to the same Gateway using the saved device token. Ordinary cloud-worker resume already uses a separate `node run --ephemeral` path and is unchanged. Missing, invalid, or revoked device credentials do not gain authority; changed saved Gateway targets remain rejected. Manual enrollment, service/session-host modes, and join URLs still require an unexpired setup credential. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow expired decoding only for direct ephemeral setup codes and forward the expiry to the existing node-host runner. That owner discards expired bootstrap auth and suppresses ambient shared credentials when recovering the saved pairing. This adds no new credential store or parallel authentication policy.

## Evidence

[Inspectable real-Gateway proof and complete reproducer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177880#issuecomment-6280840860) include sanitized CLI/Gateway output, the wire trace, and the result receipt:

- Valid bootstrap enrollment saved a real node token; expired-envelope replay then authenticated with only that device token, despite valid ambient shared credentials.
- A real `device.token.revoke` RPC revoked that same token. Replaying it produced one rejected handshake (`AUTH_DEVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH` / `device_token_mismatch`) before node admission, with no bootstrap/shared fallback. Post-revocation admissions: zero.
- All seven proof child processes settled, loopback listeners closed, and disposable state was removed.

Before the production fix, the regression failed with `Pairing setup code has expired.` while all five refusal cases passed. On repair head `294b304573a668f802e23c899123919466f1461e`:

- 55 focused tests passed under the pinned Bun fork: reconnect, existing connect CLI, node-host runner, and runner shutdown.
- All six reconnect cases also passed under Node.
- CLI graph typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet, and diff checks passed.

## Review Repair

The test now preserves the real runtime module's exports while overriding `defaultRuntime`. Its cleanup selects the foreground runner's last-registered SIGTERM handler instead of an earlier import/setup listener. No production authentication code changed in this repair; no timeout was increased or assertion weakened.

The original Linux CI log shows a successful connection before the 120-second timeout. That hang was not reproduced on macOS; fresh Linux CI must confirm the cleanup correction resolves it. Clawsweeper re-review and exact-head CI are pending.

The real proof exercises the source Gateway, registered CLI, node runtime, native SQLite, real RPCs, and loopback WebSockets with deterministic expiry. It does not establish packaged-launcher, cloud-provider/worker-lease lifecycle, Linux, or model-turn coverage. The six-case regression uses a fixed remote peer and inert command capabilities.

Local Auto Review returned HTTP 401 and was explicitly waived by the maintainer for this patch. No successful local Auto Review is claimed. No merge or auto-merge is requested.

prs.title: feat(cron): add the scheduled-run execution context (no behavior change)
prs.body:
Related: #178812
Related: #178811

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled runs decide their tools, owner status and resources in dozens of separate places that disagree with each other, and there is no single value describing what one occurrence of an automation is allowed to do.

## User Impact

User impact: none yet. This adds the scheduled-run execution context and builds it for every isolated cron occurrence, but nothing reads it. Later PRs switch each consumer to it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `src/cron/execution-context.ts` is a pure builder. From a stored job and facts read at admission (parent session row, a fresh requester check), it derives one occurrence's principal, placement, authority, tool policy, resource scopes and inference account.
  - A job linked to the exact conversation that created it (`sourceConversation` or a stored operator source) becomes a child of that conversation.
  - Jobs that store only a parent session key keep every legacy decision. So do operator-created jobs.
  - A parent-linked job with no recorded requester gets no owner authority.
- `src/cron/execution-context-admission.ts` mints the context per prompt-executor attempt and binds it to the admitted run. For parent-linked jobs, it holds the parent's session generation, so the context's `assertCurrent` fails once the parent is reset or removed; the lease is released when the admission closes. Minting errors become a `fail` result and never fail the run.
- `src/cron/admission-source.ts` holds the existing admission-source rule, moved unchanged so the timer and the builder share one owner.
- `src/cron/execution-context-projection.ts` reproduces what the existing code decides for a stored job and labels each difference from the context: `equal`, `gain-intended`, `gain-unexpected`, `loss`, `retarget` or `pause`. A later Doctor check will reuse it.
- `scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts` is a development script, not shipped. It copies a Gateway's state and agent session databases into a private temp directory with SQLite's online backup, replays every stored job against the copies, prints the labels, and can emit anonymized job shapes. The live databases are only read.
- `src/cron/execution-context.fixtures.test.ts` pins the builder and projection results for the shapes the replay found, so other installs are covered by tests rather than runtime diagnostics.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** 8 files, 114 tests pass (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`). The run covers the builder, minting, fixtures, and the existing cron tool-policy, tools-allow, message-tool-policy, manual-tool-authority and session-identity suites.
- **Static replay on a real Gateway's state copy:** 86 non-main jobs replayed. Every field is `equal` except on the 3 jobs with an exact parent link, which show only `gain-intended` (memory, automations) and `retarget` (board, event target). No `gain-unexpected`, no `loss`, no `pause`.
- **QA lab (mock-openai), existing scheduling scenarios:**
  - 8 pass: one-minute ping, natural fire no duplicate, single run no duplicate, spawn-only child delivery, send then continue, blocked outcome, condition watcher, failed-tool finalization.
  - `cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation` and `cron-empty-response-after-write-recovery` fail. They fail identically on unmodified `origin/main`, so this PR did not cause them.
- **`pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`:** format, lint, both typecheck lanes, import cycles, the SAFETY-comment and mock-export ratchets and the other guards pass. Four checks fail only on files this PR does not touch:
  - the max-lines ratchet (three `ui/src` files);
  - the core test-shard root budget (`plugins-platform`);
  - the deprecated-API guard (`src/infra/outbound/delivery-completion.shard-test-support.ts`);
  - the dead-export scan (`src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts`, `src/transcripts/capture.ts` and three test-support files).
- **Autoreview (Codex, P0-P2):** the first pass found that the parent-row read and the builder chose a job's parent with different precedence. That is fixed in the last commit, and a fresh pass is scoped-clean.
- **Not run:** the live check for runtime-only fields (final offered tool list per runtime). It needs a trace build on a real Gateway and is pending maintainer approval; it matters only for the later owner-status phase.

prs.title: fix(net-policy): redact credentials in a nested URL embedded in text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A credential inside a **nested** URL survives redaction as soon as any text precedes the outer URL:

```
redactSensitiveUrlLikeString(
  "fetching https://auth.test/a?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=<secret> now")
-> "fetching https://auth.test/a?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=<secret> now"

redactSensitiveUrlLikeString(
  "https://auth.test/a?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=<secret>")
-> "https://auth.test/a?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.test%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3D***"
```

One leading word is the whole difference. The nested-URL rules only run on the parsed-URL path (`parsedWholeUrl`); anything else falls to `redactUrlLikeFallback`, whose scan is

```js
.replace(/([?&])([^=&]+)=([^&]*)/g, ...)
```

The value class allows `?`, so `redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=<secret>` is one value, the name `redirect_uri` is not a credential name, and the inner `access_token` is never classified. The `g` scan has already consumed past it.

This is reachable with whole lines, not just bare URLs. The call sites that pass a *message*
rather than a URL are the ones that land in the fallback — see **What this does not cover** below
for which of them I measured, and which turned out to be already safe on `main`.

An OAuth-style `redirect_uri=` or a callback URL carrying a token is the common shape.

## How It Was Found

A sentinel-secret fuzz over the production redaction entry points: credential-named assignments in 33 base names × 16 spelling mutations × 15 contexts, asserting the sentinel never survives, and only requiring redaction where the shared classifier itself calls the name a credential. 83,820 checks; the surviving shape was the nested URL. The scan also flagged the same input surviving `redactSensitiveText` — that is a separate gap in the logging path and is **not** addressed here.

## Fix

Nesting is handled in the replacer, not in the grammar. The key and value classes are
**byte-identical to `main`** (`[^=&]+` / `[^&]*`); a value is scanned for a nested assignment only
when its own name is not a credential:

```ts
function redactQueryAssignments(value: string, depth: number): string {
  return value.replace(
    /([?&])([^=&]+)=([^&]*)/g,
    (match, prefix: string, key: string, entryValue: string) => {
      if (isSensitiveUrlQueryParamName(key)) {
        return `${prefix}${key}=***`;
      }
      if (depth >= MAX_NESTED_URL_REDACTION_DEPTH || !entryValue.includes("?")) {
        return match;
      }
      return `${prefix}${key}=${redactQueryAssignments(entryValue, depth + 1)}`;
    },
  );
}
```

A sensitive value is still masked to the end of its `[^&]*` run, exactly as before, so the mask
boundary of an actual credential is never recomputed. Only `?` can open a nested assignment,
because `&` cannot appear inside a value. Recursion reuses the existing
`MAX_NESTED_URL_REDACTION_DEPTH` bound, and the regex literal lives inside the function so a
recursive call cannot share `lastIndex`. Because the sensitive branch is untouched, the change can
only *add* masking.

An earlier revision of this PR instead narrowed the fallback's classes to stop at `?` and at
whitespace. That was wrong twice over and was correctly caught in review: it truncated the mask of a
sensitive value that legitimately contains a raw `?` (`password=***?bravo`), and adding `\s` to the
*key* class stopped whitespace-spliced names (`access_ token=`) matching at all. Both class edits
are gone.

One consequence worth stating: trailing prose after a *masked* credential is consumed, because the
mask runs to the end of the `[^&]*` run. `main` already drops trailing prose that way for a
top-level sensitive parameter, so this matches existing behaviour rather than inventing
safer-looking output.

## Evidence

Additivity, sentinel differential against the merge base — leading prose × trailing prose × nesting
depth (0/1/2) × sensitive name × separator (`?`/`&`) × name-splice (none, space, NBSP, `+`):

```
DIFFERENTIAL 42336 inputs | 0 regressions | 4704 newly masked (11.1%)
```

0 regressions = no input where `main` hid the sentinel and this head leaks it.

Where the change bites — 5 leading prose forms × 5 trailing forms × 3 outer parameter names × 3
credential names × both separators:

```
main         total=450  leaks=270
this head    total=450  leaks=0
```

```
in : fetching https://h.test/p?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=<sentinel>
main: unchanged — credential in full
head: fetching https://h.test/p?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=***
```

A nested value with no credential is still returned byte-for-byte:

```
in : fetching https://auth.test/a?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?page=2 now
out: unchanged
```

### What this does *not* cover, measured

`redactSensitiveUrlLikeStringAtDepth` tries `new URL()` on the whole string first and only reaches
the changed fallback when that throws. So:

- a **bare URL** never reaches it — `redactQueryString` → `redactNestedUrlValue` already recursed on
  `main`;
- the **percent-encoded** nested form inside prose is already masked on `main` by
  `redactEncodedUrlLikeString`, which decodes and recurses.

I ran the shipped `src/snapshot/git-backup.ts:71` diagnostic end-to-end (`openclaw backup git
create --push` to an unreachable remote) and `main` produces a **byte-identical** masked line,
because git normalises the remote URL into the encoded form before it reaches the redactor. That
path is already safe; this PR does not change it.

The shape this PR does fix — prose carrying a *raw* nested query — is reached from the call sites
that pass a message rather than a URL, two of which document the risk themselves:
`src/agents/mcp-error.ts:29` (a remote MCP server's error text), `src/gateway/call.ts:230`
(*"the remote-controlled close reason, which can echo a credential-bearing URL"*),
`src/security/audit-gateway-probe.ts:54,58`, `src/commands/status-all.ts:447`, and the
`formatErrorMessage(...)` sites in `src/cli/daemon-cli/probe.ts`, `src/cli/local-state-owner.ts` and
`src/cli/logs-cli.ts:611`. I have not driven one of those to terminal output, because each needs a
cooperating remote; happy to build a synthetic MCP stub if that is the bar.

## Checks (Node 24.16.0)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/net-policy/src
-> Test Files 4 passed (4), Tests 96 passed (96)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/snapshot/git-backup.test.ts
-> 22 passed, 1 skipped          (the shipped consumer the review named)

oxlint, oxfmt --check on both changed files -> clean
run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json          -> exit 0
```

Four new regressions: a nested credential behind leading prose (plain and percent-encoded, two
prose shapes), a sensitive value that itself contains a `?` or a space, and a whitespace-spliced
credential name. The last two are the review's P1s.

The test file conflicted on the rebase because `main` converted it to flat `it.each` tables; I took
`main`'s version and re-added these cases in that style rather than restoring the old `describe`
blocks.

This touches a security-sensitive file, so it will need a maintainer `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.

prs.title: fix(logging): mask credentials carried in a nested URL
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A credential inside a **nested** URL survives logging redaction. `URL_QUERY_VALUE` is `[^&#\s<>]*`, so in

```
https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>
```

the value of `cb` runs to the end of the string. `cb` is not a credential name, the nested `?token=` sits inside that value, and the `g` scan has already consumed past it. A direct `?token=<secret>` is masked correctly today — only the nested shape leaks.

The same leak has a percent-encoded form, the OAuth `redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3D<secret>` shape, where the separators are `%3F`/`%26` and the `=` is `%3D`. No assignment grammar matches that, and net-policy's URL redactor (which *does* decode nested URLs) is not on this path.

Measured on `main` with a neutral sentinel — one that no value-shape rule recognises on its own:

```
redactSensitiveText("https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>")   -> secret in full
redactSensitiveLines(["GET https://x.test/?next=%3Ftoken%3D<secret>"])      -> secret in full
redactLogRecordForTransport({message: <same>})                             -> secret in full
```

## How It Was Found

A sentinel-secret fuzz over the production redaction entry points: credential-named assignments in 33 base names × 16 spelling mutations × 15 contexts, asserting the sentinel never survives, and only demanding redaction where the shared classifier itself calls the name a credential.

A methodology note, since it bit me: the first run used an `sk-`-prefixed sentinel, which openclaw's own value-shape rules mask on their own, hiding this gap. The numbers above use a neutral sentinel.

## Fix

Nesting is handled in the scanner, not in the grammar. `visitPair()` recurses into a value **only when that value's own name is not a credential**:

```ts
if (!isSensitiveBodyKey(key)) {
  if (kind !== "url" || depth >= MAX_NESTED_URL_QUERY_DEPTH || !token.includes("?")) {
    return;
  }
  const nested = new RegExp(URL_QUERY_PAIR, "gu");
  for (let match = nested.exec(token); match; match = nested.exec(token)) {
    const nestedPrefix = match[1] ?? "";
    const nestedKey = match[2] ?? "";
    visitPair(
      nestedKey,
      match[3] ?? "",
      valueOffset + match.index + nestedPrefix.length + nestedKey.length + 1,
      depth + 1,
    );
  }
  return;
}
```

A sensitive value still reaches `splitSecretValueForMask` + `maskToken` untouched, so the mask boundary of an actual credential is never recomputed. Only `?` can open a nested assignment, because `&` cannot appear inside a value. The depth bound mirrors net-policy's `MAX_NESTED_URL_REDACTION_DEPTH`, a fresh regex per level keeps `lastIndex` out of the recursion, and offsets are threaded through so existing original-offset coverage still lines up.

**`URL_QUERY_VALUE` is byte-identical to `main`.** An earlier revision of this PR narrowed it to end at `?`; that truncated the mask of a sensitive value that legitimately contains a raw `?` (`password=***?bravo`) and was correctly caught in review. The character classes are not touched any more, which is what makes this change strictly additive: every assignment `main` masks is still masked identically, because that branch is untouched.

One preparation rule covers the encoded form on the record and line paths, masking the value of an encoded assignment whose decoded name is a credential (reusing `isSensitiveBodyKey`). Both grammars are tempered rather than greedy, so the scan stays linear — 48 KB of back-to-back encoded pairs costs **10.6 ms**.

### Keeping a serialized edit inside its scalar

A log record is redacted by scanning its *serialized JSON*, and `URL_QUERY_VALUE` admits `"`, `:`, `,` and `}`. With no trailing `&` to stop it, a value runs past the closing quote of its own scalar, and the capture was applied to every token it overlapped:

```
{"message":"https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>","level":"info"}
  ->  {"message":"https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=***","***":"***"}
```

`level` is destroyed, key and value both. `src/logging/redact-json.ts` now clamps a serialized capture to the scalar it starts in:

```ts
const firstIndex = firstIntersectingToken(tokens, capture.start);
for (let index = firstIndex; index < tokens.length; index += 1) {
  …
  if (!batch && index > firstIndex) {
    break;
  }
```

The `","` between two scalars belongs to the JSON, not to any URL or form body. Line **batches** are excluded, because there the tokens are lines of one text and a capture legitimately spans several.

**This defect is not introduced by the nested scan — `main` has it today.** A top-level credential that ends the message is enough (`{"message":"https://x.test/?token=opaque-short","level":"info"}` → `"***":"***"` on `main`), and the repo's own baseline records it: 2 of the 250 log-record entries in `redact-byte-identity-fixture.json` store `"***":"***"` where `"level":"info"` belongs, both from the *encoded form* grammar (`client%5Fsecret=`). What the nested scan changes is the reach — on `main` nested callbacks are skipped entirely, which is the leak this PR fixes — so the fix belongs on the path, not on the symptom.

## Evidence — shipped entry points

The real CLI, built from this head and run as a process with stdout piped. The *before* column is the same CLI with `src/logging/redact.ts` replaced by `upstream/main`'s copy and a forced rebuild; nothing else differs. Synthetic credential `nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij`, hosts under the reserved `.test` TLD.

**Gateway log tail** (`openclaw logs --limit 200 --plain`, reading the configured file log):

```
# main
info gateway oauth callback …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij&page=2
warn gateway retry         …?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.test%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3Dnested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij&page=2
info gateway top-level control …?access_token=***
info gateway no credential nested …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?page=2

# this head
info gateway oauth callback …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=***&page=2
warn gateway retry         …?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.test%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3D***&page=2
info gateway top-level control …?access_token=***
info gateway no credential nested …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?page=2
```

**Plain console output** (`openclaw config validate` echoes a rejected value as `got: "<value>"` through `console.error` → `redactSensitiveText`):

| case | `main` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| nested, plain | `?cb=https://y.test/?access_token=nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij` | `?cb=https://y.test/?access_token=nested…ghij` |
| nested, percent-encoded | leaks | **unchanged — still leaks** |
| top level | `?access_token=nested…ghij` | `?access_token=nested…ghij` |

The top-level row is the control: `main` already masks it, so redaction was running over these lines before this PR. The only thing that changes is nesting. The masked nested value takes `maskToken`'s own partial `nested…ghij` shape, identical to the top-level shape for the same value.

## Remaining gap, stated rather than papered over

The encoded form is masked on the record and line paths, which run the preparation rules, but **not** by whole-text `redactSensitiveText`, which does not run them — row 2 of the console table above. Closing it means teaching `couldMatchDefaultRedactPatterns` about `%3D`, and that prefilter is pinned by 468 recorded hashes in `redact-prefilter-fixture.json`. Rewriting a recorded security corpus inside a revision whose job is to undo a leak this PR introduced is the wrong order of operations; it is a follow-up PR, not a silent omission.

## Checks (Node 24)

```
src/logging/redact.test.ts                 -> 58 passed
src/logging/redact-byte-identity.test.ts   -> 3 passed
src/logging (whole directory, 64 files)    -> 716 of 716 passed, 0 failures
oxlint, oxfmt --check on the changed files -> clean
run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json         -> exit 0
```

**Recorded-corpus changes, stated explicitly:** 2 of the 250 log-record entries in `redact-byte-identity-fixture.json` are re-recorded, because they had stored `"***":"***"` in place of `"level":"info"` — the corruption described above. Their masked `message` bytes are **byte-identical**; only the clobbered sibling field is restored. The other 248 entries and all 468 `redact-prefilter-fixture.json` hashes are untouched, verified by replaying all 250 samples and confirming exactly 2 differ and both only in that field. The reason is recorded in a comment in the test file so the deviation from "byte-identical to the pre-fix implementation" is not silent.

New cases: the two `?password=alpha?bravo` regressions, a top-level/nested mask-parity assertion, the plain nested URL through the whole-text path, a nested URL with no credential staying byte-for-byte readable, the percent-encoded nested query through the line-batch path, and a record-path case asserting that a mask with no trailing `&` leaves its sibling fields intact (red on base: `expected undefined to be 'info'`).

Companion PR: #176526 fixes the same class of leak in `packages/net-policy` (URL redactor, nested URL behind leading text). The two are independent — this path does not call that redactor.

This touches a security-sensitive file, so it will need a maintainer `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.

prs.title: fix(media): allow CP932 CSV attachments without transcoding
prs.body:
Closes #178619

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes valid Japanese CP932 CSV attachments being rejected by host-read text validation before channel upload.

## User Impact

Users can attach structured CP932/Windows-31J CSV exports while retaining their original bytes and line endings for downstream importers. This does not transcode the file or expand filesystem permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

After the existing UTF-8/Latin-1 text candidates fail validation, a CSV-only fallback strictly decodes Shift JIS and requires printable, rectangular records with quoted-field handling. It preserves the existing MIME-sniffing, root, size, and generated-HTML checks.

The existing text validators move into one sibling module to keep the oversized loader from growing. No dependency, setting, transport, or runtime patch is added. The net change is +65 production lines and +37 test lines; the growth implements the missing encoding/CSV admission check.

## Evidence

- Fixed synthetic Japanese-heavy and quoted CSV tests both fail on base `79262d0571694dbf083b7d1bf5a206cc8fb93936` with the reported `LocalMediaAccessError`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/web-media.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **50 passed**, including exact original-byte comparisons, mostly-ASCII CP932, malformed/control-byte cases, renamed binary media, and existing root/size/HTML protections. A mostly-ASCII regression caught during independent review was reproduced red before its fix.
- Direct model-free `loadWebMedia` reproduction returns `document`, `text/csv`, and `exactBytes: true` on the fix.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, focused oxlint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. Shared autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings after the decoder-precedence repair.
- The whole-repository max-lines check reports existing suppressions absent from its baseline in three unchanged UI files (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`). The changed-test selector also encounters an existing test-root budget failure; the canonical `core-test-infra` type graph passes separately (`pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-infra"]'`).
- Validation is at the production media-loader boundary. No patched live Gateway/channel upload has been deployed or claimed; live Slack delivery remains to be checked after an official distribution includes the fix.


### Shipped Slack channel proof (2026-10-21)

Exact-head isolated Slack upload proof passed through the shipped `sendMessageSlack` entry point and real shared media loader/write client. The received raw upload body exactly matched the synthetic CP932 source and retained both CRLF pairs. Full sanitized evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178621#issuecomment-6306438571

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for transcripts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #145309. Claude CLI transcripts could be looked up under the Gateway's configuration directory instead of the directory selected for the child process, breaking session continuity and imported history.

## User Impact

Custom Claude configuration directories retain native session continuity and imported history. Changing or unselecting the effective profile stops access to its old native transcripts while preserving canonical OpenClaw history. A profile change during response preparation now also prevents publication of a stale native-history result and asks the client to reload.

Existing bindings gain location metadata on subsequent turns. This PR adds no public configuration option or SQL schema migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final child environment and canonical cwd select the transcript root. Execution, settlement and recovery retain that location, and readers validate it against the currently effective root. Historical cwd locates an authorized transcript; current cwd determines authorization for relative or empty configuration roots. Paired-node bindings do not trigger Gateway-local native transcript discovery.

The latest correction retains the existing authorization check through the final response boundary for history, startup, retained-transcript and individual-message responses, plus embedded TUI and tool consumers. Canonical fallbacks remain independent of native authorization. Callbacks stay local and are not serialized into worker or response payloads.

## Evidence

Current head: `41a5db29012` (merge of main `ab6c07f595e` plus an import-order formatting fix). Main reworked the session-history worker request channel around its own `onRequest` hook with an abort signal; the native-history authorization request now rides that contract instead of a parallel callback, so process-held reads still re-check authority before publication. Main also dropped `agentAccountId` and `authProfileId` from the live Claude CLI session key, and the PR's key and its two dependent tests (`session-history-worker-runtime.test.ts`, `cli-session-history.paging.test.ts`) follow that. Main removed several doctor cases; the PR keeps main's file and re-adds only its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` case. `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` was regenerated by its script. Production semantics are unchanged from the previously reviewed head.

Previous head: `e24b56fe34f` (includes main `905a74d1bad`; a second merge picked up the regenerated workboard plugin manifest from #166786). That update carried the branch over history page cursors, `sessionId`-scoped `chat.message.get`, the shared CLI binding clear helper and the embedded-gateway response owner; the native-history authority cases moved unchanged to `chat-history-handler.cli-import.claude-config-dir.test.ts` to stay within the test line cap.

### Current worker and publication proof

Local Linux / Node 24.19.0 proof passed on `6d94a10bd6cd8b6944c14a898f5a97afbc910834`. The final follow-up only removes that duplicate test; production source is byte-identical. This is a direct **real `chat.history` handler → production session-transcript Worker → filesystem / SQLite** run with synthetic native JSONL and an isolated canonical database. No worker implementation or canonical-history result was mocked.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed profile | Real worker thread 5 imported the native message and retained canonical history; 13 host authorization requests, 1 native open and 1 native read. |
| Profile changed while waiting for the first worker→host authorization reply | Rejected before native I/O: 0 old-root probes, 0 opens, 0 reads. Canonical SQLite history returned successfully. |
| Profile unset at the same boundary | 0 old-root probes, 0 opens, 0 reads; canonical history returned successfully. |
| Profile revoked during asynchronous preparation after the native page was read | Final `chat.history` response rejected with retryable `UNAVAILABLE`; no native payload published. A subsequent canonical-history read succeeded. |

The observer delegates filesystem calls and records only the synthetic native root. A transparent Worker-constructor wrapper adds the observer to `execArgv` because the production lifecycle sanitizes its environment; the production entrypoint, messaging, authorization and I/O still execute. The queued cases hold the first actual host authorization roundtrip, then change/unset `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` before the host answers. The publication case holds `readChatStartupProjection` after the actual native read and revokes the profile before releasing that preparation.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized terminal output</summary>

```text
PROOF {"case":"allowed-real-worker-import","authorizations":13,"workerThreads":[5],"nativeIO":{"readdir":2,"access":2,"realpath":2,"stat":2,"open":1,"FileHandle.read":1},"canonicalVisible":true,"nativeVisible":true}
PROOF {"case":"changed-profile-before-worker-native-io","authorizations":1,"oldRootProbes":0,"oldRootOpens":0,"oldRootReads":0,"canonicalVisible":true,"nativeVisible":false}
PROOF {"case":"unset-profile-before-worker-native-io","authorizations":1,"oldRootProbes":0,"oldRootOpens":0,"oldRootReads":0,"canonicalVisible":true,"nativeVisible":false}
PROOF {"case":"profile-revoked-during-consumer-async-preparation","nativeIOBeforeRevocation":{"readdir":2,"access":2,"realpath":2,"stat":2,"open":1,"FileHandle.read":1},"responseAccepted":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"session changed while reading history; reload the conversation","details":{"method":"chat.history"},"retryable":true,"retryAfterMs":250},"canonicalSubsequentRead":true,"nativePublished":false}
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
Test execution: 11.111s; runner wall time: 44.60s; exit 0
```

The first instrumentation attempt correctly failed its positive I/O assertion because the observer did not reach the worker. After fixing observer propagation, the allowed case recorded actual opens/reads and all four scenarios passed. No product change was needed.

This establishes the current worker handshake, guarded reader and final handler publication boundary. It does not claim a new WebSocket, live-account, mid-chunk-revocation, incognito, native Windows/macOS, restart or updater run. The queued case is the pending authorization roundtrip, not a saturated worker backlog.
</details>

### Regression checks

- Current head `41a5db29012`, local Windows / Node 24.19.0: core and test type graphs passed (21 shards); the regenerated mock-export baseline check and the paging suite (**9/9**) passed; formatting checked with oxfmt. Windows-only failures remain in POSIX-path cases (`prepare.test.ts` 13/120, `session-history-worker-runtime.test.ts` 8/33). Hosted Linux CI on this head passed all required checks (100 passing, 45 skipped).
- Previous head `e24b56fe34f` (both merges), local Windows / Node 24.19.0, `--maxWorkers=1`: core and test type graphs, focused lint/format, max-lines, mock-export and conflict-marker checks passed. The two CLI-import files passed **22/22** (233.28s). The paging suite passed **3/3**. Across the other affected suites (embedded gateway stub, publication, Claude configuration history and snapshot, attempt execution, CLI runner, doctor, worker runtime and TUI), 9 cases failed on Windows only: eight worker-runtime selector cases expect POSIX `/tmp/...` paths, and the doctor "blocked workspace" case relies on `ENOTDIR`, which Windows reports as `ENOENT`. Both files' assertions and the doctor path classification match main; the worker-runtime case this PR adds passes. After the second merge, the bundled plugin asset check, type graphs and ratchets passed again and 7 overlapping and core files passed **161/161** (457.84s). Hosted Linux CI on this head is the authoritative run.
- Earlier head: the merged candidate passed **196 tests across five files** (CLI import, Claude configuration history, publication, embedded tool history and TUI), in 188.04s. After removing the duplicate TUI case, **all 127 TUI tests passed** again (40.08s including wrapper; 37.51s Vitest), leaving 195 distinct cases across those files. Both runs used `--maxWorkers=1`; hosted CI seconds are pending.
- Core types, the affected TUI test type graph, focused lint/format, line-cap, assertion-safety, mock-export and diff checks passed. Independent review found no actionable integration or proof findings.

prs.title: feat(tasks): follow background task progress from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #123488

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can inspect durable background tasks from the CLI, but they cannot stay attached to one task without repeatedly polling `tasks show`. Gateway logs are too broad for this job, and the Control UI does not cover every remote, headless, or shell-first workflow. As a result, operators can miss progress transitions and may not know whether execution finished while completion delivery is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `openclaw tasks follow <lookup>` with human-readable and JSON Lines output. The viewer reuses the `tasks show` lookup contract, connects with `operator.read`, projects existing bounded task summaries and visible session history, filters the existing task event stream to one task, and replays durable state after event gaps or Gateway reconnects. Stable record identifiers suppress replay duplicates, execution and delivery remain separate, and Ctrl-C closes only the viewer.

The change is read-only. It adds no task or session persistence, protocol schema, cancellation, notification, delivery, or restart-recovery owner.

## User Impact

Operators can follow one subagent, ACP, cron, or CLI task from a terminal until both execution and completion delivery reach a terminal state. `--json` supports line-oriented consumers with bounded, redacted records and duplicate-safe identifiers. Existing `tasks show`, Control UI, task execution, and delivery behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `e5c7ebd3143c014fdb0412043c71b10bf66737f5`, based on `6bd21a11222af41e7c758739c0e0cd2994dee445`.
- Focused CLI, command, and Gateway callsite-guard tests: 44/44 passed, covering human output, JSONL, bounded and redacted visible history, hidden reasoning and tool-result exclusion, `operator.read`, ordered updates, event gaps, duplicate suppression, reconnect, separate execution and delivery terminal behavior, Ctrl-C viewer-only behavior, lookup failure, and the production `GatewayClient` allowlist.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed all selected core, core-test, and docs lanes. Crabbox 0.41.6 matched the current stable release but had no ready remote provider, so the repository used its documented local fallback.
- `pnpm build` passed through the rebased CLI invocation, including CLI bootstrap imports, runtime post-build module loading, bundled plugin assets, and the Control UI build.
- Built CLI help exposes `openclaw tasks follow [options] <lookup>` and `--json` as JSON Lines.
- AutoReview loop 3 reviewed the exact rebased 37,028-byte bundle with `gpt-5.6-luna` at maximum thinking. TruffleHog passed and the review reported no accepted or actionable findings.
- The original `check-lint` failure had no lint finding. Every core shard completed, then the GitHub-hosted runner received a shutdown signal while linting extensions and exited 143. The new head retriggers that infrastructure-cancelled job.

### Live Gateway transcript

This proof used a loopback-only development Gateway and a dedicated temporary state root. It did not read or operate the normal Gateway. The controlled task had finished execution while delivery was still queued, so the viewer stayed attached. I stopped the isolated Gateway, completed delivery in the same SQLite-owned task row while it was down, and restarted it. The existing viewer emitted one disconnect marker, reconnected, replayed the durable terminal state, and exited 0. The task identifier below is redacted; the event order, timestamps, state, and exit status are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: rename google-vertex display name to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Vertex AI)
prs.body:
Closes #101188

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: users configuring or selecting the `google-vertex` provider see the outdated "Google Vertex AI" name after Google renamed Vertex AI to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform on April 22, 2026.

## User Impact

User impact: the provider now appears as **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Vertex AI)** in setup and model/session selection surfaces, matching Google's current branding while bridging the old name. Existing configuration, ADC/auth flows, and the stable `google-vertex` provider ID are unchanged, so no migration or user action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Updates both public label sources: the google setup provider contract (`createGoogleVertexProvider().label`) and the built-in display-name fallback consumed by `ModelRegistry.getProviderDisplayName`.
- Adds behavioral regression coverage through setup registration and model-registry display resolution, as suggested in the issue review.
- Deliberately left unchanged: the stable `google-vertex` identifier, ADC/auth configuration, technical API/error wording that still references the Vertex AI API surface (e.g. `aiplatform.googleapis.com`, ADC errors), and the generated plugin-inventory descriptions, which are derived from provider identifiers rather than display labels.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (regression: fails on base, passes on head)

To prove the new assertions are real behavior guards (not vacuous), the same test run was executed twice: once against the **base** code (both label sources still at the old "Google Vertex AI") while keeping the new assertions, and once against the **head** code with the new label.

- **Base code + new assertions → FAIL** (proves the labels currently resolve to the old name):
  ```
  src/agents/sessions/model-registry.test.ts › falls back to the Gemini Enterprise
  public display name for google-vertex
    AssertionError: expected 'Google Vertex AI' to be 'Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Ver…'

  extensions/google/setup-api.test.ts › labels google-vertex with the current Gemini Enterprise public name
    AssertionError: expected { id: 'google-vertex', …(4) } to match object ...
      - Expected "label": "Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Vertex AI)"
      + Received "label": "Google Vertex AI"
  ```
- **Head code + new assertions → PASS**:
  - `extensions/google/setup-api.test.ts`: 8/8 pass, including the new label assertion.
  - `src/agents/sessions/model-registry.test.ts`: 13 passed / 11 failed, and the 11 failures are unrelated Windows DACL environment issues (`filesystem did not enforce the private directory DACL` / `EACCES`); the new `falls back to the Gemini Enterprise public display name for google-vertex` assertion passes.

### On where the label is shown at runtime (honest scope note)

I could not find a read-only, non-interactive CLI/product surface that renders the `google-vertex` label at runtime:

- `models auth login` requires a TTY, and `google-vertex` is filtered out there because its auth contract has no auth steps (`auth: []`), so it never reaches the label-selection prompt.
- `plugins list --json`, `models status`, and `providers` output provider identifiers, not the ProviderPlugin label.
- The label does surface in interactive setup selection and in the model/session catalog via `provider.label`, which is exactly the surface this change fixes.

Because the display surfaces are interactive and require real credentials/TTY, the evidence above relies on regression assertions (which demonstrably fail on base) rather than a scripted end-to-end screenshot. This is the honest, minimal-scope way to prove the behavior change.

### Wording decision (needs maintainer sign-off)

The label wording **"Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Vertex AI)"** is a maintainer decision that I cannot make unilaterally. My working assumption: keep a bridging parenthetical to the old, still-recognized name so existing documentation/screenshots remain findable, since the `google-vertex` identifier is unchanged. If maintainers prefer the exact canonical name ("Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform") without the parenthetical, or a different wording (e.g. "Google Gemini Enterprise"), it is a one-line change in each of the two label sources plus the two test assertions. Flagging for explicit sign-off.

## Static & CI checks (unchanged from prior runs)

- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane covering the changed files passed — typecheck core, typecheck core tests (all shards, including `agents-sessions`), typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, lint core changed files, and lint extension changed files (0 warnings/0 errors on the changed files, 292 rules), plus the line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets.
- `pnpm docs:check-links` — 15,732 internal links checked, 0 broken.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Note: verification was run on a Windows workstation, where the Bun-based formatter parity step and the plugin-sdk boundary declaration prebuild (hard-coded 300 s timeout) are unsupported/over budget; the changed files were verified with the CI formatter `oxfmt` directly (all formatted), and the extension lint lane passed standalone once the boundary prebuild was allowed to finish (0 findings).

Executable access also succeeds for searchable directories. Both the synchronous and prepared probes now require a regular file while following symlinks. Prepared probes keep pending-only I/O sharing, and synchronous successful-hit caching is unchanged.

## Evidence

Built current main `853171d64cd64d9d447b5b3b27ba924da11d0a55` and candidate `6b27f39a081d009b6c15668a5e383fea48aa4eb4` in secretless Linux isolation. Initialized configuration through shipped `config set`, then ran shipped `skills check --json` in a new process per case using the bundled gog skill and external PATH fixtures. No Google credentials or gog invocation were needed.

Captured output:

```text
                         main: gog eligible   candidate: gog eligible
missing executable       false                false
directory only, run 1    true                 false
directory only, run 2    true                 false
directory + later file   true                 true
executable symlink       true                 true
```

When ineligible, gog appears in missing requirements with binary `gog`. The focused config-eval suite passes all 18 tests on the candidate. On main, both synchronous and prepared directory-rejection regressions fail (`expected true to be false`), while the other 16 tests pass.

Whole-diff simplification retained the existing probe owners and caching behavior; no additional resolver or public SDK surface. Production +11/-6 (net +5), tests +37/-0. No new configuration or usage documentation is required; this restores existing binary-prerequisite meaning.

Thanks to @xutongxue233 for the fix and the reporter of #146187.

Merge danger: two-way door. Reverting fully restores previous behavior; there is no state migration. Blast radius is local binary prerequisite detection for skills and hooks.

prs.title: fix(workboard): finalize running execution on terminal status transitions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard dispatch slots could be permanently starved by stale execution state and uncleared dispatch claims, blocking follow-up work for the same owner agent.

Two related bugs caused this:

1. **Stale running execution on terminal transitions**: When a card left `running` status via `releaseClaim`, generic `updateCard`, `move`, or `reassign` (paths that don't pass an explicit execution patch), the execution record stayed `running`. The dispatcher's capacity predicate then counted the card as occupying the owner's slot indefinitely.

2. **Dispatch claim not released on lifecycle success**: `syncLifecycle` mapped the card to `review` and execution to `review` on lifecycle success, but did not clear `card.metadata.claim`. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` still counted the active (non-expired) claim against the owner's capacity, so the next ready card for that owner was blocked until the claim's TTL expired (30 minutes by default).

Closes #122911.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Fix 1: Finalize running execution on terminal status transitions only

`updateCard` (`store-core.ts`) is the shared owner for execution lifecycle. It already had logic to sync session keys, but lacked the symmetric finalization for execution status. The fix adds a finalization step: when a card transitions from `running` to a **terminal** status (`done`/`review`/`blocked`) without an explicit execution patch, the execution status is closed to match the card's terminal state. `done`/`review` are successful outcomes (attempt succeeds, `failureCount` resets); `blocked` is an explicit failure or abandonment path.

Non-terminal statuses (`todo`, `backlog`, `triage`, `scheduled`, `ready`) preserve execution occupancy so a worker moved aside can still complete successfully. The original broad condition (`status !== "running"`) incorrectly finalized executions for non-terminal moves, causing `completeDirect` to retain `blocked` on later successful completions (ClawSweeper P1 re-review).

The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm was removed — with execution now finalized at the owner, legacy stale rows no longer need a downstream guard.

### Fix 2: Release terminal review claims before capacity counting (ClawSweeper P1)

`syncLifecycle` (`store.ts`) is the lifecycle owner that transitions the card to terminal-for-dispatch status (`review`/`blocked`). The claim must be released at this boundary so the owner's slot is freed immediately, not after claim TTL expiry. Without this, `normalizeMetadata`'s fallback preserved the stale claim, and `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` counted it against capacity.

The fix clears `card.metadata.claim` in `syncLifecycle` when the card transitions to any non-running, non-done status. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` (`store-constants.ts`) additionally excludes `review`/`blocked` claims as defense-in-depth, covering legacy rows where `syncLifecycle` did not clear the claim before this fix shipped.

### Production LOC delta

- `store-core.ts`: +19/-1 (execution finalization at the shared owner, terminal-only)
- `store.ts`: +15/-0 (claim release at the lifecycle owner)
- `store-constants.ts`: +7/-4 (defense-in-depth capacity exclusion)
- `dispatcher.test.ts`: +12/-4 (updated review-slot test)
- `dispatcher-ownership.test.ts`: +5/-2 (use non-terminal status for claim-expiry test)

Production: +41/-5 net +36 across 3 lifecycle owners. Tests: +703/-6 net +697.

Each change lives at its architectural owner — `updateCard` owns execution lifecycle, `syncLifecycle` owns claim lifecycle, `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` owns capacity semantics. The terminal-only narrowing absorbs the ClawSweeper P1 finding without expanding the production surface: the broad `status !== "running"` condition and `finalizedExecutionStatus` ternary were replaced by a direct terminal-status check, keeping net production LOC proportional to the three owners repaired.

## User Impact

Workboard dispatch recovers immediately when a worker finishes or fails — no 30-minute starvation window. Follow-up cards for the same owner agent dispatch as soon as the lifecycle transition completes. Legacy cards with stale claims (from before this fix) also no longer hold slots. Moving a running card aside to a non-terminal status (e.g., `todo`) no longer corrupts the execution record — the worker can still complete successfully and the attempt is recorded as `succeeded`. This is a default-path fix: every operator using workboard dispatch was affected.

No config, API, default, protocol, or schema change; existing operator behavior is unchanged except that stale executions are now finalized and stale slots are released.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 22 (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper).

Rebased onto current main. The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm is removed at its canonical helper location in `store-constants.ts`, so both `dispatcher.ts` and `sqlite-store.ts` call sites are repaired in one change.

### Focused proof (two files, 46 tests)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts

 ✓ |extensions| extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts (30 tests) 166ms
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts (16 tests) 180ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 48.40s
```

### Full workboard suite — no regression

```

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 53.70s
```

### Pre-fix failure proof (12 of the new tests fail on main)

```
$ git checkout origin/main -- extensions/workboard/src/store-core.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store-constants.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts

Tests  12 failed | 34 passed (46)
[vitest] FAILED (exit 1)
```

Failures (grouped by invariant):

- `releaseClaim(status=done)` → execution stays `running` (expected `done`)
- `releaseClaim(status=review)` → execution stays `running` (expected `review`)
- `generic update(status=done)` → execution stays `running` (expected `done`)

- Legacy `done` + running execution → ready card NOT started (persisted, SQLite boundary)

- Legacy `review` + active claim → ready card NOT started (claim not excluded)

- Non-terminal move (todo) → execution marked `blocked` (expected `running`)

### Matrix-style evidence — terminal transition paths

| Path | Pre-fix (main) | Post-fix (this PR) |
|------|---------------|-------------------|
| `releaseClaim(status=done)` | execution `running` | execution `done` + ready card starts |

| `move(running→todo)` then `complete` | execution `blocked`, attempt `failed` | execution `running`→`done`, attempt `succeeded` |

### Legacy stale-row recovery (persisted fixture, dispatcher read-only)

|------------------|---------------|-------------------|
| `done` + execution `running` (SQLite) | ready card NOT started | ready card started |
| `review` + execution `running` (persisted) | ready card NOT started | ready card started |
| `review` + active claim (legacy) | ready card NOT started | ready card started |

### Regression proof — sibling paths unchanged

|------|-------------------|
| `complete` | execution `done` (unchanged) |
| `block` | execution `blocked` (unchanged) |
| `reclaim` | execution cleared (unchanged) |
| `syncLifecycle` (association) | execution patched via `executionAssociationPatch` (unchanged) |
| `syncLifecycle` (non-association) | execution patched explicitly (unchanged) |
| non-running card metadata update | execution untouched (unchanged) |
| non-terminal move (`todo`/`backlog`/`ready`) | execution `running` preserved (unchanged) |

### Production-boundary dispatch trace (SQLite-backed WorkboardStore, not in-memory)

```
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-122911-dispatch-trace.mts

prs.title: fix: hear Google Meet participants using WebAudio playback
prs.body:
Closes #178681

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Google Meet participants being inaudible to the agent when Meet renders their speech through WebAudio without `<audio>` or `<video>` elements. The browser bridge can otherwise remain connected while sending only silent PCM.

## User Impact

Managed Chrome capture can receive Meet's worklet-based participant playback while keeping microphone and assistant audio out of provider input. A restored pre-join tab reloads once to initialize observation. Existing calls are never automatically reloaded; managed capture explains when leaving and rejoining is required. Custom input commands keep their existing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture owner now accepts destination-connected playback discovered before Meet initializes its audio graph. Observation is installed when browser control selects a Meet page and does not collect audio itself. Capture excludes contexts containing media input, revokes late or disconnected sources, isolates the original speaker sink, and restores it on stop or ownership loss.

The added state belongs to graph observation and capture cleanup; the existing DOM capture and provider transport remain in place. This addresses incoming playback discovery, independently of the join-lifetime repair in #173898.

## Evidence

- Real Chrome regression through browser page selection and the production capture source: the original DOM-only implementation returns PCM with peak 0; this change returns nonzero PCM from a zero-input, three-output AudioWorklet with no media elements.
- Real Chrome also covers early/late microphone exclusion, disconnect cleanup, ownership loss, speaker-sink restoration, and non-Meet isolation. No microphone recordings or live account data are used in these tests.
- Capture implementation focused run: 8 files / 90 tests passed in 55s, including the five real-Chrome cases, DOM capture, realtime transport, Meet page selection/adapter, and shared Teams/Zoom adapters. Enable the browser fixture with `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_SNAPSHOT_E2E=1` and run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-meet-playback.chromium.test.ts`.
- Complete Google Meet extension suite: 33 files / 243 tests passed. `pnpm build` passed in 3m39s; targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The final focused run was repeated after rebasing to current main.
- Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. PR CI will provide the broader repository checks.
- In a live managed-Chrome call, participant speech reached the realtime provider and the listener confirmed an audible automatic reply. Complete voice-to-agent conversation acceptance remains pending because a separate native consultation-lifecycle defect (existing #142610 / #142692) was also reproduced. This PR addresses browser capture; it does not include that consultation fix.

- Login follow-up at `8e3ba518e058919706b1190fe11eda1e58f40a44`: four failing login regression cases reproduced before the correction; all 11 targeted adapter/page-script tests pass afterward. Google login classification is preserved without an unnecessary reload or observer latch mutation. Scoped typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, secret scan, and independent review passed.

### Redacted live-call readback

The deployed managed-Chrome path was tested in an actual Google Meet with a second participant. After two spoken user turns, the existing runtime health counters reported:

```json
{
  "providerConnected": true,
  "realtimeReady": true,
  "bridgeClosed": false,
  "lastInputBytes": 4498432,
  "lastOutputBytes": 1191360,
  "userTurnCount": 2,
  "assistantTurnCount": 3
}
```

The participant confirmed that automatic replies were audible. These are aggregate runtime counters, not a latency measurement or an assertion that every output byte belongs to a particular turn. No meeting URL, participant identity, transcript, credential, private endpoint, or recording is included.

The participant also reported that the backing agent consultation was not working correctly. Three native consultation failures matched the separate released-admission defect tracked in #142610 / #142692. That prevents claiming complete semantic conversation acceptance here, but it does not negate the observed participant-input and audible voice-output path. The consultation repair is outside this PR.
