prs.title: fix(minimax): match CN host on a dot boundary for region detection
prs.body:
## Summary

fix(minimax): bind CN region detection to the `minimaxi.com` host on a dot boundary, so look-alike hosts such as `notminimaxi.com` no longer route web search to the CN endpoint

## What Problem This Solves

The MiniMax web search provider infers the region (`cn` vs `global`) from `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or the configured provider base URL, and picks the search endpoint accordingly (`https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search` for CN, `https://api.minimax.io/v1/coding_plan/search` for global).

**代码证据**: in `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`, `isMiniMaxCnHost` used:

- `new URL(trimmed).hostname.endsWith("minimaxi.com")` — matches any host that merely *ends* with the string, e.g. `notminimaxi.com` or `evilnotminimaxi.com`.
- `trimmed.includes("minimaxi.com")` as the fallback for scheme-less values — a pure substring check that also matches look-alike hosts.

So a misspelled or maliciously crafted host like `MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com` was classified as CN, and search traffic (including the query and the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header) would be sent to the CN search endpoint derived from that wrong classification.

Trigger condition: any host value that ends with the literal string `minimaxi.com` without being `minimaxi.com` or a subdomain of it.

## Root Cause

- Violated invariant: region inference is a security-relevant routing decision (it selects which endpoint receives queries and credentials), but the host check was a suffix/substring match instead of a dot-boundary host match.
- `endsWith("minimaxi.com")` has no label boundary: `notminimaxi.com`.endsWith(`minimaxi.com`) is `true`. The scheme-less fallback `includes(...)` is weaker still.

## Why This Fix

- Option A: keep `endsWith` but prepend a dot (`endsWith(".minimaxi.com")`). Handles the URL-parseable path but leaves the scheme-less substring fallback untouched.
- Option B (chosen): extract a single `isCnHostname` predicate — `hostname === "minimaxi.com" || hostname.endsWith(".minimaxi.com")` — and use it for both paths; for scheme-less values, prepend `https://` so only the host is inspected (never the path or query), and return `false` if the value still cannot be parsed.
- Not chosen: a regex over the raw string — duplicates URL parsing logic and still mixes host and non-host content.

## User Impact

- Affected scenarios: users setting `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or a provider `baseUrl` to a host that shares the `minimaxi.com` suffix (typo'd or look-alike domains).
- Before: such hosts were classified as CN and search requests were routed to the CN endpoint.
- After: only `minimaxi.com` and its subdomains classify as CN; everything else falls back to global.
- Behavior change: legitimate CN endpoints (`https://api.minimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com`, `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`) are unaffected — still classified as CN.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** look-alike hosts sharing the `minimaxi.com` suffix were classified as CN, routing MiniMax web search to the wrong (CN) endpoint.
- **Real environment tested:** worktree `wt-minimax-cn-host-boundary` on latest `origin/main`, Node v24.19.0, importing the real `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` via tsx and calling the exported `testing.resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `testing.resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` set per case. No mocks of the functions under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  $ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs minimax-cn-host-boundary.proof.mjs
  $ npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix (8/8 PASS):**
  ```bash
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimax.io -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://example.com/redir?u=minimaxi.com -> region=global
  RESULT: ALL PASS
  ```

**Before (on main, same script, exit code 1):**

```bash
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global), endpoint=https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=cn (expected global)
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global)
RESULT: 3 case(s) show WRONG region/endpoint
```

- **What was not tested:** a live search request against the real MiniMax endpoints (requires valid credentials); the proof exercises the real region/endpoint resolution code paths end to end.

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts` — 23/23 passed, including new regression cases: apex CN domain still classifies as CN; `https://notminimaxi.com`, `https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1`, scheme-less `notminimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com.evil.com`, and a query-string-only mention all classify as global.
- `npx oxlint --deny=warn` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Before/after real-behavior proof logs are embedded above.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: unit tests on the real exported `resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` (via the module's `testing` surface), with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` as the input vector.
- Target test file: `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: suffix-sharing look-alike hosts (`notminimaxi.com`, with scheme, with path, scheme-less) and non-host mentions (query string) never classify as CN, while the real CN hosts (`api.minimaxi.com`, apex `minimaxi.com`) still do.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it pins the exact predicate that makes the routing decision, using the exact inputs that previously misclassified.

prs.title: fix(auth): tolerate invalid credential symlink targets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

External JSON credential discovery can abort with ENOTDIR when a credential symlink points beneath a regular file. The shared reader already treats missing targets and cycles as absent; this adds the distinct invalid-directory target case to that same owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep tolerant credential discovery at src/infra/json-file.ts rather than duplicating catches in each consumer. Chained-symlink resolution itself is already supplied by merged #157524; the remaining production change is ENOTDIR handling. Added filesystem regressions retain relative/absolute chains, invalid targets, dangling links and cycles.

## User Impact

An invalid legacy credential target no longer interrupts setup discovery, and readable symbolic links still reach their actual JSON payload. No configuration, default, protocol, schema, dependency, permissions or migration changes. No external authentication success is claimed. Current contribution: 2 files, production +5/-1 (net +4), tests +49/-0. AI-assisted implementation and independent source/proof review.

## Evidence

### Fresh shipped CLI and Gateway proof — October 20, 2026

- Product head: `786730fe85a60fb1698940f0b415feb3c856d8e6`.
- Authentic parent baseline: `a1a0ec6c5b553edca48d8d64f645dd0a8ae9bbc3`.
- Platform: Linux, v26.1.0, OpenClaw 2026.9.6; normal pinned-pnpm `pnpm build cliStartup` on each revision. Exact-head clean-source build stamps were checked before both runs.
- Same collector and scenarios on both revisions: SHA-256 `67bed47f29a5149374154506b03b3a6ca4db6be6005cc3b94c609bb7f449cc44`.
- Proof command on each revision: `node "$PROOF_HARNESS" "$CHECKOUT" "$PHASE"`, with PHASE=red for the parent and PHASE=green for the product head.
- Production entry: `node "$CHECKOUT/openclaw.mjs" gateway call openclaw.setup.detect --json --timeout 30000 --params '{}'`, against a normal `gateway run` in an isolated, authenticated loopback instance.
- Actual chain: public Gateway method → setup discovery → external executable discovery → Gemini legacy credential reader → shared JSON realpath owner. No production module was directly imported by this collector.
- External `gemini --version` discovery uses an explicitly controlled executable fixture. The OpenClaw Gateway, credential reader, filesystem and RPC output are real. This does not validate Gemini runtime/login or an external provider.

An owned synthetic HOME contains `.gemini/oauth_creds.json -> regular-file/credentials.json`, where `regular-file` is a file, not a directory. A legal control retargets the same link to `legal.json`. Independent file-only strace shows the actual ENOTDIR and the legal payload open; after every RPC, lstat/readlink and content readback verify the link, sentinel and payload are preserved.

Sanitized observations and commands are inline above; raw task-local traces are supplementary, not required to inspect the claim.

### Checks and remaining gates

- Existing product head is preserved. Fresh focused `pnpm test src/infra/json-file.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14/14 PASS; measured single-worker wrapper wall 9.56 seconds (native shard 8.70 seconds; Vitest 4.89 seconds). No source or test was modified during this proof-only maintenance.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report stt-tts readiness and transports in talk.catalog
prs.body:
Related: #165363 ## What Problem This Solves Android can reject a working native Talk setup because setup readiness is taken from an unrelated realtime provider, while `talk.catalog` does not expose selected-speech readiness and transport metadata. ## User Impact Configured native Talk can use device speech recognition and the selected speech provider without requiring a realtime provider. Existing device-TTS fallback is preserved for missing or unsupported speech providers; a selected, known provider without credentials still requires setup. Realtime Talk continues to use realtime readiness. No configuration migration, schema change, or new dependency is introduced. Physical-device/live-provider and fresh-install/latest-stable upgrade validation remain outstanding; the evidence below does not claim those flows have been tested. ## Why This Change Was Made - Derive `speech.ready` from the active speech row's asynchronous configured result and expose `managed-room` transport metadata. - Reuse Android's existing Talk route parser to select native-speech or realtime readiness. Native recognition does not depend on Gateway transcription readiness. - Invalidate setup readiness after configuration changes and reject stale refresh results. Label the shared setup row “Talk,” not “Realtime Talk.” - Regenerate the source-owned native localization inventory for the changed labels and configuration-error text. Translated catalogs and locale metadata remain owned by the localization workflow. Original implementation by @holny; Android route-readiness follow-up and CI correction contributed with @IWhatsskill. ## Work sessions - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/af8d6636-39eb-4922-8f37-2d4ba8a42bb8) ## Evidence ### Current localization follow-up Commit `7784d02a30ab425bfb75aef40a155ba778c3245a` changes only `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` (4 additions, 2 deletions), generated by `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`. - Reproduced the exact `native app i18n inventory drift detected` failure on `63959e26026939388010d16ca2b133d0b7a4891b` using `pnpm native:i18n:verify`. - After regeneration, `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes, including Android and Apple source-localization checks; 4,483 inventory entries. - Repeated generation is byte-identical. Verification passes again after the commit; `git diff --check` passes. Local runtime: Node 26.8.2, repository-pinned pnpm 12.9.0, frozen-lockfile dependencies. ### Android behavior and review — retained evidence for 63959e260269393 The localization-only follow-up does not change these runtime/test sources. These are prior-commit results, not a new execution of the whole suite: - The new Android admission regression failed on unchanged pre-fix Android source, then passed with the route-aware fix. - **43 focused Android tests passed:** readiness 13; NodeRuntime admission/stale-result/publication 3; Settings 1; composer 8; config parsing 10; mode manager 3; speech client 5. The selected Gradle tests and Kotlin lint completed in 48 seconds. The new 11-case admission regression took 2.137 seconds; the stale-result regression took 0.058 seconds. These are measured local times, not estimated CI seconds. - Kotlin lint, scoped formatting, documentation-content checks, and whitespace checks passed. - Two independent Codex autoreview passes over the complete implementation candidate and relevant route/fallback/lifecycle context found no actionable P0–P2 issues. ClawSweeper's October 14 review of the same head also reports no code findings, with behavior proof still outstanding. - The earlier exact-parent Gateway handler [CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38561600537/job/115844560368) passed 107 tests. This is parent-head evidence, not a current-head Gateway rerun. ### Settings screenshots Actual production Compose Settings rendering in a test harness, using French, a narrow viewport, and large text. These images demonstrate the shared label change only; they do **not** demonstrate successful Talk startup or audio. “Non vérifié” means “Unverified”: the fixture is deliberately disconnected. “Parler” is the translated “Talk” label.
BeforeAfter
### Live `talk.catalog` runtime proof Both scenarios run against an isolated loopback Gateway (`gateway.mode=local`, `bind=loopback`, port 18899) on the candidate build, invoked as `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog --params '{}'`. Scenario A - active provider present, no credentials (`talk.provider=elevenlabs`, `talk.providers.elevenlabs={}`): ```json { "speech.ready": false, "speech.activeProvider": "elevenlabs", "elevenlabs.configured": false, "elevenlabs.transports": ["managed-room"], "elevenlabs.modes": ["stt-tts"] } ``` Scenario B - same active provider after adding credentials: ```json { "speech.ready": true, "speech.activeProvider": "elevenlabs", "elevenlabs.configured": true, "elevenlabs.transports": ["managed-room"], "elevenlabs.modes": ["stt-tts"] } ``` This is the readiness the fix derives from the active speech row: the selected, known provider reports `ready:false` (`configured:false`) without credentials, and `ready:true` once configured. A synthetic key was used and does not appear in the catalog output. ### CI failure disposition and remaining proof The [CI attempt for 63959e260269393](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38570885471) failed in two independent jobs: - `native-i18n`: missing source-inventory regeneration, corrected by the localization follow-up above. - `android-test-third-party`: downloading `gradle-9.7.1-bin.zip` returned HTTP 500 before tests started. This is not a passing test result or evidence of a code failure. Its downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` also failed. New-head hosted CI remains separate from the local passing check; no manual CI rerun or merge is claimed here. The live `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog` evidence above closes the earlier runtime-proof gap; physical-device native Talk startup/audio, device fallback and unchanged realtime admission, and fresh-install/latest-stable upgrade runs with settings preserved remain outstanding. No full repository suite was run locally.
Implementation history - The initial test-only commit `ca0f5eeaa0e` did not contain the production change; `2404bf77d27` supplied it. - `33df65b6c59a` preserved main's asynchronous provider-catalog structure and corrected selected-provider readiness for missing credentials. - `63959e260269393` added Android route-aware admission, fallback preservation, configuration-refresh protection, focused regressions, and the shared Talk label. The Android admission blocker is therefore no longer excluded from this PR's scope; live proof remains open as stated above.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate private plugin bookkeeping owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several bundled plugins retain private bookkeeping or substitution layers where an existing owner already provides the operation.

## User Impact

No intentional user-visible change, public contract change, migration, or required user action. Security effect checks, ordinary process settlement, durable approval recovery, and the standalone session memory backend are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Browser atomic keyed queue, Teams account-key resolver, Codex SDK singleton map, and voice-call SDK dedupe cache. Remove unread ordinary-memory projections, duplicate Matrix reaction registration/normalization and descriptor copies, and QA Lab's test-only command/timing seams. QA fixtures now substitute the existing lifecycle module and restore their spies in `finally`; real subprocess tests still use the real settlement implementation.

Net production removal: **100 lines** (+30/−130), 11 production files, 22 total files including a shrink-only assertion baseline correction. This is a combined residue under the campaign's 100-line waiver, not a LARGE PR. Test/support changes are counted separately (+104/−39) and retain the existing assertions.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Browser: recursive native-key acquisition is replaced by the existing atomic multi-key queue. Incidental placement of a newly arriving second-key task can differ; per-key FIFO, independent keys, dashboard admission and current authority remain protected. The actual stall/worker cutover from #159599 is retained, not removed.
- Voice-call: the SDK cache prunes expired entries on new registration rather than every 64 reservations, and an expired/reinserted key becomes newest in bounded FIFO order. Authentication, ten-minute non-sliding replay protection, 10,000-entry bound, valid-date/overflow handling and ownership-checked failed-delivery release remain. Security fixes #100263, #118754 and #118235 are preserved; no human incident establishes the old incidental eviction order as a contract.
- Matrix: delivery already awaits canonical registration before seeding reactions (#62135, #146325 and the pre-seeding registration change); binding no longer repeats that write. Recovery and stop/cancellation cleanup remain intact. An internal target with empty room/event strings can now produce an opaque binding rather than null; either cleanup route reaches the same normalizing owner and no-ops.
- Matrix: private reaction descriptors are shared instead of defensively copied. All three current consumers only read them, neither public barrel exposes this helper, and #163740 provides no human incident requiring copies. Unsupported future mutation would affect later reads; adding another defensive layer for that hypothetical is deliberately declined.
- QA Lab: private command overrides and timing setters had no production consumers or public export contract (#92606, #121253, #104958). Runtime uses its existing command owner and unchanged 2000/500 ms cleanup budgets; test-specific timing belongs only to test fixtures.

## Evidence

Focused tests use isolated OpenClaw/HOME/XDG state, serial workers and lowered CPU priority. Earlier unchanged-area proof is reused: Browser 30 cases/3 files; Teams 3 selected warning cases (29 unrelated cases filtered, no added skips); Codex 15 cases; voice-call 52 security/webhook cases plus 21 replay/provider cases; ordinary memory 37 cases/3 files; Matrix 25 cases/3 files. Targeted types and focused static checks passed for those cuts.

QA Lab initially passed 74/75 cases across eight suites; the sole failure was the new esbuild fixture's missing resolve directory, before subprocess execution. Its setup was repaired without changing assertions, retries, skips or timeouts. The final lifecycle replay passed all nine cases, including real POSIX cleanup and parent SIGTERM re-raising; the other seven suites' inputs are unchanged. Targeted strict QA production/test types and focused syntax lint passed.

Independent isolated P0–P2 reviews covered each cut. The final Matrix review raised a mutable-alias concern; it is explicitly rejected under the private-data tradeoff above, not reported as a clean review. QA review found no actionable defects; the later fixture repair only supplies esbuild's resolve directory.

Whole-candidate scoped cycles passed across 2,183 production modules (zero runtime cycles/no new static components), the 21-file line-cap ratchet passed, and all 14 lint-suppression cases passed. Format/whitespace checks passed; check-changed classification ran in dry-run mode only. Broad suites/builds/whole-graph types are reserved for exact-head PR CI under the campaign's host budget. No live channel, Gateway, Docker-container, browser UI, or external-service proof is claimed.

CI on the first head found our missed stale assertion allowance (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, job118989213911, run39528495214): Codex's retired global-state cast reduced the file's assertions from one to zero. The correction deletes that allowance, tightening the baseline. Local assertion ratchet passed across 2,503 governed files, all 14 lint-suppression cases passed again, and independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defect in the one-line correction. No runtime/test source changed; the replacement exact-head CI remains the landing gate. No CI rerun was requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Session maintenance can leave stale Codex-bound sessions in SQLite when a deletion hook runs under its owning plugin scope.

## User Impact

Eligible sessions can be removed during maintenance instead of accumulating after repeated cleanup failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle guard now accepts an active invocation frame belonging to any captured harness owner, including nested owners. Existing authority, registration, and hook checks remain in place.

## Evidence

Two regressions use real wrapped plugin instances and the SQLite deletion API. On the original source, both failed with `Session mutation harness owner changed: native-owner-0`; with the fix, the deletion suite passed 27/27. Maintenance, plugin invocation, callback, memory lifecycle, and context-reset suites also passed. Core and test typechecks, format, and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted lint had zero errors and one max-lines warning in the existing deletion test file. A live Codex Gateway maintenance pass was not run.

Codex assisted with the patch and validation.

prs.title: fix: stop replaying completed turns with legacy saved replies
prs.body:
Related: #166300
Related: #166340

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed conversations restarting themselves when a legacy saved final has no durable delivery identity.

## User Impact

Routine restarts no longer run those old turns or send resumption notices. New authenticated input can continue in the same conversation. The saved reply, capture time, and route remain in one local transcript artifact explicitly marked delivery-unconfirmed; unrelated delivery notices remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pending-final owner recognizes a completed run with a matching terminal marker and no unfinished execution, delivery, harness, or started-attempt owner. It reuses atomic local settlement instead of dispatching another model turn. There is no external replay, tombstone, synthesized notice debt, age cutoff, schema change, or new state owner. Identified pending finals and genuine interrupted work retain their normal recovery path.

This handles the pending-final variant adjacent to #166340, whose draft deliberately excludes pending finals. It does not close the full unmatched-fence report. Terminal execution cannot prove historical channel delivery: the original reply stays available locally rather than being blindly resent. Recovery-owner acceptance of this historical-state disposition is requested before merge.

## Evidence

- On pinned main, an isolated SQLite startup regression reaches the actual runtime boundary and fails its zero-call assertion. With the change, it settles without runtime, model/tool, notice, or final-send calls.
- The regression checks the completed run/end time, saved text and metadata, preservation of an acknowledged unrelated notice, same-session foreground admission, and stable repeated startup without duplicate artifacts.
- 17 focused tests passed: the 13-test terminal/startup suite plus four interrupted, identified pending-final, and notice controls. The terminal suite passed again with the exact terminal-writer residue fixture (13/13; 14.98s command wall).
- Production core types, the agent-session test type graph, targeted lint/format, line-cap and SQLite-worker ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. No new main-thread SQLite calls (171→171).
- Proof uses synthetic state and a rejecting runtime boundary, not live provider/channel traffic or an installed-updater run. The full repository suite was not run.
- Focused validation passed: 17 selected tests; the final terminal-writer startup fixture suite passed 13/13. Core and affected test types, targeted lint/format, the SQLite worker ratchet, and diff checks passed.
- Independent `autoreview` reviewed all five changed files in full plus the startup, settlement, transcript transaction/CAS and foreground-admission owners; no actionable P0–P2 findings. Secret scanning of the complete candidate diff passed. This is an AI-assisted contribution.

Simplification kept classification and atomic settlement with their existing owners and cut over the sole classification caller. No competing recovery machinery was added. Production delta: +85/−20; tests: +94/−2; docs: +8.


### Shipped Gateway behavior proof (2026-10-21)

Exact-head isolated Gateway restart proof passed: no historical provider execution, saved reply retained locally as delivery-unconfirmed, and a fresh authenticated turn completed. Full sanitized evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178732#issuecomment-6306233298

Latest-stable upgrade/data compatibility proof also passed: released v2026.10.5 settings, transcript, and an identified pending-final obligation survived the documented Doctor migration and current-Gateway startup. Full sanitized evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178732#issuecomment-6306282928\n\nOnly the maintainer disposition decision remains open.

prs.title: fix(infra): database page-cache warm fails every 15 minutes on stock WSL kernels
prs.body:
Closes #177056

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on stock WSL kernels (no CONFIG_TASKSTATS, `/proc/self/io` absent) the post-ready database page-cache warmer aborts on every 15-minute cycle with a recurring `database page-cache warm failed` WARN and never warms the page cache.

## User Impact

User impact: WSL Gateways actually warm their databases after readiness; the recurring WARN disappears. On such kernels byte counters in the warm report read as zero and the pass runs unmetered, bounded by the existing per-target warm timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readIo()` treated any `/proc/self/io` read failure as fatal, but warming (residency probing and the bounded projection queries) does not depend on procfs I/O accounting. An ENOENT now zeroes the byte counters and continues — the same expected behavior the issue states — while every other read error (e.g. EACCES) stays terminal.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `src/infra/sqlite-page-cache.worker.test.ts`: with `/proc/self/io` stubbed ENOENT, the warm pass completes with zeroed counters and `limited: false` (red before: `pageCache.begin` threw); an EACCES stub still aborts (safety preserved).
- Existing worker tests (byte-budget stop, WAL snapshot retention) unchanged and green; `sqlite-readonly-worker.operations` green; format, oxlint, and tsgo core/test lanes clean.

prs.title: fix(agents): transcript admission conflicts burn retries and walk the fallback chain
prs.body:
Closes #177909

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a transcript idempotency-key conflict is classified as a model failure (`reason=unknown`), consumes empty-error retries, and walks the whole cross-provider fallback chain while every provider call in the window returns HTTP 200 — slower and more expensive turns plus a misleading "Model Fallback cleared" signal.

## User Impact

User impact: an admission conflict now fails the turn immediately at the model that hit it; it consumes no same-model retries, no model fallback, and never crosses providers.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isSessionTranscriptTurnMismatchErrorMessage` already recognizes the sibling transcript admission errors ("Pending input is no longer active in its admitted transcript", keyed-user mismatch) as terminal local errors. Adding the idempotency-conflict message to that shared matcher extends the same exclusion to all four of its consumers at once: the embedded assistant-failure abort, the `model-fallback-attempt` fallback stop gate, LLM transport retries, and subagent announce delivery retry.

## Evidence

- Embedded-entry regression in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failure.failover.test.ts`: the conflict message stops unchanged retries and model fallback — the run callback fires exactly once across a configured three-model fallback chain (red before: the turn was resubmitted per model).
- Consumer suites green: model-fallback chain-stop and core, `src/llm/utils/retry`, prompt-failure, attempt-session-replay, assistant-failure, and `subagents/announce`; format, oxlint, and tsgo lanes clean.

prs.title: fix(codex): existing Codex CLI sign-in silently discarded during import
prs.body:
Closes #177993

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: importing an existing Codex CLI ChatGPT sign-in (`openclaw migrate apply codex --include-secrets`, or the "Existing CLI sign-in" step of `openclaw models auth login`) silently imports nothing on Linux even though `~/.codex/auth.json` holds a valid, unexpired login.

## User Impact

User impact: a signed-in Codex CLI account is offered as `auth:openai` and imports successfully; the app-server's own startup `account/updated` announcement no longer discards it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reader snapshotted `getModelCatalogRevision()` and discarded the credential whenever the counter moved, but the bundled app-server emits `account/updated` on its own shortly after `initialize` while the reader is still running. The reader now subscribes via `addNotificationHandler` and applies the same-route policy already established in `inference-routing.ts` ("token rotation on the same native route is transparent"): same-route notifications (startup announcement, token rotation) keep the read valid; a cross-route mode change still discards it. A different user signing in on the same route mid-read is an accepted edge case, named in a comment.

## Evidence

- Regressions in `extensions/codex/src/migration/provider.auth.test.ts`: OAuth import survives `chatgpt` and `chatgptAuthTokens` startup announcements and API-key import survives `apiKey` (red before the fix); cross-route switches in both directions still discard the credential (safety preserved, green before and after).
- The mocked native delivers `account/updated` during the `config/read` window, reproducing the reported timing.
- Full `extensions/codex/src/migration` suite green; format, oxlint, and tsgo extensions/test lanes clean.

prs.title: fix(usage): OpenRouter usage always unavailable on Node 24 (dispatcher handed to the native fetch)
prs.body:
Closes #178133

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw status --usage` always lists OpenRouter as "Usage unavailable" on Node 24, even though the network is fine — the default usage fetch wraps the ambient global fetch, the SSRF guard treats any non-ambient implementation as dispatcher-capable and attaches its bundled-undici dispatcher, and Node's built-in fetch rejects that init (`UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG`) before any request is sent; the rejection was then swallowed into a bare transport error.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenRouter usage windows and billing appear with the default configuration on Node 24, no SNI workaround needed. When usage transport still fails, the snapshot records the failure cause (e.g. the undici error code) instead of only "Usage unavailable".

## Why This Change Was Made

The loader's default chain (no operator fetch, no ambient proxy) now runs on the bundled undici fetch, which honors per-request dispatchers — the transport the guard already assumes for non-ambient implementations, and the same choice the ambient-proxy and explicit-proxy paths make. Operator-supplied fetches and ambient proxy wrappers keep their own transport. The OpenRouter usage snapshot appends the recorded transport error message after the stable "Usage unavailable" prefix so misconfigurations are diagnosable from `status --usage --json`.

## Evidence

- Loader regression in `src/infra/provider-usage.load.plugin.test.ts`: with the global fetch stubbed to throw, the default context fetch now goes through the bundled undici transport (red before: it called the ambient global fetch); proxy routing and explicit-fetch precedence tests unchanged and green.
- Plugin regression in `extensions/openrouter/usage.test.ts`: a transport rejection surfaces its cause in the snapshot error (red before: bare "Usage unavailable"); SSRF-blocked and redirect cases assert the stable prefix.
- `provider-usage.load.test.ts` "fetch unavailable" case updated: with the ambient global fetch missing the loader now completes through the bundled transport instead of throwing — that state is structurally covered by the bundled dependency.
- Full provider-usage family and `extensions/openrouter` directory green (278 tests); format, oxlint, and tsgo core/extensions/test lanes clean.

## What Problem This Solves

The standalone board-fixture E2E writes seven manual screenshots on successful runs even when optional UI proof is disabled. Those images have no assertions or required consumers.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Normal CI avoids seven image captures; opt-in proof still captures all eight images, and the final diagnostic remains unconditional.

## Why This Change Was Made

Guard the seven success-path screenshot calls with the file's existing `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1` flag. Retain all original paths and options, all 16 cases, all assertions, all JSON artifacts, all network-idle waits, three fixture-server starts and two browser launches. The existing final.png call stays unconditional in `finally`, including failure paths. No new abstraction, fixture sharing, timing change or diagnostic policy.

Each capture already follows an explicit readiness signal. The security tests await browser policy events and native operation results; no defined observation period is removed. This is a different change from the withdrawn network-idle experiment #178867, whose timing rejection still stands.

## Evidence

Acceptance is frozen before candidate CI: at least 5% improvement in native file total F and at least 10% improvement in the sum of the four cases containing the seven optional captures, versus the source-qualified scheduled main baseline below. All 16 exact cases and all 14 UI jobs must pass. No case may regress 20% or more without exact-case, source-identical newer-main evidence. The owning shard's Test-step wall and file inventory are separate observations, not a sum of overlapping file spans. No queued-to-end metric is inferred from F.

Baseline: latest completed scheduled main [39524896041](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39524896041), head900e6aa3215fb46b933221cb490b22ab83e7d0cc. Root, server helper and suite helper blobs all match the candidate base. File F58.705s gives a cap of55.76975s; the four affected cases sum22.839s, capped at20.5551s. Those cases are profile/presence7.570s, native egress1.225s, attachments8.464s, and native plugin5.580s. All-case sum52.218s is reported separately.

| Work / proof | Before | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Default screenshots |8|1|
| Opt-in screenshots |8|8|
| Cases |16|16|
| All original AST nodes, after unwrapping seven capture guards |—|Identical|
| JSON artifacts / waits / final diagnostic |Existing|Unchanged|
| File F |58.705 s|47.536 s (-19.03%)|
| Four affected cases |22.839 s|17.337 s (-24.09%)|
| Owning mock6/9 Test step |579 s / 99 files|558 s / 100 files; different inventory|
| Frozen install, UI types, exact E2E types, scoped lint/format/diff |—|Passed|
| Independent P0–P2 review |—|Scoped-clean, confidence 0.97|

No local E2E, app build or broad suite under the campaign compute budget; CI owns runtime/timing proof. No product, startup, dependency or visual product change. Test LOC 921→938 (+17), solely guards and formatter wrapping; production and Solid refactor counts 0. No Testbox/Crabbox lease.

Run [39528319063](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39528319063) completed successfully at exact head 0b07d06450051040e49c3a58625ff91b5e583495. All 16 exact cases and all 14 UI jobs passed; every case was faster than the baseline, so no matching-main exception was used. Both frozen speed gates pass. All-case sum was 52.218→42.573 s. The four affected cases were profile/presence 7.570→5.745 s, native egress 1.225→1.045 s, attachments 8.464→6.651 s, and native plugin 5.580→3.896 s.

Causal limit: unaffected cases also improved. The 11.169-second file reduction is an observed run difference, not a claim that screenshots alone cost that amount. The owning shard improved 21 seconds with a different file inventory; no causal shard saving is claimed.

prs.title: refactor(automations): run scheduled conversation work through session admission
prs.body:
Related: #167796. Slice 2 of 4, following landed #178650. Doctor migration is slice 3; heartbeat execution and SDK retirement are slice 4.

## What Problem This Solves

An existing `session:<key>` scheduled agent turn needs to join its conversation's ordinary admission and mailbox and remain running until that turn settles. Running it through the detached executor gives execution, authority, workspace and delivery decisions a second owner.

## User Impact

Explicit conversation jobs now use the session controller and retain their authenticated source, model/account policy, managed workspace, delivery policy and recorded result. Cron records completion only after the controller settles. Main-session system events retain #178650's adoption and restart behavior. Legacy heartbeats and detached jobs remain working; this slice performs no migration.

Claw Add review accepts positive-integer `everyMs` schedules and `owner` delivery, as Peter approved on October 18. Existing cron/timezone and none/last-channel variants remain unchanged. Runtime owner delivery and portable Claw Add conversion follow in slice 3.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both execution paths share Cron's authority, inference, telemetry, workspace and prompt owners. Deferred admission revalidates policy; disallowed or malformed models and contradictory targets fail visibly. Scheduled model/account choices stay turn-local and do not replace the conversation's saved preferences. A recorded job account retains independent authorization, including replacement and revocation checks.

The shared prompt builder preserves job identity, local/UTC time, legacy Gmail/custom-hook untrusted wrapping, the existing unsafe-content opt-in and unattended guidance. Source leases and managed-worktree custody remain live through settlement and terminal writes. No authority is widened.

## Evidence

- Focused proof: 294 unique cases across 25 Cron, Gateway, reply and protocol files, with unchanged-input proof reused. Later repair selections overlap this total and are not summed into it.
- Failing-before/passing-after boundary regressions cover session routing/settlement, revoked and malformed models, terminal error loss, subagent model precedence, saved account-pin replacement, unavailable destination account with a valid recorded job binding, and legacy hook prompt wrapping/identity/time.
- Real deferred admission and account policy: 17 cases pass in 55.9 seconds Vitest / 76.4 seconds wrapper; 20 existing inference/admission consumers also pass. The earlier model/fallback selection passes 81 cases across eight files, including restart cases. These slower cases exercise actual queueing, policy publication, storage, authorization and filesystem effects.
- Authenticated continuation: all 13 fixture cases pass through the ordinary execution owner, including restart recovery and revocation during a merge attempt. Real isolated Gateway/synthetic-model continuation passes in 23.9 seconds within the unchanged 90-second timeout.
- Final prompt repair: 28 cases across the session runner, detached prompt consumer and restart regression pass in 29.2 seconds Vitest / 32.4 seconds wrapper. The new prompt cases fail on the preceding head for the expected missing-context/untrusted-wrapper assertions; their test bodies take milliseconds. The prompt-prefix stability test also passes.
- CI caught an older adapter test that still expected a locked session to allow fallbacks after the model-lock repair. The corrected table retains exact declared/empty fallback assertions for unlocked sessions and verifies suppression under a lock. All 12 file cases pass in 6.2 seconds; the existing real queued lock scenario also passes in 8.4 seconds (11.8 seconds wrapper). Production behavior is unchanged.
- Review caught a setup-watchdog gap after queued session adoption. Queue owners now report actual wait/admit transitions, including native capacity waits and policy re-admission; provider start retains its separate execution deadline. The watchdog regression fails on the preceding head, and the real deferred-session case fails before the lifecycle wiring. The corrected selection passes 32 cases, including restart, source authority and both execution adapters; no timeouts or assertions were weakened.
- The final delivery repair carries Cron’s existing resolved-tool prompt finalizer into both ordinary execution adapters. It supplies safe explicit-target metadata and automatic-delivery guidance only after actual tool availability is known; the inbound owner continues to supply routed formatting once. Five missing-guidance regressions fail before the fix; all 28 touched-suite cases, 19 restart/prefix/native-tool-policy cases and two focused CLI finalization cases pass. Shared system prefixes remain unchanged.
- CI exposed a static type-import cycle in the finalizer adapter. Moving the unchanged callback type into a dependency-free contract fixes it: the exact Madge check fails before and reports zero cycles after. Both affected type graphs, typed lint, format and nine existing prompt/restart cases pass; no runtime behavior or test assertions changed.
- A queued Gmail-hook regression showed that revoking `hooks.gmail.allowUnsafeExternalContent` could leave the old unwrapped prompt after config re-admission. Cron now retains the raw occurrence and rebuilds the prompt with each admitted config, keeping its original firing timestamp. The real Cron/queue regression fails before the fix; all 57 affected queue, source-custody, prompt and restart cases pass (108 seconds wrapper; the new case takes 3.2 seconds).
- Merged current main `f70a4ba83c2b` after GitHub reported a conflict. The sole overlap was the failure-alert fixture: it now uses main’s shared setup while retaining both execution adapters. All six failure-alert/restart cases and four Claw schema cases pass; core/Cron/infra types, typed lint, format, exact staged line-growth and zero-cycle Madge pass. No production file overlapped.
- Rejected turns now retain their actionable recovery payload in automation receipts. The context-overflow regression fails before the fix with only a generic error, then passes with the existing `/compact` and `/new` guidance. The affected selection passes all 33 cases across the initial run and focused replay; 22 handoff and three restart cases also pass. Core/infra types, typed lint, format and line-growth pass; local and committed delta reviews are scoped-clean through P2. No authority, status or delivery policy changed.
- CI9 caught a missing required `durationMs` field in the new synthetic context-overflow fixture. The owning messaging type graph reproduces the error before the one-line fixture correction and passes after it. The selected context-overflow case still passes in 3.1 seconds (14.8 seconds wrapper); typed lint, format and local/committed delta reviews pass. No production behavior or assertion changed.
- Review found that a message-tool send could retain the destination captured before queued execution. The Automations owner now composes its existing live destination check into the message capability’s occurrence fence. The real Cron/controller/message-tool regression fails before the fix; changed-route, unchanged-route and `delivery:none` controls pass afterward. All 39 affected cases, including restart, pass in 76.7 seconds; core/messaging type graphs, typed lint, format and line-growth pass. The change adds three net production lines and preserves the original occurrence authority.
- Affected compiler graphs, typed lint, format, whitespace and line-growth ratchet pass. Protocol generation/check, prompt snapshots and the package build pass without tracked generated drift. The import-cycle guard reports zero cycles. Codex reviews are scoped-clean through P2.

The prior-head Android Play CI run ([39518190275, job 118956103466](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39518190275/job/118956103466)) timed out in `ChatComposerLayoutTest.modelSelectionPinsNamedDefaultAndKeepsAdmittedEffectOwned` at its unchanged 1-second catalog wait. A secretless Linux replay with matching Java/Gradle pins and two test forks passed the exact case 3/3 on clean CI main `d6e3a30c0bfce` and 3/3 on the tested merge `439a6ede1c35`. The Android source and relevant toolchain inputs match. This is non-reproduction evidence, not an inherited-failure or repair claim; the isolated replay does not reproduce preceding suite order/load. Android Play subsequently passed in exact-head run 39520774003 on `9b4a2cabd181`.

CI run [39523844566, job 118974256949](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39523844566/job/118974256949) fails `server.sessions.create-notices.test.ts:144`: its trusted spawn fixture expects a human profile while the existing delegated-creator projection returns an agent. The original 28-file shard selection with CI's checksum-pinned Bun reproduces the identical assertion on clean current main `1989e3dc4360` on macOS; the complete selection has 1 failure/222 passes in 190.6 seconds (the first batch matches CI at 1 failure/135 passes). The test, creation handler, inheritance, provenance and row-projection inputs are unchanged by this PR. The run completed with 101 successful jobs, 20 skipped jobs, this inherited failure and its aggregate gate. The next completed run [39526422189](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39526422189) on `66a8829ab738` had 100 successful jobs, 20 skipped jobs, the same inherited creator failure, the now-repaired fixture type failure, and the aggregate gate. prs.title: fix(memory): continue after an oversized first line
prs.body:
Closes #178506

## What Problem This Solves

`memory_get` dropped the paging cursor when the first returned line exceeded the `maxChars` budget, even when later lines existed. The result contained `truncated: true` and `lines: 1` but no `nextFrom`, and the notice only said that the budget was exceeded. Repeating the same read returned the same truncated first line, leaving every following line effectively hidden.

## Fix

`hardTruncatedSingleLine` only indicates that the included line itself was cut; it does not indicate whether source lines remain after it. The continuation calculation now follows the existing `moreSourceLinesRemain || includedLines < selectedLines.length` condition without that unrelated guard.

Behavior after this change:

- An oversized first line followed by more content returns `nextFrom: start + 1`.
- The notice includes `Use from=2 to continue.` and retains the read-fallback hint when enabled.
- An oversized line that is also the final line still returns no `nextFrom`.
- Ordinary continuation, truncation, surrogate-pair, and terminal-newline behavior is unchanged.

No schema changes are introduced.

## Evidence

### Base-red

On the pre-fix implementation, the new focused regression fails as expected:

```text
expected { status: 'ok', …(5) } to deeply equal { status: 'ok', …(6) }

- "nextFrom": 2,
+ [More content available. Requested excerpt exceeded the default maxChars budget.
```

The filesystem compatibility regression also expects `nextFrom: 2` and verifies that `from=2` returns `line 2`.

### Validation

```text
packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file-manager-compat.test.ts
packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file-shared.test.ts

26 passed / 26
```

Both Vitest shards passed.

`check:changed` is not used as merge evidence on this host: its `tsgo` binary requires glibc >= 2.29, while this environment has glibc 2.28. The current main baseline also has unrelated existing `check:changed` failures around UI max-lines suppressions and dead-export checks.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal setup, ingress, and capture owners repeatedly rebuild argument/result packets for private work that has only one production consumer.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change or migration. Public SDK, protocol, CLI and config contracts, lazy imports, security checks, normal concurrency, and durable state/transcript behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep private phases with the caller that already owns their inputs. Inline the screenshot callback and OpenCode classifier, localize same-owner setup/auth/ingress/capture helpers, remove Gemini's private kind/value result protocol, and fold seven static compatibility records into their existing registry slots. Shared operations remain shared; no replacement abstraction is introduced.

The branch removes **528 net production lines** (+1,834/-2,362), excluding tests/support/generated/declarations. Twenty-eight paths change, including an exact seven-entry shrink of the wrapper inventory for the removed compatibility leaves. The only test addition exercises literal/null/mixed unions through the public Gemini cleaner, with independent expected outputs. Author simplification keeps all remaining algorithms and meaningful shared ownership.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None newly introduced. No guard, recovery policy, feature, input validation or security effect check is removed. Invocation-time captures, post-await authority, deadlines, replay/settlement, redaction, output bytes and existing compatibility dates/order are retained. No config/schema/protocol/dependency change.

The pre-existing Feishu unresolved-chat lookup fallback is tracked by #162741 and is not fixed or newly introduced here. Its future fix, #139396 durable direct-effect claims and #148842 registered interactions must be retained on overlap. The standalone Phase E memory backend and related machinery are untouched.

## Evidence

Fresh independent full-branch P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean with final source verification. Subsequent mechanical repairs rename a shadowing timeout binding without changing error text and remove exactly seven stale wrapper-inventory entries. The closure failure was ours; no test or guard was weakened.

Targeted native types and format passed for every packet. Earlier focused setup, Slack, Matrix/SMS, LM Studio, ingress/compatibility and capture suites passed, including prompt-prefix stability and OpenAI device-code/provider behavior. The capture packet passed five routed Vitest shards; this is not live provider/device proof.

The full local typed-lint attempts retain four SDK declaration-resolution diagnostics: two unchanged SMS callback annotations and two unchanged OpenCode activity union annotations. The OpenCode diagnostics reproduced on clean main `1cb69ee6228d0da0bfb79b37530e1e2ff92583ae` with the exact same source blob as the branch base. The selected other owners pass typed lint after repairing the new Z.AI shadowing issue. These are investigated local limitations, not a claim that all lint passes or that any hosted failure is inherited. No cast, suppression, timeout, retry, skip or baseline was added to hide them.

The final context packet passed **180 tests across ten owner files and seven routed shards**. The suppression audit passed all 14 checks. The repaired wrapper/eager import closure passed four selected cases; changed-source line caps, assertion safety, mock exports, and runtime/static cycle checks passed, with zero runtime cycles. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad proof. Local runtime proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG directories, nice priority and one worker; no live channel/browser/provider or upgrade claim is made.

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop publication footer stripping from backtracking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The publication description stripper used

```
(?:\s*---\s*\n\[View the OpenClaw team session\]\([^\r\n)]*\)\s*)+$
```

The trailing `\s*` sits **inside** the repeated group, so whitespace between two
footers has two possible owners — the previous unit's trailing `\s*` or the next
unit's leading one. Once the body ends in anything the pattern cannot consume,
the engine walks every split of that ambiguity before failing.

## Evidence: real publication, before and after

The production-path proof uses unmocked `runCommandBuffered`, real `git`, real `gh`,
and real draft pull requests in a throwaway public repository. It runs through
`coordinator.requestForSession` into `executeGitHubPublication`; no publication
transport or PR-creation response is mocked.

With the fix, a 1,103-byte description containing 28 unfinished footer-shaped units
published successfully in 18,213 ms as
[lzhan011/openclaw-publication-proof#3](https://github.com/lzhan011/openclaw-publication-proof/pull/3).
The resulting 1,271-byte body preserved the incomplete units and appended exactly
one canonical session footer.

With only the regex restored to `main` and the same input/setup, publication failed
with `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST`: synchronous backtracking held the thread long
enough for the publication state lease to expire before commit.

A prior real 26-unit pair was inconclusive because variable `git push` and GitHub API
latency exceeded the regex-cost difference (37,952 ms before versus 47,038 ms after);
both runs published. On that exact input, isolated pattern timing was 16,154.5 ms on
`main` versus 0.1 ms with the fix, with byte-identical output.

The focused regression test uses mocked command transport so it can assert a stable
five-second bound in CI. Its 90 ms local and 364 ms CI measurements validate the
same coordinator path but are not claimed as end-to-end GitHub timings. The real
proof above covers identity resolution, commit, branch update, push, and pull-request
creation; it drives the coordinator directly rather than through a running Gateway
server.

## Why This Change Was Made

`row.body` is supplied by the caller of the publication request — the
`github-publish` agent tool (`src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.ts:42`) or the
Gateway protocol method — and reaches this line unchanged:
`input.body` (`github-publication-coordinator-methods.ts:167`) →
`requestForClaim({ body })` → `body: request.body ?? null`
(`github-publication-store.ts:186`) → `row.body`.

The fix hoists the trailing `\s*` out of the group:

```
(?:\s*---\s*\n\[View the OpenClaw team session\]\([^\r\n)]*\))+\s*$
```

Whitespace between footers now has exactly one owner. The language is unchanged:
a differential run of the two patterns over **400,000 random strings** assembled
from footer-shaped fragments (`---`, newlines, tabs, spaces, CR, the link label,
parens, complete footers, plain text) found **0 differences**.

## Review items addressed

- **Proof through the production executor.** The numbers above come from
  `coordinator.requestForSession` running to pull-request creation, not from the
  pattern in isolation.
- **Test consolidation.** The earlier revision exported a
  `stripPublicationDescriptionFooters` helper purely so a unit test could reach
  it. That export is gone; the fix is inline again and the regression test lives
  in `github-publication-attribution.test.ts` alongside the other
  published-output assertions. Production delta is now **+5 / -1**.

## Checks

`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both changed files — clean.
`vitest run src/gateway/github-publication-attribution.test.ts
src/gateway/github-publication.test.ts` — 23/23 passed.

**Pre-existing failure, not from this change.** `pnpm tsgo:core` fails on
`src/infra/install-package-dir.ts(551,15): error TS2353`, inherited from `main`.

## How This Was Found

CodeQL `js/redos` over a `src/` database. The reachability of `row.body` and the
8 KiB cap were traced by hand, and every number above was measured.

## Diff accounting

- production: +5 / -1
- tests: +43 / -0

prs.title: fix: keep ordinary tests from reaching GitHub
prs.body:
Thanks for maintaining OpenClaw. I found this while running ordinary development tests in my fork.

## What Problem This Solves

**Ordinary tests should not contact real GitHub services or borrow the developer’s GitHub credentials.** Some fixtures did reach for real release downloads and Git remotes. This PR fixes those destinations and adds a guard against future accidental access.

## User Impact

Ordinary test runs block supported GitHub requests **before dispatch**, remove ambient GitHub credentials from test children, and report unexpected attempts even when a test catches the rejection. Intentional live tests retain a separate, explicit entry point; a flag inherited from the developer’s shell cannot silently enable access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit caught **four GitHub-bound attempts**: two release-asset downloads, a worker Git fetch, and a fork-publication Git fetch. Their fixtures now use local substitutes. The guard covers fetch/HTTP, sockets, Chromium, and child `gh`, `git`, and shell commands.

It also repairs release fixtures whose fake `gh` executable was rejected by the guard, triggering repeated polling. Moving the fake into the admitted temporary location eliminated that fixture conflict; all 44 affected release tests subsequently passed.

**The 17,331 repeated refusals were local fixture commands—not 17,331 GitHub API calls.** All four confirmed GitHub-bound attempts were blocked during the audit. We did not measure quota consumption or demonstrate a rate-limit lockout.

## Evidence

Rebased onto `e9a671bf2173` on October 21. The release-fixture conflict now preserves both initial state seeding and isolated fake tools. All 46 release tests pass (71.5 s) behind the network fence, with zero GitHub attempts; affected formatting, lint, and types pass. The original commit sequence is preserved.

The commits preserve the requested order: first the blocking guard and audit evidence, then fixture repairs with the guard retained.

ClawSweeper’s four fixture conflicts are now repaired: Git cancellation uses a held local transport; worker identity admits only its declared synthetic profile; shell inspection distinguishes literal arrays and lowercase `path` from commands and `PATH`; Chromium starts with an empty standalone page before guarded navigation. The original behavior assertions remain intact.

Affected fixture scenarios and 115 guard regression tests pass behind the OS network fence, with zero unexpected attempts. Formatting, affected lint, and five relevant test type graphs pass.

**The full ordinary-suite audit remains incomplete.** The JavaScript guard cannot fully police opaque native executables. Tests also ran behind an OS network fence. The earlier broad check recorded two inherited failures; it was not rerun for this scoped rebase.

<details>
<summary>Current validation details</summary>

- ClawSweeper repairs: browser/guard 13 passed (21.75 s); worker identity 3 passed (170.14 s); merge workflow 3 passed (31.74 s). Git lifecycle: 21 passed, one platform skip (126.48 s), then all four affected cancellation cases passed after fixture extraction (27.24 s).
- Guard regressions: 115 passed, four platform skips (24.59 s); zero unexpected attempts and 117 intentional blocking controls. Aggregate reporting omitted three control attributions; counters were retained. Browser controls added eight intentional refusals. These counts are blocked tests, not sent requests.
- Independent P0–P2 review identified Zsh’s linked `path` array; repaired and reproduced through command, script, and sourced-file entry points. Final command-guard suite: 50 passed (3.03 s), zero unexpected attempts, 49 controls; affected lint and types passed again.
- Selected 12-file run: 466.38 s, 309 passed, four prerequisite failures, four skipped. Only the four failed cases were rerun: all passed in 12.66 s, with zero incidental refusals and three intentional blocking controls.
- Initial run: 67 incidental command refusals and 117 controls. These are refusal counters, not evidence of sent requests.
- Selected changed check: 546.08 s. Types, lint, formatting, and dead-export scans passed. Failures concern three existing UI max-lines suppressions and four existing core test-shard root-count limits; their governing sources/configuration match the pinned main base.
- The historical audit retained 569 native reports from a 643-invocation plan across interrupted runs and recoveries, with 230 omitted attributions. It is not a completed full-suite result.

</details>

prs.title: fix(discord): thread replies and bindings stop working when a slow channel stop overlaps a restart
prs.body:
Related: #177691

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord thread replies and thread bindings stop working when a channel restart begins while the previous Discord task is still stopping.

This is rare, and permanent until the next provider start. That recovery is read from the code, not run.

Two entries start the replacement while the old task still runs. A start after a timed-out stop does it, at `src/gateway/server-channels.ts:557-575`. A config reload does it through the route handoff, after the 5 s stop grace. The old task must also be slow to reach its Discord stop, as voice teardown or the startup ACP binding check can make it. That check takes no abort signal and can spend up to 8 s per binding. Only the config reload was run. The rest is read from the code.

## User Impact

A late stop from an older Discord task now leaves the newest task's thread bindings alone, so bind, touch and replies keep working.

Four behaviors change.

- A task that never stops now leaves its retired adapter registered after the newest owner stops. Until it stops, the adapter reports itself available, bind and touch fail with a plain "retired" error that has no code, and the deprecated synchronous read still returns the binding. Main clears all of this at the newest owner's stop. An earlier local probe, on the same production code, showed this.
- Work the old owner has in flight when the replacement registers fails with the same plain "retired" error. A bind paused at webhook creation publishes nothing, and a webhook already created is not undone. The same earlier probe showed this.
- A native thread or webhook that the old owner created mid-bind is not published either, because the commit step still requires a current manager. On main that bind would have finished, since the old stop drains in-flight work first. Read from `thread-bindings.manager.ts`, not run. I add no code for it.
- A fresh manager applies the replacement's idle timeout and max age to new bindings, where reuse ignored them. Existing bindings keep their stored limits. The same earlier probe showed this.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each provider start now owns its thread binding manager. On main, `createLoadedThreadBindingManager` returns the account's existing manager, so a replacement shares the old task's manager and that task's late `stop()` tears it down. The change deletes that early return, four lines in `thread-bindings.manager.ts`. A manager's stop clears the registry entry and token only when it is current, and the session binding registry already stacks adapters and unregisters each by identity.

The maintainers merged the same deletion for Feishu in #169226. The refcount alternative, #170054, was closed as a duplicate of it.

PR #177691 replaces a cached manager only when its owner's runtime has retired, and this PR removes reuse of a live owner's manager, which my comment on #177691 already said needs a separate change.

I left the retry in `createThreadBindingManager` that waits for a stopping manager. Production code can no longer reach it, which I read from the code. I will remove it in a follow-up if asked.

## Evidence

### Tests

`thread-bindings.restart.test.ts` is new. It drives the real lifecycle, supervisor and manager. A restart overtakes an old task whose voice teardown is held. The replacement must still bind and touch, and must tear down on its own stop. With main's `thread-bindings.manager.ts`, all 3 cases fail. Bind rejects with `BINDING_ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE`, touch rejects with "manager is stopping", and the third case finds no registered manager. All 3 pass at `2ae50585b7c`.

`thread-bindings.creation.test.ts` changes one existing test. It keeps the replaced manager as `previous`, stops it after the existing assertions, and checks the saved token is still `token-new`. With main's manager file, the creation file fails 1 of 15 with `expected undefined to be 'token-new'`. There `previous` and `manager` are one object, and its stop clears the token. The extra stop also keeps `previous` from staying registered for the rest of the file, so this is more than cleanup. No existing assertion changed.

At `2ae50585b7c`, 170 tests pass in the 19 Discord monitor test files. The creation file passes 15 of 15.

### Built Gateway proof

I ran one sequence on two built Gateways, main at `7e81872cbbc` and this branch at `2ae50585b7c`. Apart from build metadata, their built output differs only in the deleted early return. Crabline 0.1.29 stands in for Discord REST and WebSocket, and the repo's mock model server answers for the model. There was no real Discord bot or model. Command and button interactions were synthesized and sent to the newest task's socket only, and a leaked second socket from the old task was open on both builds.

The trigger was two `channels.discord.historyLimit` edits about 3 s apart while one `GET /api/v10/gateway/bot` response was held about 10 s. The network edge delayed only that response and forwarded everything else unchanged, apart from rewriting the gateway `url` field of every `/gateway/bot` response, held or not, on both builds. The first edit restarts the channel, and the new task blocks on the held response, a wait with no abort signal. The second edit stops that task, but the held request is never aborted. After the 5 s grace the Gateway logs `channel stop exceeded 5000ms after abort` and starts a third task. On release, the old task fails with `Plugin service scheduler is closed` and its `finally` calls `threadBindings.stop()`. The throw site was not captured. The race is narrow. It needs a second stop while a startup is blocked for more than about 8 s.

| Step | main | fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control, two edits, nothing held | no stop timeout, bind and reply work | same |
| Messages after the late stop | 3 of 3 guild-thread messages, bound and unbound, got no reply and failed with `SessionWorkStartChangedError`, retried by the ingress spool for at least 142 s | replies in the unbound, newly bound and old bound threads |
| Bind in a new thread | replied `Session binding owner changed for discord:default`, no approval, no row | approved, row written |

On main, a bound turn sent after the third task started and before the release was answered. Main failed in all 4 of its runs, one of them exploratory. The fix passed both of its runs. Logpoints show the mechanism. On main the third task reuses the old task's manager, and the late stop finds it is the registry entry. On the fix it does not.

```text
main 20:00:40.200 {"ev":"manager-stop-called","accountId":"default","alreadyStopping":false,"managerIsRegistryEntry":true}
fix  20:05:42.429 {"ev":"manager-stop-called","accountId":"default","alreadyStopping":false,"managerIsRegistryEntry":false}
```

Log prefixes are trimmed. Separately, the old task opens a Discord gateway socket that stayed open on both builds until the harness killed the Gateway. This PR does not change that.
