prs.title: fix(anthropic): history replays as native login when managed settings switch auth
prs.body:
Related: #164796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` on, OpenClaw attests the native Claude login as the conversation owner and replays saved history even when Claude's admin-managed settings make the Claude child authenticate with an API key or an API key helper instead of that login.

## User Impact

Operators who opted in to native-login history ownership no longer get saved history attributed to the native login when their host administrator's `managed-settings.json` (or a `managed-settings.d/*.json` drop-in) sets `apiKeyHelper` or an auth `env` key such as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`. Those turns now behave like any other non-native login: `auth-unknown`, no saved-history replay, and the native token is never sent to the profile endpoint. Hosts without managed settings, or with managed settings that set no auth key, are unchanged. Nothing changes for installs without the opt-in.

## Why This Change Was Made

The #164796 landing review named this follow-up: "the native-login check reads user settings, `apiKeyHelper` and the spawn environment, but not Claude's admin-managed settings `env` block. Only the host administrator can write that file ... treat managed-settings auth keys as non-native."

The bundled backend passes `--setting-sources user`, but Claude Code always loads managed settings: its settings docs list `--setting-sources` values as only `user`, `project` and `local`, rank managed settings above all of them ("Nothing in your own settings files or `--settings` overrides a managed key"), and give both `env` and `apiKeyHelper` the scope "Any file". So a managed auth key switches the child off the stored login while OpenClaw still attests that login's account.

## The change in one sentence

`readClaudeNativeLoginCredential` also refuses when Claude's managed settings file or any non-hidden `*.json` drop-in beside it sets `apiKeyHelper` or one of the existing `CLAUDE_NON_NATIVE_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` in `env`, reading the managed directory Claude Code documents for the platform.

3 files, +80/-5: the production file +53/-4, one test, one docs sentence. No new config, export, state or dependency; the user-settings `env` check becomes a shared helper so both sources use one key list, and the only new option is an internal `managedSettingsDir` test seam. `readClaudeCliCredentials` and `src/agents/cli-credentials.ts` are untouched.

## Contract table

| Source | Sets | Native owner after this change |
|---|---|---|
| Managed `managed-settings.json` | non-empty `apiKeyHelper` | none (`auth-unknown`) |
| Managed `managed-settings.json` | any `CLAUDE_NON_NATIVE_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` key, non-empty, in `env` | none |
| Managed `managed-settings.d/<name>.json` drop-in | either of the above | none |
| Hidden (`.name.json`) or non-`.json` drop-in | anything | ignored, as Claude ignores it |
| Managed settings without auth keys (e.g. only `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`) | | unchanged: attested owner |
| No managed directory, missing or unreadable drop-in directory | | unchanged |
| Managed file present but malformed JSON | | ignored, same as the user-settings readers (`loadJsonFileThroughSymlink` yields nothing). Claude Code refuses to start on a malformed managed file, so no child runs under that login either way. |
| Later drop-in blanks a key an earlier file set | | refused (each file is checked alone; this can only over-refuse) |
| MDM policy (macOS `com.anthropic.claudecode` profile, Windows HKLM/HKCU `Policies\ClaudeCode`) | | not checked: deliberately unhandled, see Gaps |
| Server-managed settings | | not checked: deliberately unhandled, see Gaps |

Managed directory per Claude Code's settings docs: macOS `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode`, Linux and WSL `/etc/claude-code`, Windows `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode` (the legacy `C:\ProgramData` path is documented as not read). Drop-in rules from the same docs: "every `*.json` file in the directory in alphabetical order" and "ignores hidden files and files that don't end in `.json`". Nothing in the repo resolved these paths before; the only existing mention is the `--managed-settings` entry in the restricted-arguments list in `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts`, which blocks the flag rather than reading a file.

Fail direction for an unreadable or malformed file: matches how `userSettingsSelectNonNativeAuth` and `readClaudeApiKeyHelper` already treat user settings (no key found). Failing closed would refuse ownership on hosts where Claude itself starts without that source (an OS-denied read) or does not start at all (a parse error), with no auth to protect.

## Evidence

All runs on one macOS machine at the PR head tree `01c9f14b6f8d13d1443779cb6790c506457f2b42`, base `8d9e341071b`. BEFORE = the PR head with only `provider-auth-claude-compat.ts` restored to base (test and docs kept).

### Build

`pnpm build` exit 0 on both arms, each in its own clean checkout:

```
AFTER:  [build-all] phase timings: total 2m 40.5s; slowest write-unified-entry-dts 58.9s ...
BEFORE: [build-all] phase timings: total 1m 3.6s; slowest tsdown 20.9s ...
```

### Behaviour through the shipped entry point

The #164796 harness drives the built `openclaw agent --local` with a real SQLite session, real native-login files, `attestNativeLogin: true`, the real Anthropic Claude runtime and stream-json transport. Only the `claude` executable is a synthetic child that records what reaches it, and Anthropic's profile endpoint is a local stub that attests synthetic tokens. Turn 1 stores codeword `PINEAPPLE-7` on account A; turn 2 starts a fresh Claude session, which receives saved history only if the conversation has an attested owner.

The macOS managed directory needs root to write, so a Node preload (`--import`) redirects only paths under `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode` to a per-case fixture directory and logs each redirected call; no other path is touched. Fixtures (synthetic values): control = `managed-settings.json` with `{"env":{"DISABLE_TELEMETRY":"1"}}`; env = the same plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; helper = control plus `managed-settings.d/50-auth.json` with `apiKeyHelper`.

| Arm and case | turn 2 user message chars (PINEAPPLE-7 count) | stored boundary after turn 2 | profile requests | turn 2 refusal log | managed-path reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BEFORE control | 516 (1) | `known` | 2 | none | 0 |
| BEFORE env | 516 (1) | `known` | 2 | none | 0 |
| BEFORE helper | 516 (1) | `known` | 2 | none | 0 |
| AFTER control | 516 (1) | `known` | 2 | none | 28 |
| AFTER env | 449 (0) | `none` | 0 | `reason=auth-unknown` | 4 |
| AFTER helper | 449 (0) | `none` | 0 | `reason=auth-unknown` | 6 |

BEFORE replays the saved codeword into the fresh session under both managed auth fixtures and never reads the managed directory. AFTER refuses both, never sends the token to the profile endpoint, and leaves the control identical to BEFORE. Both turns exit 0 on every row.

### Tests

`pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-claude-compat.test.ts`:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 1.25s
```

Owning directory `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/` (after `pnpm build`): `Test Files  75 passed (75)` / `Tests  420 passed (420)`, `1 passed` / `1 passed`, `32 passed` / `287 passed`, `[test] passed 5 Vitest shards in 155.41s`.

Consumers: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-credentials.test.ts`: `Tests  17 passed (17)`; `pnpm test extensions/anthropic/`: `Test Files  37 passed (37)`, `Tests  424 passed | 1 skipped (425)`.

### Regression proof

Each mutation applied alone to the production file, the test file run alone, the file restored and the checkout verified clean:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| RED0 production file restored to base (the original defect) | `Tests  1 failed \| 28 passed (29)`, `AssertionError: expected 'uuid:uuid-a' to be undefined` |
| RED1 drop-in directory never read | 1 failed, `expected 'uuid:uuid-a' to be undefined` |
| RED2 hidden drop-ins not skipped | 1 failed, `expected undefined to be 'uuid:uuid-a'` |
| RED3 non-`.json` drop-ins not skipped | 1 failed, `expected undefined to be 'uuid:uuid-a'` |
| RED4 managed `apiKeyHelper` ignored | 1 failed, `expected 'uuid:uuid-a' to be undefined` |
| RED5 managed `env` auth keys ignored | 1 failed, `expected 'uuid:uuid-a' to be undefined` |
| GREEN | `Tests  29 passed (29)` |

The test also checks the synchronous `readClaudeNativeLoginOwner` recheck: an owner attested before the managed file gained `apiKeyHelper` is no longer returned for the same token.

### Other checks

<details><summary>Typecheck, lint, cycles, check:changed</summary>

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` | `Madge import cycle check: 0 cycle(s).` |
| `git diff --check 8d9e341071b HEAD` | clean |
| type-aware oxlint on both changed files | `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.` |
| `pnpm check:changed --base 8d9e341071b` | 36 ok, 4 failed; none involves a file in this diff, each reproduces on a pristine checkout of `8d9e341071b`: `max-lines suppression ratchet` (three `ui/src/pages/...` files), `deprecated API usage` (`src/infra/outbound/delivery-completion.shard-test-support.ts`), `dead export scan` (`src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts: PluginRuntimeResolver`, `src/transcripts/capture.ts: TranscriptsLogger`), `core tsgo graph boundary` (four core test shards over the advisory 720-root budget). The line-cap growth ratchet passed. |
| `pnpm changed:lanes --json` | core, coreTests, extensions, extensionTests, docs |

</details>

### Measured test cost

One new test, 3 ms; the whole test file runs in 1.25 s.

## Gaps, stated plainly

- MDM and OS policy (macOS `com.anthropic.claudecode` managed preferences, Windows HKLM and HKCU `SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode`) and server-managed settings are not checked. They can set `env` too. OpenClaw cannot read server-managed settings, and the MDM sources need platform-specific readers; a host that delivers auth keys only through them still gets an attested native owner.
- WSL inheriting the Windows policy chain (`wslInheritsWindowsSettings`) is not checked: OpenClaw on WSL reports `linux` and reads only `/etc/claude-code`, so a Windows-side managed auth key that WSL Claude inherits is missed, the same class as the MDM gap.
- A managed `apiKeyHelper` set to an empty string is treated as unset, like the user-settings reader; no test pins that, and dropping the check could only over-refuse.
- Claude's cross-source rules are not modeled: with the default "first-wins", a higher admin source (MDM or server-managed) can make Claude ignore the file-based `apiKeyHelper`, and a later drop-in can blank an earlier key. In both cases this change refuses an owner Claude might still use. It can over-refuse, never under-refuse, relative to the managed files.
- The shipped-entry proof ran on macOS with the managed directory redirected by a preload, because writing the real directory needs root. The Linux and Windows directories are covered only by reading Claude Code's docs, not by a run.
- Existing tests that run with `platform: "darwin"` or `"linux"` read the real managed directory of the test host; a developer machine with a managed `apiKeyHelper` would see those attestation tests refuse.
- The Claude child is synthetic and the profile endpoint is a stub; the BEFORE/AFTER difference is entirely in OpenClaw's attestation decision, which is what changed.

prs.title: fix(net-policy): match credential query-param spelling variants and remove ambiguous regex quantifiers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two robustness problems in first-party code, both found by running dynamic tools over the repo rather than by reading it.

**Credential query-param spelling variants were not recognized.** `isSensitiveUrlQueryParamName` compared a lowercased name with `-` mapped to `_`, so `access-token` and `access_token` were recognized but `accessToken` was not — and camelCase is the spelling most JSON and JS APIs emit. Measured on current `origin/main` through the two production consumers, **15 of 16** credential spellings kept their value: `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `idToken`, `authToken`, `clientSecret`, `appSecret`, `privateKey`, `hookToken`, `sessionToken`, `secretKey`, `webhookSecret`, `urlSignature`, `bearerToken`, `accesstoken`, `clientsecret`. Only `apiKey` was already covered, via the existing `apikey` entry. Those values reach gateway log lines (`redactSensitiveText`), MCP server descriptions (`src/agents/mcp-transport-config.ts`) and plugin manifest diagnostics (`src/infra/clawhub-plugin-manifest.ts`).

**Three regexes admitted exponentially many equivalent splits.** Each repeated a group whose own trailing optional whitespace overlapped the next repetition's leading whitespace, or alternated between overlapping Unicode properties. Either shape lets one subject be split many equivalent ways, so a non-matching subject degrades superlinearly instead of failing fast:

| Site | Note |
|---|---|
| `extensions/zalouser/src/text-styles-{source,ranges}.ts` | Blockquote-only line check, reached from outgoing message text. The **same literal appeared at three call sites**; now one shared constant. |
| `src/cli/command-format.ts` | Root-update detection joined a flag to its value with `[=\s]+`, letting the value matcher swallow the separator and consume the next ` --flag` chunk. |
| `extensions/telegram/src/text-width.ts` | Four overlapping Unicode properties in an alternation, folded into one character class. |

The Telegram one is **consistency, not a behavior fix**: grapheme segmentation already bounded it, because a cluster reaching that check either matches whole (no backtracking) or fails on its first character. Attacking the real entry point `renderTelegramMonospaceGrid` with thousands of joiners and variation selectors stayed in the low milliseconds, so I could not make it misbehave.

## What Changed

Spelling variants now collapse onto one canonical `_`-separated form at the single predicate every redaction path already funnels through: camelCase and PascalCase word starts, `.` alongside `-`, array and index subscripts, and the run-together spelling of each listed name, plus a small set of segment markers for `webhookSecret` / `url_signature`.

Scoped deliberately to avoid over-redacting debugging context:

- `token` and `key` are **not** segment markers, so `token_count`, `tokenCount`, `maxTokens` and `cacheKey` stay readable.
- `session_id` stays visible, matching the existing form-body expectation in `src/logging/redact.test.ts`.
- 52 non-credential names are pinned as must-not-redact.

Every normalization step is linear in the name's length (see the review follow-up below). For the three regexes, each repetition boundary is now forced: the run between `>` markers is spelled once, and the CLI matcher keeps the `=` and whitespace spellings separate so neither branch can cross whitespace.

## Review follow-up: normalization kept linear

The first revision of this PR traded one superlinear scan for two, which ClawSweeper caught. I confirmed it by measurement before changing anything — on `"[".repeat(n)` the bracket expression rescanned the remaining suffix at every `[` it could not close, and on `"A".repeat(n)` the acronym expression consumed the uppercase run and backtracked through it before failing its lowercase requirement:

| n | bracket scan | acronym scan | ms/n² (bracket) | ms/n² (acronym) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 1.5 ms | 3.8 ms | 1.49 | 3.83 |
| 4,000 | 21.8 ms | 44.0 ms | 1.36 | 2.75 |
| 16,000 | 351.7 ms | 706.9 ms | 1.37 | 2.76 |

The flat ms/n² column is the quadratic signature, and query names are unbounded here because logging and URL diagnostics call this synchronously.

Subscript stripping is now a forward scan whose cursor only advances; it removes each `[` through the first following `]`, which is exactly what the expression accepted. The acronym boundary keeps its regex but takes the leading uppercase as a fixed-width lookbehind, leaving no run to backtrack through. After the fix, 1,000,000 characters cost about 1 ms where 16,000 previously cost 350 ms.

A first attempt at the bracket side — excluding `[` from the inner class — was **rejected by its own equivalence check**: it changed how spans nest and differed on 75,302 strings. The forward scan replaced it.

## Evidence

### Real behavior through the changed production consumers

Captured after the fix. Synthetic values only; no real endpoint, key, or personal data.

`redactSensitiveUrl` — the MCP server description and plugin manifest diagnostic path:

```text
in : https://mcp.example.test/sse?accessToken=s3cr3t-value-0123456789&model=sonnet&page=2
out: https://mcp.example.test/sse?accessToken=***&model=sonnet&page=2
in : https://mcp.example.test/sse?clientSecret=s3cr3t-value-0123456789&model=sonnet&page=2
out: https://mcp.example.test/sse?clientSecret=***&model=sonnet&page=2
in : https://mcp.example.test/sse?privateKey=s3cr3t-value-0123456789&model=sonnet&page=2
out: https://mcp.example.test/sse?privateKey=***&model=sonnet&page=2
in : https://mcp.example.test/sse?apiKey[]=s3cr3t-value-0123456789&model=sonnet&page=2
out: https://mcp.example.test/sse?apiKey%5B%5D=***&model=sonnet&page=2
in : https://mcp.example.test/sse?webhookSecret=s3cr3t-value-0123456789&model=sonnet&page=2
out: https://mcp.example.test/sse?webhookSecret=***&model=sonnet&page=2
```

`redactSensitiveText` — gateway log lines (this mode masks with a length hint rather than `***`):

```text
in : mcp: connecting upstream url=https://mcp.example.test/sse?accessToken=s3cr3t-value-0123456789 attempt=1
out: mcp: connecting upstream url=https://mcp.example.test/sse?accessToken=s3cr3t…6789 attempt=1
in : mcp: connecting upstream url=https://mcp.example.test/sse?clientSecret=s3cr3t-value-0123456789 attempt=1
out: mcp: connecting upstream url=https://mcp.example.test/sse?clientSecret=s3cr3t…6789 attempt=1
in : mcp: connecting upstream url=https://mcp.example.test/sse?privateKey=s3cr3t-value-0123456789 attempt=1
out: mcp: connecting upstream url=https://mcp.example.test/sse?privateKey=s3cr3t…6789 attempt=1
```

Ordinary context stays readable through both consumers, so the change does not blind the logs:

```text
in : https://api.example.test/v1/chat?token_count=1&maxTokens=2&cacheKey=3&sessionId=4&clientId=5&page=6
url: https://api.example.test/v1/chat?token_count=1&maxTokens=2&cacheKey=3&sessionId=4&clientId=5&page=6
log: request https://api.example.test/v1/chat?token_count=1&maxTokens=2&cacheKey=3&sessionId=4&clientId=5&page=6
```

Normalization cost on the unbounded names from the review finding, measured through `redactSensitiveUrl`: 40,000 unclosed subscripts → **9.7 ms**; a 40,000-character uppercase run → **2.6 ms**.

### Before/after through both consumers

Same 16 names, run against the `origin/main` version of the file and then against this branch:

| | `redactSensitiveText` (logging) | `redactSensitiveUrl` |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | 15 of 16 leak | 15 of 16 leak |
| this branch | 0 leak | 0 leak |

### Equivalence checking

These are parsing predicates where a silent behavior change would be worse than the original problem, so every regex change was proven equivalent before landing:

- Subscript scan — exhaustive over `{[, ], a, A, 0, _}` to length 8 (2,015,538 strings) plus 500,000 random bracket-heavy names: **0 differences**.
- Acronym boundary — exhaustive over `{A, B, a, b, 0, _}` to length 7 (335,922 strings): **0 differences**.
- Blockquote matcher — exhaustive over `{>, space, tab, x}` to length 10 (1,398,100 strings) plus 500,000 random multi-space strings: **0 differences**. My first attempt here was also not equivalent (it broke tab separators) and this check caught it.
- Grapheme class — every Unicode code point (1.1M) plus 200,000 random strings: **0 differences**.
- CLI matcher — 585 realistic command tails. The only difference is `--profile= foo` (equals, then a space, then a value) no longer counting as a flag value. That spelling *is* the ambiguity, and it is not a shell invocation anyone writes; `--profile foo` and `--profile=foo` are unaffected.

### Regression tests

Each verified to fail on the pre-fix code for the intended reason and pass after:

- `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts` — 24 credential spelling variants (22 failed pre-fix); 14 non-credential names as negative controls (all already passed, so they guard against over-redaction); and two linear-time cases through the redaction owner, measured at **2.2 s and 4.4 s before, 6 ms after**.
- `src/cli/profile.test.ts` — wall-clock bound on repeated global flags (failed pre-fix on the timing assertion).
- `extensions/zalouser/src/text-styles-blocks.test.ts` — wall-clock bound at the `parseZalouserTextStyles` boundary.

Both timing tests keep their input modest so a reintroduced ambiguity still finishes and reports rather than hanging CI. One table row was dropped during review because it passed pre-fix and so proved nothing. No test was added for the Telegram change: it is equivalent over all code points, so a regression test could not fail on the pre-fix code, and the authoring gate in `.claude/skills/test-audit` rejects tests that never demonstrably failed.

### Checks and suites

`tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxlint` (core + extensions), `oxfmt`, `git diff --check` — all clean.

Tests: `packages/net-policy` (89), `packages/gateway-client` (140), `src/logging`, `src/config` (502), `src/infra/net`, `extensions/zalouser` (236), `extensions/telegram`, `src/cli/profile.test.ts`, plus the redaction consumers in `src/config/schema.hints`, `src/config/redact-snapshot` and `src/agents/mcp-transport-config` — **0 failures**.

### One fixture entry changed

`src/logging/redact-byte-identity-fixture.json` pins byte-identical output over 250 recorded samples. Exactly **one** sample changes: its parameter name ends in `_secret`, which the canonical form now recognizes, so the value is masked rather than passed through. The other 249 are untouched, and the file keeps its compact formatting (parse→stringify is byte-identical on it, so the diff is one line).

## Known Limitation

Subscript forms are normalized for URL redaction, but **not** in free log text: `src/logging/redact.ts` builds its own `FORM_BODY_KEY` grammar that excludes `[` and `]`, so `apiKey[]=…` in a log line is not recognized as an assignment at all. This is pre-existing and unrelated to this change — `token[]` and `api_key[]` are equally unmasked there on current `origin/main`, which I verified directly. Widening that grammar would change a module with its own byte-identity contract across many samples, so I left it as a follow-up rather than growing this PR's scope.

## Scope Note

Per `SECURITY.md`, ReDoS that needs trusted operator configuration input is not a vulnerability under this project's trust model — which covers the CLI matcher, since it only runs when a container hint is configured — and the zalouser plugin is excluded from the shipped bundle. These are filed as hardening, not as a vulnerability report.

Separately, `pnpm audit` on current `main` is clean apart from two dev-only transitive advisories (`http-cache-semantics` via `sigstore`, and `braces` via `stylelint`/`lit-analyzer`, the latter with no published fix). Neither is runtime-reachable, so neither is touched here.

A live SSRF sweep was also run against `fetchWithSsrFGuard` using a real loopback server and the real `fetch`, covering 35 obfuscated host encodings (decimal, octal, hex, IPv4-mapped and 6to4/NAT64 IPv6, trailing dots, ideographic and fullwidth full stops, and `localhost` variants). **All 35 were blocked**, so nothing changed there. That result covers unchanged code and is reported only to say why no SSRF change was needed.

prs.title: test(core): remove low-value tests (batch d349)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Test suites repeat fixtures, setup, and assertions that obscure the contracts under test. This batch consolidates that repetition and removes redundant cases without changing production behavior.

## User Impact

No user-facing behavior change. This is test and test-support cleanup only: 89 test/support files (+5,737/-8,837; net -3,100), plus six obsolete entries removed from `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`. Overall: 90 files, +5,737/-8,843 (net -3,106); production +0/-0.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replayed all 30 requested commits onto pinned main `1989e3dc4360a17d039440a886f71e582758a487`. No entire commit was skipped. Existing platform, security, lifecycle, and error-path proof is retained rather than pursuing a deletion quota.

Conflicting cleanup was omitted for these files, preserving the pre-pick version:
- `src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-mentions.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/control-ui-session-task-prs.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/control-ui-share.http.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/credential-precedence.parity.test.ts`
- `test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts` (later refactor omitted; initial nonconflicting cleanup retained; newer support/FAQ assertions preserved)
- `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-client.pricing.test.ts` (newer cache-write/TTL coverage preserved)
- `src/agents/agent-tools.publication-inheritance.test.ts`
- `extensions/team-reports/src/postgres-store.test.ts`
- `extensions/team-reports/src/store-conformance.test-support.ts`

Other hunks were kept. No CODEOWNERS-matched paths are changed.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <89 changed TS files>`: exit 0; no additional edits.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <89 changed TS files>`: exit 0.
- `git diff --check 1989e3dc4360a17d039440a886f71e582758a487`: passed.
- Per operator CI-only instructions: no local Vitest, check-changed, typecheck, coverage, or Testbox. No leases created. Required `openclaw/ci-gate` is the behavioral proof and merge gate.
- Independent review: one accepted finding restored the 16 KiB receipt boundary; a claimed chat-key mismatch was disproven (the host defaults to `agent:main`), while `host.sessionKey` was restored for ownership clarity. The focused follow-up review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Initial [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39525067521) exposed fixture type errors, async HTTP callback lint errors, mock-export isolation declarations, browser harness import ordering, and missing startup fixture initialization. Commit `0e7a76dbe5b5` repairs these without changing production or weakening assertions. Fresh-head CI remains the proof; no failed job was blindly rerun.
- The [second CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39526275378) confirmed the first-round fixes and exposed a Team Reports spy recursion: argument evaluation bound the already-installed spy. Commit `558694416a4e` captures original methods first, retaining the complete assertions. Its focused review was clean at P0–P2.
- The [third CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39527248886) accepted the source repairs and requested pruning the six now-obsolete mock-baseline entries. Commit `e7f4543b35b7` removes exactly those entries; its focused review was clean at P0–P2. All other entries, including same-hash entries for other files, remain.
- Auto-merge is pinned to the pushed head.

prs.title: fix(sessions): recover after worker exits before command admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A session actor could require reconciliation after its SQLite worker exited before the command received write admission. The failed command had made no session changes, but subsequent commands using the same actor were refused.

## User Impact

An early worker failure returns a clean command failure and allows the session to continue on the replacement worker. Worker failures after admission still preserve unknown-outcome reconciliation and committed-receipt handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The actor owner already records whether the native command reached its admission boundary. Use that fact to classify a rejected, never-admitted command as rolled back. Keep the existing replica invalidation and worker replacement lifecycle. No schema, worker heap limit, retry, or retention changes.

Production delta: +5/-1 lines. The small branch is required to distinguish a command that could not write from an uncertain admitted write; no new state or owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real worker regression: terminate the worker before dispatch of an actor mutation. Before the fix, the command incorrectly returns `unknown`; after the fix, it returns `rolled-back`, stored state is unchanged, and the same actor successfully commits another command using the replacement worker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-actor.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.close-wedge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 39 tests passed, 39.56 seconds wrapper wall time; new regression 1.10 seconds. Existing post-admission uncertainty and receipt-reconciliation tests remain green.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` (native tsrs), changed-file core lint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed. PR CI owns broad validation; no Testbox lease used.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no accepted P0/P1 findings.

This repairs a proven failure cascade discovered during worker OOM investigation. It does not claim to fix the memory growth itself.

| Pre-admission worker loss | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Failed command | `unknown` | `rolled-back` |
| Stored timestamp | Unchanged | Unchanged |
| Next command on retained actor | Requires reconciliation | Commits through replacement worker |

Separate source-revision probes compared `bead2a8e` and `73601c86` in two concurrent, swapped-core pairs. Both passed full streaming of 8,258 synthetic transcript events (181,210,925 raw JSON bytes), including tool results, thinking signatures, reset and cache-TTL records, under a verified 896 MiB V8 heap limit. Both also passed a 64 MiB bounded hydration window; candidate-minus-baseline latency was approximately -28 ms and +5 ms. This did not reproduce the reported OOM. There is no performance claim for the recovery change; the exact failing workload remains a gap.

Both revisions also passed real Gateway/native-worker nested flows and interrupted-run recovery using a local synthetic provider. An authenticated crash/restart probe preserved the actual child/requester identities, delivered the interrupted child's completion, and finished the retained parent continuation without a pending wake. This last result was verified from exact Gateway run logs and persisted state; the provider-request correlator did not tag the continuation. No external provider or production data was used. The original OOM remains unreproduced, so this PR alone does not establish that the affected deployment is unblocked.

prs.title: fix(skills): Workshop reviews fail for Codex-backed agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes automatic Skill Workshop reviews using the embedded OpenClaw runtime after a Codex-backed conversation, which can fail when the Gateway does not own that runtime's inference credentials.

## User Impact

Eligible conversations can run background learning through the runtime that completed the foreground work, without adding review turns to the conversation or modifying its transcript.

Attached native sessions with a separate credential-owning connection remain unsupported for automatic reviews; they fail closed and can still use foreground learning. Codex has no equivalent to the embedded runtime's 2,048-output-token cap: its two-minute deadline and eight-tool-call budget are not a token or spending cap. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the completed runtime into the existing private-review runner and retain the existing model/auth route, source-authority checks, cancellation, foreground yielding, restricted `skill_workshop` surface, and no-retry policy.

Codex reviews use a fresh ephemeral thread with the bounded source excerpt, without saving a conversation binding or running managed native hooks. The native integration also exposed two prerequisites fixed here: preserving the detached excerpt allowance and using the supplied configuration for native execution-policy checks.

The scope is configured-runtime support, not supervised-connection inheritance or a new runtime framework. Existing routing, admission, tool-budget, and context owners are reused; the hardcoded embedded-runtime override is removed. Most added code is regression coverage and the real-native fixture, which caught evidence loss that helper tests missed.

## Evidence

- Final focused run: **81/81 tests passed** across native integration, runtime setup, model/auth ownership, and execution-policy authority checks.
- The real repository-pinned Codex binary, with a private home and a synthetic loopback Responses endpoint, receives recent user/tool/assistant evidence and only `skill_workshop`. Oversized old history and foreground/workspace/client-tool instructions are excluded. Source transcript and durable session rows stay unchanged; no native rollout remains after joined shutdown.
- Earlier affected suites passed for review restrictions and budgets, source revocation, prompt-prefix stability, isolated Gateway review/notice/history behavior, detached lifecycle, managed-hook restrictions, and existing native/incognito behavior. Unchanged-input results were reused.
- Red/green regressions cover detached lifecycle, explicit-configuration policy, and the detached context allowance.
- **10 final static checks passed**, covering targeted typechecks, lint, formatting, plugin import boundaries, and whitespace. Build prerequisites passed through the test runner.
- Publication checks caught growth in an oversized binding-test file. Its existing coverage was preserved, and the detached managed-hook regression was moved to the smaller restricted-continuation suite. Both affected suites then passed **123/123 tests** in 31.52 seconds wall time, with extension-test typechecking, targeted lint, and formatting passing again. Production code was unchanged. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.

**Review status:** draft pending completion of the repository's Auto Review check. The isolated reviewer failed before producing a report with OpenAI Responses authentication errors (HTTP 401), including after the supported process-local credential-selection recovery. This is reviewer unavailability, not a clean review or a code finding.

**Coverage gap:** the native protocol proof uses synthetic provider responses, not live-provider authentication. The isolated remote attempt never obtained a host and was stopped; no live credential staging or provider call occurred. Deployed account/connection behavior remains unverified. Broad repository coverage belongs to PR CI.

## What Problem This Solves

The async-question E2E file saves 22 manual screenshots unconditionally across six cases. They have no image assertions or required artifact consumers, yet every normal CI run pays their capture/encoding/write cost. The rest of this suite already makes manual proof opt-in.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Normal E2E runs avoid manual image capture work; opt-in proof retains all images.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1` switch for these captures, retaining their original scope, file names, viewport size and animation option. A local two-caller capture factory allocates a proof directory only when enabled. All 15 cases, every assertion, explicit readiness/navigation wait, mock interaction, and failure diagnostics remain. Seven existing opt-in capture calls are unchanged. No test or production behavior is deleted.

## Evidence

Prospective current-baseline check, recorded before any candidate timing is read: scheduled run39524896041 completed after this PR opened. If its root and suite-helper sources match the pre-change candidate source, also require no regression in F or all-case sum against that newer run. Keep the original 10% thresholds and individual-case guard; the newer comparison cannot weaken or replace them. This preserves the campaign rule that an old slow baseline alone does not establish a current speedup.

Frozen before the first candidate CI: compare the unchanged root and suite-helper source in scheduled main [39515342342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39515342342). Require at least 10% improvement in native file total F (66.356 s → at most 59.7204 s) and summed printed case time (66.014 s → at most 59.4126 s). All 15 exact cases and all 14 UI jobs must pass. No case may regress by 20% or more without exact-case, source-identical newer-main evidence. There is no queued-to-end receipt for this baseline: F is the emitted file total including suite hooks, not Q. Report the owning shard separately with its inventory; overlapping file spans are not pipeline savings.

| Metric / proof | Before | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Default manual screenshots in affected six cases |22|0|
| Opt-in manual screenshots |22|22|
| Cases / assertion chains |15 / 155|15 / 155 unchanged|

| All-case sum |66.014 s|52.990 s (-19.73%)|
| Affected six-case sum |32.916 s|29.523 s|
| Other nine-case sum |33.098 s|23.467 s|
| Mock 7/9 Test step |574 s / 99 files|548 s / 100 files; inventory differs|
| Frozen install, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, exact chat-E2E types |—|Passed|
| Scoped lint, format, diff |—|Passed|
| Independent P0–P2 review |—|Scoped-clean, confidence 0.96|

Baseline cases: admitted optional answer 4.256 s; archived reminder recovery=false 6.022 s and true 5.714 s; unfinished answer 5.160 s; 390 px viewport 2.051 s; async submit active=false 7.856 s and true 5.210 s; nonblocking queue 3.064 s; rejected-answer receipt 4.378 s, reload 5.526 s, discard 4.733 s and legacy 5.213 s; saved answer 3.202 s; offline transcript 1.309 s; malformed transcript 2.320 s.

No local E2E, build or broad suite under the campaign compute budget; CI owns runtime and timing proof. No production, startup, dependency or visual product change. Test LOC 980→965 (-15); production and Solid refactor counts 0. No Testbox/Crabbox lease.

Run [39527684260](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39527684260) at723cb9ee39f8caf64c8fcca4a1687a889ca833c4 passes all15 exact cases and both timing thresholds; every case stays below the20% regression limit, without an exception. The source-identical newer main39524896041 also improves: F58.885→53.241s and sum58.492→52.990s. All14UI jobs and the complete workflow passed on the exact candidate head; all frozen acceptance criteria are satisfied.

Causal limit: the unaffected nine cases also got faster. The full13.115-second file reduction is an observed run difference, not a claim that screenshot work alone cost13.115seconds. The owning shard improved26seconds with a changed inventory; no causal shard saving is claimed. New main also adds one panel-expanded readiness assertion in this file; the clean merge preserves it and does not change the capture hunks.

prs.title: feat: enable native plugin UI without a Labs opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed native plugin interfaces still require a separate Labs opt-in even though the same infrastructure already serves bundled plugins.

## User Impact

Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI by default, without a Labs detour. Existing explicit `gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins: false` values remain off; there is no new configuration key or migration.

**Upgrade behavior:** when the key is omitted, already-enabled plugins may begin loading their native browser UI after upgrading. Native UI is trusted, unsandboxed code running with each signed-in viewer's Gateway permissions. Existing authentication, scope, provenance, asset grants, and lifecycle checks remain unchanged.

Install surfaces explain that plugins may include browser code; installed details and existing enable reviews identify native UI from the inspected manifest. No extra modal, checkbox, or permission gate is added. All plugin APIs retain their existing experimental API-stability policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move browser-execution disclosure to ordinary plugin installation and enablement instead of hiding the whole capability behind Labs. Keep the existing advanced opt-out for compatibility, and share the effective default between admission and browser refresh notifications. Update authoring guidance, agent instructions, and recovery hints so they no longer direct users to the removed switch.

## Evidence

**Current published head:** `a8765ec5a4861d9241bbaa1454d6edbf833bc161`; cleanup commit `df2e50f5d28a7b9165404d54c4fadcc9701c66a4` has the identical tree `a5d41efb0243f00d0d510363a452f4f15b5a10f2`.

**Test cleanup:** removed the deleted-Labs-row test and redundant leaf-renderer no-modal/callback assertions; retained page/E2E install/consent coverage. Tests now check disclosure-before-actions ordering, inspection-versus-inventory precedence (including explicit false), actual reactive inventory/inspection updates, and exact public proof projection from inputs containing synthetic private state. Shared backup receipts replace copied prerequisite fixtures across two suites. Both packaged updater specimens and warm-asset authorization coverage remain. The only harness execution simplification removes an existence check immediately followed by the mandatory lockfile read. Product runtime and UI rendering are unchanged.

**Cleanup proof:** 131 focused tests passed across four UI and three script suites (UI run 5.43 s; script run 8.20 s including startup). Three deliberate mutations—incorrect metadata precedence, notice moved after actions, and raw-state leakage—each failed at the intended assertion; all mutations were restored and the affected 21 UI / 4 publication tests passed again. UI-page and root-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and diff checks passed. Independent Auto Review of the cleanup through P2 found no actionable findings; its scope was the local delta and supplied source context, not a new whole-feature or packaged execution. New-head CI is attached and pending; CI seconds are not yet available.

**Size:** compared with the preceding published revision, this cleanup changes nine files (+104 / −114, net −10 lines), with zero product-runtime/UI changes. The broader feature remains larger because it includes the requested stable-upgrade harness; this is not a claim that the entire PR is net-negative.

**Proof limits clarified:** the packaged explicit-false 404 is a cold-start opt-out smoke check, not independent isolation of the final HTTP policy guard; the warm cached-asset Gateway test covers that guard. The published `operatorDataPreserved` witness means survival of a synthetic state-directory sentinel, not a plugin storage-API round trip. Previously recorded HTTP, screenshot and packaged results retain their exact source identities below; no new packaged run or browser execution is claimed for this cleanup.

**Prior conflict-refresh head:** `e22e259deca8f9daad8d984b35374a073f04353a`, incorporating main `2f7572ad13d12d5d34d21adecf5198cbb0fbb39d` through merge commit `c2881444186a306ed21eab3e40fba788a145bb6c` (publication marker has the same tree `aff591721ce111e2c5d8a985f9293286fc120deb`). The only manual conflict was `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated from the combined inputs. Labs tests and catalog rendering auto-merged with upstream changes; default-on policy, asset-authorization owner, and native upgrade harness were preserved.

**Refresh verification:** dependencies synchronized with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; **96 focused tests passed** (73 Labs/catalog, 22 native asset, 1 config-baseline). Generated config verification, canonical production UI types, targeted lint/format, and diff checks passed. The resolution adds no new feature behavior or permission change. New-head CI is pending; the earlier CI, review, HTTP trace and packaged qualification below remain bound to their recorded prior inputs, not this merged dependency/base tree. No additional hosted review was requested for this mechanical conflict refresh.

### Prior-head feature qualification

Previous published head: `bdbc278ac906246982a009f8283bdc07cf72b6d0`. Reviewed harness commit `40b3fe6ddbb94a92297e44bade5282a4011a7a0a` has the identical complete tree `fb7b709b8ddc99fc94cefddfb45f25016949cf42`; the extra commit records attributed publication only. prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422

## What Problem This Solves

Generated Markdown under an agent workspace's `memory/` tree can enter Memory Search and compete with curated notes, with no supported path exclusion for the default roots.

## User Impact

Users can opt in to workspace-relative `memory.search.excludePaths` globs, for example `memory/dreaming/**` and `memory/.dreams/**`. With no setting, indexing behavior is unchanged. Source files remain intact; changing the scope triggers index rebuilding on the next sync. This PR addresses search indexing and watcher eligibility only, not short-term recall/promotion eligibility or inline generated blocks within otherwise eligible notes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery and local/remote watchers share the same workspace-relative exclusion predicate. It applies to default roots and overlapping extra paths. The configured scope hash changes only for nonempty exclusions, so existing users retain their index identity. The core config baseline increases by four generated entries as an intentional new optional setting.

This is a draft for the open product-scope decision in #101422; it does not claim to resolve the broader coordinated include/exclude request.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: 139/139 passed across config resolution, file discovery, local/remote watch transport, manager indexing/reindexing, and path matching; the final path-boundary regression passed again (3/3).
- Core and extension production typechecks, changed-file lint/format, config baseline check, config example check, and diff whitespace check passed.
- Independent read-only review found two defects (local watcher propagation and a path-segment boundary), both fixed and reverified.
- Extension test typecheck is blocked by an unchanged `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts:675` type error on current main. The broad `check:changed` run was stopped after detecting unrelated current-main UI line-cap/test-root-budget failures; it is not claimed green.
- No production Gateway/config/index migration or live reindex was performed. A deployed release and an operator opt-in are required before existing indexed rows can be removed in a real workspace.

prs.title: feat(crabbox): opt in to private Proxmox workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #177859. Operators cannot select declared private Proxmox Crabbox workers because OpenClaw always forces public transport and rejects Tailscale metadata.

## User Impact

Adds explicit `settings.network: "tailscale"` for cold native Proxmox Linux workers, with private transport throughout provisioning and lifecycle inspection. Public remains the default and still rejects Tailscale objects, including disabled objects. AWS provisioning still requires no instance profile. Warm/prepared workers, reserves, desktops and protected setup secrets are unavailable for this opt-in.

Requires the native device-receipt/routing contract in openclaw/crabbox#2910 (current source contract inspected at `5278730354c241ef70d71badbee410bf6f84d4dd`); published Crabbox 0.78.1 does not supply it. This PR does not install either runtime, configure Serve, grant Proxmox permissions, or deploy a broker. Live VM/device cleanup and dispatch remain operator validation after coherent deployment. No merge or deployment is requested here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing plugin owns the setting, command context and admission decision. Allocation/run carry the explicit network and join policy; inspect retains private routing; heartbeat renews the already admitted lease with its supported provider/ID/idle-timeout/JSON arguments; admission requires matching lease identity, ready/error-free/enabled metadata, CGNAT IPv4 and actual device identity. Crabbox owns generation-bound receipt persistence, immutable fixed-lease replay, QGA-pinned SSH and network-independent stop. Normal authenticated OpenClaw node enrollment is reused. There is no public/LAN retry and no new state owner or protocol.

Simplification: one shared network-argument builder and one inspection network-policy check replace hardcoded call-site choices; AWS provisioning admission stays at its existing boundary. Existing public warm-image keys remain unchanged. Necessary growth versus base: production +130/-23 lines, tests +332 lines plus one existing database-worker lane entry, docs +52/-1 lines (no schema/store changes).

## Evidence

- Red-before: the added provider/profile cases failed on base `45801179f6d` at the missing network-setting contract.
- Final private-network/profile proof: **44 passed**, two files, **37.44s wall** including cold database-worker compilation (test execution below one second per file). The sibling suite preserves the existing database-worker process policy and avoids growth in the oversized provider suite.
- Reused unchanged production-path sibling proof: provider, cancellation, enrollment/replay and preparation **199 passed / 10 existing platform-dependent skips**, six files, **99.82s wall** before the test-only extraction. Command, inspect, heartbeat and lifetime coverage also passed (**190 tests**, six files, **17.18s wall**). These runs overlap; counts are not additive. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Scoped Crabbox production and test typechecks; touched production/test lint; format, `git diff --check`, line-cap ratchet, documentation lint/config examples and **15,729 internal links** pass.
- Initial independent isolated Codex review was clean at `780a0f9`. Fresh whole-patch P0–P2 review of the repaired candidate is complete: it supports the lifecycle/catalog repairs. Its sole remaining desktop suggestion was declined because `parseCrabboxProfile` already rejects Proxmox desktops through `CRABBOX_DESKTOP_PROVIDERS` before private admission (`crabbox-worker-profile.ts:206`). No accepted remaining finding. Reviewer did not execute project code or verify live connectivity.
- Synthetic external-process fixtures prove admission, consistent private argv, readiness waiting, wrong/malformed metadata rejection, fresh-provider replay, fixed-policy conflict handling, cancellation custody and exact-lease stop. They do not prove native connectivity, daemon dispatch, broker issuance or live VM/device cleanup.

## Hosted review follow-up

At `4952840ffb14a6392aa923443aad54c3ed1378aa`:

- Fixed [P1 lifecycle policy drift](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177863#discussion_r4320154758): definitive parsed network-policy rejection now stops renewal and returns `unknown`, allowing the existing Gateway owner to withdraw dedicated attestation and request teardown. Transport failures remain exceptions; provision admission and cleanup remain strict.
- Fixed [P2 unsupported private placement choices](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177863#discussion_r4320154765): private catalog projections expose Linux only, without mutating the shared public catalog.
- Red-before repair: **3 failed / 18 passed**, at the expected lifecycle-status and OS-catalog assertions. Green-after repair: **122 passed**, four files / two owning shards, **11.61s wall**. Includes active renewal cessation, transport-uncertainty preservation, same-lease teardown, private catalog projection and unchanged public choices.
- Scoped production/test typechecks, touched lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and normal commit hooks pass. No checks bypassed.

prs.title: feat: show published Claw artwork in the catalog
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claws in Agents show a generic box even when their published package has artwork.

## User Impact

Catalog cards and detail pages show each Claw’s published PNG. Missing or failed images retain the existing box fallback, and images use anonymous CORS with no referrer. Selecting an older release uses that release’s artwork, including its absence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway reuses the existing registry image URL validator: only the configured registry’s content-addressed image route is accepted. An optional `iconUrl` travels through the existing catalog protocol to one small renderer shared by cards and details. No proxy, cache, new route, or setting was added.

ClawHub publication and exact-version artwork support are deployed ([#4007](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4007), [#4008](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4008)). [Live proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178857#issuecomment-6305521493) verifies all 150 official image-bearing releases through anonymous public catalog/feed and artifact/image digest checks, plus 150 loaded PNG cards in a fresh isolated Gateway. Workflow Operator 0.1.1 shows its exact image in fully loaded details; version 0.1.0 correctly remains without artwork. The source images are in [Awesome Claws #2](https://github.com/openclaw/awesome-claws/pull/2).

## Evidence

- Before: valid hosted artwork disappeared at the Gateway boundary; card/detail tests found no image. After: trusted image URLs reach both surfaces; external/arbitrary paths are omitted and image failures fall back.
- 37 Gateway source tests passed; after adapting to current main, all 19 affected Agents UI tests passed; protocol registry, generated/native protocol checks, core/UI typechecks and changed-file lint passed.
- Real browser captures passed at 390×844, 768×1024, 1366×768 and 1440×900. Initial captures use a controlled Gateway fixture. A fresh isolated OCM Gateway now also renders the real public Workflow Operator 0.1.1 PNG at all four sizes, with 150 official Claws plus one community Claw in the catalog. Browser-aborted PNG requests retain the card and fully loaded detail fallbacks. The exact-version detail image now passes through the deployed API and Gateway.
- Historical pre-refresh check on base `b197b24e1a3`: broader `check:changed` was not fully green: the base has max-lines baseline drift, core test-root budget failures, and unrelated unused exports. The max-lines failure reproduces in an untouched checkout of `b197b24e1a3`; all flagged paths are outside this change. The exact same dead-export failures also reproduce at the untouched base.
- The full source runtime and Control UI production builds completed. The startup bundle budget is already exceeded on the untouched base (318.3 KiB versus 317.5 KiB); this branch measures 318.7 KiB.
- Live browser regression: the image server returns `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin` and public CORS headers. Default image requests failed with `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE.NotSameOrigin`; `crossorigin="anonymous"` loads the exact 256px PNG without changing CSP or introducing a proxy. The shared card/detail test now checks that request mode.
- Conflict repair onto main `73601c86` preserves the production artwork patch and current main’s fixture refactor. The adapted tests remove the retired feature flag and expose the detail container they exercise. Targeted UI types, lint, formatting, and all 19 affected tests pass. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39527640414) passed on `1befab722f38`; ClawSweeper’s review of that same head found no actionable issues and accepted the live proof.
- Simplification: reused the existing URL validator and detail shell; added only the optional projection and shared image-error fallback. No parallel artwork service or special cache.

![claw-artwork-before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfe260ed-6cf1-4d24-b987-bd33a4c6f962)

prs.title: feat: restrict Gateway-local terminals and automation host execution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway operator can open a local terminal or define host-executed automation, they can run commands with the Gateway process’s host privileges. A direct edit of a writable configuration file bypasses API-level write controls such as `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY`; accessible credentials are also exposed.

## User Impact

Deployers can independently disable Gateway-local terminals and Gateway-hosted automation execution. Authorized node terminals, scheduled agent turns, and authorized sandbox-backed stream sources remain available. Blocked persisted jobs remain visible and can be disabled or removed. Both controls default off.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_GATEWAY_LOCAL_TERMINALS=1` blocks local terminal preparation and PTY creation. `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_CRON_HOST_EXECUTION=1` blocks host-executed automation payloads, script triggers, and Gateway-hosted process sources, including persisted and manually requested jobs. Gateway configuration cannot override either launch setting. The controls are independent of `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY`; they do not isolate files or restrict tools used by agent turns.

## Evidence

CI on `a6b6650` (before the documentation and comment updates) passed the [Gateway cron service and terminal RPC tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39511181525/job/118932867946), [local terminal creation test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39511181525/job/118932868061), [node dispatch authority tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39511181525/job/118932867887), and [config environment publication test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39511181525/job/118932868133). These exercise production handlers, service wiring, and state transitions with controlled process, sandbox, agent, and node transport boundaries.

Live deployed-Gateway validation and a stable-release upgrade were not performed.

prs.title: feat(a2a): add source-authorized outbound task reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw agent that sends an A2A task to a configured peer receives a remote task ID back
(`messageId`) but has no supported way to read that task's answer. The outbound path can start
work; nothing in the shared message tool can retrieve the terminal state, an `input-required`
state, or the artifact text. Callers either poll blindly, re-send work, or read nothing.

This PR adds a narrow, source-authorized `read` action for tasks **this agent started**, and
nothing else: no new network surface, no peer-config change, no deployment specifics.

## What Changed

- `extensions/a2a/src/task-actions.ts` (new): a `read` task action issues `GetTask`, retries the
  legacy `tasks/get` only on method-not-found, and returns a bounded projection — `taskId`,
  `contextId`, normalized `state`, `terminal`, `inputRequired`, artifact `text`, `statusText`.
  It never starts further work.
- Read authority comes from a **receipt created by a prior `SendMessage`**, bound to the same
  agent, session key and incarnation, peer, account, endpoint and credential. The receipt is
  created by the send path from host-resolved identity, never from tool or model arguments.
- Receipts are in-memory (24h TTL, 500 entries) and cleared when the account stops.
- A task ID whose send was rejected as a collision **revokes** the older receipt, so a peer that
  reassigns a task ID to another source cannot be read by the earlier session.
- Unknown peers, unknown tasks and forbidden sources are refused **before** provider I/O.
- `extensions/a2a/src/message-actions.ts` (new) exposes the action for the default account;
  `extensions/a2a/message-tool-api.ts` carries the artifact type and is registered in the
  message-tool artifact contract inventory.

## Review follow-up in this branch

- **P1 — receipt reuse after a peer reassigns a task ID** (`task-actions.ts`): a cross-source
  collision now deletes the stale receipt instead of merely refusing the new one; a regression
  proves the earlier session cannot issue `GetTask` for the reassigned ID and that no HTTP call
  leaves the Gateway.
- **P2 — message-tool artifact inventory** (`message-tool-api.ts`):
  `MESSAGE_TOOL_ARTIFACT_PLUGIN_IDS` now includes `a2a`, so the full-catalog parity assertion
  matches the discovered set.
- **Lint** in the two new test files: request bodies are narrowed to `string` instead of
  `String(init?.body)`, and a redundant default type argument was dropped.
- **Second round:** receipts are pruned **before** the collision lookup, so an entry past its
  24h TTL cannot block a replacement; the peer-supplied `contextId` is stored only when it is a
  printable string within a 512-byte bound (an unbounded value stores no receipt and the read
  fails closed instead of pinning memory past the entry cap); a conforming but unenumerated
  state (`TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`) is normalized as nonterminal instead of rejecting the task,
  while a malformed non-string state is still rejected.

## Evidence

Local, on this branch head `2451dea8`:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental` | **exit 0** |
| `vitest vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/a2a` | **exit 0** — `task-actions.test.ts` 26 passed, `a2a-task-read.test.ts` 10 passed |
| `vitest vitest.channels.config.ts src/channels/plugins/a2a-task-read.test.ts` | **exit 0** — 10 passed |
| `vitest vitest.contracts-channel-surface.config.ts .../message-tool-artifact.contract.test.ts` | **exit 0** — 1 passed |
| `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` (extension test graph) | PENDING — runs sequentially after the local package build (heavy jobs are serialized on this host); the TS2554 fix is already in the branch | 

```
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/a2a
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.channels.config.ts \
  src/channels/plugins/a2a-task-read.test.ts
# the artifact inventory is owned by the contracts channel-surface shard:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.contracts-channel-surface.config.ts \
  src/channels/plugins/contracts/message-tool-artifact.contract.test.ts
```

Behavior covered by the suite: originating-session success; refusal of a guessed task ID from
another session/peer/account **before** HTTP; caller-authored identity cannot supply authority;
receipt invalidation on restart/expiry/endpoint or credential change; the reused-ID revocation
above; bounded result shape; compatibility retry; rejection of an uncorrelated JSON-RPC
response without exposing task content.

These suites replace `fetch`; they are **not** live interoperability proof. A real-Gateway
message-tool send/read round trip against an isolated loopback A2A peer (allowed-session
success, nearest-forbidden rejection, reused-ID rejection, revocation before dispatch and
during response settlement, with measured peer request counts) is **PENDING** and will be
published as redacted evidence once run.

## Related work

- #170469 (merged): messageId dedup and result correlation with the originating task — the
  mechanism this reader binds to; not reimplemented here.
- #172064 (merged): queued host notice/ack loop fix.
- #175934 (merged): dispatch failure boundary refactor.
- #150187, #156508 (open): TLS-proxy advertised scheme and notification-dispatch test coverage —
  related, separate scope.
- #161189, #162465, #165113 (open): outbound delivery-route isolation, structured outbound
  parts/taskId, SecretRef peer tokens — related, not part of this change.

No maintainer decision is claimed; this is a focused proposal for review.

Side chat needs a simpler composer and a clear distinction between hiding the panel and clearing its conversation.

## User Impact

Shows one composer and empty state without suggested questions. Desktop keeps Clear side chat in the main panel; closing its side-panel tab uses the existing confirmed reset. A failed reset leaves the content and draft open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forwards native presentation to embedded panels and preserves Open desktop in new window when the Desktop panel supplies its own actions.

## Risk and coverage

The current [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39339223713/job/118357212444) hit an inherited welcome-avatar test readiness race: it expected `50%` while the image was still pending at `9999px`. The test and avatar owners are byte-identical to upstream main `d0493286`. One observational run on each revision showed image dimensions becoming available before the component published its loaded state; both then settled at `50%` with the image visible.
