prs.title: feat(tools): per-turn per-target send budget guard for message tools
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a per-turn, per-target outbound send guard shared by the `message` and `conversations_send` tools to curb within-turn duplicate-answer storms.

The existing loop detector hashes full tool params, so a model that re-sends the same answer with slightly reworded text produces a distinct hash every time and stays invisible to it — a single healthy `200` run can emit six reworded variants of one reply. This adds a lightweight ledger, independent of the loop detector and its default-off switch, that counts *successful* deliveries per (turn, target).

Closes #119992

## What Problem This Solves

A model can emit many reworded copies of the same reply within one turn. The existing tool-loop detector hashes the full stable tool-parameter object, so each reworded body is a distinct call and evades it entirely — a single healthy run can fan out six variants of one answer to the same recipient. Nothing in the ordinary send path accounts for repeated deliveries per turn.

This change adds a shared per-agent-turn, per-destination ledger observed by both the `message` tool and `conversations_send`, giving the model a default-on nudge to finalize after the first repeat and an opt-in hard cap that blocks further sends before dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The loop detector cannot catch reworded duplicates (it is content-hash based and default-off), so the guard must be independent of it and count *successful* deliveries, not param hashes.
- The two send tools reach the same recipients, so the ledger has to be shared and keyed on one canonical destination identity, or alternating the tools would evade it.
- The ledger must run on the ordinary Gateway execution path (not just embedded/subagent paths), which requires the active run ID to reach the tools that gate on it.

Seven runtime-path defects surfaced in review are fixed here so the guard actually protects the claimed workflow:

- **Gateway path dropped the run ID.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwarded `runId` to the mediated coding tools but not to `createOpenClawTools`, so the `message` tool and `conversations_send` received `runId=undefined` and their ledger contexts declined to activate — the nudge and cap were silently inert for every Gateway-scoped turn. `params.runId` is now forwarded to `createOpenClawTools`; it stays `undefined` on the single-shot HTTP `tools.invoke` path, which correctly leaves the ledger off there.
- **Current-source key split.** `resolveOutboundActionRoute` keyed current-source sends on a literal `<current-source>` sentinel, while `conversations_send` keys on the resolved concrete target. The two never matched, so alternating a no-target source reply with `conversations_send` to the same peer split the count across two ledger slots and bypassed both the nudge and the cap. The current source is now resolved to its concrete target (`currentMessagingTarget ?? currentChannelId`), failing open when it cannot be resolved (mirroring the existing multi-target bail), so both tools share one slot for the same recipient.
- **Routable target not threaded through the Gateway/CLI-loopback chain.** The fallback above resolves to the routable delivery target only if the Gateway scope actually carries `currentMessagingTarget`, but that field was dropped across the whole loopback chain (`GatewayScopedToolParams`, `McpLoopbackRequestContext`, `RunCliAgentParams`, the CLI MCP grant context, the loopback tool cache key, and the `createOpenClawTools` call), so on a gateway turn the key always fell back to the native `currentChannelId`. On channels whose native channel id differs from the routable target, the native/routable identity split was therefore incomplete. The trusted routable target is now threaded end to end and emitted by the CLI reply producer alongside the native id. The direct HTTP path already treats the `x-openclaw-message-to` header as the routable target, so it keeps its `agentTo` fallback. Security: the routable target is trusted only from the server-minted bound grant context — the grant-authenticated header branch fails closed and a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header can never override the bound value.
- **Ledger key was not canonicalized before admission.** The key was built from the raw agent-typed target text, but the delivery path canonicalizes the recipient later, so equivalent spellings of one peer (case, provider prefix, phone formatting) produced different keys and separate ledger slots — alternating them evaded the guard, and the `message` tool and `conversations_send` did not truly share a slot. The target is now canonicalized through the same synchronous, idempotent, provider-bound normalizer the delivery path uses, inside the shared `buildTurnSendTargetKey`, so both tools converge on one slot. Async directory-alias resolution (`@username` -> id) stays out of scope by design and off the cap hot path.
- **Queued was counted as a delivery.** `conversations_send` recorded a ledger entry on a `queued` status, but `queued` is distinct from `sent` in the gateway protocol and means the intent was enqueued without confirmed delivery. With a cap of one, a queued acknowledgement suppressed the next real send and the nudge falsely reported the message had already been sent. It now counts only confirmed `sent` deliveries, matching the delivery owner and the `message` tool (which has no `queued` concept and already counted only confirmed deliveries).

- **Overlapping same-session runs evicted each other's counts.** The ledger stored one slot per session and reset it whenever a different run recorded on that session. Concurrent foreground turns can share one session key with distinct run ids (see `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`, which starts run A, completes run B on the same session, then resumes A), so an A -> B -> A interleave let run B evict run A's slot; when run A resumed, its per-target count read zero and both the nudge and the opt-in cap were silently bypassed — exactly under the concurrency the cap exists to protect. The ledger is now keyed by a composite `(sessionKey, runId)` so overlapping runs keep independent counts. Each slot stays authoritative for the whole run lifetime (no idle expiry) and is deleted by the run owner at its terminal boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun`, wired into the embedded runner's fallback-chain `finally`); terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — there is deliberately no size-based eviction, because evicting a slot while its run is still live (an idle run while many turns execute concurrently) would silently zero that run's committed counts and release the opt-in cap mid-turn. Retained slots are bounded by the number of concurrently live runs.
- **An idempotent message replay was blocked by the cap.** The message tool evaluated the opt-in per-turn cap before deriving its stable idempotency key and recorded successes with the operation-blind counter, so a retried tool call with the same idempotency key (which the Gateway resolves to the already-completed send and returns the original receipt without re-delivering) was rejected with `turn_send_budget_exhausted` — the model was told a completed send had failed. The key is now derived before the cap, the cap is skipped when that key was already recorded this turn, and success is recorded via `recordTurnSendOnce` so a replay is counted at most once; a genuinely new or reworded send still counts and caps. This matches the `conversations_send` cap, which already admits idempotent replays.
## User Impact

- **Default-on, model-only nudge**: from the second same-target send within a turn, the tool result carries a one-line, model-visible reminder to finalize instead of re-sending. It never alters the outbound message and does not pollute a `message_tool_only` final reply. Opt out via `tools.message.turnSendNudge: false` (per-agent override inherits the global).
- **Opt-in hard cap (default off)**: `tools.message.maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget` blocks a send before dispatch once the cap is reached, returning `turn_send_budget_exhausted`. Media (`sendAttachment` / `upload-file`) and broadcast fan-out are exempt from the cap but still counted.
- No hash normalization: legitimate distinct messages, multi-part replies, media, and fan-out remain fully allowed. Existing operators who take no action get only the model-visible nudge; nothing blocks delivery unless the opt-in cap is enabled.

## Design notes

- A "turn" is one agent run (`runId`). A slot is authoritative for the entire run lifetime — including long tool waits and provider-fallback candidates that reuse the `runId` — so the opted-in cap holds for the whole turn; the run owner deletes the slot at the terminal run boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` from the embedded runner fallback-chain `finally`), and that terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — retained slots are bounded by concurrently live runs, and no size-based eviction ever removes a live run's counts. Module-level, keyed by agent session, mirroring the reviewed `recentPollVoteBySession` precedent.
- Counting always runs regardless of the nudge toggle; only the reminder text is gated.
- The hard cap reserves a slot before dispatch and settles after delivery (reserve-then-settle), so concurrent same-target sends are counted synchronously; documented inline.

## Evidence

Real behavior verified at the two boundaries the guard depends on (redacted local run):

- **Gateway boundary — ledger activates only when the run ID flows through.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ runId, surface: "loopback" })` produces a `message` tool whose per-turn cap engages; reverting the `runId` forward makes this fail. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts (11 tests)
    ✓ forwards runId so the message tool per-turn cap engages on the loopback surface
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  11 passed (11)
  ```
- **Mixed-tool shared slot — no-target `message` reply + `conversations_send` to the same peer now share one ledger slot.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` the second tool is capped; reverting to the `<current-source>` sentinel makes it deliver (`status: "sent"`) instead of `suppressed`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/conversation-tools.test.ts (15 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  15 passed (15)
  ```
- **Routable-target threading boundary — native id != routable target still share one ledger slot.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` with `currentChannelId: "D123"` (native) and `currentMessagingTarget: "user:U123"` (routable) differing: a pre-seeded routable slot and a no-target source send resolve to the same key and hit the cap. Reverting the routable-param forward makes this fail (verified). The header fail-closed invariant is covered: a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header leaves the bound routable target undefined. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts / mcp-http.request.test.ts / mcp-grant-context.test.ts
  Tests  24 passed
  ```
- **Canonical shared-slot boundary — equivalent spellings collapse to one ledger slot.** `buildTurnSendTargetKey` now runs the target through the provider normalizer, so two spellings of one peer produce a byte-identical key (verified by a spelling-equivalence unit test). Because both tools flow through this one builder, `message` and `conversations_send` to the same peer share one slot.
- **Queued does not consume a slot.** A `queued` (unconfirmed) `conversations_send` result no longer records a delivery or emits the false nudge; a subsequent `sent` to the same conversation is admitted as the first counted delivery. Verified by a queued-then-sent regression under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` plus a table over `suppressed`/`queued`/`unknown`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts / conversation-tools.test.ts
  Tests  27 passed
  ```
- **Overlapping-run isolation boundary — interleaved runs on one session keep independent counts.** With the ledger keyed by `(sessionKey, runId)`, an A -> B -> A interleave keeps run A's count climbing (`record(A)=1`, `record(B)=1`, `record(A)=2`, `peek(A)=2`, `peek(B)=1`) and per-run operation-id isolation holds; the A -> B -> A regression fails on the pre-fix single-slot code (the resumed run A reads a reset count of 1 instead of 2). The new tests are anchored to the concurrent-same-session behavior proven in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (16 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  16 passed (16)
  ```
- **Idempotent-replay-past-cap boundary — a retried send at the cap reaches delivery dedup.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, a first send is admitted and counted, a replay of the same tool call (same idempotency key) is not cap-blocked and returns the completed receipt without double-counting or a false nudge, and a genuinely different send is still capped. The regression fails on the pre-fix code (the replay came back `suppressed`/`turn_send_budget_exhausted`). Delivery-layer dedup here applies to Gateway-routed sends (the `conversations.send` `operationId` store); direct-mode channels do not yet dedup on the idempotency key at the delivery layer — tracked in #125824.
- Both regressions were confirmed to have teeth by reverting each production change and observing the corresponding test fail.
- Full suite for the feature: `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint --type-aware`.
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.




- **Live-run budget retention boundary — the cap survives long idle waits and provider fallbacks.** The 10-minute idle TTL is deleted: a `(sessionKey, runId)` slot now lives for the whole run and is removed only at the run's terminal boundary. Regressions (fake timers): a capped run stays `exhausted` after an idle interval far past the old TTL (this fails on the pre-fix TTL code — verified by temporarily restoring the prune), a committed operation is still admitted as a `replay` across the same idle wait, and `clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` deletes only the exact `(session, run)` slot (siblings on the same session and same-runId slots on other sessions stay intact; missing scope/slot is a no-op). Run-entry tests prove the budget survives the fallback boundary and is cleared on both success and throw paths. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  embedded-agent-runner  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.test.ts (22 tests)
  Test Files  passed   Tests  50 passed
  ```
- **Direct-mode replay cap guard — a duplicate model-emitted tool-call id is disambiguated into a distinct cap-blocked send, not admitted as a replay.** The discriminating regression drives the real streaming normalization (`wrapStreamFnTrimToolCallNames` -> `normalizeToolCallIdsInMessage`): a model response emitting the same `message` tool-call id twice with byte-identical arguments is rewritten to two distinct ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys and the second is cap-blocked with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result while the runner is invoked exactly once. This guards the exact mechanism that keeps the replay-admission branch unreachable from a real model turn on direct channels (the delivery-layer dedup gap for an admitted replay is tracked separately in #125824). Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (253 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  253 passed (253)
  ```

- **Route-aware replay admission boundary — a replay is only admitted past the cap when the selected delivery route dedups it.** The message tool resolves the actual gateway-vs-direct delivery route BEFORE reserving and hands the operationId to the ledger only when delivery relays through the Gateway backend (whose completed-result store dedups the repeated operationId). On direct in-process routes a repeated operation is treated as an ordinary new send: cap-blocked when a cap is set, honestly counted otherwise — closing the hole where an admitted replay on a direct channel would re-deliver because the delivery layer does not dedup idempotency keys there (tracked in #125824). Route detection fails conservative: when unsure it withholds the operationId, which cap-blocks a replay rather than re-delivering it. Regressions drive the REAL delivery path (actual outbound adapter call counts): a direct-route replay is suppressed and delivers exactly once, and a Gateway-routed replay is admitted without re-delivering or double-counting. Both fail on the pre-fix unconditional replay admission. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (254 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  254 passed (254)
  ```
- **Run-terminal budget release boundary — a reused runId starts the next turn with a fresh budget, and fallback candidates never lose committed counts mid-chain.** `prepareCliRunContext` records the exact ledger slot (agent/session/run) the loopback grant mints; CLI settlement deletes only that slot, and only at the true terminal — success or the FINAL fallback attempt's failure. A non-final failure hands off to the next candidate, which must inherit the committed counts, so settlement defers; a dispatched CLI candidate (no `isFinalFallbackAttempt`) defers to the embedded runner's fallback-chain owner, keeping exactly one cleanup owner per terminal. The threw state is derived from real control flow (a `completedNormally` flag), not from `runError`, so a `settleCliAuthProfile` throw after a successful non-final candidate defers exactly like a non-final run failure instead of wiping the budget mid-chain (discriminating regression: the pre-fix `runError` proxy fails it). Cron's isolated-agent finally adds a bounded, idempotent safety net keyed identically to the loopback grant (same `canonicalizeMainSessionAlias` composition, durable session id as runId), so a chain that throws before any candidate settles still releases the slot. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.test.ts (18 tests)
  cron            src/cron/isolated-agent/run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts (1 test)
  agents-tools    src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  Test Files  3 passed (3)   Tests  47 passed (47)
  ```

### Real delivery-boundary proof (mock provider + mock channel, ephemeral Gateway, in a container)

Added `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: a real-behavior proof that boots an ephemeral Gateway child with the mock-openai provider and the `qa-channel` synthetic transport, then exercises the shared per-turn send ledger at the real delivery boundary (Gateway + qa-channel outbound bus), not by stubbing `callGateway`. It was run inside a clean `node:24-bookworm` container with container-local Linux dependencies (not just a host unit run). All scenarios pass and the run emits a machine-readable verdict:

```
test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts (8 tests)
  ✓ sanity: a plain qa-channel DM turn delivers one outbound reply
  ✓ scenario 1: second confirmed message send in one turn nudges and both deliveries land
  ✓ scenario 2: hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed conversations_send result
  ✓ scenario 3: a suppressed message send does not charge the per-turn budget
  ✓ scenario 4: idempotent conversations_send replay does not re-deliver or double count
  ✓ scenario 5: two concurrent distinct-op sends to one target admit exactly one under the cap
  ✓ scenario 6: a model-repeated direct message send under the cap is disambiguated and cap-blocked (exactly-once delivery) — proves the cap-block path, NOT idempotent admission
  ✓ scenario 7: a spoofed attach-grant principal is refused before any delivery I/O (authority chain)
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Verdict (`pass: true`), summarized per scenario:

- **Soft nudge counts confirmed deliveries** — two confirmed `message` sends to one target land on the qa-channel bus; the second tool result carries the model-visible "already sent 2 messages to this target this turn" nudge. `deliveriesRecorded: 2`, ledger `{ "qa-channel:qa-operator": 2 }`.
- **Hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed result** — with `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, only one delivery reaches the bus; the second `conversations_send` returns `status: "suppressed"` with details that pass `Value.Check(ConversationSendResultSchema, details)` (only `status`, `conversationRef`, `channel`; no `reason`/`message`) and the block explanation in the result text. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`.
- **Only visible deliveries charge the budget** — applying the production `deliveredNothing` predicate: `suppressed` and `failed` do not count (`0`), `partial_failed` counts (`1`, a visible partial reached the peer), plugin/gateway `undefined` counts (`1`), `sent` counts (`1`); no false "sent" nudge is emitted for a non-delivery.
- **Idempotent conversations_send replay** — replaying the same `operationId` returns the Gateway's completed `sent` receipt without a second bus delivery, is not cap-blocked, and does not double-count. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`, ledger stays at `1`.
- **Concurrent distinct-op sends under the cap (reserve-then-settle)** — two parallel `conversations_send` calls with distinct operationIds (NOT a replay) to the same conversation under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`: the first in-flight reservation counts toward the cap synchronously, so the second call is exhausted before it reaches the Gateway — exactly one delivery lands on the bus and the ledger commits exactly one send. This is the core concurrency regression for #119992 (the old peek→await→record path let both peek 0 and both deliver).
- **Cap-blocked model-repeated direct send (cap-block proof, NOT idempotent admission)** — the mock provider emits the SAME direct `message` send twice in one model response (identical planned call id and byte-identical args). The runtime disambiguates the duplicate model-emitted ids into two distinct tool-call ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys: the first delivers, and the second is cap-blocked before dispatch with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result fed back to the model. Exactly-once delivery is asserted on the RECEIVE side — the qa-channel outbound bus carries exactly one copy of the marker, and a re-delivered copy would surface as a second. This proves end-to-end cap enforcement for the direct `message` tool at the real delivery boundary; it proves the cap-block path, not the idempotent-admission path (a duplicate model-emitted send is always disambiguated upstream and can never be presented as an idempotent replay).
- **Authority chain — an unauthorized principal is refused before any delivery I/O (scenario 7).** The harness's own `attach.grant` method mints a real non-owner grant; the test then drives the REAL MCP loopback HTTP entry with that grant plus spoofed delivery-authority headers (`x-session-key`, message channel, account id, current channel id, and `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` pointed at a registered conversation) — every hop is the genuine defense, with no mocked resolver output: `validateMcpLoopbackRequest` → `resolveAttachGrant` → `resolveMcpRequestContext` (grant branch forces every spoofable header, including the routable target, to undefined) → owner-only tool deny. Asserted: `tools/list` does not advertise `conversations_send` for the grant principal; a `tools/call conversations_send` attempt is refused; and zero deliveries reach the qa-channel bus. Positive control on the same lane: the legitimate owner-bound path (real Gateway `conversations.send` → qa-channel bus, as scenarios 2/4/5) delivers exactly one — so the zero above is a real refusal, not a dead harness. Verdict entries carry no tokens.

Full unit suite for the feature (`turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` + `cli-run-settlement.test.ts` + cron `run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts`) passes; `tsgo:core`/`tsgo:extensions`/`tsgo:test:root` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`. Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.

### Final-head validation (HEAD `782540cd69f`)

Second upstream catch-up: the published branch was brought up to current `upstream/main` via an ordinary merge commit that merged main `36537b21828`. No published commit was rewritten, so the branch stays a descendant of its published head `97eb46dc643` and an ordinary fast-forward push applies. This second merge only resolved the generated config-documentation baseline conflicts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` / `.sha256`, core option count settles at 2450) alongside the auto-merged code; the CHANGELOG Unreleased section is byte-identical to the merged upstream parent.

Re-verified on this final head `782540cd69f`:

- **Real qa-lab per-turn-send-budget E2E: 8/8 passing.** All eight stable scenario outcomes are pre-registered and fail-closed — the run asserts no missing, duplicate, unknown, or unsuccessful outcome; every registered scenario reports its expected result and the machine-readable verdict is `pass: true`.
- **Typecheck green:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, and `tsgo:test:root` all exit 0.
- **Focused tests: 759 passing** across the feature's unit and integration suites, plus proof 9/9.
- **Config docs / lint / format / diff check green:** config docs generation, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are all clean.
- **Autoreview (honest scope note):** the final PR-tree fresh autoreview was scoped-clean with 0 P0–P2 findings on the predecessor head `97eb46dc643`, run over the PR tree against that merge commit's second parent `8e1f02805f66` (exact `upstream/main`). This second catch-up merge (`782540cd69f`) only resolved the generated config-baseline conflicts and did **not** receive a new fresh autoreview on `782540cd69f`.

Note: the Telegram (D5) live-channel proof from earlier revisions was not rerun on this final head; the validation above covers the qa-lab delivery-boundary E2E, typecheck, focused tests, config/lint/format/diff, and the prior scoped-clean autoreview.



### CI line-cap ratchet remediation (HEAD `4bcae80db14`)

CI job `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed at `782540cd69f`: the send-budget work pushed eight grandfathered files past their `check:line-cap-ratchet` baseline (deterministic against the merge base `36537b21828`). No cap was raised, no rule disabled, and no coverage trimmed — each file drops back to or below its base counted-line count by relocating cohesive helpers and the new send-budget test group into focused sibling modules:

- `message-tool-execution.ts` → `message-tool-turn-send-budget.ts` (turn-send-budget resolve/reserve/settle/nudge orchestration).
- `message-tool.test.ts` → `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` for the per-turn-send-budget group; `createChannelPlugin` and the runner-input type shared via `message-tool.test-support.ts`. The tool-assembly wiring assertion stays where its `createOpenClawTools` mocks live.
- `command/attempt-execution.ts` → `attempt-execution-auth-profile.ts` (harness auth-profile selection).
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` → `auth-profile-resolution.ts` (CLI auth-profile resolution).
- `config/schema.labels.ts` → `schema.labels.message-tool.ts` (the `tools.message.*` label block).
- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` / `gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` → `*.test-support.ts` siblings (flush-plan fixtures / schema-builder helpers).
- qa-lab `mock-openai/server.ts` → `mock-openai-per-turn-send-budget.ts` (QA-PTSB fixtures) and `mock-openai-tool-call-input.ts` (tool-call input parsers).

Validation on this head (`4bcae80db14`):

- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 36537b21828` and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base 36537b21828` both green; `git diff --check` clean.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test` all exit 0.
- `oxlint` (core + extensions) and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.
- Feature suites green: `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` + `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` (53), and the parent `message-tool.test.ts` + `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` + `mcp-http.test.ts` suites.
- Real qa-lab `per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: **8/8** passing (re-run because the QA fixture organization changed).

The eight node-compact shard failures on the prior run were single integration tests timing out at exactly 120000ms; each reproduced green locally (`message-tool.scheduled-writes` 7/7, and feishu-mutations + channel/slack read-authority 124/124), so they were CI resource-contention flakes, not a regression — left for the fresh run to clear rather than triggering unrelated edits. This change is refactor-only; no product behavior or send-budget semantics changed. The Telegram (D5) live-channel proof was not rerun.

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

## Evidence

Current author head: `bb51672d391105ad3b06ae1336ce1c1d1f5ee97e`. Integrated official main `79262d0571694dbf083b7d1bf5a206cc8fb93936` with an ordinary merge to resolve the named cached-title CI failure. It contains the adopted repairs #178510 and #178474. The existing feature patch is preserved; earlier validation below is attributed to prior head `f729bed82a2cbe2419ecfe49d0d913fd11caac58`.

- Focused current discovery tests: **2 files / 14 tests passed**.
- Core and extension typechecks, touched-source/proof type-aware lint, format, official prompt-snapshot check, and candidate diff check passed. The initial proof lint required only braces around two `for...of` assertions; no assertion changed.
- Fresh independent review of the full proposal found no P0-P2 defect. A separate fresh review of the final proof found no P0-P2 defect.
- Compiled real Gateway, public authenticated **POST /tools/invoke**: **PASS**, using synthetic configuration and standard QA child lifecycle. The committed opt-in case is `extensions/qa-lab/src/agents-list-descriptions.e2e.test.ts`.
- Public-entry proof: all **10 authorized rows** retained in order; the restricted requester sees exactly its **2 allowed rows**; the split-surrogate boundary returns **512 valid UTF-16 units**; CJK descriptions consume exactly **4096 weighted units**; late and blank descriptions are omitted without losing agent rows; configured model and current `auto`/`implicit` discovery metadata remain intact.
- The proof performs no inference or external delivery because discovery is a read-only Gateway-owned tool. It does not claim a live Slack/provider test or a package upgrade. Standard cleanup stopped owned Gateway PID 51147; process liveness readback confirmed it stopped.
- Opt-in E2E: 1 test passed, 53.50 seconds command wall time / 50.01 seconds Vitest duration (about 19 seconds test body, including Gateway startup and cleanup). Unit tests keep the cheaper budget cases.
- The first hosted run caught an unsupported, unused `label` cleanup option in the new proof (TS2353). It is removed; the canonical `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` now passes. This does not change runtime cleanup or assertions. [Prior-head CI 39421952171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39421952171) completed. Canonical `check-test-types`, all five core-test type shards and the other product/static/test leaves succeeded. The only failed leaf is [UI cold-load case 118626035515](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39421952171/job/118626035515), plus its dependent aggregate. It is the same intermittent failure recorded on official main `6a2e9a1f9ea002b14e2847e8ca89e2b90c37f59d`, [main job 118557975798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39401671859/job/118557975798): `expected 'New session' to be 'Synthetic cold-load conversation'`. No new or unclassified failed leaf remains.
- The integrated-base green CI [39417964143](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39417964143) skipped UI E2E; a later full main run [39415536071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39415536071) passed the mocked UI shards. These are kept distinct from a green control for this case. Under CONTRIBUTING's known-main-failure policy, this PR adds no unrelated CI-only repair, weakening, rerun or budget change. Maintainers retain inherited-failure acceptance; this is **not** an all-green-CI claim.

### Captured public Gateway proof output

The following is the captured stdout from the existing successful Gateway run, copied with ANSI escapes and duplicate reporter lines removed. It is not a newly generated result summary. Only fixed proof fields and the test result are retained; no credential, endpoint, IP address, configuration dump, or conversation text is included. The HTTP response bodies were not separately saved. The committed scenario's assertions check the exact full/restricted agent IDs, bounded description strings, omitted fields and metadata before emitting `AGENTS_DESCRIPTION_PROOF`.

```text
AGENTS_DESCRIPTION_OWNER {"pid":51147}
AGENTS_DESCRIPTION_PROOF {"gatewayHttp":true,"rosterCount":10,"restrictedCount":2,"unicodeUnits":512,"aggregateWeightedUnits":4096,"modelMetadataRetained":true,"noInferenceOrExternalDelivery":true}
✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/agents-list-descriptions.e2e.test.ts > bounds configured descriptions without changing the authorized Gateway roster 19298ms
✓ bounds configured descriptions without changing the authorized Gateway roster 19298ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed (1)
Duration  50.01s (transform 52%, tests 39%, import 8%, worker 1%)
```

The capture precedes the final removal of an unused unsupported cleanup label option. That one-line type fix leaves production code, response assertions and runtime cleanup unchanged; the current-head canonical test-type gates pass. This capture claims the compiled candidate tree's public Gateway behavior, not an employee runtime or official package upgrade.

Reproduce the public entry proof after installing dependencies:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  extensions/qa-lab/src/agents-list-descriptions.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Remaining Maintainer Decision

Should bounded operator-authored descriptions become model-visible within existing authorized discovery, including descriptions configured before upgrade? This branch makes that narrow proposal ready to assess; it does not assume approval.

#148757 also overlaps discovery and adds a prompt roster. Please choose one implementation owner. This PR keeps on-demand discovery separate from automatic prompt injection and does not add that broader behavior.

### Adopted official cached-title repair and current integration

The title repair is adopted upstream through #178510 (`58c3f35e0e1894bc837871e5ca58b47be78031f2`) and #178474 (`fe739f62fcfa1f91dfaa25f7a710292da190822c`). Duplicate #178478 is closed and #178470 is resolved. This branch consumes those official main commits; it adds no separate UI patch.

The feature patch-id is unchanged across this merge. The full-index feature diff and all 10 feature file contents are byte-identical to the prior validated head. 14 focused integration tests passed; applicable prior canonical review and real-owner proof are retained. On the same official UI sources, the original synthetic cached-tail Chromium case passed with en-US/CPU4 (6.831 s case, 21.85 s wrapper), retaining the official pending-hydration/first-title assertions and the original title/scroll checks. Local diagnostic setup was restored exactly after testing. No assertions, timeout, CI routing or runtime configuration were changed by this contribution.

**Integration CI:** [39469313363](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39469313363) completed **SUCCESS** on `bb51672d391105ad3b06ae1336ce1c1d1f5ee97e`: all 83 jobs terminal, 57 successful / 26 skipped / 0 failed. prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated official main `d53309cd8ea4d0761fec3ac81ae73290b81e569a` to resolve the actual merge conflicts. Current generators own the metadata/baselines. The previous nodes-tool-media format-only repair is superseded by main; its retired block is not restored.

## Evidence

Candidate: 41974794c4ab5eb235d153d7926de7dedba834f6. Current-head hosted CI completed **SUCCESS** with no nonpassing jobs: [run 39427790673](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39427790673).

Current integrated candidate: **24 Slack tests + 17 Gateway reload-planning tests pass**. Queued-before-policy-publication tests use the real handler and both implicit kinds; already-adopted work retains the existing captured-policy contract.
- **Actual isolated Gateway, real Slack plugin and core/session processing, external HTTP simulations:** both authorized synthetic bot kinds reach a timestamp-correlated `bot-missing-mention` decision. Should Slack expose this compatibility-preserving opt-in, or should the default contract change as in #160752? The contributor implementation, regression, isolated final-effect proof, and CI are ready for that decision. No maintainer acceptance is inferred from a bot rating.

The isolated native transport, received-before-publication final effects, owner regressions, and standard package-upgrade boundaries above are complete. prs.title: fix(slack): keep progress updating after native streams expire
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack native progress can freeze or look failed after Slack expires a stream while the agent continues working. Later progress and the final answer can then fail or arrive separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a bounded projection of the stream from its first append. After an explicit `message_not_in_streaming_state` rejection with a known timestamp, use `chat.update` on that same message for later progress, final text and metadata, following the [Slack SDK recovery guidance](https://github.com/slackapi/node-slack-sdk/pull/2611).

The existing scoped writer and native Stop handling remain authoritative. Ambiguous writes are not replayed. If a full-message projection cannot fit, or a definitive editing rejection prevents recovery, only the undelivered tail uses ordinary chunked delivery. Successful fallback retires its retained projection so cleanup cannot replay it onto the original card.

`chat.update` cannot retain custom username/avatar overrides. For customized streams, explicit expiry instead retires the stream and sends only its unacknowledged tail through the existing identity-aware sender.

## User Impact

Progress and eligible final replies continue on the existing message after expiry. Task state, narration order, details, outputs and source links remain available. Recovered task details/outputs use plain rich text; embedded Markdown is not interpreted. Custom authorship, cancellation and existing delivery policy are preserved. No new option or default is introduced.

## Evidence

Current head: `fe91f0cf4045cea136254caed46f893c923a8813`.

- Ordinary merge of official main `8fe652f7cef3ea1901eb6b916ec002bef90d9598` to resolve actual conflicts in two test files. The previous reviewed head `781f315d1448f1de4cd1a8342166372927e105ac` remains an ancestor. No force push. The production `streaming.ts` and `streaming-projection.ts` bytes are unchanged from that reviewed head.
- Preserved main's consolidated streaming/dispatch tests and the distinct expiry, acknowledged-prefix, custom-identity, Stop and ambiguous-write controls. **157 tests across three files passed**: wrapper wall58.57s, Vitest51.74s. After a method-binding-only lint correction, **33 streaming tests passed again**: wrapper wall40.20s, Vitest36.82s.
- Canonical extension-test typecheck, touched-file type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass after the correction.
- Fresh AutoReview at P0-P2 found no actionable issue in the patch-bearing review pass. Its separate context-only pass did not independently certify unseen hunks. The subsequent correction uses `vi.spyOn` to preserve method binding and has test/type/lint proof.
- CI result: **SUCCESS** (completed 2026-10-20T12:22:23Z). [Exact-head run39420324606](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39420324606). Prior-head CI is not used as this head's result.

### Real Slack transport evidence

The earlier live proof executed compiled production stream/client owners from measured revision `2fec06eb352ffb4fc89178b5130aa594c7c1a4d0`, real Slack SDK8.0.0 and installed public OpenClaw SDK modules. API responses were not mocked. A separate `chat.stopStream` closed only each synthetic server-side test stream, leaving the SDK object active so its next real append received the expiry rejection.

| Measured owner | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline `4d7a33874` | Start and external stop succeed; append receives expiry rejection; rejected tail absent on readback |
| Candidate `2fec06eb` | Same rejection followed by successful same-message progress update, final answer and complete task, then final metadata |

Independent native-CLI readback verified the expected bot, same message timestamp, complete tasks, one acknowledged prefix, one final answer and retained final metadata. Task details, outputs and source links survived recovery; executed bundle hashes matched after the run. Only synthetic content was used.

That is historical evidence for the declared measured default-identity recovery path, supported by source comparison and later owner/dispatch regressions. It is not a fresh live run on this integrated head, a measurement of undocumented natural-expiry timing, or screenshot-based rendering proof. The later custom-identity branch has focused production-owner and dispatch proof; it deliberately avoids `chat.update`. No employee plugin, Gateway, channel or authentication configuration was changed.

prs.title: fix(skills): retain source context in review cancellation diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A rejected Workshop experience review loses the source correlation and collapses every anchor mismatch into the same error. Operators cannot distinguish a rewritten completed turn from an unavailable anchor projection after the queued candidate is discarded.

Refs #156948, #164279. [Observed diagnostic limit and bounded scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156948#issuecomment-6288213684).

## User Impact

Existing cancellation/failure logs identify the first failed anchor field (or `unavailable`) and a source fingerprint. No new raw identity, transcript value, conversation key, path or message content is recorded. Expected cancellations remain DEBUG; actual failures remain warnings.

The historical refusal cannot be reconstructed. This is diagnostic repair, not a claim that the historical refusal was incorrect or that the broader issues are resolved.

## Change

Reuse the existing comparison owner in SQLite and committed-actor readers. Every prior predicate, exact actor scope check, and physical database-path alias rule remains. The scheduler adds SHA256(JSON.stringify([agentId, sessionId, entryId])) to its existing log. `unavailable` means no usable anchor was returned; it does not assert deletion.

No schema, config, SQL query, retry, re-anchoring, acceptance policy or authority relaxation. Maintainer decision requested: accept the fixed field names and bounded source fingerprint in these existing diagnostics. No approval is assumed.

## Evidence

- Baseline `39fb90fb35d5ae628a0316fe40cd9b7b9bbbe055`: real SQLite validation lacks mismatch reasons; five scheduler cancellation/failure cases lack source correlation. The committed-actor diagnostic also failed before its change.
- After resolving the real GitHub conflict against official main `3213e3e542c5658f4095d08942f2636e6a40153e`, all **35 focused cases pass**. Main's actor-fixture simplification is retained, together with the generation diagnostic assertion. Existing lifecycle, permissions and SQL-statement controls remain.

Ten ordinary `chat.send` / `agent.wait` turns reach the unmodified review threshold. Public `sessions.compact` changes the transcript before the real idle timer runs the queued review. prs.title: fix: deferred agents fail admission while model preparation is still running
prs.body:
Related: #173198

## What Problem This Solves

Healthy deferred agents could remain refused when finite startup model preparation outlasted the ordinary 120-second refresh deadline. Keep deferred admission pending until that generation has actually published, then accept work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deferred database admission is background startup work, but its model publication used the ordinary refresh lifetime. Reuse the existing startup acquisition owner and queue-release timer; the background caller waits for complete publication rather than foreground readiness release. Existing current-claim checks and bounded supersession retries still fence interrupted generations. Ordinary refresh deadlines, foreground startup grace, configuration supersession and queue-release behavior remain unchanged. No new timer, queue, setting or persistent state is added.

## Evidence

- On official base `dfc18caabc9f44d98e14d6250dd411d45096007a`, both isolated admission regressions fail beyond 120 seconds. The correction keeps admission pending until publication. A separate regression verifies successor preparation enters after grace while retired finite cleanup finishes. All 32 owner-focused regressions pass, including real AbortSignal cancellation/current-claim assertions; those assertions are unchanged by the proof follow-up.
- The added opt-in `extensions/qa-lab/src/deferred-startup-publication.e2e.test.ts` launches the actual compiled Gateway, uses the public provider-discovery callback, and restores a byte-identical valid canonical synthetic SQLite store. With the real 120-second deadline intact, `/startupz` explicitly reports `agent-database-inspection`, finite catalog preparation completes after 130,003 ms, actual recovery/publication follows, and an ordinary loopback synthetic Responses turn completes (`deliver:false`).
- The final proof passes with the same current pinned Bun worker revision `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de` as CI, using the existing QA Node child resolver. It was measured on actual CI merge `ad82a57c1f10a54ca80c6b6242f238c6dd904603` plus the final proof-only delta (file SHA256 `8e62d42f5a679b28f38f200ef6212b6cc0d11d0b20f4ae2783d7d27d6a9b75e3`); runner time 200.52 seconds. Canonical extension-test types, typed lint, format/diff and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass.
- Standard published-upgrade survivor proof passes from real registry `openclaw@2026.10.5` to the candidate built at production head `cecd76e89a8d6f9163d20bbbbb27ed4455bbc4f7` (tarball SHA256 `694351d0e26f2c9e61fedc5e082c94cde3f9646583f2052c3afe0fce8f609cd0`). All 49 phases pass, including baseline startup, existing synthetic settings/data survival, automatic migration, doctor/validation, upgraded Gateway startup (131 s), health/ready (1 s each) and RPC status (4 s). That production revision remained byte-identical through `f1d398be26523605e99b9ffcae8039eb57442e58`. The current official-main integration retains the same startup change: three production files stay byte-identical, and `prepared-model-runtime.ts` additionally contains only official aggregate-error reuse and the existing publisher rename. The upgrade result qualifies the measured candidate, not a second installed-package run on the integrated head. The temporary package/container were cleaned up; no registry publication or employee installation occurred.

### Shutdown proof follows the public stop contract

The proof now waits for the **specific public catalog hook's started marker**, observes OS `SIGTERM` shutdown receipt, and requires `confirmed-stopped`, no cleanup errors, no completed catalog and no recovery/readmission. This proves process quiescence during pending preparation. The existing QA lifetime [bounds an unready child's graceful stop to 1,500 ms and may force-stop it](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2d03d5632a69d04181844f85b05d5509240dcc14/extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child-lifecycle.ts#L187); it then joins pipe closure and returns the confirmed-stop result. It does **not** promise that a cooperative provider callback's abort log will finish first.

The first proof incorrectly required that extra log. CI and the paired Bun-parent/Node-child run observed actual catalog start and shutdown receipt but no abort log, so the fixture was corrected to the existing stop API's guarantee, with no production seam or timeout change. The QA [Node resolver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2d03d5632a69d04181844f85b05d5509240dcc14/extensions/qa-lab/src/node-exec.ts#L1) is also used instead of inheriting a Bun parent's executable. This does not establish Bun as the sole cause of the missing log. The earlier Node-only run at `cecd76e89a8d6f9163d20bbbbb27ed4455bbc4f7` did observe the cooperative abort marker; that historical observation and the unchanged owner-level AbortSignal regressions remain separate evidence.

### Selected observed terminal output

```text
DEFERRED_STARTUP_STAGE {"status":"starting","pendingReason":"agent-database-inspection"}
DEFERRED_STARTUP_PROOF {"realGateway":true,"catalog":"public provider discovery fixture","realDeadlineMs":120000,"finitePreparationMs":130000,"deferredPendingObserved":true,"admittedAfterCompletion":true,"ordinaryTurn":"ok","shutdownReceived":true,"shutdownStoppedProcess":true,"readmissionAfterShutdown":false,"providerRequests":1,"delivery":false}
Upgrade survivor Docker E2E passed baseline=openclaw@2026.10.5 scenario=base candidate=2026.10.5 updateRestartMode=manual idempotence=n/as startup=131s updateRestart=manuals healthz=1s readyz=1s status=4s.
```

Gateway command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/deferred-startup-publication.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, with the checkout's verified pinned Bun. Upgrade command: unmodified `scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh`, published baseline `openclaw@2026.10.5`, candidate `current`, scenario `base`.

## CI attribution and dependencies

The old broadcast-fixture timeout was separately reproduced with all four production changes restored to official base. Its equivalent repair already landed on official main at [40fc488a2089623485f0a3344604e51b6c3664ff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/40fc488a2089623485f0a3344604e51b6c3664ff). This branch cherry-picks that exact official dependency with provenance; all eight cases pass without changing assertions, deadlines or shutdown controls. Redundant #177350 was separated and closed after its equivalent head passed [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39420066604).

The previous qualified head `f1d398be26523605e99b9ffcae8039eb57442e58` passed the actual Gateway proof (165,574 ms), all three PostgreSQL shards and every other executed leaf except the two chat-replay cases; [CI39430355392](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39430355392) therefore completed FAILURE. A controlled same-runtime pair had reproduced the same provider-order signature on both the prior tested merge `ad82a57c1f10a54ca80c6b6242f238c6dd904603` (71.81 s) and clean official base `2d03d5632a69d04181844f85b05d5509240dcc14` (50.39 s), without this PR's production changes.

The cause is now fixed upstream by [c68102544feb3642b20ce17be4542e0f90ed54e3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c68102544feb3642b20ce17be4542e0f90ed54e3). #177943 added standalone recovery admission/continuation controls to the provider request. The scripted fixture selected the last user-role text, misclassified that control as ordinary chat, and issued a scripted write response even though lifecycle predecessor/peer/chat start order was correct. The official repair ignores only the canonical admission note and standalone restart-control prefix when selecting the response; merged prompts carrying real input and every ordering, authority, content, tool-effect and timeout assertion remain intact.

The existing branch now merges pinned official main `d85fcb29bec40d33dc6055fe4144cbf468b8848c`, which includes that exact repair and its dependencies. There are no conflict resolutions or new authored production/fixture changes. The chat fixture is byte-identical to official main. With the same pinned Bun revision `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`, the real Gateway owning test passes both `steer` (31.897 s) and `followup` (8.785 s), wrapper 92.82 s. The affected startup/preparation/catalog/registry tests pass 39/39, and the retained batch/owner-supersession tests pass 29/29. Targeted canonical test types (11.42 s), typed lint (20.96 s), format, diff and gating secret scan pass. Fresh independent integration review finds no defects; five contribution files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head, and the sixth preserves the same startup delta plus the official owner changes noted above.

## Scope and limits

The finite-preparation proof uses standard QA source-plugin staging, synthetic state and loopback inference; the independent survivor proof uses the actual published baseline/package updater. This is not an employee deployment, Windows-host proof, arbitrary non-cooperative callback termination proof, or a claim that every startup symptom in #173198 has this cause. Process shutdown and cooperative model-owner cancellation are explicitly separate contracts above.

Current branch head: `a4280842a3e12b05c56e11c61070996d2f88dbb0`. [Exact-head CI39437764113](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39437764113) completed **SUCCESS** at 2026-10-20T14:43:16Z: all 90 jobs terminal, zero failures and zero pending. The original chat-replay cases actually executed and passed in [job118681059560](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39437764113/job/118681059560): steer19,420ms and followup12,111ms. The added finite-preparation Gateway proof actually executed and passed in [job118681059645](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39437764113/job/118681059645), test179,338ms; all three PostgreSQL shards, both UI E2E shards and the other required checks passed. The previous inherited-failure disposition is no longer needed.

The unchanged finite-preparation Gateway and published-upgrade evidence above retain their measured heads; current CI supplies the integrated-head Gateway result. The prior [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177322#issuecomment-6267776850) found Before merge=None and Findings=None for the unchanged contribution; the mechanical official-main integration received fresh independent review with no defects. No contributor implementation or evidence work remains; maintainer acceptance is pending.

prs.title: fix(agents): detect sustained same-target write churn
prs.body:
Related: #122577

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent can repeatedly overwrite one file with different successful contents while never producing a final response. Because every write has different arguments and reports `changed: true`, current loop detection treats the sequence as ordinary progress indefinitely.

This PR proposes a conservative behavioral boundary for maintainer review. The issue is currently marked as requiring a product decision; this PR does not claim that decision has already been made.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change keeps successful writes classified as real mutations and adds a separate, warning-first run-liveness signal for a contiguous tail of content-changing writes to one resolved target. Target identity excludes document content and is stored only as a hash.

The existing loop warning threshold is reused. The warned write remains allowed. Continuity clears when the run changes tools (including read/verification), changes targets, repeats an earlier argument variant, or completes/replaces its lifecycle. If churn remains continuous through the existing stale-run boundary, owner-bound recovery can abort only that run whether or not follow-up work is queued.

The behavior is limited to the built-in `write` result contract (`details.changed === true`). It is not tied to a provider, model, transport, channel, or reported private document. No new configuration or default surface is added.

## Batch and Liveness Semantics

A whole assistant batch is admitted before its calls have outcomes. This revision therefore keeps warning and liveness behavior aligned at both lifecycle boundaries:

- successful write-mutation liveness stays inactive below the shared warning threshold;
- a sequential batch emits the same run-scoped warning before the threshold-crossing write implementation starts;
- a post-outcome fallback covers parallel or out-of-order batch completions;
- the shared warning bucket prevents duplicate pre- and post-outcome warnings;
- the existing stable no-progress classifier still includes the just-recorded outcome and activates on its original boundary.

## Scope

The write-churn changes remain in the agent loop owner. A separate memory-core test commit stabilizes the unrelated provenance-repair assertion that failed hosted CI: it holds the detached repair open while asserting that automatic candidates remain hidden, then releases and verifies the repaired result. The test moved into the existing candidate-repair suite to satisfy the line-cap ratchet. No memory-core production behavior changed.

A subsequent agent fix resets the reverse write-variant scan at the newer occurrence of a repeated variant, retaining only post-repeat writes. A replacement regression uses actual `changed: true` outcomes at the shared warning threshold and verifies that a fresh post-repeat streak can warn again.

## User Impact

Runaway same-file rewrite sequences become bounded without immediately blocking normal edits. Short rewrite sequences, multi-file work, write/read/write verification, repeated identical content, and successful writes outside the sustained same-target pattern retain their existing behavior. The latest file state and session remain available after recovery.

## Policy Status

ClawSweeper marked #122577 as requiring a maintainer product decision and disabled automated fix-PR queueing. This PR implements one conservative proposal for review; it does not claim that maintainers have approved the warning, escape, or recovery boundary. It is ready for maintainer review of that decision, but does not claim approval or merge readiness.

## Evidence

Behavioral incident baseline: `v2026.7.2-beta.7` (`dabe1915362e20c25704af91612a32a8f4c96e83`). The beta is provenance only; the patch and tests are bound to the recorded branch head and integrated base below, not an unqualified current-main merge.

Negative controls observed before their fixes:

```text
same-target detector: expected warning, received { stuck: false }
below-threshold liveness: active=true after the second distinct changed write
embedded sequential batch: 11 successful writes, warning event list empty
stable no-progress boundary: sixth completed outcome still reported active=false
default-parallel batch: warning emitted, first churn lease remained absent
loop detection omitted/disabled: changed-write churn emitted a warning
CI dependency scan: three internal helpers were exported but unused
```

## Current revision and verification

Head: `f72242e6faf82f8608abd704b16d868d8a034ada`. The branch's integrated main merge-base remains `d45155d6c51169ac10890445418a9144395d1697`; it has not been integrated with current main.

- Revision 34's staged-write-target lifecycle P2 is fixed in the shared wrapper settlement `finally`, with run-scoped cleanup on success, errors, late cancellation, source-guard refusal and disposal. Batch final-target precedence is retained. The follow-up adds three production lines and +132 net test lines across two files.
- Five regressions failed on the preceding wrapper and passed after the fix. At this exact clean head, the focused detector, warning, write-target, admission and real-Agent sequential/default-parallel suites passed 169 distinct tests across five files. This is native wrapper/Agent lifecycle evidence, not a current-head Gateway recovery proof.
- Production `tsgo:core`, the canonical `core-test-agents-root` compiler graph, focused type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and whitespace checks passed. The changed-graph selector stopped on the pre-existing 721-root/advisory-720 budget check; no config or test inventory changed, and the named graph was compiled separately. No full all-graph check claim.
- Independent read-only review found no actionable defect in the lifecycle fix. The full branch surface against its integrated base is source +475 and tests +1503 across 23 files; the added production state remains limited to target-aware detection, batch reconciliation and existing liveness ownership.
- Prior-head hosted CI failed one subagent-registry shard at `subagent-registry.test.ts:5160`, with dependent failure/cancellations; this unrelated failure was not repaired. Local passes are not a new-head hosted-CI pass.
- A merge-tree against main `3f12395208355949832da16c882e83cc5726c560` reports ten conflicting paths. Integration remains explicitly unqualified.

[The final follow-up comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122631#issuecomment-5974613163) contains the exact commands, checked-in proof links and captured terminal excerpts. No new isolated-Gateway result is claimed.

### Historical isolated Gateway proof (`27b24258c8`)

The real gateway, authenticated loopback agent RPC, embedded runner, built-in write/read tools, diagnostic heartbeat, and owner-bound recovery were exercised using a deterministic loopback model transport. No outbound-channel delivery or live-provider claim.

```text
canonical warning: argument_churn / warn / count 10 (seq 197)
later warning: argument_churn / warn / count 20 (seq 302)
continuous churn duration: 378645 ms
session.stalled: age 376954 ms, model_call (seq 361)
recovery requested: abort, same age (seq 362)
recovery completed: abort_embedded_run / aborted / embedded_run (seq 367)
healthy concurrent control: passed
post-recovery control: passed
same-session file readback: passed
target-file digest readback: matched
artifact verifier: passed, no failures
```

This trace is historical: subsequent target-hash, repeat-continuity and staging-cleanup changes have not been qualified through the isolated Gateway at the current head. No rerun is in progress or claimed; final Gateway qualification is deferred until a maintainer chooses the policy and the branch is integrated. The synthetic harness at the proof head selected the latest marked prompt because runtime context could follow it as another user-role message; no production timing constants were changed for that historical proof.

The [historical proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122631#issuecomment-5746076190) contains the sanitized event evidence and artifact digests. Raw logs, runtime identifiers, local paths, credentials, and provider configuration are intentionally not published.

## Remaining decisions

Maintainer acceptance of owner-bound abort for sustained successful writes versus warning-only remains required, including the effect for existing `loopDetection.enabled: true` installations. A maintainer must own the current-main conflicts and final hosted CI/Gateway validation, provide a bounded acceptance path, or reject the proposal. This final cleanup does not select the policy, waive checks, or claim merge readiness. Further contributor-side rebase/build/Gateway-proof cycles are paused again.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve ACP lifecycle ownership
prs.body:
## Summary

- keep spawned ACP runs under their canonical `acp` task owner while retaining a topology/control observer in the subagent registry
- stop ACP observer rows from creating duplicate `subagent` task projections, terminal delivery obligations, or child-session cleanup authority
- upgrade persisted legacy ACP mirrors during normalization and use the active ACP turn or canonical durable task as observer liveness
- emit a specific ACP owner-loss reason and preserve one-shot session state until a later corroborating maintenance pass

Fixes [GEN-6353](https://linear.app/genhealth/issue/GEN-6353/openclaw-loses-active-shrimp-acp-backing-sessions-after-the-legacy).

## What Problem This Solves

An ACP spawn created the canonical `runtime=acp` task, then the shared spawn pipeline registered the same run as a native subagent. The mirror's sweeper checked `getAgentRunContext`, which never represented external ACP liveness, so it false-failed after the stale grace and ran session-scoped cleanup. Task maintenance later treated only the process-local ACP turn marker as backing evidence, marked the canonical task lost after its grace, and could close the one-shot session in that same pass.

The observed production intervals match those two grace periods plus sweep cadence.

## Design

Patterns found and retained:

- the shared spawn registry remains the source for child topology, admission caps, status, and control
- the ACP manager/task registry remains the canonical lifecycle, progress, delivery, and cleanup owner
- observer ownership is persisted in the existing forward-compatible payload JSON; no SQLite schema change is required
- legacy ACP rows are recognized by their canonical ACP session key and normalized into observer-only state

Patterns intentionally not used:

- native subagent restart recovery and native `AgentRunContext` liveness, because Codex/ACP has a separate durable thread/session identity and resume contract
- deleting ACP rows from the subagent registry, which would regress topology and child controls
- immediate session deletion after declaring loss; cleanup now requires a later pass and rechecks the active turn

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-run-launch.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-sweeper-recovery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-run-liveness.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts`
  - 239 tests passed across 3 Vitest shards

prs.title: fix(matrix): resolve exact room session routes
prs.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the implementation and validation results.

## What Problem This Solves

Explicit Matrix room delivery could not derive a session under the default DM scope. A canonical room target was marked non-exact, so delivery failed unless the caller supplied `--session-key`, even though Matrix already had an exact room identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix plugin owns whether a normalized target is authoritative. This change treats `!`-prefixed room IDs as exact independently of the DM-only session scope while keeping room aliases (`#…`) non-authoritative. Generic delivery and binding ownership remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Commands targeting either legacy `!room:server` IDs or modern server-less room IDs can resolve their room session without a manually supplied session key. Alias and DM routing behavior is preserved.

## Evidence
