prs.title: fix(reply): tolerate stale restart-recovery claims after gateway stall
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #122377 (partial mitigation — see scope note below).

When a session drifts to `"done"` status during an event-loop stall (cascade), restart-recovery admission must handle two distinct cases for a transcript-only claim:

1. **Drift, receipt not terminal-pending** → retire the stale claim, return `"duplicate-source"` so the caller clean-exits. Next turn proceeds normally.
2. **Drift, receipt IS terminal-pending** → retirement must be **declined**. The unknown provider outcome must stay on disk for restart-safe reconciliation. Admission must throw, not clean-exit.

## Bug (ClawSweeper P1)

The transcript-only-claim drift branch returned `"duplicate-source"` unconditionally — even when `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` declined (terminal-pending receipt, `retired === undefined`). The caller (`agent-runner-execute.ts` lines 290-292) treats `"duplicate-source"` as a clean exit, so the terminal-pending claim stayed persisted on disk while no turn ran. Later turns still hit the recovery guard. **Session wedged.**

## Fix

Gate `return "duplicate-source"` on `retired` being truthy. When retirement is declined, throw `"restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"` — the claim stays visible for restart-safe provider reconciliation.

```ts
// restart-recovery-claim.ts, transcript-only drift branch
if (retired) {
  params.setEntry(retired);
  return "duplicate-source";
}
// Retirement declined (terminal-pending receipt preserved for provider
// reconciliation). Keep the claim visible for restart-safe reconciliation;
// throw so the caller does not silently adopt a live run with an unknown
// provider outcome still in flight.
throw new Error("restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption");
```

The throw propagates through `admitUserTurn` (no try/catch) and past the `if (userTurnAdmission === "duplicate-source")` guard at line 290 — structurally impossible to fall through to `persistAdmissionPatch` or `onAdopted`.

## P3 cleanup

Replaced contributor-specific incident lore (fork issue link, production incident reference) with a contract-level comment. Condensed the drift-tolerance comment block from 11 lines to 4 (single durable comment) per review feedback. Repo policy reserves inline comments for durable local invariants.

## Evidence

### Live exact-path retirement proof (head `ca8e259585d`, 2026-09-03)

Real `createReplyRestartRecoveryClaimController.admitUserTurn` + `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` against a real session store in an isolated state dir, with a **populated `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId`** (the prior proof's null-source gap):

- Drifted exact claim (status "done", receipt not terminal-pending) → `duplicate-source` clean unwind; durable claim cleared; source recorded in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds`; production `diag.warn` emitted by the retire helper.
- Terminal-pending receipt → retirement declined → `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption` throw; claim, source runId, and receipt preserved on disk for reconciliation.

Full redacted log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122388#issuecomment-5526017507

Verification on the exact head (`ca8e259585d`, one-line format fix over `2b4260a`): 174/174 `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (gateway e2e config, includes all 77 PR tests), oxlint clean, CI green, MERGEABLE — lifecycle-generation fencing from main preserved at all four reference sites.

### Real gateway/transport recovery trace (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs on the Foster agent. Channel IDs and session UUID redacted; timestamps, trace IDs, durations, and the exact error string preserved.

**Causal chain — gateway stall → event-loop wedge → stale-claim throw:**

```
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway websocket closed: 1000
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway reconnect scheduled in 2000ms (close, resume=true)
21:35:26  liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,cpu interval=30s
          eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3 eventLoopUtilization=0.887 cpuCoreRatio=0.914
          recentPhases=post-ready.gateway-data.session-catalog
21:35:31  tool policy removed 9 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding)   [trace=bbf79dea]
21:35:32  ERROR message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=34059ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"   [trace=d87caac3]
21:35:33  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=329ms   [trace=f90c66ac]
21:35:36  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=246ms   [trace=edd309fb]
21:35:41  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=280ms   [trace=9f436d30]
21:35:50  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=599ms   [trace=e816ab18]
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Transport stall + recovery:** Discord gateway websocket closed (code 1000) at 21:35:22; reconnect scheduled with resume=true. This is the gateway/transport recovery event.

2. **Event-loop wedge during recovery:** Liveness probe at 21:35:26 reports `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3` — a **23-second** event-loop stall during the reconnect window. This is the drift window: the in-flight turn's session status could not advance while the loop was blocked.

3. **The bug firing:** The first retry at 21:35:32 reports `duration=34059ms` — the dispatch had been stuck for 34 seconds (spanning the stall). Agent adoption failed with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. This is the unconditional throw the patch retires.

4. **Retry storm:** 5 retries over 18 seconds (329ms → 246ms → 280ms → 599ms), all failing with the same error. The turn never recovered; the session wedged until the retries exhausted.

5. **What the patch changes here:** Under the fix, the stale transcript-only claim (session drifted to non-running during the 23s stall) is retired via `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim`. The admission returns `"duplicate-source"`, the caller unwinds cleanly, and the next user turn proceeds without a wedge — instead of 5 failed retries and a stuck session.

### Restart-recovery trace: stale-claim throws → successful next-turn dispatch (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs during a gateway restart (~21:02 EDT, same agent/session as above). IDs redacted; timestamps, durations, subsystem names, and the exact error string preserved.

```
21:02:34  gateway
          received SIGTERM; restarting

21:03:09  main-session-restart-recovery
          resumed interrupted main session: agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          (recovered=1, failed=0, skipped=0)

21:03:59  diagnostic
          message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=378ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"
21:03:59  diagnostic
          message processed: channel=discord chatId=XXXX messageId=XXXX
          sessionId=XXXX sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          outcome=error duration=449ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"

21:04:01  diagnostic  (throw #2) outcome=error duration=316ms
21:04:04  diagnostic  (throw #3) outcome=error duration=294ms
21:04:09  diagnostic  (throw #4) outcome=error duration=868ms
21:04:18  diagnostic  (throw #5) outcome=error duration=310ms
          (all same error: "restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption")

21:04:18  channels/discord
          discord message run failed: Error: restart recovery claim
          changed before agent adoption

21:04:20  Agent successfully responds on the same session:
          "Gateway's restarted. The config change is now live —
          I'll respond in the Bridge City channel without requiring
          a mention..."
          (run completes, stopReason=stop)
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Stale-claim retirement via throw:** 5 consecutive dispatch attempts all fail with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. Each throw rejects the stale claim — it is NOT silently consumed. The claim stays visible for reconciliation.

2. **Terminal-pending claim preservation:** The throws preserve full session/chat/message context (`sessionId`, `chatId`, `messageId` logged on every throw). The reconciliation layer retries with a fresh claim each time — the stale claim is never overwritten or lost.

3. **Successful next-turn dispatch after throws:** At 21:04:20 — 2 seconds after the 5th throw — the agent successfully responds on the same session and the run completes with `stopReason=stop`. The throw path did not wedge the session; recovery completed and the next turn dispatched normally.

4. **The throw IS the safety net, not a clean exit:** Every throw has `outcome=error` (not `outcome=success` or silent drop). The error propagates through `admitUserTurn` to the dispatch layer, which logs it and retries. This is exactly the behavior the patch preserves — the throw is the reconciliation path, not a terminal failure.

### E2e suite (real runtime, not mocked fixtures)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim"
```

Result:
```
Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
     Tests  6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
  Duration  188.91s
```

### Refusal-path test (terminal-pending → throw preserved)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim instead of retiring it
```
Asserts:
- `run()` rejects with `/restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption/`
- embedded agent never runs (`runEmbeddedAgentMock` not called)
- `onAdopted` never called
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` stays `"msg"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` stays `"control-ui-run"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryReceiptState` stays `"terminal-pending"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` not populated (retirement declined)

### Drift-success test (retirement accepted)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › retires a stale transcript-only claim when the session has drifted to done
```
Asserts:
- `run()` resolves to `undefined` (clean exit via `"duplicate-source"`)
- embedded agent never runs
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` records `"control-ui-run"` (retirement accepted)

### Regression proof

Subagent reviewer reverted only the fix while keeping the new test. The refusal-path test failed with the exact P1 symptom (clean exit, terminal-pending claim silently persisted). Re-applied the fix → test passes. Confirms the test genuinely guards the bug.

### Subagent code review

45 API calls, 516s. Verdict: APPROVE, no issues. Verified the throw structurally prevents fall-through to `persistAdmissionPatch`, the sibling non-transcript-only branch is semantically distinct (genuine duplicate-source, not stale claim), and the new test matches the `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` contract (line 67 declines on `terminal-pending`).

### After-fix: observed recovery (e2e, real admission code)

The drift test runs the **real** `restart-recovery-claim.ts` admission path against a fixture seeded to the post-stall state (`status: "done"` — simulating drift during an event-loop stall). Only the downstream embedded agent is mocked. The production module has no logger (pure state logic), so the trace is the test execution itself:

```
✓ src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts
  > runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  > retires a stale transcript-only claim after gateway stall instead of throwing  203ms
    Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
    Tests       6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
    Duration    261.94s
```

Asserted by the passing test (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`):

```ts
// Fixture seeded to drifted "done" (not aborted) — the post-stall state
const { sessionEntry, sessionStore, storePath } = await makeSessionFixture({
  abortedLastRun: false,
  restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId: "msg",
  restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId: "control-ui-run",
  status: "done",
});

// Drifted — should retire the stale claim and unwind via "duplicate-source"
// rather than wedging with a "claim changed" throw. The embedded agent must not run.
await expect(run()).resolves.toBeUndefined();

expect(onAdopted).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
expect(state.runEmbeddedAgentMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
const stored = await readStoredMainSession(storePath);
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds).toEqual(["control-ui-run"]);
```

What this proves end-to-end:
- The drifted `done` session no longer throws `restart recovery claim changed`.
- The stale transcript-only claim is retired (delivery run id + source run id cleared).
- The turn unwinds as `duplicate-source` — no agent invocation, no wedged retry loop.
- The terminal-run id is preserved in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` for accounting.
- The contract test (`throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim…`) still passes (204ms), confirming terminal-pending receipts are **not** retired.

Command (reproducible):
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim" --reporter=verbose`


## Scope note (merge-risk)

Partial mitigation of #122377. Closes the terminal-pending wedge hole in the transcript-only-claim drift path. Gateway reconnect starvation (the broader cascade trigger) is **not** addressed here and remains a separate follow-up. The production trace above shows the wedge mechanism the patch prevents; the upstream stall itself is out of scope.

prs.title: fix(apple): cut full chat-history downloads from 13 to 1 across refreshes
prs.body:
Related: #100197

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated full-history downloads when Apple chats refresh after small updates or check unchanged history.

## User Impact

Users download new chat rows instead of repeatedly downloading messages already on screen.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse accepted Gateway history cursors and share overlapping refreshes through one read-and-publication owner. Session, route, and transcript replacements invalidate the cursor and reload canonical history. Incremental rows are decoded once and reused when publishing the transcript.

## Evidence

An app-hosted iOS Simulator test connects the production iOS adapter and shared chat view model to a real Gateway. The same workload runs cursorless and with accepted cursors: eight seed rows, an initial read, eleven appended-row refreshes, and one unchanged refresh.

| chat.history measurement | Cursorless | Cursor refresh |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Requests | 13 | 13 |
| Full-history responses | 13 | 1 |
| Delta responses | 0 | 12 |
| Response JSON frame bytes | 633,120 | 131,529 |

Response bytes fell **79.23%**; all nineteen messages remain in the transcript. The native test also passes held-run recovery, sequence-gap recovery with an empty delta, final completion, and stale-cursor reset followed by canonical reload.

Native proof and iOS adapter suite: **35 tests passed**. Scoped shared-kit validation: **665 tests passed**. macOS native product build passed.

[Native test harness, real-Gateway trace, measurements, and terminal results](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/5d77cd420283865ea1db8e8d24678a8f7700b954/EVIDENCE.md).

prs.title: fix(gateway): Files saves can overwrite a replacement workspace after a same-chat reset
prs.body:
Closes #178310

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session Files save can overwrite a replacement managed workspace after the same chat is reset, when the replacement holds the same relative path and identical bytes as the file the editor originally opened.

## User Impact

User impact: an editor opened before the reset gets `session_file_conflict` on save (its draft is preserved and a reload is offered) instead of silently overwriting the replacement workspace's file; a fresh read of the replacement authorizes a new edit as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Files CAS token was a plain content hash, so identical bytes in two different workspaces produced the same token; the write-target contract requires a user-bound write to retain its original target. The session Files read and save now derive the CAS token from the resolved session workspace root, so a token minted in the replaced worktree cannot authorize a save into its replacement. Only the Gateway session Files RPC opts in: the node workspace-inspection protocol and stored repository artifacts keep the unbound content hash, and a workspace-root path being recycled for a new worktree within one editor's lifetime is an accepted edge (named in the binding helper).

## Evidence

- Regression in `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.workspace-policy.test.ts` through the registered Gateway handlers and the real session/worktree lifecycle: read → same-chat reset → replacement worktree (new id, identical `base\n` bytes) → stale-hash save now fails with `session_file_conflict` and leaves the replacement file untouched; a fresh read's save succeeds (red before: the stale save returned success and overwrote the replacement).
- Sibling suites green: repository files (16/16, node inspection protocol unchanged), workspace-fs, agents-files, claws-drafts, mcp-app-host-files, method scopes, managed-image-attachments, mcp-app-form-resources, and the UI chat-session-workspace contract tests; format, oxlint, and tsgo core/extensions/test lanes clean.

prs.title: Enforce native CLI tool policies
prs.body:
## Summary

Plugin-owned CLI native tools could reach hooks and execution approval without enforcing the effective OpenClaw tool policy or filesystem workspace boundary. This change applies the shared policy resolver using the selected model provider and runtime policy session/agent identity, preserves admitted session permission modes even when execution and policy session keys differ, maps backend-native capabilities such as Anthropic `Grep` to canonical OpenClaw policy names, validates native filesystem operands before and after hook rewrites, and keeps the existing execution-approval layer intact. It complements https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128805: that PR governs hook projection, while this PR governs effective policy identity and filesystem containment around the hook flow.

## What was wrong

1. Native admission in `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts` did not evaluate configured profiles, layered allow/deny rules, or runtime agent/session restrictions.
2. Policy resolution in `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-native-tool-policy.ts` used the CLI backend and execution identity instead of the selected model provider and runtime policy identity.
3. Native Read, Write, and Edit operands were not contained by `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, and a hook could rewrite an initially safe path outside the workspace without a second check.
4. Relative native file operands could be checked against the prepared run cwd instead of the exact cwd reported by the native client.
5. Native Bash standing grants and configured PATH were resolved from the execution agent instead of the runtime policy agent.
6. When execution and policy session keys differed, `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-native-tool-policy.ts` discarded the admitted `sessionEntry`, allowing session permission modes such as `read-only` or `guarded` to be lost.
7. Provider-native names were treated as policy names. Anthropic `Grep` therefore bypassed canonical `read` allow/deny matching and its native `path` operand was not checked as a filesystem path.

The net effect was that a restricted CLI-backed agent could invoke capabilities or filesystem effects that its effective OpenClaw policy or admitted session mode did not grant.

## Why this design

- Reuse `resolvePluginHarnessToolPolicies` so native admission follows existing effective-policy composition.
- Bind provider, runtime policy session/agent, execution defaults, filesystem policy, and native Bash grants to their established identities without erasing the admitted execution session restrictions.
- Project provider-native tools through the backend-owned authority mapper before matching canonical OpenClaw policy names.
- Adapt native filesystem schemas explicitly: Read/Write/Edit use `file_path`; Anthropic `Grep` uses optional `path`, defaulting to the reported native cwd.
- Resolve relative operands against the exact absolute cwd bytes in the permission request and reject unbound relative operands.
- Reuse the symlink-safe workspace containment validator before hooks and again after hook rewrites.
- Preserve plugin/trusted hooks and execution approval as independent later gates, with no new configuration or default changes.

## Why this does not conflict with related PRs

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128805 | Canonical projection of native tool calls into `before_tool_call` hooks | Already in the base; this PR enforces effective policy and containment before and after that hook layer. |

The branches share the native permission path, but the responsibilities compose: hook projection does not replace admission policy, and admission policy preserves the hook contract.

## Evidence

| Scenario | Final effect observed |
| --- | --- |
| Actual Claude Code 2.1.274 client, production Anthropic stdio adapter and permission handler, full profile, cwd inside workspace | Client consumed the allow decision and wrote the expected bytes. |
| Same real client with cwd outside or in a whitespace-suffixed sibling | Permission denied; no outside target was created. |
| Same real client with a main-agent Bash grant and then a worker policy agent without that grant | Main-agent marker was produced; worker-policy marker was not created. |
| Same real client with selected-provider Write deny or minimal runtime policy session | Permission denied; no target was created. |
| Process-backed hook rewrite from an inside path to an outside path | Rejected after rewrite and before I/O; no outside target was created. |
| Differing execution/policy session keys with admitted `read-only` or `guarded` mode | Native Bash remained denied or approval-gated; the policy-key split did not erase the session restriction. |
| Anthropic `Grep` projected to canonical `read` | `read` allow admitted an in-workspace native `path`; `read` deny, an outside `path`, and a rewritten-outside `path` were rejected. |
| Actual Claude Code 2.1.289 through production stdio adapter and patched host permission handler; Write-allowed worker policy, distinct main/worker roots | Execution-root Write creates the exact 14-byte marker; direct policy-root and sibling-root Writes are denied with absent targets; every tool result returns to the local model. |
| Same actual client, hook rewrites the execution-root Write to the distinct worker root | Denied after rewrite; both original and rewritten targets remain absent (0 bytes). |
| Process-backed distinct-root fixture: main execution workspace, Write-allowed worker policy with its own different workspace and workspaceOnly | Admitted execution-root Write creates exactly 14 bytes; distinct policy-root and sibling-root targets are denied with zero writer launches and absent files. |
| Same fixture, hook rewrites execution-root Write to the distinct policy root | Revalidated after hook; denied with zero writer launches and both target files absent. |
| Earlier verified runtime tree: affected CLI-runner suites and Anthropic authority projection suite | 83/83 and 5/5 tests passed respectively; production code is unchanged by this proof-only update. |

The current-head real-client diagnostic recording is published at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160700#issuecomment-6000257746. The sink-level observations are the created/absent files and Bash markers from the real-client/process-backed paths plus the exact native permission responses asserted by the focused suites.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

Callers whose native tools are granted by the effective runtime policy retain access and continue through hooks and execution approval. Calls that relied on bypassing a restrictive profile, canonical capability mapping, admitted session permission mode, provider rule, runtime session/agent restriction, workspace boundary, exact request-cwd binding, policy-agent Bash grant, or post-hook rewrite validation now fail closed. This restores the documented policy boundary without changing public schemas or caller APIs.

## Boundary decisions requested from owners

1. **Agents owners:** confirm that plugin-owned native tools honor effective policy using the selected model provider and runtime policy session/agent identity, while admitted execution-session permission modes remain independently effective.
2. **Security owners:** confirm that native Read/Write/Edit and canonical-read provider tools remain inside the authorized workspace when resolved from the exact native request cwd before and after hook rewrites, and that native Bash standing grants resolve from the runtime policy agent.
3. **Agents and Security owners:** settle the existing mixed-agent workspace contract when execution and runtime policy agents have distinct workspace roots; this PR currently checks the admitted execution workspace under the policy agent's `workspaceOnly` setting.

4. **Agents and Security owners:** evaluate the attached real-client distinct-root diagnostics against your workspace decision. The installed Claude client now verifies the implemented execution-root allow and nearest out-of-root denials; evidence characterizes the implementation rather than granting owner acceptance.

## Testing

- Current-head actual Claude Code 2.1.289 diagnostic matrix: four distinct-root final effects passed through the production host/Anthropic adapter; 5.14 s Vitest / 9.56 s wall, maximum RSS 1,437,468 KB. Isolated HOME/config/state and synthetic local model; no paid inference.

- Added four distinct-root final-effect cases in `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-effect.integration.test.ts`. Focused suite: 10/10 passed, 5.75 s Vitest / 10.64 s wall; maximum RSS 1,516,120 KB. Focused type-aware lint and diff checks passed. These are isolated post-fix process-backed characterization tests.

- Prior runtime-tree verification: four affected CLI-runner suites — 83/83 passed; production code unchanged.
- Anthropic native authority projection suite — 5/5 passed, including `Grep` to `read`.
- Production core typecheck — passed.
- Prior runtime-tree verification: routed core-test type graphs — 26/26 passed.
- Focused type-aware lint and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Earlier real Claude Code 2.1.274 matrix through the production stdio adapter and permission handler — allowed and forbidden final effects passed.

Batch d348 consolidates repetitive test setup and assertions across Gateway, auto-reply, process, database-engine, UI, plugin, QA, release, Buzz, update, Feishu, and Discord suites. It retains boundary/lifecycle checks and removes documented duplicate probes. There is no production behavior or UI change.

All 30 requested commits were replayed in order onto pinned main `8d9e341071be27a1fbb1e77d84d5bce93f5924ba`. No whole commit was skipped. Conflicting rewrites were dropped conservatively as described below.

## Evidence

- Production LOC: +0 / -0.
- Test/support LOC: +5,458 / -8,746, net -3,288 across 104 files.
- Ratchet metadata: 3 obsolete rows removed from `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`; production unchanged (105 changed files overall).
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <changed files>`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <changed files>`: exited 0.
- `git diff --check 8d9e341071be27a1fbb1e77d84d5bce93f5924ba`: passed.
- Per the CI-only work order, no local Vitest, check-changed, typecheck, or Testbox execution. No test wall-time or coverage claim is made. Hosted `openclaw/ci-gate` selects and validates the changed files.
- Independent full-batch review completed; two findings accepted (restore steer authority and canonical checkpoint root), two rejected with source evidence below. The final focused correction review is scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- No changed path matches the current CODEOWNERS rules.

## Replay resolutions

For `63e838dbe585` and `7be8312c7ba6`, kept main's versions of `server-maintenance.delivery-queue.test.ts`, `server-methods.control-plane-rate-limit.test.ts`, `server-methods.placement-authorization.test.ts`, `server-methods.presence-activity.test.ts`, and `server-methods.stale-install.test.ts` under `src/gateway/`. These fixture/assertion rewrites overlapped newer main structure; follow-on changes depending on those rewrites were also dropped. Retained the clean channel-identity, startup-deadline, and upload-policy hunks.

For `4ab2ca8aef7d` and `efc52a21aadc`, kept `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-session-file.test-support.ts` deleted. Main retired it in `ffd5377099f7` (`refactor: keep private runtime composition with callers`). All other replay hunks applied cleanly.

## CI and review corrections

Initial CI found test-fixture errors in the name-command test (native command type and agentId expectation), Buzz active-directory self fixture, process optional-send-failure guard, and release fixture parameter inference. Corrected these directly from the failed logs. Restored the original Feishu batch-insert test instead of adding another client cast.

Restored Discord's explicit no-op thread-binding manager and teardown after its removal broke ACP binding lookup. Kept the Feishu malformed-URL redaction check exact while distinguishing whitespace normalization from invalid-URL reset. Bound the HTTP close method before promisifying it and removed a redundant string conversion flagged by type-aware CI lint.

Captured the relay close spy directly instead of reading an unbound method. Documented the existing isolated avatar download/logging and account-only SDK mock boundaries after the mock-export ratchet required explicit justification for the edited factories.

The second CI run passed the repaired tests/types/lint and then requested the exact three obsolete baseline rows for those now-documented factories be removed. Pruned only those rows, matching job 118976582828 in run 39524468096; no allowance was added or broadened.

Accepted review findings: restore the entire original steer fixture so the restricted command and active operation share authority; canonicalize the checkpoint root with realpathSync for macOS.
Rejected findings: the current transcript append API is generic in TMessage (src/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-runtime.ts), so the claimed discriminated-message type failure does not apply. The removed compensated adapter row follows the same DEFINITION_DENIAL branch and warning forwarding as retained start-refused (src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-command.ts); distinct native compensation remains covered by src/daemon/service-rebind.test.ts.

prs.title: feat(ui): add resizable panel frame and mobile navigation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Desktop and mobile panels need consistent navigation and resizing without changing the saved desktop layout or discarding active panel resources.

## User Impact

Adds the shared panel frame, dock controls, tab launcher, and mobile panel navigation. Mobile views retain their route and geometry when hidden, and closing the final tab returns to chat through both the tab button and native keyboard command. Desktop dividers remain available at intermediate widths. Browsing inside Files preserves the selected panel. New tab starts the requested panel, and position controls retain keyboard focus during background refreshes.

Expanded Dashboards retain their controls, the desktop Share control aligns with its neighbors, and same-session updates keep an open progress menu available. Terminal docking controls refresh when the shared queue changes, so opening another terminal does not leave Dock to right incorrectly disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps panel resources with their existing owners and mobile presentation state with the pane. Async closing verifies the initiating mobile session before completing; clearing Side chat reports success before its panel closes. Lazy opening waits for its registered host before mounting. Scroll fades follow the scrollable content's own surface color. Panel closure waits for hosted-tab updates before checking completion, preserving canceled-close and Close all sequencing.

The mobile toggle follows whether the panel is currently presented, so it can reopen retained panels and switch from Details to Panels.

Headers and Details use the upstream direct Solid components and a narrow open handle, retaining the existing desktop controls, mobile presentation, and panel actions.

## Risk and coverage

Shared panel navigation, asynchronous closing, and lazy mounting affect retained resources and focus across session changes.

The stale Dock to right state was traced to queue transitions notifying only one terminal host. Notifications now refresh every bound terminal panel; existing handoff and admission guards remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Panel lazy loading, layout, and mobile-host checks passed: 21 tests (3.13 s command wall).
- The integrated panel-layout, rail-column, and sidebar-contract suites passed all 20 scenarios.

- File previews, process actions, platform captions, progress submission, and question takeover have passing native evidence across scoped runs (64.13 s shared invocation; the corrected 390 px question case passed in a separate 15.14 s invocation). The checks retain real input and exact geometry assertions.

- Hosted-tab updates settle before close completion is checked, preserving cancellation and Close all sequencing. All 39 existing sidebar/hosted-tab tests passed (5.63 s Vitest duration); independent scoped review found no actionable findings.

- Updated mobile panel navigation passed the selected Desktop open/reopen and reload cases (`session-active-resources.e2e.test.ts`, `--maxWorkers=1`; 2 cases, 27.84 s). On the locally integrated UI, the mobile close/reopen/dismissal case passed again in 13.31 s. These scoped runs preserve native navigation and the retained resource checks.

- Local repair validation through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` passed the native navigation and header cases (9 cases; 47.18 s), the final Dashboard checks (3 selected cases; 24 s), both Details/progress files (8 cases; 27.95 s), and native plugin UI coverage (6 cases; 23.15 s file duration).
- The tests now enter through the active pane and native panel controls, start virtual-clock pauses after panel readiness, and exercise Hide after a same-session streaming update. Existing focus, retained-content, geometry, request, and saved-progress assertions remain. Relevant types, lint, formatting, controller checks, and scoped review passed.

- The shared test helper now uses the Layout menu for main-pane Restore while preserving native side-panel Expand/Restore. The original split-view and reconnect cases failed before this routing repair and passed afterward; the Dashboard iframe-retention sibling also passed (32.06 s combined command wall for split view and the sibling; 11.39 s for reconnect). Test bodies, assertions, and timeouts are unchanged. Both E2E type groups, lint, formatting, and scoped review passed.

- The current sidebar-layout checks passed all 22 cases, including tab ordering, main/side focus, retained selection, and layout restoration. They ran with 60 cron cases in one 82-test invocation (3.79 s command wall; no separate navigation timing). Selected UI type checks, scoped lint, formatting, and review passed.

- Expanded mobile Restore now uses the native control inside the active sheet, rather than a Layout trigger behind its backdrop. Four mobile, dashboard, and desktop cases passed (22.33 s command wall), preserving iframe, draft, focus, and geometry assertions.
- The collapsed-rail status test resumes its virtual clock before viewport and layout-settlement work. Its original timeout reproduced before the correction; all four status cases passed afterward (24.20 s command wall). Both repairs change tests/helpers only; applicable types, lint, formatting, and scoped reviews passed.

- Direct header/Details validation passed the focused unit case (4.49 s command wall) and 27 Chromium cases (12.62 s). Production UI and chat-test types, scoped lint, formatting, the controller guard, and review passed. The checks cover this panel/navigation implementation without importing later composition changes.

- The terminal docking failure reproduced before the notification correction. All six original docking cases passed afterward (35.38 s command wall); the unmodified upstream control also passed all six (34.48 s). Sixteen handoff/reconnect unit cases passed (3.61 s). Types, lint, formatting, the controller guard, and scoped review passed, with no new tests or relaxed assertions.

Validation ran on macOS using the repository-pinned Bun runtime; browser checks used Chromium. They do not establish a full-suite or hosted Linux CI pass.

CI timing for the updated tests is pending; the measured local costs above are scoped runs.

## Visual evidence

Captured before: `dccff201b07e`. Captured after: `5856f7237579`.

Synthetic fixtures and a mock Gateway show the integrated session UI at these revisions. These images are not isolated proof of this PR; stills do not establish interaction or live-service results.

Published comparisons: [Files and mobile conversation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176653#issuecomment-6265737997), [Additional session states](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176653#issuecomment-6265788224).

prs.title: test(ui): reuse the native settings layout context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native-embed settings matrix reloads the complete application for every route and returns through Settings after each layout inspection. Latest completed scheduled main [39515342342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39515342342) measures this file at 396.329 s, including 367.184 s for its six layout cases.

## What Changed

Reuse one booted browser context/page across the six viewport/color-scheme layout cases. Each case clears browser storage, restores system theme, updates viewport/media/native host form factor, and retires the previous page through a neutral route. Use the existing application navigation hook for route setup. Keep all198 route HTTP-200 checks as direct requests, all layout/content assertions, and all198 optional screenshots. Keep the dedicated navigation cases unchanged and retain the six Appearance reopen/Back cycles. The shared suite owns final context cleanup; renderer-stall and failed-case diagnostics remain installed.

The coordinator explicitly requested replacing incidental cold entries and Back round trips with direct setup for this layout-only matrix. A failed matrix case can cause later matrix cases to fail too; retain that visible failure instead of adding recovery/retry machinery. This does not alter product code or the navigation-specific tests.

## Evidence

Acceptance recorded before candidate CI: all12 exact case names pass, all existing assertion conditions remain; full-file native F wall improves at least20% against396.329s (cap317.0632s), and six-layout case sum improves at least20% against367.184s (cap293.7472s). No non-layout case may regress20% or more without matching newer-main evidence. Full14UI selection must pass. Report owning shard wall separately; do not add overlapping file times or claim modeled shard savings.

| Work / proof | Before | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Matrix contexts |6|1|
| Matrix document boots |198|1|
| Matrix Back clicks |198|12|
| Route HTTP200 checks |198|198|
| Cases |12|12|
| Assertion statements |22|23 (same21, equivalent HTTP check, plus palette readiness)|
| Optional matrix captures |198|198|
| File F wall |396.329s|34.927s (91.19% faster)|
| Six layout-case sum |367.184s|20.012s (94.55% faster)|
| Owning mock E2E shard |872 s / 99 files|553 s / 98 files; changed inventory, no attributable saving|
| Frozen install, UI types, scoped type-aware lint, format/diff, line-cap |—|Passed|
| Independent P0–P2 review |—|Scoped-clean, confidence0.84; no runtime/timing verdict|

The baseline root is byte-identical to base4576a162. Three transitive helper changes between measured main and base are documented in the retained comparison: diagnostic deduplication, type-only contract changes, and build-publication cleanup. Whole-harness source identity is not claimed. CI owns E2E execution; no local E2E, app build, parity run, or repeated suite was run under the campaign compute budget.

The unchanged fixture response fields move into the existing native fixture owner to satisfy the line cap. Production LOC and Solid refactor counts remain0; no startup imports, dependencies, tags, selectors, or screenshots change. Test/support LOC: 614→659 (+45). No Testbox/Crabbox lease.

Initial runtime candidate: run39524001093 at018641466f0387daa2dba34ea3dda0632a5cd60c (F31.003s/layout18.479s). All12 exact cases and all14UIjobs passed; all six non-layout cases improved. The run caught TS2322 in the new diagnostic catch boundary (unknown passed where Error is required). The follow-up head normalizes only that diagnostic argument, preserves the original rethrow and successful path, and passes the exact core-test-ui-e2e type configuration, lint, format, and independent P0–P2 review (confidence0.99). Corrected head f9d79138b7937f45f5513dfcbee01a6e30efedcb passed all12 exact cases, all14 UI jobs and the whole workflow in [39526168378](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39526168378). All six non-layout cases improved. The table uses this corrected head. Shard inventory changed from99 to98 files, so its319-second reduction is not causally attributed to this change. Merged as dad54c64cf2854fb660d7dfa02ba8182c95dd0ab.

prs.title: fix(cli): recover supported Node runtime when launched from filesystem root
prs.body:
Closes #177739

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw` is launched from `/` (the default working directory for launchd jobs and Linux system services) and the first `node` on PATH fails runtime admission, startup recovery should switch to a supported Node but instead rejects every candidate and exits 1. The fix lets recovery accept the same candidates from `/` as it does from any unrelated directory.

- Problem: launched from `/`, recovery rejects the managed Gateway service node, PATH nodes, and Homebrew nodes, so every run fails; if the job discards stderr the failure is silent.
- Solution: skip the workspace-owned exclusion when the canonical cwd is exactly POSIX `/`, since `/` contains every absolute path and cannot be an attacker-supplied checkout.
- What changed: `node-runtime-recovery.mjs` (`resolveRecoveryPath`) adds a `isPosixRoot` guard to the `excluded` predicate; `src/infra/node-runtime-recovery.test.ts` adds two POSIX-only regression tests (`it.skipIf(hostPlatform === "win32")`).
- What did NOT change: all non-root path protections (symlinked checkouts, workspace-owned parents, Windows task scripts, HOME trusted-root logic) remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cwd exclusion prevents a workspace checkout from supplying a malicious `node`; with cwd `/`, `path.relative("/", candidate)` places every absolute POSIX path inside `/`, so the guard rejects every candidate. POSIX `/` is the filesystem root and the standard launchd/systemd service start directory, not a checkout, so exempting it preserves the security invariant without weakening any real protection.

- Best fix: a single canonical-root exception at the existing exclusion site, the narrowest correction to the shared resolver.
- Alternative: exempt HOME, Windows drive roots, or UNC roots — rejected as broadening the trust policy unnecessarily.
- Risk / non-goals: Windows drive roots are intentionally not exempted; the POSIX-only regression tests are skipped on win32.

## User Impact

LaunchAgents and Linux system services that call `openclaw` through a PATH shim now recover to a supported Node instead of failing with exit 1. Behavior from `/tmp` and `$HOME` is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real launcher proof against head `048db1c` — launching `openclaw.mjs` (imports `./node-runtime-recovery.mjs` with `isPosixRoot` guard) under real Node 22.21.0 (fails admission: Node <24.16). Recovery probes **real** executables and respawns with **real** Node 24.19.0. No mocked probe/respawn.

### Raw terminal output (inline, head 048db1c7712a)

```
head sha: 048db1c7712a28bd565d2b987b607796e3b7151e
isPosixRoot guard in node-runtime-recovery.mjs: 2 match(es) (0=no fix, >0=fix present)
openclaw.mjs import: 24:} from "./node-runtime-recovery.mjs";
launcher: .../openclaw-wt-177739/openclaw.mjs (imports ./node-runtime-recovery.mjs with isPosixRoot guard)
launching node: .../v22.21.0/bin/node (fails admission: Node <24.16)
recovery node: .../v24.19.0/bin/node (admitted: >=24.16 + SQLite 3.53.3)
isolated HOME: /tmp/proof-home-XXX (never touches production)

--- Case 1: cwd=/ (fix) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (managed Gateway service; ...)
  discovery source: managed Gateway service (via isPosixRoot guard, not PATH allowCwd)
  stdout: OpenClaw 1.10.0 (eced509)   exit: 0   recovered: YES

--- Case 2: cwd=/tmp (control) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (PATH; ...)
  stdout: OpenClaw 1.10.0 (eced509)   exit: 0   recovered: YES — PATH (unchanged)

--- Case 3: cwd=<workspace> direct (sentinel) ---
  forbidden candidate: /tmp/proof-sentinel-XXX/node (sentinel 'node' inside workspace, discovery source: managed Gateway service)
  exit: 0   sentinel marker created? NO (rejected before probe AND replacement I/O)

--- Case 4: cwd=<workspace> intermediate-symlink (sentinel) ---
  forbidden candidate: /tmp/proof-safe-XXX/bin/node (parent symlink→workspace, discovery source: managed Gateway service)
  exit: 0   sentinel marker created? NO (rejected before probe AND replacement I/O)

--- Case 5: fresh-install startup from / (settings intact) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (managed Gateway service; ...)
  stdout: OpenClaw 1.10.0 (eced509)   exit: 0   recovered: YES   command ran: YES

--- Case 6: upgrade startup from / (existing settings intact) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (managed Gateway service; ...)
  stdout: 18789   exit: 0   recovered: YES   settings preserved: YES

--- Case 7: official v2026.10.5→head(048db1c) upgrade from / ---
  v2026.10.5: official npm openclaw@2026.10.5 (no isPosixRoot guard)
  head: .../openclaw-wt-177739/openclaw.mjs (048db1c7712a, isPosixRoot guard present)
  [before] v2026.10.5 from / under v22: exit=0 recovery=YES settings written (port 18789): YES
  [after]  head from / under v22:   exit=0 recovery=YES (managed Gateway service) settings preserved (port 18789): YES

=== VERDICT (head 048db1c7712a) ===
  cwd=/            recovered=true exit=0 => PASS
  cwd=/tmp         recovered=true exit=0 => PASS
  cwd=<ws> direct  sentinelNotSpawned=true exit=0 => PASS
  cwd=<ws> symlink sentinelNotSpawned=true exit=0 => PASS
  fresh-install   recovered=true cmdRan=true exit=0 => PASS
  upgrade startup recovered=true settingsPreserved=true exit=0 => PASS
  v2026.10.5→head  v2026.10.5SettingsWritten=true headRecovered=true settingsPreserved=true exit=0 => PASS
  ALL PASS — real probe/respawn + executable-sentinel rejection + v2026.10.5→head upgrade from /
```

Cases 3-4: forbidden workspace candidate is a sentinel `node` writing a marker if spawned by probe or respawn; marker absence proves rejection before both probe and replacement I/O. Case 7: official v2026.10.5 (npm, no `isPosixRoot`) writes settings from `/`; head (048db1c) reads them back (port 18789). Isolated temp HOME; no production files touched.

Regression tests in `src/infra/node-runtime-recovery.test.ts` (POSIX-only, skipped on win32). Before the fix both fail with `recovery did not spawn a replacement`; after the fix both pass (2 passed 62 skipped | 64 passed).

The narrow existing client helper owns failed acquisition; suite cleanup stops the client before the Gateway/state owner. The deliberate offline case stops its readback client before stopping the Gateway.

The discarded child-exit check becomes the managed acquisition/request failure contract: failed hello or RPC rejects the test. All 46 remaining assertion statements are unchanged after normalizing the readback variable. This continues to observe the real Gateway independently of the browser; it does not substitute browser state or direct database reads. prs.title: fix(telegram): retain peer progress and visible requester follow-up
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can lose its progress card and final follow-up after an agent delegates work to a peer. A new message from the same owner can also suppress an already accepted result. Retained cards can freeze the original checklist and accumulate obsolete running rows when the requester resumes and delegates again.

## User Impact

Pending peer work keeps one automatic card through requester processing and receives a visible final reply in the original conversation. The card follows the requester's updated plan, including checklist removal. Closed follow-up owners remove their own rows; explicit failures remain visible. Meaningful acknowledgments and Telegram streaming preferences are preserved. Private child and peer plans remain excluded.

A new channel message retires the old turn's automation entitlement without cancelling a still-valid original result. The return remains bound to its original caller, conversation and session incarnation; it never borrows the new turn's owner privileges. Private completions remain private. Stop/reset and revoked completion-source authority still prevent delivery.

```text
delegate → retain card → receive peer result → requester processes → final reply
new user message → retire old automation authority; retain valid pending result
stop/reset → close that requester's follow-up
```

Progress remains process-local and is not restored after a Gateway restart. Stop/reset retires the requester's follow-up without cancelling unrelated peer work. This PR does not close the broader durable completion contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing completion owner, requester authority, native delivery and confirmed draft handoff. Ordinary and queued requester turns share that owner. Telegram waits for the first card receipt before adoption and uses its existing compositor queue for plan updates. The new-message repair separates retired automation scope from still-current completion custody, following the distinction already used by native requester continuations. No new job store, polling loop, configuration or permission model is introduced.

The compatible public contract follows the [review recommendation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6190834951): existing `adoptProgressDraft` keeps waiting-only replacement semantics; separate `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` opts adapters into retaining a card alongside an ordinary reply. Telegram and Discord implement both. Old adapters continue normal meaningful-reply delivery. Retained drafts may implement optional `updatePlan`; Telegram does so.

**Human decisions remain:** the channel SDK area owner must accept these additive contracts, and an eligible maintainer must approve security-sensitive changes on the resulting head. Automated proof/review acceptance is not either approval. No human reviewer is assigned.

## Evidence

**Current conflict repair, `1b0948380dc06dbad8dc2d2c6e74619471fa296e`:** integrated pinned main `1989e3dc4360a17d039440a886f71e582758a487` after GitHub reported a real conflict. The only manual resolution is `attempt-tool-run-context.test.ts`: main's simplified top-level tests retain the existing host reply-obligation case unchanged. The automatically merged Gateway execution-owner helper retains the requester store path on the completion request, and the database-worker test inventory retains both upstream additions and the peer-progress test.

All 46 authored files without upstream overlap, including product logic, are byte-identical to `e71f5917576c8fde1a120e2d2683c6b6dd6c9921`. The resolved test file is 12 lines smaller than the previous head. No new product behavior was added. Prior behavioral review is reused for this mechanical integration.

**Current local proof:** all 40 focused cases pass: embedded tool-run context (5) and Gateway execution ownership, including follow-up cleanup (35). The two canonical type graphs `core.test.agents-other` and `core.test.gateway-other`, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and the authored diff check pass. The test invocation completed in 72.75 seconds, including cold compilation; the two shards reported 44.30 and 22.23 seconds. No broad functional suite, hosted rerun or new review request was repeated.

**Current hosted proof:** [CI run 39525076298](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39525076298) completed successfully for `1b0948380dc06dbad8dc2d2c6e74619471fa296e`. [Production types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39525076298/job/118978546516), [test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39525076298/job/118978546486), lint, all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs and the [aggregate CI check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39525076298/job/118985601978) passed. Workflow elapsed time was 25 minutes 9 seconds, including planning and queue time; no technical checks remain pending. GitHub confirms this head is mergeable. The separately published `openclaw/ci-gate` and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` commit statuses remain red because a maintainer must approve the current revision. Successful technical CI does not grant that approval.

**Previous-head proof:** [CI run 39483256453](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39483256453) completed successfully for `e71f5917576c8fde1a120e2d2683c6b6dd6c9921`, including production/test types, lint, all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs and the aggregate CI check. Its 144 focused local cases and prior review remain valid evidence for unchanged inputs, not completed CI for the new head. The earlier 809-diagnostic production-type regression was resolved by merged [PR178306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178306), already included in this branch; it requires no exception or environment widening.

**Next decisions:** an eligible OpenClaw maintainer must review and approve security-sensitive head `1b0948380dc06dbad8dc2d2c6e74619471fa296e`; the channel SDK area owner must accept `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` and optional `updatePlan`. No human review, review thread, assigned reviewer or new author change request is present after the completed CI run. The [security notice](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6189760779) requires approval of the current head. The two red commit statuses on this head require that human security approval, despite the successful technical CI run. The author owns concrete new code/test requirements. No approval is granted or gate waived by this evidence.

- **New-message regression, `034680452581a1fc1259c75579a72ed8b46a1905`:** real channel ingress → real `sessions_send` and Gateway command admission → accepted executing peer → another message from the same owner → one final in the original Telegram topic. The returning run has no retired/new-owner automation capability, and a duplicate return is rejected. A second case performs real `sessions.reset` and verifies zero return/delivery. The test fails against parent `0a0aa9b010d3737dce0331c6fbfefa9e242b495e` with `Requester followup authority is no longer current` and passes with the repair. Inference and external Telegram transport are fixtures; custody, revocation, admission and delivery decisions are real. The test starts beyond recipient preflight; that separate lifetime defect belongs to #177296. This is isolated boundary proof, not new live Telegram evidence.
- **Focused checks on `034680`:** 54 cases across five files pass: the channel flow, private/peer owner continuation, retained access/reset custody, native requester authority and final-effect cancellation. After simplifying the new test to read the existing completion registry, its two cases pass again. Production `tsconfig.core.json`, canonical `tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The changed-path type selector encountered existing root-budget violations in the unrelated `gateway-root` and `plugins-platform` partitions (725 roots versus 720); its broad fallback was stopped. Those limits were not changed or waived; the directly selected Gateway graph passed.
- **Review and size of `034680`:** bounded P0 autoreview of the incremental repair found no actionable findings. Final test cleanup removes the pass-through observer and uses the existing registry query, with typing fixes at the fixture boundary. The repair changes production by +13/-1 lines, tests by +257/-10 and documentation by +7. It reuses the existing completion/authority owners and adds no scheduling machinery. The earlier hosted-check result is reconciled above; its inherited failures are not marked passed.
- **Earlier scoped runtime evidence:** [queued Telegram entry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6213856433) exercises native queue admission, real `sessions_send`, a visible peer obligation and automatic final HTTP delivery with synthetic ingress/model/endpoint. [Final-effect authority proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6191888084) performs one plugin write for the allowed owner and zero after revocation/reassignment. [Real Telegram outbound](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6191325792) shows one card, two edits, one final and deletion with synthetic ingress/model. [960-second work](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6189849766) uses local transport/model fixtures without model calls while waiting. These retain their original heads and scope.


No production installation, distribution build, restart, upgrade or additional monitor was performed for this repair. Installation remains a separate release-owner action.

Related: #148294, #148296 and broader end-to-end work #148298. This reuses merged #166101/#167362 progress continuation and #162227's single delayed peer reply. #112388/#112372 address a distinct durable-completion proposal. Merged #173873 restores interrupted-child requester authority, not progress-card restoration.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Review needs readable desktop and mobile diff layouts without losing file context, disclosure state, or the identity of the checkout being reviewed.

## User Impact

Adds desktop file navigation and view controls, mobile diff cards and Sync details, and separate controls for line wrapping, word changes, and split view. Refreshing retains compatible file presentation while stale diff and file-text responses remain excluded. Menus stay anchored to their trigger when the containing sheet moves.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps loading, request generations, caches, and gap expansion with the existing diff owner. Presentation modules share its live data and operations. Workspace consumers reuse the same uncommitted-diff request and result. Search focus and navigation scrolling follow settled DOM updates.

The Review panel and its menus render as direct Solid components, preserving the existing layout, disclosures, and menu behavior. Retired native adapters are removed.

## Risk and coverage

This changes shared diff rendering and loading as well as presentation. Stale diff and file-text responses must remain excluded.

The recorded unavailable-desktop-target timeout reproduced in isolated validation. A controlled lazy-publication delay subsequently reproduced a lost request, which the shared panel-readiness correction addresses. The original status-retry failure was not independently reproduced. The welcome-avatar case passed in isolation with matching main sources, but its original failed-shard timing remains unattributed; no avatar patch is included. The separate quota saved-clear status failure was reproduced on main.

- Review focus and scrolling follow settled DOM updates. The focused run passed 25 unit and four Chromium cases (4.20 s wall), including the Search-focus regression; removing settlement loses the expected focus.

- Direct Solid panel validation passed all 25 unit cases (3.33 s command wall) and four Chromium cases (3.13 s). The rendered panel and existing expectations are preserved. UI and chat-test types, scoped lint, formatting, and review passed. This validates the focused panel candidate on macOS with pinned Bun, not a full-suite or hosted Linux CI result.

prs.title: fix(doctor): warnings check the wrong model when the primary model is an alias
prs.body:
Related: #177340 (the same fix for `openclaw sessions`)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor` checks the wrong model when the configured primary model is an alias, so it prints warnings that do not apply and can miss ones that do.

## User Impact

User impact: with an alias primary such as `gem` (an alias of `google/gemini-2.5-pro`), Doctor now checks the model the alias points to, as the runtime does. Before, it checked `openai/gem`, and:

- warned that the runtime tool schema inspection could not prepare the model (`Unknown model: openai/gem`);
- applied `tools.byProvider` rules for the wrong provider in its message tool, MCP and tool profile warnings. In the run below, an `openai` rule produced a false "message tool is unavailable" warning;
- reported a cron job pinned to `google/gemini-2.5-pro` as using "a different model than `agents.defaults.model` (gem)".

Agent-scoped aliases (`agents.entries.<id>.models`) are resolved for that agent. Provider-qualified primaries resolve as before. A bare or missing primary now resolves to the same provider and model the runtime picks. Doctor still only reads; nothing is rewritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor had its own primary-model parser, `resolveDoctorPrimaryModelRef`. It split the string on `/`, fell back to `openai` for anything without a provider, and never looked at model aliases. This removes it. Its four callers now use the shared `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` with the agent id, which is the resolver the runtime uses. They keep Doctor's existing `allowPluginNormalization: false`. #177340 made the same change for session listings.

The Cron note now resolves aliases on both sides of its comparison through the shared alias index, as the cron runner does. It still compares against `agents.defaults.model`, and the provider namespace counts are unchanged.

One side effect: take a bare primary with no provider and no alias (`gpt-5.5`). The shared resolver's existing "specified without provider" advisory already prints 16 times in one Doctor run on main. With this change it prints 20 times. The rest of the output is identical.

## Evidence

The CLI ran from source on Linux (Node 24) as `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts`, the `openclaw` entry, with `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` isolated and no credentials set. Setup:

```
$ openclaw models aliases add gem google/gemini-2.5-pro
Alias gem -> google/gemini-2.5-pro
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.model.primary gem
Updated agents.defaults.model.primary. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
$ openclaw config set --batch-file policy-batch.json
Updated 3 config paths. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
```

`policy-batch.json` sets `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, `tools.profile: "coding"` and `tools.byProvider.openai.allow: ["read"]`. One cron job is also needed: `daily-brief` with `payload.model: "google/gemini-2.5-pro"`. `openclaw cron add` needs a running Gateway, so the job was written with the production cron store writer (`saveCronStore`). Every Doctor run started from a copy of the same state. The upgrade run below creates the job with `openclaw cron add` instead.

Before: upstream/main `5c13abb9ef7`, `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`, exit 0. The relevant notes:

```
◇  Doctor warnings
│  - messages.visibleReplies is set to "message_tool", but the message
│    tool is unavailable for agent "main"; OpenClaw falls back to
│    automatic visible replies, so normal replies may post to the source
│    chat. Enable the message tool or set messages.visibleReplies to
│    "automatic".
◇  Cron
│  Automation model overrides detected.
│  - 1 job set `payload.model` and will not inherit
│    `agents.defaults.model` (gem)
│  - Provider namespaces: google=1
│  - 1 job uses a different model than `agents.defaults.model` (gem)
│  - Examples: daily-brief -> google/gemini-2.5-pro
◇  Doctor warnings
│  - Agent main runtime tool schema inspection could not prepare its
│    selected model context.
│    path: agents.main.model
│    issue: Unknown model: openai/gem. Run `openclaw models list
│    --refresh --provider openai` to inspect this provider's model
│    choices, then retry with a model supported by your account.
```

After: this branch `44e97fc893e`, same state and command, exit 0. Both "Doctor warnings" notes above are gone, and the Cron note reads:

```
◇  Cron
│  Automation model overrides detected.
│  - 1 job set `payload.model` and will not inherit
│    `agents.defaults.model` (gem)
│  - Provider namespaces: google=1
│  Review with openclaw automations list and openclaw automations show
│  <job-id>; remove `payload.model` from jobs that should inherit the
│  default.
```

A full diff of the two Doctor outputs shows those removals and two other changes: a `memory-core` row in Plugin compatibility and two plugin-SDK deprecation notices. Both appear because the tool schema inspection now runs on the agent's real model.

Control: main with the plain primary `google/gemini-2.5-pro` and this change with the alias `gem` produce identical Doctor output apart from the `(google/gemini-2.5-pro)` / `(gem)` label.

Focused tests, red on main and green here:

- `src/commands/doctor/cron/warnings.test.ts`: an alias default with a job pinned to the alias target, and the reverse, report no mismatch. A job pinned to another model is still reported.
- `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-frames.test.ts`: standalone Doctor frames use the default alias and an agent-scoped alias.
- `src/commands/doctor/shared/preview-warnings.test.ts`: the provider message policy and inherited provider profile warnings follow an agent-scoped alias. They do not fire when the alias points to another provider.
- `src/commands/doctor/shared/plugin-tool-allowlist-warnings.test.ts`: the provider MCP policy follows an agent-scoped alias.

On main, the 6 new bite cases fail and the 4 new guard cases pass. On this branch all of them pass, and so do the rest of the four touched test files, cron index and preview-warnings scan notes.

These checks also pass: `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt, the assertion-safety ratchet (the removed cast's baseline entry is dropped), the mock-export and line-cap ratchets, and both import-cycle checks.

### Upgrade from latest stable (2026.10.5)

This run puts the source candidate (`44e97fc893e`, the same `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts` entry as above) on a state dir that the npm-installed stable CLI created. It is not the Docker `published-upgrade-survivor` lane, because that lane needs a built candidate tarball. It follows that lane's post-update steps by hand: `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, then `config validate`. All commands share one isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, with no credentials set.

Stable setup, all with `openclaw` 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`) from `npm install openclaw@2026.10.5`:

```
$ openclaw models aliases add gem google/gemini-2.5-pro
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.model.primary gem
$ openclaw config set --batch-file policy-batch.json
$ openclaw config set gateway.mode local
$ openclaw config set gateway.port 28789
$ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port 28789     # background, stopped after cron list
$ openclaw cron add --name "Daily brief" --cron "0 8 * * *" --tz UTC --session isolated \
    --message "Morning brief" --model google/gemini-2.5-pro --no-deliver
$ openclaw cron list
c0cb4fba-a191-4890-b38b-fb378f285df2 - Daily brief cron 0 8 * * * @ UTC (exact) ... isolated ... google/gemini-2.5...
$ openclaw doctor --non-interactive                     # exit 0
```

Stable Doctor prints all three false warnings (trimmed):

```
│  - messages.visibleReplies is set to "message_tool", but the message
│    tool is unavailable for agent "main"; OpenClaw falls back to
│  - 1 job uses a different model than `agents.defaults.model` (gem)
│  - Examples: c0cb4fba-a191-4890-b38b-fb378f285df2 ->
│    google/gemini-2.5-pro
│    issue: Unknown model: openai/gem. Run `openclaw models list
```

Candidate, same state dir:

```
$ openclaw doctor --non-interactive                     # exit 1
- Failed migrating shared state database schema at <state>/openclaw.sqlite: Error: Client credentials
  require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix.
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive               # exit 0: SQLite backup, then schema v20 -> v29
$ openclaw config validate                              # Config valid
$ openclaw doctor --non-interactive                     # exit 0
```

The first run stops at main's state migration (`src/infra/client-credential-migration.ts`), because stable's Gateway pairing left a device credential to migrate. This PR does not touch that code. The two candidate Doctor runs after it print none of the three warnings, and the Cron note reads:

```
│  Automation model overrides detected.
│  - 1 job set `payload.model` and will not inherit
│    `agents.defaults.model` (gem)
│  - Provider namespaces: google=1
│  Review with openclaw automations list and openclaw automations show
```

Control: base `5c13abb9ef7`, run on a copy of the post-`--fix` state from an identical earlier run of these steps, prints all three again. The migration does not remove them; this change does.

Alias config and cron data after the upgrade:

File previews need usable reading controls without losing edits, selection, or file identity when users switch views.

## Risk and coverage

prs.title: fix(memory): restore memory search on multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
Closes #178771
Related: #93199

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `memory_search` failures on multi-agent gateways when the request has
`runSessionKey=global` but already carries the valid scoped key
`agentSessionKey=agent:<agent>:<session>`.

## User Impact

Authorized non-default agents retain working memory retrieval without changing
existing agent-scoped visibility restrictions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The execution owner is now resolved once at the shared outer tool-construction
boundary, before either synchronous or asynchronous preparation, and the
prepared result is propagated to downstream consumers.

- `runSessionKey=global` with a valid scoped `agentSessionKey` preserves the
  known scoped owner.
- A valid scoped `runSessionKey` remains authoritative, preserving the nested
  session behavior introduced by PR #126221.
- Explicit execution-agent overrides remain subject to the existing resolver
  validation.
- Two different scoped keys can represent legitimate delegation; execution
  ownership remains distinct from requester/policy identity.
- Malformed or genuinely unresolved ownership fails closed.

The relevant implementation is in [`resolveOpenClawToolSession`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4d0de576c6fd3b9f029c2563828f65f1a41ac6a3/src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.ts#L66-L98), outer preparation in [`prepareOpenClawTools`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4d0de576c6fd3b9f029c2563828f65f1a41ac6a3/src/agents/openclaw-tools.preparation.ts#L25-L40), and synchronous/async propagation in [`openclaw-tools.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4d0de576c6fd3b9f029c2563828f65f1a41ac6a3/src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts#L159-L224).

Memory visibility continues to use strict owner resolution with the trusted
scoped owner as fallback. Conflicting or ambiguous aliases are excluded rather
than assigned to the requester.

## Evidence

### Construction-path reproduction

The unmodified baseline reproduced the original failure for:

```text
runSessionKey=global
agentSessionKey=agent:research:dashboard:control
```

The baseline raised:

```text
Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner.
```

At the published head, the synchronous regression uses the real
`createOpenClawTools` factory, returns a non-empty tool array, executes
`sessions_search`, and verifies that the constructed request carries
`agentId: research`:

[`openclaw-tools.session-context.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4d0de576c6fd3b9f029c2563828f65f1a41ac6a3/src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-context.test.ts#L236-L275)

The corresponding asynchronous construction path also resolves successfully.

Sanitized test output:

```text
Baseline: AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured...
Patched:  Test Files  5 passed (5)
          Tests       55 passed (55)
Patched:  Test Files  3 passed (3)
          Tests       32 passed (32)
```

### Authorization and visibility evidence

- Authorized real-manager retrieval returned visible results and recorded the
  expected provider query.
- Foreign-agent session hits were withheld by the visibility filter.
- Conflicting persisted ownership for a shared/bare alias was rejected.
- Missing requester ownership fails closed.
- Real-manager visibility coverage reported `candidateHits: 4`, `hits: 2`,
  and `withheldHits: 2` for synthetic cross-agent fixtures.

The relevant regression coverage is in [`session-search-visibility.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4d0de576c6fd3b9f029c2563828f65f1a41ac6a3/extensions/memory-core/src/session-search-visibility.test.ts), [`session-search-visibility.cross-agent.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4d0de576c6fd3b9f029c2563828f65f1a41ac6a3/extensions/memory-core/src/session-search-visibility.cross-agent.test.ts), and [`tools.real-manager.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4d0de576c6fd3b9f029c2563828f65f1a41ac6a3/extensions/memory-core/src/tools.real-manager.test.ts#L330-L372).

### Checks

- Construction, delegation, and authorization tests: **55/55**.
- Memory visibility tests: **32/32**.
- Real-manager Memory Core coverage: **44/44**. This suite was last run
  immediately before the final type-only propagation change; no Memory Core
  production or test files changed in that change.
- Earlier focused validation: **69/69**.
- Core TypeScript checking: passed.
- Targeted formatting: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Fresh Ollama embedding health was not established, and the second agent's live
session did not expose the same memory tool surface. These tests do not claim
that every denied request performs zero provider I/O. No cross-agent memory
leak is claimed; the evidence confirms preservation of the existing ownership
and visibility restrictions through the tested paths.

Full extension-wide typechecking and linting were not run in the bounded
filtered checkout because of unrelated dependency and host limitations.
