prs.title: feat(cli): show plugin trust status in plugins list output
prs.body:
Closes #178411

## What Problem This Solves

Installing a third-party plugin grants it access to tools, hooks, channels and providers inside the gateway, so whether a plugin is officially trusted or not is a security-relevant signal. But `openclaw plugins list` never showed trust status in either the table or verbose output — a user scanning their plugin list could not tell official/trusted plugins from third-party ones without running `openclaw plugins inspect <id>` on each one individually.

## Why This Change Was Made

`PluginRecord.trust` (with a `reason`) is already recorded and canonical, but the list renderer omitted it. This adds a compact trust label to `openclaw plugins list`: a `Trust` column in the table and a `trust:` line in verbose output, both derived from `plugin.trust.reason`. This follows the project's existing `skills search` convention of showing a trust label in list output. Rendering-only change; trust evaluation and install policy are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users reviewing their installed plugins can now see at a glance whether each plugin is `bundled`, `trusted-official`, or untrusted (`provenance-missing`, `install-path-mismatch`, etc.) directly in `openclaw plugins list` — no need to inspect each plugin individually.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI run from an isolated state directory with a bundled plugin (`amazon-bedrock`) and a third-party config-sourced plugin (`community-tool`, no install record):

Table output (default view, `FORCE_COLOR=1`):

```
│ Name              │ ID                 │ Format   │ Status  │ Source                   │ Version   │ Trust          │
│ Community Tool    │ community-tool     │ openclaw │ enabled │ /tmp/…/community-tool/.. │ 0.4.1     │ record-missing │
│ Amazon Bedrock    │ amazon-bedrock     │ openclaw │ enabled │ …/amazon-bedrock/index.. │ 2026.10.5 │ bundled        │
```

Verbose output (`--verbose`, `FORCE_COLOR=1`):

```
Community Tool (community-tool) enabled
  format: openclaw
  source: /tmp/oc-proof-178483/plugins/community-tool/index.ts
  origin: config
  version: 0.4.1
  trust: record-missing          ← yellow (theme.warn)

Amazon Bedrock (amazon-bedrock) enabled
  format: openclaw
  source: …/amazon-bedrock/index.ts
  origin: bundled
  version: 2026.10.5
  trust: bundled                 ← green (theme.success)
  providers: amazon-bedrock
```

Trust label coloring follows `formatPluginTrustLabel`: `bundled` and `trusted-official` route through `theme.success` (green `\x1b[32m`); all other reasons route through `theme.warn` (yellow `\x1b[33m`). When no trust record exists the cell/line is omitted.

Reproduction:

```
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-proof-178483 node openclaw.mjs plugins list
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-proof-178483 node openclaw.mjs plugins list --verbose
```

Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-list-format.test.ts src/cli/plugins-list-command.test.ts` — 15 passed (10 format + 5 command). The format suite verifies each trust reason renders in verbose output and that trusted vs untrusted styling emit distinct ANSI sequences under forced color; the command suite verifies the table includes a `Trust` column with the recorded reasons.

Regression proof (red-on-base → green-on-fix): removing the `Trust` column from `plugins-list-command.ts` causes the table test to fail — `expected '┌───┬───┐' to contain 'trusted-official'` (column header and values absent from real rendered output). Restoring the column passes. The table test uses the real `renderTable` (only `getTerminalTableWidth` is stubbed to 120), covering column layout, width, and wrapping behavior.

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178809

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram offset checkpoints failing with `Telegram runtime not initialized` when ingress Worker callbacks run under stock Bun.

## User Impact

Telegram's ingress callbacks and their asynchronous offset writes retain the plugin instance that created the Worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind parent-side Worker message forwarding to its construction-time async scope. The existing assigned handler still receives each message, and runtime lookup stays with the exact plugin instance. The change adds no state or configuration and leaves the existing acknowledgment, retry, and shutdown owners in place.

## Evidence

- The new native Worker regression failed on current-main production source `9d6eda36107828acc55278351f5cee53f8dc6e3a` under supported stock Bun 1.4.3 with the reported runtime error at the real offset writer. It passes with this repair.
- Two same-ID plugin instances construct separate native Workers. An unrelated third instance assigns their callbacks. Immediate and deferred offset writes reach the matching instance's recording store, with no cross-instance writes. Only the network-facing sidecar and keyed-store I/O are fixtures; the Worker, adapter, plugin instances, runtime lookup, and offset writer are real.
- All 48 tests across the affected Worker, polling-session, offset-retry, and offset-store suites passed on Node 24.22.0. Wrapper time: 81.28 seconds across two configurations.
- The regression and three existing Worker lifecycle cases passed on stock Bun 1.4.3 and the repository-pinned OpenClaw Bun fork, revision `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`. Wrapper times: 10.73 and 12.13 seconds respectively. The new native regression itself takes tens of milliseconds; most wrapper time is source preparation.
- Targeted test TypeScript, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent P0-P2 review found no actionable findings. The final native regression was replayed after fixture type/lint corrections on stock Bun, the pinned fork, and Node, passing in 33, 30, and 63 milliseconds of test time. Wrapper times were 39.38 seconds with cold compilation, then 11.07 and 12.93 seconds with reused compilation.

Live Telegram Test Server ingress and restart replay remain unverified: the maintained doctor found no available authenticated Convex launcher, and no login or installation was attempted. This regression demonstrates runtime context and successful recording-store writes, not production SQLite durability or live channel recovery. No operator Gateway or real bot was changed.

The production change adds 8 lines and removes 3. One native regression plus its small Worker fixture protects the construction-owner boundary without adding production test hooks.

prs.title: fix(clawrouter): preserve native image input capabilities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes image requests being rejected as text-only when ClawRouter discovers known native Sol, Astra, or GPT-4.1 models without explicit input metadata.

## User Impact

Users can select these known image-capable models for image understanding through ClawRouter. Explicit text-only catalog declarations still win, and malformed declarations or unknown models do not receive new image capability. No configuration or credential changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawRouter discarded declared input metadata and relied on older model-family inference. Preserve bounded valid declarations and, only when absent, recognize six exact known native OpenAI upstream IDs. Routing, IDs, scoped discovery/cache/auth, reasoning and limits remain unchanged. This branch does not change plugin index registration or depend on the separate speech parity change.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve literal download and trace output paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser download and trace output paths silently lose surrounding whitespace when `.trim()` is applied across the CLI, route, capture, and file-writer layers. A path like `" report.pdf "` is shortened to `report.pdf`, writing to the wrong file. The route containment gate (`pathScope().writable()`) trims its requestedPath input, validating the trimmed neighbor rather than the literal destination — if `report.pdf` is a directory or symlink, the route returns 400 even though ` report.pdf ` is a safe ordinary filename (GHSA-XWJM-J929-XQ7C containment gate).

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaces `.trim()` with `readNonBlankString` (preserves whitespace, rejects blank) at all nine trim points in the browser output path flow, including the node transfer consumer (`collectBrowserProxyPaths`). The route containment gate stops passing the literal path into `pathScope().writable()`'s trimming input branch and instead routes it through the shared fs-safe empty-request branch as `defaultName`, which is never trimmed: `pathScope(root, { label }).writable("", { defaultName: literalPath })`. This preserves the operator's exact spelling while reusing the shared canonical-parent containment, regular-file requirement, and Windows namespace-alias rejection — the same admission the downstream `writeExternalFileWithinRoot` writer uses, so the gate and the writer agree on the same destination. `"~/name"` stays a literal scoped filename (never expanded to home).

## User Impact

`openclaw browser download`, `openclaw browser waitfordownload`, and `openclaw browser trace stop` preserve the exact output path supplied by the operator. Whitespace-only paths still fail. Paths with no surrounding whitespace are unaffected. The output root, existing non-regular destinations, and symlink escapes are rejected before Playwright dispatch, and Windows namespace-alias rejection is retained by the shared admission. When a browser node transfers files, the literal path is preserved through `collectBrowserProxyPaths` → `readBrowserProxyFiles` so the saved file is read, not the trimmed neighbor.

## Evidence

Product head: `7485357d8039`.

Route regression in `server.agent-contract-core.test.ts` (6 tests): output root rejected, existing child-directory target rejected, `"~/report.pdf"` treated as a literal scoped filename, parent symlink escaping the canonical root rejected, existing regular-file overwrite accepted, and an existing FIFO destination rejected. Writer regression in `output-files.test.ts` writes to `" report.pdf "` and verifies the literal file receives the bytes. Node-transfer regression in `invoke-browser.test.ts` creates `" report.pdf "` and verifies `collectBrowserProxyPaths` reads the literal file, not the trimmed neighbor.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/output-files.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 82 passed (3 files)
```

Real patched CLI + real Playwright chromium (isolated dev Gateway, loopback HTTP server, `browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork=true` for the harness):

```text
$ openclaw browser download e2 " report.pdf "
downloaded: /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf        # literal trailing space preserved
$ ls -la "/tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf "        # literal file exists, content correct
-rw-rw-r-- ... /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf
$ ls "/tmp/openclaw/downloads/report.pdf"              # trimmed neighbor absent
ls: cannot access .../report.pdf: No such file or directory

$ openclaw browser waitfordownload " wait.pdf "        # waitfordownload literal preserved
downloaded: /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ wait.pdf
$ openclaw browser trace stop --out " trace.zip "      # trace output literal preserved
TRACE:/tmp/openclaw/ trace.zip     (Zip archive; trimmed neighbor trace.zip absent)
```

Admission regressions (real CLI, rejected before dispatch — route 400, no download event):

```text
$ openclaw browser download e2 "escape-link/existing/report.pdf"   # parent symlink escapes root
GatewayClientRequestError: Invalid path: must stay within downloads directory
$ openclaw browser download e2 "report.fifo"                       # FIFO is not a regular file
GatewayClientRequestError: Invalid path: must stay within downloads directory
```

Base-failing / head-passing regression (current main trims; this PR preserves the literal name).

| Scenario | Base (current main) | Head (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `download " report.pdf "` | trimmed to `report.pdf` (wrong file) | literal ` report.pdf ` written, trimmed neighbor absent |
| `download e2 "."` | dispatches, then writer rejects (UNAVAILABLE) | rejected before dispatch (route 400) |
| `waitfordownload " wait.pdf "` | trimmed to `wait.pdf` | literal ` wait.pdf ` written |
| `trace stop --out " trace.zip "` | trimmed to `trace.zip` | literal ` trace.zip ` written |
| node-transfer `" report.pdf "` | `collectBrowserProxyPaths` trims → reads `report.pdf` → "file not found" | literal path preserved → file read successfully |

Validation: 82 passed (3 files), `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, assertion-safety, line-cap, timeout-race and mock-exports ratchets all clean. `tsgo` extensions shard blocked by worktree symlink (environment, not code).

Scope: 4 files changed (source); the admission validator reuses shared fs-safe `writable()`. No config, protocol, schema, permission, dependency or upgrade changes.

Not tested: Windows trailing-space filenames; complete repository suite.

Empty projected pages continue to the next page. - Measured VStack history and one message renderer provide stable heights for native position preservation. - Only live user admission starts a reader turn; cache and history hydration do not. - The first history page appears before optional metadata completes. ## Evidence - 515 focused chat kit tests and 2 native viewport tests passed. - Simulator paths passed: earlier-history paging, streaming question anchoring and explicit latest jump, first page before metadata, and cached-latest return/refresh. - Cached reply position changed by 0.041667 points after refresh; the first page rendered 18.833 seconds before optional metadata completed. - Native i18n verification, scoped SwiftLint, and pinned SwiftFormat passed. prs.title: fix(models): keep generated catalogs credential-free
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated plugin model catalogs still persist provider/model API keys and headers, and refresh can discard a legacy-only credential before recovery. This revision replaces the original broader runtime-auth cutover with the remaining **storage and explicit migration** repair:

- Strip keys/headers from newly planned and published generated catalogs, including direct publisher calls.
- Stop copying a plaintext auth-profile key into a missing root catalog field.
- Preserve unresolved legacy generated rows during ordinary refresh without blocking unrelated providers.
- Have Doctor import and verify recoverable keys, then remove generated copies accounted for by canonical auth or current authored configuration—including already-canonical copies.

## User Impact

Authored root `models.json` bytes and existing SDK/registry authentication behavior are preserved. **No runtime-auth selection change is introduced.** This does not promise universal Gateway root-only auth: an actual root-only Gateway attempt exposed an unchanged embedded-auth prerequisite, documented in the proof.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair retained generated copies. Doctor includes configured agents with generated SQLite catalogs but no root catalog. Unverified fields stay recoverable with warnings. Pending sidecar migration bytes remain intact until retry convergence.

Doctor rereads source/auth after confirmation, checks the current config revision and included files, and validates source state at persistence/cleanup boundaries. Concurrent logout/source changes do not authorize stale recovery or deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

[#143664](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143664) already blocks generated credentials at request time; [#143647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143647) provides logout cleanup. This PR builds on their existing owners. It adds no dependency, config option, schema migration, or broader credential-precedence policy.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `cae19faf537bb04cbd39301d8a0a82f1b4ca5ac6`. Integrated current main; conflict resolved; final independent AutoReview clean. Exact-head build and added stable-2026.10.5/fresh-publication proofs are in progress. Historical linked receipts below remain attributed to their original heads.

[Immutable evidence bundle](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/README.md) · [file manifest](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/MANIFEST.sha256) · [final runtime boundaries](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/runtime/final-stage-summary.json) · [independent AutoReview](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/review/autoreview-current-cli.md).

- **167/167 focused tests**, 12 files, pass. Includes pre-fix reproductions and repairs for confirmation-time config/include data loss, pending-sidecar recovery, and logout races.
- Targeted lint/core types, formatting, MDX and standard docs routes pass. A hosted test-type error was fixed with a non-null assertion; emitted test JavaScript is identical. Extra anchor auditing found five pre-existing broken anchors in untouched files, disclosed separately.
- AutoReview: **scoped-clean; no actionable P0–P2 findings** on the implementation diff. Final follow-up is test-type-only. The final exact-head build passes; [source/artifact binding](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/runtime/final-source-binding.json) proves all 19 previously bound launchers/changed-owner bundles are byte-identical.
- **Actual published 2026.10.3 → built candidate:** real launcher Doctor migration, canonical/recovered-key Gateway requests, retained conversation and final-head restart/recall pass against an actual CPU local model. Supported logout removes profiles; the protected receiver rejects the subsequent credential-free localhost request, with no revoked-key reuse or upstream inference.
- **Authored compatibility:** built registry/LLM SDK inference with empty canonical auth returns `ROOT-AUTH-OK`, preserving exact authored bytes. The failed root-only Gateway attempt and the invalid initial zero-HTTP-I/O expectation for localhost are retained and explained—not mislabeled passes. Reproduction sources distinguish executed receipts from adapted, unexecuted recipes.

**Current-head CI and final proof refresh are in progress.** Previous-head CI passed; it is not claimed for this integrated commit. Fresh ClawSweeper review will be requested once the new evidence is published. No merge is requested.

prs.title: fix(config): accept web search provider ids that differ only in case
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tools.web.search.provider` is matched case-insensitively at runtime, but the config validator compared the authored string verbatim, so a correctly spelled provider id written with different casing was a **fatal** config error:

```
$ cat openclaw.json
{"tools":{"web":{"search":{"enabled":true,"provider":"Brave"}}}}

$ openclaw config validate
  - tools.web.search.provider: unknown web_search provider: Brave
```

The runtime owner lowercases the configured value before matching manifest ids (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`: `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(search.provider)` then `provider.id === raw`), so `Brave`, `BRAVE`, and padded spellings all resolve to the same `brave` entry. Only the validator disagreed, and because config validation is fatal the user loses the whole config (every unrelated setting in that file stops loading) over a value the resolver would have used.

Same class and same shape as #176990 (`talk.provider` mixed-case keys), which landed this week.

## Fix

Compare the normalized value against the same ids the resolver matches, instead of matching the raw text:

```ts
const normalizedProviderId = normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(trimmed);
if (activeProviderIds.includes(normalizedProviderId)) return;
...
resolveWebSearchInstallCatalogEntries().find((entry) => entry.provider.id === normalizedProviderId);
```

Deliberately does **not** loosen matching beyond runtime parity: the runtime lowercases the configured value only and compares ids exactly, so the validator mirrors that rule and nothing else. Manifest ids stay the authority — this does not accept aliases, prefixes, or ids that the resolver would not resolve. Error messages still print the authored text (`unknown web_search provider: Brave`).

One file of production code (+8/−2), one new test case in the existing config suite. No new option, no config surface, no state.

## Evidence

Environment: Node v24.18.0, repo source tree run through its own CLI entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` containing only:

```json
{"tools":{"web":{"search":{"enabled":true,"provider":"Brave"}}}}
```

Base tree = `dd4eff8648a` (production files restored from `up-main`, test file kept). Head = `c0c1eaed902` (same patch rebased onto current `main` `97b01621f9f`; diff unchanged at 2 files, +16/−2).

| Cell | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw config validate` | **exit 1**, `- tools.web.search.provider: unknown web_search provider: Brave` | **exit 0**, `Config valid: /tmp/oc-ws-cap/openclaw.json` |
| `openclaw infer web providers --json` | **exit 1**, `OpenClaw config is invalid`, no provider selected | **exit 0**, `{"available":true,"configured":false,"selected":true,"id":"brave","envVars":["BRAVE_API_KEY"]}` |
| `pnpm test src/config/config.web-search-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | **1 failed / 7 passed** (`expected false to be true`) | **8 passed** |

The second row is the runtime cross-check: on the head tree the CLI loads the same config and the resolver selects `brave`, which is the entry the validator previously refused to let it see. On the base tree the config never gets that far — validation is fatal before the resolver runs.

The new case asserts `ok` **and** an empty `warnings` array for `Brave`, `BRAVE`, and `" brave "`, so a future change that silently downgrades these to warnings (which would have the same practical effect of surfacing a config the user did not write) fails the test.

Timings on this head (`c0c1eaed902`, Node v24.18.0): the config suite is transform-bound — base-production run `205.7 s` test / `220.7 s` wall, head run `152.9 s` test / `167.9 s` wall. CI is the broad proof.

### Upgrade cell (published driver → candidate)

Driver = published npm tarball `openclaw@2026.10.5` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)`), installed fresh in an isolated prefix. Candidate = this head `c0c1eaed902`, run from source through `src/entry.ts`. Both sides used a fresh, separate `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the config files were byte-identical before the runs (`cmp` identical, sha256 `dbb2d56c1eac09047805f38bb6b9343d14ef3fbab27c715d8fa96760d128aeb7`):

```json
{
  "tools": { "web": { "search": { "enabled": true, "provider": "Brave" } } },
  "agents": { "defaults": { "workspace": "/tmp/ws" } },
  "gateway": { "port": 12345 },
  "logging": { "level": "debug" },
  "channels": { "telegram": { "enabled": false } }
}
```

| Driver | `openclaw config validate` | Exit | Config sha256 before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| published 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`) | `- tools.web.search.provider: unknown web_search provider: Brave` | **1** | `dbb2d56c…aeb7` → `dbb2d56c…aeb7` (unchanged) |
| candidate `c0c1eaed902` | `Config valid: /tmp/oc-upgrade-post/openclaw.json` | **0** | `dbb2d56c…aeb7` → `dbb2d56c…aeb7` (unchanged) |

After the candidate run the file is still byte-identical (`diff -u` empty, no rewrite, no dropped keys), and each unrelated setting reads back: `agents.defaults.workspace = /tmp/ws`, `gateway.port = 12345`, `logging.level = debug`, `channels.telegram.enabled = false` (plus `tools.web.search.provider = Brave`). On the same candidate state, `infer web providers --json` marks `brave` as the only entry with `"selected": true`, so the resolver consumes the same value the validator now accepts.

Update mechanics: config validation runs in the CLI process that is already running, so upgrading changes validation behavior for an existing config without rewriting it — no migration step and no file change, which is exactly what the two sha256 rows show.

Note on the driver source: the pre-extracted stable tree on the shared proof host was unusable (106 of its 108 `node_modules` entries were dangling symlinks into a removed `/ws/base`, and the host has no registry access), so the released driver above is a fresh `npm pack openclaw@2026.10.5` plus `npm install --omit=dev --legacy-peer-deps`; the published tarball reports `OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)`, the same build that tree contained.

## Not tested

Config written in an on-disk form other than the schema's own JSON shape (YAML/TOML project config) — normalization happens after the loader produces the same `tools.web.search.provider` string, and the unit case exercises the validator directly, so the loader format is out of scope here rather than unhandled.

Manifests that declare an uppercase provider id are still unmatched by the runtime, and this PR does not change that; all bundled providers declare lowercase ids.

Collision note: #177228 touches `src/web-search/runtime.ts`; this PR does not modify that file.

prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled script tool calls fail after a hook plugin is replaced
prs.body:
Related: #160122

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every run of a cron script trigger fails with `Tool call blocked because before_tool_call hook failed` (`PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled`) after a plugin that registers `before_tool_call` is replaced in place. The failure continues until the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: scheduled script triggers keep running after a hook-registering plugin is reinstalled or reloaded. A Gateway restart is no longer needed to clear the stale hook.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createCronCodeModeRunner` caches one prepared trigger runtime per job, together with its plugin registry. Tool calls dispatch hooks from that cached registry through `withPluginRuntimeRegistryScope`.

1. Per-plugin replacement disposes the replaced plugin's instance in the previous registry.
2. That registry is never marked retired while the cache entry still retains it.
3. As a result, `capturePluginLifecycleAuthority(…, { scopedRuntime: true })` keeps reporting the cached runtime as current.
4. Every later run therefore dispatches the disposed instance's `before_tool_call` hook. The instance refuses, and the fail-closed hook policy blocks the tool call.

With this change, the cached runtime is current only while every enabled, loaded plugin in its registry can still admit calls (`isPluginRegistryRecordSetAdmitting`). After a replacement, the next invocation retires the stale entry and prepares a fresh runtime. Whole-registry retirement behaves as before.

## Evidence

- **Production occurrence** on a real 2026.10.10-beta.1 Gateway: `Plugin replacement applied: oncall-notice-guard` at 00:10:10Z. Every hourly run of a `main`-agent cron script trigger from 01:04Z to 06:04Z then failed with `before_tool_call hook failed: tool=exec … PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin oncall-notice-guard was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.` Later `plugins.reload` attempts stayed `queued behind 3 retained work item(s)`. Runs succeeded again only after the Gateway restarted.
- **New regression test** in `src/cron/trigger-script.plugin-reload.test.ts`. It disposes a hook-only plugin's instance without retiring the cached registry.
  - On the base it fails exactly as in production: `{"kind":"error","code":"internal_error","error":"Error: Tool call blocked because before_tool_call hook failed …"}`.
  - With the fix it passes: the runtime is prepared again, and the new guard generation runs.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/cron/trigger-script*.test.ts src/plugins/registry-lifecycle*.test.ts`: all pass except `trigger-script.mcp.test.ts`, which fails identically (5 cases) on unmodified `main` in this environment. `trigger-script.account-policy.test.ts` timed out once under the parallel run and passes 2/2 when run alone.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. Format and oxlint are clean on the changed files.
- Not yet done: an isolated-Gateway end-to-end reproduction of the replacement sequence. The production log above is the end-to-end occurrence.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate remaining async scheduling and cleanup owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Consolidates duplicate async scheduling, cancellation, and cleanup ownership in the final z34 residue.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change, migration, or operator action. Real network/process/model deadlines, user cancellation, FIFO admission, security-effect authority and write-capable shutdown settlement remain. The standalone session memory backend is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord listener admission now uses the existing shared permit pool instead of a second queue implementation. Context metadata consumes the published configuration snapshot instead of retrying synchronous config loading. Tool-loop evaluation stays synchronous after its one runtime import. Remaining cuts remove inert signals, duplicate effect checks, observer fences and cleanup that owns no resource.

This is the existing residue originally signed at `7d3ba0864acf3b39468f149a2e5714164cec634a`, explicitly authorized as one PR under rule 14. After conflict-only rebases and CI-driven corrections, signed head `5106c3490591a82e6819b202bd1db138106608f7` has 62 total paths, below the 80-file split threshold. Production: +257 / −461 = **204 net lines removed**; tests: +424 / −83 = 341 net added. Main's removal of Discord's unused threshold option and its no-argument context-cache API are preserved. No config, schema, protocol, dependency or SDK export changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Discord's private queue implementation is replaced, not its FIFO, concurrency limit, bounded backlog or failure reporting. The shared owner keeps cursor compaction and immediate cancellation removal; no listener timeout is removed.
- Context config-load backoff now trusts the runtime config owner. Before publication the metadata cache can stay empty until the next read; an internal read does not retry loading our own configuration. This does not weaken the external config boundary.
- Catalog status/publication hints can arrive from a retiring or staged owner and cause a harmless refresh. Generation, credential, selection and actual provider-effect checks remain; display hints no longer need a second publication fence. The single currency check before recording failure state stays: compatible owners share that state, so a retired callback must not poison a replacement's retained inventory.
- Dependency prewarming may continue an already-started read until the next existing effect guard after config replacement. It still stops on service cancellation and refuses stale effect commits; speculative mid-prewarm config churn no longer needs its own subscription/controller.
- The plugin catalog read owns its agent reader, not a root-state reader, so root-state retirement no longer separately cancels that path. Agent identity validation, native reader shutdown and accepted-work joins remain.
- File-transfer startup trusts its serialized lifecycle owner instead of defending concurrent replacement starts. Startup failure stops the current owned lifetime; ordinary stop and real request cancellation remain.
- Portal retirement trusts idempotent ticket cancellation, abort and stream destruction rather than a duplicate stopped flag. Physical invocation settlement still joins at shutdown, including repeated closes.
- PTY creation revalidates at the existing spawn boundary, native runtime retains workspace authority at actual effects, and worker tool execution validates before its effect. Redundant checks after settled work do not independently grant or revoke authority.
- MiniMax keeps the guarded-fetch deadline through response-body consumption and release, removing only the second private timer/controller. The original TTS feature provenance (#52720) is not a reason to delete its deadline; timeout, HTTP/body failure and cleanup coverage remain.
- Diagnostic worker capture and hello capability projection no longer create never-aborted controllers. Real capture authority and active browser-auth/session cancellation remain.
- Promise settlement and synchronous in-memory follow-up/allowlist evaluation need no extra settled flags, async wrappers or manual promise forwarding. Required listeners, actual TLS timeout, reentrancy-safe ingress settlement and durable claim writes remain.
- TUI coalescing/history and streamed block replies trust their existing serialized owner. A replaced descriptive request can finish, but final result currency and real delivery cancellation remain.
- Image-original reads do not acquire an original-source release lease, so their empty finally is removed. Download URL cleanup uses one existing helper and preserves the original 0/30,000 ms lifetimes and exact filename/byte contracts (#144480/#173161).
- Approval rows reuse the row's existing clock, preserving identical host/style/ARIA/countdown output; standalone/modal countdown clocks remain. The rendering/derivation introductions (#168791/#172008/#177481) do not require two clocks.
- Caption finalization clears its existing settle timer once after the synchronous flush instead of twice around it (#126053); no callback can run between those synchronous statements. QA TCP probes retain their real 700 ms timeout and single destroy/reject listener; both duplicate callbacks originated together in the inspector feature (#64895, extracted by #67430).

The removed guards were qualified by source/caller/history review as duplicate owners or speculative internal races, not human-reported hangs requiring those exact mechanisms. No removed machinery is an inactive activation foundation. Kept security boundaries and the named memory backend were not traded away.

## Evidence

- Final exact-head CI `39524544068` (attempt 1, `5106c3490591a82e6819b202bd1db138106608f7`) completed with 185 terminal checks: 141 success, 41 intentional skipped templates, one neutral and two failures. All 140 run jobs are terminal; there are no cancelled or missing selected suites. Actual executable extension typed-lint jobs `118977693248` / `118977693424` / `118977693281`, `security-fast` `118976571377`, and separate security/dependency reviews passed. The failed test below is baseline-reproduced, not green CI; native inherited-failure landing is explicitly selected under the standing lane authority.

| [checks-node-changed-compact-small-13-1, 118976573395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39524544068/job/118976573395) | `server.sessions.create-notices.test.ts`, “sessions.create preserves creation and notices after an unknown signal outcome,” line 144: expected delegated profile-backed human creator, received agent. Serial focused replay on actual CI merge `446a514481875f1c6a1ee578e74626a8d8b784cb` failed identically (223.6 s); exact CI base `1989e3dc4360a17d039440a886f71e582758a487` failed identically (132.2 s). Determining test/creation/provenance inputs are unchanged by this PR. Refreshed main-flake ledger and six latest completed scheduled inventories were checked; no matching signature there, so attribution rests on actual replay/source equality, not shard names. This remains an unresolved baseline defect, not a repaired or load-explained failure. |

prs.title: fix(gateway): config.patch hangs after a superseded reload until another config change lands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A persisted `config.patch` / `config.apply` can leave its RPC waiting indefinitely after an in-process Gateway restart. Retained reload candidates were not always rescheduled. Real Gateway verification also exposed a second cause: the effective-unchanged path compared a resolved secrets snapshot with an unresolved SecretRef candidate, classified the permanent mismatch as supersession, and kept retrying it.

## User Impact

Provisioning and other source-equivalent config writes receive their application acknowledgment without an unrelated follow-up edit. Existing credential activation, publication ownership, and rollback checks remain in force. No config option, schema, dependency, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Schedule another attempt whenever a superseded write candidate is retained, including candidates retained by either inner catch.
- When the candidate differs from the active resolved snapshot only by canonical SecretRefs, use the existing hot-reload owner to materialize and publish it. Compare through the existing canonicalization helper so an already-owned restart's unapplied non-secret settings keep their restart publication path.

The complete PR adds nine net production lines, reusing existing activation and canonicalization owners rather than introducing a second resolver, state, or weaker guards.

## Evidence

### Exact-head real Gateway recovery: `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`

<!-- pr177823-real-gateway-repair-b8c13e0 -->

The previously stalling workload now completes on the final fixed full Gateway: **437 ms server / 439 ms client**, after a real SIGUSR2 in-process restart and concurrent synthetic credential refresh, with **no later config edit**.

Important distinction: this final run logged **zero supersessions**. The repair prevents the permanent resolved-value/SecretRef mismatch that produced them on the older head. This is not presented as a new-head trace that throws a supersession and then succeeds.

#### Comparable real-runtime controls

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct parent `08d04a9d7b97e50849ba089c3837d2e1c3c4f7fd` | One supersession, credential restored, no additional config write | Original patch still pending at the 30 s client deadline. It answered UNAVAILABLE only during shutdown, at 50,016 ms. **FAIL** |
| Initial PR head `ebfffd5599a7ee7c6d793718b96f923107b27691` | Eight supersessions before credential restoration; retries continued afterward | Original patch still pending at 30 s; 482 supersessions were recorded before task-owned forced cleanup. **FAIL** |
| First repair `c337231afc47e7cf137f0273a9051daab79b71ae` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered in **308 ms**, but broader CI exposed a restart-reapply regression. This is prior-head runtime evidence, not the final candidate. |
| Final head `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered successfully in **439 ms**, before the credential-restoration step. Clean Gateway shutdown. **PASS** |

All runs used OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Node v26.8.1, macOS arm64, independently owned dependencies, isolated synthetic HOME/state/config/workspace, and distinct free loopback ports between control families. The final build and runtime-postbuild stamps both identify exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` with `inputsClean:true`.

No mocked hot-reload callback, injected exception, fake clock, manually settled receipt, inference call, live Mattermost traffic, operator Gateway change, or TEST/PROD mutation was used in these real Gateway runs.

#### Executed workload

1. Start the full maintained Gateway with `node scripts/run-node.mjs --profile pr177823proof gateway run --port <isolated-port> --verbose`; wait for readiness.
2. Send SIGUSR2 only to that fixture's own Gateway PID; verify **in-process restart** and readiness again.
3. Connect through the real token-authenticated Gateway WebSocket protocol (v4). Read `config.get` for the base hash.
4. Submit one `config.patch` with `response:"summary"`:
   ```json
   {"channels":{"mattermost":{"accounts":{"proof":{"baseUrl":"${PR177823_MATTERMOST_URL}"}}}}}
   ```
   The environment placeholder resolves to the existing synthetic URL; the Mattermost account is disabled.
5. After the actual `config.patch write` log, rotate a task-owned JSON file's synthetic provider key A→B and call the real `secrets.reload {}` RPC. The provider is a custom `proof/proof` model pointing at an unused loopback endpoint; no model turn is sent. Its config uses:
   ```json
   {"apiKey":{"source":"file","provider":"proof","id":"/apiKey"}}
   ```
6. Observe for 2.5 s, restore that **credential file** B→A, and call `secrets.reload {}` again. Do not edit config or send another config-write RPC. The RPC deadline stays 30 s.
7. Join Gateway shutdown. On the fixed head, the original patch had already completed before step 6.

Redacted actual fixed Gateway log; **October 19, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
18:27:43.065 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
18:27:43.192 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart
18:27:49.708 [gateway] config.patch write ... changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl
18:27:49.971 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 242ms id=proof-4
18:27:50.068 [reload] config source revision 2 accepted (write)
18:27:50.082 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 437ms id=proof-3
18:27:52.511 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 33ms id=proof-5
18:27:52.595 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 77ms
```

The original patch response was `ok:true`, with the expected changed path, `sentinel.persisted:true`, and `requiresRestart:false`. The raw trace contains one config write for the scenario and no later config write. The client observed settlement before the restoration RPC.

Raw local trace SHA-256 values (the redacted excerpt above is the submitted public evidence):

- Parent Gateway log: `4cda5b03044bf2ffb2f385b8c948d97128e7b56b13fbbb2edbab26bf1e66e79b`.
- Initial-head Gateway log: `06845c2cd190360b387e5aa8c082d10a60abbea3771cb33265794ee936afd03a`.
- Prior `c337231` Gateway log: `d37f7c8db6ada211be6733f342b11889d31bb761699d465373d9b0c07302e2c8`.
- Prior `c337231` client event trace: `5bcc6542104caff04cdd1e7b22dce04b6b5e6a47487249bac18be35b81ff0472`.
- Final `b8c13e0` Gateway log: `0134c2ff7a4d1595bb8aaffa1b3e2ef4bba573143f4156eafb8de0653a433b25`.
- Final `b8c13e0` client event trace: `efa09c7c6bb13b20dd266f86d21c419d05e2d94586e962bf559a62a42b76449e`.

These are isolated production-path controls, not a claim that the original tenant's entire environment was replayed. An earlier setup attempt expired while the source launcher was still rebuilding, before any config RPC; it is a setup failure, not a Gateway behavior verdict. The final clean-head run completed normally.

### Focused behavioral regression and checks

- Added stable-key and rotated-key cases to `server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts`. They use real secrets preparation/activation and the real config reloader/receipt. Both fail on initial head `ebfffd5` because the application receipt stays pending; both pass with the follow-up, preserving the current credential and authored source.
- Existing `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` still proves two retained supersessions followed by automatic application. Its hot-reload failures are mocked; this remains focused scheduler proof, not real-Gateway evidence.
- Maintained focused runs: **271 tests passed across 4 affected files**: config-reload plus superseded-retry (134), the complete restart/reload-handler suite (118), and managed secrets (19). After narrowing the guard, the combined run passed the first 252 but exposed the secrets fixture's identity stub; replacing that stub with production's existing `restoreCanonicalSecretRefs` helper made all 19 secrets tests pass (18.05 s wrapper / 12.12 s shard). No assertions, timeouts, or baselines changed. No full Bun/CI pass on the final head is claimed.
- Core typecheck and the canonical Gateway-server test typecheck passed.
- Targeted oxlint, formatter check, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- The first repair's full local maintained `qaRuntime` build passed; the final clean-head source launcher rebuilt and ran its own exact-head runtime and assets.
- The broad changed-test typecheck selector encountered pre-existing advisory root-budget excesses in unrelated graph inventories; the relevant canonical Gateway-server graph was typechecked directly and passed. No inventory, budget, assertion, or baseline was weakened.

### CI and review status

The final repair remains at exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`. Its [pull-request CI run 39353612934](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39353612934) completed successfully, including the CI workflow's `openclaw/ci-gate`. The separately enforced aggregate status is still **failing**, because the [security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39356909084/job/118413751307) explicitly reports “awaiting maintainer approval.” A successful policy-workflow execution is not a security approval, and no merge clearance is claimed.

The first repair's [CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39351516553/job/118396992531) timed out both existing `revalidates restart secrets after held promotion and an explicit reapply` cases at 120 s. The maintained CI classifier returned unknown/no comparable main job; the exact job log and a bounded local comparison established this as PR-caused, not inherited: both cases passed on initial `ebfffd5`, while `c337231` locally reproduced the first timeout (the second was interrupted after the same CI failure was established). The broad mismatch guard had incorrectly entered hot publication inside restart-owned reapplication. The final canonicalization comparison retains the restart owner; both cases and the full 118-test handler suite pass without changing those tests.

Prior-head dependency review passed. The [prior security-sensitive review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39351510133/job/118396555176) reports **awaiting maintainer approval** for the credential-owner change. Final-head security approval is still required; it is not bypassed or described as passing.

The local independent-review helper for this repair returned `reviewer_unavailable` without producing a report. The author explicitly approved publication for ClawSweeper review without that local review; that history is unchanged. [ClawSweeper's latest exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177823#issuecomment-6279684646), refreshed October 20 after this evidence update, rated **readiness 5/6, proof 5/6, patch quality 5/6**, with zero actionable findings on final `b8c13e0`. Its remaining checklist item is maintainer security approval. The later successful local review of a downstream integration is not relabeled as an independent review of this PR.

### October 20 refresh integration check

<!-- pr177823-oct20-refresh -->

The complete patch is retained in the downstream [refreshed native source `10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b`](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/commit/10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b), integrated with selected upstream main `2d03d5632a69d04181844f85b05d5509240dcc14`.

- On that integrated source, the maintained superseded-retry regression passed (1 test) and the complete managed-secrets suite passed (19 tests). The full native build and production typechecks also passed.
- The production reload modules changed in upstream/refreshed integration while these two regression files remained byte-identical to this PR. These results are **downstream integration evidence**, not a new exact-head upstream CI run or a replay of the original Gateway workload.
- Both real Linux architecture installers, isolated Shared/Builder configuration validation and Doctor checks, and ordinary offline Memory/Skills workers passed for the refreshed packaged source. Those checks exercise packaging/configuration boundaries; they are not credential-rotation recovery proof or a deployed customer check.
- The exact-head parent/fixed Gateway controls above remain the primary behavioral proof. No later deployment, live-provider result, merged security approval, or new-head real supersession trace is inferred from today's build.

### Earlier evidence retained with its limits

The original pre-fix incident remains a failure: after an in-process restart, a source-equivalent Mattermost URL write logged supersession and timed out after 130 s; an unrelated heartbeat edit later released the parked request at 198,627 ms.

Earlier initial-head local smoke completed in 157 ms (Mattermost URL placeholder) and 104 ms (workspace placeholder), with no supersession; a literal-value control was a no-op. A later single-supersession workload recovered on **both** the parent and initial PR head. Those cases are not patch-specific recovery proof and are not substituted for the failing controls above.

prs.title: fix(web-push): agent-finished pushes were indistinguishable across sessions
prs.body:
Closes #143946

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent-finished Web Push notifications are indistinguishable when more than one session runs under the same agent — every notification renders the generic "An agent completed its response."

## User Impact

User impact: agent-finished pushes now identify themselves with the conversation's actual reply (e.g. "Deploy finished, tests green."), prefixed with the agent name when the payload identifies it. Users who prefer not to see content keep the generic body — the existing detail-level and per-category notification preferences govern this unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#143946 noted `agent-finished` is the only remaining event-push category without a producer-owned label. This follows the same `identifiedBody` pattern `scheduled-task-failed` and `human-mentioned` already use: the first readable text of the final assistant message, whitespace-normalized, capped at 140 chars with an ellipsis, falling back to the generic body when the message carries nothing readable. Privacy posture is unchanged — `identifiedBody` is consumed only for non-private detail levels by the existing delivery gate, so `private` recipients keep the generic body and no icon.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/event-web-push.test.ts`: 43/43 passing (39 pre-existing + 4 new):
  - final assistant text lands as the identified body
  - agent label prefix when the payload identifies the agent
  - long replies truncate to ≤140 chars with an ellipsis
  - whitespace-only text keeps the generic body
- Targeted run: `vitest run src/gateway/event-web-push.test.ts` → 43 passed.
- `pnpm check` on this branch: all sub-checks pass except the pre-existing `max-lines suppression ratchet` failure, which reproduces identically on pristine `main` (three `ui/src/pages/**` files, untouched by this PR).

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): support native typed Decisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter users cannot select its native Luna Decisions route through OpenClaw's typed decision API.

## User Impact

User impact: users can select `clawrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna` independently of chat, with Boolean, choice, score, inline-image, usage, and per-question refusal results.

**Availability:** this requires the separately owned native service contract in openclaw/clawrouter#277 to be deployed and the selected ClawRouter key to grant Luna and the Decisions route. Static protocol support is not a key grant. SystemOne/SubQ remain out of scope. No migration or new config option is introduced; primary/fallback/Fast/auth defaults are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register one ClawRouter decision owner, resolve each call's eligibility against its effective key and endpoint, and use the same supported public Decisions codec as native OpenAI. Prepared router auth/transport, deadline, abort, and live authority remain authoritative; the adapter never discovers an upstream OpenAI key, adds conversation history, fabricates probabilities, or substitutes JSON chat.

Canonical manifest capabilities now feed decision selector discovery without advertising decision-only rows as chat access. The old private OpenAI codec is moved, not duplicated.

## What Problem This Solves

Session panels need consistent controls and empty-state presentation across desktop and mobile without changing unrelated surfaces.

## User Impact

Submenus use consistent chevrons. Session panels can opt into shared rails, responsive empty states, elapsed times that retain seconds, and avatars without redundant tooltips.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provides shared presentation primitives and explicit options so individual panels do not duplicate styling or change global defaults.

Elapsed time now renders through the shared direct Solid component, preserving optional seconds, formatting, polling, and cleanup.

## Risk and coverage

The enforced chat boot gzip limit temporarily increases from 1,470,000 to 1,500,000 bytes. Reducing the initial download and restoring the prior limit remain follow-up work; all other performance limits are unchanged.

The quota-recovery saved-clear status case also fails on pinned main `e75403f`: authentication recovers and an ordinary turn succeeds, but the UI remains at “Checking models…”. Source and event-order evidence point to catalog-publication catch-up in #177437; specific-commit causality has not been isolated with a repaired-source comparison. No quota fix is included here.

The previous restart (#144510) retired earlier run authority. Both current cases observe the final chat, persisted tool history/config and rendered result before completing. prs.title: fix(iOS): double-tapping Send stops the message it just sent
prs.body: Closes #176940 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes a response being stopped immediately after sending when Send is double-tapped on iOS. ## User Impact A rapid double tap on Send leaves the response running. A deliberate Stop tap works once the brief guard expires. ## Why This Change Was Made Stop appears in the spot Send occupied, so the second tap could cancel the response. Stop is dimmed and ignores taps for a fixed 700 ms whenever it appears. ## Evidence ### Behavior evidence The native simulator test sends two independent taps **410 ms apart**. With the fixed 700 ms guard, the response keeps running; a deliberate Stop tap later cancels it. The same test without the guard cancels the response on the second tap and fails. [Simulator recording](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/06cb40fc4003414c827dd3a6bf52c2ef33e5baee/production-double-tap.mp4) · [Red/green runtime trace](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/06cb40fc4003414c827dd3a6bf52c2ef33e5baee/runtime-trace.md) On a real iPhone at the shipped 700 ms guard: after Send, Stop appears dimmed for about 0.7 s, then turns active, and the response keeps running. [iPhone recording](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/e2b7c39b269e0080dd6fa432719a6c8b4214b036/device-double-tap.mp4) - Production-timing simulator regression: passes in 16.428 seconds. - Composer package checks: 24 tests in 5 suites pass. - Startup-status and streamed-reply simulator checks pass. - Touched Swift formatting and strict production lint pass. Before: Stop is immediately active where Send was. After: the response survives the rapid taps. After: a deliberate Stop cancels the response. AI-assisted.

prs.title: improve(ios): reduce screenshot test startup overhead
prs.body:
Closes #178890

## What Problem This Solves

Release screenshot capture starts XCTest and reinstalls the app separately for each screen, adding repeated startup work to an already resource-intensive iOS lane.

## User Impact

Screenshot capture uses one XCTest session per fresh iPhone or iPad simulator while keeping the same four screenshots, independent app launches, one active simulator, and unchanged Watch capture. There is no intended change to the rendered screens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The four existing tests each launch directly into their fixture destination and terminate the app afterward. Grouping them removes six XCTest startups across the two devices. Each device still gets a fresh installation; the four tests share that installation's data, which their existing fixture setup initializes for capture.

One device attempt and result bundle now replace four per-screen bundles. Capture requires all four exact test identities to pass once and all fresh PNGs to exist. Failures retain the original bundle and stop the lane without retrying. The evidence producer and reducer move together to schema 2, and CI exports and routes the shared verifier.

## Evidence

On the same Mac, Xcode 27.0 and identical compiled products:

| Device | Separate sessions | Grouped session |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| iPhone 18 Pro Max | 130.4s | 94.1s |
| iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) | 116.9s | 89.6s |

The eight XCTest commands dropped from 247.3s to 183.8s (26%) in this controlled local comparison. All eight methods passed on their first attempts. This is a local sample, not a guaranteed hosted-runtime reduction.

Focused parser, qualification, capture/failure, evidence, resource-diagnostics, checkout, and CI-routing tests passed. Changed-file lint/typechecks, workflow checks, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review passed. Before/after fixture screenshots were visually inspected.

A second grouped execution through the complete screenshot-only entry point passed all nine iPhone, iPad, and Watch captures. Its two XCTest commands took 185.4s. The complete local lane decreased from 8m34s to 7m42s (about 10%); build times were similar. No screenshot retries or release uploads were performed.

The actual integrated native artifacts also passed collection and reduction: nine PNGs, two device bundles, and four exact passing test identities per bundle.

Hosted [screenshot CI on implementation commit `44f71b748a58`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39521844120/job/118967803585) passed all eight iPhone and iPad methods on their first attempts, including strict verification of both grouped result bundles. The job then failed in the unchanged Watch runtime repair: the registered watchOS image had no mounted path, and `simctl runtime delete` returned error 30, "Removed the runtime, but did not reclaim its MobileAsset." The existing helper stopped before downloading the runtime again.

Watch runtime availability also failed before this change, after eight separate screenshot invocations, as documented in #178818. The runtime repair and simulator lifecycle are unchanged here. No directly attributable branch failure has been identified; the original cause of the missing runtime mount remains unproven. The CI failure classifier reports `unknown` because main has no comparable job result. Full hosted nine-image collection and reduction did not complete in that run.

Final-head [CI on `89cf9fb70ea8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39523960817) passed, including screenshot capture, screenshot evidence reduction, native dead-code scans, and the final CI gate. All checks have settled with no failures. The final commit updates only the setup guide's session, attempt, and bundle descriptions; the implementation is unchanged from the local measurements above.

The successful hosted run validates the complete grouped capture path. It does not establish a fix for the earlier intermittent Watch runtime mount/repair failure; Watch repair logic remains unchanged.

prs.title: feat: restore task-boundary and cache-expiry compaction
prs.body:
Restores #178021 after #178425. Related: #6757.

## What Problem This Solves

Long conversations need optional compaction at useful task boundaries and before eligible cache windows end, without repeatedly compacting short-lived caches.

## User Impact

Agents can request task-boundary compaction, and operators can opt into one idle pre-expiry attempt. Every eligible window leaves a **five-minute lead**: **30 minutes → 25 minutes; one hour → 55 minutes; an effective 12-hour Responses TTL → 11 hours 55 minutes**. Windows of **five minutes or less never trigger** this timer.

The timer remains disabled by default and respects `compaction.enabled: false`. Foreground activity cancels pending work; a later successful eligible turn can arm a fresh timer. Maintenance never rearms itself. Normal context-pressure compaction, manual compaction, prompt caching, and model-requested compaction retain their existing behavior.

**Subscription scope:** ChatGPT/Codex OAuth through the **built-in OpenClaw runtime** may use an explicitly assumed 30-minute idle window, giving a 25-minute idle trigger. This is labeled `codex-idle-heuristic`, **not a verified Codex TTL**. Native Codex app-server and generic CLI timers are **not enabled**. In particular, the native standalone compact RPC cannot carry the admitted turn generation required by ChatGPT subscription sharing; this change does not bypass that guard or silently switch runtimes.

Compaction costs inference and can lose detail; cache hits or savings are not guaranteed. No live configuration was changed and no paid-provider cache experiment was run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scheduler now applies one five-minute margin instead of its previous one-minute maximum. Existing API qualification stays intact: effective one-hour Anthropic markers and qualified direct OpenAI minimum windows still require successful cache activity. The new subscription estimate also requires positive cache usage, OAuth, the canonical `openai` provider, and the official HTTPS ChatGPT Responses backend. Unknown providers, aliases, and custom backends receive no assumed lifetime.

Provider-backed estimates retain request-start timing. The subscription heuristic starts at observed completion of model activity, so generation time is not mislabeled idle time. Existing selection, credentials, configuration, compaction-count, foreground, delivery, and lifecycle checks retain ownership of cancellation and admission.

The original restoration and earlier CI repairs remain in history. The earlier conflict refresh used `bead2a8e542740f943fe57e8391e5e6c11e9773d`. After the inventory repair, GitHub reported a new actual conflict. A history-preserving merge of pinned main `1bd22b28d632ba4082e923d88a2485be61f8c8af` resolved it: the only textual conflicts were the generated config count/hash artifacts, regenerated by their owner. Main’s tool-inheritance refactor and removal of its unused development dependency were preserved. The five-minute classifier, timer, maintenance runtime, and authored behavior docs are byte-identical across this refresh. No unrelated API-retention setting was changed.

CI then exposed a stale dependency entry in the restored plugin: main already requires TypeBox 1.3.37, while its manifest and importer still named 1.3.36. The three-line repair aligns those entries with the existing main pin. The lockfile was regenerated from the verified valid main graph; every other importer, package, and snapshot remains unchanged. No dependency policy was weakened.

## Evidence

- **Inherited creation-notice fixture only:** [CI job 118970499842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39522653992/job/118970499842) exposed an expectation predating #178493. That landed contract keeps the original isolation actor but projects the separately captured causal creator; a human isolation actor alone does not prove human initiation. The unchanged fixture reproduced the failure locally. The repaired fixture covers autonomous agent, human isolation without a human requester, and explicitly retained causal-human attribution; exact persisted-actor and required-sandbox assertions remain. **No production identity, authorization, or compaction code changed.** All 21 tests across the affected file and three provenance siblings pass on Node (58.95 s); the affected file also passes on Bun (11.84 s). Targeted Gateway test types, type-aware lint, format and diff checks pass; independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean.

- **Landed API-lifetime integration:** the actual conflict with #178695 was resolved by merging pinned main `45f9aed4ef6831def7ac483ca5acf2ed1bf7fc93`. Its request fields, defaults, compatibility rules and pricing are preserved. The model-version predicate is shared, and optional idle compaction consumes the same lifetime resolver with the prepared request policy. Qualified direct Responses requests using `12h` now schedule at **11h55m**, not 25m. Completions do not inherit this Responses-only option; the built-in OAuth assumption stays separately labeled 30m/25m. Unknown endpoints and short windows remain excluded.
- **Cross-contract proof:** 175 tests across nine complete files passed in 128.75 s, covering request builders, pricing, parameter precedence, classifier, settlement forwarding, scheduler boundaries, prefix stability and embedded-command maintenance. Three new policy cases failed before the fix. Targeted agent/package test types, nine-file lint, formatting, two-file MDX, canonical config/inventory checks, frozen install and diff checks passed. The complete candidate received a clean independent P0–P2 review against the pinned main.
- **Generated-baseline composition:** a prepublication check found new conflicts only in generated config baselines. A second history-preserving refresh pinned `510249a88634dd3e8562bfb467abe9a2052d9af5`; both canonical generators were run and checked. The reviewed cache-policy implementation remained byte-identical. Final agent types, all 16 session-prompt-state tests and all three source-built isolated-Gateway scenarios passed (236.99 s combined; Gateway test file 22.50 s). An earlier Gateway attempt failed before collecting tests because Rolldown panicked; a bounded single-thread compiler invocation passed without changing source or disabling a gate. No paid-provider experiment was used.

- **Narrow inherited Doctor repair:** [check-lint-core-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39513053484/job/118940087659) found an unbound repair method introduced on main by #178767. The affected file was byte-identical to pinned main; a fresh upstream check found no later fix. Capturing the method with `.bind(check)` preserves its original receiver without changing arguments, asynchronous results, progress, dry-run or error handling. One receiver-dependent owner regression fails before the repair and passes afterward. Focused lint now reports zero errors; formatting, the owning test-type shard and diff checks pass. The relevant Doctor invocation passed **19 tests**, with **10 Windows-only tests skipped on Linux** (50.61 s). Independent P0–P2 Auto Review is scoped-clean. That repair did not change installation, live state, provider or compaction policy; it is retained through the later API-lifetime integration.

- **Generated inventory repair:** complete retained logs for exact-head jobs [check-docs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39502533848/job/118904102920) and [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39502533848/job/118904102707) identify the same stale inventory output. The canonical check reproduced it on `0ea0dad834d3`. Running `pnpm plugins:inventory:gen` regenerated all inventory/reference outputs; the complete diff is only core plugins **73 → 74** and reference pages **174 → 175**. `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` now passes—the identical failing gate used by both jobs. Config-doc drift/count validation, two-file MDX validation, and `git diff --check` also pass. No generated content was patched by hand, and the five-minute/runtime behavior is unchanged.

- **Composed-head validation:** 77 tests across the tool-search preparation consumer (19), prompt-prefix stability (5), classifier (33), and scheduler (20) passed in 94.00 s. Targeted agent test types passed. All three isolated-Gateway scenarios passed again (22.77 s test-file duration; 263.76 s including current-source preparation). Full frozen installation, both canonical generators and drift checks, and diff checks passed. These runs validate the incoming tool-inheritance contract with the retained compaction binding; they are not paid-provider TTL or native Codex timer proofs.
- **Earlier dependency admission:** the exact frozen-lockfile mismatch from [the build-artifacts job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499611007/job/118893461313) was reproduced locally. After repair, both frozen graph validation and the full `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` pass with supply-chain policies unchanged. This was a PR integration defect, not an infrastructure retry.
- **Earlier dependency-repair proof: 59 affected tests passed on the reconciled install**, using TypeBox 1.3.37: classifier/route guards (33), scheduler (20), prompt-prefix stability (5), and the plugin capability consumer (1). Targeted agent test types also pass. The focused invocation took 61.76 s.
- **Earlier dependency-repair Gateway proof:** requested compaction before continuation without replay, disabled configuration, and rejected-summary recovery. Test-file duration: 22.08 s; full invocation: 223.67 s including current-source runtime preparation. These are runtime/non-regression proofs, not native Codex timer or paid-provider TTL proofs.
- **Initial feature proof:** 122 tests across seven full files passed before the dependency repair, including the complete embedded-command maintenance consumer, coordinator, defaults schema, and config-baseline integration. Nine intended timing/heuristic failures reproduced the previous behavior before implementation. These earlier results retain their original input binding; they are not relabeled as final-head CI.
- Fake-clock proof checks 25-minute and 55-minute boundaries, immediately before and at admission, short-window exclusion, disabled/unset opt-in, global disable, active foreground cancellation, fresh scheduling after activity, and no self-rescheduling. The cross-expiry fixture explicitly configures its existing six-minute work budget for a deliberate five-minute-ten-second clock jump; no production timeout increased.
- Incremental TypeScript/docs lint, formatting, two-file MDX validation, config generation/drift/count checks, and diff checks passed. The generated lockfile is validated by pnpm rather than hand-formatted. Fresh independent P0–P2 Auto Review is scoped-clean for both the timing change and the final three-line install repair.
- **Retained compaction proof binding:** tested composition `4f2e5da4be4c3868aa13edbcac570f787cb3c92b`, published head `f79498d7dbcfb93088c533f88a27b40913535106`, identical tree `83fdecfa36803750f3b95692dec866d4660f9975`. The publication commit changes no files. The complete inventory repair is in `70b1beb6eb6f`; the conflict-only refresh preserves it and adds main’s changes plus canonical config-baseline outputs. Earlier dependency proof remains bound to `1c5726231bf2` / tree `41988c47ccac8c233088ac8d51fed7a029a92d49`; timing implementation remains in `6195ece47dd4`.
- **Retained Doctor binding:** tested Doctor repair `f0efa49ec9476698564acddf6a6101a61c134635`, published head `0af8b98821ffb037733f0c62ed835859ecce13f0`, identical tree `59d4d6af5580491d76a4aaa0907a36d7913bcbaa`. The publication marker changes no files. At that head, only the Doctor repair owner and its regression differed from `f79498d7dbcf`; those 77-test and three-Gateway results retain their earlier source binding.
- **API-integration proof binding:** integration commit `d78f8ae85ecfc24f55540cedb9e3a8ce606b727a` / tree `8fb5d0b4b502710589c19fe76bef6328e5c48d21`; final tested composition `380d6f54d42bfc010144fb839441f615789cdb2f`, published head `c6d77dc2d88979d272f1ba09367db4bd07e72a1e`, identical tree `f81dba71e9379f42c136a094d28f74ea5dd745f3`. The publication marker changes no files.
- **Retained conflict-reconciliation binding:** main independently landed the Doctor receiver fix and equivalent regression. The later actual conflict was resolved by merging pinned main `6f8ca36775f92b8d7f2c3983ae31668a23b33ef3`, retaining its test rather than duplicating it. Doctor production/test files now match that upstream exactly. The reviewed cache integration remains byte-identical. Agent types, all **28 Doctor/embedded-maintenance tests** (55.18 s), canonical config/inventory checks and diff checks pass on tested commit `6c09f98ca6dc2a7f09c2cc09188cfca116c25e8c`. Published head `f47d6aa29124679494019523fb73a48ac5485680` has the identical tree `9285cbc3264d7cd72e91a47743a849cdf8d5e900`; its publication marker changes no files. The preceding 175-test and Gateway results retain the specific bindings above.
- **Current test-only binding:** tested commit `ce2a595a5d6722d61143c909c652dead784d8410`, published head `aa1883da081b2a5006c4f815e451b8523b8464bb`, identical tree `e3f3ed24b2b0d94da1fcb4cb0bb30efdece3dc5c`. Only `src/gateway/server.sessions.create-notices.test.ts` differs from `f47d6aa29124`; all prior runtime proof retains its stated source binding. The publication marker changes no files.

Exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper completion remain separate requirements. New-head CI timing remains pending. The PR is left unmerged.

@VACInc requested and guided this restoration. The imported X fixture correction was authored by @steipete in #177556; its original commit authorship is preserved.
