prs.title: feat: show original pull requests in guest conversations
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves A conversation prepared from an existing GitHub pull request has an explicit original-PR binding, but the conversation card currently discovers PRs from its local checkout branch and publication receipts. The imported checkout can therefore show no card until another publication occurs. Restricted guests also cannot use the broad PR reader, even when the imported PR is their own. This builds on the workspace association in #178233 and gives that association its existing conversation card before a new publication. ## User Impact Guests can see the original PR link, current status, and available checks in their own prepared conversation. Reloading keeps the association, and a newer remote commit continues to identify the same PR without implying that the newer files are already prepared locally. A revoked identity, inaccessible PR, or changed association clears previously displayed facts, including the sidebar badge and retained conversation summary. Ordinary readers retain their existing warning behavior for retryable metadata failures. An own-PR identity/access inspection that cannot complete clears the guest card until it can be verified again. The read requires current conversation access, the linked GitHub author identity, and current private-repository access. Guest roles remain unchanged. Publication, PR actions, source refresh, and merge permissions continue to be governed by their existing owners; this contribution adds no write action or configuration migration. ## Why This Change Was Made The canonical session reader now consumes the prepared binding directly and verifies its host, PR number, repository identities, and head branch. It reuses the existing GitHub identity inspection, metadata cache, request transport, and card rendering. Commit observations are kept separate from immutable PR identity so a legitimate remote update does not hide the original card. Only the existing subscription and check-detail methods opt into the narrow guest read. They retain current identity and session authority through response and event delivery, and use the selected authorized credential for private metadata and checks. Generic GitHub previews and service/public projections retain their existing admission and cache boundaries. Existing session-change notifications clear withdrawn facts without adding another polling or persistence mechanism. ## Evidence The baseline reader test returned no PR for a prepared original binding. The production-boundary tests cover discovery before a receipt, status and head advancement, immutable-target mismatch, private access denial/restoration, and clearing followed by an outage without reviving withdrawn facts. The guest fixture exercises real session admission and subscription ownership with fixed external GitHub responses, including selected credentials for private CI, public-cache separation, and revocation or unsubscribe during an in-flight read. The production implementation at `b52c866812f3` integrates the checked preparation prerequisite `2d12aaa6448f` while preserving published history. CI details retain the prerequisite's behavior: they describe the displayed PR head until its session snapshot refreshes. Remote formatting, strict source lint, registry syntax, i18n verification, and all 35 selected production/test compiler graphs passed on tree `46731e8374d5`. The focused integration batch passed 335 tests across 19 files in 104.13 seconds through the maintained test entry point. Commit hooks left the checked bytes unchanged. Earlier unchanged counterexamples prove that cached private facts remain paired with their original authority during refresh and queued delivery, and that explicit withdrawal clears both sidebar and conversation summaries while ordinary transient failures retain permitted stale summaries. The current integration batch exercises those owners and their controls. Prior browser scope tests also verify that ordinary cards disappear after scope narrowing while the active conversation can request its own PR. The exact target `2d12aaa6448f` still fails the original-binding counterexample (one expected failure with two passing controls); the same case passes in the candidate batch. The before/after evidence below uses both exact production UI builds with the same mocked Gateway scenario and guest scopes. Independent review accepted its source/build provenance, screenshots, reload/status interaction and final CI popover. It proves the UI consumer behavior; the live contract evidence below separately exercises real preparation, identity and GitHub access. The [previous b52 CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39484740560) has completed. Its only underlying failure is the unchanged mobile fling test (239px versus a 260px threshold), before the PR feature path is active; the aggregate CI gate also remains failed because of that result. All other selected families passed, and unselected families were skipped by the native plan. A prior hosted failure with matching relevant inputs establishes the inherited test failure class; #178669 owns its repair and has a named passing hosted result. The single exact-target rerun passed and is not counted as a fix or as negating the current red. ### Live Guest and private-repository evidence A separately qualified live integration build `45f7aa4da479` displayed the original private PR before any new publication and retained exactly one card after a normal reload. The Guest handshake retained only session read/write scopes. The original binding and prepared source stayed unchanged, and no own publication receipt was created. One external commit then updated the same card through its native subscription without a reload, changing the displayed additions from one to two. The owner made an actual CI-details request for that newly displayed head: ready, zero checks, no error. A second Guest could read the shared conversation but received no private PR card or snapshot; its CI request returned `UNAVAILABLE` with no payload after the authorized read had warmed the metadata. This proves a current requester boundary. Separate production-boundary tests hold an in-flight request and retire reader authority, and preserve the original guard through queued delivery, covering authority changes during awaited work. The live captures retain their actual integration-build identity. Independent review traced their applicability: own-PR inspection, linked-identity and delivery helpers match the public contribution; public cache, subscription and UI ownership have separate exact-`b52c8668` production-boundary and bundled-UI proof. The initial empty CI popover demonstrates visibility only. The later native endpoint result proves the private read; no running-CI transition or live mid-request revocation is claimed. A stopped auxiliary identity-status probe is excluded from the successful denial scenario, which ran separately. ### Connected transport-stage authority proof The test-only append `57ba636b5e69` addresses the prior Gold review's remaining transport-stage proof request. Four cases extend the existing registered own-PR fixture with fixed GitHub responses and the production admission, credential, metadata, subscription and CI owners intact. An unrelated service credential is present; each held check-runs request must use the selected own-PR credential. After the first page starts, the normal session writer replaces ownership and visibility. The retired-reader cases make exactly one request and deliver no private event or successful RPC payload; the checks RPC returns `UNAVAILABLE`. Matching unchanged-authority controls fetch page two and deliver the 101-check rollup or a CI result containing the last-page check. The complete nine-case fixture passed in 51.38 seconds (53.18 seconds through the maintained runner). Formatting, strict source lint, native type-boundary discovery and the selected `core-test-gateway-root` compiler graph passed on exact tree `5423e96699b2`. This append changes only that existing test file, so the earlier production, integration and visual proof remains applicable with its original recorded build identities. No production guard, live environment, or browser capture changed. ### Incognito admission The reported incognito identity comparison is unreachable for the supported session-only Guest path. The [PR reader applies the session entry filter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-read.ts#L307) before constructing the own-reader identity. The [profile filter rejects both incognito entries and incognito keys](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/gateway/session-sharing-read.ts#L421), including entries created by that profile. This preserves the existing incognito restriction for identified non-admin clients. An admin can pass that filter, but [admin scope satisfies general read](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/shared/operator-scope-compat.ts#L19), so the [session-only identity wrapper is skipped](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-read.ts#L331). Identityless and reserved Gateway-owner browser callers have [no operator profile](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/gateway/operator-role-policy.ts#L185), while the [own-reader branch requires one](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-read.ts#L338). These supported cases therefore cannot supply a reader-wrapped incognito target to the later workspace comparison. The existing [incognito policy matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/gateway/session-sharing.test.ts#L774) covers owner/viewer denial and admin/solo admission; the [PR subscription cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ba636b5e693d606d4d7f772d2e036e25175f8c/src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-access.test.ts#L285) exercise authorized incognito readers with admin scope. prs.title: fix(skills): explain malformed skills missing from CLI inventory
prs.body:
Closes #158816

## What Problem This Solves

Malformed installed SKILL.md files disappear from inventories without explaining why. Operators need the rejected file path and loading error, including when querying a running Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bounded rejection facts follow the canonical source reader, shared per-pass root reads, worker snapshots, local/remote preparation, skills.status and CLI formatters. Rejection facts participate in the worker fingerprint, so changing or removing an invalid file publishes a new inventory revision even when valid entries stay unchanged.

Current head `9173502aa874ab54661a0ea7da4d92557c474777` resolves three actual test-fixture conflicts against official main `dcaf3d92fcd208737f447fbc1eb3093182cc2c9b`. Main now uses native directory notifications with coalesced scans and safety reconciliation; its old minute polling stays retired. This integration retains main's watch-directory ownership, current fixture/binding cleanup and interface retirements. No parallel discovery owner or production test seam is added.

## User Impact

`skills list`, `info` and `check` explain rejected files in text and JSON. Valid siblings remain available and rejected files do not inflate loaded counts. Warnings update alongside main's published discovery facts. Output contains at most 64 diagnostics plus an omitted count, with bounded paths/messages and sanitized terminal text. No configuration, persisted-data migration, dependency or permission change is introduced by this feature.

## Evidence

- **Current source:** published head `9173502aa874ab54661a0ea7da4d92557c474777` exactly matches independently reviewed tree `48ea0449b5047ffaf2c318a5557316f97b16ed19` (no actionable P0–P2 findings, confidence 0.85). Pinned oxfmt 0.72.0 and `git diff --check` passed. No local fork source, tests or builds were executed.
- **Current CI is red:** [39356864131](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39356864131) completed with 44 successful, 29 skipped and 2 failed jobs, including the dependent ci-gate. Job [118413924436](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39356864131/job/118413924436) failed under pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+7bd4fdff3` in `session-snapshot-content.test.ts`, “ignores losing skill edits but refreshes when the precedence winner disappears”, with `WorkerTaskError: worker task timed out`. Actual tested merge `05ad3b946e88a43e362c041926631058d4a77d4d` has main parent `24afcdfebe8ea39e89ceb6b48e6a531fa48df8dd` plus this head. That test file has identical blob `52b3940454f0e9e117db1f904dfc0c83d7059daf` on both, which alone does not prove the failure unrelated. CodeQL passed. No confirmed causal upstream fix has been identified.
- **Focused native-watch proof:** [39357494176](https://github.com/chopin-op60/openclaw/actions/runs/39357494176), carrier `fa93f2661dd907885fd6a501e9e14fa1a562cece`, tests actual base `dcaf3d92fcd208737f447fbc1eb3093182cc2c9b` and product head `9173502aa874ab54661a0ea7da4d92557c474777`. The baseline failed for the intended missing diagnostics (44.652 s). The head passed 39 cases and failed one: the unchanged Windows-observation fixture expected one native watch call and received five. The new diagnostic-change/removal watch case passed in 1306 ms; its whole 15-case worker file took 72.346 s. Status/SDK/CLI recovery passed 8 cases (60.157 s), remote/Gateway host coverage 6 (57.396 s), and CLI formatting 11 (61.041 s). These results do not constitute an all-green owner suite.
- **Current live proof gap and bounded attribution:** the first native proof's after-head real Gateway/CLI step was skipped because the focused step failed. Its base live negative control did pass (159.873 s, including preparation and stopped-target no-fallback check). Separate secretless fork [39525756123](https://github.com/chopin-op60/openclaw/actions/runs/39525756123), independently reviewed carrier `3adb67033de709c47e4ba2ea8185454eb2995c07` (P0–P2 clean, confidence 0.91), completes the missing head live path independently and compares the unmodified watcher file on dcaf main plus the Bun consumer file on exact tested main/merge. The unmodified dcaf worker file reproduced the exact same Windows-observation failure (14 passed/1 failed, 40.139 s), establishing that fixture failure predates this feature. The exact tested main parent and merge each passed all 7 Bun consumer cases in single-file controls (66.863/47.400 s). These controls do not reproduce the original shared-run load/order and do not explain or repair its timeout; the original CI remains red. Current-head authenticated Gateway/CLI proof passed in 294.700 s including preparation: text+JSON list/info/check show the exact rejected path/error; diagnostic-only changes publish the new error, removal clears it, valid sibling data stays unchanged, and stopped explicit Gateway targets reject local fallback. The comparable base live negative control passed in 159.873 s in the first run.

The manual observer retains its 62 s observation window; it does not assert a 60 s production poll or establish a native-watch latency bound. No assertions, product timeouts, CI gates or published product source were changed to chase green. No CI rerun, empty commit or mechanical main synchronization was requested. Prior passed results retain their original heads.

<details>
<summary>Historical proof and failures retain their original revisions</summary>

- `f52bb29fdaaea8dd5d8561177fb377f6030fcf94`: CI39008934366 passed 47 jobs/29 skipped; this followed the verified canonical `89dbe8fb` three-alias repair. The new main refresh owner materially changed after that source, so these results are not relabeled as today's acceptance.

[real proof 38878385170](https://github.com/chopin-op60/openclaw/actions/runs/38878385170) passed baseline/fixed Gateway/CLI observations in 122.895/373.271 s including preparation. The first live attempt's synthetic retired default-marker configuration failure was corrected, without a product change or relaxed assertion. These cover the prior periodic worker owner.

The tested merge `854aaf15` was bound to main `a64e6cbd` plus that head. Official `89dbe8fb` fixes the exact calls and is included here; the old failure is not a current result.
- Earlier `7ac5d439` CI38501028070 passed 47/28 skipped after the `60c64838` formatting failure. Earlier unused-helper/Configure–Doctor-export failures, source reviews and native/catalog failures keep their historical attribution. Native skipping never established a root-cause repair.
- `fc30172d141771446fa2c4f98a757188528e03c8` passed 77 cases and an authenticated Gateway/CLI probe in 98.75 s, before the current worker owner and Curator retirement. Original real before/after `b1935b05e8814792587d26e5f1a770f38737ab9f` → `ccebc32b02d886f863c6b4f51975952be317af18` showed the missing/displayed warnings on the same fixture (160.14/175.41 s).

</details>

Current status: current-head native-watch and real Gateway/CLI behavior is demonstrated. The separate watcher fixture failure is inherited from unmodified main. The original shared CI Bun timeout remains unexplained and its gate is still red; one successful bounded replay is not a repair. No speculative code change or CI rerun is proposed without new evidence. The PR remains open for maintainer review.

prs.title: test(ui): combine mobile gutter geometry probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The 28 mobile transcript gutter cases repeatedly cross the browser protocol boundary to wait for a target, decode images, await fonts, and read geometry. Each sample costs four browser calls even though the last three operations all run in the same document.

## What Changed

Keep the target visibility wait. Decode the same thread images, wait for the same document fonts, and calculate the same geometry in one async locator evaluation, preserving their order. This reduces browser calls per sample from 4 to 2. Every case, assertion, viewport/theme change, media fixture, and geometry expression stays unchanged. The source census counts at least 456 samples on a successful run, so this removes at least 912 browser evaluations before counting poll retries.

## Proof

Acceptance fixed before candidate CI: compare native file F wall with the unchanged root and helper in run 39524001093 (native-settings PR; numeric baseline pending), require at least 10% improvement, retain all 28 exact passing cases, and pass the full 14 UI jobs. Report owning mock-E2E shard time and inventory separately; overlapping file spans do not add up to pipeline savings.

| Work / proof | Before | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Browser calls per geometry sample |4|2|
| Cases |28|28|
| Existing assertion statements and geometry return expression |Unchanged|Unchanged|
| File F / owning shard |69.504s / 560s|104.099s / 607s, same 99-file shard inventory|
| UI types, scoped type-aware lint, format/diff, line-cap |—|Passed|
| Independent P0–P2 review |—|Scoped-clean, confidence 0.97; runtime/timing not yet assessed|

No production changes, dependencies, startup imports, sleeps, or test-only production seams. No local E2E/build under the campaign compute budget. The existing optional captures and all media fixtures remain. Test support LOC246→246 (unchanged); production0, Solid refactor counts0. No Testbox/Crabbox lease.

Exact core-test-ui-e2e-chat type configuration passed.

Outcome: withdrawn. Run39524742830 retained all28passing cases, but fileF regressed49.77% (69.504→104.099s), so the fixed>=10% speed gate fails. The owning6/9 shard also rose560→607s. The initial assumption that fewer protocol calls would improve this flow is not supported by the measured result. No production changes or accepted performance claim.

prs.title: fix: parent handoff stalls after cancelling child tasks
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178565

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parent handoff failing after the parent cancels completion-required children, spawns a replacement, and yields.

## User Impact

The parent can continue automatically with its replacement child's preserved result after acknowledging its earlier children's cancellations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Confirmed cancellation retires the matching completion obligation in the existing acceptance collection before the cancellation owner releases its registry witness. Acceptance remains recorded, and stale turn-end receipts cannot revive the obligation. Retirement is limited to the current requesting run, agent, child session, and acknowledged terminal cancellation. The existing check still rejects unexplained missing children. Registry retention and persistent state are unchanged.

## Evidence

- A cancellation-through-handoff regression failed on unchanged production, then passed with the repair. The ordered regression follows spawn A, cancel A, spawn B, cancel B, spawn C, yield and verifies actual cancellation acknowledgments, retired A/B rows, C's wake, its preserved result, and exactly one parent continuation.
- On the conflict-resolved source committed as `887015e7c17571d885c9e1038049a3101066cb3a`, all 387 tests in six owner/consumer suites passed: requester settlement, requester-yield registry, lifecycle, cancellation retirement, session placement, and requester-yield tools. Wrapper time: 138.23 seconds across four configurations.
- All three native continuation cases passed on that same source: system, guest, and cancel-and-replace. Wrapper time: 68.62 seconds including cold preparation; Vitest duration: 63.35 seconds. This boundary exercise cannot be replaced by receipt-only unit tests because cancellation, registry retirement, wake creation, and continuation must agree.
- Core TypeScript checking, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects.

An upstream requester-origin fixture update caused a one-import conflict after publication. The merge preserves that fixture data. The repair's added/removed code is unchanged from the independently reviewed patch; the integration and owner/consumer checks above were rerun on the merged source. The committed tree was verified to match the tested tree.

The isolated real-Gateway/real-model flow remains unverified. The production-boundary regression uses native Gateway method owners and SQLite with a stub model producer. An earlier restricted local run encountered SQLite maintenance-ownership errors and later ENOSPC; the same candidate's five owner suites passed after normal macOS process probes and sufficient free space were available. No tests were weakened to obtain that result. Hosted CI on `887015e7c17571d885c9e1038049a3101066cb3a` exposed four test-only TypeScript errors in the new requester-settlement regression: indexing its single-item fixture was inferred as possibly undefined. The exact `agents-other` type graph failed locally with the same four errors. Commit `51d48f4e21632f909b304a9eda261b5c835315a2` types that fixture as a single-item tuple without changing runtime behavior or assertions. The affected type graph, all 19 requester-settlement tests, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed after the repair. Test wrapper time: 19.49 seconds; Vitest duration: 12.23 seconds. Earlier integration/owner proof above is reused because the repair changes only an erased fixture type. The hosted CI gate passed on `51d48f4e21632f909b304a9eda261b5c835315a2`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39524114697. Maintainer review remains pending.

The production repair adds 41 lines and removes 2. The tests add the cancellation and receipt-consumer regressions and move the existing requester-yield group into its own helper to satisfy the file-size limit. The new integration case needs the native cancellation, row-retirement, wake, and continuation owners to prove this failure.

prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled command announcements repeat after a transient channel failure
prs.body:
Closes #165154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled cron `command` or `script` announcement arrives more than once when the channel's send fails briefly around its scheduled time and the run times out.

## User Impact

User impact: each scheduled occurrence of a command or script announcement is delivered to its target at most once, and transient channel failures are still retried until that single delivery succeeds. When the Gateway can't tell whether an earlier attempt already reached the recipient, the run reports delivery Unknown instead of sending again.

This PR adds one optional property to the cron job's runtime state. It is a durability change, so it needs maintainer design acceptance under the [database schema review checkpoint](docs/reference/database-schemas.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes); see Durability below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #168996, main sends command and script completion announcements with a stable delivery intent keyed on the run's start time, so in-run retries and queue replay share one queued send. The native retry run of a timed-out one-shot is a new run, though, so it gets a new intent and queues the occurrence again while queue recovery still delivers the first run's send.

The announcement now admits one durable delivery intent per scheduled occurrence (job id + scheduled time + route) and reuses it across in-run retries, queue replay, and native retry runs. An existing completion receipt counts as delivered.

The admission is recorded once, in the existing `cron.markDeliveryStarted` transaction, so a retry never queues an occurrence a second time. If an attempt provably never reached the recipient and the queue no longer holds it, the admission is released so the retry sends normally. An attempt that finds queue recovery already sending the occurrence waits for that send, and retries if it fails without reaching the target. Isolated agent-turn delivery shares the same sender since #168996 but keeps its per-run intent; only command and script announcements opt in.

<details>
<summary>Durability</summary>

- **Record:** `CronJobState.deliveryAdmission = { occurrenceAtMs, intentId }`, an optional property inside the existing `cron_jobs.state_json`. There is no SQL change or schema version bump. It is stripped from the public job shape.
- **Owner and lifecycle:**
  - Written only by the live run's delivery fence, inside `cron.markDeliveryStarted`, while the job row still names that run as its live run, before the outbound queue takes custody.
  - Replaced by the next scheduled occurrence and deleted with the job.
  - Immediate (`force`/`if-enabled`) runs never write it; they track their intent in memory for the run.
- **Release:** a new `cron.releaseDeliveryAdmission` mutation deletes the record only when all of these hold, in one write transaction:
  - the stored `{ occurrenceAtMs, intentId }` still matches;
  - the outbound queue holds no entry for the intent;
  - no later run of the job has started or finished.
- **Canonical vs derived:** the record is canonical for "this occurrence has a queued send". The delivery outcome stays canonical in the outbound queue.
- **Upgrade and downgrade:**
  - Jobs without the record admit their next occurrence normally, so there is no migration or backfill.
  - Older builds keep the property but ignore it, falling back to pre-fix behavior. A downgrade while an occurrence's send is still queued can deliver that occurrence twice; see Compatibility.
- **Rollback:** revert the code. The stored property becomes inert.
- **Cost:** one extra row update per occurrence's first announcement, inside an existing transaction, plus one worker read per announcement attempt.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Accepted at-most-once windows and known limitations</summary>

In each of these cases the retry reports delivery Unknown rather than risking a second copy:

1. A crash, Gateway restart, or lost worker reply between the admission commit and the enqueue (the same class #159873 accepted).
2. A dropped-send release refused because a later run of the job, including an operator run, had already started or finished. This happens when the channel's send preparation outlasts the retry backoff.
3. A release refused because the state worker retired at Gateway shutdown.
4. A delivered occurrence whose completion receipt was pruned (24 h age, or more than 2,000 newer cron receipts) before its retry ran.
5. A forced run whose request time falls on exactly the scheduled occurrence's millisecond.
6. The outbound queue gave up on the occurrence's send. In-run attempts from every run of the occurrence count toward the queue's retry budget of 5, so an outage of a few minutes across a timed-out one-shot and its retry run can use it up. The failed record keeps no evidence of whether a send reached the recipient, so the run doesn't send again.
7. A run that finds queue recovery still sending the occurrence, when that send doesn't finish within the wait (up to 30 seconds). If recovery's send fails without reaching the target, the run retries it.

Behavior notes:

- Retargeting a job doesn't move an occurrence that's already queued: its retry delivers to the original target, and neither target's conversation records it as a result.
- The existing false "not-delivered" when a run gives up while the queue still holds the send (#162198) is unchanged.
- When an occurrence's in-run attempts all fail, the queued send follows the queue's recovery backoff. In the 90-second-timeout run below it was delivered once, at +638 s, as on main.

Known theoretical limitation, not addressed here: an attempt reads queue custody, then admits and enqueues as separate steps. If another owner delivers the occurrence and its receipt is pruned inside that window, which needs more than 2,000 newer cron receipts or 24 hours, the enqueue can queue it again. The same pruning can let a dropped-send release run after recovery completed a send queued more than 24 hours earlier. Closing either needs the shared outbound queue to check the cron admission inside its own transactions, which this PR intentionally leaves unchanged.

Out of scope: agent-turn delivery still keys on `runStartedAt`, and webhook primary delivery has no queue row.

</details>

## Evidence

### Injected outage on real Gateway builds

Local builds of this PR's head (`89c2bc3`) and its base on main (`a80c975`), packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` and installed with `npm install -g`, plus the `openclaw@2026.10.3` release from npm for reference. A test channel plugin fails every send with `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` from 20 seconds before the scheduled time until 50 seconds after. The job is a one-shot `command` job (`/bin/cat`, fixed text on stdin), created with `openclaw automations add`, announced to an explicit target, with `--delete-after-run`. Each run is observed for 15 minutes, and the state database is sampled every 5 seconds.

| Build | `timeoutSeconds` 30 | `timeoutSeconds` 90 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw@2026.10.3` | 4 deliveries: 3 queue replays (one per failed attempt) and the retry run | not run |
| main `a80c975` | 2 deliveries: the retry run sends under its own intent at +60.2 s, and queue recovery replays the first run's send at +135.6 s | 1 delivery, at +637 s (queue recovery) |
| this PR, `89c2bc3` | **1 delivery, at +60.2 s**: the retry run takes over the queued send | **1 delivery, at +638 s** (queue recovery) |

The first real-build run of the previous head (`b22f3cf`) exposed a defect, fixed in `89c2bc3`. Five seconds after the first failure, the run's second attempt and queue recovery's first retry race for the same queued send. When recovery won and its attempt failed, the run recorded delivery Unknown at +5 s and skipped its remaining attempts and its retry run. Queue recovery still delivered the single copy, at +150 s. The run now retries in that case. The two `89c2bc3` runs above cover both sides of the race: in the 30-second run the run's own attempts won, and in the 90-second run recovery won at +5.3 s and the run retried.

Redacted Gateway log of `89c2bc3`, `timeoutSeconds` 30. Times are seconds after the scheduled time `<due>`, and `<job>` is the job id. `[state]` lines come from the 5-second database samples, `[channel]` from the test channel, and `[runs]` from `openclaw automations runs`.

```text
  0.2s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 2/4 in 5s: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed
  4.2s [state] cron_jobs.state_json deliveryAdmission {"occurrenceAtMs":<due>,"intentId":"cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1:"}
  4.2s [state] delivery_queue_entries cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1: pending, retry 1
  5.3s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 3/4 in 10s: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed
 15.3s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 4/4 in 20s: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed
 30.1s WARN  cron: command delivery failed {"jobId":"<job>","err":"aborted | cron: job execution timed out"}
 30.1s INFO  cron: scheduling one-shot retry after transient error {"jobId":"<job>","consecutiveErrors":1,"backoffMs":30000,"nextRunAtMs":<due+60.1s>,"retryCategory":"timeout"}
 60.2s [channel] delivered once
 65.1s [state] delivery_queue_entries cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1: completed; job row deleted
       [runs] +0.1s error "cron: job execution timed out", delivery unknown; +60.1s ok, delivered
```

`89c2bc3`, `timeoutSeconds` 90, where queue recovery won the race:

```text
  5.3s WARN  Outbound delivery retry: retry failed for entry cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1:: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED
  5.3s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 3/4 in 10s: another delivery attempt of this occurrence ended unsent
637.8s INFO  Outbound delivery retry: drained delivery cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1: on outageproof
```

The same race on `b22f3cf` ended the run at +5.1 s with `ok`, delivery unknown: "another delivery of this occurrence was still in progress". On main, each run keys its queued send on its own start time (`<due+0.068s>` for the first run, `<due+60.1s>` for the retry run), so queue recovery and the retry run each deliver one.

### Regression tests

Fail-before runs use this PR's test files on main's production code (`a80c975`):

- `src/gateway/server-cron-completion.occurrence.test.ts` uses the real `CronService`, the durable outbound queue, and a failing-then-recovering test channel.
  - 14 cases; 10 fail on main. In the three native-retry cases main delivers 2 copies.
  - The new case is a run whose concurrent queue recovery attempt fails unsent. It records Unknown on `b22f3cf` and delivers once on `89c2bc3`. Main has no hand-off wait, so the case fails there before it starts its assertions.
  - The 4 that pass on main guard paths main already handles or intermediate failure modes: in-run attempts sharing one send, dropped-unsent retries, and day-late retries.
- `src/cron/service.delivery-occurrence.test.ts` covers occurrence identity on the scheduler clock. It fails on main.
- `src/cron/store/run-receipt-delivery.test.ts` covers release authorization (5 new cases, all fail on main).
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch-receipts.worker.test.ts` covers the wait's completed, unsent, and unknown outcomes.

Checks on `89c2bc3`, run locally against `a80c975`:

- `pnpm check:changed --base a80c975` passes `tsgo:core` and all 28 core test type graphs, lint and format of the changed files, import cycles, the database-first, sidecar, and boundary guards, and the line-cap, assertion-safety, database-worker, database-dialect, test-timeout-race, and mock-export ratchets. Its two failures come from current main, not this PR: the `OPENCLAW_*` count is 455 against a budget of 454 (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_REHEARSAL_COMMAND_STARTED_AT_MS`, added by #170374), and the dead-export scan flags four exports in files this PR doesn't touch.
- 31 related cron, gateway, and delivery test files pass: 456 tests, including `cron-delivery-outcomes.e2e`.
- A Codex autoreview of the fix (P0 to P1, with the queue claim, recovery, and agent-turn sources as context) found no issues.

### Compatibility: upgrade from 2026.10.3, then reopen

`openclaw@2026.10.3` (npm `latest`) creates the state. This PR's head `89c2bc3` then takes over the same state directory through the documented manual update (`openclaw doctor --fix`, then start), and restarts once (reopen). Main `a80c975` runs the identical scenario as a control. Same test channel and command jobs as above.

| Job on 2026.10.3 | Schedule | State when 2026.10.3 stops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | one-shot, `--keep-after-run` | delivered once, disabled |
| C2 | every 120 s | first slot delivered |
| C3 | one-shot, due after the upgrade | pending |
| P1 | one-shot, `timeoutSeconds` 3, due in an outage | one queued send, and its one-shot retry still scheduled |
| P2 | every 30 s, `timeoutSeconds` 3, one slot in the outage | one queued send |

2026.10.3 queues a new send for every failed in-run attempt. The 3-second timeout cuts each failed run to one attempt, so each failed occurrence leaves exactly one queued send.

Results on `89c2bc3`, identical on main unless noted:

- **Config and Doctor:** `config validate` reports valid with no warnings at every step. Before `doctor --fix`, Doctor stops on 2026.10.3's agent database on both builds, because schema 24 needs main's session-identity migration, and main's Gateway refuses to start on it. `doctor --fix` migrates the state database from 20 to 22 and the agent database from 24 to 27. Doctor then completes cleanly, and again at reopen.
- **Schema:** `openclaw database preflight` and `preflight-agent` from this PR and from main classify every copy the same way: 2026.10.3's state is `migration-required`, and the upgraded and reopened state is `exact`. This PR adds no schema change; the version changes come from main.
- **Jobs:** every job loads with its id and schedule. Right after startup, `automations list --all` shows C1 disabled and C2, C3, and P2 enabled. P1 had already run its pending retry and was deleted (`--delete-after-run`).
- **Queued sends:** queue recovery delivers each send that 2026.10.3 left queued once, right after startup (P1 and P2).
- **Schedules:** C2 delivers once per slot, 4 slots across 2026.10.3, the upgrade, and the reopen. C3 delivers once. P2 delivers once per run. This PR records `deliveryAdmission` for each new occurrence of C2 and P2 and replaces it with the next one.
- **Reopen:** the restart loads the jobs and their admissions, redelivers nothing, and the schedules continue.
- **Known upgrade limitation, same as main:** P1's retry run, still pending from 2026.10.3, sends again after the upgrade, so P1 is delivered twice on both builds. 2026.10.3's queued send has no occurrence identity to reuse.

2026.10.3 can't open the upgraded state (`incompatible`: state 22 > 20, agent 27 > 24). That refusal comes from main's schema versions, independent of this change. Downgrade to an older build that ignores `deliveryAdmission` wasn't rerun on the current port. Before the port, main kept the property intact on the branch's state and delivered an occurrence twice only when it took over an occurrence whose send was still queued, as described under Durability.

On current main the cron state codec still round-trips `state_json` unchanged, so an older build keeps the property. An older build also includes it in `cron.list` and `cron.get` results; no core client validates those results against the protocol schema.

### Test cost

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Apple M1 Pro. Test time is the sum of Vitest's per-test durations. The occurrence file was remeasured in this round with its new case, under heavier load (load average 10 to 13); the other rows are from the previous round (load average 4.7 to 5.9).

| File | Tests | Test time | Wall | Main (test time) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-cron-completion.occurrence.test.ts` (new) | 14 | 50.8 s | 82 s | n/a |
| `src/cron/service.delivery-occurrence.test.ts` (new) | 1 | 1.1 s | 15 s | n/a |
| `src/cron/store/run-receipt-delivery.test.ts` | 12 (+5) | 1.9 s | 15 s | 1.9 s |

The other changed test files only add `occurrenceAtMs` to fence fixtures, `immediate: false` to one call, or one seeded row to an existing receipt case. `server-cron-completion.occurrence.test.ts` costs about 3.6 s per case. Each case gets a fresh state directory from the existing outbound-queue fixture (`installDeliveryQueueTmpDirHooks`); main's sibling `server-cron-completion.test.ts` costs about 1.7 s per case. Each case drives the real `CronService`, the Gateway completion owner, and the durable queue, because the duplicate sends it pins only appear across in-run retries, queue replay, and the native retry run together. CI seconds aren't included; these are local measurements.

Gaps:

- The outage runs use a test channel plugin, not a live WhatsApp or Telegram outage.
- Which side wins the +5 s race depends on timing. The two `89c2bc3` runs cover one side each, and the new regression case pins the side that failed on `b22f3cf`.
- The reopen was a clean restart. SIGKILL during a run and downgrade to main were measured only before the port.
- Receipt eviction is simulated by aging the receipt, not by 2,000 real completions.
- The admission-to-enqueue crash window is analyzed, not tested.
- The full `pnpm check` / `pnpm test` gates weren't run locally; CI covers them.

prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway startup rejecting Feishu's documented `markdown.tables` option and applies the selected table mode across sends, replies, presentations, and previews.

## User Impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, missing reasoning follows it without duplicating it.

Accepted-prefix failures keep their receipts and do not replay accepted content. The unchanged post renderer still draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. The PR also declares `block` as Feishu's table default (see Table default).

The generated channel baseline gains two entries, `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. Core and plugin counts stay unchanged. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f659a3576b1/AGENTS.md#L96) permits narrow source-verified exceptions with a reason. This exception is not maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` (`b8952d477f0c`) seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. The proof head (`effbf8c7a8ab`) used that state, main (`29fc232d40be`) a copy. Both used fresh detached worktrees and separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both builds refuse the schema 24 agent database (Gateway exit 78) until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The cause is undiagnosed and both databases stay readable. This is compatibility evidence, not a clean upgrade. Replacement was manual, not the published updater. Credentials were synthetic and Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object is byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff has no `src/state` change or database migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof resolves `code` on stable and main and `block` on the proof head for unconfigured or legacy-only accounts. Legacy keys do not select the mode. In `auto`, stable and main route ordinary pipe-bordered tables to raw cards (`markdown.ts:25-27`, `outbound.ts:253-262`, `reply-dispatcher.ts:1289-1293` at main `29fc232d40be`, same logic at stable). Before captures show native grids. `block` retains them. Other modes convert before routing (`outbound-text-plan.ts:48-49`). Head lines use `948b2088919`.

Against main, standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables now get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, blockquoted and list-opened tables take posts, but forced-card sends bypass that guard. Main sent these shapes to cards in streams or beside a fence or pipe table. Table messages needing multiple static cards also take posts. These posts use `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments now convert raw rows to `code`. Explicit modes and size/fence safeguards apply.

A `code` default would fence those grids in cards (`outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:662`). `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:129-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

CI tested `cf49e1d3c83` merged with main `0858cc64613`. On that head 88 checks passed, none failed, 49 were skipped and CodeQL was neutral. In `checks-node-changed-1`, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` passed 20 tests, and the shard's seven other targets, six contract tests and a gateway e2e test, passed 115. Locally at `cf49e1d3c83`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`, four ratchets and five generated-file check scripts passed, and `extension-feishu` passed 1256 tests.

### Fresh Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through the production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. Captures compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49`, not whole deployments, and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Merges after `34f132a1bb49` left `presentation-card.ts`, `card-table-shapes.ts`, `markdown.ts` and `outbound.ts` unchanged, kept the off-mode projection in `streaming-update.ts`, and moved the reasoning formatter and close route into `reasoning-structure.ts` and `table-routing.ts` intact, so the three off-mode rows render through the same code. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping took upstream's latest-settlement shape, so that row rests on the proof head's regression tests, not the captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds exactly one reasoning-only post and keeps two actual receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The button is retained, not clicked. All eight images were verified in the saved comment. The captures used no Gateway, model or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Pinned to the commits named, not current-head proof.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` (before) and `08c0c469de4` (after). Before, `config validate` rejected `tables` at channel and account scope (exit 1) and `gateway run` refused to start (exit 78). After, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` removed no `markdown` key.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042)), registered sender, production components, real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610)), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.
- Regression tests for schema acceptance, account selection, off-mode finals, comment delivery, block posts, preview dedupe and presentation cards each failed before the fix and passed after.

prs.title: refactor(runtime): retire private native-owner adapters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private test controls still let browser, Gateway and plugin fixtures select alternate owners that production never selects. File Transfer also constructs duplicate command and policy descriptors only to discard their metadata.

## Changes

Choose the native Gateway client and Chrome/storage owners directly. Gateway fixtures retain real native subclasses and instance-scoped observations; browser fixtures supply actual group metadata instead of overriding selection policy. Native authentication, epochs, pairing, opt-out, framing and cleanup remain unchanged.

Move FaceTime's sole call base into its actual active-call implementation, remove private clock plumbing in Nostr and 1Password, and retire context-engine maintenance's test reset/publication bridge. Reef's production clock cut has already landed on main; this slice only retains its fixture's direct fake-system-time controls. Fixtures join the original maintenance operations and physical disposal rather than clearing their owner state. File Transfer invokes its real command and policy handlers directly through the existing lazy imports; registration remains the sole metadata owner. Both complete handler bodies are preserved.

This is an 80-path area split of a widely consumed fixture-owner migration, not a claim that 52 lines meets the residue floor. It removes **52 net production lines**, adds **53 fixture/support lines**, removes **90 private handwritten declaration lines excluded from production credit**, and shrinks one stale assertion-baseline row: **90 overall lines removed**. Moved and dedented bodies are fully counted; work already incorporated by main receives no duplicate credit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None of the production security, persistence, settlement, bounded-resource or realistic-concurrency guards are removed. No SDK/configuration/CLI/protocol/schema/dependency/permission/durability contract changes. Protected standalone Phase E memory is untouched. Tests now use the same native owners as production and must join their actual operations before cleanup; no alternate reset or completion contract is introduced.

## Evidence

Exact-head CI 39522020644 on 293dcb92896111ef435e3e4a4f769c9125d8bda6 completed successfully: all selected runtime, UI/E2E, production/test types, lint, ratchet, boundary and security jobs pass, including openclaw/ci-gate. The local compiled-worker prerequisite gaps below are retained as local limitations, not misrepresented as local passes. No CI rerun or extra push was used to obtain green.

CI39520299041 on prior head a0baad8e4d04a2514b099224d084ee835029eac8 completed with one owned failure: assertion-safety required shrinking context-engine-maintenance.ts from one grandfathered assertion to zero after this PR removed its private test publication cast. Every other selected job passed; the aggregate failed downstream. The repair deletes only that stale allowance row. The assertion ratchet passes (45.888s), all14 suppression-audit cases pass (24.141s driver), and independent incremental P0-P2 review is scoped-clean with no findings (confidence0.99). No production/test code, assertion, timeout, retry, suppression or baseline allowance is added. New exact-head CI remains required; prior-head checks are not represented as current proof.

GitHub reported CONFLICTING, so the branch was rebased once onto captured main 13c25be3c7138e387b111633f2504a5ebdc7ec62. Conflict resolution preserves main's relay wake-up void result and disconnect-error propagation; only the private Chrome supplier is removed. It also preserves Reef's already-landed native clock choice, cooldown/recovery assertions, and direct system-time controls. prs.title: fix(clickclack): retain tool completions during slow progress delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClickClack can silently lose a tool completion while native progress is enabled and the preceding HTTP request is still in flight. An older update moves from the coalescing map into the transport FIFO; a newer completion for that same line then waits for the next 100 ms flush. Draining the older update deletes the newer completion from the map.

## User Impact

Native progress now publishes the newer completion in order instead of leaving the tool line running until the final clear. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`flushQueuedLines` already owns removing entries when it transfers them from the coalescing map to the transport queue. Remove the redundant drain-time deletion, which can target a different, newer frame. The existing queue and map remain the only owners; no new state or synchronization is introduced.

Three net production lines removed, 37 regression-test lines added, two files total. This is an actual silent-drop bug fix under the size exception, not a LARGE cleanup PR. The deletion originated in #116683; this is source-qualified and reproduced, not attributed to a human-filed incident.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No reliability guard is weakened. Removing the second deletion fixes ordinary slow-transport behavior. Existing best-effort ephemeral delivery, FIFO ordering, 100 ms coalescing, visibility filtering, error isolation, 15-second HTTP deadline and one-second finalization grace are unchanged. Durable messages and activity are untouched.

## Evidence

The new regression holds the initial publish, transfers an older line update to the FIFO, queues a newer completion, releases the initial publish and advances the next flush. On the unchanged production baseline it fails solely because the third completion frame is absent; the first two frames match. With the three-line fix it passes in 4 ms.

Fresh-main production-owner and keeper proof: all 59 cases passed across progress, HTTP-client and inbound suites, serially with one worker (256.42 seconds wrapper; inbound 166.71 seconds and progress/HTTP 55.93 seconds, dominated by required worker preparation). The retained pre-fix baseline took 48.68 seconds wrapper and failed on the missing completion frame; the intervening main change removes an unrelated nested logger catch, not the bug. No retries, skips, timeouts, suppressions or expected values were weakened. Targeted strict production/test typecheck passed. Focused syntax lint, two-file line-cap ratchet, formatting, whitespace and the current 54-module plugin cycle scan passed (zero runtime cycles and no new static components). Fresh independent isolated P0–P2 review was scoped-clean with final source verification.

Mandatory lint-suppressions passed all 14 cases (10.21 seconds Vitest, 25.84 seconds wrapper). Host limits keep broad suites and full graph checks in exact-head PR CI. No live ClickClack/Gateway or external-server proof is claimed; the transport boundary is a controlled promise. No operator state, SDK/config/protocol/dependency/persisted shapes or protected Phase E memory machinery changed.

prs.title: fix(ui): sidebar wraps a single selected owner's sessions in a collapsible header
prs.body:
Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9807c098-f6cc-4153-9a32-8ae4f433fea9)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with sidebar sessions grouped by Person, selecting a single owner (for example **My sessions**) still wraps that owner's sessions in a collapsible owner header that just repeats the filter.

## User Impact

User impact: when one owner is selected, their sessions render directly in the sidebar with no redundant header or collapse toggle, and session titles line up with the left edge of the owner picker. "Involving me" and "All owners" keep per-owner headers, since those can span several people.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar projection already renders a lone catch-all section headerless; this applies the same rule to the single Person section produced by a one-owner filter. The projection now receives which owner filter is active (`owner` / `involvingMe` / none) instead of a boolean, so it can tell "exactly one owner" apart from "involving me". A previously stored collapse on that owner's section is inert while it is headerless (same as the existing catch-all behavior), so sessions can't get stuck hidden behind a header that no longer renders.

That inline section also drops empty leading status slots and offsets the list's negative inline margin, so titles start at the owner picker's edge (measured: picker and titles both at x=68). Rows with a running or draft indicator keep it at that edge, with their title after it.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI (Person grouping, **My sessions** selected, dark theme), same fixture before and after:

**Before**

![Before: owner section header with collapse toggle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9568e55c-0594-4af2-a531-b4ec38898538)

**After**

![After: sessions render inline, aligned with the owner picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ae7ecee-ac70-4917-930b-bdadb5de6690)

**After, with a running session**

![After: running session keeps its indicator at the picker edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5f34a6e-505a-486d-8c8c-148e43b8affa)

prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid long writer stalls during age retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long session-writer stalls when automatic age retention first encounters a large backlog of expired sessions. The measured main-agent store held 10,000 sessions and 1.05 million transcript events; one SQLite writer request performed 18,533 SQL statements, and PostgreSQL performed 13,902 SQL statements of archive work.

## User Impact

Automatic retention drains the same backlog in pages of at most 64 candidates, releasing the writer queue between settled pages so foreground writes can proceed. Retention policy, stored formats, and explicit exhaustive cleanup are unchanged. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cap-retention owner already yielded between bounded pages, but age retention selected every expired session. The same kick loop now carries an ephemeral age cursor, keeps its initial cutoff and model-run pressure decision, progresses past protected rows, and finishes age selection before applying the cap. Late historical writes reset that cursor; newly due entries keep their next deadline.

Selected transcript versions are read in one query per batch. Independent archive updates share the ordinary entry writer's preparation, policy, SQL builders, and committed publication; exceptional snapshot, conversation, actor, or generation changes keep the ordinary write path. PostgreSQL conflict keys are deduplicated, and aliases retain shared-window provenance across chunks. The writer implementation now lives in a focused module behind the existing entry-store exports.

Selected entries/transcript state and active ancestry are still validated at the writer effect. Changed entries survive finalization, referenced generations survive deletion, and durable archive storage precedes destructive cleanup. Transactions and eager PostgreSQL advisory locks remain intact.

## Evidence

The 500-session work-count regression fails on the base because one operation archives all 500. With this change it drains the exact expected set with bounded SQL and returned-row work. Automatic-worker tests cover protected first pages, foreground FIFO writes, protection changes, retained model-run pressure, late writes, and historical generations referenced across pages. A fixed-clock case proves age eligibility and the next deadline remain correct across pages. SQLite/PostgreSQL conformance compares sequential and batched writes, duplicate keys, shared windows, snapshots, rollback, cache publication, and absent/hot/cold transcript versions.

Fresh copies of the large corpus's complete main-agent store were used for the scale comparison. PostgreSQL was ported through the native verified port owner; all 35 retained tables matched, including all 1.05 million events. Every arm archived exactly the same **4,632 sessions** (archived-set SHA-256 `04674a0e95d6ac51cc69c0b233f25ae9aaf20f1a6b9dfc0e6857bedd22202511`). These are direct preparation/writer owner-call measurements, not end-to-end Gateway latency.

| Maximum per request | Before SQL | After SQL | Before wall | After wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SQLite preparation | 4,640 | 7 | 264 ms | 27.4 ms |
| SQLite writer | 18,533 | 8 | 1,224 ms | 39.6 ms |
| PostgreSQL preparation | 4,640 | 7 | 1,609 ms | 24.9 ms |
| PostgreSQL writer | 13,902 | 9 | 6,901 ms | 42.6 ms |

The backlog drains in 74 preparation/writer pairs: 72 full pages, one 24-row page, and the terminal empty page. Total SQL falls from **23,178 to 1,103 on SQLite**, and **18,548 to 1,177 on PostgreSQL**. Both candidate engines execute 1,103 calls; PostgreSQL's 74 additional SQL statements are its retained advisory locks. Total measured owner-call wall time falls from 8.515 s to 2.237 s on PostgreSQL. SQLite total wall time rises from 1.488 s to 1.786 s in this single contended sample, despite much shorter individual writer holds; no total SQLite speedup is claimed. The scale source precedes mechanical module moves, test-scope corrections, and the shutdown guard described below. The guard changes only retired-owner behavior; active-owner retention work is unchanged.

Final-source local checks: 59 focused tests and 10 SQLite/PostgreSQL conformance tests pass; production typecheck, all 29 test compiler groups, changed-file/type-aware lint, script lint, formatting, and the worker ratchet pass. The test-type command retains four pre-existing root-budget failures (721/724/728/728 roots); the exact base reproduces them. Live T1 SQL remains 171 and T1-compat remains 15. Fresh independent review is clean at P0–P2. Production TypeScript grows by 404 net lines, tests by 597; the module split shares the existing write policy rather than introducing another archive implementation.

The frozen local Gateway A/B preserves PostgreSQL warm-turn work at **11.333 requests / 37.333 bridge trips / 46.333 SQL per turn** in both arms (three causal warm turns). SQLite is 11.333 requests / 47.000 SQL before and 11.667 / 48.333 after; the entire difference is one cold auth-profile reader request containing three runtime probes and one auth-profile read. Other causal operations match; no retention work was added to warm turns.

| Local C64, 320 turns | Before turns/s | After turns/s | Before p95 | After p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SQLite | 4.925948 | 4.943189 | 14,594 ms | 13,886 ms |
| PostgreSQL | 4.166697 | 4.274396 | 17,525 ms | 16,038 ms |

Both paired arms completed 320/320 turns with zero errors/timeouts. These are single-run observations on a shared host, not a general latency claim. The original PostgreSQL baseline run hit the existing typed, retryable `startup-sidecars` refusal after restart, before C64. The supplemental PG pair preserves the 63 original frozen harness files and uses a separately hashed adapter that retries only that admission response for at most 30 seconds with the same request/idempotency. Baseline needed no retry; candidate needed one 500-ms retry before C64. Runtime was built at `3c1f9c2`; later changes fix a test fixture, relocate an unchanged type, and stop paging when physical close retires the maintenance owner. The final guard skips work only after retirement; active-owner work and the measured retention batches are unchanged. Build/source and adapter hashes are retained with the proof.

CI exposed two integration issues, both corrected: the membership guard fixture still named the moved writer, and a type import introduced a static cycle. The type-only fix passes Madge with zero cycles, production typecheck, lint, formatting, and independent review. The single [Blacksmith Testbox A/B](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39512008314) ran all eight cells (five passed) on an observed 4-CPU, 15-GiB host. Its 63 frozen harness files were unchanged. PostgreSQL warm causal work is identical at 11.333 requests / 37.333 trips / 46.333 SQL per turn; SQLite is identical at 11.333 requests / 47 SQL. Remote SQLite C64 completed 320/320 in each arm with zero errors/timeouts: 3.127422 → 3.479426 turns/s, p95 24.048 → 19.919 seconds. This small-fixture observation is not an attribution of general throughput gains to retention.

Remote PostgreSQL C64 remains unmeasured: both stress cells stopped before C64 at the typed `startup-sidecars` rejection. Candidate PG census hit the same restart boundary after all three valid warm windows. Original failures are retained rather than treated as throughput samples or successful runs. All eight cleanup records show closed ports and all four PG containers were removed. No second lease or provider fallback was used. The local admitted PG pair above supplies the completed C64 comparison.

CI also exercised physical close during pending archive finalization. Paging now rechecks the live owner at loop entry, so closing the database joins the existing finalizer without dispatching another page. The existing canonical and aliased-close tests fail before the guard and pass after it. Two maintenance tests now await archive publication and count archived victims rather than assuming every pass has a distinct plan object or archives work; the terminal empty page remains allowed, and pending-delivery, transcript, and rejection checks remain.

The shutdown repair and behavior-oriented assertions pass all 78 tests in the four affected maintenance files. Production types, all 29 test compiler groups, touched-file lint/format and fresh independent review pass; only the previously documented test-root advisory budgets remain. All three PostgreSQL shards passed on `f5c2569`. That CI run exposed three placement-test timeouts: the tests waited for a separate age probe that the terminal bounded page now completes directly. They now await the existing periodic scheduling boundary, retaining the sentinel archive, active-placement protection, and archive-after-stop assertions. All 14 placement tests pass locally; independent review is clean. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards also passed on the final head `f9c2378` in [CI run 39521576053](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39521576053); no conformance shard was skipped.

prs.title: fix: Feishu tool progress rows drop their tool glyphs
prs.body:
Fixes #177277

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Feishu tool progress rows show a plain tool name while a tool is running.

## User Impact

User impact: a Feishu streaming card prefixes each tool progress row with that tool's existing glyph, such as exec with 🛠️ and web search with 🔎. Process polls that were already hidden stay hidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared progress formatter already owns the glyph map and applies it only when a caller opts in. Feishu's card status line now passes `{ toolIcons: true }` at that existing call. The one-caller forwarding module is gone.

The dispatcher file is already over its line cap, and wrapping the third argument would have grown it. Epoch-millisecond normalization moved to `reply-dispatcher-time.ts` so the file does not grow. Behavior of that helper is unchanged.

Feishu was left plain when glyphs became opt-in. This follows ClawSweeper's recommendation to enable them. Whether Feishu should opt in is still a maintainer decision.

## Evidence

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.tool-glyphs.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed: 2 files, 83 tests. The glyph cases read the dispatched card content and expect `🛠️ Exec` and `🔎 Web Search`. The existing web-search and process-poll cases still pass.

No live Feishu account, so there is no sanitized before/after from a real Feishu chat. Format check and the line-cap ratchet passed on this head.

prs.title: fix(update): profile-backed updates refuse their own maintenance lock
prs.body:
Related: https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2112230438794367192
Additional report context: https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2112277658918863267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat-initiated updates can fail with an offline-maintenance error when the update requester's permissions are backed by a linked profile.

## User Impact

Profile-backed updates can continue through post-core plugin preparation instead of refusing their own permission read. Live foreign maintenance still blocks access, requester revocation still stops further effects, and rollback eligibility is unchanged. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resumed updater acquires temporary Doctor database ownership, then rechecks requester authority outside that maintenance scope before releasing it. A profile-backed authority check reads shared state and is refused by the updater's own ownership guard.

Release and drain that temporary database ownership first, then immediately recheck authority before runtime or plugin work. Stopped-service custody remains held; the next Doctor acquires its own database ownership.

The reporter described macOS 27, an npm stable install, and chat-agent `update.run` failures updating to 2026.10.4/.5. The defective ordering is present in both release sources. This PR fixes the reproduced profile-backed path; the original report does not yet establish its requester-authority subtype or full failure trace.

## Evidence

- The new resumed-policy regression fails with the original production ordering and passes with this fix. It uses real native executor, maintenance, and profile-policy owners, with package/subprocess effects mocked.
- Covers configured-owner success, profile-backed success, and revocation immediately after database ownership release; revocation prevents plugin work and publishes failure.
- 24 tests passed across the complete updater Doctor-authority caller suite and Doctor requester-authority sibling suite. Command wall time: 75.87 s, including compiler preparation; changed caller file: 27.83 s wall time. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.
- 11 additional native maintenance-contention and launcher-lifetime tests passed; command wall time: 40.18 s.
- Core and scoped CLI-update test-graph types, targeted lint/format, docs MDX, whitespace, and line-cap checks passed.
- Shared AutoReview completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 for the complete three-file change.

A full macOS managed npm driver-to-candidate upgrade/rollback replay has **not** been performed. The test constructs ordinary profile authority at the resumed-policy boundary, not a complete native delegated-worker/continuation-authority run. These are explicit proof limits, not claims of end-to-end coverage.

An additional repository-wide max-lines ratchet reported three unchanged UI suppressions in `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`; none is changed by this PR.

## Contributor credit

Reported by [@aygiyd on X](https://x.com/aygiyd).

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/1d5bc283-157e-4aad-b4f2-8c6767836e44)

prs.title: fix(plugins): sanitize public verification diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #135082

## What Problem This Solves

Public plugin-verification diagnostics can expose credential-like package text or oversized details through health/status responses.

## User Impact

Health and status diagnostics remain useful without exposing credential-like package text or returning unbounded detail. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing public projection removes private install paths, applies the canonical payload redactor, then truncates to 1,000 UTF-16 units without splitting surrogate pairs. Internal verification details remain unchanged.

The CLI regression now checks buffered readiness before rejecting an elapsed deadline, covering the ordering case requested in the P2 review. Its original 180-second wait limit, polling, health assertions and cleanup are unchanged. CLI children select Node, matching the repository's package scripts, even when the test worker runs on Bun. A real test-file conflict required integrating main; its readonly quarantine snapshots and new lifecycle regression are preserved alongside these diagnostic tests. No dependency, configuration, permission, migration or production transport change is introduced. **The upstream CLI readiness timeout still reproduces; this PR is not ready to merge.** The author is investigating the observation/console-format boundary rather than increasing the timeout.
