prs.title: fix(matrix): agent keeps seeing a room's old name after the room is renamed
prs.body:
Closes #177782

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Matrix room is renamed while the Gateway runs, every later message in that room still reaches the agent with the name the monitor first resolved for the room (`group_subject` / `conversation_label` in its conversation info) until the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: after a Matrix room is renamed, the next message the agent receives carries the room's current name, the same name a Gateway restart gives it today. Matrix room config and tool policy do not read this cached name (room config matches by room id and aliases; the read tool's opt-in name matching does its own fresh lookup) and are unchanged; settings that match on the agent-facing room name, such as a `channels.modelByChannel` entry keyed by it, now follow a rename without a restart. Which rooms are handled as DMs does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix monitor keeps each room's resolved `m.room.name` until the monitor restarts or evicts the entry (the cache holds 1,024 rooms). Member display names already have an invalidation hook: an observed `m.room.member` state event drops that member's cached display name. Nothing did the same for `m.room.name`.

This change records the rooms an `m.room.name` state event arrives for, and for those rooms the lookup that builds the agent's conversation info (`getRoomInfo(roomId, { currentName: true })`) reads the homeserver's resolved state again, once per rename. The cached first name and its cache are untouched: every other lookup, including the check that keeps a named room from being promoted to a DM (`shouldPromoteRecentInviteRoom`), still sees the first name the monitor resolved. DM-promotion eligibility deliberately keeps the first name the monitor resolved, exactly as `main` does; whether it should follow renames is tracked in #177884. The canonical-alias cache is unchanged.

Accepted edges, left as they are:
- A current-name lookup already in flight when the rename arrives can store the old name again until the next rename or restart. Member display names have the same window today.
- Redacting the current `m.room.name` event removes the name without an `m.room.name` event, so the agent keeps the previous name until the next rename, its eviction or a restart.
- A name cleared with `{"name":""}` is kept as an empty string, as a fresh lookup already does today: the agent gets no subject and the room id as its label (see Evidence).

## Evidence

Real Gateway against a real homeserver, before (`main` at `60f7650683f`) and after (this branch at `32ac0960560`, dist built at that commit), with the same isolated setup and the same harness files on both runs: tuwunel v1.9.3 (the image the repo's QA lab pins), one bot account, and one group room allowed by its room id (`groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, `requireMention: false`). The model is a local Responses-API-compatible test endpoint that answers with the room context it received. A second account renames the room between messages. Each value below is read from the model request for that message.

| Room state when the message is sent | Before: `group_subject` / `conversation_label` | After |
|---|---|---|
| named `Room Alpha` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` |
| renamed to `Room Beta` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | `Room Beta` / `Room Beta` |
| name cleared with `{"name":""}` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | omitted / room id |
| name cleared with `{}` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | room id / room id |
| renamed to `Room Gamma` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | `Room Gamma` / `Room Gamma` |
| first message after a Gateway restart | `Room Gamma` / `Room Gamma` | `Room Gamma` / `Room Gamma` |

DM classification is the same before and after. Same homeserver and model, a fresh bot account per run whose `m.direct` holds one unrelated entry, no `groups` / `rooms` entries (`groupPolicy: "open"`, so room messages mention the bot), `dm: { policy: "allowlist", allowFrom: [the sender], sessionScope: "per-room" }`. "group" / "DM" is the model request's `is_group_chat`; "mapped" means the room is in the bot's `m.direct` after that message.

| Room when the message is sent | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| named `Room Delta`, two members | group, subject `Room Delta` | group, subject `Room Delta` |
| `Room Delta`'s name cleared with `{"name":""}` | group, subject `Room Delta`, not mapped | group, no subject, not mapped |
| the same, message without a mention | not answered (mention required) | not answered (mention required) |
| renamed `Room Delta Two` | group, subject `Room Delta` | group, subject `Room Delta Two` |
| unnamed, three members | group | group |
| third member left, then named `Room Echo` | DM, mapped | DM, mapped |
| controls: unnamed two-member room / `Room Foxtrot` | DM, mapped / group | DM, mapped / group |

Tests and checks:
- `events.test.ts` feeds `m.room.name` events through the monitor's event handler into the real room-info resolver. One test checks that the agent's lookup returns the new name, then an empty name after it is cleared, while another room keeps its cached name; it fails against `main`'s source (the old name comes back). The other runs the DM-promotion check on the same resolver after renames in both directions (a named room cleared, an unnamed room named) and expects `main`'s results; it passes against `main`'s source and failed against this PR's previous head `019caae518d` (the named room whose name was cleared became promotable). `room-info.test.ts` checks that only the current-name lookup of a renamed room refetches.
- Focused suites pass on this branch: `room-info`, `events`, `index`, `join-intro`, `direct`, `recent-invite` and the handler `body-for-agent`, `room-policy`, `media-failure` suites (103 tests).
- Lanes for the changed files against `60f7650683f`: format, oxlint, extension typecheck for source and tests, import cycles, deprecated-API use and the test ratchets pass; `check:max-lines-ratchet` and the dead-code export check fail with the same output on a clean `main` checkout, naming only files outside this diff.

Not covered end to end: the `modelByChannel` name match was traced through `get-reply.ts`, not run.

prs.title: fix(doctor): report lingering Gateway killed after 5s on host shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves On Ubuntu, a host shutdown or reboot SIGKILLs a lingering Gateway (systemd user service) about 5 seconds after the stop begins, although its unit declares `TimeoutStopSec=330`. `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw gateway status` report nothing. ## User Impact Affects Linux installs that follow the documented setup (`openclaw gateway install` + `loginctl enable-linger`) on Ubuntu, on every host power-off or reboot (kernel-update reboots, provider snapshots taken after an OS shutdown). Ubuntu 24.04's `systemd` package ships `/usr/lib/systemd/system/user@.service.d/timeout.conf` with `TimeoutStopSec=5` ("Avoid long hangs during shutdown if user services fail/hang due to X.org going away too early"); current Debian packages (bookworm 252, trixie 257, sid 262) do not ship this file, and on other hosts the systemd default of 90 seconds applies. Service restarts (`openclaw gateway restart`, updates) are not affected. After this change, `openclaw doctor` (interactive and `--lint`/`--json`) and `openclaw gateway status` show a recommendation when the enclosing `user@.service` stop timeout is below 90 seconds, with the drop-in that fixes it. None of them suggests a Gateway reinstall for this finding. The fix itself stays an operator decision: it changes host shutdown behavior outside OpenClaw. ## Why This Change Was Made The service audit already reads the Gateway unit's effective `TimeoutStopUSec` from the user manager and reports values below 330 seconds (`systemd-stop-timeout`). On host shutdown that value does not decide anything: systemd stops the whole user manager under the `TimeoutStopSec` of `user@.service`, which belongs to the system manager. The audit now adds `ControlGroup` to its existing user-manager query, takes `user@.service` from that path, and asks the system manager for its `TimeoutStopUSec` under the same inspection budget. Units outside a user manager, stopped units (empty `ControlGroup`) and failed system-manager reads report nothing. Threshold and recommendation: the finding fires below the systemd default (90 s) and suggests `TimeoutStopSec=90` or longer, mentioning that 330 keeps the full drain. Requiring 330 would flag every lingering install on every distro and would ask operators to accept up to 5.5 minutes of extra host shutdown time; 90 s removes the 5 s distro cap and leaves time for the drain to settle and for final cleanup. Maintainers may prefer a different threshold; it is one constant. The suggested file name `zz-openclaw-stop-timeout.conf` matters: systemd applies drop-ins in file-name order across directories, so a name that sorts before Ubuntu's `timeout.conf` would leave the 5 s in effect. Reinstalling the Gateway unit cannot change `user@.service`. The audit owner therefore exports one predicate, `isHostOnlyServiceAuditIssue`, and the three consumers of the shared audit use it: - Doctor ("Gateway service config" panel): reports the finding, then removes it before the repair decision, so doctor does not offer a service reinstall that never clears it. - `gateway status`: prints the finding; the `openclaw gateway install --force` recommendation is printed only when at least one other finding is present that a reinstall can address. - Structured doctor (`doctor --lint`/`--json`, check `core/doctor/gateway-services/platform-notes`): includes the finding as a warning without the reinstall `fixHint` it adds to the KillMode findings. Before this, the structured lane dropped every audit code except the two KillMode codes. | Area | Change | | --- | --- | | Production | `src/daemon/service-audit-systemd.ts` +47/−2, `src/commands/doctor-service-audit.ts` +8/−1, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.ts` +5/−1, `src/commands/doctor-platform-notes.ts` +9/−2 (net +69/−6) | | Tests | `service-audit.test.ts` +65/−1 (4 cases through the real auditor), `doctor-gateway-services.test.ts` +17 (no repair offer), `status.install-hints.test.ts` +39 (real status printer: host-only alone → no reinstall advice; beside an embedded-token finding → reinstall advice kept), `doctor-core-platform-notes.test.ts` +29 (structured finding without reinstall `fixHint`), test helpers +13/−8, `install.definition-repair.test.ts` property list +3/−1 | | Docs | `docs/platforms/linux.md` +2, `docs/gateway/index.md` +2 | ## Evidence Host: Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.8, systemd 255.4-1ubuntu8.18, installed OpenClaw 2026.10.5. Proof head `d3fa91ef2ef`. Setup: an isolated test profile (`--profile nach177777`, own state directory, loopback port, no channels) with its own Gateway user unit installed by `openclaw gateway install`, so its `ControlGroup` is `/user.slice/user-0.slice/user@0.service/app.slice/openclaw-gateway-nach177777.service`. The host normally runs a local `user@0.service` drop-in with `TimeoutStopSec=90`; for the 5 s rows that drop-in was moved away for the duration of the commands (`systemctl daemon-reload`, nothing restarted or shut down), leaving Ubuntu's `timeout.conf` in effect, and restored by an `EXIT` trap. The production Gateway on this host was not touched (same `MainPID`, `NRestarts=0` before and after). - Before: installed 2026.10.5 CLI and Gateway. - After: CLI and Gateway built from `d3fa91ef2ef`, run from a package-layout copy of the build output (a unit pointing into the git checkout gets an additional, legitimate "source checkout" reinstall note that would hide what this PR changes). | `user@0.service` `TimeoutStopUSec` | Command | Before (2026.10.5) | After (`d3fa91ef2ef`) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `5s` (2026-10-19T22:48:41Z–22:49:14Z before, 22:54:16Z–22:54:46Z after) | `openclaw gateway status` | no service config finding | finding printed, no reinstall recommendation | | `5s` | `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` | no "Gateway service config" panel | panel with the finding, no repair offer, "Doctor complete." | | `5s` | `openclaw doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/gateway-services/platform-notes` | `"ok":true,"findings":[]` | `"ok":false`, one `warning` finding, no `fixHint` | | `1min 30s` (local drop-in, 2026-10-19T22:53:39Z) | all three | – | no finding, no panel, `"findings":[]` |
After, 5 s: openclaw gateway status (excerpt, d3fa91ef2ef) ```text Service: systemd user (enabled) Service file: ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-nach177777.service Host desktop: disabled Service config looks out of date or non-standard. Service config issue: Host shutdown or reboot stops user@0.service within 5s, cutting short the Gateway drain and cleanup; set TimeoutStopSec=90 or longer in /etc/systemd/system/user@0.service.d/zz-openclaw-stop-timeout.conf (330 keeps the full drain). (user@0.service: 5s (systemd system manager)) Config (cli): ~/.openclaw-nach177777/openclaw.json Config (service): ~/.openclaw-nach177777/openclaw.json Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=19877 (service args) Runtime: running (pid …, state active, sub running, last exit 0, reason 0) Connectivity check: ok ``` No line of the output contains `reinstall` or `gateway install`. Before (2026.10.5), the same command on the same unit printed no `Service config` lines.
After, 5 s: openclaw doctor --non-interactive (panel excerpt, d3fa91ef2ef) ```text ◇ Gateway service config ─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ │ │ - Host shutdown or reboot stops user@0.service within 5s, cutting │ │ short the Gateway drain and cleanup; set TimeoutStopSec=90 or longer │ │ in │ │ /etc/systemd/system/user@0.service.d/zz-openclaw-stop-timeout.conf │ │ (330 keeps the full drain). (user@0.service: 5s (systemd system │ │ manager)) │ │ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ``` The run ends with `Doctor complete.`; no Gateway service repair or reinstall is offered (the other `doctor --fix` hints in that run concern the test profile's plugin and skill config). Before (2026.10.5), the run had no "Gateway service config" panel.
After, 5 s: openclaw doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/gateway-services/platform-notes ```json {"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":68,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/gateway-services/platform-notes","severity":"warning","message":"Host shutdown or reboot stops user@0.service within 5s, cutting short the Gateway drain and cleanup; set TimeoutStopSec=90 or longer in /etc/systemd/system/user@0.service.d/zz-openclaw-stop-timeout.conf (330 keeps the full drain). (user@0.service: 5s (systemd system manager))"}]} ``` Before (2026.10.5): `{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":65,"findings":[]}`. At 90 s, after: `{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":68,"findings":[]}`.
Original shutdown on this host (2026-10-19, CEST, OpenClaw 2026.10.4) ```text 18:09:36.640 systemd[1]: Started snapshot-poweroff….service - /usr/bin/systemctl poweroff. 18:09:37.017 systemd[1053]: Stopping openclaw-gateway.service - OpenClaw Gateway... 18:09:38.141 [gateway] Unable to read systemd stop timeout; user manager openclaw-gateway.service: systemctl show exited 1: Failed to get properties: Transport endpoint is not connected ; using 90000ms default. 18:09:38.141 [gateway] Retaining the startup shutdown budget of 325000ms because the current supervisor stop timeout could not be confirmed. 18:09:38.157 [gateway] active-work drain settled; beginning server close 18:09:42.141 systemd[1]: user@0.service: Killing process … with signal SIGKILL. 18:09:42.152 systemd[1]: user@0.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL 18:09:42.153 systemd[1]: user@0.service: Failed with result 'timeout'. ``` In that run the drain had already settled and no data loss was found; with turns or writes in flight the Gateway would be killed mid-drain.
Tests (VPS, Node 24, `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, head `d3fa91ef2ef`): - `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.install-hints.test.ts`: 16 passed (78.5 s cold, 10.7 s warm). Counter-check with only `status.print.ts` reset to the previous head: the new "alone" case fails (`expected … not to match /\bgateway\s+install\b/`), 15 passed. - `src/daemon/service-audit.test.ts` + `src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts`: 37 + 42 passed, 15.4 s wall (warm). Counter-check from the first revision (production files reset to `origin/main`): 3 + 1 failures. - `src/flows/doctor-core-platform-notes.test.ts`: 9 passed, 13.5 s wall. Counter-check with only `doctor-platform-notes.ts` reset: the new case fails (`expected [] to deeply equal [ ObjectContaining{…} ]`). - Other tests that import the changed modules (`status.print.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`, `doctor-maintenance.service-inspection.test.ts`, `doctor-service-audit.egress.test.ts`, `install.definition-repair.test.ts`, `doctor-platform-notes.launchctl-env-overrides.test.ts`, `doctor-health.update.test.ts`, `doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`, `doctor-gateway-services.writer-order.test.ts`, `update-command-doctor-writer-order.test.ts`): passed. - `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` on changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base origin/main`: clean. - `codex review --base origin/main`: on `3da273248d2` it flagged that `doctor --lint`/`--json` dropped the new finding (fixed in `d3fa91ef2ef`); on `d3fa91ef2ef` it reported no findings. Gaps: no host shutdown was performed for this PR; the shutdown log above is from the original observation. The `gateway status` heading "Service config looks out of date or non-standard." is unchanged and also precedes host-only findings.

prs.title: fix(ui): PR links use the checkout repo across conversation messages
prs.body: Related: #165849 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes bare PR/issue references opening the checkout repository when a conversation consistently discusses another project. A real session running from an OpenClaw checkout linked `PR #126` to `openclaw/openclaw`, although its explicit GitHub links identified the KPMG repository. ## User Impact Shorthand now uses the single repository identified by explicit links in the loaded assistant conversation. Mixed-repository conversations leave unqualified numbers unlinked. Explicit repository names and matching links in the same paragraph retain their destinations. ## Why This Change Was Made #165849 corrected references beside a matching explicit link in one paragraph. This extends repository context across loaded messages. Code, quoted examples, reasoning, user messages, and tool output do not establish that context. The checkout remains the fallback when no conversation repository is known. Loading more history can change the inferred context; transcript bytes and stored session metadata are unchanged. ## Evidence Cropped screenshot from the reported conversation, published with the user's authorization. The crop excludes identities, sidebars, workspace paths, and unrelated messages. **Before — wrong checkout repository:** ![Actual conversation before: PR 126 resolves to openclaw/openclaw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0ad3010-1efc-4ddd-8abb-cbc6bbeeb162) **After — the same persisted message now resolves to the KPMG repository:** ![Actual conversation after: PR 126 resolves to the KPMG repository](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47334eb9-2f64-4379-a7dc-fa4a49421fa2) Verified in the installed native Control UI after the running task and turn maintenance settled. The Gateway served the new bundle, the client reconnected, and the original paragraph’s accessible link destination was `https://github.com/break-through-tech/kpmg-1f-ai-research-intelligence-agent-for-business-insight-translation/pull/126`. - Regression reproduced before the fix: the pane supplied `openclaw/openclaw` instead of the conversation's repository. - Focused tests on final head: **125 passed**, including navigation, mixed repositories, named checkout overrides, and persisted/streaming/sidebar rendering. - UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, line-cap checks, and UI builds passed on both the installed base and current main. Final focused run: 4 files, 125 tests (Duration 7.11s (tests 32%, transform 25%, import 20%, environment 17%, worker 5%); CI time is pending). - Independent Codex Auto Review of the final patch: no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is source review; the tests and live observation provide separate execution evidence. ### Hostname-case correction (October 19) The case-sensitive GitHub prefilter now accepts hostname case variants before the existing URL parser validates and normalizes the target. The existing chat-pane regression uses `https://GITHUB.COM/acme/research/pull/126` and verifies that a later `PR #126` links to `acme/research`, while explicit checkout references, mixed repositories, and session changes retain their behavior. - Red on the previous head: the pane incorrectly selected `openclaw/openclaw` (1 failed, 38 passed). - Green after the correction: **149 tests passed across 4 files** (repository inference, chat pane, Markdown rendering, GitHub references); two shards, 12.47s wall time. prs.title: improve(ui): use the shared page header on every built-in page
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Built-in pages used three different header treatments. Sessions and Plugins had the stacked hub header, Agents had a smaller stacked variant, and Dashboards, Usage, Automations, Systems, Activity, Meetings, Apps, and Portals put a small centered title in the toolbar row with the description floating underneath.

## User Impact

Every page in the sidebar's **Pages** list now opens with the same header as Sessions and Plugins: a large left-aligned title, the page description with a **Learn more** docs link, actions on the right, and route tabs where the page has them. Settings pages and Memory import keep their existing toolbar-row title.

## Why This Change Was Made

`HubPageHeader` is now the single owner of built-in page headers. It gained optional tabs (Sessions, Worktrees, and Plugins keep theirs), optional docs links, a subtitle override for filtered states (the Automations session filter), and a `wide` variant. Pages whose body spans the full column (Agents, Dashboards, Activity, Apps, Portals, Systems) use `wide`, so the title stays on the content edge instead of a centered 1120px column. The header's mobile inset moved from `settings.css` into its own stylesheet, so pages that don't load the settings styles get the same 12px edge.

- **Systems:** the page header shows "Systems". The selected machine name moves to the workspace toolbar as an `h2` ("Select a machine" when nothing is selected).
- **Activity:** the description now stays visible in Live mode. Activity's and Apps' titles are now real `h1` elements.
- **Mock dev server:** `pnpm dev:ui:mock` now answers `backup.status`. Without it, `/systems` crashed with "Panel failed to load".

## Evidence

Before/after screenshots of all nine updated pages (1440×900) plus mobile (390px) and wide (1920px) passes were inspected and delivered in the work session linked below. This publishing session could not upload images to GitHub, and the requester approved landing without embedding them here.

Checks on this head:

- `pnpm tsgo:ui`

- UI e2e: `native-page-header-clearance`, `systems-workspace`, `activity-session-feed.capture`, `settings-layout`, `chat-side-panel-clearance`, `plugins-hub-navigation`, `worktrees`, `session-kinds`: 8 files passed

Test updates: the toolbar-row clearance cases moved from Usage to Memory import, which still uses that layout. Usage and Automations joined the mobile hub geometry cases that Sessions uses. Systems tests read the toolbar `h2`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain metadata errors after late startup refreshes
prs.body:
Related #177455 — draft proposal; production reachability is unproven.

## What Problem This Solves
The focused in-process tests demonstrate that a late attachment refresh can overwrite a newer publication failure, allowing a subsequent auth or skills change to clear the original error. Whether this overlap occurs through a shipped Gateway entry point remains unproven.

## Proposed Behavior
For the tested overlap, the original publication error stays visible without extra metadata refreshes or change broadcasts. A later successful publication can still restore metadata normally. This is not yet a demonstrated production user impact.

### Maintainer decision requested

[The merged lifecycle simplification #173092](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173092) explicitly accepted completion-order or temporarily cached optional metadata diagnostics. This proposal narrows that tradeoff for a newer publication failure using the existing state field, without restoring event-version machinery. **Should a terminal publication error remain authoritative until a successful publication?** No maintainer decision on this distinction is recorded yet.

Focused tests establish metadata-runtime failure retention and recovery; a running Gateway trace of this startup ordering and its client-visible effect is still outstanding, as noted in [the review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177771#issuecomment-6278513882). This is a draft proposal, not an owner-approved change.

### Production ordering counterevidence
Further source tracing found that normal HTTP startup [awaits request-runtime readiness before post-attach model publication](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2977d820ffffb3e7591c2e41aa96638b288784f8/src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts#L194). Request-runtime initialization awaits the initial lifetime sidecars, which await metadata attachment; the config reloader starts later. Normal hot reload does not reattach this context. No naturally overlapping generic replacement caller was identified in a bounded investigation. The current tests deliberately delay attachment refresh across that unproven boundary; they must not be presented as a running-Gateway reproduction. An alternative embedded/reentrant path has not been ruled out. Keeping this draft until both reachability and the maintainer decision are resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made
Let attachment catch-up initialize availability only while no publication state has been observed. Publication events retain authority; existing catch-up warnings and recovery behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence
- Both new resolve/reject regressions fail on the base: subsequent skills/auth changes cause three refresh calls instead of one.
- Frozen final source: three related test files, 48/48 passed with runner exit 0. Tests use the real metadata runtime and cover original-error identity, no extra broadcasts, successful recovery, reverse ordering and shutdown.
- Core production and selected Gateway test typechecks, focused lint/format, line-cap, state-schema and three Gateway boundary checks pass.
- Canonical autoreview was attempted on the same cloud host but its Codex connection was rejected with HTTP 403; no valid automated review was produced. A separate parent-thread code/lifecycle review was performed. Full repository tests were not run.

AI-assisted implementation and tests, all executed in a managed cloud environment.

prs.title: fix(memory): report unexpected loss of remote file watching
prs.body:
Related: #177686

## What Problem This Solves
Remote memory file watching can stop silently when its subscription ends without cancellation.

## User Impact
Operators get a warning with a Gateway restart hint when remote watching is lost. Normal shutdown stays quiet; the existing index synchronization fallback remains available. This does not fix the local macOS watcher incident reported in #177686.

## Why This Change Was Made
Report unexpected subscription completion alongside the existing unavailable/error handling, without introducing a retry policy or changing subscription ownership.

## Evidence
- The unexpected-completion regression fails on the base; final manager suite: 12 passed. Tests cover the warning, real SQLite index refresh, and quiet resolve/reject cancellation with retirement joining preserved.
- Workspace client suite: 7 passed; doctor contract tests: 10 passed. Focused lint, extension source/test typechecks, formatting and diff checks pass.
- The broader changed-file checker reports max-lines failures in three untouched UI files and dead-export findings in untouched src/agents files; no claim of a fully green repository check.
- Canonical autoreview was attempted but the cloud proxy rejected its Codex connection (HTTP 403), so it produced no valid review. Manual code/lifecycle review found and addressed the missing successful-cancellation test; automated review remains a validation gap.

### Real remote-transport behavior proof

Addressing [ClawSweeper's proof request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177754#issuecomment-6278343617), this was executed on the unchanged PR head `f8aaf9210409ed69a598587eb5ea5ee4483d4dbc` in a managed Linux cloud environment.

The shipped Gateway, official `openclaw node run --commands workspace.memory` CLI, workspace client, WebSocket/node duplex transport, native Memory worker and Gateway-owned SQLite index were used. Separate test HOME/state/config directories and a read-only file-transfer policy confined access to a synthetic workspace. No user profile or external provider credentials were used. A scratch diagnostic plugin only obtained the normal persistent manager through the Memory SDK, performed initial indexing, and exposed `await manager.close()`. It did not replace `files.watch`.

**Observed:** beta reached SQLite automatically through the real subscription; injected clean worker completion produced the warning and refreshed pending gamma content; normal cancellation produced no additional warning and returned only after the worker exited.

<details>
<summary>Method and redacted execution trace</summary>

The runtime was built from the exact PR head with the repository's `qaRuntime` profile. Gateway and node connected over loopback using normal product pairing, command authorization and workspace path policy (`policyVersion: 2`). The cloud watcher reported native events unavailable and used the product's 30-second polling fallback; this does not claim inotify coverage.

Command structure (addresses, authentication values and device IDs omitted):
```sh
git switch --detach f8aaf9210409ed69a598587eb5ea5ee4483d4dbc
OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=8192 \
  pnpm exec node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime

# Separate HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH per process.
pnpm openclaw gateway run --port "$PORT" --bind loopback
NODE_OPTIONS="--import=$PROOF/node-fault.mjs" \
  pnpm openclaw node run --host "$LOOPBACK_HOST" --port "$PORT" \
  --display-name SyntheticProofNode --commands workspace.memory --auth-from-env

pnpm openclaw gateway call remote-watch-proof.run \
  --params '{"action":"start"}' --timeout 60000 --json
# Write beta; read Gateway SQLite until it changes, without search/manual sync.
# Write gamma; signal the observer to end only the --watch-files child's stdin.
pnpm openclaw gateway call remote-watch-proof.run \
  --params '{"action":"close"}' --json
# Start a fresh manager/worker, then close it normally for the cancellation control.
```

The node-only observer wrapped `child_process.spawn` without changing its command/arguments. For the actual `--watch-files` child, a marker triggered only `child.stdin.end()`; the observer recorded the child's real `close` event and whether its process still existed. It did not resolve a fake subscription promise or emit the warning. The diagnostic plugin and observer were outside the repository; production source was unchanged.

Normalized, redacted trace; SQLite capture timestamps below are result-file persistence times, not exact transaction-commit timestamps:
```text
Initial Gateway SQLite:
memory/notes.md | memory | alpha original remote proof notes.

2026-10-19T22:13:26.502818Z  Write beta; no search or manual sync.
2026-10-19T22:13:55.548048Z  Capture persisted after ~29s; real subscription updated SQLite:
memory/notes.md | memory | beta remote edit delivered through production watch transport.

2026-10-19T22:14:02.407527Z  gamma file mtime: pending change written BEFORE EOF.
2026-10-19T22:14:02.475Z     observer: fault-injection-stdin-eof pid=49711 inotifyFds=0
2026-10-19T22:14:02.492Z     observer: native-watch-worker-close pid=49711 code=0 signal=null procExists=false
22:14:02 UTC [Gateway] [memory] workspace watcher ended unexpectedly; restart the Gateway to restore remote file watching
22:14:03 UTC [Gateway] [memory] sync: indexing memory files
2026-10-19T22:14:16.243034Z  SQLite capture persisted:
memory/notes.md | memory | gamma clean-EOF fallback must refresh the Gateway SQLite index.
```

No search/manual sync was invoked during beta/gamma validation. A Gateway-local decoy file was absent from the remote index. Gamma was written before EOF: this demonstrates the completion-triggered fallback, not continued watching after subscription loss.

Normal cancellation control, using a new real worker:
```text
2026-10-19T22:14:22.117Z     native-watch-worker-spawn pid=50597
2026-10-19T22:14:38.393057Z  Call diagnostic RPC, which awaits manager.close().
2026-10-19T22:14:42.228Z     native-watch-worker-close pid=50597 code=null signal=SIGTERM procExists=false
2026-10-19T22:14:42.312026Z  CLI exitCode=0; response {"closed":true}
Unexpected-end warning count: before=1, after=1, delta=0.
Worker exit preceded the successful close response.
```

Scope: real same-host loopback Gateway/node/worker integration with explicitly injected stdin EOF. This does not reproduce the linked local macOS incident, cross-machine network failures or Electron behavior. No separate ready-frame capture was taken. Authentication values, IPs, device IDs and non-public endpoints are excluded from this excerpt.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

When a Mattermost account's pending pairing queue was full, both slash commands and model-picker interactions still rendered a pairing reply using the empty code returned by the store. Users saw an empty code block and an unusable `openclaw pairing approve mattermost ` command even though no request had been saved for them.

## User Impact

Declined users now receive the existing generic `Unauthorized.` denial instead of dead-end pairing instructions. Users with a real pending request continue to receive their valid code and approval command.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Added a small pairing-reply resolver that treats missing, empty, and whitespace-only codes as no pairing reply and skips `buildPairingReply` entirely.
- Applied it to both affected Mattermost entry points: slash command authorization and model-picker interactions. When there is no code, each path falls through to its existing generic denial.
- Added unit coverage for valid, undefined, empty, and whitespace-only codes, plus handler-level regressions for both surfaces. The handler regressions fail against the old implementation.
- Typed the authorization mock against the real `authorizeMattermostCommandInvocation` function and supplied a complete denial fixture, addressing the review's P2 type-safety finding.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/pairing-reply.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-model-picker.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.send-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 35 passed.

prs.title: fix(web-readability): preserve block boundaries in text mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` with `extractMode: "text"` used Readability's `textContent`, which concatenates adjacent block elements when the source HTML is minified. Headings, paragraphs, and list items were returned as run-on strings such as `HeadingParaalphabeta`, while markdown mode and the other text extractors preserved block boundaries.

## User Impact

Text extraction from minified pages now keeps one block per line. Models and downstream parsers receive readable headings, paragraphs, and lists instead of words fused across block boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Always serialize Readability's parsed article content with `htmlToMarkdown`, then use the shared `markdownToText` renderer for text mode.
- Export `markdownToText` through the private `openclaw/plugin-sdk/web-content-extractor` subpath used by the bundled extractor.
- Added a regression using minified HTML with paragraphs and a list. It fails on the base with the exact glued output and passes with the shared rendering path.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test extensions/web-readability/web-content-extractor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 8 passed.
- Base-red: the new regression returns `readability.Second paragraph` and `alphabeta` against the old `textContent` implementation; it passes after this change.
- `pnpm check:changed` — formatting, core/extension lint, line-cap, import-cycle, SQLite-worker, dialect, plugin-boundary, SDK export/surface, and related guards passed. The command remains blocked by environment/baseline failures: tsgo requires GLIBC >= 2.29; existing max-lines/dead-export findings are in unrelated `ui/` and `src/agents/` files.

Closes #178499

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

Current author head: `b61e37141b7760e0933aedd671d9ee9f73a78b55`. The latest ordinary merge consumes official main `6f04e7abd6c645c3c030663e7fd369834998d8ac`, including the adopted native-touch timing repair #178645. The earlier ordinary merge at `230fee6b` consumed the official cached-title repairs #178510 and #178474 from `79262d05`. The existing feature patch is preserved. Validation below attributed to `688e9537` or `230fee6b` remains prior-head evidence; current integration checks and CI are recorded at the end.

- Removed the vacuous channel-route test and duplicated mocked direct-Wiki allow/deny cases requested by review. The real-owner Wiki suite and owner-backed retrieval/denial proof remain.
- Fixed the actual `no-shadow` lint failure by reusing the existing anchor constant.
- Kept main's current session-send input parsing, target checks and authorization owner; removed two unnecessary extracted helpers. The proposal's send delta is now the propagation of existing scoped access into `runWithScopedSessionAccess`.
- Local focused authority validation: 43 tests passed. A follow-up covering Wiki and session-send siblings passed 94 tests; it resolves the temporary test-spy import failure from removing the duplicate cases.
- Core typecheck, touched-file type-aware core/extension-test lint, format, config baseline generation/check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the complete candidate found no actionable P0-P2 defect. Product acceptance remains pending.
- [Exact-head CI run 39419691631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39419691631), candidate `688e953733d74df955d692de1892f4711c76ebcc`: the previous UI boot-budget and all five core-lint lanes pass. The remaining failed [mocked-Gateway cold-load case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39419691631/job/118617967183) is the same intermittent failure already recorded on official main `6a2e9a1f9ea002b14e2847e8ca89e2b90c37f59d`, [run 39401671859 / job 118557975798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39401671859/job/118557975798): `expected 'New session' to be 'Synthetic cold-load conversation'` in `chat-cold-load-anchor.e2e.test.ts`.
- The green CI on the integrated base `d53309cd8ea4d0761fec3ac81ae73290b81e569a` ([39417964143](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39417964143)) **skipped UI E2E**, so it is not a passing control for this case. A later full main run [39415536071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39415536071) passed the mocked UI shards, consistent with an intermittent failure; the branch is not being rerun or changed merely to chase green.
- This candidate changes no UI files. Between the earlier main failure and the integrated base, the inspected chat-pane changes belong to informed persistent-stream approval #177941, not cached-title ownership; the cold-load test and transcript snapshot owner are unchanged. A local pinned-main replay reached a different, earlier `Worked for 3 minutes` wait timeout; that local result is **not** presented as reproduction of the CI cached-title assertion.
- The known main CI failure follows CONTRIBUTING's existing-main-failure policy: no unrelated test-only repair, assertion weakening, budget increase, or duplicate CI-fix PR is added here. The remaining CI acceptance is a maintainer decision, not a claim of green CI. Final exact-head readback: run 39419691631 completed. All three PostgreSQL shards and the other product/static/test jobs succeeded; the only failed leaf is the known-main cached-title case above, plus its dependent aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. No new or unclassified failed leaf remains. This is contributor-complete with an inherited intermittent CI failure, not all-green CI.

## Real behavior proof

The existing isolated published-stable upgrade proof remains valid for the unchanged native-memory path: OpenClaw 2026.10.3 persisted SQLite -> candidate offline Doctor/source Gateway with the real native memory worker. It proves same-channel retrieval, exclusion of other channels/accounts/workspaces/providers/agents, denied sibling mutations, and route reassignment denial without external APIs or live Slack.

The newly added direct Wiki proof covers the previously missing consumer boundary through the production query adapter and real Gateway disclosure owner. It uses synthetic search input; it is not a live external-provider or customer-data proof.

## Evidence boundaries and remaining work

Not claimed: the public packaged updater/install path as a whole, live Slack/customer traffic, external model calls, cross-OS behavior, or broad benchmarks. The prior reviewed head has successful hosted CI; current-head CI is tracked below. Current 47-file canonical autoreview and focused integration checks are complete. Maintainer acceptance of the retrieval-only channel config/SDK contract remains a separate product decision. No production runtime or account configuration was changed.

### Adopted official cached-title repair and current integration

The title repair is adopted upstream through #178510 (`58c3f35e0e1894bc837871e5ca58b47be78031f2`) and #178474 (`fe739f62fcfa1f91dfaa25f7a710292da190822c`). Duplicate #178478 is closed and #178470 is resolved. This branch consumes those official main commits; it adds no separate UI patch.

The feature patch-id is unchanged across this merge. All 46 non-baseline feature files retain their exact contents; the baseline keeps the same one-row deletion against main. 43 focused integration tests passed; applicable prior canonical review and real-owner proof are retained. On the same official UI sources, the original synthetic cached-tail Chromium case passed with en-US/CPU4 (6.831 s case, 21.85 s wrapper), retaining the official pending-hydration/first-title assertions and the original title/scroll checks. Local diagnostic setup was restored exactly after testing. No assertions, timeout, CI routing or runtime configuration were changed by this contribution.

**Previous integration CI (`230fee6b`):** [39469559363](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39469559363) completed **FAILURE** on `230fee6b17bc5fa24706b349f02268237feec8c9`: all 111 jobs terminal, 85 successful / 24 skipped / one failed UI leaf and its dependent `openclaw/ci-gate`. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. prs.title: refactor: keep private execution helpers with their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal execution and provider owners carry one-consumer helper modules and private argument frames that duplicate facts already held by their only caller.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change or migration. Public SDK, protocol, CLI and config contracts, lazy imports, authorization boundaries, and normal lifecycle settlement remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep private work with its existing owner instead of rebuilding forwarding packets. Fold the Crabbox command leaf into its existing lazy CLI action, localize provider/channel execution helpers, and remove three test-only production inspection seams while keeping tests at existing production entry points.

The complete branch removes **527 net production lines** (+1,800/-2,327), excluding tests and support. Thirty-one paths change; no generated files, dependency changes, persisted shapes, or new shared abstractions are involved. Author simplification found no further safe reduction without changing retained behavior.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The private Discord factory no longer handles a missing runtime: its sole public caller requires and always supplies that runtime. The frame comes from the completed factory relocation (#45660) and cleanup (#174322), not a human-reported missing-runtime incident. An invalid untyped internal construction is no longer silently accepted. Normal runtime diagnostics and all network/auth checks remain.
- No other guard or recovery behavior is removed. Request-time captures, normalized-provider precedence, payload identity, credential authority, abort ordering, HTTP body release, and ordinary write-capable settlement are retained.

## Evidence

Fresh independent whole-branch review found no actionable P0–P2 findings, with final source verification. The normalized-provider regression, public Commander boundary, native QuickJS worker lifecycle, session admission/settlement, iMessage approvals, Discord lifecycle and Gateway abort suites passed. Prompt-prefix stability passed.

Final packet formatting and targeted native typecheck passed. Focused typed lint passed for the repaired and unaffected owners. The full selected lint attempt also reported ten unchanged SDK declaration-resolution diagnostics in Tlon, OpenRouter, WhatsApp-call and Ollama discovery; the earlier QuickJS owner has one unchanged WorkerTaskChannel declaration-resolution diagnostic. These are investigated local limitations, not a claim that all lint passes or that hosted CI failures are inherited. No casts, suppressions, retries, timeouts, skips or baselines were added to hide them.

The final serial packet passed all **324 tests across 19 owner files**. The mandatory suppression audit passed all 14 checks; four selected wrapper/import-closure checks passed (18 unrelated cases excluded by the name filter, with no test skip changes). Line caps and whitespace passed. Runtime and Madge checks both reported **zero cycles**.

Exact-head PR CI is the broad proof. Local proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, one worker, and nice priority; no live provider/channel/device claim is made.

## Exact-head CI: inherited-failure exception

Run [39519464436](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39519464436), attempt 1, completed on head `c1383329980e1fa75f521545dfc36b7c46ed9891`. The native inherited-only admin exception applies; CI is red, not relabeled green.

| [checks-node-changed-compact-large-14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39519464436/job/118960109288) | The restart integration test's original-owner case receives zero announcement calls. One serial focused comparison passed all 35 cases on the PR head, then reproduced this exact failure on current main `59332fa85d39b73455814e1fb184d303914eef60` (34 passed, 1 failed). The failing test and restart recovery owner/coordinator/sweeper are unchanged by the PR in actual CI checkout `3543d2cc5068108f9a21534540f3db720cd5c55a`. |
| [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39519464436/job/118966698147) | Aggregate of that single failed leaf. All other planned jobs, including production/test types, lint and independent security-fast, passed. |

The coordinator flake ledger and six recent completed scheduled-main runs were checked before attribution. The classifier returned unknown because changed compact shards have no same-named main job; the explicit current-main reproduction supplies the evidence instead. No test, timeout or assertion changed, no CI rerun, and no underlying scheduling fix or flakiness claim. Both local replays used isolated state and one worker. The earlier passing head replay alone is not claimed as a repair.

prs.title: fix(discord): batch queued messages by thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
When a user sends several Discord messages while an earlier turn is still running, the next follow-up turn should be able to see the whole compatible queued intent instead of only the last message. At the same time, Discord transport must keep every inbound event flowing into core admission so active-run steering and `/stop`-style control inputs are not delayed behind a local plugin queue.

Related: openclaw/openclaw#103287

## Summary
- remove the previous Discord-local same-session batch lane from `message-run-queue.ts`
- keep Discord inbound work event-keyed through the plugin queue so each message reaches core admission promptly
- carry Discord batch message IDs through typed preflight/finalized context fields when the dispatcher has an aggregate context
- add core follow-up queue support for aggregate `messageIds` on collected follow-up runs
- project collected queued message IDs into execution context as `MessageSids`, `MessageSidFirst`, and `MessageSidLast` while keeping `MessageSid` as the current/latest message
- add a focused Discord dispatcher boundary proof that two debounced Discord source messages become one processed turn with both source IDs preserved

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

### Ephemeral Gateway + qa-channel proof on pushed head

Verdict: PASS on pushed PR head `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`.

This is the new qualifying proof path requested by ClawSweeper: it starts an ephemeral Gateway child, enables the real `qa-channel` plugin against the QA bus, uses the `mock-openai` provider, injects three inbound channel events, and verifies that the two queued channel messages become one executed provider turn.

Committed proof test:

- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/qa-channel-queued-message-ids.e2e.test.ts`

Redacted runtime evidence from the test:

```json

  "transport": "qa-channel",
  "provider": "mock-openai",
  "gateway": "ephemeral-child",
  "receivedMessageIds": [
    "qa-msg-pr122238-active",

    "qa-msg-pr122238-queued-last"
  ],
  "collectedProviderRequestCount": 1,
  "queuedNeedlesPresent": [true, true],
  "sameSessionForAllIngressMessages": true,
  "executedTurnChannel": "qa-channel",
  "executedTurnChatId": "pr-122238-qa-channel",
  "secrets": "none"
}
```

What this proves at the boundary ClawSweeper asked for:

- `qa-channel` receives three real inbound channel messages via the QA bus, including explicit provider message IDs.
- All three inbound messages resolve to the same Gateway session.
- While the first turn is active, two later source messages are queued through core admission.
- The queued pair is collected into exactly one mock-provider request, and that executed request contains both queued source bodies.
- This path does not mock Discord preflight or processing; it exercises a complete mock-channel/mock-provider/ephemeral-Gateway run.

Current-main merge evidence:

- Pushed PR head: `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`
- Current `origin/main`: `39b39ca6eec684f0675cd93500646b578f6e7021`

- Merge status: conflict-free `ort` merge

Additional code cleanup in this proof update:

- Removed Discord preflight `batchMessageIdFirst` / `batchMessageIdLast` fields.
- The finalized context now derives `MessageSidFirst` and `MessageSidLast` from the aggregate `batchMessageIds` array, avoiding duplicate Discord-only preflight fields.


prs.title: fix(codex): use stock broker network profile
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted Codex sessions may need to read an explicitly selected runtime, repository helper, or credential mount outside the workspace. The generated filesystem profile needs a way to grant those specific reads.

## User Impact

Operators can add literal absolute paths through `appServer.networkProxy.readOnlyPaths`. These grants are read-only and do not change project-root write permissions or network defaults. No migration is required when the setting is omitted.

## Implementation and Review Repairs

The paths are added to the existing Codex permission profile and participate in its fingerprint. Invalid paths, filesystem roots, special profile keys, traversal, glob patterns, control characters, and surrounding whitespace are rejected instead of silently granting access to a different location. POSIX backslashes remain literal filename characters.

The four actionable Clawsweeper code/documentation findings are addressed: whitespace-altered grants are rejected; both references explain private-target reachability; examples use synthetic broker hosts and paths; and restrictive limited-mode/local-binding-disabled test coverage is preserved alongside a separate broker-profile case. A regression also covers literal POSIX trailing backslashes.

The broker documentation explains the existing explicit opt-ins: `mode: "full"` permits all HTTP methods at otherwise allowed destinations, while `allowLocalBinding: true` skips the resolved-private-address guard. An allowed hostname can consequently resolve privately even if a literal private IP is denied. Repository authorization remains the broker's responsibility; any required private-address isolation must be enforced outside this profile. Neither setting is enabled by default. This documentation repair does not claim permission-owner acceptance of a deployment's broader network scope.

## Evidence for This Repair

- Reproduced three failing cases before repair: leading whitespace, trailing whitespace, and a literal POSIX trailing backslash.
- All 65 focused Codex configuration tests passed after repair, including unchanged restrictive-profile coverage.
- Scoped lint, supported extension typecheck, formatting, documentation examples, generated configuration baselines, and diff checks passed.
- Reconciled the branch with upstream base `1cb69ee6228d0da0bfb79b37530e1e2ff92583ae` through a normal merge, preserving the original contribution's ancestry. The eight net-changed files were verified byte-for-byte against the tested/review target.
- Local Auto Review was attempted again but returned HTTP 401 without producing a review. Josh Lehman explicitly opted out of the unavailable local review for publication and requested Clawsweeper re-review. No completed local review or current-head CI success is claimed.
- The live OCE evidence below is retained from the original PR, pinned to its original revision. It was not rerun on this repair. No deployment or PR merge is claimed.

### Historical runtime evidence from the original PR

At `29fe7bd8da2c5cce125c8b21b0238673c81feeb2`, 169 focused Codex configuration tests, targeted formatting/lint, diff checks, and independent source review passed. An OCE ARM64 image built from this exact OpenClaw commit passes the generated-profile stock Codex 0.156.0 Git clone/fetch/push proof, broker authorization denials, explicit-domain and non-allowlisted network denials, and home-file isolation checks. The image also passes stock binary provenance/inventory verification.

[OCE #445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/445) tracks integration. A local k3d Agent runs the stock image with the expected full/local-binding/exact-broker/read-path configuration. After correcting the broker origin and certificate to the full Kubernetes service FQDN, a real model turn cloned, fetched, committed, and pushed through the broker. Independent GitHub readback verified the exact single-file proof commit and parent; the disposable branch was then deleted with normal Git and independently confirmed absent. Native tool history also records HTTP 403 `blocked-by-allowlist` for an unlisted destination. An unbound repository read failed at broker credential acquisition with Git exit 128; the live receipt does not identify a specific internal broker handler. Slack transport was not tested.

## Credit

Continues kevinlin-openai's original implementation while preserving its commit ancestry.

prs.title: fix: interrupted child sessions ignore new messages after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a child session (for example a visible session spawned with `sessions_spawn`) that was mid-run during a Gateway restart rejects every later human message. The UI shows "Interrupted before the agent started it" and no run ever starts.

## User Impact

After a restart, the next human message in an interrupted child session starts a normal turn again. Children are still not replayed automatically, and the parent still owns finishing its task, as documented. Main sessions keep their existing resume-before-new-input behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Turn admission saves a restart-recovery delivery claim for the interrupted turn, on child sessions as well as main sessions. Main-session restart recovery resumes that claim before new input runs, but it deliberately skips child, cron, and ACP sessions (`not_main_session`). The subagent registry settles the child's run instead of replaying it. Nothing ever consumes the claim on the child session. User-turn admission then threw `RESTART_RECOVERY_CLAIM_CHANGED` for every new message, because an aborted claim from channel or WebChat ingress could only be transferred when it came from `control-ui`.

User-turn admission now retires an aborted claim when the session is not a main-session recovery candidate, using the same preconditions as the existing Control UI transfer: no pending final delivery, no ambiguous `before_agent_reply` state, and no delivery receipt. The retired source is recorded as terminal, so it cannot resume later. Explicit stop and cancel outcomes are unchanged. The skip itself stays as it is: the docs and #172017 state that human ownership and dashboard nesting do not make a child a main-session replay candidate.

<details><summary>Incident trace (team-metal, 2026-10-20)</summary>

- 21:06 shutdown: `skipped restart recovery session … reason: not_main_session` for the child; its run was aborted for restart.
- 21:07 startup: the subagent registry settled the child run as interrupted. It could not restore the parent continuation (`lacks its original operator source`; see follow-ups).
- The child row kept `abortedLastRun: true`, `status: interrupted`, and `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` set to the dead run, with ingress `channel`.
- 23:18 and 23:21: two human messages passed source claim and both barriers, then failed admission silently. Both pending inputs remain `interrupted` and unconsumed.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-subagent-custody.test.ts` ("starts a human follow-up in a child interrupted by a Gateway restart"). It drives real `chat.send` admission, real chat dispatch, the real restart-recovery claim controller, and the subagent registry; only the embedded model runner is mocked. Its state is the post-restart child row and the registry row taken from the incident.
  - Base: red. The run never starts, and the test times out waiting for the agent run.
  - Fix: green. The run starts, `abortedLastRun` clears, the old source is recorded as terminal, and the follow-up takes native child custody.
- Sibling suites pass: restart-recovery-claim (all five files), reply-turn-admission recovery, runreplyagent e2e, and main-session restart recovery.
- `pnpm check:changed`: core and core-test typecheck, changed-file lint, format, the line-cap ratchet, and the other changed-file guards pass. Three failures are inherited and do not touch these files: new max-lines suppressions in three `ui/src/pages/*` files, the core test shard root budget (`agents-tools`, `gateway-root`, `infra`, and `plugins-platform` are over 720), and an unused export `PluginRuntimeResolver` in `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts`.
- `$autoreview` (branch vs `origin/main`, P1): no actionable findings.

Gap: this was not reproduced against an isolated Gateway restarted in the middle of a real model turn. The proof stops at the owning admission boundary.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- After a restart, a human follow-up row (`replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer` with `preserveCompletedRun`) intentionally drops the completed task's `operatorRecoverySource` and binds only in-memory authority. After a restart, the private parent continuation for that row cannot be restored ("Subagent restart recovery lacks its original operator source"), so the parent is never told about the interruption. Persisting the follow-up's own source changes authority, so it needs a separate decision.
- A child whose interrupted turn also left `pendingFinalDelivery` or a `before_agent_reply` checkpoint still rejects new input, the same as before this change.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2cc7dd60-526b-4ecd-8dc0-8fe0e7fd733f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/105aa7fb-a366-4c8e-addf-7e152101ab20)

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove unused private arguments and the branches they kept alive across plugin metadata, Doctor diagnostics, agent bookkeeping, local-audio inspection, and one-shot setup. Tests use canonical module spies or the real production boundary instead of runtime-only test controls. Remove unread result members without removing their live computations or error handling.

This is the core/packages area of the widely imported core/plugin helper family, split from its extension area to keep CI attribution bounded. The campaign's area-split rule waives the usual size floor for these slices. Net production reduction: **217 lines**; tests/support shrink **49 lines**; **65 paths**. No UI, dependency, generated schema, SDK export, or database schema/durability/retention change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Retired one-shot history/pending-proposal controls are gone after the interactive fallback retirement in #139140; actual TUI history, verified inference, approval and terminal-error behavior stay. No current caller can request the abandoned prompt branch.
- The deferred-install existing-token selector has no producer after #154160. Normal explicit/config/SecretRef precedence and token generation/persistence remain; the unreachable deferred-only error is removed.
- Maintenance-lane prewarming has no producer after #176916. Foreground cold/cancellation/error handling and the underlying workers remain; no current boot path requested that extra prewarm.
- The old expected-handle recovery argument originally protected real ownership in #132122. #175837 completed the cutover to registered-owner recovery; the present diagnostic never passes it. Current injection still checks registered ownership and live authority, including after callbacks. No live recovery guard is removed.
- Plugin bundled-fallback disabling was introduced as a synthetic alternative in `8ddd9b8aac69`; callers use default/true. Keep the full bundled resolution/secret-input policy. A future private caller cannot turn it off without defining a real contract.
- Required-file hash diagnostics became orphaned when #131442 moved their actual caller to the cache-file reader. The remaining caller always passed false. File hashing/staleness/error handling and the cache reader's real diagnostics remain.
- Workspace-compatibility and async effective-plugin selectors have one live value. Keep the actual fingerprint check and effective selection unconditionally, rather than retaining private bypass/full-report modes nobody selects.
- Failed-ingress health has no worker-context supplier, so its cache branches never ran. Keep the measured Gateway cache from #171320 unchanged, including expiry, invalidation, and errors; the Doctor reader uses the same worker query and missing-database behavior.
- Systemd prompt/title overrides have no suppliers. The same label and all Linux, service-owner, confirmation, sudo, and manual-recovery behavior remain. Private tool-model/auth-message overrides likewise had no suppliers; configured policy and real failover classification stay.
- Test-only Doctor, upstream-monitor, planner, and local-audio substitutions now use their canonical dependencies. Keep currentness, read-error preservation, restrictive model policy, bounded subprocess output, idle/CAS/durable-event checks and settlement. Real local-STT repairs from #104210/#124699 remain, with actual Windows/PATH/model and backend-observation assertions retained. Only an unnecessary synchronous-lookup aggregate microtask yield disappears.
- Finalizer target-tracking forwarding is unread after #133260 moved the real accounting to its owner; execution tracking and compaction accounting stay. Unread fallback/log result fields and the unused two-argument random-integer form are removed; fallback text, stderr output bounds, errors, cryptographic randomness, and the public token/redaction APIs stay.
- Verbose descriptions keep the real 320-character boundary and UTF-16 safety. Tests exercise that real limit instead of a private small-limit override; compact descriptions retain their independently live limit.

These are unused-argument cuts, not permission to discard incident fixes or security/durability guards. No live failure scenario is intentionally dropped.

## Evidence

- All production callers were checked across core, packages, extensions, UI, and scripts; SDK/barrel escapes, introducing changes, and in-flight activations were checked before each cut.
- Fresh-main targeted native typecheck passed for the original selected changed roots. Sixty-three cleanup file blobs are identical to the individually reviewed/proved collector; the one overlapping Doctor file preserves main's newer JSON-with-comments parser and was replayed separately. The additional direct Doctor test is covered by the CI repair below.
- Focused owner/sibling tests were run serially with one worker and isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state. Retained groups include plugin metadata/status/hash fixtures, Doctor/token/repair sequencing, agent diagnostics/liveness, real upstream reader/transcript fixtures, system-agent behavior, ingress health, description boundaries, crypto/slug/telemetry, and gateway-client projection.
- Latest local-audio proof passed 27 selected cases across four files, including the nine-case production language-forwarding table; real PATH/PATHEXT and backend-observation checks remain. Its initial fixture type error was fixed without casts or weakened assertions. No live GPU/provider claim.
- Final fresh-main Doctor replay: 139 cases passed across seven focused suites. Typed lint, formatting, whitespace and all 14 lint-suppression cases passed. Runtime and Madge cycle checks both reported zero cycles.
- Independent full-area review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The original 64-file cleanup is a strict subset of that reviewed candidate: two duplicate meeting-clock files already owned by #178666 were removed before publication and are not counted here. The additional direct-test repair was independently reviewed with no actionable P0–P2 finding.
- CI repair: run `39506351602`, job `118917140531` (`check-test-types-core-5`), found a missed direct Doctor test still passing the removed private `pluginProviderIds` option. This is attributable to this PR. Remove only that argument member; retain the same JSONC fixture, warning/model/fallback assertions, and byte-exact catalog preservation. Its selected native typegraph and real canonical-discovery test passed; no replacement mock, production change, weakened assertion, or test growth.
- Named-gate integration: run `39511959813`, job `118936204233`, found an inherited unbound `HealthCheck.repair` extraction introduced by newer main in #178767. Main `e6b866d3adb8` reproduced the exact lint failure; four strengthened existing repair-flow cases also failed before the fix. Direct main repair `5d80482379b3` binds the method to its check. This branch now includes that fix after a conflict-free rebase; both cleanup commits are patch-identical by range comparison, and all 65 PR file blobs are identical to the previous head. The selected changed-root native typegraph and all 10 focused Doctor flow/startup cases pass on the integrated head. Prior-head CI remains prior-head evidence; the new exact head must pass its own hosted gates.
- PR CI on the exact pushed head is the broad gate. No full local typecheck, build, broad suite, E2E, live service mutation, or CI rerun was used.
