prs.title: fix(agents): restore saved history for fresh Claude CLI sessions on a native login
prs.body:
Related: #154716

Supersedes #156600 (builds on its account-fingerprint approach; its author is credited as co-author on the commits)

Note: #154716 carries the `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision` and `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` labels and this PR does not fix the existing-session gap described under Gaps, so it uses `Related:` and should not auto-close the issue.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Claude CLI conversation on a native Claude login loses its saved history whenever its Claude session is replaced or lost, because OpenClaw cannot name the login's owner and so refuses to replay it.

With the `claude-cli` backend on a native Claude CLI login and no OpenClaw-managed credential, the history boundary cannot build an owner fingerprint. `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` writes no `cliHistoryBoundary`, `prepare.ts` turns the missing writer into `rawTranscriptReseedReason: "auth-unknown"`, and `loadCliSessionPromptContext` refuses to seed saved history into any fresh CLI session (replacement session, cleared binding, lost native transcript). On the base commit every native turn logs `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown` (scenario 1 below). On the author's own install (a file-backed native login) all 301 session entries carry an empty boundary.

The guard exists so saved history never crosses to a different account. This change keeps that property and adds the native login as an accepted owner only when the operator opts in (`plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true`), only when Anthropic attests which account its credential belongs to, and only for the environment the Claude process is actually started with. Without the opt-in, nothing changes: the native login has no owner and saved history stays refused, as on main.

## User Impact

Nothing changes for an install that does not opt in. With `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true` on a Gateway host whose Claude CLI login is a readable credential, a fresh Claude session for a conversation that started after the opt-in gets its saved history reseeded again, with or without the `anthropic:claude-cli` profile. If the login changes, is revoked, is selected differently by the child environment, or Anthropic does not attest it, saved history is refused, as the contract table below lists.

What an operator who opts in sees differently (without the opt-in, OpenClaw never reads the native token for history recovery and makes no profile request: row 35 below, 0 requests, the same prompt as current main):

- The Gateway makes one `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` per access token it has not attested yet, with the token Claude CLI itself would send there (834 ms measured once on a real login). Later turns on the same token make no request. `openclaw agent --local` starts a new process per turn, so it makes one request per turn.
- A turn prepared within ten minutes of its access token's expiry runs without saved history, because Claude CLI rotates the token before it accepts the prompt (measured below). The next turn is offered history again.
- A turn whose writer may replay saved history fails with `CLI history authority changed before execution` if its login changes, or cannot be attested, between preparation and the prompt reaching Claude, instead of sending that history to another account. That is every turn of a conversation the native login owns, fresh or resumed, except a turn prepared within ten minutes of token expiry, which runs without saved history. Conversations the native login does not own are never refused because of it.

One new plugin config key, `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` in the Anthropic plugin's config schema, default `false`. No schema migration. Conversations that already have history and no recorded boundary stay fenced, including conversations written before the opt-in (see Gaps).

## Why This Change Was Made

Main documents opaque CLI logins as unable to authorize replay (`docs/gateway/cli-backends.md`, "History account boundaries"). That is right when the login is only a profile name or a local record. It is wrong when the Gateway host holds a readable credential and Anthropic can say which account it belongs to. An acceptable owner has to cover the no-profile install (the bundled backend sets `autoSelectAuthProfile: false`), must be bound to the credential rather than to the `.claude.json` account record beside it, must be rechecked wherever saved history is sent to Claude or a turn becomes the owner's history, must survive Claude CLI's own token rotation, and must not put a network request or a subprocess on every transcript write.

## The change in one sentence

Once the operator opts in, the native Claude login's owner is the account uuid Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint returns for the exact access token the child Claude would use, attested asynchronously at preparation and after the run, and rechecked synchronously at every spawn, prompt send, prompt hook answer that carries the turn's private context, and coverage commit against an in-process attestation cache keyed by a per-process HMAC of the token.

Shape of the whole PR against base `cab0df90f87` (seventeen commits, all signed): 23 production files +865/-143 (21 TypeScript files and the Anthropic plugin manifest), 12 test files +1785/-134, and three docs files (the contract paragraphs and the config baseline counts and hash); 38 files, +2658/-283 in total (two for the CI fix below). The attestation lives in `provider-auth-claude-compat.ts` (credential read, profile request, cache), `cli-credentials.ts` (the resolver seam), `history-boundary.ts` (async attestation, synchronous rechecks, background re-attestation, refresh window), `execute.ts` (one post-run settle call) and `prepare.ts`. The owner confirmation inside worker transactions is in the turn commit and transcript report paths in `src/config/sessions` and in the SessionManager metadata worker in `src/agents/sessions`. The check on the prompt hook answer is in `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`. The opt-in is declared in `extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.json` and read by `isNativeCliLoginAttestationEnabled` in `cli-credentials.ts`.

Simplification (`08f918dca3a`, on `13078e36c7e`): one Keychain reader instead of two (the shipped reader returns the same results); no unused `env` and `now` parameters, dead cache delete, duplicate installation-target merge or report-worker target move; `history-boundary.native-login-metadata.test.ts` folded into `history-boundary.native-login.test.ts`, `cli-history-owner-probe.test.ts` cut to one case (deleted in the second pass), restated cases dropped; `prepare-native-history.test.ts` now releases its prepared backends (it leaked one session sharing read per case). Against `13078e36c7e`: 14 files +240/-694 (production +41/-88, tests +199/-606).

Second pass (`d688a94fc48`): a native login lookup that throws (an unreadable config root) means "no owner" in one place, `readNativeOwner`, not only in the worker probe answer. So the host actor-memory check keeps such rows uncovered instead of failing the write, and a turn without saved history runs on; one with saved history is refused as before. `cli-history-owner-probe.test.ts` became one native-login case (RED11, RED12). Against `0f431092595`: 5 files +37/-41.

Third pass (`27ff3327776`, `8d822e2632d`): 75 production mutations found three unpinned paths: the host actor check on incognito sessions (a case in `history-boundary.incognito.test.ts`), interrupted inputs on a refresh-due turn, and a parseable Keychain item without a usable login. Six cases whose every caught mutation a kept case on the same path also catches are gone, and `resolveCliChildEnv` drops a `baseEnv` parameter no caller passed, so that extraction is a pure move. Against `5fffaf68380`: 5 files +93/-75 (production +6/-6).

Design:

- The attestation runs only when the operator opts in: `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true`, declared in the Anthropic plugin's config schema with default `false` and a UI hint that names the endpoint the token goes to. `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` checks `isNativeCliLoginAttestationEnabled(provider, params.config)` before it resolves the native owner, so without the opt-in no credential is read for history recovery, no request is made and the turn is prepared exactly as on main (`auth-unknown`). The rechecks below exist only on writers whose owner was attested at preparation. The run's config is read per turn, so turning the opt-in off takes effect on the next turn.
- `attestClaudeNativeLoginOwner({ env })` (`src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-claude-compat.ts`) reads the access token the CLI would use under `env` with the CLI's own precedence (Keychain first on macOS, bounded non-interactive lookups, tri-state so only `security`'s item-not-found exit 44 lets `.credentials.json` stand; then the file). It sends that token, and nothing else, to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` (`Authorization: Bearer`, `redirect: "error"`, 3 s `AbortSignal.timeout`, the process global fetch, so the env-proxy dispatcher OpenClaw installs at startup applies). Claude CLI 2.1.283 calls the same URL with the same header (bundle excerpt below). The owner is `uuid:<account.uuid>` from the response. No owner on any failure: network error, timeout, non-2xx, a body without `account.uuid`, no credential, or an access token already expired. The error is dropped, not logged. The `.claude.json` account record is no longer read.
- The cache maps `HMAC-SHA256(key, token)` to the attested owner, with `key` from `randomBytes(32)` per process, at most 64 entries, only in memory. A token belongs to one account for its whole life, so an entry can stop matching (rotation, logout) but never start naming someone else. Only successes are cached. Nothing about the token is persisted; the stored boundary keeps only the existing `cli-history-v1` fingerprint over `["native-login", "uuid:<account>"]`.
- `readClaudeNativeLoginOwner({ env })` is the synchronous recheck: it rereads the credential and returns the cached owner for that exact token, or nothing. It never touches the network. The seam stays `resolveNativeCliLoginOwner(backendId, env)` (now asynchronous, returning `{ owner?, refreshDueAt? }`) plus `readAttestedNativeCliLoginOwner(backendId, env)` for the synchronous checks; both return nothing for backends other than `claude-cli`.
- Preparation awaits the attestation for the environment the child will start from (`resolveCliChildEnv`, under the run's skill env snapshot, as before). Spawn, prompt send and coverage commits call the synchronous recheck, so the per-turn Keychain budget stays at 10 lookups for a readable item.
- Claude CLI rotates its access token itself, before it answers `initialize` and so before the prompt is sent, once the token is within 5 minutes of expiry (bundle: `now + 300000 >= expiresAt`; probe below). Two rules follow:
  - A turn prepared with a token that expires within 10 minutes runs without saved history (`writer.replaysHistory === false`; `prepare.ts` treats it like `auth-unknown`), and still covers its rows.
  - A boundary check on a turn without saved history that sees a token this process has not attested starts a background attestation of it. Coverage waits until it settles and stops for good if it names another account. A turn carrying saved history refuses an unattested token outright.
- After the child exits and before the turn's rows commit, `writer.settleNativeLogin()` awaits any background attestation and, if the prepared token had entered the refresh window, attests whatever token the child left behind.
- Worker coverage confirms the owner from inside the worker's write transaction. The host no longer decides before it dispatches the command. When coverage is about to advance, the worker puts a probe (a `SharedArrayBuffer` cell) on a transaction admission request (turn commits) or on the commit admission of the write (transcript reports). The host answers the cell with the live owner check, synchronously, right before it grants that admission, and the worker reads the answer after the grant. A missing answer, a missing owner check or a check that throws means the owner does not hold. On a mismatch the rows commit and coverage is not advanced. The check runs once per coverage commit, so the Keychain budget is unchanged. The in-process path checks inside its transaction as before.
- A resumed Claude session also receives saved data: durable reference context from the transcript and the conversation's interrupted inputs. So any native turn whose writer replays history counts as carrying saved history at spawn and prompt send, fresh or resumed, including a conversation's first turn. A turn prepared inside the refresh window runs without saved history and receives no interrupted inputs either.

- Claude asks for the turn's private context (interrupted inputs, durable reference context) through its `UserPromptSubmit` hook after it has received the prompt, so the hook answer is the last place that saved data leaves OpenClaw. The stdio transport writes each answer through a closure the Claude runtime returns, called synchronously at the final write. The host passes the bundled Claude runtime a host-internal `assertPrivateInputCurrent` (set only for a native-login writer, like the forwarded auth credential: it is not part of the plugin SDK `CliBackendExecuteContext` type, `ClaudeCliExecuteContext` in `cli.runtime.ts` declares it), which runs the turn's full `assertCurrent` (on a native login: reread the credential and require this process's attestation of that exact token for the same owner). The runtime calls it before it sends the prompt and again when it answers a `UserPromptSubmit` hook with `additionalContext`. If the second check fails, Claude receives an empty hook answer and the saved context is withheld. The public execution context is unchanged from main.

- SessionManager appends committed by the metadata worker take the same host owner check. The probe rides on the command's one transaction admission and the host answers it before it grants. Coverage facts that ask for the check advance coverage only on a confirmed answer, so a write path that cannot ask keeps its rows and leaves coverage where it is. Writers whose owner cannot change during the run (a static credential or a named OAuth account) carry no owner check.
- What a mismatch does depends on what is at stake, as before: a turn that may carry saved history is refused before Claude receives it; a change after the prompt was sent withholds the turn's private context from the prompt hook answer; that change, or one on a turn prepared inside the refresh window, lets the turn run, and its rows are kept but not covered, so coverage stops and the next turn is refused that history until `/new` or an empty reset.

`docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` states the contract: what is attested, the request and its timeout, fail-closed cases, what is held in memory and what is persisted, the synchronous rechecks, the refresh window, and the restart limitation.

## What changed in the port onto current main

Base moved eight times by merges of main (port commit `5f246effb0c`); latest: `53ff5be1f3b` (`79506514289`), `57501c047f7` (`051bf6fa4d0`), [`12b692d36b0`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/569a03394261b75cbfbee17303b673a8c94996a4/head-12b692d3/README.md) (`cab0df90f87`). Contract unchanged.

CI fix (`9385a46b41d`): `test/gateway-openai-compaction-replay.e2e.test.ts` (selected by this PR's changed files) fails on main since 07b59a0976d (#177050): it persists internal retry prompts, and #136236 still appends the retained compaction instruction to the next invisible retry, so the model got it twice. Once its internal prompt is persisted, the retained copy is dropped (`session-prompt-state.ts` +4, one unit case +12). The e2e test fails 3/3 on main and on the previous head, passes 3/3 with the fix ([bisect and runs](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/4f3045c9fa6da01d97ed9dd4711ae1dc8cd2ad49/head-57501c04/README.md)). The seventh merge (`57501c047f7`): two conflicts with main's #178173, kept beside it; gates, RED1 to RED14 and harness rerun; check failures as on main.

The sixth merge (`53ff5be1f3b`): main's #177839 folded `live-session-fingerprint.ts` into `createCliLiveSessionCapability` in `cli-live-session-registry.ts`, so the warm-reuse `nativeLoginOwnerHash` field moves there unchanged (RED13).

Earlier merges (`5fffaf68380`, `0f431092595`, `13078e36c7e`, `9134c56b403`) resolved import lists, `cli-runtime.test.ts` (main's rewrite absorbs the private-input tests) and generated baselines.

The first merge (`5fa23ce27fc`, `5f246effb0c`): `execute-process.ts` is identical to main, which checks private history at send time itself (async `assertReadable`), so the native-login recheck stays in `execute.ts` and `execute-plugin.ts`; the metadata worker takes main's `bindSqliteWorkerDatabase` shape with the owner probe re-applied on top; `history-boundary.test.ts` uses `history-boundary.test-support.ts` on main's admission fixture.

## What this PR decides, and why

The question is what may authorize native replay: the local account record beside a readable credential, or an identity bound to the credential itself. This PR binds the owner to the credential with Anthropic's own account lookup (option C below), and only for an operator who opts in. Every other install keeps D, main's behavior.

| | A: local account record | B: `claude auth status` | C: authenticated profile request (this PR) | D: keep native replay fenced |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Owner source | `.claude.json` `oauthAccount.accountUuid`, read from the child's environment while a credential exists | the same record, as the CLI reports it | the `account.uuid` Anthropic returns for the exact access token the child would use | none |
| Credential for account B beside a record for account A | owned by A: history replayed to B's credential | owned by A | owned by B: A's history refused | refused |
| Bound to the executing environment | yes | yes, if run with the child env | yes: attested for the child env at preparation, rechecked at spawn, send and every coverage commit | not applicable |
| Cost per turn | 10 Keychain lookups (readable item) | one subprocess per check, 135 to 1673 ms measured | the same 10 lookups; one request per new access token (834 ms measured), none for a token already attested | none |
| Token rotation by Claude CLI | owner unchanged | owner unchanged | the rotated token is attested before the turn's rows are covered; a turn prepared inside the refresh window runs without saved history | not applicable |
| What it sends where | nothing | nothing | the access token, to the Anthropic endpoint Claude CLI itself sends it to | nothing |

Why C:

- A and B cannot detect the mismatch. Run against synthetic files with the real Claude CLI 2.1.283, `claude auth status --json` reports a fake token as logged in and returns whatever account the record holds; editing the record moves the same credential from account A to account B ([identity/claude-auth-status-probe.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/final/identity/claude-auth-status-probe.txt)). The CLI's own refresh path never rewrites `accountUuid` or `emailAddress` ([identity/cli-bundle-excerpt.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/final/identity/cli-bundle-excerpt.txt)).
- Anything keyed on token material alone changes owner on every refresh: one real refresh rotated both the access and the refresh token while the account stayed the same ([identity/refresh-rotation.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/final/identity/refresh-rotation.txt)). C keys the cache on the token but takes the owner from Anthropic, so a rotation needs one new attestation, not a new owner.
- The profile request is the one Claude CLI makes itself. The bundle's `AFe(e)` is ``gt.get(`${BASE_API_URL}/api/oauth/profile`, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${e}`, ...}, timeout: 1e4})``, validated against `{account: {uuid, email}, organization: {uuid}}`. OpenClaw already sends Claude OAuth tokens to the same host for usage (`src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.claude.ts`, `GET /api/oauth/usage`).
- D keeps native conversations losing history when their Claude session is replaced. It stays the default: C sends the token to Anthropic, so it runs only for an operator who sets `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin`.

## Contract table

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Native login, `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` unset or `false` (the default) | no owner, no credential read and no request for history recovery, history refused: unchanged from main (row 35) |
| Opt-in removed after a covered turn | no request; history refused; the stored boundary becomes `unknown` (row 36) |
| Opt-in set after a conversation already has rows | those rows stay fenced; a conversation started after the opt-in recovers (row 37) |
| The cases below assume `attestNativeLogin: true` | |
| Native login, no profile selected, credential attested | owner named, history seeded into a fresh session |
| Native login with `anthropic:claude-cli` pinned | same |
| Credential for account B beside the unchanged account-A record | owner is B: A's history refused |
| Account record relabelled to B beside account A's credential | owner is still A: history seeded |
| Login switched A to B between turns | history refused |
| Credential removed between turns | history refused |
| Profile endpoint times out (3 s), returns 401/5xx, or returns no `account.uuid` | no owner, history refused; the turn runs |
| Access token already expired and not attested in this process | no owner, no request made, history refused |
| Access token attested earlier in this process, now expired | same owner |
| Access token within 10 minutes of expiry at preparation | turn runs without saved history; the token Claude rotates to is attested after the run; rows covered; the next turn is seeded |
| Turn on a native login whose writer replays history (fresh or resumed Claude session, including the conversation's first turn); credential replaced or removed after preparation, before spawn or send | step refused with `CLI history authority changed before execution`; nothing reaches Claude |
| Same turn; credential replaced or removed after the prompt is sent, before Claude's `UserPromptSubmit` hook is answered | the hook answer carries no private context; the turn runs; rows kept, coverage stops; the next turn is refused history (rows 33, 34) |
| Turn prepared within 10 minutes of token expiry (runs without saved history); credential replaced by an unattested token before send | turn runs; the token is attested in the background; rows covered only if it is the same account |
| Credential rotated to another account's token during a turn, then switched back | coverage stops for the run |
| Credential replaced during an awaited worker commit preparation | rows recorded; coverage not advanced |
| Credential reassigned to another account while the coverage command is queued for the SQLite worker (turn commit or transcript report) | rows recorded; coverage not advanced; the next turn is refused history (scenario 22) |
| SessionManager append committed by the metadata worker while the login holds | row recorded and covered |
| The same append after the login is replaced by an unattested credential | row recorded; coverage not advanced |
| Same-account token rotated after send, outside the refresh window | rows recorded; coverage not advanced; next turn refused history |
| Skill `env` config selects another config dir, on every turn | that login's attested account is the owner; history recovered |
| Skill `env` config selecting another login is added mid-conversation | that turn is a login switch: history refused, the turn runs |
| Backend `env` selects another config dir than the Gateway process | owner is the one in the child's environment |
| Child environment, or its user settings `env` block, selects an API key, token or cloud provider | no owner, history refused, no request made |
| Relative `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, split credential roots, `apiKeyHelper` | no owner, no request made |
| macOS Keychain item exists but is unreadable, or both lookups fail, stale `.credentials.json` beside it | no owner, no request made |

### Real built binary

The real `openclaw agent --local` (built `dist`), a real SQLite session and worker threads, synthetic login files on disk, the real Anthropic Claude runtime and stream-json transport. The `claude` executable is a synthetic child (`harness/bin/claude`) that speaks the control protocol and records every record that reaches it, with the account named by the login's `.claude.json` record (`loginAccount`) and by its credential (`credentialAccount`) at that instant. It can rewrite the login at chosen moments: `FAKE_ON_INIT` after it initializes and before the prompt is sent, `FAKE_ON_USER` after it receives the prompt. It answers OpenClaw's `UserPromptSubmit` hook before each prompt and records the context that comes back (interrupted inputs, durable reference context; `.context-*` files). By default it writes no Claude project transcript, so every later turn enters the fresh-session reseed branch; with `FAKE_WRITE_TRANSCRIPT=1` (scenarios 23 to 26) it writes one under the session id OpenClaw passed, so later turns resume. Each turn is a new process.

**The Anthropic profile endpoint is a local STUB** (`harness/profile-stub.mjs`), reached through a preload that redirects only that one URL (`harness/shim/profile-fetch-shim.mjs`). Synthetic tokens `synthetic-<account>` attest to `<account>`, and the stub can answer 401 or hold the request open. Production code is unchanged and always calls the real URL. Scenarios 10 to 13 also shim the Keychain at the `child_process.execSync` seam (`harness/shim/security-shim.mjs`); the others use the real `security` binary, which finds no item and exits 44.

### Queued reassignment

A login reassigned while a coverage command is queued for the SQLite worker does not advance coverage. The worker asks the host from inside its write transaction (see the design bullet above). Scenario 22 adds one preload, `harness/shim/queued-switch-shim.mjs`. It wraps `Worker.prototype.postMessage` and, right after the host posts turn 2's final `session.turn.commit` (the rows plus coverage) to the SQLite worker, runs the "reassign the login to account B" script synchronously, while the worker has not opened its transaction and the host has not serviced its admission request. Turn 3 then returns the login to account A.

Main transfers the worker command buffer, so the shim decodes the command before `postMessage` ([queued-switch-shim.fixed.mjs](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/head-5f246eff/harness/queued-switch-shim.fixed.mjs)); product code is untouched. With it the row reads `t1:known/2 t2:known/3 t3:unknown`, 3 profile requests, as at the previous head, and turn 3 is 451 characters with no canary. Turn 2's rows stay (seq 3 and 4), coverage stops at seq 3, and turn 3 on account A is refused that history. The tests `does not cover a turn commit whose login is reassigned while the command is queued` and `does not cover a transcript report whose login is reassigned while the command is queued` in `history-boundary.native-login.test.ts` wrap `Worker.prototype.postMessage` the same way and assert that the switch happened, so they cannot pass vacuously. Typecheck, all `EXIT 0`: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` ([f-tsgo-core.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/cfbce32426eac5ff7dd1ecdd412752dc40d5b482/head-8d822e26/gates/f-tsgo-core.log), [f-tsgo-core-test.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/cfbce32426eac5ff7dd1ecdd412752dc40d5b482/head-8d822e26/gates/f-tsgo-core-test.log), [f-tsgo-extensions.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/cfbce32426eac5ff7dd1ecdd412752dc40d5b482/head-8d822e26/gates/f-tsgo-extensions.log), [f-tsgo-extensions-test.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/cfbce32426eac5ff7dd1ecdd412752dc40d5b482/head-8d822e26/gates/f-tsgo-extensions-test.log)); the exit codes of the typechecks and of the lanes below are recorded in [summary.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/cfbce32426eac5ff7dd1ecdd412752dc40d5b482/head-8d822e26/gates/summary.txt).

Owning directories, the runner's own summary lines:

That file is not in and does not import this diff, and passes alone here three times out of three ([repro-registry-recovery-1.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/cfbce32426eac5ff7dd1ecdd412752dc40d5b482/head-8d822e26/gates/repro-registry-recovery-1.log)).

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 372095136ef` ([f-check-changed.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/cfbce32426eac5ff7dd1ecdd412752dc40d5b482/head-8d822e26/gates/f-check-changed.log)): 42 checks `ok`, 2 `failed`. - `max-lines suppression ratchet`: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`. No `ui/` path is in the diff; pristine `372095136ef` against itself (empty diff) reports the same three files ([main-check-max-lines-ratchet.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/ce220637124f62d4bbe03509b8f6ac6dbd5cce1b/head-5fffaf68/gates/main-check-max-lines-ratchet.log)).

### Earlier captures

The subsections below ran at earlier heads of this PR on base `0816aa1b57dc` (the earlier heads), each stated in its first line. Their production behavior is the same as at the pushed head except where the table above differs (row 6, and turns that resume a Claude session). Captures: [attested/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/attested/README.md), [queued/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/queued/README.md), [real/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/real/README.md).

### A real attestation

Ran once on the Mac Studio during the `c276e5e3b6c` round; it exercises only the endpoint, not OpenClaw. One real `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` with the access token of the Studio's logged-in Claude CLI 2.1.283 account returned `status=200 latencyMs=834`, an `account` object with `uuid` (equal to the `.claude.json` record) and an `organization` object, and left the credential on disk unchanged; a synthetic token returned `status=401 latencyMs=96` ([identity/real-profile-attestation.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/attested/identity/real-profile-attestation.txt)). No token, uuid or email was printed or stored. Not exercised against the real endpoint: an expired real token (the code never sends one), a revoked token, a token without the `user:profile` scope, and a request through an HTTPS proxy.

### When Claude CLI rotates its token

Ran once during the `c276e5e3b6c` round against the real `claude` 2.1.283 binary with a synthetic login whose token had expired, its HTTPS sent to a local CONNECT proxy that logs and refuses each connection, so nothing reached Anthropic: the CLI tried the refresh (`CONNECT platform.claude.com:443`) 213 ms after spawn and before it answered `initialize`, and OpenClaw sends the prompt only after that answer. So a rotated token can already be on disk at the send check, which is why a refresh-due turn runs without saved history ([identity/refresh-timing.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/attested/identity/refresh-timing.txt)).

### Real Claude recovery proof

Real `claude` 2.1.283 (Keychain-held claude.ai login), real `api.anthropic.com` profile attestation and real model replies (`claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5`), through the built `openclaw agent --local` with an isolated state dir and no Gateway, at `69861729ddf` (AFTER) and the PR merge-base `0816aa1b57d` (BEFORE). Two turns per arm; between them the Claude session is dropped by deleting that run's own Claude project dir, so turn 2 starts a replacement session (`reuse=invalidated:missing-transcript`).

```
AFTER  turn 2: promptChars=771 historyPrompt=present   reply: PINEAPPLE-1296762355   boundary known seq 2
BEFORE turn 2: cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown
               promptChars=260 historyPrompt=none      reply: UNKNOWN
AFTER, login changed between turns (synthetic CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR): reason=auth-unknown, promptChars=260, historyPrompt=none, boundary unknown
```

Covers: authenticated replacement-session recovery with the real binary and real attestation, the BEFORE refusal, and refusal after a login change. Does not cover: a second real account (the switch uses a fake credential, so the log reads `auth-unknown` and does not separate "owner differs" from "owner unattestable"; the stub scenarios do), repeated runs (one run per arm), a long-lived `claude setup-token` login (see Gaps), and the queued-coverage window with the real binary.

### Keychain cost

Counted at `69861729ddf` on base `0816aa1b57dc` with the scenario 10 harness: 10 `security` lookups per turn for a readable Keychain item, against none at base; 20.9 ms p50 per readable lookup with the real `/usr/bin/security`, about 0.21 s per turn. `history-boundary.native-login.test.ts` pins the split.


## Gaps

- **The access token leaves the process, for an operator who opts in.** Only with `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true` (default `false`, row 35: no request without it). It goes only to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile`, once per token not yet attested in the process, with redirects refused, a 3 s timeout and errors dropped unread. The token is never logged, stored, refreshed or written back. A proxy was not exercised. The opt-in's UI hint names the endpoint.
- **An idle, expired token after a Gateway restart has no owner.** An access token that expired while the Gateway was down cannot be attested until Claude refreshes it. The first turn on it has no owner, and that conversation's history stays refused until `/new` or an empty reset. Persisting attestations across restarts would mean persisting a token-derived value, which this PR does not do.
- **A refresh-due turn runs without saved history.** A turn prepared within 10 minutes of token expiry runs without saved history, because Claude rotates the token before the prompt and the send check could not prove the new one. The next turn is offered history again (scenario 20).
- **A rotation outside the CLI's refresh window stops coverage.** If the CLI rotates the token outside that window (for example after a server-side revocation and a 401 recovery), the new token is not attested before the turn's rows commit, so coverage stops and later turns are refused history (scenario 21). Detecting this would cost a Keychain read after every turn; the settle reads only when a rotation is expected.
- **Transient failures fence the conversation.** A profile request that fails at preparation, and a Keychain lookup that fails at a coverage commit, stop coverage until `/new` or an empty reset. The reply is kept. Only successes are cached, so a failed attestation retries on the next turn.
- **A login without the `user:profile` scope has no owner.** A long-lived `claude setup-token` credential carries only `user:inference`; the real profile endpoint answers it with HTTP 403 (`OAuth token does not meet scope requirement any_of(user:profile, user:office)`). Run against a login like that, the branch refuses saved history exactly as BEFORE does (`reason=auth-unknown`, `historyPrompt=none`, reply `UNKNOWN`), so those installs get no recovery. That is the fail-closed outcome; the run is in the evidence folder, `mini-setup-token`.
- **Some endpoint behaviors were not exercised.** A real successful token refresh, a revoked token and an HTTPS proxy were not run against the real endpoint; the harness endpoint is a stub.
- **Sessions that already have history and no recorded boundary stay unknown.** Only conversations that start empty after the opt-in benefit (row 37); `/new` or an empty reset establishes the boundary. History written by v2026.10.4 is kept and not adopted (scenario 27).
- **Plugin-defined backends wrapping Claude** (`id` other than `claude-cli`) are not covered.
- **A last-instant window remains in worker coverage.** The worker asks the host for the owner check from inside its write transaction and the host answers right before it grants. A credential replaced between that answer and the end of the same SQLite transaction (microseconds on the worker) is not seen for that write, and is caught at the next boundary. The worker cannot read the Keychain or the attestation cache itself, so a fully atomic check is not possible. A reassignment while the command is queued, or during any awaited preparation, is seen (scenario 22 and the queued tests).
- **Saved notes are not shown reaching a resumed session.** A note reaches a Claude CLI turn only when its row is covered, and no shipped path reachable from `openclaw agent` writes a covered note into a claude-cli conversation (the plugin-SDK append in row 32 is uncovered, as on main). The resumed-session context that is shown is the interrupted input (rows 28 to 31). The refusal does not depend on which saved data is present (rows 24, 25, 30, 31, 33, 34; RED3, RED4).
- **The metadata-worker path is shown by a test, not by the built binary.** The CLI runner never posts `session.metadata.append` or `session.transcript.appendMessage` (row 32), so no shipped CLI flow reaches it. `history-boundary.native-login.test.ts` runs it, in one case, on the real worker thread and SQLite (RED1, RED2).
- **The real Claude recovery run was not repeated at the pushed head.** It ran at `69861729ddf` on base `0816aa1b57dc`; at the pushed head the same paths are shown by the harness scenarios above with a synthetic child and the stub endpoint.
- **Three checks fail without this change** (max-lines ratchet, core test shard budget, env-var count); each fails identically on pristine `372095136ef`, on files this diff does not touch (Tests and checks).
- **Incognito sessions on a native login may stop coverage.** The in-memory incognito actor confirms the owner only through the running turn's writer when that writer is in scope; otherwise it keeps the rows and stops coverage. `history-boundary.incognito.test.ts` covers the in-scope case; no harness scenario runs an incognito session.
- **One new plugin config key.** `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` grows the plugin config surface by two entries, so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` raises the plugin budget by two (4759 to 4761 on this base) and `config-baseline.sha256` is regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- **Unrelated suites were not run.** The full suite, the e2e and live lanes, and the Docker lanes were not run. `check:changed` selects `core`, `coreTests`, `extensions`, `extensionTests` and `docs` for this diff, all of which ran above together with the owning-directory lanes.

prs.title: fix: memory sync warnings hide the real error cause
prs.body:
Closes #169718

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `memory sync failed` warnings show only the wrapper text (e.g. `memory sync failed (search): storage-error`) when the underlying exception is silently discarded, so operators cannot diagnose the real cause.

## User Impact

User impact: operators reading logs now see the full error cause chain (real message, error code) in every `memory sync failed (...)` warning, so storage failures are diagnosable without a debugger.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lock-acquisition wrapper threads the real exception as `Error.cause`, but the warn sites formatted errors with `String(err)`, which drops the cause. All `memory sync failed` warn sites in `memory-core` now use the plugin-sdk `formatErrorMessage`, which already merges cause details and applies redaction, matching how other log sites in the same files format errors.

## Evidence

- Focused tests on the touched surface:
  - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` + `local-file-watcher.test.ts` — 45 passed
  - `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` — 18 passed
  - `local-file-watcher.integration.test.ts` — 1 passed
- The lifecycle test's warning assertion now expects `formatErrorMessage(failure)` and passes, proving the cause chain (`<wrapper> | <real cause>`) reaches the log line.
- Grep-verified: `String(err)` no longer appears at any `memory sync failed` warn site in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/`.
- Gap: no screenshots — log-text change with no UI surface.

prs.title: Add shared enterprise-managed authorization for MCP
prs.body:
## Summary

```text
operator OIDC sign-in → shared IdP ID token in SQLite
MCP 401 → IdP ID-JAG → resource authorization server → MCP bearer token
```

Add opt-in `auth: "enterprise"` for HTTP MCP servers with pinned IdP and resource issuers. The client advertises the EMA extension on every request, refreshes the IdP assertion, constrains challenged scopes, and drops cached resource tokens after logout or a new sign-in. `mcp login`, `status`, `doctor`, and `logout` manage the shared session.

This slice deliberately requires `enterprise.identity: "shared"`: all permitted Gateway senders use the operator's enterprise account. Per-requester enterprise SSO is not part of this PR.

Implementation follows the [MCP EMA guide](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization) and compares the [VS Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostXaaAuthProvider.ts) and [MCP Inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/blob/main/core/auth/ema/wire.ts) clients.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw currently accepts only MCP OAuth, so an organization using IdP-managed MCP authorization cannot connect its approved servers through OpenClaw. Operators need an OIDC sign-in and ID-JAG exchange that honors the organization’s resource policy.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `main` accepts only `auth: "oauth"`; an EMA server config is rejected.
  **After:** schema and protocol tests cover explicit shared identity, HTTPS issuer pinning, loopback callback, ID-JAG redemption, `client_secret_post`, per-request capability metadata, scope containment, and cached-token invalidation after logout. The scope and logout tests failed on the initial implementation and pass with this patch.
- **Live, two independent resources:** Used the free XAA developer playground with browser OIDC sign-in and a disposable OCM Gateway. One shared IdP session authorized both XAA Todo0 and a separately registered, publicly tunneled MCP resource with its own resource client and `proof.read` scope. The custom resource verified the bearer JWT signature, issuer, audience, and scope through XAA JWKS before serving requests. `mcp status` reported both entries `enterprise authorized`; `mcp doctor --probe` reported `ok` for each after stopping the Gateway. The built transport connected to both: Todo0 listed four resources and read `todo0://todos`; the custom resource listed one resource, read it, and completed `ema_identity_check` with a verified bearer. The live Gateway catalog exposed both servers' tools; an agent turn successfully invoked the custom tool and read Todo0 resources through OpenClaw's search/describe/dispatch path with no tool failures. The first 4B local-model prompt found the tool but did not call it; explicit discover/describe/dispatch prompts completed both calls. The temporary XAA registrations, Gateway, server, and tunnel were removed after proof.
- **Upgrade, paired output:** A published `2026.10.5` OCM environment and its branch-migrated clone each reported `requester: streamable-http oauth 1-principal-connected` and `shared: streamable-http oauth authorized`. The MCP config SHA-256 and both `mcp_oauth_stores.store_json` SHA-256 values matched exactly before and after; only synthetic test tokens were present.
- **Checks:** 61 focused tests pass across five files, including eleven real-store exchange/retry cases, three composed real-owner/guarded-HTTP cases, and two transport dispatch tests. Core and core-test TypeScript checks, focused lint, config docs generation, the import-cycle check, and the runtime build pass. Earlier security, MCP Events, upgrade, and signed-callback suites also passed. A broad local `check:changed` run passed all TypeScript graphs but was stopped after that stage; local-strict ratchets flagged three UI suppressions outside this PR diff and overfull advisory test shards. The first-party mock ratchet passed after fixture comments were added. Hosted checks on this head are pending. A local matched-base run before rebase with Node 24.19 measured 326,003 startup JS bytes against a 325,476-byte limit; route boot JS grew only 312–315 bytes over base. The committed baseline moved from 324,590 to 324,900 bytes, still below its 325,000-byte cap. The discrepancy appears build-environment dependent and remains visible here.
- **Vendor reach:** blog examples such as Asana, Linear, Atlassian, and Supabase advertise the ID-JAG grant, but their enterprise SSO/domain requirements prevented live authorization with fresh free tenants. The live exchange proof is against the standards playground, not those vendors.

## Security review repairs and final-effect proof

- **Credential incarnation and final effect:** Enterprise event connections now capture the same IdP SQLite authorization owner used by login/logout. Their principal identity includes its authorization ID. The infra test verifies direct callback/recovery guards after logout and account replacement. A second test runs the real MCP Events service with a real SQLite enterprise grant: the first account subscribes; logout rejects the retained callback guard, revalidation, and renewal before another remote request; the replacement account gets a distinct principal and can subscribe; the first principal still cannot issue a request. The outbound MCP request is intercepted at the final transport boundary. A third test sends a correctly signed webhook through the plugin's real HTTP callback and SQLite ingress: before logout it returns 200 and enqueues one event; after logout it returns 410, enqueues nothing further, and reconciliation sends no subscription renewal. Its source wrapper delegates enterprise authority to the real credential-connection owner while reusing the plugin's existing protocol fixture.
- **OIDC network effects:** Both CLI login and runtime refresh pass an OpenClaw guarded fetch to `openid-client` discovery; that fetch remains attached to code and refresh grants. The CLI fetch also retains operation cancellation and before-request admission, while refresh retains the SQLite lease signal. A test supplies untrusted IdP metadata with a private token endpoint and verifies `openid-client` routes its grant through the guarded fetch, which rejects that private target.
- **Revocation during awaited exchange:** Each same-origin enterprise request captures a real SQLite authorization owner; its synchronous `assertCurrent` runs in the guarded HTTP transport's final `beforeRequest` hook, after DNS/preparation and before the network effect. The SDK discovery/ID-JAG fetches also check the original authorization ID before and after I/O. Ten infra cases pause the IdP response, resource authorization-server response, or preparation immediately before IdP exchange, resource redemption, or the final bearer retry, then log out or replace the account through the real credential writer. The old request rejects and issues no post-revocation request; a fresh request under the replacement account completes the chain. Two transport tests separately pause the actual guarded fetch during DNS preparation and confirm that stale resource and authorization requests never call the network fetch. Config tests verify malformed issuer/redirect strings return validation errors instead of throwing.
- **Live retry repair:** The two-resource run exposed a `try`/`finally` lifetime error: the final bearer retry returned its promise before the authority guard completed, so `finally` disposed the guard too early. The fetch now awaits the retry. A real-store success case verifies the unchanged authorization can complete both resource requests; the revocation cases still prevent a late request. Concurrent first requests can also race while publishing the initial canonical credential owner; the client retries one `MCP_AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE` capture, while retired authorization errors still fail closed. A focused test covers this race and the live concurrent list/read path passed on both servers.
- **Node-host boundary:** Before this repair, the shared MCP schema accepted an enterprise entry under `nodeHost.mcp.servers`, but the node-host startup excluded only OAuth, so that entry entered connection and retry handling without node-host SSO support. The node host now excludes enterprise entries (including an explicit enterprise config), logs an actionable instruction to configure the server in Gateway `mcp.servers` and run `mcp login` there, and leaves ordinary node-host servers available. A valid-schema regression test asserts one healthy sibling connection, zero enterprise client/transport calls, and zero later retries after five minutes of simulated time. The requested node-host, recovery, and schema suites passed: 65 tests. The node-host documentation now states this limit.
- **Composed final-effect trace (redacted):** `mcp-enterprise-composed-authority.test.ts` keeps the real `resolveMcpTransport` → `withMcpEnterpriseBearer` → SQLite authorization owner → `buildMcpHttpFetch` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path. Only DNS, the final network effect, and the SDK transport container are fixture-owned. The test runs IdP discovery, ID-JAG exchange, resource-server redemption, and the first 401, then pauses DNS for the final bearer retry. Its assertions produce this paired trace:

  | Credential action while DNS is paused | Resource calls before release | Resource calls after old request settles | Result |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
  | Unchanged | 1 | 2 | Retry 200; exactly one new network effect |
  | Logout via real SQLite writer | 1 | 1 | Old request rejects; total network calls unchanged |
  | Replacement via real SQLite writer | 1 | 1 | Old request rejects; total network calls unchanged |

  Both revocation cases then authorize the new account and reach resource call 3. The test also asserts that IdP and resource-AS token calls occurred before the pause. This directly joins the real credential writer to the production guarded fetch's synchronous final `beforeRequest` hook; the mock observes whether the final network effect was invoked.
- **Stored-data compatibility:** The `v2026.10.5`-format test inserts an OAuth credential row directly with `format_version=1`, the released store-key grammar, and no authorization ID. The current reader returns its tokens unchanged, captures a valid authority, and keeps the row intact; the released per-requester OAuth config also parses unchanged. Separately, I ran published OpenClaw `2026.10.5` in a disposable OCM environment with synthetic shared and requester OAuth rows, cloned its full state directory, then ran this branch's backed-up `doctor --fix` migration on the clone. `mcp status` before and after was identical: `shared ... oauth authorized` and `requester ... oauth 1-principal-connected`. The MCP config digest and both OAuth row digests were identical across the stable original and migrated clone. The table DDL and row format also match tag `v2026.10.5`. No live vendor OAuth tokens were used in this upgrade test.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. The feature is opt-in per MCP server.

**Blast Radius:** MCP authentication. A misconfigured enterprise entry will omit that server from the agent catalog until the operator signs in or fixes its configuration; ordinary OAuth and stdio entries retain their existing path.

## What Problem This Solves

Private construction and reset controls still expose choices that serving callers never select. Some tests bypass the native owner through those seams, while three search providers wrap fixed metadata in single-caller factories.

## Changes

Remove the fixed status Tailnet/update suppliers, ACP's private injected clock, active-memory's private grace/circuit/map-reset controls, and the migration state-directory reset. Tests retain the original asynchronous operations and native database cohorts, join them before cleanup, and use existing per-run operations or reload the original owner graph. The product's grace period, leases, migration algorithms and persisted shapes stay unchanged.

Inline Brave, Perplexity and Parallel Free's sole metadata bases into their actual provider descriptors without loading search execution eagerly. Remove Firecrawl's unused private DNS callback plumbing; native DNS and every SSRF guard remain.

Image, video and music constructors now choose the native background scheduler directly. Tests hold external results, observe the actual terminal publication, and join the cron fixture's real cleanup tail before retiring mocks. GitHub publication uses the native in-process caller; integration tests retain actual request/authorization dispatch behind a per-invocation module-boundary transport. Transcripts capture the native state directory and logger; delayed fixture constructors explicitly select their own isolated directory. Catalog helpers rely on the already-required application context while preserving connection, scope and asynchronous identity checks.

This accumulated residue removes **101 net production lines across 70 paths**. Tests/support grow by **472 lines**, for **371 overall lines added**. Fixture growth replaces production test controls with original-operation lifetime observation; the migration fixture's sequential import graph, restart/reopen operation and recall tracking live in sibling test-support modules. Moved metadata and fixture code are fully counted.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No public SDK/configuration/CLI/protocol contract, persisted shape, dependency, permission, durability, security guard or realistic-concurrency behavior is removed. Phase E standalone session memory is untouched.

- A malformed internal catalog caller violating the owner's already-required application context now fails at the first read instead of silently skipping refresh. The optional old host context dates to #112853; #174714 replaced that host with required context inputs but retained the stale helper branches. Context replacement after awaited bootstrap still checks exact identity.
- Private reset operations no longer erase unresolved native work or rewrite the product's grace interval for synthetic fixtures. Tests must settle their original operations and then retire their own IDs/keys or reload their closed graph. No serving cancellation or shutdown behavior is removed.

Completed exact-head CI (39516699338, attempt 1) passes every selected runtime, type, extension, architecture, boundary, UI, PostgreSQL and security gate, including the repaired resource-publication and transcript fixtures. The only substantive failure is inherited Doctor lint118951551770: `src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts:73:28`, `typescript(unbound-method)` on captured `check.repair`; aggregate118963727543 is downstream. The repair captures and explicitly delegates to the native completion/failure owners before observation; all assertions that native operations actually publish success/failure remain. The installed Vitest spy API reproduces the original suppression and the corrected delegation. Independent P0-P2 repair review is scoped-clean with no findings (confidence 0.99), before only mechanical receiver binding required by lint. Final repair types (5.890s), format (9.880s), lint (39.011s), line-cap ratchet (5.540s), and all 14 suppression-audit cases pass. The focused resources/donor-resources replay stops at the compiled-worker prerequisite before cases; it is not a runtime pass. Exact-head hosted CI must validate the repaired fixture graph.

The changed transcript fixture published plugin metadata before setting its isolated state directory, invalidating the metadata environment fingerprint and allowing unintended cold discovery during provider-absence retries. prs.title: fix(skills): cancel experience review on explicit /stop
prs.body:
Closes #120558

**AI-assisted: yes.** The patch was authored by an AI coding agent, reviewed by independent local passes and ClawSweeper, and the end-to-end trace below was executed against a real Gateway child running this head.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an explicit `/stop` aborts the foreground reply but leaves the Skill Workshop Experience Review for that session alive. About 30 seconds later the detached review starts, makes model calls, and can auto-apply a skill — so the agent appears to have ignored the stop.

Deep user-aborted turns are intentionally eligible for learning (`#115887`), and the review runs as independent Gateway root work (`#116040`). The Stop path had no connection to the review scheduler, and even cancelling the queued review raced the stopped turn's own `agent_end`, which re-armed it.

## User Impact

After an explicit Stop, no queued or in-flight Experience Review for the stopped session continues in the background, and the stopped turn's own completion cannot re-arm one. This covers every explicit Stop surface: ordinary channel `/stop` through fast dispatch, the `/stop` command handler, `chat.send "/stop"`, plain `chat.abort`, and the exact-run `chat.abort` that Control UI and native chat clients send for ordinary local runs. A Stop that is rejected — wrong owner, stale/reassigned conversation target, or revoked authority at the effect point — leaves review state untouched. Turns interrupted without an explicit Stop remain eligible, preserving #115887.

## Why This Change Was Made

One scheduler contract, one bridge, applied at each Stop owner after that owner's live-authority boundary:

- `experience-review-scheduler.ts` — one review at a time with a tracked `AbortController`/session key; `cancelSession` clears the queued timer/pending candidate/iteration counter and aborts the matching in-flight review. A bounded one-shot run-scoped suppression makes the stopped run's later `agent_end` consume its id, drop that session's pending review/counter, and return without arming. Later turns carry different run ids and schedule normally. A review rejected after its owned controller aborts is classified as cancellation (debug).
- `experience-review.ts` — cleanup (`listWorkshopChanges`, notice) now runs after the model outcome; a review failure plus a cleanup failure, or a cleanup-only failure after a successful model run, surfaces as an `AggregateError` instead of being hidden behind the aborted signal, so the scheduler keeps the existing classifier protection and warns for the independent failure.
- `experience-review-default.ts` — `stopSkillExperienceReview({ sessions, runIds })` is the single bridge: it drops every selected session's review, aborts its in-flight review, and suppresses the stopped run ids. Best-effort per effect; it never fails Stop.
- `abort-operation.ts` (channel fast dispatch and `/stop` command kernel) — the bridge runs from `afterQueued`, which the shared kernel reaches only after `assertCurrent()` revalidates the captured Stop's live target. `ChannelStopCapture.reviewTargets` retains one identity per combined capture, so an ACP target plus its ordinary source conversation cancels both reviews.
- `chat-abort-session-plan.ts` (Gateway session Stop) — opts in through `cancelExperienceReview` and runs the bridge inside the plan's accepted boundary: after `assertCurrent`, after the unauthorized-owner rejection, and after hook-context validation, immediately before the cancellation effects. A rejected Stop returns before the bridge. The plan's exact selected run ids are suppressed.
- `chat-abort-exact-run.ts` (exact-run Stop) — bridges inside `abortChatRunById`'s `onAbortPrepared` boundary, after the exact target is validated and immediately before cancellation commits. Queued-input discard and maintenance aborts stay unmarked.

Provenance: this restores the #177561 intent (`cee90c3`) that a conversation reassignment during preparation rejects cancellation before effects — the review effects are now behind that boundary — and restores the cleanup classifier's explicit `AggregateError` protection.

No new config, scheduler, store, or persistent session-level suppression. Queue order, rate limiting, one-at-a-time review, eligibility, and workshop-mutated/errored-completion behavior are unchanged.

## Findings addressed

- **Exact-run Stop proof (before-merge item)** — scenario 4 uses the shipped `chat.abort { sessionKey, runId }` path against the real scheduler: the queued review is cancelled, the stopped run's eligible completion does not re-arm a review, and a later turn recovers.
- **[P3] Preserve cleanup-only failures after the model has succeeded** — a cleanup-only rejection is now an `AggregateError` (`Skill experience review cleanup failed`) instead of a bare error, so the scheduler's existing classifier protection keeps it at warning level even when the controller signal is aborted. Covered by `experience-review.test.ts` for both model-succeeded and model-failed outcomes with an aborted cleanup, plus a scheduler cleanup-only case.
- The earlier P1/P2 authorization-ordering, combined-target, and exact-run coverage items are resolved above; the low-value fake Stop scaffolding was removed from the command trigger test.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway trace (head `2240d36a1`)

An isolated loopback Gateway child was started from the built production entry of this branch with a temp state dir and a deterministic local OpenAI-completions stub. The cancellation scenarios ran on `207c6be9e`; the later commits only narrow test typing (`b95817ee0`, `cac37a0f5`), classify cleanup-only failures (`9b3b4b169`), and normalize the rethrown review failure for the type-aware lint (`2240d36a1`). The real Gateway, session controller, Stop authorization, Workshop review scheduler, detached work admission, and skill-write path ran unchanged; only model responses are scripted. Raw output is under `.openclaw/proof/178145/` (`gateway-proof.log`, `evidence.json`).

```text
[check] PASS queued-review Stop accepted :: {"ok":true,"payload":{"ok":true,"aborted":true,"runIds":[]}}
[check] PASS queued review never started after explicit Stop :: {"reviewRequests":0,"waitedMs":40114}
[check] PASS later turn still schedules exactly one review :: {"reviewRequests":1,"reviewCompleted":1}
[check] PASS in-flight-review Stop accepted :: {"ok":true,"payload":{"ok":true,"aborted":false,"runIds":[]}}
[check] PASS in-flight review request was aborted before acting :: {"reviewAborted":1,"reviewCompleted":1,"abortedAfterStop":true}
[check] PASS in-flight review was running when Stop was sent :: {"reviewStartedAt":…,"stopAt":…,"reviewAbortedAt":…}
[check] PASS aborted in-flight review never completed :: {"reviewCompleted":1}
[check] PASS held foreground turn is active :: {"heldForeground":true,"foregroundAborted":0}
[check] PASS non-owner session Stop is refused as unauthorized :: {"ok":false,"error":"unauthorized"}
[check] PASS non-owner Stop left the owner's held stream open :: {"heldForeground":true,"foregroundAborted":0}
[check] PASS non-owner Stop did not abort the owner's active turn :: {"terminal":null}
[check] PASS owner's held turn completes normally :: {"state":"final"}
[check] PASS queued review survives the refused non-owner Stop :: {"before":2,"after":3}
[check] PASS turn 8 final (queues a review) :: {"state":"final"}
[check] PASS exact-run turn reached an eligible iteration count :: {"heldForeground":true}
[check] PASS exact-run Stop accepted :: {"ok":true,"payload":{"ok":true,"aborted":true,"runIds":["proof-turn-9"]}}
[check] PASS exact-run Stop aborts its own run :: {"state":"aborted"}
[check] PASS exact-run Stop cancelled the queued review and suppressed its stopped completion :: {"baseline":3,"afterWait":3,"waitedMs":40095}
[check] PASS later turn final after exact-run Stop :: {"state":"final"}
[check] PASS later turn still schedules a review after exact-run Stop :: {"baseline":3,"after":4}
[proof] ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

What each scenario shows:

1. **Queued review cancelled, later turn recovers.** A foreground turn queued a review; a plain `chat.abort` was accepted inside the 30s idle window. Forty seconds later the review request count was still 0. A later eligible turn then scheduled exactly one review, proving the stop is run-scoped and did not leave a session-wide block.
2. **In-flight review stopped before it can act.** A later review was held open at the provider while it ran. A `chat.abort` then aborted that model request (10 ms after the Stop; timestamp-asserted to be after the Stop and after the review started), it never completed, and no skill-write call was produced.
3. **Non-owner refused; review survives.** A second Gateway caller (a local backend connection with `operator.write`, different connection and no device identity, so owner matching cannot pass) issued a session Stop while the owner's turn was held open. The Gateway returned `INVALID_REQUEST` / `unauthorized`; the owner's model stream stayed open (`foregroundAborted: 0`), its turn finished normally, and the queued review still ran (`reviewRequests` 2 → 3). The rejected Stop never reached the review bridge.
4. **Exact-run Stop.** A completed turn queued a review, then the next run was held at model iteration 11 — an eligible completed-turn shape. The owner sent `chat.abort { sessionKey, runId }` (the Control UI/native client shape); the Gateway accepted it (`aborted: true`, `runIds: ["proof-turn-9"]`) and the run ended aborted. Forty seconds later the review request count was unchanged (the queued review was cancelled and the stopped run's own completion did not re-arm one), and a later 10-iteration turn scheduled exactly one review (`3 → 4`).

Reassignment is proven at the shipped channel Stop kernel, which is the owner of that ordering: `checks the published conversation at the Stop effect (rebound=true)` runs for both fast dispatch and the `/stop` command, rebinds the conversation after preparation, expects the foreground Stop rejection, and now also asserts that the review bridge is not called. No live Discord credentials were available for a transport-level trace, so that path is covered by the kernel fixture rather than a live channel. Revocation immediately before the effect is rejected at the same synchronous `assertCurrent` gate (the existing “stops issuing effects when cancellation releases its active publisher authority” fixture still passes).

### Tests and checks

```text
gateway chat.abort experience-review              5 passed
chat.send "/stop" pre-admission                  31 passed
auto-reply Stop kernel/handoff (fast + command)   56 passed
ACP combined Stop targets (abort.test.ts)         35 passed
stop command trigger                              2 passed
experience-review cleanup cases (new)             2 passed
experience-review-scheduler                       21 passed
tsgo:core (production sources)                    clean
core test type shards (src)                       clean
oxfmt --check (changed files)                     clean
oxlint (raw, changed files)                       0 warnings, 0 errors
git diff --check                                  clean
```

The scheduler suite reports one additional Windows-only file failure in the pre-existing “waits for ten accumulated iterations even when turns use a learned skill” case: `vi.getTimerCount()` also counts the unrelated `owned-directory-observation` fallback timer that `resolveWorkshopSkillsDir` arms when `fs.watch` is unavailable; the other review-behavior tests pass and Ubuntu CI runs that lane green. The Stop kernel file reports an `EBUSY` teardown error removing a Windows temp directory after all 56 tests pass. Under this heavily loaded local run, four pre-existing experience-review source-change cases also hit their 180s hook timeout; they are untouched by this diff and the two new cleanup cases pass. None is a behavior failure.

The earlier failed `check-test-types-core-2` was inspected: the synthetic abort-context typing was fixed in `392395cba`, and on that head all `check-test-types-core-1..5`, `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, and lint shards pass.

### Proof boundary

The Gateway, session/session-controller, Stop RPC and dispatch, detached review admission, scheduler, 30s idle timer, and skill-write path are real; only model responses come from the local stub, because the behavior under test is Stop cancellation rather than model quality. Bundled plugins were disabled for the proof run to keep the isolated Gateway startup short; they do not own any code under test. No live channel transport trace is claimed for the reassignment case (see above).

prs.title: refactor: reuse plugin parsing and scenario owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins repeat small parsing, normalization, and scenario-target operations that already have an implementation at their owner.

## User Impact

No supported feature, configuration, SDK, protocol, or persisted-data change. The voice-call CLI now reports an actionable error for an unsupported older Gateway instead of sending a second legacy continuation request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse existing SDK normalization/JSON functions and plugin-local scenario and mutation owners. Remove the superseded private implementations and their orphaned code.

This is the plugin area of a measured 90-path cleanup, split by area to keep CI attribution bounded; core is #178821 and UI is separate. It removes **140 net production lines across 23 production files**. Nine boundary-test files grow by 86 net lines. One assertion-baseline file shrinks to match the removed casts. No new SDK export, dependency, public contract, cross-plugin seam, or cache is introduced. The standalone session-memory backend and its machinery/tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- An older/mismatched Gateway without `voicecall.continue.start` now returns the existing restart/upgrade error, without a second blocking RPC. First-party plugins release with the current host; older-host fallbacks are explicitly unsupported. The retry originated in #75459's synthetic source review; human issue #72345 concerned duplicate webhook listeners, whose Gateway-first routing remains. #125458 also identifies this as a legacy-method fallback; its authority, restart, settlement, and redaction fixes remain. The public blocking RPC itself is not removed.
- WhatsApp QA observations reuse the target validated before each attempt. A fabricated internal callback or one that mutates the group identifier after preparation now observes the pinned route or fails ordinary QA instead of a redundant late missing-group error. Typed scenario implementations do not perform that mutation. #95622 hardened quiet-window/identity checks and #106547 split the modules; neither establishes a human incident requiring that post-preparation guard. Quiet windows, unknown-sender rejection, activation restoration, and security-effect checks remain.

All external-input validation, live authority, artifact integrity, FIFO ordering, realistic concurrency, and ordinary durability protections remain.

## Evidence

On the original plugin slice, **721 tests across 32 focused files passed**, without skips, across 11 serial configurations (722.2 seconds including wrapper/preparation). Targeted native types, formatting, plugin syntax lint, and the 14 suppression checks passed. After CI investigation, the only production restoration is Levanto's original validator; its existing validator and guarded-HTTP suites had also passed all 47 cases on that original source before the proposed extraction. Unchanged-source proof is reused rather than claiming that all 721 cases were repeated after the restoration. All local proof runs use isolated state, low priority, and one worker.

Runtime and static import-cycle checks both found zero cycles; the restoration adds no module edge. Independent isolated P0–P2 review of the original 33-path proposal finished clean. Fresh complete-candidate P0–P2 review also finished clean (0.98); targeted native types (9.7 s), assertion ratchet (2,503 files), and all 14 suppression cases (47.7 s) passed for the repair at `389bbbaf47f16faf97593d58377ad21628491b36`. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

### Conflict-only rebase

GitHub reported an actual conflict with main's #178830 ClickClack ownership refactor. Rebased onto `4213136ceea79e9c39e3aa9f15f8c2f52df7a183`, preserving main's account-owned event handler and backlog loops. Only the old private socket JSON parser is removed; the existing SDK parser call remains. No retired module-level event-processing implementation is restored. Range comparison shows only the expected surrounding gateway context change; the CI-repair commit is patch-identical. Signed rebased head: `e1dc11fff50c2a34725d8f9038f55fe5930ce26c`.

Fresh conflict proof passed: both gateway consumer files, 25 cases without skips (155.9 s wrapper, 138.5 s Vitest with 91% transform and 1% tests); three-root native types (7.3 s), formatting (1.0 s), plugin syntax lint (9.1 s), all 14 suppression cases (38.3 s), runtime cycles zero (87.7 s), and static cycles zero (195.9 s). Earlier unchanged-consumer proof and independent review are retained, not represented as reruns on the rebased head. The new exact-head CI is still required; the earlier head's results below are historical attribution only.

### CI repair and quarantine

The first head's assertion-ratchet job identified four owned shrink omissions: browser proxy and ClickClack gateway each fall from two assertions to one; Discord channel access falls from one to zero and voice response generation from two to zero. This repair reduces or removes those baseline rows; no allowance grows.

Its extension-bundle job also failed `extensions/levanto/registration.test.ts`, in the native-usage case at line 105: it received `unavailable` rather than `ok`. The unchanged fixture has a 500 ms request deadline; CI reported 769 ms, which is not attribution by itself. A selected Bun replay could not start because the installed revision does not match the repository's pinned fork. No timeout, retry, skip, binary download, or runtime guard was changed.

Under the campaign's import-graph quarantine rule, only the reachable changed production file, `extensions/levanto/sage-validation.ts`, is restored byte-for-byte to fresh main (also unchanged from the original base). The nine-line extraction is preserved on pushed branch `deslop/z33-parked-levanto-probability-owner-20261015` at `99dd82049e5eb150f5c7de31692d43beda88dd2b`, without a PR, pending qualified matching-runtime proof or attribution. The failure is not claimed fixed or inherited. No other production family is dropped.

Prior type-aware plugin lint reported declaration-error types at unchanged `SearchConfigRecord` and `PluginRuntime` annotations in Parallel/ClickClack. Those diagnostics remain unresolved; they are not called inherited CI, fixed, or a passing typed-lint result. The supported bounded alternative used targeted native types plus plugin syntax lint, without casts, suppressions, fabricated declarations, or a broad local build.

### Earlier-head CI attribution

On repaired head `389bbbaf47f16faf97593d58377ad21628491b36`, run `39513922014`, job `118942566656` (`check-lint-core-2`) fails `typescript(unbound-method)` at untouched `src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts:73:28`. The inspected CI checkout merges this head into main `de1d7d0c757e5d0438954a92a043285127a16469`. A focused one-file typed-lint replay on that exact main base fails with the same path, line, column and diagnostic (90.2 s). Main's progress change #178767 introduced the unbound `const repair = check.repair`; this PR does not modify the file or its defining health-check contract. This is matching-signature inherited evidence, not a successful lint result or a waiver of other exact-head checks. All remaining jobs still require individual accounting before landing.

The unsupported legacy voice continuation's new registered-CLI case was red on the original code because it made two physical SDK requests instead of one; its retained CLI/registration tests pass after the cut. Other changes are green refactors, not new bug-fix red/green claims. No live vendor, phone, or channel call, device, local build, or E2E proof is claimed. Hosted CI supplies per-job timing; no CI test-seconds estimate is claimed before it runs.
