prs.title: feat(models): operator text for a provider's own refusals, such as an empty prepaid balance
prs.body:
Related: #167341

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: people are told to sign in again when a provider or proxy refuses a request with an error type of its own sent as a 401 or 403, such as an empty prepaid balance.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can set the text people see for a provider's own error types, keyed by the `type` in the provider's error body:

```json5
{
  models: {
    providers: {
      "acme-proxy": {
        failureCopy: { insufficient_balance: "Your balance is empty. Top it up on the billing page." },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Channel replies, Control UI replies and the run's error event then show that text, with a leading ⚠️ like the built-in messages, instead of "Couldn't sign in to the AI service…". Nothing changes without the setting. The copy is static operator text and never includes the provider's message.

Unchanged: classification, fallback and cooldowns. The refusal still counts as `auth`. Known gaps:
- Chat history rebuilds a failed reply with the built-in copy.
- While the key or auth profile cools down after the refusal (30 s, then 1 min, then 5 min), requests fail before reaching the provider and show the built-in message.
- When every model of a fallback chain refuses, the reply and the run result show the last attempt's provider copy, but the run's error event keeps the summary of every attempt it shows today ("All models failed (2): …"), which includes each provider's own message. 2026.10.5 shows the same summary (below).

## Why This Change Was Made

Any 401 or 403 is classified `auth`, and the copy follows the class. A proxy can't make OpenClaw say the balance is empty:
- Rewriting the reply in a `reply_payload_sending` plugin misses the run's error event. Registering that hook also turns off Telegram preview streaming for every reply.
- Sending it as a billing failure would disable the auth profile for 10 minutes to 24 hours, so a top-up wouldn't take effect.

How it works:
- The provider's `errorType`, already on the failed assistant message, now travels on `FailoverError`. It goes through `describeFailoverError`, the reply's failover facts and fallback attempts, so the last attempt of a fallback chain carries it.
- `renderProviderFailureCopy` looks up `failureCopy` for the failed request's provider and error type. The run's error text (`formatUserFacingAssistantErrorText`) and the auto-reply error handler (channel and Control UI replies) use it before the class's copy.
- When profile rotation for an overloaded provider reaches its cap and model fallback takes over, that failure keeps the provider's error type and uses its copy too, so a capped provider that is a chain's last attempt still finds its text.
- Only static operator text is shown:
  - at most 300 characters, so the run error event's 400-character text preview carries it whole;
  - keys are up to 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, looked up with `Object.hasOwn`.
- The `models.*` field labels move to `schema.labels.models.ts`, next to the models help. That keeps `schema.labels.ts` under its line cap.

#167341 proposes `messages.failureCopy` keyed by failover reason. This change keys the copy per provider by the provider's own error type instead. A refusal the provider names gets its own text, and real sign-in failures keep theirs.

**Needs a maintainer decision:** this adds a config option. Is per-provider copy keyed by error type the shape you want, or a global map keyed by reason as #167341 proposes?

## Evidence

### Through the CLI, upgrading from the latest stable release

A local harness (not part of this PR) runs `openclaw gateway run` from the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` (npm `latest`), then from this branch's `pnpm build` at `1ed01ac776`, on one state directory. Config changes go through `openclaw doctor --fix` and `openclaw config patch`. One local server stands in for eight OpenAI-compatible providers, and each refuses every request with HTTP 401 and an error type of its own (synthetic: `{"error":{"message":"Your balance is empty. Top up to continue.","type":"insufficient_balance","code":"401"}}`). A backend client sends with `chat.send` and reads the run's `chat` error event and its `agent.wait` result. A refusal cools the key down across restarts, so each check uses a provider nothing has called yet.

1. **Latest stable:** 2026.10.5 shows the built-in copy, and an exhausted fallback chain's error event is the per-attempt summary.
2. **Upgrade with existing settings:** after `doctor --fix`, this branch loads the same config and behaves as before.
3. **Configured refusal:** `config patch` adds `failureCopy` to providers the config already had. The error event and the run result read the operator's text, `failoverReason` stays `auth`, and the provider's message does not appear.
4. **Unconfigured type:** a type the provider's `failureCopy` doesn't name keeps the built-in copy.
5. **Fallback exhausted:** when both candidates refuse, the run result carries the last attempt's provider copy, and the error event keeps the summary (the gap above).

```text
[01] openclaw 2026.10.5 (npm): openclaw gateway run, providers without failureCopy
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="acme-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS acme-proxy refused with insufficient_balance: built-in copy (released behavior)
[02] 2026.10.5: agent released-chain -> echo-proxy, then fallback foxtrot-proxy; both refuse
     chat error event: errorMessage="All models failed (2): echo-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth) | foxtrot-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth). Re-authenticate with: openclaw models auth login --provider 'foxtro..."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="foxtrot-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS released behavior: an exhausted chain's error event is the per-attempt summary
[03] stop 2026.10.5: exit 0
[04] this branch (1ed01ac776): openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive: exit 0
[05] this branch: openclaw gateway run, same state directory and config
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="bravo-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS the existing config loads and behaves as before: built-in copy in the event and the run result
[06] stop: exit 0
[07] openclaw config patch (failure-copy): exit 0
[08] this branch: openclaw gateway run with failureCopy on charlie-proxy, beta-proxy and delta-proxy
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Your prepaid balance is empty. Top it up on the billing page."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="charlie-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Your prepaid balance is empty. Top it up on the billing page."
     PASS configured refusal: the operator's text in the error event and the run result
     PASS classification stays auth, and the provider's own message is not shown
[09] agent typed -> beta-proxy, which refuses with quota_exceeded (its copy names insufficient_balance)
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="beta-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS unconfigured type: built-in copy
[10] agent chain -> gamma-proxy (no failureCopy), then fallback delta-proxy (failureCopy); both refuse
     chat error event: errorMessage="All models failed (2): gamma-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth) | delta-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth). Re-authenticate with: openclaw models auth login --provider 'delta-p..."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="delta-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ The backup provider's balance is empty too. Top it up on the billing page."
     PASS fallback exhausted: the run result carries the last attempt's provider copy
     exhausted-chain error event starts with "All models failed": true
[11] stop: exit 0
     provider requests: {"acme":1,"bravo":4,"charlie":4,"beta":4,"gamma":4,"delta":2,"echo":1,"foxtrot":1}
```

### Tests

- **Tests that fail on `main` and pass here:**
  - `error-text.test.ts`, "provider failure copy": the copy for the matching provider and type; the built-in copy for another type, another provider, no type, and `toString`; never the provider's text; a ⚠️ added once.
  - `agent-runner-execution-provider-failures.test.ts`, "a provider refusal with operator copy": chat app and Control UI replies; another type keeps the class's copy.
  - `assistant-failure.failover.test.ts`: the error type on the run's failure, and through the real `runWithModelFallback` with two candidates. The fallback case also fails without this PR's fallback-attempt change.
  - `assistant-failure.failover.test.ts`, overload rotation cap: the error type and the operator's copy on the capped failure, the built-in text without copy, and the type on both attempts of a two-candidate `runWithModelFallback` chain. It fails on `1ed01ac776` and passes from `bd6f4aa153`.
- **Checks:**
  - The `assistant-failure`, `failover-error`, `schema.help.quality` and `zod-schema.core` suites pass.
  - `pnpm tsgo`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, the line-cap ratchet, `config:docs:check`, `config:schema:check` and `git diff --check` pass.
  - `1ed01ac776` drops the `max-lines` suppression in `schema.labels.ts` that moving the model labels made unused, and its baseline entry; type-aware oxlint on the changed files and the line-cap ratchet pass.
  - `cd5f044375` merges `main`; its one conflict, `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, is regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
  - At `bd6f4aa153`: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, type-aware oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `config:docs:check`, `config:schema:check`, the line-cap ratchet, and the `assistant-failure`, `error-text`, `agent-runner-execution-provider-failures`, `failover-error`, `schema.help.quality` and `zod-schema.core` suites pass. The CLI run above is from `1ed01ac776`; the later commits merge `main` and add the overload-cap fix, which the tests above cover.

prs.title: fix(slack): fallback bot answers replies in another bot’s thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a fallback Slack bot also handles an unmentioned reply in a thread started by another bot when both apps are installed in the same channel.

## User Impact

User impact: an unmentioned thread reply stays with the bot that started the thread; the fallback bot still handles unmentioned top-level posts, and an explicit mention of the fallback bot still reaches it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack does not repeat the root message's bot mention on later replies. The fallback account's `ignoreOtherMentions` check therefore needs to inspect the thread starter before accepting an unmentioned reply. Unknown or non-bot roots keep the existing policy.

## Evidence

- On a running Gateway with the patched plugin, a real owner-authored reply in another bot's thread was rejected by the fallback account with `other-bot-thread`.
- Added a two-account routing matrix covering the same unmentioned thread reply, an explicit fallback-bot mention in that thread, and an unmentioned top-level post; each case asserts both acceptance and rejection. The owner account uses the existing `requireMentionInBotThreads:false` policy, while both accounts use `ignoreOtherMentions:true`.
- `git diff --check` passed. The changed-extension CI job passed on head `6215ad73a2`; its Slack two-account routing case passed. The full repository test runner was unavailable in the sparse checkout.

prs.title: feat: attribute delegated work to the initiating human
prs.body:
Related: #169139 (closed predecessor), #157806 (upstream requester identity plumbing).

## What Problem This Solves

Agent-delegated sessions and automations can appear agent-created even when a verified human initiated the work, leaving that human without creator-only management controls.

## User Impact

New sessions created through agent tools, native/visible/ACP delegations, and agent-created automations retain the verified initiating human as creator. **This is normal behavior, not a Lab. No configuration change is required.** The previously proposed toggle and experimental setting have been removed.

- Creator identity affects discovery, sharing/public-link management, archive/restore, attribution, and creator-based owner/personal-profile fallbacks—not only archiving. Assigned ownership remains separate.
- Existing creators are not rewritten. A selected tool-execution user is not automatically the initiating human. Autonomous work without a retained human stays agent/system-created.
- Execution authority, model/tool permissions, required sandbox containment, and its original identity namespace remain separate from creator attribution. Public links still require explicit publication; anonymous access, exclusions, revocation, and subsequent-message behavior are unchanged.
- Compatible older readers use their original creator semantics and preserve the nested attribution for a later upgrade. Ordinary schema-compatibility safeguards still apply: this does not make unrelated newer database formats downgradeable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Build on the existing requester-provenance path from #157806 rather than treating assignment or selected execution identity as evidence of who initiated the work. Creator attribution is retained inside the immutable creation record; the original actor remains available to isolation owners and compatible older readers. No database schema/version change is introduced.

The creator/admin archive rule is retained. No Labs UI or configuration-schema delta remains against main. Documentation lives in the normal sessions guide.

Requested by and developed with @VACInc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5288680a-9b75-4e62-93a1-b542110788b0)

## Evidence

Latest head: 3f0e121451973deef51ee10f1c63f0e36c6f4319.

**Default-attribution fixture repair:** CI39515202388 exposed eight stale fixture/assertion failures across hosted session scopes, independent input transfer, and cron validation. All eight were reproduced locally. Human-initiated test callers now explicitly carry their authenticated request origin; scheduled/unidentified callers remain un-attributed. Autonomous cron expectations retain the original isolation actor and separately expect agent creator attribution. No production permission or creator logic changed in this repair. All 202 selected tests across six files pass (32 hosted/read/real-Gateway + 170 input/cron/transport); three-file type-aware lint and formatting pass. Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Exact-head [CI39519573314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39519573314) passed on attempt1 (73 jobs successful, 24 skipped, none failed/pending). ClawSweeper revision9 cleared this head with no findings or before-merge items.

**Inherited CI repair:** the preceding run exposed typescript(unbound-method) in src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts, introduced upstream by #178767. The extracted callback lost the direct check's receiver. This revision binds that callback to the check; it does not alter creator attribution. The new regression failed on the unchanged implementation, then passed with all 11 selected Doctor tests (38.23s Vitest duration; approximately 0.6s test time), type-aware lint, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review. ClawSweeper revision 8 cleared that exact 715efead head with no findings; its CI subsequently exposed the fixture failures repaired above.

Earlier integration 194ab6d6d460ef5156ad34d3ac4f296be7b6da0e incorporates main 598e945b9ff5366d1c4976c9078b26cd57d19239 after GitHub reported a conflict; removal of the setting eliminated the generated-config overlap, so no manual merge resolution was needed.

- **Default-behavior regression:** the real Gateway test first failed against the gated implementation because the causal creator stamp was missing. It passes after removal without enabling any experimental setting.
- **Real Gateway final effects:** an isolated TLS Gateway authenticates four synthetic principals and executes the actual agent sessions-create tool. The causal human can publish/unpublish and archive/restore; selected execution/isolation identity and assignee cannot. Live role revocation after admission prevents the persistent mutation. Model-provider HTTP responses are replayed, not live external inference.
- **Delegation:** 95 tests pass across the full native spawn seam and production-boundary files, including hidden/visible/queued delegation, guest-owned children, cancellation, rollback, and retained requester custody. Seven ACP authority tests and seven provenance tests pass. Guest fixtures now supply the authenticated causal request separately from execution authority; assertions retain model restrictions and required isolation.
- **Refreshed-main proof:** 11 Gateway, cron, and provenance tests pass on the integrated candidate. Cron coverage checks causal-human, autonomous, and explicit no-human origin with a selected execution user; updates preserve the original creation stamp.
- **Static checks:** core TypeScript checking, type-aware lint of all 27 changed TypeScript files, formatting, diff checks, and generated configuration baseline checks pass on the removal revision. Frozen dependency installation and config-baseline verification pass after integration. Independent P0–P2 review of the removal revision found no actionable findings; it reviewed supplied source/evidence and did not independently rerun tests.
- **Current-head CI and ClawSweeper:** exact 3f0e121451973deef51ee10f1c63f0e36c6f4319 passed CI39519573314 attempt1. [ClawSweeper revision9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178493#issuecomment-6294276782) cleared the same head. All currently reported checks are passing or intentionally skipped; no inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was used for this head.

<details>
<summary>Retained compatibility evidence and limits</summary>

Published OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (build 1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8) created synthetic state through released production writers. After producer processes stopped, the original four state/config files were backed up and byte-compared; SQLite integrity checks passed. Candidate Doctor, SDK writes, and fresh-process cold reopen passed on earlier head 48aef8bfd0d3c867d5c681418702d6de04d039d0.

Original creators, assigned owners, settings, two crons, all six transcript events, dedicated ACP metadata, and required isolation namespaces were preserved. New causal-human and autonomous sessions/crons survived reopen. Earlier same-schema baseline → candidate → baseline-write → candidate proof preserved three sessions and three crons. Six selected automatic-rollback owner scenarios passed, including refusal to discard post-migration writes.

This removal does not change the persisted representation, but those historical runs are not claimed as exact-current-head full upgrade tests. These are isolated stored-state and controlled rollback-owner proofs, not production deployment, live external model inference, container startup, complete updater package swapping, or cross-schema downgrade. No production settings/state were changed. Exact first-party package-age exceptions used for disposable historical installs did not relax third-party, integrity, or global policy.

</details>

prs.title: fix: updater refuses replaced retained runtime files
prs.body:
Closes #178823.
Related: #177877 and #165822.

## What problem this solves

Updater runtime retention inventories the installed package before it materializes a retained worker tree. If a trusted local process replaces an inventoried pathname just before the updater hard-links it, current behavior can retain different, same-size bytes and continue the update.

This change checks the retained file's identity after the link. An unchanged device/inode keeps the existing fast path. A changed device/inode must match the inventoried size, mode, and SHA-256; an equivalent filesystem copy-up is accepted, while a different replacement is rejected.

This is P3 integrity hardening. The reproduction requires a trusted process that can already replace installed OpenClaw code; it does not create a new attacker boundary. Writes through an already-linked inode remain trusted-host best effort.

## Maintainer policy decision pending

The unresolved policy question is whether this narrower changed-identity admission rule should supersede the relevant part of the best-effort concurrent-source-edit policy accepted in #177877.

- #177877 deliberately removed full identity recertification and accepted concurrent source edits as best effort.
- This PR keeps that policy for the ordinary same-device/same-inode hard-link path.
- It adds one narrower rule when the retained entry has a different device/inode: accept exact size/mode/content equivalence (including copy-up), otherwise stop before using the retained generation.
- ClawSweeper's initial review recommends preserving #177877 absent an observed production incident. This PR recommends the narrower rule because it closes the deterministic pathname-substitution case without hashing the ordinary fast path or rejecting content-equivalent copy-up.

No owner approval is claimed here; the explicit decision remains a merge gate.

## Real owner-path behavior proof

The proof harness invokes the production owners directly:

```text
src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-tree.ts#prepareUpdateCandidatePluginTrees
src/infra/update-retained-runtime-tree.ts#linkUpdateCandidatePluginTrees
```

It uses a synthetic on-disk fixture, inventories a real file, intercepts that file's actual `fs.link` operation, and exercises two filesystem outcomes deterministically. The base is the immutable parent `a29367087a4ea9dd98adb9fd9870e3f68e83f6d8`; the patch is `3551d3661aafffefcb8d44b9add2a67c0e59705d`. This is owner-path fault injection; the separate upgrade-survivor run below exercises the packaged `openclaw update` flow.

The inventoried file is 38 bytes, mode `0444`, SHA-256:

```text
d6437415b40d984a61de45212809aaa6379678a0b8fbb007de05e43ce9816985
```

The same-size foreign replacement is 38 bytes, mode `0444`, SHA-256:

```text
897c3c4c4a1d7464d27dfff811bb83e3bab9dbb77dc7f6ea10c77861e868b34b
```

Observed results:

| Revision | Scenario at `fs.link` | Device/inode | Retained bytes | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| parent `a2936708` | Path renamed and replaced with foreign same-size bytes | changed | foreign hash | **accepted** (`linked: 1`) |
| patch `3551d366` | Path renamed and replaced with foreign same-size bytes | changed | foreign hash | **rejected**: `Plugin entry changed after snapshot inventory: <fixture>/source/dist/unique.js` |
| parent `a2936708` | Content-equivalent different-inode copy-up | changed | inventory hash | **accepted** (`linked: 1`) |
| patch `3551d366` | Content-equivalent different-inode copy-up | changed | inventory hash | **accepted** (`linked: 1`) |

Redacted machine output:

```text
BASE replacement
revision=a29367087a4ea9dd98adb9fd9870e3f68e83f6d8
intercepted=true sameSize=true bytesDiffer=true
outcome=accepted linked=1 copied=0
destination.identityMatchesInventory=false
destination.sha256=897c3c4c4a1d7464d27dfff811bb83e3bab9dbb77dc7f6ea10c77861e868b34b
destination.bytesMatchInventory=false

HEAD replacement
revision=3551d3661aafffefcb8d44b9add2a67c0e59705d
intercepted=true sameSize=true bytesDiffer=true
outcome=rejected
error=Plugin entry changed after snapshot inventory: <fixture>/source/dist/unique.js

BASE copy-up
revision=a29367087a4ea9dd98adb9fd9870e3f68e83f6d8
intercepted=true outcome=accepted linked=1 copied=0
destination.identityMatchesInventory=false
destination.mode=0444
destination.sha256=d6437415b40d984a61de45212809aaa6379678a0b8fbb007de05e43ce9816985
destination.bytesMatchInventory=true

HEAD copy-up
revision=3551d3661aafffefcb8d44b9add2a67c0e59705d
intercepted=true outcome=accepted linked=1 copied=0
destination.identityMatchesInventory=false
destination.mode=0444
destination.sha256=d6437415b40d984a61de45212809aaa6379678a0b8fbb007de05e43ce9816985
destination.bytesMatchInventory=true
```

Artifact SHA-256 values:

```text
base-replacement.json     0c2563e27e3a4317e51d9fc27d6d43461b982e826a156aae0a9fa4fe0c71fb22
patched-replacement.json  ee966ad829fc77dfcfd51b8690a36a3650a6bea092ce773c98098a73e4f8227e
base-copyup.json          0aeb17fcc579675bf5f59d0d574378dd96073324825ef51f9c2b7ebd05481cab
patched-copyup.json       f9db005408641f32e7efef957439157b5189c8260ea1916569d716b2eb14189c
```

## Latest-stable upgrade and state survival

The repository's published-upgrade-survivor Docker harness installed `openclaw@latest` (`2026.10.5`), then ran `openclaw update` to the package built from exact head `3551d3661aafffefcb8d44b9add2a67c0e59705d`.

Candidate package:

```text
version=2026.10.5
buildId=2026.10.5-3551d3661aaf-2026-10-20T22-55-44.951Z
tarball.sha256=e7f2d5716226e844b134f9ac2ab075b1e97e8368c1cab85be85234c23fb56313
```

The first hop passed each required phase:

```text
install-baseline                         passed
validate-baseline-config                 passed
candidate-package-identity               passed
assert-baseline                          passed
update-candidate                         passed
installed-package-identity               passed
assert-automatic-migration               passed
mobile-pairing-candidate-first           passed
mobile-pairing-candidate-restart         passed
doctor                                   passed
validate-post-doctor-config              passed
assert-survival                          passed
```

`assert-survival` executes the harness's production-grade config and state assertions after the update. It verified the seeded update, Gateway auth, model/provider, agent, skill, plugin, channel, and logging configuration; workspace identity; legacy session and migrated session metadata; execution-approval policy; configured plugin installs; and retained runtime-dependency state. This is the requested latest-stable-to-candidate upgrade with settings and data intact.

## Additional compound-lane observation

The broader `update-restart-auth` lane continued after that successful latest-stable first hop into a synthetic second update (`2026.10.5` exact head -> `2026.10.6-first-hop.0`). It **did not pass overall**, so it is not counted as green validation.

The second update receipt itself reported `status: ok`; all four admission checks were `ok`; runtime retention completed (`40,535` entries, `36,204` linked, `1,578` copied); the future package installed; and Gateway verification reported `serviceRunning: true`, `versionMatch: true`, `readyz: true`, `channelsReady: true`, `settled: true`, with no plugin errors.

The lane then exited 1 at `recovery-update-result-assertion` because the receipt contained a failed core step:

```text
post-plugin doctor: exit 1
Original state capture was unavailable: file not found.
Automatic database restoration cannot attribute migration writes:
SQLite migration source changed after update capture.
```

The post-plugin Doctor failure was classified in the receipt as `recoverable-maintenance`; its follow-up lint contained zero errors (`43` warnings, `18` info) but also exited 1. This compound-lane failure is outside the retained-file identity change and is disclosed here rather than represented as a pass.

## Validation

Passed:

- `pnpm test src/infra/update-retained-runtime-tree.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-tree.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-retained-runtime-files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- Targeted Oxlint and formatting checks for the changed TypeScript and docs files
- Documentation content, formatting, and link checks
- `git diff --check`
- Exact-head package build and integrity inspection; all 107 npm package locks validated
- Codex Security immutable patch-risk assessment: `merge` / `human_review_required`; no actionable security defect was found in the patch, and the intentional policy change requires the owner decision above
- Repository autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; TruffleHog clean

`pnpm release:check` completed the build/package stages and then exited 1 on existing plugin-version drift. The same focused check fails identically on the parent and patch revisions:

```text
Synced plugin versions to 2026.10.5. Updated: 2. Changelogged: 0. Skipped: 169.
  update required: @openclaw/levanto
  update required: @openclaw/subq
Run `pnpm plugins:sync` and commit the plugin version alignment.
```

The drift is unrelated to this four-file updater change and was not altered in this PR.

prs.title: improve: keep typing responsive during streamed replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming a reply into a long conversation repeatedly prepares unrelated pane and composer state, increasing CPU work and typing latency.

## User Impact

Typing stays more responsive while replies stream. Message contents, synchronous state reads, terminal-event ordering, and reader scroll ownership remain intact.

The Solid campaign coordinator explicitly accepted this measured tradeoff: script CPU median 5,017 → 3,366 ms (−33%), p95 5,363 → 3,495 ms; typing run-median 11.75 → 9.30 ms (−21%); frame-gap run-p95 unchanged (16.7 ms); estimated dropped frames median 0 → 1 (p95 1 → 2) — an absolute change of about one estimated frame over a ~21 s / ~1,290-frame stream with overlapping ranges ([0–1] vs [0–2]) and no frame-gap movement. Accepted by the Solid campaign coordinator as a net improvement; the dropped-frame estimate is recorded, not waived silently.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing run-state owner separates text-only publications from non-text changes. Render adapters retain lazy stream getters through Solid `merge`, and the composer derives whether a stream exists. Geometry commits continue to follow growing content; locked readers also receive same-height unread notifications. No second store or batching owner is added.

The committed benchmark retains publication, pane preparation, resize, HTML parsing, geometry, style, and frame counters. It also checks that the actual pane grows and finishes within two pixels of the native scroll bottom without manually requesting a render. Existing frame coalescing already works: 645 writes in six-delta bursts produced 108 publications, so no new queue is needed.

## Evidence

Ten serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, 400 synthetic messages, 645 snapshots at 30/s, native keyboard input every 500 ms, release bundles, untraced. Values are **median / p95 [min–max]** across ten runs per side. Typing measures trusted keydown to next animation frame; dropped frames are estimated from animation-frame gaps, not physical presentation timestamps.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Script CPU, ms | 5017.28 / 5362.54 [4811.48–5429.99] | 3366.11 / 3494.89 [3222.43–3538.96] |
| Task CPU, ms | 9217.84 / 9702.85 [8968.26–9808.93] | 7346.13 / 7583.04 [7082.86–7651.78] |
| Typing run-median, ms | 11.75 / 13.36 [9.70–13.40] | 9.30 / 10.63 [7.70–10.90] |
| Typing run-p95, ms | 17.82 / 19.05 [16.60–19.07] | 16.78 / 17.59 [15.93–17.69] |
| Frame-gap run-p95, ms | 16.74 / 16.80 [16.70–16.80] | 16.70 / 16.80 [16.70–16.80] |
| Estimated dropped frames | 0.00 / 1.00 [0.00–1.00] | 1.00 / 2.00 [0.00–2.00] |
| Pane preparations | 978.50 / 986.65 [974.00–988.00] | 353.00 / 354.55 [351.00–355.00] |
| Rectangle reads | 382.00 / 384.55 [378.00–385.00] | 307.00 / 309.55 [301.00–310.00] |
| Style reads | 4804.50 / 4818.15 [4789.00–4824.00] | 3466.00 / 3494.60 [3457.00–3500.00] |

All 20 runs delivered every delta, grew the transcript by 12,625–12,626 px, and ended exactly at the scroll bottom. Rendered markup matched; raw HTML differed only in empty Solid comment markers. Screenshots below are inspected synthetic fixtures.

Measurement caveat: an HTML character-diff diagnostic briefly used one CPU core near pair five before being stopped. No samples were excluded. The first three candidate runs already showed the frame difference before this interruption; it is included in the coordinator's acceptance rather than explained away.

The accepted measurement used `1d5a36ccc2d` against `e2a44c21e27`. The requested rebase onto `0f46faecf63` produced a byte-identical patch at `d520ca1945e`; no benchmark rerun was used to seek a different result.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused ownership suite | 9/9 passed on rebased head, default pinned Bun, one worker |
| UI types | Passed on rebased head, default tsrs |
| Scoped lint / format | Passed on rebased head (three Solid analysis warnings) |
| Production Knip | Passed on rebased head |
| Independent P0–P2 review | Clean on identical accepted patch; synchronous writes, terminal publication, locked arrivals, and lazy props reviewed |
| Startup | Final-head CI `control-ui-performance` passed: **325,707 B gzip**, 7 JS requests, **1 CSS request**; advisory size warning retained. Local measured pair: 325,922 → 325,919 B gzip, 1 CSS request each. CI is authoritative per coordinator |
| Broad proof | Final [`ci:full` run 39518656498](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39518656498), attempt 1, on `865e964f4e5`: **50 passed, 22 skipped, no failures**. All UI units, nine mocked UI E2E shards, both real-Gateway shards, startup performance, security, and aggregate CI gate passed |

Command: `OPENCLAW_CONTROL_UI_BUILD_ID=85886a1ef08d6e0a7822efa658891a4a8fefbb30 NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts --bundle-dir <baseline-ui> --compare-bundle-dir <candidate-ui> --streaming-reply --transcript-messages 400 --face chat --runs 20 --untraced --output <artifacts>`.

A retained midpoint profile (#323, 7,752 characters) measured 0.30 ms delivery plus microtasks, followed by 8.85 ms sampled reactive work in a 34.1 ms window. This is browser rendering proof with synthetic WebSocket traffic, not a live provider throughput claim.

Whole-file LOC across 17 changed files: **8,613 → 8,893 (+280)**: production +58, tests +87, benchmark/docs +135. The additional notification channel removes broad invalidation; regression checks protect invalidation and scroll ownership, and instrumentation exposes remaining work. Solid checklist in touched production: effects 1 → 1, intentional initial `untrack` snapshots 2 → 2; render effects, raw listeners, DOM queries, `flush`, and owner capture 0 → 0. No dependency, startup import, or lazy-boundary change.

Related: #178618. Supersedes the unmerged experiment in #178675; this PR retains main's geometry subscription.

![After: synthetic streamed reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ebb7983-57f3-4c0f-9999-b6662817f984)

## CI failure attribution

Run [39493552958](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39493552958) fails `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` at `mock-exports`: `src/commands/doctor-database-network-storage.test.ts:15: ./doctor-database-engine-inspection.js`. The identical check and source-location failure occurs in the scheduled main run [39493026824](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39493026824) at this PR's merge base `0f46faecf63`. The affected test, checker, and baseline are unchanged by this PR. This is retained as an inherited failure, not reported as passing CI. The same run passed all three UI unit shards and both real-Gateway shards. Control UI E2E shard 6/9 also exposed an obsolete expectation in `commits a streamed delta burst in frame-bound transcript batches`: it required a full page/pane commit, which this optimization deliberately removes. The test now requires zero such commits while retaining the final rendered-text wait and 2–180 DOM mutation batch bounds. All counters remain. Focused browser replay passed (1.62 s test; 15.64 s Vitest wall), and independent P0–P2 review is clean. The correction changes only this assertion and explanation; production code and accepted performance measurements are unchanged. Correction head: `d66a95698046`; fresh `ci:full` CI is requested on that head. All earlier passing proof with unchanged production inputs is retained, not rerun.


The replacement run [39508921549](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39508921549) passed all UI units and every mocked UI E2E shard, including the corrected stream-burst case. Its real-Gateway shard exposed `opens Settings pickers from publication and acquires only on Refresh or Retry`. That name passed the sampled main runs, so it was not classified as inherited. Merged current `main` to include the existing fixture-owner repair from #178735; the single real-Gateway case then passed locally (4.75 s case, 43.86 s Vitest wall). Refreshed tsrs and production Knip passed. Main integration produced `c66cb83a6a30`; the complete PR patch against main is byte-identical to the reviewed patch before integration. No new production changes or benchmark reruns. Fresh full CI: [39514295386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39514295386), head `c66cb83a6a30578854aeb1c836e41376e67142e5`.


Pre-integration run [39514295386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39514295386), attempt 1, completed on `c66cb83a6a30578854aeb1c836e41376e67142e5`: **47 jobs passed, 22 skipped**, one inherited lint root and its downstream aggregate failed. The sole root is `check-lint-core-2`: `src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts:73:28`, `typescript(unbound-method)`. Running the same linter against that file at this branch's main merge base `e9e4dae427fc57bc0e8a79d307fc8e1898355efb` reproduces the identical diagnostic. The entire `src/flows` tree, `.oxlintrc.json`, `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` are byte-identical between that reproduction, actual CI baseline `e213fdbeef1c81e5c44b0ed6bf6d9f94346188db`, and tested merge `d1bae5f658774089b7f23562d2a79bef9db32619`. Native admin evidence binds the checkout, exact failure, local baseline reproduction, source objects, and final job inventory by SHA-256. Pre-integration CI startup measurement: **325,700 B gzip, 7 JS requests, 1 CSS request**; `control-ui-performance` passed with its recorded advisory size warning. This is the coordinator-designated authoritative startup result.

The existing lazy-prop fix now lives in that owner, with obsolete question wiring removed; composer stream-presence derivation is retained. prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove redundant delivery and private bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins duplicate existing delivery and setup owners, retain unread state, and repeat already-validated work.

## User Impact

No supported feature, configuration key, protocol, or persisted shape changes. Security effect checks, ordinary durability, account isolation, response bounds, and real concurrency remain. Current-host-only Canvas calls now propagate node.list errors directly; explicit Nostr sends can retry a relay that has recovered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing core delivery and Plugin SDK setup/text owners, share Claude migration's bounded scanner, and remove private bookkeeping or test-only operations. The remaining small cuts eliminate repeated canonicalization, no-op forwarding, duplicated deadlines, unmeasured executable caching, and immutable package self-checks. Credential and HTTP catalog caches with real scope contracts stay.

Production delta: 371 net lines removed across 17 plugins. The change is a final residue bundle; no SDK exports, dependencies, schemas, or public options are removed.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Nostr's five-failure/30-second send suppression came with the initial implementation (7b6cbf58697c), with no human incident found for it in inspected history. A still-down relay may be retried on each explicit send; bounded library attempts, preferred healthy relays, and fallback remain.
- QuickJS worker assets are fixed for a process lifetime. The initial implementation (#154522) compared the resolved URL on every call without a human report requiring mid-process package replacement. Replacing those assets now requires restart rather than pool replacement.
- Canvas is bundled with its current host, as extensions/AGENTS.md requires. The older-host fallback from 330ba1fa3194 is removed; an incompatible Gateway now returns its clear error. The human-reported error propagation repair in #126609 is retained.
- Linux executable discovery no longer retains the process cache introduced in #107193; no measured benefit was established in its provenance. Discovery performs ordinary executable-access probes and observes installation/removal instead of preserving a stale result.
- The llama.cpp media catalog no longer checks its immutable compiled build constant against a second literal. Release changes still need recipe verification; actual executable version/checksum checks and activation/resource constraints remain.
- ClickClack's error callback is the runtime logger. The nested logger-throws catch from #116683 has no human incident in its inspected provenance; an unexpected logger failure now propagates rather than being silently swallowed. Transport errors remain caught and reported. Tests use the real 700ms coalescing interval on a simulated clock instead of a test-only option.
- Wiki timestamp callers supply real clocks or valid internal timestamps. The triple fallback from #124808 covered only a synthetic invalid injected clock; such misuse now throws the ordinary Date error. External imported timestamp validation and filesystem fallback remain.
- Wiki lookup no longer re-matches the ID after reading the selected path (#166433; no human incident found for that extra check). If a page ID changes between scan and read, the result is the current visible contents at that selected path. Filesystem and visibility validation remain.

Other removals do not relax guards: Xiaomi's existing guarded fetch owns its deadline through body consumption; Google timestamp/mark implementations are no-ops; Team Reports' removed operation had only test callers after #159101; LINE IDs are normalized at their provider boundary; cookie values are canonicalized before comparison; Hugging Face's existing SDK owner does not mutate the supplied catalog.

## Evidence

The first CI run found two PR-caused proof issues: the setup test unnecessarily awaited a synchronous SDK method, and the assertion ratchet required removing the allowance for two deleted casts. Both are repaired without changing production or assertions. The repair passes all 3 setup tests and 14 suppression tests (49.33s serial wrapper), targeted production/test-file types, focused syntax lint/format, and the assertion-safety ratchet. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is clean. Full typed lint could not start locally because SDK declaration preparation reached its existing 300000ms limit under shared-host load; the next exact-head CI owns that gate. No deadline was raised or job rerun.

Focused runtime batches passed: 133 tests for setup/Canvas/QuickJS/migration; 121 for the remaining changed owners; 15 for Hugging Face and existing SDK onboarding contracts. The earlier checkpoint's focused proof covers Zalo and Nostr, including real loopback core message delivery/authority and WebSocket relay recovery controls. These are retained batch results, not a unique test total; collision-held slices were dropped afterward. No retries, skips, or raised deadlines were introduced.

The final ClickClack/Wiki cuts pass 46 focused tests covering durable activity, ephemeral progress and failures, status/Doctor, concurrent 200-page scans, path/ID lookup and visibility, ingest, and preservation of human notes. The typed warning-code lookup trusts the warning owner's finite union instead of guarding it again.

Targeted production package typechecks and explicit QuickJS test-helper types pass. Changed-file syntax lint/format, mandatory lint-suppressions (14 tests), whitespace, and scoped runtime/static cycle checks pass with zero cycles. Author simplification and independent P0–P2 review are complete, with no actionable findings. Exact-head hosted CI is the broad gate; no paid or live provider/channel request was made. PostgreSQL runtime parity remains a hosted-environment gap; its dispatch/conformance changes only remove the retired operation.

prs.title: fix(update): keep the operation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` arms its operation deadline with `Date.now()` (wall clock) but settles the timeout through `setTimeout` (monotonic clock). When NTP sync, sleep/wake, or a manual clock correction rewinds the wall clock 90 seconds mid-update, the deadline recalculates an inflated remaining budget and delays cancellation past the configured timeout.

- **Problem**: `createUpdateOperationDeadline` seeds `deadlineAtMs = Date.now() + timeoutMs` and passes it to `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` / `awaitWithinDeadline` without a `now` override, so both default to `Date.now()`. `setTimeout` consumes that budget on the monotonic clock — a cross-clock-domain mismatch.
- **Solution**: Switch the seed and all comparisons to `performance.now()` and pass `() => performance.now()` into `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` and `awaitWithinDeadline` so the entire chain stays on one monotonic clock. At the SQLite admission boundary (`withSqliteDatabaseAdmissionWait`), translate the monotonic deadline's remaining budget back into an epoch timestamp (`Date.now() + max(0, deadlineAtMs - performance.now())`) to preserve the relay's `Math.max(0, deadlineAtMs - Date.now())` epoch contract.
- **What changed**: `update-operation-deadline.ts` — 4 clock call sites + 1 admission-boundary epoch translation. 7 test files — `performance.now` spies folded into existing `fakeTimers()` blocks + 1 regression test for the epoch translation.
- **What did NOT change**: No signature changes. No config, persistence, or telemetry changes. `deadlineAtMs` is purely process-internal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `absolute-deadline.ts` canonical owner already supports a `now` parameter (`node-registry.invoke-stream.ts` uses `performance.now()` + `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline(..., () => performance.now())` as the correct pattern). `status.ts` already seeds its admission `deadlineAtMs` with `Date.now() + timeoutMs` (epoch) — this PR aligns the update-operation-deadline caller with both patterns: monotonic internally, epoch at the admission boundary.

- **Best fix**: Reuse the existing `now` parameter; translate at the boundary the relay already owns.
- **Risk**: Minimal. Deadline is process-internal, not persisted.

## User Impact

`openclaw update` operations respect their configured timeout budget reliably, even when the system wall clock jumps (NTP correction, sleep/wake recovery). Stalled updates no longer hang past their timeout, and healthy updates are no longer killed early by forward clock jumps.

## Evidence

### Real `openclaw update` CLI — clock-skew proof through shipped dist (head `b58654a5`)

Real `openclaw update` run with an ESM loader preload that intercepts the shipped `update-command-executor` dist module. The preload forces a 1000 ms activation budget and injects a −90 s wall-clock rewind 50 ms after the deadline is seeded. `performance.now` and `setTimeout` run genuinely; only `Date.now` is patched to inject the skew. Same script, only the deadline clock source differs (pre-fix = revert source to `Date.now`).

```console
# POST-FIX (performance.now) — 90s wall-clock rewind injected after deadline seed
[PROOF] Deadline seeded: timeoutMs=1000, deadlineAtMs=231106.521767, clock=post-fix, wall=rewind
[PROOF] Clock jumped -90000ms (rewind) at 230166ms
Phase: finished
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: update-activation-timeout.
Admission checks: config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok.
VERDICT: BOUNDED — deadline fired within budget despite 90s rewind

# PRE-FIX (Date.now) — same script, 90s wall-clock rewind injected after deadline seed
[PROOF] Deadline seeded: timeoutMs=1000, deadlineAtMs=1791873142594, clock=pre-fix, wall=rewind
[PROOF] Clock jumped -90000ms (rewind) at 1791873051657ms
Phase: finished
ℹ️ OpenClaw update skipped: already-current.
Admission checks: config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok.
VERDICT: UNBOUNDED — deadline never fired; update ran to completion past the 1000ms budget
```

The seed values show the clock-domain difference: pre-fix seeds `deadlineAtMs=1791873142594` (epoch `Date.now()`); post-fix seeds `deadlineAtMs=231106.521767` (monotonic `performance.now()`). After the −90 s rewind, the pre-fix epoch deadline is inflated by 90 s and never fires; the post-fix monotonic deadline is unaffected and fires `update-activation-timeout`. SQLite admission checks ran in both runs (`config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok`), confirming the epoch boundary translation preserves the relay contract.

### Epoch admission boundary — pre-fix vs post-fix

The SQLite relay computes `Math.max(0, deadlineAtMs - Date.now())`. Before boundary translation, `deadlineAtMs` was raw monotonic (~5000), underflowing against epoch `Date.now()` (~1.79e12):

```
PRE-FIX:  admissionDeadline=61443  Date.now()=1792473168708  remaining=-1792473107264 → immediate timeout
POST-FIX: admissionDeadline=1792473223756  Date.now()=1792473163785  remaining=59971 → correct budget
```

### Normal-mode upgrade (latest stable v2026.10.5 → reviewed candidate with PR fix)

Real `openclaw update` from the npm-published latest stable v2026.10.5 to the reviewed candidate (head `b58654a5`, containing the `performance.now()` deadline fix). The candidate tarball was built from the worktree dist; an ESM loader preload redirects `@openclaw/ai/*` imports to the workspace dist so the candidate's updated exports resolve correctly. Isolated `HOME` with default `~/.openclaw` state, `--no-restart`:

```console
Phase: requested
  ✓ package-install (118.54s)
Phase: staging
Phase: validating
  ✓ updater-runtime-retention (170.03s)
  ✓ candidate-state-snapshot (36.46s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor (68.83s)
  ! candidate-doctor-lint (51.77s)  — advisory deferrals only
  ✓ candidate-config (9.65s)
  ✓ candidate-plugins (10.73s)
  ✓ candidate-recovery (12.22s)
  ✓ candidate-gateway-startup (45.4s)
Phase: activating
  ✓ database snapshot (14.76s)
  ! openclaw doctor (17.99s)  — recoverable: process-inspection failure (host busy)
Phase: finished

⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: openclaw doctor.
```

auto_merge.commit_title: fix(update): keep the operation deadline on the monotonic clock (#169151)
auto_merge.commit_message:
The update operation deadline seeded its absolute deadline with Date.now()
and fed the remaining budget to setTimeout via scheduleAbsoluteDeadline and
awaitWithinDeadline, which default to Date.now() for their clock reads.
setTimeout runs on the monotonic clock, so a wall-clock correction (NTP sync,
sleep/wake) stretched or shrank the configured budget: a backward jump let
the update operation hang past its timeout, a forward jump killed healthy
updates early. Seed and compare against performance.now() and pass
() => performance.now() into the deadline utilities so the whole chain
stays on one monotonic clock.

Ref: BUG-117-update-operation-deadline-wall-clock (local finding)

prs.title: fix(cron): preserve whitespace in command cwd CLI options
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw automations add --command-cwd "/repo/job "` (or `--on-exit-cwd`/`--stream-cwd`) silently rewrites the working directory to `/repo/job` before the cron command runs, so the command executes in the wrong directory while reporting success. On Unix `/repo/job ` is a legal, distinct directory. This switches all cwd CLI options and downstream normalization/identity/lookup sites from trimming readers (`normalizeOptionalString`/`.trim()`) to whitespace-preserving `readNonBlankString`, matching `command`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair spans every cwd trim site end-to-end:

- **CLI boundary**: `schedule-options.ts` (`onExitCwd`/`streamCwd`), `register.cron-add.ts` (`commandCwd`), and the edit path `register.cron-edit.ts` (edit still parsed cwd with a trimming reader while add already preserved it).
- **Gateway normalization**: `normalize.ts` (`coerceSchedule` `cwdRaw`), `normalize-payload.ts` (`payload.cwd`).
- **Schedule identity** (`schedule-identity.ts:71,87`): on-exit/stream identity used `normalizeOptionalString(schedule.cwd)`, so a cwd edit `/repo/job` → `/repo/job ` looked unchanged → `scheduleChanged=false` → a running on-exit payload with `deleteAfterRun=true` could delete the job. Now uses `readNonBlankString`.
- **Windows executable lookup**: `executable-path.ts:34` and `windows-command.ts:74` resolved against `options.cwd.trim()`. Both now use raw cwd, matching the spawned child cwd.

`readNonBlankString` is the same primitive each function already uses for `command`, removing within-function inconsistency. Blank cwd still returns `undefined` (rejected), unchanged.

## User Impact

Pass a cron cwd with leading/trailing whitespace and the command runs in exactly that directory. Cwd-whitespace-only edits are detected as real changes (preventing accidental job deletion). Windows relative-executable selection agrees with the spawned cwd. Blank cwd still rejected; other paths unaffected.

## Evidence

Before/after — stored cwd at each layer for input `"/repo/job "`:

| Layer | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CLI add + edit | `"/repo/job"` (trimmed) | `"/repo/job "` (preserved) |
| Gateway normalize | `"/repo/job"` (trimmed) | `"/repo/job "` (preserved) |
| Schedule identity | trimmed → edits look identical | preserved → edits detected |
| Windows lookup | trimmed cwd | raw cwd |

Gateway + schedule-identity + executable-path regressions (pre-fix RED / post-fix GREEN): `coerceSchedule`/`normalizeCronPayload` store `"/repo/job "` verbatim; blank rejected; identity detects cwd edits (RED); executable-path resolves ` job/tool` (RED). `vitest`: 40 passed.

Windows production fn proof (pre-fix vs post-fix):

```console
$ tsx windows-selection-production-fn.mts
FIXED   resolveExecutablePathCandidate('bin/tool.exe',{cwd:".../job "}) -> .../job /bin/tool.exe
PRE-FIX resolveExecutablePathCandidate('bin/tool.exe',{cwd:".../job"})  -> .../job/bin/tool.exe
PATH case: relative entry `bin` resolved vs raw cwd -> .../job /bin/tool  (PASS)
```

Full shipped CLI → Gateway → SQLite → spawn (local dev Gateway, Unix, head `bffc5d6`):

```console
$ openclaw cron add proof-job --command "sh ./marker.sh" --command-cwd "/tmp/oc-proof-work/job " --every 1h
{ "payload": { ..., "cwd": "/tmp/oc-proof-work/job " } }
$ openclaw cron run <id> --wait   # status ok, exitCode 0
$ ls "/tmp/oc-proof-work/job "/ran-in-*   # only trailing-space dir has marker
```

Native Windows proof (GitHub Actions `windows-latest`, shipped `openclaw.mjs` → dev Gateway → SQLite → spawn, head `bffc5d6`):

```console
=== CASE 1: Relative executable (bin\tool.cmd), trailing-space cwd ===
Stored cwd: C:\oc-winproof\job  (length 19 — trailing space preserved)
Summary: selected_executable=C:\oc-winproof\job\bin\tool.cmd  child_cwd=C:\oc-winproof\job
Diagnostics: command ok: "bin\\tool.cmd"  ExitCode: 0

=== CASE 2: Bare executable (tool) via PATH=bin, trailing-space cwd ===
Stored cwd: C:\oc-winproof\job  (length 19 — trailing space preserved)
Summary: selected_executable=C:\oc-winproof\job\bin\tool.cmd  child_cwd=C:\oc-winproof\job
Diagnostics: command ok: "tool"  ExitCode: 0
```

Case 1 tests `resolveExecutablePathCandidate` (relative executable with separator); Case 2 tests `resolveWindowsCommandFromCwdOrPath` (bare executable via relative PATH). Stored cwd preserves trailing space (length 19) through CLI, Gateway, SQLite, and executable resolution. Both commands executed (exitCode 0). `selected_executable`/`child_cwd` reflect Windows `CreateProcessW` trailing-space trim on `lpCurrentDirectory` (OS-level, outside this PR's scope). Unix full-chain (above) shows end-to-end execution in trailing-space dir.

Real upgrade proof (stable v2026.10.4 → candidate, same SQLite, head `bffc5d6`):

```console
# stable v2026.10.4 creates job with trailing-space cwd → stored TRIMMED (bug)
# kill stable, launch candidate on same state → existing job loads/runs (status ok)
# candidate creates new job → stored cwd preserved (fixed), marker in trailing-space dir
```

| Created by | Stored cwd | Runs in |
|---|---|---|
| stable v2026.10.4 | `/tmp/oc-dm-work/job` (trimmed) | plain dir |
| candidate `bffc5d6` | `/tmp/oc-dm-work/job ` (preserved) | trailing-space dir |

Existing settings/jobs load and work after upgrade; no schema/migration change. Edge cases: empty/undefined cwd → `process.cwd()`; all-blank → `undefined`.

Full cwd-relevant shard: 7 files, 164 tests passed.

## Maintainer fixup

Maintainer fixup (cfdf580): the shared executable/Windows lookups now keep #172814's blank-cwd fallback. A non-blank cwd is used verbatim (whitespace preserved); a whitespace-only cwd still falls back to `process.cwd()`. `src/infra/executable-path.ts` stays as on main, and `src/process/windows-command.ts` uses the same rule, with blank-cwd regression tests for both.

prs.title: fix(x): recheck administrator authority before paid lookups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An administrator can lose current authority while X refreshes its OAuth token for an allowlist username lookup. The handler refuses the eventual allowlist write, but the intervening paid username request still goes out: that single-user API method did not forward the existing dispatch-authority callback.

## User Impact

An in-flight allowlist add no longer buys an X username lookup after administrator authority is retired during preparation. The existing signal-cancellation behavior and grant-write authorization remain intact. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thread the existing private `XAssertActive` capability through the single-user lookup, as the batch lookup already does. The administrator handler supplies the final synchronous current-authority assertion; the existing request/fetch owner runs it immediately before dispatch, after OAuth and asynchronous preparation. Keep the single-user endpoint, response parsing, OAuth rotation, budget reservation/settlement, post-lookup authorization and commit guard unchanged.

This is an adjacent real bug fix under the campaign's any-size exception, not a LARGE cleanup: nine production lines added and 65 net test lines added across three files. The original allowlist path came from #165138; this is a reproduced defect, not a claimed human-filed incident.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No reliability guard is removed. Calls already dispatched while authority was current remain ordinary in-flight paid work and retain their existing settlement semantics. This fix prevents a new dispatch after retirement; it does not cancel shared OAuth refresh or claim to undo an external request.

## Evidence

The registered Gateway handler is composed with the real X API and spend owners, using a controlled synthetic external fetch. The regression holds OAuth refresh, retires the captured current-administrator callback without an abort signal, then releases refresh. Baseline dispatches the extra `/2/users/by/username/maintainer` request and fails. The access-policy-abort control already passes on baseline. With the fix, both cases require no paid HTTP request, zero estimated spend and no added grant.

Baseline: one failed and one passed selected case, 141.70 seconds Vitest / 171.66 seconds wrapper, including mandatory worker-cache preparation of 101.281 seconds. Fixed admin, API-authentication and cost suites: all 70 cases across three files pass in 52.77 seconds Vitest / 71.14 seconds wrapper. Targeted strict production/test types pass.

Focused syntax lint, three-file line-cap ratchet, formatting and whitespace pass. The 43-production-module plugin cycle scan has zero runtime cycles and no new static components. Mandatory lint-suppressions passes all 14 cases (24.14 seconds Vitest / 30.25 seconds wrapper). Independent isolated P0–P2 review is scoped-clean with final source verification; author simplification retained the existing owners and the single primary boundary regression.

One ordinary lint invocation automatically began package-wide declaration preparation and was stopped/joined before using focused syntax-lint mode; it supplies no passing proof. An additional repository-wide max-lines-suppression ratchet reports existing entries in `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts` and `sessions-page-state.ts`; none is changed here, and no baseline was edited. The actual touched-file line-cap check and mandatory suppression suite pass. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

No retries, skips, timeout changes, suppressions or baseline weakening. No live X, actual invoiced charge, full WebSocket role-change or SQLite proof is claimed; the host authority callback is controlled in the existing handler harness. No operator state, public SDK/config/protocol/dependency/persisted shapes or protected Phase E memory machinery changed.

CI repair: head `0ce15ad0e0285503081909be946ce8628213f089`, [run39516164098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516164098)/[job118950151146](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516164098/job/118950151146) failed `typescript(unbound-method)` on the new test fixture's detached `api.getUserByUsername` reference. This failure was ours. The fixture now forwards through a bound closure using the API method's existing parameter tuple. No production code, assertion, timing or import changed. Both selected retirement cases pass (134.20 seconds Vitest/152.60 seconds wrapper, including117.273 seconds mandatory worker preparation;26 cases name-filtered, no added skips). Strict targeted production/test types, focused syntax lint, changed-file line cap, format and whitespace pass; mandatory suppression14 cases pass in14.11 seconds wrapper/9.99 seconds Vitest. A first untyped forwarding draft failed the tuple typecheck and was corrected before push; it is not represented as passing. Prior unchanged production type/cycle and70-case proof remains valid. New-head hosted CI is still required, including typed lint; old-head passing jobs are not current-head proof. No CI rerun or unrelated-failure exception is used for this repair.

Exact repaired head `4407dbba343d11975deed2bf3df6867341e4f2f4`: [run39518090271](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39518090271) completed successfully. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An intentionally tool-free agent fails before answering ordinary messages when it inherits a nonempty global `tools.allow` or `tools.alsoAllow` setting. A resolved wildcard denial removes the tools, but the catalog validator classifies the empty result as an invalid allowlist.

## User Impact

Ordinary first and subsequent turns can reply with zero exposed tools. An explicit command-time `toolsAllow` request that conflicts with deny-all still fails. No new setting, migration, grant, or tool-filtering path is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize `explicitToolDenylist.includes("*")` in the existing intentional-disable condition. The branch incorporates upstream #177945's catalog-owned validation; it does not restore the retired helper. Against incorporated upstream `4763b77ba572eefaef3bed12c0c17c305cd12738`, the authored change is two files: the catalog condition and its producer regressions (production +3/-1, tests +45/-4).

## Evidence

Current source and built runtime: `0fb5c5d8feff30e64175b701f7cdb24945a339de`.

- The actual current catalog regressions fail without the repair: 2 failed / 20 passed, covering inherited allow and additive grants. With the repair, all 22 tests pass, including explicit runtime `toolsAllow` refusal.
- Core and owning agent-test type graphs, scoped lint, final formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review found no actionable defect; the subsequent change was formatter-only fixture wrapping.
- A real configured subscription model completed two ordinary authenticated `chat.send` turns through an isolated compiled Gateway and the built-in embedded runtime. Both replies were saved under their original runs in the same session. Actual compiled catalog coverage was observed before each serialized model request, and each request exposed zero tools. This is real external inference, replacing the earlier mock-only proof.
- The observer forwarded the original model request unchanged; it did not replace responses, tools, policy, or catalog output. The configured model and all private identifiers are aliased below. An independent raw-receipt audit checked build/source pins, request/catalog pairs, acknowledgment/terminal/history identity, and cleanup.

prs.title: feat(plugins): tell approval onResolution who resolved the request
prs.body:
Related: #171201

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that gates a tool call with `requireApproval` learns only the decision, so it cannot write an audit record of who resolved the approval or when.

## User Impact

Plugin authors get the approval ledger's recorded attribution: `onResolution(decision, details)`, where `details` is `{ resolvedAtMs, resolver?: { kind: "device" | "channel" | "runtime" | "system", id? } }`. Existing one-argument callbacks are called exactly as before. Execution behavior does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper asked a maintainer question on #171201: should resolver metadata stay informational, or should native plugin approvals also support enforceable self-approval and human-only reviewer policies?

**This PR takes the informational answer and leaves enforcement out.**

- **Enforcement belongs to the approval owner, not this callback.** `onResolution` is not awaited and cannot veto, and an existing test pins that. A self-approval or human-only check here would be advisory at best. Per "one owner per responsibility", such a policy belongs in the Gateway approval owner (resolve-time admission), as its own design with SDK and security review.
- **Host-proven fields only, and no new ones.** The details are exactly what the approval ledger already records and what `approval.get` / `approval.history` already return to `operator.approvals` readers. `plugin.approval.waitDecision` needs the same scope, so no reader gains access to facts it couldn't already read. No new collection, retained fields, or schema. This follows the audit doctrine "provenance = opt-in, never authorization".
- **Disclosure is documented honestly.** `runtime` ids can be client-chosen labels. `channel` ids are `<channel>:<accountId>` (the bot account), not the person who sent `/approve`. The docs say attribution is descriptive and must not be used to refuse self-approval or require a person.
- **System cases are explicit.** A Gateway timeout arrives with `resolver.kind: "system"`. `details` is omitted when the Gateway recorded no resolution: embedded runs, cancellations, no approval route, `report`/`deny` modes, and Gateway failures.

Not included, and needing a maintainer decision if wanted: recording the channel sender (`reviewer.senderId`), device role/scopes, or any enforceable reviewer policy. Each widens retained identity fields or adds a gate.

Single-phase timeouts: a hosted single-phase request ends with `decision: null` both on timeout and with no route, and the agent read every immediate null as no-route. The single-phase response now carries `terminalReason`, as `waitDecision` already does. A recorded `timeout` is reported as a timeout (`onResolution("timeout", { resolver: { kind: "system" } })`, "Approval timed out") instead of a no-route cancellation. Older Gateways without `terminalReason` keep the previous behavior.

Implementation: the live approval record keeps the ledger's `resolver {kind, id}` in place of the write-only `resolverKind`. The shared wait and single-phase request responses add optional `resolvedAtMs` / `resolver`. The agent passes them through only when the response belongs to the same approval id.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, real WebSocket, distinct reviewer device** (`test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-plugin-approvals.e2e.test.ts`). The requester and reviewer are separate paired devices on an isolated token-auth Gateway:
- The reviewer resolves `allow-once` with `plugin.approval.resolve`. The requester's `plugin.approval.waitDecision` returns `terminalReason: "user"`, `resolvedAtMs`, and `resolver: { kind: "runtime", id: "plugin approval reviewer" }`. That id is the reviewer's client label, which is the descriptive attribution the docs warn about.
- A single-phase request with `timeoutMs: 250` returns `decision: null`, `terminalReason: "timeout"`, `resolver: { kind: "system" }`.

```
✓ gateway-plugin-approvals.e2e.test.ts > delivers a generated request to a distinct reviewer and resolves one terminal decision 2831ms
Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Owning boundaries:**
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-approval.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 28 + 77 passed.
- New gateway cases fail on the previous head (`0cfb08a`) and pass on this one: `expires immediately when no approval route` (now asserts `terminalReason: "no-route"`) and `reports a single-phase timeout with its system attribution`.
- Agent cases: recorded attribution reaches `onResolution`, and a recorded single-phase timeout yields `timed_out` with `onResolution("timeout", { resolvedAtMs, resolver: { kind: "system" } })`. The existing one-argument and "does not await onResolution" tests stay green.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxlint` on the changed files, `run-format.mts --check`, `git diff --check`: clean.

**CI failures on `0cfb08a`:**
- `check-docs`: this PR's docs table padding. Fixed here.
- `checks-node-changed`: `gateway-authorized-continuation.e2e.test.ts` timed out at 90 s. It passes locally on this branch.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-9`: `src/plugins/hooks.before-tool-call.test.ts > records shared memory hidden in Error.cause` also fails locally with this PR's source files reverted to `origin/main`, so it is pre-existing.

**Gap:** the hosted in-process caller (`hasInProcessGatewayToolCaller`) is covered at the agent boundary with a recorded Gateway response, not driven by a real model turn.

prs.title: fix: avoid false failure logs during Gateway shutdown
prs.body:
Related: #178798

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading provider-catalog, cron-startup, and session-recovery failure messages during normal Gateway shutdown.

## User Impact

Expected shutdown cancellation and refused background admission stop appearing as failures. Genuine provider, storage, and cleanup errors remain reportable. No configuration changes, migration, or operator action are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog lifecycle now identifies its intentional close with a distinct error type. The affected background loggers reuse the existing Gateway drain classifier, which requires a direct draining error and current restart/drain state. Wrapped, aggregate, and identical-text errors remain visible.

The existing owners still decide admission, cancellation, durable recovery, and cleanup. The simplification pass retained those owners and the distinct boundary regressions: four production files change by +39/−17 lines, tests by +246/−56, and documentation by +8. No additional manager, state, or dependency is introduced.

## Evidence

- All four targeted diagnostic regressions failed on the unmodified base at the expected logging assertion; seven selected negative/existing controls passed.
- **108 focused tests pass:** 104 across the four affected files, plus four existing lifecycle/admission sibling cases. Real worker shutdown rejects unfinished discovery, joins the worker, retires its publication, and leaves no tasks. Real SQLite recovery preserves the complete row on refused admission and resumes the same cycle in a fresh lifecycle without spending an extra durable attempt.
- Production types and the affected `agents-root`, `agents-other`, `agents-sessions`, and `gateway-server` test type graphs pass. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, docs MDX syntax, whitespace, and the source line-cap ratchet pass.
- Independent Codex AutoReview and the hosted ClawSweeper review found no actionable code findings in this exact patch. The installed-entry-point proof limitation remains explicit below.
- The separate repository-wide max-lines-suppression check fails identically on the unchanged base index for three untouched UI files (details below). It is not reported as passing.

This is focused macOS boundary and compiled-worker proof. Installed-package/Linux smoke is a separate post-merge follow-up; no new live-provider or application-performance claim is made here.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and inherited check qualification</summary>

Measured full-file commands used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` with pnpm 12.12.1, the Node 26.4.0 launcher, and the repository-pinned Bun/Vitest runtime. Wall times include launcher/compiler preparation. The four changed files also passed all 104 cases in exact-head CI run 39516560707. Observed hosted costs follow the local table.

| Test file | Cases | Wall |

| `src/gateway/server-runtime-services.test.ts` | 36 | 43.25 s |
| `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-admission.test.ts` | 26 | 34.48 s |
| `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts` | 13 | 56.98 s |
| `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts` | 29 | 17.02 s |

| Changed test file (hosted job) | Cases passed | Sum of case times | Enclosing suite files / tests | Vitest suite | Wrapper shard |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [Gateway services](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516560707/job/118950565533) | 36 | 0.507 s | 6 / 52 | 11.83 s | 14.37 s |
| [Recovery admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516560707/job/118950565414) | 26 | 20.028 s | 4 / 50 | 35.60 s | 38.65 s |
| [Catalog worker pool](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516560707/job/118950565639) | 13 | 36.082 s | 5 / 35 | 50.10 s | 81.48 s |
| [Catalog owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516560707/job/118950565403) | 29 | 3.462 s | 2 / 34 | 12.76 s | 43.48 s |

Case sums omit shared setup. The verbose CI logs do not report standalone file wall time; suite and wrapper durations include sibling files and orchestration. These are test costs, not application-performance comparisons.

The new worker-settlement case took 2.249 s, and the recovery persistence/restart case took 1.201 s. Those contracts require real worker/SQLite boundaries. Scheduling controls use fake time; the new cases add no real sleeps or polling.

The first implementation run left the new session-delivery assertion failing because the check was placed in the maintenance catch. That placement was corrected; the assertion was retained, maintenance behavior is unchanged, and the final full Gateway file passes all 36 cases.

`check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base d32a3b6eb827783aa79dc0feffdfaf3999eb8619` reports existing suppressions in:

The same three failures reproduce with `--staged` against the unchanged index at that base. The files, suppression baseline, and check implementation are unchanged by this PR. No baseline exception or unrelated UI repair was added. This is pinned-base local evidence, not a claim about current hosted CI.

</details>

## Hosted CI qualification

The exact-head run completed with **51 successful jobs, 25 skipped jobs, and two failures**: the inherited lint failure and its consequential CI aggregate. The independent security job passed. It reports an inherited `check-lint-core-2` failure: `typescript(unbound-method)` at `src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts:73`. The [failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516560707/job/118951315187) actually checked out `b46b79f411afa1c76c414f487b8ffbdd48c6d165`, with ordered parents upstream `abe00d4c097400cef91e611dbbd6f0ebf62d1e97` and this PR head.
