prs.title: fix(whatsapp): newly-paired senders receive no approval confirmation
prs.body:
Closes #56619

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users pairing a WhatsApp sender would never receive an approval confirmation message. The shared pairing-approval path is documented and works for Slack, Feishu, and Synology Chat, but WhatsApp's channel adapter ships no `notifyApproval` callback, so the shared notifier (`src/channels/plugins/pairing.ts`) returns early and the approval is a silent no-op. The Control UI also hides the "notify on approval" option for WhatsApp, because `notifySupported` is derived from `Boolean(adapter.notifyApproval)`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the missing `notifyApproval` callback to `whatsappPlugin.pairing`, modeled on the existing Slack implementation. When an approval fires, WhatsApp resolves the account, normalizes the sender JID, and sends `PAIRING_APPROVED_MESSAGE` (the shared confirmation string) via `sendMessageWhatsApp`. The change is purely additive — the shared notifier and the `notifySupported` UI surface already handle the optional callback, so no shared, gateway, or protocol code is touched. WhatsApp's send path is simpler than Slack's (no write token or team-scoped target formatting), so the callback stays minimal.

This is a small, scoped gap-filler that brings WhatsApp to parity with the three sibling channels that already ship this callback. The broader operator-approvals refactor (`docs/refactor/operator-approvals.md`, #103505) is a future reshape of the approval lifecycle; this PR does not introduce a new approval abstraction — it wires the existing per-channel notify seam that the shared notifier already calls, so it composes with rather than preempts that later work.

## User Impact

WhatsApp senders who complete pairing approval now receive a confirmation message, matching the behavior of Slack, Feishu, and Synology Chat. Operators also see the "notify on approval" option enabled for WhatsApp in the Control UI.

## Evidence

- New test `extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.test.ts` asserts `whatsappPlugin.pairing.notifyApproval` is defined and sends `PAIRING_APPROVED_MESSAGE` to the paired sender. Red on `main` (callback is `undefined`); green on this branch.
- `pnpm test:extension whatsapp` — the two new tests pass (included in the 1341 passing). The 7 failures in `session.test.ts` are pre-existing on `main` (verified: same 7 fail on an unmodified `main` checkout — they require WhatsApp credential/auth state unavailable in the test environment and are unrelated to this change).
- Prior art: Slack (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`), Synology Chat, and Feishu all implement the same `notifyApproval` callback.

prs.title: fix(imessage): own-device approval taps in direct chats are credited to the other person
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/imsg#358

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an operator's own approval tapback or poll vote from a paired Apple device, inside a direct chat with someone else, is authorized as that other person instead of the operator.

## User Impact

User impact: approval taps and votes sent from the gateway's own Apple ID in a direct chat now resolve as the local account (`destination_caller_id`), the same way they already do in groups and self-chat, and the other person in the chat can no longer stand in as the approver. Operators who approve this way need their local account handle in `channels.imessage.allowFrom`; if only the other person is listed, the tap is now denied instead of approved under their name. No config or data migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

For self-sent direct-chat rows, `imsg` reports the other person as `sender` (fixed in openclaw/imsg#358, not yet merged). Tapbacks used `sender` directly as the approver, so the operator's own tap was credited to the peer. Tapbacks now use the existing `resolveIMessageApprovalControlActor` owner that poll votes already use, which prefers `destination_caller_id` for self-sends. Because the actor is now the local account, the direct-chat binding key takes the peer from `chat_identifier` for self-sends, so it still matches the `{handle: <peer>}` key that `send.ts` registers. Both imsg behaviors produce the same result, so this does not depend on which imsg version is installed. Sender identity used for routing is unchanged; self-sent rows still drop before routing as in #120751.

Received tapbacks now go through the same owner as votes, so a received row whose sender is imsg's local-identity fallback is no longer treated as the operator.

## Evidence

- **Red on base, green here:** two parameterized regressions (`approval-reactions.test.ts`, `approval-polls.test.ts`), one case per imsg payload shape. On base `cab0df90f87` all four fail: the peer-as-sender shape is authorized as the peer, and the local-as-sender shape misses the binding (`handled: false`). All pass here.
- **Live Gateway through the shipped entry points:** an isolated `openclaw gateway run` (temp HOME/state/config, loopback, token auth) with `channels.imessage.cliPath` set to a wrapper and `dbPath` to a synthetic `chat.db` (Messages schema, fictional handles). The wrapper forwards reads (`watch.subscribe`, `messages.history`, chat lists) to real imsg under a macOS sandbox that denies Apple Events and the real Messages and Contacts stores; `send` and `poll send` get imsg-shaped receipts and are recorded as outgoing rows, so nothing reaches Messages.app. Each run creates the approval with `openclaw gateway call exec.approval.request` (turn source: the iMessage DM), inserts the operator's own tapback or Polls vote row (`is_from_me=1`, peer `handle_id`, local `destination_caller_id`), and reads the outcome from `approval.history`. Every row holds for both the tapback and the vote:

| imsg build | allowFrom | base `cab0df90f87` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `e01f113` (sender = peer) | local | not settled | **allowed** by `imessage:default`, notice credits local |
| main | peer | **allowed by `imessage:default`, notice credits the peer** | not settled after 75 s |
| openclaw/imsg#358 (sender = local) | local | allowed (tapback via the 60 s reaction poller) | **allowed**, ~2 s |
| openclaw/imsg#358 | peer | not settled | not settled after 75 s |

<details><summary>Trace: this PR, imsg main, allowFrom = local (paths redacted)</summary>

```
$ openclaw gateway run --port 28791
[imessage] [default] starting provider (<proof>/fake-imsg db=<proof>/chat.db)
wrapper  forward watch.subscribe
$ openclaw gateway call exec.approval.request --params '{"command":"echo synthetic","host":"gateway","turnSourceChannel":"imessage","turnSourceTo":"+15555550123","turnSourceAccountId":"default","twoPhase":true,"timeoutMs":300000}'
wrapper  stubbed send {"to": "+15555550123", "guid": "PROOF-407F56C21215"}   # approval prompt
chat.db  + is_from_me=1 handle=+15555550123 destination_caller_id=+15551230000 type=2001 -> p:0/PROOF-407F56C21215
wrapper  stubbed send {"to": "+15555550123", "guid": "PROOF-F318AD737B5E"}   # "✅ Exec approval allow-once. Resolved by iMessage approval (+15551230000)."
$ openclaw gateway call approval.history --params '{"kind":"exec","limit":10}'
{"id": "27eb830b-83a7-440e-9e57-184197d98ee7", "status": "allowed", "decision": "allow-once", "resolver": {"kind": "channel", "id": "imessage:default"}}
```
</details>

- **In-process settlement, nothing mocked:** the same payloads through `handleIMessageApprovalReaction` / `maybeResolveIMessageApprovalPollVote` into canonical `approval.resolve` on a real `ExecApprovalManager` with the bundled iMessage plugin (shape of the Teams custody test in `server-instance-runtime.approvals.test.ts`) also cover revocation before commit (settlement fails and stays pending; replay under the revoked policy stays pending), replay after success (no re-settle), and the Gateway's own reviewer policy (a direct `resolveApprovalOverGateway` with a mismatched reviewer is rejected).

- `pnpm test extensions/imessage`: 843 tests passed. Changed-file format (oxfmt), oxlint, extension boundary lints, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and `git diff --check` passed. Single-worker wall time: `approval-reactions.test.ts` 28 s (95% transform), `approval-polls.test.ts` 10 s; the new cases run in about 2 ms each.
- Production +18/-11, tests +46, docs 1 line. The tapback-only `sender` read is removed in favor of the shared actor owner; no new helpers or state.
- Messages.app transport was not used: sends stop at the imsg boundary, so this is not a live iMessage send claim.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): selected 200K context window runs on the full 1M window after model discovery fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session that selected the 200K context window on the direct Anthropic route is budgeted, compacted and cleared as 1M once the Gateway's live model discovery has failed and no attempt has succeeded since startup (a failing, slow or blocked `GET /v1/models`).

Closes #177701
Related: #167762

## User Impact

User impact: on the direct Anthropic route a session's 200K selection now applies even while model discovery is failing. The run budget, the provider-side compaction trigger, tool-result clearing and the recorded session budget all follow it. Sessions without a selection, runs after a successful discovery and the CLI-backed route keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

With an empty runtime model registry the embedded runner gets its model row from the plugin's hand-built forward-compat row. That row already copies the catalog's `compat` from the plugin manifest for exactly this case (#114695), but it dropped the declared `contextWindows` / `contextWindowDefault`. The runtime policy then found no option for the stored `200k` and used the full window, while the catalog view, which keeps the manifest rows when the listing fails, kept offering and accepting the choice. The row now carries the manifest's choices for the `anthropic` provider, next to `compat`. Rows that declare no choices and the CLI-backed provider rows are unchanged. The choices can only lower a session's budget: the effective budget stays the smaller of the selected (or default) option and any authored `models.providers.*` limit. Production change: +12/-3 in `extensions/anthropic/register.runtime.ts`.

## Evidence

Real behavior on an isolated Gateway (fresh home, state and config; own port) in a private network namespace with real internet egress. `api.anthropic.com` resolves to its public address, held locally by a TLS stand-in that records request bodies and answers `GET /v1/models` with `401`, a 7 s delay (past the 5 s discovery timeout) or a normal listing. Synthetic API key. Default config: only `agents.defaults.model.primary`, set to a bundled catalog model with the `200k` / `1m` choices. Each leg creates sessions with `contextWindow: "200k"` through `sessions.create` and through `sessions.patch`, plus one without a selection, then runs one `openclaw agent` turn per session and one `chat.send`. Same harness for every leg; base `a983378e474`, fix `e9b4dd24bfb`.

```text
discovery   build    200k sessions (agent, patch, chat.send)        no selection
                     agentMeta   compact / clear    stored          agentMeta   compact / clear
401, 401    before   1000000     700000 / 300000    1000000         1000000     700000 / 300000
401, 401    after    200000      140000 / 60000     200000          1000000     700000 / 300000
7 s, 7 s    before   1000000     700000 / 300000    1000000         1000000     700000 / 300000
7 s, 7 s    after    200000      140000 / 60000     200000          1000000     700000 / 300000
ok          before   200000      140000 / 60000     200000          1000000     700000 / 300000
ok          after    200000      140000 / 60000     200000          1000000     700000 / 300000
```

`agentMeta` = `meta.agentMeta.contextTokens` of `openclaw agent --json`; `compact / clear` = the `context_management` triggers of every main-model request; `stored` = `contextTokens` in the session row. In every leg the Gateway accepted the selection (`sessions.create` and `sessions.patch`), `sessions.describe` and `models.list` listed the `["200k","1m"]` choices, and the stored rows kept `contextWindow: "200k"`; only the base build with failed discovery ignored it. An `agents.defaults.models` alias entry for the model gives the same before/after result under `401`. With the fix, rows written while discovery fails on this route record the same budget provenance (`contextTokensSource`) as rows written after a successful discovery.

Regression test: `extensions/anthropic/forward-compat-generation.test.ts` "carries manifest context-window choices onto hand-built modern rows" reads the window-bearing ids from the plugin manifest; it fails on the base (the row has no `contextWindows`) and passes with the fix. The whole `extensions/anthropic` suite passes (37 files, 416 tests). Cost: `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` takes 32 s wall (29 s in vitest, 94% of it module transform, the same as the unchanged file on the base); the new test runs in 6 ms.

Local gates (the `check:changed` lanes for this diff, run one by one): `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxlint` and `format:check` on the touched files, and the extension boundary and ratchet lanes pass. `check:max-lines-ratchet` reports three `ui/` files on the clean base too (not touched here). The SQLite worker ratchet was left to CI (no database code in the diff).

What was not tested: OAuth / setup-token credentials (no token; the fix depends only on the empty registry, not the auth mode) and the CLI-backed route (unchanged by design: it takes its choices from its own catalog rows). With an explicit `models.providers.anthropic.models` entry the runtime row already carries the choices, so that configuration is outside this change.

AI-assisted; the contributor reviewed the change and is responsible for it.

prs.title: fix: keep Linux worker cleanup working as processes exit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Linux worker cleanup failing when an unrelated process exits during the process-group census. A failed cleanup can leave the native source closed and make subsequent daemon runtime-pin migrations fail with `Native worker source is closing`, blocking service resume or post-update Doctor.

## User Impact

Linux process churn no longer makes a valid census row abort cleanup. Existing ownership, native settlement, malformed-input refusal, and cleanup deadlines remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Linux [`do_task_stat`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.8/fs/proc/array.c) initializes the process group to `-1` and can retain that value when a task is reaped during the read. The parser accepted only unsigned process groups. Accept the kernel's `-1` sentinel; consumers still require a positive matching owner group before signaling.

The unsigned parser originated in `2d345fa899ee` (#139948), before the reported hourly window. The [reported CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39508589544/job/118924063220) proves that broker cleanup failed before the later daemon migration errors, but its combined error does not distinguish malformed rows from a deadline expiry. This fixes the independently reproduced parser defect without claiming that the unavailable CI row was captured.

## Evidence

- Native Linux ARM64 probe: 425,510 procfs reads captured 93 real exiting-task rows with `pgid=-1`, including `X 0 -1 -1` and `Z 0 -1 -1`.
- Deterministic regression fails on unmodified production code (`expected true, received undefined`). With the fix, it finds an owned live child after the reaped row and correctly reports no live members after that child is removed.
- Local owner/consumer proof: 256 passing cases across 14 files, one existing platform skip, all with `--maxWorkers=1` (60.56s + 14.83s wrapper time).
- Linux with the pinned Bun runtime: 89 passing cases across seven files, two existing macOS-only skips, including actual broker child cleanup and daemon runtime-pin migration (43.77s wrapper time).
- Targeted services test-graph typecheck, type-aware lint, format, and `git diff --check` pass. The changed-path typecheck selector hit pre-existing 728-root graph budget failures; the affected canonical services graph was checked directly instead.
- Independent P2 autoreview: scoped-clean. The change is two files, +12/-1, with no new helper, retry, or timeout change.

The full package build passed in 2m58.5s, and tarball validation passed. The complete published `openclaw@2026.10.4` → candidate `2026.10.5` `legacy-operator-state` survivor passed: update status `ok`, all Doctor steps exited 0, pending delivery and schemas survived, cron owners and mobile pairing survived restart, the candidate served an agent turn, same-version update and clean Doctor passed, plugin repair passed, and backup rollback passed.

Packaging captured base `d6e3a30c0bfc` just before commit `bfaf11442fbb` was created, so the embedded build stamp names the base. The packed broker/anchor/state-lease worker binaries were independently checked to contain the fixed parser and match the reviewed build bytes. No source changed after review or proof.

Latest main recheck: `863a3cdc6dc7`, with no changes to either touched file since the base. No CI dispatch or rerun. Landing remains with the lead.

prs.title: feat: restrict model automation administration through Gateway policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OCE needs caller-scoped scheduling without giving model turns an administrator’s authority over other automations or Gateway command jobs.

## User Impact

Set `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations` to `{ scope: "caller", allowCommandJobs: false }`. Administrator-started model conversations retain ordinary scheduling within caller scope. Model calls cannot create, convert, edit, enable or manually run command jobs or on-exit command watchers. Direct authorized human administration remains available.

The policy is optional. Changes require Gateway restart or replacement after affected old work ends, matching merged #174547. Ordinary deployments and native Codex tools retain their existing behavior. Stream schedules, scripts and triggers retain their separate controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool/action filtering cannot distinguish ordinary schedules from administrative job operations. The existing automation grant, ownership and commit checks enforce those distinctions using the deployment policy, while retaining live expiry and revocation checks. Job creation retains the existing stream-approval safeguards.

Required worker schedules avoid capturing ambient Gateway inference credentials; native Codex schedules use the selected Harness’s authentication plan. Explicit account selections retain validation.

Implements RFC-0021 items 3, 4 and the automation portion of 8 in [the RFC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/2367).

## Evidence

[Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39517948111) is running for `3ee6a025e6b`.

- Frozen install succeeded with the pinned lockfile. Canonical config generation/check pass. The core baseline increases from 2578 to 2581 for exactly `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations`, `.scope` and `.allowCommandJobs`; channel/plugin counts and hashes are unchanged.
- Seven focused test files passed (356 tests), covering config validation, restart classification, automation tools, Gateway authorization and inference bindings. After the description cleanup, all three affected tool/schema/policy files passed again (91 tests). Targeted type-aware lint, docs config examples, all eight prompt snapshots, source formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- Description selection now lives in its existing helper. Independent correctness and maintainability reviews found no material issue; all 324 description variants are byte-identical, and authority binding/execution remain unchanged. Local native autoreview remains unavailable because its isolated app-server startup hits a read-only filesystem.
- The preceding CI run’s separate [Doctor lint failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39514022652/job/118943274998) is inherited unchanged from integrated main; this PR does not modify that file or lint configuration.
- Required-worker provider I/O with selected-account/revocation controls, and upgrade from `v2026.10.4` preserving existing jobs, remain unqualified. Focused fixtures do not establish those deployment guarantees.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep QR approval commands in the selected profile
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw --profile <name> qr` prints approval commands without the selected profile, so copying them targets the default profile instead.

## User Impact

User impact: users can copy both printed device-list and approval commands while retaining their profile or container context. Default-profile output is unchanged; pairing credentials, access, JSON, and setup-code-only output are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing CLI command formatter for both hints, including its established container-over-profile precedence. No new state, configuration, or formatting policy is introduced. The legacy `clawbot qr` alias uses the same command implementation.

## Evidence

- Before: [real supported CLI baseline](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/39515866791), source `829ccbc8376471642ce22e90c62db0061a7a2cff`. The default control passed; both named-profile hints failed. The diagnostic workflow succeeded because it reproduced that product failure, not because baseline behavior was correct.
- After: [exact-head proof and focused checks](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/39517383241), product source `f7d9fd82f8ef590b0045deb0142fa9b6b96ca7d1`. Original `qr-profile-fixed` artifacts were inspected: default `qr`, named-profile `qr`, and named-profile `clawbot qr` all passed. Each generated a real setup code, kept authored configuration unchanged, and completed cleanup. Setup credentials are redacted from saved output.
- 45/45 focused tests passed across QR, profile/command formatting, and CLI profile startup (no skipped/todo tests). Core types, the config/CLI test type graph, touched-file typed lint, and oxfmt/Bun format parity passed. The source checkout remained clean.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 source review of product head `f7d9fd82f8ef590b0045deb0142fa9b6b96ca7d1`: no actionable findings. Review is separate from runtime and CI results.
- [Upstream ready PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39518287977) passed on the same product head; required `openclaw/ci-gate` is SUCCESS (attempt 1). This is CI evidence, not maintainer approval.

For the same `--profile proof qr --no-ascii --url ws://127.0.0.1:18789` invocation, the sanitized terminal excerpt changed from:

```text
Approve after scan with:
  openclaw devices list
  openclaw devices approve <requestId>
```

to:

```text
Approve after scan with:
  openclaw --profile proof devices list
  openclaw --profile proof devices approve <requestId>
```

The runtime proof uses isolated synthetic configuration and the actual supported CLI, including real local bootstrap-token issuance. It does not claim a mobile scan, a Gateway approval exchange, or a real container runtime (container precedence is covered by the QR regression and existing formatter tests). Broad upstream PR CI and maintainer review remain separate gates.

prs.title: fix: hide unavailable browser notification setup for guests
prs.body: Fixes #178085. ## What Problem This Solves An authenticated guest with session-only scopes sees **Ready** and **Enable notifications** in browser notification Settings, even though the Gateway denies the required Web Push calls. The automatic first-send prompt has the same gap: browser support alone makes it eligible to ask for consent before registration predictably fails. ## User Impact Settings now shows that browser notification management is unavailable for the current Gateway access, while retaining the real browser-support and permission values. Enable and test actions are unavailable, and the automatic prompt does not consume its one-shot opportunity for a connection that cannot register push. Existing browser subscriptions can still be unsubscribed locally when remote removal is denied. Read-only connections can inspect their existing preferences through disabled native controls, keeping labels and values available to assistive technology. Authorized personal and admin connections keep their existing setup flow. This does not grant guest scopes, change notification consent or device/profile binding, or add push delivery support. ## Why This Change Was Made The capability now derives current read and write access through the existing Gateway method-access helper. The fixed core push methods include intentionally unadvertised methods, so method-catalog presence is not treated as a permission requirement. Settings and the synchronous first-send prompt consume the same capability state. The runtime checks current access before requesting browser consent and before later Gateway or subscription effects. Access changes and disconnects invalidate displayed subscription/preferences state; an existing browser subscription without registration authority is identified as local rather than presented as registered with this Gateway. ## Evidence The added owner regression fails on the unchanged production baseline because a session-only guest requests browser permission; the other 17 existing cases pass. The candidate covers denied setup, read-only preferences with local opt-out, same-client access changes, disconnects and revocation while consent is pending. Existing authorized registration, device-mismatch and preference-save cases remain in the same harness. The qualified integration browser run uses unchanged real guest/admin admission. Guest Settings removes the unusable enable action; Admin Settings retains it. A guest's first accepted new-session send and background-palette send each make **zero permission requests** and leave the automatic-prompt marker absent. In the transport control, a real Admin WebSocket closes while synthetic consent is pending. The native close handler publishes disconnected access before consent is released: **zero raw push attempts, zero wire push RPCs and zero browser subscriptions** follow. Read-only, loading, disconnected and local opt-out component scenarios use explicitly synthetic state in the actual served renderer. All 21 read-only native fields are disabled while labels and values remain in the accessibility tree. Clicking Unsubscribe invokes its synthetic callback once and no other mutation callback. This does not claim a real subscription was removed. Three existing isolated role-owner cases also pass, tracing canonical role mutation through policy invalidation and client disconnect; actual live role writes and full notification delivery are outside this proof. A later real authorized registration control is recorded below. Remote formatting, lint and English-catalog verification pass. All 20 type graphs selected by native consumer discovery are qualified; unchanged results were reused and affected inputs rerun after corrections. Eight selected test files cover 107 passing cases. The final accessibility correction passed 43 affected owner, Settings and browser cases in 5.76 seconds including the wrapper. The additional three role-owner cases took 43.36 seconds, primarily cold transforms. [Original-source CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39382807465) passes on `e04d232a7fe9`; successful selected jobs total 4,279 elapsed job-seconds. Skipped lanes remain skipped. The original guest and transport-loss media below comes from native integration producer `d1f7a5961450`, containing the qualified notification inputs from PR source `e04d232a7fe9` on the preserved lab base. It is not a deployment of the entire PR checkout. The notification renderer, access helper, auto-prompt module and English notification section match; runtime differences are comments only. Older shared controls, Gateway presentation and listener registration remain in that integration and were checked for the relevant disabled-control and connected-access behavior. Exact PR-source component tests remain separate evidence. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Guest Settings incorrectly advertises Ready and Enable notifications](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53f75ad7-809e-46a9-899a-b1e9bdc0dcc1) | ![Guest Settings explains unavailable Gateway access while keeping browser support and permission unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e25aa5a1-4980-4782-a6d8-88967817d620) | ### Actual connection closes before held synthetic consent is released; address redacted, playback at half speed https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/993254b4-ba99-424e-8837-41e0d4dd93bc ### Visual verification - Baseline: 46110002bf93db2af023262752dc5262a58dfd0d with unrelated lookup\-message UI changes - Exact head: `d1f7a596145000e56b1d9834526368d39d0310de` - Scenario: Actual guest Settings before and after the access fix; actual Admin transport loss while a synthetic consent result is held\. Supplementary read\-only controls use explicitly synthetic values\. - Runtime/build: Native integration build d1f7a5961450, tree cd6b9e327f5b39a064b5846da227b1187048faf5; notification inputs qualified from PR source e04d232a7fe9\. Renderer, access helper and auto\-prompt module are byte\-identical; runtime differs only in two comments and the shell retains its earlier listener registry\. - Guest first sends: 0 permission calls; browser permission default; automatic\-prompt marker absent - Connection\-loss control: 1 real socket close; access false before release; 0 raw push attempts, 0 wire push calls, 0 browser subscriptions - Read\-only fixture: 21 native fields disabled with readable accessibility values; one synthetic unsubscribe callback and no save/test/subscribe callback - Actual browser consent, Gateway scopes, profile bindings, keys and subscriptions remained unchanged\. - The baseline JPEG was decoded to PNG without editing its content; the original and its digest are retained\. - Matching guest route, theme, viewport and authority; navigation hover/focus and the genuine build footer differ\. - The recording uses real UI/client/transport/store state with synthetic held consent and push\-side\-effect observers; full authorized push delivery and live role writes are not claimed\. - Original recordings and actual source/build provenance are retained; only the curated clip is published\. ### Authorized and read-only controls The first image is the actual Admin Settings control. “Guest Lab” is the Gateway display name; the connection has `operator.admin`. The second is a scrolled synthetic read-only fixture showing disabled values, including quiet hours and browser preferences. | Actual Admin | Synthetic read-only values | | --- | --- | | ![Actual Admin retains enabled notification setup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c93d758a-3fc6-426e-8b04-339c17280dd8) | ![Synthetic read-only preferences remain visible in disabled controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d3c96db-7315-4573-aaef-330021c681f2) | Synthetic local opt-out interaction, at half speed; one unsubscribe callback and no other mutation callbacks: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4bde345-e1ee-4042-90f1-f8a49066f18a ## Actual authorized registration control A disposable persistent Chrome profile connected through the existing configured Admin identity and trusted-proxy authentication. The normal Settings **Enable notifications** action reached the real browser push service and Gateway registration; browser methods and Gateway responses were not mocked. Notification permission was granted only to that disposable profile through browser automation. This run used native integration producer `617f152e8112`, tree `61d29b1f65c1f03bc510a1248e20e699feef75cf`; the notification inputs from `e04d232a7fe9` retain the qualified source correspondence described above. Sanitized observations from the pass-through browser and Gateway receipts: ```text Initial state: permission=default; browser subscription absent Settings Enable actions: 1 push.web.vapidPublicKey: success PushManager.subscribe: 1 call, 1 resolved, 0 rejected push.web.subscribe: success push.web.preferences.get: success; durableIdentity=true Browser afterward: permission=granted; subscription present Cleanup through the same native identity and device: Reconnect reconciliation: same subscription ID; no new browser subscribe push.web.unsubscribe: success; removed=true PushSubscription.unsubscribe: 1 call; returned true PushManager.getSubscription: null Durable subscription: absent Created device: removed; pre-existing devices, scopes and profiles preserved Original fixture routing: restored ``` The initial test keypair was created through the existing native owner and retained. Existing keys, profiles, roles, preferences and browser permissions were preserved. No test notification was sent; this establishes registration and cleanup, not delivered push notifications. **Earlier integration result (`617f152e8112`):** Settings remained on **Checking…**, displayed the stale **Not requested** value and never exposed its Unsubscribe button. Checking was already visible before Enable; the recording preserves the failure to refresh after registration. Cleanup used the native subscription owners because the UI control was unavailable; no successful Settings-unsubscribe claim is made. This is a separate pre-existing Web Push presentation defect: [Settings forwards the mutable owner snapshot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e04d232a7fe9be357fb5b7cbb53d87a1088f35db/ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts#L941) into a [reference-memoized Show value](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e04d232a7fe9be357fb5b7cbb53d87a1088f35db/ui/src/pages/config/notifications-section.tsx#L671). Both boundaries exist on the pre-change baseline, and this PR does not change the snapshot contract. That same boundary can retain old access controls after a same-user reconnect with reduced scopes. Runtime guards still deny unauthorized effects, but the shared correction landed in #178640 and is included in this branch. Native notifications already replace their snapshots and are not included in that diagnosis. A focused consumer check passes on this PR’s unchanged `e04d232a7fe9` source combined with the exact production change from `7419dcdeba38` in #178640. It keeps the real mutable Web Push capability and Settings page mounted while the same user reconnects with Admin, read-only and guest access. Unavailable Enable/test actions disappear, readable preferences remain disabled, guest preferences disappear, and local Unsubscribe still works without a permission request or an unauthorized push call. The case asserts that the owner snapshot retains its identity; the fixture does not clone it. Gateway admission and browser interfaces are synthetic. The single case passed through the native UI runner in 4.67 seconds (6.30 seconds including the test wrapper). The shared correction landed in #178640 and is now incorporated into this candidate. Its authorized test fixture declares the two access fields required by this PR. The integrated candidate passed current fast checks, all 20 selected compiler graphs, and all 27 Settings cases (5.43 seconds in Vitest; 7.07 seconds including the wrapper). Independent review is clean on integrated head `c0851fe203fe`; ClawSweeper rates that head Diamond (5/6), with no findings. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39511633749) has 28 successful jobs and 26 skipped jobs. Its only substantive failure is the inherited Doctor `unbound-method` lint error; the aggregate gate reports the same failure. The error reproduces on the unchanged CI base. [The independently landed repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5d80482379b376f9ad921b6acff0df9bc2ce8c80) is effective in the combined result and has qualified passing lint and receiver-behavior evidence. The failed CI result is retained; other selected jobs pass. Non-skipped jobs total 4,675 elapsed job-seconds. The accepted synthetic case remains separate from the subsequent live Settings completion below. The continuous recording below is cropped to the actual notification controls, with the unrelated sidebar removed. It shows the single Enable interaction and the stale resulting UI; it does not substitute a fabricated successful after-state. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2417983-0c67-41a8-951a-fb956904d7b1 ## Settings completion with the shared correction The actual authorized Settings scenario now succeeds with the correction from #178640 in retained integration producer `d76083dff482`, tree `5a50037043c9fc8b138356d1c605d73e3082a05e`. The relevant notification path differs from the previously qualified `617f152e8112` producer only by that exact snapshot-copy production hunk. This is qualified integration evidence, distinct from this PR’s public head. The UI changes from **Ready / Not requested / Not subscribed** to **Subscribed / Granted**, exposes **Unsubscribe**, and returns to **Ready / Granted / Not subscribed** after that action. There is no stuck Checking or error state. Exactly one browser subscription and one Gateway registration succeed; one UI Unsubscribe then produces Gateway `removed:true`, native browser unsubscribe success and a null browser subscription. The durable subscription count returns to zero and the disposable device is removed through the native owner. All current device IDs, roles and scopes and all four profiles are preserved during this scenario, along with the existing VAPID pair and configuration; the original fixture routing is restored. Permission was granted through browser automation only for the disposable origin. The observed browser and Gateway operations were not mocked; this is not a recording of a human granting consent. No test notification or delivered push notification is claimed. The new recording is one contiguous 33-second interval with both UI actions and their settled results, without retiming, splicing or reconstructed product pixels. It is a separate capture from the earlier failure clip. ![Corrected integration: Subscribed and Granted with Unsubscribe available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70044993-484c-41c8-b7b3-6e9f8b27015e) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f86ddf7-572b-41dd-9359-a221bdf20138

prs.title: feat: prepare existing PR source in a managed workspace
prs.body: Depends on #178055 for own-PR inspection, including copied GitHub `/changes` links. ## What Problem This Solves A guest can identify their own existing GitHub PR, but that does not put its source in the conversation's managed sandbox. Starting from the selected project's current base can also give the guest different files from the PR they intend to continue. This adds explicit `github_publish` preparation by PR URL on top of the own-PR inspection contract. It covers an existing managed project workspace or an explicitly empty managed workspace. ## User Impact `prepare_pr` verifies the current linked author, original PR source and publisher write eligibility, then installs the exact PR head into a clean workspace. It preserves the conversation's workspace directory, sandbox scope and guest Git history. Dirty, untracked, staged or unrelated unpublished initial work causes a clear refusal with that work intact. An interrupted first import resumes its original accepted source. Repeating a completed same-head preparation leaves subsequent edits and indexes untouched. If the remote head has advanced after preparation, this action refuses rather than silently resetting or merging source; later-head updates are a separate contribution. Preparation records the original PR association without publishing. Existing publication and PR actions refuse an imported association until their original-PR handling is implemented, so an earlier publication receipt cannot select a different target. Ordinary unbound-chat adoption is outside this PR. No configuration or database schema migration is required. ## Why This Change Was Made The current managed workspace reconciliation owner already coordinates the canonical checkout and sandbox projection, retains interrupted file effects and preserves the running workspace location. Preparation uses that owner with the verified PR head as its explicit initial source. It checks both workspace copies before initial synchronization and retains the original head through native Git recovery state. An accepted transfer is settled before any guest command on retry, because interruption can leave the registered runtime paused until that owner completes recovery. The minimum original PR identity and accepted source are stored with the existing session worktree binding. They survive reuse of that same workspace, while newly allocated workspaces remain unbound. Permission observations are not stored as durable authority. Existing base refresh keeps its merge behavior; the imported PR's review comparison uses its common ancestor with the PR base, without merging a newer base into the imported files. ## Evidence The registered action tests exercise the real requester, session, Git and workspace reconciliation owners with synthetic GitHub reads and local fixture fetches. They cover same-repository and maintainer-edit fork sources, a newer clean project base, an immutable empty source, prior-work refusal, current permission refusals, same-head idempotency and interrupted initial import while the remote head advances. Remote validation passed on the candidate, with unchanged results retained across scoped corrections: - Changed-file formatting/lint and the enforced line-cap ratchet passed. The source integration and session binding responsibilities are in bounded modules. - `pnpm protocol:check` passed registry validation, schema generation, Swift/Kotlin contract and determinism checks, and the protocol version guard. All selected production, consumer and test type graphs passed. - The current integrated tree passed 143 cases across seven related files: preparation, inspection, base refresh, publication workflows, tool dispatch, registration and inheritance. The joined native test batch took 209.80 seconds. The four shard durations were 52.28, 100.24, 10.16 and 52.11 seconds; the last two ran concurrently. All 35 selected compiler graphs passed. Broader owner/caller results are retained only where their inputs and behavior are unchanged. - The registered-runtime control reproduced failure on the preceding source: a retry tried to probe Git while the runtime remained paused. With owner settlement moved ahead of the probe, that same test passes. It uses the production sandbox binding, filesystem bridge, runtime registry and reconciliation owner; external container I/O is simulated. A separate control retains the database close/reopen path. The current private-source cases include an authorized control, refusal of the wrong author before fetching, and real synthetic-profile role revocation and verified-email reassignment after a successful awaited head fetch. These calls go through the registered action and real Git/session owners. Each denial preserves both workspace copies’ HEAD, index, status and binding, leaves the PR-only file absent, and performs no GitHub write. GitHub reads and the fetch transport are fixtures; the protected live guest identities were not changed. The interruption scenarios observe the existing owner's recovery-required error after canonical acceptance, then prove that a retry completes the originally accepted PR head even after GitHub advances. It retains guest refs and excludes the newer head's files. The existing base-refresh action and same-workspace lifecycle controls also pass. The current head `7f2098a779bd440ef910f668b1627db969f7293c` integrates the checked inspection prerequisite and its deployment tool policy while preserving published history. Preparation remains in both the callable and static action definitions, including preparation-only inherited policies. It remains discoverable before managed workspace allocation; refresh and evidence keep their separate sandbox capability checks. The committed tree is identical to the remotely validated tree. The preceding head `2d12aaa6448ff98c9da2eb5d25ed59b07139acc7` had clean independent review, [Platinum automated review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178233#issuecomment-6286285981) and [passing hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39479199441). Those are prior-head records. Fresh independent review, automated review and hosted CI are pending for `7f2098a779bd440ef910f668b1627db969f7293c`. ### Actual managed-workspace verification A restricted guest used natural UI requests through the admitted tool on the combined runtime `617f152e8112ae21211e84f3461d74efdff218b4` (tree `61d29b1f65c1f03bc510a1248e20e699feef75cf`). The preparation, source-transfer and binding contribution is unchanged. Supporting runtime-quiescence and retained-session-read updates from the prerequisite were rechecked in the integrated registered-action batch. Broader caller and UI integration code differs, so the captures establish the listed ordinary-container scenarios rather than a deployment of the entire current PR checkout. - A public own-fork PR and an authorized private same-repository PR were prepared with exact source-file sets and blob hashes. Original PR identity, author, refs and state, the conversation binding, directory and running sandbox were preserved. - Repeating preparation after staged, unstaged and untracked edits returned no changed paths. Independent before/after comparisons found identical files, logical indexes, status, HEAD and branch in both workspace copies. - First preparation with existing untracked work refused before applying source or recording an association; the original work, indexes and runtime stayed intact. - A controlled write failure left canonical source accepted, the original association incomplete and the actual container paused. After restoring only the workspace's original directory permissions, a second native preparation call in the **same run** completed through the existing owner and resumed that **same container**. There was one user send, with no manual unpause, restart, rebind or handler invocation. Native pending journal/database rows were not directly inspected; the correlated tool results, Git state, binding and container state establish the observed recovery. Both explicit empty workspaces and worktrees from a selected registered project were exercised. In the selected-project case, one later natural PR-link message imported all eleven exact PR files; the original project’s main commit, index, clean status and ten file hashes were unchanged, while the guest kept its original HEAD, branch and history. Role/link revocation, cold-load compatibility and newer-head refusal retain separately identified source-level checks; they are not claimed as live variants here. Ordinary unbound-chat adoption, later remote-head imports and publication remain separate contributions. The PR remains open for maintainer review. ### Persisted-data compatibility The changed contract is an optional field inside the existing worktree JSON value. The [v2026.10.5 canonical session projector](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8/src/config/sessions/store-entry-shape.ts#L30) has a byte-identical projection function to the candidate and preserves the nested worktree value. This PR changes no stored-entry format, schema version, migration or update driver. Registered action tests begin with the existing association-absent worktree shape, preserve prior work on refusal, and retain the new association after actual database close/reopen and reuse of the same worktree. This is compatibility proof for that persisted contract; a full deployed v2026.10.5 upgrade was not run. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Managed workspace before and after preparation | ![Empty managed workspace before preparation, with directory and branch visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9ab41f1-7869-4b66-866e-b3daa63a55a3) | ![Preparation completed with exact PR files in the same workspace and branch; original PR card is a separate feature](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38e5e905-f06e-46a1-8838-399f710d113b) | | Selected project before and after preparation | ![Clean selected\-project worktree before receiving the PR link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9c8d531-bc1b-4c1b-be10-7fac5dfc8e44) | ![Original PR source prepared with guest branch and history preserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c31f4a0-95e2-443c-8e05-bc4b7f30c7ca) | ### Selected\-project continuation through preparation, 34\.76 seconds https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e61db744-ef0b-49a7-b9c0-80694770f30c ### Visual verification - Baseline: 617f152e8112ae21211e84f3461d74efdff218b4 before the preparation action; not a historical pre\-feature build - Exact head: `617f152e8112ae21211e84f3461d74efdff218b4` - Scenario: Prepare an original own PR from either an explicitly empty managed workspace or a new worktree of an existing registered project\. Keep the conversation, guest history and original project intact\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.4, served producer 617f152e8112, tree 61d29b1f65c1f03bc510a1248e20e699feef75cf\. The preparation and recovery source corresponds to PR head 4d7b78638392a95b9109cf6cbd4d79e97ba415d1; this is a qualified combined runtime, not the entire individual PR checkout\. - Empty workspace: Exact public own\-fork source prepared; original guest history preserved - Selected project: All eleven PR files exact in host/guest; original main, index and ten project file hashes unchanged - Runtime identity: Same session/worktree/container and guest Git history within each case - Recording: Selected\-project continuation: 34\.76 seconds, 25 fps, 869 consecutive frames - Actual admitted guest actions and native file/Git/session/container observations corroborate both completed preparations\. - Each pair uses matching 1170 x 640 framing and theme\. Private labels, URLs and commits are masked without replacing the observed response\. - Full recordings were independently inspected and frame coverage/hash identities verified; existing empty\-case uploads are reused unchanged\. - Selected\-project creation is a separate earlier capture\. Its continuation clip begins before the one later PR\-link send, with no internal cuts\. - No ordinary unbound adoption, PR publication or later remote\-head import is claimed\. ### Empty managed workspace recording The earlier 43-second continuous preparation recording remains available: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f86fde8-8beb-44e9-a4c5-b368144b3ee1

prs.title: fix(codex): unblock parents after native follow-up completion
prs.body:
Related: #172837. Follow-up to #175246.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parent requests being refused with `Codex thread <id> is claimed by active work; stop it first.` after a native follow-up finishes while its result is still awaiting acknowledgement.

## User Impact

A parent can cold-resume to receive a completed follow-up result. Active child execution stays protected, and pending results and persisted submission receipts remain available until their normal acknowledgement.

## Why This Change Was Made

#175246 releases the monitor-owned parent pin after all children finish. A follow-up accepted and admitted while its foreground parent is still registered also holds a separate submission-owned pin. That pin survived until result acknowledgement, keeping the same refusal alive.

Release that redundant execution retention only after successful monitor admission. The monitor retains active execution; completion custody and receipt settlement keep their existing owners. No dependency, schema, retry-policy or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Baseline: `b8f91cb249b8c702cfc02befd6d2fb11215928f3`. Both new cases fail at the actual `releaseCodexBoundLiveThread` guard after the follow-up ends; the other 20 tests in the custody file pass. The cases cover predecessor acknowledgement before and after successor admission.
- Fixed: 87 distinct tests pass across seven lifecycle/receipt suites, including parent retention, release retry, completion contention, submission storage and `sessions_yield` follow-up custody. The changed custody file passes all 22 tests; its standalone command took 9.11 s wall time (7.48 s Vitest duration, approximately 70 ms test execution).
- Real Codex 0.162.1 stdio protocol replay: a synthetic Responses backend drives actual native spawn and `send_input`. On the baseline, terminal execution plus pending delivery retains one extra parent/client/child hold and the guard rejects. With this fix, active execution still rejects release; after completion, the guard allows unsubscribe and actual `thread/resume` succeeds while the receipt remains in the fixture binding store. Acknowledgement then consumes the receipt once. This is a real app-server/production-owner protocol proof with a controlled provider and delivery callback, not a live-model Gateway reproduction.
- Independent lifecycle source assessment and `autoreview` completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Isolated real Gateway + authenticated V1-capable model + Codex 0.162.1: the same native child completes A, accepts and completes `send_input` B, and the next ordinary user request succeeds (`LIVE_A_OK`, `LIVE_B_OK`, `LIVE_NEXT_OK`). Native persisted output contains the accepted submission ID matching B's completed turn. This is a healthy live-flow smoke; the pending-acknowledgement interval is tested separately by the controlled protocol replay above.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39301606325) passed on `1cb15871a7f99b0f7af6346f2a04581344dd1928`; required `openclaw/ci-gate` reports that CI and applicable security review requirements passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, targeted type-aware Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

This PR fixes the separate submission-owned execution pin. Durable retirement after retry exhaustion or blocked recovery is already handled by merged #173018. These are distinct fixes related to #172837; this PR does not change delivery retry or abandonment policy.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, environment, commands and scope</summary>

### Reproduction

1. Complete native child turn A, then accept and persist a `send_input` receipt for B while the foreground parent is still registered.
2. Start/admit B before unregistering that parent. Check that cold resume is refused while B executes.
3. Complete B while result delivery remains pending or returns undelivered. Call `releaseCodexBoundLiveThread` for the parent. Baseline: the claimed-by-active-work error remains. Fixed: unsubscribe/cold resume is allowed and the submission receipt is unchanged.
4. Acknowledge delivery: the receipt is consumed once. The parameterized regression runs with A acknowledgement before and after B admission, and checks parent protection inside every release callback.

Apply the regression-test change to the base without the production change to reproduce the two failures. Run the same command on this PR for the passing result.

### Environment

OpenClaw and bundled Codex plugin source at the base/head SHAs above; Codex app-server 0.162.1; macOS arm64; Node 24.19.0; pnpm 12.12.1; repository-pinned Bun; Vitest 5.0.3. Synthetic thread/result fixtures for regression and protocol replay; fresh isolated Gateway state and a supported authenticated V1-capable model for the live smoke.

### Commands

```sh
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.release-retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-completion-delivery.contention.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-followup-custody.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:extensions
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-submission-owner.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts
pnpm format:check -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-submission-owner.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts
git diff --check
```

macOS arm64; Node 24.19.0; pnpm 12.12.1; repository-pinned Bun; Vitest 5.0.3. PR CI supplies broad coverage; the successful CI run took 681 s elapsed including setup, parallel checks and gate publication (not per-file execution time).

Live-proof accounting: the initial observer counted only `function_call_output`, so it incorrectly reported no submission receipt when the real model used CodeMode's `custom_tool_call_output`. The original failure is retained; independent native-rollout and Gateway-terminal readback verified the matching submission/child turn and all three visible replies without rerunning the successful workload. Earlier V2/model-unavailable attempts are not counted as V1 proof. The separate GitHub Codex review integration failed without publishing findings; local independent review completed.

`pr-simplify`: existing lifecycle owners suffice; no new owner or production seam. Production delta +3/-2 (one release plus ownership comment); tests +84/-36, reusing the existing submission binding-store fixture. Tests keep the actual client identity, explicitly retire pending delivery custody during cleanup, and inspect protection at release callbacks during the active handoff.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inspectable redacted execution capture: real Codex pending-ack replay and live Gateway</summary>

These are excerpts from captured execution output, not expected-value examples. Only relevant fields are shown. Synthetic UUIDs are consistently aliased as `P` (parent), `C` (child), `A`/`B` (child turns), and `P_B` (parent follow-up turn); local paths/endpoints are omitted. No production data or credentials were used in this replay.

Runtime: `codex-cli 0.162.1`, real stdio app-server and native spawn/`send_input`; synthetic Responses output and a deliberately held completion-delivery callback. The guard calls below are the production `releaseCodexBoundLiveThread`. This replay is distinct from the live-model Gateway smoke at the end. Receipt writes/consumption use the production binding mutation API with its existing in-memory test-store backend; this replay does not prove disk durability or restart recovery. Native app-server execution, completion notifications, unsubscribe/resume, and the separately captured native rollout files are real.

### Baseline — `b8f91cb249b8c702cfc02befd6d2fb11215928f3`

```jsonl
{"at":1792432690644,"event":"receipt-record","receipt":{"parentTurnId":"P_B","callId":"SEND_B","childThreadId":"C","submissionId":"B","predecessorRunId":"codex-thread:C","predecessorNativeTurnId":"A"}}
{"at":1792432690681,"event":"active","claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":2,"parent":2,"child":1},"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."},"receiptCount":1}
{"method":"turn/completed","params":{"threadId":"C","turn":{"id":"B","status":"completed","items":[{"type":"agentMessage","text":"B_RESULT"}]}}}
{"at":1792432690687,"event":"delivery-pending","params":{"childSessionId":"C","childSessionKey":"codex-thread:C:turn:B","result":"B_RESULT"}}
{"at":1792432690886,"event":"terminal-pending-ack","claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":1,"parent":1,"child":1},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."}}
{"event":"result","pending":{"claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":1,"parent":1,"child":1},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."}},"ack":{"receiptCount":0,"deliveryCount":1,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0}},"outcome":"RED"}
```

Captured `receipt-consume` calls after releasing the acknowledgement gate: **1**.

### Fixed source — later committed unchanged as `1cb15871a7f99b0f7af6346f2a04581344dd1928`

Submission-owner SHA-256: `69fea86a827910ecb12536e52b77e73a79b69b8e5454130f558a6936738acd9d` (matches the committed file).

```jsonl
{"at":1792433382642,"event":"receipt-record","receipt":{"parentTurnId":"P_B","callId":"SEND_B","childThreadId":"C","submissionId":"B","predecessorRunId":"codex-thread:C","predecessorNativeTurnId":"A"}}
{"at":1792433382672,"event":"active","claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":1,"parent":1,"child":0},"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."},"receiptCount":1}
{"method":"turn/completed","params":{"threadId":"C","turn":{"id":"B","status":"completed","items":[{"type":"agentMessage","text":"B_RESULT"}]}}}
{"at":1792433382677,"event":"delivery-pending","params":{"childSessionId":"C","childSessionKey":"codex-thread:C:turn:B","result":"B_RESULT"}}
{"at":1792433382882,"event":"terminal-pending-ack","claimed":false,"protected":false,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"released":true}}
{"event":"result","pending":{"claimed":false,"protected":false,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"released":true},"coldResume":{"threadId":"P","status":{"type":"idle"}}},"ack":{"receiptCount":0,"deliveryCount":1,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0}},"outcome":"GREEN"}
```

Captured `receipt-consume` calls: **1**. In the fixed run, the `coldResume` fields are the actual awaited `thread/resume` response, obtained **before** releasing the acknowledgement gate.

### Isolated live Gateway — committed head `1cb15871a7f99b0f7af6346f2a04581344dd1928`

Real authenticated V1-capable model, real Codex 0.162.1 and fresh isolated Gateway state. No delivery fault injection in this healthy-flow smoke. The following fields were read back from actual Gateway terminal receipts, native lifecycle notifications and the persisted native rollout:

```json

  },

  ],

  ],
```

</details>

prs.title: feat(openai): opt into 12-hour prompt caching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persistent OpenAI API agents need an opt-in way to reuse stable prompt prefixes across gaps longer than the default cache lifetime.

## User Impact

Users can set `params.promptCacheTtl: "12h"` (or `"30m"`) per model, globally, or per agent for GPT-5.6+ Responses requests. Unset configuration, older models' retention behavior, Chat Completions, and ChatGPT/Codex behavior are unchanged. This requests a minimum cache lifetime, not guaranteed cache hits or a deletion deadline. **12h writes cost more:** 2.5× ordinary input versus 1.25× for 30m writes; reads retain the same rate.

## Why This Change Was Made

[OpenAI's current caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime) specifies `prompt_cache_options.ttl` for the Responses API, distinct from older models' `prompt_cache_retention`. The request-level value also applies to implicit breakpoints; this change does not add explicit breakpoints or change caching mode. [Current pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) confirms total write rates, not additive surcharges. Upgrading valid 30m coverage to 12h charges a new 12h write without credit for the earlier write.

Reuse the existing cache-parameter owner and compatibility gates across provider and managed transports. Preserve `cacheRetention: "none"` precedence, validate invalid TTLs without logging authored values, and account for the higher write rate in local estimates. Existing open-ended provider-parameter schemas already accept the option, so no new top-level config field, schema migration, dependency bump, or parallel cache implementation is needed. The wire contract handles the API's new value without patching or casting around the pinned SDK.

Simplification review retained one lifetime decision owner; production growth is option plumbing and write-cost selection, not new state or infrastructure.

## Evidence

- Regression requests fail on the original implementation (missing TTL) and pass with the change.
- **117 focused tests passed** across Responses builders, write pricing, existing Chat Completions policy, config-to-stream precedence/validation, proxy forwarding, and prompt-prefix stability.
- **3 live OpenAI Responses cases passed** on `gpt-5.6-luna`: unset, `30m`, and `12h`. These prove API acceptance and completed streamed replies, not 12-hour elapsed retention or realized billing savings.
- Production `tsconfig.core.json` typecheck, changed-file format check, documentation config-example validation, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the supplied diff.
- Full `pnpm build` passed (3m 33.6s); changed-file typed lint passed with 0 warnings/errors. An isolated, authenticated Gateway started on its own profile, state, workspace, and port. Its real-agent CLI probe was refused by the agent-exec inter-session attribution guard before inference, so full Gateway-to-model proof remains incomplete. No alternate CLI/RPC route or guard bypass was attempted.

**Live-proof limitation:** full Gateway-to-model proof remains unexecuted because the agent-exec attribution guard refused its CLI invocation. Direct provider API acceptance is proven; this does not claim that missing Gateway boundary. @steipete instructed landing with the documented evidence and limitations; enforced GitHub review, security, and CI gates still apply.

Known verification limits: the changed-test typecheck wrapper failed its existing global test-root budget preflight and was stopped while waiting for generated artifacts (plugins-platform 727 > 720; no test roots are added here). One additional native-worker environment probe failed with `502 Secret egress proxy refused the request`; its other cases passed. No egress guard was bypassed. PR CI is the broad-check owner; CI timing is pending. Local focused suites took 99.5s total (most time in compiled agent-worker setup); test execution stayed below 5s per changed non-live file. Live cases took 24.2s wall time.

**Settlement-baseline repair:** 5aedeae5e5d77891427690607673929543308fd1 integrates existing main settlement fix 4453edcc7db9 via baseline 1c4b27072712 for the launch-wire missing-file failure in [run 39481201843](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39481201843/job/118830768677). The complete feature diff is byte-identical to the original reviewed patch. All **117 focused feature tests passed again** on the integrated head (32.72s). The local full launch-wire attempt hit a synthetic-provider ECONNRESET during baseline inference before the original settlement assertion, so no local full-file pass is claimed. Fresh current-head GitHub CI is required; original build/live evidence above remains prior-head evidence.

**Current repaired head: eeb556b73cacea28c5078ff6beb8f96e931937c1.** The CI package-type error was reproduced and fixed by retaining the complete SDK request shape and the API-optional TTL field; the exact package test-type graph now passes. The review finding about mixed cache lifetimes is also fixed: coherent reported 30m/12h buckets override the request default, with compatibility fallback when absent. Six new pricing cases were red before the repair and now pass through both Responses paths, including zero 12h writes. Current accounting/lifecycle suites: **78 passed**; type-repair caller/request suites: **122 passed**. Typed lint/format/diff checks and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. Prior settlement-failure job checks-node-changed-10 is green on the integrated baseline. Fresh CI on this head remains required; previous full-build/live evidence and the stated Gateway/host limitations are not relabeled as current-head proof.

Requested by @steipete.

prs.title: feat: prepare existing PRs from ordinary chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A sandboxed conversation that starts without a project can inspect its author's existing PR, but preparation requires a managed workspace to be bound already. This breaks a natural continuation request when the PR link arrives after the conversation has started. The registered preparation path rejects the unbound conversation before importing the PR.

## User Impact

A conversation can prepare the PR in a new session-owned workspace and continue in the same chat. Original files stay in their original source, earlier message links open them read-only, and sibling conversations keep their workspaces. Current PR files remain editable through the existing Files source precondition; an old editor cannot overwrite a same-named current file with identical bytes.

Adoption waits for a clear current-session boundary. Queued or preparing input, background work and unobserved results, pending children, and terminals cause a visible refusal or deferral without draining that work. Existing managed preparation and plugin reload retain their behavior. This extends preparation; the original PR identity, linked author, publisher eligibility and guest restrictions remain enforced by their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changing the active turn's directory would leave tools and pending work associated with the previous source. Preparation therefore yields the requesting turn, waits for its cleanup, uses the existing managed-workspace allocation and binding operations, and resumes through the existing session-event path. GitHub eligibility and live authority are checked again around binding and import, and uncertain commit results preserve an already-accepted checkout for retry.

One private session relation records the original admitted file source and persisted-message boundary. Existing preview, download and HTML-asset routes use that message identity to read the original files under current access checks. Those responses carry no editable hash or current managed-source descriptor. Canonical persistent and incognito transcript rewrites carry that relation forward using surviving message identities and their committed positions. Removing the original boundary message preserves earlier surviving links; an unresolved relation refuses access instead of choosing the current source. The relation follows the existing reset/detach lifecycle and is omitted from public and plugin session projections. Ordinary configured symlink workspaces are compared by their canonical identity, with the existing filesystem guard checked again before binding.

This PR is stacked on #178298. The general Files source descriptor and reopen recovery come from #178336; this diff adds adoption-specific enforcement and historical-source reads.

## Evidence

The registered pre-change action rejected an ordinary sandboxed conversation without a managed binding and preserved its entry and files. Focused source tests exercise the yielded handoff, retained operator identity, Stop and failure results, actual managed allocation and SQLite binding, lost native completion after commit, queued/background refusal, historical versus current same-name files, relative assets, stale/fresh saves and sibling preservation.

After integration with the checked parent, remote validation passed changed-file formatting/lint, protocol registry and native-model checks, the enforced line cap, and all seven selected production/test type families. The affected 35-file batch passed **485 tests** in **512.9 seconds**, with one opt-in Podman projection case unrun. This covers the newer retained Files read owner, source-change recovery, current handoff/reload callers, managed preparation/refresh, and persistent workspace/event siblings. Unchanged earlier proof was reused rather than repeating the full related batch.

The transcript-lifecycle correction also covers persistent and incognito media/full/suffix rewrites, removal of the original boundary message, manual compaction, and ordinary configured symlink workspaces. Applicable results from the 47-file correction batch were retained while failed writer/fixture paths were corrected and rechecked. The final adoption case passed in **45.8 seconds**, including old/current file responses after the existing projection-readiness boundary. All six direct test-registry consumers passed **620 tests** in **219.0 seconds**. Seven existing platform or opt-in cases in the correction batch remain unrun. These batches overlap and are reported separately.

The tests ran through the saved native test recipe with literal file selection. Fixtures use real Git, persistence and file effects with synthetic GitHub/container I/O; they do not establish live native-thread continuity. Connected guest preparation, sanitized before/after screenshots and a recording, independent review, and current-head hosted CI remain pending. Hosted CI time is therefore not yet available. This PR stays open until those readiness obligations are completed.
