prs.title: feat: inspect existing own pull requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A person can paste an existing GitHub PR into a conversation, but the publication tool cannot verify that it belongs to their linked account or identify its original source and target. The existing `inspect` action requires an earlier session publication and full operator write access.

## User Impact

Adds `github_publish` with `action: "inspect_pr"` and `pullRequestUrl`. It returns the verified author, canonical PR URL and state, base and head repository IDs, branches and observed commits. Copied Files changed links (`/changes` and the older `/files` path), Commits and Checks links, query strings, and comment or review anchors resolve to the same PR. Closed and merged states remain visible, and a deleted head repository returns a null head.

Inspection performs no workspace or GitHub writes and creates no publication receipt. It does not adopt a PR or prepare its source. Existing publication and administrator-only actions keep their current targets and permissions; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action uses the existing Gateway requester and shared publisher owners. It compares the PR author's immutable account ID with the requester's current verified linked identities on the configured host, including secondary linked accounts. A private base repository requires verified account access before the PR is read, and a private head requires the same qualification before disclosure. Current requester, session, identity and publisher checks surround awaited work and run again before returning the result.

Only validated repository and PR identifiers reach fixed API endpoints; query strings and fragments are discarded. Observed account and repository owners support GitHub managed usernames. The result carries reference data. Any later operation must establish its own current authority, write eligibility and head preconditions.

## Evidence

The registered tool/Gateway boundary covers same-repository and fork references, secondary linked identities, private access, wrong authors, missing identities, revocation during awaited reads, configured hosts, managed usernames and malformed references. Scope and scheduled-continuation tests preserve administrator-only actions. The original baseline rejects inspect_pr at the action schema. Actual /changes and anchored links failed both host cases before the URL correction, while the other 19 cases passed.

The accepted inspection implementation is unchanged by this baseline integration. Its prior 21 inspection and 12 continuation cases, 170-case related batch, and 81-case managed-login correction, protocol/native generation, affected type/scope/routing/prefix proofs remain applicable where inputs are unchanged. The live results below were captured from one restricted conversation between 09:52 and 10:04 UTC on October 20. Each row used one admitted `github_publish.inspect_pr` invocation. Numeric match fields compare the returned author with the recorded linked identity; reference match fields compare the returned repository IDs, branches and commits with the pre-inspection GitHub facts. Private identifiers are omitted.

| Actual native case | Observed action result | Independent access/reference facts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Own public PR, using the copied `/changes#diff-…` link | `toolError: false`; canonical URL returned; numeric author matched the linked account | Both original repository IDs, branches and commits matched; returned keys were exactly `url, host, number, author, state, base, head`. |
| Own private PR | `toolError: false`; numeric author matched the linked account; original reference returned | Real GitHub permission for that linked ID was `write`; both original repository IDs, branches and commits matched. |
| Private control inaccessible to the linked account | `toolError: true`; `descriptorReturned: false`; `alternateReadAttempted: false` | The configured publisher could read the PR, while the linked account's real permission was `none`. |

The denied action returned: “The PR could not be verified as yours with current repository access. Check its URL and your linked GitHub account.” All three recorded post-checks preserved the PR state, draft flag and base/head refs. The conversation's workspace binding stayed null; inspection prepared no files.

The live resolver and requester-owner blobs are respectively `60dfed7a59da41bf9021857c2a3ba9b354b44a1d` and `9a00129a15f671b747ba3f130b998542c6b9e6af`, identical to those files at the current PR head. Independent review also qualified the surrounding caller differences for these exercised paths.

Live proof used the qualified combined runtime containing the same inspection implementation and requester owner, not the entire present checkout. Denial before PR metadata reading is source-derived alongside the observed denial and real permission facts; outbound HTTP sequencing was not captured. In-flight revocation was not induced against protected live profiles and remains covered through real local owners at the registered boundary with synthetic GitHub I/O. Enterprise variants retain source/test proof.

The integration against `73f2bf22959c26cc49fd5fd8533084badab2bd08` preserves main's sandbox-specific base-refresh/evidence filtering and deployment tool/action allowlists. The callable action schema and inherited tool metadata both declare `inspect_pr` and its PR URL. An explicit deployment allowlist can include or exclude inspection; it does not require a managed sandbox. Inspection's identity, private-access and result contracts are unchanged.

Head `abe439a06a846a45842ea74e3949622756d51cdd` passed formatting, type-aware lint with no warnings or errors, native graph-boundary discovery and all 29 selected core-test type graphs. All 164 cases across nine affected files passed, including registration, publication inheritance, deployment-policy Tool Search/Code Mode/final-hook checks and issued-worker-handle enforcement. The tool suite's 25 cases took 9.91 seconds; the native joined test batch took 229.00 seconds. The authenticated source tree `2a44ded69b81d0917faf2133016d3e84590a4ba7` exactly matches the committed tree. Independent engineering review is clean on that commit.

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review are pending. An earlier head's X-publication Bun check failed with HTTP 503; the attempted historical-baseline reproduction stopped during dependency preparation before that test ran, so it does not establish inherited-failure attribution. Current-head CI will be reconciled separately. The PR remains open and inspection does not prepare or publish changes to an inspected PR.

prs.title: fix(feishu): stop inbound mentions from cascading into replies
prs.body:
Closes #121921

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu group replies would automatically mention every non-bot participant mentioned in the inbound message, even when the agent's reply did not request those mentions. Error and fallback replies could therefore wake multiple bots and create an unintended cascade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound mention targets remain available as agent context, but they are no longer passed into the reply dispatcher or automatically attached to generated replies. Explicit outbound mentions, native Feishu `at` rendering, and bot-authored required mentions (`requiredMentionTargets`) remain unchanged.

This restores the boundary introduced by #71396 without reverting the native mention-rendering improvements from #93522.

## User Impact

Feishu users and multi-agent groups no longer receive unrequested `@` notifications from ordinary, error, fallback, card, streaming, block, or chunked replies. Agents can still explicitly mention users when the outbound content or message-tool request asks for it.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage verifies non-streaming final/error replies, static cards, streaming card closes, and independent block/chunk delivery do not inherit inbound mention targets.
- Existing coverage verifies `requiredMentionTargets` still reaches every required text chunk and static card reply.
- Focused Feishu tests pass:
  - `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: **124/124**
  - `bot.test.ts` + `send.test.ts`: **131/131**
  - Total: **255/255**
- `oxfmt --check` passes for all 3 changed files.
- Focused `oxlint` passes for all 3 changed files.
- `git diff --check` passes.

prs.title: fix(agent-core): bound runaway loops with turn/error-batch/idle-repeat guards (#120962)
prs.body: Closes #120962 [AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where a worker agent could enter an unbounded retry loop inside the native runLoop: an external service returning HTTP 429 (masked inside a "successful" tool output) drove 219 assistant turns / 177 tool calls / ~15M tokens over 6h42m, stopped only by the global `stuckSessionAbortMs` timeout rather than by any active guardrail. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds three opt-in hard cutoffs to the agent-core runLoop, each activating independently when set to a positive integer in `tools.loopDetection`: - **`turnLimit`** — max assistant turns per run; ends gracefully with a terminal message instead of another provider request. - **`maxConsecutiveErrorBatches`** — max consecutive all-error tool batches; any success resets the streak. - **`maxIdleRepeatCalls`** — max consecutive identical tool calls (same name + args); catches errors hidden inside successful output. Steering-skipped calls are excluded. `enabled: true` alone does not engage hard cutoffs (preserves upgrade contract). `enabled: false` disables both layers. Resolved config propagates through sessions, compaction, and worker launch descriptors. The launcher fences guard-enabled turns on worker bundles lacking the `worker-loop-guard-v1` capability; configless and `enabled:false` turns are unaffected. ## User Impact Operators who want the guardrails set at least one guard key (e.g. `turnLimit: 200`) in a `tools.loopDetection` block. Existing configurations gain no new hard termination behavior unless a guard key is explicitly set. Public package consumers see no change unless they opt in. ## Evidence **Focused tests (all pass):** - `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.guard.test.ts` — 23 tests: maxTurns, error-batch, idle-repeat, steering-skip exclusion (sequential + parallel), steering requeue - `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-guard-transport.test.ts` — real `AgentSession` through local HTTP/SSE transport, 3 repeated calls → graceful termination, no 4th request - `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-config.test.ts` — 9 tests: per-key activation, `enabled:false` kill switch, per-agent cascade - `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.loop-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests: launcher fence, serialization, guard-off compatibility - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.test.ts` — 25 tests: loop-guard capability in worker protocol features

prs.title: refactor(runtime): retire private native test seams
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private construction and reset forwarding expose fixed implementations or test substitutions that serving callers never select. Tests can observe existing native owners without adding those choices to production APIs.

## Changes

WhatsApp and Signal fixtures capture the same real SDK reaction stores and use their unchanged public reset operation directly; private forwarding exports retire. Codex's private close owner calls the same native child-release function directly instead of receiving that fixed callback. Approval, persistence, replay and accepted child-completion settlement are unchanged.

iMessage's private reaction and poll resets retire together. Its local pending-poll map requires consistent subject-graph reloads rather than only SDK-store capture. Persistent/replay fixtures reuse the existing native state helper, preserve the same database across restart checks, and reattach actual held-write/deletion gates to the current owner. Existing public SDK controls and approval, tombstone and replay assertions remain.

The observer uses its native preparation/completion adapters directly. Tests capture distinct module-boundary spies for each constructed observer, restore native exports, and rearm only those captured functions. Read/persist overrides, source-authority checks, FIFO and accepted-work settlement remain unchanged. UI consumers expose only their two receiver-free retry operations rather than the private retry object. Other retained boundary-fixture migrations exercise unchanged production owners.

Final accounting against the PR merge base: **50 paths, 26 net production lines removed, 227 fixture/support lines added, 201 overall lines added**. This is the surviving area slice after mandatory CI-attribution withdrawal, not the original 140-line candidate. Fixture growth replaces private production controls with native owner observation and consistent restart graphs; moved bodies are not counted as removed behavior.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No speculative guard is removed in the surviving slice. No public SDK, configuration, CLI, protocol, persisted shape, dependency, permission, durability or realistic-concurrency contract changes. Native effects keep their current authority and settlement checks. Private test fixtures now manage actual native stores and graph lifetimes rather than invoking private forwarding resets; they must finish their own work before reloading an owner.

## CI attribution and scoped withdrawal

The final 23-path repair passes expanded targeted types (4.853s), formatting (9.758s), typed lint (117.894s), the 50-source line-cap ratchet (3.718s), and all 14 lint-suppression tests (9.808s driver). Original core/UI targeted types and typed lint pass. prs.title: fix: message-tool sends drop model-based reply prefixes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `messages.responsePrefix` uses model or thinking tokens (`{model}`, `{provider}`, `{modelFull}`, `{thinkingLevel}`), replies sent through `message(action=send)` go out with no prefix at all, while normal replies keep it. The tool send path only had the agent identity, so any template with a model token stayed unresolved and the prefix was skipped.

## User Impact

In shared chats where several agents or models post, people rely on the prefix to tell who's speaking. Message-tool sends, which are often the ones that cross into another conversation, lost that label.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool already runs inside an agent turn that knows its provider, model and thinking level. This passes that run metadata through the message-tool options into `runMessageAction`, so the send path interpolates the prefix the same way direct replies do. Callers without run metadata keep the existing behavior: unresolved placeholders still skip the prefix instead of sending a literal `{model}`. The prefix helper moves into its own small module so the tool execution and the model-context wiring share it.

## Evidence

- `src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.core.test.ts` gains two cases at the real send boundary: active metadata renders on the requested recipient, and an already-prefixed message isn't prefixed twice.
  - Against the pre-fix production code, both fail on their assertions (the send receives no prefix); the other 24 cases pass.
  - With the fix: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.core.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 26/26.
- Docs: `docs/gateway/config-agents/messages-and-talk.md` notes that message-tool sends use the active run metadata.

Closes #165615

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the message tool cannot update an existing Discord Components V2 card, rejecting component-only edits and dropping card data when text is supplied.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can replace an existing card in place after a decision, including edits without a plain-text message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public edit adapter now forwards the component specification and callback context. The runtime uses the existing component-edit writer, which builds the V2 PATCH without `content` and refreshes callback registrations. Component payloads are also exposed for enabled edit actions. Ordinary text edits and retained progress edits keep their existing path; account, action, target, and request-authority gates remain in place.

This is scoped to the documented component-spec object format and existing V2 cards. It does not establish conversion of classic text messages or native component-array edits.

## Evidence

- Source trace against upstream `553841e490220a6c723da84a4fdd3caf0dcb2a11` confirms the two failing boundaries: the public edit adapter omitted components, and the runtime required content and used the content-only writer.
- Added regressions in existing suites for public forwarding with optional text, edit discovery, disabled/blocked targets, and retained progress rendering with an irrelevant malformed component payload.
- Added a loopback REST regression through the public action and real component-edit writer that asserts V2 flags and components, without PATCH content or create-message nonce. This test is authored but **not executed**.
- Fresh independent source review of the final seven-file patch found no actionable P0–P2 defects. `git diff --check` passes.

AutoReview could not run because neither the Codex nor Claude CLI is installed; independent source review is not a completed AutoReview result.

prs.title: fix(build): stabilize declaration cache reuse
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes package builds whose runtime chunk layout changes when declaration emission is toggled. Stable outputs avoid invalidating restored declaration caches. Current main's final runtime-only build pass remains unchanged; this repair addresses the package graph producer rather than removing that existing mitigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime JavaScript and declaration emission now use separate, stable tsdown config partitions for AI and all workspace packages, including agent-core, while preserving main's consolidated full declaration program and SDK-only selection. The build wrapper owns DTS mode for the default, main, and AI configs, including CAC's `--dts=true` and `--dts=false` forms; arbitrary custom configs and `--no-config` retain their original arguments.

The compiler-input snapshot, cache namespace algorithm, cache format, dependencies, and environment surface are unchanged. The shared config-splitting helper is reached through the canonical generator import closure, so edits invalidate the producer stamps without a new hard-coded input list. Current package compiler options, runtime-cache ownership and runtime-only plugins remain intact. Cleanup now receives the same effective DTS mode as compilation.

## User Impact

Warm full builds can reuse restored declaration artifacts after runtime-only rebuilds instead of recompiling all declaration groups. Explicit DTS CLI overrides continue to work without recombining the runtime and declaration graphs.

## Evidence

### Published Current-Main Correction

Current head: `b41ff62b3156c9140f43fe1a551372bd565eb1fb`, tree `a184bd5d7b9f17d86d736dcded8acdc4c508fbae`. The signed four-file follow-up migrates Knip to the split AI runtime config, adds a real manifest-compiler regression for both shipping manifests, and reflows two tests without changing their assertions. It checks merge `4ad45e6b` of this head into `551431ec`. Format/parity, affected test types and all required aggregate gates still must pass; no complete CI/native qualification is claimed.

Predecessor native integration: `097b5b637185ff7f085ae23c093146f2a289b08a`, tree `bee60f2ffb07e34dac4563c56a655b62dbe1ab7c`. The signed native baseline integration preserves `b98fd8a322c54f2f2dbafa3a648bfc92f8ce6a33` as first parent and pins [main6deac372](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6deac372d6436b389cf6735e424bb6b122a2175c) as second parent. This consumes the canonical main UI typecheck repair without adding a UI change to the PR's 15-file build/cache product diff. The emitted-asset and explicit-build-cwd repairs, all original ancestry and current compiler/cache/worker/fixture owners remain intact.

Independent source review verified the exact materialized resolution: unconditional real lockfile copy, physical fixture boundary, installed-dependency protection and opt-in Mistral license. Current client-credential worker and Darwin native-asset contracts remain intact. Fresh full-diff AutoReview raised one standalone-build finding. Parent and independent review rejected it as an introduced regression: that owner deliberately retains its unchanged full-DTS, clean-output, uncached build contract; build-all's repaired cache route calls a different owner. The existing real standalone test remains mandatory hosted coverage. Source review is not runtime qualification.

Both substantive historical ClawSweeper findings are addressed in source: spaced boolean DTS values are consumed with their option, and the native declaration emitter removes maps owned by excluded runtime stub chunks. Effective DTS mode also reaches cleanup, and sequential CLI tests check retained declaration bytes rather than incorrectly expecting removal. Cache tests retain cold/warm/mixed-hit/disabled cases, actual runtime imports, declaration restoration and byte/hash comparisons; watch tests require two completed generations.

**Predecessor proof has two retained failures; successor proof is pending.** [CI39336508914](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39336508914) binds `0b512449`, not this successor. Actual Linux logs show `tsdown-config` 62 passes, declaration-resolution 24 passes/four platform-capability skips, build-all 59 passes, and plugin-SDK declarations 11 passes/one skip. These remain predecessor results, not qualification of the new head.

The current three-file correction emits the license through the bundler's asset owner instead of an out-of-band copy, and includes physical asset provenance in runtime-cache signatures. This preserves both license restoration and invalidation when its source changes. The existing cache test now exercises a non-module asset, unchanged restoration and isolated source invalidation; the real mixed-cache fixture, complete artifact hashes, declaration signatures, cache reuse and license/streaming assertions are unchanged. Installed tsdown/Rolldown contracts were inspected directly; independent source audit and fresh scoped autoreview found no actionable P0-P2 findings. prs.title: fix: reuse clean SQLite proof after runtime upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Node/Bun or SQLite patch update can turn an otherwise clean restart into a full database scan, even though the checkpointed database bytes and schema have not changed. Large databases can spend minutes in that scan.

## User Impact

Clean, recently verified databases reuse their admission proof across runtime and SQLite version/source changes. The original full-verification timestamp remains unchanged. No quick check or full integrity scan is added for these changes.

Legacy seals still require an exact combined-hash match. A legacy mismatch takes the existing full path once; the next clean close writes decomposed identity components.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original runtime/library tuple conservatively invalidated cached validation; it did not establish a data-integrity requirement for rescanning unchanged bytes. This separates informational runtime/library versions from schema, policy, and compile-feature compatibility. All compatibility components are compared, so a runtime difference cannot mask a schema, policy, or feature mismatch. The normal clean-close owner re-mints the seal.

The only compile-option exclusion is `COMPILER=...`: [SQLite's generator](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/blob/a9a1fac1801f083b7de9dc862899b69da3dcb149/tool/mkctimec.tcl#L360-L370) constructs it solely from compiler identification/version macros. Every other reported option, including defaults and limits, remains compared. Actual-library WAL-safety, iterator, and extension admission retain their behavior.

File metadata, checksum, empty journals, quarantine, schema, policy, malformed-proof handling, and the seven-day full-verification age remain admission requirements. The existing #169649 edge is accepted: metadata-invisible latent corruption remains bounded by normal detection and seven-day/explicit full verification. A runtime or patch update no longer adds an early scan. Explicit verification remains full.

Removed the runtime/sqlite mismatch refusal branches and their obsolete expectations. No SQL, transaction, schema, worker-request, or SDK surface changes. Production +35 lines, tests +74, docs +6; the growth represents decomposed persisted identity and its compatibility-boundary proof.

## Evidence

- Two independent Codex reviews: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Changed-file type-aware lint and diff checks passed.
- Actual Homebrew SQLite 3.54.0 and 3.54.1 dylibs: the same 54 reported compile options, or 53 after removing only `COMPILER`. Compared SHA-256: `849651217ff5fb7188fb8157278bfeae1f32aeee40e30965222f036a57345686`. No feature/default/limit differences.
- Both new runtime/library regressions fail on the base because they observe `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and pass on this candidate without either integrity scan. They verify timestamp preservation, re-minting, and the next fast restart. Feature/schema/policy mismatches alongside runtime changes retain the full path. All seven focused owner/sibling test files pass (142 tests); two stale startup fixtures were corrected to create genuine legacy/policy mismatches. Production types, all 29 test-type groups, type-aware lint, format, T1/dialect/mock-export ratchets, Madge (zero cycles), and export-collision checks passed. `check:changed` retains three inherited failure classes: three UI max-lines suppressions, four test-root budgets, and 16 production/one full-tree unused exports. A focused replay on main `d48ab9cd0ad6` reproduces the same rules/files and Knip findings; the candidate has one fewer plugin test root (727 vs 728). No new static findings.
- Standard fixture: three alternating base/candidate pairs at base `097a2f70d0c4` and head `8f82f97d4f0f`, using a forced library-only identity change followed by two normal restarts. Restart SQL median [min–max] **565 [565–565] → 298 [297–303]**, worker requests **120 [120–121] → 102 [101–102]**, MAIN **98 [98–98] → 38 [38–38]**. Warm-turn per-arm medians are **46 SQL / 11 requests / 0 MAIN** in every arm. Two full plus two FK checks per base restart become zero canonical scans; original verification times are preserved, new identities are minted and the next restart accepts them.
- Standard observed restart time: **8.964 [8.549–9.263] → 8.007 [7.332–10.340] seconds**. Full integrity-check time: **2.287 [2.136–2.448] ms → 0** on approximately 5.2 MB of canonical databases. Shared-host variation includes one slower candidate; this is not a guaranteed latency claim. Removed work includes cold admission 132→29 SQL / 2→1 requests, preflight 44→3 MAIN SQL, native lifecycle 61→17 SQL and deletion snapshots 38→21 SQL / 9→5 requests.
- Measurement uses the frozen observer/counting rules in a local derivative, with initial native version/source injection and no seal-file edits. The unrelated 300-second idle dwell is omitted symmetrically; ten warm turns, settling and restart phases remain. One successful baseline was reanalyzed after correcting an overbroad reporting assertion about helper processes; no standard workload rerun. Large fixture: one successful alternating pair, 20 agents and 2.1 million synthetic events, approximately 3.51 GB in 21 canonical databases after preparation/workload. Restart through recovery readiness: **6,930→3,190 SQL / 1,091→1,070 requests / 155→113 MAIN**, **26.316→15.873 seconds**. All 21 full checks and 21 FK checks become zero; summed full-check elapsed time **21.019→0 seconds**, FK time **3.761→0 seconds**. All 21 owner receipts preserve verification time and re-mint identity; the next restart accepts. Warm medians/ranges match: 53 [53–56] SQL / 12 [12–13] requests / 0 MAIN. Whole-workload totals: 75,221→70,477 SQL / 6,873→6,038 requests / 653→371 MAIN. This is one pair on a shared host, not a latency distribution or a benchmark of the historical 43.6 GB installation.
- Two base-only large setup attempts sent chat before saved-input recovery completed and are excluded. `/readyz` and `sidecars.ready` intentionally precede chat unlocking; the final derivative waits for both existing delivery/subagent recovery completion traces in both arms, without chat retries or product edits. Original `/readyz` observations are retained separately (22.100→15.141 seconds). Large restart counts include this recovery work and are not directly comparable to the standard phase boundary. Native check durations are summed elapsed time, not CPU time. Operation placement changes too: native lifecycle 612→17 SQL and preflight 44→3 SQL, while session-row facts rise 0→1,331 SQL / 332 requests and shared facts rise 0→313 SQL / 313 requests in that window; aggregate savings remain as reported.

PG review approved the production changes and renewed approval for final head `8f82f97d4f0f`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39507967205) and the required `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. The queued test shards eventually received runners and all passed; the runner-starvation exception was not used. No CI rerun was needed.

prs.title: feat(telegram): prepare attachments before native message handling
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A voice-transcription adapter cannot provide prepared text and suppress the original Telegram attachment before native media processing. Existing dispatch hooks run too late. This PR proposes an optional `before_channel_ingress` hook for admitted ordinary noncommand singletons.

## User Impact

A registered preparer can return text and `suppressAttachments: true`; Telegram retains the original sender, chat/topic, message/update identity, reply context, dispatch claims and retry ownership. Original control commands, command-config grants and all album members bypass preparation and retain their native authorization and collective media owners. Installations without a preparer keep existing handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport factory binds preparation to the exact update and invokes it after native sender authorization and accepted fresh-message dispatch claims, before attachment I/O. Edits retain their existing silent authorization path. The event carries copied transport facts, not authority. Consumers must enforce their own current binding and consent after awaited work and before private effects.

Native cancellation, scoped liveness, claim rollback and late-result fencing stay with their existing owners. Failed rollback remains nonretryable. The focused `plugin-hook-runtime` subpath exposes the existing runner getter; generated package/entrypoint metadata stays aligned. Telegram exposes its existing native fetch bridge and token-scoped throttler. Small unchanged DTO/reducer blocks are extracted to preserve existing source-size ratchets.

The concrete consumer is our privately maintained personal-assistant voice adapter, implemented as a source candidate. It uses its selected account’s read-only file client and existing audio request/result receipts, waits for the audio owner, then supplies prepared text to avoid duplicate native media work. It adds no poller, sender, consent store or inference authority. Consumer source preparation is not an activation or migration claim. Maintainer acceptance of this public contract remains required.

## Evidence

Current ready head: `e3c9c0e22ce9b71822c04b2f5efc7e1142276704`, tree `94b0900bb516132108b3d5e8297201b789c8f22f`. The command/media P1 is fixed. This head removes only the requested nondiscriminating factory case: 16 deleted lines, no additions/import changes. Every other tracked byte and mode, including production, manifests and the integration fixture, matches parent `7b1b60779992eee09d73fb174f1a2b18e28f8bcf`.

- Ten remaining factory cases, their owning test type graph, format, assertion/mock/source-cap ratchets pass on the current head. Six native containers settle at zero, PID zero, no OOM, and are removed.
- **126 distinct cases qualified = ten freshly rerun plus 116 on byte-identical production and other suites at the parent.** This is not 126 fresh executions. The parent had 127 passing cases across 12 local phases, including four type graphs, typed core lint and unchanged ratchets.
- The identical final 22-case integration fixture gives 13 passes/nine causal failures before the two command/album eligibility guards and 22/22 after. Registration, hook runner, grammY, authorization, SQLite, dispatch claims and keyed album ownership are real; downstream services are synthetic. Allowed albums resolve two file IDs into one two-media delivery. Plain command cases prove original delegation/preparation bypass, not a final command-delivery assertion.

### Concrete consumer authority correction

The consumer review exposed a real local race: preparation queued behind another download could later start file lookup/download using stale consent. The private correction rechecks its existing consent owner after waits and before the next lookup, download, body consumption, write transaction and transcript handoff. Withdrawal returns the existing terms placeholder without waiting for a job never accepted. Already accepted transactions and receipts remain intact without inference replay.

The actual registered consumer, preparation adapter, selected-account read-only client, consent-status reader and audio artifact owner were exercised together with synthetic external transport/status responses. The identical ten regressions have seven causal failures before repair; all **33 focused tests pass** after repair in isolated Node 24.22.0 containers: network disabled, read-only source, 512 MiB/one CPU, terminal PID zero/no OOM, removed. Cases include account mismatch with zero effects, queued withdrawal, withdrawal during lookup/response/body/result adoption, service stop, terminal placeholder without polling, exact-once download and unchanged accepted receipts. All fourteen published private module/test blobs match the final fixture. Its zero-read-ahead body case also fails causally when only the pre-write consent guard is removed: the forbidden pending artifact exists; this is the same distinct case, not an additional passing test.

This is concrete source-boundary proof, not an installed Gateway/model/Telegram result. A status read cannot atomically revoke an I/O already started with valid authority; subsequent effects and handoff are fenced.

### SDK qualification

[Complete eight-phase run 39510326876](https://github.com/ChuLaiTheGreat/openclaw/actions/runs/39510326876) **succeeded**, terminal 23:54:43 UTC, on exact production-bearing parent `7b1b607`, tree `0f411c8e3367a04462077192003a7cfa4e8e01f8`, against pinned main `5a0b5006`. This is not an exact build of test-only child `e3c9c0e`; the byte-identical production and the separately qualified test deletion are attributed above.

| Native phase | Result | Seconds |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| SDK exports | Pass | 0.57 |
| Full build | Pass | 429.45 |
| Qualified Telegram cold-import profile | Pass | 2.17 |
| Native API difference report | Pass | 1,824.66 |
| Proper extension typed lint | Pass, zero warnings/errors | 152.98 |
| Core production types | Pass | 19.97 |
| Full native package boundary, 133 plugins | Pass | 763.61 |
| Database-worker ratchet | Pass | 278.09 |

All eleven actual container outcomes (dependencies, pinned-`rg` qualification and eight SDK phases) have native exit zero, terminal PID zero, no OOM, clean unchanged input head/tree/status, and completed removal. The terminal job log was downloaded once; SHA-256 `6b7598499a43f9ff7d043f8e6ec166de45f268db9c76148a16c7bde60ef699e0`. Commands, caps, budgets and assertions are unchanged.

The database guard runs its original 4096 MiB Node command: T1 calls **171 → 171**, deprecated-only compatibility calls **15 → 15**. Extension lint emits 13,046 native DTS files before checking the actual changed paths. The API report records one new entrypoint, four added/169 affected exports and ten reachable declaration changes; acknowledgement digest `493581ec` is report metadata, not owner approval. The qualified cold-import snapshot is 186.83 MiB RSS against 47.12 MiB baseline, not Gateway idle RAM or a 10.5 comparison. Full build retains the UI startup gzip advisory, 317.8 KiB for 317.5 KiB; no baseline was raised or global-budget success claimed.

[Attempt 39509742678](https://github.com/ChuLaiTheGreat/openclaw/actions/runs/39509742678) stopped at anonymous API quota before checkout/tests; the isolated host now consumes its ephemeral read-only job token for fixed public preflight reads and removes it before all subprocesses. [Older run 39488465765](https://github.com/ChuLaiTheGreat/openclaw/actions/runs/39488465765) had six passing phases on older production plus extension-test lint failures and missing-`rg` setup; none are relabeled as current production proof. Cold-import RSS is not Gateway idle RAM or a 10.5 comparison.

### Current CI failures: exact base/merge controls

The current [CI run 39512771329](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39512771329) tests merge `b5dfc2a8a9a591218ca74f9b85238a7482e291c4` into base `5c6611f9f59692fd89e8b0c8b7328e265d23eeb7`.

- Doctor typed lint: the owning-file command reproduces the same `typescript(unbound-method)` at `src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts:73:22` on both exact base and merge. That file and guard inputs are unchanged by this PR. This is an inherited failure, not repaired here.
- SDK surface: the native registered checker passes on the base and fails on the merge for the proposed public API growth below. Both retain all shipped names and unchanged deprecated/local-only surfaces. No budget was increased, test weakened or whole compact shard claimed green.

| Public surface | Base/default ceiling | Proposed merge |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Entrypoints | 156 | 157 |
| Exports | 3,810 | 3,814 |
| Callable exports | 2,208 | 2,209 |

The delta is the focused runtime subpath, three ingress hook types and runner getter. This quantifies the **existing SDK/security owner decision**: accept or decline that bounded contract and its corresponding ceilings. It is not recorded as approved. All four targeted control containers settle without OOM, PID zero, clean unchanged sources, and are removed. These controls do not rerun the entire CI shard.

Historical global max-lines failures on three unchanged UI owners and earlier pinned-Bun Codex contention failures retain their actual base comparisons; they are not attributed to this later merge. No allowance was added to hide them.

Still required before merge: SDK/security owner acceptance and authorized team Gateway/model/Telegram broker proof of permitted/denied/revoked private-I/O paths, suppression, cancellation and replay without duplicate dispatch. Private accounts/configuration, client deployment, production migration, merge and release publication are outside this submission. The PR is ready for review.

prs.title: test(ui): make widget touch velocity deterministic
prs.body:
Related: #178578, #178614

## What Problem This Solves

The mobile widget-scroll test sends each touch move only after the previous CDP command returns, so CI transport timing currently determines the gesture's velocity and whether Chromium starts a fling.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. The test still drives Chromium's native touch emulator and verifies drag distance, inertia, monotonic movement, and reader preservation during streaming with the same thresholds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the existing twelve 20-pixel moves explicit timestamps 16 ms apart, followed by release 2 ms later. This defines the intended 1,250 px/s input independently of CDP delivery delays. Record scroll and touch-release observations with `performance.timeOrigin + performance.now()` so the drag/inertia comparison uses actual callback observation times rather than mixing native observations with the synthetic input clock.

The pinned Chromium 156.0.8078.4 [input handler preserves explicit timestamps](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/156.0.8078.4/content/browser/devtools/protocol/input_handler.cc#130), and its [velocity tracker resets after a 40 ms move gap or 80 ms release gap](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/156.0.8078.4/ui/events/velocity_tracker/velocity_tracker.cc#44). The native touch emulator and all existing assertions remain in place; no sleeps or alternate gesture path are added.

## Evidence

[CI run 39468934916, E2E 8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39468934916/job/118788808491) observed 235 px total motion where the widget fling assertion required more than 260 px. Its text control passed with 225 px drag plus 55 px inertia. The failure did not retain the widget gesture's timestamps, so this change makes the input deterministic without claiming that transport timing is the proven cause of that particular failure. The same total-motion assertion subsequently failed in independent [run 39471705469](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39471705469/job/118797881052) at 235 px and [run 39472679610](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39472679610/job/118801250050) at 251 px. These observations identify a shared fixture concern; they do not establish the cause of any individual sample.

The canonical UI E2E chat test type graph, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent P0–P2 review is `scoped-clean`, including explicit review of injection and observation clock domains. The change is one test file (+20/−7), 302 → 315 lines (+13), with no production code changes. The exact widget-scroll case passed in [CI run 39474657403, E2E 7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39474657403/job/118807903541): 7.411 seconds for the case, 7.601 seconds for the file. Both text and widget gestures recorded 235 px drag plus 295 px inertia, and the upward-return and streaming assertions completed. The full CI run completed successfully for head `6184287244b1a4d366d29bf3b9d77fd961d4cd9c`; no local E2E/build battery was run.

prs.title: refactor: simplify private plugin status and lifecycle state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin-private status and lifecycle owners carry unread projections, duplicate state, and repeated checks of already-admitted inputs.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or migration. Existing commands, browser actions, authentication, audio suppression, approval evidence, and public configuration remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use existing owner facts directly: Codex's Computer Use enums and visible replies, Browser's admitted click options, AutoReview's settlement signal, Mattermost's registered commands, xAI's required credential resolver, FaceTime's live Talk driver and consult controller, and Mantis's already-admitted generated watcher inputs. Remove their unused copies and private alternate paths without adding a shared abstraction or SDK surface.

115 net production lines removed (+45/-160),20 production files; six net test/fixture lines removed (+17/-23),27 files total. This is a bundled residue under the campaign's100-line exception, not a LARGE PR.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Browser no longer revalidates private normalized ref/selector/click delay. `/act` and file-chooser ingress still validate external inputs. #173065 accepted the same normalized-private-input assumption in sibling actions; #163709 owns delay admission. Unsupported direct internal calls now get ordinary Playwright errors rather than a second admission pass. Navigation/SSRF/current-authority/cancellation checks stay.
- Mattermost deactivation deletes the authoritative account entry instead of first clearing its detached object's fields. Unsupported retained private references may retain their old fields; routing can no longer find the account. #32467 introduced this state scaffold, not a human-reported stale-reference failure. Token validation, current credentials, routing ambiguity/capacity and cleanup stay.
- xAI requires the per-connect credential resolver that its sole factory has always supplied since #106267. Unsupported direct private construction without it now fails the type contract instead of taking an unwired fallback. Public key/profile/environment and agent-scoped current credential resolution stay.
- Mantis trusts the checkpoint directory, supported scenarios, discovered browser and hydrate enum supplied by its own parent script. #85141 introduced these repeated guards as feature scaffolding, not a human incident. Manually detaching or altering the generated private script may produce ordinary filesystem/JSON/spawn errors; public options and externally configurable timeout remain validated. #117344's real stale-artifact and approval-identity protections stay.
- Mantis drops only the unread `.watcher-complete.json` aggregate; per-checkpoint atomic acknowledgements, screenshot verification and watcher exit/wait remain the actual completion facts. The aggregate has no source, test, docs or workflow reader. Raw PID metadata stays; only its unread private projection is removed.
- Other cuts remove no failure guard: unused Codex DTO messages/timing/repair copies, AutoReview's signal-identical boolean and FaceTime's write-only suppression mirror/optional holder. Actual native installation/repair/security, live suppression, consult cancellation and write settlement remain intact. The provenance inspections retained #103331/#160133/#166575's real Computer Use fixes and #119291's FaceTime privacy/consent behavior.

## Evidence

Retained unchanged-input focused proof: Codex Computer Use52 cases across4 files,5 selected command cases,64 assistant/projector cases; Browser71 cases/6files; AutoReview16; Mattermost account50/5files; xAI51; FaceTime53/3files. Targeted strict production-owner types passed for every slice. Codex's earlier test-inclusive scratch config had augmentation and unchanged session-helper errors; this is not represented as a passing test-graph check.

Mattermost slash proof retained18 passing cases and one local baseline failure: the first loopback-capacity assertion saw zero of eight initial unauthenticated requests. One serial pre-change exact-case replay failed identically. No credential effect had been reached; authorization/revocation/rotation/error-release cases passed. The failure is recorded, not fixed or called green.

Mantis existing runtime/artifact suites passed24 cases/2files (71.53s Vitest,84.01s wrapper); targeted strict production and test roots passed. All tests retain actual stale-artifact, mismatched identity/decision/acknowledgement, credential cleanup and invalid public-option oracles. No skips, timeouts, retries or baseline increases added. Independent P0-P2 reviews cover each incremental slice with final source verification. Final scoped1617-production-module cycle proof found zero runtime cycles and no new static components; focused syntax lint,26-file line-cap ratchet, format and whitespace passed. Mandatory suppression suite passed all14 cases (8.87s Vitest,13.71s wrapper).

Host-budget limits: no broad local build/full graph check or broad suite; check-changed classification only. Exact-head PR CI is the broad gate. No live browser, channel, inference or native-device claim. No real operator OpenClaw state touched. Public SDK/config/protocol/persisted shapes/dependencies and protected Phase E backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests are unchanged.

CI repair: initial head `1764f6740e9dcc50207bcc1e6984abd4316b58f2`, run39510976255/job118932281830 failed because `attempt-startup-computer-use.test.ts` still asserted the removed private `liveTest.durationMs` projection. This failure was ours, not inherited. Removed only that orphan assertion; staged clock waits, two attempts, strict error reason, no user-thread start, two unsubscribe requests and no reload/archive checks remain. All four startup cases passed locally (163.69 seconds Vitest,181.46 seconds wrapper, dominated by preparation/imports; strict case232 ms). Incremental independent P0–P2 review was scoped-clean with final source verification. Focused syntax lint,27-file line-cap ratchet,format and whitespace passed; mandatory suppression replay passed14 cases in32.41 seconds wrapper. Prior production type/cycle proof remains applicable because the repair changes no production code or imports. New-head hosted CI remains required; prior-head passing jobs are not represented as current-head proof.

## Exact-head CI attribution

Head `9a8c91b9aa538f1281655e05c7fbea2db8bd52f8`, [run39513488577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39513488577), attempt1 completed. Native inherited-failure exception selected under standing campaign land authority; failed CI is not called green.

prs.title: test(qa-lab): check replayed history against a plugin tool under a core name
prs.body:
Closes #168610
Related: #101866

## What Problem This Solves

There is no production-boundary test showing that a non-bundled plugin tool registered under a core tool name cannot get its managed media paths replayed into a later turn's history as if a trusted core tool had produced them.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. QA Lab gains a scenario that fails when a plugin borrows a core tool's media trust through replayed channel history, and a mock-provider directive that lets scenarios script exact tool calls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grounding change in #101866 decides media trust when a tool result is written and checks it when history is replayed. Its review asks for proof with an actual plugin under a core name, through the real writer, ending at the final model request. Two pieces were missing:

- The mock OpenAI provider could not be told to call a named tool with chosen arguments. `QA tool plan: {"calls":[{"name":"<tool>","args":{...}}],"reply":"..."}` in the current request now does that: each call in order, then the reply, with `{{media:N}}` replaced by the first media path the Nth call's result carried (structured media, a `MEDIA:` line, or a POSIX or drive-rooted Windows path in plain text). A call that Code Mode runs counts once its `wait` settles it: each output is read through `readScenarioToolCompletion`, and while the latest is a `waiting` receipt the server's existing Code Mode handling issues the `wait`. Calls go through the Tool Search dispatcher when the tool is not declared directly. A step the request cannot call replies `BUG-QA-TOOL-PLAN-UNDECLARED <name>`. Only results after the plan's own user turn count, and a plan quoted in history never starts.
- A channel that merges session history into the next prompt. QA Channel does not set `sessionTranscript`; Crabline Telegram runs the real Telegram plugin, which does.

`telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history` installs a run-owned, non-bundled plugin that registers `music_generate` and returns one file under the managed media store. No music provider is configured, so the core tool of that name is absent and the plugin's tool is the one that runs; the scenario checks its output text in the provider log. Turn 1 calls it and replies with its path and an unmanaged control path. Turn 2 reads the conversation context in the provider request and requires the plugin path to be replaced by `[unverified media reference removed]` while the control path stays as written.

The directive joins the existing scripted-turn chain beside the cron planners, so `server.ts` does not grow under the line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

<!-- remediation-2026-10-20:start -->
### October 20 integration

Pushed `ce1095ab83725303f10c0497a7bbe8a5a7da9705`, merging `main` `f629720edbb9f4b458adae30c7506c1dc5d1adc6` into the existing branch without conflicts. The four PR files and the surrounding tool-routing, input, cron-planner, test-harness and QA Vitest-config blobs are unchanged from `c18878a22b6565fa2265413b8157ffb0939ac6b0`. The lockfile changed with main. [Upstream repair `b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87) restores the missing `createDeferredCore` import in `src/gateway/local-http-probe.test.ts` and is included here.

Fresh local validation used Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.12.1 and a frozen dependency install on Linux, with four-CPU affinity and one test worker. All runs used tree `59bcba6c9fe25b9a62a01608de7667ad54538145`, the published commit's tree:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-qa.config.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.tool-routing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **25 passed**, 49.12 s wall. Both cron send/continue regressions pass.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/mock-openai-tool-plan.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.tool-routing.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts`: exit 0, no warnings or errors, 122.72 s including official SDK declaration preparation.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/qa-lab/tsconfig.json`: exit 0, 1.50 s after that preparation. The first attempt exited 2 before preparation because `openclaw/plugin-sdk` declarations were absent; its complete failure log is retained. The same command passed after the repository wrapper emitted the declarations.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/mock-openai-tool-plan.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.tool-routing.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts qa/scenarios/channels/telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history.yaml --threads=1`: exit 0 using the documented local `oxfmt` mode. `git diff --check` passed. Tracked raw blobs, modes, symlinks and index matched before and after validation; no nonignored untracked source or listed surviving test process remained.

The complete four-file source review finished through P2 with no findings. That review inspected source; it did not execute the tests. The two intended failures from removing `planCronSendContinueTurn` below are historical results on `c18878a2`, not a new mutation run on this integration. The affected blobs remain identical, but the lockfile changed.

[Current CI 39501568612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39501568612) finished with **102 jobs: 71 success, 27 skipped, 4 failures**. Three runtime jobs failed; the fourth failure is the [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39501568612/job/118940123024) propagating them. The actual tested merge is `7141f747882188d281af7cb5eba8ec5863d5a230`, tree `27c1d89572a6edd304d6b6039d10416b00050952`, with parents `2f7572ad13d12d5d34d21adecf5198cbb0fbb39d` and this head `ce1095ab83725303f10c0497a7bbe8a5a7da9705`. This is a different base from the local integration above. Full logs show successful preceding builds and these failures:

- [changed-9, job 118912696602](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39501568612/job/118912696602): MCP app-grant revalidation fails with `McpAppViewExpiredError` / `UNAVAILABLE`.
- [changed-17, job 118912696389](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39501568612/job/118912696389): five chat ownership permutations return empty placement rows; four other chat cases pass.
- [changed-20, job 118912696735](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39501568612/job/118912696735): OTel Gateway startup times out at 120,040 ms with zero spans.

Completed six isolated controls against that exact base and CI merge, with measured Node `24.19.0`, pnpm `12.12.1` and Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de` (full commit `ef37c31de3d3c5c59243bba51d420f9efda9d689`). Each cell had its own frozen install, `pnpm build qaRuntime`, private state/cache/output directories and the original ordered shard targets. Used two-CPU affinity, observed requested concurrency 2 / admitted 1, and inner parallelism 1. The original test deadlines and assertions were unchanged.

| Shard | Exact base | Actual CI merge | Complete result in each arm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| changed-9 | exit 1, 196.086 s | exit 1, 188.182 s | Cron opt-in skipped; MCP fails; canonical 2 planned / 2 completed / 2 invoked / 1 failed |
| changed-17 | exit 1, 245.129 s | exit 1, 241.045 s | Five ownership failures, five passes, one opt-in skip; canonical 3 / 3 / 3 / 1 failed |
| changed-20 | exit 0, 192.949 s | exit 0, 192.699 s | OTel passes in 113,684 / 114,750 ms; OpenShell opt-in skipped; canonical 2 / 2 / 2 / 0 failed |

The MCP case/error and the five chat case names/empty-row assertions occur on the exact base as well as the merge under this recipe. That shows these signatures do not require the PR delta in this environment. The hosted MCP log does not establish the failing RPC: its stack reports `176:18`, while both replays report `206:25`. Bun stack locations do not map directly to raw source; the chat logs report `461:81`, while the raw placement query/assertion is at lines 547-553. I am not treating those line numbers as evidence of identical execution stages. Both current OTel controls passed, so the hosted startup timeout was not reproduced. These controls do not establish the original hosted cause or a fix.

Reproduction uses `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` from each exact checkout with `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1`, `OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY=bun-all`, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, requested workers 2, and the original targets under `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/`:

- changed-9: `gateway-cron-idle-timeout-finalization.product-proof.e2e.test.ts`, then `gateway-mcp-app-grant-revalidation.e2e.test.ts`.
- changed-17: `gateway-rpc-chat.e2e.test.ts`, then `gateway-timeout-recovery-subagent.e2e.test.ts`, then `heartbeat-mcp-runtime-retire.product-proof.e2e.test.ts`.
- changed-20: `openshell-agent-workspace.e2e.test.ts`, then `otel-gateway-runtime.e2e.test.ts`.

The complete specifications, environment and procedure are retained in package SHA-256 `8d663d8dc69d33692f281d7d427f144bae66b04239163e933131c0fe93db2256`; terminal 24-phase record SHA-256 `466b13d919374f2add92160e826a9d06f10f1a312430468d26146f3e5a7bd6b3`. Independent receipt inspection verified all 324 transferred payloads, exact tracked source/index/modes before and after all 24 cell phases, toolchain boundary hashes including the selected pnpm payload, and all six complete canonical results. Final readback matched all 61 frozen files and found none of the 1,831 captured process identities still present. No outer timeout or supervisor signal occurred in these six cells. This is captured-process evidence, not a whole-host census, and boundary hashes do not prove continuous immutability.

The builder has approximately 66.1 GB RAM versus the hosted worker's approximately 8.2 GB, a different CPU model/load, and no access to protected compile-cache seed `39483410762`. Cells began with fresh private artifacts; prerequisite targets could generate outputs within their own cell. No cross-cell warming or cross-arm artifact equivalence is claimed. These controls leave the hosted CI failure in place.

The older [CI 39320419061](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320419061) is terminal: **102 jobs, 70 success, 27 skipped, 5 failures**. The missing-import static failures have the included upstream repair. Its separate controls used base `0548086d6a95525d7bad7f1905d2ae8c8d2de3ef`, actual merge `d8ed4d1eb1f7637c879b1b7b10444d86f0bf81a8` and older Bun `7bd4fdff3`: MCP failed on both at `board.widget.put`; warmed OTel passed on both. Fresh-build OTel failed on base during startup with zero spans and passed on merge. That differs from the original hosted send-phase timeout with 31 spans. Observed load, preparation time and artifact history differ; those results do not establish the original cause. All 14 historical phases passed independent receipt consistency checks. Historical pnpm version/launcher/JS-entry identities were retained, but the selected native payload hash was not; the newer controls above retain it.

[The hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168611#issuecomment-6101756069), updated October 20 at 21:46:37 UTC, covers `ce1095ab83725303f10c0497a7bbe8a5a7da9705` with zero findings and no target execution. [#101866](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101866) remains open and unmerged at `0ff83d79b6c1a40e5d75fd31a2a3797a1fc91327`; the October 21 00:01 UTC discussion readback found no new maintainer acceptance. Land that runtime grounding repair first, or obtain an explicit maintainer decision accepting this selectable scenario's known failure until it lands. The historical M4 Crabline runs below remain contributor evidence; I have not rerun that scenario on this head.
<!-- remediation-2026-10-20:end -->

### October 19 evidence, retained as history

<!-- remediation-2026-10-19:start -->
Refreshed on 2026-10-19 at `c18878a22b6565fa2265413b8157ffb0939ac6b0`, merging `main` `2cd23b665868c75bfb02537cef9eb9f2b329667a` into the existing branch. The one conflict was mock-provider dispatch. Cron failure repair, send-then-continue, and blocked-outcome handling still run before a generic QA tool plan.

Local proof on Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.12.1, Vitest 5.0.3:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.tool-routing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 25 passed, 109.85 s wall (mostly worker compilation; the earlier positive run was 145.15 s wall). The new send/continue cases exercise both `write` and `exec_command` through the mock HTTP server, with an overlapping generic tool plan.
- Removing only `planCronSendContinueTurn` from the chain makes both new cases fail at the expected message call: 2 failed, 23 skipped, 84.18 s wall. The route was restored; neither mutation is committed.
- Both edited files pass the repository formatter and `git diff --check`. Targeted type-aware lint reached its 120 s local deadline while preparing mandatory plugin-SDK declarations, before lint diagnostics (bounded runner exit 124, 125.33 s wall). I did not skip that preparation; the normal PR CI lint/build gate remains required.
- The independent source review completed through P2 with no findings on all four changed files. It inspected source and did not independently execute the tests. Its reviewed tree `a7584e24932147a4931d74e043fe4d5e78a5313e` is this commit's tree.

The failed [CI run 39010031941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39010031941) tested merge `e6bf187f074d479c4de60cb3c5af22db6940dd2a`, not this head: 72 successful jobs, 27 skipped, 2 failures including the aggregate. Its two `Symbol.dispose` errors reproduce in a scoped compiler control using the actual store type and fixture declarations from both that merge and exact base `489323a0f01fb3530eb05a43986880f4914650a1`. [Upstream fix 7b727f04d23f76d0aefcb4c1c5a0f5b071d8e7af](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7b727f04d23f76d0aefcb4c1c5a0f5b071d8e7af), now included, passes that same control. The full config-cli typecheck on the old base timed out after 127 s; that run is not a passing result. The CI classification had called this new; the equal source blobs and scoped reproduction provide the narrower base attribution.

[New-head CI 39320419061](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320419061) tested merge `d8ed4d1eb1f7637c879b1b7b10444d86f0bf81a8` into exact base `0548086d6a95525d7bad7f1905d2ae8c8d2de3ef`. At the latest check it is incomplete, with two failed test jobs:

- [Job 118293491476](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320419061/job/118293491476): `otel-gateway-runtime.e2e.test.ts` reaches its 120 s deadline in phase `send OTEL-GATEWAY-SUCCESS-OK`, with 31 captured spans and no pending cleanup owners.
- [Job 118293491330](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320419061/job/118293491330): `gateway-mcp-app-grant-revalidation.e2e.test.ts:206` fails on `board.widget.put` with `McpAppViewExpiredError`.

Both fixtures, Gateway setup/artifact/readiness owners and lockfile are identical on that base and CI merge. The mock provider differs as expected. Source parity does not establish a runtime base failure: I have not reproduced either case on the exact base with the pinned Linux Bun build and Gateway artifacts. [The existing base CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320267109) is incomplete and has not supplied a matching runtime control. [The fresh hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168611#issuecomment-6101756069) completed on this head with no findings; its assessment used source inspection and the attributed contributor proof. #101866 is still open at `0ff83d79b6c1a40e5d75fd31a2a3797a1fc91327`; land it first, or have a maintainer explicitly accept the scenario's expected failure without it. I have not rerun the Crabline scenario on this candidate. The earlier M4 runs below are historical evidence, not new runs for this update.
<!-- remediation-2026-10-19:end -->

On an M4 Pro, `pnpm openclaw qa suite --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history --concurrency 1`:

- On `main` `7b125134f386` it fails at the history check, as it should without replay grounding:

  ```
  second-turn history kept the plugin's core-named path /private/tmp/openclaw/<run>/state/media/generated/qa-core-named-46ce4ffd.mp3 as written
  #session:<id> ... OpenClaw: QA-CORE-NAMED-46ce4ffd plugin /private/tmp/openclaw/<run>/state/media/generated/qa-core-named-46ce4ffd.mp3 unmanaged /tmp/qa-core-named-46ce4ffd-unmanaged.txt
  ```

- With that PR's head `ef8a251fe9a` merged in, it passes:

  ```
  #session:<id> ... OpenClaw: QA-CORE-NAMED-b38c88e3 plugin [unverified media reference removed]/generated/qa-core-named-b38c88e3.mp3 unmanaged /tmp/qa-core-named-b38c88e3-unmanaged.txt
  ```

Re-run on 2026-10-10 against `main` `0aa79d6d1065`, with this branch merged in cleanly: the scenario fails the same way without that PR (`second-turn history kept the plugin's core-named path ... as written`) and passes with it merged (78 s for the whole `qa suite` command).

Merged main `6485b1906e7` on 2026-10-17 (clean, no conflicts). On the merged tree, on an M4 Pro:
- `server.tool-routing.test.ts`'s four new cases pass.
- The mock OpenAI provider tests and the scenario catalog tests pass: 30 files, 303 tests.
- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` pass. A planted type error gives rc=2.
- oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.
- In `check:changed`, every lane but two passes. The two red lanes are the max-lines suppression ratchet (three `ui/src/pages/...` files) and the dead export scan (unrelated `src/` and `extensions/tavily` exports), and both fail the same way on that main alone.

I did not re-run the scenario on this merge. On this machine the Crabline transport refuses to start from a checkout under a group-writable volume ("Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal"). #101866 is still open, so the scenario is expected to fail at the history check until that PR lands, as above.

No live channel, credentials or Convex lease are used.

Cost: the scenario takes 24 to 29 s inside the suite (gateway boot, one restart to load the plugin, two turns); the whole `qa suite` command is about 70 s wall with a warm build. It is crabline-only and its primary coverage ID, `plugins.plugin-tools`, is not in the `smoke-ci` profile, so it runs only when selected; nothing per-PR picks it up. Adding it to `smoke-ci` would put it on hourly `main` and Full Release Validation, which I'd leave to maintainers. `server.tool-routing.test.ts` with the four new cases: 24 tests, 20 s and 7 s wall on two runs with `--maxWorkers=1` (Vitest 17.6 s and 4.6 s, mostly transform); the four take 1 to 3 ms each. The two added for review (a Windows path in a plain-text result, a Code Mode step that reports `waiting` first) fail against `eb769e1d47c`'s `mock-openai-tool-plan.ts`. The scenario's expected suffix uses `path.sep`; on macOS and Linux it is the same string, and I have not run the scenario on Windows.

Gates against `main` `7b125134f386`: oxfmt, oxlint, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, the scenario catalog tests, and the line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race and mock-export ratchets pass. The max-lines step fails on the env-var budget (456 `OPENCLAW_*` names against 455), which fails the same way on `main`; it stops `check:changed`, so the ratchets after it ran one by one and the remaining `check:changed` steps did not run.

Not covered: a trusted core tool whose managed path survives. QA Lab has no synchronous core tool that returns a managed file: `image_generate` runs in the background in session chats and delivers its result in a later turn, and `view_image` marks its media `outbound: false`. The control is an unmanaged path, so a replay that redacted every managed path would also pass here; the trusted-path half stays with that PR's own in-process tests.

prs.title: improve(ios): reduce resource diagnostic process polling
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iOS resource collector repeatedly scans processes even after a scan times out on a busy screenshot runner.

## User Impact

No app behavior changes. Qualification, screenshots, and release diagnostics retain host metrics while doing fewer process scans. Process detail becomes sparser and stops after the first process-probe timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep host sampling at approximately 15 seconds, but run process scans at most once a minute and disable them for the rest of the run after a timeout. Record intentional skips explicitly and retain the CPU baseline across cadence skips; failed probes still reset it. The first stalled probe can still delay host samples until it returns. Workload exit, cancellation, privacy filtering, and output limits are unchanged.

## Evidence

- [Completed screenshot run 39513251899](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39513251899) recorded eight process-probe timeouts, with the slowest taking 99.066 seconds. Probe wall time is asynchronous waiting, not measured extra release duration.
- The actual CLI regression fixture failed before the change because it kept scanning every 15 seconds and after timeouts. It now verifies six scans across 24 host samples, preserved CPU attribution across skips, baseline reset after an unavailable probe, continued host metrics after timeout, and sanitized output.
- All eight focused workload-boundary tests pass (258 ms test time; 1.70 seconds including the repository wrapper). Targeted lint, typecheck, syntax, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent P2 review completed without actionable findings.
- [Hosted PR screenshot job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516519905/job/118950417279) passed iPhone, iPad, and Watch capture. Its [resource diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516519905/artifacts/12309965965) recorded 52 host samples: four successful process probes roughly 60 seconds apart, 12 cadence skips, one real process timeout (89.007 seconds), then 35 host samples with process polling disabled. Host memory observations continued throughout those 35 samples. Wrapped screenshot duration was 890.615 seconds; this is not an A/B speedup claim. No build was uploaded.

CI attribution: [check-lint-core-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39516519905/job/118950855796) reports `typescript(unbound-method)` in `src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts:73` (`const repair = check.repair`). That line is inherited from main commit `c6f14b27a93` (#178767); the file, lint configuration, dependencies, and lockfile are unchanged by this PR. The automatic classifier calls it new because its older comparison main job passed and it does not compare scope; source attribution establishes that it is unrelated to this branch.
