prs.title: fix: Claude CLI turns stall 15 minutes and end as "CLI run aborted" when stream output hits the limit
prs.body:
Related: #143396, #150132, #153545, #159930, #119445

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Claude CLI (`claude-cli`) turn that exceeds the stream-json output limit keeps running blind for about 15 minutes. Stuck-session recovery then aborts it with `CLI run aborted`, and the output-limit error is never reported.

## User Impact

User impact: when a turn exceeds the output limit, it now fails straight away with the error that says so (for example `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output.`). There is no 15-minute silent stall, and the CLI no longer keeps editing files and running commands that OpenClaw can no longer see. The Claude session binding is kept, so the next turn resumes the same Claude session. As after a stuck-session abort today, the interrupted tool call is left unanswered in the Claude transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the stream-json parser hits a limit (8 MiB of output per turn, 8 MiB per line, or 20,000 lines), it records the error and then silently drops everything after it. The CLI itself keeps running:

- stdout is still drained, hashed and captured;
- no more tool starts, tool results or text reach OpenClaw;
- the record that tripped the limit is usually a tool result, so that tool stays active forever in diagnostics;
- while a tool is active, raw stdout does not count as progress, so after the 15-minute blocked-tool floor (`BLOCKED_TOOL_CALL_ABORT_FLOOR_MS`) stuck-session recovery aborts the run.

The turn was already lost when the parser tripped, because `executeCliProcess` always throws that error as a `format` failover once the CLI ends. The CLI either finishes blind and the turn fails then, or, more often in long turns, recovery aborts it first. In that case the only error is `CLI run aborted` and the limit is never logged. The #143396 thread now includes a trace showing this pattern with background subagent traffic.

This change stops the CLI at the first parser refusal and throws the parser's own error right away:

- **Supervised child process:** the managed run is cancelled with `manual-cancel`. The run falls through to the existing parser-error `format` failover because it was not caller-aborted. A refusal that arrives before `spawn` resolves is handled once the run handle exists.
- **Plugin-owned transport** (the Anthropic claude-cli path): the stream loop throws the same `format` failover. The loop's existing `finally` aborts the plugin turn and closes the iterator.
- **Error path:** the error is the same one `executeCliProcess` already threw after a blind finish, so failover classification and session handling are unchanged. A `format` failover does not clear the CLI session binding.

The same path serves every `output: jsonl` CLI backend, not only Claude. The parser limits apply to all of them, and the turn was already doomed there too.

**Trade-off:** any work the CLI would have finished blind after the limit is not done. That work was already invisible to OpenClaw, and the turn was already going to fail. Stopping early means the user sees the real cause in seconds rather than an unrelated "aborted" 15 minutes later, and unseen file edits stop accumulating. The alternative, letting the CLI finish and then failing, still leaves the 15-minute window in which recovery aborts the run under the wrong error, which is the observed failure.

**Scope:**

- **Not covered:** the paired-node transport (`executeNodeClaudeRun`) is left unchanged.
- **The limits themselves:** unchanged, and no setting is added (#111382). #153545 (partial-delta accounting) and #159930 (stops charging Edit/Write file echoes) reduce how often the limit trips. This PR changes what happens when it does.
- **Overlap:** this PR touches only `execute-process.ts` and adds a test file. There is no file overlap with #153545. #157498 edits the lines next to the `executePluginOwnedProcess` call, so whichever lands second may need a trivial rebase.
- **#143396:** marked Related, not Fixes. A turn that hits the limit still fails; it now fails fast and names the cause, and the progress-marker freeze reported in #143396 no longer turns into a 15-minute stall for this trigger. The issue also covers other triggers, and background subagent records counting toward the parent budget is a separate question.

## Evidence

**Production failure.** OpenClaw 2026.9.5, claude-cli, Opus, WSL2. This was an overnight cron driver turn on Sep 27, 2026 (local time):

- The turn made seven edits to a 599 KB test file. Each edit's tool result echoes the whole file, and `--include-partial-messages` deltas were also charged.
- Its last visible activity was at 6:42:21 AM. Nothing reached OpenClaw after that, while the CLI kept working.
- At 6:57:48 AM (15 min 27 s later), `stuck session recovery … action=abort_embedded_run` ended the turn as `agent run aborted | OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT` / `CLI run aborted`, after 147.8 minutes of work.
- No `CLI JSONL output exceeded` line was logged.

An earlier run on Sep 26 (45.8 min, three edits each to 831 KB and 761 KB files) failed the same way.

**Real run on this branch.** Claude Code 2.1.281, `claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5`, WSL2. The run used this branch alone, without #159930. It was built from the checkout and run as embedded `openclaw agent --local` turns with a scratch state dir and workspace, all on one session key:

1. A small turn read two lines of a 1.47 MB file. This established the Claude session binding.
2. The next turn resumed that session (`useResume=true`). It asked for ten one-line Edits to the file, one tool call per message. Each Edit result echoes the whole file, so the sixth result takes the turn past 8 MiB. The sixth result was written 12.9 s into the turn:
   - The turn ended at 14.7 s with `FailoverError` (`reason=format`): `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output.`
   - The Claude process had exited about 1 s after the crossing record, sampled every 250 ms.
   - Edits 7–10 were never applied, and no CLI process was left running.
3. The next turn used the same session key. Its prompt said only that the previous turn had been cut off and asked it to pick the task up:
   - It resumed the same Claude session (`useResume=true`, same resume fingerprint). Claude Code filled the interrupted turn with its own `No response requested.` placeholder.
   - The model worked out the remaining task from its own history, applied edits 7–10, and ended normally in 13.8 s.

The same first two turns were also run with a build of the base commit (73880b0bef):

- The sixth result crossed the budget in the same way.
- The CLI kept running for another 6.9 s and applied edits 7–10, which OpenClaw never saw.
- The turn failed only when the CLI finished by itself, at 20.3 s.

In a long turn, that blind stretch is what runs into the 15-minute stuck-session abort described above.

**Tests.** New file `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.output-limit.test.ts`:

- Supervised CLI: an 8 MiB + 1 line arriving before `spawn` resolves, and after it, cancels the managed run with `manual-cancel` and rejects with `FailoverError { reason: "format", message: "CLI JSONL line exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output." }`.
- Plugin-owned CLI: a transport that keeps emitting 1 MiB records and never ends its turn by itself rejects with `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output.` right after the record that crosses the budget. The plugin turn is aborted and its iterator closed.
- On `main`, the two supervised cases hang until the 120 s test timeout (the blind stall). The plugin case fails after the no-output watchdog fires (about 59 s), and it shows the transport was pulled for all 12 records instead of stopping at the one that crossed the budget. With the fix all three pass: 3/3, about 280 ms of test time.

Commands run:

- `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/execute.output-limit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, with `claude` removed from `PATH`: 3/3 pass in 28 s wall time locally (23.8 s Vitest, 90% of it module transform). The tests themselves take about 0.3 s, so CI cost should be a few seconds in a new file. The test resolves no host executable and uses no polling.
- Adjacent suites still pass, also with `claude` removed from `PATH`: 327 tests across `src/agents/cli-output-*`, `execute.supervisor-capture`, `execute.pending-cancellation`, `execute-plugin` and this file, plus 94 in `cli-runner.reliability`.
- The `check-changed.mjs` steps for the core and core-test lanes passed when run individually: format, the line-cap, max-lines and assertion ratchets, oxlint on the changed files, the tsgo core boundary, `tsgo:core`, the changed core-test typecheck shards (`--changed-paths-json`), and the repo guards.
- The knip dead-export scan was skipped locally because it is too slow on this machine. This change adds no exports.

prs.title: feat: support actions on imported pull requests
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves A conversation can prepare a contributor's existing PR without publishing anything, but its next metadata, readiness, review-request or evidence action still requires a completed shared publication receipt. That leaves the original PR unusable through these actions until another source publication exists, even though the workspace already records which PR the contributor is continuing. This PR stacks on #178233 and adds action support for that existing association. The diff is limited to the action path and its directly required protocol, documentation and tests. ## User Impact Guests can edit their own original PR's title or body, mark its draft ready, request the fixed ClawSweeper re-review, and upload inspected workspace evidence before pushing more source. These actions preserve workspace files and Git history. An older publication from the conversation cannot redirect them to a different PR. Full-write operators retain their existing inspection, closing and merging actions, including an authorized publishing child. An administrator joining a guest conversation does not elevate later guest turns. Current linked-author, repository-access, target and authority checks remain in force. ## Why This Change Was Made The action handler now selects the workspace's bound original PR before consulting publication receipts. Imported actions return a `pullRequest` descriptor and the currently observed remote head; they do not fabricate a `published` result or request ID. Their writes require `expectedHeadCommit`. Actions backed by a real publication receipt continue to require that receipt's `requestId` and head preconditions. The existing requester, own-PR inspection, write-preflight and GitHub transport owners supply authority and effects. The target check preserves immutable repository IDs and branch identity while allowing inspection to observe legitimate newer commits. File-import completion remains separate from these non-source operations. Metadata preconditions use the PR observation already read during eligibility checks, so a human title/body change seen there is preserved before PATCH without another API request. Fixed review text, evidence-byte checks and uncertain-write handling retain their existing behavior. The final GitHub read/PATCH race remains non-atomic. ## Evidence The registered tool/Gateway reproduction failed on the prerequisite at the deliberate imported-action refusal. The corrected path passed the required tests through real session, requester and action owners with synthetic GitHub I/O. Coverage includes no prior publication, older-receipt precedence, pending source preparation, newer remote heads, changed author/access/authority, guest/admin separation, metadata/readiness/re-review and imported evidence uploads. On the integration with the checked preparation parent, changed-file formatting and lint, the line-cap check, protocol generation and Swift/Kotlin contracts, and all seven selected production/test compiler groups passed. Seven related files passed 140 cases: the five Gateway files passed 106 cases in 127.38 seconds, the protocol file passed 17 cases in 2.34 seconds, and the tool file passed 17 cases in 9.68 seconds. The complete test batch took 141.01 seconds. The two metadata counterexamples first reproduced an overwrite on the previous implementation, then passed with zero PATCH calls after the correction. These are focused checks; current-head hosted CI supplies the broad checks. Independent engineering review found no remaining actionable issues on this integration. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39486731974) completed successfully with 63 selected jobs; its 8,903-second workflow wall time includes queueing. One earlier ClawSweeper dispatch was canceled by its concurrency policy; a later dispatch on the same head succeeded. Dispatch success is not a completed review. Retained integration builds exercised Guest metadata read/edit/readback, draft-to-ready, the fixed re-review request, and one evidence upload on the original bound PR without source publication. The readiness case changed only the draft flag. Re-review posted exactly one fixed command and explicitly left review acceptance and completion unconfirmed. Captured PR identity, source head, metadata outside the requested edit, workspace and session state were preserved. These are supporting integration results, not an exact deployment of this PR head. The metadata title matched exactly; the model omitted one requested final newline from the body, and GitHub received the exact tool argument. That literal requested-body assertion did not pass. The upload returned the inspected PNG's hash and size with access explicitly unverified. A separate body edit then associated that same asset, exactly preserving the requested bytes and existing body prefix, without another upload. The intended reviewer account, with current private-repository access, downloaded matching PNG bytes through its existing authenticated GitHub route. Anonymous access still returned 404. This proves access for that tested account, which is also the shared publisher; it does not establish another account's access or browser rendering. The earlier action recorders stopped on strict tool allowlists after extra read-only workspace checks. Native run and GitHub results were reconciled without repeating those actions, and the original recorder failures remain recorded. The distinct association recorder completed successfully with only the exact previously inspected read-only command admitted. The remaining live authority and administrator cases, their proof, and current-head ClawSweeper review are pending. The existing cases do not establish those remaining outcomes. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Original PR card showing draft before the Guest request](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65da3bd8-fea3-4516-becb-1bf2cd2333c3) | ![The same original PR card ready for review after the Guest action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d737a98-5d20-4abe-97d7-a65ddfc00a64) | ### Continuous request and ready result on integration 45f7aa4 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c95047f-a7d3-4bed-b648-0f4393754efd ### Visual verification - Baseline: Integration build 45f7aa4 before the readiness request, with the original PR still draft\. - Exact head: `45f7aa4da479adb8cec5910bf49f59d6f8e93898` - Scenario: A Guest asks to mark the original imported draft PR ready\. The action changes draft state while retaining source and metadata\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.4, commit 45f7aa4, tree aa8132e; original 1280 x 720 dark UI\. This retained integration is not a deployment of PR head 71145c0\. - Action: One natural Guest send and one ready mutation using the observed head, without a publication requestId\. - Observed result: Original PR changed from draft to open; captured source and metadata were unchanged\. - Recorder limitation: The strict allowlist stopped after extra read\-only checks, before its final dedicated assertion\. Native and GitHub results were reconciled without replay\. - The continuous recording uses the original source frames without replay, splicing, retiming or added holds\. - All 972 output frames were inspected; matched stills and key input/result frames were also checked\. - The inspected hashes match these media files, with private context masked\. - Native and GitHub observations confirm the requested state change and preservation of captured source/session state\.

prs.title: test(e2e): tolerate Kitchen Sink 0.4.1 registrar probe diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: release/2026.10.6 equivalent fix (ab50ab03e09)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the `plugins--kitchen-sink-plugin` Docker E2E lane fails with `unexpected kitchen-sink diagnostic error: ...` when it installs `npm:@openclaw/kitchen-sink@latest`, now 0.4.1 (published 2026-10-20 ~18:57Z).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The Kitchen Sink plugin E2E lane on `main` accepts the 0.4.1 probe diagnostics again, and any other unexpected diagnostic still fails the lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

Kitchen Sink 0.4.1 adds generic no-op probes for `registerAgentExecutorController`, `registerGatewayAccessPolicy`, `registerDecisionProvider`, and `registerStorageProvider`. Their payloads are intentionally incomplete, and the package's own `KITCHEN_SINK_EXPECTED_DIAGNOSTICS` lists the resulting errors as expected. `assertExpectedDiagnostics` treated them as unexpected.

This change allows the exact messages `main`'s registry emits for those payloads. They are optional, not required, because older published packages do not emit them:

- `Gateway access policy requires an authorize handler` (`src/plugins/registry-registrars-operations.ts`)
- `invalid versioned decision provider contract` (`src/plugins/registry-registrars.ts`; release/2026.10.6 says `invalid version 1 decision provider contract`)
- `storage provider registration missing label` (`src/plugins/storage-provider-registry.ts`)

`registerAgentExecutorController` was retired from the plugin API in e604de4c242, so on `main` that probe hits a missing method. The package's own `safeRegister` catches the TypeError and logs a warning, which adds no registry error diagnostic. The release-branch message `agent executor controller requires an absolute workspaceDirectory` therefore stays out of `main`'s allowlist.

## Evidence

- Inspected the published `@openclaw/kitchen-sink@0.4.1` tarball (`npm pack --ignore-scripts`, read only and never executed): all four probes call the registrar with the generic `payloadFor()` object (id/name/description/handler-style fields, no `authorize`, `contractVersion`, `evaluate`, `label`, `open`, or `workspaceDirectory`).
- Ran a throwaway local check (not committed) that fed a synthetic copy of that payload shape to `main`'s `createTestPluginRegistry().createApi(..., { registrationMode: "full" })`. `registerAgentExecutorController` is undefined, and the registry recorded exactly the three error diagnostics listed above.

prs.title: fix(sessions): let a coordinator steer its running Claude CLI child
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178822 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a coordinator cannot add guidance to its own running child when the child runs on the Claude CLI runtime; `sessions_send` with `mode: "steer"` returns `Active run has a different requester; use mode: "followup".` and the child finishes without the guidance. ## User Impact User impact: "Guide your running child" (`docs/concepts/session-tool.md`) now works for Claude CLI children, not only for embedded/native runtimes. Requests from another human, with an incompatible tool policy, or from a revoked source are still refused. This affects every agent team whose child agents run on `claude-cli` (default when an agent uses a Claude CLI subscription). The only workaround today is to wait for the child to finish and send a follow-up turn. ## Why This Change Was Made Guarded steering (`requesterToolAuthority`) reads the requester principal and the requester policy projection only from the attempt authority on the controller attachment. Native attempts register that authority; CLI runs never do. Session lanes hand the turn to the CLI through a placeholder native owner (`deferred-lifecycle-owner.ts` `handoffToCli`) that has a handle but no tool authority, and the CLI backend then attaches to the same operation. So `acceptsRequesterOrigin` was `undefined` and the request was rejected as `requester_origin_mismatch` before any principal comparison; the requester fingerprint projection was missing as well. When the receiving backend is the CLI and no attempt authority is registered, guarded injection now uses the reply operation's admitted authority, the same owner that human overlay steering into CLI turns already uses: - acceptance: the operation's requester principal (bound by CLI preparation from the admitted run, `captureCliRunToolAuthority`) must equal the incoming requester principal; a missing principal still refuses; - policy: the operation's requester projection must reproduce the active fingerprint (`tool_authority_mismatch` otherwise); it also re-checks the admitted operator source, so a revoked source refuses. Native attempts keep their attempt authority unchanged. No own-child shortcut: the parent/child relationship plays no role in the decision.
Simplification pass (pr-simplify) - Defect: CLI-backed turns carry no attempt tool authority, so requester-guarded steering rejected before comparing principals. Invariant: guarded steering joins a running turn only for the same requester principal and a policy projection equal to the turn's fingerprint, decided by the owner that admitted the turn. Fix: for CLI backends without attempt authority, read both from the reply operation. - No new module, state, export or adapter. Production delta against the merge base: +18/−4 in `session-controller.message-injection.ts`. Test delta: +163 in the existing Claude steering suite. - Superseded during this change (not in the diff): a first revision keyed the fallback on backend-only attachments; the live run showed the real CLI path also registers the `handoffToCli` placeholder handle, so the discriminator is now the receiving backend kind. The regression test drives that placeholder. - Test group: one test, four cases, each with a distinct failure: same requester accepted and delivered to Claude stdin (the defect), other human refused, incompatible requester policy refused, revoked operator source refused.
## Evidence **Regression test** (`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.steering.test.ts`, "steers a spawned Claude child for its requester and refuses other sources"): real Claude CLI transport and fixture process via `executePluginOwnedProcess`, child admitted with an operator source like `sessions_spawn`, direct turn bound by the real `captureCliRunToolAuthority`, real `handoffToCli` placeholder, and the steering request built like `sessions_send` delivery. | Run | Result | |---|---| | base `f6ed6616297` | ❌ red: `{ status: "rejected", reason: "requester_origin_mismatch" }` for the same requester | | fix | ✅ green (2/2 in the file, 60 s wall time with `--maxWorkers=1`) | | fix reverted (counter-check) | ❌ red again | Related suites with the fix, all green (22 files, 555 tests, 275 s wall time with `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`): `session-controller.steer`, `session-controller.native`, `session-controller-model`, `harness/tool-authority.runtime{,.admission,.participants}`, `openclaw-tools.sessions-steering`, `openclaw-tools.sessions-send-child-coordination`, `openclaw-tools.sessions`, `cli-runner/execute-plugin{,.policy,.steering}`, `cli-runner/prepare`, `message-injection-order`, `followup-turn-execution.steering`, `reply-run-registry{,.visibility,.control-owner}`, `chat-send-message-injection`, `chat-send-profile-steering`, `agent-session-steering-authority`, `sessions-send-policy`. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware`, the test mock-export ratchet and a narrow `tsgo` check of the changed files pass. **Live, isolated Gateway** (loopback, fresh state per run, agent `main` on `claude-cli`, Claude Code native login). The coordinator turn is sent from the real Control UI (owner profile): spawn a child that runs `sleep 45`, wait 15 s, then `sessions_send` with `mode: "steer"` and the text "append STEUER-99". | Build | `sessions_send` result | Controller log | Child answer | |---|---|---|---| | base `f6ed6616297` | `status: "error"`, `Active run has a different requester; use mode: "followup".` | 23:08:03.306Z `injection-outcome … reason: "declined"` | `KIND-C-FERTIG KEINE-ZUSATZ` (guidance lost) | | fix | `status: "accepted"`, `targetDisposition: "steered"` | 23:25:04.458Z accepted, 23:25:34.653Z `reason: "consumed"` | `KIND-C-FERTIG Zusatzanweisung: Hänge an deine Antwort das Wort STEUER-99 an. STEUER-99` | | fix, coordinator turn via `gateway call chat.send` | `targetDisposition: "steered"` | 23:28:23.276Z `reason: "consumed"` | contains `STEUER-99` | Control UI, coordinator conversation on the isolated Gateway (real UI, owner profile): | Before (base `f6ed6616297`) | After (fix) | |---|---| | | | (All times UTC, 2026-10-20.) A diagnostic run on the first revision showed the actual attachment state of the spawned CLI child: `handle: true`, no attempt tool authority, operation principal and incoming principal both `["operator","gateway-owner"]`, turn kind `direct`. **Gaps:** the refusal of another human, an incompatible policy and a revoked source is proven by the regression test, not live (the isolated Gateway has a single operator profile; both live drivers resolve to the same owner). Embedded/native runtimes are unchanged and covered by the existing steering suites. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698 (open refactor of session input authority) touches the same file but keeps the attempt-only requester checks, so it does not cover this case; the two may need a small textual rebase.

prs.body:
WITHDRAWN: the newer completed scheduled-main run39508589544 has the identical pre-change root and takes55.916s. Candidate63.395s is13.38% slower. The original frozen-baseline criterion passed, but this experiment does not establish a current speed gain and will not land. All16 target cases pass; fullCI is being cancelled to avoid further compute. No auto-merge request was armed.

## What Problem This Solves

The standalone board-fixture E2E waits for network silence after navigation even where its next action already waits for the required UI state. Remove nine such call sites (ten executions, including both themes), retaining default navigation load and the existing content/actionability checks. Add visible-widget readiness before focus and composer readiness before attachment insertion or the negative community-card assertion.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The test suite retains its existing cases and assertions while reducing unnecessary setup or waiting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native-egress navigation keeps its network-idle wait: its full-board screenshot spans several widget frames, and the existing single-frame predicate does not establish readiness for all of them. No new screenshot-readiness mechanism is introduced. All 16 cases, eight mandatory screenshots, original matchers, two reloads, 19 navigations, two browser launches, three private Vite processes, and the intentional caretaker/admission delays remain.

prs.title: refactor(ui): derive model picker search presentation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completes the model picker's move from imperative search synchronization to Solid-owned presentation while preserving the existing interaction contract. Related: #178593.

## User Impact

The model picker retains its appearance, filtering, keyboard navigation, and catalog-refresh behavior. Selected model rows and account rows still consume digit positions without advertising global shortcuts, and nested menus retain keyboard ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lazy picker panel supplies its catalog to the existing search owner. JSX derives row visibility and rank, provider disclosure, shortcuts, and ARIA relationships; DOM refs remain for focus, scrolling, and activation. The old synchronization effect, DOM ordering, ID assignment, and shortcut mutation helpers are removed. Provider/account domain ownership is unchanged; the search owner holds picker presentation only.

## Evidence

The current head `7be9b0ad561903ad7cf4a8e0b8089aabce67a1d6` integrates main at `c7387f7f8bf163b89d4cee56f2fc7a43db3421be`, including the landed catalog fixture repair #178735 and touch timing repair #178645. Main's simplified overlay test helpers are preserved with one real model-picker mount for Escape/search-clear/focus/ARIA behavior. Main now independently includes the New Session import-settlement cleanup, so that file no longer differs in this PR.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Conflict-resolved overlay and New Session suites | 22/22 passed together (2.48 s Vitest); overlay 10/10 and New Session 12/12 |
| Affected UI chat test type graph | Passed after conflict resolution |
| Targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks | Passed after conflict resolution |
| Final integrated controller guard | Passed |
| Final integrated production Knip | One inherited unused export: `extensions/agentsapi/config.ts: DEFAULT_NATIVE_TOOLS`. The identical production Knip command also exits 1 with that sole finding on exact merge base `c7387f7f`; no model-search findings |
| Final independent review | Canonical independent P0–P2 review completed with no findings |
| Current full CI | [39515375257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39515375257) completed: 42 successful jobs, 24 skipped, only independently reproduced inherited Doctor lint and its aggregate gate failed; all test jobs pass |
| Recap failure diagnostics | Affected UI E2E chat type graph, targeted lint, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review pass; no further local E2E run |
| Earlier picker behavior proof | Rank, keyboard, global shortcuts, ref lifecycle, and nested native-menu ownership passed; the unfiltered close/reopen/Enter regression failed before its reset-handler repair and passes afterward |
| Focused model-controls search suite | 3/3 passed; tests moved intact from the oversized chat-view suite |
| Original build/performance and synthetic visual proof | Passed; details and reuse limits below |

The conflict-free main integration left all 13 original PR files byte-identical to the already-reviewed conflict candidate. Those focused test results are reused. The current 14-file diff adds failure-only diagnostics to the managed-media test; production source is unchanged. Two later bounded candidate/base replays prepared their required runtime/UI builds, as detailed below. No broad local suite was run.

### Earlier CI repairs and remaining attribution limits

The initial run 39467746739 exposed two stale test boundaries: the overlay fixture bypassed the Solid model-search owner, and ArrowUp/ArrowDown composition checks read DOM in the same stack as signal writes. The repair mounts the production picker and awaits committed `aria-activedescendant` in the browser while preserving synchronous event-consumption assertions. These are test changes, with unchanged production markup.

Run 39471705469 later reported duplicate `openclaw-chat-question-card` registration during successor-event suite collection. The preceding New Session fixture triggered lazy composer imports without joining them before teardown. Bounded replays passed both before and after the fixture cleanup, so the historical failure was not reproduced locally. Later run 39475801766 passed the repaired unit lanes. Main's equivalent `vi.dynamicImportSettled()` cleanup is now retained without a PR diff.

Runs 39471705469 and 39475801766 also reported a mobile widget-scroll fling assertion (`235 > 260`). The integrated, landed #178645 supplies explicit event timestamps while preserving drag and inertia assertions.

Run 39475801766 failed the Settings Refresh catalog case: expected three total provider acquisitions, observed four. Browser diagnostics showed one explicit `models.list(refresh:true)` and two overlapping provider reads; that overlap does not identify the owning runtime. Three bounded source-Gateway diagnostics did not reproduce it, but began with four acquisitions and both inventories warm, unlike the failed browser fixture's one acquisition. They are not equivalent reproductions. An exact-base Testbox attempt was stopped immediately when capacity queued; no build or test executed and no baseline verdict is claimed.

Landed #178735 explicitly publishes both configured owners before the fixture's global acquisition measurement, preserving every acquisition, UI, Refresh, Retry, and selection assertion. Its full CI run [39487705697](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39487705697) passed all 56 jobs. This establishes the test's already-published-catalog setup; it does not definitively attribute the historical extra request or claim that cold-start behavior is defect-free.

Stale model-search run [39480783871](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39480783871), on `468a8f36f3ffb7b4ec5c163f06152b0f589058e3`, was cancelled after the head conflicted with main. Partial successes are retained as history, not a passing full-CI result. The cancelled merge request is retained for supported native replacement recovery after fresh CI.

### Managed-media recap timeout

Fresh run [39509396144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39509396144), on `da46f1a16b85`, completed with 43 successful jobs. `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (1/2)` and the aggregate gate failed because the managed-media case waited 30 seconds for a visible `.chat-turn-recap` inside the assistant group. Persisted image order, canonical history adoption, and decoded live images had already passed; the failure was not an image-order mismatch. The browser diagnostics reported a connected, ready page without a renderer stall. This failure is not attributed to baseline and is not waived.

One focused replay on the candidate passed (scenario 8.538 s, file 21.370 s, Vitest 53.22 s, total 166.24 s including required runtime/UI build and setup). One replay on exact merge base `c7387f7f` also passed (scenario 8.395 s, file 26.686 s, Vitest 53.33 s, total 156.69 s). Temporary diagnostic probes were removed. Passing replays do not explain or repair the original timeout.

The current test-only follow-up preserves the original locator, timeout, assertions, and thrown error. On failure, it uses the existing diagnostic owner to record only booleans, counts, and runtime: recap presence/visibility/location, terminal-row state, and whether the terminal run matches the persisted assistant. Collection is bounded to one second and adds no success-path wait or production hook. It improves recurrence evidence; it is not claimed as a behavioral fix. Final run 39515375257 passes both real-Gateway shards and all browser test jobs.

### Inherited Doctor lint exception

The final run's only root failure is `check-lint-core-2`, job `118947105668`: `typescript(unbound-method)` at `src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.ts:73:28`, where newer main captures `const repair = check.repair`. CI tested merge `9f41398827d1af872591274be5382ff61a9a7d67`, combining main `176482f971749c12ef4cce7e64b6113791209b9b` with this exact PR head. The identical core stripe 5/5 command reproduces the same sole error on that clean tested main after frozen install. The Doctor source, check types, lint config, and stripe runner match the tested PR merge.

The automatic table labels this new relative to an older passing scheduled-main job and explicitly says selected scope was not compared. The actual tested-main reproduction establishes inheritance. The native exception covers this lint root and its downstream gate only; CI remains failed, and all tests, security, and review requirements remain enforced. Main's later receiver fix `5d80482379b` is supplemental context, not the attribution proof.

## Visual proof

Synthetic catalog, 1280 × 900, dark theme. Full viewport frames and crops were inspected and are byte-identical before/after.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open catalog | ![Model picker before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/adb0ee9d-b2ec-45b1-a4e9-06280e6ea6e5) | ![Model picker after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61241fee-79c4-43cf-a3e1-ac3895be42e8) |
| Filter across collapsed provider | ![Filtered model picker before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/372ae7de-71e2-4f6b-af64-0814c0b25838) | ![Filtered model picker after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af30fe33-cba5-47a2-9249-55074db24bdb) |

| Startup JS requests | 7 | 7 |
| Startup CSS gzip | 38,445 B | 38,445 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,447,271 B | 1,447,067 B |
| New-session boot JS gzip | 1,005,457 B | 1,005,262 B |

Measured on the same machine for the original refactor. The reused baseline build is from `59797f91`; its production UI and build inputs match the original `f20c3c758bb` merge base (intervening UI changes were test-only). The lazy panel boundary remains intact. Follow-up repairs preserve the picker production code and markup, so those inspected captures and measurements are retained. They are not fresh aggregate bundle measurements after the main integrations.

Final-run performance job [118946651144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39515375257/job/118946651144) passed with an advisory startup-size warning. It measured **325,707 B startup JS gzip, 7 JS requests, 38,445 B CSS gzip, and 1 CSS request**. Startup exceeded the printed 325,166 B limit by 541 B; its printed committed budget baseline is 324,590 B plus 512 B growth and 64 B build variance, not a measured paired startup base. Printed paired boot measurements were chat **1,447,617 → 1,447,415 B** (24 → 24 requests) and New Session **1,005,286 → 1,005,071 B** (19 → 19 requests). These current CI figures are separate from the original strict paired proof above.

## Scope and simplification

Against final merge base `c7387f7f8bf163b89d4cee56f2fc7a43db3421be`, the six changed production modules total **1,649 → 1,711 lines (+62)**. The seven changed test/shared-fixture files total **6,508 → 6,698 lines (+190)**, including three tests moved intact into a focused search suite. The typed catalog and declarative bindings replace one effect and fourteen direct attribute writes. These modules contain no `createEffect`, `untrack`, raw event listeners, or island queries; the retired synchronization helpers have no remaining callers or exports.

prs.title: fix: interactive widgets missing from public conversation links
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interactive widgets (`show_widget` visualizations) are missing from public conversation links, and the public page shows a raw `[embed ref="cv_…" … /]` line where the widget should be.

## User Impact

User impact: a signed-out reader of a publicly shared conversation now sees the same saved inline widgets the Control UI shows, read-only and sandboxed. Pinned dashboard widgets, prompts, host APIs, and Gateway access stay unavailable to public readers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public reader only published message text, images, and one-line tool summaries. A widget created inside code mode is persisted as a nested tool record, which the reader filtered as private tool activity, and the assistant's embed shortcode was rendered as Markdown text. Docs had described executable widgets as omitted; this changes that product contract deliberately.

The reader now projects hosted inline widgets from assistant `[embed]` shortcodes and from `show_widget` results (top-level or nested), once per page, merged into the same-turn shortcode the way the Control UI does. Each renders as a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` iframe served by the existing public media route as `?widget=<widget token>`. The widget token is minted by the existing public-session codec under a separate AAD with a `doc` claim, so the frame URL carries no publication bearer: widget code can read only a link to its own document, and share and widget tokens never resolve as each other. The route serves a document only when the published session generation contains its inline widget result (the guest `canvas.document.view` transcript match) and that result itself passes the public visibility boundary (`readPublicWidgetReceipt`, shared with the projection), with the canvas host enabled and a script-sandboxed document. Responses carry the widget sandbox CSP (`sandbox allow-scripts`, `connect-src 'none'`) plus `frame-ancestors 'self'`; the page CSP only gains `frame-src 'self'`. The page fits frames to the widget's reported height. Live refresh now reconciles transcript rows in place by `data-public-item` + `data-public-revision`, so unchanged widget frames are never detached (state survives refreshes and new messages); reorders or duplicate keys fall back to full replacement.

The reader's intro no longer claims interactive content is omitted. The two changed `publicReader` strings are left to the post-merge locale refresh; other locales show the English text until then.

The inline-widget receipt rule moved into one reader (`readInlineWidgetReceipt`) so guest authorization and public publication share a definition; canvas document path parsing and preview coercion are reused rather than duplicated.

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

- Production LOC: about +340 net (new public capability: projection, sandboxed serving route with a document-scoped token, frame sizing, in-place refresh reconciliation). Shared helpers and the existing token codec were reused instead of adding parallel parsers or a new credential system.
- No config, schema, or protocol changes and no new copy keys (two existing intro strings changed). Iframe titles use the widget title, falling back to the conversation title.
- Non-hosted embeds (YouTube, external URLs) keep today's behavior on the public page; follow-up candidate.
- Locally, `check:changed`'s max-lines suppression ratchet flags three untouched UI files on pristine `origin/main` too (suppressions from #173575, #173811, #173802 missing from `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`); main CI is green, so this is unrelated to this change.

</details>

## Evidence

- Focused tests, all passing: 22 files / 247 tests across the public reader (render, entry script, live refresh, media/widget route, publication read, HTTP, card, locale, concurrency), canvas render/documents, transcript matching, and the guest canvas RPC paths. New regression tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- Path-scoped `check:changed`: format, typecheck, lint, and guards pass for the changed files (except the pre-existing max-lines ratchet noted above).
- Codex autoreview (P0–P2) on the first revision and again on the full branch after the ClawSweeper fixes: scoped-clean both times.
- Codex connector P2s on `30be7697` addressed: a model-authored `[embed ref]` whose id fails the widget token contract now omits only that frame instead of turning the whole page into a 503, and with Canvas hosting disabled the page emits no widget frames (HTTP-boundary test covers both; autoreview scoped-clean).

- ClawSweeper findings on `9b542819` addressed: publication token no longer reaches widget code (document-scoped widget token); disclosure uses the public receipt visibility boundary; live refresh preserves unchanged widget frames. Regression tests for each fail on the prior head.

In the Control UI the agent called `show_widget` twice: once with a malformed shortcode (tool-result path) and once with a valid quoted `[embed ref="cv_…" title="Release timeline" height="320" /]` (shortcode path). Public access was enabled through `session.publicShare.set`, then both `/share/session?token=…` and the canonical `/chat/main` URL were opened in a fresh, signed-out Chromium context:

- Both widgets render once each; the tool-result widget sits at its tool position, the shortcode widget inside its final message (no duplicate, no literal shortcode). Frames auto-size from the requested height to content (420→173 px, 320→230 px).
- Widget responses: `200 text/html`, CSP includes `default-src 'none'`, `connect-src 'none'`, `sandbox allow-scripts`, `frame-ancestors 'self'`.
- Inside the frame: `self.origin === "null"`; `document.cookie`, `parent.document`, and `localStorage` all throw `SecurityError`.
- Widget scripts run: clicking “Sort by count” reorders the bars.
- An unknown widget id on the same token returns 404.

Before (`main` renderer, same transcript) — the shortcode prints as text:

![before: literal embed shortcode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41c82eb6-fb69-4266-9b35-449f76247e87)

After — the widget renders inside its message:

Same isolated Gateway state, rebuilt from the fixed head, signed-out browser:

- No share token in any frame `src` or in the widget's own `location.href`; frames use `?widget=<token>` only.
- Clicked “Sort by count”, then forced the first (ETag-less, 200) refresh: the same iframe elements (tagged before refresh) stayed in place and the sorted state survived.
- Appended a message with `chat.inject`, refreshed again: same iframe elements, sorted state intact, new row rendered.
- Cross-use rejected: share token as widget token → 404; widget token as page token → 404; widget token as image token → 404; old `token+widget` shape → 404; the real widget link → 200.

![after fixes: widget state kept across refresh with new message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/738e8aa2-f55a-4adc-bb52-3d6b588b7ddd)

Rebased onto `f6ed66162970`, preserving the pure Canvas URL parser while adopting #178666’s option-less document APIs. Generated locale files match main; the existing English copy changes remain. Refreshed head: `ad9af28f16d5d90fd2d5da8e2f42d25cbd8110a8`.

CI run [39511408337, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39511408337) tested head `ad9af28f16d5d90fd2d5da8e2f42d25cbd8110a8`: 51 jobs succeeded and 23 were intentionally skipped. prs.title: fix(google): video errors can expose the request API key
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google video generation errors can expose an active API key when an upstream SDK or HTTP response reflects it.

## User Impact

Video failures keep useful provider diagnostics without echoing the request credential. Existing HTTP statuses, text-only 404 fallback, retries, response limits, and download cancellation remain intact. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing Plugin SDK request-aware redactor at the video adapter's SDK, REST operation, and download diagnostic exits. SDK errors retain their safe name/status/code without retaining raw credential-bearing cause or response objects. Downloads use the actual URL key, including a key already supplied by Google. The existing JSON reader receives request headers so malformed responses cannot retain raw parser causes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. This is an adjacent reproduced credential-reflection defect, not removal of a guard or feature.

## Evidence

Seven controls failed on the original production adapter for the intended credential-reflection reason: SDK create, SDK poll, SDK completed-operation error, REST body, REST status, REST completed-operation error, and download status. The malformed-JSON control already passed on the original Bun parser; it is retained in its existing test as parser-cause coverage, not claimed as another reproduced leak.

The simplified candidate passes all 40 tests in the video suite (61.87s wrapper, 53.81s file under shared-host load; setup/import/transform dominate). Existing captured-stream cancellation, REST retry, deadline, size, input-mode, and fallback tests remain. External SDK/HTTP I/O uses synthetic fixtures; no paid or live provider request was made. Hosted exact-head CI is the broad gate.

Targeted Google package types, focused syntax lint/format, whitespace, mandatory suppression checks (14 tests), and scoped runtime/static cycle checks (zero) pass. Author simplification and independent P0–P2 review are complete with no actionable findings (confidence 0.91). Only formatter line wrapping followed review.

Production delta: +26 lines. Test delta: +65 lines.

prs.title: feat(migrate): import Grok Bot configuration like Hermes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Add Grok Bot to the existing one-time migration workflow used by Hermes, accepting local/account sources, offline snapshots, recipes, and marketplace/share URLs.

```text
source → preview + backup → native agents / workspace / supported config
                         → explicit skipped items and integration setup guidance
```

## User Impact

Imports owned-agent identity/icons, instructions, skills, complete explicitly exported memory, timezone, supported disabled cron jobs, and compatible disabled MCP connection definitions. Supports fresh onboarding and standalone migration into existing state with conflicts and repeat-apply handling.

Credentials are not copied, even with `--include-secrets`. Private cloud memory is not requested, and partial memory is skipped, including recovery from an older saved plan. Grok sign-in is used only to read source definitions. Known plugin IDs receive curated setup guidance for AgentMail, X/xurl, Gmail/Sheets/gog, Slack, and manual Salesforce MCP. No automatic plugin installation or drop-in tool parity is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requested product is configuration migration rather than individual Claw packages. Patrick further narrowed scope to verified transfers and explicit handling of unsupported content. This uses the existing detect/plan/apply owners rather than a parallel importer.

Depends on [native migration capabilities #178768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178768). Replaces the product direction of [the earlier URL-to-Claw importer #174960](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174960). Scope and proof are tracked in [CLAW-1180](https://linear.app/my-openclaw/issue/CLAW-1180/import-grok-bot-configuration-through-the-migration-framework).

## Evidence

- **Before:** new boundary regressions fail because credentials are still planned, partial memory is still copied, and hosted private memory is requested. Default token-only discovery cannot reopen its source on apply. Imported skills cannot be selected by their names.
  **After:** 22 focused tests pass across source/provider/integration boundaries and the real migration/config/agent/cron owners (48.80s wrapper wall time). Credentials are omitted, complete memory and existing state are preserved, partial memory and old credential actions are rejected, source discovery round-trips, and the actual CLI selector accepts `Research`.
- **Plugin installation:** the official `clawhub:@agentmail/agentmail@0.2.1` package installed successfully in the stopped isolated OCM environment; required dependencies are present. Inspection confirms explicit `enabled=false`, `activated=false`, `status=disabled`. `--no-enable` preserves defaults rather than forcing disable, so the setup guide now includes `plugins disable agentmail`. No sign-in or mail operation was performed.
- Real-owner integration verifies multi-agent creation, icons, instructions, memory, skills, timezone, disabled MCP/cron, conflicts, repeat apply, and saved-plan recovery. It does not execute external integrations or schedulers.
- Earlier real built-CLI Stalk proof: 28 migrated, 9 manual/skipped, zero errors/conflicts, verified backup; all 9 exported memory entries and 19 skill bodies retained exactly. Stalk completed a real local Ollama turn and displayed its imported purple avatar. The current native-migration screenshot is attached to CLAW-1180; screenshots on the older PR show a different Claw-package flow and are not proof of these migration effects.
- Extension production/test types and root integration types pass. Scoped lint and candidate build receipts are recorded with the final revision below. Broad pre-existing line-count, graph-budget, and agentsapi unused-export findings were not waived or modified.

- Final combined head `12dcad3075c` builds successfully in 4m22s (existing UI gzip warning retained). Native head: `73ca0a4d30b`. The rebuilt CLI selects only `stalk-setup` by name, emits all six curated integration paths, and plans no secret actions. Real Stalk repeat apply completes with 25 migrated, 12 skipped, no errors/conflicts, and a verified backup; all 19 skill bodies, 9 exported memories, and instructions remain intact, with one memory import block.

Live owned-account qualification remains blocked by the MacBook's Grok Keychain item denying SSH access. The local cache contains metadata including rooms, not full bots. No account-wide completeness or integration execution claim is made; private memory is now deliberately outside hosted import scope. Source conversations were not read and no messages were sent.

Review repairs are owned by the local stack coordinator. ClawSweeper's current guidance says repair/merge execution lanes are retired; review is requested after coherent stack updates. Nothing is merged or activated in personal state.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

Code can be reverted; imported state uses the migration framework's verified backup for restoration. Source Grok data is unchanged.

**Blast Radius:** Migration

Hosted definitions depend on Grok's current private API and source sign-in. Schedules and connections remain disabled until their tool scope, authorization, and delivery are reviewed.

prs.title: fix(agents): requester-settle pause test fails when a stale /tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite exists
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `subagent-announce.requester-settle-pause.test.ts` > "wakes once for a paused child before its frozen sibling settles, then delivers completion" fails with `SqliteSchemaMismatchError: OpenClaw agent database /tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite uses schema version 19` on any host that has a stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers and CI hosts no longer get a host-dependent failure from this suite, and the requester-settle tests stop reading or writing the shared `/tmp` root.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared requester-settle fixture mocked `resolveSessionStorePathCore` to the literal `"/tmp/sessions.json"`. In the final wake of that test, both children finish with visible `ok` completions, so `readSubagentRunAnnounceResultUsing` (`src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-result.ts`) resolves that store path. The fixture's mocked `findTranscriptEvent` misses, so the code falls back to the **unmocked** `findSessionTranscriptArchiveEventReadOnly`. That fallback opens the agent database next to the store path, which is `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. This is the only test in the fixture's seven consumers that reaches that branch.

The fixture now gives each test its own store path inside a directory from `useAutoCleanupTempDirTracker(afterEach)` (`test/helpers/temp-dir.ts`), so the real archive read stays in that directory. No env overrides, no extra mocks, and the consumer test is unchanged.

Pre-existing: reproduced on #177698's head, its parent, and current `main` (`deb5f800a70`).

## Evidence

All runs used a host with a stale schema-19 `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` present.

- Before (`origin/main`): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-pause.test.ts`: 1 failed / 6 passed. Stack goes through `session-accessor.sqlite-history` → `decodeSessionTranscriptWorkerReadError` → `SqliteSchemaMismatchError ... /tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. The run updated the `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm` mtime.
- After: same command, 7/7 passed. `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite*` mtimes did not change.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce`: 33 files / 418 tests passed, all seven fixture consumers included. `/tmp` DB still untouched.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `scripts/report-test-temp-creations.mjs` are clean.

Test-only change: +8/−1 in one `*.test-support.ts` file, no production LOC. The existing test is the regression proof: it fails on base with a stale shared DB and passes after the fix.

Follow-up worth a look (not changed here): other announce tests still hard-code `/tmp/...` store paths (`subagent-announce.test.ts`, `subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`, `subagent-announce-output.test.ts`, `subagent-announce-result.test.ts`). They inject the archive reader or never reach it, so they passed against the stale DB. They are not leaking today, but the literal paths would leak the same way if a real reader were ever reached.

prs.title: feat: update a guest's original pull request
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves A guest can prepare their own externally opened PR in a managed conversation, but source publication still rejects that association. Publishing must update the existing contributor branch while preserving the PR and its history. This contribution builds on #178233 and connects the prepared association to the existing shared publisher. An accepted update can also lose confirmation before its tool response returns. Dropping the request identity in that case leaves the guest unable to distinguish pending publication from failure. Another default publication call creates a new request rather than recovering the accepted one. ## User Impact Guests can publish saved changes back to the original PR through the configured shared GitHub account. Updates retain the original PR number, head repository and branch, commit ancestry, author, discussion, and draft state, including a full revert of the original contribution. Publisher credentials remain outside the sandbox. Publication checks the currently linked author, repository access, publisher write permission, and remote head. Incomplete source preparation and unaccepted remote changes prevent a new write while preserving saved work. A completed newer preparation can become the publication baseline even when an earlier publication receipt exists. Final merging remains an administrator operation. When an accepted original-PR update is awaiting confirmation, the tool retains its request ID and actual pending status. Its guidance tells the agent to finish the turn and await that request's result in the conversation, without submitting another publication. Reading PR metadata does not settle the receipt, and the eventual notice does not resume the agent. ## Why This Change Was Made The managed checkout branch and the original PR branch have different responsibilities. Local Git and index recovery retain the managed branch, while trusted pushes and genuine publication receipts use the bound PR head. The current receipt reader carries that association through its existing storage owner. The publisher reuses own-PR inspection and write preflight, then selects the exact original PR instead of creating another one. Imported branch-change refusals preserve the original target and local work. Ordinary bot-owned publication keeps its author protections. Imported-target support remains confined to shared source publication; personal publication and other PR operations retain their admission rules. Recovery verifies the recorded commit, tree, parent, request marker, and original PR identity. Once the request's accepted commit is observed, recovery performs readback without another push. This also preserves a later remote branch rewind when GitHub's PR response still shows the accepted commit. The coordinator now handles an imported request's recovery-pending result by reading that exact session-bound receipt, checking current requester authority before and after the read, and returning the stored outcome. Terminal outcomes remain terminal. This uses the existing recovery and reporting owner without adding a recovery action, polling, or another state representation. Ordinary publication errors retain their existing path. ## Evidence Remote Linux checks passed formatting, pinned Bun parity, type-aware lint, and the selected production and test compiler families. The latest correction passed 131 cases across five files: 15 original-PR publication cases, 17 tool cases, and 99 ordinary publication, requester and boundary cases. A final assertion was strengthened to discover the returned request ID through its original idempotency key; the affected file's format, lint, two compiler graphs and all 15 cases passed again on the final tree. The production files and other test inputs were unchanged, so their completed results remain applicable. The final `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-existing-pr.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` run took 64.76 seconds wall time. The tool file took 36.81 seconds. The three supporting suites took 123.62 seconds in Vitest; their 218.61-second wrapper also included the required runtime build. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39514086809) passed: 54 executed jobs and 25 intentionally skipped jobs, with 12,012 summed job wall seconds across a 1,947-second workflow job span. These GitHub intervals include setup and possible waiting overhead; they are not CPU time or the marginal cost of these tests. The fixture exercises real local Git, session ownership and durable receipts with synthetic GitHub I/O. It covers same-repository and maintainer-edit fork updates, original ancestry and PR preservation, full reverts, unchanged publication, identity/permission/head denials, pending preparation, and publication after a completed source refresh. Prior branch-rewind and full-revert regressions failed before their corrections and now preserve the original PR with no extra push. The new receipt cases reproduced the generic error before correction for a lost push response and unavailable post-push PR observation. They now retain the original request ID and recover that same request without another publication or push. Controls cover an active local turn and closed or revoked requesters. Native recovery is invoked directly in these tests; they do not establish elapsed scheduler behavior. Actual guest runs on an earlier composed runtime appended two updates and a full revert to the same PR while preserving history and metadata. Two responses were initially unconfirmed, but the original requests later reached published status without a second request. In the full-revert case, the native completion notice arrived 9.3 seconds after the guest's final response. Those observations establish the caller gap, but do not identify the underlying post-effect exception. Live acceptance of this receipt correction, remaining fork and authority scenarios, and visual evidence for those cases are still pending. The retained recordings below demonstrate a successful append and unchanged-source reuse on the earlier composed runtime. A later live conflict case also reached the publication owner and was refused while preparation was pending, despite an earlier genuine published receipt; its saved work and remote head were preserved. A separate completed refresh is now the input for the next publication case. Independent calibrated and adversarial review is clean at f6103b07ceb1d6779421ffcce4fa03195b1d43af. Previous guidance and full-revert findings remain closed. prs.title: feat(migrate): add native agent and cron import effects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Migration providers need to create additional agents and scheduled prompts without bypassing native lifecycle or scheduler ownership. This adds lazy migration SDK operations that require the admitted offline state owner and reject onboarding staging.

```text
migration apply (final state, offline owner)
  createMigrationAgent → native createAgent → exact retry or conflict
  applyMigrationCronJob → native CronService.add → exact retry or conflict
```

Existing agents and changed jobs are preserved. Migration explicitly refuses held-store restoration; the exact agent reuse path runs after deletion/recovery gates; cron import does not start the scheduler. This is the lower capability layer for Grok configuration migration, tracked in [CLAW-1180](https://linear.app/my-openclaw/issue/CLAW-1180/import-grok-bot-configuration-through-the-migration-framework).

## User Impact

Migration providers can preserve multi-agent setups and scheduled prompts through OpenClaw’s native owners. Existing agent creation behavior is unchanged unless the provider explicitly requests exact-state reuse.

## Why This Change Was Made

Grok configuration migration needs agent creation and cron insertion after onboarding promotion, under the admitted offline state owner. These shared operations keep lifecycle and scheduler writes out of provider-specific code. The dependent provider is [#178769](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178769).

## Evidence

- **Before:** the native migration boundary regression failed with `createMigrationAgent is not a function`.
  **After:** targeted agent creation, native migration-agent and cron tests pass, including stale/cancelled ownership, staging refusal, retries, conflicts, and no scheduler execution. Core/SDK/agent test typegraphs, targeted lint, formatting and SDK export checks pass; full candidate build passes.
- The dependent provider's real-owner integration additionally exercises existing-state preservation and saved-plan recovery; its confirmed-only scope excludes credential copying. No unrelated agent or cron writer was introduced.
- The exact committed Plugin SDK API comparison passes: migration-runtime remains an existing host-local-only facade, so the published compatibility surface is unchanged. Broad local gates report inherited line-count, shard-budget and agentsapi unused-export failures; all affected paths are unchanged against the captured base. No unrelated baseline was relaxed.

- Hosted CI exposed a type-only back-edge in the existing-agent result helper and duplicate cron helper export names. The native-layer correction removes the back-edge, gives implementation functions distinct names, and tests cron through the provider facade. Both exact failing guards now pass locally, with 26 affected native tests, core types, formatting and scoped type-aware lint.

- **Recovery review regression:** before the fix, an imported definition returned `existing` and cleared a recovery hold. With `restorePaths: []`, both matching and conflicting definitions preserve the hold, config, and held database bytes until explicit recovery. Agent/cron SDK tests pass (3 tests, 70.10s wrapper / 25.02s Vitest under host load), with SDK test types and two-file lint.
- **Final-effect authority proof:** releasing the real offline owner while native workspace preparation is paused returns an SDK error and leaves config unchanged, with no agent/session database or provenance. Only the already-created empty directory remains. This proves the composed agent boundary; no new direct late-revocation cron case or published-driver upgrade was run.


- Final combined head `12dcad3075c` builds successfully in 4m22s (existing UI gzip warning retained). Native head: `73ca0a4d30b`. The rebuilt CLI selects only `stalk-setup` by name, emits all six curated integration paths, and plans no secret actions. Real Stalk repeat apply completes with 25 migrated, 12 skipped, no errors/conflicts, and a verified backup; all 19 skill bodies, 9 exported memories, and instructions remain intact, with one memory import block.

Review coordination: the local stack owner handles repairs and propagation between these dependent branches. ClawSweeper's current contract says repair/merge execution lanes are retired. ClawSweeper review is requested on the updated heads; neither PR is claimed merge-ready while live-account qualification and hosted checks remain pending.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

Code can be reverted; completed migrations retain their created state and use the migration framework's backup for restoration.

**Blast Radius:** Migration

The new SDK operations admit effects only under the selected offline owner. Existing createAgent callers retain their current behavior; reuse is opt-in.

prs.title: fix(fal): report unsupported video overrides for MiniMax and HeyGen instead of claiming they were applied
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclaw infer video generate` and the `video_generate` tool report `ignoredOverrides` so users know which requested options the selected model did not honor. For the fal default model `fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live` and for `fal-ai/heygen/v2/video-agent`, the provider sends only the prompt (plus an optional image), yet aspect ratio, resolution, size, and audio requests were reported as applied: `ignoredOverrides` stayed empty while the overrides were silently dropped. The same happened for `--audio` on the Kling and Wan fal models, since only Seedance 2 forwards `generate_audio`.

## Root cause
`extensions/fal/video-generation-provider.ts` declares one provider-wide capability set built from the Seedance 2 model list, so every fal video model advertises `supportsAspectRatio`, `supportsResolution`, `supportsSize`, and `supportsAudio`:

```ts
// before
capabilities: {
  generate: buildFalVideoModeCapabilities(SEEDANCE_2_VIDEO_MODELS),
  imageToVideo: { enabled: true, ...buildFalVideoModeCapabilities(SEEDANCE_2_VIDEO_MODELS), ... },
```

while the request builder returns early for the prompt-only models:

```ts
// before
const normalizedModel = normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(model);
if (normalizedModel === DEFAULT_FAL_VIDEO_MODEL || normalizedModel === HEYGEN_VIDEO_AGENT_MODEL) {
  return requestBody;
}
```

and `applyFalSeedanceControls` only sets `generate_audio` for Seedance 2. The runtime sanitizer trusts the declared capabilities, so it never moves these overrides into `ignoredOverrides`.

## Fix
Add a per-model `resolveModelCapabilities` overlay, the existing provider hook the video runtime already consults, and share one prompt-only predicate between the overlay and the request builder:

```ts
// after
function resolveFalVideoModelCapabilities(model: string) {
  const unsupported = isFalPromptOnlyVideoModel(model)
    ? { supportsAspectRatio: false, supportsResolution: false, supportsSize: false, supportsAudio: false }
    : isFalSeedance2Model(model)
      ? undefined
      : { supportsAudio: false };
  return unsupported
    ? { generate: unsupported, imageToVideo: { enabled: true, ...unsupported } }
    : undefined;
}
```

MiniMax Live and HeyGen now report aspect ratio, resolution, size, and audio as ignored; Kling and Wan report audio as ignored; Seedance 2 models keep the full provider-level capabilities unchanged.

## Why this is the right boundary
The fal provider owns the knowledge of which fal models accept which knobs, and `resolveModelCapabilities` is the provider SDK hook built for per-model capability differences, so no core runtime change is needed. The request builder and the capability overlay now use the same `isFalPromptOnlyVideoModel` predicate, so they cannot drift. Request bodies are unchanged for every model; only the reported capabilities change. `videoToVideo` is only offered for Seedance 2 reference models, which the overlay leaves untouched.

## Verification
- Added a colocated case in `extensions/fal/video-generation-provider.test.ts` asserting the resolved capabilities for MiniMax Live, HeyGen, Kling, Wan, and Seedance 2. Local lint, typecheck, format, and test runs were skipped for this push; GitHub Actions CI is the gate.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `openclaw infer video generate` with a fal MiniMax Live model and `--aspect-ratio 16:9 --resolution 1080P --audio` sends only the prompt to fal but reports no ignored overrides.
Real environment tested: the shipped `openclaw` CLI (`openclaw.mjs` from a freshly built dist with the bundled fal plugin) on macOS, built once from pristine main and once from this patch on identical inputs, with an isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and `FAL_KEY` set. Everything stayed real (CLI parsing, plugin loading, the video generation runtime and its override sanitizer, the fal provider request builder, the SSRF-guarded fetch path, output file saving) except the fal HTTP API itself, which was replaced by a `--import` preload that answers queue.fal.run submit/status/result and the media download URL and logs the submitted request body.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `FAL_KEY=fal-test-key OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp> node --import ./fal-http-seam.mjs openclaw.mjs infer video generate --model fal/fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live --prompt "a lobster surfing" --aspect-ratio 16:9 --resolution 1080P --audio --output <tmp>/out.mp4`
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 2cd23b665868)
[fal-seam] POST /fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live body={"prompt":"a lobster surfing"}
video.generate via local
provider: fal
model: fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live
outputs: 1
<tmp>/out-before.mp4

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
[fal-seam] POST /fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live body={"prompt":"a lobster surfing"}
video.generate via local
provider: fal
model: fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live
ignoredOverrides: [{"key":"aspectRatio","value":"16:9"},{"key":"resolution","value":"1080P"},{"key":"audio","value":true}]
outputs: 1
<tmp>/out-after.mp4
```
Observed result after fix: fal receives the same prompt-only body in both runs, and the CLI now reports aspect ratio, resolution, and audio as ignored instead of silently implying they were applied.
What was not tested: no live fal account or real generation; HeyGen, Kling, and Wan were not driven through the CLI (covered by the colocated capability assertions); the `video_generate` agent tool path, which uses the same runtime sanitizer, was not driven separately.

prs.title: fix(cli): pin runtime config before plugin load in config set model validation
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclaw config set` (and `config patch`) of a model reference validates the ref by loading provider runtime plugins, but never publishes a runtime config snapshot first. Any plugin that reads `api.runtime.config.current()` during `register()` throws `Runtime config is not prepared`, its provider never registers, and the command rejects a valid model with `Unknown model: ...` (exit 1, config not written).

## Root cause
`src/cli/config-model-validation.ts`, `createRuntimeModelRefResolver`, acquires the prepared model runtime with `loadRuntimePlugins: true` straight from the candidate config:

```ts
// before
const [modelRuntime, preparedRuntime] = await (modelModules ??= loadModelModules());

await using lease = await preparedRuntime.acquireReadOnlyPreparedModelRuntime(
  { agentId: targetAgentId, agentDir, config, workspaceDir, loadRuntimePlugins: true },
```

Since runtime config reads became strict (`readRuntimeConfig` in `src/config/runtime-snapshot.ts` throws when no snapshot is published), the CLI process has no snapshot at this point, so plugin `register()` calls that read config fail.

## Fix
Pin the candidate config before acquiring the lease, the same way `doctor-lint-runner.ts` and `plugins/cli.ts` already do:

```ts
// after
const [modelRuntime, preparedRuntime] = await (modelModules ??= loadModelModules());
await loadPinnedRuntimeConfigAsync(async () => ({ config }));
```

## Why this is the right boundary
The resolver is the single place where config validation loads runtime plugins for `config set` and `config patch`, so pinning there covers both commands. It publishes exactly the config being validated, which is what plugins should see. The Doctor paths (#170445, #170984) and plugin CLI loading already pin the same way; this is the remaining caller that loads runtime plugins without a pinned snapshot. No other behavior changes.

## Verification
- Added a regression case in `src/cli/config-model-validation.runtime.test.ts` with a provider plugin that reads `api.runtime.config.current()` in `register()`; it fails on main and passes with the patch.
- Local lint/typecheck/vitest skipped by choice; GitHub Actions CI runs the full gates.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `openclaw config set agents.defaults.model.primary <provider>/<model>` rejects a valid model when the provider plugin reads runtime config during registration, because validation loads plugins without a published runtime config.
Real environment tested: Built OpenClaw CLI (`node scripts/run-node.mjs` rebuild, then `node openclaw.mjs`) on pristine main 8b1ac41c314 versus this branch, isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, with a local provider plugin loaded via `plugins.load.paths` whose `register()` reads `api.runtime.config.current()`. Real config IO, real plugin loader, real prepared model runtime and real model validation; nothing mocked, provider baseUrl is never contacted.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: seed config `{"plugins":{"allow":["pin-config"],"load":{"paths":["<dir>/pin-config/index.cjs"]},"entries":{"pin-config":{"enabled":true}}}}`, then `node openclaw.mjs config set agents.defaults.model.primary pin-config/exact-supported` followed by `node openclaw.mjs config get agents.defaults.model.primary`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 8b1ac41c314)
$ node openclaw.mjs config set agents.defaults.model.primary pin-config/exact-supported
[plugins] pin-config failed during register from .../plugins/pin-config/index.cjs: Error: Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.
Cannot set model reference "pin-config/exact-supported" at agents.defaults.model.primary: Unknown model: pin-config/exact-supported. Run `openclaw models list --refresh --provider pin-config` to inspect this provider's model choices, then retry with a model supported by your account. Run openclaw models list to list available models.
exit 1

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
$ node openclaw.mjs config set agents.defaults.model.primary pin-config/exact-supported
[pin-config] register saw runtime config: plugins.entries.pin-config.enabled=true
Updated agents.defaults.model.primary. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
exit 0
$ node openclaw.mjs config get agents.defaults.model.primary
pin-config/exact-supported
```
Observed result after fix: The plugin now reads the candidate config during registration, its provider registers, and `config set` accepts and writes the model reference instead of failing with `Unknown model`.
What was not tested: Bundled plugins that read config lazily (for example Codex) were already unaffected in this run; no gateway hot-reload path was exercised, and no live provider request was made.
