prs.title: fix(heartbeat): end the turn after heartbeat_respond is accepted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #86324: in a heartbeat run, an accepted `heartbeat_respond` does not end the turn, so some models keep calling it until the run budget times out.

Observed on 2026.9.6 with `gemini-3.8-flash` through an OpenAI-compatible provider. One call was accepted, then six duplicates followed over about 100 s. The summaries were reworded and one flipped `notify` to `true`. Each duplicate got `ToolInputError("heartbeat_respond already accepted for this turn")`, which the model treated as retryable. The run ended with `timedOutByRunBudget`, and the cron heartbeat job logged a timeout. Argument-hash loop detection did not trigger because every retry used different arguments.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The agent loop already ends a turn when a tool batch's results are all `terminate: true`, but `heartbeat_respond` never set it.
- A duplicate call was an error, which invites a retry. It is now a terminal, non-error `already_accepted` result. The first decision (outcome, notify, scratch) is kept.
- Repeated failed `heartbeat_respond` submissions now share one signature in `observeRepeatedToolError`. A run that keeps sending invalid responses with varying arguments therefore stops via the existing repeated-tool-error breaker after 3 attempts. Thresholds for other tools are unchanged.

## Changes

- `src/agents/tools/heartbeat-response-tool.ts`: `terminate: true` on accept, and a terminal `already_accepted` result for duplicates.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.completion.ts`: only the first `status: "accepted"` result is recorded as the heartbeat response.
- `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts`: a single repeated-error signature for `heartbeat_respond`.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.ts` and `.../run/incomplete-turn-resolution.ts`: an accepted heartbeat response counts as a usable turn outcome, so a tool-terminated turn is not reported as incomplete.
- `docs/gateway/heartbeat.md`.

## Evidence

- New regression test `src/agents/tools/heartbeat-response-tool.loop.test.ts`. It drives `runAgentLoop` with a model that keeps calling `heartbeat_respond` with reworded arguments. It asserts one model request, a lifecycle status of `ok`, the first decision retained, and no budget abort. Invalid-response and invalid-schema variants stop after 3 requests with `REPEATED_TOOL_ERROR_CODE`.
- `heartbeat-response-tool.test.ts` was updated for the terminal accepted and duplicate results.
- Local run on Node 24.21.0 (linux arm64): targeted files 69/69 passed. `test-projects --changed origin/main` passed except 3 environment-only failures: running as root breaks two permission-denial tests, and one is a ctime timing assertion. `tsgo:core` and oxlint on the touched files were clean.
- Not yet verified against a live model. A downstream test install is next.

prs.title: fix(cli): sanitize terminal controls in marketplace list output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw plugins marketplace list <source>` prints plugin names, descriptions, and the marketplace name directly to the terminal. A malicious or compromised marketplace source can embed terminal control characters (ESC/BEL/OSC/CR) in these fields, and the operator's terminal interprets them — clearing output, retitling the window, or forging extra report lines — the moment the command runs.

## User Impact

User impact: marketplace, plugin-name, and plugin-description fields display control characters safely while retaining normal Unicode in human output. JSON consumers keep the original values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing terminal sanitizer (`sanitizeTerminalText`, the canonical owner in `packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.ts`) at the human-rendering text boundaries, before styling — the same owner already guards sibling CLI report paths (registry search, model selection, channels, cron list). No routing, auth, configuration schema, defaults, dependencies, or migration changes. The `--json` branch (`writeJson`) intentionally preserves raw values for scripted consumers, so sanitization is applied only where a human reads the report.

## Evidence

Real CLI binary, isolated HOME, local malicious marketplace fixture (no network), same command before/after the fix:

| Actual CLI `plugins marketplace list <fixture>` | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| human report control bytes | present (ESC/OSC/BEL/CR) | 0 |

- **BASE (pre-fix)** — raw control bytes reach the terminal:
  `Marketplace Market^[]0;marketplace-title-pwned^Gplace`
  `^[[31mred-plugin^[[0m v1.2.3 - drops ^M` / `^Gbell and ^[[2J clear`
  (OSC retitle + BEL, ANSI SGR color, raw CR, clear-screen sequence)
- **HEAD (fix built)** — sequences stripped, `\r\n` rendered as literal `\r\n`, safe text survives:
  `Marketplace Marketplace`
  `red-plugin v1.2.3 - drops \r\nbell and  clear`
- **`--json`** — preserves the raw injected bytes byte-for-byte (`"name":"Market\u001b]0;...\u0007place"`, `"\u001b[31mred-plugin\u001b[0m"`, `"\r\n\u0007bell and \u001b[2J clear"`).

Focused regression suite: `src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts` — 14/14 passing, including the new sanitization case folded into the existing `plugins marketplace list` describe block (pre-fix RED on raw-ESC assertion, post-fix GREEN).

prs.title: fix(health): surface restart-required runtime config drift
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw health` reports `ok` when the running Gateway still uses an older model, provider, auth or secrets config than the one on disk, for example after an edit under `gateway.reload.mode: "off"`, a failed reload, or while a required restart is pending.

The diagnostic also compared only `secrets.providers`. Changing `secrets.defaults.env`, which selects the active provider alias, therefore produced a false `ok` result even after the reloader completed the new source observation.

## User Impact

`openclaw health --json` includes optional `runtimeConfig` state:

- `ok`: monitored runtime values match the latest completed reload observation.
- `drift`: they differ, with redacted path names and default-model labels.
- `unknown`: one authoritative source is unavailable.

Text health prints a warning for `drift` or `unknown`. The diagnostic never emits config fingerprints, secret values, source paths, parse excerpts, or observation errors.

`openclaw health` advertises `runtime-config-health`. Every other client (Control UI, native apps, nodes, third-party v4 clients) receives hello, `health` events, and `health` responses without `runtimeConfig`, the same shape as main.

Since #111527, `hot` and every mode other than `off` resolve to `hybrid`, so lasting drift now mainly comes from `mode: "off"`, failed reloads, writes whose writer skipped runtime application, and restarts that are still pending.

Update behavior: no config, default, SQLite, migration or protocol-version change. A new CLI talking to an older Gateway sends a capability that Gateway ignores, so the field and the text line are simply absent; an older CLI talking to a new Gateway doesn't advertise it and sees today's payload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config reloader owns one generation-fenced, immutable latest-completed source observation. The shared health owner compares that observation with the published runtime source snapshot. RPC, connection hello, broadcasts, cached health, and CLI text all read the same redacted projection. Monitoring canonical parent `secrets` covers provider declarations, provider-default selection, and the restart-owned egress proxy without adding another config or API surface.

Every reloader transaction that reads the source publishes that read when it finishes, and only while its source revision is current. A write's own same-source watcher echo is published by the echo's reload pass: main removed the in-transaction echo catch-up in #168980. That covers watcher reloads, in-process writes (which publish the canonical reread their notification carries), and plugin lifecycle applications.

The alternative was to read disk or reconstruct reload state in each health consumer. That would duplicate policy and recreate mixed-generation results during debounce, in-flight reads, supersession, and bootstrap awaits.

`runtimeConfig` is sent only to clients that advertise the `runtime-config-health` client capability, so existing strict v4 decoders never see it (details under Protocol compatibility).

## Protocol compatibility

An ungated field is rejected by the pre-change strict v4 decoder. Measured at `a78f6e3c2fd` with its own lockfile: that head's `sendGatewayHello`, carrying a drift value from its real `buildRuntimeConfigHealth`, validated with TypeBox `Value.Check` against the pre-change strict v4 decoder (`snapshot.ts` byte-identical to `bf83a4dde8f`; `frames.ts` has no diff between base and head, so `HelloOkSchema` is the same with the base snapshot swapped in):

```text
head HelloOkSchema, drift hello                      : true
base HelloOkSchema, control hello (no runtimeConfig) : true
base HelloOkSchema, drift hello                      : false
  /snapshot/health  additionalProperties  "must not have additional properties"  {"additionalProperties":["runtimeConfig"]}
base SnapshotSchema, drift snapshot                  : false
  /health           additionalProperties  "must not have additional properties"  {"additionalProperties":["runtimeConfig"]}
```

So the field is capability-gated. It uses the negotiation the protocol already has (`GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS` in `client-info.ts`, `ConnectParams.caps`, `hasGatewayClientCap`) and adds one entry, `RUNTIME_CONFIG_HEALTH: "runtime-config-health"`. The field is projected per connection on all three surfaces:

- hello-ok: the cached snapshot is projected per connection; on the uncached path the diagnostic is read only for advertising clients.
- `health` events: through the broadcaster's existing per-recipient projection hook in `server-connection-state.ts`. The node-subscription fanout has no per-client caps in scope, so it always drops the field.
- `health` RPC: both the cached and the refreshed response.

The shared health cache is never mutated by the projection. The closed `HealthSnapshotSchema` is reachable only through hello-ok's `snapshot`: the `health` RPC result already carries `modelRuntime`, which no schema in `packages/gateway-protocol` declares, and I found no payload schema there for the `health` event. I gated all three anyway so a client never sees the field without asking for it; a hello-only gate would be about 20 production lines smaller.

Which contract to keep is the Gateway owners' call, and nothing here claims that decision. One set of data points for it, each measured with `git show <sha> | grep -E 'GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS|hasGatewayClientCap'` (0 hits each): main has added optional fields to closed v4 hello-snapshot objects without a capability gate, for example `suspension` in #136220 (`e0ab9907621`), presence `clientId` in #145559 (`0141569e798`), health `ingressFailed`/`ingressPressure` in #123234 (`b233ea79575`), and, since the last review, health `childRuntime` in #157190 (`92c86fefcd4`).

## Evidence

### Current revision: October 20

Pushed [`426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2), tree `9190bd4b0c36a0219455cec5566bedf0b9b65b4c`, as an additive merge of `832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04` and upstream `f629720edbb9f4b458adae30c7506c1dc5d1adc6`. The normal push and remote head were verified. [CI run 39499291024](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499291024) completed successfully: **112 jobs, 89 successful and 23 skipped**, with no failed, running or queued jobs. The fully paginated capture at `2026-10-20T23:42:26.369785+00:00` records `filter=all`: 180 completed checks (1 neutral, 57 skipped, 122 success); `filter=latest`: 180 completed checks (1 neutral, 57 skipped, 122 success). The [preflight job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499291024/job/118892385712) checked out merge [`5c19327872dac9e8382503fe89163559452f54b4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5c19327872dac9e8382503fe89163559452f54b4), tree `29fc941f9313770bccb92a973fad06d5fdd00492`, with parents `8f0973e37405d683e242e217f4d7c30a1efc4118` and this head `426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2`. That executed merge differs from the locally validated integration tree. The [last queued shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499291024/job/118912285234) is included in the terminal result.

The integration preserves upstream health-summary and hello-on-demand behavior alongside the optional runtime-config capability. It also fixes two demonstrated defects:

- The runtime-config event projection could restore `agents` and `sessions` after the broadcaster had removed them for a summary-only client. The existing per-recipient callback now applies both projections before serialization. The generic broadcaster matches pinned main. [Production callback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server-connection-state.ts#L137-L153), [eight serialized-event combinations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts#L730).
- Clearing and republishing the runtime snapshot can reuse a numeric revision. The cache key now compares the reload-observation generation and the runtime owner's stable publication object identity, so a different publication cannot reuse stale cached or in-flight health. The key remains internal. [Freshness checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server/health-state.ts#L137-L162), [cached and pending reset cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts#L390). These cases call the actual runtime reset/publication owner and summary builder with controlled collection and reload observations; they are not a full Gateway restart test.

The [hello table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts#L442) covers all 16 combinations of cached health, runtime-config capability, hello-on-demand and health-summary capability.

Executed on the private Linux builder with Node v26.8.2, pnpm 12.12.1, frozen dependencies and one Vitest worker:

| Control | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Event-composition regression before the repair, tree `f84da04ee18080546e35ac732673768b22516d81` | One intended payload assertion failure with `runtimeConfig` present; the absent case passed, eight unrelated cases skipped. The loop stopped at its first affected recipient, so this is one observed failure. Exit 1, 144.13 seconds, no timeout. |
| Actual reset/republication regressions with the old numeric key, tree `de0fdb18b3033c0876e41a261bb4d65e1d89ee62` | Two intended failures: stale cache returned instead of invalidation, and stale pending collection returned instead of recollection. 24 skipped, exit 1, 57.23 seconds, no timeout. |
| Final tree `9190bd4b0c36a0219455cec5566bedf0b9b65b4c` | Five suites, 114 tests passed, exit 0, 79.31 seconds. Both reset cases, all event and hello combinations, RPC controls and broadcaster serialization are included. |
| Scoped static checks on final tree | Incremental core TypeScript: exit 0, 6.26 seconds. Gateway-server test TypeScript: exit 0, 7.55 seconds. Seven-file typed lint: zero warnings/errors, exit 0, 13.82 seconds. |
| Source identity and review | Before/after index trees and all 58,328 tracked blob hashes match the final tree. Two separate source reviews found no actionable P0-P2 issue; the reviewers did not execute target tests. The peer review independently inspected the complete positive/negative logs and identity receipts. |

Reproduce the positive set:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts \
  src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/health.runtime-config.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-broadcast.serialization.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

For the event negative control, retain the final tests and remove only summary composition from the runtime-config per-recipient replacement, then run the connection-state cases. For the reset control, retain the tests but replace publication-identity comparison with the old observation-generation/numeric-revision key, then run the two reset cases. Restore the exact production bytes after each control. Neither mutation is in the branch. The final runs reported no remaining process-group children; tracked-blob checks do not certify untracked files or the entire runtime environment.

The integration includes upstream [`b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87), which fixes the missing `createDeferredCore` import reported by the previous head's static jobs. Those old failures also occur in the exact-base main CI; the old runtime jobs completed. The earlier SIGKILL/137 remains unexplained and is not classified as OOM.

The [fresh hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89526#issuecomment-4604300916) completed October 20 at 21:30 UTC on `426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2`, against main `4b065f50d724f380dca1fa09b387c2b0e42a80a0`, with zero findings. It accepts the supplied historical Gateway proof and current regression evidence. This was source inspection, not an independent execution of the target code. Its two remaining items are Gateway-owner acceptance of the capability-gated health contract and current-head maintainer security approval. Primary CI is now complete as recorded above. The separate `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` commit statuses remain failure; `openclaw/dependency-review` is success.

Maintainer security approval and Gateway-owner acceptance of the optional `runtimeConfig` contract remain open. A successful Security Review workflow does not grant the required approval. The historical sections below retain their original heads and are not new executions at `426d7295`.

### Historical integration: October 19

Head [`832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04) is an additive merge of the previous head `56b8e57fe36d33313e80af541820b11e02ab9a2e` and upstream main `2cd23b665868c75bfb02537cef9eb9f2b329667a`. GitHub reports the conflicts resolved. No rebase or force-push.

The six conflict resolutions retain main's health-event deduplication, pinned config paths, connection-row delivery-loss handling, and `hello-health-on-demand` behavior alongside this PR's runtime-config capability gate. Clients advertising both health capabilities receive an empty hello health snapshot; requests and events still carry the opted-in diagnostic. The [hello tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04/src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts) cover all eight combinations of cached health, runtime-config capability, and hello opt-out.

A new [health-owner regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04/src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts) reproduced an old `ok` diagnostic being broadcast after its observation was superseded. The pre-fix resolved tree was `022244e3589d615e8b58745e6ab6ca9cd7edb9c8`; it failed with `expected generation: 7, received generation: 8` while both values carried `state: ok`. The fix removes the async helper hop between the final config check and publication. A separate regression checks that an equivalent diagnostic at a newer generation refreshes the cache key without another event.

Local author-run validation of the current tree (`a08c6662c26a9fb90f366284fadae4dceec13144`):

- Four focused Gateway suites: **88 passed**, wrapper wall time 266.55 seconds. This includes the red-to-green publication regression, strict legacy decoder controls, capability projection for hello/events/RPC, and main's health deduplication tests.
- Core production TypeScript: passed, 47.75 seconds. Gateway-server test TypeScript shard: passed, 48.38 seconds.
- Targeted type-aware lint and formatting on the repaired files: passed. `git diff --check` against pinned main: passed.
- Workboard's asset build, the consumer previously affected by capability-registry changes: passed, 5.14 seconds. This is a focused consumer build, not a full build claim.
- Independent canonical `autoreview`: three completed passes, `scoped-clean` through P2 on the full candidate diff against pinned main. The reviewer assessed supplied patches and did not execute tests. Helper SHA-256: `b95e51b79d9f68fe445cdc9d6c1e07b01507188bba1bfe8a59f14c378e5ac3a5`.

Reproduce the focused runtime checks from this head with its frozen dependencies and repository test wrapper:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/health.runtime-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json --incremental
```

Exact-head CI [run 39320268759](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320268759) finished with two failing jobs plus the aggregate gate, both in a file this PR does not touch. `check-test-types-core-4`: `src/gateway/local-http-probe.test.ts(154,25): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'createDeferredCore'`. `check-lint-core-1`: `src/gateway/local-http-probe.test.ts:178:53` (`prefer-promise-reject-errors`). #177670 (`2cc639d7023`) broke that file on main and `b6bd9e8bd0c` fixed it at 2026-10-19 21:24Z; the run's base `0548086d6a95` predates the fix. Every other job passed or was skipped, so the earlier SIGKILL in `checks-node-changed-compact-large-22` (run 39007736518) did not repeat. `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` is the open approval gate below, not a test result.

The Gateway-owner contract decision below and the maintainer security approval remain open; this update claims neither approval nor landing readiness with green CI.

### Historical author-reported evidence

The evidence below belongs to the named earlier heads and has not been promoted to current-head proof.


Head `8606a2df718`: six commits on the earlier head `5d5ad44f5f6`. `6d62aefe5a1` merges `main@6b2afbfe981` (the branch was CONFLICTING), `32548a164ba` moves the external-change audit appender out of `config-reload.ts`, `82be5c6edc6` fixes the plugin lifecycle publication gap, `759130f4cc7` brings the health mocks inside main's mock-export ratchet, `3ee3413ef5e` rechecks cached health after its awaited reads, and `8606a2df718` removes three mock-shaped tests. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against `main@f3f9bf90c69` (2026-10-09) exits 0.

Since then, `615fde1ef66` merges `main@bb642e181e1` and `56b8e57fe36` merges `main@4af30f64ca7`. Neither changes an added or removed line of this branch's own diff; the merge notes below cover both.

### Plugin lifecycle publication (the P2 from the last review)

`applyPluginLifecycleChange` reads and applies the source outside `runReload`. It could consume a pending write and accept that write's watcher echo, and accepting the echo cleared the queued reload, so nothing published the source it applied. It now publishes through the same per-transaction tracker. Regression in `config-reload.observation.test.ts`, run on the same tree with and without the three production lines:

```text
without the fix   publishes a plugin lifecycle read that consumes a pending write and accepts its echo
                  AssertionError: expected { generation: 15, …(1) } to deeply equal { generation: 16, …(1) }
                  observation still agents.defaults.model = openai/gpt-5.6-sol; readSnapshot called twice, onHotReload once
                  Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
with the fix      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

### Cached health after awaited reads (the P2 from the re-review)

The cached branch of the `health` RPC read the shared snapshot, awaited the delivery-queue and context-engine summaries, then answered from the captured copy even when a config observation had retired that snapshot in between. It now rereads the shared cache after the awaits and answers from a refresh when the snapshot is no longer the current one. Regression in `health.runtime-config.test.ts`, run with and without the production change:

```text
without the fix   refreshes when the cached snapshot is retired during its diagnostic reads
                  AssertionError: expected { state: 'ok' } to deeply equal { state: 'drift', …(3) }
                  Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
with the fix      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The tracker keys on `source.observation.revision`. Main's #168980 removed the in-transaction echo catch-up, so the accepted-echo marker this PR had added is gone too. `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` is the maintainer approval gate for `connect-hello.ts`.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject conflicting positional and --channel in channels add
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclaw channels add <channel> --channel <other>` silently ignores the positional channel and configures the `--channel` one instead. Any credential flags meant for the positional channel (for example `--token`) are then written to the other channel's config, with exit 0 and a success message.

## Root cause
`src/cli/channels-cli.ts`, `resolveChannelsAddOptions`:

```ts
// before
return {
  ...forwardedOpts,
  channel: forwardedOpts.channel ?? channelArg,
};
```

When both the positional `[channel]` and `--channel` are supplied, the flag always wins and the positional value is dropped without any signal, even when they name different channels.

## Fix
```ts
// after
async function resolveChannelSelectorId(selector: string): Promise<string> {
  const normalized = selector.trim().toLowerCase();
  const { resolveChannelSetupCliOptionMetadata } =
    await import("../channels/plugins/cli-add-options.js");
  const { selectedChannel } = resolveChannelSetupCliOptionMetadata(normalized);
  return selectedChannel?.id?.toLowerCase() ?? normalized;
}
...
if (
  flagChannel &&
  channelArg &&
  (await resolveChannelSelectorId(flagChannel)) !== (await resolveChannelSelectorId(channelArg))
) {
  throw new Error(`Conflicting channels: positional "${channelArg}" and --channel "${flagChannel}". Pass only one.`);
}
```

Both selectors are resolved through the same alias-aware metadata lookup (`resolveChannelSetupCliOptionMetadata`) that already picks the channel's setup flags, and only genuinely different channels are rejected. An alias plus its canonical id (`zl` / `zalo`, `imsg` / `imessage`), the same id in different case, and either selector used alone all behave exactly as on main. The metadata import only happens when both selectors are present.

## Why this is the right boundary
`resolveChannelsAddOptions` is the single place where the positional and the flag are merged for `channels add`, so the check covers every channel and both the interactive and non-interactive paths. The error goes through the existing `runCommandWithRuntime` handler (stderr message, exit 1). `channels remove` has no positional channel, so it is unaffected.

## Review follow-up (ClawSweeper on 43a8b6e8d0a)
- **Compare canonical channel identities (P2):** fixed. Selectors are canonicalized through `resolveChannelSetupCliOptionMetadata` before comparison; new regression case covers an alias plus canonical id pair. Real CLI run below shows `channels add zl --channel zalo` was rejected on the previous head and now configures Zalo, same as main.
- **Preserve ExitError in the runtime mock (P2):** fixed. The `../runtime.js` mock in `src/cli/channels-cli.test.ts` now spreads `importOriginal()` and only overrides `defaultRuntime`, so `runCommandWithRuntime` can import `ExitError` and the rejection case reaches its assertions.
- **Maintainer decision (flag precedence):** this needs an owner call and I am not trying to dodge it. #112176 made `--channel` win for option discovery so `telegram --channel signal` would register Signal's flags. That precedence is kept for discovery; what this PR changes is that the command then refuses to write config when the two selectors name different channels, because the positional channel's credentials (`--token` etc.) end up stored under the flag's channel with a success message. The change follows the review's recommended option: reject only genuinely different channels, keep aliases and single-selector use unchanged. If maintainers prefer to keep silent flag precedence, this PR should be closed rather than widened.

## Verification
- `src/cli/channels-cli.test.ts`: a conflicting positional and `--channel` is rejected without calling `channelsAddCommand`; a case-only match still forwards; an alias plus canonical id is accepted and forwarded.
- Local lint/format/typecheck/vitest skipped on this machine; relying on GitHub Actions.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `openclaw channels add telegram --channel discord --token abc` silently configures Discord with the token and ignores `telegram`, while `openclaw channels add zl --channel zalo --token abc` (alias plus canonical id) must keep working.
Real environment tested: the real `openclaw` CLI entry point (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`, Node v26.9.0, macOS) with a fresh `{}` `openclaw.json`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `HOME` per command, on pristine main 34f6f1ba01c, on the previous PR head 43a8b6e8d0a, and on this head 506f28cdfdc. Nothing stubbed; the bundled Discord and Zalo setup code ran for real against on-disk config.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$S OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$S/openclaw.json HOME=$S node --import tsx src/entry.ts channels add <args>; echo exit=$?; jq -c '.channels' $S/openclaw.json` for each of `telegram --channel discord --token abc`, `zl --channel zalo --token abc`, `discord --channel discord --token abc`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# before at 34f6f1ba01c
$ openclaw channels add telegram --channel discord --token abc
Added Discord account "default".
exit=0
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
{"discord":{"enabled":true,"token":{"source":"store","provider":"default","id":"CHANNEL_SETUP_42413149BFB6B5DF60E335858CD6967F"}}}
$ openclaw channels add zl --channel zalo --token abc
Added Zalo account "default".
exit=0
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
{"zalo":{"enabled":true,"botToken":{"source":"store","provider":"default","id":"CHANNEL_SETUP_FE48A4B50F1D6923B7C549DE033D08D7"}}}
$ openclaw channels add discord --channel discord --token abc
Added Discord account "default".
exit=0
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
{"discord":{"enabled":true,"token":{"source":"store","provider":"default","id":"CHANNEL_SETUP_416856F310B9D1AD784E271569FBDC5E"}}}

# oldhead at 43a8b6e8d0a
$ openclaw channels add telegram --channel discord --token abc
Conflicting channels: positional "telegram" and --channel "discord". Pass only one.
exit=1
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
null
$ openclaw channels add zl --channel zalo --token abc
Conflicting channels: positional "zl" and --channel "zalo". Pass only one.
exit=1
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
null
$ openclaw channels add discord --channel discord --token abc
Added Discord account "default".
exit=0
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
{"discord":{"enabled":true,"token":{"source":"store","provider":"default","id":"CHANNEL_SETUP_35836176A0E80F59D514FA2E0965B4D8"}}}

# after at 506f28cdfdc
$ openclaw channels add telegram --channel discord --token abc
Conflicting channels: positional "telegram" and --channel "discord". Pass only one.
exit=1
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
null
$ openclaw channels add zl --channel zalo --token abc
Added Zalo account "default".
exit=0
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
{"zalo":{"enabled":true,"botToken":{"source":"store","provider":"default","id":"CHANNEL_SETUP_7F6A93AC5366C3E680D798D7E3071769"}}}
$ openclaw channels add discord --channel discord --token abc
Added Discord account "default".
exit=0
$ jq '.channels' openclaw.json
{"discord":{"enabled":true,"token":{"source":"store","provider":"default","id":"CHANNEL_SETUP_53C8EFA077533873FFC50DAD57960C17"}}}
```
Observed result after fix: on 506f28cdfdc, different selectors (`telegram` vs `discord`) stop with a clear error, exit 1, and leave the config untouched instead of writing the token to Discord. An alias plus canonical id (`zl` vs `zalo`) now configures Zalo with exit 0, matching main, where the previous head wrongly rejected it. Matching selectors still configure the channel.
What was not tested: no live Telegram, Discord or Zalo connection. Runtime-only plugins whose aliases are not in bundled or catalog metadata fall back to a case-insensitive raw comparison.

prs.title: improve: make official support discoverable across OpenClaw
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People seeking official OpenClaw support are sent to Discord or cannot find a support link in the apps.

## User Impact

Users can reach official OpenClaw support at https://community.openclaw.ai/ from the Web UI, native About screens, macOS update recovery, CLI help/status, agent documentation guidance, GitHub issue chooser, and canonical English documentation. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use **Support** and **Get support** consistently, add a discoverable docs support guide with safe diagnostic guidance, and replace support-specific Discord handoffs. Keep self-service docs, Discord social links and contributor coordination, actionable GitHub bug reports, and private security reporting separate. Translations and published/generated documentation stay with their existing downstream workflows; only the prescribed native source inventory and docs glossary input change here.

## Evidence

- Focused Web UI About, Apps, and sidebar tests: 99 passed, 9.95 seconds wall time. Updated regressions exercise official support links while retaining Discord and self-service documentation.
- Actual source CLI entry point `pnpm openclaw --help` with isolated state passed and prints `Support: https://community.openclaw.ai/` while retaining Docs. CLI root/group/subcommand help regression passed, 1.48 seconds wall time. Full CLI file has one existing parse-error test failure, reproduced against the original `help.ts`; the added support assertion passes on the candidate and fails on the baseline.
- Agent support guidance regression passed, and assembled system prompt/prefix stability coverage passed. The support regression fails against the original implementation. Existing status-rendering coverage: 30 passed, 1 skipped.
- Core and UI TypeScript checks passed; touched TypeScript lint passed.
- Docs internal link audit: 15,767 links, zero broken. Docs glossary and UI/native localization verification passed.
- Swift syntax parse and pinned SwiftFormat passed. macOS touched-source SwiftLint passed. iOS test-file lint has three inherited findings reproduced on the baseline. Native runtime tests/screenshots remain unavailable here: no Android Java runtime, no generated iOS Xcode project or simulator devices; the full macOS suite was not run on the shared operator desktop.
- Docs anchor audit has the same five existing broken anchors on base and candidate, none in changed support pages. Ordinary internal route/link audit passes.
- CI: draft-time broad CI and native jobs were skipped, not passing runtime evidence. The PR is being marked ready under the explicit landing request so normal exact-head CI can attach; CI seconds remain unmeasured.
- Pinned local ClawSweeper completed on exact final head `51c13cab4889f599f0229b951dd60111a91ef7a1` against base `2f7572ad13d12d5d34d21adecf5198cbb0fbb39d`: checkout access verified, no actionable correctness/security findings, no low-value tests. Earlier test-quality observations were addressed. Native runtime evidence remains incomplete; the review explicitly requests native About and failed-update support-action captures. Report: `/Users/hrudolph/Data/clawsweeper-local-reviews/official-support-product-20261020-final-1610/0.md`.

### Visual proof

These captures use an isolated local test UI with a reserved example identity, not the live app. **Native captures remain outstanding and block merge under the screenshot completion gate.**

![Before: About](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7de950c-68a4-4d96-a3b8-d1326e5f545e)

![After: About](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98fe5ff1-6508-4ada-8b7d-c8fdaaa05c3e)

![Before: Help](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55086526-9385-4b77-ad45-3b61d6e17ed9)

![After: Help](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f40cc2c-7321-4be6-bd59-0671a4377c1f)

![Before: Apps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/042bbd5d-836c-49da-b46a-efd0289d1fa6)

![After: Apps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/043b0312-e1c6-431f-8d47-1c456679b927)

![After: About mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb4d4cdd-8b7f-4ff9-bd6f-cedb20d9e316)

### Scope and simplification

Reuses existing resource-link rows, menu entries, localization owners, and CLI footers. No new support service, state, configuration option, menu logic, or native transport was added. The only new production module is the requested canonical English support guide; test additions exercise the changed public links and assembled agent prompt. Exact changed/retained source inventory is recorded in the local handoff. Histories, release notes, Discord product integration docs, and downstream generated documentation are untouched.


### Landing evidence reassessment

The native edits add fixed HTTPS links through existing About link controls and change only the macOS failed-update action label and destination. They do not change the update driver, recovery state machine, browser transport, permissions, or configuration. Existing web/CLI, localization, Swift parse/format/lint and exact-head local review evidence remains valid; a full native suite or stable-upgrade matrix is not an additional local requirement for these literal link changes. Normal PR CI remains authoritative for its required checks.

The repository screenshot completion gate still applies to the rendered native additions. Before/after native About captures and the macOS failed-update action capture are not available and are not waived by the request to merge. Verified environment gaps: Android has no Java runtime; Xcode 27.1 is installed but has no simulator runtimes/devices, no generated iOS project, and no xcodegen; the paired iPhone is disconnected. The shared macOS operator desktop is not a qualified app-test sandbox. No native app, update, Gateway, release, or live Discord operation was performed.


### Product CI follow-up

The first ready-state CI run exposed a stale exact-footer assertion in the existing status report test. The follow-up changes only that expectation to include Support, retaining its redaction notice, self-service troubleshooting link, blank-line boundaries, diagnostics and ordering checks. The exact existing case reproduced the CI failure before repair, then the complete file passed 15 tests in 7.913 seconds wall time with operator OPENCLAW environment variables removed. Targeted formatting, lint and whitespace checks pass. Production bytes and earlier web screenshots are unchanged. Final follow-up head: 272accc3cffc4f9a9446cd857085d976d05fd5c4. Native screenshot gaps remain explicit; no native acceptance or full new CI success is claimed.

prs.body:
# OpenClaw pull request

## Title
fix(workshop): isolate detached review transcript writer

## What Problem This Solves
A detached Skill Workshop review can inherit the completed foreground turn's transcript-writer context. Because the review writes to a different internal session, persistence is rejected with `session writer claim changed before transcript persistence`.

The `hetzner-foundry` host running OpenClaw 2026.9.7 recorded this exact error four times on 2026-10-14. The newest occurred at 2026-10-14T13:10:56.720Z with trace `34567d6281ff337cb71d118348bcc7e5` and review run `skill-workshop-review:1f4461d0-6bdf-4fd5-8c4a-c73a352ce9b5`.

Upstream recipient: maintainers of `openclaw/openclaw`, especially the Skill Workshop background-learning scheduler owners reviewing issue #164279.

## Fix
`runWithGatewayDetachedWorkAdmission` creates independent Gateway work admission but does not clear AsyncLocal transcript-writer ownership. The production diff therefore keeps that admission boundary and changes only its callback from:

```ts
() => runSkillExperienceReviewInner(candidate)
```

to:

```ts
() => runWithoutOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites(() => runSkillExperienceReviewInner(candidate))
```

This uses OpenClaw's existing isolation primitive to remove the unrelated foreground ownership context. The review still establishes its own internal-session writer fence. Existing Gateway admission, drain refusal, and source transcript read fences are unchanged.

## Evidence
The added mechanism-level regression test installs a conflicting foreground writer claim, executes `runSkillExperienceReview` through the actual detached review boundary, and asserts the internal review-session commit. Before the production-line change, it fails with the exact writer-claim error. On the final branch:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  10 passed (10)
Duration  41.31s
```

Validation:
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/skills/workshop/experience-review.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- targeted oxlint: 0 warnings/errors
- formatting and `git diff --check`

Related report: #164279

## Isolated shipped-entry-point Gateway proof
Exact head `1bca8a61bc727b0baba693cd491cbb8c1007f140` was exercised in an isolated loopback-only non-production Gateway/profile using ordinary `chat.send` + `agent.wait` calls until the shipped scheduler naturally ran the delayed review. Direct redacted Gateway output:

```text

2026-10-14T14:43:16.528Z experience review finished: session=<redacted-proof-session> changes=0

prs.title: fix(copilot): use monotonic clock for isolated completion deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A copilot isolated-completion request can hang well past its configured timeout when the wall clock moves backward, or be killed early when it jumps forward. The completion now honors its real elapsed-time budget on the monotonic clock.

- Problem: `extensions/copilot/src/isolated-completion.ts` seeds the boundary deadline and reads the remaining budget with `Date.now()` (wall clock), while the consuming `setTimeout` in `raceWithTimeout` is monotonic. A wall-clock rollback of Δ inflates the remaining budget by Δ and delays the timeout by Δ; a forward shift prematurely rejects healthy completions.
- Solution: seed the deadline with `performance.now()` and read the remaining budget with `performance.now()`, keeping the whole boundary on one monotonic clock domain.
- What changed: `extensions/copilot/src/isolated-completion.ts` (2 lines); updated `isolated-completion.deadline-clock.test.ts` regression to use the shipped `runCopilotIsolatedCompletion` entry point through a complete typed pool fixture.
- What did NOT change: `timestamp: Date.now()` on the assistant message is kept as a wall-clock reporting field (not fed to any timer); the `remainingMs <= 0` guard stays on the same monotonic domain.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deadline was seeded once and reused across several `awaitWithinCompletionBoundary` calls (getPool → proxy → acquire → session), so a wall-clock shift between the seed and a later read distorts the remaining budget. Using `performance.now()` for both the seed and the read is the minimal fix that keeps the deadline immune to wall-clock adjustments. Alternative: reading `Date.now()` consistently — rejected because the consuming `setTimeout` is monotonic, so a mixed clock domain is the defect. Risk/non-goals: no change to abort semantics, error messages, or the reported assistant `timestamp`.

## User Impact

Copilot isolated completions now respect elapsed time: a stalled acquire still times out at the configured `timeoutMs` after any clock correction, instead of hanging or failing early. No configuration, output-format, or API changes.


## Evidence

**Real-transport proof** — shipped entry path through a real Copilot client over a real TCP loopback:

```
createCopilotAgentHarness (shipped export, extensions/copilot/harness.ts)
  → harness.runIsolatedCompletionV2 (shipped AgentHarnessV2 method)
    → await import("./src/isolated-completion.js") (shipped dynamic import)
      → runCopilotIsolatedCompletion (shipped plugin function, extensions/copilot/src/isolated-completion.ts:114)
        → pool.acquire → sdkFactory → new sdk.CopilotClient (REAL SDK client)
          → RuntimeConnection.forUri("127.0.0.1:PORT") (REAL TCP loopback socket)
            → JSON-RPC session.create frame (REAL RPC; peer never responds)
```

The `sdkFactory` wraps the DEFAULT factory: it loads the real Copilot SDK (`loadCopilotSdk`) and constructs a real `CopilotClient`, only injecting `connection: RuntimeConnection.forUri(loopback)` (and stripping `gitHubToken`/`useLoggedInUser`, which `forUri` forbids). The peer answers the SDK `connect` handshake (JSON-RPC over TCP, `Content-Length` framing) but never responds to `session.create`, so `pool.acquire → createSession` stalls on the real client transport. No live provider, no credentials — the transport is real TCP + real JSON-RPC, and the stall happens on the real `session.create` RPC.

Wall-clock skew is armed inside `runCopilotIsolatedCompletion` right after the boundary deadline is seeded (line 128) and before `remainingMs` is read (line 63). `performance.now()` stays real and monotonic. PRE-FIX source obtained by reverting the two `performance.now()` lines to `Date.now()` on disk (tsx overrides ESM loaders for plugin files, so the revert is a direct file edit, restored via `git checkout` after each run).

| Variant | Clock | Wall-clock skew | Elapsed to `TimeoutError` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST-FIX (the PR's fix) | `performance.now()` | +5000ms forward | **2057ms** | on-time ✓ |
| POST-FIX (the PR's fix) | `performance.now()` | −5000ms backward | **2036ms** | on-time ✓ |
| POST-FIX (the PR's fix) | `performance.now()` | none | **2060ms** | on-time ✓ |
| PRE-FIX (bug) | `Date.now()` | +5000ms forward | **51ms** | immediate timeout ✗ |
| PRE-FIX (bug) | `Date.now()` | −5000ms backward | **7061ms** | delayed timeout ✗ |

Configured budget: 2000ms. POST-FIX stays on the monotonic clock regardless of wall-clock skew (all three rows ~2s); PRE-FIX `Date.now()` is polluted by the skew — `remainingMs` goes negative (forward → 51ms immediate) or inflated (backward → 7061ms delayed, ~budget+5000ms).

### Raw terminal output (inline, current head 57359500fda4)

```
POST-FIX +5000ms forward:  wall clock jumped forward 5000ms; TimeoutError after 2057ms  outcome=on-time
POST-FIX -5000ms backward: wall clock rolled back 5000ms;  TimeoutError after 2036ms  outcome=on-time
PRE-FIX  +5000ms forward:  wall clock jumped forward 5000ms; TimeoutError after 51ms    outcome=immediate-timeout
PRE-FIX  -5000ms backward: wall clock rolled back 5000ms;  TimeoutError after 7061ms  outcome=delayed-timeout
```

**Regression test** — `isolated-completion.deadline-clock.test.ts` calls the shipped `runCopilotIsolatedCompletion` with a complete `CopilotClientPool` fixture. Only `Date`/`setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` are faked — `performance.now()` stays real and monotonic. Both rows assert the acquire is still pending after microtask flush (not prematurely rejected), then fires at the deadline timer.

What was not tested: live GitHub Copilot provider latency (no credentials). The loopback peer is a real TCP + real JSON-RPC transport; the `session.create` stall is a real transport-layer stall, not an injected `getPool` promise.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve whitespace in /codex bind --cwd paths
prs.body:
Closes openclaw/local-code-analysis#BUG-202

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a quoted workspace path with significant whitespace silently binds a Codex conversation to a different directory when passed via `/codex bind --cwd`.

- Problem: `normalizeOptionalString` in `parseBindArgs` and `requestedCwd?.trim()` in `resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd` both strip whitespace from the `--cwd` argument, so `--cwd "/repo/job "` becomes `/repo/job`.
- Solution: replace both trim points with the existing `readNonBlankString` helper, which preserves significant whitespace while rejecting blank-only input.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/command-handler-args.ts` (parser), `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-permission-policy.ts` (permission owner), `extensions/codex/src/commands.test.ts` (command-boundary regression via `it.each`).
- What did NOT change: blank-only input is still rejected, `isPathInside` containment is unchanged, default cwd resolution is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users who pass workspace paths containing significant whitespace via `/codex bind --cwd` will now have the exact requested directory bound. All other users are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filesystem path bytes are significant on Unix; trimming them silently selects a neighboring directory. `readNonBlankString` is the existing SDK helper that already encodes the intended "reject blank, keep content" contract, so no new owner or configuration option is needed. Production delta is +4/-3; test delta is +22/0 across 3 files total.

- Best fix: yes, both trim points must preserve path identity and the existing SDK helper supplies that behavior.
- Risk / non-goals: Windows `CreateProcessW` trims trailing whitespace from `lpCurrentDirectory` at the OS level; that is an OS limitation outside this PR's scope.

## Evidence

Input: `--cwd "/tmp/.../work/job "` (trailing space). Single continuous capture (`proof-202-gateway-native.mts`) on head `cc956be3e35` (Linux, Codex 0.162.1): `/codex bind` → shipped Gateway dispatch → binding store → shipped permission resolver → real Codex `thread/start` → MARKER read.

### Before/after matrix

|---|---|---|
| `parseBindArgs` cwd | `/work/job` (trimmed) | `/work/job ` (preserved) |
| Gateway binding `workspaceDir` (shipped SQLite) | `/work/job` (trimmed) | `/work/job ` (`endsWithSpace=true`) |
| `resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd` | `/work/job` (trimmed) | `/work/job ` (`endsWithSpace=true`) |
| native `thread/start` cwd | `/work/job` (wrong dir) | `/work/job ` (correct dir) |
| `MARKER.txt` read | `MARKER_NO_SPACE` (wrong) | `MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE` ✅ |

### Raw terminal output (inline, current head `cc956be3e35`)

```

[proof-202-gw-native] /codex bind dispatched (runId=idem-bind-53738137-189c-4b8f-9bd5-1983830aaa71)

[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd resolvedCwd="/tmp/.../work/job " endsWithSpace=true
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: thread/start params cwd="/tmp/.../work/job " (len=50)
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: initialize OK, userAgent=codex_vscode/0.162.1 (Linux Unknown; x86_64) dumb (bug202-gw-native; 1.0.0)
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: thread/start ACCEPTED, threadId=01a151da-9983-7c92-9766-0b7b5fa2aa59
[proof-202-gw-native] Part 2: native response cwd="/tmp/.../work/job " (len=50, endsWithSpace=true)

Key facts established inline (current head, no external retrieval): fix point #1 `workspaceDir=".../work/job " endsWithSpace=true` read from shipped SQLite; fix point #2 `permissionMode="read-only"` (truthy → exercises changed line), `isPathInside=true`, `resolvedCwd=".../work/job "`, real Codex 0.162.1 `thread/start ACCEPTED threadId=01a151da-...`, native `cwd=".../work/job " (len=50)`, `MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE ✅`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude/Codex Node session discovery reporting failures during background catalog refreshes, including healthy refreshes that briefly light the sidebar warning.

## User Impact

Healthy pending discovery keeps the existing session lists without manufacturing an error. A genuine failure remains visible during a pending retry and clears after a successful refresh, including an empty result on the next ordinary poll. Existing discovery settings do not need changing.

No authentication, pairing, session ownership, persistence, polling interval, or rendering style is changed. Local/Node deduplication and concurrent node-pairing collapse remain outside this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two verified failures occurred along the same background discovery path. Registered native work outlived the request's caller custody and failed with `Gateway caller authority is no longer active`. After repairing that lifetime, healthy pending discovery still returned `catalog_pending` through the error field, which the existing renderer treats as a failure.

Retain the original caller custody through registered native work, preserving revocation checks. Represent pending discovery separately and retain only the current failure in the existing bounded, caller-owned cache until a successful refresh replaces it. Keep the original per-host events and 30-second fallback. No snapshot event, refetch loop, new animation, or persistent failure history is introduced.

The former conditional polling patch is withdrawn by an ordinary commit, not a history rewrite. Its earlier synthetic tests did not establish the live cause because this installation never advertised the event on which that hypothesis depended.

## Evidence

### Current integration (2026-10-20)

Published head: `cc4f00526720c1e56df1258d5022b3c2552ce12c`. This normally merges the contributor head `bceb219022020194072f540849b2f8b8bfc9545f` with pinned main `c83c2e85f8bba2f9562eb30309742736a844a88d`. The existing fork branch was updated by a normal fast-forward push; no history was rewritten.

Independent P0–P3 review covered the complete 16-path feature delta and returned no actionable findings. A separate incremental review covered the final two test-only quality corrections. Those corrections rename a shadowed fixture and apply canonical formatting/import order; assertions and expected values are unchanged. Final focused formatting and lint passed for both corrected files. The unchanged portion retains its preceding scoped quality evidence.

Focused tests on the preceding source candidate passed 7 schema cases and 6 UI catalog cases. The Gateway custody run stopped during worker preparation before assertions; retention/budget tests did not execute. Those gaps remain open, and no longer timeout or weaker assertion was introduced. This does not prove the installed Mac preparation delay, live revocation, a full native journey, or an upgrade.

The automatic [CI run 39493978256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39493978256) completed successfully on this exact head: 71 jobs passed, 23 were skipped, and none failed. Skipped jobs are not execution proof. This is hosted CI evidence, not a new local custody/runtime result, a Mac installation or maintainer product selection/acceptance; those boundaries remain as stated above. Earlier runtime and CI observations below retain their original revisions and limits. No new private logs, screenshots, continuous-soak claim or bot review request is included.

### Earlier evidence

- **Actual Gateway before/after.** On source `b92e6a6eef77`, same-connection catalog requests returned `catalog_pending` with no host errors and retained sessions. After official updater adoption of `043af6f4c337`, requests at 0/30/60 seconds returned pending status without catalog or host errors. Both Node catalogs were populated at 30 and 60 seconds. These are normalized observations, not attached raw private logs.
- **Actual UI.** The existing browser loaded the new served asset; Claude/Codex Node sources were populated, with no warning in two DOM observations and a visual inspection. The reporter subsequently observed several normal refresh cycles without recurrence; exact duration and cycle count were not recorded. The automated continuous warning watch failed at the browser's CDP boundary after three seconds. No successful continuous recording or passed long-duration soak is claimed; sanitized before/after screenshots remain unavailable.
- **Canonical CI repair.** [Run 38637240846](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38637240846) failed the stored-password browser sign-in recovery case in UI shard 3/3 at merge `242af9167656` (head `4d9ee0513e34` into base `1af5d71f9b95`). Commit `6d2ad958a17b` adds three fixture lines: follow the existing Sign in path and wait for the visible Check again control to become enabled before simulating renewed access by focus. Exact credential, single-restoration and modal-close assertions remain. The 12 owner-file tests passed locally; formatter and diff checks passed. Local typed lint could not execute because declaration dependencies resolve outside the checkout; its guard was not bypassed. In [new-head run 38644718111](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38644718111), all three UI shards, lint, production types and test types passed. The original failed run remains failed; this is not proof of focus arriving during an already-pending probe.
- **Roster-budget CI repair; new CI not yet qualified.** [Run 38644718111, shard 116132565709](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38644718111/job/116132565709) failed at `352 <= 320` using pinned Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715` on Linux x64, merge `1e4dd5dae246` (head `6d2ad958a17b` into base `5930f05a68b6`). The exact merge reproduced the same failure on Windows/Node 24.20. Temporary tracing attributed 320 reads to an eagerly evaluated compatibility-owner fallback for already-qualified keys, plus 32 selection reads. Commit `a5b622e0004c` parses qualified keys first and returns the same normalized agent identity; other keys retain the existing strict fallback. After restoring all instrumentation and verifying the original test blob, the two owner suites passed 13/13 with no skips on that exact merge plus the one-function patch. Targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed. The bound and assertions are unchanged. This is Windows/Node regression evidence, not a Linux/Bun or current-head full-CI pass; the old run remains failed and new-head CI qualification is pending.
- **Regression controls.** The original caller-custody regression failed with the exact authority error before the lifetime fix and passed afterward; the revocation-negative control remained passing. The focused pending/failure/recovery budget suite passed 13/13, and the UI state suite passed 6/6, including preserving a real failure during retry and clearing it on success. Core/UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- **Independent source review.** Official Codex autoreviews covered the custody patch and the reduced status patch. The reduced patch's terminal result was `scoped-clean` through P3 with no actionable findings. The later three-line fixture correction also received `scoped-clean` through P3 against its exact diff and three complete production/helper contexts; that review did not include the complete test fixture. The one-function roster repair received a fresh `scoped-clean` review through P3 against its diff and seven complete public contexts, using the documented GPT-6 Sol fallback after GPT-6.1 account unavailability. These are source reviews, not runtime or full-repository proof.
- **Current published state and CI.** Head `bceb21902202`, based on `a46ecb4350fc`, is open, non-draft, and reported `MERGEABLE` on the latest readback. The older run [38717746541](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38717746541) remains failed: 66 jobs succeeded, 23 were skipped, and the required [checks-ui-e2e (2/4), job 116365017997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38717746541/job/116365017997) plus aggregate [openclaw/ci-gate, job 116371237604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38717746541/job/116371237604) failed. Its log showed `chat-pull-requests.e2e.test.ts:167` expected `#103469`, received `openclaw/openclaw#103469`. At the pinned base, main's formatter/renderer and component unit tests already use `owner/repo#number`; commit `e8eef4f656d0fa1010e2450a02e5327429adc265` introduced that contract, while the E2E assertions remained stale. A second short-label assertion in the same test would otherwise remain stale after the first was fixed. The required UI shard is classified `unknown` by the run's classifier (no matching job on main), so this is not a formal inherited-failure or main-baseline pass claim. Commit `bceb21902202` changes only those two E2E expectations to `openclaw/openclaw#103469`; product code, assertions about the surrounding UI behavior, and the Mac installation were not changed. The official Codex autoreview completed `scoped-clean` at P1 with no findings, using the permitted GPT-6 Sol fallback after GPT-6.1 was unavailable; its context included the changed E2E lines, formatter, renderer, and component unit tests, but not the complete surrounding E2E fixture. The affected E2E was not run locally because its linked dependencies resolve outside this checkout and the repository guard was not bypassed; `git diff --check` passed. Normal push/readback confirms head `bceb219022020194072f540849b2f8b8bfc9545f`. New canonical CI run [38724009644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38724009644) was `in_progress` at the latest check; no result is claimed yet. This test-only commit does not install the roster repair or change the earlier operational proof, which remains limited to the installed catalog candidate.

Related context is deliberately limited. #166652 concerns concurrent pairing collapse, not this reproduced catalog state/lifetime failure. #130115 owns Local/Node duplication. This PR does not close either issue or claim to complete the identity umbrella. @skyzhao1223's #172508 is an overlapping consumer-side alternative for the false warning that preserves the existing RPC encoding; it does not address the separate caller-custody failure. Maintainer selection or consolidation remains open.

prs.title: fix(android): connect through HTTPS proxies requiring Basic login
prs.body:
Related: #162240; related recovery report: #173578. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes Android onboarding and saved-Gateway connections through HTTPS reverse proxies requiring HTTP Basic, including recovery when a connected node does not give chat a verified user identity. ## User Impact Users can configure proxy login during manual or QR/setup-code onboarding, rotate a saved password, and recover from proxy or verified-identity failures without losing existing Gateway credentials. Chat/operator and phone/node connectivity are reported separately. HTTP Basic requires Android CA trust and hostname verification; a saved pin is additional. The proxy must authenticate Basic and strip its Authorization header before forwarding. Named operator roles also require administrator-configured verified identity on WebSocket upgrades. A LAN setup code and connected node do not establish that identity. Recovery opens a blank setup-code field and explains requesting a fresh code for the authenticated proxy address with `openclaw qr --url`. This implements HTTP Basic, not browser-only SSO/OAuth/OIDC. Android does not manufacture identity headers or weaken roles. Basic usernames and identity forwarding do not isolate history within one Gateway; mutually untrusted users need separate Gateways and isolated state. Connected/token-bearing Gateways permit same-username password rotation. Remove retains the username binding; changing username requires Forget and re-add. Forget clears Android-local credentials, role tokens, pins and cached chat, **not** persistent device identity, server pairing or server history. Re-add can reuse pairing and retrieve history still authorized by the Gateway. No live deployment configuration is changed. ## Why This Change Was Made The shared proxy form uses encrypted, destination-scoped storage. The repair reuses the admitted Add Gateway lifecycle, restores recovery from the existing registry, and commits proxy login before destructive setup replacement. Failed persistence preserves old authentication and the composer draft. Source icons use capability-checked, authenticated `controlUi.linkPreview`, with a globe fallback. The earlier native run exposed a late transport-close callback erasing the structured identity error. The connection attempt now retains ownership of failed-handshake diagnostics; successful responses still drain issued-token persistence before a real disconnect is reported. The October 20 maintainer review also found that Add Gateway silently dismissed a failed proxy Save or Remove for an already-saved destination. The confirmation now retains its staged action, displays the persistence error, and closes only after a successful retry; existing Gateway credentials, pairing and the composer remain untouched. Original implementation by @DonnieFi. Repair, scope decisions and verification with @IWhatsskill. ## Work sessions - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/261a2cb8-209d-4eb4-bda3-ae36c5b32e91) - [Native Android verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0c87876b-823a-435d-a74e-59e628d7e6ab) ## Evidence ### Camera review cancellation — a446c15d767847fa91a8d11c90e8f5328b36340e Canceling a scanned Gateway confirmation, including Android Back, now closes the camera preview and returns to **Scan QR code**. Reopening starts a fresh scan rather than silently ignoring subsequent codes. This adds one production lifecycle change; existing credentials and the previous recovery fixes remain unchanged. - **66 focused tests passed**, no failures/errors/skips: SetupQrSelectionTest (5), OnboardingFlowLogicTest (58), and OnboardingProxyRecoveryTest (3). Gradle process wall: 67.024s. The new camera cancellation regression takes 6.012s; the complete QR test class takes 11.498s. CI timing for this new commit is not yet available. - The identical new test on pre-fix production 3e7903ac8bf930c6f88845d0d713cb508ed7cce2 fails at the expected missing **Scan QR code** assertion after Cancel. The fixed test exercises the production-registered CameraX analyzer, real onboarding callbacks, Cancel, dialog Back, and subsequent scans without saving or connecting. - Repository-native scoped **ktlint passed** for both changed Kotlin files. After behavioral proof, only test import ordering changed; source equivalence was verified. Final whitespace check passed. - Fresh independent AutoReview with both complete changed files and dialog context: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. This completed before publication; no additional review was requested for the push. - Tests and captures ran on an isolated, secretless AWS runner, now released. Screenshots are **Robolectric native Compose**, not device screenshots. Camera hardware, real ML Kit decoding/executor scheduling, and live Gateway transport are not claimed. Current-head CI is separate from this local proof and from older results below. | Before: camera stranded after Cancel | After: scanner can be restarted | | --- | --- | | ![Before: canceled review leaves the one-shot camera open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b91def9-6ecc-4a45-a320-c7a7e81fe1b0) | ![After: canceled review returns to the Scan QR code action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92e9e1b3-d6c6-4802-976f-828136a3e76c) | ### Onboarding failure recovery and cleanup — `3e7903ac8bf930c6f88845d0d713cb508ed7cce2` Failed proxy-login persistence now displays the storage/header error, diagnostics and **Go back**, instead of remaining on Connecting. Existing Gateway, device and proxy credentials stay unchanged. Expired scanner/gallery codes use the scan-error dialog; another valid image reaches connection review. Removed the historical prototype HTML/image bundle, condensed duplicate documentation, and simplified duplicate path validation and test-fixture names. Runtime drawables, security policy and lifecycle checks remain. - **183 focused tests passed**, no failures/errors/skips: onboarding recovery, QR selection, onboarding logic, proxy forms, bootstrap authentication and session headers. Gradle process wall: 85.248s. All three new regressions fail on original `b8214567154995073dd81c60e1233660d7577c59` at their intended visible-error assertions. Per-case times: failedProxyCommitShowsActionableRecoveryWithoutReplacingSavedSecrets 6.715s; conflictingProxyHeaderShowsActionableRecoveryWithoutReplacingSavedSecrets 0.63s; onboardingExpiredGalleryCodeShowsErrorThenAcceptsAnotherImage 4.432s. CI times for this head are not available. - Pinned standalone **ktlint 1.8.0**, actual Android configuration: eight changed Kotlin files clean, exit 0. A control reproduces the earlier native Gradle finding. The only post-test source change is its missing blank line, exactly matching the native formatter output. This is not a Gradle-task rerun. - Independent AutoReview of the complete local delta plus unchanged persistence/recovery context: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Whitespace and document-link checks passed. - Tests ran on a secretless, no-role AWS runner, now released. These are production Compose screens rendered by **Robolectric native graphics**, not device screenshots. No new APK/device or live-proxy run is claimed; earlier device evidence retains its original source binding. - New-head CI is pending. Previous-head CI and security approval are not claimed for this commit. No manual CI dispatch or rerun was requested. #### Failed proxy persistence | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before: failed proxy persistence remains on Connecting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8a2d0e7-2c8d-4d1a-9eb9-993edc4232ab) | ![After: proxy persistence error and Go back](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e69ab114-d66c-479e-bcbd-f9c900cfae32) | #### Expired gallery code | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before: expired gallery code has no visible error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c900384-5d1a-46dd-8088-c04116ab3ce7) | ![After: expired-code dialog offers another image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a01cd03-378d-4a18-8b7a-bb4e40dead62) | ### Main synchronization — `b8214567154995073dd81c60e1233660d7577c59` At the requester’s direction, incorporated the current `main` snapshot `594eeb5223ef050dfbce67ad8e113f7056c6afca` (17 commits beyond the historical CI parent) into the existing contributor branch. Both integrations were conflict-free. The complete PR patch against this main snapshot is byte-identical to the previously reviewed patch against `304123679dd890c63f6f8612a69967f08b4fa146` (binary diff SHA-256 `0cca471a6cf8fa7d268e8129c625e8558932bcabddde9d90bde0f9de09dfca10`); the entire `apps/android` tree remains `bb6f8d6b02bfe5ed1a1907b032fe08e33fe056e0`. Whitespace validation passed. No conflict resolution or Android source/test/build input changed, so prior scoped review, tests and native evidence are retained with their original source bindings rather than repeated or relabeled as fresh execution. The PR has not been merged. **Previous-head CI passed:** [run 39462468274](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39462468274), attempt 1, on `b8214567154995073dd81c60e1233660d7577c59`: **40 jobs passed, 26 intentionally skipped, no failed or pending jobs**. Android Play, ThirdParty, Wear, ktlint and both 4 KiB/16 KiB native-access jobs passed. The CI-gate job and published `openclaw/ci-gate`, `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and `openclaw/dependency-review` statuses all passed. The original separate catalog timeout did not recur in this run; its underlying cause is not claimed fixed. Two superseded canceled dispatch/context checks in the aggregate display have successful replacements and are not failed CI leaves. ### CI follow-up — `1c3d8f4685e0db9d3b10f4143f9fa95abcfb391c` The follow-up integrates the exact main parent used by the failing CI run and changes only the QR integration test relative to that tested merge. No additional production behavior is changed by the repair. The scanner test now confirms the displayed HTTPS destination explicitly before expecting Pair Gateway, and verifies that scanning alone has not saved a Gateway, changed the manual host, started a connection, or invoked TLS. - Original CI: run [39446407061](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39446407061), attempt 1, tested merge `0770752449f5f2a513340935faaf4c5ec6d56a2e` (main parent `304123679dd890c63f6f8612a69967f08b4fa146`; PR parent `952b53fd37484e180ac87b610d977b7e071ae7f2`). Both Android flavors failed the same missing Pair Gateway assertion. - Reproduced that exact QR failure in both flavors and in the original full ThirdParty order (3,734 tests; only that QR failure). After the 12-line test correction: **121/121 tests passed in Play and 121/121 in ThirdParty**, no failures/errors/skips; complete focused runs took 106s and 109s. Coverage includes NodeRuntimeAgentSelectionTest, SetupQrSelectionTest and adjacent onboarding/identity-recovery tests. - Fresh independent AutoReview of the scoped delta: no actionable P0–P2 finding; five completed passes. Final source hash matches the isolated tested file. - Changed QR test case: 0.786s Play / 0.744s ThirdParty. Whole SetupQrSelectionTest class: 12.224s / 12.272s, including existing Compose coverage; no new test process, timers, sleeps or retries. Pinned standalone ktlint 1.8.0 checked the changed file with repository configuration: one file scanned, zero errors (565ms). Whitespace check passed. - **Original CI timeout (not reproduced or separately fixed):** the original ThirdParty job also timed out in NodeRuntimeAgentSelectionTest.publicationsRefreshOnlySelectedAgentCatalogsWithoutDiscovery while joining every newly observed runtime child, before consuming catalog requests. That test and relevant dispatch/cache owners are unchanged from the tested main parent. All 40 class tests passed in original focused Play/ThirdParty and the full original ThirdParty order; this is a failed reproduction, **not a fix**. Source inspection found that the broad join includes unrelated chat/cache work; the precise blocked child is unknown. No speculative synchronization change, timeout increase or removed assertion was applied. - Validation used a fresh secretless AWS Linux runner, SDK/build-tools 37, Gradle 9.7.1 and Temurin 21.0.12+8. CI declares Temurin 21.0.12+101.0.LTS; exact JDK-build parity is not claimed. The full repaired suite was not rerun; focused changed/sibling proof is above. No CI rerun or workflow dispatch was requested. Existing native screenshots, upgrade proof and earlier review remain linked below with their original source identities; they are not represented as a new native run of the integrated head. Current-head CI remains separate from local proof. ### Native repair proof — `952b53fd37484e180ac87b610d977b7e071ae7f2` **Real Android API 35 / x86_64 emulator, Caddy TLS/HTTP Basic, and a disposable OpenClaw Gateway.** - Reproduced Add Gateway → manual setup → **Already saved**: failed Save and Remove dismissed the confirmation silently on the old production code. On the repair, both retain the staged selection and show the storage error; retry without edits persists the change. Save reconnects through Basic authentication. Remove persists None; the still-protected proxy then refuses access as expected, while the preserved direct Gateway reaches Ready. - Direct same-signer upgrade from rebuilt stable source `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8` (`v2026.10.5`) to the repair preserved five preference/identity files byte-for-byte before first launch, plus Tide/Dark/125% settings, pairing and the saved TLS pin. Both direct and pinned-TLS connections reached **Connected / Ready** without credential re-entry or certificate re-acceptance. - **146 focused tests passed, zero failures/errors/skips** across GatewayBootstrapAuthTest (93), SecurePrefsCommitTest (6), MainViewModelTest (16), SidebarGatewayPickerTest (27) and GatewayProxyAuthenticationTest (4). New Save/Remove regression: **0.268s**; exact red-only test fails at the intended retained-request assertion. Cold focused build/run: 349s. Debug APK build: 149s. Four-file Kotlin lint: passed (56s); native i18n generation/verification: passed, 4,511 entries; whitespace check: passed. - Fresh scoped AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 finding. Final deslop inspection retained one persistence owner and removed the now-unused admission callback. Post-review changes are generated string inventory and test formatting only; production bytes match the tested/reviewed patch. No CI dispatch or rerun requested; current-head CI and required approvals are separate, not claimed green by local proof. **Upgrade limit:** this is a synthetic-signed debug rebuild of stable release source, **not** an official Android distribution or verified Play-production APK. No physical-handset or broader Android matrix claim. Strict full locale parity remains a previously documented gap; the inventory verification above is not a claim that every locale is translated. #### Failed Save — before / after Before: silent dismissal, old credentials unchanged. Targeted ktlint for GatewaySession.kt and GatewaySessionReconnectTest.kt passed (65.611s). - Earlier integrated candidate: **497 tests across 17 classes passed** (156.812s wall), all test sources compiled and broader scoped lint passed. Strict parity is not claimed green. - Fresh independent review completed all 23 passes. Its sole finding identified the known pre-fix index race; staging the exact reviewed guard/regression resolved it.
