The content-normalization conflict preserves main's shared `assignOtelContentAttr` helper and this PR's bounded normalization path. [Upstream `createDeferredCore` import repair `b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87) is included. | A registered `synthetic-private-prefix password="opaque-value` at the start of a log body, then 20,000 or 100,000 characters | keeps `synthetic-private-prefix password="`, then `***` | starts `synthe…alue` | starts `synthe…alue` |
| `postgres://deploy:` + a 5,033-character password holding a `/`, `@` past the lookahead, on all five export paths | password's first 32 characters exported | password masked | `deploy:***` |
| Tool input of 64 keys x 8 strings of 5,000 characters | the 64-character `max_redaction_work` summary | 70,135 characters (64 keys, 128 a string), 27,205,560 redacted, 2,687 ms | 66,715 characters (16 keys, 512 a string), 656,539 redacted, 102.9 ms |

Following the database URL grammar has one cost, pinned by a test: a credential-free `postgres://host:5432/path...` whose path runs past the window loses its port and path, but only in a string past the whole-string budget. Within the budget the string is redacted whole and keeps them, as on main.

The stall stays fixed. One model-call capture, `3425a53b077` (best of 7) against main's production code at `657f09fea18` (one run), same machine:

| Input | Main's code: redacted | Main's code | This head: redacted | This head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 200 tool results x 5 parts of 15,000 | 338,341,331 | 34.9 s | 2,114,200 | 276 ms |
| 200 tool results of 100,000 | 369,908,788 | 38.1 s | 2,091,962 | 245 ms |
| 138-message transcript, text only (1.6M) | 22,430,657 | 159 ms | 987,358 | 11.9 ms |
| the same plus six tool results with 4M-character images (25.6M) | 374,038,049 | 15.6 s | 987,940 | 30.7 ms |

On `4e5f4e1055c`, best of 7, the 200 x 5 parts capture redacts the same 2,114,200 characters in 246.7 ms. The transcripts are synthesized in the measuring test: 23 rounds of prose user turns, assistant turns with thinking, 20,000-60,000 characters of text and a tool call, tool results, and short follow-ups. `a98c2d54130` gives the same redaction counts on all four, and times within 6%.

**Against main's production code.** The 65-test file from `1c876fefe03` against main's `service-content-normalization.ts` and `service-genai-content.ts` at `27e3afbd8fc`, same M4 Pro: 14 failed, 51 passed. Main's file imports the redactor directly, so for this run its one import line points at the plugin barrel, where the test's counter sees it.

- 8 work cases fail because main's work doubles when every string doubles. Characters sent to the redactor for one capture, main's code against this branch (branch counts from a separate run at `40e00389277` that prints them):

  | Fixture | Main's code | This branch |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 6 tool results of 150,000 | 5,550,918 | 247,046 |
  | 200 tool results x 5 parts of 15,000 | 338,341,331 | 2,114,200 |
  | 200 tool results full of masked secrets | 248,588,788 | 6,284,762 |
  | log body of 150,000 | 150,000 | 8,192 |
  | log body full of masked secrets | 195,000 | 27,724 |
  | log body full of quoted secrets | 186,000 | 23,029 |

- The long-registered-secret case redacts 369,908,788 characters against a bound of 2,359,296, and the cap case exports main's truncation where this branch exports the `max_redaction_work` summary.
- The line-start assignment case fails with the password in `gen_ai.input.messages`.
- 3 of the 5 URL-password cases (log body and both tool call paths) fail on the mask shape at their first URL: main masks the 5,000-character `https://` password in the whole text as a token (`A1b2C3…pppp`), where this branch's window masks it as `deploy:***`. The password body is not in that export. The cases stop there, so the 10,000-character and `postgres://` URLs were not reached on those three paths.

Summed test time for the file's 65 tests on that machine, which is mostly redaction: 152.7 s on main's production code against 1.9 s here. The 200 x 5 parts case alone takes 88.4 s on main's code and 0.54 s here, and the long-registered-secret case 33.4 s against 0.20 s. Main's redactor changes since the last merge (#161480, #166701) don't change the picture: the capture path still sends it hundreds of millions of characters for one model call.

**Where the 150 s went.** In-gateway V8 CPU profile (`diagnostics.cpuProfile`) of one 159.1 s block on the affected gateway, before any of this:

- 97.9% inclusive in `recordModelCallFinished` -> `assignOtelModelContentAttributes` -> `safeJsonString`
- 89.7% in `truncateJsonTextForOtelAttribute`, 8.1% in `stringifyJsonForOtelAttribute`
- 85.4% self in `replaceRedactPattern`, 8.2% self in `replacePatternBounded`, 2.0% in `matchAwsSecretAccessKeys`
- By caller: `assignJsonAttribute` (the `gen_ai.*` and `input.value` pair) 91.2 s, `normalizeOtelContentValue` (`openclaw.content.*`) 64.5 s

The sample timeline shows 3 whole-value redaction passes (3.7-4.7 s each) and 14 truncation attempts at about 10 s each. With `captureContent: false` the same session ran at under 1% CPU with a 22 ms maximum event-loop delay.

**Before/after on the real code path, measured before the merge.** The two tables below are from `452a23f4716` and earlier heads against main as of 09-27 (`1d7e5b0813d`), on an Apple Silicon laptop with Node 24.18. I have not re-timed them at this head. Main's redactor has changed since then (#161480, #166701), so its wall times here may not match current main. The character counts depend on the plugin's code, and the control above reproduces main's count for four of the rows at `27e3afbd8fc` (150,000, 5,550,918, 338,341,331 and 369,908,788).

`assignOtelModelContentAttributes` with capture on, deterministic synthetic 138-message agent transcripts (thinking, text, tool calls and tool results, seven assistant turns of 20-60K characters), 2-3 runs each, no configured `logging.redactPatterns`:

| Transcript (serialized size)                                    | Before       | After     | Characters sent to the redactor |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------- | ------------------------------- |
| 1.4M chars, text only                                           | 888-1,020 ms | 59-68 ms  | 16.9M -> 0.90M                  |
| 25.4M chars, same text plus six tool results with 4M-char images | 29.9-32.5 s  | 90-108 ms | 473.6M -> 0.96M                 |

For both transcripts every exported attribute was byte-identical before and after (sha256 compared per attribute), through `452a23f4716`.

With two configured rules (`acme-internal-[a-z0-9-]+` and `api[_-]?key`), the cost fixtures from the test file and the two transcripts above, one in-process run each. Every exported attribute matched main (sha256 per attribute):

| Input | Redacted on main | Redacted here | Main | Here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| log body of 150,000 | 150,000 | 150,000 | 13 ms | 14 ms |
| log body of 5M | 5,000,000 | 5,000,000 | 431 ms | 463 ms |
| tool output of 5M | 5,000,000 | 5,000,000 | 418 ms | 412 ms |
| 200 tool results x 5 parts of 15,000 | 338,341,331 | 30,235,162 | 27.6 s | 2.7 s |
| 6 tool results of 150,000 | 5,550,918 | 1,899,590 | 473 ms | 164 ms |
| 200 tool results of 100,000 | 369,908,788 | 40,248,762 | 32.2 s | 3.5 s |
| 6 tool results of 3M | 108,150,918 | 36,099,590 | 8.5 s | 2.8 s |
| tool input object, 64 x 8 strings of 5,000 | 27,205,560 | 2,630,135 | 2.2 s | 198 ms |
| 1.4M-char transcript | 24,371,528 | 2,303,890 | 237 ms | 29 ms |
| 25.4M-char transcript | 480,824,887 | 50,325,988 | 11.3 s | 1.2 s |

JSON attributes sent 2.9-11.2x fewer characters to the redactor than main; log bodies and tool outputs sent the same.

**Tests.** New `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service-content-normalization.test.ts`, 102 tests, `src/logging/redact-open-secret.test.ts`, 22 tests, and `test/diagnostics-otel-registered-secret.test.ts`, 2 tests. The registered-value case is a root test because a plugin test cannot register an arbitrary value; it reaches the normalizer through a new test-only `extensions/diagnostics-otel/test-api.ts`, since root tests may only import a plugin's public barrels. Redaction work is counted by wrapping the plugin's own `redactSensitiveText` import, not by timing:

- Redaction work does not change when every string in the capture doubles, and stays under the attribute-budget bound: large tool outputs, 200 tool results x 5 parts, and a long log body.
- A token that starts before the export cut is still masked, on all five export paths (message part, tool result, log body, and the two 128K tool call paths).
- A private key cut off before its END line is not exported.
- A line-start `password=...` in content that fits untruncated is masked in `gen_ai.input.messages` and `openclaw.content.input_messages`.
- A quoted secret whose closing quote lies past the lookahead is masked, for each quoted rule, on the message part, tool result (including the 128K string paths) and log body exports; also behind a run of zeros, with 260-300 spaces between key and quote, and wherever the probe's key context starts (a sweep over the cut offset).
- A fixed-length secret the cut splits after earlier masks shorten the window is masked.
- Cost rows for a long escape run, a long separator run, and secret-dense quoted text keep the probes bounded.
- A JWT that starts 200 characters before the cut, with its signature past the lookahead, is masked on all five export paths, for a 6,364-character token with compact claims, a 6,780-character one with indented claims (payload `ewog...`), and the compact one with an `EYJ` prefix. Base64url JSON with no dot that crosses the window end is kept.
- An `ATATT`, `ATCTT3xFfG` or lower-case `atatt` token, and a `code=` form value, that start 200 characters before the cut with their `=` suffix or `&state=x` 5,120 characters later are masked on all five export paths.
- A `code=` form value whose redaction window ends at the `&` of its next pair, or inside its key (`&st`), is masked on all five export paths.
- `findTruncatedSecret` reports the secret's start for each covered rule cut before its closing part, the closing quote for a JSON secret and a quoted form value, and the value's start for a form value before its next pair's `&` or a clipped next key. It reports nothing for a complete URL password, a web URL's port, a dot-free `eyJ` run, a token prefix inside a word or in a `;base64,` data URL, a form key no rule masks, a form value before its whole next pair or before `&` and a digit, or a closed private key.
- A registered secret longer than the lookahead (4,608 characters, registered through `generateSecureToken({ redact: true })`) that starts 10 characters before the cut is masked on the same five paths.
- With `logging.redactPatterns: ["SECRETSTART[q]{5000}END"]`, a match that starts 200 characters before the cut and ends past the lookahead is masked on the message part, tool result and log body exports. The two 128K tool call paths are left out of this one case: configured patterns run in 16,384-character chunks (`src/logging/redact.ts`, `replacePatternBounded`) and that cut is a chunk boundary, so a whole-value pass cannot match across it on main or here. That is read from the code, not measured at this head.
- A URL password of 5,000 or 10,000 characters that starts 200 characters before the cut, with its `@` past the lookahead, is masked on all five export paths, for `https://` and `postgres://` URLs, and so is a `postgres://` password holding a `/`, past the budget and within it. A port and path that cross the cut are kept for `https://`, and for `postgres://` within the whole-string budget; past it a `postgres://` port and path are dropped.
- With a 65,536-character secret registered, a model call with 200 tool results of 100,000 characters stays under the model-call work bound.
- An object of 512 strings of 5,000 characters, whose smallest truncation fits the attribute but not the redaction cap, exports 16 of its 64 keys with 512 characters a string and no token body. With a 1,048,576-character secret registered, a 2,000,000-character tool input exports the `max_redaction_work` summary.
- A message past 4x the attribute holding a JWT with a 600,039-character payload is exported whole and masked, with 320 or 22,400 characters of text after the JWT; a registered value holding `password="` at the start of a log body is masked whole, within and past the whole-string budget.
- JSON over the budget that fits once masked is exported whole, including one long string with tokens across the 16,384, 32,768 and 65,536 offsets; a value under 4x that does not shrink is truncated within its work bound; one just over 4x gets no whole-value pass; and a token at the cut is still masked after a whole-value pass that does not fit.
- The existing cut cases now put 1,100,000 characters after the cut, past 4x and past the whole-string budget, so they keep exercising the windows.

Branch history, each measured at the time: the two cut-boundary tests fail on this branch if the lookahead is set to 0 or the private-key guard is removed, and removing the 8x cap fails the 200 x 5 case. 13 open-quote tests fail on `87eb422f779`, the first version of this branch, and the later ones fail on the commit before their fix. The 5 registered-secret tests fail on `e3bfb598ff6` with the secret's first 10 characters in the export. The 5 JWT tests fail on `a6477692e1d` with the JWT header in the export, and the indented-claims token fails on `a395b25f21d` on both 128K tool call paths. The base64url case fails if any `eyJ` run is masked. The 3 configured-pattern tests fail on `b6a7955897d` with `SECRETSTART` in the export. The 5 URL-password tests fail on `4ab95960e9d` with the password in the export. The 65,536-character cost test fails at 26,667,962 characters if the cap counts only the 4,096-character minimum lookahead, and the summary test gets `max_attribute_size` on `3c9a420fc33`.

`getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` is covered in core by `src/logging/secret-redaction-registry.test.ts` (1 test): the length follows registration, drops when the longest value is evicted at 512 registrations, and returns to 0 on reset. Keeping the cached length across membership changes fails the first after the eviction (`expected 32 to be 24`). `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()` is covered in `src/logging/config.test.ts`: true for a configured list, false for an empty one, which keeps the default rules. Treating an empty list as configured fails it (`expected true to be false`).

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/diagnostics-otel
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/logging/config.test.ts src/logging/secret-redaction-registry.test.ts src/logging/redact.test.ts src/logging/redact-open-secret.test.ts
```

**Test cost.** `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on an M4 Pro, Node 26.10.0 (the first two at `3425a53b077` merged with main, the other two at `40e00389277`):

| file | wall | Vitest duration | tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service-content-normalization.test.ts` | 15.0 s | 12.8 s, 29% of it in tests | 82 |
| `test/diagnostics-otel-registered-secret.test.ts` | 8.9 s | 6.7 s | 2 (new) |
| `secret-redaction-registry.test.ts` | 1.6 s | 0.53 s | 2 (1 new on this head) |
| `config.test.ts` | 1.6 s | 0.52 s | 10 (1 new in this PR) |

Summed test time for the normalization file is 3.6 s for 82 tests, against 2.5 s for 72 at `a98c2d54130`. The 13 cases for ClawSweeper's latest review take 0.59 s together; the slowest, the capped 512-string object, takes 0.23 s. The cut fixtures carry 1,100,000 characters after the cut so they stay on the window path; within the whole-string budget each would redact its whole string. At `70e38024d0b`, on the shared M4 Pro at load 12 to 19, the 92-test normalization file took 10 to 22 s wall across three runs and `redact-open-secret.test.ts` 1 to 2 s.

**CI.** Run 37976075567 on `a98c2d54130` (merged into main `164210c355e`) is red on five jobs, none in this diff. Four trace to main commits that main has since repaired; the fifth did not reproduce:

- `checks-node-changed-3`: `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive.gateway.test.ts` > "migrates local onboard plugin install records in the setup write", `TypeError: lease.assertCurrent is not a function`. Main's #167702 (`f4cb17e8408`) added the `lease.assertCurrent()` call and the onboarding fixture still fabricated the older lease shape. Main fixed the fixture in `e69931d6e6a`, after that base.
- `checks-ui-e2e` 1/9, 7/9 and 8/9: `chat-session-prefetch-gating`, `chat-flow.history-recovery` and `session-prefetch` (`expected +0 to be 1`, `Timed out waiting for 1 chat.history requests`). Main's #167906 (`b0fb3ac3321`) made history prefetch intent-only, 23 minutes before the run; main updated the three tests in `8cc90d08c0a`.
- `checks-ui-e2e` 2/9: `chat-widget-sandbox.e2e.test.ts`, `elementHandle.hover: Timeout 22ms exceeded` at the end of a 41.7 s run. Not reproduced: 3 of 3 passes at about 17 s on main alone and 3 of 3 with this branch.

Controls on the M4 Pro. Main alone at that base `164210c355e`, with none of this PR's code: the onboarding file 1 failed, 17 passed with the same error and stack, and the three UI files 3 failed, 5 passed with the same messages. This head merged with main `f8239ea9470`, which has both fixes: onboarding 18/18, the three UI files 8/8, the widget file 3 of 3. This PR changes no file under `ui/`, `src/commands` or `src/plugins`. The earlier red on `452a23f4716` (run 36369333378, `session-accessor.sqlite-cleanup-race.test.ts`) is not among this run's failures.

**Risks.**

- The whole-value pass covers JSON up to 4x the budget, and past it a value whose size comes from strings the window cut open inside a secret, up to 8x the budget of such strings per attribute. Any other value past 4x whose redacted JSON would still fit, which needs masking to remove more than three quarters of it, is exported truncated where main exports it whole: knowing its masked size means redacting all of it, which is the work this PR removes.
- That pass is extra main-thread work for every captured value between 1x and 4x the budget, whether or not it ends up fitting: at most 8x the budget per JSON attribute, about 2.1M characters for a model call's two input serializations. Measured above on an M4 Pro: +15 ms for prose and +172 ms for unbroken alphanumeric runs. Not measured on slower hardware. Main redacts the same values whole and then again for each truncation attempt.
- With configured `logging.redactPatterns`, a value between 1x and 4x that fits once redacted now exports whole, as on main, where before it was clipped. Configured patterns run in 16,384-character chunks on long strings (see the chunking bullet below), so a configured match split by a chunk boundary deep in such a string is exported, as it is on main.
- A clipped string is no longer redacted past its lookahead, unless `logging.redactPatterns` is set. Quoted values, private keys, JWTs, URL passwords, Atlassian tokens, form first-pair values and registered secrets that run past the lookahead are masked from their start. The check is each core rule's own matcher, so whatever that rule could still match is dropped: base64url data with an `eyJ` prefix in any letter case and a dot, a run starting with `ATATT` or `ATCTT3xFfG` at a token boundary, and the value of a form key the core rule masks, when they cross the window end. Not covered: `SG.` keys, Slack webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens and `FlyV1 fm<digits>_` also need text after an unbounded run, but that run is an identifier (key id, team and bot ids, bot id, version) and would have to pass 4,096 characters before the secret part reaches the export. Within the whole-string budget such a string is redacted whole instead, as on main. Not covered: a JWT whose header alone runs past the lookahead exports its header up to the cut (the header carries JOSE parameters, not claims or the signature).
- Past the whole-string budget, a database URL's port and path that run to the window end without whitespace or `@` are dropped from the port, and a web URL's port followed by a run without `/`, whitespace or `@` to the window end is dropped from the port. Main keeps both.
- Gateways with configured `logging.redactPatterns` keep main's whole-value redaction and main's attributes, so a large model call still blocks the main thread for seconds there: 3.5 s for 200 tool results of 100,000 characters, against 32.2 s on main, measured on 09-27.
- Configured patterns still run in 16,384-character chunks with no overlap on text over 32,768 characters (`src/logging/redact-bounded.ts`), so a configured match crossing a chunk boundary is missed. The 128K attributes' cut at 131,072 is one of those boundaries. Main behaves the same; built-in rules scan the whole text since #161480.
- Without configured rules, the 8x cap keeps less content than main when a transcript clips hundreds of strings. With the test file's 200 tool results x 5 parts, `openclaw.content.input_messages` is 25,379 characters against 101,491 on main (`gen_ai.input.messages` is the same 119,491 on both), for 2.1M characters of redaction against 338M. An object of 512 strings of 5,000 characters exports 66,715 characters (16 of 64 keys, 512 characters a string), where main redacts 27.2M characters and exports 70,135 (all 64 keys, 128 characters a string). The 138-message transcripts above are unaffected.
- A long registered secret widens every clipped string's window by its length, so redaction work grows with it and JSON attributes keep fewer items to stay under the cap. Measured before the merge, without configured rules, with the longest registered surface form at each length:

  | Longest registered secret | Log body of 5M: redacted | Tool output of 5M: redacted | 200 tool results of 100,000: redacted / results kept in `gen_ai.input.messages` | 6 tool results of 3M: redacted / export |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 4,096 or less | 8,192 | 135,168 | 2,091,962 / 200 | 247,046 / all 6 |
  | 6,144 | 10,240 | 137,216 | 1,660,238 / 100 | 271,622 / all 6 |
  | 20,000 | 24,096 | 151,072 | 2,113,338 / 50 | 437,894 / all 6 |
  | 65,536 | 69,632 | 196,608 | 1,640,618 / 10 | 984,326 / all 6 |
  | 1,048,576 | 1,052,672 | 1,179,648 | 2,166,058 / 10 | 126 / `max_redaction_work` summary |

  1,048,576 is the default file-provider `maxBytes` (`src/secrets/resolve.ts`). Log bodies and tool outputs keep their full budget in every row. The last cell predates `3425a53b077`, which tries fewer object fields before the summary; I have not measured that row again.
- This adds three public plugin SDK functions in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core`, `findTruncatedSecret()`, `getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` and `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()`, and raises the public export and callable budgets by three each (3,742 and 2,195 after merging main `4a05c7c5d59`). The first returns a position and a closing quote for text the caller already holds; the second returns a length and no values; the third returns whether `logging.redactPatterns` is set. Plugins run in-process as trusted code (SECURITY.md, "Plugin Trust Boundary"). I didn't have core mask a partial registered value at the cut instead, because that matcher would tell a caller whether some text is the start of a registered secret. `src/logging/secret-redaction-registry.ts` is in the credentials tier of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`, so the new head needs a maintainer's `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.
- `max_redaction_work` is a new `reason` value in the truncation summary. Main has no redaction cap. It is now reached only when even one string's window is over the cap, as with a 1,048,576-character secret registered.
- Bounded masking lives in the plugin, which asks the shared redactor about whole strings and probe text; the alternative is one bounded operation on the shared redactor, which would be a different public SDK function than the two this PR adds. That is a maintainer decision this PR does not take.

prs.title: fix(release): recover FRV before plan seal
prs.body:
## Summary

- checkpoint the exact attempt-one FRV preparation inputs before execution-plan sealing
- restore publication admission and seal a final plan from that immutable checkpoint when no final plan exists
- preserve attempt-one child identity while digest-binding and authenticating the later sealer attempt

## Ledger

Fixes RRI-61: failures before immutable plan sealing previously had no supported FRV recovery path.

## Safety

- the recovery artifact is scoped to the same workflow run and attempt 1, and cannot be overwritten
- retries validate frozen source/publication admission against the current request without new registry observations
- recovered plans retain parentRunAttempt 1 and record a separate sealParentRunAttempt
- final-plan publication remains non-overwriting and requires a successfully uploaded/restored attempt-one checkpoint

## Validation

- 285 focused FRV workflow/state/publication/cancellation tests passed (2 skipped)
- package workflow contract tests for the changed paths passed
- full package workflow suite: 564 passed; one unrelated local failure because the host lacks the zip executable
- scripts typecheck passed
- oxlint passed
- workflow YAML parse and git diff checks passed
- independent semantic review: no P0/P1/P2 findings

prs.title: fix(subagents): unblock startup while interrupted runs recover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delayed subagent registry activation after a Gateway restart leaves interrupted child runs to reconcile.

## User Impact

Startup no longer waits for interrupted child settlement after restoring source custody and completion ordering. Recovery remains tracked for shutdown, excludes duplicate attempts, and checks that queued work still belongs to the current Gateway. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requester groups already activate concurrently, but interrupted children within each group were recovered serially and awaited by activation. The existing sweeper now owns that background work, with a shared limit of eight recoveries. The existing obligation index still selects activation work; completed history with unresolved requester claims must retain its custody restoration.

Recovery also reuses the physical SQLite path already admitted by its session reader, removing redundant target resolution. Startup subspans are cumulative across groups, so their sum can exceed activation wall time; interrupted settlement now has a separate background trace.

Runtime source changes are +112/-109 lines (net +3), mostly moving the existing coordinator body inside bounded scheduling. The small growth preserves shutdown drainage and error reporting while deleting repeated target preparation. Benchmark support is separate from runtime code.

## Evidence

- Regression is red with the old awaited activation and green with this change: activation still waits for custody, then returns while shutdown drains recovery.
- Recovery regression proves eight concurrent slots across requester groups, duplicate exclusion, one finalization per live run, and no queued preparation after Gateway retirement.
- Focused files passed: restart recovery (84), persistence resume (24), sweeper lifecycle (9), startup trace (16).
- Changed-file formatting and lint passed; one targeted core typecheck passed using the repository's native checker.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. No full local suite or build; broad validation is delegated to PR CI.

Four simultaneous A/B pairs on an isolated Linux sandbox, with exclusive measurement lock, 16 CPUs per side and swapped CPU halves. A is `8f0973e37405`; B adds this runtime patch. Subsequent rebases do not change the measured registry, startup-trace, session-reader, or benchmark files. Times are milliseconds; deltas are candidate minus baseline.

| Pair | Activation A → B | Activation delta | Spawn → /readyz A → B | Readiness delta | Last recovery A → B |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1600.1 → 1083.2 | -516.9 | 6564.1 → 6626.3 | +62.2 | 7790.6 → 7528.5 |
| 2, swapped | 1840.7 → 1254.5 | -586.2 | 6488.3 → 6560.5 | +72.2 | 7706.8 → 7441.4 |
| 3 | 1682.6 → 1024.3 | -658.3 | 6089.4 → 6232.4 | +143.0 | 7488.7 → 7195.2 |
| 4, swapped | 1732.0 → 942.4 | -789.6 | 6298.5 → 6427.8 | +129.3 | 7502.3 → 7212.9 |

Mean paired activation improvement: **637.8 ms (37.2%)**. Last recovery improves **277.6 ms (3.6%)**. Spawn-to-ready is **101.7 ms slower (1.6%)**, consistently in these four pairs; this is a small measured tradeoff, not a readiness speedup. Readiness is a separate earlier gate; these measurements do not establish the cause of the small readiness difference. All eight runs passed the recovery invariants. CPU busy across the measured halves averaged 8.6–9.3% per pair (context, not an exclusion criterion); sandbox dirty pages remained well below 2 GiB.

The reproducible fixture has 86 retained obligations, eight running/interrupted children across two active requester cohorts, and a writer killed after committed SQLite writes. It verifies eight unique recovery events, eight terminal error outcomes, retention of all 86 records, and preservation of 78 completed outcomes. It uses missing-source reconciliation and does not measure successful restoration of real operator authority. Binding remains serial within each requester group because it restores source custody; successful authority restoration awaits local profile, paired-device and requester-session reads, not a remote service. This fixture therefore does not reproduce the incident's much slower successful-authority bind path; SIGKILL targets the fixture writer, not a predecessor Gateway/model turn. The first smoke failed before registry activation because a renamed baseline build directory prevented worker resolution; its timings are excluded.


A separate baseline-only diagnostic used canonical synthetic profiles and captured operator recovery snapshots. An observer forwarding the original binding operation confirmed eight successful authority installs; canonical decoding afterward confirmed all 86 original rows and eight terminal interruption outcomes. Its trace reported authority restoration 288.2 ms and binding 306.8 ms. This is diagnostic evidence only: the observer moved an import earlier, the standard report parser failed on legitimate completion envelopes after shutdown, and spawn-to-ready was not retained. A parent continuation reached an unavailable-model lookup and stopped before provider invocation. Paired-device restoration and a real model turn interrupted across a predecessor Gateway remain untested. This does not reproduce or explain the full reported slow successful-authority path.

GitHub Codex review and ClawSweeper reported no actionable findings on the original pushed runtime patch (`a25d06d88a6d802c76be2d37ce56ae488cdc7b97`).

The first CI run caught a test-support mock-export ratchet failure caused by the changed admitted-reader fixture. The fixture now preserves the real module exports, and the canonical ratchet generator removed its obsolete baseline entry (7,983 → 7,982). No runtime code changed in this CI repair. The affected recovery file passed again (84 tests; 23.16 s Vitest wall time, including a cold compiler cache), changed-file formatting/lint passed, and independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects.

## Owner acceptance

**ACCEPT — October 20, 2026.** The owner accepts the measured tradeoff: activation improves **37.2% (1.714 → 1.076 s)** across four paired comparisons, against **1.6% (+102 ms)** slower spawn-to-ready. The readiness increase is small relative to Team's approximately 19 s readiness time. Landing is authorized when the required checks pass; proven unrelated failures may use the established inherited-failure landing policy. Pending checks are not waived.

## Final CI and landing

Merged as [`2bb2af2355b31d294534d4e59ae7b24d782a38dc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2bb2af2355b31d294534d4e59ae7b24d782a38dc) after the required gate passed on `03a47b646b7fea971a31ee057845e8a36f5440e9`. [CI run 39506992997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39506992997) completed with 48 successful jobs, 25 skipped jobs, and no failures. The repaired baseline ratchet, changed-code checks, and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. Runner assignment delayed the 16- and 32-vCPU jobs; no CI reruns or inherited-failure exception were needed.

prs.title: fix(ui): prepare mascot inputs before drawing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Rendering the mascot in Custodian and other lazy pages emits Solid strict-read warnings because its animation effect prepares reactive inputs, then its apply callback and native callbacks read those reactive values again.

## User Impact

No visual or interaction change. The mascot retains mood and tease timing, high-DPI sizing, theme replacement, reduced motion, visibility pauses, and animation cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing effect now consumes its prepared inputs. Three plain committed values—drawing size, optional reduced-motion pose, and playback eligibility—serve the asynchronous canvas frame and observer callbacks. They are native animation inputs, not a second reactive presentation store. The animator remains the gesture/clock owner; visibility changes still resume playback without resetting tease timing.

The canvas effect remains an allowed external-system synchronization. No shared primitive owns this timestamp-driven drawing loop. No imports, lazy boundaries, tags, classes, CSS, or domain owners change.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Native mascot suite on original production | All three cases fail specifically on `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED`; drawing/lifecycle assertions pass |
| Native mascot suite on fix | 3/3 pass; after main integration: 56 ms cases, 2.87 s Vitest / 4.58 s wrapper |
| UI types (`pnpm tsgo:ui`) | Pass |
| Test types (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-components.json --noEmit`) | Pass after the type-only fixture repair |
| Targeted lint, format, diff check | Pass |
| Production Knip | Files/dependencies pass. Full export check exits 1: only `extensions/agentsapi/config.ts: DEFAULT_NATIVE_TOOLS`, reproduced identically on clean merge base `c7387f7f8bf1` |
| Independent review | Canonical isolated P0–P2 review: scoped-clean; no actionable findings |
| Wave-zero guard | Pass; no baseline changes |
| Broad proof | Full `ci:full` [39509539042](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39509539042) passed for `26004caaa380`: all 65 jobs complete, no failures, including both real-Gateway shards |
| CI performance job 118927330861 | Head startup **325708 B gzip / 7 JS requests**, CSS **38445 B / 1 request**. The passing job emits a startup warning above its 325166 B limit; this is not a strict-green claim |
| Same-runner route comparison | Chat **1447466 → 1447512 B (+46)**; New **1005301 → 1005340 B (+39)**; startup CSS unchanged. Actual base startup-JS bytes are not printed by the report |
| Visual proof | No visual/styling change; canvas inputs and lifecycle tested directly |

Touched-file production LOC: **150 → 153 (+3)**; tests: **79 → 135 (+56)**. The small production increase makes the imperative callback boundary explicit. Checklist counts: effect **1 → 1** (canvas animation); controllers, render effects, `untrack`, direct listeners, queries, `flush`, and owner capture APIs **0 → 0**. No guard baseline increase.

Related: #178593 (wave-zero survivor audit).

Initial CI run [39474603479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39474603479) passed the UI suites but found TS2352 in the new canvas fixture: inferred Vitest mock members prevented its canvas-context assertion. The fixture now names the two canvas method signatures with `Pick`; no runtime values or assertions changed. The failed UI-components test-type graph passes locally. Replacement CI passed this repaired type graph.

Replacement run [39478166263](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39478166263) has one unresolved failure: `Control UI catalog publication with a real Gateway > opens Settings pickers from publication and acquires only on Refresh or Retry`, `command-palette-catalog.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts:350`, expected 3 acquisitions but received 4. Latest completed scheduled main run 39476345087 passes the matching job; this is not classified as inherited. Its full-label run 39487705697 passed and it landed as `c7387f7f8bf163b89d4cee56f2fc7a43db3421be`. This branch now includes that landed main commit. Both mascot files are byte-identical to the prior reviewed repair; a frozen install, UI typecheck, affected test-type graph, all three focused tests, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. Fresh full CI 39509539042 passed for the integration head at 23:14:01 UTC on 2026-10-20. The historical extra request’s owner remains unproven; no inherited-failure waiver is claimed.

Performance evidence: [control-ui-performance job 118927330861](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39509539042/job/118927330861) compared CI merge `5a8ef4b63860f34a9b514b55c71680b06d7720a2` with base `8496db795978e95001800d7971778357ed990054` on one runner (Node 24.21.0, Vite 8.3.4, Pako 3.0.2). prs.title: fix(sessions): context token count stays stale for the whole of a long agent turn
prs.body:
Related: #164550

## What Problem This Solves

The session's context count (`totalTokens`) can stay at its pre-turn value throughout a long embedded agent turn. This change publishes the latest settled model call's prompt context while the turn is running, so status readers can follow it. Turn completion still writes the final accounting result.

Current head: [`a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33), tree `8c12cdbff4ede6b87277c5f43317dac3876f5c30`. This merges the preceding head `7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf` with upstream `92638b29a6f2115661217498a8d5767e85fd0235`, preserves the upstream cleanup changes and adds a prompt-failure drain regression. The normal push was verified through the fork ref and PR API at 21:03:49 UTC on October 20. [CI run 39497256630](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630), attempt 1, completed successfully: 70 jobs passed and 27 skipped, with no failed jobs. The complete inventory was read at 23:17:13 UTC on October 20; earlier CI and measurements retain their original revisions. The Goal accounting policy is unchanged.

## User Impact

The embedded runner publishes each available settled context snapshot. The latest snapshot can replace a larger one. The writer serializes writes, fences them to the admitted session/run, and drains before final accounting. Detached and incognito attempts, and follow-ups that preserve user-facing session state, do not use this writer. [Writer and eligibility checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-context-total-tokens.ts).

Goal accounting retains its existing peak-usage policy. The store-backed test starts a Goal with a 50,000-token budget, publishes 40,000, then 60,000, then 30,000 tokens. Current context finishes at 30,000; Goal usage remains 60,000 and `budget_limited`. The test publishes a lower snapshot through the real writer and store; it does not execute the compactor. [Exact assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-context-total-tokens.test.ts#L115-L147).

Maintainer decision needed: should Goal usage retain that 60,000 peak within the current budget window after context falls to 30,000? My recommendation is to preserve that policy in this change. Explicitly resuming a limited Goal starts a new budget window at the current fresh context count and resets `tokensUsed` to 0; the limit is not permanent. [Resume transition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/config/sessions/goals-transitions.ts#L115-L140), [existing resume test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/config/sessions/goals.test.ts#L75-L85). Automatically crediting the Goal after compaction would change budget semantics and needs an explicit owner decision. No such approval is claimed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The per-call subscriber and fenced writer make context visible before turn completion. Final accounting must still supersede intermediate values, including an explicitly unknown final context.

The October 19 integration carries `contextTotalsAccounted` through the current cron writer's closed operation and clears it only after the acknowledged write. The real SQLite-backed test covers both numeric and unknown final context while preserving a concurrent label change. [Production operation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.ts#L248-L293), [production-writer tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.context-total.test.ts).

The merge also preserves attachment-aware detach and writer abandonment in `finally`. A silently nested provider-response test was reproduced as a failing case and restored to top-level collection. [Settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-settle.ts), [separate model-state tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f9e238a3d8871192affc39b7efe064d2bad37bf/src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.model-state.test.ts#L488-L570).

## Evidence

### October 20 cleanup integration

The only merge conflict was `attempt-settle.ts`. The resolution retains upstream inline stream cleanup, attachment-aware detach, deferred ownership and error collection. The context writer still closes before final accounting and drains through an awaited `abandon()` in `finally`. [Production settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-settle.ts#L258-L364).

The new [prompt-failure test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts#L870) holds `abandon()` pending and requires settlement to remain pending. Its cleanup releases the drain before awaiting the outcome, so the negative control can finish safely.

Validation used Node v26.8.2, pnpm 12.12.1, frozen dependencies and the repository wrappers on the private Linux builder, one Vitest worker:

| Evidence | Result and exact scope |
| --- | --- |
| Integration tree `6da66065564d4f28a678f55479f3eed7d90d949e` | 39 tests passed across five files: context writer 9, stream subscription 1, settlement 25, final session context 2 and final cron context 2. Four wrapper shards completed, exit 0, 182.90 seconds. |
| Remove only `await` from `contextTotalTokensWriter.abandon()` | The new test failed as intended: settlement finished while the drain was pending; one failure, 24 skipped, exit 1. |
| Restore exact production bytes | The new test passed, 24 skipped, exit 0. |
| Scoped checks | `agents-other` TypeScript and typed lint for both settlement files exited 0. The first formatting check failed on the new callback's layout; applying only that formatting produced final tree `8c12cdbf`. Final formatting and authored-diff checks exited 0. |
| Final formatted tree `8c12cdbff4ede6b87277c5f43317dac3876f5c30` | The new drain test passed again, 24 skipped, exit 0, 14.57 seconds. Source and index identities were verified. |
| Separate source review | The complete 20-file PR delta on `6da6606` had no actionable P0-P2 finding. A separate review of the entire formatting-only delta to `8c12cdbf` found no actionable issue. These reviewers did not independently execute tests or provide maintainer policy approval. |

Reproduce the positive set with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-context-total-tokens.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-prepare.context-total.test.ts src/agents/command/session-store.context-total.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.context-total.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. For the negative control, replace only the production `await contextTotalTokensWriter.abandon()` with `void contextTotalTokensWriter.abandon()`, select `-t 'waits for the context writer to drain before returning a prompt failure'` in the settlement file, then restore the exact production bytes and rerun. The mutation is absent from the published branch.

A read-only merge check against then-current main `bead2a8e542740f943fe57e8391e5e6c11e9773d` completed without conflicts. A final read-only `git merge-tree` check at 23:19:39 UTC also found no conflict between this head and main `f3587df33881db4cd5c0b3e41d9b5d9b05074d1c`, producing tree `23cb5a12883ae3ec92a3a2e5c39c23e9fc22711a`; that check did not execute CI or change the branch. The Goal policy decision remains open.

### October 20 completed CI

[Run 39497256630](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630), attempt 1, finished successfully with 97 terminal jobs: 70 passed and 27 skipped. Its [preflight log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118885402808) records checkout [`b135c9bf482f11d15a13441fc077a8f3a535ffd3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b135c9bf482f11d15a13441fc077a8f3a535ffd3), with first parent/exact base `bead2a8e542740f943fe57e8391e5e6c11e9773d` and second parent/current head `a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33`, tree `1a84dd2b85dc3fcf59d8b42066c266f37d950097`. The PR event's base `92638b29a6f2115661217498a8d5767e85fd0235` is older than the merge actually tested.

The full job logs explicitly record these 39 regression cases passing. Each job checked out `b135c9bf`, and each test file is byte-identical to the published `a1bdfb50` head:

| Test source at the published head | Passed cases | Hosted job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Context writer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-context-total-tokens.test.ts) | 9 | [118912287323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118912287323) |
| [Real stream subscription](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-prepare.context-total.test.ts) | 1 | [118912287261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118912287261) |
| [Settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts) | 25, including the prompt-failure drain test | [118912287217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118912287217) |
| [Final session context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33/src/agents/command/session-store.context-total.test.ts) | 2 | [118912287230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118912287230) |
| [Final cron context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.context-total.test.ts) | 2 | [118912286953](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118912286953) |

The current [UI shard 1/2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118912286961) passed 81 tests across 21 files, including both previously failing 390px and 1280px sidebar recovery cases. [Extension test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630/job/118928496340) completed `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` with compiler exit 0. Those earlier failures did not recur in this run. This PR adds no separate UI or xAI repair, and the cancelled [exact-base CI run 39496239863](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39496239863) supplies no executed passing control.

At 23:17:13 UTC, all 176 head check records were terminal: 102 success, 72 skipped, one cancelled and one neutral. `filter=all` and `filter=latest` agreed. All 31 workflow runs were terminal: 22 success, eight skipped and one cancelled. The cancelled administrative [PR context and evidence run 39497933241](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497933241) has a later [successful run 39503872426](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39503872426); no cancellation cause is claimed. The latest `openclaw/ci-gate`, `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and `openclaw/dependency-review` statuses are all success, recorded by [run 39513870997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39513870997). These CI results do not supply the maintainer Goal-policy decision. The October 19 results below remain historical.

### October 19 integration

The integration commit `5125da02158281f58db57ec2a10f73e67895d0e3` has tree `d7a7d855fb0672672e676899abcbe144d9f901fe`. Both the fork ref and PR API were read back after the normal fast-forward push. Original ancestry is preserved.

Local validation used Node v26.8.2 on macOS, an independent frozen pnpm installation, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, and the repository wrappers with one Vitest worker:

| Evidence | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Initial candidate `14f752cfc9af3ba551eed63ade9ede955d54195c` | 54 tests passed: context writer 9, settlement 24, cron session state 19, cron final context 2. Wrapper exit 0, 315.81 seconds. |
| Final tree `d7a7d855fb0672672e676899abcbe144d9f901fe` | Model-state 13 and cron final-context 2 passed. Wrapper exit 0, 214.03 seconds. These are the only two test files changed after the initial run; production files and the other three tested files are byte-identical. |
| Nested-test negative control | The selected cost-only case failed with `Calling the test function inside another test function is not allowed`. After repair, all 13 model-state tests passed. |
| Cron marker-removal mutation | Removing only the forwarding of `contextTotalsAccounted` made both real-writer cases fail: 190,000 remained instead of 120,000 or `undefined`. Restoring the exact source bytes made both pass. Mutation exit 1; restored exit 0. |
| Scoped TypeScript | Both `services-cron` and `agents-other` test graphs completed with exit 0, using the official wrapper, 120-second limit, `GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB`, `GOMAXPROCS=2`. |
| Type-aware lint and formatting | Seven repaired files passed the official lint wrapper with the core tsconfig. All 20 PR-delta files passed formatting; `git diff --check` against integrated main passed. |
| Separate source review | Exact final tree reviewed with no actionable P0-P2 finding. That review did not execute tests and is not a maintainer approval. |

Reproduction commands for the positive suites:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-context-total-tokens.test.ts \
```

prs.title: refactor(ui): keep chat question disclosure with its pane
prs.body:
Related: #178593

## What Problem This Solves

Question disclosure was copied from rendering props into shared composer state by an effect, while native and plugin composer views can be replaced inside a retained chat pane.

## User Impact

Keeps question selection and collapsed state with the pane across composer replacements and reconnects. Gateway questions continue to preserve interrupted IME drafts and restore composer focus. There are no intended markup or styling changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single writable derivation now owns question disclosure at the pane lifetime. Native and plugin companion renderers receive that owner explicitly, as do the two standalone creation lifetimes. Async question presentation is assembled once; the former question fields and optional presentation fallback are removed. The existing composer state still owns imperative input and dictation custody.

The remaining question effect handles native IME and focus only. Independent review exposed an explicit-expand/navigation path that set the takeover flag before capturing the composition draft. The effect now owns that transition completely, with a regression covering both actions.

CI run `39468934916` exposed three incomplete caller migrations. The dock now explicitly loads its native card registration, preserving lazy controls and disconnect/reconnect behavior. Composer fixtures supply real async-question messages and connection epochs, and the confirmed-discard regression reads through the pane owner so it observes the live outbox queue. The registration dependency already existed in the original runtime graph; interactive controls remain lazy, so no additional local build was run for this repair. All existing assertions remain. The five-file repair is net zero lines; simplification removed the redundant fixture props alias.

The same prior run also failed the mobile widget fling-distance assertion (`chat-widget-scroll.e2e.test.ts`: 235 px versus a >260 px expectation). That test already includes the touch-emulator repair and matches current main; this question repair does not claim to fix that separate observed failure. Prior repaired-head [CI39473260292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39473260292) completed successfully on `073a9b4cf4ec9a9898c2e007d07f772c4fbe5d91`, including this shard and both real-Gateway E2E jobs. The old assertion did not recur; that does not establish its original cause. The timing-harness follow-up is tracked separately in #178645.

Native admission later found four test-file conflicts after main advanced. Integration head `8d121b7ac535013afc27291518648bd1f2cf332b` merges main `6a6ba1da` without rebasing. It preserves main’s fixture simplifications and all assertions while passing the pane question owner through the updated mounts and direct frame call. All 15 affected tests passed; an initial comment-pins setup import typo was corrected before commit, then its three tests passed. Chat test types, four-file lint/format, and the full-candidate independent review passed. There is no additional production change in the conflict resolution. The earlier successful run remains prior-head evidence; [CI39477616652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39477616652) failed the same widget-fling assertion at 225 px versus >260 px, now assigned to shard 5/9. prs.title: fix(auth): temporary OAuth refresh failures force repeated sign-in
prs.body:
Related: #89278 (OAuth timeout symptoms, not a claim to fix its older Codex timeout path).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a temporary xAI OAuth refresh failure discards the saved login and forces manual sign-in on every later request.

## User Impact

User impact: after an admitted transient xAI token-endpoint failure settles, users can retry with their saved login instead of signing in again. Definitive rejection and invalid successful responses remain terminal. Already-terminal saved credentials are not repaired; no data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider owns retry admission. xAI marks only identified transport failures/timeouts before any HTTP response, connection resets, and token-endpoint 429/5xx responses. Unknown exceptions, HTTP 200 parser/body/validation errors (including `xAI OAuth token response is missing access_token`), credential rejection, and uncertain post-success settlement remain terminal. A 120-second observer timeout never releases or duplicates an in-flight request: restoration waits for provider settlement and exact-fence comparison.

Health recording stays with the auth-candidate owner. Read-only runs and local failure policy write no shared cooldown; ordinary read-write runs record the existing bounded timeout cooldown once (30 seconds initially, at most five minutes). Personal restoration rechecks credential and account-selection authority after provider work and before publication, so disconnect/reassignment cannot revive the old grant.

### Maintainer decision: narrow replay policy

This proposes changing the intentional post-I/O retirement policy only for the provider-admitted outcomes above. A rotating token may still have been consumed before a transport response was lost or a server returned an error. Recovery is best effort; a later definitive rejection remains terminal. Maintainer acceptance of that replay tradeoff and security-sensitive-change approval are still required; neither is claimed by this evidence.

## Evidence

Validated against main `0061cdde5f9a06274ee1015d8a2fa2da4579fba1`; final local head `32625d2d4c318b51aa882d0ade5fde918c4d7993`.

- Fail-before tests reproduced incorrect restoration for the exact xAI missing-access-token/unknown errors, persisted read-only/local cooldowns, and double-counted read-write health. Separate authority regressions exposed same-account reassignment and valid personal-restoration failures; these are fixed.
- The focused 17-file sweep passed 253 tests (445.89 s). After restoring original assertions and consolidating fixtures, the final affected three-file sweep passed 47 tests (150.68 s). The xAI extension lane passed 422 tests in 41 files (182.49 s); provider cases include post-200 body-reset rejection.
- Targeted core/extension lint, core types, all core test-type graphs, the final affected test-type graph, formatting, line-cap and diff checks passed. Knip files/dependencies passed. The broad changed-check is not globally green: export findings, three UI max-lines suppressions and four advisory test-root limits reproduce on pinned main; no new test root was added. Earlier branch-only type/lint/line-growth findings were corrected and affected checks rerun.
- Real production-path proof below uses the native manager, the public registered xAI refresh hook, real HTTP transport/parser and isolated SQLite with synthetic credentials. Main ran in 363.92 s; final branch ran in 272.71 s. A test-only loopback endpoint/TLS override and inner fetch budget of 150 seconds allow the unchanged real 120-second manager deadline to fire; the production inner budget remains 30 seconds. This is not live xAI, a release bundle, or a Gateway deployment.
- Main-created normal and failed-fence SQLite rows load unchanged on the branch: normal is usable, failed fence remains terminal, exact payload hash matches, no migration.
- Independent autoreview: one pass, scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Its assessment is diff-scoped and did not execute the project or inspect unchanged helpers; executed behavior proof is recorded separately above.

<details><summary>Main versus final branch proof output</summary>

```text
PROOF variant=main; real_xai_http=true; isolated_sqlite=true; manager_hard_timeout_ms=120000; fixture_inner_fetch_budget_ms=150000; production_inner_fetch_budget_ms=30000; synthetic_credentials_only=true
PROOF hang_after_real_120s=pending-fence; request_count=1; duplicate_io=false
PROOF hang_settled=terminal; next_use=blocked; request_count=1
PROOF http_503=terminal; next_use=blocked; request_count=1
PROOF http_200_missing_access_token=terminal; next_use=blocked; request_count=1
PROOF http_401_invalid_grant=terminal; next_use=blocked; request_count=1
PROOF personal_disconnect=rejected; stale_credential_publication=false; subsequent_provider_io=0; selected_link_grant_retired=true
PROOF personal_reassignment=rejected; stale_credential_publication=false; subsequent_provider_io=0; selected_link_grant_retired=true
PROOF physical_http_requests=6; provider_dispatch_calls=6; hidden_retries=0
PROOF sqlite_row_payload_sha256=5fd6968472a3b614eb8ccf8f906d2461f7b13b2c173582e7153a2d6ca9282c47
PROOF sqlite_compatibility=created_on_main; normal=usable; failed_fence=terminal; row_payloads=unchanged; migration=none
PROOF PASS

PROOF variant=branch; real_xai_http=true; isolated_sqlite=true; manager_hard_timeout_ms=120000; fixture_inner_fetch_budget_ms=150000; production_inner_fetch_budget_ms=30000; synthetic_credentials_only=true
PROOF hang_after_real_120s=pending-fence; request_count=1; duplicate_io=false
PROOF hang_settled=restored; next_use=rotated; request_count=2
PROOF http_503=restored; next_use=rotated; request_count=2
PROOF http_200_missing_access_token=terminal; next_use=blocked; request_count=1
PROOF http_401_invalid_grant=terminal; next_use=blocked; request_count=1
PROOF personal_disconnect=rejected; stale_credential_publication=false; subsequent_provider_io=0; selected_link_grant_retired=true
PROOF personal_reassignment=rejected; stale_credential_publication=false; subsequent_provider_io=0; selected_link_grant_retired=true
PROOF physical_http_requests=8; provider_dispatch_calls=8; hidden_retries=0
PROOF sqlite_row_payload_sha256=5fd6968472a3b614eb8ccf8f906d2461f7b13b2c173582e7153a2d6ca9282c47
PROOF sqlite_compatibility=loaded_main_rows_on_branch; normal=usable; failed_fence=terminal; row_payloads=unchanged; migration=none
PROOF PASS
```

</details>

## Round 1 responses

1. **Successful-response validation (P2):** removed the permissive unknown-exception classifier. Only explicit provider admission permits restoration; the exact xAI missing-access-token error and post-200 parsing/body failures stay terminal.
2. **Read-only/local health policy (P2) and 0a8313efd18:** removed refresh-store usageStats writes. The existing candidate owner remains authoritative, preserving caller suppression and recording an ordinary shared failure once. Regression tests drive the real manager through the controller boundary.
3. **Security concern and merge risk:** current personal authority is checked after awaited refresh and before owner/peer publication. Tests cover disconnect, different-account replacement and same-account replacement while refresh is pending, plus unchanged-grant recovery. The real HTTP proof verifies disconnect/reassignment rejection, no stale publication and zero subsequent provider I/O. Clearing a default still does not generally revoke existing explicit session pins; this change refuses restoration when the selected authority changes during pending work.
4. **Data-model compatibility:** actual main-created SQLite rows and their identical payload hash are exercised above; existing terminal fences are deliberately not resurrected.
5. **Real behavior proof:** the trace uses the real registered xAI transport, with the true 120-second observer deadline, later settled recovery/rotation, 503 recovery, terminal invalid HTTP 200 and 401/invalid_grant, and authority retirement. The endpoint independently counts physical requests; there are no hidden retries.
6. **Maintainer decision / publication:** the narrow replay tradeoff remains explicit above. Maintainer security approval and any ClawSweeper re-review remain outstanding repository review steps; this local package does not issue or claim them.

prs.title: fix(doctor): systemd drop-in settings reported as unrecognized
prs.body:
Related: #161977

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor and `openclaw update status` call valid systemd directives "unrecognized settings" when they come from an operator drop-in, and print identical lines when two drop-ins set the same directive.

## User Impact

User impact: operators see which drop-in sets each directive and that OpenClaw leaves it unchanged, instead of a warning that reads like invalid systemd configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Drop-in findings reused the wording for unknown edits in the managed base unit. They now name their source drop-in and say the setting is preserved. Classification is unchanged: drop-in directives are still reported, still block automatic policy repair, and are never rewritten. Base-unit wording is unchanged.

The issue's PATH half is not changed here: the non-minimal PATH check already exempts expected service PATH entries (covered in `src/daemon/service-audit.test.ts`), which is why this is "Related" rather than "Closes".

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (head `cc5efb14`, Ubuntu 24.04.4, systemd 255, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.5.1)

Real user systemd manager. A unit rendered by the repo's own installer code (`buildGatewayInstallPlan` + `buildSystemdUnit`) installed as a user unit with two operator drop-ins, `operator.conf` (`CPUWeight=1000`) and `zz-operator.conf` (`CPUWeight=500`), then `systemctl --user daemon-reload`. The service was never started or enabled.

```
$ systemctl --user show openclaw-gateway-ocproof.service -p LoadState -p ActiveState -p UnitFileState -p DropInPaths -p CPUWeight
CPUWeight=500
LoadState=loaded
ActiveState=inactive
DropInPaths=~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-ocproof.service.d/operator.conf ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-ocproof.service.d/zz-operator.conf
UnitFileState=disabled
```

Before, upstream main `fa95e3c7` (`OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (fa95e3c)`):

```
$ openclaw --profile ocproof update status
...
Warning: Systemd Service.CPUWeight contains an unrecognized setting.
Warning: Systemd Service.CPUWeight contains an unrecognized setting.

$ openclaw --profile ocproof doctor --non-interactive
◇  Gateway service definition ────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - Systemd Service.CPUWeight contains an unrecognized setting.  │
│  - Systemd Service.CPUWeight contains an unrecognized setting.  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

After, this PR `cc5efb14` (`OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (cc5efb1)`), same unit and drop-ins:

```
$ openclaw --profile ocproof update status
...
Warning: Systemd Service.CPUWeight is set by operator drop-in ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-ocproof.service.d/operator.conf; not changed.
Warning: Systemd Service.CPUWeight is set by operator drop-in ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-ocproof.service.d/zz-operator.conf; not changed.

$ openclaw --profile ocproof doctor --non-interactive
◇  Gateway service definition ──────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - Systemd Service.CPUWeight is set by operator drop-in                       │
│    ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-ocproof.service.d/operator.conf;   │
│    not changed.                                                               │
│  - Systemd Service.CPUWeight is set by operator drop-in                       │
│    ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-ocproof.service.d/zz-operator.conf;│
│    not changed.                                                               │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

`update status --json` on both builds reports the same `kind: "unknown-edit"`, the same `reason: "Operator drop-in overrides installer policy."` and a separate `sourcePath` per drop-in; only `message` differs, so automatic policy repair stays blocked. Home path redacted to `~`; the profile name `ocproof` is a throwaway.

### Tests

- New regression in `src/daemon/service-audit.definition-facts.test.ts`: two drop-ins both set `CPUWeight`. Before: two identical `Systemd Service.CPUWeight contains an unrecognized setting.` findings. After: each finding names its drop-in path.
- `pnpm test src/daemon/service-audit.definition-facts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 60/60 passed.
- `pnpm test src/daemon`: 100 files, 2,239 tests passed, 15 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, the format check on both changed files, conflict-marker, line-cap, assertion-safety, database-worker and test-timeout ratchets, `config:docs:check`, boundary report, wrapper shadowing and deps pins all pass.
- Known red on main and unrelated: `check:env-var-count` (477 > 476) and 3 tests in `settled-turn-finalization.provider-error.test.ts`.
- The `checks-node-compact-small-2/3` failures on this PR are `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` and `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`, which fail identically on a clean `main` checkout and on every other PR opened in the same hour (#163556, #163557, #163558); this PR does not touch the wrapper inventory.

prs.title: fix(doctor): recognize standard systemd unit and drop-in settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor, update status, and Gateway status label standard systemd directives in customized units and drop-ins as “unrecognized setting.” Fixes #161977.

Supersedes #163555, thanks @kohjunhao.

## User Impact

Standard `[Unit]`, `[Service]`, and `[Install]` directives are reported as custom settings that are not changed. Misspelled keys and keys in the wrong section still warn. Existing customization and rewrite safeguards remain unchanged; directive values are not validated by this check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service-definition audit confused OpenClaw’s narrow installer policy with systemd’s accepted directives. It now recognizes the complete set from systemd v260’s parser table, including execution/resource-control macros and legacy aliases, through a reproducible generator. The existing audit remains the single owner; no new runtime subprocess, configuration, dependency, or repair path is introduced.

Release-note context: fixes false unrecognized-setting diagnostics for customized Linux service definitions in Doctor, update status, and Gateway status; credited to @kohjunhao.

## Evidence

CI follow-up on `262d3409315113e765c9320afc1efbec0867754c`: job `118871896476` failed the **mock-export ratchet**, not line-cap or generated-file inventory. It found an inherited closed mock in `doctor-database-network-storage.test.ts`. Applied the exact fix already on main in [2466488c29e2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2466488c29e25f6fdafe0d6419387116e4194ade): spread the real inspection module exports, then override the tested function. No baseline or generated-data changes.

Local verification: the mock-export ratchet reproduced the original failure, then passed (`7983 grandfathered factories`) after the fix. The line-cap ratchet passed (`8 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth`). The affected network-storage test passed (23 ms test time; 21.67 s wall time), as did focused lint/format and an isolated P0–P2 review. Commands: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base 0f46faecf63c927841e84177f09527f27ced5f51 --no-merge-base`, the same command with `check-line-cap-ratchet.mts`, and `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-database-network-storage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. State-resolving commands used isolated home/state directories. This follow-up adds one net test line and zero production lines.

The two new regressions fail on the original diagnostic and pass with the fix (base unit: 12 ms; drop-in: 15 ms). All 43 tests in the owning definition-facts suite pass, with 421 ms total test time. The consumer run passed all 15 test files importing the owner directly or through `service-audit`: 308 passed, one pre-existing skipped test, seven shards, 184.55 seconds wall time. Shared worker compilation took 51.56 seconds; no individual test exceeded 30 seconds or file exceeded 120 seconds.

A Linux container ran the real filesystem-backed `auditSystemdUnit` without mocks using an isolated home/state directory. The original logic failed on valid directives; the fixed build passed recognition, preserved the drop-in bytes, and warned only for `Service.RestartStpes` and wrong-section `Service.OnFailure`. This exercises the manager-unavailable filesystem fallback, not a running systemd user manager or a full update/install.

Core and service-test TypeScript checks, focused oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the import-cycle check passed (`0 cycle(s)`). Independent expansion of the upstream parser table matched all 423 generated keys. Full `check:changed`/SQLite inventory was skipped for time; PR CI is the broad check. The broader test-graph selector reported inherited root-count limits (721/724/725/727 against 720); the services graph passed directly.

Autoreview could not start: its macOS isolation preflight rejected the temporary-directory location even with `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP` unset. No review verdict is claimed; the PR head needs lead review.

Net LOC: +128 runtime production (+125 generated directive data, +3 audit logic), +42 generator tooling, +45 tests, +2 docs. The complete upstream inventory accounts for the necessary production growth; no unrelated deletion was added to offset it.

<details>
<summary>Local proof commands</summary>

All state-resolving commands used an isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under `.artifacts/systemd-directives/`.


prs.title: refactor(plugins): retire unused private state and result paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several plugin-private interfaces still carried unused state or behavior: Discord's request queue exposed a clearing operation with no runtime caller, Teams created empty polls through a seed-vote writer and copied an unused certificate thumbprint, Browser returned relay status/auth projections nobody read, and Copilot wrapped token lookup and attached unused result labels.

## What changed

Remove the unused paths at their plugin owners and update only their obsolete test expectations. Keep Discord's ordinary FIFO/fairness, queue bounds, rate-limit retries, request authorization and deadlines; Teams' normal vote writes, replacement cleanup, account isolation and stored rows; Browser's authentication proofs, native request/settlement and reconnect handler; and Copilot's credential selection, tenant checks, account validation and catalog outcomes.

This is a 100-net-production-line residue cleanup across four plugins, not a LARGE campaign PR. Production +16/-116; handwritten declarations, tests and test support are excluded from that figure. No public SDK/config/protocol/persisted-schema/dependency changes. The standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Discord: no unused private queue-clearing operation or generation fences around it. Source history f0adbd48 and bd20f8e / #75338 introduced the operation and synthetic queued-retry protection; current source has no production caller. Actual rate-limit retry behavior remains.
- Teams: new polls start without preloaded votes, as the sole production caller already requested after the legacy importer retired in b9aade4b1262. Private seed-vote machinery is retired, not ordinary voting or existing stored votes. Certificate auth still consumes the PEM path; the unused thumbprint copy was never passed to Azure identity. Public config remains accepted.
- Browser: ignored ensure-relay response classification and unread auth-client projections disappear. #120526 and #128379 introduced real auth/daemon features, which remain; the sole reconnect caller already ignores the result and owns rejection handling. Unexpected wake-up responses remain best effort; pairing responses still require their original validation.
- Copilot: private returned hasProfile/source labels are no longer available to hypothetical callers. Reference tracing found no production reader. /user validation introduced by fbd6b842 and strict/advisory catalog behavior from #139791 remain unchanged; both existing callers now check the token directly instead of a nullable wrapper.

## Evidence

Focused retained proof: Teams credentials/SDK 55 tests and polls/outbound 24; Discord REST/scheduler/proxy/authority 33; Browser auth/native/background/lifecycle 59. Tests for retained behavior remain, including real transport and vote persistence. Independent isolated P0–P2 reviews for these cuts returned scoped-clean, with final source verification. Local commands use isolated OpenClaw state and one worker, serially.

Copilot auth/models/embedding/index proof passed 113 tests across five files (190.34s wrapper, 115.41s and 38.34s shards). Its independent P0–P2 review returned scoped-clean with final source verification. Targeted strict types passed for every changed owner graph. Scoped import-cycle proof covered 949 production TypeScript files across the four plugins: zero runtime cycles and zero new static components; Browser JavaScript import edges are unchanged, not claimed as scanned by that TypeScript check. Focused syntax lint, line-cap ratchet, formatting and whitespace passed. Mandatory lint-suppressions: 14 passed, 11.12s wrapper.

Check-changed is classified by dry-run only under the campaign's host budget; hosted CI on the exact published head is the broad gate. CI duration is pending. No live channel, browser-device, or external Copilot inference claim.

CI caught one missed test-only type member: check-test-types job 118893945074 on the initial head reported TS2741 in connection-bound-ids.live.test.ts because its handwritten auth-result type still required the removed source label. Removed that orphaned type member; no test logic or assertion changed. The exact live-test file now passes a targeted strict typecheck without executing live credentials or inference. Focused syntax lint, line-cap ratchet, format/whitespace and all 14 suppression checks passed for the repair. Hosted CI on the repaired head remains the broad gate.
