prs.title: fix(ui): long picker menus jump while scrolling under the pointer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the sidebar's owner menu (and other long searchable pickers and multi-selects) jumps while you scroll it with a wheel or trackpad. It happens whenever the pointer passes over a half-visible row at the top or bottom edge of the list.

## User Impact

Long picker menus, such as the session-owner filter with many teammates, now scroll smoothly under the pointer. Keyboard navigation, opening the menu, and search still scroll the highlighted row into view.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pointer hover highlights the row under the cursor, and every highlight change also ran a "reveal" that scrolled the highlighted row fully into view. When the pointer rested over a clipped edge row during a scroll, each reveal pushed the list back against the user's scroll. Pointer-driven highlights now skip the reveal. Keyboard, open, search, and catalog-correction highlights still reveal. The shared picker (`select-picker-view.tsx`) and the shared menu machine's retained-focus reveal (`menu-machine.ts`, used by `MultiSelect`) each had this behavior, and both are fixed.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced through a real pointer in Chromium.** On `origin/main`, a real mouse move onto a half-clipped bottom row scrolls the list on its own: picker 326 → 344px, multi-select 631 → 646px. The new regression tests fail with exactly those values before the fix and pass after it.
- **Keyboard reveal still works.** Each new test then presses an arrow key after the pointer highlight and checks that the next row scrolls into view.
- **Consumers.** All browser test files that cover the menu machine, picker, and multi-select consumers pass: 74 files, 907 tests.
- **Static checks.** `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint` on the touched files are clean. Autoreview (Codex) found nothing at P0–P2.
- **Test cost.** `pnpm test ui/src/components/select-picker.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` takes 10.6s wall time, and `pnpm test ui/src/components/multi-select.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 4.2s. The new tests add about 0.35s and 0.28s respectively, with no timers, sleeps, or new fixtures.
- **No screenshots.** This is a behavior-only fix with no visual change, so the real-pointer browser tests are the proof.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c20e99a8-728f-4cd1-8297-a8314cb2fc9c)

prs.title: fix(subagents): don't re-list delivered child results because of a retained settle marker
prs.body:
Fixes the render half of #166267 and the `failed` case of #154834.

## What
`hasOutstandingCompletion` (`subagent-active-context.ts`) listed every terminal child that still carries a `requesterSettleWake` marker under `## Child results awaiting delivery`, whatever its own `delivery.status` was. On a busy top-level requester the marker is retained until no descendant is running, so results that were delivered long ago get re-injected into every turn and grow without bound (138 entries over 5 days in the report; restart does not clear them because the markers are persisted).

The change:
- a retained settle marker makes an entry outstanding only while its own delivery is still open (not `delivered` / `discarded` / `not_required` / `failed`);
- `failed`, the terminal give-up state written by `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp`, is no longer treated as awaiting delivery (#154834).

Pending, in-progress and suspended deliveries are listed exactly as before.

## Not in this PR
Releasing or ageing out the marker itself (in `maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled` and the sweeper) is described in #166267. That change touches settle-wake lifecycle and batching, so I left it for a maintainer decision.

## Tests
`subagent-active-context.test.ts`:
- delivered / failed / discarded + retained marker → not listed
- pending + marker → still listed

I have not run the suite locally.

prs.title: perf(agents): compact retained prompt-cache diagnostics
prs.body:
## Owner acceptance (verbatim)

> I ACCEPT #178676. Reasons: retained fingerprints fell 72% (128 → 36 MiB) in both pairs, idle heap growth roughly halved (30% → 17%), reopen and first-text p50/p95 are neutral, and zero session runtime objects were retained. GC was mixed in both directions (reopen minor GC +12% / −8%, major GC −17% / +3%), not a consistent regression. The initial-turn promotion increase (+1.7% / +9.3%) is accepted against ~90 MiB less retained heap. Mark the PR ready, rebase onto latest main if needed, let CI finish (no reruns; use the inherited/unrelated-failure rules if needed), and merge. Report the merge SHA.

## Result

The two concurrent, swapped-core Gateway pairs reduce retained diagnostic fingerprints by **71.61% and 71.58%**, meeting the 70% memory threshold. The owner accepts the measured initial-turn promotion increase against the retained-memory reduction. The complete per-pair measurements and limits remain below.

## What Problem This Solves

Prompt-cache diagnostics retain per-message Maps, arrays, and digest objects after runtime sessions are released. The initial 100-session probe attributed 118.50 MiB to this owner after six minutes idle. The current concurrent baselines retain about 127.8 MiB.

## User Impact

Idle sessions retain about 90 MiB less diagnostic heap across this 100-session workload, while preserving history-change diagnostics. The owner accepts the measured initial-turn promotion increase; no user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Store full SHA-256 history digests in flat Latin-1 strings with a shared field-name layout. Materialize diagnostic Maps only on divergence. Reopened equal messages reuse the previous baseline; the temporary layout index is discarded after each observation. Provider-request prefixes also pack their full ordered message digests into one string, preserving the existing first-32-message field diagnostic window and 512-message digest bound. Field hashes and public wire diagnostics remain hexadecimal. No provider payload, configuration, schema, retention limit, or cleanup policy changes.

The measured Gateway flow also exposed a separate import-time lifetime: the module-level uninitialized-state Error in `src/claws/tool-policy-runtime.ts` captured the importing session through lazy stack frames. Construct that Error only in the existing failure branch. The message, cause, consent decision, and fail-closed behavior are unchanged. Both measured sides include this prerequisite, isolating compact fingerprint storage from the independent retention repair.

Runtime production delta: **+41 lines**. Full hashes, ordered field diagnostics, and lossless compact encoding/decoding account for the growth; the retained object graphs are replaced rather than supplemented by another cache. Related: #178536, #178602.

## Evidence

Both concurrent Gateway pairs passed all transcript checks and session-disposal censuses. The tables below retain the measured memory, latency, promotion, and GC tradeoffs.

### Measurement

Baseline: `4a4d1e330fdfe92de7fe464d25a6bdf8fd033849`. Candidate: `c6b4d2f8e2c1a3412b3eec6a5d1d472e161872a2`. Both sides receive identical measurement instrumentation and the Error-lifetime prerequisite. Source-performance builds were generated sequentially, with 227 source hashes per tree verified before and after builds. Existing identical dependency installations were reused on both sides (including typebox 1.3.36 and zod 4.6.6).

The committed synthetic Gateway workload uses 100 sessions in cohorts of ten, 655 seeded entries per session, 128 KiB prompts, and six minutes idle before reopening. The roster has 5,000 sessions and 6,000 retained runs. Each pair runs simultaneously under the exclusive measurement lock: baseline on cores 96–111 and candidate on 112–127, then swapped. Separate state directories and loopback ports; outside load recorded. Each side supplies 100 reopen and first-text samples.

After timed reopening, a second six-minute disposal interval precedes fingerprint attribution. Every run passed all 100 append-only transcript checks and had zero reachable SessionManager, AgentSession, and Agent instances. Separate plain forced-GC samples before and after clearing diagnostic observations measure retained fingerprints; this clear never precedes timed reopening. External-memory and array-buffer attribution deltas were zero. Natural main-isolate promotion excludes worker isolates and forced census collections.

Workload command, with separately generated matching synthetic state:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts \
  --state-dir <synthetic-state> --scenario session-idle-retention \
  --sessions 100 --runs 10 --history-turns 163 --chunks 1 \
  --chunk-interval-ms 0 --prompt-kib 128 --duration-ms 360000 \
  --memory-interval-ms 30000 --diagnostics --trace-gc \
  --fingerprint-retention --entry src/entry.ts \
  --start-at <shared-epoch-ms> --port <loopback-port> --mock-port <provider-port>
```

| Metric | Pair 1, baseline → candidate | Pair 2, baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained fingerprints (MiB) | 127.74 → 36.26 | 127.83 → 36.33 |
| Idle heap growth (%) | 30.58 → 16.48 | 30.18 → 17.04 |
| Reopen p50 (ms) | 3673.96 → 3649.62 | 3329.28 → 3223.06 |
| Reopen p95 (ms) | 17920.76 → 17626.88 | 18351.28 → 18425.55 |
| First text p50 (ms) | 3137.05 → 3143.77 | 2725.94 → 2689.54 |
| First text p95 (ms) | 17361.77 → 17072.47 | 17752.44 → 17846.65 |
| Touch promotion (MiB) | 6901.69 → 7016.37 | 7067.36 → 7721.83 |
| Reopen promotion (MiB) | 4124.25 → 4546.53 | 4103.23 → 3919.31 |
| Reopen minor GC count | 711.00 → 786.00 | 661.00 → 615.00 |
| Reopen minor GC time (ms) | 2701.51 → 3023.58 | 2608.89 → 2405.64 |
| Reopen major GC count | 8.00 → 6.00 | 7.00 → 7.00 |
| Reopen major GC time (ms) | 462.80 → 385.29 | 453.50 → 467.63 |
| Reopen main CPU (ms) | 33567.21 → 36009.68 | 30004.17 → 27386.91 |
| Reopen process CPU (ms) | 108645.42 → 110374.51 | 98873.35 → 98077.77 |

Pair 1: -71.61% retained fingerprint change (-91.48 MiB).

Pair 2: -71.58% retained fingerprint change (-91.50 MiB).

Initial-turn GC, outside the reopen window:

| Metric | Pair 1, baseline → candidate | Pair 2, baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Minor GC count / time (ms) | 1401 / 4937.89 → 1350 / 4785.18 | 1361 / 4983.80 → 1538 / 5447.46 |

The promotion increase is not explained by the current aggregate operation counters. A read-only source audit found no added timer, event, or persistence call in compact diagnostics; the generic patch counter includes no-op attempts and the transcript-worker counter combines request kinds. Those counts are diagnostic clues, not grounds to normalize away or waive the promotion gate.

### Focused proof and limits

- The provider-prefix change passed 46 focused tests across model-request-body, prompt-cache-observability, and provider-prompt-state. Earlier history/observation/provider-state/prefix-stability proof passed 85 tests; the benchmark profile helper passed nine tests and the consent-policy files passed four. Changed-file format and lint passed.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2, including the provider-prefix change. The requested same-engine retry after the initial rate limit succeeded. The final rebase was patch-identical for the reviewed change and its supplied caller context.

The PR context check initially rejected nonstandard body headings; restoring the repository template headings fixed that body-only failure. No manual CI rerun, broad local suite, extra local install, or additional typecheck lane was used for this follow-up.
- The deterministic synthetic provider does not establish real-provider reconnect or prompt-cache-hit behavior. The source-runtime absolute timings are not a packaged-runtime comparison.

prs.title: fix(release): reuse admitted changelog descendants
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/maintainers/blob/main/release/retrospectives/issue-ledger.md#rri-12

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes candidate-owned Full Release Validation reuse refusing a release candidate whose code parent was already qualified and whose only descendant changes are the selected split changelog files.

## User Impact

Release operators can carry product validation forward across a proven changelog-only descendant instead of rerunning every FRV child for hours.

## Authority Model

The production request authenticates both revisions independently:

- retained evidence and its immutable children remain bound to admitted parent `A`;
- the executing workflow, current request, and current admission remain bound to descendant `B`;
- the existing comparison policy proves `merge-base(A, B) = A` and permits only the selected changelog paths/statuses;
- publisher authority, repository, coverage, baselines, policy/source digests, and every non-revision input must remain identical;
- changed inputs, code deltas, changed publisher authority, and revoked authority all fail before release consumers run.

The shell prefilter checks the retained root against its authenticated `A` admission, while the shared validator separately authenticates `B` and proves the A→B delta. Exact-target reuse keeps the stricter full admission-identity equality.

## Evidence

prs.title: feat: drop files into new sessions from the command palette
prs.body:
Related: #142880

## What Problem This Solves

Files dropped onto the Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette are ignored, and attaching an image still leaves unrelated navigation choices visible.

## User Impact

Users can drop images and files into the palette to prepare a new background session without disturbing the current conversation. The first attachment switches to New session mode immediately; closing and reopening preserves that draft in memory for the same Gateway/account. Reloading the app does not preserve it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the composer's existing admission, preparation, previews, removal, and nested-drag handling. Pending, ready, and failed attachments establish new-session intent, retire search and its keyboard selection, and expose an instructions placeholder and session-specific shortcuts. Removing the last attachment retains intent while instructions remain; clearing both restores navigation. Failed attachments must be removed or reattached before submission, so a partial draft is never sent silently. Startup drops transfer raw Files once to the canonical draft; clipboard intake remains image-only.

No new configuration, dependencies, persistent storage, or Gateway protocol changes. Dropping never starts a session by itself; the existing button or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter remains required.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the base: real-browser drops produced zero attachments at both 1280px and 390px; focused regressions also reproduced discarded attachment drafts on dismissal.
- 105 focused tests pass across attachment handling, draft ownership, cold input custody, lazy actions, lifecycle, and platform shortcuts (7.93s Vitest run; 8.90s wrapper wall time).
- 9 real Chromium tests pass against the production Control UI bundle, covering mixed image/PDF drop payloads, draft reopen, deliberate background creation, unchanged foreground draft/focus/route, image overflow, and first-open/IME flows (58.04s including the production build). Synthetic Gateway responses, real application rendering and file APIs; no live provider/model run is claimed.
- UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, CSS lint, Solid ownership guards, i18n verification, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings on the complete candidate.
- [Real application before/after screenshots: desktop dark and narrow light](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178842#issuecomment-6303605889). Captured from the real Control UI, not the design visualizer.

Requested by @jalehman.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e02ac4c2-d3dc-4c87-8f77-b99f0e135e6b)

Google media and speech errors could expose the active request credential when an upstream response reflected it. Runway video polling dropped the proxy/private-network policy already resolved for submission.

## User Impact

Google media failures retain their useful provider details without echoing the request key. Runway task polling uses the same configured transport policy as submission. No configuration, protocol, dependency, or persisted-format change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry existing request context to the existing Plugin SDK owners: requestHeaders for Google error redaction, and allowPrivateNetwork/dispatcherPolicy for Runway polling. Downloads of generated third-party assets deliberately do not inherit submission trust or credentials.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. These are reproduced adapter bugs; no guard or supported behavior is removed.

## Evidence

All three new regressions failed on the original adapter paths for their intended reasons. The fixed candidate passes all 52 tests across the three touched suites. Runway proof exercises the real SDK poller and observes guarded transport selection; Google proof exercises the real SDK error redactor, including an actual request-header override.

prs.title: feat(agents): preserve stores during controlled Gateway handoff
prs.body:
Related: #178748

## What Problem This Solves

An agent's identity and history should survive a change in where it runs. An operator may start an agent on a shared Gateway, then move it to a dedicated Gateway for capacity or isolation. Today there is no supported per-agent removal operation for that handoff: `agents.delete({ agentId, deleteFiles: false })` still requests session-store purging. Keeping files does not preserve sessions.

With PostgreSQL, the durable agent data can already stay in the same database. The missing operation releases the source Gateway's use of that store without deleting its contents.

## User Impact

An administrator can:

1. Stop routing new work to the source and wait for `agents.detach({ agentId })` to succeed.
2. Transfer the closed original anchor and required workspace files, keeping the agent ID and PostgreSQL namespace.
3. Use existing `agents.create` on the destination, verify retained identity/history, restore destination settings, then switch routing.

This enables planned capacity changes and maintenance without resetting the agent's history or copying its PostgreSQL rows. The prototype moved shared → dedicated → shared carrying an 8 KiB anchor; workspace files remain a separate transfer responsibility. This is a new operator capability, with no claim of a current outage or regression.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changing `agents.delete` would weaken its cleanup contract. Editing the roster or copying an anchor alone bypasses admission closure, draining and restart recovery. Detach makes retention explicit while reusing those lifecycle owners.

The implementation records durable detach intent, drains work, closes database owners and retains the store/files. Recovery and destructive retries cannot convert a pending detach into deletion; offline CLI deletion refuses a pending detach.

Core supplies the local lifecycle primitive; a controller or plugin orchestrates placement and routing. There is no database schema-version change, new adoption RPC or distributed ownership manager. Three unchanged session-policy constants move out of the method table to meet the repository's file limit.

## Scope and Compatibility

This is administrator-controlled sequential handoff. The controller owns exclusive assignment, routing, database permissions and file transfer. Source tombstones refuse ordinary writes after restart, but cannot prevent explicit source recreation or duplicate adoption.

Detach removes Gateway-local bindings, cron jobs, execution approvals and provenance; restore required destination settings explicitly. Existing restrictions on the sole configured agent and shared/inherited credential owners remain. Local shared state and anchors can remain SQLite.

The new journal phases are a compatibility commitment: older binaries reject retained detach journals, including completed records. Keep a compatible runtime while those records remain.

## Evidence

- Recorded local validation: 74 distinct focused tests covering journal persistence/fencing, detach/restart/adopt, destructive-retry refusal, authority/discovery, offline deletion, deletion recovery and published-stable phase-less journal upgrades.
- The added public-RPC integration test retains session ID/transcript, refuses source writes before and after restart, keeps a neighbor usable and permits re-adoption and another write. It uses one local state directory.
- An isolated PostgreSQL 16 prototype experiment used separate Gateway processes and retained store UUID, namespace, session ID, transcripts, synthetic credentials and keyword memory through a round trip. Interrupted detach completed safely after lease expiry. This ran on the prototype base, not the exact PR head; no live inference or active-active ownership was exercised.
- Recorded lint, core typecheck, protocol/schema and native-contract checks, formatting, documentation checks and CLI startup build passed after the final mechanical extraction. Isolated autoreview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Required PR CI remains a landing gate.

## Maintainer Decision and Remaining Proof

**Decision requested:** should OpenClaw support `agents.detach` through the existing lifecycle owner, including durable retention intent and older-binary refusal? If an SDK lifecycle hook is preferred, guidance on that interface would help settle the implementation direction.

The [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178755#issuecomment-6301090114) requests:

- [ ] Redacted, inspectable exact-head proof: two independent Gateways/state directories, retained PostgreSQL identity/history, source refusal after restart and interrupted-detach recovery.
- [ ] Administrator success, `operator.write`-only rejection before mutation, and replaced deletion-lease rejection before configuration/database effects.
- [ ] Upgrade proof from v2026.10.5 preserving settings, sessions and deletion-journal behavior; older phase-less fixtures alone do not cover this.
- [ ] Maintainer acceptance of the API and retention contract, plus security approval for the final head.

Prototype results establish feasibility; these remaining items are not claimed satisfied by the local test count.

## Historical status, October 11

## User Impact

The embedded Dashboard receives the admitted Access session before loading, scoped to the exact Gateway authority, and is retired when ingress authority changes. Native operator connections can use Access-only routes without introducing shared credentials. Existing direct/Tailscale admission and OpenClaw pairing/permissions remain separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

This update composes the existing Dashboard fix with Vincent's latest native ingress work, preserving his commits and ownership. Neither dependency is represented as merged or superseded. No additional Cloudflare feature PR, pairing system, role or provider store is introduced.

The composition repair restores current native connection callbacks and cancellation/backoff ownership, retains failed sign-out retirement receipts for recovery, and distinguishes explicit departure from passive retirement reconciliation. ## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, a person can sign in through Cloudflare Access and connect native Gateway clients, yet the embedded Dashboard opens without that Access session. This PR carries the admitted session into the Dashboard and prevents the iOS client from silently reusing a stored operator grant under a different Access principal.

## Why This Change Was Made

This builds on Vincent Koc's iOS Access drafts #147238 and #147244, preserving his native browser/profile admission and connection work. The follow-up addresses the embedded Dashboard boundary, exact-authority cookie admission and account-switch handling. Vincent's work remains credited; these drafts are not represented as merged or superseded.

The design is vanilla-first: Access is the entry gate, while existing OpenClaw identity, pairing, permissions and reconnection remain authoritative. Current main `99a2b25` still does not provide this iOS handoff. There is no new pairing system, role or Gateway scope policy.

The test audit removed four redundant files while retaining their unique cases in the existing suite. Later cleanup removed a test-only production wrapper. The current helper cleanup reuses an existing connection context rather than adding an abstraction or disabling lint. Main was integrated through a normal merge; original attribution and unrelated upstream changes remain intact.

## User Impact

The WebView receives the current Access session before its first load, only for the exact Gateway authority, and is retired when ingress changes. Access-only routes can start the native operator connection without a shared token. Existing direct and Tailscale routes retain their own admission path.

Cloudflare sign-in alone does not grant `operator.admin`: the existing Gateway pairing/full-access flow still controls that permission. The iOS client refuses automatic reuse of unbound or differently bound operator tokens; same-principal renewal can retain its pairing. This is a client safeguard, not server-enforced protection against a modified client. prs.title: fix(subagents): completed child results recur after closed delivery and fallback sends can duplicate
prs.body:
Closes #151769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: completed child results keep recurring in the requester's active-context after their delivery state is already closed, and the message-tool fallback send of a child's terminal result can execute more than once across concurrent callers or restart replays.

## User Impact

User impact: child-agent results are delivered exactly once per delivery generation even when the primary announce path fails or the gateway restarts mid-delivery, and requesters no longer see stale "awaiting delivery" entries for children whose delivery already finished.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two defects in the subagent registry delivery path:

1. **Stale recurrence** — `hasOutstandingCompletion` treated a retained `requesterSettleWake` object as outstanding even when the delivery state was closed (delivered/discarded/not_required/intentional_non_delivery), so the awaiting-delivery render block kept re-rendering a finished child and re-attempting delivery. The guard is narrowed so a closed delivery state suppresses the block regardless of retained wake objects.
2. **Non-durable fallback send** — `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp` gated the outbound channel send only on in-memory state, so concurrent same-process callers, foreign claims at the same generation, and restart replays could each issue the terminal-result send. A per-run, per-generation durable fallback claim with a per-acquire token is now persisted through `delivery.fallbackClaim` before the send: same-process in-flight retries carry the same token, foreign claims and restart replays observe the tombstone and drop without sending. `commitDeliveredFallback` rolls back the in-memory delivered mutation on persist throw so restart recovery sees the pre-commit authoritative state, and `closeAmbiguousFallback` closes the entry as suspended/intentional_non_delivery while retaining the claim as a tombstone when the send throws.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests (24 passing, 1 file)** on a worktree branched from current `main` (308113ca06): `subagent-registry-lifecycle.message-tool-fallback.test.ts` covers the closed-delivery guard, helper-level at-most-once acquire/release, lifecycle-level overlapping `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp` callers with a barrier producing exactly one outbound send, delivered-commit persist failure with rollback and re-entry, redrive generation bumps, and same-owner idempotent re-entry. Targeted run: `1 passed / 24 tests passed`.
- **Live observation of the defect**: in a gateway running the pre-fix code, a completed child (`outcome=ok; delivery=failed`) recurred in the requester's active-context across repeated LLM boundaries, re-attempting failed delivery each time.
- **Port note**: type additions live in `subagent-registry-read.types.ts` (upstream's split-file layout); behavior is otherwise identical to the verified live-branch repair.
- Full suite (`pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test`) targeted to run on the submission branch; targeted lane for the touched surface is green as above.

prs.title: fix(agents): background exec sessions disappear from prompt context after mid-turn starts
prs.body:
Closes #151768

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the "Active exec sessions" runtime-facts fragment shows `none` for the rest of a turn whenever a background exec is started after the turn's first model step, and the listing can be computed against a different process scope than the one the exec tool registered under.

## User Impact

User impact: model steps after a mid-turn background exec start can discover, poll, and steer the running session instead of reporting "no sessions", and active-exec listings reflect the attempt's own registered scope rather than ambient state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three layered defects in the runtime-facts pipeline:

1. **Scope forwarding** — `buildRuntimeFactsContext` re-derived the process scope key from ambient params per read (`resolveProcessToolScopeKey`), while exec registration used the attempt's actual scope. When the two diverged (session key changes, subagent/cron contexts), the active-exec listing missed the attempt's own sessions or showed another scope's. The attempt's resolved scope key is now forwarded explicitly.
2. **Scope resolution timing** — the key was resolved independently at registration and at each facts read, so split identities could disagree. It is now resolved once per attempt and pinned as the run identity (`processScopeKey`) shared by registration and runtime facts.
3. **Stale carrier at boundaries** — the runtime-facts carrier is assembled once per attempt, so every following LLM boundary re-projected the pre-registration snapshot. The current-turn active-exec fragment is now refreshed at each LLM boundary by querying the live process registry with the pinned scope key. **The refresh appends a NEW carrier after the last existing one rather than mutating previously emitted carrier bytes**, preserving provider prompt-cache prefixes and reasoning continuity for append-only sessions. This refresh runs for both version 3 and version 4 session projections.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests (28 passing, 3 files)** on a worktree branched from current `main` (308113ca06):
  - `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` — active-exec snapshot honors the attempt's process scope key.
  - `attempt.process-scope-key.test.ts` — scope key resolved once per attempt and pinned across split identities.
  - `attempt.active-exec-boundary-refresh.test.ts` — pipeline-level test driving the real `runEmbeddedAttempt` tool loop: a background exec started mid-turn is listed at the next LLM boundary and dropped after the registry confirms exit.
  - Targeted run: `3 passed / 28 tests passed`.
- **Live acceptance** (gateway PID 3305110 running the repaired build): background exec started in session `mild-meadow` (pid 3309537); the next LLM boundary listed the running session; after a termination request the process registry confirmed SIGTERM exit; the following boundary reported `none`; cleanup verified.
- **Captured boundary trace** (see [comment #5986775200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151770#issuecomment-5986775200)):
  - Boundary 1 (assembly): `Active exec sessions: none`
  - Boundary 2 (mid-run): `Active exec sessions: - <session> running pid=<pid> ...` — session appears in a NEW appended carrier
  - Boundary 1 replayed at step 2: `Active exec sessions: none` — original carrier byte-identical (prefix preservation proof)
  - Boundary 4 (after stop): `Active exec sessions: none` — session removed after termination
- **Branch**: commit `0dcc7f19` on top of `7f040a5`, single additional commit addressing all three ClawSweeper findings.
- Full suite (`pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test`) targeted to run on the submission branch; targeted lanes for the touched surfaces are green.

## ClawSweeper findings addressed

| Finding | Severity | Resolution |
|---------|----------|------------|
| Preserve the prefix when runtime context is append-only | P1 | Refresh appends a new carrier instead of mutating the existing one |
| Include scope fields in the prompt assembly input type | P2 | `processScopeKey` and `execOverrides` added to `PromptContextAttempt` |
| Refresh active exec facts for readable version 3 sessions | P2 | Refresh moved before `usesEscapedRuntimeContext` version check |

prs.title: perf(ui): isolate config state test fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

State-only Config and Memory unit tests load the entire Config renderer through their shared fixture. Four affected files spent 11.769 seconds in collection in the latest completed scheduled main run.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This reduces incidental test collection work while preserving every existing case, assertion, real renderer mount and fixture lifecycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing context/state fixture functions and their single publication WeakMap together into a state-only helper. Renderer tests retain the original mount helper, which uses the same context completer. All consumers move together; there are no compatibility reexports or duplicate state. prs.title: fix(storage): defer WAL timers during owned offline maintenance
prs.body:
Related: #166413, #170022

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated lock-refusal warnings when background SQLite maintenance runs during the same process's offline work.

## User Impact

Background maintenance waits for offline work to finish, or stops waiting when canceled. Repeated reader/busy warnings stay compact; real storage errors remain visible. Explicit checkpoints retain their existing authority checks. There are no database schema, stored-format, permission, retention or durability changes and no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Optional timer work should wait for its verified local maintenance owner instead of repeatedly attempting work that must be refused. Release resumes the existing cadence without polling; cancellation and ownership loss remain distinct. Detailed WAL health remains available separately from compact logs.

The conflict repair composes this behavior with upstream's current cold-creation writer-lock checks, schema-only fact invalidation, shared Darwin process inspection and single benchmark-schema catalog. Superseded local migration code was removed rather than retained as a second owner.

## Evidence

- **Implementation checkpoint:** `fd05473b5b2d5376474d965cac6769e095095cbd`, tree `60edd7189a30bad1681a68c749d4168d109cd050`, preserves the ordered history of `678358f72f56356d9b6f2c71265322972be3b952` and frozen upstream `cbfaa0d8b7dfb9b55aabd5db6fbe42c468036f35`. The net change against that upstream pin is 15 files. Published head `715abae3ac59e8ef6fb4ecd756af29f4a649fdb1` is the Gateway’s verified same-tree publication-marker child of this checkpoint. Local proof below binds that exact source composition; published-head CI failed as detailed below.
- **71 distinct runtime cases passed** across the affected ownership, WAL, creation, integrity/seal, wrapper and fixture boundaries. This is 82 executions because the 11-case Darwin inspection fixture ran under both Node and pinned Bun on Linux; it is not physical Darwin proof. The 174 cases excluded by explicit selectors are not passes. Index-repair proof reached both DELETE and WAL crash/reopen paths, preserving the 16,384-row hash and idempotence. The dependency-free package fixture exercised its unknown-argument rejection, not an installable product package.
- **Static results: 11 of 14 commands passed; three investigated local failures remain RED.** Production-core types passed. All 29 test compiler graphs passed through the normal owner's fallback, but the changed-test boundary command failed and its consumer narrowing did not complete. Focused typed lint, formatting, Kysely and the other selected guards passed; the database-worker guard independently reported 171→171 live and 15→15 compatibility calls.
- **Fresh independent P0–P3 source review:** six complete responsibility-based cohorts covered all 15 net paths and their full final owner/caller contexts, with no actionable findings. This is static review evidence, not runtime or installed-product proof.
- **Published-head CI:** [run 39494839215](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39494839215), attempt 1, **FAILED**: 135 jobs—110 passed, 23 skipped, one failed test job plus its aggregate gate. Checkout was merge `02286978f3e15d4989180617bb1a2c3738b8ebd7` against base `c909114f55fc5889076bf4fbbb61f6ab32bf8146` plus the published head above, not frozen `cbfaa0d8`. The sole failed test was Bun Bifrost API-key parity: malformed-URL validation throws before key resolution. Source comparison attributes it to the tested base, not a baseline execution; Bifrost is absent from the published head and frozen base. [Upstream fix 7df11be5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7df11be5ab10e47980973ed9d2ef60f488fa7820) is not integrated or tested in this candidate. Dependency/security statuses passed; CI remains failed.
- **Still pending:** full candidate packaging/build and the isolated published-driver update cell have not run. No current-head durable review, ready-for-review, installed-runtime, live PostgreSQL or physical Darwin acceptance is claimed. The separate shared-state-reader/Doctor drainage issue remains unresolved.

<details>
<summary>Investigated local failures and retained historical evidence</summary>

Local validation remains `tests.result: fail`, with these failures retained in `tests.investigatedLocalFailures`:

1. **Core-test root budget:** gateway-root 721/720, infra 723/720 and plugins-platform 727/720. All 207 TypeScript configuration files, the boundary owners and tracked test membership match the frozen upstream input. The feature adds no test-root file. The normal fallback's 29 compiler passes do not make the boundary pass; later bundled-extension membership validation did not run.
2. **Max-lines:** `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts` and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts` have incoming suppressions absent from the incoming baseline. The whole-index check is independent of the feature delta. Its nested environment check short-circuited, so the standalone check was executed separately.
3. **Environment names:** the standalone guard reported 459 names against 452. Counted names in all eight changed production files are unchanged from the frozen base, and the remaining production sources, guard and budget are incoming-exact. Historical 453/452 belongs to the earlier composition, not this count.

These are source-bound inherited diagnoses, not separately executed baseline passes. No cap, baseline, suppression, environment-severity override or guard waiver was used. A bounded upstream search found no complete repair to import for these causes. Existing GitHub Actions warning policy does not erase the local REDs or establish a current CI pass.

The [prior published-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38900010210), attempt 1, remains failed: 92 successful jobs, 15 failed (14 underlying jobs plus the aggregate), and 23 skipped. It tested published head `aeb5a23205b66f631e879b02b59ca3834543a5d2` through merge `e9b84bd1d084f8d83e0c80717e521c536d8fd7f0` against base `5ce763a03eb12089663cf3bc665e33549bb96e0a`; it is not CI for this new composition. Its integrity-proof invalidation and extracted-owner inventory defects were repaired locally and then converged onto upstream's owning implementations. The Darwin census, benchmark catalog and CLI-copy fixtures now use the current upstream contracts. The historical malformed-secondary-ownership failure passed on later inputs, but its exact cause remains unproven; a passing replay is not a causal repair. Focused passes do not blanket-reclassify the other old CI failures as fixed.

Earlier 18-case, 17/65-case and other focused results remain historical. The [older concurrent-claim failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38839838033/job/116777730816) and its deterministic red/green regression evidence are retained. [CI run 38796748726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38796748726) passed on `42ef154`; it does not qualify the current head.

The [durable ClawSweeper comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167048#issuecomment-6055542333) still reviews `16cf632c8bb374ab548cb57b210199d0b7485202`: no code findings, a historical conflict hold and an installed-entry-point proof gap. It is not a review of this composition. The current read found no formal reviews or inline threads. No merge or auto-merge is requested.

</details>

Requested and co-authored by @RomneyDa.

prs.title: test(ui): reuse compiled assets for worker update fixture
prs.body:
## Problem and change

The service-worker update E2E compiles the same source twice to give deployments A and B different identities. The existing terminal case explicitly requires their entry assets to be identical. The second compile alone takes 19.63 seconds in the retained scheduled-main log.

Compile A once, copy its output to the existing pristine B directory, then call the production `refreshControlUiBuildOutput` owner with B’s identity. This is the same owner used by the production cached-build path. It regenerates HTML identity, the offline manifest, CSP and service worker while keeping the immutable bundles. Each scenario still gets its own deployment copy; the terminal scenario cannot mutate the pristine worker.

No production code, browser or Gateway lifecycle, test cases, assertions, selectors, timeouts, capture behavior, or lazy boundaries change. All five cases and 31 matcher sites remain; everything from `findBuildAsset` through the last case is byte-identical.

## Proof

| Check / metric | Before | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full Vite compiles in the suite | 2 | 1 |
| Production deployment identities | 2 | 2 |
| Expanded cases / matcher sites | 5 / 31 | 5 / 31 |
| E2E file wall in CI | 65.502 s | Pending exact-head CI |
| Missed chat activation case | 27.091 s | Pending exact-head CI |
| Mocked E2E shard 8/9 test step | 782 s | Pending exact-head CI |
| Existing cached-output owner unit test | Retained | 1 passed; 0.772 s runner / 4.21 s wrapper |
| UI typecheck | — | Passed |
| Targeted lint / format / independent review | — | Passed; no actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Test file LOC | 759 | 769 |
| Production LOC delta | — | 0 |

Baseline: scheduled main [39476345087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39476345087), commit `00cb4b3c512e02a7265d6f80c182d8906b556553`; relevant source matches this branch’s base. The initial compile took 25.32 s; the second took 19.63 s. File wall includes setup and is not the sum of printed cases. These observations are not yet a claimed candidate improvement.

Acceptance recorded before CI: remove the second compile, preserve all five passing cases, and demonstrate a material file-wall reduction (about 10 seconds or more). Report actual per-file and per-shard before/after without attributing unrelated inventory or concurrency changes. No shard weight change until timing evidence supports one. Revert this optimization if CI shows no gain.

Newer completed scheduled main [39484133203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39484133203), commit `52714b572789b3d4bbc503075b94349aeadf5c71`, runs the unchanged source in **40.495 s** (five passed; missed-chat-activation case 18.351 s). Candidate acceptance must also beat this newer baseline; the older 65.502 s observation alone will not establish a gain.

Local command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/app/vite-config-cache.node.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` using the default pinned Bun. This existing unit test verifies identity/CSP/manifest changes, immutable compressed bytes and idempotence. `pnpm tsgo:ui` also passed after frozen install. Broad browser/update behavior is delegated to `ci:full`; no local E2E or app build under the campaign budget. No visual output changes or new screenshots. Startup bytes are not remeasured: only test fixture code changes, with no production import graph change.

## Exact-head CI measurement

Run [39506266962](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39506266962), head `3c0428115ca00e51601a10406b398092685f8f43`, retains all five exact case names and assertions. The source before the change is byte-identical to the newer scheduled-main file.

| Metric | Newer main | Candidate | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| File wall | 40.495 s | 37.377 s | -3.118 s (-7.7%) |
| Full Vite compiles | 2 | 1 | -1 |
| Mocked E2E shard8/9 step, same100-file inventory | 626 s | 682 s | +56 s observed |

The candidate improves the newest source-qualified baseline by only3.118seconds, missing the approximately10-second acceptance target. The older65.502-second baseline does not rescue this result. The slower shard is also retained as evidence; this run establishes no total shard saving. The experiment is rejected. Cancellation raced with auto-merge: native reconciliation confirmed merge248be4909feb9cc58c1f021f2d25281de3e26abb. A focused rollback is being prepared to restore the original implementation. At rejection13/14 UI jobs passed, with real-Gateway2 pending; the five cases themselves passed. Main keeps its unchanged implementation.

Rollback: #178847 restores the exact pre-optimization source; full CI is pending.

prs.title: fix(ui): chat header loses title and run details when the session is off the loaded page
prs.body:
Split from #177698 (session-input consolidation) so that PR stays scoped to the SessionController lifecycle. The change is by @enki; I moved it unchanged onto current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI chat header lost the open chat's title and run metadata (status, last run, runtime) when that session was no longer on the loaded sessions page, for example after a forced refresh returned a page without it.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the session list has already observed the session, the chat pane now projects transcript metadata from the observed row for the same session incarnation, instead of dropping to nothing. Metadata from a different incarnation is still ignored, and deleting the session still clears it.

## User Impact

The open chat keeps its title and last-run details until the session is actually deleted, regardless of which sessions page is loaded.

## Evidence

- New test `keeps off-page descriptor title and transcript metadata until the session is deleted` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-offline-metadata.test.ts` fails on current `main` and passes with this change. The file passes 7 of 7 (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-offline-metadata.test.ts`).
- The test covers the off-page title, the transcript metadata fields, a different-incarnation guard, and clearing after `sessions.delete`.

prs.title: fix(ios): recover Watch screenshots when the runtime becomes unavailable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iOS screenshot runs that finish the iPhone and iPad captures, then stop because the Watch runtime is no longer available. Run [39494550226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39494550226) exposed a gap before the existing simulator-creation repair could run.

## User Impact

CI can repair an unavailable Watch runtime once immediately before Watch capture. Local runs continue to leave runtime installation to the operator. Failed boots and captures still stop the lane; screenshot attempts are not repeated.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared Watch admission step now handles both missing runtime selection and the existing missing-runtime-path creation failure. It replaces the early shell check and separate CI probe, so release screenshots, PR CI, and standalone Watch capture use the same owner. Recovery logs availability, image state, and mounted-path existence without runtime filesystem paths.

The OS-level reason the runtime became unavailable remains unproven; this fixes the observed recovery gap. Production changes add 69 lines and remove 79. The existing lifecycle test gains coverage for the missing boundary, the one-repair limit, and Watch-specific boot/cleanup failures; obsolete probe and shell-provisioning tests are removed.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the base after eight screenshots with no Watch creation, then passes with the fix.
- 116 focused Fastlane/release/device-selection tests pass, including cleanup, failed runtime download, persistent unavailability, and unavailable selection followed by creation failure without a second repair.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, format, Ruby/Bash syntax, and workflow checks pass.
- Independent review completed; findings addressed.
- [Final-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39508484527) on `5b2c11955c04`, including native screenshot capture and screenshot evidence validation. ClawSweeper reviewed the same commit with no actionable findings.
- Native `ios watch_screenshot` passes on Xcode 27A266a with pinned Ruby/Fastlane/Rust: real Watch boot, inspected fixture PNG, and simulator cleanup. This exercised the healthy path; recovery fault cases are covered by the regression fixture.
- [Full hosted screenshot validation passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39507216313) on production commit `57ed570ebb3`; the follow-up changes tests only. This run encountered a real `runtime path not found` creation error, repaired the Watch runtime once, then completed capture and cleanup. The new unavailable-selection branch is covered by the deterministic regression.
- [Retained artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39507216313/artifacts/12304204466): nine valid PNGs, all eight iPhone/iPad captures succeeded on attempt one, all 24 diagnostic phases succeeded, and all three simulators were cleaned up. Resource timeline retained with exit code zero. No build was uploaded.

prs.title: fix(muse): streamed replies lose their beginning when OpenClaw attaches mid-turn
prs.body:
Split from #177698 (session-input consolidation) so that PR stays scoped to the SessionController lifecycle. The change is by @enki; I moved it unchanged onto current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Muse runtime replies lost the beginning of their streamed text when OpenClaw attached to a turn after Muse had already started streaming. Live output in chat started mid-sentence, even though the saved final answer was complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw kept its own accumulator built only from deltas it received after subscribing. It now reads accumulated item text from the Muse SDK's session fold, which already owns prefixes received before the subscription. That removes the competing accumulator instead of patching it.

## User Impact

Streaming replies from the Muse runtime show the full text from the first character, including content produced before OpenClaw attached to the turn.

## Evidence

- `extensions/muse/src/events.test.ts`: with the production change reverted and the new tests kept, 1 of 4 fails; with the change applied, 4 of 4 pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/muse/src/events.test.ts`, on current `main`).
- Gateway stream proof from the original PR, which exercises this exact change through authenticated chat RPC, the production Muse harness and SDK 1.4.4: a prefix frame arrives before the native command ACK, and the client sees `["started:", " hello"]`, matching one saved `started: hello`. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698#issuecomment-6297282981.

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain device source identity across reconnects
prs.body:
## Local deployment checkpoint (2026-10-20)

The operator explicitly opted into a combined local deployment containing main consolidation `7605b4fc8c28a628cd4d6b9a3e63bc9f1304ce10`, reply-obligation candidate `66eea4b4ef10f196ba1640398d186884d5557cdd`, reconnect candidate `de1dfafe07c8f0762b9e5fc16d4dfc6b36a3fbeb`, and selected-requester candidate `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`, alongside existing local integrations and the separately restored saved-attempt UI work. The resulting local build is `764886a56987d82f3a3934e2dd7d6a2416ef98da`.

Operational readback confirms the exact loaded build, readiness, health, Node 24, unchanged service environment, and all 25 previously active plugins. This is a combined integration deployment, not standalone validation of each PR or security/session-owner acceptance of any extracted policy. No new business-message, native-effect, revocation or reassignment proof is inferred from operational health. The earlier isolated traces below retain their recorded revisions, scenarios and failed-collector qualifications.

## Relationship to the consolidation

[#177698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698) at `d383dd4e9bb180d5dd880f21029ac7d586052130` extracts verified cross-socket reconnect comparison sharing from the lifecycle consolidation. This remains the focused reconnect proposal; it is **not superseded** by that narrowed head. The existing continuation/principal-transfer contract and live source checks stay in the consolidation. Security-owner acceptance of comparison sharing remains required here. The focused reconnect proposal and historical captures are unchanged; their results are not claimed as behavior implemented by the narrowed consolidation.

## What Problem This Solves

After an authenticated Control UI device-token connection reconnects, a new parent turn can receive a different model-source identity from a native child still running under its valid retained source. Native `collaboration.send_message` and `followup_task` then fail the existing “same admitted model source” check. The CLI presents that refusal as “Native hook relay unavailable,” although the request reached the Gateway and the child continued running.

## User Impact

An established browser device-token connection can reconnect and keep comparison identity with its retained work. Each request still owns a separate live authority. The native guard still checks both sources, and the child keeps its original model authority and admission ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fix the identity issuer. Share a comparison record only when the host-verified device credential generation, profile, role, scopes, client/origin, policy generations and exact access/ingress owners match. The existing revocation owner retains records only while captured work holds them. A host-transferred principal can use that record; a copied client cannot borrow it.

Different devices, rotated tokens, profiles, reduced scopes, unproven authentication and distinct access grants stay separate. Reconnect matching grants no replacement permissions. No configuration, protocol, schema, native-model guard, or credential-storage change is introduced.

## Evidence and current revision

Current integration head: `de1dfafe07c8f0762b9e5fc16d4dfc6b36a3fbeb`, an automatic merge of the preceding standalone `42aff70a9169d5043a4faf559f13c63bc248bb4f` with upstream `f629720edbb9f4b458adae30c7506c1dc5d1adc6`. The latest completed ClawSweeper review examined `42aff70a` and credited the source-qualified matching-reconnect and foreign-device evidence. The determining feature owners and unchanged reconnect regression retain their bytes; historical runtime captures below retain their stated revisions. Security-owner acceptance remains outstanding.

### Current CI integration and causal baseline

This automatic upstream merge addresses the named inherited xAI test-type failure, adopting upstream's canonical `0449ef26` / #177830 repair. It introduces no local dependency workaround, budget change or manual conflict resolution. Core production types, owning Gateway test types and the extension-test graph that previously failed on xAI now pass, as do scoped type-aware lint and formatting.

The existing reconnect regression was also executed unchanged under the current supported harness with only its three determining production owners restored to exact pre-fix `9509fc22f772876605df5121d99f97923074a21e` bytes (which equal incoming upstream): **one intended failure and two passing controls**. The failure is the original source object-identity assertion for a verified matching reconnect; restoring the candidate owners makes **all three cases pass**. Seven sibling suites pass **87 cases**, covering source lifetime, policy closure, device revocation, operator profile/model restrictions and cross-module identity. This is a three-owner determining-source rollback, **not** execution of the entire historical base tree. The initial old-harness compiler mismatch failed before tests and is not counted as RED.

No fresh runtime/native capture is claimed for this merge. Existing accepted native receipts stay revision-qualified, including the failed collector and cleanup qualifications below. Current hosted CI is separate from these local checks; no security-owner approval is inferred.

The [combined alternative’s published runtime receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698#issuecomment-6279938739), contains actual synthetic native reconnect evidence captured at `b579b5c49caee812795fb486739e93aafcadc541`. This is **qualified source-owner reuse, not execution of this standalone head**:

- After an authenticated matching device-token reconnect, an actual advertised native `collaboration.send_message` reached the original still-running child. A correlated native completed-interaction receipt, subsequent child provider request, one attributed native peer MESSAGE echo and the consumed final all identify that same original child turn.
- A different paired device with the same authorized profile and scopes reached the native source-comparison guard and was refused. No child interaction or forbidden guidance appeared in the original child provider requests/journal; that original child turn completed unchanged. This demonstrates refusal before child-input effect, not absence of all native metadata or sender I/O.
- The previously audited standalone `42aff70a9169d5043a4faf559f13c63bc248bb4f` and captured `b579b5c49caee812795fb486739e93aafcadc541` revisions have byte-identical credential attestation, authenticated dispatch, device comparison records, operator authority, admitted context, retained host source, native source/child monitor, compatibility check and submission/final-check owners. Comparison sharing still does not share execution authority or replace either source’s original/current model ceilings.

Both child cases used fresh temporary state and scripted loopback provider responses with the actual native `0.163.0` binary; the source dependency pin remained `0.162.1`. The private synthetic model-metadata V2 adaptation is disclosed. All owned native processes joined with exit0/signal:null; ordinary teardown forwarded two SIGTERMs after selected native turn terminals in each case. Gateway cleanup reported confirmed stopped with no errors. These captures prove neither external-model performance nor historical incident token continuity.

### Remaining boundaries

The combined revision also captured canonical device revocation during genuine **human steering** preparation: the original admitted request was denied after preparation resumed, with no observed native steering input. That case used a materially different combined continuation owner, and its native process required SIGKILL containment; the original failed clean-exit qualification is retained. It is not a clean passing native-child preparation-revocation case for this standalone branch.

The new native child-send control below exercises canonical credential revocation during genuine preparation. Its observed cancellation/no-input result and its failed collector qualification are reported separately. The native-hook waiting implementation, host active-closure implementation and human continuation owners also differ between the standalone and combined revisions; whole-binary equivalence is not asserted. A security-owner decision is still required.

Earlier focused unit/static/build results remain evidence of their named historical revisions, not fresh checks of this head. The production-dispatch regression establishes the issuer mismatch and keeps authority objects distinct; the combined native captures extend that mechanism to allowed delivery and the nearest foreign-device refusal. No review approval or complete standalone proof is inferred.

### Native child-send preparation revocation at preceding `42aff70a`

An additional isolated, synthetic native-child control ran against exact preceding standalone `42aff70a9169d5043a4faf559f13c63bc248bb4f` (source declares Codex 0.162.0; QA used the explicitly pinned 0.163.0 binary and a scripted local provider). The actual child-send preToolUse hook started, and its genuine metadata response was held unchanged. The original device credential was canonically revoked 88 ms after the hold; the identical response bytes were released 102 ms after the hold. The retained source cancelled the sender before that release; the exact native parent turn interrupted, and the runtime reported `operator source authority is no longer active`. The child received no guidance marker, no child-input write or send interaction was observed, and its original turn finished unchanged. Both native processes exited 0/signal:null; normal cleanup forwarded two SIGTERMs after all selected turn terminals; Gateway and provider joined.

**The collector exited 1, not a full passing capture:** cancellation produced no matching hook/completed receipt, so its strict stopped-receipt observer failed and the QA owner retained task state for audit. This demonstrates source cancellation during genuine child-send preparation with no observed child input; it does not isolate the post-await guard, claim a completed tool-refusal receipt, or claim task-state removal. The separate canonical runtime build passed; the earlier full build remains blocked by the declaration-size budget.

Root independently checked the actual native hook start, metadata request/response correlation, canonical revocation receipt, cancellation timing, stopped child journal, native exits and all 276 frozen source/generated/fixture/binary pins.

```json
{
  "originalCollectorExit": 1,
  "originalCollectorQualified": false,

  "actualQaOverride": "0.163.0",
  "nativeHookStartedForExactSend": true,
  "realMetadataResponseHeld": true,
  "canonicalOriginalCredentialRevoke": true,
  "heldResponseByteIdentity": true,
  "timingRelativeHoldMs": {
    "canonicalRevocation": 88,
    "revocationReceiptObserved": 97,
    "originalBytesReleased": 102
  },

  "actualGatewayTerminal": "error/rpc",
  "actualSourceError": "operator source authority is no longer active",
  "sourceErrorLoggedAfterReleaseMs": 72,
  "targetChildGuidanceAbsentInStoppedJournal": true,
  "nativeChildInteractionsAfterArm": 0,
  "hostChildInputWritesAfterArm": 0,
  "nativeHookCompletionAbsent": true,
  "nativeProcessExits": [
    {
      "code": 0,

    },

    }
  ],

  "providerStopped": true,
  "cleanupObserverFailed": true,
  "taskStateRetainedForAudit": true,
  "limits": [
    "No hook/completed tool-refusal receipt; original collector remains failed.",
    "Cancellation of live retained source during preparation observed; no isolated proof that post-await assertion rather than source abort propagation caused denial.",

  ],

```

### Hosted CI attribution

The actual tested CI merge was `aa9b9e15646651ec935a45aece51fde3220d3fcf`, merging preceding standalone `42aff70a9169d5043a4faf559f13c63bc248bb4f` into `45801179f6d99ffc1db9480320ef4bc189a4b8d7`. The two failed jobs have incoming-base determining source:

- Extension test types: `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts:675` supplies `{status:400}` to the numeric-status `jsonResponse` helper. Both the tested test and helper blobs exactly match that incoming base.
- UI recovery: the 390/1280 viewport cases attempt Retry while the recovery button is disabled/busy. The tested gateway-status component, test and shared support blobs exactly match that incoming base. The standalone head has an older component; attribution uses the actual tested merge.

Root independently verified all five cached tested blobs against the incoming-base Git tree. This is source-based attribution, not a separately executed base types/browser reproduction or a claim that hosted CI is green. Those failures are not assigned speculative repairs in this authority PR.

Published evidence is allowlisted synthetic observations only; raw credentials, identities, endpoints, paths and transcripts remain private.

This batch consolidates repetitive test fixtures, setup, assertions, and table cases across Codex, Discord, plugins, Gateway, subagents, UI, and infrastructure. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <changed files>`: exit 0.

Rejected: invalid-proxy mock concern; `createDiscordGatewayPlugin` calls the real `validateDiscordProxyUrl` before the mocked agent factory, and that validator rejects `bad-proxy`. The fallback remains exercised without duplicating validation inside the mock.

prs.title: improve(postgres): reduce model-context navigation read work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL model-context reads repeatedly parse canonical transcript JSON and serialize/reparse intermediate JSONB while deriving navigation and exact byte costs. The bounded navigation-page query now parses each selected row once, shares message/content and model projections, and keeps intermediates as JSONB until the result boundary. Native object construction replaces repeated jsonb_set chains.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL model-context navigation does less repeated projection work per read, with byte-identical context accounting. Canonical INSERTs and SQLite storage remain unchanged. Existing stored envelopes still bypass canonical payload parsing. No schema, protocol, transaction, advisory-lock, or freshness-probe changes are included.

## Performance

Owner acceptance: the directly measured effect is −73.6% navigation SQL time and −50.6% combined SQL time with byte-identical output; INSERT is unchanged. The pooled p95 +21.3% comes from pairs on a busy local host that disagreed in direction, so it's treated as noise. A consolidated interleaved A/B/A/B Testbox re-measure runs after the pgopt wave.

## Evidence

### Exactness and work proof

An independent copy of the original PostgreSQL expressions supplies the byte oracle. The real-PG fixture compares navigation strings and exact model/retained byte counts for messages, tool calls/results, custom and system updates, reset, compaction/branch summaries, missing/null/unknown fields, synthetic missing-tool markers, provider replay, private upstream-user text, Unicode/non-BMP/escapes, and numeric scale/exponents. Stored-envelope reads also work with an unavailable canonical payload. Independent review checked 340 additional output/error cases against the old SQL.

For the same 20-row synthetic query, canonical event_json::jsonb occurrences fall from 54 to one and jsonb_set calls from 12 to zero. Ten interleaved EXPLAIN samples matched every output byte and reduced median server execution from 6.9255 to 1.3245 ms (80.9%). These are query-level measurements, not application latency claims.

## Frozen local A/B

Both variants use the same verified 63-file frozen harness, Node 24, and Homebrew PostgreSQL 17. Baseline is d4a2c1fea7444516a92ca66f1dcf75d71f248828. The measured runtime matches 910d2b9a6717b4ee2ec902f84ca58c0de54401a7 and final head 529121807bf7891e86627f120a666f76936b1ab5 byte-for-byte; the later commit only corrects dialect classification and its test.

Acceptance: target at least 50% less navigation execution per call/turn; reject below 30% or on any byte difference. INSERT implementation and counts must stay unchanged.

| Warm census, per turn | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Causal R/T/S | 11.333 / 48.333 / 57.333 | 11.333 / 48.333 / 57.333 |
| Navigation calls | 0 | 0 |
| INSERT calls | 3 | 3 |
| INSERT server time, ms | 0.8483 | 0.5286 |

| C=64, per turn | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Navigation calls / rows | 1 / 18.4 | 1 / 18.4 |
| Navigation server time, ms per call and turn | 3.9709 | 1.3144 |
| INSERT calls | 7.6 | 7.6 |
| INSERT server time, ms | 0.9525 | 1.2039 |
| Navigation + INSERT server time, ms | 4.9234 | 2.5183 |
| Observed turns/s | 2.7197 | 1.5647 |
| Observed p95, s | 34.399 | 48.442 |

Navigation time falls 66.9%, exceeding the 50% target; combined navigation and INSERT time falls 48.9%. Both C=64 cells complete 320/320 without errors/timeouts and visit the same 5,888 rows. All 2,515 final rows retain NULL navigation envelopes, confirming the write-time implementation is absent. INSERT SQL and work counts are identical; its small timing movement is reported above.

The host was shared, with full conformance running concurrently with the candidate. The wall-time figures are not a controlled latency comparison and no throughput improvement is claimed. C=64 uses runtime-only observation, so a client R/T/S ledger is unavailable.

Original frozen baseline census and C=64 attempts encountered the known startup-sidecars restart admission refusal; their failures are retained. The separate paired C=64 measurements use the same explicitly labeled adapter, retrying only that pre-admission refusal for at most 30 seconds with unchanged parameters. All original 63 files remain unchanged. The candidate original census completes including restart.

## Serial A/B/A/B repeat

After local conformance ended, four serial C=64 cells completed 320/320 each with zero errors. Each cell used the same frozen admitted runner, fresh database, and hash-verified source/build. Counts remain one navigation call / 18.4 rows and 7.6 INSERT calls per turn. The host remained shared, with starting load averages of approximately 45, 36, 36, and 25 on 32 CPUs.

| Pooled over 640 turns per variant | Baseline | Read-side candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Navigation ms/call and ms/turn | 3.9238 | 1.0371 |
| INSERT ms/turn | 1.3381 | 1.5643 |
| Navigation + INSERT ms/turn | 5.2619 | 2.6014 |
| Turns/s | 2.8445 | 2.8817 |
| p95, seconds | 32.2670 | 39.1275 |

Navigation falls 73.57% and combined SQL time falls 50.56%, confirming the requested SQL improvement. INSERT SQL and call counts remain identical. Throughput moves +1.31%, while pooled p95 moves +21.26%. Tail direction reverses between pairs: 26.687 → 39.679 seconds in A1/B1 and 32.829 → 19.959 seconds in A2/B2. These shared-host wall observations do not establish an application latency improvement. The pooled p95 crosses the performance workflow's 20% review threshold; the owner acceptance above records the decision to land the SQL-scoped change with this wall-time limitation.

## Checks and remaining gates

The PostgreSQL byte fixture, all 60 existing payload/context/history/report consumer tests, core and scripts typechecks, targeted lint/format, Kysely guardrails, 30 dialect tests, and two independent autoreviews pass. The dialect guard correction is limited to known PostgreSQL functions/operators and four exact native helper declarations; SQLite operations in those helpers and unrelated code remain counted. SQLite dialect counts remain 25 to 25.

Final-head local PostgreSQL conformance covered all 602 selected cases. The full command finished with 599 passes and three Doctor snapshot mismatches: the benchmark-only pg_stat_statements extension appeared in the diagnostic inventory. Clean baseline reproduced precisely that extension-only diff. With the CI extension set (vector, pg_trgm, unaccent), all five Doctor cases passed on the same final head; no snapshots or application code changed. The earlier username-free DSN attempt was stopped after environment-cleared workers exposed the missing username and is not counted as valid conformance evidence.

The serial A/B/A/B repeat is complete as reported above. Owner performance acceptance is recorded above. Final-head CI run [39488602811](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39488602811) actually ran PostgreSQL conformance; all three shards passed, including their Run PostgreSQL conformance steps. Final CI completed with 87 successful jobs, 24 skipped jobs, and two failed test jobs plus their aggregate CI gate. The two test failures are qualified below for native inherited-failure admission; all three actual PostgreSQL conformance steps and security-fast passed.

Two unrelated CI failures are retained and investigated. The OpenAI compaction-replay E2E fails at line 102 with split length 3 instead of 2 on both this head and clean main; the test and prompt-state owners are identical across baseline, CI base, and tested merge. The startup-recovery admission case fails in CI but passes in the full 23-case file on both this head and clean main. Its 59 inspected ownership files are identical, and source tracing confines this fixture to SQLite session metadata (session.entry.read and entry-field replacement), without entering model-context navigation. That timing/cross-file cause remains unresolved; the passing replays are not claimed as a fix. The native inherited-failure route retains both failed results and this source-based qualification; no PR-caused test failure is waived. The diff is 381 additions and 69 deletions across seven files; 121 added lines preserve the independent legacy SQL oracle.

## Rejected write-time experiment

The previous revision populated the full native envelope during every INSERT. Its byte proof passed, but it paid for full projections across 7.6 INSERT calls per turn and later rewrites discarded some envelopes. JSONB-to-text-to-JSONB intermediates amplified that cost. The bounded read range is the appropriate optimization point.

| Rejected local C=64 server ms/turn | Baseline | INSERT envelope |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Navigation | 4.9069 | 0.7040 |
| INSERT | 1.0934 | 15.4192 |
| Combined | 6.0004 | 16.1233 |

That candidate regressed combined SQL cost 168.7% and was not landed. A single Testbox A/B independently measured warm INSERT time 0.4274 to 11.1332 ms/turn with unchanged R/T/S. Its restart admission failure prevented remote C=64; the lease was stopped. This PR's branch history now contains only the read-side implementation and its classification repair.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid startup restart loops while Tailscale needs login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A supervised Gateway can repeatedly fail startup while Tailscale needs login or machine approval. Restarting the Gateway cannot satisfy that operator prerequisite.

Related: #167072

## User Impact

After a supervised Tailscale Serve startup fails, the Gateway finishes cleanup and waits without listeners. It tells the operator to sign in or approve the node. Once Tailscale reports Running, it attempts normal startup once. The Serve claim and Gateway readiness checks must still pass before service starts.

Foreground startup, Funnel, unknown failures and route conflicts retain their existing failure behavior. The change does not sign in to Tailscale, modify routes, or change Gateway authentication.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway run loop owns recovery. A typed error identifies the missing Tailscale prerequisite. Status checks use increasing intervals capped at 30 seconds. Shutdown cancels the wait and waits for its cleanup. A completed authentication-prerequisite failure does not count toward the crash-loop breaker. Other startup failures and unfinished boots still count.

Recovery restores transport availability. Gateway authentication and personal-identity rules continue to govern access.

## Evidence

### Current revision, October 21

Current head is [`2ca59ca9e667907432836f290e9288d1058bd728`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2ca59ca9e667907432836f290e9288d1058bd728), including main `2ad4d4c` through ordinary merges. A startup failure is now recorded before either tracked startup cleanup or the recovery waiter rethrows a genuine failure. A pending login recovery is not recorded as completed early. The existing one-completion guard and authentication-prerequisite distinction remain intact.

The added regressions cover terminal recovery errors, including an undefined rejection value, retained cleanup, and completion ordering. Affected formatting and lint passed. Independent P0-P3 reviews were inspected against the source; accepted findings were repaired, and one later finding was rejected because ordinary failures already complete before entering the recovery path. The final main merge required no manual resolution and preserved the reviewed contributor changes.

The new owning regression assertions have not executed locally: worker preparation stopped before assertions. The new automatic [CI 39512571006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39512571006) is in progress on this exact head. Older green CI and installed parking/cancellation results below retain their actual revisions. They do not prove this revision, resolve the old Doctor timeout, or establish authenticated restoration, stable upgrade or approval of the waiting policy.

### Previous revision, October 15

Head `04b36b54161b85b4ab6c2e034029bcb03183aa8a` removes a redundant copy of `worker-heap-flag.mjs` from the isolated runtime fixture and cleans up comments. The later identical copy remains. No assertion, timeout, recovery API or production control flow changed.
