prs.title: fix(telegram): replies finalized in the streaming preview leave no gateway log line
prs.body:
Refs #49889
Related: #111064

#49889 is labeled `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` and `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`; I am sending this anyway because one behavior-neutral info line is a concrete thing to accept or reject, and the gap got wider for us on 10.1 (numbers under Evidence).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with Telegram streaming, final replies that land by finalizing the preview leave no info-level line in the gateway log, so operators cannot tell a delivered reply from a missing one.

## User Impact

User impact: every final answer now logs one info line naming how it reached Telegram, or why nothing was sent. Delivery itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

With streaming on, the final answer is usually edited into the preview the user is already looking at. That path never reaches `deliverReplies`, which owns the existing per-message success line, and the lane deliverer logs only through `logVerbose`. `deliverFinalAnswerText` is where each final answer's outcome settles, including the progress-mode branch that sends without the lane deliverer, so the line goes there:

`telegram final delivery outcome=<kind> chat=<id> [message=<ids>] [reason=<suppression reason>]`

It carries ids and the suppression reason only, no content. The first commit on this branch logged preview finalizations only; the second replaces that with the outcome line.

Now logged, one line per final answer:

- `preview-finalized`: final edited into the preview, with the preview's message id.
- `preview-finalized-partial`: the preview shows the final but a follow-up step failed (buttons, prompt-context record, media follow-up). The existing `telegram final reply failed` error line also fires.
- `preview-retained`: the preview send may have landed but returned no message id (`reason=adapter_returned_no_identity`).
- `sent`: final sent as new message(s), with their ids.
- `skipped`: nothing sent, with the suppression reason, e.g. `cancelled_by_message_sending_hook` on the durable path, `channel_transform`, `no_visible_result`.

Already logged before this change, unchanged:

- Transport failure (the send throws): `telegram final reply failed: <error>` at error level from `handleReplyError`. Not written under `errors.policy: "silent"`, or for a repeat inside the `"once"` cooldown.
- Each message the reply deliverer sends: `telegram text delivery ok chat=<id> message=<id>`. Each durable send: `telegram outbound send ok ...`. Both still fire for `sent` finals, next to the outcome line.

Not covered by the new line: finals that bypass `deliverFinalAnswerText` (media-only finals and status notices still get the send lines above), finals dropped before delivery (superseded turn, payload normalized away, exec-approval suppression, silent skip, adopted progress draft), non-final preview finalizations (blocks, `ask_user` questions), and the reasoning lane.

Overlap checked: #170069 (the #169930 fix) and #165510 touch other files. Once #170069 lands, the follow-up finals it fixes log `preview-finalized` instead of `sent`.

## Maintainer decision (October 20, 2026)

My recommendation remains to accept the narrow info-level outcome line at head `e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c`. The decision is whether settled text-final outcomes should appear in default Gateway logs. If the owner wants this only under verbose/debug logging, this PR needs that change before landing. No owner approval is recorded in the [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170110#issuecomment-6131057156) or the [linked issue discussion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49889).

The [log formatter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts#L453) includes the outcome, chat ID, returned message IDs and suppression reason, with no reply content. It runs at [the early channel-transform skip](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts#L493) and [the settled text-final result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts#L547). Existing per-message send lines remain, so a `sent` final can have both records. This is a diagnostic outcome, not proof that the human saw the message, and it does not cover finals that bypass this owner.

## Evidence

### Current-head validation (October 20, 2026)

Pushed [e633886c9f1c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c) to resolve the lifecycle-test conflict with main `62639573d1bca08810a1316972ef0ed77d786cc2`. The merge preserves the original branch history and the same 19-line production addition. Its test adaptation keeps upstream's shared fixtures and parameterized recording/replacement/second-final cases, then restores the outcome assertions. The final candidate tree is `4c67a161aa8ec33f0a6c596f4b8029ee9f22b366`.

The cancelled-answer case now checks exactly one visible status notice and exactly one `outcome=skipped` diagnostic. Current main [creates that fallback as a status notice](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c/src/agents/reply-completion.ts#L32), and [Telegram sends it through a separate path](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-reply.ts#L361) before the text-answer logger. The first integration run failed on the old notice wording; correcting that exposed the obsolete expectation of a second `outcome=sent` line. Both failures are retained in the validation record. Production behavior was not changed to satisfy those assertions.

Ran on an isolated Linux checkout with Node `26.8.2`, pinned pnpm `12.12.1`, its own frozen dependencies, temporary HOME/state and one test worker:

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: exact-main control `62639573d1bca08810a1316972ef0ed77d786cc2`, **11 passed**, exit `0`, wall `83.704 s`; final candidate `e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c`, **14 passed**, exit `0`, wall `80.032 s`.
- Negative control: retained the candidate tests and replaced only `bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts` with the exact-main version. **6 failed, 8 passed**, exit `1`, wall `104.130 s`. All six failures were the missing outcome-line assertions. Restored the production file and verified the candidate tree and file hashes.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`: exit `0`, wall `0.206 s`.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`: exit `0`, wall `152.667 s`, including required SDK declaration preparation. Final type-aware lint: **0 warnings, 0 errors**, 2 files, 292 rules, 1 thread.
- `git diff --cached --check` against the pinned main checkout: exit `0`. A merge-tree check against newer main `f91bca9546f5a5cc59a801efe3592d6910a58d80` is clean, tree `13a2be42c0a8e7df1ae1c07e20203881f38392aa`.

The test file exercises the real draft stream, delivery and shared dispatch owners over a stubbed Bot API. Its official worker preparation transforms 13,985 inputs; the wall times above include that cost. This refresh did not send live Telegram traffic. The early `channel_transform` recovery skip still has no targeted test.

Independent source review found no actionable P0-P2 issue in the logging/test adaptation. The final status-notice compatibility delta was separately checked against the current main sources above. Those reviews did not execute tests or approve the default-INFO policy. The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170110#issuecomment-6131057156) now targets `e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c` (reviewed October 20 at 21:27 UTC): no actionable findings. It accepts the current-head dispatch tests and logger-removal negative control as supporting the unchanged contributor-supplied production proof. That review ran no target code, and its remaining blocker is the maintainer decision on default INFO logging.

[Primary CI run 39496465505](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39496465505) for `e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c` finished successfully on October 20: **29 successful jobs, 30 skipped, 0 failed**. The executed merge was `856d95eaa1f7cb6b7a88285cdb3fac2621838519`, tree `3f977b465506ff1861d4d83bb759ede51aa2e527`, with parents `bead2a8e542740f943fe57e8391e5e6c11e9773d` and the published head. The complete preflight log and commit record establish that identity separately from the locally tested integration base.

[Hosted lifecycle job 118911270008](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39496465505/job/118911270008) passed all **14 cases** in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts`, matching the final local case names. Its complete 197,053-byte log records one planned target, one completed target, one invocation and zero failed targets. The production and test blobs match the published head. The successful [CI run 38296174975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38296174975), 30 successful and 29 skipped jobs, belongs to `13060bc3c1d688f4864c201bf7adb16b3982bd1f` and is historical evidence only.

### Historical contributor-supplied evidence

The production trace and earlier broader test runs below were recorded before this merge. They were not independently rerun for `e633886c9f1cb50dcbab8a5697a2d59e60578b3c`; current-head execution is listed above.

Production, 2026-10-12, one Telegram account on a build based on v2026.10.1 with local patches, `streaming.mode: "partial"`, no preview tool progress: 8 text replies since 2026-10-11 22:06. Telegram's sent-message records hold all 8; gateway.log has an info-level line for 3, so 5 of 8 reached the user with no line. The same bot on v2026.9.9 had 1 of 8 without a line.

Tests in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts` (real draft stream and reply deliverer over a mocked Bot API), each asserting the exact outcome lines:

- new: final finalized in the preview -> `outcome=preview-finalized` with the preview id
- new at the original base: durable send cancelled by a `message_sending` hook -> `outcome=skipped reason=cancelled_by_message_sending_hook`, then `outcome=sent` for the no-reply notice. Current main routes that notice separately; the current-head test above expects only the skipped-answer diagnostic.
- new: preview send that may have landed without an id -> `outcome=preview-retained reason=adapter_returned_no_identity`
- extended: prompt-context record fails after Telegram accepted the final -> `outcome=preview-finalized-partial`
- extended: final sent as a new message -> `outcome=sent` with its id
- extended: rejected second final -> an outcome line for the first answer only, plus `telegram final reply failed` at error level

Earlier recorded results, not current-head claims:

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 passed, Vitest shard 27.6 s locally; each new case runs in about 1 s.
- Revert control: removing the two log calls fails 6 of 14.
- 11 Telegram test files (the one above, `bot-message`, `bot`, the dispatch `delivery-transcript`, `progress-card` and `fallback-topic-media` suites, `lane-delivery`, and the four dispatch `telegram-http` suites): 190 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 84ce5954d111` with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1`: every lane passes (typecheck extensions and extension tests, lint, format, guards). Without the skip, the dead export scan fails at this base on `ui/src/**` exports this diff does not touch.

Gaps: no Telegram Test Server userbot run, and the production numbers above were taken before the fix. The early `channel_transform` skip (final payload recovery returns nothing) has no test.

## After-fix proof (production, 2026-10-13/14)

The build carrying this change: v2026.10.1 plus local patches. Its `bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts` change is line-for-line the change in this PR. It was deployed on 2026-10-13 to two gateways.

- **Gateway A:** 3 Telegram accounts, `streaming.mode: "partial"`. Its log since the restart has 33 outcome lines: 8 `preview-finalized` and 25 `sent`.
- **Gateway B:** replies through the message tool only. It has 11 outcome lines, all `sent`, as expected.

One turn from gateway A, with the chat id and bot name redacted:

```
2026-10-14T12:58:44.039-04:00 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:group:<group> -> @<bot> (group, 39 chars)
2026-10-14T12:59:03.228-04:00 [telegram] final delivery outcome=preview-finalized chat=<group> message=46883
```

- **No other send line.** Neither `outbound send ok` nor `text delivery ok` appears for this turn, because the final was edited into the preview.
- **Telegram's record.** The sent-message record for message 46883 (`plugin_state_entries`, namespace `telegram.sent-messages`) was created at 12:59:03, the same second as the outcome line.
- **Before this change,** a reply like this one left no info-level line at all.

prs.title: fix: native Muse rejects supported Meta reasoning levels
prs.body:
Related: #177531

## What Problem This Solves

Native Muse sessions reject Meta's supported `xhigh` reasoning setting while the Meta runtime plugin is inactive. This revision repairs pre-activation policy lookup when the Meta plugin is present. The standalone Muse installation remains affected, as identified in review.

## User Impact

With the Meta policy artifact available, native Muse session validation can accept the reasoning levels already supported by Meta's existing policy. This revision does not yet provide that artifact to installations containing only `@openclaw/muse`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing resolver through the lightweight provider policy artifact and reuse it after runtime registration. Native catalog capability isolation and the existing model-specific restrictions are preserved.

## Evidence

- With the artifact absent, the real native session projection rejects `xhigh` with the reported error while all four existing route controls pass. Restoring it gives 5/5 passing route tests.
- 31 public-artifact checks and 85 other affected Meta, Muse harness, thinking-default and catalog-isolation checks pass.
- Targeted extension/core-test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, the line-growth guard and `pnpm build` pass. Importing the built policy artifact retains `xhigh`.
- Pre-submission independent Sol/high review had no findings, but subsequent exact-head Codex review identified the valid standalone-install gap below.
- Exact-head CI39314854648 succeeds: 59 jobs, 29 successful and 30 conditionally skipped. CodeQL, Critical Quality and Security pass.
- Measured wall times: route suite 49.83s, artifact suite 52.23s, primarily cold transforms.

## Remaining Review Requirements

- The source-checkout tests discover Meta's directory. The published host excludes it, and standalone Muse neither installs a Meta companion nor owns a discoverable Meta policy artifact. The current tests therefore do not prove the documented Muse-only installation. See [the exact-head finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177673#discussion_r4318326020).
- A repair must preserve one policy owner and native catalog capability isolation, then cover an installed layout with Meta absent.
- ClawSweeper requires an installed Gateway selecting `xhigh` and executing a real native Muse turn. This host has no `muse` executable; no Meta authentication or live-model execution has been performed. Local harness checks and green CI do not satisfy that requirement.

The standalone repair and live proof remain open. No fresh bot review is requested while those requirements are unmet.

Full `check:changed` is not claimed green. Its base has unrelated UI suppression-inventory failures and over-budget core-test root inventories. This change adds no test root or suppression; targeted typechecks pass.

Implemented and tested with agent assistance. Live Muse/model execution was not run.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep mixed-case plugin ids enabled on reinstall when settings use the lowercase policy key
prs.body:
## Summary
Reinstalling a plugin whose manifest id is mixed case (for example `MyPlug`) ignores settings stored under the documented lowercase policy key `plugins.entries.myplug`. `openclaw plugins install` reports that the plugin "requires configuration first", writes a second `plugins.entries.MyPlug` entry with `enabled: false`, and the loader (which resolves the lowercase key) then sees the plugin as disabled. A plugin that was enabled and configured ends up disabled after a reinstall or update.

## Root cause
#164683 moved the loader, validation and enable/disable paths to the normalized (lowercase) plugin id, but install persistence still reads policy by the raw manifest id.

`src/plugins/plugin-config-enablement.ts`, before:
```ts
const entry = params.config.plugins?.entries?.[params.pluginId];
const hasConfig = isRecord(entry) && Object.hasOwn(entry, "config");
```
`src/plugins/install-persistence.ts`, before:
```ts
if (!Array.isArray(deny) || !deny.includes(pluginId)) {
...
const explicitlyDisabled = reconciledConfig.plugins?.entries?.[pluginId]?.enabled === false;
```
`src/plugins/enable.ts` `prepareConfigForDisabledInstall`, before:
```ts
const entry = config.plugins?.entries?.[pluginId];
...
[pluginId]: { ...policy, enabled: false },
```
With manifest id `MyPlug` and settings under `myplug`, the required-config check sees no config, so the install is staged disabled under a new `MyPlug` key, and the deny/explicit-disable lookups also miss the canonical entry.

## Fix
Resolve every install-persistence policy lookup through the same normalized id the loader uses.

after:
```ts
const config = normalizePluginsConfig(params.config.plugins).entries[
  normalizePluginId(params.pluginId)
]?.config;
```
```ts
const policyId = normalizePluginId(pluginId);
if (!Array.isArray(deny) || !deny.some((id) => normalizePluginId(id) === policyId)) {
```
```ts
const resolvedId = normalizePluginId(normalizeChatChannelId(pluginId) ?? pluginId);
const next = setPluginEnabledInConfig(config, resolvedId, false, { updateChannelConfig: false });
```
`prepareConfigForDisabledInstall` now goes through `setPluginEnabledInConfig`, the same helper `openclaw plugins disable` uses, so a staged disabled install lands on the canonical lowercase key and keeps its existing policy (minus `config`).

## Why this is the right boundary
Install persistence is the only remaining reader of `plugins.entries` that keys by the raw manifest id; the loader, config validation, and enable/disable already normalize. Fixing it here aligns install with the canonical identity rather than adding a second lookup. Lowercase ids are unaffected because `normalizePluginId` is the identity for them, and all existing install-persistence cases keep their behavior.

## Verification
- Added two regression cases in `src/plugins/install-persistence.test.ts`: a mixed-case id with settings under the lowercase key is enabled without a "requires configuration" warning and without a duplicate entry, and a mixed-case id with missing settings is staged disabled under the lowercase key with its deny entry cleared. Both fail on pristine main and pass with this patch.
- Local lint, format, typecheck and test gates were not run on this machine; GitHub Actions runs them on this PR.

## Upgrade and existing-data compatibility
The review asked for an upgrade from the current stable release with an existing mixed-case plugin, settings, and an explicit disabled preference. The proof below seeds state with the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` npm package only (install, `config set`, `plugins enable`, `plugins disable`), then points the built CLI from this branch at that same state directory with no edits in between.

- No config migration is introduced. The patch only changes which key install persistence reads (`normalizePluginId`, the same normalizer the loader and `plugins enable/disable` already use since #164683), so a config written by 2026.10.5 loads unchanged; `plugins list` on this branch reads it before any write.
- Lowercase-keyed settings and an explicit `enabled: false` both survive a reinstall on this branch, and no extra key is written.
- State already damaged by 2026.10.5 (a reinstall there writes a duplicate `MyPlug: {enabled:false}` next to the configured `myplug` entry) still loads on this branch with every setting intact. This branch deliberately does not auto-delete that raw-case `enabled:false` key on reinstall, because it is indistinguishable from an operator-authored disable; the existing `openclaw plugins enable MyPlug` collapses the alias and the plugin then stays enabled across reinstalls (shown below). If maintainers prefer an automatic repair, that is a policy call I would rather take as a follow-up than fold into this fix.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: Reinstalling or updating a plugin whose manifest id is mixed case (`MyPlug`) ignored its settings stored under the canonical lowercase key, staged it disabled, and wrote a duplicate raw-case `{enabled:false}` entry. The review asked specifically for an upgrade from 2026.10.5 with existing settings and an explicit disabled preference.
Real environment tested: macOS, Node 26.9.0. BEFORE: the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` npm package (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)`). AFTER: this PR head b0531dfe4e841ca7194d47007bb557a4abb14092 rebased on origin/main 34f6f1ba01c, built to dist and run through the shipped `node openclaw.mjs` entry point (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (b0531df)`). Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; two real local plugin directories with manifest ids `MyPlug` and `OtherPlug`, each with a configSchema requiring `token`. Placeholder tokens only, no credentials or endpoints.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: (1) With 2026.10.5 only: `plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/myplug`, `config set plugins.entries.myplug.config.token abc`, `plugins enable MyPlug`; same for `OtherPlug` with token `xyz`, then `plugins disable OtherPlug`. Archive that state dir. (2) BEFORE: restore it, reinstall both plugins with 2026.10.5. (3) AFTER (upgrade): restore the same archived 2026.10.5 state, run `plugins list`, reinstall both plugins with this branch, print `plugins.entries`, run `plugins list`. (4) Existing-damaged-data: restore the state left by step (2), run the same commands on this branch, then `plugins enable MyPlug` and one more reinstall.
Evidence after fix:
```
# (1) state written by openclaw 2026.10.5
{"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}}}
│ MyPlug                        │                   │ openclaw │ enabled  │ global:MyPlug/index.js         │ 1.0.0     │
│ OtherPlug                     │                   │ openclaw │ disabled │ global:OtherPlug/index.js      │ 1.0.0     │

# (2) BEFORE: reinstall on 2026.10.5
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
$ openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/myplug
Plugin manifest id "MyPlug" differs from npm package name "myplug"; using manifest id as the config key.
Installing to $TMP/stable-state/extensions/MyPlug…
Config warnings: plugins.entries.myplug: plugin disabled (disabled in config) but config is present; plugins.entries.otherplug: plugin disabled (disabled in config) but config is present
Installed plugin "MyPlug" without enabling it because it requires configuration first. Configure it, then run `openclaw plugins enable MyPlug`.
Installed plugin: MyPlug
$ openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/otherplug
Installed plugin "OtherPlug" without enabling it because it requires configuration first. Configure it, then run `openclaw plugins enable OtherPlug`.
Installed plugin: OtherPlug
# plugins.entries in $TMP/stable-state/openclaw.json
{"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"MyPlug":{"enabled":false},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false}}
$ openclaw plugins list
│ MyPlug                        │                   │ openclaw │ disabled │ global:MyPlug/index.js         │ 1.0.0     │
│ OtherPlug                     │                   │ openclaw │ disabled │ global:OtherPlug/index.js      │ 1.0.0     │

# (3) AFTER: same 2026.10.5 state, upgraded to this branch
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (b0531df)
$ openclaw plugins list
│ MyPlug                      │                        │ openclaw │ enabled  │ global:MyPlug/index.js      │ 1.0.0     │
│ OtherPlug                   │                        │ openclaw │ disabled │ global:OtherPlug/index.js   │ 1.0.0     │
$ openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/myplug
Plugin manifest id "MyPlug" differs from npm package name "myplug"; using manifest id as the config key.
Installing to $TMP/stable-state/extensions/MyPlug…
Config warnings: plugins.entries.otherplug: plugin disabled (disabled in config) but config is present
Installed plugin: MyPlug
Saved for the next Gateway start.
$ openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/otherplug
Plugin manifest id "OtherPlug" differs from npm package name "otherplug"; using manifest id as the config key.
Installing to $TMP/stable-state/extensions/OtherPlug…
Config warnings: plugins.entries.otherplug: plugin disabled (disabled in config) but config is present
Installed plugin: OtherPlug
Saved for the next Gateway start.
# plugins.entries in $TMP/stable-state/openclaw.json
{"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}}}
$ openclaw plugins list
│ MyPlug                      │                        │ openclaw │ enabled  │ global:MyPlug/index.js      │ 1.0.0     │
│ OtherPlug                   │                        │ openclaw │ disabled │ global:OtherPlug/index.js   │ 1.0.0     │

# (4) state already damaged by 2026.10.5, loaded on this branch
# plugins.entries before
{"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"MyPlug":{"enabled":false},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false}}
$ openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/myplug
Installed plugin: MyPlug
$ openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/otherplug
Installed plugin: OtherPlug
# plugins.entries after (unchanged, no further duplicates, settings intact)
{"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"MyPlug":{"enabled":false},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false}}
$ openclaw plugins enable MyPlug
Enabled plugin "MyPlug". Saved for the next Gateway start.
# plugins.entries
{"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false},"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}}}
$ openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities $TMP/src/myplug
Installed plugin: MyPlug
# plugins.entries
{"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false},"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}}}
$ openclaw plugins list
│ MyPlug                      │                        │ openclaw │ enabled  │ global:MyPlug/index.js      │ 1.0.0     │
│ OtherPlug                   │                        │ openclaw │ disabled │ global:OtherPlug/index.js   │ 1.0.0     │
```
Observed result after fix: Upgrading a 2026.10.5 state to this branch and reinstalling keeps `MyPlug` enabled with `token: abc` and keeps the operator-disabled `OtherPlug` disabled with `token: xyz`; no "requires configuration first" message and no duplicate raw-case entry is written. The same reinstall on 2026.10.5 disables both and writes `MyPlug`/`OtherPlug` `{enabled:false}` duplicates. State already damaged by 2026.10.5 loads on this branch with all settings intact, is not damaged further by reinstall, and `plugins enable MyPlug` restores it so it stays enabled across the next reinstall.
What was not tested: npm or ClawHub registry installs (same persistence path, different fetch source); a running Gateway picking up the plugins after restart.

prs.title: fix(doctor): agents lose inherited logins after doctor when the auth inheritance owner is not main
prs.body:
Related: #178421

Fixes the Doctor path, which is how the reporter's install was switched over (its ledger names main's store as the Doctor source). The fresh-install switch-over has the same mismatch and remains open under #178421; it needs a separate change because that code cannot see the config.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents lose an inherited login after `openclaw doctor --fix` when `agents.defaults.authInheritance.agentId` names an agent other than `main`. Doctor moved `main`'s login store into shared state and turned inheritance off, so the owner kept its login and every other agent had none.

## User Impact

- Doctor moves the configured owner's store when that owner holds the logins and `main` holds none. Other agents can then use the owner's logins, which is what `authInheritance` documents.
- **Behavior change to review:** agent turns before relocation never actually read the owner's store (on 2026.7.1 and 2026.10.5 peers used `main`'s store; see Details). So for these installs, other agents get the owner's logins for the first time after this Doctor run. Agents' own private logins are not copied.
- If both `main` and the owner hold logins, Doctor skips this one move with a recoverable warning naming both stores, and the install keeps its current layout and behavior.
- Unchanged: installs whose owner is `main`, `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` relocation, installs whose owner holds no logins (`main` still moves), and the existing refusal to delete the configured owner.
- Not covered: installs already switched over by an earlier Doctor keep their current state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Until the move, the configured owner is the documented inheritance source, so the move carries the owner's store. Doctor picks the source from its own selected config, refuses to choose when both stores hold logins, and re-checks the source right before copying. The copied-update planner checks the owner's store against its snapshot boundary too.

Example of the fresh-install path left open (`shared-store-bootstrap*.ts`): on 2026.10.5, `openclaw models auth paste-api-key --agent main` on such an install switches the store over and leaves the owner's logins behind.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The source comes from `sourceConfigBeforeMigrations ?? cfg` via `resolveLegacyInheritedAuthAgentId`/`resolveLegacyInheritedAuthAgentDir`; there is no process-wide config fallback.
- Same store: an owner whose `agentDir` is `main`'s directory, directly or through a symlink, is treated as `main` (`isSameOpenClawAgentDatabasePath`). This check runs only in the repair path; outside Doctor repair, detection still returns before touching any source file.
- At the point of effect, under the migration lock: a source agent deleted with its database retained after detection is skipped as held, and the source database is opened under the resolved agent id, so a database recorded for another agent is refused before any copy or cleanup.
- Both stores holding logins: on 2026.7.1, peers sent `main`'s key, while the upgraded config names the owner. Moving either store alone would change which credential peers use, so Doctor leaves it to the operator. An unreadable store payload counts as holding logins.
- Why peers never read the owner before: `run/auth-plan.ts` loads an agent's store without the inherited directory, so turns fall back to `main`'s store. That is a separate runtime issue, not changed here.
- `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` still relocates only `main`'s store, which matches how the owner's `agentDir` is resolved.

</details>

## Evidence

Isolated containers, network off, and a fake OpenAI-compatible model server that records the key it receives and returns 401 unless it gets the owner's key. Each run first checked that the built output contains this branch's code.

**Upgrade from stable 2026.10.5** (login only on `ops`, `authInheritance.agentId: "ops"`, agents `ops` and `dev`), then two `openclaw agent --agent dev` turns through a real Gateway:

| Doctor | Shared store after | `dev` turns | Key the model server received |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.10.5 | empty; ledger source `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` (does not exist); `ops` keeps `mock:ops` | 401, 401 | `auth=<none>` |
| this branch | `[mock:ops]`; owner's local copy cleaned; ledger source `agents/ops/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` | `AUTH_OK`, `AUTH_OK` | `Bearer <owner key>` |

### Real Gateway proof: direct upgrade from 2026.7.1

**Direct upgrade from 2026.7.1** (default agent `ops`; logins added with 2026.7.1's own CLI). On 2026.7.1 itself, `dev` sent no key when only `ops` had one, and sent `main`'s key when `main` also had one.

| Install | 2026.10.5 Doctor → `dev` sends | This branch's Doctor → result, `dev` sends |
|---|---|---|
| login on `ops` only | no key (401) | owner moved; `Bearer <owner key>`, `AUTH_OK` |
| logins on `ops` and `main` | `main`'s key | skipped with the warning below, nothing moved; `main`'s key (as on 2026.7.1) |

```text
- Shared auth migration skipped: agents.defaults.authInheritance names agent ops, whose credentials other agents inherit from <state>/agents/ops/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite, but <state>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite also stores credentials. Keep the credentials agents should share in one of these stores, then run openclaw doctor --fix.
ownership: <none> (legacy-main); ops local: [ 'mock:ops' ]; main local: [ 'mock:main' ]  (unchanged)
```

### Real CLI proof: authority checks (2026.10.5-built state)

```text
### peer dev has its own login (mock:dev), then this branch's doctor --fix
before: ops local [ 'mock:ops' ]   dev local [ 'mock:dev' ]   shared: none
after:  shared [ 'mock:ops' ]      ops local: null            dev local [ 'mock:dev' ]  (not copied)
### openclaw agents delete ops --force (before relocation)
"Agent "ops" owns inherited credentials through agents.defaults.authInheritance.agentId and cannot be deleted. Relocate those credentials, then re-point or remove that binding before retrying."
ops local after the attempt: [ 'mock:ops' ]
```

### Real Doctor proof: rejection after detection

Fresh install on this branch's build, login on `ops` only (old layout). Doctor's shared-auth detect and migrate functions, with the owner retired or reassigned in between:

```text
##### owner retired between detection and copy
1. detected: {"ownerId":"ops","sourcePath":"<state>/agents/ops/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite","hasLegacy":true}
   owner store: {"profiles":["mock:ops"],"agentId":"ops"} sha256: ec59c8376b0262b3 shared keys: []
2. after detection: agent ops deleted with its database retained (deletion journal completed)
3. migrate: {"changes":[],"outcome":"skipped","warnings":["Shared auth migration skipped: store held for agent ops at <state>/agents/ops/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite; run openclaw doctor --fix after restoring the agent."]}
4. owner store: {"profiles":["mock:ops"],"agentId":"ops"} sha256: ec59c8376b0262b3 (unchanged) shared keys: []
##### owner reassigned between detection and copy
1. detected: {"ownerId":"ops","sourcePath":"<state>/agents/ops/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite","hasLegacy":true}
2. after detection: the owner directory's database reassigned to agent 'other'
3. migrate: {"changes":[],"warnings":["Failed relocating the shared auth store: SharedAuthStoreSourceInspectionError: Cannot read legacy shared auth database <state>/agents/ops/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: OpenClaw agent database ... belongs to agent other ..."]}
4. owner store: {"profiles":["mock:ops"],"agentId":"other"} unchanged by the migration; shared keys: []
```

**Regression tests.** These fail on `main` (or on an earlier commit of this PR, for the review fixes) and pass here:
- the owner's logins move for its peers, with a standard and a custom `agentDir` (peer's own store stays private)
- both stores hold logins → skipped, nothing moved
- the planner refuses an owner store outside the copied snapshot
- with `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` set, the configured owner's store still moves
- an owner `agentDir` symlinked to `main`'s directory is treated as `main`
- an owner deleted after detection is never relocated or cleaned (`state-migrations.retained-deleted-agent.test.ts`)
- outside Doctor repair, detection returns before touching an unreadable owner `agentDir` (no `EACCES`)

Guards for unchanged behavior: an owner with no logins → `main` moves as before; an owner database recorded for another agent → refused, untouched.

**Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. `oxlint` on the changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. A wider run of 112 related test files fails only in suites that fail identically on unmodified `main` in the same container: terminal-UI PTY timeouts, `.clawdbot` → `.openclaw` rename tests, and a few timing-sensitive suites. `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck-all, import cycles, plugin boundaries and the database-first guard. Its remaining failures are outside this change: `max-lines` in untouched files, the existing core test-shard root budget, and two steps that need network.

prs.title: refactor(canvas): render the A2UI v0.9 catalog with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Canvas A2UI v0.9 still loads Lit to render its basic catalog even though the host uses Solid.

## User Impact

All 18 catalog components render with Solid while retaining their existing tags, classes, bindings, validation, actions, and styles. Text bodies now render sanitized basic Markdown. Native dialogs support Escape and return focus. Date/time controls retain uncommitted edits through unrelated property updates. Weighted Text layout and custom primary-color variants match the upstream catalog. Date bounds and fractional sliders now follow the v0.9 schema; the old catalog ignored bounds and rounded fractional ranges.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer consumes web_core's existing message processor, node resolver, schemas, functions, and writable bindings. It does not replace the synchronous data owner or change the v0.9 protocol. Tree shaking removes the unused universal/Lit renderer from the shipped v0.9 bundle. Transitive Lit stays in the dependency graph: there is no dependency override or package patch.

The landed v0.8 port (#178583) is integrated from main. Both dialects now use the same native dialog lifecycle and alignment helper; their binding adapters remain separate. This removes 33 lines from the v0.8 renderer. Canvas uses the DOMPurify 3.4.17 and Marked 18.1.1 versions already adopted on main; there are no dependency overrides or Solid version changes.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Built v0.9 catalog corpus | All 18 components rendered; date drafts survived unrelated property updates and newer model values still applied; edited form values arrived in action context; live server updates, template rows, validation, tabs, modal Escape/focus return, sanitized Markdown, date bounds and fractional ranges checked |
| UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed |
| Control UI build and strict performance comparison | Final base a79d49bc8bfa and head: **325,951 B gzip startup JS, 7 requests; 38,445 B gzip CSS, 1 request**; **0 B growth**. Both strict checks report the same inherited startup ceiling violation (325,951 B against 325,166 B); no budget or ignore changed |
| v0.9 bundle, same machine/toolchain | **999,579 → 1,015,334 B raw; 245,606 → 245,647 B gzip** (+41 B gzip, including safe Markdown, native draft preservation, and restored presentation); no Lit runtime in emitted bundle |
| Lint / production Knip | Targeted lint and final production Knip passed (1m 27.3s) |
| Independent review | Independent reviews of the port, date draft fix, presentation repair, and final shared adapter found no actionable P0–P2 findings; reported findings addressed |
| PR CI | **Passed**: [run 39504273685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39504273685), exact head `5eabbdf32559c`, with `ci:full`; 50 successful checks and no failures. UI unit, UI E2E and real-Gateway shards passed. |

The presentation regression was reproduced through production bundles: weights 1:2 gave 248/496 px in Lit, 28.19/37.83 px in the initial port, and 248/496 px after repair. A custom green primary button likewise retains the exact upstream green hover color after repair. Both behaviors are asserted in the existing catalog test.

The final combined production bundles passed dialog open, Escape, focus return, explicit close, and reset while open in both dialects; v0.8 alignment mapping also passed. The v0.9 corpus and edited-action/sanitization interactions passed again after aligning the dependencies with main. Sharing adds 157 B gzip to the independent v0.8 bundle (147,667 → 147,824 B).

prs.title: fix(telegram): steered answers quote the wrong input
prs.body:
Closes #178120.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can quote the wrong input when an embedded run consumes another message while an earlier answer is buffered. Capture each assistant message’s consumed input synchronously, retain it through buffered delivery and native transcript persistence, and preserve its implicit reply classification through final threading and pending-final recovery.

## User Impact

Answers retain the input they consumed. Implicit targets respect `off` / `first` / `all`; explicit quotes and quote suppression retain precedence. Legacy transcript JSON remains readable. The optional source fact needs no configuration or database migration.

## Evidence

Current head: `09517e7ab48747e2935ffbab41d3c90d2bde4202`. Its actual conflict with main `94dacc48dfb325197481e95cc0fe3fd863eec645` is resolved. The pending-final test retains the entire upstream consolidation plus this contribution’s six regressions. The native database-worker inventory retains both the reply-source case and upstream update-repair cancellation case, once each. Independent review found no actionable resolution defect.

On this exact resulting tree, secretless Linux containers with Node 24.22.0 and dependencies installed from the new frozen lockfile pass:

- **32 focused native cases:** all three subscriber source cases, all 28 pending-final owning-file cases, and the real persisted implicit-source retry case. The other 194 restart-recovery cases are excluded by an explicit name filter, not claimed as executed.
- Production core types and all three affected native test-type graphs: `core-test-agents-root`, `core-test-agents-sessions`, `core-test-messaging`.
- Native type-aware core and test-inventory lint, formatting on all 17 contribution paths, and contribution whitespace checks.

prs.title: fix: canceled child wakes can strand session replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Canceled or suppressed subagents can retain a requester-settle wake after their completion obligation is retired. Treating that wake as recovery custody can leave a delivery claim blocking later messages; restoring it as an unbound FIFO reservation can also block new human input.

## User Impact

Retired child wakes stop occupying recovery or mailbox admission. Live pending and dispatching completions retain custody, and Stop can still retire an already pending wake. Direct admission failures retain their actual error through finalization and identical-key replay. No configuration, schema, or operator retirement API is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `owesRequesterCompletion` predicate for yielded recovery selection and commit revalidation. Stop has an explicit separate purpose: canceling a pending wake must remain possible even after its child is already canceled.

The restored-completion owner checks whether the obligation is still owed before reserving an unbound FIFO slot. After requester lookup, it rechecks current ownership and completion status while preserving captured batch identity. Valid work keeps its ordering.

Gateway finalization publishes abandonment terminals only for queued inputs. Direct pre-adoption rejection stays with its dispatch owner; admission guidance is an error, rather than a successful no-op.

Related: #167007, #176913, #170562, #118839. This focused repair is included in consolidation #177698; both remain available for maintainer choice.

## Evidence

Current source: `9ff52d486edc91aecbdb66e81491a5a88c0b61d5`, incorporating the same named upstream `4763b77ba572eefaef3bed12c0c17c305cd12738`, adds the mixed-batch repair below. The earlier seven-file byte-identity map is against `384256c3795e241c3f9c8de0de172ded947cccb5`; it is not a whole-file equivalence claim for the changed restored-batch owner.

### Mixed frozen-batch FIFO repair

The latest review found that a retired first member could prevent a still-owed sibling from reserving its batch. The repair selects a surviving representative while retaining the complete frozen batch identity and owed timestamp. It rechecks every exact member after requester lookup and selects a current survivor there too. Entirely retired or replaced cohorts still cannot reserve; no authority or Stop guard changes.

The final regression bytes on the preceding standalone `384256c3795e241c3f9c8de0de172ded947cccb5` reproduce both reported cases: **2 failed, 11 passed**, with both failures at the missing reservation. After repair, **52 tests across all four requested owner files pass**, including Stop, recovery, dispatch and the actual mailbox selector. Production and owning test types, scoped lint, formatting and whitespace pass. The two-file before/after source is byte-identical to the independently reviewed consolidated repair; that P0–P2 review found no actionable defect.

The matrix covers a leader retired before startup, leader retirement during requester lookup, whole-cohort retirement, and sibling generation replacement. Positive cases retain the full source identity, block a later human until the owed input settles, then admit that human; negatives reserve nothing. An earlier dependency/setup failure ran no tests and is not a product RED. The canonical root-only dependency repair reused cached packages and left the lockfile, local native dependency and runtime artifacts unchanged.

No new native runtime capture is claimed for this patch. Earlier native/upgrade captures remain evidence of their recorded revisions. In particular, the old full-file comparison is against `384256c`; the current restored-batch owner now differs by this mixed-cohort repair. Its determining single-retired guard remains intact and the updated four-file regressions cover both retirement and still-owed FIFO.

[Inspectable synthetic Gateway traces, stable-upgrade receipts, and qualifications](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177661#issuecomment-6284522805):

- The actual restored-wake owner→real mailbox selector regression is RED before the repair: killed, suppressed, and lookup-retired cases block human admission (3 failed, 6 passed). With the fix, the two affected suites pass all 27 tests, including the still-owed FIFO control.
- Stop regression attribution is now explicit: exact upstream `4763b77` passes all 8 tests; the PR's pre-repair predicate fails the pending-wake case; the repaired current branch passes all 8. Recovery's owed-completion filter caused the regression by being reused for Stop. The purpose split repairs that cause.
- The real Gateway role-policy rejection preserves its specific error on identical-key replay and leaves canonical messages unchanged. This is an independently audited partial trace from a failed collector, not a full collector pass. Two automatic naming calls occurred; zero total provider I/O is not claimed.
- A genuine native managed-child interruption/restart case passed on the combined revision `5c831c77681`: external authenticated cancellation created a real `killIntent` plus pending wake, which survived an intentional isolated Gateway SIGKILL and all old native process joins. The replacement restore owner skipped it, and fresh human input completed once. All four native processes exited zero. Against the pre-mixed-repair `384256c` source, six of this PR’s seven production owners were byte-identical and the seventh differed only in types. The current mixed-batch owner change is qualified above. Native neighboring steering/admission code differs, so this is scoped shared-owner evidence, not execution of the standalone binary. The interrupted kill HTTP request ended with 502; no final kill ACK is claimed.
- A current-version managed-child Stop/restart control preserves child identity/history and completes a fresh human turn. This is also a qualified partial trace: an extra marker-routed utility assertion failed after the main control passed.
- A **complete passing official packaged 2026.10.5→candidate upgrade** uses the same synthetic state and canonical Doctor. Kept child identity/provenance/history survive. Read-only inspection verifies all original stored column values across nine nonempty tables, including 15 transcript events, 15 identities, 13 active events, and 21 trajectory events. A fresh human turn has a correlated saved final. Both Gateways exit zero; owned state/provider are removed. No native Codex binding continuity is claimed.

The earlier `384256c` conflict repair resolved the xAI OAuth and UI reconnect fixtures without changing production guards. **26 xAI, 15 browser, and 8 Stop tests pass**; core types, xAI production-package types, scoped lint/format, diff check, and fresh P0–P2 conflict review pass. The UI e2e type graph reports `TS2367` in unchanged upstream `session-scoped-delivery.e2e.test.ts:103` (exact base/candidate blob equality verified). Broad extension-test types remain for hosted CI; production-package types are not presented as test-type coverage.

## Remaining Scope and Limits

The new native case supplies a canonical producer for a genuine kill-intent plus pending wake at startup. It does not reproduce the historical suppressed terminal/dispatching shape, execute this standalone binary, or demonstrate a baseline runtime hang. The source-equivalent determining restore guard is exercised directly; earlier actual-owner/mailbox regressions supply the before-fix failure and still-owed FIFO control. The separate stable-upgrade case preserves stored data, rather than claiming native binding continuity. No records were manually inserted or edited.

Earlier deployment-health statements remain operational observations, not end-user delivery proof. Captures use scripted loopback inference and synthetic state; no real conversations, credentials, private endpoints, or production database writes are published. No live deployment of this refreshed revision is claimed. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

Plugins cannot judge image evidence through native TypeSafe Jev even though the Decision runtime already has a tagged V2 image contract.

This replaces the earlier referenced-assets proposal with the existing V2 image representation. The TypeSafe adapter translates the image into the vendor wire format and owns the experimental header. A small prepared-runtime compatibility repair lets the registered catalog owner declare an already-selected custom decision ID before the usual routing, capability, and auth checks; it does not fabricate chat capabilities or require users to register previously working text routes manually.

Red/green proof at the real prepared-runtime boundary reproduced and repaired the custom-route regression: all 16 prepared-host scenarios pass, including undeclared/mismatched route refusal and existing auth, routing, cancellation, and deadline cases. prs.title: perf(agents): coalesce unchanged workspace attestations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Populated workspaces still refresh their attestation on every unchanged warm turn, costing seven SQL statements and one worker request. Reuse the workspace owner's receipt-published attestation to skip that write until its timestamp is older than one hour. First attestations and changed generated-file hashes still write immediately; future-dated timestamps still reach the existing clock-repair path.

## User Impact

Unchanged populated-workspace turns avoid a redundant durable refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows #178711 without adding a read, freshness probe, cache, schema change, or transaction path. The existing filesystem and final authority checks remain. Accepted edge: persisted disappearance/reseed protection after the last unchanged preparation is at least **23 hours**, instead of exactly 24, including across a restart. SQL shapes and PostgreSQL execution are unchanged; only the owner's decision to issue the existing writer changes.

## Evidence

The unchanged-warm request-count regression and coalesced timestamp assertion both fail on base `9f3ff0d52ff789ad81d97d00efad2f59bb1cd845` for the intended reasons. On head `21798295712a08bb3f3b46ff697ac27b6526ac1a`, six focused suites pass 101 tests with one existing platform skip. These cover hourly refresh, changed hashes, restart survival, disappearance/reseed, alias changes, and write authority.

Production types, all 29 test-type groups through the repository tsrs lane, changed-file type-aware lint, Madge (zero cycles), export collisions, and T1/dialect ratchets pass. `check:changed` reports only independently reproduced baseline findings: three UI max-lines suppressions, four test-root budget findings (721/724/726/727), and Knip exports (16 production, one full-tree, zero scripts). Exact-baseline replay matches every finding; zero new findings.

Two Codex P0–P2 review rounds are complete with no accepted/actionable findings. PostgreSQL owner review approved this exact head: SQL and PG execution are unchanged. CI lint, production/test types, source contracts, architecture guards, and security checks pass. The initial PR-context formatting failure was corrected in the body; [replacement run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39504907540) passed.

Three alternating pairs (M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3) passed the complete live workload, restart, shutdown, and child cleanup, with no retries. Base was `9f3ff0d52ff789ad81d97d00efad2f59bb1cd845`; candidate was `21798295712a08bb3f3b46ff697ac27b6526ac1a`. The v3.1 populated-fixture variant adds one synthetic workspace seed and an isolated internal temporary directory; frozen instrumentation is unchanged. Each arm used Node 24.22.0, a 5-second settle and 300-second connected idle, under one ordinary proof slot.

Counts below are **SQL / requests / MAIN**, each as median [min–max]. Warm run medians use ten causal turns per run; pooled ranges retain all 30 individual turns.

All shared warm read-family counts and all non-workspace warm operation medians are unchanged. The full screen retains occasional background-window increases in entry-cache snapshots and row facts. Total-workload differences also include unrelated operation variation, including a 30-statement install-status occurrence in one baseline. Restart-first-turn window totals rise slightly despite removing seven attestation statements; that window includes unrelated work. The exact claimed owner saving is 105 SQL / 15 requests per workload and 7 SQL / 1 request per unchanged warm turn. No latency claim is made on the shared host.

Production +62/-35 (net +27); tests +36/-5 (net +31); documentation +4/-2. The production increase replaces unconditional refresh work with one owner-held decision. The existing helper moves into the sibling workspace-preparation module to respect the line-growth ratchet on workspace.ts; its superseded definition is removed. No SDK or update/Doctor/migration/plugin/service-lifecycle surface changes.

Landing used the explicitly approved runner-backlog exception for [CI job `checks-node-changed-compact-large-1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39504391733/job/118910197500): queued since 21:58:21 UTC, over 45 minutes with runner ID 0 and no assigned runner. At landing it had not run or failed. All other CI jobs were successful or skipped, and required security checks passed. The local exact-head equivalent is the six affected workspace suites (101 passed, one existing skip), plus the completed production/test types, type-aware lint, Madge, export collisions, Knip inheritance check, and worker/dialect ratchets. All three live workload/restart pairs are now complete and passed. prs.title: fix: keep sidebar groups and icons across isolated heartbeat runs
prs.body:
Closes #166216

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an isolated heartbeat loses its saved sidebar group and icon when the next scheduled run starts.

## User Impact

The heartbeat keeps its label, group, and icon across runs. Each run still gets a fresh session ID under the same logical session key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry `category` and `icon` through the existing fresh-session preference list. The current SQLite entry writer already persists both fields on the logical session node, so this needs no storage or schema change.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the regression through `runHeartbeatOnce` failed after the first scheduled run: the saved label remained, but `category` and `icon` were absent. The other four heartbeat tests passed.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.isolated-key-stability.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 24 tests. The new regression runs two scheduled heartbeats and reads the saved entries after each run. It checks the stable key, changed session IDs, and retained preferences.
- Measured locally on Node 26.7.0 with pinned pnpm 12.5.1: heartbeat file 158.09 s, including an 83.873 s cold worker rebuild; the new two-run test took 6.666 s. The cron file took 35.66 s, with the updated preference test taking 10 ms. The combined command took 202.58 s. The integration test uses the existing heartbeat fixture to check the real rollover and persistence path; a builder-only test cannot prove that contract. CI timing is not yet available.
- Repository Auto Review completed `scoped-clean` at P2. It found no actionable defects in the selected diff and supplied context.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed, including the core typecheck, all 27 core-test type graphs, formatting, changed-file lint, and the repository guards. `git diff --check` passed.

AI-assisted change. No browser smoke test or full repository build/test suite was run.

prs.title: fix(retry): honor nested channel hints behind invalid metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: empty or invalid `parameters.retry_after` metadata on an outer error prevents the shared channel retry runner from honoring a valid hint in its response or nested error. For example, it can retry after the 400 ms backoff despite a nested response requesting one second.

## User Impact

Channel requests using the default hint reader wait for the available provider-requested delay even when an earlier wrapper contains incomplete metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the first finite hint in the existing root, response, nested-error order. Missing or invalid hints fall through; finite hints, including zero, retain their precedence. The existing runner continues to own retry admission, injected readers, backoff, jitter, and delay caps. No public signatures, configuration, or exports change.

## Evidence

- On the original production code, six new fake-clock timing cases failed and 28 cases passed. Those failures observe premature retries through `createChannelApiRetryRunner`, rather than testing a private reader in isolation.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/infra/retry-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 34 passed; 3.50 seconds wall time and approximately 0.34 seconds of tests. CI seconds are pending publication. The new cases reuse the existing fake-clock helper and add no real sleeps or process startup.
- Ten new cases cover empty/nonnumeric/nonfinite outer metadata, nested-error fallback, first-finite and zero precedence, and default backoff. Existing tests cover injected readers, caps, and strict retry admission.
- Independent autoreview at P0–P2: scoped-clean. A separate fresh review of the owner and retry scheduler found no actionable findings. `git diff --check` passed.
- Production types (`pnpm tsgo:core`), the owning test type graph (`pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-infra"]'`), changed-file type-aware lint, and formatting passed.
- Validation gaps for this draft: full `check:changed`, full build/test, broader test type graphs, live channel/API execution, and CI are unrun. This changes the default error-envelope reader; the fake-clock proof does not claim a live provider result.

prs.title: fix(doctor): post-session plugin repair fails when a historical transcript is deferred
prs.body:
Closes #153502

Original contribution: @jayzhou2309.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e73ea8c2-4672-4a46-a44c-b48bce38ec86)
- [Initial main reproduction](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/db9540d3-cfef-4bd8-923a-2271f8df30e1)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/5ed8746c-939d-4a3c-888d-b68a19828261)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: post-session plugin repair fails and leaves verified retained session sources unsettled when a session store also has a deferred historical transcript (`historical_transcript_deferred`, including unrecognized historical records).

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw doctor --fix` and `openclaw update repair` finish the deferred plugin repair (such as Codex) for these stores instead of reporting `retained_plugin_source_settlement_failed`. The deferred historical original is still kept in a protected archive with its bytes unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`historical_transcript_deferred` is a warning (`src/infra/session-sqlite-migration-issues.ts`), and the Doctor guide says retained historical conflicts do not block post-session plugin repair. But `settleRetainedDoctorSessionSources` gated on `isRetainedSourceIssue`, which does not list that code, so settlement threw on the first deferred historical transcript.

The fix treats `historical_transcript_deferred` as settleable inside `settleRetainedDoctorSessionSources` only. The shared `isRetainedSourceIssue` predicate is unchanged, because it also gates import-time source capture and receipt recording, and widening it there would change what goes into a receipt. Store archiving during settlement uses the same local predicate, matching the normal import path, which already archives a store that carries only warnings.

## Evidence

### Exact-head CI follow-through (October 20, 09:57 UTC)

[CI run 39402331678](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39402331678) completed on `94fc59b0172bd1f2aae373c7715fe0d07c19af5b` with a failed production-typecheck job ([check-prod-types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39402331678/job/118561302286)). All **809 ordered compiler diagnostics** match the previously independently executed clean-main baseline `37e60afc6d2ffb3dab5dee16a52f2aae2554d4ab`; no additional compiler diagnostic differs. Main's `src/gateway/chat-display-replay.test-support.ts` imports UI replay consumers into the Node-only core compiler graph, producing the same DOM/JSX diagnostics. No compiler-policy broadening, suppression, workflow rerun, or main-branch repair was used. This is **attributed failed CI, not a green CI gate**.

The earlier `checks-node-changed-6` historical-fixture failure is absent from this completed run: that shard passed after the fixture repair.

The original contributor runs below are historical, at their stated heads; filename/header mismatches alone are now accepted by main #178146. Current integration and CI attribution are recorded in the CI follow-up below.

- New test `settles verified retained sources when a historical transcript stays deferred` in `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retained-source-verification.test.ts`. It records a verified `codex` receipt, adds a transcript whose header does not match its filename, and runs settlement. On `main` (test-only commit) it fails, 1 failed and 14 passed, with the `Primary transcript header does not match its original filename` error thrown from settlement. With the fix, 15/15 pass. It asserts the retained sources are archived as protected with original bytes, the historical original sits in one protected `unreferenced-history` archive with original bytes, and a rerun reports only the boot transcript's `historical_transcript_deferred` warning. Before #162771 the rerun reported 0 issues. Since #162771, Doctor re-discovers archived historical transcripts after a retained source index rebuild, so the mismatched header stays a warning, and the test now expects exactly that one warning.
- Rebased onto `06d2de9d9e8` (main CI green). The test file passes 15/15 on the branch. With only the test commits on that main, the new case fails (1 failed, 14 passed): settlement rejects with the header-mismatch error.
- All 34 `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite*.test.ts` files: 392 tests pass (rerun after rebasing onto `0783e3f28d4`). The helper now lives in `doctor-session-sqlite-types.ts` beside `isRetainedSourceIssue`, so `doctor-session-sqlite.ts` does not grow past the line-cap ratchet.
- Test cost. `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retained-source-verification.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on an Apple Silicon Mac: 24.7s Vitest duration warm (26.2s wall), 42.9s cold, 15 tests; the new case takes 989ms of that. CI for head 7d835e5df93 (run 36484133455, job `checks-node-changed-compact-large-8`, shard `agentic-commands-doctor-sessions-cron`): the file's 15 tests sum to 53.6s, and the new case to 2.3s. The new case adds no timers, sleeps, polling, Gateway or process boot, serial config, or worker pin. It reuses the file's existing fixtures.
- `oxlint --deny-warnings` and `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview` (codex engine, branch mode against `main`): no actionable findings.
- Real CLI run, `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` from source on macOS, main 5c3d2ee8972 against this branch at 7d835e5df93. The state was built on disk by the published `openclaw@2026.9.6` CLI (`doctor --session-sqlite import`, which records a verified codex `plugin_migration_source_retained` receipt). It has two codex transcripts with app-server sidecars, a `boot-2026-06-12_...jsonl` whose header id does not match its filename, a pending `deferred-plugin-migration:codex` row (inserted with `sqlite3`, the one non-CLI step), and `sessions.json` moved aside as in the unit test. Identical twins were seeded in place, since receipts bind to path and inode. `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointed at a scratch dir.
  - main, exit 1: `Plugin session repair did not settle: ... boot-2026-06-12_01-38-43-539-a2a5aeed.jsonl: Error: Primary transcript header does not match its original filename.` then `Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue.` The settlement manifest records `retained_plugin_source_settlement_failed` and codex stays `pending`.
  - branch, exit 0: `Deferred state migration completed for plugin "codex".` then `Doctor complete.` Codex ends `completed`, and the manifest has no `failedAt`. A second `doctor --fix` exits 0 with no session SQLite issues.
  - The two legacy transcripts are archived as `protected/indexed-historical-primary` and the boot file as `protected/unreferenced-history` (disposal `retained`). sha256 of each archive file matches the pre-repair original on both builds.
- On main a second `doctor --fix` then exits 0 and settles, because the first run moved the sources before it threw. So the user-visible failure is that first run: exit 1, `retained_plugin_source_settlement_failed`, and every later Doctor repair skipped. The branch completes in one run.
- Existing-state upgrade. Published 2026.9.6 `doctor --fix` on this state exits 0 but does not reach settlement ("installed plugin has not confirmed"). This branch's `doctor --fix` run after it then upgrades the state DB from schema 18 to 19 and completes codex with matching hashes. main run in the same order fails with the header-mismatch error.
- `openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart` (local fixture plugin via `plugins.load.paths`) exits 0 on both builds and holds the plugin back ("Package convergence must wait until the updating parent releases its install records"). The follow-up `doctor --fix` it asks for reproduces the split: main exit 1 with the header error, branch exit 0 with the plugin `completed`.
- Published updater (ClawSweeper revision 7). The candidate tarball was built from b5d32c8927c with `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog`, which passed its tarball integrity check (`dist/build-info.json` commit b5d32c8927c). Two twins were installed from npm `openclaw@2026.9.7` (c074824), each with its own npm prefix and scratch state, and both were seeded with the fixture above by the published CLI. On one twin, published 2026.9.7 ran `openclaw update --tag <candidate .tgz> --yes --no-restart`, which exited 0 and printed `OpenClaw updated to 2026.9.7 (from 2026.9.7)` and `Admission: candidate (2026.9.7)`. After that, `--version` reports `(b5d32c8)`, and `grep -rl isSettleableIssue` in the installed `dist` finds 4 files where it found 0 before. The other twin stayed on 2026.9.7 as the control.
  - The npm package does not bundle `codex`, so on both twins the update's own Doctor pass left codex `pending`. `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/codex` (2026.9.7 from ClawHub) was run on both twins before Doctor.
  - Control, published 2026.9.7: `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exits 1 with `Plugin session repair did not settle: ... Primary transcript header does not match its original filename.` The manifest records `retained_plugin_source_settlement_failed`, and codex stays `pending`.
  - Updated by the published updater: the same command exits 0 with `Deferred state migration completed for plugin "codex".` and `Doctor complete.`. Codex is `completed`, and the three originals are archived (`protected/indexed-historical-primary` x2, `protected/unreferenced-history`, disposal `retained`), each with a sha256 that matches its pre-repair original. A rerun exits 0 and reports only the deferred boot warning.
- Not verified: settlement inside the update run itself (codex was not installed yet at that point, and installing it before the update was not tried), a candidate with a distinct version string (the tarball reports the same 2026.9.7 as the release), gateway restart and service management (`--no-restart` was used, and service management was skipped for the non-default state paths), `update repair` itself reaching settlement, the reporter's own operator state, and Linux or Windows.

### Additional missing-original coverage (#167385)

Related: #167385. Native deletion followed by removing its generated `.jsonl.deleted.*.zst` already settles on main; that canonical archive-copy case is distinct from a missing retained `session-sqlite-import-archive/*.imported-*` original. The canonical fix is #165854.

The added storage-boundary regression creates historical duplicate claims through the real manifest producer, removes an import original, and invokes real Doctor import/settlement under its maintenance lock. It requires an actual retained plan and verifies the legacy index is archived, so a successful no-op cannot satisfy it. The missing original remains absent, its manifest claim stays retained, and the surviving copy keeps its bytes. Receipt capture and recovery/retention policy are unchanged.

- Preserved main reproduction at `692a4d02d3ce528cf460c744baf19899c17e7534`: canonical deleted-copy case passes; missing import-original case fails at settlement with `artifact is unexpectedly missing; original retained`. The five relevant storage/settlement owner files are unchanged at the current task pin `ce3f47b60a55d9302c70936c680319a039a68eed`.
- Exact existing contributor head `025b16d167be42b3e6a2595558e08500ae73de5b` plus the initial regression: 13/13 pass in secretless AWS, covering the new two-case file, retained-source verification, and both exact-content missing-source recovery cases. Cold three-file wrapper wall: 125.50s (126.35s outer); added cases: 3.879s and 1.136s.
- Fresh independent review found one no-op coverage gap; it was repaired as described above. Final P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. The revised two-case file passes 2/2 on the original contributor head in secretless AWS: 4.562s and 1.080s native test time; 79.11s cold wrapper wall (79.93s outer, dominated by worker compilation). Narrow oxlint and oxfmt pass; the commands-doctor typecheck passes (73.81s), and the staged-content guard passes. These exact bytes are committed in `efce8fd766013610fb87db94bc89c5f96b965d29`, directly on contributor head `025b16d167be42b3e6a2595558e08500ae73de5b`, with no production changes or rebase. prs.title: fix(status): strip terminal control sequences from status --all tables
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw status --all` renders untrusted text — channel plugin labels, remote channel error messages, agent names, admission-refusal reasons, and the Diagnosis channel issues — without stripping C0/C1 control characters. A compromised channel server or malicious plugin can embed ESC/BEL/OSC in `plugin.meta.label`, `statusIssues[].message/channel/accountId/fix`, or `account.lastError`, so `status --all` echoes those controls into the operator's terminal (title rewrite, screen clear, fake content).

- Fix: sanitize each external field with `sanitizeTerminalText` at the row-builder layer (before theme wrapping) and in the Diagnosis `emitLimited` renderer. Legit themed ANSI, the Store `\n` layout, and `--json` raw values are preserved. `issue.kind` is a trusted `stringLiteralUnion` and is not sanitized; `--json` is a separate path that never renders Diagnosis `channelIssues`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sanitization sits at the rendering boundary (row builders + Diagnosis renderer), not the data source, to preserve the `--json` raw-value contract and keep the fix in one owner. A whole-table swap to `renderTerminalSafeTable` was rejected — it would `stripAnsi` the themed state colors and collapse the Store column's multi-line layout. Per-field sanitization before theme wrapping matches the existing `message-format.ts` pattern.

## User Impact

Operators run `openclaw status --all` safely even when a channel error, plugin label, or Gateway `statusIssues` payload contains ESC/BEL/OSC. Injected controls are stripped; legitimate table colors, the multi-line Store layout, and `--json` raw values are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real `openclaw status --all` (shipped CLI) with an injected hostile channel plugin

Ran the worktree-built CLI with an ESM loader injecting a hostile channel plugin whose `meta.label` is `ESC ]0;hostile-status BEL ESC [2J QQ Bot\r\nAdmin` (OSC title + BEL + clear-screen + CRLF row forgery) and whose `collectStatusIssues` / Gateway `statusIssues` return `Account is blocked: …restart me\r\nnow`. The same hostile input runs on **main (unfixed)** and on this HEAD.

### Before / after byte matrix (real CLI, same hostile input)

| byte | before (main) | after (HEAD `42d0fb8a`) |
|---|---|---|
| `0x1b` ESC | 10 | 0 |
| `0x07` BEL | 5 | 0 |
| `0x9d` C1 OSC | 0 | 0 |
| `0x0d` real CR | 2 | 0 |
| real CRLF row break | 2 | 0 |

**Before (main)** — hostile `meta.label` splits the cell across a real CRLF, forging an empty `Admin` row; Diagnosis leaks the raw controls:

```console
│ ]0;hostile-status[2JQQ Bot │ ON │ WARN │ Account is blocked: ]0;status-issue[2Jrestart me │
│ Admin    │    │    │ now · gateway: ]0;status-issue[2Jrestart me │
! Channel issues (1)
  - hostile[default] runtime: ]0;status-issue[2Jrestart me
```

**After (HEAD)** — every external field is sanitized; `\r\n` is a visible two-character literal (no real CR/LF), so no row forgery and no executed controls:

```console
│ QQ Bot\r\nAdmin │ ON │ WARN │ Account is blocked: restart me\r\nnow · gateway: restart me\r\nnow │
! Channel issues (1)
  - hostile[default] runtime: restart me\r\nnow · fix: resolve the reported channel error, then restart the channel
```

**`--json` contract unchanged** — `status --all --json` is a separate path and never renders these fields; its output key set is identical (21 keys) on main and this HEAD, with 0 ESC/BEL/CR bytes and no hostile label, so the fix does not touch raw JSON values. Byte-level check of the captured text stdout (`proof-cli-status-all-head.txt`) confirms the `0x1b`/`0x07`/`0x0d` counts above.

### Regression tests (pre-fix fail / post-fix pass)

| probe | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| channel label / issue / agent / detail / Diagnosis fields with ESC·BEL·OSC | control bytes reach cells | stripped |
| Diagnosis issue.channel/accountId/message/fix with BEL (`\x07`) | BEL reaches Diagnosis line | stripped (false pass impossible: harness `stripAnsi` keeps BEL) |
| themed `warn("WARN")` | `\x1b[33mWARN\x1b[0m` | preserved |
| Store `\n` multi-line | path\nreason\nrepairHint | preserved |
| `--json` raw values | raw (separate path) | raw |

Pre-fix (source reverted, regression tests kept): 3 failed. Post-fix: all 30 pass; the Diagnosis suite (23-failing on main due to a missing `sessionsPath` in the `status.test-support.ts` fixture) now passes 24/24.

<details>
<summary>Scope and validation cost</summary>

Covered: `channels-table.ts` (`row.label`, `issue.message`, `row.detail`); `report-tables.ts` (`agent.id/name/sessionsPath`, `admissionRefusal.reason/repairHint`, `detail.title` + every cell); `status-all.ts` Diagnosis `issue.channel/accountId/message/fix`. Overview rows are locally computed — out of scope. CI: `check-lint-core-2`, `check-test-types-core-4`, `checks-node-changed-1` addressed.

A hostile plugin proof harness (ESM loader `proof-loader.mjs` + `injected-read-only.mjs`; main-side `proof-loader-main.mjs`) and both captured run outputs live in the evidence dir (`proof-cli-status-all-head.txt` = after, `proof-cli-status-all-prefix-main.txt` = before). The row builders and `emitLimited` are the single rendering seams for the four status tables and the Diagnosis line; the real CLI runs above (before on main, after on this HEAD) are the end-to-end confirmation.

Open PR collision check: searched `sanitizeTerminalText`/`renderTerminalSafeTable`/terminal-injection PRs. Related wangmiao-series PRs cover other render paths (#172873/#175600 plugins-list, #175181 plugins-search, #176266 message-format, #175978 hooks-cli, #175601 skills-cli, #150599 pairing-render). None touch `src/commands/status-all/*`.
</details>
