prs.title: feat(gateway): add deployment-scoped tool and action policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deployment owners need to limit which Gateway tools and actions model-directed work can use, including administrator-started conversations and plugin-provided tools. `tools.gatewayPolicy` applies a tool allowlist and explicit action lists after ordinary grants, then authorizes final arguments after preparation and hooks.

Tools capture the deployment policy when assembled. Adding, changing or removing it requires Gateway restart or replacement after affected old work ends. Ordinary tool-policy reloads, direct human administration, native Codex tools and deployments without this setting keep their existing behavior.

Tool Search, Code Mode, HTTP/MCP invocation and dedicated workers share the policy rules. Both turn and stable session catalogs are filtered. Children retain their parent's applicable whole-tool restrictions and apply the deployment's action policy themselves. Workspace-dependent delegation uses the shared publisher schema and existing policy evaluator without inserting a callable publisher into the parent's catalog.

This provides [RFC-0021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/2367) items **1/2**, caller-independent propagation for **3**, and native execution coverage for **8**. Automation restrictions, Codex adapter integration, OCE policy delivery and Harness-local protection remain separate work.

## Evidence

- Merged main at `92477a723819` in `8c9d271c2cc`. Fresh correctness and maintainability review confirms the publication merge preserves sandbox-specific actions and fields, operator permissions, explicit publishing and omitted-action compatibility.
- Scoped lint, formatting, generated-config and whitespace checks pass. The canonical generator exactly reproduced main's tracked baseline before adding the six policy entries; the PR still changes the same 52 paths.
- [CI for `8c9d271c2cc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39493877248) passed, including the final CI, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review gates. Local focused suites could not execute because the installed TypeScript package lacks the required `typescript/ast` export.
- Native Auto Review was unavailable at helper startup (read-only filesystem; no report). The resolved publication changes received a fresh independent source review.

Real-Gateway runtime qualification remains pending. An isolated driver with fake credentials and a scripted local provider is prepared for allowed/denied tool effects, hook rewrites, human administration and activation after joined replacement. No current-head runtime qualification is claimed.

Closes #154636

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` awaits checks and repairs without identifying the pending work. Expensive database and configuration preparation also occurs before the contribution loop.

Doctor identifies preparation stages, contributions, and structured checks before awaiting them, then prints elapsed milliseconds. Void contributions report `finished` or `failed` as lifecycle facts; their existing health notes describe unresolved issues. Structured checks retain finding- and validation-based outcomes. JSON omits human progress, and other repair callers retain their silent default.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause:** reporting belongs at the existing Doctor execution owners. The bounded updater digest, or a counter populated by only some legacy warning writers, cannot supply an authoritative health verdict for a void contribution.

**Changes:** report at those owners, cover pre-contribution preparation, remove the partial warning counter, and preserve ordered awaits, cancellation, cleanup, post-commit failures, and repair results. Migration and installation preparation stay in the existing startup sibling so the coordinator respects its unchanged line cap.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` can spend minutes checking or repairing state without showing which section is running.

Fixes #154636.

## User Impact

Doctor prints each section as it starts and repeats its name with elapsed time every 10 seconds while work remains pending. Progress goes to stderr; JSON remains free of human progress output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Doctor heading owner now owns the phase timer. The contribution and repair runners report their existing boundaries, including check, repair, and validation. Startup, backup, migration, config, and final cleanup sections use the same output. The delayed config-preflight spinner and its obsolete prompt-cleanup callback are removed. Existing preparation stays in the startup owner, preserving operation order and keeping the flow within its line budget.

prs.body:
Related: #158143

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot configure cron and hook concurrency through a supported setting.

## User Impact

`cron.maxConcurrentRuns` accepts a positive integer and defaults to **8**. It controls the cron-service execution cap and shared cron-agent/hook lane budget. Command/script jobs use the service cap without consuming the agent/hook budget. Existing scheduling boundaries remain intact; capacity one retains forward progress.

This restores a deliberately retired control: retained config values become effective and Doctor preserves them. Higher limits increase resource and provider demand. The bounded-stop setting has moved to #165180; this draft now contains only concurrency behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing resolver supplies the configured value to service admission, Gateway lane budgets, and slot acquisition. The existing hook reservation remains bounded by available capacity. There is no new shared scheduler, environment variable, database format, or lease policy.

## Evidence

Standalone head: `2e17633288ee324f944a8322e4b57f54958f6c36`.

Standalone split validation: **250 tests passed across four shards in 66.90 s**, covering config validation, Doctor migration, shared lanes, and cron admission. A byte-equality audit verifies that retained production files match the reviewed combined candidate, opposite-feature files match upstream, and generated config counts add only this setting. Generated config metadata, focused formatting, and diff checks passed.

The prior combined candidate passed regression RED/GREEN and focused coverage for config validation, Doctor preservation, mixed hook/cron-agent contention, default eight, configured twelve, single-slot progress, admission overflow, cancellation, and release. Its independent cumulative review found no actionable P0/P1/P2 issues. This split preserves those reviewed production bytes and the concurrency test changes; no additional review round was commissioned.

Retained package proof used candidate `516a94ee`: the published `2026.9.8` updater preserved capacity **12** through update and Doctor, and a separate fresh install admitted **8** by default. Both real foreground Gateway scenarios verified mixed hook/cron-agent traffic, overflow HTTP 503 without model I/O, and completion after release. These are historical combined-candidate results, not package proof of the new standalone head. The combined opt-in harness remains available at commit `55215079819821a750a6a7967823558bb5a3b836`; it is excluded from both split diffs because it requires both settings.

**Still draft:** maintainer acceptance of this restored public control remains outstanding. CI excludes drafts, so required exact-head CI is not claimed green. Full aggregate `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` remain incomplete. Prior package results do not replace standalone-head CI or package validation.

<details>
<summary>Retained receipts and failures</summary>

The original head merged upstream `e9edda34` normally; this split adds a follow-up commit without rewriting shared history. Prior guards, production/test typechecks, npm lock policy, formatting, and docs checks passed. The root typecheck wrapper timed out after three partitions; only the unfinished fourth was resumed and passed. Broad lint failed on inherited max-lines findings in five unchanged blobs. Integrated-tree metadata checks, formatting, Stylelint, and diff checks passed.

Original changed-test wall times (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`): Doctor 6.57 s; shared lanes 28.73 s; admission 1.97 s; config 25.53 s. Prior package cell: updater 398.26 s; upgraded scenario 89.09 s; fresh install 32.93 s; fresh scenario 62.54 s. Exact-head CI seconds remain unavailable.

Raw failures remain recorded: two combined package fixtures violated service/Doctor ownership ordering before correction; initial build orchestration and wrong-tsconfig lint failed; the repository review helper failed before the permitted cumulative review completed. Integration hit a partial-clone fetch error and an ignored-generated-file formatter error before recovery and generator validation.

The combined build's report-only startup gzip was **373537 B** versus a **373454 B** budget; same-environment base was **373524 B**. The **13 B candidate delta** is not fully attributed to inheritance. No budget or gate was waived. Shutdown, real-systemd, and backup-recovery evidence is carried in #165180 and the existing evidence comment; it is not claimed as concurrency-only proof.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): omit unconfigured Gateway computer target from surface
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #178604.

Supersedes #178744, which was auto-closed by the repository's 20-active-PR limit.

On a host whose Gateway has no computer provider configured and whose only screen belongs to one paired node advertising `computer.act` and `screen.snapshot`, the `computer` tool surface still advertised `target: "gateway" | "node"` and listed "the Gateway desktop" first. Models opened desktop turns with `target: "gateway"`; `resolveComputerBinding` then threw "Gateway computer is unavailable; enable its computer provider and desktop session" before node discovery, so desktop turns started with a recoverable failed call. Only the retry without `target` reached the paired node.

## Solution

- `computer-tool-schema.ts`: the `target` enum and description now derive from the resolved Gateway computer status that already travels with the prepared paired surface. When `configured: false`, the schema advertises only `target: "node"` and states that `target: "gateway"` is unavailable. A configured or unknown status keeps both targets, preserving remote/override callers and hand-built tools. The cached-schema key includes the new flag.
- `computer-tool-guidance.ts`: guidance tells the model to omit `target` for automatic routing, and when the Gateway has no provider it describes the paired node instead of the Gateway desktop.
- `computer-tool-bindings.ts`: an explicit `target: "gateway"` against an unconfigured Gateway now reports the missing provider and names the paired-node retry (`Omit target, or use target: node`). Explicit host selection is still never redirected silently.
- `docs/nodes/computer-use.md`: documents the selector behavior.

The schema depends only on `configured` (a config/provider-lifecycle fact already resolved for the turn by `loadPairedComputerUseAvailabilityForSurface`), not on volatile readiness. The tool surface was already rebuilt per turn from those owner-held facts, so this does not introduce a new prompt-cache input class.

## Impact

- Hosts with a paired desktop and no Gateway computer stop advertising an unusable target and route the first call to the node.
- Explicit `target: "gateway"` keeps its documented semantics: configured-but-unavailable reports the provider error; unconfigured now points at the paired-node recovery instead of telling the operator to enable an unwanted provider.
- No config, protocol, or public API changes. No CHANGELOG edit.

## Evidence

Base `bbc5e3a7c` (new tests applied, fix absent):

- `computer-tool.schema.test.ts` new case failed: `properties.target.enum` expected `["node"]`, received `["gateway","node"]`.
- `computer-tool-guidance.test.ts` new case failed: the description still began "Control the Gateway desktop, ..." instead of naming the unconfigured Gateway.

With the fix:

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/computer-tool.schema.test.ts src/agents/tools/computer-tool.gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/computer-tool-guidance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` -> passed 3 Vitest shards, 58 tests (39 + 15 + 4).
- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/computer-tool.node-resolution.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` -> passed 2 shards, 25 tests (20 + 5), including prompt-prefix stability.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` -> passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json --incremental` -> passed.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <touched files>` -> passed for all 8 files.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <touched files>` -> 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` -> clean.

Reproduction boundary and real-behavior evidence: the new tests exercise the production tool-registry composition (`loadPairedComputerUseAvailabilityForSurface` -> `createComputerTool` -> `resolveComputerBinding`) with the Gateway unconfigured and one eligible paired node, using the repository's mocked Gateway/node transport.

Real desktop proof (bounded, synthetic fixtures; sanitized traces below, raw files under `.openclaw/proof/178783/`):

- A real Gateway built from this head (isolated state, Gateway computer provider intentionally unconfigured) served a real agent turn driven by a local deterministic OpenAI-compatible model (`proofmodel/proof-vision`). The model request captured the published `computer` tool with `target.enum` exactly `["node"]` and the unconfigured-Gateway description below.
- A real paired Windows desktop node (this tree's built CLI running `openclaw node run` in an interactive desktop session, `cua-computer` enabled, win32 CUA driver artifacts) connected, was approved, and advertised `computer.act` + `screen.snapshot`.
- An **owner-started** turn through the shipped `openclaw agent` CLI surface then called `computer {"action":"screenshot"}` with no target. The real node-side CUA call succeeded and the assistant answered "Screenshot taken.".
- A first attempt through the operator `chat.send` RPC was correctly refused by the computer tool's owner-authority gate ("this turn was not started by the owner"), so the successful evidence uses the shipped owner CLI surface; no gate was bypassed or stubbed.

Captured evidence (sanitized; no IPs, tokens, credentials, or desktop content):

```jsonc
// published computer tool schema, as sent to the model on the real agent turn
{
  "targetEnum": ["node"],
  "targetDescription": "Computer host. The Gateway has no computer provider configured, so target: gateway is unavailable. Omit target for automatic selection of the sole connected computer-capable node, or use target: node. Later calls retain the selected host."
}
```

```jsonc
// real paired Windows desktop node (isolated fixture)
{
  "displayName": "edy-proof783",
  "platform": "windows",
  "connected": true,
  "approvalState": "approved",
  "computerCommands": ["computer.act", "screen.snapshot"]
}
```

```jsonc
// shipped owner CLI turn: openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:proof783b
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "provider": "proofmodel",
  "model": "proof-vision",
  "terminalReceipt": { "successfulToolNames": ["computer"] },
  "finalText": "Screenshot taken."
}
```

```text
// real transcript, tool result (desktop image block discarded during sanitization)
toolResult: screenshot 1200x675 (screen 0, frameId <redacted-id>)
assistant: Screenshot taken.
```

The misleading "Gateway computer is unavailable; enable its computer provider…" path did not occur in either turn. Gap stated plainly: no vision model exists in this environment, so the deterministic model only issued the action and the reported multi-turn model-choice frequency is not measured.

**AI-assisted: yes.** Authored by an AI coding agent; every check below executed in this checkout.

prs.title: refactor: keep private runtime composition with callers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal CLI, tool, and plugin flows expose private factories and result objects used by only one production owner, with some tests coupled to those private seams.

## User Impact

User impact: no intended user-visible change, migration, or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compose these operations where their inputs and lifecycle already live: CLI rendering/parsing, Doctor diagnostics, MCP serving, proxy capture, outbound media staging, native plugin authentication, provider registration, artifact pagination, and agent image/computer results. Retire the single-consumer modules and forwarding hops, and move useful private-helper coverage to the registered command, provider, or public operation.

Keep public SDK/config/protocol contracts, lazy runtime imports, effect authority, filesystem containment and permissions, image sanitization, cursor bindings and limits, encrypted-delivery worker operations, ordinary cancellation, and shutdown settlement. The standalone session memory backend is untouched.

Net production LOC: **512 removed** (+1,761 / -2,273), excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated files, declarations, and ratchet inventories. The candidate touches 76 paths. Test/support migration adds 244 net lines; the whole diff removes 272 net lines.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Remove duplicate private Reef peer validation: since the factory's introduction in #168340, its sole caller already synchronously validates and normalizes the same peer. The send boundary still performs that check before any worker work or dispatch; no external validation is removed.
- Remove the factory's second copies of the caller-fresh message body and already-copied recipient identity. The same introducing caller constructs/captures those facts synchronously, and no reference to the private body escapes. The owner still snapshots external recipient/key/guard facts before awaits. No security, durability, ordinary-concurrency, recovery, or effect-authority guard is removed.

## Evidence

- Each committed slice passed focused owner/consumer proof, targeted native types, lint, formatting, and fresh independent review through P2. Retained proof is reused only for unchanged source inputs.
- The media/channel forwarding slice passed 60 cases. Image/export proof passed 47 selected cases, including real filesystem writes, containment, overwrite permissions, collisions, corrupt-image handling, execution cancellation, and all five prompt-prefix cases. Artifact/X proof passed 40 cases, including image pagination, sharing/policy revalidation, registered request authority, redacted failure routing, and sticky outcomes.
- The DeepInfra registered-source suites passed 28 cases and five prefix cases. Its unchanged built-provider contract requires runtime asset preparation and remains hosted-CI proof; no local build or passing built-artifact result is claimed.
- Reef/computer proof passed **116 cases**: 53 encrypted-delivery/worker/authority cases, 58 delivered-image/observation/frame cases, and all five prompt-prefix cases. Targeted native types, typed lint, formatting, and line caps pass. These include real storage and cryptography with synthetic relay/model boundaries, not live service or desktop-input proof.
- Final assertion/mock ratchets pass with no new allowances. All 14 suppression-audit cases and four selected wrapper/import-closure cases pass; 18 unrelated closure cases were excluded by the focused name filter, with no test skip changes. Runtime and Madge checks both report **zero cycles**. Formatting, line caps, and whitespace pass.
- All proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, nice priority, one worker, and serial heavy commands. No local broad suite, whole-graph typecheck, build, or E2E is claimed. Exact-head PR CI is the broad gate.

One local lint issue introduced by the computer projection fold was fixed by renaming a shadowed local; no suppression, timeout, retry, or skip was added.

prs.title: fix(daemon): repair JSON-quote-corrupted service env files through doctor (#103804)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103804. Generated LaunchAgent service env files can carry values wrapped in a literal JSON quote pair inside the shell quotes (`export AWS_REGION='"us-east-1"'`). The shell delivers the quotes as data, so consumers break (`Region not accepted: region=""us-east-1""`). The corruption also self-perpetuates: the install plan reads raw process env (`collectConfigSecretRefServiceEnvVars` → `params.env[key]`), so any shell or service that inherited the corrupted value faithfully re-persists it on the next restage — which is why the issue reports hand-edits "persist until the next env file regeneration".

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous revision healed values inside the runtime reader (`launchd-plist.ts`), gated on `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS` membership. ClawSweeper's review rejected that twice over, correctly: managed-key membership is not value-format provenance (a legitimate quote-bearing env-backed SecretRef would be silently altered on every read), and legacy files written before the metadata existed — exactly the population carrying the corruption — took the early return and never healed. It was also a runtime fallback reader, which repo doctrine forbids ("legacy shapes normalize only in doctor/migration code").

This revision is a full redesign:

- **The reader stays lossless.** The runtime shim is gone; runtime never rewrites values.
- **Doctor owns the repair**, at the env file's format owner (`launchd-service-files.ts`): `detectLaunchAgentEnvFileJsonQuoteKeys` (read-only) and `repairLaunchAgentEnvFileJsonQuotes` (line-based rewrite that strips exactly the wrapping quote pair; every other line passes through byte-for-byte, file mode stays 0600, and the rewrite is convergent — a second pass is a no-op).
- **Doctor warns on the always path** (`maybeRepairMacGatewayServiceEnvQuotes`, wired into the gateway-services health runner): a healthy gateway with broken provider credentials must still surface this, so it does not hide behind the unhealthy-gateway repair flow. The warning names the file and keys (never values) and the fix command; the rewrite runs behind the standard `confirmDoctorServiceRepair` prompt (`doctor --fix` applies it). Both the gateway and node LaunchAgent labels are swept.
- **Legacy files heal** (review finding 2): detection is shape-based, so files without the managed-keys metadata are covered.
- **The feedback loop is named to the operator**: after healing, doctor flags any healed key whose corrupted value is still inherited by the current shell, so a reinstall from that shell does not re-persist it.

Named tradeoff (review finding 1): a deliberate operator value whose bytes are exactly a wrapping quote pair is also stripped — but only through the operator-confirmed doctor prompt on an OpenClaw-generated ("Do not edit") file; declining leaves the file byte-identical. General value-format provenance does not exist (the issue thread confirmed the shipped writer emits this shape only when its *input* already carries the quotes), so operator confirmation is the proof this repair runs under.

Sibling surfaces: systemd's env file uses separate machinery (systemd itself strips wrapping quotes in `EnvironmentFile=` parsing) and Windows scheduled tasks do not use this file format; the reported corruption shape is launchd-specific.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` now tells macOS operators when their generated service env file carries the #103804 corruption, names the affected keys, and `doctor --fix` repairs the file in place with a restart hint — including for installs created before the managed-keys metadata existed. Runtime behavior is unchanged (lossless reads); production delta is +163 lines, justified as an operator-visible repair capability at the owner boundary replacing a doctrinally-forbidden runtime shim (+24 lines removed with its test).

## Evidence

- `src/daemon/launchd-service-files.env-quote-repair.test.ts` (5 tests): heals wrapped values and leaves every other line byte-identical (interior quotes, escaped quotes, metadata line preserved; mode stays 0600; second pass converges to null); heals legacy files without managed-keys metadata; documents the named operator-literal tradeoff; clean files and missing files return null untouched.
- `src/commands/doctor-platform-notes.env-quote-repair.test.ts` (3 tests): the doctor step warns + repairs a real seeded file when the operator accepts, warns but leaves the file byte-identical when declined, and stays silent off darwin / on clean installs. These drive the real repair path end-to-end (real temp files, real prompt gate — no mocks of the repair).
- Full `src/daemon` suite: 37 files, 1181 passed. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` green (format, oxlint 1.79, tsgo lanes, import cycles, boundary guards).
- Live CLI proof attempted and blocked by design: `openclaw doctor --fix` gates all service management on the default install identity (`service management skipped: non-default state dir or config path` under both an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and an `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` state dir on this machine), and running doctor repairs against the operator's real `~/.openclaw` service is not authorized from this session. The doctor-step behavior tests above exercise the identical code path the gated CLI flow invokes.


### Real managed-macOS proof (head `6365ed8cac3`)

Executed on a real macOS LaunchAgent gateway service, isolated under a dedicated profile so no operator service or state was touched:

- **Setup**: the branch head was packaged (`scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` tarball) and installed via `npm install -g` into a profile prefix; `openclaw --profile qaenvproof gateway install` created the real LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.qaenvproof.plist`, `service-env/ai.openclaw.qaenvproof.env`, env-sourcing wrapper) and launchd started the gateway listening on its port.
- **Corruption**: `export AWS_REGION='"us-east-1"'` appended to the generated env file (the exact #103804 shape). A `gateway install --force` reinstall preserved the corrupted entry — confirming the issue's premise that the corruption persists through service rewrites.
- **Repair flow observed** (interactive `openclaw --profile qaenvproof doctor`, real PTY):
  1. Detection note rendered: `~/.openclaw-qaenvproof/service-env/ai.openclaw.qaenvproof.env has 1 value(s) wrapped in literal double quotes (AWS_REGION)` / `This is the #103804 serialization corruption...`.
  2. The shape-gated prompt (`Rewrite 1 quote-corrupted value(s) ... now?`) required an explicit interactive accept — three earlier `doctor --fix` runs on the same corrupted service never auto-stripped the value, live confirmation of the `requiresInteractiveConfirmation` contract.
  3. After accepting: `Rewrote 1 value(s) (AWS_REGION). Restart the gateway service (openclaw --profile qaenvproof gateway restart) so the healed values take effect.` — the correctly-named owning-service restart command.
  4. File healed to `export AWS_REGION='us-east-1'`; after the instructed restart, the **live relaunched service process env** read directly off the running pid showed `AWS_REGION=us-east-1` while the service listened on its port.
- **Flow finding fixed in the same push**: the proof surfaced that `doctor --fix` engages gateway maintenance, which skips the gateway-services section hosting this repair — so the note's old claim that `doctor --fix` rewrites the entries was unreachable in practice on a managed service. The note now points operators at the interactive `openclaw doctor` prompt (commit `6365ed8cac3`).
- Environment note: the packaged install was required because a launchd-spawned service cannot read a dev checkout under `~/Documents` (macOS TCC `Operation not permitted`) — the packaged path also makes the proof match a real operator install.
- Teardown: `gateway uninstall` + profile state removed; no operator service existed on this machine at any point.

prs.title: fix: avoid duplicate Claude MCP servers with node execution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local Claude CLI turns with effective `tools.exec.host: "node"` start another copy of each configured stdio MCP server, even though the Gateway already owns those connections.

Related: #164690. The per-server supervisor-wrapper cost remains open there.

## User Impact

Configured MCP tools use the existing Gateway bridge as `<server>__<tool>`, eliminating Claude-spawned duplicates. Native Bash stays on the Gateway host, the separate bridge `exec` targets the selected node, and Claude retains its native tools, user settings, and permission handling.

An affected existing conversation can start one fresh native Claude session when its MCP surface changes; OpenClaw history is preserved. Node-placed model sessions and default-host custom backends retain their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured-MCP ownership was coupled to exact native-tool selection. This separates those decisions while reusing the existing bridge catalog, grants, policy checks, and connection owner. Configured-server overrides apply to that catalog without disabling the internal bridge when a user server is also named `openclaw`. Unrelated native overrides, including WebSearch, remain effective.

No new public API, configuration option, or acquisition path is added. Default managed turns keep using the bridge.

Release-note context: local Claude CLI turns using node execution reuse Gateway-owned configured MCP servers without spawning duplicate stdio children.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateways and real Claude Code were exercised on macOS arm64 with Node 26.12.0 and pinned Bun 1.4.4. Three real stdio fixtures and an independently paired execution node verify process ownership, MCP effects/hooks, local native Bash/settings, and node-targeted execution. The model provider is synthetic and local; no paid-provider call is claimed. The measurement workload was adapted from #178316 and remains outside the source tree.

The complete-build performance cohort passed 22/22 runs: five serial baseline/candidate pairs per runtime plus managed-turn controls. Every baseline had six fixture processes and three Claude-spawned duplicates; every candidate had three fixtures and zero duplicates. Each passing run had one configured MCP effect and expected hook, and shut down with zero survivors without forced cleanup.

| Runtime | Median fixture RSS | Median invocation → catalog | Maximum invocation → catalog |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Node | 418.06 → 207.95 MiB (−50.3%) | 4.379 → 4.763 s (+8.8%) | 5.470 → 5.363 s (−2.0%) |
| Bun | 348.08 → 183.11 MiB (−47.4%) | 2.677 → 2.869 s (+7.2%) | 2.991 → 3.005 s (+0.5%) |

All declared min/median/p95/max latency, RSS, and process-count gates stayed within the original 20% worsening threshold; no sample was replaced. Whole-process-tree RSS median changed +1.2% on Node and −2.8% on Bun. This claims duplicate-server savings; supervisor-wrapper overhead remains unresolved.

That cohort precedes the final override-collision repair. Four additional current-head runs cover node-exec and managed turns on Node and Bun with a disabled configured server named `openclaw` and native WebSearch disabled. All four preserve the expected settings and effects, run three fixtures with zero duplicates, and shut down with zero survivors. They are distinct correctness scenarios, not replacement performance samples.

The duplication and name-collision regressions both failed before their fixes. The final focused configuration/consumer suites pass 26 tests, including the unchanged default-host consumer and generic exclusive-config behavior. The changed test file separately passes five tests in 45.08 seconds including compilation/wrapper work; the cases take 6.828 seconds and exercise real HTTP MCP and Gateway lifecycle behavior. The same file passes all five tests in 13.45 seconds in CI. Typecheck, targeted lint/format, line-cap, docs links, build, and independent review through P2 pass.

Current head: `416f4488da18720fd5f972b5afbed2c8b9e5a6f8`. CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39496653870 — passed on this exact head (35 successful jobs, 27 intentionally skipped). Six Security High checks also passed.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep screen awake during voice activity
prs.body:
Closes #120245

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Browser Talk or holding the composer voice-dictation control on a mobile browser can have the interaction interrupted when the device's normal screen timeout expires.

This was reproduced on a Huawei P30 Pro using Brave Browser on Android.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the browser Screen Wake Lock API while microphone-driven Talk or dictation is active, release the lock when the activity stops, and reacquire it when the page becomes visible again. The feature is progressive: unsupported browsers and rejected wake-lock requests continue with the existing microphone behavior, with no new configuration, dependency, or backend protocol.

## User Impact

Mobile users can continue a Browser Talk session or voice dictation without periodically touching the screen solely to prevent display timeout. The screen is allowed to sleep normally again as soon as the microphone activity ends.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the change on a Huawei P30 Pro in Brave Browser on Android: allowing the normal display timeout to expire disrupted the active Browser Talk interaction.
- Verified the reversible Control UI backport on the same device: the display remained awake while Browser Talk was active and returned to normal timeout behavior after the session ended.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/screen-wake-lock.test.ts` — 3 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-lifecycle.test.ts` — 21 tests passed.
- Focused wake-lock, Talk, and dictation test suite during initial implementation — 43 tests passed.
- Formatting across all seven changed files — passed.
- Production Control UI build, precompressed-asset verification, and performance checks — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- The Browser Talk Playwright fixture and assertions cover wake-lock acquisition and release. Local Chromium execution is unavailable on this host, so that E2E scenario was not run locally.
- The standalone composer-dictation test invocation is blocked before test collection by the repository browser-test harness resolving `node:` imports (`ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE`); no dictation assertion failed.

No visual layout changes are introduced, so before/after screenshots would be identical. The relevant before/after evidence is the device screen-timeout behavior described above.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used to inspect the codebase, implement the change, add tests, run validation, and draft this PR. Matt  reproduced the original issue and manually verified the live behaviour on the stated Android device and browser. The submitted diff and evidence were reviewed before publication.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep retention running after database startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cron session retention repeatedly failing after background agent-database startup preparation ends.

## User Impact

Expired cron sessions can be cleaned up after startup while recent sessions, ordinary conversations, and protected running sessions remain intact. Pending databases stay excluded until preparation completes. No configuration, storage-format, or retention-policy change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An early database-topology notification can carry temporary startup admission. The scheduler preserves its registration context, so retention could inherit that temporary authority, fail after a worker read, and rearm its retry with the same expired context.

Bind the existing retention scheduling callback to the Gateway's maintenance context when maintenance starts. This preserves current admission checks and Gateway resources without restoring a global startup barrier or changing the scheduler's context contract. The documentation also removes the obsolete claim that retention waits for all startup preparation.

The simplification pass retained one existing owner and two distinct regressions: pending-admission isolation with owner context preserved, and completion/rearming after preparation ends during an asynchronous read. Production changes are +24/−23 (mostly moving the existing callback); tests add 88 lines, and one documentation paragraph changes.

## Evidence

- Exact-head CI [39505011052](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39505011052), attempt 1, completed successfully: 30 passed and 28 skipped jobs, including `security-fast` and the Actions CI gate. The separate older commit-status badge still says pending because its resolver refreshes only open PRs; the PR was already merged when CI finished. No CI rerun or status override was used.
- Both new regressions failed before the production fix. The second reproduced `Agent database preparation has ended: main` on the initial sweep and its retry.
- 85 tests passed across cron lifecycle, real SQLite retention/snapshots, session-registry maintenance, Gateway scheduling, and database admission. These cover protected running sessions, pending/failed admission, cancellation, rollback, notifications, and shutdown.
- The final 21-case lifecycle file passed again after a test-only Promise-join correction. Core production types, the affected services-cron test type graph, targeted typed lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent local P0–P2 review found no actionable issue. The production diff is unchanged since review; later fixture-only initialization/join corrections passed their focused tests and checks.
- Two isolated macOS/Node 26.4.0 Gateway starts exercised real preparation, durable pruning, preservation, restart, and clean process/listener cleanup. Neither logged the expired-preparation failure. The original driver remains qualified because its final broad hash check detected the intentional test-file edit during the CLI build; production bytes stayed identical. Final admitted-sweep logs arrived while graceful shutdown joined background work.
- Canonical packaging and normal npm installation passed on isolated AWS Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, at exact commit `17f41b6dd50ed6a6cc927638af1f10987965ec0b`. Archive SHA-256: `701c79e15695820496c09ac53604c2c2bb86b493c70baf96bb1cd47381fad927`. Two installed Gateway starts exercised pending preparation, admitted retention completed before shutdown, durable expired-session pruning, unchanged recent/ordinary rows, and restart. Both exited 0 with all captured descendants gone and listeners closed. The exact 17,929-file runtime inventory matched the archive before and after; tracked source stayed clean. This does not assert dependency-directory equivalence or deterministically reproduce the race covered by the regression tests.
- The first Linux driver stopped at an incorrect process-identity assertion: OpenClaw deliberately replaces its process title. That failed receipt remains intact. The corrected observer checks the installed launcher's resolved path/hash, actual launch ancestry, and pinned Node executable; the fresh-state repeat reused the unchanged archive/install and unchanged behavior assertions. No production workaround or rebuild was used.

<details>
<summary>Selected installed-runtime records</summary>

Fields below are reduced to the maintenance owner's timestamp, outcome, and counts; full runtime inventories and original failed observer evidence are retained.

```text
Start 1:
2026-10-20T21:59:08.289+00:00 retention completed; pruned=0; skippedStores=1
2026-10-20T21:59:09.415+00:00 agent database preparation completed
2026-10-20T21:59:12.158+00:00 retention completed; pruned=1; skippedStores=0
2026-10-20T21:59:12.258Z SIGTERM sent after admitted sweep; exit=0
Start 2:
2026-10-20T21:59:20.047+00:00 retention completed; pruned=0; skippedStores=1

```

Both runs preserved the exact recent/ordinary database rows; all captured descendants exited and both final listener probes returned `ECONNREFUSED`.

</details>

Test cost: `pnpm test src/cron/maintenance-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 12.69s wall on the earlier equivalent fixture; the final direct repository-wrapper run took 37.07s. These are test costs, not application-performance measurements. CI job `checks-node-changed-1` passed all 21 lifecycle cases on this exact head, including both new regressions: 7.80s Vitest duration and 10.71s repository-wrapper time in the Bun shard ([job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39505011052/job/118912330610)).

### Remaining qualifications

The aggregate changed-check is not green: it reports existing max-lines suppressions in three untouched UI files, unchanged test-graph root budgets, and unused exports in untouched agentsapi/QA-lab/board files. The suppression failure reproduces against the unchanged base index; graph inputs and reported export owners/configuration match the base. A separate whole-base Knip replay was not performed. The initial type run stopped at the now-corrected fixture error after 24 passing graphs; the affected graph passed separately, and four later unrelated graphs were not run.

The local live proof was not warning-free: the source seeder logged an unexplained automatic session-maintenance warning before Gateway startup; shutdown logged provider-catalog lifetime closure and background-work draining refusals. Those diagnostics are outside this narrow repair and are not claimed fixed. No model calls or provider credentials were used.

The Linux proof likewise retained warnings: expected loopback-only `auth:none`/disabled-cron notices and provider-catalog lifetime closure after SIGTERM. Its seed had no warnings/errors, and neither completed run logged a maintenance failure or expired preparation. Build/install advisories remain recorded; npm's lifecycle receipts confirm the install scripts completed despite its allowScripts advisory. prs.title: refactor(plugins): trust concrete setup and replay owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams setup widened its concrete factory into an optional finalizer contract, and QA JSONL replay retained injectable-runner/parity plumbing although its sole CLI caller only supports the fixed mock runner. Teams pending cards also copied metadata that their sole runtime consumer never reads.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or migration. Teams authentication/approvals and QA's supported mock JSONL replay keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trust the concrete setup finalizer, build the existing JSONL mock cells directly, and stop copying unread pending-card metadata. Keep mutable setup credentials, every real authentication mode, CLI validation/options/report shapes, transcript prefix bytes, ordering, mock-cell status and estimates, and historical drift rendering. Approval binding still uses the canonical request and view; card contents, expiry wording, allowed decisions, tokens, current-effect authority and delivery fallback stay unchanged. No public SDK/config/protocol/persisted-shape/dependency changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A hypothetical replacement Teams setup factory lacking a finalizer or result no longer receives fallbacks. The introducing implementation explicitly said the factory always provides finalize and described the branch as hypothetical forward compatibility (#51646; commit 355794c24a39). A malformed internal replacement now fails its concrete contract instead of silently falling back.
- JSONL replay no longer supports a private injected alternative runner or synthetic per-turn divergence. Commit cf0657852f65 anticipated a future Phase 1 runner; no production activation was wired, and the sole CLI caller rejects non-mock provider modes. A real future runner needs an explicit implementation. Historical reports still render divergence; actual runtime parity classifiers and confidence canaries stay.
- No edge-case fallback is removed by dropping the three Teams card metadata copies. They were introduced with native cards (#129997), not to repair a human-reported copy-loss incident; authoritative request/view data remains available at binding.

## Size

101 net production lines removed (+43/-144), five production files. Test/support: 91 net removed (+47/-138). Eight files total, including one exact shrink-only assertion allowance repair. This is a residue PR under the campaign's 100-line exception, not a LARGE PR.

## Evidence

Completed unchanged-input proof: 30 Teams setup/delegated cases, JSONL 3 cases, the actual CLI mock-report case, runtime-parity execution-order 4 cases, and one selected confidence negative-control canary. Strict targeted Teams/QA types pass. 617 production files have zero runtime cycles and no new static components. Focused syntax lint, line caps, format and whitespace pass; assertion allowance cli.runtime tightens from 4 to actual 2. Independent P0-P2 review was scoped-clean with source verification.

Incremental proof passed: 18 card/binding/submit cases across three suites (60.10s Vitest; 69.39s wrapper), strict targeted types, all 14 mandatory suppression cases (16.34s Vitest; 20.69s wrapper), 617-file scoped cycles (zero runtime/no new static components), exact five-file assertion allowances, focused syntax lint, seven-source-file line caps, format and whitespace. Incremental independent P0-P2 review was scoped-clean (.98), with final source verification. No source changes followed review. Broad check-changed was classified with dry-run only; hosted CI on the exact PR head is the broad gate. No live Teams claim. Standalone Phase E memory backend untouched.

## CI attribution

Exact-head run [39490489640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39490489640) has an inherited failure in [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets / job 118862895213](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39490489640/job/118862895213): the mock-export check names `src/commands/doctor-database-network-storage.test.ts:15`, introduced on main by #178672, not changed by this PR. The native single-file mock scanner reproduces the exact unlisted factory on both the CI main base (`503ae08`) and retained fresh main (`f629720`), with identical test bytes and unchanged scanner code. The actual CI merge (`64713a27`) has those same failing inputs as its main parent. Every other ratchet subcheck passed, including this PR's assertion allowance repair.

The coordinator's flake index and latest six completed scheduled main runs were checked: their ratchets passed before that new test landed; the index's other mock-export case is not being substituted as evidence. Run39490489640 attempt1 is now complete. The only other failed job is downstream aggregate118924645487, whose log names only the baseline ratchet failure. All205 exact-head checks were enumerated:67success,133skipped,2cancelled metadata runs with successful same-head successors,1neutral CodeQL,2failures. CodeQL warns that17 configurations were not present; this is a scanning coverage gap, not a full CodeQL success claim. Native version1 evidence retains the actual tested merge, ordered main/head parents, unchanged failure inputs, baseline reproduction, and aggregate attribution. The scoped campaign authorizes the native inherited-failure exception; this is not a claim that CI is green. No CI rerun or green-only push.

MCP view and board unit tests evaluate the full Gateway protocol schema barrel to obtain one error predicate and its discriminator. The retained scheduled-main run spent 3.817 s collecting board-view and 2.990 s collecting mcp-app-view.

Use the existing public `@openclaw/gateway-protocol/gateway-error-details` entry for `isMcpAppViewExpiredError` in the owner and `GatewayErrorDetailCodes` in its test. prs.title: perf(sessions): fuse prepared PostgreSQL entry writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session entry writer prepares its node and side-table rows together but sends them separately to PostgreSQL. A normal warm turn pays three avoidable round trips across acceptInput, completeTurn, and entry.patch.commit.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL can write each eligible prepared pair in one statement inside the existing transaction. SQLite behavior, committed entry data, snapshots, window ownership, locks, and final commit authority stay the same. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The entry owner selects node+window when both changed and snapshots did not, or node+snapshot upserts when both changed and no snapshot was removed. Each child consumes the node's RETURNING key, including on first creation. The query owner reuses its existing node/window upserts; the snapshot owner supplies the same conflict policy to both paths. Snapshot revisions remain trigger-owned.

Unchanged writes remain omitted. Snapshot removals retain their ordered path. If snapshots and the window both change, the node/snapshots pair is followed by the existing window write. Conversation writes and cache publication stay at their current boundaries.

## Evidence

The real actor regression is red on base `1f56bd7d3ed6`: acceptInput, completeTurn, and entry.patch.commit each require two entry-table statements. The candidate requires one each, with unchanged BEGIN/COMMIT/advisory-lock counts. Both engines pass exact entry/window/snapshot state, no-op and one-table writes, rollback after the statement, and revoked final commit grant checks.

Additional both-engine cases cover first-creation foreign keys, trigger revisions, idempotent replay, snapshot deletions, shared-window claim/retain ownership, interleaved one/two/one-row snapshot batches, and legacy provenance replacement and omitted-column preservation. All six conformance cases and 61 tests across six existing consumer suites pass. Core and infrastructure test typechecking, scoped lint, formatting, Kysely guardrails, and Madge import-cycle checking pass. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on final head `380ba8b3688e` in [CI run 39491271867](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39491271867). CI run 39491271867 completed on head `380ba8b3688e`: all selected checks passed except the inherited Doctor mock-export finding at `src/commands/doctor-database-network-storage.test.ts:15` and its downstream CI aggregate. Its test, target, scanner, checker, and baseline ledger are byte-identical to the PR base. Landing uses the native inherited-failure evidence route; failed CI is not reported as green. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Production delta: +275/−166 lines (net +109); regression tests: +550; test routing: +1. Most query-builder deletions/additions are mechanical indentation from reusing the existing builders.

## Performance

Owner acceptance: the deterministic effect is −3 PostgreSQL wire trips and SQL statements per warm turn (matched owner work 34/121/148 → 34/112/139), with transactions and locks unchanged. Server-side, the fused statements cost about the sum of the statements they replace (node+snapshot fused 0.36–0.38 ms mean vs standalone snapshot ~0.29 ms plus the separate node upsert; node+window fused 0.15 ms), so the fusion introduces no plan pathology. The initial local −32%/+66% C=64 result did not reproduce under the controlled attempt (partial −4.96%/+6.28%, within single-pair noise; Testbox unavailable, host load gate unmet). A consolidated interleaved re-measure runs after the pgopt wave.

Measurement protocol used during the earlier owner hold: require exactly three fewer PostgreSQL wire trips per warm turn with unchanged requests, transactions, locks, and results. The requested re-measure was to run three back-to-back A/B pairs on one host: base `1f56bd7d3ed6` PostgreSQL, base SQLite, candidate `380ba8b3688e` PostgreSQL, candidate SQLite, repeated three times. Every cell runs the unchanged frozen C=64 workload (64 sessions × five turns) and census; each PostgreSQL cell uses a fresh cluster. Record `uptime` and start only at one-minute load ≤ observed CPU count / 4, waiting at most 20 minutes per cell. Prefer one Testbox attempt through the campaign remote slot, with a 30-minute allocation cutoff and no provider chaining; otherwise use the same local load gate. Report each pair’s throughput/p95, absolute PG-minus-SQLite differences, control-adjusted candidate/base ratios, and the affected statements’ pg_stat_statements calls/mean/max execution times. Persistent adverse movement beyond the SQLite control requires query-plan, lock-duration, and FK/trigger investigation and a fix or withdrawal. The previous uncontrolled pair remains evidence; the final owner decision is recorded verbatim above.

Frozen local PG17 comparison, three warm turns per arm, with all 63 frozen harness hashes verified:

| Per warm turn | Base `1f56bd7d3ed6` | Candidate `380ba8b3688e` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Requests / wire trips / SQL statements | 11.3333 / 40.3333 / 49.3333 | 11.3333 / 37.3333 / 46.3333 |
| BEGIN / COMMIT / advisory locks | 9 / 9 / 9 | 9 / 9 / 9 |
| PostgreSQL errors / rollbacks | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

This removes exactly **three wire trips and three SQL statements per warm turn**. acceptInput uses 7→6 trips; completeTurn and entry.patch.commit each use 4→3. The two append requests remain at 13 trips. Both arms completed all five ordinary turns and restart/readback, each with one bounded retry of a definite pre-admission startup refusal. Local census wall times are not a performance claim.

The initial Testbox request received no machine within the 30-minute total allocation budget. It was stopped; no remote workload ran. That original measurement stage used no second allocation or provider.

The permitted fallback ran once on a shared 32-CPU arm64 macOS host with 512 GiB RAM and Homebrew PostgreSQL 17, using fresh database/Gateway state per arm and the unchanged C=64 workload (64 sessions × five turns). Both runtime-source trees were byte-verified; the two candidate-only test/routing paths were excluded from baseline runtime input.

The following results led to the earlier hold; the final owner acceptance is recorded above. This is one loaded local-host pair, not Testbox qualification or a production latency claim.

| Local C=64 metric | Base | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Completed turns | 320/320 | 320/320 |
| Errors / timeouts / unattempted | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Throughput, turns/s | 4.06230 | 2.74271 |
| p50 latency, seconds | 15.7466 | 21.0453 |
| p95 latency, seconds | 17.3973 | 28.8896 |
| p99 latency, seconds | 17.7970 | 29.0704 |

Throughput worsened **32.48%** and p95 worsened **66.06%**. Both arms completed 320 tool requests/results and ordinary/restart readback. The host's one-minute load moved 18.53→13.44 across the baseline and 17.84→25.89 across the candidate. The differing load is a confounder; it does not prove that load caused the regression or that the change is harmless. Per-turn-index p95 for indices 0–4 (64 samples each) was 16.701 / 14.864 / 15.686 / 17.797 / 16.381 seconds on baseline and 29.070 / 21.444 / 21.415 / 27.129 / 27.698 seconds on candidate: all five groups worsened. This breakdown does not establish causality. No additional pair was run during that original stage. All six local PostgreSQL/Gateway/mock ports are closed and task-owned databases/fixtures were removed. The never-allocated Testbox lease is terminal; its wrapper recovery receipt remains retained because no GitHub run was associated with it.

### Controlled re-measure after the owner hold — incomplete

The planned series was three four-cell pairs on one host: base PostgreSQL, base SQLite, candidate PostgreSQL, candidate SQLite. A new Testbox attempt used the campaign remote slot and ended after 1,782.72 seconds including source preparation, without an assigned host. Native state is completed and the slot was released; no remote workload ran. Its wrapper recovery records remain retained because there was no GitHub run association. No other provider or lease was tried.

The local fallback used the same 32-CPU host, fresh PostgreSQL 17 clusters, separate stress/census fixtures, and the required one-minute load limit of 8 before every cell. All 63 canonical harness files remained byte-identical. The separately hashed adapter added top-level identity and min/max/stddev execution columns to its existing PostgreSQL statistics snapshot; it added no query or planning instrumentation.

| Completed C=64 cell | Turns | Turns/s | p95, seconds | Start load |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Base PostgreSQL | 320/320 | 4.49640 | 15.50883 | 7.92236 |
| Base SQLite | 320/320 | 5.65659 | 12.31788 | 7.82764 |
| Candidate PostgreSQL | 320/320 | 4.27318 | 16.48322 | 7.91260 |

All three completed stress cells had zero errors/timeouts and passed their census/readback checks. The raw PostgreSQL movement is −4.96% throughput and +6.28% p95. **These are partial observations, not acceptance evidence:** the candidate SQLite control never started. Its gate timed out after 1,200.05 seconds with 41 uptime/load samples, a minimum one-minute load of 8.9707 and maximum of 28.9341. The controller then stopped the remaining series without repeating a cell. There are zero complete four-cell pairs, so PG-minus-SQLite changes and control-adjusted ratios cannot be calculated. The requested three-pair regression-versus-noise decision remains unresolved; The full requested measurement remains incomplete; the owner has accepted the evidence above for landing.

The partial census records raw R/T/S per warm turn of 11.6667/40.6667/49.6667 on base and 11.3333/37.3333/46.3333 on candidate. Base contains one extra `authProfiles.read` (one request/trip/statement across three turns); that difference is not credited. Matched owner operations still prove exactly −3 trips and −3 statements per warm turn: acceptInput 7→6, completeTurn 4→3, and entry.patch.commit 4→3, each observed three times. BEGIN/COMMIT/advisory-lock counts remain 27/27/27 across three turns, with zero causal errors/rollbacks.

Partial C=64 ramp `pg_stat_statements` measurements below are top-level only. Means are call-weighted, maxima are individual statement maxima, and nested trigger work is not added again. Shared standalone shapes have different caller mixtures after fusion, so their means are component diagnostics, not matched per-operation server costs.

| Revision / statement family | Calls | Mean exec, ms | Max exec, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Base: session_nodes | 1890 | 0.0939 | 8.5880 |
| Base: two snapshots | 320 | 0.2888 | 2.1581 |
| Base: session_windows | 936 | 0.0553 | 0.1505 |
| Base: one snapshot | 64 | 0.2925 | 0.6584 |
| Candidate: node + retained-owner window | 814 | 0.1536 | 1.6922 |
| Candidate: node + two snapshots | 320 | 0.3756 | 0.7238 |
| Candidate: session_nodes | 687 | 0.0920 | 0.3789 |
| Candidate: node + one snapshot | 64 | 0.3558 | 0.6415 |
| Candidate: session_windows | 128 | 0.0512 | 0.1407 |

Planning time remains unmeasured. The smaller raw PG movement does not establish that the original −32.48% / +66.06% result was noise. With no complete control pair, this incomplete attempt alone does not settle the regression-versus-noise question. The owner acceptance above supplies the performance landing decision. Synthetic database dumps, phase-level statistics, per-operation traces, source/hash receipts, and gate history are retained for the follow-up. All 14 PG/Gateway/mock ports are verified closed; live task fixtures/data are removed and source restored.

The rewrite+append prior-event SELECT/conditional UPDATE and extra window touch remain outside this change; they require a resident-payload invalidation contract.

prs.title: fix: refresh notification settings after Web Push updates
prs.body: Fixes #178631 ## What Problem This Solves Settings → Notifications can stay on Checking and Not requested after Web Push registration completes, leaving users without the Unsubscribe action until they reload. Progress publications can also leave the Enable notifications label unchanged while registration is running. ## User Impact The mounted Settings page updates its Web Push status, preferences and available actions when the existing notification capability publishes state. Browser consent, registration and unsubscribe behavior stay with their current owners. This change adds no configuration, permissions, persistence or dependencies. ## Why This Change Was Made Web Push updates one mutable snapshot in place. Settings already observes each capability publication, but forwards the same snapshot object through a downstream Solid equality check. The page now derives a shallow presentation value at that existing boundary so each publication reaches the rendered controls. Native notifications already replace their snapshot and are unchanged. The regression mounts the existing ConfigPage once, publishes loading and registration/preferences updates from a stable snapshot, checks the visible controls, then clicks Unsubscribe and verifies the disable action. It exercises the rendering boundary that the existing direct snapshot assertions could not cover. ## Evidence On unchanged production baseline `432bada3bd86902d7486472f6dbc973e2d4898cf`, the mounted regression fails because the button remains Enable notifications after the loading publication. The focused baseline command is `pnpm test ui/src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "renders Web Push registration publications"`; Vitest reported 4.17s, with 5.52s for the native test invocation. The corrected tree passed changed-file formatting with Bun parity, source lint, UI catalog verification, and all 14 selected compiler graphs. The related test batch passed 139 cases across nine Settings files, including the complete ConfigPage file and its loading, granted/registered, preference and Unsubscribe assertions. The native test batch took 24.71s; its two Vitest shards took 9.16s and 11.26s. Hosted CI [run 39473923740](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39473923740) passed. Its three UI unit rows took 432s, 376s and 365s, and its selected mocked UI E2E row took 116s; these include the wider selected suites, not just this regression. Actual browser verification on a built integration runtime containing the same presentation change completed **Ready → Subscribed/Granted → Ready/Not subscribed** without reloading between the actions. Exactly one browser/Gateway registration and one unsubscribe completed, leaving no browser subscription. The owned test device was removed through its native owner and existing authority/configuration was preserved. Independent review accepted this evidence together with the public-head regression and CI. The recording's integration producer is `d76083dff482e736914be6da5a237b736f76c4a8`, distinct from public PR head `7419dcdeba3810c347dc6ed545181d001bc825d1`. Scoped source comparison confirms that the recorded baseline-to-candidate notification path differs only by this PR's snapshot-copy hunk. Browser permission was granted in the isolated test profile; this does not demonstrate a human consent dialog, and no notification delivery was tested. The older capture already showed Checking before Enable; the comparison establishes stale state after successful registration, not the cause of its initial Checking state. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Earlier build: registration succeeded but Settings stays Checking with no Unsubscribe](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7b8ef11-fb77-4ccd-a1fd-6f079cfe5faf) | ![Corrected integration build: Subscribed and Granted with Unsubscribe available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70044993-484c-41c8-b7b3-6e9f8b27015e) | ### Continuous registration and unsubscribe on the corrected integration runtime https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f86ddf7-572b-41dd-9359-a221bdf20138 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 617f152e8112ae21211e84f3461d74efdff218b4 - Exact head: `d76083dff482e736914be6da5a237b736f76c4a8` - Scenario: Enable browser notifications, observe Subscribed and Granted without reloading, then use Unsubscribe\. Browser permission is pre\-granted in an isolated test profile; no human\-consent\-dialog or notification\-delivery claim\. - Runtime/build: Built integration runtime d76083dff482e736914be6da5a237b736f76c4a8, tree 5a50037043c9fc8b138356d1c605d73e3082a05e; contains the exact Settings presentation change from public PR head 7419dcdeba3810c347dc6ed545181d001bc825d1\. Public\-head mounted regression and CI are separate proof\. - Actual effects: One browser/Gateway subscribe and one browser/Gateway unsubscribe; final browser subscription absent\. - Final state: Ready, Granted, Not subscribed; no Checking or error state\. - Same Notifications card, dark theme, 1280×720 source viewport and x400/y40 crop to 880×360\. Separate captures, not synchronized; baseline already showed Checking before Enable\. - The only changed file in this notification path between the retained baseline and corrected integration producer is the exact shallow snapshot\-copy hunk\. - All 825 frames of the continuous 33\-second interval were inspected; no splice, retiming or synthetic product content\. - The test device was removed through its native owner; existing device authority and profiles were preserved\. - Existing keypair/configuration preserved\. Permission grant is not human\-consent\-dialog proof; no notification was sent\.

prs.title: fix(slack): default account stops starting once a named account is added
prs.body:
Closes #121446

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the default Slack account failing to start after a named account with its own credentials is added while top-level credentials use SecretRefs.

## User Impact

The implicit default keeps its credentials alongside named accounts in socket, HTTP, and relay modes, including user-token identity. Existing explicit-default and disabled-account behavior is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Secret collection omitted the implicit account that Slack account discovery still starts. The shared account surface now includes that consumer when the plugin's existing readiness rule says it exists. Slack reuses the same transport-specific check as account discovery; Discord and Feishu share the insertion mechanism while retaining their credential and alias rules.

Thanks @555aaditya for the original fix and reproduction.

## Evidence

- Regression: four socket/HTTP/relay/user-identity cases fail on base with unresolved root refs, then pass with the fix. Explicit-default, disabled-channel, and incomplete-credential controls stay inactive. The shared SDK, runtime siblings, Slack account behavior, and Discord/Feishu contract suites pass on the integrated branch (56 tests), including Feishu normalized default aliases. The follow-up Slack case/whitespace alias regressions fail on the prior head with `SECRET_REF_NOT_FOUND`; all 28 affected shared/Slack-runtime/Discord/Feishu tests pass after the correction and latest main integration.
- Credential-free product proof: an isolated Gateway on base logs two inactive root refs and fails default startup; real `channels.status` reports the stopped default. On head `de4b5205d489a72b94e15befa19ae6ac79651225`, both accounts reach Slack authentication with synthetic tokens, with zero inactive-root warnings and no unresolved refs. The real status RPC and a Gateway-backed mock-model turn succeed without fallback. Owned processes, ports, and temporary state were cleaned up; real Slack send/receive remains pending below.
- Final ClawSweeper review: no actionable code findings on `de4b5205d489a72b94e15befa19ae6ac79651225`; authenticated Slack messaging and same-state stable-upgrade proof remain outstanding.
- Production: 8 fewer lines; regression tests: 115 added lines. The collector-only tests from the original proposal are replaced by runtime-boundary coverage.
- Autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings after moving normalized explicit-default exclusion into the shared owner for Slack, Discord, and Feishu. Core/extension production and test typechecks, targeted lint/format, import cycles, and export scans passed. The broader local changed-file run reports existing UI max-lines suppression failures and core test-shard count limits; both repeat after the main refresh, with their inputs unchanged by this PR. The final qualified Slack cold-import check passed at 98.6 MiB peak RSS. At handoff, [CI run 39486353158](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39486353158) has 41 completed jobs with no failed jobs and 8 queued; CI remains pending. The security-sensitive gate requires the maintainer-only `/allow-security-sensitive-change` command for this head because the shared secrets owner changed; that command remains outstanding.

PENDING-CREDENTIALS: authenticated Slack send/receive proof awaits `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SITE_URL` and `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SECRET_CI`; the prepared scenario uses one leased default bot beside a disabled named fixture. Run from the final checkout:

```sh
TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-ct-slack pnpm openclaw qa slack --sut-account default --scenario-file "$HOME/.cache/clawtrib-2026-10-20/slack/slack-implicit-default.yaml" --output-dir "$HOME/.cache/clawtrib-2026-10-20/slack/channel-live"
```

<details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): reap adopted children during supervised shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Linux Gateway shutdown failing with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` when an outer process supervisor retains an adopted zombie while the Gateway waits for that child's process group to disappear.

## User Impact

Gateways running under nested process supervision can complete child cleanup and exit successfully. The mixed regression now covers twelve active runs and requires a clean exit within five seconds of managed SIGTERM.

The separately reported 84-second `session-effects` stall was not reproduced and is not claimed fixed. Pending-close diagnostics now identify remaining effect custody to make a recurrence attributable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Linux subreaper previously reaped adopted children only during final cleanup, after its application root exited. A synthetic Gateway reproduction proved a Git zombie belonged to the outer supervisor while the Gateway's spawn broker was waiting for its process group to disappear.

Observe `SIGCHLD` after admitting the root and reuse the existing native drain to reap adopted exits immediately. Tracked root statuses remain owned by Node, and final cleanup still requires authoritative extinction. The effect diagnostic projects existing owners into the existing bounded trace without changing their release barrier.

Production code grows by 33 lines for the missing active reaping and owner diagnostics. The existing native and mixed-workload fixtures cover both invariants; no new test file is added.

## Evidence

On an isolated Linux sandbox with synthetic data, Node 26.8.2, baseline `8f0973e37405`:

| Functional shutdown proof | Before | With subreaper fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Twelve active runs, managed SIGTERM | Exit 1 after 7,774 / 7,893 ms | Exit 0 after 789 ms |
| Session shutdown work | 424 / 538 ms | 471 ms |
| Git / Node child extinction | Broker group cleanup timed out | Passed |

These are observed functional-test timings, not a performance benchmark. The workload includes held provider streams, nested delivery, subagents, a parent lifecycle wake, real exec/Git child work, and interrupted provisioning.

- New native regression: red on the unchanged owner because the adopted child remained unreaped while the root was alive; green with the fix, preserving root exit code 37.
- Expanded `test/gateway-restart-abort-settlement.e2e.test.ts`: passed, including the under-five-second and child-extinction assertions.
- Existing process shutdown/recovery fixture passed on baseline and again with the fixed owner (62.01 s). Managed SIGTERM exited cleanly in 826 ms; raw SIGTERM took 20.81 s including its configured 20 s drain. Exactly-once history, five interrupted sessions, explicit Stop, reset authority, and another restart/SIGKILL during recovery all passed.
- `src/gateway/server-close.test.ts`: all 63 tests passed. Its diagnostic regression was red before the trace change and green afterward, while retained writes continued blocking close.
- Changed-file formatting/lint and diff checks passed. Independent Codex reviews of the complete production changes and final mixed regression found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Coverage gaps: no code-mode-specific or cron-nested workload in this fixture; no production restart performed; the original 84-second retained-effect owner remains unidentified. The runtime proof used baseline plus the subreaper fix; the additional trace-only change has focused close-handler coverage.

The change removes one Gateway lifecycle and adds one Chromium lifecycle. It adds no UI build or preview startup. Production and startup bundles are unchanged. No shard-weight change: real-Gateway placement uses audited parallel eligibility, not numeric E2E timing weights.

The separate focused fixture repair #178716 is merged and included through a normal merge of main. The replacement head is `8ef7f85874ce2e0c917e816abed227e6de14b4eb`; its real PR diff remains one test file.

## Evidence

Acceptance requires all four unchanged behavioral cases passing plus improved full-file timing against recent main. Failed-run timing is excluded from gain claims; owning-shard elapsed will be reported separately.

| Metric | Before | Candidate / after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Latest full main file / body | 121.614 / 110.864 s | Pending repaired-head CI |
| Earlier full main file | 101.786 s | Pending repaired-head CI |

| Cases | 4 | 4 |
| Static assertion chains / asymmetric matchers | 27 / 2 | 27 / 2 |

Full PR CI is the runtime proof; no speed gain claimed yet. Solid production refactor-checklist counts unchanged.

The full run [39493594211](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39493594211) passed all 14 UI jobs, but failed the speed criterion against newer unchanged-source scheduled main [39484133203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39484133203): file 96.115 → 106.490 s, body 87.650 → 92.977 s, and collection 8.454 → 13.492 s. The auto request merged before that acceptance check completed. No speed gain is claimed. [Rollback #178831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178831) restores the exact parent file and all four original cases, assertions and captures.
