prs.title: refactor(core): remove unused private helper arguments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal helpers still exposed cancellation, dependency, clock and limit arguments
that no production caller supplied. Tests kept those alternate paths alive even
though runtime always selected the same behavior.

## What changed

Remove unused wrapper arguments and inline the actual defaults across transcript
readers, worker artifact transfer, Canvas widgets, session preparation and a few
small core helpers. Tests use existing module spies or the real fixed boundary
instead of production-only test injection.

This is the core/packages area of the original 83-path private-argument family, split from
the extension area to keep CI attribution bounded. Net production reduction:
143 lines across 24 production files (50 paths including tests/support/baseline). Already
landed UI changes are excluded. No config keys, CLI flags, public SDK or Gateway
protocol fields, persisted shapes, schema, retention or permission policy change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Transcript scanning keeps streaming, 64 KiB reverse chunks, UTF-8 framing and
  iterator cleanup. Unused chunk overrides/clamping and never-supplied cancellation
  disappear. The original #54296 memory-bound repair remains; tests now exercise
  the real chunk boundary and consumer early-break cleanup.
- FIFO reservations no longer accept a signal no production waiter passed, nor
  return an unread boolean. Ordering, mixed-key exclusion, idempotent release and
  restart/close settlement stay unchanged; cancellation of a hypothetical future
  waiter is no longer offered by this private interface.
- Workspace wrappers lose four unsupplied signals. Completed responsiveness and
  batching work (#147626, #150057) remains: actual lower worker cancellation,
  security/effect authority, digests, resource bounds and accepted cleanup stay.
- Session-source preparation loses its unsupplied signal/race wrapper, not its
  shared preparation, failure recovery, path watches or current-source check.
- Artifact transfer uses the existing secure-token owner and real clock instead
  of test-only overrides. Bearer validation, expiry, live authorization, serving
  limits, revocation and transfer settlement remain.
- Canvas uses the existing state and Gateway owners, fixed HTML limit and existing
  32-document scope bound. No caller selected a different bound; CSP, alias/link
  refusal, report durability, grants and partial-failure behavior remain.
- Private transcript export/notes/utterance wrappers, delivery target forwarding,
  thread lookup and credential collection lose unused argument alternatives; the
  lower owners' real modes and public contracts stay intact.
- Test-only greeting planner, Funnel exec and clock options
  use their existing real owners. Inference authority, Funnel route validation,
  waveform evidence and terminal-result retention remain. The separate Git-path
  platform cut is excluded because PR tooling imports that signature.

These are caller-contract cuts, not a claim that the underlying delivery,
authorization, durability or concurrency repairs were speculative. Phase E's
standalone session memory backend and all its machinery/tests are untouched.

## Evidence

Per-owner focused tests, native typechecks and fresh independent reviews passed
before assembling this area. Retained proof includes transcript streaming and
library/store readers; FIFO/delivery ordering; Canvas document/widget/presenter/
report/session behavior; artifact transfer and installer paths; context/templates/
BTW parsing; wizard retention; waveform verification; greeting and Funnel behavior.

Latest workspace proof: four selected manifest adapter/cancellation cases plus
all 43 reconciliation/publication/checkpoint cases passed. Five unchanged
maximum-size manifest cases were not selected locally; hosted CI owns them.
Targeted native graphs and typed touched-path lint passed. No new runtime import
edge was added; the existing zero-cycle proof is retained. Local proof is serial,
isolated and limited to focused tests; no broad build/E2E claim.

Original-head area integration passed: the native targeted 51-root typecheck, typed lint
of all 51 touched paths, all 33 lint-suppression/import-closure cases, zero runtime
cycles, zero Madge cycles, formatting and `git diff --check`. Each transplanted
file is byte-identical to its independently reviewed collector version, and no
owner changed upstream between those reviewed versions and this area's base.
Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad landing gate; no hosted-CI success is
claimed at publication time.

CI repair: the assertion-safety job correctly required deleting the stale
`transcript-stream.ts` baseline row (zero assertions now, previously one). That
shrink-only repair changes no runtime or test behavior. The UI hover-preview
navigation failure reaches only the retry clamp and fast-test environment hunks;
both files are restored byte-identically to current main under campaign rule 8,
with those two cleanup hunks reserved for a parked branch. Local browser E2E is
outside this lane's proof budget. All other reviewed cleanup remains.

The old Node shard's five Windows lifecycle failures are inherited from the
tested merge baseline, not this PR: serial focused replay passed all five on
`aef3bf54246b`, then failed all five with the exact CI signatures on its actual
baseline `6a6ba1da8dcb`. The untouched fixture has the same SHA-256 in both trees.
Baseline #178624 (`00cb4b3c512e`) moved enabled-state mutations to PowerShell COM;
this fixture still intercepts only `schtasks` through `runCommandWithTimeout`,
so its expected disable/enable effects never occur. This evidence does not claim
the main-side fixture is fixed. No test expectations, skips, retries or timeouts
were changed. New exact-head CI remains the broad gate after the repair push.

prs.title: fix: warn when utility models disable session assessments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #175646: a selected utility model can fail repeatedly and silently stop session-observer assessments while chat continues. Thanks to @xtimor for the report and reproductions.

## User Impact

Known CLI tool-cap mismatches now warn during config validation, Doctor, and status. Read-only JSON status exposes a generic corrective warning without private configuration details. When repeated failures stop observer assessments, the existing live notice surface shows one warning for that run, naming the resolved model and suggesting a capable utility model or `utilityModel.fallbacks`. Private aliases and auth-profile suffixes stay out of the notice. Per-agent warning paths preserve the authored configuration key, including its case. Manifest model aliases and explicitly pinned CLI auth profiles receive the same capability warning as their resolved route.

Explicit routing remains selected, the next run tries again, and model-free activity remains available. No new configuration, schema, or migration. Notices use the existing live surface, not a persistent alert history.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status owner shares the exact-tool-cap predicate with CLI preparation and resolves explicit primary/fallback routes using existing configuration and descriptor owners. It reuses one selected manifest metadata view and the existing synchronous roster batch, avoiding repeated discovery and roster scans. The existing profile-to-CLI mapper is shared from the CLI-backend owner, without reading credential stores or changing runtime-pin precedence. The observer emits through existing run-owned notice events at its existing failure cutoff; its disable/retire lifecycle supplies deduplication. There is no new cache, state, or notification mechanism.

Production: **+262/-44** lines; tests: **+456/-19**; docs: **+12/-0**; wrapper inventory: **+14/-0**. Remaining production growth is the diagnostic collector and consumer plumbing. The profile mapper moved out of its previous module instead of duplicating routing policy; no unrelated deletion was added to meet a line quota. No model-facing prompt/tool change: token delta **0**.

## Evidence

Proof ran locally on macOS arm64 with isolated state/config and ports. The operator Gateway and shared model servers were untouched.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Real Gateway, separate chat and failing utility fixtures | Four invalid observer replies. Before: log-only cutoff, zero notices, chat completed in 41.90s. After: exactly one model/recovery notice, chat completed in 43.57s. |
| Capable utility control | Four observer digests, zero notices, completed chat. |
| Notice privacy through real Gateway | Identical synthetic alias/profile configuration: before the privacy repair, one notice exposed both names (42.42s); after, one notice showed only `fixture/utility-broken` (42.20s). Replay after main integration passed again in 42.193s. Chat completed after 14 tools. This case exercises preparation failure before utility inference. The final notice-label follow-up also uses the selected manifest metadata; its paired real Gateway proof is described below. |
| Real local model control | `pnpm openclaw --profile utility-degradation agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:ollama-control --model ollama/qwen2.5:7b --message 'Reply exactly LOCAL_MODEL_OK. Do not use tools.' --thinking off --timeout 120 --json` returned `LOCAL_MODEL_OK`, provider `ollama`, model `qwen2.5:7b`, no reroute; 42.58s CLI wall. |
| Real CLI diagnostics | Authored-key `config validate --json` accepted the explicit route and returned exactly one warning at the authored `agents.entries.Worker.utilityModel` path in 2.852s; Doctor warned without replacement (58.18s), text status warned (21.78s), and online JSON status returned exactly one redacted warning with `collection.source=gateway` (6.76s). |
| Final manifest-only notice label | Same config bytes and real Gateway flow: before, one notice exposed `fixture/private-manifest-alias` (42.557s); after, one notice names only `fixture/utility-broken` (41.717s). Both chats completed 14 tools. Two actual CLI exact-cap preparation failures and zero utility inference requests per run. |
| Final alias/profile CLI replay | `config validate --json` now warns once for the shipped Kimi alias (4.388s) and canonical spelling (2.723s); the alias previously returned zero warnings. A unique synthetic CLI profile warns once (3.062s), while the same route pinned to `openclaw` stays quiet (3.323s). All configs remain valid and byte-identical. No credential stores or inference were used. |
| Configured-route work budget | The acceptance rule, recorded before measurement, requires fewer than 200 roster reads for the existing 200-agent status workload, with unset and explicit utility routes. Explicit routing failed at 1,609 reads before batching; both cases now pass the unchanged budget. This is an operation-count result, not a latency claim. |
| Regression proof | Missing notices, missing config warnings, read-only status projection, private alias/profile exposure, and configured-route roster work each failed before their corresponding repair. Normal/capable controls stay quiet. |

Focused suites passed: observer **41/41, 45.95s**; config **15/15, 49.57s**; status rows **11/11, 16.89s**; summary **29/29, 31.34s**; roster **2/2, 42.15s**; runtime aliases **16/16, 48.30s**; CLI backends **11/11, 9.42s**; selected CLI exact-cap cases **6/6, 256.33s**. Cold worker preparation dominated the CLI timing. Full import-closure **19/19, 33.32s**; final canonical wrapper assertion **11.64s**. Representative native provisioning cases passed in **50.32s/75.28s**; the remaining Linux-only case is left to PR CI.

Core types passed in **3.22s**, commands test types in **2.96s**, config test types in **3.13s**, and Gateway test types in **5.48s**. Scoped lint passed; the final observer-file lint and format checks passed in **11.68s / 0.15s**. Line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, config-docs, and plugin-inventory checks passed. A full build passed before the follow-up repairs; final-head `pnpm build qaRuntime` passed in **59.63s**. Exact-head CI is recorded below.

The Gateway entry point was `pnpm openclaw --profile utility-degradation gateway run --port 19674 --bind loopback` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. A normal signed local WebSocket client subscribed and called `chat.send`; the synthetic chat executed 14 harmless `printf` steps. Sanitized Control UI screenshots are below.

Review dispositions: notice privacy, configured-roster work, authored-agent keys, static manifest aliases/profiles, and runtime manifest labels are fixed. The final repair removes an empty-metadata override in notice selection. Its supported manifest-only Gateway fixture exposed the alias before repair (42.557s), and its regression failed before repair (15.36s). Active Kimi already normalized runtime labels through its provider hook; it proved only the separate static-diagnostics gap. That public-validation regression failed before repair (19.96s); the explicit CLI-profile regression also failed while its `openclaw` pin control stayed quiet (17.54s). Automatic-route static diagnostics remain outside this fix: automatic CLI inheritance can be discarded when direct credentials are available, so descriptor-only diagnostics could falsely warn. Automatic routes still receive runtime degradation notices.

Final-head [CI run 39499722463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499722463) is **pending** as of 21:30:56 UTC: 36 completed jobs (14 passed, 22 skipped), 42 queued, zero running, zero failures, and no passing `openclaw/ci-gate`. All 42 queued Blacksmith jobs have no assigned runner and no executed steps despite satisfied upstream dependencies. This establishes a runner-admission wait; its underlying capacity cause is unknown. Landing remains blocked on the required gate. No CI rerun, remote cancellation, or capacity change was made.

Final head: `ff5d8116e1df02d1ea8dc53b2aa9331c14ad6c9e`, integrated base `503ae08b7b16f62492914c8107dcf350b962b724`. Full-branch Codex autoreview is **scoped-clean at P2 and above** on this head (**38.76s**). GitHub required a main integration; the sole conflict was adjacent status-test imports, and both utility and main's reasoning-warning paths pass.

Inherited local checks: max-lines fails on unchanged suppressions in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`; mock-export checking fails on the untouched `src/commands/doctor-database-network-storage.test.ts` mock. Both failures reproduce from exact integrated-base blobs using the owners' staged mode and a separate temporary Git index. No baseline was relaxed.

Limits: observer failure/control responses are deterministic fixtures; the real Ollama run proves CLI → Gateway → native harness → local model, not inherent model incapability. Live proof is macOS-only. No live channel or stable-version upgrade was exercised; no schema/state migration changed. The [fresh ClawSweeper request for the final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178655#issuecomment-6301780263) failed input scanning and published no code verdict. Final issue/review/inline census found no new current-head finding. The hosted review is unavailable, not clean; no scanner policy was changed.

Before: completed chat with log-only observer shutdown (synthetic data; avatar redacted).

![Before: silent observer shutdown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db518fdc-92e3-4333-8ec6-8aa1fef12a51)

After: one corrective notice and completed chat (synthetic data; avatar redacted).

prs.title: fix(plugins): don't treat the global plugin root as a workspace root
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw doctor` runs from `$HOME`, the workspace plugin root
`<home>/.openclaw/extensions` is the same physical directory as the global plugin
install root. Discovery used to scan it again as a workspace root, which could
relabel globally installed external plugins and drop their install-record trust.
Main merged the production repair in
[#178724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178724) (`8cf7e492c5e1`).

This PR keeps only the missing **negative-provenance** regression: an untracked
package or a `source: "path"` package in that overlapping directory must remain
untrusted, so it can never reach the Doctor health-API execution boundary. The
production guard is not duplicated here.

## What this PR now contains

Main already merged the equivalent production repair in
[#178724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178724) (`8cf7e492c5e1`).
This branch has been merged with current main and now keeps **only the missing
regression coverage**: the negative-provenance cases that the merged acceptance
test does not cover. `src/plugins/discovery.ts` matches main; the production guard
is not duplicated here.

## Why this test is distinct

Main's `discovery-checkout.test.ts` covers official-install acceptance when the
workspace is home/state. It does not cover what the shared-root skip must **not**
do: turn an unverified package in that overlapping directory into an official one.

`keeps overlapping-root installs untrusted without official install provenance`
(added to `src/plugins/discovery.test.ts`) puts the recovery workspace and the
global extension root in the same physical directory (`$HOME` /
`$HOME/.openclaw/extensions`) and checks two forbidden provenance cases:

- an untracked package with no install record → `trust.reason: "record-missing"`
- a `source: "path"` record → `trust.reason: "origin-path"`

For both, discovery must return exactly one `origin: "global"` candidate, and the
manifest registry must not mark it `trustedOfficialInstall`. This pins the
invariant that only a matching install record — not the shared-root scan decision
— grants official trust, so an unverified overlapping package can never reach the
Doctor health-API execution boundary.

## Evidence

The test passes against main's merged guard (`f1a05b0de`):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/discovery.test.ts \
  -t "keeps overlapping-root installs untrusted without official install provenance"
# 1 passed | 49 skipped
```

Before the merge, the same behavior was exercised end to end through the built
shipped CLI (`node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json`, `OpenClaw 2026.10.5`) with
an isolated `$HOME` and a seeded install ledger. That head's production guard is
now on main, but the final-effect evidence remains valid for the test's invariant:

| Case (cwd) | Checks | Codex finding | `api.js` evaluated |
|---|---:|---|---|
| official `clawhub:@openclaw/codex`, cwd `$HOME` | 40 | none | yes |
| official `clawhub:@openclaw/codex`, cwd distinct dir | 40 | none | yes |
| untracked package, cwd `$HOME` | 39 | `core/doctor/codex-session-routes` | no |
| `source: "path"` record, cwd `$HOME` | 39 | `core/doctor/codex-session-routes` | no |

The rejected runs reproduced the reported warning exactly and never imported
`api.js`:

```json
{
  "checkId": "core/doctor/codex-session-routes",
  "severity": "warning",
  "message": "Plugin \"codex\" is unavailable: The selected Codex plugin is not a bundled or verified official installation. ...",
  "source": "codex"
}
```

Config and plugin file SHA-256 were identical before and after every run.

## Checks

```
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental
OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json \
  src/plugins/discovery.ts src/plugins/discovery.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/plugins/discovery.test.ts
```

All pass. `src/plugins/discovery.ts` is byte-identical to upstream `main`
(`f1a05b0de`), so the production behavior is main's merged guard.

No local E2E, app build or parity run under the campaign's compute budget. No production or visual changes; no screenshot changes. Startup JS/CSS unchanged. No dependencies or leases. Touched test/helper LOC: **541 → 542** (+6/-5). Solid checklist: production files changed 0; production effect/listener/DOM-query/flush/owner counts unchanged.

**Not included:** changes to the migration receipt schema, new config surfaces, or behavior changes for non-terminal receipts.

prs.title: fix(doctor): reuse verified auth migration archives
prs.body:
Closes #176062

## What Problem This Solves

When a byte-identical legacy auth-profile source reappeared after its terminal migration receipt had already been recorded, Doctor created another `.migrated-<stamp>-<uuid>` archive on every run. Repeated regeneration therefore grew the archive directory without bound and repeated the same archival work.

- Problem: the terminal-receipt branch checked only the receipt status, then unconditionally called `archiveAuthProfileMigrationSource` with a newly generated UUID destination.
- Solution: read the archive path recorded by the terminal receipt, verify that the reappeared source and the recorded archive are both readable and match the receipt's source hash, then remove the redundant source without creating another archive.
- What changed: the terminal archive inspection now returns its verification state and recorded path; the Doctor caller reuses only a fully verified archive. Missing, unreadable, malformed, or hash-mismatched archives fall back to the existing re-archive path.
- What did NOT change: terminal receipt ownership, credential import semantics, source locks, recovery behavior, archive naming, and the rule that an unverified source must never be deleted without a surviving copy.

## User Impact

Repeated `openclaw doctor --fix` runs no longer accumulate duplicate `.migrated-*` files when an external writer recreates the same legacy source. If the recorded archive cannot prove it contains the exact source bytes, Doctor preserves recoverability by re-archiving instead of deleting the reappeared source.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receipt already records the archive path and source SHA-256, so the idempotency decision belongs in the receipt owner and can be made without replaying credentials.

- The source key includes the resolved path and source bytes, so an identical reappearance selects the same terminal receipt.
- Verification reads both files and requires both hashes to equal the receipt hash; path existence alone is insufficient.
- A recorded path equal to the source path is rejected because removing the source would not leave a surviving archive.
- The existing fallback remains responsible for producing a fresh archive when validation fails, which keeps the missing/unreadable/tampered cases recoverable.

## Evidence

The new regression first reproduced the original defect against unchanged production code: after migration, recreating identical source bytes produced a second archive.

```text
FAIL src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.test.ts
AssertionError: expected [ ...(2) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]
  Received includes the original archive and a newly minted `.migrated-*` file
```

After the fix, the final focused test run covers the successful reuse path plus missing, unreadable, and mismatched archive fallbacks:

```text
$ pnpm test src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-auth-migration-receipts.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-auth-source-owner.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.reappeared-source.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       63 passed (63)
Duration    164.70s
```

Additional checks passed:

```text
$ pnpm tsgo:core
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json --incremental
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>
$ pnpm check:import-cycles            # 0 runtime value cycles
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base origin/main
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <changed files>
$ git diff --check
```

`pnpm check:changed` was also run. Its changed-file line-cap check now passes; the command still stops on two repo-wide blockers already present on `main` and unrelated to these files: missing max-lines baseline entries for three untouched UI files, and the existing core test graph root-budget advisory (`gateway-root: 730`, `infra: 740`).

## Shipped CLI and latest-stable compatibility (2026.10.5)

Verified with isolated synthetic HOME/state; no live OpenClaw data or provider credential was used. This supersedes the earlier `2026.10.4` run and now starts from npm `latest` at the time of writing.

Upgrade source: published `openclaw@2026.10.5` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)`) created the legacy `agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json`, imported it into SQLite, recorded a completed terminal receipt, and produced one `.migrated-*` archive. The exact source bytes were then recreated and the PR-head CLI ran on that same state:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
...
Removed a previously migrated legacy auth source because its existing archive was verified
...
Doctor complete.
```

- Preserved settings: `gateway.port=19123`, `gateway.mode=local`, `gateway.auth.mode=token`, and the configured workspace were unchanged. The complete config SHA-256 before/after candidate was `f28d00d69e2f4c983793c4f3b92539347c8485c7254e46da43b0c5731d8023e5` on both sides.
- Preserved credential: `openai:default` remained an API-key profile in `config_machine_state.authProfiles.store`; the store SHA-256 stayed `6004fec2578a6950887295b8cd6eba915cdfa80b7c5222ff9945b61120e3023e`.
- Preserved receipt and bytes: the receipt remained `completed` with `removed_source=1`, one archive remained, the source was absent, and the archive still matched the original source SHA-256 (`d976e902de968a89ff6217e271d641b1b9765b83555ac11b01b7410cbec7db1f`). The receipt retained the same source path/hash and recorded archive path.

Missing-archive fallback used a second isolated state from the same published `2026.10.5` package. Its recorded archive was moved out of the state, the identical source was recreated, and the candidate produced:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
...
Archived a previously migrated legacy auth source without replaying credentials
...
Doctor complete.
```

After recovery: source absent, one replacement archive whose bytes match the source SHA-256 (`d976e902...`), and the credential store hash remains `6004fec2...`. The ledger retains the original archive path as terminal evidence; the unavailable-archive fallback therefore remains recoverable rather than deleting source bytes.

The candidate identifies itself as `2026.10.4 (6cc959b)`, older than npm `latest` `2026.10.5`. This proves compatibility from a real latest-stable config/state into this candidate; it is not described as a version-number increase.

Focused rerun after the proof:

```text
    src/commands/doctor-auth-migration-receipts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       11 passed (11)
```

Scope: this validates one isolated local upgrade and Doctor recurrence; no live fleet recurrence was executed.

prs.title: fix(doctor): stop duplicating reappeared auth-profile archives
prs.body:
Fixes #176062.

Supersedes #176132 and #176341, thanks @xiaopan-xydt and @patelmm79.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor creates another `.migrated-*` archive whenever an external writer recreates an identical, already-migrated auth-profile source. Repeated repairs accumulate duplicate credential archives indefinitely.

## User Impact

Repeated Doctor repairs reuse a verified archive and remove the redundant source without replaying credentials. Changed content still follows the normal migration flow. Missing, corrupt, unreadable, and non-file archives never justify deleting the only intact copy.

This also applies to update-time Doctor. There are no schema, dependency, CLI, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receipt owner now handles the complete terminal-source operation. It looks for a regular sibling archive with the same SHA-256, rechecks the current source under the existing source lock, and only then removes that source. Otherwise, it uses the existing verified archival path. Looking beyond the originally recorded path also reuses replacement archives after an original archive is lost, without rewriting terminal receipts.

The old caller-side wrapper and boolean receipt query are replaced by one owner operation. Production delta: +42/-26, net +16 lines; tests: +123/-6, net +117; documentation: +2. The remaining growth is the verified-copy check and safe fallback; no additional state or abstraction was introduced.

The cross-lane checks also exposed an intermittent invalid-config failure in the security test fixture. That suite explicitly substitutes the core-only secret registry, but its fixture used a Telegram-owned token field. It now uses the core `gateway.auth.token` field with the same three shorthand/reference/plaintext assertions, removing the unmodeled plugin dependency.

Release-note context: Doctor no longer accumulates duplicate auth-profile archives when identical legacy sources reappear; different bytes remain recoverable. Thanks @xiaopan-xydt and @patelmm79.

## Evidence

- Regression on unchanged base: 6 failed / 1 passed; identical sources created a second archive, and replacement archives were duplicated on the next recurrence.
- Fixed regression: 7 passed. Covers three identical recurrences for completed and archived-unparsed sources; missing, corrupt, directory, and symlink archive cases; changed-content import without replacing existing SQLite credentials. File wall time 94.17s, approximately 22s test time; compilation dominated the rest.
- Core type check, focused test type check, focused oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge passed (0 cycles).
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

- Real CLI compatibility: installed published `openclaw@2026.10.5` in an isolated directory, ran its Doctor to create the terminal receipt, then restored the same source before each of three candidate runs:

  ```text
  pnpm openclaw --profile l1741-stable doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
  runs 1–3: exit=0, archives=1, source_removed=true,
            archive_bytes_unchanged=true, state_unchanged=true
  ```

  HOME and OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR were isolated under the worktree. `state_unchanged` compares the auth-store hash, terminal receipt, configured port, and workspace with the published-release result. All runs reported `Doctor complete`. This covers Doctor compatibility and recurrence, not a full package-update rollback. The host emitted its existing original-state snapshot staging warning for the volume ancestor; all fixture data was synthetic.

- All 19 importing sibling files now have passing final results (367 tests across the selected runs). The first pass exposed the security fixture failure above at `snapshot.valid`, before auth migration; its isolated base group passed (3 tests), confirming intermittency. prs.title: perf(sessions): remove repeated export session predicate
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Batched transcript export repeats its session filter: each bounded OR arm names its session, then an outer IN binds and checks those sessions again.

## User Impact

Transcript exports do less predicate and binding work while returning the same ordered rows. Per-request admission bounds, incremental sequence ranges, independent projections, byte budgets, cold handling, and read transactions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete the redundant outer IN. Every row admitted by an OR range necessarily belongs to that same batch. No authority check, ordering rule, compatibility path, schema, or state owner changes; no new visibility edge is accepted. Production delta: one deleted line. Test delta: eleven added lines, one removed line.

The existing repeated-session admission test checks the parameters reaching the actual payload statement while retaining exact independent-result assertions. Two requests still execute one payload query, with at most four bindings instead of five. The regression fails on the base at the expected binding assertion. Existing sibling tests cover committed appends, rewrites, cold transitions, incremental slices, and bounded delivery.

## Query-plan evidence

A synthetic four-session, 384-row batch fits the existing 4 MiB budget. Exact ordered-row equality was checked before 31 alternating warm timing pairs at each fixture size. Bindings fall from 12 to 8. Both SQLite plans retain MULTI-INDEX OR, four indexed session/sequence range searches, and the ORDER BY temp B-tree.

| Fixture | Before median [min–max], ms | After median [min–max], ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Small | 0.295500 [0.286375–0.358500] | 0.258916 [0.247875–0.292208] |
| Large | 0.303375 [0.296791–0.483958] | 0.264708 [0.260125–0.418958] |

These are loaded-host statement observations, not Gateway latency claims. Statement and request counts are structurally unchanged.

PostgreSQL owner review approved the query after a PG 17.11 probe over two million rows and 4,000 sessions. Custom and forced-generic plans use BitmapOr with three primary-key bitmap scans without the outer IN; the IN adds the membership restriction to each index condition and a heap filter. A 128-arm probe remains indexed. Recorded planning times were 0.40 ms without versus 3.05 ms with the outer IN; these are that probe's observations, not application latency. Exact-head REVIEW-OK covers the final head below.

## Evidence

Two isolated Codex reviews completed with no actionable findings in their P0–P2 scope. The second covers the integrated delivery-helper test change; the first full-query review remains applicable because the production blob is unchanged. Final focused proof passes all 17 cases across the worker, read-hold, and export-budget suites. The regression is red on the exact base.

Final production and all 29 test typecheck lanes, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, T1/dialect ratchets, Madge (zero cycles), and export collisions pass. The Doctor mock-export ratchet passes after integrating its upstream repair. No SDK surface or update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle behavior changes in this PR.

The following static failures reproduce on the exact main base with identical findings and unchanged files:

- Max-lines suppressions: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`.
- Core test-root budgets: agents-tools 721, gateway-root 724, infra 725, plugins-platform 727 against 720.
- Knip production: `extensions/agentsapi/config.ts: DEFAULT_NATIVE_TOOLS` plus 15 exports in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-{media,process,session}.ts`. Full-tree: `src/boards/board-notices.ts: resetBoardEventNoticeStateForTest`. Scripts: zero findings. Exact-base and candidate finding sets are equal; zero new findings.

No limits, baselines, or unrelated source files were changed.

## Gateway count non-regression

Final measured head: `cf6b50fc5f9ae1776567fab5c9ffbb542e2755c9`; main base: `c909114f55fc5889076bf4fbbb61f6ab32bf8146`. Three alternating M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3 pairs use frozen harness v3.1 with its existing zero-connected-idle option on both arms. All turns, spawn, cron, compaction, five-second settle, restart, and shutdown remain. All six arms pass without retries at matching Node 24.22.0 / SQLite 3.54.0 and frozen harness hashes. This is not the full 300-second-idle workload.

SQL / requests / MAIN, median [min–max]. Workload/phase cells have three samples per side; causal warm cells have 30 turns.

| Scope | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whole workload | 2901 [2893–2923] / 755 [754–756] / 98 [98–98] | 2897 [2879–2926] / 755 [750–756] / 98 [98–98] |
| Compaction + settle + idle | 277 [277–278] / 46 [46–46] / 0 [0–0] | 277 [277–277] / 46 [46–46] / 0 [0–0] |
| Warm causal turns | 46 [46–53] / 11 [11–13] / 0 [0–0] | 46 [46–53] / 11 [11–13] / 0 [0–0] |
| `session-entries` | 8 [8–8] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] | 8 [8–8] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] |
| `transcript-stats` | 4 [4–4] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] | 4 [4–4] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] |
| `session.actor.read` | 10 [10–10] / 3 [3–3] / 0 [0–0] | 10 [10–10] / 3 [3–3] / 0 [0–0] |

Every Gateway trace executes one export payload query in compaction/settle: the base has the outer IN and 12 parameters; the candidate has no outer IN and 8. The owner remains exactly 8 SQL / 1 request in every arm.

- `NO_REQUEST / AsyncWorkScope.enter`: +1 / +0 / +0.

CI is not described as all green.

The coordinator explicitly approved landing this head past unassigned test shards, conditioned on running every test file that directly imports or mocks the transcript-read module. That condition is covered by the local importer proof below. The E2E runtime build, production and all 29 test type lanes, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, T1/dialect, Madge and export-collision proof are complete; exact-base static attribution is described above. Six alternating Gateway workloads exercise the changed statement end to end.

The resumed ordinary batch passes 520 cases across 24 files, including the 245-case E2E suite. The E2E runtime build also passes. Test runtime remains the repository-pinned Bun; HOME and TMPDIR stayed on the internal disk for PostgreSQL staging.

prs.title: docs(cli): document ASCII prompt markers for screen readers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Screen reader users can't tell which option is focused in interactive CLI prompts, because the cursor marker (`●`) and the other options (`○`) are announced the same way (for example, as "circle").

## User Impact

User impact: blind and low-vision users on Linux can make OpenClaw's select and multi-select prompts readable by ear with a one-line shell alias, without changing `TERM` for the rest of their terminal session.

## Why This Change Was Made

`@clack/prompts` already falls back to ASCII markers (`>`, `[+]`, `[ ]`) when `TERM=linux` on non-Windows platforms. This PR documents that existing behavior in the CLI reference, right after the color palette section, so screen reader users can find it. Docs only; no code changes.

The section relies on the Unicode detection in the pinned `@clack/prompts` 1.8.1. If a future upgrade changes that detection, this section should be revisited. A dedicated accessibility option could replace it later.

## Evidence

- Tested by the PR author, who is blind, using the NVDA screen reader over SSH to a Linux host: with `TERM=linux openclaw`, the focused option in interactive menus is announced as `>`, so it can be identified by ear. Without it, every option is announced as "circle".
- Confirmed the fallback in `node_modules/@clack/prompts/dist/index.mjs` (`isUnicodeSupported()` and the `unicodeOr()` symbol table) for the pinned `@clack/prompts` 1.8.1.
- The bash/zsh alias and the fish function were both tested on a live shell (fish 4.2.1) with a stub executable: the stub confirms it runs with `TERM=linux`, receives the forwarded arguments, and does not recurse into the wrapper.

prs.title: fix(codex): restore scheduled apps when native defaults deny access
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled runs losing all tools for an admitted app when native configuration disables apps by default and relies on per-thread admission.

## User Impact

Scheduled runs can use admitted app tools while explicit native app/tool denials, approval rules, and captured authority limits remain enforced. This targets the October branch; live deployment and recovery are not yet verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduled transform was reapplying native deny defaults after admission, producing enabled apps with every tool explicitly disabled. Use admitted app policy only as defaults for absent native fields, preserving explicit native settings and the existing authority intersection.

## Evidence

- Both new regression cases fail before the fix and pass afterward, covering captured-cap and current-owner-default execution.
- 147 scheduled-authority and sibling admission tests pass. After splitting the fixture for the existing file-size limit, all 62 scheduled-policy tests pass again.
- Final local regression shard: 62 tests across two files in 24.72s wrapper wall time (21.91s Vitest duration), including compiler-cache rebuild. Separate per-file and CI timings are unavailable.
- Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and independent Auto Review pass with no P0–P2 findings.

prs.title: docs(gateway): explain how to check a session after a create timeout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If the Gateway creates a session but its reply is lost, a caller using `--json` sees the same timeout as a caller that never sent the request. Repeating `sessions.create` is not a safe way to find out which happened.

Show callers how to choose a fresh session key before the create and look up that key with `sessions.resolve` afterward. A match establishes that the session exists, not that a particular call created it or that its first turn ran. One missing result does not prove the original request stopped.

## Evidence

- Reproduced a lost reply in an isolated Gateway: let one create complete, withheld its successful response, then recovered the same session with read-only access, including after a Gateway restart. Did not send a second create.
- Checked the command and its interpretation against the current CLI, the Gateway's deadline test, and the session-resolution contract. The controlled run above used an earlier packaged Gateway; it is not a deployment or latency claim.
- The changed page passed the repository formatter and `git diff --check`. Only documentation changes; no CLI output or retry behavior changes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): session titles show the model's explanation instead of the title
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automatic dashboard session titles show the title model's own explanation ("Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, nic…") or a label prefix ("Session title: …", "Titel: …") when the first message is vague, e.g. "Explain whether this could be useful for us too" or "What do you think about this?".

## User Impact

User impact: new dashboard, iOS and node chats get the title the model actually proposed instead of a cut-off explanation sentence or a "Title:"-style prefix. Saved titles also name worktree branches, so the same fix applies there.

Affected: setups where titles run on the Claude CLI runtime with the automatic utility model (Haiku 5.5, since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168603 ), i.e. no explicit `agents.defaults.utilityModel`. Measured on an isolated Gateway with 15 first messages × 5 runs: 13 of 75 titles were unusable on 2026.10.5, 9 of them in the two shapes this PR targets. Other utility models may produce the same shapes; I only measured Haiku.

## Why This Change Was Made

The title model often answers in two parts: a sentence about its task, a blank line, then the title. Two things in the existing owner dropped the title:

1. `runLabelAttempts` cut the answer to the 60-character title cap *before* calling the caller's `normalizeLabel`, so the dashboard normalizer only ever saw the start of the explanation.
2. `normalizeDashboardSessionTitle` took the first line and only stripped an English `title:` prefix.

Now the generator normalizes the whole visible answer and truncates afterwards. The dashboard normalizer skips lines ending with `:` (they introduce the next line), prefers a line the model introduced as the title, otherwise keeps the first line — unless that first line is over the title budget and contains a later line exactly as a quoted span (`… a fitting title is "X".\n\nX`; open and matching close quote directly around the text, using the quote pairs of the existing wrapper removal from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167584 , now a shared constant) —, strips a closed set of title introductions ("Title:", "Session title:", "Conversation title:", "Concise title for this session:", "Label:", "Titel:", "Sitzungstitel:", "Richtiger Titel:" …) and unwraps a title wrapped in `**bold**`. Topics that merely contain these words stay intact (`Fix button label: Save changes`, `Fix subtitle parsing: "Invalid cue"`, `PR 177777: Proof for the title fix`). Single-line outputs keep today's behavior, except that a line ending in `:` is rejected so the existing fallback chain (regular model, then slug) runs.

| | Production | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Lines | +58 / −27 (2 files; includes moving the existing quote-pair table to module scope) | +77 (1 file) |

No prompt change. `normalizeLabel` has one caller (`src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.ts`).

## Evidence

**Live, isolated Gateway** (loopback, own state, agent on `claude-cli`, utility model resolved automatically to `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` via Claude CLI), driver `gateway call sessions.title.prepare`, same 15 messages (10 vague, 5 clear controls, German and English), 5 runs each. Before = installed 2026.10.5 package, after = package copy of this branch's build (`d3249a9` before review round 1, `3864f35` after round 1). The live runs were not repeated for `0311964`: review round 3 only tightens which later line may replace the first one (exact quoted span instead of plain substring), so it can only keep more first lines than `3864f35`; it is covered by the tests and the replay below. Classification of the saved title by hand from the JSONL output:

| Build | Calls (UTC, 2026-10-20) | Explanation or "Title:"-prefix instead of title | Answer instead of title | Over-long title cut at 60 chars | Model call failed (`null`) | Usable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`) | 75, 19:27–19:33 | **9** | 2 | 2 | 0 | 62 |
| `d3249a9` (before review) | 75, 20:45–20:52 | **2** | 6 | 3 | 1 | 63 |
| this PR (`3864f35`) | 75, 21:29–21:35 | **2** | 1 | 3 | 0 | 69 |

Haiku varies a lot between runs, so only the targeted column is a fair comparison. Review round 1 found that the length/punctuation preamble rule in `d3249a9` could replace a long punctuated first-line title with the explanation after it; `3864f35` drops that rule. A long first line is now kept (truncated, as on `main`) unless it quotes the later line. Cost of that change: one long explanatory sentence followed by the bare title (no `Title:`, no quote) keeps the base behavior; on `3864f35` this was 1 of the 2 remaining targeted misses (`Erkennung: Die Aufgabe ist … etwas wie "Nutzen für unser Team prüfen" oder ähnlich.\n\nNutzen für uns prüfen` — the quoted phrase differs from the final line). The other one uses an introduction outside the closed list (`Ein Titel für diese Sitzung: **…**`); I kept the list closed rather than guess more phrasings. Answers instead of titles are single-line replies to the user and pass through unchanged before and after.

<details><summary>Examples (raw model output → saved title)</summary>

```text
2026.10.5
"Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, nicht die Frage zu beantworten. … Ein passender Titel wäre: „Nützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen“.\n\nNützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen"
  → "Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, nic"
"Concise title for this session: **Assessing usefulness for our team**"
  → "Concise title for this session: **Assessing usefulness for o"
"Session title: Gateway Docker persistent state volume"
  → "Session title: Gateway Docker persistent state volume"

this PR (3864f35)
"Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, … Ein passender Titel wäre: „Nützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen“.\n\nNützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen"
  → "Nützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen"
"Fix Docker startup failures on Windows. Restore volume permissions\n\nThis captures the main topic."   (review example, test row)
  → "Fix Docker startup failures on Windows. Restore volume permi"
"Generiere einen kurzen Sitzungstitel (3–6 Wörter, max. 60 Zeichen) …\n\nIch antworte auf deutsch, aber für diese Aufgabe gebe ich nur den Titel zurück.\n\nTitel: Nützlichkeit für unser Team erklären"
  → "Nützlichkeit für unser Team erklären"
"Conversation title: Checking a request"
  → "Checking a request"
```

</details>

**False positives:** replaying the old and new line/prefix selection (head `0311964`) over 227 existing dashboard titles from a real installation changed 0 of them. Over 475 raw outputs collected in all runs it changed 34: 28 unusable → usable, 5 only by trailing whitespace (trimmed afterwards anyway), 1 usable → a different usable title (the model returned two candidate lines and introduced the second with "Session title:").

**Tests** (`src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.transport.test.ts`, real OpenAI-compatible transport through `maybeGenerateDashboardSessionTitle`, asserts the persisted `displayName`): 17 new rows in the existing "persists a usable title" table — an English and a German explanation quoting the title before it (`… Ein passender Titel wäre: „X“.\n\nX`), an introduction ending in `:`, explanations before an introduced `Title:` line, `Titel:`, `Session title:`, quoted and bold titles after an introduction, an introduction without a title (falls back to the slug), and eight titles that must stay unchanged (a long title that merely contains the next line, unquoted (review round 2: `Investigate intermittent Docker startup failures caused by Permission denied\n\nPermission denied`), a long punctuated title before an explanation (review round 1), `PR 177777: …`, `Debug Docker: "Permission denied"`, `Fix subtitle parsing: …`, `Fix button label: …`, a long quoted title before a short explanation, a title before an explanation).
Counter-check: with only the two production files reset to the merge base, the 9 rows that need extraction fail and the 8 unchanged-title rows pass (41 tests, 9 failed). Against the previous head `3864f35`, only the new review-round-2 row fails (41 tests, 1 failed).

```text
pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1 (VPS, 2 CPUs, head 0311964)
src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.transport.test.ts            41 passed  106 s
src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts                      32 passed   21 s
src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.incognito.test.ts             2 passed   17 s
src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts        19 passed   22 s
src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-title-preparation.test.ts    5 passed   33 s
src/gateway/server.sessions.create.titles.test.ts                 9 passed   41 s
src/gateway/server-methods/session-discussion.test.ts             8 passed   22 s
src/commands/doctor-session-title-repair.test.ts                  6 passed   35 s
pnpm test <transport> <dashboard-session-title> <conversation-label-generator> --maxWorkers=1: 92 passed, 81 s
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` and `git diff --check` clean on the changed files. The branch merges into current `main` without conflicts; `main` has not touched these three files since the merge base.

**Gaps:** single-line answers to the user, over-long single-sentence titles, and a long explanation followed by an unquoted bare title are unchanged; they need a different signal than this normalizer has. Title phrasings outside the closed introduction list still pass through. Measured with Haiku 5.5 only.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): per-agent verboseDefault is ignored by replies, /verbose, /status and openclaw agent
prs.body:
Closes #177612

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent's `agents.entries.<id>.verboseDefault` is accepted by config and shown by the native `/verbose` menu, but that agent's replies, text `/verbose` and `/status`, and `openclaw agent` runs still use `agents.defaults.verboseDefault`.

Related: #73680 (the verbose half only; per-agent `elevatedDefault` is untouched).

## User Impact

User impact: setting `verboseDefault` on one agent now changes that agent's verbose behavior (tool summaries, tool-failure details) and what `/verbose` and `/status` report. Agents without their own value keep the global default, and a session `/verbose` override still wins.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply path already reads the agent entry for thinking and reasoning defaults, and the native command menu already reads the agent's verbose default through `resolveAgentConfig`, but the run itself read only the global default. The reply-run resolution and the `/verbose` / `/status` level resolver (also used by the plugin SDK status runtime) now read the agent entry first, and `openclaw agent` reads it through `resolveAgentConfig`, which already merges it. The mixed-message directive lane now receives the agent entry too, so a `/verbose` (or `/reasoning`) query inside a normal message reports the level the turn actually runs with; that lane had never been given the entry since per-agent defaults were added. The docs now list the per-agent key.

Not changed here (follow-ups):
- Tool-event visibility fallbacks still seed from the global default when a session or run carries no verbose level (`tui.ts`, `tui/embedded-backend.ts`, and the Gateway's `chat-history-handler.ts` / `server-chat.ts`). All four files are at or over the line cap, so the same change needs a module split first.
- The native-command `/status` fast path, the `session_status` tool, and the Control UI's client-side bare `/verbose` ignore verbose defaults entirely, the global one included.

Both lookups agree: the reply path reads the raw agent entry like the adjacent thinking and reasoning defaults, `openclaw agent` reads the merged `resolveAgentConfig` value, and both fall back to the global default for agents without an entry.

## Evidence

Proof head: `cf69415074d68c4b03fb0a084bc80c0a95d7e02e` (branch head `73bfe3762b3` adds only `main` merges; one of them adapts the added `commands/agent` case to upstream's test rewrite). The rows below were captured at `fcb33365d1a`; the only later commit rewrites one test. The upgrade run further down used the proof head.

Real Gateway, before (`main` at `7cb1ea1f8e8`) and after (this branch), same isolated setup on both: `agents.defaults.verboseDefault: "off"`, `agents.entries.ops.verboseDefault: "full"`, `main` without its own value. The model is a local Responses-API-compatible test endpoint scripted to call `read` on a missing file and then return an empty reply, so the runner sends its tool-failure warning, which includes the error only at verbose `full`. Channel rows use the repo's `qa-channel` plugin against a local QA bus, one session per conversation; chat rows use the Control UI chat path (`chat.send`).

| What | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ops` chat `/verbose` | `Current verbose level: off.` | `Current verbose level: full.` |
| `ops` chat `/status` Modes line | `think off · fast off` | `think off · fast off · verbose:full` |
| `ops` reply on the channel | `⚠️ Read failed` only | tool summary, tool output, `⚠️ Read: … failed: File not found: …` |
| `ops` channel message with text + bare `/verbose` | ack `off`, then `⚠️ Read failed` | ack `full`, then summary, output and the detailed warning |
| `main` reply on the channel (no per-agent value) | `⚠️ Read failed` | `⚠️ Read failed` |
| `ops` channel conversation after `/verbose off` | `⚠️ Read failed` | `⚠️ Read failed` |
| `openclaw agent --agent ops --json` | `requestShaping.verbose: "off"`, `⚠️ Read failed` | `"full"`, `⚠️ Read: … failed: File not found: …` |
| `openclaw agent --agent main --json` | `"off"`, `⚠️ Read failed` | `"off"`, `⚠️ Read failed` |

<details>
<summary>Channel and CLI output (state directory shown as <state>)</summary>

```text
before: main 7cb1ea1f8e8
u-ops-1 > Please read the verbose probe file.
    [isError] ⚠️ Read failed    (toolCalls: read)
u-main-1 > Please read the verbose probe file.
    [isError] ⚠️ Read failed    (toolCalls: read)

    ⚙️ Verbose logging disabled.

after: this branch

    Read: from verbose-probe/missing-file.txt    (toolCalls: read)

    [isError] ⚠️ Read: from verbose-probe/missing-file.txt failed: File not found: <state>/workspace-ops/verbose-probe/missing-file.txt.    (toolCalls: read)
```

Tests and checks:
- With only this PR's test files on `main` (`7cb1ea1f8e8`), 6 tests fail with the global value where the agent's value is expected and pass on this branch: level resolver, reply-run resolution, `openclaw agent`, and 3 `get-reply-directives-apply` rows that run the real directive handler and compare the displayed `/verbose` answer (directive-only reply, mixed-message acknowledgement) and the mixed-message `/reasoning` answer. The directive-only `/reasoning` row passes on both by design.
- Cost budget (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall / CI seconds, summed Vitest test durations in this head's CI run): `directive-handling.levels` (10 tests) 6 s / 0.06 s, `get-reply-directives-apply` (15) 11 s / 4.7 s, `get-reply-directives.target-session` (12) 9 s / 0.09 s; `agent.thinking.test-support.ts` adds one case to the unchanged `commands/agent` (59, 120 s / 110 s): 1.0 s / 1.3 s.

prs.title: fix(agents): retain requester selection for returned peer replies
prs.body:
## Local deployment checkpoint (2026-10-20)

The operator explicitly opted into a combined local deployment containing main consolidation `7605b4fc8c28a628cd4d6b9a3e63bc9f1304ce10`, reply-obligation candidate `66eea4b4ef10f196ba1640398d186884d5557cdd`, reconnect candidate `de1dfafe07c8f0762b9e5fc16d4dfc6b36a3fbeb`, and selected-requester candidate `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`, alongside existing local integrations and the separately restored saved-attempt UI work. The resulting local build is `764886a56987d82f3a3934e2dd7d6a2416ef98da`.

Operational readback confirms the exact loaded build, readiness, health, Node 24, unchanged service environment, and all 25 previously active plugins. This is a combined integration deployment, not standalone validation of each PR or security/session-owner acceptance of any extracted policy. No new business-message, native-effect, revocation or reassignment proof is inferred from operational health. The earlier isolated traces below retain their recorded revisions, scenarios and failed-collector qualifications.

## What Problem This Solves

A returned legacy peer result may need the original requester's personal-tool selection after the originating tool invocation has ended. The existing continuation retains operator source authority but deliberately removes its ambient tool caller. Reconstructing a fresh caller later can select the wrong requester or reject valid return work.

This is the personal-requester proposal extracted from [#177698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698), presented separately so its authority decision does not hold up the lifecycle consolidation.

## Proposed Behavior

Capture the requester selection while the originating caller is live. Only the legacy `replyMode: peer` return flow opts into re-entering that selection under its existing retained operator source. Completion custody follows its existing path; peer messages retain separate turns. The ended invocation's receipt and operational-run instance are not restored.

The retained source's device/Gateway lifetime, release and operator-policy checks remain. The selected person's authority is intersected with the existing caller's scopes. No schema, configuration option, dependency, storage migration or native Codex change is introduced.

## Maintainer Decision

Should accepted returned peer work be allowed to re-enter the originally selected personal-tool requester under its retained, live-checked source authority? This is a policy proposal, not inferred approval from matching profiles or session identifiers. It does not authorize reviving the ended invocation or replacing recipient execution permissions.

Recommendation: permit this bounded return path only with the original selection, live checks and the full-flow/final-effect proof below. Review it independently of #177698; that consolidation excludes this machinery.

## Evidence

### Actual returned-peer personal-tool effects

An isolated Gateway built at `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45` completed the genuine public `sessions_send` return using the built-in OpenClaw runtime and scripted inference. Configured trusted-proxy authentication established distinct synthetic Alice and Bob profiles. Bob's explicit human steering was actually accepted into Alice's original execution before the provider selected Bob through the advertised tool. The original invocation and peer ended normally. The returned result then started a distinct execution in the original Gateway session, retaining Bob and the original read/write ceiling without the ended invocation's receipt, operational run or full-permission flag.

The returned execution made three actual advertised `personal_instructions` calls: get and set on Bob's permitted agent succeeded and matched Bob's authenticated canonical readback; set on an agent permitted to Alice but forbidden to Bob returned the exact current-role error. Canonical history attributes all three tool results to that returned execution, with two successes and one error. Alice's own-file readbacks on both agents and five confined filesystem observations remained unchanged; no Bob file appeared on the forbidden agent. The returned execution ended normally with one visible final, one attributed forwarded peer row and an empty pending-input queue. Four main provider requests covered this returned tool/final cycle; background utility requests are counted separately.

The collector exited **0, qualified=true** without timeout or forced containment. Raw facts retain stale initializer fields (`status=UNRUN-unqualified`, `pass=false`); the final `bodyQualified=true` and `passed=true`, exercised assertions and joined exit0 determine qualification. Raw records were not rewritten. The Gateway exited0, all eight observed task processes exited0 and were absent afterward, clients/proxy/provider joined, and task/bootstrap state was removed. The allowlisted trace below uses fixed aliases and relative timing; raw identifiers and state remain private.

**Scope and retained failures:** the API is self-only. This proves a personal effect on an Alice-permitted/Bob-forbidden **agent**, not a foreign-profile file target API or every recipient permission. This is built-in runtime/scripted-provider evidence, not native Codex or real-model inference. Profile reassignment and source revocation are not exercised by this effect case; the separate revoked-source trace retains its own scope. No owner/security approval is inferred. Three prior effect captures remain unqualified setup failures (multi-agent ownership marker, missing private workspace, then the implicit QA workspace suffix); none reached a provider or personal-effect call. Each was preserved and corrected through the supported fixture contract, without changing production guards or permissions.

### Actual authenticated returned-peer and revocation boundaries

At source `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`, an isolated authenticated Gateway and the built-in OpenClaw runtime exercised genuine public selection: Alice and Bob became real participants; Alice selected Bob in `sessions_send`; the original and peer runs completed normally before the separate returned execution. The observed requester remained Bob with the original read/write intersection, without borrowing the ended receipt, run, or full permission. One returned main-execution request and one attributed peer history entry produced a normal final. The original positive collector exited **1** because it incorrectly required a user-role history row; the canonical display projection returns that forwarded entry as assistant. The saved raw observations were audited after the run; this is not a whole-collector pass.

A separate revoked-source capture exited **0**. A metadata-only pause held the actual prepared result before its unchanged consumer; the revocation record timestamp was 49 ms after the hold; the successful RPC confirmed persistence by 52 ms, before resumption/source refusal at 54 ms. There were zero returned main-execution requests and zero attributed peer entries. Auxiliary label inference is distinct: two positive and one revoked-case label requests also contained peer text, so this evidence makes no global zero-model-I/O claim. Gateway, provider, proxy, task state and bootstrap cleanup joined without forced containment in both captures.

This uses a scripted local provider with actual loopback provider I/O and disclosed in-memory observation of original owner code, not native Codex. Personal-tool effects, recipient execution permissions and reassignment remain unproved by these captures. Earlier failed collectors remain preserved.


The original positive collector's final history-role assertion remains a failed collector result. Its successful target observations were independently correlated against the real controller, provider, attributed history and normal terminal receipts; the negative capture passes its complete collector. No failed attempt is relabeled. The earlier authentication/omitted-explicit-steer fixture failures remain preserved as setup/admission evidence. Both cases use the actual public `chat.send` with explicit steer and advertised `sessions_send` user selection; the observation records the original successful acceptance after participant registration, and pauses the original returned preparation without replacing authorization, return values or errors.

### Selected-requester producer repair at `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`

The new actual reply-flow composition exposed a real producer mismatch: after Alice selects Bob, the retained continuation correctly holds Bob's authority, but `prepareSessionsSendReplyContext` copied Alice's plain caller origin into the outgoing `agentToolCaller`. The factory now takes requester origin from the existing canonical selected-operator resolver, with its required-origin check, while retaining the original caller's agent/session bindings. No authority fallback or new policy owner is introduced.

The composition exercises the real requester factory, canonical session readers and communication receipts, detached reply custody, A2A flow and AgentStep. A held peer returns only after the originating invocation/receipt ends. On the preceding candidate, three controls pass and the selected-Bob row fails specifically because outgoing origin says Alice. With the repair, all four cases pass: normal return, selected Bob with original read/write scope ceiling, canonical source revocation, and requester session replacement. No ended invocation, receipt or full-permission flag is restored. A separate determining-owner rollback to original upstream also reproduces the missing-requester failure; this is not a whole historical-tree execution.

The 4 composition cases, 4 retained-source cases and 7 AgentStep siblings pass (**15 total**, 62.48s canonical wrapper). Core production and owning agent-tools test types, scoped typed lint, formatting and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. The exact committed runtime build also passes (120.3s). These compositions intercept transport; the separate Gateway captures above establish their own stated runtime boundaries. No claim of Alice-only personal-tool denial, reassignment rejection or recipient execution permissions follows from these tests.


The original extracted candidate `9ec7457c42d80015ef85ca36d77bee3cafc38bdd` was based on upstream `1429fd5487b508d59b0466fb83a9618c8022f162`. Its retained-owner suite separately covers release, device revocation, Gateway replacement and selected-person scope intersection. These owner tests do not stand in for Gateway/final-effect evidence.

The proof fixtures above are synthetic. No operator Gateway or business session was changed, restarted or deployed to collect them.

## Related Work

[#162299](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162299) already separates accepted reply custody from the original invocation's lifetime. [#177296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177296) clears stale ambient caller context when starting a recipient; it does not restore the originally selected requester for this returned personal-tool path. [#177618](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177618) fixes pre-ACK run-scope binding, which stays in #177698.

## Remaining Merge Gates

- Security/session-owner acceptance of the bounded requester re-entry policy remains required. Passing checks do not grant that approval.
- Source reassignment and native Codex personal-tool effects are not claimed; the canonical source-revocation capture exercises the requested revocation alternative.
- Hosted CI and any security-sensitive-change approval remain subject to the repository's normal maintainer gates.

This PR remains **draft** while its extracted authority-policy proposal is reviewed independently of the lifecycle consolidation.

prs.title: fix(agents): human messages queue during optional completion turns
prs.body:
## Local deployment checkpoint (2026-10-20)

The operator explicitly opted into a combined local deployment containing main consolidation `7605b4fc8c28a628cd4d6b9a3e63bc9f1304ce10`, reply-obligation candidate `66eea4b4ef10f196ba1640398d186884d5557cdd`, reconnect candidate `de1dfafe07c8f0762b9e5fc16d4dfc6b36a3fbeb`, and selected-requester candidate `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`, alongside existing local integrations and the separately restored saved-attempt UI work. The resulting local build is `764886a56987d82f3a3934e2dd7d6a2416ef98da`.

Operational readback confirms the exact loaded build, readiness, health, Node 24, unchanged service environment, and all 25 previously active plugins. This is a combined integration deployment, not standalone validation of each PR or security/session-owner acceptance of any extracted policy. No new business-message, native-effect, revocation or reassignment proof is inferred from operational health. The earlier isolated traces below retain their recorded revisions, scenarios and failed-collector qualifications.

## Relationship to the consolidation

[#177698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698) at `d383dd4e9bb180d5dd880f21029ac7d586052130` extracts optional-work human reply promotion from the lifecycle consolidation. This PR remains the focused behavior proposal; it is **not superseded** by that narrowed head. The recommendation and maintainer decision below remain open. The consolidation preserves ordinary compatible human steering and leaves required human input against optional work in separate-turn custody. Its extracted positive tests and implementation remain in the published parent history for a future focused port; this standalone branch and its revision-qualified evidence are unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes human messages being queued instead of steering when a visible embedded turn is processing an optional-reply task completion.

## User Impact

Human input can join the active turn and retain its answer requirement. Private completions, stale authority, and backends that cannot promote that requirement keep their existing admission rules. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current equality guard rejects required human input against an optional completion. Simply accepting that input would leave finalization free to return no answer. The embedded runtime now advertises support for promotion and records the stronger requirement only when the input is actually accepted. Retry and finalization read that same run-owned fact; a new execution clears it. Explicit result requirements remain stronger than ordinary required replies.

Related: #175763, #175810. This covers promotion of a visible optional completion; the Codex backend producer fix in #175810 addresses a different missing-value case.

## Maintainer decision requested

Approve bounded reply-obligation promotion for compatible human input joining a visible optional embedded turn. Hidden turns, unsupported backends and current authority refusals retain their existing admission policy. This extends the previously deliberate follow-up policy; no owner approval is presumed.

## Behavior decision

The [review asks whether compatible human input may join a visible optional completion and promote its reply obligation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176245#issuecomment-6251664781). I recommend bounded promotion because the mismatch guard protects required answers. [#152786](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f2dff0dcf9cca6e11aba8cbdf35a3005027894d3) establishes that model-authored silence cannot erase the input owner's answer obligation. [#158699](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158699) retained followup when optional background turns could not honor that obligation.

This PR supplies that missing guarantee for supporting embedded sinks. [Admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/894223358d3135608c628ad133b2686914ee85b5/src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.message-injection.ts#L67) retains visibility and matching-authority checks; promotion is recorded only at actual acceptance. [Completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/894223358d3135608c628ad133b2686914ee85b5/src/agents/reply-completion.ts#L141) retains the strongest accepted requirement, including result-required, for the same execution. Rejected input does not create an obligation; unsupported or hidden turns retain followup.

Codex's [steering owner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_input.rs#L803) validates the active turn and its output-schema contract before appending input to that turn. This supports retaining the execution owner, but proves no OpenClaw optional-reply guarantee. The remaining product question is whether a separate turn is required even when actual acceptance transfers the answer obligation safely. This intentionally changes the old fallback while preserving its reason. Current public proof covers embedded acceptance and empty-final recovery; native promotion is not claimed for this public head.

## Evidence

### Current upstream integration

Current candidate `66eea4b4ef10f196ba1640398d186884d5557cdd` merges the preceding public head `1b57590afc4b3e5ba9d5e7d46b6a6f2ab8699bd7` with upstream `42a73b62bb18abd0dc6b68fca0daf50f62331f79`. The sole conflict retains the reply-promotion capability alongside upstream's referenced delivery-mode type. The shared backend-contract extraction keeps the independent human-reply fact and native predispatch persistence predicate; no consolidated adapter/accounting cutover is imported.

**75 affected checks across four files pass**, including embedded promotion, pending-question controls, stable prefixes and the controller-adapted Codex persistence regression. Core and extension production types, scoped typed lint/format, whitespace, a fresh complete P0–P2 review and the exact-candidate runtime build pass. The build retains its UI gzip-size advisory; no budget was changed. The local review is source/test evidence; the new native transport capture below supplies the previously missing ordering trace.

Upstream's declared native dependency is now **0.162.1**. Earlier native evidence and failed collectors remain at their recorded revisions and runtime versions. The new exact-head capture below closes the controller-adapted human commit-before-dispatch/exactly-once proof gap. The reply-promotion product decision remains open; that capture claims neither a local deployment nor maintainer approval.

### Exact-head native persistence-before-dispatch proof

A fresh isolated Gateway capture at `66eea4b4ef10f196ba1640398d186884d5557cdd` uses the exact built standalone source and its declared official Codex **0.162.1** app-server, without a native version override. Two genuinely authenticated synthetic profiles exercise actual controller adaptation. The actual human-input recorder is deliberately held before invoking its original implementation: no native correction dispatch or positive controller acceptance occurs while it is held. After release, the original recorder commits **6.45 ms before** the actual native `turn/steer` dispatch; its ACK and controller acceptance follow. The native consumed-input events, provider continuation and journal identify the same original native thread/turn and correction. Canonical history and the native journal each contain that correction once, with one corrected visible final and no pending inputs. No native interrupt was sent; both native processes exit normally with code 0, and task Gateway/provider/proxy/state cleanup succeeds.

This is actual Gateway/controller/recorder/official-native-client proof with scripted local inference and hash-pinned observations, not simulated native RPC. It proves this ordering and exactly-once requirement for an ordinary required human turn; **it does not prove native optional-work reply promotion**, profile reassignment, restricted model-policy changes, or answering another requester's pending question. No authority result or recorder implementation was replaced. The earlier restricted-role collector remains a failed setup, rather than being relabeled as passing evidence.

Source/build/native/observer pins and raw receipt correlations were rechecked. The outgoing allowlist received three automated privacy passes, a complete manual read, and an independent 93-check accuracy/privacy audit. Only synthetic observations and relative timings are published.
