```json
    "This capture establishes adapted-human persistence-before-native-dispatch and exactly-once transcript recording for the current standalone revision.",
    "It does not establish optional-work reply promotion, profile reassignment, restricted model-policy enforcement, or authority to answer another requester pending question.",
    "Prior failed collectors remain failed evidence. The earlier restricted-role capture never reached the native provider because its direct route could not enforce model policy; this run uses legitimate unrestricted synthetic writer roles, without replacing that guard."
  ]
}
```

</details>

### Collaborative reply-promotion repair at `cb730e6fe3ab5bb3d9112bd54134070759cf6697`

Addresses the [current P2 collaborative reply-loss finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176245#issuecomment-6251664781). The controller captures the admitted human-message fact before adapting pending-question eligibility. The embedded acceptance callback uses that fact to retain the human reply obligation, while another requester's pending question remains protected. No question, visibility, authority, or strongest-result guard is relaxed.

Both collaborative required/result-required cases fail against the prior production code: input is accepted but the expectation remains optional. They pass with the repair and assert pending-question protection, accepted obligation, missing-empty-final classification, and actual correction consumption by the original AgentSession continuation. **120 affected checks across five suites pass**. The unchanged seven-case promotion group moves into a coherent sibling test-support module to preserve the line cap without another harness or baseline exception; its 38-case owning suite passes after extraction (4.73 seconds Vitest / 24.49 seconds wrapper wall).

Core and owning test types, typed lint, formatting, line/mock/assertion ratchets, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. Final unused-import cleanup is test-only. These are synthetic owner/AgentSession regressions, not a new authenticated Gateway collaborative capture. Earlier shipped-entry evidence retains its stated revision and scope. Hosted CI and the separate human-promotion behavior decision remain outstanding. No operator Gateway was changed or restarted for that capture.

### Documentation follow-up at `44747a5a4ae7fe656ee76acb77e62ac177e827e5`

Addressed the [queue-steering documentation finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176245#issuecomment-6251664781). Visible optional completion turns may accept compatible human input in a supporting embedded runtime; only runtime acceptance promotes the required visible reply. Hidden turns, unsupported backends, and different execution routes retain followup and cancellation behavior. This is a one-paragraph documentation correction only. Production and test sources are unchanged from `6e6642ca99e5a7eb450c8f6711a0db438ed32a9b`, so the revision-qualified runtime evidence below is retained. Formatting, Markdown lint (1,359 files), MDX checks (1,381 files), whitespace and ordinary Git hooks pass. Hosted CI is red only on an inherited UI absolute-budget breach: the base and candidate both measure 1,050,200 B against a 1,050,000 B limit, with zero added bytes and identical UI/build/dependency trees ([exact-head failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39211232534/job/117925292836)). The other completed checks, including docs, pass. The fresh exact-head review has no findings and resolves the documentation comment; the maintainer behavior decision remains open.

### Earlier upstream integration at `03ed0db`

Head `03ed0dbcd3923f6e0760e594ba0c14aff5f3129d` merges upstream `9509fc22` to repair the named inherited Control UI performance gate. This adopts the complete upstream boot-work repair (#177117), preserving both histories. No local UI feature, budget, baseline or dependency exception was introduced; the reply-promotion proposal is unchanged.

**The canonical UI performance comparison now passes** against pinned upstream with the same installed toolchain. New Session boot JavaScript is **1,026,041 gzip bytes** against the unchanged **1,050,000-byte cap** (base 1,025,701 bytes; +340 bytes). The earlier head measured 1,050,200 bytes and failed. Precompressed assets and all absolute/growth budgets pass; no suggestion to lower an unrelated baseline was applied.

**150 affected checks pass in four suites** (50.9 seconds canonical wrapper wall time): stream acceptance, ask-user forwarding, reply registry and source-reply completion. Core and four owning test type graphs, scoped typed lint, formatting, line-cap and whitespace checks pass. Integration is an automatic merge with no manual source edits; the prior independent review remains qualified to its original revision. Exact-head CI and hosted rereview are requested. Historical authenticated runtime evidence below retains its original source qualification.

The explicit maintainer decision on human reply-obligation promotion remains open. No operator Gateway was changed or restarted for that capture.

### Historical boundary evidence

Earlier head `894223358d3135608c628ad133b2686914ee85b5` fixes the four CI failures caused by the ask-user helper's obsolete nine-argument assertion. It now checks exactly one delivery and exact forwarded text/images while allowing the new acceptance callback. Production is byte-identical to `139b7a08a03d48172c88ae860636bda39933475a`, whose exact built runtime was used for the capture below.

- **Causal pre-fix proof:** with unchanged current regression cases and the twelve production files restored to exact base `ca5ac6f5b69aa8704b653fade36e2fa59937c7fb`, the required/result-required admission cases fail at the actual acceptance assertion; three rejection controls pass. All production bytes were restored before current checks. The base run took 44.1 seconds wall / 13.5 seconds Vitest.
- **Current focused proof:** 35 stream and 29 ask-user cases pass (64 total; 55.4 seconds wrapper wall). The repaired ask-user owner takes 10.3 seconds Vitest. Targeted types, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace checks and a fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. Earlier direct-completion and authority-sibling evidence remains scoped to its original revision; current broad checks belong to PR CI.
- **Actual shipped Gateway proof:** a connected synthetic owner calls the built authenticated `agent` handler, then sends required human input through unchanged `chat.send` while the original provider response is held. The actual admission guard observes matching authority and optional→required promotion support. The real AgentSession acceptance sink records the stronger requirement before the provider is released. The human marker reaches the original continuation's next model request. An empty assistant final triggers actual required-reply recovery; the third provider request yields exactly one final on the original run, and terminal metadata reports `required`.
- **Fixture qualification:** a task-only in-memory loader selects optional host policy at the existing authenticated handler's `startTurn` call. Authorization, preflight/current authority, steering, runtime, and finalization execute unchanged. The Responses wire is scripted on an isolated local provider; this is an embedded-runtime proof, not an external model-service or actual child-completion lifecycle claim. The earlier unauthenticated-producer attempt and the backend-only-parameter setup refusal remain failed fixture attempts, not passing evidence or bypasses.
- The compatible backport remains locally deployed with the previously recorded health, session-identity and plugin checks. This test-only repair requires no runtime activation, and no operator Gateway was restarted for these tests.

```json
{
  "source": "139b7a08a03d48172c88ae860636bda39933475a",
  "syntheticInputsOnly": true,
  "entryPoint": "authenticated Gateway agent RPC and chat.send",
  "qualification": "Task-only loader supplies optional host policy at the existing agent-handler startTurn boundary. No actual child-completion lifecycle or external model service is claimed. Authorization, admission, current-authority guards, runtime and finalization are unchanged.",

```

All inputs, owner identities, provider responses and credentials in these tests are synthetic. Published evidence is allowlisted aggregate facts: no transcripts, credentials, hostnames, endpoints, paths or session/run identifiers are included. Task Gateway, provider and fixture state were cleaned up.

### Codex transcript-custody follow-through

The Codex consumer now uses the preserved human-input fact when committing steering before native dispatch. The separate pending-question eligibility flag remains unchanged. Internal guidance still waits for native acceptance before persistence; human input is committed once before sending and is not persisted a second time after consumption.

The regression exercises the real SDK → controller → Codex path, holds the transcript recorder, verifies zero native steering requests before commit, then confirms correlated native consumption and one canonical user message. It failed on the preceding producer-only revision. The final focused run passed 39 tests across three files; the owning extension test type graph, scoped typed lint, formatting, and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. This is simulated-native boundary proof, not a live-provider or deployment claim, and does not establish the cause of every queued-message incident.

prs.title: feat(plugins): identify retained references blocking reload
prs.body:
Related: #165059

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin reload drain timeouts report a reference count without identifying the host acquisitions that keep the plugin alive.

## User Impact

Administrators can inspect current plugin reference IDs, acquisition owners, reasons, ages, and cleanup state through `plugins.inspect`; drain logs include bounded, owner-redacted snapshots. This adds diagnosis, not force-release or changed reload behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing instance lifetime owner now records scalar acquisition facts beside its authoritative live tokens. Agent preparation, generation leases, invocation scopes, and service startup supply host attribution where available; unknown owners remain explicit. Inspection requires current administrator authority and the request's Gateway registry, returns at most 64 references with an omitted count, and never executes plugin code.

Acquisition ownership is not proof that a session is still executing or that a plugin leaked. In particular, a reload requested by a turn retaining the plugin can wait on itself, but aggregate counts alone cannot establish that cause. No payloads or cleanup error text are included.

## Evidence

### Refreshed head: `9d8ed3f053f835a7c91276a48b77ebb4a58898ee`

The branch preserves the original PR commits and merges main at `66cddbc140730ca449acfd582c0ee8f03273f551`. Conflict resolution keeps current call expiry, owner-joined work, service cleanup, self-reload handoff, and bounded reload waits. The obsolete consumer-lifecycle extraction and duplicate value-adoption traversal were removed; diagnostics observe the existing lifetime owner without changing admission or release.

- Full `pnpm build` passed on the clean committed head (155.8 seconds).
- Focused diagnostics, inspection, drain, schema, prepared-reply, and runtime-work tests passed. Adjacent instance/consumer/retention, services, local-command, and wrapper-inventory regression tests passed; affected instance/inspection/drain/wrapper tests were replayed after the final simplification.
- Final core production typecheck passed after simplification. Seven affected test-type graphs passed during the refresh; their public type contracts were unchanged by the final inline consumer cleanup. Targeted lint/format, line-cap, import/Madge-cycle checks, Swift/Kotlin protocol contract/determinism, and documentation links passed.
- Fresh independent structured review of the complete refreshed candidate found no actionable P0–P2 issues. This is separate from ClawSweeper.

### Real Gateway acceptance

A disposable compiled Gateway and real OpenClaw agent were exercised through public RPC with a paused synthetic loopback model provider. The supported repository compiled-subprocess test runner completed successfully (one acceptance test). Both build stamps identified the committed head above with clean inputs.

- Administrator `plugins.inspect` observed nine live references, including a prepared-generation lease and six calls attributed to the exact admitted session and run.
- An independently connected `operator.read`-only client received no `runtimeRetention` field.
- After releasing the provider and successful `agent.wait`, references dropped **9 → 0 on the same instance and registry generation**, without reload or replacement.
- Public chat history contained the completed assistant response with the matching run identity.
- Gateway/process, owned ports, synthetic provider, temporary state, and temporary test-fixture cleanup were verified.

Limit: queued-drain log owner redaction is covered by focused tests, not by this live Gateway scenario. Earlier acceptance attempts failed at fixture setup/observation boundaries; they are not claimed as product failures or successful acceptance. Local disposable proof files were removed after inspection; the linked work session retains the reported observations.

### Current CI remains failed; inherited failures are explicit

[CI run 39346552341, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346552341) tested merge `1641e53b57a962d37d1fdaf39ac5ad9f9732401f`, whose parents are main `d1e59da91a9290344c2c92c327d054d8cdf00e77` and this PR head. The three failed test jobs were inspected against that exact main parent:

- [Node compact-small-22](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346552341/job/118380866510): the typed Stop test still pauses `projection.ensureMaterialized()`, an explicit checkpoint retired by main [#177787](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177787). The test and relevant Stop owners are byte-identical between tested main and the CI merge.
- [UI 1/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346552341/job/118380865607) and [UI 7/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346552341/job/118380865349): older reconnect fixtures try manual Retry while their mock connection attempt is pending. Main [#177690](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177690) disables/guards Retry in that state. The entire UI tree, browser client, manifests/lockfile, and relevant build configuration match the tested main parent. These browser fixtures mock the Gateway and do not execute the plugin-retention server implementation.

This is **source/log attribution, not an executed base-versus-head replay**. The failed jobs and aggregate CI gate remain failed; no rerun, suppression, or passing-CI claim is made. Security/dependency review statuses for the head were successful at the landing preparation check.

<details>
<summary>Historical verification and CI notes for the original head</summary>

The following notes describe the pre-refresh head `dde9e3e9c4e2194558ba8e5d0ad03fd743164aa7`; references there to the current head, source inventory, and CI are historical, not claims about the refreshed head.

## CI follow-up status

Current remote head remains `dde9e3e9c4e2194558ba8e5d0ad03fd743164aa7`. Completed CI run [37852731605](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37852731605) tested merge `03b24fe6d97b6341dee485ebee0469933b161cda` with main `6ae2aee12eb0641b623e8c34840b47de9cff2022`. The branch began on freshly fetched main `8879e5ef4b98e7ff17b0ac04e7695f66f3e143b2`, not an intentionally stale checkout.

**Seven red rollup entries are five failed test jobs plus two aggregate gate statuses—not seven independent defects.** There are 81 successful and 20 skipped workflow jobs. No unchanged CI reruns, weakened checks, or merge were requested.

- **PR-caused defects: fixed.** The initial Madge type-import cycle triggered 57 cancellations, not 57 independent failures. The subsequent missing wrapper-inventory entries were also ours. Commits `3321e15bd97d7b38af72ef37b3770ade4f2f1c58` and `dde9e3e9c4e2194558ba8e5d0ad03fd743164aa7` repair these; architecture, wrapper inventory, typechecks and lint are green on the current head. All **15 new diagnostics cases pass in CI**, with 0.418 seconds summed test-body time (shared setup excluded).
- **Node changed-1: inherited, reproduced.** The skill-refresh E2E creates a managed worktree from a local-only repository without an origin or explicit base. Main's remote-default admission rejects that fixture. The identical missing-origin failure reproduces on exact CI main `6ae2aee12eb0641b623e8c34840b47de9cff2022` without this PR (48.72s). Introduction: `253d988bfd8d39ee19b5f788950532a07d7a9061`. A separate local spawn-broker cleanup warning is not the hosted failure; recovery state remains preserved.
- **Node compact-large-3-2: inherited fixture defect, causally reproduced.** The metadata-reader test resolves its drain milestone on both pre-quiescence retained-work waiting and later ordinary-call draining. The former correctly leaves `acceptingCalls=true`. Adding one controlled retained-work hold reproduces the exact assertion failure on both PR head and exact CI main (baseline 144.32s runner wall, 42.093s test body). A phase-specific observation passes the existing case (67.06s runner wall) and all 208 cases in the same 11-file shard on Node 24.19.0 with eight workers (124.24s). Fresh structured review is clean. Main independently landed the same phase-boundary repair in `f59e40793210d69e73bdc6695040fde0a69fed5c`; the duplicate local patch was removed, keeping this PR narrow. The original CI acquisition identity was not logged and remains unknown; the fixture defect does not require inferring that identity.
- **UI shards 3/9 and 7/9: inherited.** Exact CI main reproduces the suspended-dashboard and sidebar roster timeouts plus the stale prompt attachment (three failures, same assertions). Bootstrap request parking from `d51345aaf72cbfb13e1e31c081ecb4f15096cab8` parks the roster for 60s while these fixtures require it within 30s before they can resume admission; main fixes the fixtures in `9d606a28e0d5d10fcc77cc70ac810f782e0e6770`. Draft retirement from `082c68a9cbd83c20579e6e532d82e08cff17996f` starts IndexedDB cleanup without awaiting it before navigation, and both failing draft tests close the document immediately after the URL changes. The durable-writer variant did not reproduce locally; its cause is supported by that exact shared cleanup/navigation path and mocked Gateway execution, not by a passing rerun. Main fixes retirement-before-navigation in `a5106ecf04913d4ff5374d0991dac148faf06510` and strengthens fixture retirement waits in `114d443b2f8e6d7459491b627f363a8a2a631f22`. These browser fixtures replace the Gateway WebSocket with a mock; this PR's server retention code is not executed.
- **Android Play: outside this PR's executable/data path.** `ChatCompletedWorkLayoutTest.earlierTextAndToolResultReplacementRefreshesAnUnchangedTail` times out after 1s at line 478; 3,556 other tests pass. The test uses Android `ScreenshotFixture` mode and a literal in-process `chat.history` response, not a TypeScript Gateway. Android sources and build/dependency inputs match the exact baseline. The PR does change schema input to native generation, so source-path exclusion alone is insufficient: rerunning the actual Kotlin generator on exact CI main, then with the PR's two schema-file changes, produces **byte-identical GatewayProtocol.kt and OpenClawProtocolConstants.kt**. Native generation also succeeded in CI. Thus the diagnostics changes cannot supply different code/data to this assertion. The exact Android scheduling/loading condition that exceeded 1s remains unproven; no Android reproduction or timeout increase is claimed.
- **Aggregate gates:** the failed Actions `openclaw/ci-gate` and commit status summarize these job failures. The separate Security Review publisher succeeded; its red commit status is not an additional security finding.

CI remains historically red on this head because of these evidenced inherited failures. No new source push or rebase was made merely to obtain green status; the branch remains mergeable, and this task does not authorize merging. The new diagnostics do not identify the original live Knowledge holders until deployed and observed.

## Evidence

- Deslop follow-up: **15 newly added test cases**, down from 22 (6 reference/lifetime cases, 7 inspection cases, 2 drain cases). Existing suite totals below are regression coverage, not tests added. Production TypeScript net growth fell from **436 to 413 lines**; test TypeScript net growth fell from **566 to 495 lines**.
- Fixed the PR-created static import cycle: execution-frame type contracts now import schema-derived retention facts from the existing leaf type module, not the runtime diagnostics implementation. The full `pnpm check:architecture` command passes, including both runtime and Madge import-cycle scans.
- Follow-up lifetime/access regression run: **83 tests across 8 files passed** (101.64s). The retained consumer lifecycle extraction remains necessary to satisfy the existing lifetime-owner line cap; no new lifecycle policy or release path was introduced.
- Initial PR regression run: **145 tests in 13 files passed** (126.31s), including real instance references, GC/lifetime regression coverage, multiple owners, derived consumers, release, pending/failed cleanup, bounded payload-free output, administrator revocation, and request-registry isolation.
- Shared plugin contracts: **1,140 tests in 48 files passed** (244.38s).
- Earlier wider reload/local-command regression run: **252 tests in 14 files passed** (341.98s); this preceded the mechanical consumer/value-association extraction.
- After the final limit-normalization correction, all **6 diagnostics cases passed** again (48.16s). The reduced **7-case inspection suite passed** independently (18.64s).
- CI source-closure repair: the new runtime modules are now included in the existing trusted-wrapper inventory. The original inventory failure reproduced locally; all **17 existing eager-import closure cases passed** after the two-line correction (27.62s), with a clean fresh autoreview. No new tests or relaxed checks were added.
- Follow-up static proof: core typecheck, all **27 core-test typecheck graphs**, changed-file lint, formatting, whitespace, and line-cap ratchet passed.
- Follow-up structured autoreview: **no actionable findings**. Accepted the first review’s request to preserve existing finite/integer limit normalization; the final review covers that correction.
- Full build passed (245.4s). Formatting, documentation links, protocol generation/determinism, core typechecking, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, and pre-deadcode changed-file guards passed. The build preceded removal of three unused private-helper export modifiers; focused validation covers that final cleanup.
- `pnpm check:changed` stopped at the dead-export scan. Three diagnostics-only unused exports were made private; the remaining unrelated `ClientVoiceToolEffect` export in `src/talk/client-voice-session-store.ts` is unchanged from the base and has no external references there. prs.title: improve(cron): surface scheduled jobs blocked on a missing creator channel and guide recovery
prs.body:
Related: #162087

## What Problem This Solves

A capped automation created from a direct (DM) conversation before creator origins were recorded fails closed on every scheduled run: the account-scoped liveness check cannot resolve a channel from a DM owner key with no recorded origin, so it reports the (configured) account as unavailable. The only recovery today is recreating the job, which demotes it to broader `trusted` authority. The jobs are also undiscoverable: nothing surfaces which saved jobs are blocked, and the run error suggests re-adding the account even when the account is fine.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now discover blocked jobs and recover them without demoting their authority. `openclaw automations status` reports a `reauthorizationRequired` count, each affected job's details and list entries flag `reauthorizationRequired: true`, and the run error names the real cause and the least-privilege recovery: re-save the job's tool cap from the creator's authenticated turn (which records a fresh origin via the existing reauthorization path), or recreate it from the intended account.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the guided-recovery side of the failure mode recommended by the security review on #162087 ("require guided reauthorization: keep the fail-closed boundary and add a clear operator or creator recovery flow"). It does not change the boundary: the liveness guard still fails closed; the change only detects the exact blocked class, surfaces it, and makes the error accurate. The trigger-path origin threading is already merged (#176158) and is not touched here. The detection predicate mirrors the guard precisely (named account, unknown origin, non group/channel owner key), so it flags exactly the jobs that fail and no others.

## Evidence

- `cronJobNeedsCreatorReauthorization` unit tests: DM-key account job with no origin → flagged; recorded external/local origin → not flagged; group-key owner → not flagged; trusted mode / default account / no cap → not flagged.
- Error-message tests: the no-creator-channel path now asserts the new accurate message; the removed-account path still asserts the original message (both pinned fixtures updated/verified).

prs.title: fix(macos): settle core repair on successful repair warnings
prs.body:
Closes #168534

**AI-assisted: yes.** Authored by an AI coding agent; every executable check below was run in this checkout (Swift test availability is stated explicitly).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw.app runs `openclaw update repair --json --timeout 900 --yes` on every launch, even when the installation is up to date. The repair unloads the `ai.openclaw.gateway` LaunchAgent, so the Gateway is unreachable for about two minutes, and the next launch repeats it.

Root cause: the launch decision is receipt-driven. The app persists a PostUpdate receipt and runs core repair while `coreUpdatePending` is set; it completes the receipt only when the repair result is accepted. `openclaw update repair` reports a completed finalization with nonfatal advisories as `status: "warning"` and exits successfully, but the app rejected **every** warning result as failure (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/CLIInstaller.swift`), so the receipt never completes and the repair runs again next launch.

## User Impact

App launches no longer stop the Gateway for a two-minute repair loop when the repair actually completed with nonfatal advisories. Deferred maintenance still keeps the receipt pending: a standalone repair exits nonzero (exit 2) when Doctor maintenance remains, and that case still fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CLIInstaller` now accepts a `warning` repair result only when the repair process exited successfully (`repair && reportedStatus == "warning"` with `response.success`). Nonzero/deferred results still take the failure path, so pending work is retained. No retry policy, CLI contract, or migration behavior changed.

## Evidence

```text
# regression added in apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/CLIInstallerTests.swift:
# successful warning (exit 0) completes the receipt;
# deferred maintenance (exit 2) still fails and keeps it pending
```

**Local compile.** `swift build --build-tests` passes with 0 errors, so the app and the new test target compile on this head.

**Swift test execution limit.** `swift test` cannot run in this environment: the package minimum deployment target, and therefore the test bundle's `minos`, is macOS 26.2, while the host is macOS 15.8.1. The macOS Swift CI lane is also not selected for ordinary pull requests: `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` sets `run_macos_swift` only for non-`pull_request` events, and `macos-swift` is skipped on this PR (as on recent macOS PRs). The new Swift Testing regression therefore runs in the main/scheduled native lane after merge; a maintainer can dispatch native validation against this head before merge if it is required for landing.

The launch-decision trace was source-verified against `PostUpdate.swift` (`coreRepairAction`, receipt completion) and `CLIInstaller.swift` (acceptance gate). PR CI is green (`openclaw/ci-gate`), with the macOS native lane skipped as described.

**Residual risk.** `status: "warning"` is accepted only on a successful exit; if a future CLI version reports warning with a nonzero exit, behavior stays as today (failure). Completed-finalization advisories are accepted for the receipt but not separately surfaced in the app UI; the CLI JSON retains the details. The issue's repeated-launch symptom is fixed by completing the receipt, not by skipping repair.

## CI verification (2026-10-21)

Verified on the exact head `54494a794e9f`:

- Required PR CI is green: 20 checks pass, `openclaw/ci-gate` SUCCESS ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39441170849/job/118692832539)).
- The native Swift test lane cannot run on ordinary pull requests. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gates the job with `if: needs.preflight.outputs.run_macos_swift == 'true'` (line 4818), and `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` computes `run_macos_swift = runMacos && ...` where `runMacos = !ordinaryPullRequest && ...` (lines 358 and 1756-1757; `ordinaryPullRequest = workflowEventName === "pull_request"`, line 19). On this head preflight did detect the macOS changed paths (`OPENCLAW_CI_RUN_MACOS: true`; changed paths `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/CLIInstaller.swift`, `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/CLIInstallerTests.swift`), yet `macos-swift` is SKIPPED ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39441170849/job/118691927493)).
- macOS CI did compile the added regression on this exact head: the `macOS Periphery Dead Code [report]` workflow's `Build macOS Periphery reports` job (`runs-on: xcode-27`) ran `cd apps/macos && swift build --build-system native --scratch-path ../../.cache/periphery-swift --build-tests --enable-index-store` and finished `Build complete! (688.96s)` ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39441170892/job/118691512075)). Its log compiles `OpenClaw CLIInstaller.swift` and the `OpenClawIPCTests` module including `CLIInstallerTests.swift` (e.g. warnings at `CLIInstallerTests.swift:299:9` and `:351:9`). This upgrades the earlier local compile claim to macOS-runner compile evidence, but it is compile-only: no test is executed.

### macOS execution paths surveyed (none available here)

- **No macOS host:** this workstation and the fallback verification host are Windows; no Parallels/`prlctl` guest manager is present on either.
- **No crabbox/Testbox:** `crabbox` is not installed, there is no `.crabbox` config or lease, and no prepared SSH macOS target is configured.
- **No GitHub dispatch:** the account has read-only repository permission (`"pull": true`, no push/maintain/admin), and the API shows no `workflow_dispatch` run on this head.
- **No derivable red-on-base:** the regression is added by this PR, so no existing macOS CI run on a base revision executes it.

### Remaining requirement (unchanged)

1. Execute the added native regression on macOS: `swift test` filtered to the new `CLIInstallerTests` cases against the base revision (red) and this head (green), using the package's macOS 26.x toolchain/deployment target.
2. Run the isolated app flow from latest-stable state: launch OpenClaw.app so a successful-advisory repair (`status: "warning"`, exit 0) settles the receipt and no repeat repair/Gateway interruption happens on relaunch; an exit-2 deferred repair must still remain pending; settings and data preserved.

A maintainer with macOS capacity can dispatch the native lane against this head. No code changed and no re-review is requested until that execution evidence exists.

prs.title: feat(doctor): show actionable Node lifecycle advice
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor does not explain when an admitted Node runtime has entered upstream maintenance or reached end of life.

## User Impact

Standalone `openclaw doctor` emits maintenance information or an EOL warning when applicable. It respects the app that owns the runtime and omits executable paths. Updater-owned Doctor, `doctor --lint`, and status retain compatibility checks without adding standalone lifecycle advice to update results.

Acceptance of the EOL warning and unhealthy classification remains a maintainer decision. This conflict repair preserves that proposal and introduces no new flags, config, schema, dependencies, protocol, permissions or service policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing diagnostics owner separates Node SQLite admission from upstream lifecycle advice. The canonical Doctor context carries its environment and mode through that owner; updater markers keep standalone advice out of update-result IPC.

A normal merge preserves original contributor ancestry, including [51509e6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/51509e645ad606c0296a4516d54c5ff7f89c4dc8) and [9c40ec8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9c40ec890359fb9d4a9405670180f2bf9e0aaf8f).

## Evidence

Current head: `8c6d5660ff8599405276b8be8a693461a7f23b7b`, normally merging author head `09b21f5d60edd169d38a572ace41df428cb13135` with official main `08e32fdb4df002c9d4eea158b855d6521dd1e916`.

- **Actual conflict before repair:** both `git merge-tree` and a normal merge fail in `doctor-host-runtime.test.ts`. Main consolidated its host-owned repair and health cases into two top-level tables. The resolution takes the complete main file and restores only the unique EOL/host-owner case. Unsupported-service, CLI TEXT capability failure and CLI-only daemon controls stay in the existing tables; no duplicate cases, weakened assertions, longer timeout or production test seam are added. The runtime diagnostics implementation is unchanged from the author head.

The test worker prepared **16,752 source inputs /21,691 outputs in 73.831 s**. It does not perform a real upgrade or Gateway restart.
- Actual **Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.12.1** satisfy the integrated manifest. Package, lockfile and workspace bytes match qualified installed inputs and pinned main; no install or dependency patch was made. Format, affected-file line-cap, native mock-export and assertion-safety guards, docs sanity and diff checks pass. No full release build, platform or shipped-runtime replay is claimed.
- The [official Node release schedule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json) was rechecked on October 20, 2026 (Asia/Shanghai); the retained Node 24/25/26 maintenance and EOL dates match it.
- Fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview is **scoped-clean**. Its source-bearing pass inspected the complete seven-file diff; the other two evidence partitions lacked raw-parent diffs and add no independent full-diff or runtime proof. The reviewed source/index/commit bytes match. The author simplification pass retains one EOL regression and main's consolidated controls.

**Retained local failure:** the global max-lines guard reports existing UI suppressions in `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts` and `sessions-page-state.ts`. Those three files, the baseline and checker are byte-identical to pinned main. **Current-head broad CI:** [Natural CI 39329972269](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39329972269) completed **success** on `8c6d5660ff8599405276b8be8a693461a7f23b7b`, with **70 jobs: 41 successful executions and 29 skipped**. Observed workflow elapsed time was **5029 s**, including waiting; successful jobs sum to **7649 job-seconds**. These are workflow/job wall times, separate from local file/case timings and not billing. No rerun, dispatch or no-op push was requested. This CI result does not supply the installed/shipped upgrade, platform/app ownership or maintainer product decision listed below. Earlier [09b21f5 CI 38972349677](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38972349677) remains prior-head evidence.

**Remaining proof/review:** registered-command behavior on the installed/shipped runtime, latest-stable upgrade behavior and real app/service ownership on supported platforms remain unverified, alongside maintainer acceptance of the EOL severity/health classification. No operator Gateway, service restart, model/provider API, paid host, release or upstream merge is claimed. Prior isolated Gateway permissions do not transfer to this head.

<details>
<summary>Earlier-head evidence and retained historical failures</summary>

The material below belongs to its explicitly named earlier heads; it is not fresh runtime proof for this merge.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

## Evidence

After correcting the old installation-module mock to preserve real exports, the affected update-flow file passes again (**9 cases / 65.471 s** wrapper wall); the unchanged 31-case diagnostics/host-runtime results are reused. These scoped results are not one additional final all-suite replay. Tests cover real result IPC with synthetic isolated state; updater/service operations are mocked. No actual update or Gateway restart is performed.
- Production types pass **111.140 s**; the three-file test-consumer closure passes **101.740 s**, then **15.567 s** after the mock correction. Six-file type-aware lint passes **31.689 s**, with the changed test replay **18.483 s**. Formatting, whitespace and seven-file growth ratchet pass. The mock-export check initially rejects the old whole-module installation mock (**21.442 s**); preserving actual exports fixes the guard (**21.164 s**), without a baseline exemption.
- Fresh final full-candidate independent P0–P2 review is scoped clean; its patch pass inspected all seven changed files. The review is static and does not establish execution of live updater behavior or acceptance of the lifecycle-warning policy. All seven committed blobs match the final reviewed copy. prs.title: fix(macos): stop re-running update repair on every launch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #168534: the macOS app can repeat successful update repair on later launches when the CLI reports nonfatal advisories, stopping the Gateway again unnecessarily.

Supersedes #178487, thanks @HeZ2z.

## User Impact

Completed repair stays settled even when it reports warnings or a later reconnect fails. Deferred maintenance and failed repair remain pending so the app can retry unfinished work. Existing installed-version verification and service authority checks remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now reports typed `coreUpdate: "completed" | "pending"` facts at the repair result boundary. Completion is published after convergence, service restoration, handoff completion, and recovery reconciliation. The native consumer uses that fact instead of treating every warning as failure.

A successful exit alone is insufficient: an inherited updater can exit 0 with maintenance deferred. That path explicitly reports pending, as does retained recovery custody. This closes the gap in the warning-only fix without adding another receipt owner or changing update policy.

Production: **+18/-2 (net +16)**. Tests: **+80/-1 (net +79)**. Documentation: **+10/-0**. The small production increase is the typed producer/consumer contract; no unrelated cleanup is included.

## Evidence

- TypeScript regressions fail on the unchanged producer because the completion fact is absent; focused regressions pass with the fix. All 15 directly importing consumer test files pass: **286 tests**, three shards in **816.98 s**, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <consumer files> --maxWorkers=1`.
- Swift builds with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --jobs 4`. The seven-case native regression executes real shell fixtures, parses the CLI result, persists/reloads the receipt, and checks the next-launch repair decision. It covers completed advisories, deferred maintenance with exit 0, real process failures, and absent/unknown completion facts. It fails against the unchanged native consumer (including the advisory/relaunch assertion), then passes all seven cases on the restored fix in **0.853 s**.
- Native execution uses SwiftPM's testing helper inside an audited OS sandbox with isolated HOME/state, operator files and Keychain/preferences services blocked, and network access denied. This is a native result/receipt boundary proof; a full packaged-app upgrade and live Gateway restart were not run.
- Scoped CLI-update tsgo, oxlint, oxfmt, SwiftFormat, production SwiftLint, `git diff --check`, and madge pass; madge reports **0 cycles**. Independent Codex review found no actionable issues.
- Full `check:changed` was omitted under the campaign's SQLite inventory time-budget allowance; scoped checks above replace it, with PR CI providing broad proof. The Swift test file has 16 unchanged lint findings, verified against the base. Existing consumer suites remain slow: shard durations **173.78 s**, **356.82 s**, and **219.08 s**; the lease suite spends about 95% in tests. This patch only adds assertions to those TS cases and does not add timeout/retry allowances.


**Windows CI follow-up.** The failure in [checks-node-changed-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39481990487/job/118833501610) was inherited from the CI merge base: #178624 moved enabled-state mutations to PowerShell COM, while this lifecycle fixture still intercepted only `schtasks`. Main fixed the fixture in `52714b572789b3d4bbc503075b94349aeadf5c71`. This branch now includes that landed correction. The completion implementation is unchanged, and all task settlement, ordering, compensation, and final-state expectations are preserved.

Commands used `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, isolated HOME/state/config/temp/cache, Node 26.12.0, and the pinned Bun 1.4.4 fork. The integrated candidate additionally selected the five reported cases with `-t 'starts (update|doctor) triage when native|settles native Windows task enabled state'`; its tested tree matches the new commit. prs.title: fix(ui): keep custom session icon entry open while using the emoji viewer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: picking an emoji in the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space) for a custom session icon closes the **Icon & color** submenu, and the emoji is not set. The custom icon hint recommends exactly this shortcut ("Paste an emoji or SVG. Press ⌃⌘Space for the system emoji picker.").

Steps to reproduce on `main` (Chrome on macOS):

1. Right-click a session in the sidebar → **Advanced → Icon & color** → **…** (Custom icon).
2. With the cursor in the custom icon field, press ⌃⌘Space.
3. Click an emoji in the Character Viewer.
4. The submenu closes; reopening it shows an empty field and the session icon is unchanged. Pasting the same emoji from the clipboard and clicking **Set** works.

Cause: the Web Awesome dropdown closes a submenu 100 ms after a mouse move outside it (`handleGlobalMouseMove`, the hover-leave "safe triangle" check). Clicking into the Character Viewer blurs the Chrome window; the next mouse move Chrome sees is wherever the viewer was, usually outside the submenu. The submenu closes before the window gets focus back, so the viewer's `insertText` has no visible field to land in. The same check applies to every text entry inside a hover-opened submenu, for example the **Assign to…** people search.

## User Impact

User impact: a custom icon can be picked with the system emoji viewer as the hint suggests; the field keeps the emoji and **Set** applies it. Hover-opened submenus without a focused text field still close when the pointer leaves them, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hover-leave close lives in the repo's existing Web Awesome patch (`patches/@awesome.me__webawesome@3.13.0.patch`), which already owns this submenu branch logic. The change adds one condition there: the delayed close is skipped while a text entry inside the submenu (`textarea`, text-like `input`, `contenteditable`) has focus. The focused element is read from the item's own root (`getRootNode().activeElement`), which keeps the textarea while the window is blurred by the viewer. Keyboard, Escape, outside clicks and closing the menu are unchanged.

| | Production | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lines (+/−) | patch: +4/−1 per bundle (`dist`, `dist-cdn`), lockfile patch hash | +48 |

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway on the Mac (loopback port 19789, own state, one session with one real model turn), built from `main` 6d9db828732 (base) and from this branch (fix, head 046938852dc), same state. Chrome for Testing 153 with its own profile; Playwright opened the menu (**Advanced → Icon & color → …**), the Character Viewer was used with the real keyboard and mouse. Event log recorded in the page; times UTC, 2026-10-13.

| Run | after clicking an emoji in the viewer | field value | submenu | session icon |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base 6d9db828732 (23:06:02) | window blur → `mousemove` over the chat → `submenu-closing` 106 ms later → window focus | empty, no `input` event | closed (also **Advanced**) | unchanged |
| Fix 046938852dc (23:08:27) | window blur → `mousemove` over a menu row outside the submenu → window focus → `insertText` "❤️" | ❤️ | open, also after moving the pointer over the chat | ❤️ after clicking **Set** (`sessions.list`) |

Before (base, after clicking an emoji in the Character Viewer):

![Before: after clicking an emoji in the Character Viewer the submenu is closed and the field is empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/446417e1-d1a8-40f2-bffd-f14e98305848)

After (fix, same steps, emoji inserted, submenu still open):

![After: the emoji is in the custom icon field and the submenu stays open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/657ecf38-8162-4d4a-88b8-93892dad46f2)

<details><summary>Page event logs (ms since the custom field opened)</summary>

```text
base 6d9db828732
5747 window:blur
5747 blur (textarea) value=""
6528 mousemove x=825 y=731 target=chat-thread
6634 submenu-closing value=""
6837 window:focus

fix 046938852dc
15659 window:blur
15659 blur (textarea) value=""
16185 mousemove x=734 y=628 target=session-menu__item
16271 window:focus
16271 focus (textarea)
16279 beforeinput insertText "❤️"
16283 input insertText value="❤️"
```

</details>

Tests (VPS, Chromium, `--maxWorkers=1`):

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/session-menu.browser.test.ts` → 4 passed, 11 s wall. Through the rendered menu: hover **Advanced** and **Icon & color**, click **Custom icon…**, type an emoji, move the pointer outside, advance the 100 ms close timer → the submenu stays expanded and **Set** applies the emoji. With the base patch the new case fails (`aria-expanded="false"`, expected `"true"`). A second new case checks that the submenu still closes when the pointer leaves without a focused text field (passes on base and fix).
- `web-awesome-dropdown.browser.test.ts`, `web-awesome-dropdown-owner.browser.test.ts`, `session-menu.test.ts`, `session-icon-picker.test.tsx`, `appearance-picker.browser.test.ts` → 130 passed (2 runs, 45 s wall).
- WebKit (Playwright WebKit 26.6 on macOS, `OPENCLAW_UI_WEBKIT=1 pnpm --dir ui test --project webkit src/components/session-menu.browser.test.ts`) → 4 passed, 6 s wall; with the base patch the new case fails the same way (`aria-expanded="false"`).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed test file: clean.

Gaps: the chat header session menu and the **Assign to…** search use the same submenu path but were not checked live. The live run used Chrome for Testing; Safari and Firefox were not checked live.

prs.title: fix(database): first chat fails after PostgreSQL admission reuse
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a first accepted chat turn failing with `Search extensions require an admitted PostgreSQL store` after a SQLite-to-PostgreSQL port when the agent store reuses admission from another handle or worker.

## User Impact

Ported installations can lazily admit memory and standing-intent search on first use. No manual memory-index rebuild, migration, config change, or admission bypass is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Physical PostgreSQL admission already travels through the shared database admission owner, but its schema definition lived in a separate per-anchor `WeakMap`. Opening another handle could reuse physical admission while losing the definition needed for search-extension registration. The schema definition now follows the same schema-dependent admission lifecycle, including transaction staging, rollback, and worker transfer. The obsolete manual definition rollback is removed. Migration recipes stay with the opener because their backup descriptors can contain callbacks; workers receive only the current schema definition.

The secondary `Agent publication binding did not settle` error follows the synchronous admission exception; it is not a settlement timeout.

## Evidence

- Native regression is red on the base with the reported admission error and green with the fix. It opens a new handle to an already admitted agent store, admits a new search extension, and reuses the committed definition.
- PostgreSQL admission, schema, and Doctor migration tests: 32 passed, including real predecessor backups, restores, and foreign-write rollback. Standing-intent product tests also pass. The migration-callback snapshot regression is red with `DataCloneError` before the follow-up correction and green after it.
- Small product controls: native PostgreSQL and a three-agent SQLite-to-PostgreSQL port both complete their first accepted chat turn with memory enabled and no prebuilt memory indexes. A fresh 20-agent large-copy baseline reproduces the exact error; the final head completes its first accepted turn and its existing 50,001-event conversation from another fresh original-artifact copy. All 20 agent stores admit standing-intent search, and the original admission/maintenance error scan is empty. A single-agent control reused attempted state, so it is not treated as isolated evidence of agent count.
- All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on final head `30fd58062fe444d40330a8ea8a22c13b9c87806f` in CI run [39498128897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39498128897). These jobs actually ran against PG17 with unaccent, pg_trgm, and pgvector.
- Independent review: no remaining actionable P0–P2 findings. Core and affected state/infra test type checks, lint, and formatting pass. The broad local type-graph selector hits unchanged root-count budget failures, reproduced on clean main (721/724/726/727 roots versus 720); the targeted compiler graphs pass. Modified admission files take about 1–4 seconds of test execution each; the Doctor migration suite supplies the longer update/rollback proof.

Earlier qualification #178005 enabled keyword-only memory, ran `memory index --agent main` after porting, and explicitly skipped live model turns. It admitted only `memory.text`, so it did not cover an untouched port followed by first-turn standing-intent admission.

The hosted fallback dependency check reports inherited unused exports in Agents API, QA Lab, and board notices. Every reported finding reproduces on the clean PR base `bead2a8e542`; their source, consumers, dependency configuration, and scan configuration are unchanged by this PR. No suppression or unrelated code change was made. The separate local changed-type-selector root-budget failure also reproduces on the base.

prs.title: fix(doctor): release legacy agent leases proven older than boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can remain blocked after a Windows reboot by a legacy agent database lease whose PID has been reused and whose recorded process start identity is missing.

Fixes #137925.

## User Impact

Doctor can release a proven prior-boot legacy lease and logs a warning naming that lease. Same-boot leases, records inside the five-minute safety margin, unreadable boot evidence, and unfinished admission still block repair. The refusal tells users to stop the Gateway and other OpenClaw processes or reboot, then rerun `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lease-provenance owner now reuses the platform boot reader and five-minute Windows boot-time comparison established for managed handoff recovery in #178184. Boot evidence is read at most once per scan, without retaining it across repairs. Timestamp ordering against another process's creation time is not used. Linux and macOS boot identities are opaque, so they do not establish this legacy timestamp proof.

Read-only admission and writable drainage use the same stale-lease decision. Reclamation invalidates integrity verification and publishes the lease warning after commit. The public diagnostic allowlist preserves the new fixed guidance; bounded wait diagnostics keep that guidance within the existing failure-fact limit. No schema, dependency, or option changes.

## Evidence

- The new real-SQLite prior-boot regression failed on the baseline at read-only Doctor admission. It covers prior boot, the exact margin, same boot, unreadable boot time, and unfinished admission.
- Focused and consumer proof: all 10 touched test files passed after correcting stale wording expectations (373 tests; one existing skip), and the final nine-file consumer/replay run passed (136 tests; one Windows-only skip). The original 68-file importer run exposed the wording and fixture issues fixed here; its other tests passed.
- Scoped production and test tsgo: exit 0. Touched-file oxlint and oxfmt: exit 0. Madge: `0 cycle(s)`. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings; the later change was one matching test-string correction.
- A sibling handoff-history test exposed host-path-dependent receipt truncation. Its fixture now redacts all sibling roots; the complete settled-family assertions remain intact.
- Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget. PR CI supplies broad proof. Windows OS live proof and a stable-to-current installation upgrade were not run on this Mac; the Windows boot reader is reused unchanged and the admission regression uses real SQLite with synthetic boot facts.
- Production LOC +94/-32 (net +62); test LOC +54/-12 (net +42); docs +6/-0. The additional production code owns one boot observation per scan and post-commit warning publication; the duplicate handoff comparison was removed.

Commands ran with `HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home"` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/state"`. Focused/consumer tests used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <test files> --maxWorkers=1`; types used `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/tsconfig.followup-{prod,tests}.json` with changed-file roots; lint used `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig tsconfig.json <changed TypeScript files>`; format used `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <changed files>`; cycles used `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain continuation authority for every child run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#178186 fixed children newly spawned by a restart-recovered parent turn, but only through a caller-passed special case (`agentRunTracking === "native_subagent"` → `independentContinuation`). Children that were already running when the Gateway died take a different path. Restart recovery resumes them through `sessions_send`/`nested:<child>`, which still retained the parent's run-scoped recovery claim. When the recovered parent turn ended, every resumed child failed:

> Restart recovery operator run is no longer active.

Live, on latest main with #178186 (Codex app-server parent, Gateway `kill -9` while the parent was still in its first turn): 2 of 2 runs lost all 8 children, with 16 authority-lost failures and nothing merged.

## User Impact

Children resumed after a Gateway restart retain continuation authority when the recovered parent turn finishes. Explicit parent Stop and operator revocation still cancel child work. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The decision is now structural, made at the shared run-retention boundary. `retainGatewayOperatorRun` chooses the independent continuation authority from the admitted session's persisted `spawnedBy` lineage, so callers can no longer pass `independentContinuation`.

- The `native_subagent` special case is removed. One rule covers native spawns, restart-resumed children, nested-lane continuations, follow-ups and steers to a child, and collector children.
- Agent, chat-send and Talk admission all supply the lineage.
- Original authority validation, scope intersection, the model-policy ceiling, live source checks, revocation and parent Stop cancellation are unchanged.
- The choice is only between the operator's already-registered continuation authority and the inherited one, so no new authority can be minted.

## Evidence

- `subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts` "resumed child": red on base (`admitted run operator authority is no longer active` at `admitted-run-context.ts:384`) and green with the fix. 18 focused recovery, resume, cancellation and Talk files pass, including `operator-run-recovery*`, `server.startup-recovery-*`, `subagent-registry-restart-recovery`, `server.sessions-send-resume`, `session-subagent-resume`, `in-process-subagent-resume`, `subagent-parent-recovery.restart-integration`, `chat-send-subagent-custody` and the Talk authority suites. The full spawn file passed 64/64. One later repeat hit an existing sandbox-fixture model-entry wait under heavy local load; it is unrelated to authority (no authority error or abort in its diagnostics).
- Live Crabbox A/B, identical first-turn kill, Codex parent, same moment:
  - main: 16 authority-lost failures and nothing merged.
  - this branch: 0 authority-lost failures, and the fleet recovered to 8/8 merged (35/35 tests) about 3 minutes after the kill.

prs.title: fix(browser): fail text-mode snapshots blocked by a pending dialog
prs.body:
Related: #148531

(Deliberately not `Closes`. The issue reports a browser stall; this change fixes a narrower,
verifiable CLI defect found while investigating it and does not establish the stall as
resolved.)

## What Problem This Solves

When a pending dialog blocks the page, `GET /snapshot` deliberately answers with
`blockedByDialog: true`, the dialog details in `browserState`, and an empty payload
(`snapshot: ""` or `nodes: []`) so the caller can dismiss the dialog and retry.

Outside `--json`, `openclaw browser snapshot` threw that flag away:

| Case | stdout | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `about:blank`, healthy capture | empty | 0 |
| dialog pending (`blockedByDialog: true`) | empty | 0 |

A script or agent reading text output cannot tell "the page is empty" from "a dialog is
blocking the page". With `--out`, the empty payload also replaced an existing snapshot
file and the flag was lost.

## What Changed

`extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-inspect.ts`, snapshot command only:

- Text mode (`ai` and `aria`): a `blockedByDialog` response now exits 1 with a message
  naming the tab, the pending dialog id/type/message, and the command to dismiss it
  (`openclaw browser dialog --dismiss --dialog-id <id> --target-id <tab>`). Nothing is
  printed to stdout.
- `--out` (with or without `--json`): a `blockedByDialog` response exits 1 and leaves the
  existing file untouched.
- `--json` without `--out`: unchanged. The full response, dialog details included, is
  still returned so recovery code keeps working.
- Healthy captures, including genuinely blank pages: unchanged. They print (or write) and
  exit 0.

No route, client type, or Gateway change. This replaces the earlier revision of this PR,
which added a `captured` marker at the producer; per review on #148531 that went beyond
what the evidence supports, so the scope is narrowed to the CLI contract above.

## Tests

`browser-cli-inspect.test.ts`, new `dialog-blocked snapshots` block:

- `ai` and `aria` text mode → exit 1, message includes tab, dialog details and the
  dismiss command, nothing logged to stdout
- `--out`, with and without `--json` → exit 1, existing file byte-identical, no JSON
- `--json` without `--out` → JSON still carries `blockedByDialog` and `browserState`,
  exit 0
- genuinely blank page (`snapshot: ""`, no dialog) → prints `""`, exit 0

prs.title: fix(sessions): backport history reply performance fixes to release/2026.10.10
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backports upstream long-history reply performance and memory fixes onto the `release/2026.10.10` release branch.

On long conversation histories, environments running the `2026.10.10` beta series experience severe local reply latency (>2 seconds overhead per turn before model inference) due to repeated unindexed SQLite table scans and uncompacted actor context hydration. This backport resolves the issue without introducing schema, protocol, API, prompt, or configuration changes.

### Backported Changes (authored by Peter Steinberger)
- **#172892**: Retain tree fields in actor navigation instead of rich context projections.
- **#172970**: Hydrate a bounded 512-event actor tail and retain indexed durable lookup for old identities, parents, and anchors.
- **#174435**: Reuse committed model navigation and byte costs; update appended/revised pages through existing write receipts.
- **#174700**: Retain selectable context suffix and compact prefix/tool-pairing facts; use canonical reconstruction when branch/reset/compaction/restart requires it.
- **#174275**: Select indexed custom/reset/null identity candidates before exact active/payload joins in cache TTL prefix queries, eliminating repeated linear history scans.

## Earlier performance qualification

### Test & Correctness Parity
- All 119 focused unit and regression tests pass across the affected areas (`src/agents/sessions`, `src/config/sessions`).
- Context reconstruction verified across private 33,000+ event test histories: provider-visible conversation histories and the 17-event production context hash match baseline identically.
- Indexed retrieval at arbitrary sequence positions (e.g. seq 1, 500, 1000, 15000, 32700) matches baseline.

### Measured Benchmarks
Across alternating baseline vs candidate runs under isolated conditions:

| History | Phase | Pairs (n) | Baseline median / p95 (ms) | Candidate median / p95 (ms) | Delta |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Large** | **Warm** | 9 | 2115.0 / 2149.4 | **332.8 / 379.8** | **-84.3%** |
| **Large** | **Cold** | 3 | 6621.8 / 6806.3 | 4803.7 / 5109.1 | -27.5% |
| **Large** | **Restart** | 3 | 5818.5 / 5824.0 | 4282.3 / 4309.7 | -26.4% |
| **Small** | **Warm** | 6 | 233.6 / 283.4 | 241.1 / 266.4 | +3.2% |
| **Small** | **Cold** | 2 | 3653.0 / 3662.8 | 3652.2 / 3718.5 | ~0% |
| **Small** | **Restart** | 2 | 3790.6 / 3795.8 | 3884.0 / 4061.3 | +2.5% |

Warm local reply overhead on long histories dropped by ~84% (from ~2,115 ms down to ~332 ms) by eliminating redundant full-history scans and query re-execution on warm turns.

## Evidence: receipt-retention repair and runtime proof (October 20)

Receipt follow-up: `3a2ccb1ba2cc31642a1798d3ce0301169cc524de`. Adapted Peter Steinberger's upstream [receipt-retention repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/aeec7f27b3d71f91a5b5b0dfc15dec987d38bbc4) to this release branch's admission/publication API. Idle receipts have a 1 MiB estimated-byte budget per database/isolate; session deletion also retires page partitions. Active completion and Workshop effects retain their shared receipt cells and admission until release, while writes/deletion still invalidate them. No persisted schema or data-retention policy changes.

Production-owner pressure reproduction (160 synthetic long-key reads): original PR/base retained 162 scopes / 1,356,506 estimated bytes and preserved the cold token; repair retained 124 scopes / 1,042,704 bytes, retired the cold token, and kept the hot token current. The repair run asserts the budget and token behavior.

### Real Gateway continuation and restart

Executed the built release-branch CLI with a disposable state directory, supported Doctor import, real Gateway and embedded agent, and deterministic loopback Responses provider. No operator installation change, live-provider calls, or channel delivery. Workload: 33,000 historical events, three initial replies, and one reply after stopping/restarting the isolated Gateway. The fixture contains 33,010 events including its header/reset/current-context rows.


prs.title: fix(agents): stop model-catalog worker from discarding incrementally-loaded plugins on scope growth
prs.body:
Related: #162230

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated plugin registration when a prepared model catalog expands from its initial provider scope.

## User Impact

Catalog scope growth reuses unchanged plugin registrations and captured source instead of rebuilding them. No configuration, storage format, permission, or public API change is intended.

The historical sustained refresh loop is already addressed by independent main changes, including #160055. This repair targets the remaining bounded scope-growth overhead, not a newly reproduced endless loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep signature matching in the existing plugin loader. During successful same-context catalog promotion, transfer retained registration resources through the inspection owner and adopt instances through the existing lifecycle owner. Abandoned builds leave predecessor custody intact; final successor retirement disposes resources exactly once.

Keep exact-scope reuse and main’s fingerprint replacement/failure invalidation (#169321). Do not reuse predecessor configuration across fingerprint changes. The current-main repair deliberately excludes the older candidate’s cross-fingerprint rollback machinery and Windows source-copy work.

Original report and candidate implementation: @netcrazed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): publish one chat terminal when the message tool delivered the reply
prs.body:
Closes #167271

**AI-assisted: yes.** Authored by an AI coding agent, locally verified; every command and run below was executed in this checkout or on an isolated proof host.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a turn's reply is delivered through the message tool, the Gateway publishes a second chat `final` for the same run containing stale text (often an earlier progress reply), so the Control UI appends it after the real answer and it reappears under the next prompt. A run must publish exactly one terminal reply.

## User Impact

Message-tool-delivered turns show exactly the real answer: no duplicate terminal, no stale progress text appended after the answer, and no resurrection in the next history snapshot. Normal turns, failed/undelivered message-tool turns, and host status notices keep their existing terminal behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The artifact is assembled by `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-source-finalization.ts`. Base suppression relied on a later transcript idempotency lookup that requires `mirror.idempotencyKey` plus an active anchor, so a transcript-owned reply without that identity was re-broadcast. The owner fact already exists: `sourceReplyTranscriptMirror.transcriptOwner` is recorded after the message tool persists its row.

The fix makes that recorded ownership the decision boundary: transcript-owned mirrors are excluded from broadcast content, their prepared `persistedContent` is still retained for media rewrite/attach, and their presence counts as delivered for the drop check (preserving error-terminal semantics). Nothing else is published once only owned mirrors remain; normal turns and non-owner host/status payloads are untouched.

Two follow-ups in this revision:

- **Media-failure fallback.** The first suppression pass cleared the prepared broadcast content for an owned mirror but the final projection still expanded every content state. For a delivered image+caption with no usable persisted lookup key, `backedManagedOutgoingContent` stayed false, so the projection used the "Media reply could not be displayed." fallback and published it as a second terminal even though delivery succeeded. Transcript-owned mirrors are now excluded from the final projection, including that fallback path, while their transcript/media rewrite work still runs. A captioned owned-media regression covers it.
- **Production type error.** The ownership helper passed a possibly-undefined payload to `getReplyPayloadMetadata(object)`, failing `tsgo:core`/`ui`/`extensions` (TS2345). That single error also failed every type shard, the lint shards' plugin-SDK d.ts boundary step, the extension package-boundary compile, and `ci-gate` on the prior head. The helper now narrows the payload before reading metadata.

## Evidence

### Real isolated Gateway run (real agent, real message tool)

Production Gateway server (`src/gateway/server.ts` from this branch) started in-process on a private, isolated state directory and loopback port. The agent runtime, `message` tool, internal source-reply persistence, and finalization path are unmodified production code; only the model responses come from a local deterministic OpenAI-completions endpoint, because no hosted provider credential is available in this environment. The scripted model calls the real `message` tool twice (progress, then a captioned image reply) before its final answer, then a second prompt arrives.

Redacted excerpt:

```text
[check] PASS sessions.subscribe
[check] PASS chat.send accepted (proof-turn-1) :: {"runId":"proof-turn-1","status":"started"}
[check] PASS turn 1 publishes exactly one chat terminal :: {"terminalCount":1,"states":["status","status","status","delta","delta","final"]}
[check] PASS turn 1 terminal does not repeat source-reply content :: {"terminalText":"Both subagents finished."}
[check] PASS no media-failure placeholder in turn 1 events
[check] PASS progress text not re-broadcast as a terminal
[check] PASS message-tool replies persisted in history :: {"assistantRows":5}
[check] PASS owned media attachment persisted in history :: {"mediaRows":1}
[check] PASS progress reply persisted exactly once
[check] PASS chat.send accepted (proof-turn-2)
[check] PASS turn 2 publishes exactly one chat terminal
[check] PASS turn 2 does not resurface the stale progress text
[check] PASS earlier history rows are unchanged by the next prompt :: {"rowsBefore":5,"rowsAfter":6}
[check] PASS first-turn progress row still appears exactly once
[check] PASS the answer is persisted exactly once in the first-turn rows
[proof] ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

The single terminal is the delivered answer; the captioned image reply is persisted once with its managed `artifact_managed_image_…` outgoing route, the progress text "Both A and B are still running." appears in exactly one assistant row, and a later prompt neither re-publishes it nor rewrites earlier history rows.

The same run also drives the **unkeyed owned-mirror variant** through the shipped `sessions.send` RPC (same dispatch and source finalizer, no exact webchat source-turn id). There the message tool persists transcript-owned rows without a delivery-mirror identity, and its progress and captioned-media sends arrive as parallel message-tool calls in one native turn — the path the review flagged:

```text
[check] PASS sessions.send accepted :: {"runId":"proof-sessions-send","status":"started"}
[check] PASS sessions.send turn publishes exactly one chat terminal :: {"terminalCount":1,"states":["status","status","status","final"]}
[check] PASS sessions.send turn does not repeat source-reply progress
[check] PASS sessions.send persisted unkeyed owned-mirror rows (no delivery-mirror identity) :: {"newRows":3,"unkeyedOwnedRows":[{"idempotencyKey":"…:message-tool:…:call_…_0","hasDeliveryMirror":false},{"idempotencyKey":"…:message-tool:…:call_…_1","hasDeliveryMirror":false}]}
[check] PASS cross-session turn leaves earlier history rows unchanged :: {"rowsBefore":6,"rowsAfter":9}
[check] PASS unkeyed turn persisted its own progress row exactly once
[check] PASS unkeyed turn persisted its captioned media answer row
```

Those two persisted rows carry a message-tool idempotency key but no delivery-mirror marker, so the finalizer's committed lookup cannot resolve them: the committed branch is bypassed and only recorded ownership suppresses the re-broadcast. The run still published exactly one terminal, left the earlier rows byte-identical, and kept both owned rows (progress and captioned media) in history.

### Tests

- New regression in `chat.directive-tags.source-media.suite.ts`: message-tool persisted row, caption plus managed image, unusable mirror key; asserts no chat terminal (so no placeholder and no duplicate caption) and that the persisted row keeps its working attachment.
- Updated the existing owned rewrite-refusal case to expect no gateway terminal for an owned mirror.
- Prior evidence retained: the new lifecycle test asserts one sequenced terminal plus stable history for unkeyed text-owned replies.
- Format/lint: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean (0 warnings, 0 errors) on the changed files.
- `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types*`, `check-lint-core-*`, `check-additional-extension-package-boundary`, and changed-node shards are the CI gates for this fix.

**Residual risk.** Failed/undelivered message-tool turns never get `transcriptOwner`, so they keep the existing final/error path; external/non-internal source replies do not persist through this owner and are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(workboard): diagnostics refresh no longer rewrites unchanged cards
prs.body:
Closes #176223

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a board-wide diagnostics refresh (`workboard.cards.diagnostics.refresh` RPC / `workboard_list({ refreshDiagnostics: true })`) rewrote `workboard_cards.updated_at` and emitted a card event for every diagnostics-bearing card on each sweep. That defeated `updated_at`-keyed staleness rules (stale-ready detection, age-based retention), and on a card's *first* observation it reset the activity age, so age-based warnings (`blocked_too_long`, `stranded_ready`) could appear and then flicker off a minute later.

## User Impact

A diagnostics refresh is now observability-only for card activity. Repeated sweeps no longer move `workboard_cards.updated_at` or append routine card events, so `updated_at` reflects real card activity and age-based warnings stay stable; the diagnostic observations shown in card details (first/last seen, occurrence count) stay current.

## Why This Change Was Made

`refreshDiagnostics()` routed every card through the ordinary card-update path, which always advances `updatedAt` and appends an event. This adds a dedicated diagnostic-only write (`recordCardDiagnostics`, new sibling module `store-diagnostics.ts`) that persists the merged diagnostics while keeping the parent row's activity timestamp and event history unchanged, and retains the revision compare-and-swap so concurrent writers are not clobbered. It always merges (so `lastSeenAt`/`count` advance on every refresh) and skips only archived cards and cards with nothing to record. This restores the original observation-persistence intent introduced in `61031d1b` that the later concurrency repair had accidentally dropped.

Both entry points (`workboard.cards.diagnostics.refresh` and the `workboard_list` tool) funnel through this single method, so both are covered.

## Maintainer decision requested (token semantics)

Question: should diagnostic-only refreshes preserve `updatedAt` even though it also serves as the public optimistic-concurrency token? **Recommendation: accept observation-only refreshes.** Why:

- The CAS is intact: `recordCardDiagnostics` writes via `registerIfUpdatedAt(id, row, current.updatedAt)` — the same preserved token. If any real writer advances `updatedAt` between read and write, the refresh loses the CAS and throws `WorkboardCardConflictError`, exactly the protection the concurrency repair added.
- The refresh RPC accepts no `expectedUpdatedAt` and clients do not use it as a concurrency channel; the token-invalidation semantics of the mutation RPCs (`update`/`move`/`delete`/…) are unchanged, because real card mutations still advance `updatedAt` and append events as before.
- This is the behavior of the original design (`61031d1b`): diagnostics are observability data, not card activity.

## Evidence

**Running-Gateway proof (shipped entry point, real transport).** Booted a real `openclaw gateway` process (source checkout, isolated state dir, token auth) with the workboard plugin loaded (`http server listening (1 plugin: workboard)`), connected a real `GatewayClient` over WebSocket (hello-ok), created a blocked card via `workboard.cards.create`, aged it 25h in the persisted store, invoked the shipped `workboard.cards.diagnostics.refresh` RPC twice, and dumped the raw `workboard_cards` / `workboard_card_diagnostics` / `workboard_card_events` rows.
