prs.title: fix(gateway): recover session previews past long hidden transcript tails
prs.body:
Part of #127630

**AI-assisted: yes.** Authored by an AI coding agent; every check below executed against this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

`session.preview`/Talk show an empty preview when a short visible history sits behind a long tool-only (non-projectable) transcript tail. On current main the readers already read bounded tail pages (64 events / 1 MiB, then 1024 / 8 MiB) instead of materializing the whole transcript — but the recovery page stopped at 1,024 events, so a visible history behind a longer `toolResult` tail exhausted the window, the projection produced no items, and `sessions-read` published `status: "empty"`. The same widening loop was duplicated in three places.

This PR adds the final ceiling-sized window and stops widening when the previous page was limited by bytes rather than events, so a byte-capped recovery page no longer re-reads the same 8 MiB tail.

## User Impact

Session previews and Talk model context recover the newest visible messages instead of showing an empty preview (or reading unbounded history) for sessions with long tool-only tails. Short histories and small limits behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New `src/gateway/session-transcript-preview-bounds.ts` owns one bounded widening policy with explicit `SESSION_PREVIEW_SCAN_MAX_EVENTS = 2048` and `SESSION_PREVIEW_SCAN_MAX_BYTES = 8 MiB` ceilings: a small page, a recovery page, and a final ceiling-sized page, stopped early when the requested count is reached or no older events remain.
- The shared policy also stops before a window that cannot make progress: if the previous page selected fewer events than its event cap, the byte budget stopped it, and a next window with the same byte budget would repeat the same tail.
- The exact selected-row count comes from the bounded active-context hydration result (`selectedEventCount`, excluding the session header and injected boundary events) and is carried to Talk through an internal bounded-selection record. Every bounded hydration producer reports it: SQLite, actor-backed incognito history, and the empty-memory snapshot. `SessionManager.onTruncated` stays `() => void`, so this adds no public SDK callback surface. Display and incognito readers report their selected-event counts directly.
- The display preview reader, Talk model-context reader, and incognito in-memory history path all use the shared policy instead of three copies of the old 1,024-event loop.
- Projection stays on the bounded page (`buildSessionPreviewItems`); output shape and ordering are unchanged; the sync reader handles display/incognito, the async reader handles Talk.
- The new module is listed in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`, so the trusted-anchor PR wrapper inventory stays closed over runtime imports.

## Evidence

Regression tests prove the base/fixed split (64 visible rows + 1,500 `toolResult` rows, limit 12):

```text
base reader (1,024-event recovery): status "empty", items []
fixed: newest 12 visible rows (visible 52-63)
Talk model context, limit 16: base [] / fixed newest 16
incognito memory preview: base [] / fixed newest 12
incognito model context (actor-backed hydration), limit 16: base [] / fixed newest 16
byte-capped recovery: stops after [64, 1024] windows instead of repeating 8 MiB
byte-capped Talk page (header + 1,023 selected rows): windows [64, 1024];
  a header-inclusive count regresses to [64, 1024, 2048]
hidden tail beyond the ceiling: [64, 1024, 2048] windows, no unbounded scan
```

Local checks on head `f80d0b291`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/sessions/session-actor-transcript-replica.test.ts
  -> 1 file, 16 tests passed (typed Bounded fixture now reports selectedEventCount: 2)

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --noEmit --incremental false
  -> passed

git diff --check -> clean
```

The removed helper-only `session-transcript-preview-bounds.test.ts` window-count cases are covered by the production reader regressions in `server.sessions.preview-resolve.test.ts` (explicit tail scan ceiling, and Talk byte-cap stopping) and `session-transcript-readers.memory.test.ts` / `session-actor-memory-history.test.ts` (incognito recovery).

### Real behavior proof

Isolated state dir, 64 visible assistant rows + 1,500 `toolResult` rows seeded through the session accessor, local Gateway started from the repo CLI entry with `gateway.mode=local` and auth `none`, then the public RPC:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call sessions.preview \
    --params '{"keys":["main"],"limit":12,"maxChars":120}' --port 39481 --json
{
  "previews": [{
    "key": "main",
    "status": "ok",
    "items": [
      { "role": "assistant", "text": "visible 52" },
      ...
      { "role": "assistant", "text": "visible 63" }
    ]
  }]
}
```

Talk's shipped realtime history boundary (`readTalkRealtimeInitialItems`, called by `talk.client.create`) returned 16 items on the same seeded session:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/proof-talk.mts
{ "kind": "talk-realtime-initial", "count": 16,
  "items": [ "visible 48", ..., "visible 63" ] }
```

Shipped-caller proof (raw log: `.openclaw/proof/178512/shipped-caller-proof.log`). Both scenarios go through `readTalkRealtimeInitialItems` — the exact Talk history function the shipped `talk.client.create` RPC handler invokes. Real isolated state dir, real SQLite store, real incognito memory actor; no mocks. The only instrumentation is a pass-through wrapper around `SessionManager.openBoundedAsync` that records the widening windows the shipped policy requests.

Byte-capped stopping, durable session — 64 visible rows behind 130 x ~64 KiB `toolResult` rows (limit 16 items / 8,000 bytes). The 8 MiB recovery page is byte-limited below its 1,024-event cap, so the shared policy stops; the 2,048-event window (same 8 MiB budget) is never read:

```text
caller: readTalkRealtimeInitialItems (invoked by talk.client.create)
scenario: 64 visible + 130 x ~64 KiB toolResults; limit=16 items / 8,000 bytes
window opens: [{"maxEvents":64,"selectedEvents":15,"truncated":true},
               {"maxEvents":1024,"selectedEvents":127,"truncated":true}]
items: []
```

Incognito model-context recovery through the same shipped caller, on the shipped session-actor storage binding — 64 visible assistant rows + 1,500 `toolResult` rows:

```text
caller: readTalkRealtimeInitialItems (invoked by talk.client.create)
scenario: 64 visible + 1500 toolResults; limit=16 items / 8,000 bytes
count=16
items=[{"role":"assistant","text":"visible 48"}, ...,
       {"role":"assistant","text":"visible 63"}]
```

**Boundary (external service / local peer).** `talk.client.create` resolves a configured realtime voice provider and asserts its secret owner before reading history (`src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-create.ts`). This environment has no live realtime provider credential, and the shipped OpenAI realtime provider cannot be pointed at a local peer in the browser-WebRTC path: `createBrowserSession` throws `OpenAI realtime baseUrl requires gateway-relay; browser WebRTC is not supported` when a `baseUrl` is configured (`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts`), while the non-`baseUrl` path contacts the live provider. With the gateway-relay configuration the handler reaches its browser-session branch and the history read, then fails at provider session creation, so the RPC cannot return a history response. A real isolated Gateway on this caretaker host also fails agent-database activation with a worker timeout when the seeded 8.5 MiB transcript is present, so this lane could not be captured locally. The closest real execution supplied instead is `readTalkRealtimeInitialItems` — the exact function that handler calls (line 190) — against real SQLite stores and the real incognito memory actor; window accounting is pass-through instrumentation, not a mock. Both scenarios are also covered by committed regressions that fail on the base reader. A maintainer with a configured realtime provider can replay the same `talk.client.create` call against the seeded sessions.

**Host limitations.** A full isolated-Gateway repro stalls on the Windows caretaker host (agent-database startup worker timeout under load), so PR CI is authoritative for that lane; the earlier built-Gateway `sessions.preview` RPC evidence above was captured at `301269dec`, whose display path is unchanged at this head.

**CI note.** `check-test-types` passes on this head (the typed `Bounded` fixture fix). `checks-node-changed` is red on `test/gateway-openai-compaction-replay.e2e.test.ts:102` (`"Continue from the compacted transcript"` split length 2 vs 3). The identical failure is present at every head that ran that job (`301269dec`, `6005d42a9`, `89de4013f`, `f80d0b291`), the failing test is not modified by this PR, and its retry path (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts`) is untouched by this diff; the last behavior change there is #178192, merged before this branch's base. Main pushes skip the node CI jobs (verified: node checks are `skipped` on recent `main` check runs), so a same-job main comparison is not available; the repo's own `test:ci-failed` classifier reports `[unknown] No matching job on main` for this job. The failure is deterministic across heads, so a retrigger is not expected to change it. Treat this check as inherited/unattributed, not caused by this change.

**Residual risk / boundary.** A tail longer than the 2,048-event / 8 MiB scan still yields `empty` with no truthful truncation field — surfacing truncation needs a preview result-shape change and is deliberately out of scope here. Byte-heavy tails can stop at the 8 MiB page budget below 2,048 events, and the policy now stops there rather than re-reading the same tail. Oversized single rows remain omitted by the existing SQLite reader; filters needing history older than the ceiling cannot recover. The linked issue's remaining truthful-truncation contract is why this PR is `Part of` rather than closing it.

prs.title: refactor(canvas): render the A2UI v0.8 catalog with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Canvas A2UI v0.8 still loads the upstream Lit catalog and theme context after its host moved to Solid.

## User Impact

The v0.8 Canvas surface now renders through Solid while preserving its host tags, bindings, templated lists, contextual actions, and status feedback. Native inputs and a native dialog replace the catalog's shadow-DOM controls; local date inputs retain the requested calendar date.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore the reviewed v0.8 port from `009e7ccb4976` onto current main, adapt its browser regression to the current shared fixture, and finish the dependency cutover. The existing web_core processor still owns protocol validation, data contexts, and binding writes. The renderer consumes its component tree without adding a second data model.

Remove `@a2ui/lit` from both manifests, its obsolete theme provider and Knip allowances, and the bundle preflight's dependency probe. Update the Solid guide to reflect the v0.8 cutover. **The v0.9 renderer remains unchanged. `@a2ui/web_core` still depends on Lit transitively; this PR deliberately leaves that dependency in the lockfile and adds no override or patch.** No protocol or dependency version changes.

## Evidence

Same-machine comparison against `251c9d69393`:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| v0.8 renderer, raw | 742,978 B | 579,649 B |
| v0.8 renderer, gzip | 166,079 B | 147,667 B (−11.1%) |
| Control UI startup JS, gzip | 325,089 B | 325,089 B |
| Startup CSS requests / gzip | 1 / 38,445 B | 1 / 38,445 B |
| Strict UI performance check | pass | pass |
| Renderer production LOC | 505 | 795 |

The +290 renderer lines replace an external catalog with an owned 18-component renderer; the removed 229-line theme adapter is included in those totals. Whole diff: +831/−291 lines, including +289 lines of browser regression and −33 lockfile lines. Refactor census: controllers 0→0, effects 0→0, render effects 0→0, untrack 1→1, listeners 3→2, DOM queries 0→0, flush/owner escapes 0→0. The surviving untrack captures the existing host-lifetime model; the paired listeners belong to the plain action model.

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | pass |
| Scoped Oxlint / format / `git diff --check` | pass |
| `pnpm test test/scripts/bundled-plugin-assets.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 11 passed; 3.41 s Vitest, 4.83 s runner |
| Targeted production-browser capture, each side | synthetic card, field, list, choices, date, button, modal, Escape dismissal, and edited-field action context pass; no page errors |
| `pnpm ui:build` + `pnpm ui:check-performance --json`, each side | pass; no startup growth |
| `pnpm deadcode:knip` | pass on repaired head; 2m 16.3s; no new ignores |
| Independent review | complete P0–P2 review: five old INDEX-only findings confirmed corrected before commit; ClawSweeper also reviewed `f049fc10d2dd` with no findings or security concern |
| PR CI | `ci:full` applied; run `39482999688` tests repaired head `f049fc10d2dd`. Integrated main fixes: #178617, #178660, #178645. |

The retained browser regression exercises write-through bindings, date/time edits observed in emitted action context, choices, contextual actions in templated rows, and input identity across server updates. It also covers safe/unsafe validation events, horizontal-list scrolling, supplied divider color/thickness, and visible slider values and edits. The migration codemod was retired from main in `399b740ce04`; this restores the already-reviewed Solid implementation rather than reintroducing the retired tool. No `TODO(solid2)` markers remain.

### CI attribution

Full run [39482999688, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39482999688/attempts/2) tests head `f049fc10d2dd` through merge `e73da04f862b6` (main parent `0f9cf386d235`). All 186 jobs are terminal: **164 passed, 20 skipped**, and the inherited receipt job plus its downstream aggregate failed. All three UI unit shards, all nine UI E2E shards, both real-Gateway shards, and security-fast passed. The Blacksmith 32-class job remained unassigned through the coordinator's 30-minute deadline; after confirmed cancellation, the single authorized failed/cancelled-job retry completed and that job passed. No final-attempt coverage is cancelled or pending.

Failed job [118897756246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39482999688/job/118897756246) reports exactly these two cases:

| Failing test | Matching baseline evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Native completion durable receipts > settles a receipt received during queued retirement without an undelivered note | 120,000 ms timeout on both CI and untouched merge base `b7c858fcf245` |
| Native completion durable receipts > keeps a durable delivery receipt when its next ownership read fails | Line 112: expected `failedReads` 1, received 0 on both CI and that merge base |

The exact-name baseline command ran once: 2 failed, 3 filtered/skipped, 312.07 s. The relevant Codex app-server files are unchanged between the replayed base and CI main parent; the Canvas diff does not touch them. These are inherited failures, not passing coverage. No different failure receives this attribution. Automatic CI classification timed out, so native inherited-failure admission uses the exact-name baseline reproduction, unchanged source objects, actual checkout attestation, and complete final job inventory.

The independently reviewed catalog wait fix #178617, speech timeout fix #178660, and main's widget timing fix #178645 are integrated. The original Control UI startup comparison remains applicable because the renderer repairs stay inside the existing lazy Canvas catalog. The repair reran the Canvas build, targeted production-browser captures, UI typecheck, scoped lint/format, and production Knip.

### Synthetic Canvas host screenshots

Screenshots use the built v0.8 renderer, synthetic data, and the same viewport on both sides.

**Catalog before**

![Canvas v0.8 catalog before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22f0b4d2-2e8e-44fd-b4fe-007ac4e554ce)

**Modal before**

![Canvas v0.8 modal before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/249b5a00-14d7-43f4-88e2-6447b04b592e)



### Review corrections

Reproduced and fixed all five ClawSweeper findings through the built Canvas entry point: unsafe validation patterns bypassed the public checker, the textarea used for `longText` ignored HTML pattern validation, horizontal cards shrank instead of scrolling, dividers lost color/thickness, and sliders lost their displayed number. The renderer now consumes web_core's public `isSafeRegex` owner and preserves upstream's ordinary text input for `longText`; there is no second regex policy. The checker increases the lazy bundle relative to the first revision, so the final reduction is 11.1%, not the earlier 21.5% claim. v0.9 remains byte-identical.

The image usage-hint suggestion does not describe a new regression: the pinned upstream image already uses width:100%, and the existing OpenClaw theme supplies no hint-specific classes. That behavior is preserved. The collapsed-choice suggestion was also checked through the repaired bundle: Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2 both keep options hidden → visible → hidden across closed/open/closed states, with matching hit-test results and no page errors. No CSS workaround is needed.

The following inspected synthetic captures show the corrected catalog/modal and the review-regression fixture before/after repair. No real or private data appears.

prs.title: fix(state): name the failing state database when gateway startup admission hits a corrupted store
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #177440

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw gateway run` against a corrupted state database would see `Reason: database disk image is malformed` without the failing file's path, turning systemd restart loops into multi-cycle debugging sessions (the reporter's fleet lost three debug cycles before a manual replica run surfaced the real stack on a WAL-truncated database).
- **Related:** #177440 — the clawsweeper issue review confirmed current main still loses the known pathname when a schema-read exception traverses both startup catches; the generic foreground-gateway `Reason:` line itself was already added by #172107 / #172053.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** every gateway-startup schema-read refusal now identifies the inspected store — `OpenClaw state database <path> failed startup inspection: <underlying error>` reaches ordinary stderr through the existing CLI renderer.
- **Out of scope:** no global error-output changes and no stacks by default; typed refusal classification (instanceof / name / cause matching in `isStartupConfigRefusal`) is untouched because the annotation happens in place on the original error at the startup rethrow.
- **Highest-risk area:** the startup rethrow in `preflightOpenClawDatabaseSchemas`; cancellation reasons must keep flowing to their abort owner unmodified.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** annotation only applies when the failure is an `Error` whose message does not already contain the pathname, and never while the admission signal is aborted.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** on a corrupted or truncated state database, `openclaw gateway run` prints the exact file it could not inspect before the doctor hint; exit status, redaction, and debug-only stack behavior are unchanged.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `annotateStartupStateInspectionFailure` in `src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-migration-required.ts`, the startup rethrow in `src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.ts`, and the regression test `names the failing state database when gateway startup admission hits a corrupted store` in `src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.schema-only.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** yes — an isolated state dir initialized via `openclaw doctor`, main state database truncated to 512 bytes, then `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<dir> node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run` executed from this PR's worktree (Node v26.7.0).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp> node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts doctor    # initialize a valid state DB
  truncate -s 512 <tmp>/state/openclaw.sqlite                                    # corrupt the main file
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp> node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-migration-required.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.schema-only.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/failure-output.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-schema-preflight.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json --builders 1
  pnpm tsgo:core
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
  [openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw state database /tmp/oc-e2e-177440-aMES/state/openclaw.sqlite failed startup inspection: database disk image is malformed
  [openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
  ```
  Exit status 1 (unchanged). With `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` the same message leads the stack trace; stacks remain debug-only. The new regression test passes: the thrown startup refusal contains both the state path and `not a database|disk image is malformed`.
- **Observed result after fix:** ordinary stderr now names both the failing file and the underlying SQLite error; redaction, exit status, and stack gating are unchanged.
- **Before evidence:** on origin/main the same corrupted-database run prints `Reason: database disk image is malformed` with no path, and the regression test fails with `expected 'file is not a database' to contain '<state dir>/state/openclaw.sqlite'`.
- **What was not tested:** agent-store admission refusals were not changed (they already carry their own per-store paths); PostgreSQL-backed state startup was not exercised.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review. CI lanes pending.

Note: `src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.ts` already exceeds the advisory `max-lines` lint budget on origin/main (704 counted lines); this PR keeps the counted total unchanged (net +0) and adds no suppressions.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PowerShell completion falls back to filenames or root options after a quoted subcommand, such as `openclaw 'completion' --shell f` or `openclaw 'models' 'auth' --`.

## User Impact

User impact: quoted literal subcommands receive the same completions as their unquoted equivalents. Regenerate and reload installed PowerShell completion scripts to pick up the fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command-path parser now uses PowerShell's parsed value for string literals, so quote delimiters no longer become part of the command name. Other expressions retain their existing handling and are never evaluated.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through `pnpm openclaw completion --shell powershell` and native PowerShell 7.6.5 completion on the unchanged base: both quote styles lost the `fish` choice, and quoted nested commands lost `--agent`; the unquoted controls worked.

prs.title: perf(agents): retain workspace snapshots after owner writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A populated workspace refreshes its attestation during ordinary turn preparation. The committed receipt discarded the workspace snapshot, so the next turn reopened a registration read solely to recover facts the writer already held. The extra operation costs five SQL statements and one worker request on the measured populated-workspace path.

## User Impact

Populated-workspace preparation reuses the state just committed by the workspace owner, avoiding a redundant database read on the next turn. Disappearance protection, reseeding authority, and persisted attestation freshness remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Publish complete setup/attestation snapshots from the existing transaction kernels and install them in the existing bounded workspace cache. Workspace deletion publishes a keyed tombstone; alias changes and uncertain outcomes still invalidate cached resolutions. No SQL shape, schema, transaction boundary, or final filesystem/recovery/authority check changes.

Retain the attestation timestamp refresh even when hashes match. Suppressing it would shorten the persisted 24-hour disappearance protection after a restart and could authorize reseeding a workspace that was active recently. The existing restart regression explicitly covers this contract. This change removes the redundant snapshot request; it does not claim to remove the seven-statement attestation write.

## Evidence

The two changed regressions fail against the unchanged base: populated consecutive preparations dispatch the extra snapshot operation, and reading after a setup write dispatches another worker request. The runtime-identical implementation passes six focused workspace owner/sibling files: 100 tests passed and one existing platform-specific case skipped, using the pinned Bun runtime. Both changed files were rerun on final head `194c4230ca58`: all 22 tests pass. Coverage includes disappearance/reseed behavior, timestamp durability across restart, recovery holds, alias repair, rollback, and lost replies.

Two Codex review rounds found no actionable P0–P2 issues. CI caught a type-only publication/kernel import cycle; shared types now live in a leaf contract and all direct consumers are migrated. The final Madge scan reports zero cycles. PostgreSQL owner review approved the publication change, with approval extended to the final head after verifying the type-only move and main integration. Production/test typechecks, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, export collisions, and database worker/dialect ratchets pass. Local whole-tree checks reproduce three existing UI max-lines suppression findings and four test-shard root-budget findings on the exact baseline. Final Knip has one production finding (`extensions/agentsapi/config.ts: DEFAULT_NATIVE_TOOLS`), zero full-tree findings, and zero script findings. The sole production finding also reproduces on main `e8839dc75f92`; the affected source and Knip config are identical, so this PR adds no findings.

All three alternating populated-workspace v3.1 fixture pairs passed, including restart and shutdown. Values below are SQL / requests / MAIN, each as median [min–max].

| Scope | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Warm turn (per-run median) | 58 [58–58] / 13 [13–13] / 0 [0–0] | 53 [53–53] / 12 [12–12] / 0 [0–0] |
| Whole workload | 3199 [3193–3205] / 826 [814–829] / 98 [98–98] | 3119 [3118–3119] / 812 [810–816] / 98 [98–98] |

The attributable saving is exactly **75 SQL / 15 requests per workload** in every pair: `workspace.snapshotAndRegister` falls from 89 / 18 to 14 / 3. This removes ten warm requests, three second-session requests, one cron request, and one restart-first-turn request. The removed envelope is BEGIN + three parameterized SELECTs + COMMIT. Initial preparation remains 9 SQL / 2 requests; required post-restart preparation remains 5 / 1. `workspace.replaceAttestation` stays at 7 / 1 per warm turn and 113 / 16 per workload.

The raw whole-workload median difference (−80 SQL / −14 requests) includes conditional/background variation and is not the causal saving. Shared warm-read families show no increase, including paired individual-turn outliers. Outside warm turns, observed variations include up to +1 exact-entry fact statement/request, ±2 row-fact statements, and +1 whole-workload entry-cache statement; no touched workspace operation increases. One baseline alone has a 30-SQL `installStatusTracking` burst. No latency claim on the loaded host.

The required security checks pass and no current-head CI job failed. A maintainer-authorized runner-backlog exception covers nine jobs still queued without an assigned runner since 19:57 UTC: `check-lint`, `check-lint-core-1`, `check-lint-core-2`, `check-test-types`, and `check-test-types-core-1` through `check-test-types-core-5`. The exact-head local equivalents passed: changed-file type-aware oxlint/format checks, production types, and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` across **all 29 test type groups**. Madge, export collisions, worker/dialect ratchets, and all 22 changed-file tests also pass; the inherited Knip finding is documented above. The pending CI jobs are not being reported as green. The separate empty-workspace pair passed: warm counts remain 46 [46–46] SQL / 11 [11–11] requests / 0 MAIN on both sides, with identical counts in all ten paired warm turns and unchanged workspace operations. Raw whole totals are 3023 / 792 / 98 → 3030 / 797 / 98; the increase comes from background lifecycle/prewarm/archive work, not workspace operations. All eight measurement arms passed without retry.

Production delta: +42 lines; tests: +22 lines. The added receipt decoding/application replaces invalidation-only publication and eliminates the repeat registration read. No new cache, manager, refresh timer, schema, or configuration surface.

prs.body:

Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

type: user-facing description

Related: [openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#1705](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1705), the companion Reactor welcome-screen consumer of this Gateway catalog.

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Native clients need the connected Gateway's welcome text and starter prompts without copying the web strings and manually keeping them synchronized.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: native clients can display the same localized welcome hint, recent-chats label, and ordered starter prompts as the installed web dashboard. Existing web copy and layout remain unchanged.

This is an additive, authenticated `operator.read` method. Older Gateways remain unsupported rather than silently receiving copied native strings. Missing or invalid installed assets return actionable `UNAVAILABLE`; restart the Gateway after updating its installation. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

`controlUi.welcome.get({ locale? })` returns a versioned catalog with requested/resolved locale and stable suggestion IDs, display text, and send text. The renderer and build generator share one ordering/key owner, the existing English catalog and translation-memory materializer, and the same locale fallback rules.

Normal runtime postbuild generates and packages the 21-locale artifact. The Gateway lazily reads and validates it once per process, with retry after a failed load. Requests do not fetch GitHub, scrape compiled JavaScript, load UI source, or require the Control UI HTTP server. Agent identity and recent-session data keep their existing owners.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Local validation used Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.7.0 on Windows:

- `pnpm test test\scripts\control-ui-welcome-catalog.test.ts ui\src\i18n\lib\registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed, 14 tests. The integration changes the English source and verifies both the web translator and generated installed-catalog RPC receive it; stale translations fall back to current English. It also covers invalid parameters, missing/corrupt assets, repair/retry, ordering, and locale negotiation.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and `pnpm tsgo:scripts`: passed.
- `node scripts\run-tsgo.mjs -p test\tsconfig\tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental`: passed.
- Type-aware lint passed for every changed production, build-script, and test TypeScript file using the repository's matching core/scripts/root-test configurations.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm ui:welcome:check`, `node scripts\check-docs-mdx.mjs docs\gateway\protocol\operator-methods.md`, targeted Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- All normal `pnpm build` phases completed through guarded recovery after host file-metadata instability; this was not an uninterrupted green invocation or a runtime-only build. Canonical `package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` packaging with `--allow-unreleased-changelog --skip-build --pnpm-pack` passed its required bundled-dependency, extraction, inventory, and import-graph checks. The packaged welcome catalog matches the generated artifact byte-for-byte.

**Known gaps:** a later combined test run passed the catalog integration again but the existing `src\gateway\server-methods-list.test.ts` suite failed before test execution when compiler snapshot preparation reported changed metadata for `extensions\xai\package.json`. Its later UI shard did not run; the earlier 13 browser-locale tests passed. The UI build printed a startup-gzip budget violation: 373,503 bytes against 373,454 bytes (49 bytes over). Full repository checks/tests and installed native-client RPC proof are not claimed. The required shared autoreview helper was attempted but its reviewer service returned `401 Unauthorized`; no independent review result is claimed.

The latest integration test body took 1.587 seconds and its file took 22.21 seconds locally; the earlier combined 14-test run took 173.71 seconds. CI seconds have not been measured. No visual change is intended.

prs.title: fix(chat): preview HEIC photos before sending
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes broken image previews and unreadable image attachments when users upload or paste HEIC/HEIF photos in web chat.

## User Impact

HEIC photos now show a working thumbnail and full-size preview before sending. Uploads and pastes are converted to JPEG, including files whose browser MIME type is missing or generic. Failed conversions remain removable without discarding valid sibling attachments.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize HEIC through the existing queued, cancellable image-preparation worker before registering the attachment payload. Conversion is bounded to a 5 MiB source/output limit, 25 million decoded pixels, a 4096-pixel output edge, and the existing active-processing timeout.

The pure JavaScript decoder preserves the current Content Security Policy. Its measured 751.9 KiB gzip cost is loaded only when preparing a HEIC file. A dedicated guard allows one deferred decoder asset up to 768 KiB gzip, rejects initial/chat/new startup preloads, keeps it in total JavaScript accounting, and preserves the ordinary 215 KiB chunk cap.

## Evidence

- Browser coverage passes: HEIC/HEIF upload, generic MIME input, untyped clipboard paste, decoded thumbnail, lightbox, and JPEG `chat.send` payloads; all 4 tests in the attachment-errors suite pass.
- 29 neighboring attachment/lifecycle tests pass. The focused performance suites pass all 31 tests, including over-budget, duplicate, startup-preload, and lookalike-name rejection.
- Focused type, lint, and format checks pass; the Control UI build succeeds. Independent P0–P2 reviews of the behavior, paste handling, and budget guard found no actionable findings.
- The existing startup-size warning remains visible: 325,418 B gzip versus a 325,166 B limit; the pre-change build was already over that limit at 325,398 B. Startup limits and baselines are unchanged. PR CI will provide the current-head broad result.

Before and after, using a synthetic green HEIC fixture:

| --- | --- |
| ![Before: HEIC photo shows a broken composer preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84790324-93ec-4567-af52-24eaebbfd7ce) | ![After: HEIC photo shows a decoded green composer preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60190966-658d-4421-be87-f013534e673d) |

Closes #161863

**AI-assisted: yes.** Authored by an AI coding agent, locally verified, every command below executed in this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the self-updater's completion notice can be silently dropped with `Transcript idempotency key "update-run-finished:<uuid>" conflicts with the admitted message`. The update succeeds, but the run record is missing its completion entry.

Two owners wrote the finished notice under the same transcript key (`update-run-notice.runtime.ts` and the restart sentinel). The rendered text depends on terminal status, and a terminal outcome legitimately changes (an interrupted `failed` run is reopened and finished `succeeded`), so the second writer can propose different text for the same key. The delivery receipt is written after the append, so a crash/failure between them leaves the key admitted with stale text and every later attempt conflicts.

## User Impact

The update's own completion notice is delivered exactly once and its run record records `noticeDelivered` truthfully, even when the terminal outcome changed between snapshots or an earlier attempt crashed after admission. Genuinely different messages under that key still fail closed instead of being swallowed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New single owner `src/gateway/update-run-finished-notice.ts` (`deliverUpdateRunFinishedNotice`), called by both writers. It re-reads the ledger immediately before rendering so the payload is stable, returns early when the receipt is already set, and falls back to the caller's captured wording only if the ledger read fails.
- On a typed `TranscriptIdempotencyConflictError`, the owner reconciles only when the admitted assistant message under that exact key matches this renderer's terminal notice text (`isUpdateRunTerminalNoticeText`), then records `noticeDelivered: true`. It never appends on reconciliation, so no duplicate notice is possible; arbitrary/foreign/in-progress text still fails closed.
- The conflict error type is preserved across the state-worker boundary (`src/state/openclaw-state-worker-error-identity.ts`) so typed handling survives the worker hop.
- Review follow-up: the rejection regression now keeps `finishUpdateRun()`'s finished record and passes it to the notifier. It previously passed the original running snapshot, so `renderUpdateRunNotice(run, "finished")` returned null, the notifier exited at its rendering gate, and the seeded in-progress transcript message never reached the conflict-rejection path; the test could pass even with terminal-message validation removed.

No new config, session flag, transcript key, or second notice owner; route-delivery receipts are untouched.

## Evidence

### Running-Gateway proof on a state upgraded from OpenClaw 2026.10.5

Isolated state dir (temp, loopback, no external services, no real credentials). It was first used by the released `openclaw@2026.10.5` Gateway (`gateway run --dev --auth none`), which wrote existing settings (`openclaw.json`, `lastTouchedVersion: 2026.10.5`) and a state DB whose `PRAGMA user_version` was 20. Current main requires the documented doctor step for that jump, so `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (PR head `d8e37aae`) migrated the same state to `user_version = 29` and retained the pre-migration SQLite backup:

```text
# state written by the released 2026.10.5 Gateway
PRAGMA user_version -> 20
# after openclaw doctor --fix on the PR head
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: <state>/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-<id>.bak
PRAGMA user_version -> 29
```

The PR-head Gateway then ran on that upgraded state (`gateway run --port <loopback> --auth none`). Each scenario seeds the update state an interrupted updater leaves behind (terminal run + durable restart sentinel), lets the real Gateway start and drain its restart-sentinel wake, reads the run back through the shipped `gateway call update.runs.get` RPC, and reads transcript rows back through the shipped session accessor.

**1. Fresh completion** — terminal failed run, no admitted notice (run `24d55178-…`):

```text
seed: status=failed reason=restart-unhealthy; transcript before: 1 pre-upgrade message
gateway run: [gateway] starting... (listening on loopback)
# restart-sentinel wake delivered the completion notice
gateway call update.runs.get -> "verification": {"noticeDelivered": true}
transcript:
  - "Existing session transcript preserved from the pre-upgrade install."
  - update-run-finished:24d55178-…
    "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish updating.\nFor details, open Settings → Updates in the Control UI or run `openclaw update status` in your terminal."
```

**2. Conflicting-notice reconciliation** — the run settled `succeeded` while an earlier `failed` terminal notice was already admitted under the run's one completion key (the crash window this fix targets; run `c21f06a3-…`):

```text
seed: status=succeeded; admitted failed notice under update-run-finished:c21f06a3-…; receipt absent
after Gateway start and wake:
  update.runs.get -> "status": "succeeded", "verification": {"noticeDelivered": true}
  transcript -> exactly one notice for that key (the earlier failed headline is retained, no duplicate append)
```

**3. Non-terminal rejection** — an in-progress payload under the same completion key must fail closed (run `b55789c2-…`):

```text
seed: status=succeeded; admitted in-progress notice ("🔁 Checking that OpenClaw is ready…")
      under update-run-finished:b55789c2-…; receipt absent
after Gateway start and wake:
  update.runs.get -> "verification": {}   (no noticeDelivered)
  transcript -> unchanged, one in-progress message under that key
  Gateway log (restart-sentinel wake):
    [restart-sentinel] internal restart notice append failed; falling back to wake:
    Transcript idempotency key "update-run-finished:b55789c2-…" conflicts with the admitted message.
    sessionKey=agent:main:main
```

### Data-model compatibility

- The diff adds no persisted schema, transcript, ledger, or config migration; existing formats are read and written by the same owners.
- The state above was written by the released 2026.10.5 Gateway (`user_version = 20`), migrated by the documented doctor step, then served by the PR-head Gateway: the existing `openclaw.json` settings and the pre-upgrade transcript message were still present and readable after the upgrade (scenario 1).
- A run record written before this change (no `noticeDelivered`) decoded and received its receipt through the new reconciliation path (scenarios 1 and 2).

### Checks

- Touched file `src/gateway/update-run-notice.test.ts` has 7 cases; the follow-up only changes which snapshot the notifier receives (same case count).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched file: pass; `git diff --check`: pass.
- **Known local gap.** A local touched-test shard could not complete on the shared build machine (the repo's vitest worker build, then the no-output watchdog, on a 100% CPU host); the required CI checks (`checks-node-changed`, `check-test-types`) are the authoritative result on this head.

prs.title: feat(telegram): embed local files in rich messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Closes #128992. With `channels.telegram.richMessages: true`, permitted local photos, videos, audio, and voice files can appear inside rich replies. Explicit document, voice-note, and video-note sends retain their selected native routes; unsupported attachments remain ordinary attachments. Existing accounts that enabled rich messages receive eligible local media inline under that same opt-in. When Telegram rejects a rich page, plain-text fallback preserves the original payload attachment order and every repeated occurrence. For example, `[document, photo]` remains `[document, photo]` instead of becoming `[photo, document]`. Files already delivered in accepted rich pages are not sent again. ## Implementation - Resolve files through the existing host media-access contract and grammY multipart transport. Code examples and unsupported markup do not read files; caller media roots still apply. - Track each payload occurrence by its original index, independently of the per-path read cache. Keep ordinary batching, cancellation, reply ownership, inline controls, and partial-delivery receipts. - Discover HTML media with the existing quote-aware tokenizer and canonical attribute parser. Apostrophes, quoted `>` characters, source-like text inside other attributes, and encoded ampersands no longer hide or corrupt the actual local source. - Expose the canonical Markdown image-span parser through the existing text-chunking SDK subpath. Adjust the handwritten surface budgets by exactly two exports (function + result type) and one callable; add no wildcard exports or new subpath. - Integrate main `4d2504ccb5b0a141375fbc28a02044771209d617`, preserving its unified rich-block/Markdown splitter and attaching matched local media to each resulting page. Retain the upstream SDK surface comments and add only this feature's two exports and one callable. The existing `richMessages` opt-in remains the product choice for maintainer review. This update does not add another configuration switch. ## Evidence Current candidate: `0b9743b2c2538e65e73bfd8b112496f6ab22dd3a` (2026-10-19). Merge conflicts are resolved against main `4d2504ccb5b0a141375fbc28a02044771209d617`. **Live Telegram source-outbound proof at `5a1ac7d2ad71979201fa6cf05f960618656cc509`.** The candidate's outbound adapter sent synthetic files through a configured Telegram Bot API in a non-leased environment. Cases exercise `richMessages: true` and an explicit `false` control override with isolated runtime state. The installed Gateway was not updated or restarted. | Case | Actual Telegram Bot API trace | Result | |---|---|---| | Native control (`richMessages=false`) | `sendPhoto` 200 | One ordinary photo; no rich request. | | Existing opt-in, repeated file | `sendRichMessage` 200 | Two photo blocks from two occurrences of the same local file. | | Quoted HTML sources | `sendRichMessage` 200 | Four correct uploads: apostrophe in filename, quoted `>` in an attribute, source-like text inside another attribute, and `&` in the path. | | Mixed attachment rejection | `sendRichMessage` 400 `RICH_MESSAGE_DEPTH_INVALID` → `sendMessage` 200 → `sendDocument` 200 → `sendMediaGroup` 200 | Fallback order is text, document, photo, photo; both repeated occurrences and all four receipt IDs are retained. | | Partial acceptance | First `sendRichMessage` 200 → second `sendRichMessage` 400 `RICH_MESSAGE_DEPTH_INVALID` → `sendMessage` 200 → `sendDocument` 200 → `sendPhoto` 200 | First 50-photo page stays delivered; fallback sends only the document and remaining photo. The accepted 50 are not resent; all four receipt IDs are retained. | The two rejection cases explicitly inject excessive details nesting into the selected serialized outgoing request. Telegram itself returns the real 400; responses are not simulated. This exercises recovery after server rejection, not a claim that normal authored content bypasses the depth normalizer. An initial unmodified 20-level authored case was correctly clamped to 15 and accepted; that attempted rejection setup remains recorded as unsuccessful and is not counted as rejection proof. Only the two rejection scenarios were rerun. **Recipient verification.** Separate recipient-side protocol readback confirms all five successful cases, including the actual attachment order and all 51 photo occurrences in the partial-acceptance case. Rich-message previews are expanded using `messages.getRichMessage` before counting blocks. Downloaded documents match the synthetic source bytes exactly; downloaded photos match decoded pixels after Telegram reencoding (maximum mean absolute RGB error 1.8214/255). The initial accepted depth-normalization observation was reconciled separately. **Recipient screenshots.** [Nine cropped Android Telegram screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/133406#issuecomment-6277125562) cover all five cases above, including the complete final native photo after partial acceptance. The retained pixels match the original phone screenshots; only private UI and unrelated messages were cropped out. All nine GitHub image attachments were verified to load publicly and match the prepared PNG bytes. The partial-acceptance total of 50 rich photos plus one fallback photo is established by protocol readback; the screenshots show rendering and the delivery boundary. **Source equivalence after the live run.** The follow-up commit `0b9743b2c2538e65e73bfd8b112496f6ab22dd3a` only renames three shadowing local bindings in `extensions/telegram/src/outbound-adapter.normalize-payload.test.ts` and formats that test. Production sources, configuration, dependencies, fixture values, assertions, and expected payload shapes are unchanged. The existing test file passes 16/16 cases after the rename (91.42 s wrapper wall / 84.54 s Vitest); direct type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Live sends were not repeated for this test-only change. **Compatibility.** Six persisted synthetic configurations, covering nine effective-account cases, pass the canonical config loader and Telegram schema on live-tested `5a1ac7d2ad71979201fa6cf05f960618656cc509`: absent setting, root opt-in/out, account overrides, and named default account. Explicit HTML mode retains its native behavior; invalid string booleans are rejected; every persisted fixture remains byte-identical after loading. This PR adds no configuration-schema, database-schema, or migration change. These checks do not claim a packaged-Gateway upgrade or database migration test. **Validation on the live-tested revision.** - 120 tests passed across six Telegram files: rich local media, text delivery, HTML mapping (79; 116.61 s wrapper wall / 107.35 s Vitest), payload normalization, button types, and channel-action contracts (41; 48.02 s wrapper wall / 43.48 s Vitest). - Canonical SDK surface: 3,812 public exports, 2,209 callables, zero wildcard re-exports; no unauthorized removals from shipped v2026.10.5. Package-export synchronization passed. - Type-aware lint and formatting passed for the two conflict-resolution files. Diff whitespace, changed-source line-cap, and assertion-safety checks passed. Independent source review of the integrated change reported no new actionable findings. - The max-lines check reports three existing UI suppressions (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`). Those files, the baseline, and the validator are byte-identical to integrated main; this failure is inherited. No unrelated UI files were changed. - The standard lint wrapper's broad SDK declaration preparation was stopped after excessive host memory/swap use. Direct targeted type-aware lint completed. A complete build and broad typecheck are not claimed locally; hosted CI results and the test-only follow-up are described below. **Hosted CI on the current candidate.** The [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39314532310/job/118277329737) and [PR context and evidence check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39314588378/job/118272649432) pass on `0b9743b2c2538e65e73bfd8b112496f6ab22dd3a`; the current-head snapshot has no failed or pending checks. The previous candidate's [checks-node-changed-compact-large-25](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39308539302/job/118252639076) failed the existing image-generation test `uses the canonical image cap when mediaMaxMb is non-finite` (58 pass, one expects 6,291,456 bytes and receives `Infinity`). Its implementation and test are byte-identical to integrated main. That older run also reported three `no-shadow` errors, fixed by the test-only follow-up above. These historical failures do not describe the current candidate's CI result. **Remaining review gates.** Current recipient screenshots are linked above; historical screenshots below remain evidence for their recorded older heads only. The live run uses a non-leased Telegram route and exercises the source outbound adapter rather than full packaged-Gateway startup. Maintainers still need to accept this proof scope and decide whether the existing `richMessages` opt-in should enable eligible local attachments and whether the two SDK exports are appropriate.
Historical validation and live screenshots from the previous PR head Candidate: `6da8d970ea79a322da38be05a3a1bbfee406c8c4`. **Review finding: repeated attachments.** A new adapter case sends one payload with the same permitted local photo twice and simulates a `RICH_MESSAGE_MEDIA_INVALID` rejection. It asserts that the rejected rich message carried two photo blocks, that the fallback sends one plain `sendMessage` and one `sendMediaGroup` whose two uploads both match the fixture bytes, and that the receipt keeps all three message IDs. Negative control on this head: with only the resolver reverted to its pre-fix version, exactly this case fails (1 of 29; the fallback sends a single `sendPhoto`); with the fix, 29 of 29 pass. Cost: the rich-local-media test file with `--maxWorkers=1` takes 23.8 s command wall (19.9 s Vitest); the new case runs in 56 ms. **Live proof at this head, with recipient screenshots.** The candidate's own outbound adapter sent three cases through the server's bot and local Bot API to a private owner chat in 30.3 s. A relay recorded only Bot API methods, statuses, errors, and message IDs: | Case | Payload | Bot API trace | Delivered | |---|---|---|---| | A | Markdown inline local photo, plus local video and audio attachments | `sendRichMessage` 200 | one rich message (73488) | | B | The same local photo attached twice | `sendRichMessage` 200 | one rich message showing both occurrences (73489) | | C | 20 nested `details` (a real depth rejection), plus the same photo twice | `sendRichMessage` 400 `RICH_MESSAGE_DEPTH_INVALID` → `sendMessage` 200 → `sendMediaGroup` 200 | plain text and both photos; receipt keeps 73490, 73491, 73492 | Recipient view in the author's Telegram Desktop client, cropped to the bot messages (files: [`proof/133406-live`](https://github.com/aspalagin/openclaw/tree/0571d51171c0a869c8040e19fbce53d6a58a10e9)): | A | B | C: fallback text | C: fallback album | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | | In the fallback text, `repeat.png` marks each place an embedded file appeared; the files follow as ordinary attachments. **Other validation at this head** (host, memory-capped): - Tests: 32 Telegram test files that import changed modules, including the six Telegram test files in this PR: 719 passed. Markdown image-span, SDK text-chunking, and format-capability tests: 17 passed. - Types: `tsgo` core, extensions, and packages tests. The full extension test-type graph exceeds this host's 8 GB cap, so the Telegram tests were typechecked in a focused graph of every Telegram test plus the full graph's global declaration files and lib references: 0 errors. - Type-aware oxlint on the 21 changed TypeScript files, oxfmt, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. The max-lines ratchet flagged only a stale `extensions/msteams` baseline entry that exists at this PR's base and is already removed on current main. - An independent static review of the fix found no correctness issues. The four live cases recorded at `35a2ff57a5150ce9fc36509231acf776b009d509`, including a Markdown upload named `chart(1).png` and literal local-file examples with zero file reads, remain evidence for that SHA. The owner selected the Telegram bot and Bot API already configured in the server's OpenClaw as the live test environment. Checks use the candidate's own source sender, synthetic fixtures, a private owner chat, and isolated state; the working Gateway and its configuration were unchanged. Packaged Gateway startup and the Convex-leased Test Server environment were not exercised. Acceptance of the recorded evidence remains a maintainer decision.

prs.title: fix(agents): clear emoji/avatar on agents.update empty or null
prs.body:
<!-- maintainer-local-candidate-119930 -->
## Maintainer status — local candidate, not published

**This PR remains open at contributor head `a86cfd4e370614dfbbaffc05b23a26dd9710af0c`.** The integration described here is an uncommitted, unpublished maintainer candidate (staged tree `4862cde3fbe12995820c4fc4b088fe9988ce170b`), not the current PR branch. Original work and contributor ancestry from @zyw02 are preserved.

### Proposed repair and user impact

Related: #119929. Remove → Save clears a stored avatar; clearing the custom emoji input clears that stored value. The proposed API clear contract is explicit `null`; empty, whitespace, and omitted API fields preserve existing values.

On a configuration-write failure after the identity file changes, the candidate saves the previous bytes (or a prior-absence marker) and returns an actionable pending-recovery error. It never restores or deletes the current identity file, which may contain a newer external edit. Operators must compare the recovery artifact, current file, and configuration before retrying and remove the artifact after reconciliation. **This is not automatic rollback or a multi-file transaction.** The earlier conditional-rollback claims below are historical contributor notes, not an accepted correctness claim.

Current ownership checks, authenticated avatar rendering, generated protocol declarations, and legacy Swift initializer call shapes are retained. Text-only default avatars do not expose a misleading Remove action after reload.

### Candidate validation

- The unchanged baseline reproduced the null-schema failure and all four failed-config recovery cases.
- Focused protocol, identity-file, agent-config, Gateway, and UI suite: 221 tests passed before the final UI regression additions.
- Final acceptance passed all four selected Vitest shards: Gateway mutation coverage, 38 UI tests, a real Gateway serving the built Control UI, and SDK coverage. One optional external-live SDK test was skipped; this is not authenticated external-service proof.
- The real served-UI test verifies empty/omitted RPC preservation, Remove → Save, persisted config/file clearing, unrelated Markdown preservation, and browser reload with no remaining Remove action.
- 16 final validation lanes passed. Unavailable/failing final lanes: FINAL-LINT-APPS, FINAL-MACOS-CI. See limitations below. Task-file lint and Swift generated-output consistency passed. These are local results, not exact-head CI.

### Inspected served-UI proof

These sanitized, synthetic-state screenshots are from the **unpublished candidate** and a real local Gateway, not a mocked Gateway.

Before removing the stored avatar and custom emoji:

![Before Remove and Save — unpublished maintainer candidate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c4beb5b-4ef2-4896-a437-51dbd9f7e1df)

After Save and browser reload (generic avatar and default emoji placeholder, no saved custom values):

![After Save and reload — unpublished maintainer candidate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee70a744-4b3b-4a29-bbf1-e2540589eed0)

### Remaining gates

Independent source-bound review remains unavailable under the inherited quota hold; no unchanged retry or provider switch was made. Explicit additive-null/pending-recovery contract acceptance and current required owner review remain pending. Swift compatibility compilation/tests, app lint, and the macOS CI lane (142 passed, 10 failed) are blocked by this host's unaccepted Xcode license/SourceKit setup; generated-output consistency is not compilation or lint proof. Originating-chat screenshot delivery is not established by this PR update. Reviewed publication, exact-head CI, and native landing remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor notes for the published head (not current maintainer validation)</summary>

## Review feedback addressed

Follow-up on `479698f24256882db910081831bc1e9ce4d0fe12`. New head: `a86cfd4e370614dfbbaffc05b23a26dd9710af0c`.

ClawSweeper review on `479698f` required the IDENTITY.md rollback to be conditional at its final write, not only before an awaited restore. This tip:

1. **[x] Make the rollback conditional at its final write (P1)** — `restoreWorkspaceFile` re-reads current IDENTITY.md bytes immediately before write/delete and skips when the file is no longer this mutation's content. Same-process `agents.files.set` of IDENTITY.md now takes `withConfigMutationExclusive`, serializing it with `agents.update` rollback. Regression: `does not restore IDENTITY.md over a concurrent agents.files.set edit that lands after the rollback comparison`.
2. **[x] Prevent rollback from overwriting concurrent IDENTITY.md edits (P1)** — after a config-commit failure, restore the previous file only when IDENTITY.md still contains this mutation's write at the mutating syscall. A concurrent `agents.files.set` edit is left in place. Also covered: `does not restore IDENTITY.md over a concurrent agents.files.set edit after config commit failure`.
3. **[x] Preserve partial raw Swift identity initializers (P1)** — generated mixed `AgentsUpdateParams` overloads now cover none (`agentid:modelvalue:`), emoji-only, avatar-only, and both String labels. Mixed labels still omit defaults so the raw initializer stays unique. Compile-oriented coverage is in `GatewayModelsCompatibilityTests`.
4. **[x] Make file and config identity updates failure-safe (P2)** — snapshot destination `IDENTITY.md` before rewrite, write rebuilt content, then commit config. If that later commit throws and the file is still this mutation's write, restore the previous file bytes (or remove a newly created file) before rethrowing. Regression: `restores IDENTITY.md when it still contains this mutation's write after config commit failure`.
5. **[x] Current-head CI caused by this diff** — Control UI Remove-avatar fixture no longer uses `agentsList.scope: "workspace"` (`check-test-types-core-2`); `mergeAgentIdentity` iterates `IDENTITY_PATCH_KEYS` instead of an uncommented `Object.entries` assertion (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`); dropped invalid `NodeInvokeRequestEvent.sessionKey` Swift coverage (`macos-swift`). `android-ktlint` 429 / promisor fetch on the previous head was infrastructure. Current-head `macos-swift` failure on `479698f` was `CronJobsStoreTests` (`GatewayProcessManager.shared.status → .starting == .stopped`), unrelated to this identity-clear diff.
6. **[x] Resolve merge conflicts (P1)** — replayed on `42f5717` from `2db308f06b9` onto `671e41a8773bb9df6f044372fe227f7415a45b38`. Conflict files: `src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts`, `src/commands/agents.config.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/types.ts`, `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts`, `ui/src/pages/agents/view.test.ts`.
7. **[x] Preserve current agent ownership safeguards** — `agents.delete` still uses `agentOwnsSharedAuthStore`, `isInheritedAuthStoreOwner`, `tryResolveSoleAgentId`, and `normalizeAgentIdStrict`. Roster updates still pin `ownership: "explicit"` and `pinLegacyInheritedAuthOwnerForRosterTransition`.
8. **[x] Keep SDK types on the protocol contract** — `AgentsUpdateParams` stays a re-export from `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` (nullable emoji/avatar live in the schema, not a local SDK duplicate).
9. **[x] Make Swift raw-model overloads non-overlapping** — mixed String-label initializers omit defaults so `AgentsUpdateParams(agentid:modelvalue:)` uniquely matches the raw initializer.
10. **[ ] Served Control UI proof** — still outstanding: redacted Remove → Save against a real Gateway. The existing UI E2E remains mock-gateway and is not claimed as served-UI proof.

Empty-string vs null remains the existing null-only tombstone contract (ClawSweeper recommendation: keep null-only clearing). Direct empty/whitespace requests still preserve stored identity.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #119929: agents.update empty/null emoji/avatar handling must clear intentionally without breaking shipped Swift call shapes or turning legacy empty-string requests into destructive clears.

## Why This Change Was Made

Null is the additive clear tombstone. Empty-string requests remain non-destructive for compatibility. Generated Swift keeps String-facing and raw AnyCodable initializers, including mixed modelvalue plus none / emoji-only / avatar-only / both String labels, without overlapping `agentid:modelvalue:` call sites. File-first identity writes stay unsafe-write gated; config-commit failures restore the previous IDENTITY.md bytes only when the file is still this mutation's write at the final syscall, so a concurrent `agents.files.set` edit is not overwritten.

## User Impact

Explicit null clears identity fields through config and IDENTITY.md. Empty-string updates no longer wipe stored emoji/avatar. Existing Swift clients compiling mixed update initializers, including emoji-only and avatar-only raw-model calls, keep working. `AgentsUpdateParams(agentid:modelvalue:)` compiles as the raw initializer. A failed config commit after a successful identity rewrite no longer leaves a cleared IDENTITY.md against the retained roster identity, and no longer clobbers a concurrent authorized IDENTITY.md write that lands after the rollback snapshot.

## Evidence

```text
PREV=479698f24256882db910081831bc1e9ce4d0fe12
TIP=a86cfd4e370614dfbbaffc05b23a26dd9710af0c

git diff --check
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
  src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts
node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen-swift.ts --check

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \

prs.title: fix(gateway): report active unmanaged restart startup accurately
prs.body:
Closes #119958

## Summary

Fixes the unmanaged SIGUSR1 restart path that reports a 60-second health timeout even when the same gateway process has accepted the restart and is still progressing through startup.

## Root cause

The CLI sends SIGUSR1 and then polls only listener health. An in-process restart can retain its PID while the listener is intentionally absent, so PID and port state cannot distinguish active startup from a dead restart.

## Fix

The gateway loop owns a short-lived renewable startup-progress lease while awaiting each startup. The unmanaged listener waiter accepts a typed `still-starting` result only when that lease is fresh, belongs to the signaled gateway process, and began after this restart request. The normal 60-second listener window is not extended. Missing, stale, expired, or non-progressing lease evidence still fails the restart.

## User impact

A bounded still-starting result tells operators to run `openclaw gateway status --deep` instead of treating a healthy slow boot as failed and applying destructive recovery.

## Validation

Run the focused lifecycle, listener-health, run-loop, and lease regressions; then `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:changed`.

## Credit

Thanks @islandpreneur007 for the source reproduction in #119958.

prs.title: fix(ui): localize copy when the Gateway ends a provider sign-in
prs.body:
Closes #178274

**AI-assisted: yes.** The patch was authored by an AI coding agent and every command below was executed in this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the Gateway ends a provider sign-in on its own (session expiry, provider abort, another tab), the Control UI model-setup dialog shows a red alert with only the raw server word `cancelled`, and the Custodian auto-setup card shows `cancelled` or the Cancel button label. Neither is a translated sentence, so the operator is told nothing useful in any locale.

The Gateway's wizard owner records its own cancellation as `status: "cancelled"` with `error: "cancelled"` (`src/wizard/session.ts`). The UI only substituted its localized fallback when the server text was empty, so the bare sentinel won.

## User Impact

Gateway-ended sign-ins now explain themselves with the existing localized sentence "Provider sign-in was cancelled." in both the model-setup dialog and the Custodian setup card. A provider-supplied cancellation reason is still shown verbatim; only the known bare sentinel is replaced. User-triggered Cancel/Esc still closes without a callout.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `ui/src/pages/model-setup/state.ts`: `wizardStateFromResult` maps the known cancellation sentinel (case-insensitive, trimmed `"cancelled"`) to the caller's localized fallback, while preserving any other server text.
- `ui/src/pages/custodian/custodian-auto-setup.ts`: the auto-setup card uses the same `modelSetup.wizard.cancelled` copy instead of the `custodian.cancel` button label.
- No new i18n keys and no English catalog changes (the key already exists), so no translation-memory or baseline churn. No server/API or wire contract change.

This follows the closed PR #178276 (closed by the author PR-limit bot, not for quality); the same reviewed approach is reimplemented here with the reporter's before/after evidence context.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green with the fix** (tests added first):

```text

ui/src/pages/model-setup/state.test.ts
  × shows the localized sentence instead of the Gateway's bare cancelled word
ui/src/pages/custodian/custodian-auto-setup.test.ts
  × explains a sign-in the Gateway cancelled
      expected 'cancelled' to be 'Provider sign-in was cancelled.'
Tests  2 failed | 15 passed (17)

# fixed
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  17 passed (17)
```

Commands:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts \
  ui/src/pages/model-setup/state.test.ts ui/src/pages/custodian/custodian-auto-setup.test.ts
```

Cases covered: bare `cancelled`, padded/case variant, empty text, and a provider-supplied reason that must remain verbatim; the custodian card alert is asserted end to end through the mocked Gateway wizard.

**Checks:**

```text

oxlint (4 files): 0 warnings, 0 errors.
check:test-mock-exports: Mock factory ratchet OK.

This is a text-only copy fix (no layout or styling change), so no before/after screenshot is included; the DOM alert text is asserted in the unit test.

## Real behavior proof (real Gateway cancellation → rendered UI)

Method (this revision, `6095e08d`): started this checkout's production Gateway (`dist/index.js`) with an isolated state dir and loopback origin, loaded a local provider fixture that admits an app-guided sign-in and holds on a Gateway-executor progress step, then drove the bundled Control UI with Chromium through the normal flow.

**Model Setup.** `/settings/model-setup?firstRun=1` → expand the sign-in options → start the fixture sign-in (real `openclaw.setup.auth.start` + `wizard.next`). Cancellation came from the Gateway's wizard owner, not the dialog's Cancel action: `wizard.cancel` returned `{"status":"cancelled","error":"cancelled"}` and the pending `wizard.next` settled with that terminal result. The shipped `ModelSetupWizardRunner` passed it through `wizardStateFromResult`, and the rendered `openclaw-modal-dialog` alert showed:

> Provider sign-in was cancelled.

**Custodian card.** `/custodian?onboarding=1` → the real `openclaw.setup.auto` returned `needs-sign-in` with the ChatGPT sign-in → start the sign-in, then cancel from the Gateway. The card's `role="alert"` rendered:

![Custodian setup card after a real Gateway cancellation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35a2b766-b9b6-4e96-b0ad-a3588758d495)

issues.title: web_search (DuckDuckGo): no retry/backoff — back-to-back searches fail with "No results found"

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With the default search provider (DuckDuckGo, no API key), consecutive web_search calls in the same turn fail with an error that reads like an empty result set:
  Error: DuckDuckGo search failed (No results found.)

The same distinct queries, spaced a few seconds apart, all return results. The underlying cause is that _search_duckduckgo has no retry/backoff (while _search_brave already retries once on HTTP 429), and neither the tool nor ddgs paces calls, so back-to-back searches hit the upstream rate/anti-bot rejection. The error message is also misleading: it reports "No results found" where the upstream response is actually a rejection, not an empty result set.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Keep the default provider (tools.web.search.provider = "duckduckgo", empty api_key), no proxy.
2. In one turn, issue several distinct web_search calls with no pause between them (a normal multi-query research turn does this).
3. Observe that a subset of the calls fail with the "No results found" error; repeating the same queries with a pause succeeds.

Isolated library repro (no nanobot involved), same host:
  from ddgs import DDGS
  qs = ["capa galaxy a12 preco", "fone bluetooth barato", "notebook i5 usado", "cadeira gamer preco",
        "tenis corrida promocao", "panela eletrica preco", "mochila escolar", "lampada led preco"]
  d = DDGS(timeout=15)
  # no pause -> 0/8 results, all DDGSException: No results found
  # 3 s pause between queries -> 8/8 results

### Expected Behavior

- A rate/anti-bot rejection should be distinguishable from a genuinely empty result set in the error text, so the agent does not report "nothing found" to the user.
- The tool should absorb a transient rejection with a short retry/backoff before giving up, the way the Brave provider already does.
- Ideally, pacing/backoff should be tunable under tools.web.search for users of the anonymous providers.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
Two calls issued in the same second, then the failure (Telegram turn, 17/10/2026):
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:44 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:32:50 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:32:54 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:33:40 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:33:51 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.

Additional measurements
- 8 distinct queries with no pause: 0/8 returned results (all DDGSException: No results found).
- The same 8 queries with a 3 s pause: 8/8 succeeded.
- The host recovers after idling, and a second host on a different IP served results while the first was failing — transient and rate/IP dependent, not a permanent block.
- exclusive=True only keeps DuckDuckGo out of the parallel batch; it does not pace calls, so consecutive searches still go out immediately.
- The per-turn guard in utils/runtime.py (_MAX_REPEAT_EXTERNAL_LOOKUPS = 2) only blocks repeating the same query or URL, so it does not help with distinct queries.
- ddgs 9.16.0 itself has no retry/backoff (checked its sources).
- Checked todays `main`: _search_duckduckgo is unchanged there.
```

issues.title: Proposal: budget model-visible MCP schemas for large tool sets

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

I've been looking at the context cost of large MCP tool sets.

Currently, `ToolRegistry.get_definitions()` keeps a stable built-in prefix followed by MCP tool schemas, and `AgentRunner` passes those definitions to the provider.

With a large number of MCP tools, this means all registered MCP schemas can become model-visible even when a task only needs a small subset. `enabledTools` can reduce this statically, but it requires users to know in advance which tools they will need.

I also found #1504 and #1759, which explored tool ranking and lazy schema loading, but both were built against an older tool path and take somewhat different approaches.

I'm wondering whether there is still interest in addressing this for large MCP setups.

### Proposed Solution

I'm considering a narrower, opt-in approach:

- always keep all built-in tools unchanged
- only apply selection when the MCP schema size exceeds a configured budget
- select a deterministic subset of MCP schemas for the current turn
- fail open to the full MCP set when relevance is unclear
- keep `ToolRegistry` itself unchanged and apply selection only to the model-visible view
- preserve the current behavior when the feature is disabled

The goal would be to reduce model-visible MCP schema size without changing tool execution or introducing another LLM/embedding request.

I would also benchmark both schema-size reduction and tool recall before treating this as an optimization.

Would this direction be useful for nanobot, or is there another preferred direction for scaling large MCP tool sets?

### Alternatives Considered

I considered a few alternatives:

- fixed Top-K tool ranking, similar to #1504, but tool count does not directly correspond to schema size and it can also prune built-in tools
- lazy schema promotion, similar to #1759, which keeps discovery but adds an extra model iteration when a full schema is needed
- MCP server-level routing, which may be safer for multi-step workflows but helps less when a single server exposes many tools
- exposing generic `search_mcp_tools` / `call_mcp_tool` tools, which would keep provider-visible schemas very small but changes the current direct function-calling flow substantially

For a first version, an MCP-only budgeted view seems like the smallest change with no default behavior change.

### Related Component

Other

### Additional Context

Related prior work:

- #1504
- #1759

If the direction is useful, I can put together a small prototype and report measured schema-size reduction and tool-retrieval recall before opening an implementation PR.
