issues.title: Add heartbeat-specific model override
issues.body:
## Summary

Please add a heartbeat-specific model override so the Heartbeat service can run on a cheaper/dedicated model instead of always using the main agent model.

## Current behaviour

In the current implementation, `HeartbeatService` is initialised with the main agent model:

```python
heartbeat = HeartbeatService(
    workspace=config.workspace_path,
    provider=provider,
    model=agent.model,
    ...
)
```

The heartbeat decision step then calls the provider using `self.model`, so a deployment using `openrouter/auto` or a premium default model also pays that model cost for routine heartbeat checks.

Dream already appears to support a model override via `agents.defaults.dream.modelOverride`, but heartbeat does not appear to have an equivalent setting in the config schema.

## Why this matters

Heartbeat can run frequently, e.g. every 30 minutes, and often only needs to make a lightweight decision such as whether there are active tasks in `HEARTBEAT.md`. If the main agent uses an expensive or auto-routed model, background heartbeat checks can add unnecessary recurring cost.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional heartbeat model override to the gateway heartbeat config, for example:

```json
"gateway": {
  "heartbeat": {
    "enabled": true,
    "intervalS": 1800,
    "modelOverride": "openai/gpt-4o-mini"
  }
}
```

Then initialise heartbeat with the override when present:

```python
model=hb_cfg.model_override or agent.model
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `gateway.heartbeat.modelOverride` or equivalent is supported in config.
- If set, heartbeat decision and post-run evaluation use the heartbeat-specific model.
- If unset, behaviour remains backwards-compatible and uses the main agent model.
- Startup/logging or diagnostics make it clear which model heartbeat is using.
- Documentation includes an example for using a low-cost model for heartbeat.

## Related idea

For some deterministic heartbeat tasks, an LLM may not be needed at all. This issue is specifically about allowing a cheaper model where the current LLM-based heartbeat flow is still used.

prs.title: fix(update): support Windows long paths in atomic I/O
prs.body:
## Why

Windows installations with `LongPathsEnabled=0` can fail the update shutdown handoff when a 228-character reply path becomes a 266-character atomic temporary path. Normalize paths at Windows filesystem I/O boundaries instead of requiring shorter directories or a registry change.

Stacked follow-up to #6168 for [NAN-309](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-309), based on `codex/live-update-ui` at `58ff96a8024d9692d3ad2a6251888e14a369e700`.

## What changed

- Share extended-length path conversion across atomic temporary creation, snapshot reads, handle-based replacement, record metadata access and installation/data file leases. Keep ordinary paths in durable identities.
- Route shutdown plan reads through the share-delete snapshot reader, and handle reply-directory creation at the same I/O boundary.
- Freeze the new stdlib I/O dependency into protected planning children before acquiring their lease. Add ordinary-input Windows path, replacement, lock and failure-safety regressions plus a real isolated planning-child test.

## Scope

This is an independent child of #6168, without NAN-308 UI changes. No system settings, timeouts, installation layout, parent branch or existing runtime/data are changed. Real `LongPathsEnabled=0` managed WebUI upgrade acceptance remains with the coordinating verifier in a new isolated environment.

## Tradeoffs

The existing atomic sibling naming, fsync policy, share-delete snapshots, byte-range locks and genuine I/O errors are preserved. Paths are normalized only for I/O; this is not a global file-tool path refactor or a claim that every updater filesystem operation supports arbitrarily deep directories.

## Blast Radius

The atomic utility is shared by persisted configuration/session records and the frozen updater. The lease module is also frozen into isolated inspection/worker children, so its new dependency must remain stdlib-only and available before target site/package initialization. Broad update, persistence and gateway regressions cover these consumers.

## Verification

All final local results use tree `f812462db80126ef3fd93b3a9d18fbd15f79a4d8`, committed unchanged as `ed9012f9b50a2ef5ca81dad9b7a24557398f4215`; Windows 11 build 26200, Python 3.14.6, **LongPathsEnabled=1** throughout.

- Focused path/atomic/lease/stop and real planning-child tests: **76 passed / 1 skipped**; skip is unavailable directory-symlink privileges.
- Update/release/persistence/gateway selection, excluding the separately scheduled jobs file: **793 passed / 20 skipped** (`pytest -n 2 --dist load`).
- Complete `tests/test_update_jobs.py`, including real frozen children, local pip installs, recovery and lease lifetime: **81 passed / 5 skipped** (`pytest -n 4 --dist load`). Disjoint broad total: **874 passed / 25 skipped**. Skips cover platform-specific behavior and symlink privileges; no assertion or timeout was relaxed.
- Real inspection-child comparison: intermediate WIP failed before site initialization; the exact parent passed; the repaired candidate passed. This introduced regression is fixed in this PR.
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py scripts/check_import_boundaries.py`: PASS. Import boundaries: PASS, 13 rules / 215 files. Task dependency consistency: 192 packages compatible.
- Full `basedpyright`: **FAIL, 2 errors** in `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py` for missing/unknown `setproctitle`; exact frozen parent fails with the same diagnostics in the same environment.
- Base-interpreter `-I -S` frozen-worker `--status` over synthetic metadata: exit 0. Native job tests use private local wheel fixtures, not an official signed release chain.

The local registry setting means these tests do not replace the pending `LongPathsEnabled=0` real WebUI prepare → confirm → handoff → install → restart/reconnect/data-continuation acceptance. Full-project Python coverage, WebUI coverage and native POSIX/macOS/UNC execution were not newly run. Detailed commands, skip reasons, intermediate failures and snapshot mapping are retained in the local handoff artifacts `nan309-windows-update-long-path/REPORT.md`, `EVIDENCE.md` and `verification-summary.json`.

prs.body: ### Summary The `message` parameter of the `cron` tool was described as "Reminder message (for add)", causing the LLM to treat it as a static text payload rather than a task instruction. Created the job with a static placeholder message instead of an actionable instruction 2. Immediately told the user that cron "can only send fixed messages" and "cannot auto-execute weather queries" — contradicting the actual capability 3. Suggested the user request the weather manually after the timer fires The task execution mechanism was fully functional; only the agent's understanding of the parameter was wrong. ### Change `nanobot/agent/tools/cron.py` — one-line change to the `message` parameter description: ``` - "Reminder message (for add)" + "Task instruction or reminder text (for add). The agent will execute this as a full task when triggered — e.g. 'Check the weather and report' or 'Remind me to drink water'. You can write any actionable instruction here." ``` ### After Fix When a user requests "tell me the weather in 3 minutes", the agent now: 1. Sets `message` to a proper task instruction 2. When triggered, correctly interprets the message as an executable task, calls the weather skill, and delivers the result to the user's channel

prs.title: fix(webui): stabilize earlier-history loading and reclaim space
prs.body:
## Why

Loading earlier messages could leave a large empty band at the old page boundary, and completing a prepend could move the text being read. Make the loading area temporary, keep reading stable where real scroll bounds permit, and use quieter theme-aware feedback without hiding failures.

## What changed

- Hold the 48px loading/error area only while needed, then reclaim both the completed slot and its redundant old-boundary gutter. Keep the real Shell's loading presentation active until its separately owned display projection adopts the visible older-page boundary; hidden command rows and empty/error results do not leave it stuck.
- Use muted theme colors for normal 20px Blocks and the destructive theme color for 24px error Blocks, with hover/focus details and direct retry. Motion owns spring integration and interruption velocity; the existing thread camera remains the scroll-position owner. Reduced-motion feedback remains functional without the decorative animation.
- Keep older/newer/jump request feedback with its owner, prevent duplicate pagination requests, preserve the three-page navigation cache and task-disclosure identity, and retarget loaded-prompt navigation as deferred layout materializes rather than restarting the camera.

## Scope

WebUI history-boundary presentation, scrolling and retry/navigation behavior, regression coverage, and its user/developer documentation. No gateway API, WebSocket protocol, persisted-history format, authentication, or compatibility-floor changes. Both dependency lockfiles and MIT third-party notices are updated for Motion.

## Tradeoffs

At an actual scroll bound, reading-position compensation clamps honestly instead of retaining invisible spacers or permanent transforms. A failed request keeps its functional area and waits for explicit retry rather than triggering repeated automatic requests.

## Blast Radius

Wheel, touch, keyboard and prompt-rail navigation share this timeline behavior. Regression coverage protects completion spacing, reading anchors, deferred layout, task disclosure state, failure/retry, reduced motion, navigation cancellation and bounded page retention.

## Verification

- `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`; WebUI typecheck, browser TypeScript, lint and import-boundary checks: passed.
- Import-checker tests: 41 passed, 1 Windows-only platform skip.
- Full Vitest: 172 files / 3018 tests passed.
- Full Chromium browser suite: 143 tests passed with zero retries.
- `bun run build`: passed.
- Exact-head GitHub CI on `d4c053ec0`: WebUI checks/build, Docker and the merged-base browser suite (167 tests, zero retries) passed ([run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39488755942)). Motion-sensitive cases retain <1px anchor checks, including completion before the first spring frame and again after resuming it. Python/TUI jobs were path-filter skipped.
- Built assets served by an isolated authenticated gateway: light/dark themes, desktop/touch emulation, reduced motion, controlled HTTP503 with details and explicit retry, and loaded-prompt navigation all passed. Served JS/CSS bytes matched the built assets.
- Real-page old-boundary gap: **116px before → 20px after**, matching the normal 20px reference; **0px measured reading drift**, no completed slot, no permanent transform and no page errors in all five production scenarios.

The real-page checks use synthetic history on Linux/Chromium. Physical touch hardware, Safari/Firefox and actual model execution were not verified; the separate historical F5 residual symptom was not reproduced and is not claimed fixed. Local test evidence is distinct from GitHub CI and review approval.

prs.title: fix(gateway): request graceful Windows shutdown
prs.body:
## Why

Windows `gateway stop` used non-forced `taskkill` against a windowless process tree, discarded its failure, waited the default 20 seconds, then force-killed the gateway. Give the gateway an instance-specific shutdown request so it can run its existing cleanup before process termination.

Tracks [NAN-306](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-306).

## What changed

- The foreground gateway owns a latched Windows kernel event with a current-user-only protected DACL. Its random token is published with the actual PID/birth identity; stop validates the target and connects the event to the existing `shutdown_event`.
- Drain the native waiter on cancellation and close its handle with the foreground lifetime. Let the orphan monitor skip a busy transition lock so an explicit stop cannot block its own cleanup.
- Keep the 20-second grace for delivered requests. If the channel is unavailable or the grace expires, warn, recheck process identity, and use one bounded, PID-tree-scoped forced termination.

## Scope

Windows gateway lifecycle and its CLI documentation/tests. No new flags, network shutdown endpoint, console-control broadcast, timeout reduction, POSIX behavior change, or frontend changes.

## Tradeoffs

A private kernel event works independently of HTTP configuration/readiness and uses one native-wait worker per Windows gateway. The worker is explicitly awakened and drained before its handle is closed. Gateways without a usable event take the warned force path rather than spending the grace period on an undelivered request.

## Blast Radius

`ManagedProcessRuntime` now treats Windows `taskkill /T /F` as terminal cleanup, not cooperative shutdown. Its other consumer, `ApiRuntime`, also loses the ineffective non-forced taskkill/grace phase. Gateway stop/restart, startup PID handoff, foreground/background ownership, and on-demand lease locking are covered by the relevant tests; POSIX termination is untouched.

## Verification

- Real public-CLI regression on a windowless gateway: baseline exits **1** without application cleanup; candidate exits **0** and logs `Agent loop stopping`.
- Three alternating baseline/candidate pairs on the same Windows host/interpreter/dependencies, each with a connected stdio MCP fixture and no model request:

  | Public `gateway stop` | Baseline | Candidate |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Median | 22.65 s | 3.33 s |
  | Maximum of 3 runs | 22.98 s | 3.91 s |

  Candidate request-to-observed-process-exit: **0.61–0.88 s**, including normal MCP teardown in every run. These are total CLI measurements for this fixture, not a guarantee for busy workloads.
- Real managed background start → restart → stop: new PID/token, old and new processes/events removed. Real WezTerm `uv run --no-sync nanobot gateway stop`: **3.01 s**, exit 0, caller PowerShell survives, MCP/health port/state/event cleaned up.
- `python -B -m pytest tests/gateway tests/cli/test_gateway_commands.py tests/cli/test_gateway_runtime.py tests/cli/test_commands.py -q`: **270 passed, 4 skipped**. Includes real Windows DACL/identity/latching, listener cancellation, failed startup publication, hung/missing-channel process-tree cleanup, and transition-lock contention.
- Changed-file Ruff, import-boundary checks, changed-production-file BasedPyright, and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Full-project BasedPyright on Windows: **failed with 2 missing-`setproctitle` diagnostics in unchanged `cli/process_identity.py`**; the exact baseline produces the same 2 errors with the same interpreter and dependencies. Changed production files have zero diagnostics.

Detailed measurements and raw local evidence are recorded in NAN-306. The existing shared gateway/config/history were not modified or restarted.

## Why

Typing into a multiline draft can make the completed transcript jump up and back by 49px. Collapsing the live textarea for autosize briefly enlarges its sibling scrollport and lets the browser clamp scrollTop; a second layout-effect measurement runs after the old input-event restoration.

Keep the composer's footprint stable during measurement instead of adding another transcript scroll correction. Fixes NAN-307.

## What changed

- Share a composer-owned autosize helper that reserves the input wrapper's height only during measurement, then releases it for real growth/shrink.
- Remove duplicate input/RAF measurements and the viewport's input-bubbling scrollTop workaround; retain programmatic focus, composition-commit sizing, width changes and post-typography preference sizing.
- Add seven real-browser regressions for frame-by-frame tail/history stability on desktop/narrow layouts, growth/cap/shrink, composition and live reading-size changes.

## Scope

Composer layout only. No camera policy, history paging, pending-input scheduling, provider/gateway behavior, CSS metrics, dependencies or timeout changes.

## Blast Radius

Textarea resizing and focus are shared by ordinary typing, programmatic drafts, mentions and IME. The synchronous minimum-height reservation is released in finally, so genuine shrinkage and the existing 260px cap remain effective.

## Verification

- The new desktop-tail regression fails on baseline with a 49px rendered-frame displacement. The equivalent fixed source replay stays at `scrollTop = 3640` across 26 input events (same 99px input / 775px transcript viewport).
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports` (42 tests) and `bun run build` pass.
- `bun run test:browser`: 164 passed, one worker, zero retries, Chrome 155.
- Isolated production-build gateway with a local deterministic streaming provider: desktop/narrow tail and history reading all show 0px displacement; multiline draft restoration, wrapping, cap/internal scrolling, width changes, real cross-tab reading preferences and mention overlay checks pass.
- Real Windows Chinese IME via native `SendInput` / HKL `0x8040804`: composition and commit of `中文`, Backspace and selection pass; 123 rendered frames remain at 0px displacement. This is separate from the browser regression's CDP composition test.
- `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=1`: all 3014 tests pass in an isolated run; lines/statements 93.63%, functions 91.22%, branches 88.17%. Exact baseline under the same settings passes all 3015 tests with the same coverage percentages (one obsolete mock compensation test is replaced by real-browser coverage). Earlier runs overlapping build/browser checks failed with navigation/timeouts; those failures are retained in the evidence rather than counted as passes. Assertions, timeouts and coverage thresholds are unchanged.

Original user video, diagnosis and fixed replay are attached to [NAN-307](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-307). The fixture replay uses synthetic history rendered by production components; the built-gateway checks use isolated local data. User visual acceptance on the original instance and remote CI are pending.

prs.title: fix(webui): make task state backend-authoritative
prs.body:
## Why

After reload, reconnect or switching topics, the sidebar and Composer can disagree about whether work is still running. Local sends, uploads and transcript history are not authoritative evidence that an execution is alive or that its final reply has arrived.

Related: [NAN-263](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-263).

## What changed

- Publish gateway-owned execution snapshots for real admitted owners, including work targeting a WebUI session from outside its WebSocket. Track queued, running and stopping independently from input delivery, transcript recovery and final-result settlement.
- Keep one FIFO worker/inbox per scheduled session and await a separate task for each root. Targeted Stop cancels only that root, waits for settlement and continues the original FIFO; it does not cancel/recreate the worker or re-admit later roots. Session discard/shutdown retain their worker-level cancellation boundary.
- Put early reservations, immutable admission identities and Stop intent in `ExecutionLifecycle`. The gateway receives its narrow control port explicitly; `RunStateAuthority` only projects facts and the event publisher no longer creates owners. Internal continuations enter the ordinary enqueue boundary rather than writing the raw inbox.
- Add optional `webui.runs.v1` snapshots with instance identity, monotonic revisions and bounded completion receipts. State-only sidebar subscriptions do not attach every topic's transcript. Disconnect means unknown; replaced sockets and stale HTTP responses cannot restore freshness.
- Use the same confirmed per-topic state for sidebar, Composer and Stop. Accepting Stop is not proof of exit. Preserve early cancellation before persistence/FIFO admission, retire provisional unified-session steering receipts and rejected journal admissions without affecting another owner, acknowledge only explicitly owned follow-ups, and do not block the global inbound consumer while awaiting a scoped Stop.
- Commit the final reply before releasing result fences or automatically sending queued input. Require confirmed idle state and preserve recovery authorization; never automatically resend an unconfirmed input. Keep invalid no-argument command errors outside the agent lifecycle.

## Scope

Execution lifecycle/admission, WebUI transport and client state consumers, with regression tests and user/developer documentation. No persistence-schema, dependency, provider-API or core protocol-floor change. Older protocol-1 hosts retain basic chat; confirmed execution indicators, scoped Stop and automatic queued sending require the optional capability. This does not unify direct-call and scheduled entrypoints or introduce another scheduler/general hook framework.

## Tradeoffs

Execution authority is process-local and versioned, not inferred from history or elapsed time. Completion receipts are bounded and do not certify result delivery; missing evidence remains unknown. Reconnection converges on confirmed state rather than promising instantaneous equality across a disconnected network. Existing bounded subagent cancellation remains unchanged: resistant child work stays tracked, not certified physically terminated. Older clients may still leave a local candidate for malformed inline commands; this is not an active backend owner and is not claimed fixed universally.

## Blast Radius

Agent admission/cancellation, root-task context and continuation lifecycle, WebUI HTTP/WebSocket projection, reconnect, sidebar, Composer/Stop and queued input. Channel transports forward only an optional trusted frozen admission identity. Gateway composition explicitly shares the agent's execution control; its fixture updates do not introduce an adapter-owned fallback. Tests protect early/queued Stop, unchanged worker/FIFO identity, cleanup barriers, non-overlap, unified-session steering/rejection, in-flight journal handoff, cancellation during recovery admission, concurrent owners, stale epochs/revisions, lost acknowledgements and final-text ordering.

## Verification

- Exact-head [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39450750395) for `b22780b92b44344beb14a29e8e38564ddf709465`: passed; Python 3.11/3.14 and Windows, Windows process compatibility, WebUI checks/browser and Docker succeeded; unrelated TUI matrix was skipped.
- Python full suite: 10,121 passed / 51 skipped; separate serial CLI suite: 163 passed / 1 skipped.
- `uv pip check`, Ruff, import boundaries, BasedPyright and `git diff --check`: passed.
- WebUI typecheck, lint, import checks, all 3,040 unit tests and production build: passed. No frontend source changes were needed for this lifecycle refactor; existing thresholds were not changed.
- Browser component suite: 139 passed, one worker and zero retries.
- Built UI with a real isolated authenticated gateway and deterministic loopback provider: running/queued state survives navigation and controlled WebSocket disconnect/reconnect; final text is committed before exactly one queued send; a second tab stops the intended running owner; reload remains idle with the completed replies. Real write/read/edit/exec tools ran only in the fresh isolated workspace. Authenticated replay confirmed completed/cancelled receipts separately from history.

Verification boundaries: the final browser flow had no page errors, but recorded an initial missing-thread HTTP 404. Gateway logs again recorded the previously observed `websockets` EOF assertions; no causal attribution or clean-log claim is made. The original incident browser trace remains unavailable. Local review is not a published GitHub approval; remote checks are evaluated against the pushed head. Daily instances, real sessions/secrets and forwarding processes were not changed.

prs.title: feat(update): integrate managed installs and recoverable in-app updates
prs.body:
## Summary

Provide one Stable / Preview update flow with installation-owner-aware guidance and bounded service recovery. The gateway owns policy, durable state, shutdown and execution. WebUI presents the reviewed target, explicit consent and authenticated reconnection. This PR does not publish a release or activate the public update channel.

## Integration status — 2026-10-21

Current head: `58ff96a8024d9692d3ad2a6251888e14a369e700`. It contains main `28f6c26946ebb7fa5dd69b64b172a1033f9a840f`. [Current CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39477107843) is running; previous green results are not current-head evidence. Merge is authorized only after current checks and required independent approval pass. A review has been requested from @chengyongru. No admin bypass, publication, signing change or main-rule change is authorized.

- Integrated @chengyongru's #6280 with both original commits and authorship preserved. That PR is incorporated into this branch, not independently into main.
- Addressed all three maintainer findings: pre-stop revalidation shares rollback-protected catalogue history; the supervisor validates the exact confirmation before its first journal write and retains that identity during recovery after launch expiry; interrupted preparation offers explicit lease-checked settlement without granting new installation consent. The review threads are resolved. No approval was submitted on the maintainer's behalf.
- Resolved the new About gallery conflict without dropping either localized controls or Preview/update feedback. Feedback follows language changes without resetting the selected preference. All ten gallery locales include the new messages.
- Fixed a demonstrated integration failure in main's new QQ connector. A live QR session now participates in update admission; cancelled, closed or expired sessions cannot save a late portal result. Credential-writing threads remain owned after request cancellation, and cleanup waits for them before the runtime can become idle. Gateway admission remains strict for unknown connector types.
- Retained main's TUI packaging, typography, gallery localization and history changes. Update protocol 1, worker request schema 4, installation/data identities and recovery policy are unchanged.
- Preserved the previous CI repair: real terminal-pipe tests run first in a fresh serial CLI process on all three Python platforms. This avoids the reproduced `select()` descriptor limit without deleting tests or weakening coverage. Windows full-suite budget remains 30 minutes; per-test assertions remain unchanged.
- Fixed the new Windows CI failure in the existing late-theme animation test. A renderer flush can finish before the timer repaints styled status chunks. Controlled timing reproduced one old color before the tick and five theme colors afterward. The test now waits for the painted frame using its existing two-second limit and retains the color assertion; production animation code is unchanged.
- Integrated the subsequent main change for model-error recovery and chat controls. Its optional recovery metadata does not change storage identity, update protocols or the frozen recovery program. Focused tests cover saved-context continuation, restart, duplicate-action refusal and update interaction together.

## Product and installation scope

| Installation owner | Supported update experience |
| --- | --- |
| Official managed install | Review the exact target, prepare verified files, stop idle reviewed gateways, back up, install offline, restart and verify the running version; bounded automatic service recovery. |
| Compatible POSIX uv 0.11.16 registry tool | Reviewed inline transaction retaining the recorded manager policy; no claim of managed-venv program restoration. |
| Other uv, pipx, ordinary pip, source, containers, OS services and Desktop | Version discovery and owner-specific instructions: the correct machine/account, applicable copyable commands and running-version/data verification. No silent adoption or fallback to another manager. |

Preview is visible but opt-in. Changing the subscription never installs, restarts or downgrades. Returning to Stable keeps an installed newer Preview until a newer stable release exists. Stable patches need not wait for a monthly feature release. Maintainers trigger packaging manually; this PR does not schedule daily publication.

macOS WebUI uses the approved original cat on a white tile. The gateway owns the optional Dock helper for managed background launches, recreates it after protected activation/recovery and removes it on stop. Closing the icon hides the shortcut, not the service. `--no-dock` preserves the instance preference. The helper owns no installation/data lease and is not loaded by the frozen updater.

## Safety and compatibility

- Exact plans, confirmation generations, installation/data leases and capability negotiation remain gateway-owned.
- Both channels require release metadata bound to the fixed official release-approval identity before download. Bytes are verified, and the reviewed release is revalidated before shutdown. Verification failure does not permit an unsigned fallback. Signing remains disabled.
- Recovery can retry the admitted exact target once, then restore only the original **program**, before activation and while protected data remains unchanged. It never overwrites current configuration or conversations with an old backup.
- Restored service is not reported as update success. Changed data, ownership changes, persistent disk faults, missing base Python or loss of both recovery processes can require operator repair. This PR makes no absolute reliability or supply-chain security claim.
- Scheduled delivery participates in maintenance and current backups. Old protocol-1 startup grants are not widened: the lazy delivery store takes its own ordinary lease and cannot write before activation.
- No new breaking change is intended by this integration. User guidance, implementation contracts and release procedures remain in `docs/updating.md`, `docs/update-protocol.md` and `docs/releasing.md`.

## Verification

Current source:

- QQ and channel plugin contracts: **150 tests passed**, including late portal responses, request cancellation during credential writes, cleanup and update-admission checks.
- Gallery/localization/About: **39 tests passed**. Update interaction, Preview preference and saved-job recovery UI: **60 tests passed**. Full frontend TypeScript and lint passed. Focused Python strict types and Ruff passed.
- Update/settings regressions: **114 tests passed**. Corrected late-theme cases: **40 repeated passes**; complete local TUI suite: **274 passed / 13 platform skips** and typecheck passed.
- Latest merged-source checks: **191 Python tests** for session recovery, model fallback/retry and update settings; **344 frontend tests** for recovery, streams, thread controls, localized gallery/About, update dialogs and channel settings. Full frontend TypeScript and lint passed.
- macOS arm64 package `0.3.7.dev2026102101`, candidate `f86fc72bb6e07a26cbd2bc28b248dddc9d33a655`, source `cde8e4cf2`, SHA-256 `3ee2a1c528a3705f14decd3132ebb9d8e7b9fcd89a8246e6850c4a96ec581284`: fresh public-installer probe and **nine scenarios / fifteen hops** passed. A real retained `0.3.7.dev2026101902` updater also passed upgrade, backup-failure restoration and its subsequent update (**two scenarios / three hops**), including data and Dock lifecycle checks.
- Refreshed macOS package `0.3.7.dev2026102102` is built from source `58ff96a80`, candidate `e2970026d8cdb95e86a2686913ee9c02fa7c389c`, SHA-256 `c1a557174023f9373044ec58441b234e981148be2c86d1c3a8a15ec8414a8748`. Its fresh public-installer probe passed **379 assets**, native protocol 1 without TUI downloads/frontend build tools, gateway readiness and graceful stop. The actual historical package passed direct upgrade, backup-failure restoration and a subsequent successful update (**two scenarios / three hops**), including all data-preservation, second-start and Dock lifecycle assertions. Earlier full fault evidence remains bound to the earlier bytes and the unchanged worker/recovery contracts, not labelled as a fresh full-matrix run of this wheel.
- The first local macOS packaging attempt omitted the required ad-hoc code-signing step and failed the native executable probe. Invalid-signature bytes are excluded from acceptance. The replacement follows the existing documented packaging procedure; no release-authority signing setting was changed.
- Run `39474358876` for `ea274293f` completed its Linux native installer and **nine-case / fifteen-hop** matrix. Reports bind test merge `0465a090a69b41a0d470d12638d88b2fac25832d` to main `688976b` and that head. This does not prove the newer main integration. Linux/Windows native journeys remain required in the new CI; pending checks are not counted as passed.

[Previous CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39387523044) passed all eleven checks for head `bc93d3efb` and test merge `f920f8272`: 3,060 WebUI tests, 103 browser cases, all configured Python/Docker checks, and Linux/Windows native nine-case/fifteen-hop matrices. Previous macOS package and real retained-old-updater journeys also passed data, subsequent-update and Dock lifecycle assertions. These are historical evidence, not proof of the newly changed TUI/package bytes.

Native acceptance checks configuration, canonical SQLite and display history, scheduled delivery, authenticated discovery, continued writes, second start, recovery followed by another update and final process stop. Private feed/fault fixtures do not establish official-signed public-download compatibility. Windows' separate installed-startup probe uses forced cleanup and is not evidence of graceful shutdown.

## Remaining gates

- [ ] Complete current-head CI and native package acceptance; obtain required independent approval before merge.
- [ ] Select the final immutable version/source and obtain separate publication authorization. Public baselines without this updater need an original-owner first upgrade.
- [ ] Review runtime dependency trust and release-protection settings. Enable signing only with separate authorization, then verify official-signed public old → candidate → next-version and failure-recovery paths.
- [ ] Build and retain the same-batch five-platform wheels, sdist, native archives, manifest, checksums and proof. Bind native and supported-old-version/owner-bootstrap acceptance to those bytes. Three native platforms do not prove macOS x64/Linux arm64; container replacement and volume preservation remain separate.
- [ ] Confirm corresponding-source/relinking offers, retention responsibility, licenses/notices and source availability.
- [ ] Separately approve GitHub/PyPI publication and protected catalogue advancement; verify public bytes and installation before advertising availability.

Daily configuration, conversations and the user's active worktree are untouched. CI retains small reports. The optional candidate handoff is bounded to one day; no paid macOS runner is added.

- Clear an old error when reconnecting to a saved recovery decision or an active continuation.
- Sync main `688976bcb`: retain reading-size preferences, font-aware menu offsets, chat-loading skeletons and the shared composer width.

## Verification

- 186 focused Python tests passed, including real agent/session integration with a controlled provider, saved tool results, explicit continuation, repeat failure, restart, and stale/duplicate actions.
- After the main sync, 555 focused frontend tests passed for composer, messages, recovery, reconnection, typography preferences, loading state and viewport behavior.
- Browser coverage checks small/standard/large desktop menu alignment, narrow-screen action-row placement and bottom-sheet access, plus notice/composer alignment with large reading text. Main's typography, preference persistence and loading-skeleton cases also pass. The verified source tree passed 3,015 WebUI unit tests and 157 browser tests, including 18 chat-failure cases. prs.title: fix(qq): clarify QR binding states and setup actions
prs.body:
## Why

Reopening QQ setup currently loses the visible saved-credential state, while generic connection labels blur QR binding and a running channel. Make the state and next action clear with short labels and existing UI controls, rather than adding explanatory paragraphs.

## What changed

- Keep a persistent configured summary with App ID and a separate runtime badge; use explicit bind, rebind, refresh and retry actions. Show the warning only after clicking Rebind bot: rebinding may interrupt other apps, and apps using an old App Secret need the new one if it is reset. Cancelling sends no request, and confirming opens a new QR code. No warning remains on the configured summary.
- Keep manual setup reachable during scanning and group its fields by credentials, access, behavior and advanced options. Align shared QR presentation with the existing typography and button variants.
- Distinguish temporary portal/transport retries, expiry, failure and cancellation. Clear retry feedback on recovery without losing cancellation errors, and localize the QQ states in all ten supported languages.

## Scope

This is a follow-up to #6333. QQ credential storage, decryption, channel enabling and protocol 1/core requirements are unchanged. The optional `retrying` response field is additive; clients that do not use it retain their existing pending behavior. No agent execution or security-policy changes.

## Blast Radius

The shared channel setup title, connect-mode manual-field grouping and QR presentation also serve other channels. Shared polling now tracks the failed action so a recovered poll clears only its own error, successful cancellation clears stale feedback, and a failed cancellation remains visible until resolved. Existing credential-mode forms and save handlers are retained.

## Verification

- Python: QQ tests, channel setup/plugin/contracts and WebUI settings services/routes/client-contract suites — 311 passed. Optional channel dependencies were installed in the isolated worktree environment before the successful run.
- Frontend: QQ view/adapter recovery, channel settings, identity, locales, registry, WeChat views and component gallery tests passed. After moving the warning into a rebind confirmation, the settings, QQ adapter, locale and gallery suites passed again (56 tests); the integration test checks that cancellation makes no request and confirmation starts one QR flow.
- Frontend lint, production build, typecheck, Python Ruff, import-boundary checks and `git diff --check` passed. The production build reports a large-chunk warning.
- Isolated authenticated loopback gateway: real QQ QR creation and cancellation; manual setup and lower controls reachable at 375px; English/light and Chinese/dark rendering checked in Chromium. Configured/offline reopening and retry/expiry/failure displays were checked with explicitly simulated display fixtures, without saving fake credentials. The rebind confirmation was checked on desktop English/light and 375px Chinese/dark: Cancel and post-animation Escape restore focus without starting a request, and confirmation starts exactly one real QR flow.
- Conditional-warning follow-up: all ten locale warnings and the English fallback were checked without changing keys or interpolation tokens. The same 56 frontend tests, lint, typecheck and production build passed; Vitest/Vite used Node after the local Bun config loader failed to start them, with no dependency or configuration changes. Chromium gallery checks at 1280px English/light and 375px Chinese/dark confirmed the longer warning fits and Cancel/Escape restore focus; no gateway or QQ requests were made.
- No real QQ account was scanned or authorized during this change. End-to-end QQ messaging and non-Chromium browsers were not revalidated.

prs.title: fix(tools): web_search DuckDuckGo 增加退避重试并区分限流拒绝与空结果 (#6285)
prs.body:
## 问题

默认搜索 provider（DuckDuckGo，免 API key）在一个 turn 内连续调用 `web_search` 时，上游反爬/限流会拒绝请求，而 ddgs 把这类拒绝包装成 `DDGSException("No results found")`。原实现存在两个缺陷（#6285 有 8 查询 0/8 成功的隔离复现）：

1. **没有任何重试**——`_search_brave` 已有 HTTP 429 单次重试先例，但 `_search_duckduckgo` 一次失败即放弃；
2. **错误文案误导**——最终错误 `DuckDuckGo search failed (No results found.)` 与真实空结果集无法区分，导致 agent 把"被上游拒绝"误报为"没搜到结果"转述给用户。

## 修复

- `_search_duckduckgo` 增加**指数退避重试**：默认 1 + 2 次尝试（等待 1.0s / 2.0s），仅对异常重试；成功返回的空列表是真实空结果集，**不重试、不报错**，单次调用即返回 `No results for: ...`
- 全部尝试失败时**区分错误文案**，不虚构空结果：
  - `DDGSException` / "No results found" → `Error: DuckDuckGo search rejected after N attempt(s) (upstream rate-limit/anti-bot, not an empty result; ...)`，并建议拉开调用间隔或配置 API-key provider
  - 其他异常（超时、网络错误）→ `Error: DuckDuckGo search failed after N attempt(s) (...)`
- `tools.web.search` 新增两个可选配置（保持默认行为合理，无需用户调整即可受益）：
  - `retries`（默认 2，设 0 恢复单次行为）
  - `retry_backoff`（默认 1.0s 指数退避基数，第 k 次重试等待 `backoff * 2**(k-1)`）
- `DDGSException` 导入做了 `ddgs.exceptions` → 顶层双路径兜底，兼容 ddgs 9.x 的导出差异

## 测试

新增 5 个回归测试（`tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`）：

| 用例 | 断言 |
|---|---|
| 瞬时拒绝重试后恢复 | 3 次尝试、sleep 序列 `[1.0, 2.0]`、返回结果 |
| 持续拒绝报 rejected | `rejected` / `not an empty result` / 建议文案，is_tool_error_result |
| 真实空结果不重试 | 单次调用、无 sleep、返回 `No results for: ...` |
| retries=0 单次行为 | 1 次尝试、无 sleep |
| retry_backoff=0.5 | 退避序列 `[0.5, 1.0]` |

本机验证报告（Windows 11 / Anaconda Python 3.12.4 / ddgs 9.16.0）：

```text
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py -q
→ 96 passed（92 既有 + 4 重写/新增通过；含全部 5 个新回归用例）

python -m pytest tests/config -q
→ 159 passed, 1 skipped（新配置字段无 schema 回归）

python -m pytest tests/tools/test_search_tools.py
→ 本机段错误（0xC0000005）；经 git stash 对照，未修改的 main 上同样复现，
  为本机 Windows 环境既有问题，与本次改动无关
```

既有 `test_duckduckgo_timeout_returns_error` 显式设 `retries=0`，保持其单次超时的原语义与速度。

Closes #6285

prs.title: fix(deps): allow websockets 17 while preserving Feishu installs
prs.body:
## Why

A browser or HTTP client can disconnect while the WebUI listener is preparing an HTTP response, causing the upstream `assert not self.eof_sent` race. The [websockets 17.0 handshake fix](https://github.com/python-websockets/websockets/blob/17.0/src/websockets/asyncio/server.py#L202-L205) addresses this case, but our current `<17` ceiling excludes it.

## What changed

- Allow `websockets>=15.0,<18.0`, without raising the minimum or changing channel SDK requirements.
- Add native and `BinaryHTTPBridge` regressions for full-close and TCP half-close during an HTTP response, followed by HTTP and WebSocket health checks. Capture errors independently of channel logging setup.
- Exercise the default 17.x transport in the Python CI matrix before optional channel installation can select an older version.

## Scope

This permits 17.x for installations without conflicting SDK constraints; it does not force existing environments or lockfiles to upgrade. There is no production transport rewrite or Feishu SDK override.

## Tradeoffs

`lark-oapi 1.7.5` requires `websockets>=11,<16`. Keeping the 15.x minimum lets an installation containing Feishu resolve to `15.0.1`, but that shared environment still does **not** receive this EOF fix. Installed SDK requirements apply even when the corresponding channel is disabled. Raising the minimum to 17 would instead make the latest Feishu SDK incompatible with a normal installation.

The new EOF regressions therefore skip below 17.0; existing compatibility tests continue to cover the older supported resolution.

## Blast Radius

The resolved version is shared by core WebSocket consumers and installed channels. The new default-transport check runs on the existing Linux/Python 3.11, Linux/Python 3.14, and Windows/Python 3.14 jobs, while the existing all-channel suite continues after channel dependencies are installed.

## Verification

Local Linux / Python 3.12.10:

- The exact focused pytest selection added to CI: **194 passed** with websockets **17.3**.
- All four EOF regressions: **passed on 17.0**, including with global websockets log propagation disabled. A diagnostic control explicitly removed the version skip on 16.1.1 and detected the expected upstream EOF assertion in all four cases.
- Feishu's actual installer was verified to select lark-oapi **1.7.5** and downgrade websockets **17.3 → 15.0.1**. Dependency consistency checks pass for both the default and all-channel environments.
- All-channel `python -m pytest -q -n 2 --dist loadfile --ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py`: **10,063 passed, 57 skipped**; serial CLI tests: **163 passed, 1 skipped**. This environment uses websockets 15.0.1.
- Final binary HTTP selection on 15.0.1: **8 passed, 4 skipped**.
- Full Ruff check with **0.17.1**, strict BasedPyright with **1.40.2** and the base CI's **filelock 4.2.4**, import boundaries, and `git diff --check`: passed. Tooling was isolated from the daily environment.

No real channel accounts or daily gateway were used. Local checks do not establish Windows or cross-Python runtime compatibility; those checks remain with this PR's CI.

prs.title: fix(agent): don't resume abandoned work after max_iterations
prs.body:
Part of #5924 — addresses the cross-turn part raised in the thread (what happens *after* a turn stops at max iterations), not the within-turn loop detection.

## Problem

When a turn stops at `max_iterations`, the history ends with the repeated tool calls/results and a final assistant message, with nothing telling the model the turn was cut off. On the next message the model sees that unfinished work as the most recent thing it was doing and tends to pick it back up, even when the user has moved on.

## Fix

- `_persist_turn` records `_stopped_at_iteration_limit` in session metadata when a user turn ends with `stop_reason == "max_iterations"`, and clears it after any other outcome.
- A runtime context provider registered in `AgentLoop` adds a short note to the next user turn while that flag is set: the previous turn stopped at the iteration limit, its unfinished tool calls were abandoned, and they should not be resumed unless the current message asks for it.
- Skipped for ephemeral requests and internal continuation turns (e.g. sustained goals), which legitimately continue work.

The note goes through the existing runtime-context path, so it is not stored as persistent history text and only applies to the one turn after the cut-off.

## Tests

- New `tests/agent/test_loop_iteration_limit.py`: a fake provider makes turn 1 hit `max_iterations` (2) with a failing `exec` call; asserts turn 2's request carries the stop note and turn 3's does not.
- Revert check: the test fails on `main` without the `loop.py` change and passes with it.
- `ruff check nanobot/`, `basedpyright` on the changed files: clean.
- Full `pytest`: 8101 passed; 13 failures in `tests/webui/test_remote_*` / `test_ssh_config.py` fail identically on `main` in my environment (SSH-related, unrelated to this change).

prs.title: feat(wecom): handle inbound video messages and quoted replies
prs.body:
## Summary

The WeCom channel drops inbound video messages and quoted replies.

The WeCom SDK dispatches a generic `message` event for every inbound frame and only adds per-type events (`message.text`, `message.image`, `message.mixed`, `message.voice`, `message.file`) for the message types it knows about. `video` is not among them, so a video frame only ever fires the generic event — and the channel subscribed to the per-type events alone, so videos were never processed.

This change subscribes to the generic `message` event and dispatches on the payload's `msgtype`. That covers every message type the platform can currently deliver, plus any type added later, without another subscription per type.

On top of that:

- **Video messages** are downloaded and decrypted like the other inbound media, and forwarded as an attachment.
- **Quoted replies** pass the quoted text to the model as reply context (`[Reply to: ...]`), matching how the QQ and Feishu channels surface quoted messages. Quoted text is capped at 200 characters.

## Verification

- `pytest nanobot/channels/wecom` — 65 passed.
- `ruff check nanobot/channels/wecom/` — clean.
- `basedpyright nanobot/channels/wecom/` — no new findings (the 3 remaining errors are the pre-existing unresolved optional `wecom_aibot_sdk` import).
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` — passed.

New tests cover the SDK dispatch contract (a video frame reaches the generic `message` event), video download, quoted-text context, and quote truncation.

## Notes

- The event registration change is behaviour-preserving for the message types that already worked: the SDK fires the generic `message` event for those types as well, so nothing is delivered twice.
- Media download keeps using the existing `WECOM_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (200 MB) limit and the shared filename sanitizer.

## Related

The WeCom protocol and SDK surface referenced here (message types, `quote` payload, media download/decrypt) are documented in [WecomTeam/aibot-node-sdk](https://github.com/WecomTeam/aibot-node-sdk) and mirrored in [dividduang/aibot-python-sdk](https://github.com/dividduang/aibot-python-sdk).

prs.title: feat(webui): edit and resend messages in the same session
prs.body:
## Why

Users need to correct a sent message without creating another sidebar topic. This implements the approved in-place edit: keep the prefix before the selected user message, replace that message and its entire suffix, and generate a new reply in the same session.

Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息).

## What changed

- Add **Edit message** beside Copy in the existing desktop/mobile message actions, using the existing `EditIcon`. Edit directly inside the same native user-message bubble, preserving its background, typography and natural sizing. The focused editor has its own draft, Cancel and Resend controls, actionable errors, and concise translations in all 10 locales; Composer drafts, attachments and waiting input stay separate.
- Route replacement through gateway idle admission and the session-state owner. Revision-bound anchors, an SQLite transaction, a recoverable display-transcript journal and persisted retry receipts preserve session identity and accept the new input exactly once.
- Fence discarded history by generation across drafts, streams, HTTP pages, trace details, navigation caches and late subagent results. Invalidate obsolete summaries/provider continuation and reuse the shared history-prefix boundary while preserving the existing **New conversation** fork behavior.
- Settle interrupted edit journals under the transcript deletion lock. Restore old display files only while the original canonical generation still exists; deletion or recreation retires the journal instead of resurrecting removed messages. Close the recovery SQLite connection explicitly on Windows.

## Scope

The first version supports persisted ordinary user text in saved WebUI sessions. Attachments, quotes, session/CLI/MCP mentions, slash/shell commands and special/system deliveries are explicitly rejected rather than resent with lost metadata. Temporary Chat has no persisted edit target; shared history cannot be edited from an individual conversation. The WebUI and gateway ship together: message editing has no per-feature compatibility gate or gateway-unsupported fallback.

Resend is the only destructive authorization, with no second modal. The URL, session ID, handle, title, creation identity, workspace, permissions and model settings remain unchanged. There is no backup topic, branch picker or version tree. Previously executed file/Shell effects are not rolled back.

## Tradeoffs

Canonical history lives in SQLite while the display transcript remains file-backed. A temporary rollback journal coordinates their commit and crash recovery; it is removed after settlement and is not a retained conversation version. Pre-acceptance failures preserve the previous effective history. A model failure after acceptance keeps the new failed turn instead of restoring the discarded suffix.

## Blast Radius

This touches session admission/persistence, WebUI transcript reads and WebSocket delivery, frontend history reconciliation, and subagent result ownership. The main risks are cross-client races, stale events restoring a removed suffix, and retry/crash behavior around the two persistence projections. Existing new-fork behavior is covered separately; this does not redesign subagent cancellation or external-effect rollback.

## Verification

Published source: `6fc74f88896877b2b8c8b3010546d95cef63cc75`, based on `909b277e7a5a7ecd2aebdba9611e5febe86988d9`. The latest follow-up fixes interrupted-edit recovery after deletion/recreation, removes the new edit capability gate, and replaces the misleading conversation/gateway-unavailable error with the actual shared-history restriction in all 10 locales. Missing required edit services are composition errors, not optional older-gateway behavior. The earlier native-bubble integration, helper-line removal, strict typing/task-context fixes and test-only CLI fixture fix remain intact.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh related Python tests | **110 passed** across message editing, pre/post-commit crash recovery and delete/recreate regressions, forking, client contract, agent admission and transcript/thread helpers |
| Fresh full ThreadShell and editor component files | **123 passed**, including saved-message edit/Resend through the full shell without an edit capability flag |
| Fresh i18n tests and 10-locale content audit | **29 passed**; only the obsolete unavailable error key is replaced with the shared-history error in each locale |
| Fresh Ruff; strict BasedPyright; Python import boundaries | **PASS**; BasedPyright reports 0 errors/warnings/notes, import boundaries cover 10 rules / 166 files |
| Fresh WebUI lint; `git diff --check` | **PASS** |
| Fresh `bun run build` | **PASS**, with the existing Vite >500 kB chunk warning; output is isolated outside the retained preview |
| Fresh `bun x tsc --noEmit` | **FAIL**, exit 2, **473 diagnostics**. Normalized `(file, TS code, message)` diagnostics exactly match committed head `723e670f62ea4df73611702f086acdfdae943be0`, with none added or removed. |
| Fresh authenticated public-wire crash/delete probe | **PASS**: real child exits after SQL commit, journal survives startup scan, WebSocket `session.delete` succeeds before first replay, history returns HTTP 404, the topic is absent from the complete session list, and canonical/display/journal/stage data remain absent. Owned listener closes and temporary data is removed. |
| CI for the newly pushed head | Not yet verified; the earlier green run below belongs to `723e670f`, not this new head. |

The earlier deletion-fix broad backend command had **882 passed, 18 skipped, 2 failed**. Both failures are Windows remote-discovery tests whose `getpass.getuser()` cannot find username environment variables in this execution sandbox; the exact committed tests and owning modules reproduced the same failures. No environment/config workaround or unrelated remote-discovery change was made. The 110-test final-snapshot run is focused verification, not a replacement claim that this broader command passed. The previous 11 session-delete HTTP route cases also passed; their owning behavior is unchanged by removing the edit capability gate.

Earlier [Test Suite CI at 723e670f](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39382896974) passed the applicable Python 3.11/3.14, Windows process compatibility, WebUI checks/build/browser regressions, Docker and change-detection jobs; the unchanged TUI matrix was skipped. GitHub tested synthetic integration snapshot `aeb1a671f3c80eb48eeb297ed734244ff5d02032` against main `a1bca7dc50c993a30e3730d8bc63baea457991a9`. This is historical evidence, not CI for the latest commit. The local branch was not rebased or merged.

At `723e670f`, task-owned Chrome for the helper removal checked English and Chinese at desktop and 390×844 touch-emulated widths against the retained production-build preview. All four cases passed: the editor stays inside the same native bubble, only Cancel/Resend controls appear beneath its text, and cancelling preserves the original input without sending a replacement. There were no page errors. The served index was checked against the new build; no gateway restart or history reset was needed.

The earlier full native-bubble browser pass exercised an isolated gateway, SQLite/display storage and a deterministic OpenAI-compatible HTTP provider fixture: desktop mouse/keyboard and focus/cancel, first/middle/paginated edits, Composer draft/quote/mention/attachment/waiting-input isolation, busy/stale rejection, refresh, real socket disconnect/retry, same-turn retry with a different request ID, post-acceptance provider failure, and stable identity/topic count. Seven core groups and the independent **New conversation** regression passed with no page errors. That browser run remains evidence for the unchanged native editor, input/admission and replacement behavior; the newer deletion/recovery change is covered by the fresh crash/delete probe and focused tests above. No fresh browser or model E2E run is claimed for this follow-up.

Earlier contract evidence remains scoped to the unchanged owning behavior: the original candidate's related Python scope had **1885 passed, 21 skipped** and the earlier local full frontend run had **2968 passed / 169 files**; the previous head's local CLI run had **163 passed, 1 skipped**, with strict BasedPyright and backend checks passing; canonical history, authenticated display history and complete provider prompts matched; SQL/display fault injection and real subprocess exits before/after commit covered journal recovery; native subagent tests covered old children returning during and after the replacement reply. These earlier runs are inherited evidence, not freshly rerun final-head local full-suite results.

Physical touch hardware, external-model acceptance and user visual acceptance remain unverified. The separate browser-verification runtime has been cleaned; a user-requested local preview remains available. No production configuration/history was used. Maintainer review is still required.

## Why

A completed subagent task can be summarized again when the gateway's idle timeout expires. This does not help task execution and creates unnecessary summary work and persisted checkpoint changes. Exclude private subagent sessions from idle scheduling while keeping their execution-time context-budget compaction.

## Scope

Automatic idle scheduling only. Runner-managed context-budget compaction and explicit manual/SDK compaction APIs remain unchanged. No new configuration, storage migration, or cleanup of existing summaries.

## Blast Radius

The gateway's periodic idle-session scan. Existing tests cover ordinary conversations, heartbeat, Dream exclusion, active-session protection, and subagent context-pressure compaction.

Opening an uncached conversation shows a mostly blank message area with a centered “Loading conversation…” label even though the header and composer are already ready. Show a message-shaped skeleton without replacing usable controls or briefly reverting to the welcome layout when history arrives.

Fixes [NAN-302](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-302).

## What changed

- Reuse the shared accessible skeleton status, localized loading label, neutral theme tokens, and message-column spacing for initial conversation history.
- Keep the composer docked during loading and retain the skeleton until nonempty history reaches the rendered message list; do not mistake a completed empty or hidden-system-only history for continued loading.
- Add focused shell and real-component browser regressions for uncached switching, cached content, empty results, reduced motion, draft continuity, and the full loading-to-content layout transition.

## Scope

Frontend presentation only, shared by desktop and mobile. Existing messages remain visible during revalidation. No gateway protocol, history storage, model execution, dependency, or run-state changes. Artificial history delay is confined to a separate local acceptance harness and is not part of this PR.

## Blast Radius

Conversation viewport layout while initial history is unavailable. Welcome layout, live-message ownership, camera behavior, and externally docked composers retain their existing contracts.

## Verification

- Regression-first: the original text-only implementation fails the accessible loading-status check; a browser transition observer also caught the intermediate `thread → hero → thread` handoff before the final correction.

Fresh Chromium contexts passed the loading-to-content flow at 314×647 light, 390×844 dark, and 1440×936 light, with a real WebSocket ready frame, unchanged header/composer bounds, retained drafts, and no page errors. Windows localhost also returned HTTP 200. The reporter approved visual acceptance. prs.title: feat(qq): add QR scan connection for QQ bots
prs.body: ## Summary Connect a QQ bot by scanning the official QR binding page instead of copying the AppID and AppSecret by hand. This matches the QR-first setup WeChat, Feishu, and WhatsApp already have. Available from **Channels → QQ** in the WebUI and from the CLI: ```bash nanobot channels login qq ``` The scanned credentials are written to `channels.qq`, and the existing post-connect flow enables the channel. ## Why QQ setup currently requires opening the [[QQ Open Platform](https://q.qq.com/)](https://q.qq.com), creating a bot, and copying two credentials into config. The QQ portal already exposes a bind-task API used by its own OpenClaw onboarding page, so the manual step is avoidable. ## How it works - `POST https://q.qq.com/lite/create_bind_task` with a locally generated 32-byte AES key returns a `task_id`; the QR encodes `https://q.qq.com/qqbot/openclaw/connect.html?task_id=…`. - `POST /lite/poll_bind_result` returns the scan status. On completion the portal returns `bot_appid` and `bot_encrypt_secret`. - The secret is AES-256-GCM encrypted with the key generated here (`iv = raw[:12]`, rest = ciphertext + tag), so it never travels in plaintext. Decryption happens locally. - Credentials are persisted before the post-connect enable step reads config, avoiding the stale-config pitfall fixed earlier for WeChat. ## Changes - `qq/connect.py`: New `QQConnectStore` connector implementing `start` / `poll` / `cancel`, plus CLI login. Credential writes share the Settings config file lock. - `qq/manifest.py`: Registers `connector`; WebUI entry renamed from `index.ts` to `index.tsx`. - `qq/runtime.py`: `QQChannel.login()` skips the scan when AppID and secret are already configured, and updates the caller's config model after scanned credentials are committed. - `qq/webui/`: `QQConnectFlow` wraps the shared `ChannelQrConnectFlow`; setup mode moves to `connect` with manual credential entry kept in **Advanced**. Its shared presentation view also supplies a gateway-free Gallery preview. - `locales`: New `custom.*` strings in all 10 locales. - `docs`: QR-first setup in `docs/chat-apps.md` and `docs/guides/qq-ai-agent.md`. - `tests`: Connector/config and WebUI QR-connect tests, plus regressions for concurrent Settings saves, onboarding's final save, and forced-login success/failure. ## Preview ## Testing - `pytest nanobot/channels/qq/tests tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py` — 211 passed. - Follow-up regression: `pytest nanobot/channels/qq/tests tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py tests/agent/test_onboard_logic.py tests/webui/test_settings_services.py tests/config` — 565 passed, 1 skipped (POSIX file-mode check on Windows). - Full Python Ruff/import-boundary checks and BasedPyright on the changed QQ sources — clean. - `vitest run src/tests/settings-channels.test.tsx src/tests/channel-locale-registry.test.ts src/tests/channel-ui-registry.test.ts src/tests/channel-identity.test.ts` — 45 passed. - `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` and `eslint` on the channel WebUI sources — clean. - End-to-end on Windows against a real QQ bot: QR scan wrote the credentials, the channel enabled and authenticated (`QQ bot ready`), and messages sent to the bot received replies.

prs.title: refactor(session): unify model and display history storage
prs.body:
## Why

Model history and WebUI display history currently commit to SQLite and JSONL/segments independently. Put both logical histories behind the existing SQLite session owner so lifecycle operations no longer need cross-store coordination. Refs NAN-299; prerequisite for NAN-92.

## What changed

- Persist transport-neutral display facts separately from model messages, including completed segments, tool activity/diffs, actual response sources, usage, and terminal outcomes. Keep token deltas transient and display fields out of provider context.
- Replace file-backed replay, rotation/manifests, and sidebar sidecars with snapshot-based SQLite projections. Fork commits both prefixes atomically; generation-checked appends cannot resurrect deleted sessions.
- Import legacy JSONL/segments once, atomically, before admission. Preserve source files as inert backups and retain namespace ownership after deletion; diagnose corrupt or ambiguous input instead of guessing.

## Scope

Preserves history paging, navigation, lazy trace detail, refresh/reconnect, and fork/delete behavior, including WebSocket/TUI and unified-session routing. No frontend changes, edit/resend UI, provider capability changes, or attachment-resource migration. NAN-92 still owns destructive replacement and live-event fencing.

## Tradeoffs

Keep two logical histories rather than inventing model messages for display-only facts. Normal turns persist facts incrementally, without a transaction spanning model/network work. Initial import materializes legacy records and can require substantial memory; malformed/ambiguous ownership stops startup. Stop older writers first; downgrade requires a coherent pre-upgrade backup.

## Blast Radius

Session schema/owner, WebSocket delivery/recovery, and WebUI history APIs. Migration and generation routing are the main risks. Existing v1 schema migration remains unchanged; upgrades append v2. Sidebar preferences and external media remain in their existing stores.

## Verification

- Final `763b51197`: session/WebUI **966 passed, 20 skipped**; Ruff, full BasedPyright (411 files), and import boundaries pass. The final fork timestamp regression failed before the fix in both reachable paths.
- Broad Python matrix at parent `24a65a523`: **9893 passed, 129 skipped, 2 failed**; serial platform files: **221 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed**. All three failures reproduce on exact base: Scoop rg shim, Windows symlink privilege, Rich output wrapping. This is not an all-pass matrix.
- Unchanged frontend: full typecheck/lint/build pass; **2995 tests / 170 files pass** with two workers.
- Final-head real subprocess crash checks, authenticated HTTP/WebSocket migration comparisons (pages/navigation/trace detail), fork/delete, and private Chromium refresh after forced CLI gateway restart pass. Provider is a local deterministic fixture, not an external model.
- Five equivalent 500-turn/3000-fact AB/BA pairs: history p50 **24.760 → 7.322 ms**, p99 **64.583 → 27.029 ms** (medians of per-run percentiles). A sidebar tail outlier remains: candidate worst-run p99 **20.051 ms**, baseline **13.752 ms**. No zero-regression or RSS claim.

[Snapshot-bound design, full results, performance tails, and migration limits](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-299设计边界与最终快照验证-0d3ea7d9ae62).

prs.title: feat(attachments): support local files and video attachments
prs.body:
## Why

WebUI rejects videos before they reach the existing upload backend, and native TUI path pastes remain plain text. Add video attachment entry points and let both clients reference files the gateway can already read, without uploading or copying their contents.

Related to [NAN-284](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-284).

## What changed

- Share lightweight `attachment.inspect` checks and send-time workspace/readability/format/size validation in the gateway. Mixed messages use local paths or existing HTTP upload tokens and retain the current limits: one MP4/WebM/MOV video up to 20 MiB, plus four non-video attachments up to 6 MiB each / 24 MiB total.
- Add WebUI video picker/drop support and standalone-path conversion in WebUI/TUI, with removable attachments and retained text/drafts on failure. Preserve browser `File` and clipboard-image uploads, including first-message rejection/retry.
- Serve borrowed local references in place through session-scoped signed media URLs; recheck permissions, support byte ranges, reflect source changes, and keep borrowed originals out of upload/temporary-chat cleanup. Persist attachment origin so immutable uploads retain their original signed URLs and private immutable HTTP cache policy, including after canonical history replay.
- Start uploaded-video playback from the durable URL returned by `message_accepted` and preserve that player/source through canonical history hydration. Pending user bubbles do not retain the encoded video body; fresh history/reloads use the same signed URL. Local path references keep reading their original file.
- Skip upload-store inspection/pruning for text-only and local-only sends. Remove the redundant preliminary upload resolution while retaining batch validation before commit; uploaded sends return from three staging scans to the original two.
- Resolve the previously failing verification: make Windows fixtures independent of symlink privileges, copied Scoop shims, and optional username environment variables; include the process-naming type dependency in the dev environment; fix stale typed WebUI fixtures/mocks and load Vite declarations in the full-project typecheck. Make the stream idle-renewal test independent of host scheduling while retaining real timeout/cleanup checks. No tests or type checks are disabled.

## Scope

WebUI, native TUI, and their shared gateway attachment ingress/media replay are covered. The frontend and gateway ship together and use the matching release's attachment contract; no independent-upgrade compatibility layer is added. Other channels' receive/download/storage behavior is unchanged. Videos still enter the agent context as `[Attachment: path]`; native provider video input, transcoding, frame extraction, and transcription belong to NAN-190.

## Tradeoffs

Borrowed references intentionally follow the current original file rather than a snapshot. Removing a draft, discarding uploads, or deleting a session must not delete that file. Only borrowed references use `Cache-Control: no-store` to reflect changes and current permissions; managed uploads retain `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Assistant outbound staging remains unchanged. Browser files still use the existing upload pipeline, but an uploaded video no longer pins an encoded preview in its message/player state.

## Blast Radius

The shared upload batch policy, WebSocket message admission, user-media signing/replay, and both composers are affected. Signed borrowed-media URLs recheck the session workspace instead of staging a copy; managed-upload signing keeps its original ownership and cache behavior. Test/config-only follow-up commits repair the existing full-project verification failures separately from the attachment behavior changes.

## Performance follow-up

Five alternating same-machine runs compare `4e908b1` with the performance candidate `f38412977`; the original feature base (`909b277`) is also included in the send-path comparison. These measurements were not repeated after the rebase or test-only CI repair. Workloads and failures are preserved in the local evidence bundle.

| Measurement | Before → after |
| --- | --- |
| Staging scans per text / uploaded send | 1 / 3 → 0 / 2 (original base: 0 / 2) |
| 20 MiB video, settled CDP backing-storage delta after GC, median | 28,637,774 → 674,746 bytes (26.67 MiB less; not browser RSS) |
| 49,701-byte upload, second normal HTTP fetch | 50,001 → 0 transferred bytes, with identical decoded body |

The real WebSocket test completes 300 accepted/answered turns per source (50 measured + 10 warmups per run). Admission p50/p95/p99 medians are 9.13/16.04/18.97 → 9.56/15.37/17.52 ms; the original base is 9.41/14.12/17.68 ms. Completion p95/p99 medians are 128.40/173.09 → 129.42/180.89 ms, with overlapping run ranges. These results establish removal of the extra scans and the measured cache/encoded-storage costs, not blanket latency or total-memory parity. JS used-heap delta medians are 5,815,068 → 6,044,652 bytes; concurrency and other machines are not covered.

## Verification

Current source: `1cfbf6b7356fa4c38e99171f62dc4d2395a92cfe`. The latest follow-up changes only `tests/providers/test_internal_streaming.py`; production timeouts, CI commands and coverage thresholds are unchanged. All 12 renewal cases pass with a controlled 350 ms scheduling pause and fail as expected under an injected incorrect whole-call deadline. Earlier failed attempts remain archived.

| Check | Result and source |
| --- | --- |
| Full local Python, parallel suite + serial CLI, with coverage | PASS at `1cfbf6b73`: 10,152 passed, 131 skipped; 86.19% coverage against the unchanged 75% gate |
| Python full `basedpyright --outputjson` | PASS at `1cfbf6b73`: 411 files, 0 errors / warnings |
| Stream regression module | PASS at `1cfbf6b73`: 37 passed |
| Touched Python `ruff check`; full PR `git diff --check` | PASS at `1cfbf6b73` |
| WebUI full `bun run typecheck` | PASS at rebase source `95c735e84`: 0 diagnostics |
| WebUI full `bun run test --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1` | PASS at `95c735e84`: 3,002 tests / 170 files |
| WebUI lint, production build, import boundary and boundary tests | PASS at `95c735e84` |
| WebUI `bun run test:browser` | PASS at `95c735e84`: 103 Chromium tests |
| TUI full check/tests/build and import boundary/tests | Inherited PASS at `4e908b1`: 268 tests, 0 failures; unchanged TUI source |
| [Current-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39399851820) | PASS at `1cfbf6b73`: all 11 jobs, including Linux Python 3.14 + coverage, both WebUI jobs, both TUI jobs, Windows/Python compatibility and Docker |

Recorded task-owned Chromium + gateway checks at `f38412977`, supplemented by rebase reruns at `95c735e84`, cover local-reference zero-upload/zero-copy, quoted/relative paths, real Windows unreadable ACLs, invalid/moved sources and retry, source updates, history/reload, ownership cleanup, and video playback. A controlled history gate reproduced the uploaded-video interruption before the fix; both normal and empty-MIME browser `File` inputs now start playback from the accepted signed URL before history is released, keep the same playing DOM node/source across hydration, and play again after reload. The multi-turn upload/failure/retry scenario also plays without reloading first. Browser WebM upload was verified at 49,701 bytes.

Inherited real WezTerm checks at `4e908b1` cover path-only sends, retained failures/retry, clipboard upload, and the one-video-plus-four-non-video quota. The uninstrumented resize run preserves all four local references through 9 real window resizes across 76/140/176 columns, then sends five path references with no upload or copied media. The mixed clipboard run sends four paths plus one upload token with an actual 434-byte screenshot, preserving the originals; WebUI replays and plays the resulting video.

The deterministic HTTP provider fixture verifies context transport, not native model video understanding. Terminal drag/drop, mobile browsers, and arbitrary codecs are outside these acceptance claims. All task-owned test runtimes are stopped. Detailed source hashes, logs, screenshots, historical failures, and cleanup records remain in the local evidence bundle; runtime data and credentials are not committed.
