prs.title: feat(tui): render Mermaid diagrams as terminal images
prs.body:
## Why

Render completed Mermaid fences as real terminal images with Pele 1.6.0, while retaining the authoritative source and a keyboard-operated viewer.

Related to [NAN-288](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-288).

## What changed

- Add transparent inline previews after streaming completes, plus `Ctrl+G` / `/diagrams` for zoom, pan, diagram selection, source viewing/copying, cancel/retry, and returning without losing the draft or reading position. Preserve natural diagram size and rasterize zoomed vector viewports at the terminal's actual pixels.
- Measure and outline labels with the same installed fontkit fonts, including synthetic oblique for CJK italics. Initial and interactive frames use native resvg without a second font-loading rasterizer. Hide the selected inline picture underneath the viewer while preserving its layout and native image reference.
- Share one terminable layout/raster child under explicit image-demand ownership. Source-only viewing, cancellation, errors and offscreen previews release it; cached frames can return without eagerly launching a child. Keep bounded jobs, IPC, cancellation/reaping, source/output/pixel limits and native-image accounting.
- Retain offscreen SVGs in one transcript-owned **4 MB LRU**, shared with pinned visible layouts. Key by source, layout width, fonts and palette; reuse layout for raster-only geometry changes. Theme/session changes clear the cache, and obsolete requests cannot repopulate it.
- Enable ESM bytecode and minification with preserved names in the Bun 1.3.13 production build. Keep the x64 baseline CPU target and initialize OpenTUI before dynamically loading the UI graph; renderer children avoid UI imports.
- Pin rendering dependencies, prepare target-specific native bindings, and include matching notices, source and relinking information.

## Scope

TUI presentation and packaging only. WebUI rendering, gateway execution, session storage and model-context content remain unchanged. Missing fonts/glyphs, parser failures and unsupported diagrams retain their original source. Pele syntax/theme compatibility is unchanged: the original 40-diagram corpus still has the same failures at cases 18, 22 and 37.

## Tradeoffs

Five interleaved repetitions on the same Windows machine, using identical C4Dynamic/Chinese-flow/Chinese-sequence inputs, Microsoft YaHei 16, 1026 px and the same viewport/palette, compared the saved pre-follow-up candidate with this source snapshot:

| Decode-readiness endpoint | Before median (min–max) | After median (min–max) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First diagram | 465.5 (430.3–732.2) ms | 352.3 (313.2–421.0) ms |
| Three diagrams complete | 596.1 (521.0–649.9) ms | 400.9 (370.8–508.7) ms |

These include fresh renderer-process startup, IPC and NativeImage.decode, not final terminal paint. The same-window WebUI medians were 65.3 ms and 131.7 ms; WebUI uses two workers, while the TUI uses one child. Performance parity remains unmet.

A separate five-pair interaction window measured normal image-mode first zoom at 18.7 → 18.6 ms and offscreen return at 369.7 → 174.7 ms (new range 172.0–240.3 ms). Releasing the child in source mode has an explicit cost: its next uncached raster changed from 14.2 ms with the old retained process to 190.5 ms with a new process (172.4–198.5 ms). Cached-image recovery needs no new process.

The raw Windows executable grows from 130.27 to 149.96 MiB. In three paired three-diagram/six-zoom runs, child peak Private Bytes medians were 591.8 → 592.1 MiB and peak Working Set medians 363.7 → 387.0 MiB. Three passes over the full 40-diagram corpus reached approximately 685 → 688 MiB peak child commit and 455 → 476 MiB peak Working Set. These exclude the TUI parent; pixel/vector budgets are not whole-process memory caps. Real terminal checks confirm that source-only/cancel/offscreen paths remove the child entirely.

## Blast Radius

The Markdown code-fence hook, physical terminal geometry, theme changes, viewer focus, transcript/session teardown and native packaging are affected. The compiled entrypoint ordering is intentional: renderer dispatch runs first, and OpenTUI initializes before the dynamic UI import. Ordinary Markdown and parser-worker assets were exercised in the independently extracted Windows package.

## Verification

Source snapshot `229ce4912fbde51c6ab4c97d3cf7cea15dbdabb60faec4b88ac98481f88e95a8`, published in `da19201f9`; Bun 1.3.13 / Windows x64 baseline:

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run check`, `bun run check:imports`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `bun test`: **284 passed**, 0 failed, 1,819 assertions. Frozen install, full typecheck and all tests passed again after cross-target preparation.
- `bun run test:imports`: **41 passed, 1 existing skip**, 0 failed.
- Windows production build, notices and release packaging: passed. The independent archive passed all nine manifest checks, corresponding-source checks and standalone execution without `node_modules`.
- Original 40-diagram corpus: **37 successful PNGs**, all byte-identical to the saved pre-follow-up executable; unchanged failures at 18/22/37.
- Linux x64/arm64 and Darwin x64/arm64: target preparation, compilation, notices, packaging, manifest/source and ELF/Mach-O architecture audits passed. This host's automatic GitHub Bun runtime download/extraction failed; cross-build verification instead supplied SHA-512-verified official `@oven/*@1.3.13` npm runtimes through `compile.executablePath`, with the other production options unchanged. Runtime behavior on those operating systems remains unverified.
- Actual task-isolated WezTerm / Kitty, light and dark: each completed **24 lifecycle/action stages**, covering image sharing, source-only release, cached-image recovery, new zoom demand, cancellation/retry, offscreen return, narrow resize, streaming-only source and completion, multi-diagram navigation, parser-error feedback and session switching. Exact C4Container/C4Component/C4Deployment/Markdown Strings, zoom/pan, copy action, draft retention and ordinary Markdown/code were exercised. Screenshots were actually inspected. Task terminal and fixture processes were closed afterward.

Terminal checks use a deterministic gateway fixture, not a real model or production sessions. Other operating-system runtimes, Sixel, other terminals, real-model/persistence E2E and full OS clipboard readback remain unverified. Snapshot manifests, raw paired timings, memory samples, package audits and terminal evidence are retained locally. Final-head CI is reported separately; no merge or Linear closure is implied.

### Viewer review fixes (`4882113e4`)

- Give the viewer its own releasable SVG lease, allowing old targets to return to the existing 4 MB LRU. Cancel/error cleanup retains the selected target for source/image retries.
- `bun run check`, `bun run check:imports`, and `git diff --check`: passed. Full TUI tests: **286 passed**, 0 failed, 1,855 assertions; import tests: **41 passed, 1 existing skip**.
- The Windows baseline rebuild and an isolated real WezTerm run passed: **23 observation stages**, including eight diagrams in both directions, cancel → source/image recovery, parser-error source retention, draft/inline restoration and session switching. Task processes were closed.

The committed sources match the verified local candidate. Earlier paired performance measurements and cross-platform package audits above remain tied to their stated snapshot; they were not rerun for this focused fix.

prs.title: test(webui): synchronize touch composer typography snapshots
prs.body:
## Why

[The failed main run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39394217542/job/118532888289) read 18px/27px from the touch Composer's mention overlay and 16px/24px from its textarea, which also failed the downstream `webui` summary gate. The test read the two layers separately without first waiting for the selected reading size to reach the DOM, leaving a comparison window across preference updates.

## What changed

- Wait for the requested `data-reading-text-size` and expected textarea font size in both the short-draft and overflowing-draft loops.
- Read both layers in one `evaluateAll` snapshot and retain full metric equality; assert the exact expected touch font size, including the 16px editable minimum.
- Preserve the existing touch-target, autospace, scrolling, caret, zoom and send assertions.

## Scope

Only `webui/browser/typography.spec.ts` changes. Production code, fixtures, dependencies, timeouts, retry policy and CI configuration are unchanged. No fixed delays are added.

## Blast Radius

The typography spec's shared metric reader now samples matching nodes together. Its single-element wrapper still waits for finite metrics while Streamdown settles; the full browser suite covers those existing consumers.

## Verification

Local Windows / Bun 1.3.6 / Playwright Chromium:

- `bun run lint` — passed.
- `bun run typecheck` — passed, full-project TypeScript check.
- `bun run test:browser` — 133 passed, one worker and zero retries.
- `bun run test:browser typography.spec.ts --grep "touch composer" --repeat-each 20 --trace retain-on-failure` — 20 passed.
- Controlled fixture scheduling, using the baseline and candidate metric helpers: hold preference-event delivery, read the old overlay, release the update, then read the new textarea. The old split comparison rejects 18px/27px versus 16px/24px; the candidate waits for the requested size and reads matching 16px/24px layers. A deliberately mismatched overlay is still rejected.

The scheduling experiment explicitly controls event delivery; it is not a capture of the original CI interleaving. The original failure did not recur in the earlier natural local reruns, and the subsequent unmodified main run also passed.

prs.title: fix(update): close revalidation and recovery gaps
prs.body:
## Why

Stacked follow-up to #6168, targeting `codex/live-update-ui`. This addresses the three confirmed review findings: [catalogue history at handoff](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673476), [stale first supervisor launch](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673485), and [interrupted preparation recovery](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673488).

## What changed

- Reuse the installation's `releases` cache for final handoff revalidation, so a catalogue rollback cannot erase an already observed withdrawal before shutdown.
- Validate confirmation identity before the first supervision journal is published, and keep recovery/restoration bound to that confirmation while allowing an admitted completion to outlive its launch window.
- Offer **Review update** for preparation jobs restored after reconnect. Clear the saved job only after successful gateway settlement, then show a fresh review requiring another installation confirmation; keep refused or lost responses recoverable.

## Scope

The three update-flow fixes and their regression tests, plus documentation cleanup. The update guide now focuses on user actions and recovery; a separate `docs/update-protocol.md` owns developer API and lifecycle rules. The quick start and CLI reference link to the owning guide, the release checklist removes repeated explanations, and Markdown paragraphs use one source line each.

No dependencies, capabilities, persistence formats, release artifacts/workflows, or installation permissions change. Normal preparation confirmed in the current tab continues without an extra recovery prompt; handoff settlement remains gated by its existing optional capability.

## Blast Radius

Final pre-shutdown release checks, automatic-recovery supervisors, and restored WebUI update dialogs. Stale supervisor launches now stop before taking a newer confirmation's recovery budget. Preparation settlement still relies on the gateway's real ownership checks, refuses live owners, and does not prepare or install another update automatically.

## Verification

Documentation follow-up checks: Markdown AST inspection across nine related pages found no manual paragraph wraps and validated 231 local links. All 18 release-guide headings and nine command blocks were preserved. `tests/test_documentation_build.py` passed **3 tests** with one Windows-only skip; the actual documentation build hook copied all **60 documents** byte-for-byte in a disposable tree, including the new protocol guide. CLI flags were checked with isolated `nanobot update --help`; no update or publication was run.

The behavioral checks below ran at `66f6da20b6a492be931756102544cb495b7f7516`. The follow-up changes only Markdown; runtime code, tests, configuration and dependencies are unchanged, so those results are carried forward rather than presented as reruns.

- Python 3.12: `pytest -q tests/test_update_jobs.py tests/test_update_stop.py tests/test_release_feed.py tests/test_release_trust.py tests/webui/test_update_plans.py tests/test_update_plan.py tests/test_update_channels.py` — **237 passed**, two metadata deprecation warnings. A host-only launcher used symlinks for disposable fixture venvs because this standalone Python cannot execute copied binaries; updater code and frozen helpers were unchanged.
- `cd webui && bun run test` — **2,841 passed** across 163 files. `bun run build`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run check:imports` passed; `bun run test:imports` passed 37 tests with one Windows-specific skip.
- Touched-Python Ruff, focused basedpyright, Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All three new regression scenarios failed on the original implementation before passing with the fixes. The supervisor regression uses real frozen supervisor/worker processes and offline pip in disposable fixture installations, with synthetic preflight/restart bodies.
- Chromium plus an isolated gateway: both saved preparation phases survived refresh, settled to `preparation_failed`, and opened a new review without sending prepare/execute/retry. A real preparation lease produced 409 and preserved read-only recovery. Saved jobs were synthetic and only the fresh-plan response was substituted; this is not a crash-to-upgrade E2E. Browser, lease child, and isolated gateway were cleaned up.

prs.title: fix(webui): merge consecutive waiting messages
prs.body:
## Why

While a response was running, typing `1` + Enter, `2` + Enter, then empty Enter sent only `2` and left `1` behind. Separate queue items and a latest-item shortcut made continuous guidance overtake itself. Treat it as one waiting message instead.

Related: [NAN-285](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-285). Desktop and narrow screenshots are attached there.

## What changed

- Accumulate consecutive input in order and use one complete-message sender for canonical completion, empty Enter, Send now and the send arrow; replace independent queue rows/reordering with one editable/deletable preview.
- Preserve attachments, quotes and captured session targets; validate aggregate ingress limits before clearing input, fold legacy v1 queues without clipping text or excess editable attachments.
- Keep pending delivery owned by its topic across composer unmounts; preserve a manual draft after Stop or failed upload, including navigation during acceptance.

## Scope

WebUI composer behavior, draft restoration, translations, documentation and regressions. Backend scheduling, protocol and NAN-275's stale-browser-queue authorization policy are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Continuous queued inputs are now intentionally one send/edit/delete unit. Text uses newline separators, and multiple selections share one quoted-context block. Legacy aggregates over current limits remain editable rather than being silently split or truncated.

## Blast Radius

All WebUI composer variants share the pending-message behavior. Existing draft attachments and session targets can restore over the current send limits so users can remove excess content; sending still validates the complete payload.

## Verification

- `bun run test` — **2933 passed**, 168 files.
- Focused composer, draft storage, attachments, pending-message and thread-shell tests — **302 passed**.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports` — passed.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — **fails** with the same 473 baseline diagnostics; normalized file/code/message comparison has no added or removed diagnostics.
- Real Chrome / production bundle / isolated gateway / local deterministic model fixture: reproduced the original overtaking, verified whole-message forced and automatic sends, persisted transcript, refresh/edit, Stop, and failed attachment upload followed by navigation and retry. Desktop and 390px layout inspected. No external-model or real-touch-device run.

Browser evidence is pinned to `590c33ce3`; the follow-up only removes mention clipping when restoring an over-limit edited legacy draft, with a failing-then-passing refresh regression and final-head tests. None of the recorded browser scenarios changes under that delta.

The final full suite passed without changing unrelated tests or timeouts; earlier runs had unrelated file-preview/temporary-navigation timing failures, recorded with the local evidence. User visual acceptance remains pending.

prs.title: fix(webui): recognize typed session handles as references
prs.body:
## Why

Typing or pasting a valid session handle could leave it as plain text unless that session had already been selected in the draft. This also omitted the structured reference when sending, so identical text behaved differently depending on how it was entered.

Fixes [NAN-286](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-286).

## What changed

- Resolve session mentions against the available session catalog using the existing mention parser; menu selection and sidebar dragging are no longer prerequisites.
- Pin resolved session identities across catalog refreshes, and persist the same active references used for highlighting and sending. Keep session/App/MCP name precedence consistent with the palette.
- Add behavioral regressions for typing, clipboard paste, deduplication, editing, late catalog loading, draft restoration, name collisions, stable queued references and the eight-chat limit; update the user guide.
- Use the same text-derived references and insertion eligibility for palette completion, drag preview and drop; protect handle reuse and the eight-session limit.
- Remove the unused private `WebuiSessionAccess._metadata()` helper; keep the active async validation path unchanged.
- Recognize handles separated by Chinese/ASCII punctuation without spaces, using the same boundaries for highlighting, palette completion, drag/drop and sent-message links. Embedded email/path handles remain plain text.

## Scope

Behavior changes remain frontend-only; the backend diff only removes an unused private helper. No new API, persistence format, dependency, or backend access-policy changes. Unknown handles remain plain text; titles are not addresses. More than eight distinct references still produce an explicit send error rather than silently losing references.

## Blast Radius

Composer highlighting, outbound session-reference metadata, sent-message mention rendering, drafts and queued guidance. The shared parser also renders existing App/MCP mentions. Existing bindings intentionally retain their session identity when the sidebar catalog refreshes; backend validation remains authoritative when sending.

## Verification

### Punctuation-boundary fix (`2e64d3fb8`)

- Regression-first: the previous code failed **8 relevant cases**; after the fix the focused four-file suite passed **269 tests**.
- Full WebUI Vitest suite via Node: **168 files / 2,952 tests passed**.
- WebUI lint, production build (including TypeScript), client import boundaries and `git diff --check` passed. Import-checker tests: **41 passed**, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Built WebUI through a separate authenticated loopback gateway and bundled Chromium: the reported `@bime、@luma， @luma` input highlights all occurrences; native clipboard paste, punctuation-adjacent completion without extra leading spaces, and native sidebar drag passed.
- Real outgoing WebSocket data preserves the original text and attaches two distinct target identities; persisted transcript and reload retain all three reference links. Nine punctuation-separated references are explicitly rejected without sending. Embedded email/path handles remain plain text. No browser console, page or HTTP resource errors were observed.
- The disposable gateway was stopped and its runtime removed after verification; the existing user acceptance instance and daily gateway were left untouched. Live model responses, coverage and the full browser suite were not rerun for this fix.

### Follow-up cleanup (`098a1c1fe`)

- Full WebUI Vitest suite via Node: **168 files / 2,944 tests passed**.
- Python session-reference and session-handle tests: **19 passed**. Ruff and Python import-boundary checks passed.
- WebUI lint, production build (including TypeScript), client import boundaries and `git diff --check` passed. Import-checker tests: **41 passed**, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Built WebUI through an isolated gateway and bundled Chromium: palette completion, native sidebar dragging, outgoing reference identity, persisted reference metadata, and correct reference links after reload passed. No unexpected browser console or page errors were observed.

### Earlier feature verification (`8fcd7d7e9`)

The coverage and full browser-suite results below are historical evidence for the original feature commit; those two checks were not rerun for either follow-up.

- Regression-first: the original implementation failed seven relevant cases; the focused four-file suite now passes all 209 tests.
- Full WebUI suite and coverage: **168 files / 2,941 tests passed**, with 93.58% statement/line coverage and 88.04% branch coverage.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build` (including TypeScript), `bun run check:imports`, and `git diff --check` passed. Import-checker tests: 41 passed, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Full `bun run test:browser`: **94 passed**.
- Built WebUI through an isolated gateway and real Chromium: typing without selection, system clipboard paste, duplicate/case-insensitive handles, unknown handles, outgoing reference identity, persisted-history reload, palette completion and native sidebar dragging passed. Light/dark screenshots are attached to NAN-286.

The isolated provider deliberately points to an unused loopback port: this verifies reference admission and persistence, not live model behavior, and makes no paid model requests. No native mobile/Windows/OS-IME acceptance was performed. No production configuration, sessions or running service were modified.

## Why

Mermaid text and lines become blurry when zooming the image viewer even though copying the original image stays sharp ([NAN-297](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-297)). The persistent `will-change: transform` hint lets the compositor retain a fit-size raster instead of repainting the SVG at the new scale.

## What changed

- Remove the forced transform-layer hint from the shared `ImageViewport`, leaving its sizing, transform, gestures and camera state unchanged.
- Extend the existing browser regression to 338% zoom and check the computed raster/compositor policy. CDP screenshots can repaint the image and conceal this failure.

## Blast Radius

`ImageViewport` is shared by Mermaid and ordinary image previews. The change leaves layer selection to the browser; it does not alter the SVG Blob/inert-image boundary, source, worker, theme, resource ownership or zoom limits.

## Verification

- Reproduced using the complete reported sequence diagram in headed Chrome 155 on Windows. Native window-render captures show clear → blurry → clear when adding and removing only `will-change: transform`; removing only the 3D translation does not fix it. A same-size 338% before/after comparison is attached to [NAN-297](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-297).
- Browser regression failed before the fix (`transform` instead of `auto`), then `bun run test:browser diagrams.spec.ts` passed all **8 tests**.
- `bun run test src/tests/image-lightbox.test.tsx src/tests/mermaid-block.test.tsx src/tests/diagram-image.test.ts src/tests/diagram-runtime.test.ts`: **56 passed**.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:imports` and `bun run test:imports`: passed (**42 import-rule tests**). The build retains its existing large-chunk warning.
- Built WebUI served by an isolated real gateway, with the reported diagram seeded as a saved display transcript: desktop and narrow/DPR 2 passed 338%/759% zoom, keyboard pan, reset, Escape/focus restoration and refresh. No model calls or production-data changes.

The reporter's exact browser/device has not yet been confirmed; native visual reproduction here is Windows Chrome, while the narrow/high-DPR checks use browser emulation.

## Why

The history-boundary work in #6322 left `No earlier messages` visible whenever the viewport stayed at the top, including short conversations immediately after opening. [NAN-300](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-300) tracks the regression: this should be feedback for pulling past the beginning, then disappear when the feedback settles.

## What changed

- Let the history spring report feedback start/end transitions, independently of its animated displacement.
- Show the exhausted hint only during that feedback; clear it on settlement, leaving the boundary, or switching conversations. Keep real loading and retry states independently visible.
- Cover idle short conversations, wheel/touch input, repeated feedback, refresh, session switches and reduced motion in regression tests.

## Scope

Frontend-only exhausted-hint visibility. Pagination, request triggers, exhaustion detection, spring constants, copy and persistent state are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Reduced motion still renders zero displacement. The bounded logical spring now settles normally so input feedback has the same natural end boundary without a dismissal timer. React is notified only at feedback transitions, not on animation frames.

## Blast Radius

The shared `ThreadViewport` and its history spring are affected. Loading, error/retry, local cached expansion, navigation-owned history, reading anchors and the existing no-per-frame-message-rerender contract remain covered by the focused tests.

## Verification

Verified source: `08223af1273bb42a55ddfd15a4865d06ebd634bf`, based on `816c9221a0c4ad690d76e165ba255aadd4e235b6`.

prs.title: feat(webui): add reading text size preferences
prs.body:
## Why

WebUI reading text currently mixes local pixel sizes and inherited Markdown styles, making the effective hierarchy inconsistent and leaving readers without a size preference. Introduce shared typography roles and a browser-local reading-size control while keeping navigation and toolbars stable.

Related: [NAN-295](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-295)

## What changed

- Add Small / Standard / Large reading text preferences under **Appearance → Local preferences**, with three equal-width A options, localized accessible names and tooltips in all 10 languages, keyboard radio navigation, immediate updates, and refresh persistence through the existing local-preferences owner.
- Define shared reading, heading, code, dense-diff, Composer and interface text roles. Coordinate Markdown headings, lists, quotes, tables and code; share the mono stack; keep the textarea and mention overlay on identical metrics with a 16px editable minimum.
- Match the compact size control to adjacent settings: 34px visual height and 60px desktop rows, retaining a 44px touch hit area without increasing row height. Add browser coverage and concise usage/component documentation.
- Keep settings and file-preview skeletons aligned with the rendered typography: include the reading-size row, use shared text/code/heading metrics for reserved line boxes, and check layout parity at all three reading sizes. Update the touch-field regression to cover the semantic desktop role while preserving its 16px touch baseline and CSS cascade assertions.

| Reading body size | Small | Standard (default) | Large |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop, ≥640px | 16px | 18px | 20px |
| Narrow, <640px | 15px | 16px | 18px |

Latin line height remains 1.625; Chinese, Japanese and Korean retain 1.8. Heading and code sizes preserve their relative hierarchy. The standard sizes were compared with Steph Ango's rendered typography rather than copying its theme.

## Scope

Frontend typography and browser-local display preferences only. The existing preference schema remains version 1; missing or invalid sizes use Standard and other preferences are preserved. No gateway settings, session content, TUI, history-fetching logic, or scroll-spring changes.

## Blast Radius

Shared Markdown, code/diff, form-control and settings typography consumers are affected. Navigation, toolbar sizing, the root font size and the rem layout grid remain independent of the reading preference. Composer resizing follows preference changes without taking focus. Initial settings/file-preview skeletons reserve the corresponding reading/control geometry.

## Verification

Current source: `ef6a4d6d519d8808042ecab58ba4fa742ef420a5`, rebased onto `main@a1bca7dc50c993a30e3730d8bc63baea457991a9`. The checks below cover the same candidate bytes committed and pushed at this head; no source changes followed them.

| `bun run test:browser` (includes browser-project tsc) | PASS, full suite 113/113 |
| `bun run typecheck` | PASS, complete application/unit-test TypeScript project |
| `bun run lint` | PASS |

It also aligns read-only settings placeholders with their shared interface line height.

prs.body:
## Why

Earlier-history loading was easy to miss, and reaching the loaded edge did not distinguish more history from the start of the conversation. This adds a shared wheel/touch spring and distinct boundary states.

Refs [NAN-287](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-287).

## What changed

- Use loading.dev Blocks for loading, an exhausted message at the conversation start, and static error Blocks for retry, with actual error hints and accessible labels across all ten locales. Keep actual loading/errors visible when the reader leaves the top.
- Reuse the same `ThreadHistoryStatus` in subtask history, including real loading/retry state and actual error text; remove the duplicate spinner, error control and obsolete locale keys.
- Add a bounded presentation-only spring: touch loads on armed release, wheel packets feed one continuous spring, and real loading holds a stable pocket. Stop at rest and reset on conversation changes; preserve reduced-motion behavior.
- Cover real history/navigation hooks with browser fixtures and regression tests; include the Blocks MIT notice without adding a dependency.

## Scope

Frontend history-boundary and subtask-history feedback only. Existing hooks still own requests/pagination and the thread camera still owns scrolling/anchors. No backend, protocol, persistence or history-ordering changes; no artificial request delay or minimum loading duration.

## Tradeoffs

Earlier candidate measurements, not rerun for the current subtask-unification follow-up: the nine-block loader has a measured animation cost: under 4× CPU throttling, median main-thread task time during a 1,300 ms held request increased from 241.715 to 309.562 ms; p95 frame interval was 16.7 → 16.8 ms, with zero layout and zero extra application RAF callbacks. Total production JS/CSS gzip grows by 2,031 bytes (about 1.98 KiB).

## Blast Radius

The shared conversation viewport changes for normal history and prompt-navigation windows. Native gesture behavior, prepend anchoring and weak-CPU long-list scrolling are the main risks. Physical-device hand-feel acceptance and further confidence in long-list tail behavior remain outstanding.

prs.body:
## Why

The WebUI job in [run 39375772664](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39375772664/job/118473499752) took 8m27s: coverage consumed 3m27s and browser checks 3m44s, serialized on one runner. Give these independent workloads separate runners and remove real waiting from the existing invalid-input tests.

## What changed

- Run imports, lint, coverage and production build in `WebUI checks and build`, alongside an independent `WebUI browser` job after path detection.
- Preserve the existing `webui` check as an aggregate that succeeds only when both jobs succeed; failures, cancellations and unexpected skips cannot turn it green.
- Advance the same 750ms validation window with scoped fake timers in nine existing Settings cases instead of sleeping for 6.75s in total. Assertions and timer cleanup remain intact.

## Scope

Two files only. Acceptance commands, dependency versions, coverage thresholds and path filters are unchanged. Browser tests keep one worker and zero retries, so rendered-motion and Worker-deadline checks do not gain CPU contention. Fixture refactoring and DOM/Node test reclassification are left for separately measured work.

## Tradeoffs

This reduces the WebUI critical path, not its compute workload. It adds one dependency installation and a small aggregate job on standard `ubuntu-latest` runners, with no new cache, artifact upload or paid action. Based on the original step timings, approximately 4.5–5 minutes is the scheduling estimate before queue effects; a new Linux CI result is still needed to measure the actual workflow gain. Other Python/Windows jobs may remain the full-suite bottleneck.

## Blast Radius

CI scheduling and the required `webui` result are affected; application behavior is unchanged. Both lanes retain all original acceptance checks, and the aggregate explicitly validates both upstream results.

## Verification

- PASS: `actionlint 1.7.12 .github/workflows/ci.yml`; workflow/DAG inspection confirms unchanged acceptance commands, path selection and unrelated jobs. The actual aggregate Bash command accepts only success/success across all 16 upstream-result pairs.
- PASS: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`.

prs.title: feat(heartbeat): add heartbeat-specific model override
prs.body:
## Problem

The heartbeat cron job runs on the main agent model for both the execution turn and the post-run notification evaluation. Heartbeat can run frequently (default every 30 minutes) and usually only makes a lightweight decision, so deployments using a premium or auto-routed model pay that cost for routine background checks. `agents.defaults.dream.modelOverride` already lets Dream run on a different model, but heartbeat has no equivalent setting.

## Solution

Add an optional `gateway.heartbeat.modelOverride`. For each heartbeat run, resolve an immutable runtime via `runtime_resolver.resolve_override(model=..., config=...)` (which also resolves the correct provider for the requested model); when the override is unset, snapshot the current default via `runtime_resolver.current()`. The same resolved provider/model is used for both the heartbeat turn and the notification evaluation. The main agent model and provider are never mutated, and unsetting the field keeps today's behaviour exactly.

## Changes

- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — add `model_override` to `HeartbeatConfig` with `modelOverride` / `model` aliases.
- `nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py` — resolve the heartbeat runtime and pass it to `process_direct`; use its provider/model for `evaluate_response`; startup output shows the effective heartbeat model.
- `docs/configuration.md` — document the new option with an example.
- Tests: config alias/serialization cases and a runtime case (default + override) asserting both the execution and evaluation use the resolved model while the main agent model is unchanged.

## Testing

**Environment**
- Runtime: Python 3.13.16
- OS: Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
- Arch: AMD64

**Test Commands & Results**
1. `pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py tests/config/test_gateway_config.py -k heartbeat`
   -> 20 passed, 150 deselected
2. `pytest tests/config tests/cli tests/agent`
   -> 2781 passed, 30 skipped, 0 failed (baseline: 2776 passed, 30 skipped, 1 flaky timing failure; the 4 added tests account for the count difference)
3. `ruff check nanobot tests`
   -> all checks passed
4. `basedpyright nanobot/config/schema.py nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py`
   -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

**Pre-existing Failures**
- `tests/agent/test_runner_injections.py::test_websocket_followup_is_admitted_before_recovery_queue` raised an asyncio `TimeoutError` once during the baseline full run. It passes in isolation and passed in the post-change full run; it has no file intersection with this PR and is a pre-existing flaky timing test.

## Notes for Reviewer

- The earlier attempt #4549 was withdrawn without the feature landing; this re-implements the same requested behaviour against the current code, using the side-effect-free `runtime_resolver.current()` for the default case.
- Kept this PR to a model override only (no separate provider override) to match the issue scope.

Closes #4431

prs.title: fix(webui): make browser notification failures actionable
prs.body:
## Why

Refs [NAN-227](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-227).

Browser notification opt-in can fail silently, and the `Notification` constructor can throw on mobile browsers. Make permission and delivery failures actionable while keeping alerts bounded by the page's actual capabilities.

## What changed

- Add a separate **Settings → Notifications** destination with independent browser-notification and completion-sound switches. Use compact grouped rows, shared help hints, visible recovery guidance, and an opt-in-only test action. Update all ten locales and the WebUI guide.
- Deliver through an active service worker, with bounded permission, readiness, and display waits. Probe the notification protocol so an older worker produces an explicit retry/reload message. Permission revocation disables the local notification preference; allowing permission again still requires explicit opt-in.
- Observe live task events outside the mounted chat, use generic task-status text, and deduplicate across tabs/reconnects. Route clicks to the owning gateway/chat with normal authentication; remote views can reveal only an existing online connection.

## Scope

The existing browser-preference key and default-off behavior are preserved. Completion sound remains an independent page chime; its trigger behavior is unchanged. This changes the frontend and service worker, not backend execution, session storage, model prompts, or tool schemas.

This does not add Web Push or an all-gateway notification center. New task alerts depend on an open, connected, non-suspended page. Temporary chats require their original connection.

## Tradeoffs

An active worker that implements the notification protocol is required; there is no unverified constructor fallback. **Test notification** reports submission to the browser, not confirmed OS display. Worker receipts are limited to 256 events within 24 hours; restricted browser storage can reduce deduplication after a worker restart.

## Blast Radius

Touches settings routing/localized copy, the client-side live-event subscriber, service-worker notification handling, and the remote-host reveal bridge. The main compatibility risks are stale workers and notification click routing across independently updated pages/hosts. These still need the real-device/upgrade acceptance below.

## Verification

- Reviewed and verified follow-up head `6b17841fd29cb41f9ea1a390517f962260a8520a`: permission and click ownership survive route/auth transitions, stale discarded Temporary Chat events do not notify, and Appearance/Notifications loading skeletons match their loaded layout.
- Full WebUI suite: `bun run test --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2` — **169 files / 2989 tests passed**. The initial default-parallel attempt failed (6 files; 99 failed tests; 121 skipped). Source and timeouts were unchanged between runs.
- `bun run test:browser` — browser TypeScript check and **98 Playwright tests passed**, including the four desktop/narrow English/Chinese settings parity cases.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build` (production TypeScript + Vite), the **382-file** client import-boundary scan, and **42** import contract tests passed. Focused notification/worker/client/settings regression: **4 files / 160 tests passed**.
- Real isolated gateway and production build: permission revocation outside Settings disables the saved preference; another tab cannot restore it through an unrelated setting; permission regrant still requires explicit opt-in. Completion sound stays enabled independently. Test submission through the real worker was returned by `getNotifications()`.
- On the real App sign-in screen, a controller-validated notification-click message changed the destination, which survived sign-in. This exercised the page/worker protocol; OS-banner clicking remains in the draft acceptance below.
- Earlier Chinese/English/French, light/dark, desktop/390px/320px, keyboard-help and touch-layout evidence remains applicable to unchanged copy and controls. The retained isolated preview now serves the verified build; no production runtime or credentials were changed.

### Outstanding draft acceptance

- A user-operated OS permission prompt, visible system banner, and clicking a real OS notification.
- Android Chrome, iOS normal tab/Home Screen, and the reported embedded browser.
- Complete old-page/new-worker and new-page/old-worker upgrade flows, plus multi-host end-to-end notification clicks.

Responsive screenshots, Chromium touch emulation, and browser submission are not proof of device support or OS-banner visibility. No production gateway was restarted, and no production browser permission or provider credentials were changed.

issues.title: [Bug]: Interrupted turn (exit 130) delivers zero user feedback — silent death until user re-pings; no distinction between deliberate stop and client disconnect

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: tool/terminal
labels.description: Terminal execution and process management

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

issues.body:
### Summary

When a tool call is interrupted (exit 130, `[Command interrupted]`) — which in the webui happens on client disconnect / request cancellation via `agent.interrupt()` — the turn ends with `reason=interrupted_by_user` and **no response is delivered to the user** (`response_len=0`). The session appears dead and the user must re-ping it. A tool that merely hits its **timeout** (exit 124) is treated as a normal tool error and the turn survives.

Two distinct issues are conflated here:

1. **Silent death**: an interrupted turn (by design, any `agent.interrupt()` source) delivers **zero feedback** to the user. `close_interrupted_tool_sequence` adds an `"Operation interrupted."` placeholder, but only to the model's history — not to the user (still `response_len=0`).
2. **No distinction between "user deliberately stopped" and "connection/client cancellation"**: both kill the turn identically and silently, and the next turn's replay labels the result `[Orphan recovery: ... effect is UNKNOWN ...]` — technically conservative for a side-effecting tool, but misleading/over-cautious for a clean deliberate stop.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
- Platform: webui (API server gateway), Linux
- Gateway process persists the agent between turns

### Evidence — real logs from `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` (session `20260811_195549_1aae95`)

**Turn 1 — terminal tool interrupted at 180s → turn killed, zero response:**

```
20:02:05,424 WARNING [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.tool_executor: Tool terminal returned error (180.36s): {"output": "[Command interrupted]", "exit_code": 130, "error": null}
20:02:05,777 INFO  [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=interrupted_by_user model=big-pickle api_calls=10/150 tool_turns=10 last_msg_role=assistant response_len=0 session=20260811_195549_1aae95
```

**Turn 2 — same pattern: a fast tool ran fine (0.30s), then a long tool was interrupted at 180s → turn killed, zero response:**

```
20:38:21,663 INFO  [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.tool_executor: tool terminal completed (0.30s, 45 chars)
20:41:25,422 WARNING [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.tool_executor: Tool terminal returned error (180.64s): {"output": "[Command interrupted]", "exit_code": 130, "error": null}
20:41:25,561 INFO  [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=interrupted_by_user model=big-pickle api_calls=2/150 budget=2/150 tool_turns=12 last_msg_role=assistant response_len=0 session=20260811_195549_1aae95
```

**Turn 3 — two tool timeouts (exit 124) → turn did NOT die, agent delivered a full response:**

```
20:59:54,458 WARNING [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.tool_executor: Tool terminal returned error (90.20s): {"output": "[Command timed out after 90s]", "exit_code": 124, ...}
21:02:38,678 WARNING [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.tool_executor: Tool terminal returned error (120.20s): {"output": "[Command timed out after 120s]", "exit_code": 124, ...}
21:07:51,105 INFO  [20260811_195549_1aae95] agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=text_response(finish_reason=stop) model=big-pickle api_calls=26/150 tool_turns=37 last_msg_role=assistant response_len=6723 session=20260811_195549_1aae95
```

### Observations / analysis

1. **The 130 path is by design, and it is a real agent-level interrupt.** The webui calls `agent.interrupt()` on client disconnect/cancellation (`tui_gateway/server.py:7586`, `:13314`; required by `tests/test_sse_agent_cancel.py:205-207`: "When the client disconnects, agent.interrupt() must be called so the agent thread stops making LLM API calls"). `interrupt()` sets `_interrupt_requested=True` (`run_agent.py:3145/3151`) and the per-thread bit (`run_agent.py:3185`); the running terminal tool aborts via `is_interrupted()` with `[Command interrupted]` exit 130 (`tools/environments/base.py:1195`); the loop breaks at the next `_interrupt_requested` check (`conversation_loop.py:1649-1651`) with `reason=interrupted_by_user`.
2. **A timeout (124) is a normal tool error** — the loop continues and the agent delivers a response (turn 3 survived two 124s).
3. **The real defect is the silent death**: `close_interrupted_tool_sequence` (`agent/message_sanitization.py:296-325`) appends an `"Operation interrupted."` placeholder (line 323), called from 8 sites in `conversation_loop.py` + `turn_finalizer.py:291-292`, but that placeholder goes into the model's message history — the user still receives nothing (`response_len=0`).
4. **`[Orphan recovery: ... effect is UNKNOWN ...]` only appears in the model context of the NEXT turn**, injected by `strip_interrupted_tool_tails` (`gateway/run.py:1443` → `agent/replay_cleanup.py:84-100`); it is never a visible bubble for the user (the persisted `[Command interrupted]` is what the user sees). Its wording is conservative-correct for a side-effecting tool killed mid-run, but over-cautious for a clean deliberate stop, because nothing distinguishes the two: `is_interrupted_tool_result` (`replay_cleanup.py:30-39`) only does substring matching on `[command interrupted]`/`exit_code 130|-1`; `terminal_tool.py:3470` stores `approval='...then interrupted.'` as text, not a structured field; `chat_completions.py:315` strips `effect_disposition` before the API call. Read-only tools already get accurate wording ("interrupted read-only tool did not complete.", `replay_cleanup.py:98/172`).

### Related issues

- #35309 (closed): ThreadPoolExecutor worker threads leaking interrupt state — different mechanism, same domain of "interrupt leaves the session unusable".
- #60920 (open): interrupt message duplicated by `_replay_output_history` after terminal recovery.
- #63069 (open): `read_file` falsely reports "File not found" when interrupted mid-read.

### Suggested fix

1. **Guarantee user-facing feedback on interrupted turns.** When a turn ends with `response_len=0` due to an interrupt, always deliver a non-empty closing message to the user (reuse/extend `close_interrupted_tool_sequence` so the placeholder reaches the user, or emit a distinct "turn interrupted" message). Today the placeholder only lands in model history.
2. **Propagate a structured stop-kind field** from the interrupt source (webui/gateway `agent.interrupt(message)` → `run_agent.py`) through the tool result (e.g. `result_dict['stop_kind']`/`interrupted_by_user`) so the system can distinguish "user deliberately stopped" from "client disconnected / request cancelled". Use it to: (a) word the user-facing closing message accordingly, and (b) let `strip_interrupted_tool_tails` pick precise wording — e.g. clean stop + side-effecting tool: "You stopped this tool; its effect may be UNKNOWN — inspect state before retrying" vs crash: "Hermes stopped unexpectedly; effect UNKNOWN". Read-only tools already have correct wording; only the side-effecting case needs refinement.
3. **Optionally stop stripping `effect_disposition`** in `chat_completions.py:315` (or document why the model must not see it), so the model can reason about interrupted tool results.

---

**🛠️ Dev:** Halldrix
**🤖 Sidekick:** Hermes Agent v0.20.0
**🐞 Reproduction:** ✅ Confirmed (webui, 2026-08-11)

issues.title: Epic: non-user interrupt → bounded model recovery (never silent; user_stop stays terminal)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Summary

Non-`user_stop` interrupts currently **tear down the turn** (often with empty user-visible text). The model is **not** given a recovery step to diagnose what failed, verify external side effects, continue or change plan, and tell the user what happened. The user only discovers the unfinished work later and must re-ping — then wait again for diagnosis.

**Desired contract**

| Stop kind | Behavior |
|-----------|----------|
| **`user_stop`** (explicit Stop / deliberate cancel) | End the turn. Surface a clear reason. **Do not** auto-wake the model to continue or argue. |
| **Any other interrupt** (tool orphan/timeout-as-hard-stop, client disconnect, lease loss, system lifecycle, explicit runtime stop that is not user stop) | **Do not** end as a blank ticket. Feed a structured event back into the agent loop for a **bounded recovery step**: model may re-check live state (e.g. did the push land?), retry only when safe, try another approach, and **must** produce a user-visible status or blocker. |

This is the product epic. Existing issues/PRs cover slices (silent death, inject interrupt reason on next turn, startup resume continue, dangling-tool prune). Nothing yet ships the full **in-loop recovery for non-user interrupts**.

## Motivation (user experience)

1. If the user asked for work and a tool fails or is yanked, the agent should be smart enough to **diagnose** and the user **deserves to know** without coming back later.
2. Even when a tool has no clean output, the brain can **re-evaluate** (check commit/push, inspect processes) and decide retry vs alternate path — the same work we already do **after** the user notices an unfinished turn.
3. True user stop stays terminal (no wake).
4. Retry budgets can be model-judged with a hard ceiling; the user can still interrupt if it takes too long. Agentic models are trained for this loop.
5. Memory/skill lines (“never empty turn”) only bias the **next** recipe card. They cannot restart a cancelled ticket or force the host to re-enter the loop.

## Current behavior (gap)

Normal path:

`brain → tool call → tool result → brain → … → final reply`

Hard / orphan interrupt path today is closer to:

`brain → tool call → [yank] → turn cancelled`  
often `response_len=0`, sometimes mislabeled `interrupted_by_user`, next message may see orphan/UNKNOWN recovery only if the user starts a new turn.

Timeouts that stay in-loop as ordinary tool errors already survive; hard interrupts and many system stops do not get the same “tool failed, your move” treatment.

## Proposed solution (epic acceptance)

### A. Classify stop kinds (host)

- Persist and propagate a real `stop_kind` (at least `user_stop` vs non-user: `client_disconnect`, `tool_orphan`, `tool_timeout_hard`, `lease_lost`, `system`, …).
- Do not collapse non-user cancels into deliberate user stop.

### B. Never empty user-visible settle

- Every interrupted turn that would have empty final text must deliver a concrete reason line to all surfaces (CLI/TUI/Desktop/WebUI/gateway/API/Relay).
- Partial assistant text should persist when present.

### C. Non-user interrupt → bounded recovery step (core)

When `stop_kind != user_stop` and the turn still has an unpaid user goal:

1. Host injects a **structured system/tool event** (not only a transcript footnote for a future turn), e.g. interrupt kind, which tool/call id, effect disposition (`unknown` / `failed` / `cancelled`), any partial output.
2. **One more model step** (or a small budgeted N) with fixed guidance:
   - Verify external effects before blind retry (push/commit/file/process).
   - Do not re-run tools that already completed successfully this turn.
   - Prefer diagnose + user-visible status; continue work only when safe.
   - Respect a recovery budget (e.g. max recovery rounds / max tool calls after interrupt).
3. Then settle with non-empty final text (done, blocked, or “paused with reason”).

### D. Safe resume / dangling tools

- Unanswered tool calls after crash/kill must not be silently pruned in a way that erases the action and invites double side effects. UNKNOWN-effect recovery must actually run.
- Startup / empty auto-resume on interactive gateways should continue the unanswered user request (not only “session restored, type continue”), with the same verify-before-retry rules. Real new user messages still take precedence / steer.

### E. Out of scope for this epic (related, separate)

- Changing deliberate user Stop into auto-continue.
- Unbounded retry storms without budget.
- Phone-only display fixes without host reason (client companions still needed).

## Related work (do not duplicate; link and layer)

**Silent death / visible reason**

- #84207 — Interrupted turn delivers zero user feedback; stop kinds conflated
- #142161 — TUI renders system interrupt as normal quiet end
- #118628 — Desktop tile close: interrupt never rendered (`error_retained=False`)
- #136160 / #136191 — Persist partial assistant text on interrupt
- #138011 — `fix(interrupt): always surface a user-visible stop reason` (visibility floor)
- #84236 — earlier visible closing message + `stop_kind` (closed; lineage for #138011)
- Codename-11/hermes-relay#634 — Android show interrupt reason when host sends one

**Tell the model / continue without waiting for the user**

- #111644 — feat: tell the model why the previous turn was interrupted (next-input guidance)
- #94942 — continue interrupted interactive turns on startup resume
- #139979 — resume interrupted tasks; empty auto-resume continues unanswered request
- #131019 — resume prunes unanswered tool calls so UNKNOWN recovery never runs (safety blocker for continue)
- #71871 — stall after hardline + orphan recovery, effect unknown
- #133561 — barge-in hard-interrupts tools instead of steering (same “adapt, don’t kill” instinct)

**Suggested implementation slices**

1. **Visibility** — land #138011 (and Relay #634); close the blank-bubble class of #84207.
2. **Provenance** — finish `stop_kind` end-to-end; never mislabel system/tool stop as user stop.
3. **Model awareness** — #111644 inject interrupt reason + do-not-blind-redo on next model input.
4. **Dangling-tool safety** — #131019 so recovery/continue cannot double-push.
5. **Continue without re-ping** — #94942 / #139979 policy + **new work**: in-loop recovery step for non-user interrupt (this epic’s core, still missing as one merged design).

## Non-goals / constraints

- Per-conversation prompt caching remains sacred; recovery injection must follow existing turn-context / gateway-note patterns, not ad-hoc mid-turn system-prompt rebuilds.
- Side-effecting tools: verify-then-act; prefer idempotent checks over blind re-exec.
- User can always hard-stop; recovery must remain interruptible.

## How to measure done

- [ ] Non-user interrupt mid-tool never settles with empty assistant text on Desktop/WebUI/TUI/gateway.
- [ ] Logs/`stop_kind` distinguish user stop vs client disconnect vs tool/system interrupt.
- [ ] After non-user interrupt, model receives a recovery event in the **same** turn or an automatic continuation turn **without** requiring the user to notice and re-ping.
- [ ] Recovery path verifies at least one external side effect class (e.g. `git` push tip) before re-running an equivalent mutating command in tests.
- [ ] Explicit user stop does **not** auto-continue the prior goal.
- [ ] #84207 / #111644 / #131019 acceptance either closed by layered PRs or explicitly superseded with links.

## Environment / context

Discussed against current main-line interrupt finalizer + orphan recovery behavior; reproduced operationally as quiet empty turns after tool orphan / explicit runtime stop, with diagnosis only after a later user message.

issues.title: [Bug]: Dashboard /sessions shows a blank pane on cold load (works after clicking Sessions)
issues.body:
## Summary On v0.22.2 the dashboard's `/sessions` route renders **only the page title** on a fresh page load — the whole right pane below it is empty. Clicking **Sessions** in the sidebar immediately afterwards renders the list normally. `/sessions` is the default post-login landing route (`App.tsx`: `/` → `Navigate to="/sessions"`), so this is the first thing a user sees after logging in. The backend is healthy: the same listing handler returns 20 rows in 0.02 s against this store. The difference is entirely on the cold-boot client path. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.22.2, commit `d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8` (install stamped `dirty: true`) - Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64 - Dashboard: `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --no-open --skip-build`, basic-auth provider, reached over Tailscale - Store: `~/.hermes/state.db`, 174 MB, WAL, 260 session rows (258 unarchived, 1 archived), ~23 600 messages, 8 sources - Browser: Chrome with DevTools ## Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the dashboard. The SPA lands on `/sessions`. 2. Observe: sidebar and the "Sessions" title render; the content area below is blank — no category chips (Chats/Automation/All), no source filter, no search box, no table, and **no empty-state message** either. 3. Click **Sessions** in the sidebar. 4. The page now renders fully (260 total, 259 in store, 1 archived, 8 sources, Connected platforms, Recent sessions). Pasting `http://:9119/sessions` into the address bar of an already-authenticated browser reproduces the blank pane the same way. ## Evidence from the browser Network panel Two page loads of the same route, same URLs: | Request | Load A | Load B (after nav click) | |---|---|---| | `GET /api/sessions?limit=20&offset=0&order=-created&exclude_sources=cron,tool,oneshot,api_server,acp,hermes` | 200, 35.99 kB, **~20.5 s** | 200, 36 kB, 387 ms | | `GET /api/sessions/empty/count?profile=default` | 200, 316 ms | 200, 212 ms | | `GET /api/sessions?limit=50&offset=0&order=-created&exclude_sources=…` | 200, 94.2 kB, 2.07 s | 200, 94.2 kB, 691 ms | All requests return `200` with a full payload — the first one merely takes ~20 s, and nothing else in the pane renders while it is in flight. No console errors were visible. (Note: the URL shown was `order=-created`; the deployed `web_routers/sessions.py` rejects any `order` other than `created`/`recent` with HTTP 400, so either the panel URL was misread on my side or the built bundle sends a direction prefix that the router does not accept. Worth checking on your side — if it is really `-created`, every listing call is a silent 400.) ## Server side, measured against the same store ``` list_sessions_rich(limit=20, offset=0, compact_rows=True, exclude_sources=[cron,tool,oneshot,api_server,acp,hermes]) -> 0.02 s, 20 rows session_count(exclude_children=True, same filters) -> 0.00 s, total 79 _maybe_auto_archive_for_profile(None) -> 0.82 s (no-op, auto_archive disabled) whole cold process incl. imports + first DB open -> 2.5 s ``` So neither the query, the store, nor auto-archive explains a 20 s first response. ## Suspected client-side failure paths (all in this repo) 1. `web/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx` — the only render path that produces an empty pane is a bare early return: ```tsx if (loading) { return (
) } ``` There is no page frame, no skeleton and no "still loading" copy — while the first listing call is outstanding, the pane is effectively blank. 2. Same file, `loadSessions`: `.catch(() => {})`. A failed first call is swallowed completely — no error state, no toast, no retry. The load effect runs once per mount (`[loadSessions, page, refreshEmptyCount]`), so nothing re-fetches until the route is remounted by a nav click. That is exactly the reported "works when I click Sessions" behaviour. 3. `web/src/lib/api.ts`, `fetchJSON`: on a 401 whose body is `{error: "unauthenticated"|"session_expired", login_url}`, it stores the location, calls `window.location.assign(body.login_url)` and then ```ts return new Promise(() => {}); ``` — a permanently pending promise. If that navigation does not win the race (parallel boot requests, or a gate 401 on one call while the cookie is actually valid), every `await` on it — including the one in `loadSessions` — hangs forever and `loading` never clears. 4. `web/src` has **no error boundary at all** (no `componentDidCatch` / `getDerivedStateFromError` anywhere). A render-time throw therefore blanks the entire app rather than the failing route; the fact that the sidebar survives here is what rules a render crash out and points at the hung/never-resolved fetch instead. ## Expected behaviour - While the first listing call is in flight, render the page frame plus a loading state, not an empty pane. - If the call fails (or its promise never settles within a timeout), surface the error and retry, rather than silently rendering zero sessions. - A cold boot at a deep link should not behave differently from clicking the same nav item. ## Workaround Click **Sessions** in the sidebar after logging in. Data is intact and the store needs no repair.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On a custom OpenAI-compatible provider whose `base_url` is a local gateway (`127.0.0.1`), every request to a Gemini model relayed by that gateway dies with:

```
Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "options": Cannot find field.
status: INVALID_ARGUMENT
```

The same gateway and the same model return 200 when the `options` field is not sent, so the field itself is what kills the request.

### Root cause (verified locally)

1. `agent/agent_init.py::_configure_ollama_num_ctx` runs the Ollama probe for **any** `is_local_endpoint(base_url)` — `query_ollama_num_ctx()` → `detect_local_server_type()` in `agent/model_metadata.py`.
2. A local aggregation gateway that answers `/api/show` in Ollama's shape (200 + `details.context_length` + `model_info`) is classified as Ollama, and `num_ctx` is taken from that payload.
3. `plugins/model-providers/custom/__init__.py:61-62` then writes `extra_body["options"] = {"num_ctx": <n>}` whenever `ollama_num_ctx` is truthy.
4. The gateway forwards `options` upstream (gateway-side bug, reported separately), and Gemini's field validation rejects it. Non-Google routes on the same gateway ignore the field, which is why only Gemini models break.

The probe result is visible in `~/.hermes/cache/local_endpoint_probes.json` as `ollama_num_ctx:<gateway>|<model>` — proof the detection fired on a server that is not Ollama.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a local OpenAI-compatible gateway that also answers `/api/show` in Ollama's shape (common for compatibility layers/aggregators).
2. Configure a custom provider pointing at it; select a Gemini model served through it.
3. Any prompt fails with the 400 above; the outgoing body carries `options.num_ctx`.
4. Setting `model.ollama_num_ctx: 0` makes it work — nothing else changes.

### Expected Behavior

`options` (an Ollama-only field) is only injected when the backend is actually Ollama, not whenever `/api/show` answers 200 with similar-shaped JSON.

### Suggested fix

- Gate the injection on the provider profile being Ollama (or on a second, shape-specific check: `details.format` / `model_info` carrying Ollama-specific keys), instead of "200 + looks Ollama-ish".
- Complement with the strip-and-retry rung: classify Google's `Unknown name … Cannot find field.` wording as a parameter rejection (same class as #125497), so a wrong injection self-heals instead of failing the model outright. `#105218` is the same bug shape for `stream_options`.

### Workaround

`model.ollama_num_ctx: 0` — an explicit 0 skips both detection and injection.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.5+12940
- Linux aarch64, custom provider → local gateway

issues.body:
Tracking issue for [#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742) (`feat/unified-gateway-runtime`). **#106742 merged to `main` on Oct 14** (merge commit `eb75627f`, branch head `2c01eb59`). This issue now tracks the post-merge fixes. Goal: every surface that talks to a **local** backend (CLI, TUI, locally-spawned Desktop, API/Responses, ACP, bots, cron, Kanban) attaches to one gateway-owned session with one FIFO, one durable queue and one writer, instead of each running its own agent on the same `state.db`.

**Status (Oct 20, 11:10 UTC):** 332 rows tracked (recounted; the last line said 329). 291 fixed on `main` and 32 not reproducible or verified unchanged on `main`, all listed in [Fixed on `main`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6152635021) and its continuations ([1](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6238639946), [package 12](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6263764122), [package 13](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6276623343)). 9 open, below. Package 1's PRs (#140676, #140678, #141090 to #141096, #141105 and #141110) merged on Oct 20 and #141573 (package 3, lane 3) on Oct 19; their 15 rows have moved to [the continuation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6238639946). #141105 fixed only T1's `/cron`; `/voice`, `/debug` and `/reasoning` are still open. #141839 and #140778 are in review on GW-19. The other seven open rows came from package 13's reviews (GW-25, GW-26, CLI-41, CLI-42, TUI-27, RT-47, CI-2) and have no PR yet. Open work is grouped into packages #139158 and #140762.

**Scope:** the local/gateway cutover only. The browser dashboard and Desktop URL / Cloud / SSH modes still talk to standalone `hermes serve`; that cutover is a staged fast-follow and is out of scope here.

Every finding reported in the comments below is collected in **[Open findings](#open-findings)**. The most recent live pass ran on `b5112db885`. The 49 commits between that head and the merge only bring in `main` and touch no gateway code, so its results apply to `main` as merged.

## Found a problem on `main`? Report here

**Report anything you hit with the unified gateway as a comment on this issue**, not as a new issue. Each report gets triaged into the tables below. The fix PR is linked back on your comment so you can retest.

Include, where you can:

- **Build:** `main` SHA (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), plus Desktop version/commit from Settings → About if Desktop is involved
- **Surface and topology:** CLI / TUI / Desktop (local) / API / ACP / bot / cron; OS; native, container or WSL; single profile or multiplexed
- **Steps, expected, actual**
- **Evidence:** the relevant lines from `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`, `errors.log`, and Desktop's `desktop.log`; for turn-state bugs, the `session_admissions` row (`intent`, `status`, `outcome`, `owner_epoch`)
- **Redact** tokens, cookies, tickets and session URLs before posting

Fixing an item? Name its ID (e.g. `CLI-15`, `N1`) in the PR so it can be ticked off here.

## Contract under test

- Queued admissions survive owner restart and run FIFO **exactly once**.
- A started admission that loses its owner becomes **unknown/interrupted** and is **never replayed automatically**.
- Retry reuses the original admission identity and committed payload.
- Clients are readers/submitters; the gateway is the only canonical writer.
- Profile, provider/issuer, generation and revision boundaries hold across every transport.

Deliberate limits (not bugs): the served profile set is a start-time snapshot (adding a profile needs `hermes gateway restart`); hosted-room execution across two profiles on one multiplexer is not live-certified.

## Verified working

| Test | Head | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hermes gateway restart` during a 40 s tool call | `86e81c4` | ✅ admission `started` → `terminal/interrupted` in 7 s; tool killed, **not replayed**; lease released; owner epoch 2 → 3; follow-up completes |
| Container network down 45 s mid-turn | `86e81c4` | ✅ model call waits with the lease held; completes 33 s after reconnect; no replay; follow-up completes |
| Stop right after submit, and on the first turn after a restart | `b5112db885` | ✅ via Ctrl+C: row `interrupted`, follow-up completes, same on owner epoch 2 (`/stop` does not work, see N4) |
| Two viewers sending identical text | `b5112db885` | ✅ 8 ms apart → 2 admissions run FIFO; one submission id sent 3× → 1 admission |
| Cron fire → `/compress` → human input | `b5112db885` | ✅ order kept; all 9 admissions terminal once; each prompt reached the model once |
| SSE approvals over `/v1/chat/completions` | `b5112db885` | ✅ `approval.request` on the stream; `/v1/runs/{id}` reports `waiting_for_approval`; approval POST completes the run (cosmetic: `last_event` stays `approval.request`) |
| Cron paused → resumed → restart | `b5112db885` | ✅ job stays enabled and fires once after a gateway comes back (depends on N1) |
| Long-session storage growth | `b5112db885` | ✅ ~0.46 MB per 100 turns, down from 8.4 MB (still linear for a live session, see LC-9) |
| API contract | `b5112db885` | ✅ `X-Hermes-Session-Id` on a CLI-owned session → 409; Idempotency-Key `/v1/runs` retry after restart replays without re-running; a different body → `idempotency_key_conflict` |
| Desktop marks a running turn ended after 45 s silence (RT-1) | `b5112db885` | ✅ fixed by `c3ecea58a8`; a second viewer sees `working` through a 60 s tool |
| Restart and reconnect (N1, N2), live in a container | `6930bb0c` | ✅ `gateway restart` on a CLI-started gateway starts a new one (twice in a row); the idle CLI's next prompt reconnects and runs once on the new owner; `/sessions` and `/bg` work before any prompt, with no local fallback; `/new` stamps `end_reason='new_session'` |

Fix commits that claimed to close a review finding before the merge (`cb8d692` → `86e81c4`): dashboard token `9112cb59`, legacy WS scope `bf7ea215`, `/compress` memory hooks `4279636b`, Kanban worker exit codes `fffab163`/`43cbb0e4`, hosted admission reauth `835aac9c`, headless cron `cdf36315`, replay gaps / ACP cancel `37662b16`, delete takes the compression chain `a942a715`/`c5ea1989`, runs `waiting_for_approval` `e6cc0fa5`, Windows local attach `145d58b7`/`996d9beb`/`2e6d4fe0`. **Claimed, not re-verified** except where a row above covers them.

## Open findings

**Open work packages:** #139158 (package 1, classic CLI; @kshitijk4poor; only T1's `/voice`, `/debug` and `/reasoning` left) · #140762 (package 11, session ids after a prune or delete, Windows clients and an elevated gateway, and stable-channel updates; @unsupportedpastels). Packages 2 to 10, 12 and 13 are closed. Rows added by package 13's reviews (GW-25, GW-26, CLI-41, CLI-42, TUI-27, RT-47, CI-2) aren't in a package yet.

**Status:** 🔴 confirmed live · 🟡 static read, not reproduced yet · ⚪ refuted or not reproduced · 🔵 needs a maintainer decision · ⬜ not tested yet · 🟠 fix in progress (no PR yet) · 🟣 fix in review (a member's PR linked) · 🟢 fixed on `main` (PR linked)

**Maintainer decisions:** rows marked "decided Oct 16" follow [this comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6207210244).

**Severity:** **broken** = fails or gives a wrong result · **degraded** = silently does less · **security** · cosmetic

**Fixed rows** move to [the first comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6152635021) once their PR lands on `main`, to keep this body under GitHub's size limit. That comment is full; later rows are in [its continuation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6238639946).

**Outside PRs:** a row is 🟣 only while a Nous member's PR is open on it. A PR from an outside contributor does not cover a row: it is listed as "outside PR to salvage", and a member still has to pick the row up, review the PR, and salvage it with credit or fix the row fresh.

**Added Oct 15, afternoon,** from @teknium1's triage at [13:57](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6193843246), [14:43](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6194816077), [15:29](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6195812785), [16:16](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6196764695), [17:47](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6198555678), [18:42](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6199619643) and [19:29](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6200538566).

**Added Oct 15, evening, and early Oct 16,** from @teknium1's triage at [21:00](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6202175381), [21:46](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6202949380), [23:17](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6204277193), [00:03](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6204859485), [01:34](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6206006907) and [02:20](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6206583465).

labels.name: provider/openrouter

labels.name: P2

labels.name: area/billing
labels.description: Account usage, credit usage, billing (cross-cutting)

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
### Summary

Cost estimates go sharply negative for routed / variable-price model slugs served through OpenRouter, because OpenRouter publishes those slugs with a negative pricing sentinel and Hermes prices the sentinel at face value.

Observed on the OpenRouter Jev router:

```
model.default: typesafe/jev-router
model.provider: openrouter
```

One ordinary turn (2 API calls, 78,487 input tokens, 64 output tokens) was recorded as:

```
estimated_cost_usd: -78551.0
cost_status:        estimated
cost_source:        provider_models_api
```

The same negative figure lands in `session_model_usage.estimated_cost_usd`, so `/insights`, `/usage`, any cost-based reporting, and any automation that gates on spend are all corrupted by it.

### Root cause

`agent/usage_pricing.py::_pricing_entry_from_metadata` reads the OpenRouter catalog pricing and multiplies the per-token number by one million:

```python
value = _to_decimal(raw)
return None if value is None else value * _ONE_MILLION
```

OpenRouter does not publish a fixed price for router slugs. `GET /api/v1/models` returns:

```
typesafe/jev-router         pricing: {"prompt": "-1", "completion": "-1"}
openrouter/auto             pricing: {"prompt": "-1", "completion": "-1"}
openrouter/pareto-code      pricing: {"prompt": "-1", "completion": "-1"}
```

-1 means "the price is set by whichever model actually serves the request". Multiplied by 1e6 the entry becomes -1,000,000 per million tokens, hence the negative estimate. Any `-1`-priced catalog entry hits this, not just jev-router.

### Suggested fix

Treat a negative catalog price as "unpriced" and let the cost fall back to unknown:

```diff
     prompt = per_million("prompt")
     completion = per_million("completion")
     request = _to_decimal(pricing.get("request"))
+    # Routed / variable-price slugs (OpenRouter's ``typesafe/jev-router``, ``openrouter/auto``,
+    # ``openrouter/pareto-code``) are listed with a NEGATIVE sentinel instead of a number: the
+    # price is set by whichever model actually served the request. Pricing them from the sentinel
+    # produces a large negative estimate, which then poisons /insights, /usage and any
+    # cost-based reporting. Treat such a route as unpriced so cost falls back to unknown.
+    if any(value is not None and value < 0 for value in (prompt, completion, request)):
+        return None
     if prompt is None and completion is None and request is None:
         return None
```

Verified locally: with the guard, the same session flips from `estimated_cost_usd: -78551.0` / `cost_status: estimated` to `estimated_cost_usd: 0.0` / `cost_status: unknown`. The pricing test selection (`pytest -k pricing`) passes: 137 passed, 1 skipped.

### Related improvement

For these routes OpenRouter returns the real per-call cost in the response body (`usage.cost`), so an actual-cost source exists without a catalog lookup. Reading it when the catalog price is missing or negative would give accurate numbers instead of `unknown` for router slugs.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.6+131.g38880bd (git install, install dir `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`)
- Provider: OpenRouter (`provider: openrouter`, `api_mode: chat_completions`)
- Router metadata confirmed the request was served by an upstream model (`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` in two runs) while the session row carried the negative estimate
