prs.title: fix(agents): recognize LM Studio at-most-zero audio rejection (#8171)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After `send_file_to_user` delivers an audio file, the tool-result keeps an audio `DataBlock` in session history. On later turns, `OpenAIChatFormatter` serializes it as `input_audio`. LM Studio (OpenAI-compatible, audio input limit = 0) rejects with:

```
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=audio)', 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': 'audio', 'code': 400}}
```

Neither `_is_audio_fallback_error()` nor `_EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS` matched this wording on `main`, so strip → retry → learn never ran and the session stayed permanently wedged.

This is a third rejection shape in the family of #7015 / #7024. Open PR #7654 covers DashScope URL-shape and llama-server `audio input is not supported`, but **not** this LM Studio `At most 0 audio(s)` body — verified against #7654's diff before opening this PR.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8171

## What Changed

- Extend `_is_audio_fallback_error` to recognize `at most N audio(s) may be provided in one prompt` and the accompanying `(parameter=audio)` / `param: audio` markers so the existing strip → retry path learns `rejects_audio`.
- Keep image/video `at most N` limits off the audio-strip path (they stay request-scoped media signals and do not teach `rejects_media` for a pure audio cap).
- Regression tests: classifier True/False cases + strip-and-retry / learn for the LM Studio body.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add clean unload and rollback-safe hot reload
prs.body:
## Description

Add a clean plugin unload path and rollback-safe hot reload so plugin install / update / uninstall no longer rebuilds every live workspace, and a failed update does not leave users on a half-applied new version.

This PR introduces a two-layer teardown ledger (`PluginInstance`) and a `PluginLifecycle` facade (`load` / `unload` / `reload` / `update_config`):

- Official `register_*` entries record real teardowns (HTTP, provider, control command, middleware, prompt section, channel, tools, hooks). Workspace contributions are projected and revoked by name via `WorkspaceProjector` (`start_one` / `stop_one` for channels). Uninstall no longer calls `_schedule_all_agents_reload`.
- Unload modes (`shutdown` / `unload` / `uninstall`) share one ledger. Author shutdown / uninstall hooks run before table rows are dropped. `shutdown` only stops hosted resources (`custody` / `effect`) and does not clear tables or disk.
- Reload probes new code into `plugin_<id>__probe` first; import failure does not tear down the old instance. Hosted resources that do not go quiescent abort the swap. Rollback restores the previous directory / modules and does not run legacy uninstall hooks. Boot recovers interrupted “updating” / “migrating” markers.
- `update_config` rebuilds contributions without reimporting; a half-successful `register()` is torn down before the old config is restored. Disable is `config.plugins[<id>].enabled = false` (reserved framework key).
- Boot dependency policy is local-only: missing deps mark the plugin `FAILED` without installing. Explicit install / update / `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` still go through `DependencyGate` (imported host-package blacklist → require restart). Console repair / status UI is intentionally not wired.
- CloudPaw no longer monkeypatches `PluginLoader.unload_plugin`; agent cleanup is an `api.provision` teardown (uninstall only).
- `LifecycleDelegate` is the single predicate at the reserved branch points (`owns_commit` / `owns_dependency_env` / `notify_unload`). Name collisions fail loudly and name the occupant.

Out of scope (documented as deferred): `SourceWatcher`, dry-run / interval-intersection gate enhancements, and Console repair / last-unload UI.

**Security Considerations:** Dependency installation stays gated: boot never networks when deps are already satisfied; colliding with an already-imported host package (e.g. `httpx`) refuses the install and does not write site-packages. Unload / reload only revoke registrations owned by the plugin id; user `agent.json` / provisioned files are not deleted on `mode=unload`. Provision / directory swap are skipped when `owns_commit` is false.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

prs.title: fix(agents): recognize llama-server and DashScope URL audio rejections in audio-fallback classifier
prs.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #7015 (fixed by #7024). The modality-aware audio stripping works, but its reactive learning entry point (`_is_audio_fallback_error`) only recognizes DashScope's "incorrect modal" rejection. Two rejection shapes still fall through and kill the entire agent turn *after* `send_file_to_user` has already delivered the audio file to the user:

1. **DashScope URL-shape rejection** — the first failure mode documented in #7015: local audio serialized as raw base64 is rejected with HTTP 400 `"The provided URL does not appear to be valid"`. This wording never reaches the audio classifier, so no strip-and-retry happens, no `rejects_audio` capability is learned, and **every subsequent turn re-crashes** while the audio block remains in session history (reproduced: the user had to switch the active model to recover the conversation).
2. **llama.cpp `llama-server`** (self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a vision-only mmproj, e.g. Qwen-VL-family GGUFs) rejects `input_audio` with HTTP 500 `"audio input is not supported - hint: ..."`. Same outcome: turn dies, nothing learned.

Both shapes were reproduced in production on QwenPaw 2.2.0 (Windows 11, Python 3.12.13):

- provider `aliyun-tokenplan` / model `qwen3.8-max` → shape 1
- custom provider → local `llama-server` (b10715) serving a Qwen-VL GGUF with vision mmproj → shape 2

The fix reuses the existing strip → retry → learn machinery: both shapes now classify as audio-fallback errors, so the turn recovers and `rejects_audio` is learned for the model key (subsequent requests strip audio proactively while images keep working).

**Related Issue:** Relates to #7015

**Security Considerations:** None. The change only widens error-message classification for the existing audio strip-and-retry path; no new inputs are accepted and no credential/config handling is touched. The URL-shape match is gated on a 400-class status and, at the call site, on `_last_wire_request_had_audio()`, so malformed image/video URLs cannot be misclassified as audio rejections (addressing the concern raised in #7015 about matching the URL error broadly).

## Description

Internal task identities, trajectories and private evidence remain outside the website. Summary metadata retains release/artifact identity, budgets, benchmark revisions, judge configuration, confirmed costs, coverage and elapsed time.

The default view selects GAIA, SpreadsheetBench Verified, SWE-bench Verified and PawBench at 25% each. Users can edit the selected benchmarks and relative weights in an anchored desktop panel or mobile sheet; applying a draft updates scores, costs, runtimes, rankings and the frontier together. Missing selected benchmarks remain incomplete, rather than receiving a different weighting per record.

Execution/scoring exceptions count as zero. Each benchmark's confirmed model and judge spending is divided by its full task count, with coverage retained; CNY amounts use the fixed rate of 7 CNY per USD. Runtime averages use recorded task durations. Public inputs retain the reviewed QwenPaw 2.2.2 cohort across qwen3.8-max, glm-5.2 and deepseek-v4-pro; the DeepSeek cohort reuses the release-equivalent evaluation with its original artifact digest, scores and timestamps. ## Description

Fix two connected UX problems in the thinking-strength control:

1. **Misleading fill:** the full rail is colored even at Low, because the rail has
   the gradient while the selected track is transparent.
2. **Flicker / rollback while saving:** every preference write dims and disables
   the whole panel. The panel also receives the last confirmed value rather than
   the existing preview, so its label can briefly revert to the previous strength.

### Complete fix

- Use the existing neutral `--app-fill-strong` rail and `--app-accent` selected
  track; keep Ant Design's own value-dependent track width.
- Remove the full-width budget gradient override and its unused custom property.
  Hide selected fill and thumb when the effective default is unresolved.
- Feed the same latest preview to the panel and trigger indicator. Ordinary
  strength saves no longer dim or disable the whole panel.
- Serialize writes so an older request cannot finish after and overwrite a newer
  selection. Older confirmations do not clear a newer preview, including a drag
  still in progress. A failed latest save restores the last confirmed value.
- Scope queued writes and responses to their originating chat. Reads wait for
  outstanding writes; switching chats invalidates queued work and old responses.
- Preserve the existing advanced decision-setting API and its edit lock. Cover
  both saved chats and new chats; decision updates retain the thinking state.

The complete PR changes **four existing frontend files**, including regression
tests. It adds no dependencies, business integration code, backend changes, public
API changes, or model/inference functionality.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8286

**Security Considerations:** UI state and styling only. No changes to authentication,
permissions, credential handling, or backend endpoints. Review fixtures contain
no real account, model calls, or business data.

## Type of Change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks (no auto-fixes required)
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass: full frontend suite with coverage
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed): N/A, no new feature, API, configuration, or usage steps
- [x] Ready for review

Channel contract checks and Python backend tests are not applicable to this
frontend-only change. No channel implementation or contract changes.

## Testing

1. Open a model's thinking-strength control and select a lower strength. Color
   should stop at the thumb; the remaining rail stays neutral.
2. Add network latency to the preference PUT request. Click a different strength:
   the title and thumb should immediately retain the new choice without dimming.
3. Click multiple levels rapidly and drag while an earlier save completes. The
   latest selection must stay visible and the final persisted value must match it.
4. Check exact numeric budgets, off, the compact settings control, hover and dark
   mode. An unresolved default should imply no selected amount.
5. Exercise the advanced decision-setting switch and verify that thinking edits
   remain functional in both existing and newly created chats.

Five regression cases were added in `SessionThinking.test.tsx`: delayed ordered
saves, failure rollback, chat-switch invalidation, and advanced-settings
compatibility for an existing chat and a new chat. The original unchanged-state
and pending-model tests are retained.

## Evidence

Based on official `main` at `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`.
Complete fix head: `ae88d83f` (includes the original fill correction).

npm ci

**Real browser, fill:** Chrome 155; low ~1/3, medium ~2/3, high 1, off 0 for
fixture levels off/low/medium/high. Both `qwenpaw`/`ant` prefixes, exact budgets,
compact height, unresolved defaults, hover and dark mode were checked.

**Real browser, saving:** Electron 22 / Chromium 108, actual official
`SessionThinking` with fixture HTTP responses delayed 650 ms. **322 timed renderer
samples** retained the expected label, value, track color, and panel geometry:
no value rollback, whole-panel dimming, or layout shift. Real mouse clicks and a
held drag were exercised. Requests were sequential, the final saved value matched
the last choice, and the existing advanced decision switch saved successfully.
No runtime errors or unhandled rejections; the isolated dev fixture records one
React development-mode forwardRef warning separately.

Custom channel configuration without a `config_fields` schema renders arrays and objects as `[object Object]` in the Console. Editing these inputs can replace structured configuration with a string.

prs.title: fix(matrix): normalize pasted connection credentials
prs.body:
## Description

Pasting a Matrix user ID or access token with surrounding whitespace prevents the channel from starting. A padded user ID is compared literally against the successful `whoami` response and rejected as a different account; a padded token is sent in the Authorization header and rejected by the homeserver.

Strip surrounding whitespace from the homeserver URL, user ID and access token when constructing `MatrixChannel`. This covers configuration and environment entry points. Preserve passwords, internal credential characters, letter case and the existing account-owner check.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #2882

**Security Considerations:** Authentication remains mandatory and token ownership validation remains strict. Password whitespace is preserved. The HTTP reproduction uses synthetic credentials against a local server; no real account tokens are included.

prs.title: fix(channels): retain consumers until shutdown cleanup finishes
prs.body:
## Description

A channel reload can discard a cancelled consumer while it is still awaiting asynchronous cleanup. `UnifiedQueueManager.stop_all()` waits five seconds and then clears `_queues`; after the replaced manager loses its owner, the task/future cycle can be collected and asyncio emits `Task was destroyed but it is pending!`.

Keep shutdown consumers in a module-level set before cancelling them, then release them and retrieve any exception when they actually finish. The existing five-second shutdown deadline and queue cleanup behavior are preserved. A manager-local collection would not suffice because it would be part of the same collectable cycle.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #3361

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, channel transport, permissions or message content handling changes. The fix keeps cancelled cleanup tasks alive until they complete.

- [x] Existing contract tests implement `create_instance()`
- [x] All contract verification points pass
- [x] Unit regression tests cover the queue manager shutdown lifecycle

## Testing

Linux 6.8.0-138-generic x86_64, Python 3.11.15; base `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`; isolated environment installed with `uv pip install -e ".[dev,test,full]"`.

The reproduction runs the real queue manager and asyncio event loop, enqueues a `feishu` message, and lets the consumer enter asynchronous cleanup on cancellation. It waits the actual five-second shutdown grace period, releases the manager, invokes garbage collection, and captures the loop exception handler. Only weak references to the task and cleanup future remain outside production code. The fixed run also finishes or cancels cleanup and verifies both task and manager are collected afterwards.

This reproduces the reported queue lifecycle failure on Linux.

## Evidence

Exact baseline source:

```text
stop_all: 1 consumer(s) still pending after 5s
queues_after_shutdown: 0
consumer_alive_after_manager_release: False
loop_errors: ['Task was destroyed but it is pending!']
```

Fixed source:

```text
stop_all: 1 consumer(s) still pending after 5s
queues_after_shutdown: 0
consumer_alive_after_manager_release: True
loop_errors: []
consumer_released_after_cleanup: True
manager_released_after_cleanup: True
```

Both expect HTTP 404/400 for GET requests to routes that support other methods and currently return HTTP 405. They do not exercise the code changed by this PR.

prs.title: fix(drivers): preserve concurrent policy updates during driver reload (#7850)
prs.body:
## Description

When `DriverManager.reload_driver()` executes, it performs a read-modify-write on the driver card whose read and write were separated by the slow `_build_and_init_handler` step. The final save was unconditional: a background reload whose card snapshot predated a concurrent policy write (via `sync_driver_policy`) would persist the stale snapshot after the policy write, overwriting the policy on disk (`ask` overwriting `allow`). In addition, the newly initialized handler never had the authoritative policy reapplied, leading to in-memory policy drift.

This pull request resolves the issue by:
1. Eliminating the redundant `self._card_store.save(card)` in `reload_driver()`. Driver reload is a lifecycle consumer rather than a persistence writer.
2. In the locked publication phase (`_swap_reloaded_handler`), re-reading the authoritative card from disk and reconciling the newly built handler with the latest policy (`handler.set_policy(latest_card.policy)`) and runtime metadata (`handler.sync_runtime_metadata(latest_card)`).
3. Safely retiring and shutting down handlers outside the lock if the card was disabled or removed during initialization.
4. Applying the same policy reconciliation logic to `register_driver()` to prevent potential drift during initial driver registration.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7850

**Security Considerations:** Ensures that access-control policies configured by users or workers (such as `allow` effects) are strictly preserved and enforced without silent regression to default `ask` prompts.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

Reproduce and verify the concurrent policy write during driver reload:
1. Register an MCP client that requires slow handshake/initialization.
2. Concurrently send a policy update (`PUT /api/mcp/policy/{client_key}` with `default_effect: allow`).
3. Wait for the background reload to finish.
4. Verify that `GET /api/mcp/policy/{client_key}` retains `allow` and does not revert to `ask`.
5. Run driver unit tests and integration tests:
   `pytest tests/unit/drivers -v`
   `pytest tests/integration/test_mcp.py -v`

## Evidence

The bug and its fix have been verified locally through pre-commit code quality checks, the full driver test suite, and deterministic Before/After concurrency replays on a live server process.

**1. Pre-commit Code Quality Gate**
```bash
$ pre-commit run --all-files
check python ast.........................................................Passed
check docstring is first.................................................Passed
fix python encoding pragma...............................................Passed
detect private key.......................................................Passed
trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed
Add trailing commas......................................................Passed
mypy.....................................................................Passed
black....................................................................Passed
flake8...................................................................Passed
pylint...................................................................Passed
```

**2. Automated Test Suite Results**
```bash
$ pytest tests/unit/drivers -q
415 passed in 9.79s

$ pytest tests/integration/test_mcp.py -q
10 passed in 19.45s
```

**3. Live Runtime Concurrency Verification (Before vs After)**

Before Fix (Broken State - Lost Update on Disk):
```text
[workerflow_repro_1] Step 1: POST /api/mcp to register client (triggers slow background reload)...
[workerflow_repro_1] Step 1 POST status: 201
[workerflow_repro_1] Step 2: Concurrently PUT /api/mcp/policy/workerflow_repro_1 to 'allow'...
[workerflow_repro_1] Step 2 PUT status: 200
[workerflow_repro_1] Immediate GET readback (before reload ends): default_effect = allow
[workerflow_repro_1] Step 3: Background reload completes build and unconditional save...
[workerflow_repro_1] Step 4 GET readback (after reload completed): default_effect = ask
>>> BROKEN STATE DETECTED: Policy reverted from 'allow' to 'ask'! (Lost Update)
```

After Fix (Verified State - Policy Preserved on Disk and Handler):
```text
[workerflow_allow_1] Step 1: POST /api/mcp to register client (triggers slow background reload)...
[workerflow_allow_1] Step 1 POST status: 201
[workerflow_allow_1] Step 2: Concurrently PUT /api/mcp/policy/workerflow_allow_1 to 'allow'...
[workerflow_allow_1] Step 2 PUT status: 200
[workerflow_allow_1] Immediate GET readback (before reload ends): default_effect = allow
[workerflow_allow_1] Step 3: Background reload completes with state reconciliation...
[workerflow_allow_1] Step 4 GET readback (after reload completed): default_effect = allow
>>> PASS: Policy successfully preserved as 'allow' on disk and live handler!
```

prs.title: feat(console): refine model management experience
prs.body:
## 背景

模型管理页面同时承载全局模型、提供商配置和智能体模型设置，作用域与交互层级不清晰；部分高频操作需要进入完整弹窗，对话页模型管理态也缺少明确退出入口。

本 PR 将模型管理、智能体运行配置和对话模型选择按作用域重新分层，并补齐思考能力联动、自动保存和响应式验证。

## 修改内容

### 全局模型与提供商

- 明确“全局默认模型”的作用域，模型页聚焦提供商、凭据和模型目录
- 修正搜索空状态、接入变体名称和提供商操作术语
- 支持在提供商卡片内直接添加或修改 API Key，完整配置仍由设置入口承担
- 延迟加载非首屏提供商图标，减少重复辅助技术朗读

### 智能体运行配置

- 将当前智能体的主模型、思考强度、子智能体模型和备用模型迁入“运行配置 → 工作环境”
- 统一四类设置的行级布局和自动保存行为
- 备用模型调整为“先启用、再选择模型”的两步交互

### 思考能力联动

- 统一模型默认思考与高级思考能力声明
- 声明变化时清理不兼容的档位、预算和开关
- 智能体思考强度同时约束主模型、子智能体模型和备用模型

### 对话页模型选择器

- 管理态时将右上角齿轮替换为始终可见的“完成”
- 提供商“管理模型”只负责展开或收起局部候选区
- 退出管理态不关闭选择器、不切换模型，也不修改模型池

## 验证

- 模型页面、运行配置、自动保存和思考联动相关定点测试通过
- `ModelSelector.test.tsx`：61/61 通过
- 相关文件 ESLint、Prettier 与 `git diff --check` 通过
- localhost:5176 完成桌面端与 390px 小尺寸实际交互验证
- “完成”按钮实测为 62 × 32px；退出后移除控件消失、齿轮恢复，浏览器无错误日志
- GitHub Frontend Tests、Vitest、Pre-commit、格式检查、Playwright Smoke 与 CodeQL 通过

## 边界与已知问题

- 未新增依赖，不修改后端配置契约
- 不改变提供商启停、模型卡片尺寸和模型启用开关的业务语义
- 390px 下主要模型配置流程可操作；运行配置页仍存在横向溢出，作为后续响应式修复项

prs.title: fix(security): protect skill directories against prompt-injected deletion (#7859)
prs.body:
## Description

This PR implements path-based integrity protection for agent skills and knowledge directories against destructive operations and prompt-injected deletion attacks (#7859).

### Architectural Design & ACI Alignment
In line with the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) and modern harness security principles (least privilege, capability tiering, and infrastructure immutability):
- Prompt filtering via regex blacklists is fundamentally brittle and cannot serve as a reliable security boundary against prompt injection.
- Security boundaries must be enforced at the **capability and execution layer** (Tool Guard / File Guardian).
- Agent skills constitute the agent's executable knowledge infrastructure and must be protected as **immutable assets**:
  - **Read operations** (e.g., `read_file`, `view_text_file`) are classified as PURE/read-only and remain permitted so the agent can execute skills normally.
  - **Mutation operations** (e.g., `write_file`, `edit_file`, `append_file`, `delete_file`) and destructive shell operations targeting protected skill paths are intercepted by `FilePathToolGuardian` with `PROTECTED_SKILL_MODIFICATION` findings (HIGH severity).
- Protects `<workspace>/skills`, `skill_pool`, and builtin skills directories.
- Configurable via `security.file_guard.protect_skills` (defaults to `True`) and exposed in the REST API.
- Expands `TOOL_CMD_DANGEROUS_RM` in `dangerous_shell_commands.yaml` to include directory removal commands (`rmdir`, `rd`, `erase`, `ri`).

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7859

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [x] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

Run unit test suite for tool guard:
```bash
pytest tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_file_guardian.py \
       tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_rule_guardian.py -v
```

## Evidence

The security protection mechanism has been verified with comprehensive unit tests and deterministic Before/After reproduction on positive and negative control suites.

**1. Unit Tests**
```
collected 191 items
tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_file_guardian.py .......................................................................................................... [ 55%]
tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_rule_guardian.py ..................................................................................... [100%]
============================== 191 passed in 0.81s ==============================
```

**2. Protection Verification (Positive & Negative Controls)**
```
=== REPRODUCTION AFTER EVIDENCE ===
- rmdir skills command: is_safe: False, findings: ['PROTECTED_SKILL_MODIFICATION', 'TOOL_CMD_DANGEROUS_RM']
- write_file to skills: findings: 1 ['PROTECTED_SKILL_MODIFICATION']
- edit_file on skills: findings: 1 ['PROTECTED_SKILL_MODIFICATION']
- rd skills (Windows): is_safe: False, findings: ['PROTECTED_SKILL_MODIFICATION', 'TOOL_CMD_DANGEROUS_RM']

=== NEGATIVE CONTROLS (Legitimate operations NOT blocked) ===
- read_file on skills: findings: 0 (Allowed)
- cat on skills: is_safe: True, findings: 0 (Allowed)
- write_file to ordinary workspace project file: findings: 0 (Allowed)
```

## Additional Notes
None.

prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
- `_maybe_cap_total` spends the budget as each media source is formatted and
  returns a placeholder once the next one no longer fits.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- Every `format()` scopes the budget to its own call via a `ContextVar`, and
  resets it in a `finally`.

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
45 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

Each of the 6 budget tests fails with the cumulative check neutralised
(verified by reverting `_maybe_cap_total` to a no-op):

```
FAILED test_budget_spends_down_and_then_caps
FAILED test_undersized_media_still_spends_the_budget
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingOpenAIFormatter]
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingAnthropicFormatter]
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingGeminiFormatter]
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingDashScopeFormatter]
6 failed, 38 passed
```

Wider runs — no regressions; the failures listed are pre-existing on clean
`main` in this environment (git-version dependent, and two need a real
container runtime):

```
$ pytest tests/unit -q
# main:               23 failed, 17021 passed
# this branch:        23 failed, 17037 passed   (+16 = the new tests)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- `model_factory`'s tool-result video path (`_video_oversize_placeholder`)
  applies its own per-file cap and is untouched — it does not go through
  these formatters, so it is not covered by the cumulative budget. Worth a
  follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.
