prs.title: fix(web): keep the in-flight prompt when chat hydration replaces local state
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The gateway commits a turn's user prompt only when the turn finishes, so a chat transcript fetched while a detached turn is still running does not contain the prompt the browser already showed. Hydration replaced the local transcript with that snapshot and the mirror effect then overwrote `localStorage`, so the prompt disappeared on reload (and on a round trip to another conversation) while the turn kept running.
  - Hydration now keeps the uncommitted tail of *this conversation's* browser copy: it starts at the earliest pending prompt the browser composed itself (`local: true`) and runs to the end of the copy. A prompt is pending when it occurs more often in the browser copy, up to and including itself, than in the snapshot; the gateway commits turns in order, so the committed occurrences are the earliest ones. Counting occurrences, rather than testing presence, keeps a repeated prompt such as "continue" from being mistaken for one the snapshot already holds. Earlier pending prompts are included only while no finished turn lies between them (a turn that already has its final answer, an agent reply that is not a tool call, is not pending), so a second prompt queued behind a running turn does not displace the first one.
  - The browser copy is read from `localStorage` for the conversation being hydrated, before the mirror effect can overwrite it. A session switch empties the in-memory transcript, so reading it from state lost the prompt on A → B → A.
  - The comparison lives in a new pure helper (`chatHydration.logic.ts`) that strips the runtime's `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: <date> <tz>]` prefix from the rows that came from the server before comparing, so a committed prompt is not shown twice. Rows the browser composed (`local: true`) are the user's verbatim input and are compared as they are, so a prompt the user typed with that prefix is not duplicated either.
- **Scope boundary:** this PR changes only how hydration reconciles the browser copy with the server snapshot. It does **not**: consult `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` or keep the composer disabled while a turn runs (that is #9002); add `beforeunload` handling; recover the partial streamed response or add live replay (#7759); persist the prompt on the server when the turn is accepted (see *Server-side half*); restore tool, cron or error bubbles of finished turns (the server never persists them); strip the `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]` prefix from hydrated user bubbles for display (observed on `master`, separate finding). See *Known limits* below.
- **Blast radius:** `web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx` (the hydration effect and one import), a new `web/src/contexts/chatHydration.logic.ts`, tests, and the `test:contexts` script in `web/package.json`. No change to `chatHistoryStorage.ts`, the `localStorage` format, the API, config, or any Rust. #9002 (draft, not merged) also edits `AgentContext.tsx` (it adds `recoverDetachedTurn` and its import hunk is near the one here), so whichever lands second should rebase; this PR changes only the initial hydration effect.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11517. Related #9002.

### What this does, simply

With session persistence on (the default), reloading the dashboard while the agent is still working on a turn made the question you had just asked vanish, together with your browser's copy of it, even though the agent kept going. The server only stores a question once its answer is finished, so the page was rebuilding the chat from a copy of the server's record that did not have your question yet.

This change makes the page keep the question it already showed until the server's record contains it. If the server's record already has it (the turn finished), nothing extra is shown, so the question never appears twice. Switching to another conversation and back while a turn runs is covered the same way.

**Known limits (not addressed here; the root cause is server-side: there is no turn id or commit at accept time, so the client can only compare text):**

- A repeated prompt can still be dropped when the browser copy was truncated to its 100-bubble cap, or when another client already committed the same text and this browser's identical prompt is still running. This is not worse than `master`, which drops the in-flight prompt in every such case. Unit tests pin both (`known limit: …`).
- A local prompt that the gateway has already trimmed away (default cap of 50 whole turns, `max_history_messages`) can reappear and stays until the next locally composed prompt. By reading the server code (`history_trim.rs`, `kept_turns = max_turns.max(1)…`) the newest turn is always kept, so this needs 50+ later turns that did not go through this browser's copy, for example from another browser or device or the session message API. This is inferred from reading; it was not reproduced.
- A conversation deleted outside this browser (through the API or another client) brings back its last exchange when it is opened here again, and keeps it in the browser copy. `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` answers 200 with no messages both for a session that no longer exists and for a turn that has not committed yet (`api.rs`, `handle_api_session_messages`), so the client cannot tell them apart. `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` does answer 404 for a missing session, but consulting it is outside this PR and overlaps #9002. Only the last exchange comes back, not the whole cached chat, and `master` would show an empty chat in that case. A test pins it (`known limit: a conversation deleted elsewhere keeps its last exchange in this browser`).

### Server-side half (not part of this PR)

The limits above come from one cause on the server, which this PR does not change: the gateway writes a chat prompt to the session store only when the turn ends.

- At accept time the WebSocket handler marks the session `running` and does not write the transcript (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs`, `// Set session state to running`). The only `.append(` of a chat message in the gateway is the REST handler (`api.rs`, `backend.append(&session_key, &message)`); there is none in `ws.rs` (searched with a pattern that matches the `api.rs` line).
- The prompt then lives only in the agent's in-memory history (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs`, `append_streamed_user_message_to_history`) and reaches the store through `persist_agent_conversation_state` when the turn finishes (`ws.rs`, the success and the error branches).
- Observed with a real gateway in the manual A/B below: while `/state` was `running`, `GET /api/sessions/<S>/messages` returned `[]`, and the prompt row appeared with a `created_at` about 60 s after `turn_started_at`, 12 ms after the mock logged `stream finished`.

Making the prompt durable when the turn is accepted (for example by appending it before the session is marked `running`) would put it in the snapshot during the turn. From reading the helper in this PR (not tested), that would remove the first limit above in both variants, because the snapshot would already hold the prompt. It would not by itself remove the second limit, which also needs the client to stop merging its local copy, or a turn id; and a dashboard talking to an older gateway would still need the merge. By reading the code, it would also cover a gateway restart in the middle of a turn, which this PR cannot. I did not analyze how an earlier write interacts with the per-connection transcript watermark, nor how a transcript that ends in an unanswered user message should be re-seeded into the agent. This is context for reviewers, not a design proposal, and nothing here depends on it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes (optional): the automated tests below cover the logic; a manual A/B shows the user-visible delta.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (dashboard chat).
- **Setup / preconditions:** gateway running with the web dashboard served and `session_persistence = true` (the default), and a model provider that streams slowly enough to reload mid-turn (a local mock that emits chunks once per second is enough). `quickstart` needs a terminal, so a headless setup can use `zeroclaw config set` instead.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the dashboard chat and send a long prompt, for example "Write a 3000 word essay on the history of printing".
  2. While the turn is running, confirm `GET /api/sessions/<S>/state` is `running` and `GET /api/sessions/<S>/messages` does not contain the new prompt.
  3. Reload the page (F5) and check the chat and `localStorage › zeroclaw_chat_history_v1:<S>`.
  4. Repeat step 3 a second time before the turn ends.
  5. Wait until `/state` is `idle`, then reload once more.
  6. Variant: with the turn still running, switch to another conversation and back. (Covered by the automated tests only; I did not run this one in the real interface.)
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the prompt stays on screen and in `localStorage` after each reload (steps 3 and 4) and after the round trip (step 6); after the turn commits (step 5) the prompt and the answer appear once, with no duplicated prompt (the prompt still shows the raw `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]` prefix, as on `master`). Unchanged by this PR and visible in the screenshots: the composer stays enabled while `/state` is `running` (#9002), and the screen does not update when the turn ends until the next reload.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** after the reload the chat shows "Send a message to start the conversation", `localStorage` holds `{"messages":[]}`, and the composer is enabled while `/state` is still `running`. Observed twice with a built gateway, the real dashboard and Chrome, using a mock streaming provider (not a real model): on `master` at `74362c2d` (2026-10-01) and again on 2026-10-06 with the gateway built from this branch and the dashboard bundle built with the base `AgentContext.tsx` (see "How I tested").

### How I tested

Automated, on the branch head `5d69cdf84` (two commits on top of `f5f3b8d5c`, parent `e654b4b7`; as of 2026-10-06 `master` has moved on to `b9ec3e9a` without touching `web/` and a trial merge is clean). The regression tests are in `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` (harness already in the file) and in the new `web/src/contexts/chatHydration.logic.test.ts`.

- `F5 while a detached turn is still running keeps the prompt the browser already showed`: red on the unpatched `AgentContext.tsx` (`AssertionError: hydration must not drop a locally-sent prompt the server has not committed yet`), green on this branch.
- `an uncommitted prompt does not follow the operator into another conversation` (includes the return to the first conversation): red unpatched, green patched.
- `reloading twice while the same detached turn is still running keeps the prompt each time`: red unpatched, green patched.
- `a second prompt queued behind a running turn does not displace the first one on the next reload`: red on the previous head (`f5f3b8d5c`, which kept only the last prompt), green now.
- `known limit: a conversation deleted elsewhere keeps its last exchange in this browser`: green on both; it pins the behavior described under *Known limits*.
- `F5 after the detached turn committed shows the prompt once, with its answer` and `returning to a conversation whose turn committed meanwhile shows the prompt once`: green both ways; they guard against duplication. Their fixtures use the real prefix (`[CURRENT DATE & TIME: <date> <tz>]\n\n<prompt>`, `agent.rs` `enrich_user_message`) and the real row shape `{role, content, created_at}` (`api.rs` messages handler).
- Helper unit tests (13): prefix stripping, empty snapshot, already-committed prompt, only the last prompt and its tail, repeated prompts, server-rebuilt bubbles from an earlier reload, no local prompt, the two `known limit:` cases, and four added with the second commit (every pending prompt is kept, an earlier committed prompt is not brought back, answered turns are not brought back, a typed prefix is compared verbatim). Three of those four were red against the previous helper; the "answered turns" one guards against bringing back more than before.

How this maps to the criteria in the triage comment on #11517: the uncommitted prompt survives a reload (the first and third tests above, and the two-prompt test); no duplicates once the turn committed (the two guard tests); no cross-session carryover (the second test checks that the other conversation gets only its own snapshot and that returning keeps the first one's prompt); repeated prompts (`a repeated prompt is not mistaken for the committed one`, `server-rebuilt bubbles from an earlier reload count toward the local occurrences`, plus the two `known limit:` tests for the edges that remain); server-prefixed content (the guard tests use the real `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]` prefix and `strips the runtime date prefix the gateway persists on user rows` covers the helper).

The "red unpatched" runs used the `AgentContext.tsx` of the previous base (`3c8a6763`); `web/` is byte-identical between that commit and `e654b4b7`. The red runs for the second commit's tests used the helper of `f5f3b8d5c` (the previous head).

```sh
# Windows 11, Node v24.14.0, web/ (sessionLifecycle: 8 tests with includeChat=true also fail on a clean master here)
JITI_JSX=1 JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS=1 npx jiti src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts
ℹ tests 26 / ℹ pass 18 / ℹ fail 8      # the same 8 fail on clean master (19 tests / 11 pass / 8 fail before this change's tests)

# Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu), Node 24, api-generated.ts regenerated with `cargo web check`
JITI_JSX=1 JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS=1 npx jiti src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts
ℹ tests 26 / ℹ pass 26 / ℹ fail 0
npm run test:contexts            # pretest:contexts hook (8 + 14 + 26 tests) then the node --test files (45)
ℹ tests 45 / ℹ pass 45 / ℹ fail 0
npx tsc -b                       # exit 0
npm run build                    # exit 0 (only the chunk-size warning)
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Web Permission Tests` runs `npm run test:contexts` (`ci.yml`, `run: npm run test:contexts`), and npm runs the `pretest:contexts` hook first, which executes `sessionLifecycle.test.ts`; together with the new `chatHydration.logic.test.ts` registered in `test:contexts`, CI covers the regression tests. The checks on the current head `5d69cdf84` finished with no failures (checked on 2026-10-06): 47 succeeded and 7 were skipped, including `CI Required Gate` and `Web Permission Tests`. The previous head `f5f3b8d5c` also finished green.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known. Note for reviewers on Windows: 8 tests of `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` fail on a clean `master` there (`useAgent must be used within AgentProvider`, only the tests that mount `AgentChatInner`); the cause was not established. They pass on Linux.
- **Commands run and tail output:** see the block above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** An A/B end to end on 2026-10-06 with one gateway (built from this branch, WSL2) and two dashboard bundles, one built with the base `AgentContext.tsx` and one with the fix, driven by the same script in Chrome with a mock provider that streams 60 chunks at one per second. Without the fix, after a reload while `/state` was `running` the chat was empty and `localStorage` was `{"messages":[]}`, on two consecutive reloads. With the fix, the prompt stayed on screen and in `localStorage` (`"local":true`) after both reloads while `/messages` was still empty; after the turn finished, one more reload showed the prompt and the answer once. The first-ever run of the "before" side was discarded: the agent failed to start because the test config lacked a risk profile, so no turn was running. **Not verified:** the second commit in the real interface (the A/B above ran on `f5f3b8d5c` and was not repeated; the second commit is covered by the automated tests only); a real model provider; the conversation round trip in the real interface (only in the automated tests); two tabs or two devices on the same conversation; the second known limit beyond reading the server code; repeated runs (one run per side).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head `5d69cdf84` for the automated tests and `f5f3b8d5c` for the manual A/B and the screenshots (parent `e654b4b7`); interface `web` (dashboard chat), Chrome stable headless at 1280×800 on Windows against a gateway in WSL2; the gateway was built from a copy of this tree without `.git` (so `--version` prints `unknown`). Dimensions are recorded only because the screenshots are viewport captures.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** posted in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11571#issuecomment-6020347025): `1-before-F5.png` (turn running just before the reload; the same in both runs), `before/2-after-F5.png` (empty chat after reload, without the fix), `after/2-after-F5.png` and `after/2b-after-second-F5-turn-running.png` (prompt kept after one and two reloads, with the fix), `after/4-reload-after-commit.png` (prompt and answer once after the turn committed). In the file names "after" means after the reload (F5), not after the fix; the captions in the comment say which run each one is.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** reload twice while a turn is running, then once after it finishes. Without the fix the prompt disappears from the screen and from `localStorage`; with the fix it stays on screen and in `localStorage` until the server has it, and appears once together with the answer after the commit. The composer is still enabled during the turn and the screen still does not refresh on its own when the turn ends; both are outside this PR.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --locked`, `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh` and `./dev/ci.sh all` were skipped because the diff touches only `web/` (no Rust). `cargo web check` was run (it regenerates the API types and runs `tsc -b`).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (fixtures use generic text such as `long task`, `continue`, `from B` and a fixed example date)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No (the change only decides which locally composed text the dashboard keeps showing; nothing is sent to the model)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (the `localStorage` entry keeps the same shape; `chatHistoryStorage.ts` is not modified)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

The issue is labelled `risk:medium`, so:

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` (single commit, `web/` only)
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** client-side only, there are no logs or metrics. prs.body:
# PR title

feat(channels): make acknowledgement reactions configurable

# PR body

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** The acknowledgement reactions the channel orchestrator puts on an inbound message were hard-coded (👀 on receipt, then ✅ on success or ⚠️ on failure) and `channels.ack_reactions` could only switch the whole lifecycle on or off. Operators could not match a house emoji convention, and there was no way to show progress and then leave no reaction behind. This PR makes the three emoji configurable under `[channels]`, adds alias-scoped overrides on the channels that already carry alias-scoped acknowledgement config, and adds an explicit empty-string "withdraw the acknowledgement and add nothing" mode.
- **Scope boundary:** Telegram is deliberately unchanged (see below). No other channel's acknowledgement behavior changes, no new dependency, no CLI or env-var surface, and the no-reply intent emoji is untouched. Per-alias overrides are not added to Discord, Signal, or the Git forge channels.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (schema), `zeroclaw-api` (a defaulted `Channel::inbound_ack_emoji` method), `zeroclaw-channels` (orchestrator resolution plus the Lark inbound fast-ack), and the channels documentation. Every new field is optional and every default reproduces today's behavior byte for byte, so an existing `config.toml` behaves identically.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11753. Related #11739 (Telegram `remove_reaction`), which the Telegram side of these settings depends on. Filed as an ordinary feature request, because the RFC process lists a "configuration field or default change" as explicitly not RFC-shaped.

### What this does, simply

When a message arrives on a channel, ZeroClaw puts a reaction on it so the sender knows the agent picked it up, and swaps that reaction for another one when the answer is ready. Those emoji used to be fixed in the code: eyes while working, a check mark on success, a warning sign on failure. The only knob was `ack_reactions`, which turned the whole thing off.

This PR adds three keys under `[channels]`:

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ack_reaction_in_progress` | 👀 | Added while the agent works. An empty string disables the in-progress acknowledgement. |
| `ack_reaction_done` | ✅ | Replaces the in-progress acknowledgement once the turn completes. An empty string withdraws it and adds nothing. |
| `ack_reaction_error` | ⚠️ | Replaces the in-progress acknowledgement when the turn fails. An empty string withdraws it and adds nothing. |

Slack, Matrix, and Lark instances can override each value per alias, the same way the existing `ack_reactions` override works. An override that is left out keeps the global value, so a single key can change without restating the others:

```toml
[channels.slack.work]
ack_reaction_in_progress = "⏳"
ack_reaction_done = ""
```

That instance shows ⏳ while the turn runs and leaves no reaction on the message afterwards, which was previously impossible without turning reactions off entirely. An explicit empty override is stored as an empty string, not treated as "unset": `zeroclaw config set channels.slack.work.ack_reaction_done ""` keeps the override instead of clearing it back to the global value, so the withdraw-only mode survives a round trip. Leaving the key out is still what inherits the global value.

Defaults are exactly today's behavior. On Slack the value may be a Unicode emoji (`⏳`) or a Slack short name (`:hourglass_flowing_sand:`); the Unicode-to-name map gained ⏳, and anything outside the map keeps the existing colon-trimming pass-through, so workspace emoji names still work.

Telegram is not covered by these emoji settings. It posts its own acknowledgement from the fixed set the Telegram Bot API accepts (⚡️, 👌, 👀, 🔥, 👍) and does not go through the orchestrator's add/remove lifecycle, so `ack_reactions` remains its only switch. It keeps its current behavior here. **This PR depends on a separate bug-fix PR that adds Telegram `remove_reaction`; the Telegram emoji can only be wired to these settings once that lands.** Because Telegram's default `add_reaction`/`remove_reaction` are no-ops, the orchestrator's emoji calls never reach the platform, so there is no stranded reaction and no behavior change.

Lark is covered, including its inbound fast-ack: the emoji the Lark channel adds on ingress is now the resolved in-progress value, and the channel records that emoji per message so the orchestrator withdraws exactly the reaction that was added instead of leaving a second 👀 behind. This holds even when the setting changes between receipt and cleanup: the orchestrator withdraws the emoji the channel actually posted and waits for the channel's add to finish first, rather than recomputing the value and missing the reaction. Both readers resolve the configured value from the canonical live config for each message, so a change published after startup reaches the next message without rebuilding the channels.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` for the config surface; no channel credentials are needed.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (config file and `zeroclaw config`), channel `slack`, channel `matrix`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Any working config file. No bot tokens are required to verify parsing and resolution.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw config set channels.ack_reaction_in_progress "⏳"`
  2. `zeroclaw config set channels.ack_reaction_done ""`
  3. `zeroclaw config get channels.ack_reaction_in_progress`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** All three keys are accepted and read back, and the orchestrator adds ⏳ while working and leaves the message reaction-free when the turn ends.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `zeroclaw config set channels.ack_reaction_in_progress "⏳"` is rejected as an unknown key, and the acknowledgement is always 👀 and always ends as ✅ or ⚠️.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `fmt`, `lint`, `check`, and `test` legs cover the changed Rust surface; the `installer-drift` leg plus the in-suite review-docs freshness tests cover the tracked generated surfaces; `Docs Style` covers the two changed Markdown files. The config reference (`docs/book/src/reference/config.md`) is a gitignored generated file, so a config-schema change requires no committed regeneration, and the tracked generators (`installers`, `sop-syntax`, `review-docs`) do not read the config schema. I re-ran all three anyway.

prs.title: fix(security): block high-risk shell commands even when allowlisted
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** `validate_command_execution_for_shell` skipped the `block_high_risk_commands` gate when a command was a literal `allowed_commands` entry, so the reported profile with the hard block on and `rm` in its allowlist could execute `rm -rf` after shell auto-approval. The gate now applies to every high-risk command, which is what the config schema documents the field to do. The Balanced and Locked Down preset help and the PowerShell sandboxing guidance are reworded in the same change, because they promised an explicit-allowlist exemption the code no longer gives.
- **Scope boundary:** The allowlist itself, the medium-risk approval gate, and the supervised high-risk approval gate are unchanged. The `"*"` + `block_high_risk_commands = false` escape hatch is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** `SecurityPolicy::validate_command_execution_for_shell`, which the shell tool, the skill shell tool, and cron shell jobs all call. A profile that allowlists a high-risk command with the hard block on now gets it blocked instead of executed.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11058
- **Labels:** `bug`, `config`, `domain:security`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `risk:high`, `runtime`, `security:policy`, `size:S`, `tool:delegate`.

### What this does, simply

A profile lists the commands an agent may run in `allowed_commands`. Putting a command there used to do two things at once: it allowed the command, and if the command was high-risk it also switched off the `block_high_risk_commands` hard block for that command. Only the first effect is documented, and the second is how an allowlisted `rm` ran silently while the profile had the hard block turned on.

The config schema documents `block_high_risk_commands` as "Block high-risk commands even when allowlisted", so this makes the code match that sentence. The allowlist still decides whether a command may run at all; the hard block just applies on top of it. If you do want a high-risk command to run, `block_high_risk_commands = false` is the switch for that, and it's untouched.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — this is a pure policy function covered by the crate's own unit and integration tests; a manual agent run would exercise the same function without adding signal.

### How I tested

On `master`, before the change, the existing `validate_command_explicit_rm_bypasses_high_risk_block` passed. It builds a policy with `autonomy = Full`, `allowed_commands = ["rm"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = true` and asserts `validate_command_execution("rm -rf /tmp/test", true)` returns `Ok(CommandRiskLevel::High)`. That is the silent-execution path from the issue: the command clears validation and the shell tool runs it.

I added `validate_command_blocks_explicitly_allowlisted_high_risk` (its comment quotes the schema sentence) and ran it before touching the code:

```
running 1 test
test policy::tests::validate_command_blocks_explicitly_allowlisted_high_risk ... FAILED

---- policy::tests::validate_command_blocks_explicitly_allowlisted_high_risk stdout ----
thread '...' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs:6588:13:
expected the hard block, got: Command requires explicit approval (approved=true): high-risk operation
```

That failure is the bug. The allowlist entry cleared the hard block, so an unapproved call fell through to the approval gate instead of being blocked; with `approved = true` the call returns `Ok` and the command runs.

After the change, on the tested revision:

```
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1775 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (lib)
     Running tests/comment_writer.rs        — 8 passed; 0 failed
     Running tests/migration.rs             — 99 passed; 0 failed
     Running tests/nodes_mdns_config.rs     — 5 passed; 0 failed
     Running tests/powershell_policy_probe.rs — 9 passed; 0 failed
     Running tests/repro_8636.rs            — 1 passed; 0 failed
     Running tests/schema_v4_external_saas.rs — 1 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib validate_command
test result: ok. 15 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1760 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib independent_delegate_denies_prompt_required_skill_tools_without_approval_route
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5698 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::shell::tests
test result: FAILED. 64 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5634 filtered out
# shell_child_cannot_open_owners_controlling_terminal is the failure: its own
# openpty() call returns EACCES in this sandbox before any ZeroClaw code runs,
# and the same denial reproduces with a standalone libc call outside the repo.
# The other 64 pass.

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
(clean)

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
0 error(s)

$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

The `validate_command` set covers the three cases the issue names: a high-risk command with an explicit allow entry is blocked for both `approved` values; an ordinary allowlisted command (`ls`) still returns `Ok(Low)` without approval; a high-risk command that is not allowlisted still fails with `Command not allowed by security policy`. One test also pins the opt-out: with `block_high_risk_commands = false`, an allowlisted `rm` still returns `Ok(High)`.

Five existing tests needed to move with the policy. Three asserted the old exemption directly and now assert the block. Two PowerShell allowlist-path tests set `block_high_risk_commands = false` so they keep exercising the path-match rule they exist for rather than the high-risk gate. `independent_delegate_denies_prompt_required_skill_tools_without_approval_route` used an allowlisted `rm` to reach the approval gate, so its fixture now turns the hard block off; with it on the command would stop at the high-risk gate instead of the prompt.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust quality gate (fmt + clippy) and the workspace test job cover the changed crate and its callers.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:** listed above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I confirmed the risk classifier and the allowlist both live in `SecurityPolicy`, so the change sits in the function that owns the decision and covers all three callers (`tools/shell.rs`, `tools/skill_tool.rs`, `cron/mod.rs`) rather than one entry point. I did not run a live agent turn against a real model.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `c29e071cfd325c5b7bb6e6e14d016c54b21e8bba`, `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime`, Linux x86_64, Rust 1.97.0. The branch is rebased onto current `master` (`d03325172eb6c64272f01042b60fd7f66d74c711`), so these runs are against the merged result rather than the old base.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `N/A`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `No`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: keep `block_high_risk_commands = true` to retain the hard block. Profiles that previously relied on an explicit high-risk exemption will now receive `Command blocked: high-risk command is disallowed by policy`, with no process spawned. Choosing `block_high_risk_commands = false` permits allowlisted high-risk commands subject to the remaining approval, path and sandbox checks, but is an explicit security opt-out rather than an equivalent migration. With `"*"` in the allowlist, it also admits other high-risk commands and disables the existing shell syntax restrictions. Removing the wildcard and enumerating intended commands avoids that wildcard syntax bypass, but changes the previous broad low-risk allowance. This also affects allowlisted PowerShell executables classified as high risk.

  The Windows default profile is where a stock install feels this. `runtime.shell` defaults to PowerShell on Windows (#10956), and under PowerShell a command name the classifier doesn't recognize is high risk. 18 of the 27 entries in the Windows default allowlist are high risk, including `python`, `node`, `grep`, `find` and `where`. The `default` and `locked_down` profiles set `block_high_risk_commands = true`, so on Windows those 18 move from an approval prompt to a hard block that approval can't override, and a stock Windows install can no longer run them. POSIX defaults are essentially unaffected: the same names classify as low risk under the POSIX classifier. `block_high_risk_commands = false` restores them under the ordinary approval gates.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the merged change using its landed commit SHA

prs.title: feat(goal): extract transport-neutral Goal policy contracts [Goal V1 proposal 3/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

> **Draft hold:** Security and the aggregate CI Required Gate failed on inherited TLS dependencies. No gate is waived; this PR remains Draft pending the dependency-repair scope decision.

Slice **03 of 12**, prepared for review as an unmerged Goal Mode V1 proposal. This prefix is not a complete, independently enabled Goal feature. The incremental comparison is `8b0d412a4532fea4da49fad6094dd0946d9100cd..5e18ccec46eaf58e8f289e85c84af5edc9c2c43d`; the master-targeted diff also includes its unmerged predecessors.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Extract transport-neutral Goal policy, task and execution-host contracts into `zeroclaw-goal`, without moving SQLite or concrete runtime capabilities into that crate.
  - Validate the current canonical Goal configuration before Start/Resume binding, controller mutation and execution-lease acquisition. Preserve structured validation errors and keep administrative commands available when verifier settings are invalid.
  - Preserve exact-principal fencing when replacing an ended Goal and retain the old runtime task-type import path as a direct re-export.
  - Isolate two loopback-HTTP webhook test fixtures from synchronous native-certificate loading, using a scoped, thread-bound `cfg(test)` guard. Production TLS, HTTPS, original assertions and deadlines are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** No production Matrix/ZeroCode driver, model execution loop, provider router, new ledger/session store or broad runtime extraction. Accounting, deferred turn controls, restart/revocation, transport integration and presentation arrive in later slices. No merge, deployment or live-room validation is requested.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust contracts, shared command validation, Goal admission and SQLite principal fencing. Runtime capability implementations stay with their existing owners; the webhook adjustment compiles out of production.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8303; Related #10341; Depends on #11879.
  - https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  - https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341
  - https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11879

### What this does, simply

Gives Goal Mode one shared policy boundary instead of letting each transport interpret commands independently. Before that boundary hands out execution capability, it checks the current configuration through the existing config validator. Invalid verifier settings cannot bind a new session or start execution, but they do not prevent an operator from inspecting, pausing or cancelling a Goal.

This PR supplies contracts and guarded control behavior, not the finished Matrix or ZeroCode feature. Later adapters must supply fresh configuration and preserve their ordinary authorization, session and presentation behavior. Enabling Goal with zero budget defaults is the proposed explicit-unlimited choice; that interpretation remains subject to maintainer review.

### Stack-wide scoped runtime-placement request (not approved)

Request a Core-reviewed bounded runtime exception or authoritative ownership decision before merge. The completed stack proposes Goal policy/contracts/execution in `zeroclaw-goal`; this slice supplies the contracts and control boundary. The requested residual scope is the existing runtime SQLite/control-plane implementation and bounded agent/session/accounting/provider/tool/RPC/daemon host adapters used by this stack. Their destination remains the corresponding planned kernel/agent-loop, control-plane and RPC owners, not a new general Goal subsystem in runtime. Reconsider at those extraction design reviews or before broadening the host seams or authority. Any accepted exception must be recorded separately through the required Core-reviewed policy row/ownership process; this feature proposal cannot approve its own exception. The full runtime path diff remains subject to that bounded-scope decision.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — this prefix has no wired user-facing Goal adapter. The real-SQLite and execution-host contract tests below are the meaningful reproducible boundary checks; live provider/channel tests would overstate this slice's coverage.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate for this head](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39503786120) completed: 38 jobs succeeded, six were conditionally skipped, Security failed, and CI Required Gate consequently failed. Passing jobs include the full default workspace Test, workspace Lint and Rustdoc, parallel runtime tests, opt-in/channel tests, platform builds/checks and MSRV. [Code Analysis / Semgrep](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39503785750) also passed. This is not an overall CI pass.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Security stopped at `cargo deny check`. Its later lockfile integrity, YAML/helper validation and `cargo audit` steps did not run. The local config/gateway commands below are filtered; full default workspace test coverage and workspace lint/Rustdoc now have successful CI execution. Native Goal transport integration and the incomplete full stack are not certified.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The following checks were independently executed locally during whole-diff review at `5e18ccec46eaf58e8f289e85c84af5edc9c2c43d`, with Rust 1.98.1:

| Command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | exit 0 |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-goal` | 9 passed; 0 failed |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-commands` | 18 passed; 0 failed |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config goal` | 19 passed; 0 failed; 1,816 filtered out |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test goal_execution_host_contract` | 38 passed; 0 failed |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test session_goal_control_plane_contract` | 26 passed; 0 failed |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway api_config::tests` | 84 passed; 0 failed; 579 filtered out |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib hooks::builtin::webhook_audit::tests -- --test-threads=16` | 42 passed; 0 failed |

| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh` | 58 passed; 0 failed |
| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` | Comment hygiene gate passed. |
| `bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` | All three runtime and all three channels runs passed at 16 threads |

Representative literal tails from the independent parallel run:

```text
test result: ok. 5793 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 38.57s
test result: ok. 2005 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 14.73s
```

The parallel script completed all six runs; these two lines are representative output, not the full transcript. The macOS linker `__eh_frame section too large` warning recurred and was also observed in the frozen-base comparison. No suppression, warning-free release build or footprint claim is made.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Static end-to-end tracing plus automated boundary tests: invalid verifier/defaults cause no bind/write/acquisition; administrative commands retain access; valid state survives lifecycle and SQLite reuse; exact principal checks fail closed; Debug omits sensitive configuration and identity content. Whole-diff independent review returned **PASS+ADVISORIES**, not an approval to merge. No live model, daemon or native transport was manually exercised.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no wired rendered interface changes in this slice.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `5e18ccec46eaf58e8f289e85c84af5edc9c2c43d`; fixture host/store and ordinary webhook tests, not native channel output. Literal results are included above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for visuals; test output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Invalid Start/Resume/acquisition fail before their protected effect; valid lifecycle, administrative controls and fixture delivery tests pass.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No accepted local slice gate was skipped. CI intentionally excluded push-only debounce and benchmarks, unselected Nix/relay/package-preflight/targeted-Windows-Clippy jobs, and the separate opt-in Windows advisory workflow. Required Windows compile, service and task-owner tests ran and passed. Security's later checks were not executed after its failure; they are not counted as passes. Full-stack native transport/live-model/rollout checks are not claimed.

Earlier failed runs remain recorded; the current six-run pass replaces the current parallel-gate failure claim, not its history or proof of the precise old scheduling interleaving.

### Current CI blocker

[Security failed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39503786120/job/118907514645) on four locked package records, representing three advisories:

- `rustls-webpki 0.103.15`: RUSTSEC-2026-0382.
- `webpki-root-certs 1.0.7`: RUSTSEC-2026-0383.
- `webpki-roots 0.26.11` and `1.0.9`: RUSTSEC-2026-0381.

These complete package records are identical in the frozen upstream base, the prepared predecessor and this head. Ordinary runtime/config/channel dependency paths already use them. This establishes inherited inputs, not a passing security scan or proof of a particular exploit path. No TLS policy, dependency version or advisory ignore was changed in the fixture repair. Dependency repair would extend the approved test-only scope and remains a separate decision.

The [aggregate gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39503786120/job/118915972168) failed because Security failed; all other executed jobs in that workflow succeeded. A duplicate risk-report run was canceled by the body's edit-triggered concurrency rule; its [same-head replacement succeeded](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39503797448). No check was silently retried or waived.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes — capability contracts, not new grants.** The typed host/driver boundary mediates existing execution and durable control capabilities. Exact session/principal/epoch checks and current-config admission guard the boundary; actual transport adapters and their authorization remain later work.
- New external network calls? **No.** No new network client or provider route; webhook production behavior is unchanged.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** Settings and ingress Debug implementations omit private data; no credential store or operator configuration change.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Tests use neutral fixture identities.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes — contract inputs.** Objective/history/candidate inputs are represented by execution contracts for later model-facing adapters, not promoted to authorization. This slice does not assemble a new prompt or prove the later adapters' injection/egress handling.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for consumers of the earlier unpublished host API; existing runtime task-type paths are preserved.** Goal task contracts are re-exported rather than duplicated. The new Goal crate is additive relative to the prepared predecessor.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes, admission behavior; no new syntax/key here.** Enabled Start/Resume and execution acquisition now reject invalid canonical verifier/default settings. Disabled precedence remains unchanged; status, budget mutation, pause, cancel and help are not gated on verifier validity.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No declared floor change.**
- **Exact upgrade steps:** Host consumers must construct `GoalHostSettings::from_config(&Config, owner_pid, owner_boot_id)` from current full canonical configuration for each command and separately for each acquisition. The candidate-only `new` constructor and `PartialEq` implementation are removed. Do not retain a config lock across an await or reuse settings as a validity snapshot. Use the existing structured config-error chain. Runtime task-type re-exports remain available; new consumers may import `zeroclaw_goal` directly. No live database migration is requested for preparing this proposal.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, use `git revert <this PR's squash commit>` in a rollback PR, after reverting any dependent slices in reverse order. If the completed feature is later enabled, disable Goal admission and settle/drain work first; preserve the durable task database and usage ledger. Do not drop data to undo a contract extraction. No rollback command is executed for this unmerged proposal.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `[goal].enabled = false`; this prefix must not be enabled as a finished feature.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Start/Resume validation errors, lost/stale principal/session fencing, or failure to acquire a valid execution lease. Check the structured config code/path and durable task/epoch state; no live rollback was exercised.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — no superseded PR is claimed.

---

### Remaining proposal and merge gates

- Keep the predecessor dependency and later slice order explicit. Review of these fourteen paths does not certify the complete stack or native Matrix/ZeroCode behavior.
- Matrix history must be sender-scoped; both ZeroCode transports, executor settlement after acquisition refusal, accounting, restart/revocation, ordinary spend limits and event parity still require their later-slice proof.
- The harmless redundant default-limit validation is retained under the accepted scope. The linker warning remains disclosed.
- Earlier failure records remain historical, not claims that this head fails the same tests. Current default workspace tests and selected CI feature legs passed; the extra strict no-default/all-targets leg from the old stack audit was not run here and is not claimed passing. Full-stack transport/restart/accounting proof and RFC footprint measurements remain open.
- Required exact-head CI is currently failed and must be resolved before merge. CODEOWNERS/Core review and the separately recorded runtime-placement exception or authoritative ownership decision remain separate pre-merge requirements. This proposal grants none of them.
- No merge, deployment, live-room test, service restart or operator-configuration change was performed.

prs.title: feat(tools): add Firecrawl web search provider
prs.body:
Hey, I'm Juampi from the Firecrawl team.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds Firecrawl as a `web_search_tool` provider (`search_provider = "firecrawl"`, aliases `firecrawl-search` / `firecrawl_search`). It calls `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search` with the key as a Bearer token and asks for web results only (`sources: ["web"]`), so each result is a title, URL and short description like the other providers. Full pages stay with `web_fetch`. Disclosure: I work at Firecrawl.
  - The key is a new optional secret, `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key` (`#[secret]` / `encrypted_secret`, same as the other keyed providers). It is resolved and decrypted from `config.toml` on every call, so adding, rotating or removing it needs no restart. When the loader applies `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`, the runtime factory passes that effective value to the tool; a blank override means "not configured" and never falls back to the stored key.
  - Responses go through the shared helpers: non-2xx statuses use `http_search_failure` (so a 429 is `search_status=unavailable`), the body is read through the bounded reader (1 MiB), a `success: false` answer on a 2xx is a failure, a missing `data.web` means no results, and titles, URLs and descriptions are whitespace-collapsed, results without a URL are skipped, and titles and descriptions go through `cap_result_content`. The query is cut to the 500 characters the API accepts, and redirects are disabled on the Firecrawl client.
  - The default provider is unchanged (`duckduckgo`).
- **Scope boundary:** No changes to the other providers, the default provider, `web_fetch` (including its existing Firecrawl fallback), plugins, tool registration, approvals or Fluent strings. No new dependency or feature flag. The key resolver follows the existing per-provider resolvers instead of refactoring them into a shared helper, to keep this PR to one concern; happy to do that as a follow-up if you want it.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-tools` (routing and tool), `zeroclaw-config` (one new optional secret field, defaults to `None`, existing configs parse unchanged), `zeroclaw-runtime` (passes the effective env override into the tool), and the tools overview page.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

`web_search_tool` can already use several search backends, chosen with `[web_search] search_provider`. This adds Firecrawl to that list. Someone who sets `search_provider = "firecrawl"` and a `firecrawl_api_key` gets web results from Firecrawl instead of the default DuckDuckGo scrape. Nothing changes for anyone who does not opt in.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. It needs a Firecrawl API key, created at <https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys>.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (any surface that runs `web_search_tool`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[web_search] search_provider = "firecrawl"` and `firecrawl_api_key = "..."` in `config.toml`, or `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key` in the environment.
- **Steps to run:** ask the agent to search the web for anything, or call `web_search_tool` with `{"query": "what is the rust programming language"}`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `Search results for: what is the rust programming language (via Firecrawl)` followed by numbered results, each with a URL and a description of at most about 500 characters.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `search_provider = "firecrawl"` is unknown, logs `Unknown web search model_provider 'firecrawl'; falling back to 'duckduckgo'`, and scrapes DuckDuckGo.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Test job runs the `zeroclaw-tools`, `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime` suites, which hold every new test (aliases, key resolution and rotation, env override, secret-safe parse errors, request shape on a mock server, bounded body reads, redirect rejection, 429 handling, render caps). Docs Style covers the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the live endpoint is not exercised in CI, same as the other providers; request shape is pinned by wiremock tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (rustc 1.96.0, at `55a5b4e`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   clean
./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh                            clean (dispatch gate clean)
cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   clean
cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime    clean
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib web_search
  test result: 181 passed; 1 failed (test_serply_connection_refused_error_is_query_free, see below)
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib web_search      1 passed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib api_key_override   2 passed
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh, scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh  clean on the changed lines
```

  The one failure is the existing Serply refused-connect test, which fails on macOS here and is tracked by the open #11312. This PR does not touch it, and every Firecrawl test passes.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A real search through `WebSearchTool::execute` against `api.firecrawl.dev` with the key supplied as `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`: 5 results in about 1.4 s, output labelled `(via Firecrawl)`, every result a title, URL and usually a description, and the key does not appear anywhere in the output. Descriptions can come back as long multi-line excerpts (one was over 10,000 characters before the cap), which is why the text is whitespace-collapsed and capped. Not verified live: a real 429 (covered by a wiremock test).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`. The only user-visible change is the `web_search_tool` plain-text result block, which is deterministic and unstyled.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `55a5b4e`, `cli` (`web_search_tool` output as returned to the model). Locale and terminal width do not shape the output.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

```text
Search results for: what is the rust programming language (via Firecrawl)
...
2. Rust Programming Language
   https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US
   Rust's rich type system and ownership model guarantee memory-safety and thread-safety, enabling you to eliminate many classes of bugs at compile-time.
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** set `search_provider = "firecrawl"`, called `web_search_tool` with `{"query": "what is the rust programming language"}`, and got the Firecrawl-labelled result block instead of the DuckDuckGo fallback log line.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace `cargo nextest` run was not done locally; the hosted run covers it. The local `cargo clippy` on the whole workspace with `-D warnings` stops on an existing lint in an untouched file (`zeroclaw-infra/src/acp_session_store.rs`) with the newer local toolchain, so clippy was run on the three touched crates with `--no-deps`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (reuses the existing web-search tool surface and config read path).
- New external network calls? Yes. `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search`, made only when the operator sets `search_provider = "firecrawl"`, through the same proxy-aware client builder (`apply_runtime_proxy_to_builder`) as the other providers. The request carries the query, the result limit, `sources: ["web"]` and a fixed `origin` value of `zeroclaw` that names the caller.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. One new optional secret field, `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key`, on the existing `#[secret]` / `encrypted_secret` path. The key is sent only as a Bearer header, never in the URL, body or logs. Redirects are disabled, success bodies are limited to 1 MiB before decoding, and malformed-TOML errors expose only a stable code and a derived line number.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test fixtures use placeholder keys and neutral queries.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Firecrawl result titles, URLs and descriptions are provider-controlled text returned to the model and must be treated as untrusted. Provider opt-in and the per-result and total output caps limit exposure and volume, but do not sanitize prompt injection.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: opt-in egress to one provider-scoped host; the key is handled by the established encrypted-secret path; output is bounded.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes

prs.title: feat(providers): add Opper model provider
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add a typed provider slot `opper` for Opper, an EU-hosted, OpenAI-compatible AI gateway. Operators select it by name, and ZeroClaw fills in the endpoint and bearer auth.
  - The endpoint lives in one constant, `OpperEndpoint::DEFAULT_URI`. The factory's `DEFAULT_URL` reads it, and a test guards the pair.
  - Opper is already on models.dev as `opper`, so the slot sets `MODELS_DEV_KEY = "opper"`. The model picker lists Opper models before a key is set, through the existing models.dev path. With a key, the shared client reads the live `/models`.
  - The API key comes only from the typed alias. A test checks that the constructor does not read `OPPER_API_KEY`.
- **Scope boundary:** No new client implementation, no `ModelProviderKind` variant, no context-window discovery, no alias shims, no `wire_api` handling. Other providers and existing configs do not change.
- **Blast radius:** The provider registry, the config schema (a new `providers.models.opper` map), the catalog source table, the generated "All slots" table and the provider list. The slot is inactive unless an operator configures it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11583. Related #8396.

### What this does, simply

Before this PR, an Opper user had to write a `custom` provider with the URL. Opper did not show in the provider list, and the model picker stayed empty until a key was pasted.

This PR adds a named `opper` slot. The operator sets `model` and `api_key`. ZeroClaw then sends Chat Completions requests to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat`. Model ids are bare names such as `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and Opper picks the route for each request. The slot is for chat only.

### Why a first-class family (not `providers.models.custom`)

- **Model list before a key is set.** Opper is already listed on models.dev as `opper`. The slot reuses the existing models.dev catalog path, as `vercel` and `synthetic` do. A `custom` alias has no catalog source, so its picker stays empty until a key is pasted.
- **Maintained defaults.** The endpoint and bearer auth come from one constant, so operators cannot mistype the base URL. The `/v3/compat` path is easy to get wrong by hand.
- **Discoverability.** Opper shows in the provider list and in the generated catalog next to the other gateways.
- **No new client code.** The slot is data on the shared OpenAI-compatible client. The intake decision is in #11583.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. You need an Opper key from https://platform.opper.ai.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:**

  ```toml
  [providers.models.opper.default]
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
  api_key = "..."

  [agents.opper]
  model_provider = "opper.default"
  risk_profile = "supervised"
  ```

- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw models refresh --model-provider opper.default`
  2. `zeroclaw agent -a opper -m "hello"`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The model list loads and the agent replies. Without `api_key`, step 1 lists the models.dev `opper` catalog.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `opper` is not a known provider slot, so `model_provider = "opper.default"` does not resolve and config validation fails.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, `Check`, `Test` and clippy cover both changed crates. That includes the slot coverage tests `every_canonical_family_has_a_catalog_table_entry` and `listed_model_providers_match_canonical_slots`, and the 8 new tests. `Docs Style` covers `catalog.md`.
- **Mock request coverage (added in b488e30a5):** `opper_factory_sends_bearer_and_model_ids_to_compat_endpoint` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/factory.rs` points the Opper provider at a local mock server under `/v3/compat`. It asserts that chat requests go to `/v3/compat/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, that the pool name `claude-sonnet-4-6` and the pinned id `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` are sent unchanged, and that the model list goes to `/v3/compat/models` with the same header and returns both ids.
- **CI result on b488e30a5:** run 37914489616 concluded success with no failed jobs, including Format, Lint and Test, and the Test log shows the new test passing.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI makes no live provider request. The mock server test covers the request shape only. The live smoke from #11583 (`zeroclaw models refresh --model-provider opper.default` and `zeroclaw agent -a opper -m "hello"`) has not been run yet; its results will be added here when it is.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  git diff --check origin/master HEAD
  # exited 0, no output

  curl -s https://models.dev/api.json | jq -c '.opper | {id, api, env, models: (.models | length), has_default: (.models | has("claude-sonnet-4-6"))}'
  # {"id":"opper","api":"https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat","env":["OPPER_API_KEY"],"models":57,"has_default":true}

  curl -s "https://api.opper.ai/v3/models?limit=2000" | jq -c '[.models[] | select(.model == "claude-sonnet-4-6" and .pooled == true and .type == "llm")] | length'
  # 5
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The models.dev `opper` entry and the model id used in the tests and docs, shown above. No live chat or model list request has been run yet (see the coverage gap above).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No rendered interface changes. The new provider list entry is data from `list_model_providers()`.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I did not run `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` or `cargo test` locally, because this machine has no Rust toolchain. This PR relies on required CI for them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `Yes`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Only when an operator configures `providers.models.opper`, ZeroClaw sends requests to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat` through the shared OpenAI-compatible client. The keyless model list uses the existing models.dev fetch. Credentials stay on the typed alias `api_key` or the `ZEROCLAW_*` schema-mirror override.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: This adds the `providers.models.opper.<alias>` slot. It is additive. `ModelProviders` is a public exhaustive struct, so a downstream struct literal needs `..ModelProviders::default()` for the new `opper` field. Existing `custom` configs keep working. To move to the typed slot, create `[providers.models.opper.<alias>]`, set `model`, and set `api_key` directly or bridge it with `ZEROCLAW_providers__models__opper__<alias>__api_key="$OPPER_API_KEY"`. `opper-ai` and `opper_ai` are not runtime aliases.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` this commit, or remove the `opper` slot from `providers.rs`, `schema.rs`, `factory.rs`, `catalog.rs`, `lib.rs` and the catalog doc entry.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Without a configured `[providers.models.opper.<alias>]` entry, the provider is inactive.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Provider construction errors that mention `opper`, failed `/models` calls to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat/models`, or chat errors from the compatible provider path.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? `No`
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A

Disclosure: Opper is my startup.
