prs.title: fix(infra): preserve created_at of retained rows when replacing a session transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replacing a SQLite session transcript deleted every row and reinserted them all with one timestamp, so from the second turn on `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` returned the time of the last write for every message. The replacement now aligns the new transcript with the stored rows and lets every row that lines up keep its `created_at`; only genuinely new messages get the time of the write.
  - The alignment is the longest run of stored rows that equals the start of the new transcript (earliest run on a tie, which drops the fewest rows). That covers an appended turn, a trim from the start, a trim plus a new turn, and any of these with a changed last row. The usual per-turn case inserts only the new tail and deletes nothing.
  - The history-trim breadcrumb is identified by the stored and incoming flags, never by its text. A newly inserted breadcrumb takes the time of its first write; a retained one keeps its own. The bare `rewrite_messages` leaves the stored flag untouched and says so by passing no incoming flag (`Option<bool>`), so it cannot disagree with the stored one.
  - The three replacement paths now open their transaction as `IMMEDIATE`, because they read before they write. `last_activity` stays the time of the write, never an inherited message time.
  - Tests cover both SQLite replacement paths, the gateway restore-time trim, the gateway end-of-turn write (with and without a history cap) and the RPC chat restore-time trim. A criterion benchmark covers the write paths.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No backfill: rows that were already flattened are inherited as they are; no historical times are invented.
  - Not changed: the JSONL backend (it stores no per-row times), the ACP store (`acp_messages.created_at` has the same flattening mechanism but a different writer; tracked in #11675), and how channel hydration decides the breadcrumb flag from the text of the first row (a different mechanism, outside this change; it will be reported separately if its analysis confirms it). The API shape, the schema and the configuration are unchanged.
  - Known limits, each pinned by a test: when identical messages cannot be told apart after a trim, the write drops the fewest old rows, so a retained row may inherit the time of an earlier identical one (this is the behavior agreed in the issue thread); and an incoming breadcrumb flag with no breadcrumb row makes the first row inherit the time of the stored first row.
- **Blast radius:** every consumer of SQLite session transcripts: gateway WebSocket chat, RPC chat and channel sessions, and whatever shows the times returned by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` (the dashboard Sessions view; #11622 reads them in ZeroCode). Channel sessions reach the changed code through `replace_conversation_state` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`). Every replacement now reads the stored rows before writing; see the measurements below.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11420. Related #11593 (an earlier attempt by the same author, closed without merging). Related #11622. Related #11675 (the same mechanism in the ACP store).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw keeps each chat session as a list of messages in SQLite, and every message row has a `created_at`: the time it was first saved. At the end of every turn the agent hands the backend its whole current history, and the backend used to delete all the rows of the session and write them again with the time of that moment. Messages from earlier turns therefore all showed the time of the latest turn, and the original times were lost for good.

This change makes the backend compare the new history with what is stored. Messages that are still there keep the time they were first saved, and only messages that are really new get the current time. When the agent trims old turns, the turns it keeps keep their times too. When a turn only adds messages, nothing is deleted. Sessions that were already flattened are not repaired, because the original times no longer exist anywhere.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (gateway WebSocket chat and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`) and `tui` (RPC chat, `session/new` restoring a session). No channel surface is exercised by an end-to-end test.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Rust toolchain and a Linux or WSL checkout. Building the `zeroclaw-runtime` tests is memory-heavy: on a 6 GB machine I used `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On this branch:
     ```sh
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --locked --lib session_sqlite
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib websocket_turn_end
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib websocket_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows
     ```
  2. For the old behavior, put only the two backend source files back to `master` and rerun the gateway and runtime commands (the backend tests live inside `session_sqlite.rs`, so they disappear with it):
     ```sh
     git checkout origin/master -- crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_sqlite.rs crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_backend.rs
     ```
     Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_sqlite.rs crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_backend.rs`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** all four commands pass.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the four integration tests fail, each on a time comparison:
  - `websocket_turn_end_keeps_created_at_of_earlier_turns_in_sqlite`: `row 0 of the first turn must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `websocket_turn_end_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows`: `turn 2: "[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]\n\nprompt number 1" must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows`: `retained row "turn two request" must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `websocket_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows`: `retained row "turn two request" must keep its original time`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format` (rustfmt), `Lint` (`clippy --all-targets` compiles the new benchmark; the comment hygiene gate covers the new comments) and `Test` (runs the new unit and integration tests on the changed crates).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the benchmark is compiled by the lint job but never run in CI, and the performance numbers below are from one machine. The `bench` job only compiles `agent_benchmarks`.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux (WSL2, rustc 1.98.1), on the final commit unless noted.

  ```text
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --locked
  test result: ok. 334 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib
  test result: ok. 651 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at
  test rpc::dispatch::tests::session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5699 filtered out

  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::drop-non-drop
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s)

  python scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.py <changed files>
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```

  `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on each changed `.rs` file passes (I did not run `cargo fmt --all` because the workspace does not resolve on my Windows host). The runtime test above was run on an earlier commit of this branch whose `dispatch.rs` is identical to the final one.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Regression checks: with the two backend source files from `master`, the four integration tests above fail with the messages listed; with the branch they pass. For the backend, the two original reproduction tests from the issue (`rewrite_keeps_created_at_of_unchanged_rows` and `rewrite_if_exists_keeps_created_at_of_unchanged_rows`) fail on `master` at `ea4a54bb5` and pass on the branch.
  - `t19_replacements_do_not_fail_with_database_is_locked_under_contention` passes 12 of 12 runs and fails 11 of 12 when the `IMMEDIATE` transaction is changed to a deferred one, so it does catch that change (it is a race, not deterministic).
  - Alignment: a standalone copy of the pure alignment functions was checked against an independent oracle on 60,000 random transcripts (append, trim, trim plus append, changed last row, changed last row plus trim, with and without a breadcrumb) with 0 mismatches, and the fast "insert only the tail" path never fired when stored rows differed from the requested ones.
  - Performance, one machine (WSL2), `opt-level = 3` and no LTO through `CARGO_PROFILE_BENCH_*` (the repo's release profile optimizes for size), binaries for `master` and the branch run alternately in rounds with the order rotated, paired by round. Median time per call at 1000 messages:

    | case | messages of ~230 B, `master` → branch | messages of ~20 KB, `master` → branch |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | rewrite, unchanged transcript | 37.5 ms → 0.40 ms | 245 ms → 13.5 ms |
    | rewrite plus one new turn | 32.7 ms → 0.82 ms | 268 ms → 25.2 ms |

    Both improvements were in the right direction in every one of 7 rounds. `append` (unchanged code) and `load_with_timestamps` showed no consistent difference.
  - **Cost:** with messages of ~20 KB, rewrites that drop most of the transcript are slower, because the stored rows are now read before they are replaced. Compaction at 1000 messages went from 83.5 ms to 93.2 ms (median of 11 rounds; the branch was slower in 10 of them, sign test p = 0.012, which does not survive a correction for the five cells I compared). A half trim went from 161 ms to 197 ms (median of 7 rounds; slower in 6 of them, p = 0.125, inconclusive). Peak memory of the unchanged rewrite with a ~20 MB transcript rose from about 39 MB to about 51 MB. Round-to-round variation of the same binary was 1.5x to 2x, so small differences should not be read as findings.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` (no presentation change; the values of an existing field change)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A (see above)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I did not run the full workspace tests, the full `zeroclaw-runtime` lib suite, the `zeroclaw-channels` tests, or anything on Windows or macOS; I did not run a real provider, the dashboard or a browser against this branch. The gateway tests use a real gateway and the SQLite backend with a local provider fixture. `clippy` is run with `-A clippy::drop-non-drop` on the three changed crates because that lint fails today on unchanged code in `zeroclaw-channels` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, three `drop(dispatch_ownership)` calls), which is identical on `master`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: none. For the record: `created_at` was already returned by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`; this change only makes it return the time each message was first saved instead of the time of the last write. The new SQL statements use bound parameters, and the transcript and breadcrumb flag are still written in one transaction, with the deleted-session guard of `replace_conversation_state_if_exists` unchanged (it still returns `false` and writes nothing).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` (no schema change; existing databases work as they are; rows already flattened stay flattened)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: not applicable. The benchmark adds `criterion = "0.8"` as a dev-dependency of `zeroclaw-infra`; `criterion` is already in the workspace, and `Cargo.lock` gains only that one dependency line.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

prs.body:
Reason: MiniMax-M3 image and video inputs were serialized as plain text despite the model supporting multimodal content parts.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Advertise vision for aliases configured with MiniMax-M3, using the configured model as the source of truth.
  - Keep M3 system messages separate so user images reach the existing image-normalization path while literal system media examples stay text.
  - Convert explicit user video markers into video content parts across all eight chat entry points, including streaming and native tool requests.
  - Document accepted HTTPS and MiniMax file references and preserve text for unsupported video references and non-user roles.
- **Scope boundary:** Local video loading, video uploads, embedded video data, pricing, endpoints, and model defaults are unchanged; MiniMax-M2.7 retains its text-only behavior.
- **Blast radius:** MiniMax adapter request shaping, its factory capability reporting, and provider documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A MiniMax-M3 alias can send normalized user images and explicit `[VIDEO:https://example.com/clip.mp4]` or `[VIDEO:mm_file://file_id]` references as multimodal input. System prompt examples remain text. Local videos must be uploaded separately before supplying a MiniMax file reference.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; the regression test captures the emitted HTTP payload for all eight adapter entry points.

- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust development dependencies; no live API credentials needed.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers minimax --lib`

prs.title: feat(memory): honor the preference subtype only for user-authored turns
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** The consolidation model labels each Core memory update with a semantic subtype, and `classify::kind_of_core` trusted a model-emitted `preference` unconditionally. `Preference` is a provenance claim — "the user themself expressed this" — but nothing verified a user was present in the turn. Both current consolidation callers (channel orchestrator, gateway WS chat) happen to be user-authored surfaces, so the claim holds by accident of wiring, not by contract; the first autonomous caller would silently mint preferences out of the model's own inference.
- This PR states the invariant at the layer that applies the label: `TurnOrigin::user_authored()` in `zeroclaw-api` (true only for `Interactive` and `Channel`; exhaustive match, no wildcard, so future origin variants force an explicit decision), `kind_of_core(result, origin)` downgrades an autonomous-turn `preference` to `Fact` (content survives, preference authority does not), and `consolidate_turn` / `MemoryStrategy::consolidate_turn` gain an `origin` parameter with each caller passing the origin its surface already stamps. The downgrade is logged at DEBUG.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to what gets stored, deduped, merged, or superseded — only to the `kind` metadata a non-user-authored `preference` receives. Non-preference subtypes are origin-independent. No config surface, no prompt change, no change to the verbatim autosave paths (heartbeat Daily stores, Conversation stores), which never classified.
- **Blast radius:** `MemoryStrategy` is a public trait in `zeroclaw-api` and its `consolidate_turn` gains a parameter — a compile-time break for external implementers (one implementer and two callers exist in-tree, all updated). Callers of `zeroclaw_memory::consolidation::consolidate_turn` likewise. Behavior changes only for a model-emitted `preference` on non-user-authored turns, a path no in-tree caller currently exercises.
- **Linked issue(s):** N/A
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `agent`, `channel`, `gateway`, `memory`, `runtime`, `tests`, `distinguished contributor`, `channel:core`, `domain:security`, `priority:p2`, `risk:high`, `size:M`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the changed behavior (subtype metadata on a not-yet-wired autonomous consolidation path) has no user-visible surface today; the deterministic tests below are the observable contract.

### How I tested

Written test-first. With the `origin` parameter threaded but the downgrade not yet implemented, the new regressions failed and the negative controls passed:

```
failures:
    classify::tests::preference_alias_spellings_downgrade_identically
    classify::tests::preference_downgrades_to_fact_on_turns_no_person_authored
test result: FAILED. 7 passed; 2 failed
consolidation::tests::preference_from_the_model_is_stored_as_fact_on_autonomous_turns
  Daemon: stored kind must reflect turn provenance: left: Some(Semantic(Preference)) right: Some(Semantic(Fact))
```

After the one-match implementation, all green. New coverage:

- `user_authored_is_true_only_for_a_person_typing` + `default_origin_is_not_user_authored` (zeroclaw-api) — the full truth table per variant, and the serde fail-closed default is also provenance-fail-closed
- `preference_is_honored_when_a_person_typed_the_turn` — Interactive and Channel keep preference authority (negative control; passed at red)
- `preference_downgrades_to_fact_on_turns_no_person_authored` — Cron, Daemon, AgentDirect, SubTurn
- `preference_alias_spellings_downgrade_identically` — `pref`, `user_preference`, ` Preference ` get no side door
- `non_preference_subtypes_are_origin_independent` — facts/decisions/entities untouched (negative control; passed at red)
- `preference_from_the_model_is_stored_as_fact_on_autonomous_turns` — end-to-end through the real `consolidate_turn` store path with a scripted provider: the same model output stores as `Preference` for Interactive/Channel and `Fact` for Daemon/Cron, so the clause cannot silently detach from the store path

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory     # 506 passed; 0 failed (+4, 0)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-api        # 166 passed; 0 failed (+1)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime    # 3737 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels   # 1391 passed; 1 failed (see note)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway    # 436 passed; 0 failed (+9)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-runtime \
  -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                # clean
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                   # passed
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the workspace test and lint gates over the five touched crates; the trait change is compile-checked by every consumer in the workspace matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none specific to this change.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The full-suite `zeroclaw-channels` run had one failure, `tts::tests::edge_tts_timeout_kills_child_and_removes_temp_output` — a TTS child-process timing test this diff does not touch; it passes twice consecutively in isolation, so it is parallel-load flakiness, not a regression from this change. I verified both production call sites pass the origin their surface already stamps: the gateway stamps `TurnOrigin::Interactive` on its turn envelopes (`gateway/src/lib.rs`), and the orchestrator consolidates channel peer turns.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no live-provider consolidation run; the scripted-provider e2e drives the identical store path.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — this narrows what a model-emitted label can claim: consolidation output can no longer assert user-preference provenance on turns no user authored.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** — `MemoryStrategy::consolidate_turn` and `zeroclaw_memory::consolidation::consolidate_turn` gain an `origin: TurnOrigin` parameter (compile-time break for external implementers/callers).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No`: pass the `TurnOrigin` of the turn that produced the user message — `Interactive` for operator chat surfaces, `Channel` for channel peer messages, `Cron`/`Daemon` for scheduled work. If the origin is unknown, `TurnOrigin::default()` (SubTurn) is the fail-closed choice: consolidation still runs, but preference authority is withheld.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; no data or configuration migration. Memories already downgraded to `Fact` keep that kind — no stored data changes shape in either direction.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** the downgrade only engages when `memory.types.enabled` is on (the only mode that classifies at all).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a preference stated by a real user in chat being stored with `kind: fact` — grep DEBUG logs for "downgraded preference to fact" with an `Interactive`/`Channel` origin attribute, which would indicate an origin mis-stamped upstream.

prs.title: fix(mcp): replay a tool call rejected for a stale HTTP session
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A Streamable HTTP MCP server that has terminated a session (idle eviction, restart) must answer every request carrying that `Mcp-Session-Id` with HTTP 404, and the client must start a new session ([spec, Session Management](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports#session-management)). The HTTP transport already maps this to `McpTransportError::StaleSession`, but the request stays marked outcome-unknown, so `dispatch_rpc` recovers the session in the background and fails the call with `outcome unknown and request was not replayed`.
  - The 404 is a definitive answer: the server rejected the request at session lookup and never executed it. This PR marks such a request as rejected-unexecuted (back to the pre-write phase, same epoch) before returning `StaleSession`, so the existing bounded pre-write path resets the transport, re-runs the handshake and replays the call on the new session.
  - In practice every first tool call after the server dropped the session failed. With a server that evicts idle sessions after 30 minutes, that is the first call of almost every conversation with a low-traffic agent.
  - This restores, for Streamable HTTP only, the replay that #7351 added (`call_tool_reconnects_on_stale_session`) and #9418 removed together with the other post-write replays. The test #9418 rewrote into no-replay is rewritten back.
- **Scope boundary:** Only the Streamable HTTP transport's 404/410-with-session branch. Timeouts, dropped streams and other post-write failures keep the no-replay rule from #9418. The legacy SSE transport is unchanged: its 404 stays outcome-unknown (`sse_post_404_is_not_replayed_to_derived_endpoint` untouched). A sessionless 404 is still a plain error (`call_tool_does_not_retry_sessionless_404` untouched).
- **Blast radius:** HTTP MCP servers only: a call that got a stale-session 404/410 is now replayed after the reconnect instead of failing. `MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` (2) bounds it: a server that keeps answering 404 after fresh handshakes gets three attempts in total, then the error surfaces (new test `call_tool_stale_session_replays_are_bounded`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9418, Related #7351

### What this does, simply

When an MCP server forgets a session, for example after the session sat idle for half an hour, it answers the next request with "404, no such session". ZeroClaw already understood that answer and reconnected, but it threw away the request that got the 404, so the user's tool call failed even though the server had done nothing with it. Now ZeroClaw reconnects and sends that same call again; if the server keeps rejecting it, ZeroClaw gives up after two retries. Calls whose fate really is unknown (a timeout, a connection that dropped mid-request) are still never repeated.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the wiremock tests reproduce the server's 404 deterministically; a manual run needs an MCP server with a short idle-session TTL.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `zeroclaw-tools` unit tests cover the transport phase change and the client replay path.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ rustc --version
rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)
$ cargo test -q -p zeroclaw-tools --locked --lib mcp_
test result: ok. 245 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1120 filtered out; finished in 1.20s
$ cargo clippy -q -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
(no output)

# same tests with the mcp_transport.rs change reverted (master behaviour):
thread 'mcp_client::tests::call_tool_replays_once_after_stale_session' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/mcp_client.rs:3096:14
thread 'mcp_client::tests::call_tool_stale_session_replays_are_bounded' panicked at .../wiremock-0.6.5/src/mock_server/exposed_server.rs:367:17
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 2 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The updated tests fail on `master` (the call is not replayed there) and pass on this branch. I hit the bug with a production MCP server that evicts idle sessions after 30 minutes: the agent's first wiki tool call after each pause failed with `outcome unknown and request was not replayed`, the next one succeeded. I have not yet run this build against that server.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** edda708, `cargo` in a `rust:1.98` container (the CI toolchain).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the command output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace `cargo test` was not run: the change is confined to `zeroclaw-tools`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. The replayed call goes to the same configured server, and only after it has proved it did not execute the first attempt.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

prs.title: fix(runtime): raise and expose ping-pong loop-detector threshold
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add `pacing.loop_detection_ping_pong_min_cycles` (default **8**) and wire it
    into `LoopDetector`. The prior hardcoded minimum of 4 aborted multi-tool
    workflows at six A↔B cycles (#11777).
  - When the configured threshold would outrun the sliding window, raise
    `window_size` to at least `2 * (min_cycles + 2)` so Warning/Block/Break
    stay reachable.
- **Scope boundary:** Loop-detector ping-pong threshold + window sizing only.
  No other pacing detectors or agent-loop behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Agent tool-loop pacing; operators can lower the threshold
  via config. Undersized windows are auto-raised at detector construction.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11777

### What this does, simply

Ordinary multi-file read/write loops were tripping the ping-pong circuit
breaker too early. Raising the default threshold to eight full A↔B cycles
gives normal workflows room; the detector also keeps enough history so that
higher configured thresholds cannot silently disable Break.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — covered by focused unit tests.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh `CI Required Gate`
  on `e0ccdd758` once green (`Format`, `Lint`, `Test`).

prs.title: fix(agent): bound repeated tool failures and preserve completed work
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Resolve existing root pacing policy for configured Agent turns instead of forcing loop detection off.
  - Give repeated identical successful results one advisory. Contain repeated identical completed failures with a correction, one final retry, and a recoverable stop that retains completed results.
  - Use the executed tool's canonical identity so short/full aliases cannot bypass the retry budget. Keep approvals, exclusions and cancellation outside executed-failure evidence.
- **Scope boundary:** No blanket duplicate suppression, successful-polling hard stop, permanent blacklist, model setting, context/iteration-limit change, new config key or public API shape change. Standalone builders without full/live config and legacy channel detection keep their behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Both configured Agent APIs and their ACP consumers. Shared tool resolution and history closeout require coverage across sequential/parallel batches, aliases, hooks and cancellation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11484.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded recovery scope is covered by the approved exception merged in #11436.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw runs the model's requested tools and sends their results back so it can decide what to do next. A model can keep requesting the same action even after it gets the same error. Configured Agent turns previously forced the repetitive-tool safeguards off, so that cycle could continue until the general iteration limit.

After three identical completed failures by default, the next model request now receives a correction. The model can change approach or make one final identical retry. If that retry fails identically and nothing else in the round makes progress, ZeroClaw ends the turn with an explanation and keeps every completed result. Extra identical requests in that recovery batch get paired skipped results instead of more executions. A new user turn can retry normally.

An unchanged successful result is not proof of a stuck turn. Successful polling gets at most one reminder and can continue; changing results and successful recovery can continue too. This is a runtime retry policy, not a claim that a network error is permanent or that every model loop can be recognized.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The larger diff is one connected repair. Actual-dispatch provenance, recovery admission and transcript-preserving closeout must agree. Simply enabling the old arguments/names-only detector would stop productive polling and can discard the final completed round. The focused test module supplies deterministic Agent-boundary coverage; the runtime reuses the existing policy, executor and shared turn engine rather than adding another orchestration layer.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Whether a particular model repeats a call is nondeterministic; the focused tests deliberately repeat after correction through the production Agent APIs.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39020947601) passed at `6e7508873e3f0108efdd44173b67a689c643efaa`, including workspace tests, Lint, Format, Landlock, PostgreSQL memory and channel suites. That head merges current master (`bec5a3f04c0b744038ed6114da3ada7df4f6279d`) and updates two recovery/steering tests: mid-turn steering now yields the tool loop after a round (#11725), so each test queues its steering message at the round it exercises. The guarded behavior is unchanged: queued steering cannot restart an exhausted turn, and reentry keeps the advisory and the spent recovery budget.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** A live Woof/MLX-LM turn and complete ZeroCode UI replay were not captured. The deterministic tests reach both Agent APIs, including the streamed entry point used by ACP.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The result below was obtained at `6e7508873e3f0108efdd44173b67a689c643efaa`. Formatting, Clippy with `-D warnings` and comment hygiene were rerun at the same head. Catalogue checks confirmed unique IDs and retention of all four recovery messages and the incoming HTTP-timeout message.

```text
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(agent::safety_net) | test(agent::tool_execution) | test(steering) | test(tree_budget_final_completion) | test(single_tool)'
Summary: 118 tests run: 118 passed, 5682 skipped

cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished

cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

The macOS debug test harness emits a linker warning because its `__eh_frame` section exceeds the 16 MiB compact-unwind offset limit. Section inspection confirms that cause. Linking and all selected tests completed successfully; this is not production-build performance evidence.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected canonical policy ownership, the two Agent callers, private loop compatibility, actual completion provenance, alias resolution, paired skipped results, hook abandonment and append-before-stop ordering. Successful polling, final-attempt recovery, changed arguments, useful work in the same batch, ignored aliases, live-policy refresh and queued steering are exercised by automated Agent tests.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for presentation. This PR changes runtime enforcement, not a renderer or layout; responses and `TurnEvent::Chunk` supply the relevant automated boundary evidence.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** This PR's candidate source, streamed and non-streamed Agent APIs; `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/safety_net_loop_recovery.rs` plus existing safety-net and executor tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `repeated_failures_close_both_agent_apis_after_correction_and_preserve_pairs` checks the full correction in the next outgoing system prompt, four actual executions, preserved result IDs and the localized terminal response. Streaming cases also check matching call/result IDs and the terminal chunk.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A scripted provider disregards the correction and repeats the failure. The turn completes recoverably after its final retry rather than requesting another summary/model round. Sequential/parallel recovery batches execute only one matching retry and pair the extra calls with skipped results.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local workspace-wide tests and Clippy are delegated to fresh required CI instead of duplicating that breadth. No interactive model/UI smoke was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. The guard limits existing repeated dispatches.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Existing executor egress scrubbing is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Fixtures use synthetic tool names and arguments.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Runtime-owned localized correction and stop messages are model-visible. They interpolate no tool arguments, remote error bodies or credentials; evidence retains hashes only. Existing tool output remains subject to the same security and approval policy.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for public API/config shape, standalone defaults and legacy detector behavior. Configured Agent turns intentionally begin honoring the existing enabled pacing policy.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new fields or commands. Existing `pacing.loop_detection_enabled`, `loop_detection_max_repeats` and `loop_ignore_tools` govern the Agent guard. The legacy elapsed-output setting does not delay this failure recovery.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users: No migration. Configured turns use the existing policy; opt out with `pacing.loop_detection_enabled = false` when needed. Canonical ignore entries cover short aliases of the executed tool.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits, or disable `pacing.loop_detection_enabled` in the supported config editor and begin a new turn after configuration reload.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `pacing.loop_detection_enabled`; existing repeat threshold and canonical `loop_ignore_tools` entries remain available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A useful retry is stopped unexpectedly, recovery skips lack paired result IDs, or the user sees a recovery-exhaustion message despite changed completed work. The Agent-boundary tests cover these contracts. A finite retry budget can stop before a later transient network recovery; retrying in a new turn is the recovery path.

prs.title: fix(agent): stop repeated calls before dispatch and retain closeout
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Refuse exact-repeat calls before dispatch after the existing detector threshold, including repeats within a parallel batch. Failed attempts now participate in the detector.
- Preserve advisory handling of equal outputs from different arguments: empty searches and silent commands alone must not terminate a valid investigation.
- Retain every completed tool outcome before closing the tool phase. Reuse the existing bounded tools-free summary path to distinguish verified work, failures and pending actions.
- **Scope boundary:** no retry-limit increase, new remediation authority, SSH implementation, or turn engine. The independent time-gated aggregate-output guard is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** shared tool-loop preparation, result collection and graceful closeout. Disabled detection and ignored tools retain their opt-outs; error-at-cap callers retain a typed stop.
- Closes #11866.

### What this does, simply

When a tool keeps making the same failing request, the old code logs that it blocked the call but continues executing repeats. Eventually it aborts and discards the terminal tool round. This change stops another identical dispatch and lets the agent report the work it actually completed instead of returning only the circuit-breaker exception.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces exercised:** shared runtime used by CLI, web and messaging channels; regression fixtures exercise the tool-loop seams without external services.
- **Setup / preconditions:** default loop detection; a repeatable tool exempt from ordinary deduplication; provider requests identical arguments repeatedly.
- **Steps to run:** run `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::turn` and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib loop_detector`; exercise a mock provider returning repeated calls and a tool returning a connection failure.
- **Expected after:** the fourth identical dispatch is refused before execution at default thresholds, terminal outcomes remain available, and the tool phase ends with a tools-free closeout.
- **Prior behavior:** execution continues after a logged block, failed outcomes bypass the detector, and a later break drops the terminal round.

### How I tested

Review follow-up (f361da7ab): carry the preflight gate decision as a batch-local fact rather than reconstructing it from later detector state; drain already-queued SOP work through the existing authorized driver before closeout; render refusals through the existing Fluent key. Two full-loop regressions cover a hook-cancelled sibling before a refused repeat and a completed sibling that queues a SOP step.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` on changed Rust files: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Added regressions for preflight thresholds, disabled detection, parallel-batch suppression and hook abandonment, repeated failed outcomes, and retaining completed results.
- After recovering the build filesystem, `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::turn` passed: `380 passed; 0 failed`. Includes the provider-boundary regression asserting exactly one tools-free closeout with a visible stop reason. The separate detector suite passed: `28 passed; 0 failed`.
- **CI checks relied on:** new-head CI is pending. Local turn tests passed (380) and detector tests passed (28). The previous head had a dependency-download HTTP 502 before opt-in tests; this revision triggers a fresh run.
- **Known coverage gap:** new-head full CI and an actual channel closeout capture remain pending. Equal outputs from different arguments remain advisory, covered by the retained regression.
- **Visual interface evidence:** pending exact plain-text closeout evidence; no graphical layout change.
- **Tested revision/evidence:** f361da7ab; focused runtime suites and local formatter/whitespace checks. No real-channel closeout evidence claimed.
- **Skipped commands:** no local full workspace suite; focused runtime suites cover the changed loop boundaries while full upstream CI remains pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new endpoint. Yes to one already-supported tools-free summary request on this closeout path, bounded by existing budget, timeout and cancellation checks.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Guard feedback is generated by the runtime; tool outputs remain untrusted evidence. The closeout instruction explicitly forbids retries and unverified success claims, and the summary request contains no tools.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for config and API consumers; deliberately stops repeated unsuccessful/blocked work earlier.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new setting; new localized guard/closeout text.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback:** revert this PR's commit and rebuild.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** existing loop detection enable/ignore settings; no new bypass.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unexpectedly early loop closeout or missing tool outcomes; inspect loop-detector events and tool history.

prs.title: ci(docker): bound arm64 build memory and add a dry-run dispatch to docker-publish
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Legs that build `linux/arm64` now add the same bounded 8 GiB swap that the release workflow gives its Linux ARM64 build (`scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh prepare`, then `cleanup` with `if: always()`). The arm64 build of the `dist` image runs out of memory in its final link. The same Dockerfile leg in `docker-image-pr.yml` was killed with `ResourceExhausted` on #11347's approved head ([run 39040526108](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39040526108)) and on earlier runs with the v0.8.6 `dist` feature set.
  - Those legs also set up Buildx with `max-parallelism = 1`. One job builds amd64 and arm64, and this keeps the two release links from running at the same time. Legs without arm64 keep the default Buildx setup.
  - The `publish` job timeout goes from 60 to 120 minutes. A two-platform leg now builds one platform after the other. The `all-features` Containerfile leg alone takes 41 to 64 minutes in `docker-image-pr.yml`, so 60 is already too tight.
  - Manual dispatch gains three inputs: `release_ref`, `stems` and `push`. `push` defaults to false for a dispatch and to true for `workflow_call`. A dispatch can now dry-run the release legs without publishing anything. It can also rebuild one variant of a release, for example only `dist` for a tag.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the Dockerfiles, Rust profiles, LTO or codegen settings (#11741 proposes per-variant LTO), runner classes, the tag matrix in `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, or the release workflow. The maintainer CI docs (`docs/book/src/maintainers/ci-and-actions.md`) are not updated here.
- **Blast radius:** Release Stable's `docker-matrix` job, which calls this workflow at the release tag, and the tag-push trigger. Both still push, sign and scan, because `push` defaults to true for `workflow_call` and the tag-push path checks `github.event_name == 'push'`. Manual dispatches change behavior: they no longer push unless `push` is set.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11828. Depends on #11347 (adds `scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh`). Related #11741.

### What this does, simply

When a stable release is published, the release workflow calls `docker-publish.yml` to build four container image variants from source. The `dist` variant is built for both amd64 and arm64 on one hosted runner. With the v0.8.6 feature set, the arm64 build needs more memory than the runner has, and the build is killed near the end. That would leave v0.8.6 without a `dist` image.

This change gives those builds the same extra swap the release workflow already uses for its own ARM64 build. It also makes BuildKit run one step at a time, so the amd64 and arm64 links never overlap. It doubles the time limit to cover the slower serial build.

It also makes a manual run safe to use as a rehearsal. Today any manual run of this workflow pushes and signs every image. After this change a manual run builds without publishing unless someone ticks `push`. It can also be limited to named variants.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A maintainer with write access runs the dry run below. The branch must be in this repository, because the build job only runs in `zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None of the product surfaces. GitHub Actions `workflow_dispatch` of `docker-publish.yml` only.
- **Setup / preconditions:** #11347 merged (it has); this branch is based on master after it.
- **Steps to run:** `gh workflow run docker-publish.yml --ref <branch> -f stems=dist,all-features`. Leave `push` unset; it stays false.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Only the `dist` and `all-features` legs run.
  - The `dist` leg prepares swap, builds both platforms and releases the swap.
  - Both legs finish within 120 minutes.
  - "Sign container image", `publish-relay`, `scan`, `scan-relay` and both SARIF uploads are skipped.
  - Nothing is pushed to GHCR.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Do not dispatch `master`'s version to compare: there, every dispatch pushes and signs all four variants and the relay. On `master`, the comparable evidence is the `docker-image-pr.yml` arm64 Dockerfile leg, which is killed on `ubuntu-latest` (run 39040526108).

### How I tested

This has **not run in GitHub Actions yet**. The checks below were run locally on Linux x86_64 against the patch file. The planned Actions check is the dry run above.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None cover it. No PR workflow runs `docker-publish.yml`. The architecture tests `tests/architecture/container_release.rs` and `xtask/src/generate/docker_tags.rs` assert strings in this file; I checked those strings by hand (below) but did not run the test suites.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The memory change only proves itself in Actions. That is the dry run above. Pushing and signing are exercised only by a real release or a dispatch with `push` set.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  # git apply --check, temporary index per tree
  master  8ed287bd4b  docker-publish.yml blob 01cdf944e7
  #11347  7d2bef733d  docker-publish.yml blob 01cdf944e7
  apply --check OK on 8ed287bd4b
  apply --check OK on 7d2bef733d
  # applied on the #11347 tree
   .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml | 83 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
   1 file changed, 77 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
  scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh present

  # YAML parse (PyYAML 6.0.1)
  triggers: ['push', 'workflow_call', 'workflow_dispatch']
  workflow_call inputs: {'release_ref': ('string', None), 'push': ('boolean', True)}
  workflow_dispatch inputs: {'release_ref': ('string', None), 'stems': ('string', None), 'push': ('boolean', False)}
  job publish: timeout=120
  job publish-relay: if="github.repository == 'zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw' && !inputs.stems"
  job scan: if="github.repository == 'zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw' && (inputs.push || github.event_name == 'push')"

  # actionlint 1.7.7 (expression, schema and action-input checks; shellcheck not installed)
  actionlint: no findings (patched)
  actionlint: no findings (unpatched)

  # stems filter: the workflow step's yq (v4.44.3) + jq, run against dev/ci/docker-tags.toml
  stems=''                       -> minimal, default-features, dist, all-features
  stems='dist'                   -> dist (linux/amd64,linux/arm64)
  stems='dist,all-features'      -> dist, all-features (linux/amd64)
  stems=' dist , all-features '  -> dist, all-features
  stems='all' / 'dis' / 'nope'   -> error: No docker-tags.toml stem matches

  # architecture-test strings
  'ref: ${{ inputs.release_ref || github.ref }}' count: 3
  tag-push trigger kept
  relay pinned-tag strings kept

  # pinned action inputs, read from action.yml at the pinned SHAs
  docker/setup-buildx-action@37fe631 (v4.3.0): buildkitd-config-inline present
  docker/build-push-action@1dc7386 (v6.18.0): push, default 'false'
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Release Stable's `docker-matrix` job passes only `release_ref`, so `push` takes its `workflow_call` default of true.
  - `dist_runner_memory.sh` already runs on hosted runners. Its prepare and cleanup steps passed on the `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` legs of Cross-Platform Build [run 39001999557](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39001999557).
  - `stems` reaches the shell only through `env` and `jq --arg`. It is never interpolated into the script.
  - Not verified: that 8 GiB of swap is enough for the arm64 link inside BuildKit, and the runner's disk headroom with the swap file in place. The dry run answers both.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Patch applied to `7d2bef733d` (#11347's merge head, tree `1d64325b`, the same tree as master `bf38521f` this branch is based on); checks above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The workflow itself was not run, because any run of `master`'s version publishes. The dry run above is the first Actions check. Cargo tests were not run; the two architecture tests were checked by their asserted strings only.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Job permissions are unchanged. The swap file is created under `RUNNER_TEMP` with `sudo` on the hosted runner, by the script the release workflow already uses.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. A dry run still logs in to GHCR with the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, as before. It does not push.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

**Please read the push gating closely.** Pushing and cosign signing now happen only when `inputs.push || github.event_name == 'push'` is true. The expression appears on both build steps (`push:`) and both signing steps (`if:`). The scan jobs use the same condition, so they never scan a tag a dry run did not push.

- The release path keeps publishing because `workflow_call` defaults `push` to true.
- The tag-push path keeps publishing through the `push` event check.
- A dispatch with `push` ticked publishes from the dispatched ref, which is what every dispatch does today. Without `release_ref`, the tags come from that ref's `docker-tags.toml`.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the release and tag-push paths. A manual dispatch no longer publishes by default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Product config, env and CLI are unchanged. The workflow gains three optional dispatch inputs.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Maintainers who dispatch this workflow to publish must now set `push: true`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. One workflow file; no state to migrate.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. A dispatch with `push: false` is the dry run.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - In a release run, "Publish Docker Variant Matrix" legs show "Sign container image" as skipped, or `scan` as skipped. Either means `push` resolved to false.
  - "Prepare bounded build memory" fails with "Need 8 GiB for swap plus 8 GiB of build headroom".
  - The arm64 leg still ends with `signal: 9, SIGKILL` or `ResourceExhausted`.
  - The cleanup step prints "Swapfile retained" or "Refusing cleanup".
  - A leg hits the 120-minute timeout.

prs.title: feat(gateway): move plugin webhook admission and dedup into a core ingress
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. **Depends on #11318** (plugin webhook golden frames and CI leg) and **Depends on #11339** (the reservation store move). The branch merges #11339 at `59875788c1`; both show in the diff until they land.
- **Restacked onto #11339 (maintainer decision on this PR):** #11339 lands first and moves the reservation store into `zeroclaw-api` with no behavior change. This PR now uses that store, `WebhookReservationStore`, instead of a store of its own, and keeps the ingress (route lookup, queue admission, the deadline) in `zeroclaw-infra`. On top of #11339 it makes the dedup behavior change described under **Behavior change** below.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Channel-plugin webhook dispatch was split between the gateway handler (route lookup, queue admission, the 10 s deadline) and the gateway's idempotency store (message dedup), both reached through in-process handles. A gateway in another process could reach neither. This moves all four into one core-owned service with a single entry point, so the next PR can expose it over RPC unchanged.
  - `zeroclaw-infra`: new `plugin_webhook` module. `PluginWebhookIngress` owns the route registry, per-route queue admission, the deadline counted from enqueue, and message dedup in #11339's `WebhookReservationStore`, with the same owner, in-flight, rollback and generation-fencing semantics as before. `dispatch(request, cancel)` returns a typed outcome; dropping or cancelling it cancels the worker's copy of the request.
  - `zeroclaw-api`: shared limits and path grammar, the route owner (`PluginWebhookOwner`), a validating `PluginWebhookRequest` (redacting `Debug`; header names limited to what `http`'s `HeaderName` accepts, values to what `HeaderValue::to_str` yields), and `PluginWebhookOutcome`. Routes now carry their owner.
  - `zeroclaw-gateway`: the `/plugin/{path}` handler is an HTTP adapter over `dispatch` with a pure outcome-to-response mapping. The idempotency store keeps only the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay path.
  - The gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store keeps #11339's `WebhookReservationStore` backing, with a store of its own for each gateway run.
- **Behavior change (dedup, on top of #11339):**
  - **Lifetime:** plugin webhook dedup lasts for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run. A gateway restart inside the generation keeps it; a reload or daemon restart still clears it.
  - **Budget:** plugin deliveries get a committed-key budget of their own (`gateway.idempotency_max_keys`), no longer shared with `/webhook` and `/sop/*`. A burst of generic keys can no longer push out plugin keys, or the reverse. The worst case is twice that many committed keys across the two stores.
  - **Key:** dedup keys include the owning plugin and channel alias, so two instances never collide and a path that changes owner starts clean. #11339's pinned unscoped key no longer applies.
  - Tests that pinned the old behavior in #11339 (per-run lifetime, shared budget, unscoped key) are replaced by `plugin_webhook_dedup_state_outlives_a_gateway_router`, `plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets` and `dedup_key_separates_every_identity_component`. #11339's store tests stay in `zeroclaw-api`.
- **Follow-up from the review, not in this PR:** a per-owner share of the dedup budget, #11565.
- **Webhook paths stay out of failure logs (`fc5f3e95b9`, from Audacity88's review of #11322):** some vendors use an unguessable webhook path as their shared secret, and log records are persisted as written. The ingress's `plugin_webhook_route_closed`, `plugin_webhook_reply_dropped`, `plugin_webhook_unauthorized`, `plugin_webhook_invalid` and `plugin_webhook_unavailable` records and the gateway's `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` record no longer carry the path; the owner's plugin and channel alias still identify the route. `dispatch_logs_route_and_worker_failures_by_owner_without_the_path` and `plugin_webhook_bounds_record_keeps_a_secret_path_out` send requests to secret-shaped paths and assert that no record contains them. The gateway's `plugin_webhook_rate_limited` record still logs the path, as on master. #11320 merges the same commit, so #11322 carries it too.
- **Scope boundary:** No other HTTP-visible change: the PR 1 plugin webhook golden frames replay byte-identical. No WIT, config schema, `zeroclaw-plugins`, or `zeroclaw-channels` change. No RPC surface (next PR).
- **Blast radius:** plugin webhook ingress in the supervised and standalone gateway; the gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store (same behavior, #11339's implementation, its own budget); route publication in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/plugin_runtime.rs` (mechanical: routes gain an owner, and the grammar and queue depth come from shared definitions; no new functionality, so no holding-crate exception row is needed for it).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000.

### What this does, simply

When a chat platform calls a channel plugin's webhook, several things have to happen before the plugin sees the request: find which plugin owns the URL, check its queue has room, start a deadline, and make sure a message the platform retries is not delivered twice. That work was spread across the web gateway. This PR puts it in one place in the core, so a gateway running as its own process can later ask the core to do it.

One thing changes on purpose. The core remembers delivered message IDs for as long as the daemon runs its current configuration, not just while one gateway process lives, so restarting the gateway no longer forgets them; reloading the config still does. Plugin messages also get their own memory, so a flood of other webhooks cannot make the core forget them, and each plugin channel's IDs are kept apart. This only suppresses platform retries; it is not a security check, which stays with each plugin's signature verification.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the PR 1 golden frames replay the public HTTP contract byte-identical, and the root e2e test drives a real WASM guest through the ingress.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (plugins gateway ingress)` (gateway plugin webhook tests and golden frames), `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with the real guest, runtime plugin admission tests), `Test` (infra and api units, gateway default-feature tests), `Lint`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-api` alone does not compile on master (its manifest lacks tokio's `time` feature, which `channel.rs` uses); the api tests run through workspace feature unification, as in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `98e1666b31`: this PR on master `a0f70b7925` with #11339 `59875788c1` merged; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
test result: ok. 292 passed ; test result: ok. 331 passed   (api includes #11339's store tests; infra includes plugin_webhook::*)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib
test result: ok. 636 passed ; test result: ok. 653 passed   (includes plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --test golden_frames plugin_webhook   (x2)
test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; fixtures unchanged
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --test golden_frames -- --include-ignored
test result: ok. 12 passed
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e
test result: ok. 5 passed (includes a_repeated_message_id_is_delivered_once_through_the_core_ingress)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime::
test result: ok. 17 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-gateway [--features zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm] --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings ; cargo clippy --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings (all three)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check ; bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh ; bash scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh ; docs quality gate on the changed docs

```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each caught by the new tests: a longer or shorter deadline, the wrong log level, key or alias, dropping `"` from the allowed header-name bytes, removing the header-name length bound, and one eviction assertion. A 256-byte sweep compares the header-name rule with `http::HeaderName` byte by byte.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Log path redaction (`fc5f3e95b9`, head `a63bcc6f89`):** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib plugin_webhook` (17 passed), `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib plugin_webhook` (15 passed), and clippy on `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-infra` and `zeroclaw-gateway` with and without `plugins-wasm` (no warnings). Mutation check: putting the path back into either record fails its test.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace clippy with `ci-all` is left to CI. The comment hygiene gate did not run locally for the redaction commit (this machine's ripgrep cannot load its pcre2 library); CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (plugin secrets stay in the guest; header values pass through as before). The new and moved failure records leave out the webhook path, which some vendors use as their shared secret.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The ingress re-validates every request with bounds that are supersets of what the HTTP layer admits, so nothing new reaches the guest.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for HTTP clients and plugins. Intended behavior changes, relative to #11339 (which keeps today's behavior):
  - Dedup lives for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run, so it survives gateway supervisor restarts; it still starts empty after a daemon reload or restart. In plain terms: restarting the gateway no longer lets a platform's retry of an already-delivered message through.
  - Dedup keys include the owning plugin and alias, so a path that changes owner starts clean.
  - Plugin dedup has its own capacity (from `gateway.idempotency_max_keys`) instead of sharing the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` store; the worst case is twice that many committed keys across both stores. In plain terms: heavy traffic on one kind of webhook no longer makes the other kind forget recent message IDs.
  - Dedup remains best effort: a key can still be displaced inside its TTL once the plugin store is full, and it is not replay protection (the plugin docs now say so).
  - Outcome logs (`plugin_webhook_unauthorized`, `plugin_webhook_invalid`, `plugin_webhook_unavailable`) now come from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook` with plugin and channel alias, and no longer the path. New WARN keys `plugin_webhook_route_closed` and `plugin_webhook_reply_dropped` replace two silent 503 paths. A request outside the ingress bounds gets 400 `invalid webhook` with `plugin_webhook_request_invalid`, also without the path (the HTTP listener's own header and URI limits normally refuse such a request first).
  - Rust API: `PluginWebhookRegistry::get` returns a `PluginWebhookRoute`; `GatewaySupervision::new` takes `Arc<PluginWebhookIngress>` in place of #11339's registry and per-run store, so #11339's `zeroclaw_gateway::plugin_webhook_reservations` and `IdempotencyStore::shared` are removed; `zeroclaw_gateway::IDEMPOTENCY_MAX_KEYS_DEFAULT` moved to `zeroclaw_infra` (no workspace users). Experimental crates.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. No persisted state, WIT, or config changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `plugins.enabled = false` or a build without `plugins-wasm` disables plugin webhook routes, as before.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_*` error keys from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook`; duplicate deliveries after a gateway restart would indicate dedup regressions; golden-frame drift in the plugin gateway CI leg.

prs.title: fix(mcp-builder): support mcp>=2 streamable_http_client import and custom headers
prs.body:
Fixes #1668

### Problem
In `mcp>=2.0.0`, `streamablehttp_client` was renamed to `streamable_http_client`, and custom HTTP headers are configured via `create_mcp_http_client` / `http_client` rather than as a direct kwarg to `streamable_http_client`.

Because `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py` unconditionally imported `streamablehttp_client` at module scope, importing `connections` or running `evaluation.py` fails on startup when installing `requirements.txt` (which specifies `mcp>=1.1.0` without an upper bound):

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../scripts/evaluation.py", line 19, in <module>
    from connections import create_connection
  File ".../scripts/connections.py", line 10, in <module>
    from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client
ImportError: cannot import name 'streamablehttp_client' from 'mcp.client.streamable_http'
```

### Solution
1. **Compatible import:** In `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py`, import `streamable_http_client` and `create_mcp_http_client` with fallback to `streamablehttp_client as streamable_http_client` for `mcp<2.0.0`.
2. **Context configuration:** In `MCPConnectionHTTP._create_context()`:
   - When `create_mcp_http_client` is available, create `http_client` with custom headers and pass to `streamable_http_client(url=self.url, http_client=http_client)`.
   - On `mcp<2.0.0`, pass `headers=self.headers` directly.
3. **Regression tests:** Added `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py` testing import resolution, stdio/sse/http transport factories, context manager creation, and validation error cases.

### Verification
- Ran `pytest skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py -v`: all 5 tests passed.
- Verified `python skills/mcp-builder/scripts/evaluation.py --help` under `mcp 2.1.1` and Python 3.14: cleanly displays full usage and exits 0.
- Verified compilation with `python -m py_compile`.

prs.title: fix(skill-creator): isolate trigger evals and handle Windows and runtime failures
prs.body:
## Problem

Trigger evaluation can report false misses or invalid scores: per-worker command probes compete, select() on subprocess pipes fails on Windows, and unrelated tools stop the scan. Runtime failures also become non-triggers, incorrectly passing negative examples and misleading optimization.

Fixes #556.

## What changes

- Install one real candidate skill at `<temporary project>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, preserving its production name and candidate description. Parallel workers share it; concurrent runs use distinct UUID-based roots.
- Leave caller files untouched. The legacy `project_root` argument remains accepted but is no longer used.
- Reject same-name personal skill collisions, including those under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- Resolve the Claude executable, including Windows npm shims. Read stdout/stderr with portable threads instead of select(). Close stdin and cap probes at eight turns.
- Keep scanning after Bash/Glob and other orientation tools. Match exact Skill names or skill-entrypoint Read paths, including Windows separators.
- Stop the probe process tree during cleanup: `taskkill /T /F` on Windows; a separate session/process group on POSIX.
- Treat error results, timeouts, truncated output and worker failures as invalid evaluations. Abort the batch instead of assigning zero trigger rates. Cancel pending work where possible; active workers finish their bounded cleanup.
- Preserve successful evaluation JSON. Initial optimization failures propagate; later failures preserve completed iterations. Empty and partial reports render correctly.
- Write candidate artifacts as UTF-8.

## Validation

Latest revision: Windows, Python 3.14.

```sh
# From skills/skill-creator
python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
uvx ruff check scripts/run_eval.py scripts/tests/test_eval_failures.py scripts/tests/test_stream_probe.py
git diff --check
```

- **21/21 tests pass.** Coverage includes artifact isolation, exact matching, late triggers, configuration collisions, invalid batch rejection, cleanup and partial-result recovery.
- A real Windows .cmd wrapper launches a Python child; the regression verifies that the child cannot continue after timeout. This test requires process-termination permissions and was run outside the restricted sandbox.
- Ruff passes for the files changed in the latest revision. Whitespace checks pass.
- Tests make no model calls and need no credentials. Instructions and limitations are in `scripts/tests/README.md`.

## Scope and limitations

The temporary project excludes caller-project files and configuration. Queries requiring local fixtures need those fixtures made available separately. Personal and managed Claude configuration is not fully isolated.

The original investigation included live routing experiments on Claude Code 2.1.149. Those historical observations are not a claim about every current version. This revision has not rerun live model evaluation or POSIX integration. The candidate uses the standard skill layout independently of legacy command behavior.

Related work: #794, #996, #1027, #1755 and #1757. This PR combines a real-skill artifact with portable stream handling, full-turn detection and explicit failure semantics.

### Summary
Adds `proofcore-contract-auditor`, an Agent Skill for Web3 developers that performs automated static analysis of Solidity and Rust smart contracts and anchors cryptographic audit proofs onto the public TON Blockchain using ProofCore's zero-storage Merkle protocol.

### What this skill does
- **Security Audit:** Scans `.sol` and `.rs` files for common vulnerabilities (reentrancy, overflow, access control).
- **Data Boundary Isolation:** Explicitly isolates untrusted contract source code as passive data to prevent indirect prompt injection.
- **Cryptographic Notarization:** Generates an immutable SHA-256 Merkle root of the audit report and anchors it on-chain without storing proprietary contract code on remote servers.
- **Safe Execution & Fallback:** Binds natively to `mcp__proofcore__seal_content` if an MCP server is configured, with a safe file-based Python fallback (`scripts/anchor.py`) that prevents shell command injection.

### Verification & Testing
- Validated against the `agentskills.io` standard format.
- Tested locally with Claude Code CLI.
- No root or elevated privileges required.

prs.title: skill-creator: harden eval viewer (script breakout, DNS rebinding, cross-site POST, escaping)
prs.body:
## What

Hardens the `skill-creator` eval viewer (`generate_review.py` + `viewer.html`). The viewer is a local page that renders eval outputs (model-written, so untrusted) and saves feedback via a small HTTP server on localhost. Three gaps:

1. **Script breakout.** The page data is embedded as JSON in an inline `<script>`. A value containing `</script>` ended the block and the rest ran as HTML. Now `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 are escaped as `\uXXXX` in the embedded JSON; it still parses to the identical object.
2. **No Host/Origin check on the local server.** Any web page open in the same browser could POST to `/api/feedback`, and a DNS-rebinding page could read the data back. Now `do_GET` and `do_POST` return 403 unless `Host` is `localhost:<port>` or `127.0.0.1:<port>` and `Origin`, if present, is one of those hosts. Requests without `Origin` (curl, same-origin GET) still work.
3. **Incomplete HTML escaping in `viewer.html`.** `escapeHtml` did not escape quotes and several fields (`metadata.timestamp`, `evals_run`, `runs_per_configuration`, the delta fields, `configLabel`, `run_number`, including a `title` attribute) went into `innerHTML` unescaped. `escapeHtml` now escapes `& < > " '` and returns `""` for null/undefined, and is applied to those fields.

## Testing

Ran the same script against the original and patched files (Python 3 + Node):

| Check | Original | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| `</script>` payload does not add a closing tag | fails | passes |
| Embedded JSON round-trips to identical object | passes | passes |
| `escapeHtml` escapes `"` and `'` | fails | passes |
| Same-origin POST `/api/feedback` | 200 | 200 |
| POST with no Origin | 200 | 200 |
| POST with foreign Origin | 200 | 403 |
| GET with foreign Host (rebinding) | 200 | 403 |
| GET `/` | 200 | 200 |

`py_compile` is clean. The browser page only calls relative `/api/feedback`, so the normal flow is unchanged. A separate read-only review of the diff found no blocking issues.

## Not covered (follow-up)

- A port-less `Host: localhost` is rejected; browsers always send the port here because it is non-default.
- Some other values still reach `innerHTML` unescaped: `r.passed`, `r.total`, `r.errors` in the benchmark table, and `summary.passed/failed/total` in `renderGrades`. They are normally numbers; I left them out to keep this change focused. Happy to extend the patch.
- The same files exist in `anthropics/claude-plugins-official` (`plugins/skill-creator`); I have not opened a PR there.

prs.body:
## What changed
`skills/docx/scripts/accept_changes.py` now returns an Error when `soffice` times out instead of reporting success, and only claims success after checking that the output DOCX no longer carries revision marks (`w:ins` / `w:del` / `w:moveFrom` / `w:moveTo`) in `word/*.xml` parts.

## Why
Defect 1 in #1770: `soffice` operates in place on a copy and the macro stores/closes the document itself, so a timeout leaves the output in an unknown state (possibly untouched, possibly partly processed) while the caller was told "Successfully accepted all tracked changes". `__main__` keys on `"Error" in message`, so the process also exited 0.

## How verified
LibreOffice is not installed in this environment, so the fix is verified with mocked `subprocess.run` plus real DOCX fixtures:
- Timeout (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired`): returns an Error mentioning the timeout, never "Successfully".
- `returncode == 0` but the output still contains `<w:ins>`: returns "tracked changes remain in output document".
- `returncode == 0` with a clean output DOCX: still reports success.
- `_docx_still_has_tracked_changes`: True for each revision marker (`w:ins`, `w:del`, `w:moveFrom`, `w:moveTo`) and for a non-zip file, False for a clean DOCX.
- `python -m py_compile` clean; no new third-party imports (`zipfile` is stdlib).

The macro-setup path (`_setup_libreoffice_macro`) is untouched.
